_childDocuments_.review: Right out the gate, one should be aware that this is a visual NOVEL.I've been seeing a lot of reviews and discussions related to how little autonomy there is in this game and this is fairly common in the VN genre. When they Cry... series is notorious for it, so I don't think SoNY or its predecessor necessarily deserves criticism for that.I enjoyed the previous title immensely when it came out but like many others, I felt that the ending was especially jarring. Luckily, this game offers two distinct "paths" that you can take and I feel like the endings are both very different from each other. The writing is really good and I'm glad that they chose to focus on one single character, meaning they had more time to flesh her out and give her more of a personality and a "voice" than the three fledglings from the previous game.The graphics are very similar to the previous title and the artwork is gorgeous, with nice little details going on in the background of scenes. Likewise the music is somber and impactful and I think it goes well with both the themes and the main character who is a Lasombra.I finished this game twice and I'd imagine that's about as much shelf life this title has. That's not necessarily a bad thing, of course, but be aware of that when you buy it. It's nowhere near as versatile as, for example, Bloodlines, but I think that would be an unrealistic expectation.Overall, I thought it was a fun romp in New York City and it connected to the original story nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the first game of the series, I was super excited to get my hands on the sequel. Unfortunately, it's not as good.⠀The story is quite interesting as it revolves around a strange murder investigation. The main character, Julia, is as badass as you would expect a Lasombra vampire to be. The backgrounds, while being mostly recycled from the first game, are all spectacular.⠀Shadows of New York plays more like a kinetic VN with seemingly insignificant choices that actually matter since they determine which of the two real endings you'll get. The side stories are very short and forgettable. The other characters are not nearly as fleshed out as they were in Coteries of New York.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Eh. It has a nice presentation and I personally enjoy Julia as a protagonist. But it's very short, especially for the price tag, and a mystery story where neither the player nor the character do any meaningful investigating. I also personally dislike the way in which whether or not the mystery gets resolved is determined by your moral choices instead of your ability to find and interpret clues, and, more nitpickingly, how the game objectively labels the 'evil' ending the 'Good End' and the 'kind' ending the 'Bad End', as if you're playing Vampire (or at least Clan Lasombra) wrong if you're not catering to the trite stereotype of being smugly, one-dimensionally evil./EDIT: Changed from Not Recommended to Recommended because this ended up leading me down a long spiral towards becoming an Anarch Lasombra main, lol. My criticism still mostly stands, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A stand-alone expansion to Coteries of New York, Shadows of New York invites you to revisit the amazing World of Darkness and spend a few more bloody nights in V5 New York. The story follows a newly turned Lasombra vampire. That's right you are playing a member of the night clan this time, making this I believe the first time in a video game. Yes true, the game offers minimal gameplay so mechanically it doesn't really make all that much of a difference. Story wise though it allows for some nice extras. It allows for the more prominent role of shadows for instance. Also being a member of this widely mistrusted new addition to the Camarilla does put the player character in the fairly unusual position of the necessary evil. A catalyst for certain interesting dynamics.The game takes place, for the most part, about a year after Coteries. Most of the cast from the previous game is back and we get to explore somewhat what happened in their unlives in the meantime. The familiarity this breeds is one of the game's strongest elements. There is some new characters too, including the protagonist. The biggest name here is easily Katherine Weise, aka Ecaterina the Wise. Yes, the agitator of Prague. Now that's what I call fanservice. The main plot is basically a murder mystery. It's nothing to write home about. The resolution is a tired cliché that has been done to death. At least it doesn't offend. I did quite enjoy the powerplay behind the murder mystery, unfortunately though both available endings underwhelmed me. I couldn't really quite accept either as plausible.The game is extremely short. It can be finished in a couple of hours. It's also pretty far from great. It's no more than passable. If you are not a fan of the World of Darkness setting you may skip this. I'm pretty sure there are much better visual novels out there for you. On the other hand, for the fans, this is the short and sweet kind of experience. I do recommend it. As a fan, I had fun with it and I wish they'll make more. I certainly will keep buying them.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I blew through Coteries of New York in one sitting--a really engaging game, very well-written and with interesting characters. So I was excited to play this sequel but was bored almost immediately. You don't choose your character--you play as the woman on the cover art of the game. She has a very specific personality (the biting, aggressive, i'm too cool for life kind of privileged hipster perpetually judgmental cynic). She provides plenty of un-enjoyable monologues in this vain, while Coteries had a more neutral approach in it's protagonist's writing. I couldn't bring myself to retry and read more after my first death here. I really just don't like the character or the writing this time around. This game feels like it has an undeserved chip on its shoulder and I only played roughly ten minutes of it :-\you'll either LOVE this main character or won't at all. I didn't like her at all. Not for everyone I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of navel-gazing here.  Lots.  Could not relate to the protagonist; I haven’t been a teenager for a long time unfortunately. The story arch has its fair share of arbitrary leaps, and the game fails to build a proper Masquerade atmosphere.Still, it starts with its own feel of neon noir and manages to keep it alive for a while.The last chapters look rushed, lacking the nice faux animated background of the beginning, at least in the story line I ended up with.Fairly short, get it if you’re a fan of the VTM universe, but at a strong discount or in a bundle like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I THINK I understand why many people prefer this to Coteries but I don't feel the same. Coteries was a great introduction to the World of Darkness for someone like me who had no prior knowledge. While the main story was paper thin, getting to know this secret society and it's intricaties was very interesting. And while the main protagonist might not have had much of a pre-defined personality, the characters you met on the way all very much did and their stories were all worthwhile.The protagonist in Shadows does have a personality but in contrast you don't have any influence on it. Apart from the few instances you make choices that affect the ending, non of the "choices" are really choices. Most of the time they are exactly the same. It made me feel less connected to the character, not more. Despite there actually being two endings, the game felt much more linear to me. The narrative was even thinner than before too. I mean, sure, the ending was exciting. But during the game you're getting nowhere and it's only at the very end when everything is suddenly explained. That might make it sound deep and intelligent to some but it's all a farce, just like the masquarade. The previous 6 hours were useless. I'm disappointed. Even though the good ending was satisfying and luckily is was rather short getting there, I cannot recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: -----I don't usually write long reviews for games I'm recommending. Just a - "it's good whadya want?" But this one was something different. And so it's getting a long review. Maybe Julia's journalistic spirit inspired me?----- The soundtrack is beautiful, that's the first thing I want to say. I love a lot of things about this game. But number one. Is the soundtrack. The way it evokes exactly the right feelings, is a stupendous achievement in my opinion. Especially what I am relatively certain was cellos. There is a particularly fantastic piece with cellos, and now I may have to buy the music if I'm being honest, because wow. Whoever composed these pieces went for it, and achieved. (EDIT: I did buy the soundtrack, would like to report that the song that I especially loved is called "Julia's Fate" although there are actually several songs that I just love.)The art is of course gorgeous, but you will know this already if you've played Coteries of New York as it is the same art style, however I appreciate the added frames of the scene in this one instead of how Coteries left you staring at the same pictures for whole conversations. It was a nice touch, and helped frame the scenes much better. And finally, the writing - when it's on point it is incredible. And I mean incredible. There are points in this game where the story devoured me whole. Which is really what you want in a game like this. I didn't even always like Julia, but even when I didn't like her, I was compelled to see what would happen to her next. I finished this game very quickly by my standards because it was a story I just couldn't leave unfinished. -----I believe a lot of people have said it. But it's not reeeeally a game. It is definitely a visual novel. Heavy on the novel. I've played through twice, unlocked every achievement, and read every scene. There are exactly  choices, that will make a difference in the ending. In certain ways this is a step up from the prior game, . But in other ways, it very much took the game aspect right out of it. If you're up for a long kind of melancholic novel about vampires, this is the visual novel for you. If you're looking for a game. Not so much, best to just wait for Bloodlines to drop. The only other comment I'd make is that a little more consideration for Chekov's Gun could have been made in regards to the writing. There was a number of moments where the story has strange breaks for a conversation about opinions on current events. But often these opinions feel irrelevant to the actual story, even though I generally found myself agreeing. If it was more of a game I'd say they're grounding elements, but since this is definitely a novel, I think it really didn't need a number of these things, as they mostly just served to pull me out of the story. -----This, is the most Polish game about New York that I think has ever existed. Maybe will ever exist. I didn't realise when I started playing that the developers were Polish, obviously I realised the protagonist was. I mean, I think one of the first things you find out about her is that her surname is Sowinski. But I hadn't realised the devs were. At the start of the Pandemic I was in Poland, and wound up being there for months. So as the game went on, and there were more and more things ringing familiar to me, I finally went to go see who had written this, and ding ding ding, there it was. There are several things in this game that will be uniquely entertaining if you've spent time in Poland, or around Polish folks.Specifically, it was somewhere around when Julia said  when I had to pause and google some things. (If you have spent time around Polish people you will immediately understand why this phrase sent me off to find who'd written the game.)My only other comment on this entire game is a bit of a ramble, and a bit of a spoiler, so feel free to skip the following:  All in all a good story. With some excellent highs, and very few lows. If you're the type of person that likes to read. This is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first one: 'Coteries of New York', which had great writing and a surprising amount of player choice, but 'Shadows of New York' clearly has different writers and did not come close to the previous writing - which is quite dire since VNs are all about their writing. Reams and reams of trite, rambling monologues that don't progress the story anywhere, with very little player interaction other than clicking 'next'. Scene 1 must have around 50 or more text boxes with occasional player choices limited to saying the same thing using 3 different phrasings. And this was just to learn that you're fired. Eventually the tedium gets too much and you start quick-clicking through just to see something happen. And this is pretty much the same for the rest of the game. Additionally there's no choice to play different characters, and the default 'angry-emo girl' you play is pretty scripted - you don't get to shape your character at all. I think perhaps the writers come from other fields and have never written for games before?
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Coteries, I was genuinely thirsty for a bit more WoD and the recent changes on the Camarilla, Anarchs and Sabbat in NYC. Coteries allowed me to have a "feeling" of decision making, and it felt rather interesting. This game, though, is all about the story of the main character and how she either tries to battle or accept her own misery. Her lines are extremely biased on her own perception of the world, and the little choices there are, are shallowed by the same perspectives.Not a complete waste of time due the nice story background behind WoD brought up to the present day, but definitely not a game I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed my first play through, However I attribute that more to my rampant WoD fanboyism than the quality of the title.Second play through brought to light that the writing is pretty bad, and the fact that as far as I can tell you get 1 (ONE) choice throughout the entire thing.I think the thing that annoyed me the most was the bringing back of the original coterie, leading one to believe that there would be some more light shed on the goings on of the previous title. (the opening of the first title certainly suggested that there was more to that particular story.)Alas, that thought led only to disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's art is good. The locations and characters look absolutely solid, with a little variance for taste. Similarly, the soundtrack is enjoyable, and some tracks have kept with me even after playing. it nailed the atmosphere and the "Visual" in visual novel game.Unfortunately, this is where the other shoe drops. The text box is arguably the weakest part of that game, and that really hurts when you're a visual Novel. Julia, the main character, spends a lot of time in her head and that's not a particularly fun or interactive place to be. The game is chock full of pop culture and media references. Things that may have aged like milk by the time you play this. At times, it can feel downright preachy.The plot and characters aren't necessarily bad, but as someone starting with Shadows, they don't get much deeper then the images you're presented with of them. There's not much here to get your teeth into. The real nail in the coffin is it isn't much of a "Game". The choices are rare and you don't get to really begin making meaningful ones that shape Julia (Traits) until somewhere near the one hour mark, which is a lethal mistake in a four hour game. I wouldn't blame anyone for bailing before getting deep enough.The sad truth is if I want to revisit Shadows of New York, the Artbook and OST are probably going to be more enjoyable then replaying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire: the Masquerade - Shadows of New York is a good game to spend an evening with. On those Sundays where you have all day to relax or those randomly dreary days when any kind of chore feels like too much. That’s when this game will feel just right. Getting both endings doesn’t take long, so it’s easy to play and move on. The main word that comes to mind is: simple. Some parts are good, others tiring. It works as a way to get into some of the worldbuilding involved with Vampire the Masquerade games, but as a standalone visual novel I don’t think it will appeal to the masses.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Years ago, a group of VTM players had a space in the same old warehouse as me in Chicago.  One of them would ride the Green Line, at night, to the warzone that was Garfield Park WEARING A FUZZY TAIL.  VTM is no joke.This game's story is amazing.  It has surprisingly hilarious pop culture reference jokes, and the "deep" parts are believable and well written.  It's beautiful to look at and the soundtrack rips.  I was surprised at how much I liked it.  I'm off to buy that fuzzy tail now...

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you played Coteries of New York, because it's a direct sequel and it's a good book.Notice I said book and not game.  Mainly because there aren't any real choices.You play a Camarilla chick who won't actually consider leaving the Camarilla, and she's a former Catholic no matter what you believe or want.  Her reactions are automatic and not up to you.It's a good read, but it really isn't much of a game.Exciting story, though.  I only wish we could've heard it from a non-Cam perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a very linear narrative set in the WoD universe. If you are looking to get your fill of Vampires the Masquerade content while you wait for Bloodlines 2, and you enjoy visual novels this may a good fit. If you are looking for an immersive experience where you feel like you control the narrative, stay away. More details below.The good:-Beautiful visuals and sound-An interesting peak into WoD universe-Overall very good writing and the story itself was good, albeit not very dynamic-Characters  for the most part are well written, and the protagonist is quite fleshed out.The meh:-The protagonist was very fleshed out as I said in the good section. The downside of this is that it wasn't immersive at all. Personally, although somewhat hollow, I felt like I could define who the protagonist was moreso in Coteries of New York. -The game took about 4 hours to complete with no real replayability; I think the price is pretty meh for that much gameplay.The bad:-This is a very singular narrative where there is very little in terms of branching. Given that the protag's character is so fleshed out though it feels as though there is very little point in your responses.-Unlike the last game, choice matters, but VERY LITTLE. There are a total of 5 questions out of all the dialogue that impact your ending. These choices dont impact your journey, just the very end.-Speaking of impacting your ending, there are 2 different endings and neither are very subtle. I think a spectrum of 3-5 would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: Never in my life did i think i would look forward to play visual novel games but playing with a friend (through screen share) was what convinced me.We voice over characters or thoughts and it's fun to perform it. Thinking about which decisions to choose is also interesting.I'm definitely looking forward to exploring this new genre venue of visual novels with the friend :D

_childDocuments_.review: Despite using the same game engine and artwork as "Coteries OF New York," this is less a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure game with multiple branching paths, and more a graphic novel where you just click the Next button as text spools out. And the text is largely the internal monologue of your only choice in protagonists (you don't get to choose from multiple characters as you did in "Coteries"). She spends most of the game ruminating on how sad and anxious she is, interspersed with a lot of subcultural name-checking and vaguely sociopolitical pablum ("soulless corporations are running the world and that's why no one will publish my poetry").We've all been at a party where This Person corners you and talks your ear off until you validate their coolness. If a first-person experience of BEING this insufferable hipster sounds appealing to you, then you might enjoy this game. On the other hand, if that appeals to you, then you probably are this person already. GOTH KID INCEPTIONPS She's a super-hot, chain-smoking  bisexual New York  vampire who got fired from her writing job at a political magazine because she Asked Too Many Questions. So now she goes home to her also-super-hot girlfriend, to take molly and drink her blood and probably have pillow fights. Also she can talk to ghosts. I'm still not reading her poetry.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the predecessor, but not this one. The atmosphere is there, but the characters are highly exaggerated and feel unrealistic. Most of them are very stereotypical and predictable.There is no real plot: Very little happens and everything is drawn out so much that despite the great atmosphere, playing/reading can feel tedious. Choices seem to matter very little. Lastly, the relationship between Julia and her partner is not for everyone.The soundtrack is good, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows of New York takes place after the events of Coteries of New York and continues that overarching plot of vampire high society scheming in the shadows with the fledglings being little more than pieces on the board. Shadows, in my opinion, is much better than Coteries. How is it better? The narrative is better, the protagonist is more interesting and relatable, and the Lasombra are a far more interesting clan than anything on offer in Coteries. Shadows also introduces multiple endings that are determined by certain choices that end up giving you character traits. The traits themselves are minor but they do contribute to the development of Julia as a character with free will caught in a game she has little chance of winning.All of this said, I would recommend playing both games just to get the full story from multiple perspectives and at multiple points in time. If you have to choose just one I'd choose this one but expect to be in the dark about some past events.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: The game "Shadows of New York" is a disappointing experience because it isn't a game which often give you the chance to choose your way. Most of the time you're just following a linear story like you're reading a book and not play a game based on Vampire: The Masquerade. The protagonist is a character who can easily be compared to Chloe from Life is Strange, the same unnerving attitude which is fun at first but later it's just annoying. Julia acts like a child, and the player can only choose how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ she is adressing her surroundings. In no way comparable to the first game "Coteries of New York." There are a few moments and character appearances that were definitely enjoyable like her embrace, or the reunion with Ecatharina, the Wise. The weakest point are the character portraits that lacks emotion. It doesn't matter in what kind of situation the character or the NPCs are, they always looks the same and that shouldn't be the case in a "Visual Novel."For that reasons I can't recomend that game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, I’m the dumbass for playing this game first before Coteries of New York or playing it as my first ever Vampire Masquerade game. I’m sorry, I was too attracted by the visual of this game or I’m just immune to Sophie's charm from the other game, either way still my fault not the game's.In all seriousness, putting my bias aside of this VNs being a learning curve for me to get into, that I needed to pause and do some research and write some notes in between, it is still a mixed bag game in terms of not having as much agency over your character. I gonna skip ahead, but just know we’re playing Juila who had recently been Embrace into a vampire and is getting used to the lifestyle of sucking other people's blood in the night for a few months. In the present, as Julia was a journalist, she is tasked with looking into the murder of  This could have been the immersive experience in choosing where to investigate, finding clues, and figuring out who the murderer was, but in all honesty, the game was rigged from the start without spoiling too much. Every corner we look into is a dead end and a waste of time, it became less of a murder case and more of proving to ourselves we can outsmart the vampire who set us up. All is determined by the 5 chosen beforehand that come out of nowhere, which would choose how Julia would respond in the final chapter. I was quite disappointed after learning all that after finishing the game I wasn't able to control my character from the start, but more so the game does, it would have been nice to discover that we were set up and choose how to deal with it for ourselves. That's my main criticism now the other stuff. The main reason I’m recommending this game is for its style and presentation. Despite the story being directionless a lot of times, I will thank it for introducing me to the Masquerade series or vampires in general and becoming a fan of it like I never was before. _childDocuments_.review: I've read a lot of criticism regarding this game, which I guess is all fair: it is a bare bones, quite short and linear visual novel with two possible endings. The story is quite simple and takes place during and after the events of Coteries of New York, which does a better job fleshing out the secondary characters and the world they live in, but fails in delivering a satisfying ending after the extremely good expectations set during the first half. Shadows offers two endings, both satisfying, which is a huge step forward. Choices kinda matter in the end, but don't expect a complex branching storyline.Despite their flaws, these games stuck with me. Shadows in particular manages to nail the Vampire atmosphere perfectly, something I haven't felt since the good old Bloodlines days: the soundtrack and artstyle are perfect, the writing is good, the characters charismatic. It's not a masterpiece, but it's just the perfect thing I needed to dive back in the World of Darkness and enjoy every second of it. It might be the perfect thing for you too.

_childDocuments_.review: , the predecessor of , was criticised for lack of meaningful choices and ways to influence the in-game events. It didn't bother me in , because, after the release of , for a long time, there were no new  releases for PC, and I am just happy about any decent  title. So, I took  for what it is — a visual novel — and enjoyed the story. However, if, in , the narration was about 70% of the game, and 30% was interaction, then in  the ratio is 9:1. And that is just too much narration for a video game. It felt to me that I as a player am being forced to follow through protagonist's cringy internal monologues. The previous game was criticised for having only one ending (apart from untimely death on the first night) and that it didn't actually matter what you did or said, the result was always the same. Here you have two possible endings (apart from untimely death on the first night). I got the "bad ending", but, because of the rigid and straight progression, I'm not even interested in replaying the game. The devs have introduced traits, which determine which ending you get, but you get the traits for insignificant and minor choices during dialogues. These choices are so irrelevant to the main story that I find hard to care about which traits I get. I would also say that the trait system is just a poor attempt to mask the lack of player's agency in the game world. ended on an abrupt cliffhanger.  pretends to tie the loose ends from the previous story, but all it does is give false hope. It just revisits some of the previous NPCs and that's it. Not a word about the whereabouts or fate of the previous protagonist.What the game gets right is the dark and hopeless atmosphere of  world. But that's just a flavour. I also need some kind of meaning and development in a story. But I don't see any. The whole story is about helpless young woman who is a victim of the Masquerade. She starts as a pawn and ends as a pawn. The game travels a circle, and, largely, everything stays the same (unless you get the "good ending", in which the protagonist betrays everything she stood for).If I have to describe this game with one word, it would be "disappointing".I could recommend this game only to die-hard  fans who want to explore every bit of work in the franchise.:

_childDocuments_.review: This one is finally good.Shadows of New York is the follow-up of Coteries of New York. You play as Julia, a young vampire who has been looked down upon, investigate the death of a high-up vampire. Many characters from the previous game return and are involved in the main plot. If you play the first game, you will have more knowledge of these characters but it is not necessary. Skipping the first game is perfectly fine since it does not require any knowledge of the previous game.Coteries of New York is a bad game. , I wrote about what problems it has: an unengaging story that hardly involves the MC (main character); too many unnecessary subplots (topics) with the focus shifting too often; inconsistent writing and characteristic; lazy artwork; ambiguous choice description; inadequate clues to pick the best choice; only one ending causing choices meaningless. As if the dev read my review before it is even written, all mentioned issues are addressed in Shadows of New York, making it a genuinely satisfying experience.For starters, the story is all about the MC Julia, not those side characters you care nothing about, which is so great since it addresses the fundamental issue I have with the previous game. There are some subplots in the game, some are kind of like hints of the main plot, some feel like portrayals of New York (or say big city) life. But unlike Coteries of New York shifting focus from topic to topic so often, the main focus of this game is always what Julia thinks and feels and it is coherent throughout the whole game. These subplots serve as a way to consummate the personality of Julia, so I don’t think they are superfluous as the first game. Additionally, some inconsistency is addressed. Despite much fewer use of exquisite words as the last game, the writing is consistent with beautiful and easy to digest language. In both games, different characters use certain tones in their conversations depending on their personalities and social statuses. While the first game has some inconsistency when it comes to tones, this game does not have such a problem. What is more impressive is that even the dictionary (a mechanic that explains Vampire the Masquerade terminology) has the same tone as Julia, just like reading Julia’s note.Artwork is as aesthetic as the last game. With animation added, this time it is much better in terms of number and variety, presenting the scenarios quite well. For choice design, on top of the clearer description, the dev removed the meaningless feeding mechanic in the last game and added the trait system: certain choices will determine Julia’s traits which further determine which ending you have. In this way, the dev made choices meaningful with different endings and worked around the choice design as these key choices are based on your free will instead of provided clues.I actually don’t have many negative opinions on this game. I like it a lot. That said, there is something I think they could have done better.Julia is a typical movie rebellious lesbian character. It is a little cliché, but the dev pulled it off and made her a vivid character.The dev handled two endings in a quite interesting way. This game and the previous game both have superb sound effects. On top of that, this game has a great soundtrack. However, it suffers a minor problem that the music ends abruptly in a few scenes.I like a lot about the sweet conversations between Julia and her girlfriend Dakota and it is my favorite part of the game, but the conflict  between them is not that believable. In my opinion, it is one of the two major weak points in the script.  I mean, I freak out if a stranger pulls this on me, but since they are already a couple, their reactions do not make much sense to me. I watched the referred movie. Why it is creepy and unacceptable in that movie is because of the relationship between the protagonist and antagonist, which is completely different from Julia and Dakota. So expecting a similar reaction as the movie is unreasonable. Fortunately, one ending redeems this flaw by showing a rational and reasonable response, though the damage is already been made.Another weak point in the script is the secret of Katherine in one of the endings. The game never mentioned anything about it in the process, like forgetting this character even exists. But at the end, the game suddenly shows Julia knows everything about it with a rushed and sloppy explanation, which makes no sense.It took me 7 hours for the first playthrough, another 1.3 hours for the second ending and full achievement with most dialogues skipped. I say it is a reasonably long visual novel and an easy pickup to kill time. Shadows of New York is certainly not perfect, but it is an easy recommendation to those that interest in visual novels and Vampire the Masquerade universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it's an improvement over Coteries of New York, animated backgrounds just make the already stunning art really pop out. Characters also look more defined, as if the artist matured into working with VtM material.Music is almost on par with Coteries but feels like it's lost its bite. It's there but it's dangerously close to generic while Coteries made me think I'm playing something Bloodlines adjacent.The gameplay is identical to Coteries, its a visual novel, you read a lot of text and make a few choices here and there. The introduction of traits was a nice touch that IMO replaced character creation quite well. You develop your nosy kindred along the way, always a plus.Storywise, hey, not bad, cute little sequel to Coteries, shows us a side of the Masquerade not many know about. Kindred accountants anyone?If you read this far then you think 'Ok so why did you give it a thumbs down if you like it so much. Well, the reason is quite annoying. Just like the 5th edition this game is based on, there's the inevitable preachy moment to make sure you conform to the current social situation. In this case the story takes a sharp turn into 'Religious country bad. Persecuting homosexuals bad. Religious country bad. BAD.' Yes... we are aware of it. Sure there's people that still live in the 1860's but for the love of Cain, read my pixels.WE. DON'T. NEED. PREACHY. GAMES.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend you to play Vampire the Masquerade - Coteries of New York before playing Vampire the Masquerade - Shadows of New York for more lore of the story and characters in general, but it is not absolutely necessary. Hell, if you want, you can skip Coteries of New York altogether - only if you are already familiar with VtM lore or have played Vampire the Masquerade - Bloodlines before.What I also don't recommend is playing SoNY before CoNY because you might be disappointed. I feel like SoNY does a better job at sucking its players in as the narrative only focuses on one main character while CoNY told everything in a generic point of view (which makes sense, as CoNY feels like an introduction to the World of Darkness). Julia Sowinski is such a strong yet in the shadows character (pun intended). I loved playing as angst-filled Julia but I can see some players not enjoying her "♥♥♥♥ the man and the world" personality. What intrigued me, other than the main character, is the traits system. Certain choices in the game allow you to develop certain traits, which depending on what you choose, will lead towards different endings for Julia that actually make sense for her.The music in this game is great as always, I even put it on to listen to sometimes because it sets the mood well. One thing I would've liked to see is a few more new locations in the game, or more changes to old locations as it felt as if I was looking at the same backgrounds from time to time. However, that's just a small gripe for me. I still enjoyed playing this game and hope the developers do more Vampire the Masquerade-related stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot describe the love I have for this game. I have played through it over and over, and still the story takes me away. It's not really a romance dating sim, keep that in mind, but the novel itself is still phenomenally written and I honestly don't think that it could have been made better. Both this game and the original are worth playing. I just finished the second ending, so I felt it was time to write this review after I have seen everything the game had to offer to me. The protagonist is a lovely ball of gloom, and the art is absolutely stunning. Having a gay character was also a plus for me, just because I'm queer myself. I felt like their dynamic really added to the background of the main character before her life changed, and the writers did a great job at continuing the world building in this game that I saw in the last one. It was nice getting to see the characters again, this time with a set character. The audio in this game is also really lovely. 10/10 recommend for visual novel enjoys :)

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastically uninteractive. But sadly,  uninteractvely fantastic.Although summarizing it with one sentence, a two word one at that, may be unfair. A degree of railroading has to be accounted for with the medium, and that is usually fine. You (better) know what you're going to be dealing with in the CYOA type stories, however sophisticated or slick in presentation. It helps when it's disguised so to keep the illusion of choice going for as long as possible, but in the end, it's a straight road with a few branches if you're lucky.The previous game had more paths along that road, even if they only introduced cosmetic changes, they were still there to make this your story. At least a bit.This time around you're only there to push the "Continue" button and let the story unfold. It might be a good one, but if I'm going to read a book, I'll read a book, don't need it to read itself at me.Disappointed, hoped the studio would be something to watch for. Why yes, Steam, I would.Really wanting to give this thing a chance still, I've just had to click the "continue" icon a whopping 37 times, without being asked for a choice once. The characters chatter on, the events happen, the protagonist drives her own monologue - that's it, I'm out of this railroad party. Not because the story is trash (it might be, don't know yet) or the stakes lacking (seems so, but can't say for sure) - it's because a player is not needed here. You watch passively, and once in a while you can choose between the  path and the main menu screen, because you have to restart.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Clearly better than Coteries of NY, which I strongly recommend you play first, but not ground-breaking. Still, would definitely recommend.PROS: - They kept the dictionary function like in Coteries, which makes the game easier to understand for people new to Vampire: The Masquerade. A fun thing about it is that this time, the definitions are written from Julia's perspective instead of in a completely objective tone.- It has a skip function for when you want to re-play the game or in case you lost your save files.- Gorgeous art, just like in the previous game.- The writing is better than in the previous game in my opinion. It's not just the style that seems better, but the plot as well.  The ending did not feel as rushed as the one in Coteries, and it felt - There are two endings this time, if you don't count the one where you die prematurely, which is not really an ending.- Because there are two endings, it does feel like your choices impact the game more than in Coteries.- Julia is, unlike the plain and boring playable characters in Coteries, a character with a strong personality, with virtues and flaws, that feels relatable and actually goes through some character development during the story, which you influence.- Just like in the previous game, the Camarilla characters aren't always seen as the bad guys and the Anarchs as the good and courageous ones. Each character has their own morals, motivations and agendas, regardless of affiliation. It's a perspective I think some people sometimes fail to approach.CONS:- Just like with Coteries, there is no Save function for saving your progress before taking on a side-quest or making a decision. This is a very big flaw for a visual novel.- Another big flaw for this type of game is the lack of more endings. Two is definitely better than one, but doesn't quite explore all the nuanced possibilities. Three or four actual endings would have suited this game and story better.- Your choices matter more than in Coteries, but not by much. Most dialogue options lead you to the same outcome. I would have at least liked the characters to act and talk differently to me depending on my choices, even if it didn't influence the outcome, but the ending you get really depends on 5 key moments in the game. Any other choices besides those 5 do not have any real importance.- Even those options are very few and far between. It might not occur to you if you're playing for the first time and if you take your time to read and take everything in, but when you replay the game you find yourself holding down the skip button for ages until you have to make a choice. Even if you don't give the player a meaningful choice to make, even an unimportant one like an answer to a trivial question can at least give the illusion of choice to the player. But we do not even get that.- This being a story revolving around solving a crime, we should have had more points in the game where we could try to come up with deductions and theories ourselves that could either be proven as wrong or right, but Julia's answers and findings regarding the crime are out of the player's hands and can't be influenced.- Some character interactions don't make sense. Julia manages to fool and outsmart kindred way more powerful and experienced than her with little to no effort, to which they respond unusually calmly and with too much understanding and patience. This basically acts as plot armor for her in order for the game to move forward.- This might just be an isolated case, but my game crashed a few times, freezing my computer, making me lose my save file and have to start over each time.- You won't recognize a lot of references and characters that show up in the game if you haven't played Coteries of NY first. Shadows of NY essentially takes place after the events in Coteries.Despite its flaws and shortcomings, I would still recommend this game to anyone interested in another VtM game and especially people who enjoyed Coteries of NY in the slightest. Julia is a solid protagonist for her age in my opinion, and the story did not disappoint me. Not a lot of replayability to this game, but it sure is worth playing once.

_childDocuments_.review: At heart, Shadows of New York is a political drama, mixed with some detective suspense. At first, I thought I was in for a pretty boring and confusing time. Political stories have never been appealing to me; I just never manage to understand the story completely. However, this one proved to be the exception. Before I knew it, I couldn’t stop reading. On the days I couldn’t play, I kept thinking about finishing the story, finding out about who did it, and how. The story was clear enough, though I did get a bit confused here and there. See, the game has a ♥♥♥♥ ton of characters. And honestly, this was very nice for a visual novel of this length. It’s not long, but it isn’t afraid to bring into the story as many characters as necessary, full with their designs, dialogue, objectives and everything. There are many characters, yes, but I didn’t feel like any of them were unnecessary. Each of them has their own role in the story. And yet, this only contributed to making the game more overwhelming.Shadows of New York is a game made with the purpose of introducing new people to the world of VTM. And how do I know it is for newbies and not for fans that are familiar with the setting? Because the game has a lot of new terminology, and to help understand it, an in-game dictionary. Every time a new word that is exclusive to the world of VTM appears in the story, a pop-up will appear telling you to check the dictionary, where you’ll find a full definition of the word in question, told by our Julia herself. That, aside from the way the whole story goes, makes it evident that this game is meant to draw new people into the setting. And that’s great. It was really fun to learn more about the world. The problem is that it’s a lot of information at once. And that’s not mentioning how annoying it was to have to pause my reading of the story every time a new term appeared, which happened often during the first hours of gameplay.And this is where the big cast of characters becomes a downside rather than an upside. When you’re trying to assimilate all this new information, you will get confused with a long list of names to remember as well. No matter how smoothly written their introductory scenes are, it’s just a lot to digest at once. So, I did end up having a hard time remembering who was who by name alone, particularly in the scenes where the characters were talking about someone that wasn’t in the scene.The pacing could’ve been a bit slower so all the new information didn’t come at once and it didn’t get so overwhelming, but aside from that, both the story and the narration were amazing. The story makes sense and foreshadows the correct amount; the characters were more than great, and if I had to complain about them, it would be that many of them had too little screen time.  Their personalities really shone in that short time, and they did fulfill their role in the story… But it almost felt like a waste. Many characters that I loved, I barely saw for some minutes of gameplay, and I really would’ve liked some more time with them.First, every character, no matter how minor they are, gets a sprite. And this was great! Some characters had one or two lines of dialogue, but still got one of those amazingly drawn sprites. The art style really fits the tone of the game, too, being some semi-realistic digital painting pieces that imitated oil paint. Sprites and backgrounds alike have an amazing level of detail, and are honestly worth looking at for several seconds the first time they appear on screen, just to really take the designs in.However, while this game’s sprites were gloriously gorgeous, they had one flaw: lack of variety. Because every single character gets a sprite no matter how minor they are, but… When I say a sprite, I mean a sprite. There are exceptions, but the vast majority of character sprites have no expression variants whatsoever. Julia does have three expression sprites, but they are quite literally just Serious, Serious2, and Pissed Off; so there isn’t a lot of expression variety, even with her. It made the characters feel terribly static, and the narrative didn’t always fit the expression on the character’s faces.Aside from the lack of variety in the sprites, I have another small complaint about the art. Think of any visual novel you might have come across before. The disposition of the elements typically consists of a background, a bottom text box taking about a third or a fourth of the screen, and on top of it the sprites of the characters that are present on the scene. This is this way for a reason: It allows for the reader to have all important elements in their field of view at all times. However, Shadows of New York has only one active sprite at a time, all the way to the right of the screen, while the text box is in the bottom left. This has one advantage: the extra space on the top left is great to let you pay attention to the beautifully detailed backgrounds . But it also has one big disadvantage: The two important elements of the game (character faces and text) are literally as far apart as they can be, on the opposite corners of one another. This means you can’t look at the sprites while you read. FFS, the highlights of the sprites are animated and I didn’t notice until I was one or two hours in! How can the game direct your gaze so far away from the sprites that you fail to notice their glowing red eyes?!There were three different kinds of choices: those that mattered (which determined which one of the two available endings I got), those that didn't matter (which added flavor to the dialogues but didn’t actually change anything), and those that added some extra scenes (which took me to different parts of the city, usually to find some unsuspecting victim to feed off of). Despite it not being exactly an innovative system, I actually quite liked it. It kept the inevitably monotone gameplay of the VN fresh enough, which is always a welcome trait.However. This game has one fatal flaw. And that is… being a visual novel made with Unity! //ominous thunder. It’s obvious that that engine doesn’t do Shadows of New York any favors. There are many things that are considered crucial to enjoy a visual novel with multiple endings: multiple save files within the same run, being able to save without quitting, quicksaving, autoplay, a gallery, etc. All things that Shadows of New York doesn’t have, because the engine doesn’t make it specially easy. Luckily, you can skip text, but a good saving system would have saved me a lot of time. Developers: Ren’py exists!I loved the story, the characters are very well written, the MC’s inner monologue is super entertaining, the art is gorgeous, and it definitely did achieve its goal of making me want to check the TTRPG out and give it a try. However, it’s also a game plagued with small flaws that can pile up, that can be annoying for fans of the genre. Still, it’s an approval from me. The good stuff far outweighed the bad stuff, luckily. I’ll surely be checking out the other VN in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Something about Shadows annoys me endlessly. I think it’s because I don’t feel as if I have any control over the main character whatsoever.Lack of substantial player choice (in a visual novel, no less) was already a problem in the first title after it became apparent that choice of clan, dialogue options, allies and so forth had no bearing on the story, but at least that game gave you plenty of flavor choices. In Shadows of New York the protagonist is so set in stone, more often than not, you don't even get to pick dialogue options at all. The game will just roll along, dialogue after dialogue where you do nothing but press the 'next' button to advance the story, sometimes for 20 minutes stretches.That our main character is semi-annoying in all of her try-hard, goth vampire, fanfiction-y glory obviously doesn’t make the lack of input afforded me as a player any less annoying.I realize a set protagonist can work in story driven RPG's - see The Witcher - but that is only if the player is given some agency in how they mold the details of said main character. In Shadows, no such thing is possible. You're just a powerless spectator in a narrative the developers apparently loved so much they decided it was better without my input, and so this interactive novel, like its predecessor, feels like it’s all novel and zero interaction, albeit for different reasons.Because yes, I realize Shadows is supposed to have two endings which obviously implies some amount of choice, but after three and a half hours of scrolling through investigation scenes where the main character does all the investigation, sees all the clues and draws all the conclusions, I simply did not care to even reach them.I actually prefer Coteries, which at least let me pretend I was behind the wheel for a while. Both games are, when scrutinized, all style and no substance, only worth a few dollars or so when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Vampire: The Masquerade and World of Darkness world since 2004's bloodlines and I used to play the TTRPG back when it was reasonable to assemble a group of people to play it. I also like detective stories and studied journalism, so this should be right up my alley. That said, definitely can't recommend it.The art is really good, but the character you play is an insufferable cynical edgelord. And almost everyone you meet for the first two thirds of the game is either boring, hostile, or boring and hostile. You're functioning as a detective, but it isn't a fun whodunit mystery, it's a Sam Spade style noir mystery where you smoke and bumble around and get threatened until the pieces fall into place. There's a dictionary system to help you with the VTM vocabulary, but there's a new entry every couple of minutes. Even with a casual familiarity with the world it felt like a bit much. You also barely get to do any vampire stuff (I think I drank.. one girl's blood?) and you're barely a detective, so what are we even here for?Eventually, stuff does fall into place and you do see glimpses of cool characters (If we met the homeless nosferatu at the beginning the game would have been a lot more fun) and I did enjoy the ending, but it's hard to recommend a three hour game that only gets interesting in the last half hour and then ends.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows of New York is a standalone sequel to Coteries of New York. Both are visual novels, so be prepared to read lots of text.Having an actual named protagonist gives the game a tighter narrative than Coteries overall. It's hard to say whether Shadows is a better game, as it is thematically very different from Coteries. Coteries was about a newly Embraced kindred learning the ways of the Masquerade and getting caught up in vampire politics, in Shadows you're playing a jaded, somewhat bitter character at the fringes trying to make her mark with the vampire elite. She's not necessarily likable (nor is she meant to be), but she is true to the Lasombra archetype: ruthless and cynical.As a story experience, Shadows is more linear than Coteries, but it also benefits from being more focused and somewhat better written too. Though this time you at least have a say in how your character turns out with several key choices that impact the ending. There are a lot of callbacks to Coteries; it's not necessary to have played its predecessor, but your experience in Shadows will definitely be richer for having played it first.Pros: - Your choices actually have an impact to the ending this time, but it's still a very linear game boiling down to two endings.- Soundtrack is pretty good. The Camarilla theme is particularly memorable, and you're given two versions.- Visuals look good, even better than Coteries (which was already pretty good), and there's a bit more animation to the scenes. It's still a visual novel, so don't expect a lot of interactivity,- Your main character is more well-developed than the ones you use in Coteries (but at the same time, less relatable. I'm fine with her character, but she will rub some players the wrong way, especially if you don't like Lasombra clan archetypes).- Nice to see many characters and locales from Coteries revisited.Cons: - You don't really get to do much vampire stuff (no real feeding even)., The game is at heart a detective visual novel with vampires (and vampire politics) instead,- Shadows of New York is very linear. Your actions in Coteries ultimately mattered little past the tutorial, but it at least gave you the illusion of choice.Verdict: if you're new or interested in Vampire: The Masquerade, it's worth getting the Coteries and Shadows of New York bundle while on sale. The soundtracks and digital artbooks are also pretty worth checking out. Each game will roughly take about 3 hours for a first playthrough (Coteries does have a bit better longevity and replay value because there are 3 protagonists to choose from, although their stories will largely play out the same past their opening prologue).
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Visually striking with gorgeous animated backgrounds and strong character portraits, well-written, and with an appropriately eerie soundtrack, this is a character-driven visual novel about conspiracies and shadows, full of vampire intrigue. Playing predecessor Vampire: The Masquerade - Coteries of New York first is recommended but not required. You'll simply get more out of Shadows because a lot of Coteries characters return here.Where Coteries of New York allowed you to choose between three different characters, Shadows of New York is solely about Julia Sowinski, formerly an investigative journalist, now a vampire belonging to the enigmatic Clan Lasombra, masters of darkness and shadows. Your choices influence Julia's overall personality (is she kind or is she ruthless? pacifist or violent? that sort of thing), but she is not a blank slate. I can understand why her overall personality might not be to everyone's liking, but I really enjoyed spending time with her.Honestly, as a big fan of the World of Darkness setting, Clan Lasombra, and rebellious sadgirl protagonists, this is a bit of a dream game for me. The only thing I didn't like was how short it was. If it was 10-20 hours instead, it would've easily become one of my new all-time favourites. Heartily recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a sort of epilogue to the other title in this series - Coteries of New York and I highly recommend playing that one first.This one is a stark contrast to the other game, however, in that it's significantly more railroaded and linear than Coteries. Almost all the options for what you do in your free time is just filler story in between the main story with no consequence whatsoever, and only certain significant dialogue options actually affect anything, with the "trait" system essentially just being "did you earn enough 'Lasombran' personality traits to get the 'good ending'?" so the traits feel a bit less weighted in that regard.Still, even though you're more taking a backseat to steering Julie on her path to becoming the Lasombran Primogen, I still highly recommend it as a thrilling conclusion to the adventures of all the faces you met in Coteries.I guess a good comparison between the two is that Coteries is you making your own character from scratch for a V: TM campaign whereas Shadows is you being given a premade character by your game master. With that in mind, I think you can decide for yourself if this seems up your alley, but I highly recommend it for fans of the V: TM world as it was a very fun narrative to be a part of.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong. The dynamic art style is great (kudos there) and there's a good amount of main character sass. It's good to see female figures having a relationship that is more than tripping over themselves.The problem for me is the story falls incredibly flat. It's do or die. There isn't a lot of room to be your own vampire in this tale. It's a singular narrative that way. I'm a bigger fan of narrative games that give you more ways to differ from the expectation and still find a result. Linear stories don't invoke a lot of empathy into the character perspective I'm reading from.I've got all the achievements after four hours. The changes you make to receive both are pretty much night and day. You can enjoy it for the art and the sassy comebacks, but I just don't think I would suggest this for an in-depth adventure into another person's mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hesitant no. Like the first game, I don't regret purchasing it and I don't regret playing it. But ultimately, its not something I'd particularly recommend.The plot is pretty good, though the specific writing didn't always hit the mark for me. There was an abundance of real world references that mostly came off... unneeded? I really wanted to get lost in the murder mystery and Julia's vampire tale... yet I constantly found myself dragged back into the real world. The devs are legit good writers, but some of it just came off as hamfisted and sloppy.This is all made worse by Julia's personality. She is intentionally aggressive, off putting and cynical.  Half of the dialog choices are either:  - Pick between 3 insults - Pick between 3 statements that all mask an insultThere is like 5 choices that matter in the game, and the rest rarely even branch the dialog for a single line. I really didn't mind the kinetic novel feeling,  but its worth explicitly noting.Probably, my only legit complaint about this game is the saving system... or lack thereof. It autosaves by line and you cannot manually save at any branch. I accidentally hit the SKIP SCENE button while checking a discord message and my only options were to read the journal entry... or replay the entire game. That definitely killed the mood.I don't want to sound too harsh about the game because I did still enjoy it. But you have to know what you're getting into.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I got this after I had a lot of fun playing Coteries. It satisifed my itch, but there was definitely a drop in quality. (there are some spoilers here)The biggest problem was that I thought I was being jerked around for most of the story.1. Your character, Julia, is toxic and aggressive. You don't have any choice to have social grace, and she starts and escalates conflicts that drive part of the story without player input.2. You have little control over what happens. You're Embraced, just to turn into a low-level representative for a clan no one likes. You're forced into conducting a bogus investigation where everyone intends for you to fail.The game tells you where to look, what to say, and even what order you investigate the suspects in. I think it would make sense that the decisions you make during an active investigation would contribute to how much evidence you get/what you find out. There's a bit of dialogue earlier in your investigation where some one insults you for being foolish during the investigation, but, like, you didn't actually have any control over how the investigation went.There are a couple of opportunities where you get free time to have an interaction in some part of of the city that doesn't get followed up on or affect the story in any way.3. The ending. This is sort of an extension of 2-basically, certain choices you make in the game will give you traits, which will affect whether or not you get a 'good' ending, where you stand up against the facade and use your investigative skills to leverage into a high-ranking position in the Camarilla, or a 'bad' ending where you don't, and leave town with your girlfriend. This seems neat, but-The decisions you make, as I mentioned above, don't really affect the story. You're defining your principles based on how they affect isolated incidents; in one situation, you get a trait literally just by affirming or denying your loyalty to the Camarilla. At the same time, if the player doesn't know this, they'll make decisions based on what one would think is honestly most helpful to the investigation, not knowing how it affects the ending.-You don't make this decision. The (arguably) most important decision the main character makes isn't up to the player, but pre-determined by actions that they took previously. 4. Some parts of this story, specifically related to the vampire stuff, just didn't make sense to me.-Why does a former Sabbat clan that's obsessed with controlling the weak have a problem with Thralls? Strictly for story purposes, so the protagonist can have a girlfriend who leaves her, and someone for the Camarilla to hold against her in the ending. I've also seen from VTM:B that thralls are generally pretty happy with their situation, involuntary as it may be.-The COVID stuff. It's mentioned, but there are only unrelated uses of masks, and there's no concern for being a creature that literally sucks the bodily fluids out of people to survive (in VTM:Bloodlines, it was established that vampires could cause a pandemic with viruses that don't personally affect them.) There's even an interaction with Julie from CoNY, who's known for having good blood and just lets any vampire she sees feed off her.-Certain feeding interactions here made me a little uneasy. Specifically, the one where Dakota (Julia's girlfriend) doesn't want Julia to feed off of her, and keeps on making excuses for why she doesn't want to do it. Julia thinks to herself that Dakota really wants it, but is making excuses so that Julia will take the initiative. Dakota gives in, throwing her arms up, after Julia says that she wants to do it raw, or without Dakota taking drugs.The interactions between Julia and her girlfriend seemed sexual to me, and so this interaction seemed analogous to one person pressuring another to have sex with them until they finally gave in. The fantasy element doesn't really help here: Julia is supernaturally powerful and can literally force humans to submit to her through Domination. There's also the complication of Dakota's health (one of her excuses is that feeding will contribute to her iron deficiency), and that Dakota often uses drugs when feeding so that Julia can get high.Thoughts that I had about this scene made me want to look again at other feedings, where I noticed that there were all analogous to sexual interactions: Julia takes an overly-drunk Tinder date (she's completely sober) into an alley and sucks his blood up, or goes to a club to find 'Diva's Delight', the Julie from CoNY hanging around a nightclub just waiting for a vampire to feed off her (which I think is much better, for the record.)I understand that vampires are predators, and that by their nature they cannot tell people that they want to feed/the ramifications, but I think a line was crossed there.Even though this is a visual novel/I don't really expect them to make changes, I like to tell people how they could improve. Going off of the numbers above:1) Julia could just be less of a jerk, and have options to be nicer to people. The blood mechanic from CoNY combined with limited feeding opportunities could have the player forced to pick between feeding to be kind to have better interactions/get more out of people, or advancing their investigation in other ways.2) Much more control over the investigation. You could pick what order you investigate the neonates from CoNY in, and the player's choices would impact how much evidence they got in their investigation. The trait-defining moments could impact whether a player receives crucial information in addition to changing Julia's behavior. The moments you have for free interactions could be used to follow storylines that would improve your relationship with your girlfriend, allow you to feed to use power/retain humanity, or help your investigation in some way, all while being interesting in their own right.3) You decide how you want to handle the presentation of the findings, with a combination of the evidence you found and the traits you've picked up impacting how the Camarilla reacts. Being particularly crude or dishonest, for example, might help you pick up evidence, but will make it more difficult for the council to trust you. A combination of allies and strong evidence will be needed to get everything you want from this.A player who doesn't want to press the issue will still have to make friends and show a relatively competent investigation to fulfill their role in this scheme and be left unmolested.4) I think these would be pretty easy to change.-Dakota can be your personal secret, a human who's aware of vampires but useful to them/generally left alone like Julia or that weird businessman Adelaide sends to you. If you're forced to 'take care' of her as a concession, you could make her into a thrall as an alternative to killing her.-A greater prevalence of masks to prevent spread, as well as some dialogue/decision-making to prevent COVID, in addition to some degree of Dakota/other vampires getting mad at you if you don't take the proper precautions.-I get the sense that this interaction might be part of the decline of Julia/Dakota's relationship. There could be other ways that their relationship breaks down, or the decision to feed could be voluntary on the player's part.I would have felt a lot better about this if Dakota mentioned "You keep pressuring me to let you feed when I don't want to and I tell you that it's hurting me" during their argument to highlight that this was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing to do. On a side note: Women who smooch other women don't get a lot of happy endings in media, and the issues that Julia & Dakota have aren't, in my opinion, so compelling. It would have been more pleasant if they were happier with each other.TL;DR/to conclude: If you're a fan of V:TM, I think this is worthwhile. If you're a person who has to look at the reviews to see if you want this, I think your money/time would be better spent elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the first game this is a lavish production with incredible art, atmospheric music, and a beautiful dynamic background system. I only wish other visual novels were as well produced.Unfortunately, that's where the good ends. The game feels like a step back from the first through being almost entirely linear far more than its predecessor, with few choices of side-content, and that content never tying back into the main story. The feeding system is also seemingly abandoned and your powers a seeming irrelevance. It attempts to rectify this with the traits system, where choices you make predetermine things that happen later, but it culminates in another deeply unsatisfying ending and doesn't come close to making up for the lack of impact you otherwise have.It commits the ultimate sin of being an investigative story where nothing except the last 15 minutes matters, and the key discovery happens off-screen and is something you character knows and you don't. It was further let down by trying to reveal a twist, but I was at an utter loss what the author was trying to convey and had to look it up in the wiki. The game has a dictionary to explain universe terminology, and then decides to stop using it at this key juncture.Ultimately, if you didn't like the first game you probably won't like this either. While the first ends in an unsatisfying way, I enjoyed the journey and shaping my own story, but here I was too much a passenger.

_childDocuments_.review: If you bought Coteries of New York, then you probably already bought this. But it is worth knowing that Shadows of New York is much shorter - 4 hours to finish, instead of 7 or 8 hours. It's also feels more like a novella in which your responses don't really matter much, even though the marketing claims it does. It's a lot of click-and-read, not a lot of decision-making or options. Overall, it's atmospheric and neatly captures the vibe of Vampire: The Masquerade and its clans of vampires. But it's a little overpriced for a game which only lasts 4 hours and has limited replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick initial impression. I like the "Darkwave" tone the devs put into this game. The soundtrack and the sound overall is good, captivating and so much better than the previous game. I get lost in the ambient music of this one. Also the level of story detail so far has been great even though it kinda feels like reading a book with a few choices (I am still loving the ride). I love the emotional roller-coaster in the beginning and the sensual "transition." I feel that I can relate more with the protagonist of this game. Way more than I did with the 3 options present in Coteries of NY. I have a feeling I'm going to enjoy this more than the previous game. Lastly, having more than 1 ending and your choices actually mattering is a welcome addition (choose wisely or pay the price, literally...). Definitely worth the price imo for any WoD or VtM fan. ....editAfter ending the game and achieving the "good ending" I have no idea what happened to the fledgling I got to play in Coteries of New York. Still it did tie some lose ends and man what a ride. I love this game. Just wish I would have gotten to know what happened to the player character of that game other than being told that it just disappeared. Still amazing game!

_childDocuments_.review: Recently played Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York, the recent visual novel/adventure game. Have some thoughts on it - which is a follow-up and/or sequel of sorts to Coteries of New York, by the way - so here we go.You play as Julia, who recently got turned into a vampire and found herself in this new life as a vampire. You are trying to navigate this new life, as you were a journalist when all of this mess went down. You wind-up having to investigate a whole bunch of incidents, which may or may not be related, to you losing your job - and also a murder that happened to someone important to vampires. Something's not right, as it feels like you were set-up into this position - but regardless, you're to figure out what happened, why, who did it, and all of that good detective stuff.In this game, you'll mostly be doing lots of reading of the really well-written prose and looking at the nice hand-drawn style art here, which do have some moving backgrounds and whatnot. Regardless, the writing, story, characters, and dialogue are the reasons to play and read this game, as this is what this game does best. There's some sound effects here & there and the music's really good - but that's really about it here, as there's no voice-acting here; not that this game really needed it, TBH (To Be Honest).You will make decisions here & there of who to meet; what to decide when decisions come about; and things of that sort - but that also doesn't feel like this game's main draw here, as it's more about the story being told here, in which that story's quite good.Like the previous title, when in dialogue, there's plenty of Codex to read and learn about VTM (Vampire: The Masquerade) type of terms, lingo, Lore, and whatnot - so just like Coteries, these two titles can be really good for players to learn a lot of the Lore & Codex stuff related to this franchise.While Steam's hours of a little over 1 hour or so here won't line up w/ mine b/c I did play a good portion of this while offline, it did take somewhere b/t say 3-4 hours on my 1st playthrough. In some ways, it is an improvement of Coteries - yet in others, it feels like there might be less choice and options (or illusions of so-called "choices"). I'd have to replay it, to see if there was much changes in the actual journey & the final outcome.B/c I'm not sure on the actual replay value and b/c of the lack of length of this title b/ of its brevity - if you can get this cheap, on sale, and/or in bundle, that would be the best way to probably get this game. Certainly worth playing, if you can do so - especially if you like VTM; vampires and their politics; and/or visual novels/adventure games.While I do wish there was more choice or illusion of such here - regardless, even despite its brevity, I did really enjoy my 3-4 hours or so spent with this & I was certainly more satisfied w/ the ending I received here over Coteries of N.Y.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly tried to give this a fair chance (about three times I started over), but I simply couldn't make it past the bloated edgy pick-me-girl writing style. On top of that, if someone actually managed to relate to the overbearing, navel-gazing, abusive, absolutely entitled hag of a main character, let me give this woman/man a medal.Compared to the first game (especially right after finishing it four times), this feels like some garbage Mary Sue Wattpad fanfiction. It didn't feel honest, hating on it without finishing, but when the main character (yet again) pulled an unnessesarily complex string of insults out of her ass in an attempt to casually pick on an NPC, my frustration got the better of me. No one, I promise you, no one in real life speaks that way.A special stab in my heart was Qadir, who in the first game radiated menace and danger, but as you progressed, slowly softened towards you. It was beautiful. Here though, Julia just straight out calls him an ass kisser in the first ten minutes of the game and he is fine with it.And it’s not the only occasion when Julia gets away with calling names, insulting, or straight up abusing other characters. Considering she is a newcomer, and almost all the rest of the NPC’s are well known to those who played the first game, she becomes really annoying really fast. It's just embarrassing. There’s one word to perfectly characterize this game: a disappointment.
