_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a very mixed bag of a side scrolling action game that's based on classic side scrollers like Contra and Strider, alright then the story. In the not so distant post-apocalyptic future of America a young boy loses his parents to a would be despot, now having grown up he vows to get his revenge against the evil despot and his underlings. So then the likes, well the graphics are really good very beautiful with an incredible use of color, detail, character designs and backgrounds that feels like a homage to traditional side scrollers like Contra: Hard Corps and it’s an absolute joy to behold.The levels are really good each one quite diverse with interesting scenery that just makes you want to stop and stare at it all and see all the detail and colors. The enemies and bosses are really good, each one has their own unique designs that does not feel like it would be out of place in a Strider game. The music is fantastic with very good soundtracks that fit the game very well. The story was good, a pretty simple get revenge on the bad guy story nothing too complicated. The gameplay well I'll get to the problem with it in the dislikes but the positive of it, I did like the idea of the grappling hook and the electric whip was a cool weapon.So then the dislikes, the gameplay is god-awful, stupidly hard and complete bunk, now before anybody comments I should get good I played plenty of Souls like games and other games that are inspired by Contra and Strider and those games felt a lot fairer than this. The game just throws way too much at you even on normal difficulty and a lot of enemies, bosses and even some levels are extremely cheap, especially the final boss. Normal should not feel like extreme hard mode were it gets to the point where it's not fun, it's just torture.I mean there's a reason why a lot of indie games inspired by Contra and Strider or hell even Contra its self turned down the difficulty and I know this game is short, but it doesn't have to be bullcrap difficult. I also feel like the grappling hook was not really utilize that well, I mean there were some segments where it was quite handy but those were few and far between and it could be difficult to use a lot of the time, like during the first level there's this elevator shaft were supposed to get up, but every time I tried to hook on something it wouldn't hook and I just fell to my death, seriously that was just a really painful experience to try and use the damn thing.I also wish there was a way to skip certain cutscenes especially the cutscene for the final boss because after dying to him like 20 or 30 times and seeing the cutscene repeat over and over again that was really, really frustrating.Okay now that I said all that Steel Assault is a very mixed bag of a side scrolling action game that's based on classic side scrollers like Contra and Strider, it has really good graphics, really good levels and really good enemies and bosses.But ultimately what really hurts this game and prevents me from giving it a thumbs up/recommendation is the gameplay, again normal mode should not feel like hard mode/extreme mode. But if you do still want to get it I suggest getting it when it's on sale to save a couple bucks and also playing it on an easier difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: From my perspective, Steel Assault is a very fun solid platformer, with a clever balance of mechanics, that has the added perks of superb music and visuals on par with some of the best of the 16/32-bit era (or GBA/NDS catalog). As a child of that era, I don't doubt for a second that I would have burned through several weekends on repeated rental copies as a kid, and immediately yanked any Steel Assault action figure I could find off the shelf. I finished this game wanting more, but loved every bit of what was there at the same time. (For real, some of these sprite designs are really dang good!)However, while I enjoyed this game, its high bar of presentation definitely puts it in an interesting place right now. The presentation is so good, that after watching a couple minutes of footage, you might find it very easy to project on to it whatever aspects you might imagine for your favorite retro action platformer. Some of us might take a glimpse at this game and expect lots of MMX-style upgrades, others might expect Rondo-style branching paths, and others might expect Contra/Ninja Spirit difficulty. I think this game does the smart thing of only checking the boxes it felt was appropriate for its own design, but unfortunately that means some people will naturally come in feeling very excited, but leave very disappointed for a wide variety of reasons that may or may not seem fair.A particular substantive criticism revolves around the game's current length. Much like older titles, Steel Assault's length definitely favors its harder difficulty settings. Again, as a child of the early console era, this is pretty much what I expected coming in, so I only view it as a criticism as far as where I feel it may limit the game's overall potential. Without the challenge provided on harder settings, this game unfortunately doesn't have enough length to feel quite as epic as some of the best 16-bit classics, like say, Contra Hard Corps or Castlevania: Bloodlines. However, if you're coming in with more of a classic NES level of expectations (think Batman NES), then you should leave more than happy after finishing a run of Arcade Mode.I'm glad I attempted my first run on Expert, because after spending close to a half-hour dying on the 2nd level, it helped me appreciate just how much easier my follow-up run on Normal really was. I'm looking forward to attempting Expert again with more time and some prior game knowledge, and I think that's the type of mindset you need to have for this game to feel really satisfying right now. Let it be known, this game's Normal mode settings and below are for the crutch, not the clutch!I hope the developer will consider some content patches down the road though. There is a lot of really fun stuff in this game and I would love to see even more creative ideas handled using the game's current wealth of stage assets and gimmicks. At the very least, adding a Boss-Rush mode (including mid-bosses), as well as a scoring system, would seem like a no-brainer!

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a really fun and challenging sidescroller game where you are a cyborg with an electric whip and punch as your means of attack. You make your way through each level, of which each has multiple sections until you reach the level boss at the end.The gameplay feels excellent when using a gamepad, everything is very responsive and tight. It's super fun to play and the action is top notch. Enemies can shoot at you and you can destroy their projectiles in mid-aid as long as they are not flashing, otherwise you need to dodge. You can also do a slide dodge for a short distance.Most importantly, you also have a zipline just like out of Sky Commanders and this is necessary for certain parts of the game and to defeat certain enemies much easier. It's very fun using the zipline.The levels all flow together perfectly and have incredible pixel art graphics that are great to look at as you play. This all feels like a brand new top tier SNES game or Sega CD game.The only downside to this game is how short it is and how short the levels are. While each has multiple parts those parts don't take that much to get through. The entire game took me 1.5 hours on normal difficulty but the end boss was so hard I couldn't beat him, I lost over 40 times. Eventually I had to restart and run through the game on an easier difficulty, but after that I destroyed him and saw the end of the game.Amazing game for sure, I would definitely say it's worth a play for sure. I hope they make a 2nd Steel Assault.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I would highly recommend buying on a sale. You only get about 6 levels to go through, and as much as I love the background, the graphics pops like eye candy. Pixel art perfection, and the game's presentation is outstanding. Still, this game does fall a little bit flat in some other areas. Wish there could be more than one character to choose from, different weapons to choose from, health upgrades. One of the few things this game has going for it is that it looks great, and it's incredible representation of a truly retro inspired game made for fans of arcade like 2D platformers with fast-paced action. If you choose to play on the Normal difficulty, you'll be able to finish it within an hour. The bosses in this game are not so challenging, except for the final boss (that was really fun).  I tried the hardest difficulty in this game, and that is unforgiving. One death, and it's all the way back to the beginning of the game. How are you suppose to get through 6 levels without even dying once. That's masochistic. Hopefully I can tackle that challenge on another day. But for now, I do recommend this game but wait for a sale drop.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a short, yet action packed roller coaster, made for people that enjoy old school challenging retro 2D platformers and arcade games. I get a strong feeling that the developer wanted to make a difficult game that recreates the arcade experience of playing near perfect trying to 1cc, since Expert mode doesn't have checkpoints, and Arcade mode only has 1 life. HOWEVER, for those that are not super hardcore into playing perfectly, they have Very Easy, Easy, and Normal difficulty modes which balance the experience to your tastes. I do wish there was one more difficulty mode that was in-between Normal and Expert, as I would like to play with the added challenge of Expert mode (take more damage and other slight differences), but without the try hard nature of no checkpoints so it would be easier to gradually build skill for Expert and Arcade mode.Overall, a fantastic game, and I hope they make a sequel!

From what I understand the game is super short so it makes me think the difficulty is to cover up for it's short length. Well Bleed 2 is short and can be challenging with of being BS so I actually replay that...you know what I am going to replay Bleed 2 and you should buy Bleed 2 instead

_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a wonderful arcade experience that's easy to pick up and play. I consider the game length to be a benefit - it's honestly the perfect length for just taking an afternoon to replay it, something not true for longer games. I'll probably end up spending more time with it overall than many longer games just because the barrier to replaying it is so low. Its time is also well within the standards of 90s arcade games.The gameplay itself consists of adrenaline-pumping boss battles and gorgeous pixel art. On top of that, the movement mechanics make Steel Assault a really unique experience, even within the well-explored arcade genre. It turns vertical levels into acrobatic wonders of exciting gameplay. I love every second of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is the only new game I have genuinely enjoyed through start to finish and been satisfied with purchasing it.Among the sea of "roguelite" "metroidvania" convoluted narrative indie trash, Steel Assault ironically stands out as a traditional arcade-style platformer with some of the best visuals, THE best soundtrack in the business (with 2 versions, both of them fantastic) and not a single unenjoyable level or boss fight.It is sadly incredibly short even with replaying on Expert and Arcade difficulty, especially if you're competent in Contra or Mega Man X styled games. This makes it a hard sell for £12 but I believe it's well-worth the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me a lot of 90's arcade platformers. The pixel art is really good and the controls feel very responsive.There were some aspects I thought were flawed: some levels are so busy visually it can be hard to quickly identify where the enemy projectiles are, I think the grapple mechanic underutilizing overall, and some bosses can feel overly frustrating (the last boss in particular). The game isn't very long, but it feels right for the genre and there is replayability in trying higher difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo short, so little content. I've beaten this game on normal mode (2nd hardest outside of arcade) in under 90 minutes). And all that because the game has reasonably challenging bosses. A good player could finish it in literally under an hour.There is a whole dedicated mechanic of replenishing the sub-weapon's charges by hitting enemies up close. But there is only one sub-weapon in the whole game! There are 3 pickups in total: health, shield and the electric sub-weapon. This feels really underwhelming for a game with such a price tag. Same money could get you (at least in my region) games like Axiom Verge, Cyber shadow, Dead Cells, Cuphead.. Heck, you could get Hollow Knight for about the same money (even outside of the discount season)! Yes, some of those are metroidvanias with inherently more backtracking and time consumption but even outside of that they seem to have much more work put into them and provide so much more meaningful gameplay time.Don't get me wrong, the presentation, the polish of what is already in the game is great. But it's still so little.I'm not refunding it, because it's still kind of a good game but boy, I can't help but feel disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way to short and feels incomplete for the price. Over before it even starts. Refunding this. It is a shame because they were working with something great. _childDocuments_.review: This game is perfect for what it sets out to be, which is a love letter to the 16 bit era, especially Genesis stuff. I've played literally every Genesis game ever made, and this'd be perfect in that library.Good style, the presentation is nearly immaculate (though the flashing can be a bit much). The game itself may be simple to some. I think it's worth the 15 bucks, but I beat my first playthrough on Normal in 45 minutes. Good length for what its trying to do, and better short than way too long. The story is also very simple, fitting in with the classic 16 bit style. I would have liked more characterization of the bosses? But that's okay.One thing that got me during the game though, was that I wasn't quite sure where to grapple sometimes? Specifically in the bosses. The deaths are VERY forgiving, so it wasn't FRUSTRATING, but I literally did say out loud "what does this game WANT from me?" in the 2nd level boss, until I found a weird way you could grapple the platform that wasn't exactly obvious. PROBABLY just me being an idiot? But, could be frustrating to some.TLDR: This game is a mashup of Castlevania and Ninja Gaiden, with some Contra thrown in. It's pretty good. The music and art is absolutely pheonominal. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sick game! Great level and boss design. It'd be a great way to practice difficult sections for that 1cc.- I'd like to be able to skip the dialog, end stage/chapter start screen, and the VS screens. They're super slick, but I'd really like to get straight to the action after seeing them a few times.

_childDocuments_.review: I can only say Yes or No, so I'm going to say no. The game is okay, but There is no reason for it to be 4:3. The "retro" thing is fine, but even games like Shovel Knight go for modern aspect ratios. This is probably the least big deal out of everything. The game is short, but it's also an arcade game. That's fine.The real problem lies with how the difficulty works. A lot of reactions required to do certain task are insanely fast. If you are doing anything when you need to react, the character actually is not responsive enough for you to do so. Also, to make it "harder" a lot of things follow you, so if you react, but you do so TOO FAST, you will lock yourself into a position where the boss is going to track you towards, instead of where you were. Also, a lot of the difficulty in the level comes from things appearing from nowhere on the screen and hitting you with no warning or indication. To top this off, the game is so visually busy half the time it's hard to even see anything that is an indicator on the screen. They will paint the screen red, then give you a red indicator and .5 seconds to find it on your screen. In the end, you will just memorize the sound and go through a memorization motion. If you are a die hard arcade game fan, this game is okay. It's honestly far more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than most arcade games I play like Metal Slug or DoDonPachi, which are both really hard but never feel like utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like this, but I'm a masochist so I will keep going. I don't think for a normal player anything offered is compelling enough. Maybe if the screen was less visually busy, but alas.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is an absolute piece of art, there's no doubt about it. This goes beyond gorgeous visuals and a banger OST - this thing truly captures the essence of nineties' shooters at their best, cleverly hiding modern game design under retro look&feel. The level design is generally more thought out and balanced, there are no blatantly unfair or frustrating things to be found, and the controls are as tight they ever were. For me, these things already make up the asking price. Now, the game is not without it's problems, though. People tend to complain about the amount of content. That criticism I don't agree with. Most people complaining about that have played the normal difficulty through in a couple of hours and feel the game is through. But as the devs have explained, the real game is the hard mode. I'm pretty sure most of us will NOT clear that on the first sitting, and there's plenty of game left after normal mode playthrough. But alas, the execution of the hard mode is where the problems begin for me. I like the difficulty, I like the challenge - but man, one life no checkpoints within chapters becomes dull pretty soon when you can consistently run the level not getting hit once but then die in the boss battle. There is no reasonable game mode to practice the bosses on, and in 2021 I won't be repeating the sections that I have mastered ten times over to practice the boss section. I'd propose to have a game mode where you could practice boss fights separately of the main game.And a bonus complain point.. what's up with not having xInput mappings out of the box? I have tested three different xInput controllers, and none were recognized by the game. Basically I had to do Pad -> KB mapping in Steam myself. All of these controllers work in all my other 50+ Steam titles, so that's pretty embarassing achievement in 2021. I can help you out with this one: X=whip, A=jump, B=dash (yeah, add a button for dash), Y=zipline. Otherwise, I totally recommend this title for everyone with an itch for 16bit blast from the blast.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10You can tell this game was made by people who don't just love 16-bit games, but they know what makes those games good. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. I have some gripes but I'll start with the (really) good.Pros:1. Amazing pixel art. This game do be gorgeous. It also has a fun little CRT filter.2. Sick af boss fights. They have the classic retro design where they loops a set of patterns until there health is depleted. Sometimes they have multiple phases. A tried and true design well executed. They don't really throw any crazy curve balls at you so you can be pretty consistent at fighting them with a bit of practise.3. The zipline mechanic is super creative. Lets the player get creative with their movement. It more or less functions as a portable wall/ceiling for you to climb on. Wait 'til you see what happens when you attach it to a conveyor belt. This might be one of the most clever additions to the action platformer genre that I've ever seen.4. Overall great game feel. Whipping enemies, deploying the zipline, sliding, all of it's accompanied by some very satisfying audio-visual feedback.5. Very good musicCons:1. Too fast paced for my liking. This game reminds me a lot of Gunstar Heroes. They both have very fun and creative mechanics but both move too fast for you to really appreciate what's all going on. Either longer or more stages that gradually ramp up in intensity would probably make the game less stressful/more fun. If you're fine with Gunstar Heroes' pacing you'll probably be fine with this.2. It's occasionally unclear what you're supposed to do to progress. Sometimes I can't tell the difference between a level exit and background art. There's a boss that forces you to jump towards a bottomless pit to get to safety below and it is not obvious if there are any wall hitboxes you need to worry about. These sorts of flaws only really had a teensy bit of trial and error into the mix. Not really a big deal.3. This game seems to be under the impression that I have a SNES controller plugged in. It refers to buttons ABXY in the SNES layout. Pretty confusing at first considering I'm using a 360 controller.Overall a very fun game with some flaws to consider.

_childDocuments_.review: Stuck on an infinite loop of death at level 4. Not sure if it was level 4 or 5 but it was right after you fight the Twin boss. Cut scene plays. My character grapples to the top and just falls to his death. I mashed buttons, mashed jump, held the directional keys, and even just let it play out thinking the creator is pulling a Metal Gear Solid 3 with the Sorrow but no. Just stuck in a perma death loop.I'm sorry. I know this was a one-man show but I requested a refund until this is addressed. There's also some conveyance issues that I didn't like: the mid boss in level 2, I try grappling over him and nope, not supposed to do that. Try jumping over him when he does that bull rush attack and just couldn't do it. I ended up beating him (on Normal) by just taking the hit. Get to the boss of level 2 and it's clear how the creator wants you to dodge the flame attack where fire is on the platform. So, I hold down and jump and no, you slide instead of dropping down like in almost every action platformer ever created up to and including Contra: Hard Corps where the idea of the invincible slide is taken from. Okay, I walk off the platform and use the grappling hook but I aim at an angle and it doesn't work and I die. Do it again thinking that I aimed at the wrong part of the thing to grapple to. Nope. Try something else thinking that I'm not supposed to do that, nope. Try again, this time I walk off the platform, I double jump towards the center and do the neutral grappling thing and then it works. There's just some bad conveyance as to where you're allowed to use the grappling hook and where you are not. Another reason why I give this an 8 is the difficulty. Normal difficulty is kind of insultingly easy and makes the game too short whereas Expert is (you guessed it) way too hard. On Expert you take more damage and there's no checkpoints so when you die once you restart the entire level all over again. I feel like a happy middle could have been achieved by offering checkpoints or a life system or something. That all said, I give it an 8 out of 10. It sucked refunding it but I got stuck at a loop that I already mentioned that didn't allow me to proceed further. Furthermore, as a huge fan of Shatterhand on the NES I would have LOVED to play the original 8 bit version of this that played more like Shatterhand. So I more than understand Kickstarter backers that feel ripped off that they didn't get a Shatterhand spiritual sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Grapple mechanic seems interesting, but even on very easy the game's platforming feels like a chore with enemies constantly knocking you off a jump.  Since the grapple line disappears when you jump you have to commit from those hits or lose a ton of ground.You can beat the game in about 30 minutes.  I understand this is supposed to be like an arcade game or a throwback to a SNES game, but if I had bought a SNES game ine 90s that had five levels I'd have lost it.  Game is not an arcade game where I feel the need to improve my score or get a 1 CC run, enemies feel too cheap for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be entirely honest, I want to like this game, I do.The aesthetics are top notch; art's amazing, music is killer,  hell, the ideas put into it are all quite cool.Unfortunately the gameplay itself is complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Stages and bosses want you to make split-second responses to attacks when your movement is manageable at best? Invuln frames on a slide that won't get you through most things unless timed exactly or near-exactly perfect, a double jump that's only just worth using, and a wire mechanic that will likely go in the wrong direction if you happen to be attacking at all when you use it since both it and your attacks follow input direction. This, coupled with very poor tells for attacks makes each boss fight feel more like a damage race then any real honest challenge.The game as a whole feels like it's trying a little too hard to hit that 'retro-classic' difficulty - and it nearly does, then veers right into the 'GOTCHA!' type difficulty where you feel more like you were cheated on an error than that you made any real mistakes.Absolutely not worth your money in any situation, barring maybe at a 90% discount to appreciate the artwork and music in motion.

_childDocuments_.review: Off the bat and right away, this game is SHORT. As of this review, my playtime is at 62 minutes, and I already beat the game (normal mode). That's not a flex either, this game is just way too short. Take away a few minutes for the few bathroom breaks I had in between, and the unskipable credit crawl, and I'd say this can definitely be beaten in under an hour. I died quite a bit also, so I would even dare to say that some of you gamepad masters out there might only get about 45 minutes out of this ride. This is the biggest negative I have about the game by the way, so if the length doesn't bother you for it's price, then go for it. There's a great deal of fun to be had here for as short as it is. It's packed with exaggerated amounts of enemies and explosions, and the bosses are all really awesome. Unfortunately though, the game itself lacks a meaningful amount of content and gameplay mechanics, leaving this feeling half baked.Taro (your character) has an electric whip and a zipline that he can easily attach to any wall within reasonable range. It's a great gameplay mechanic, and it was a very interesting to see how the devs incorporated the zipline into the some of the bossfights. Unfortunately, out of the 5 bosses here, a lot of them can be half beaten by tanking their damage while spamming the whip right in their faces. You can't get away with doing this for the entire fight on any of these bosses, but I found myself able to do it quite a bit, especially when the tide shifted in my favor. I would have liked to have seen a more pressure based approach to some of these bosses to discourage that kind of gameplay. Panzer Paladin, for example, breaks its boss fights into sections based on the bosses health. The boss will start behaving differently based on the amount of health that it has, and it leaves things unpredictable. In this game, however, once you have the boss on the ropes, you can confidently go right up and spam since the pattern never changes.The electric whip is a cool idea and a great concept for a hero in this kind of an action game. Unlike Contra, which this game seems to take a heavy inspiration from, Taro never picks up a gun. However, his whip does get a power up that allows him to fling electricity at enemies to catch them at a distance. This was a great way to keep the entire idea of playing as an unarmed man (well, unarmed as far as firearms go) intact, however, this is the only power up in the game. As cool as I just described it to be, it's actually pretty underwhelming after you realize that this is all that Taro gets. The only other thing in his arsenal of tricks is that he gets a short baseball slide, that if timed correctly, he can pass through enemy projectiles.The way this game plays is fantastic for what it is. It's just unfortunate that there isn't enough content to make this feel like a full experience. I'd say content wise, this game would need to be at least double of what it currently is to make it worth its asking price. What's on offer here inside of 5 stages is great, but unfortunately, there just isn't enough greatness here for me to recommend this to anyone. And don't get me wrong, I've played short games before and still recommended them. Summer of '58 was a game that I was able to beat in under 2 hours, and I would still recommend it. But the difference between this and a game like Summer of 58 is that Summer of 58 goes out of its way to leave an impression you. It had a story to it that sucks you into its atmosphere and provokes thought. For something so short to stay with someone even after the credits role makes it worth it. A game like Steel Assault, however, is basically just "check your brain at the door and kill some stuff". It's just the nature of the beast with these kinds of games, so the value falls on content and gameplay here. As cool as some of these stages and bosses are, none of them have enough to them to stick in your mind, so when you get to the end of this game, all you're really going to notice is.... "Man, this was short!" Followed by, "I WISH THERE WAS MORE!" You can think of it like going to a restaurant, and getting a tiny amount of food, but it tastes fantastic. It's going to leave you wanting more, and not in the good kind of way. That's basically this game.I'm going to refund this game just for now. I do want to own it in my library some day, but not at this price point. There just isn't enough on offer here. I know that some people are saying that the value will come from the extra modes, but I disagree. The main mode IS the game. Extra modes are just...extra. For instance, the arcade mode is just the main story again with a harder difficulty. At that point, you've seen it all already. If challenging yourself with extra modes is worth it to you, I'm not knocking anyone, but I don't feel like extra modes should make up for more than half of this games asking price, and honestly, that's how I would value this game. At half. It feels like half a game, and would be more appropriate at half the price, so when it hits a sale, I'll own this again, but for now, I can wait on it.P.S. If you think it's wrong to refund a game that you beat, you aren't considering your own money for value here. Simply reaching the end of something doesn't mean you got your moneys worth out of it, and it certainly doesn't warrant keeping something. The average length of a movie is about 1 hour and 45 minutes. If you went into a movie theater and watched something that only lasted 45-50 minutes, would you automatically consider that to be fair? Or would you have some things to consider at that point? Was that short ride packed with memorability for the price tag? Or did the curtain close just as the movie felt like it was hitting its stride? Getting to the end of something doesn't automatically make it worth your money, and it doesn't automatically warrant having to hold onto a purchase. If the value just isn't there, the length of the game is irrelevant.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of promise.It definitely presents a bit of a challenge at various points, the grappling hook is a clever mechanic, the art and music are on point, and the controls feel AND play quite nicely.Why then do I not recommend it? It's too damned short especially so for its price point. What's too short in this case? One can beat the whole thing in about 2 or 3 hours.I also came across a couple of soft lock glitches.What would change my opinion? Any of the following:If there was more meat to each of the levels If the second "mode of play" offered something more interesting than "same game but you have only 1 life for the whole thing" Or even had this game simply been a bit cheaper then I'd be more than happy to tell folks to give it a go.It's a shame really, because you can tell the devs did in fact put a lot of love into making the game, and I commend them for the good points they've managed to accomplish with it. It just needs a bit more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, animations and music completely ruined by balance issues. I'd warn anyone who isn't into extremely difficult games (a la Ninja Gaiden) to stay away. Unfortunately anything below normal mode is also extremely easy. Hopefully devs takes some notes from this game for their future releases as I believe everything else besides difficulty is phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen others lament how everything visually and aesthetically is spot on, yet the gameplay is far too unforgiving.  And I agree with them.  But the gameplay is far too unforgiving in a lot of sections, especially when it comes to covering the distance with your double-jump or hooking onto something just in the nick of time. The room for error when it comes to dodging projectiles is SO small too, even if you've died over and over and can (mostly) tell what's coming.  (Also one mini-boss lets you shoot a turret, but the fact that it gives you so little time to use it before you're hit by something makes it almost..deceptive?)  The pixel art and soundtrack are *astounding*!  BUT, I think the visual splendor also hurts clarity.  So much is going on at once, and it's hard to tell what your rope can and can't latch onto.  If they just balanced the art and the gameplay more equally, this could've been a hard but fun hit.  As it is now, it's a gorgeous but nigh-unfair romp.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: THE BAD:- The story mode is too short.- The difficulty need to be rebalanced. It's too easy on Easy Mode, tough on Normal Mode and too tough on Hard Mode.- The character designs are really cool, but the devs didn't take the time to tell their stories further.THE GOOD:- Everything about the game made me feel like I time traveled back to 1994 and played this on a coin op arcade. Amazing job devs!- Great visuals and animation. The animations of the characters and environments are smooth as silk.- Cool character designs. I wanna see them more!- Intense action. Sometimes it's too tough but you'll git gud in no time.- Amazing soundtrack. Again, the music brings me back to the 90's- I WANT SEQUELS!OVERALL : 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through the game twice now, and I have to say that the game is short but awesome. I may be bad at gaming, but even I have noticed how quickly you progress in Steel Assault. It teaches you the way it wants to be played by throwing you into action sequences that you have to overcome. Then to use that knowledge in the next sequences. Very rewarding and exciting game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: It has problems to be sure, specifically at this price point. It lacks enough length to matter and relies on harder difficulties to pad out more time. The levels have a very lackluster set up, where you feel like you are getting into the flow, then all of a sudden it becomes a boss fight. All levels make decent use of the zipline, the problem lies in the less than stellar layout making some platforms seem usable, but aren't. Music and visuals are pretty good, with the visual aspect being a little off in some cases. Mostly due to the weather effects in particular. The controls are fine if a little stiff, definitely possible improvement.Overall, needs more content and depth at this price point. At $5 I would recommend, anything higher needs more substance.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steal Assault is totally worth your time despite it's length, it is a well polished product. Reminds me of the Gameboy Advance in a good way, though it's very clear that it takes some inspiration from the SEGA Genesis and some more modern faux-retro titles.I beat the game on normal in about an hour.The hard difficulty took me about 4 hours to beat, but now I'm very good at the game and find it very fun to blast through.If you would like to watch gameplay, I have recorded a full playthrough here:This game is a fast paced action game reminiscent of Contra, Castlevania, Mega Man, and a boatload of Treasure games, especially Gunstar Heroes. You take your electric whip, whip enemies with it, and the enemies explode in some really nice looking pixel art. Get to the end of the stage and defeat a pretty crazy boss. Do this 6 times and you win the game. Also rock out to the soundtrack.You always feel in control, and the grappling hook mechanic gives you a lot of freedom in the air, once you get the hang of it. Protip: Don't hold "up" when you jump.The difficulty is also very reasonable on normal, the only times I died was when I misunderstood a exactly what I was supposed to do. So only a few times really. I would not call this game a frustrating experience.You can grapple onto almost any surface, and using your grapple gives you a bit of extra air time, which is more novel than you think.Despite the fact that this game starts with an extremely ugly bilinear filter, you can turn it off in the options. Other than that, the sprite work is amazing, detailed, and has quite a bit of animation. The final boss is a little choppy, but other than that, it's a treat for the eyes.You also have your scanline/CRT filters built into the game, but I don't typically touch those. I know the sharpened pixel look bothers a bunch of people with no taste, but the "raw" pixel look is very nice as it is. If I want to, I can (and do) play games on a CRT to get the CRT feel, and since this game is in 4:3, you should have no problems viewing it on a CRT if you have one. I think this game will look really nice on my CRT.Despite the pixel aesthetic and "retro 16bit" inspiration, the soundtrack would be at the level of CD quality audio. So like PS1+.Since there are few levels, there is only a few tracks, but all of the music is good.You can also choose an FM only version of the songs that are good in their own right, though I prefer the "CD" quality audio.There is no way around this. I beat the game on the normal difficulty in ~49 min. This is not a problem for me, and I tend to replay games once I get the hang of them to see how far I can push my skills. I don't know if I'm one of those people who "master" games, but a second playthrough at least on shorter titles usually makes me appreciate it more once I know what I'm doing. However, if you are one of those strange people that only play a game once, and only because they are new, then you will feel disappointed due to the game's length. That's more of a you problem than a knock against the games quality.I do understand that for ~$15 you have your choice of games that are many times longer and just as enjoyable, and I think it is reasonable to consider the length of this game.I think the best way to put it is, if you are looking for this kind of game, and what you saw in the trailer looks good, you should purchase this game.I do not regret my purchase, and would easily recommend this to anyone looking for that Treasure/Contra vibe. Now if they would only put Mischief Makers on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.It has an interesting use of the grappling hook. Fast, fun, and beautiful. Execution is very tight. You don't have much margin for error and timings are very strict. However, the big health bar will give you plenty of survivability.Even though it may be short to some people, it seems to me like it has about the length of a Metal Slug game. I like this arcade feeling.So far, my only complaint is not having an option to skip boss dialogues. The game could also use a rebalance in the boss fights. Some are either very easy or you can just cheese your way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: You have to get used to the grappling hook. Its harder to use than in games like Bionic Commando.My biggest gripe is not knowing where to throw your hook since you can't see what to latch onto. So you basically have to fling the thing around aimlessly and die a lot until you get lucky and attach to something. Then after that you have to remember where it was you grappled to and memorize the location. Then if you don't hit the buttons exactly right, you'll fall to your death. It's super difficult. I only recommend this if you have a lot of time to practice, which i don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to the Sega Genesis and SNES era with plenty of references to some games from those consoles. It has great pixel-art, controls are super responsive and gameplay is addicting and fun. Dificulty will take some getting used to but it's never unfair. Well, not unless you play Arcade mode that is, but that's completely optional along with many different dificulty options.For a 2 hour game, even after finishing it I started another playthrough right after just because I liked it so much. And that is because of a combination of fast and frantic action with a bit of platforming. There's always something happening on the screen, forcing to be on the lookout and react accordingly. And the Music? It's Godlike. It complements each stage perfectly and are overall just bangers to listen to.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation is top notch, but the rest of it is not. It's got great music and a good look, but games need more than that.It's extremely short. I beat it on normal mode in 60 minutes. I got stuck in 2 places due to their bad design. The abysmal level 2 and the final boss. I really wanted to like this game and I was excited for it. When I finally got to play it, I discovered it was very shallow and disappointingly short with problems in it's mechanics.I deeply love old Castlevania, Megaman, Contra and similar games and I'm quite good at them. The opening video is kick-ass. The aesthetics are great with sweet unique music per stage and art that just feels right (except when Taro's face is inconsistently drawn). It's mostly similar to Ninja Gaiden and Contra but not as precise as those games generally are. When you have a game this short, your gameplay needs to be razor tight and this wasn't.The game is shallow in many ways. The gameplay is too simple to be very engaging. You jump, attack, slide(dodge), and use ziplines. Keeping with the Contra and Ninja Gaiden similarities, it's better for you to go fast and skip most things that aren't directly in your way. This helps avoid infinitely respawning enemies and prevent others from getting into position where they would be annoying. There is no exploration to speak of. It's almost a game on rails. You can take your time, but it will probably be worse for yourself and there aren't even little secrets for a powerup or something. Powerups are laid in front of you and you honestly have to avoid them intentionally to not get them. There's a "story" but there really shouldn't be in a game like this. An opening and ending video like Hard Corps Uprising is all you need. This game has two side-kick characters who only say a few lines here (no voice acting) and there if you even notice. Sometimes they even talk to you when you're in battle so obviously you won't be paying attention to them at all. They are really pointless; both in what they say and how/when they say it. While the environments can look nice and there was an effort to create a sense of world-building, it's sometimes nonsense. I think it's supposed to be a kind of post-apocalypse. One level features a derelict city overgrown with plants. But it also has working TVs, lights, and capitalistic advertisements. So which is it? An old abandoned derelict city or a technologically alive modern dystopian nightmare?This game's gimmick is a zipline that you hardly use outside of roughly one attack per main boss and maybe one elevator section in a level or two. And you can't even use it for a direction that would help you the most (down-right, despite the tutorial saying you can use it for 8 directions). The game says there are subweapons but there is only one, electric (which simply extends your whips range via three projecticles). It's a good one to be sure, but there are problems. The others are health and a two-hit shield. They are also in pre-placed areas so you won't encounter them randomly or via enemy drops. And shield and electric overwrite each other, so you can't even get both at once if you're good enough to keep one. And there are hardly any little detours so there is no exploration to find them either. And there is no health item past level 3. On normal mode, this doesn't matter as checkpoints are decent enough. But on hard and arcade where the intent is to beat it in one life, that's when it becomes awful. The punch-to-regain energy is pointless because there is only one "subweapon" to recharge. It appears about once a level. That subweapon basically just extends your whip. But that means the mechanic and the only powerup it serves to help are in conflict with each other. If you use all your energy, even if you regain it through this mechanic, doesn't matter, the powerup is gone. You also lose it on death, so you're out of luck by the next checkpoint. So the only powerup in the game never lasts long unless you go out of your way to conserve it which generally isn't a good or feasible idea.The gameplay is not great. It's simultaneously too easy and also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at too many parts. It's too simple and almost never requires you to improve. It's shallow, it's inconsistent, and also bounces radically between unfairly hard and sleep-inducingly easy. I've had too many dropped inputs on a brand new controller, and invincibility frames after taking damage aren't consistent either so you can get unfairly double-dipped. The hitboxes are also not consistent. Too often things that hit, shouldn't; things that shouldn't, do. The whip itself is a mess to look at. The sprite is not defined enough and even has weird triangles at the end of it. This is your only attack, there should be no confusion with it and it should be awesome every time. Sometimes the bad hitboxes are in your favor (not fun) and sometimes they aren't (super not fun). Same with contact damage. Sometimes I overlap with an exploding enemy or phase through bullets for no reason and nothing hits me, other times I'm obviously not touching anything and I get hit and wonder why.The dodge-slide is a few frames too short from being useful. For example the final boss has a flamethrower attack that can hit you even though you slide through it. It's the only way to dodge it and yet it's inconsistent. Come on now.Again, if your game is this short, the physical gameplay has to be consistently good.Some bosses die before you can even see what they can do like the miniboss robot-mastodon with a chainsaw-nose.The faster you play, the easier it is. You can kill some minibosses before they even turn around. You can defeat main bosses before they even get off three or more attacks. You can do this even on accident. But if you don't know how, or naturally play slower, it becomes unfair without trial and error. Bosses are pattern based but also not challenging enough to let you see what they can do, so you feel shortchanged. And if you do let them do more attacks, it usually starts to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The mark of good level/boss design is near-death situations that demand "perfection" from the player, but perfection derived from practice, not memorization or exploiting. The key test for "real" or "fake" difficulty is: could a person theoretically make it through a stage on their first try assuming their reaction time and skill is good enough. That's not this game. It's entirely trial and error for the rare parts where it's actually hard. Most of the time, enemies are mainly placed where you'd naturally jump and whip or something similar. Some enemies are already shooting before you see them on screen so you'll end up jumping directly into their attacks. Also everything does two damage so it's pointless to have all the extra pips on your life bar when every attack does the same anyway. Might as well have half the pips and everything do one damage. It's the same either way. It's an unnecessary illusion.I feel no desire to 1cc this because of those factors unlike Hard Corps Uprising which was much harder.It also wouldn't have been hard to include a boss rush mode or level select. To play arcade mode without mastering boss patterns is a death sentence of frustration and not worth it on top of all the inconsistency in gameplay. Arcade mode is even worse actually. Only some item boxes can actually change between shield and electric powerups. And pits are deaths instead of just damage, which kick you back to the start. Extra fun when an enemy shoots you from off screen while you jump to the only platform available which then knocks you into death. So yeah, very poorly designed.Level 2 is probably the worst stage I have ever played. All the worst attributes of the game come out. Random enemies that randomly explode, off screen shooting, all the above. Stupid power up placement (shield first and then health in the very first section WHERE YOU DON'T NEED THEM). Unbelievable.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I played this sooner! Because then I could have refunded it as it would have been in the 14 day grace period.First off, credit where credit is due: The graphics and music are very good! However, It may be very pretty, but it plays like ****, the mechanics are poorly thought out, or seem like there are mechanics missing: -you have 10 health but every single attack does at least 2 damage.-when you get close you do a short range melee attack that's worse than your normal attack - it restores subweapon energy but there's only one and it's a drop from chests so you'll almost never have a subweapon. -The dodge is bound to down+jump even though there are a ton of free buttons. Also it covers no distance whatsoever.it's extremely short, and it's extremely frustrating. This game geuninely feels like the devs either ran out of time, money, or just said **** it, because it feels unfinished. It could have been great (the pieces were there and the art is wonderful) but sadly it's not.If this game is on sale for $5 and you happen to have $5, still don't buy it and go for a walk instead. Seriously, this is not a fun game, stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I really cannot recommend this game unless you are super fan for this genre, it's short, difficult and has some bullet hell elements, nothing special in the level design either, sometimes it gives you the feeling of "this level/enemy was not tested enough"the positives are great art and soundtrack, some good mechanics
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very brutal, tightly designed, and has some kick ass visuals and music. That being said, this review is for people who like hard, arcade like games. It only takes about an hour and a half to beat and it will punish you to hell and back if you don't learn from your mistakes. There are a scant few moments where its unclear how to maneuver or deal with an attack but overall it was a very fun experience.I do agree with a lot of the negative reviews though, the game's levels are incredibly short and it never gets a chance to breathe and expand on some of the stage mechanics. So maybe when it's on sale for 10 dollars or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember every c*ck sucking and bullsh*t stuff from old NES and SNES games. For example, knockback when you get hit, instakill death pits, enemies appearing out of nowhere and hitting you, 2 phase boss fight that doesn't refill your health bar and doesn't have a checkpoint between phases. Put all these ♥♥♥♥ into one game and you get Steel Assault. A game that only took the worst parts of the retro games and forget the fun and enjoyment. As soon as you start level 1, the game starts sending enemies from left and right. This is just first level, let me get used to controls. Nope, this game has no mercy, You have to master the controls and play without making a mistake from level 1. You don't time to make mistakes because if you do, you will die. Some of the bosses cover the floor with electric and flame and you have to fight them while on a zipline or wait for floor to return to normal. Another c*ck bending and unnecessary game mechanic. The game only has 5 levels. It is too short. You can literally finish it under 1 hour and refund it. I finished the game both on easy and normal mode in 2 hours. In order to compensate for the short length of the game, they made it criminally hard. Steel Assault is exactly that. Also this sh*t released in 2021 and it doesn't have widescreen, 2k or 4k support. It forces 4:3 ratio. Don't say it adds retro aesthetic, it's complete bullsh*t!
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: It's just too short to recommend. The game should have additional content, but instead feels rushed with the bare minimum seemingly to appease the kick-starters (I assume).However with that said, the game does have a high quality polish to it. It makes me wonder why the devs didn't build a "complete" fully-lengthed game and go big, knowing that pushing out a small vertical slice like this would be perceived as underwhelming.-Initial impressions are that this game is polished and gameplay is very smooth. I really have nothing to complain about at this time - excellent pixel graphics, responsive controls, good OST and I personally like the art/aesthetic.I would recommend but I have only made it 5 minutes past the first level on the highest difficulty.

Wait what?Okay, this game has some pros and cons, but in the end, I enjoyed the game.The visuals are beautiful.The music is epic all the way through.Levels are well designed but short, and that hits me with a big oof. Makes it feel more like a boss rush.Story is basic but it works.Only gripes with the bosses is the second last (too much of a waiting game) And final boss. other than that, they are fun.As others have said, this game relies on one move that is the Star of the show: The Grapple Hook.I wish there was more mobility in the game but its like the game is trying to tell you simple moves are all it takes to evade the waves of led & fire that you see on the screen. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: this game is 15 bucks which is about 14 too many in quarters that I'd be willing to spend on it. very cheap kills and you die extremely fast. The presentation and music and design is topnotch but the actual moment to moment gameplay absolutely sucks ass and most deaths do not feel like it's your fault and instead feel like the game is kicking you while you're down. Added to this is that you can't slide into slide and that's your main way to avoid damage since you have I frames during the slide. This game doesn't feel like it was play tested by anybody outside of the team and instead was just circulated around by people who already knew what to expect and from where. On top of this the bullets, very obviously on level 4-2, do not contrast with the environment and you can get clipped by seemingly nothing. Also there's only 5 levels in the entire game and absolutely NO replayability at all.The game is beautiful. The game sounds great. The game sucks ass to play. Go play the megaman x/ zero/ classic collections. play 20xx/30xx. go play anything else to scratch that SNES action platformer itch, just don't PLAY steel assault.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, even though the sprites are on the small side. Sound and music is great. The game-play is unique with the grapple mechanic and is tight, even though some of the platforming can get quite frustrating. This game would have been a perfect fit on the SNES and Genesis back in the day. The only real knock I can give it is that it is short and can be beaten in under an hour on its easiest setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the Mega Man X series on the SNES and PS1 and Steel Assault brought back the nostalgia of the fast paced action of my youth.  In addition to the speedy combat, the style is fresh.  I don't consider this a Mega Man clone but there is certainly inspiration reflected in the design.Instead of a gun type weapon as the primary, this game utilizes a whip so you are fairly close during enemy engagements.  The encounters are more frantic during this style of close range combat and quick enemies.The game is short and the story and characters are lightly written in retro style.  Still if you enjoy fast platformers, I think you will have fun.  The soundtrack is also rockin' which was a great plus for me!*I did encounter one recurring bug and as far as I can tell it is rare among users.  I could almost never get the upper right zip line to deploy when using the keyboard.  I was able to beat the game even with the bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a fast paced 2D Action Platformer that will test your skills, the game has a unique mechanism which is called the wall hook, where you need to hook 2 walls or 2 platforms and hold on to the rope while platforming which makes it even more fun and interesting.The combat is fast paced you will need lots of dodging / sliding to overcome multiple sections and then faced a major boss at the end of each stage.The Boss fights designs were very nice and the music is really top notch, It took me back to those childhood days where I used to go to the arcade and insert the coins to play those games.Very recommended action platformer with an overall rating 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique gameplay with the zip n' whip mechanics, despite being short (It took me about 1 hour to beat), everything in it is very well polished. The artwork is great, the gameplay mechanics, enemies, bosses, it is all great. 100% worth to do the 1 live to beat mode since it is very short.Also, play with the CRT and Billinear filter on, the game looks amazing with them.I'm craving for a Steel Assault 2. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the pixel art is immaculate, soundtrack is great and it has an interesting mechanic with the wires you can deploy and climb on. The main issue is that the game is extremely short, it doesn't feel like it has the time to properly flesh out its own mechanics or really push them so that the player has to get good with them and the developers could do more with it. Outside of the bosses and a few key sections during the levels it doesn't really get much use. I would have much preferred the game had a few more levels making use of the same settings/visual design across more levels, rather than having 2 or more different locations for every single level if it meant the game was longer.This is still a great game, but unless it looks like your dream game I'd say wishlist it and wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very good gameFinishing the game on arcade mode was pretty funCool OST👌Only problem i had with the game was some bugs, like when switching scenarios, if you go outside the screen the game just freezes. And also, for some reason the last boss just disappeared in the middle of the fight in one arcade mode run 😅8.5/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. Like others have said, it's a short game but I thought it was worth picking up. The description of the game says that this is a 16-bit retro style action game but truth be told this reminds me so much of the Gameboy Advance, which is technically 32-bit. But you would never get sound out of the GBA like this game. I really dig the soundtrack. And props to the devs for giving the option for a nice CRT filter. Not everybody likes them but I enjoy them when done right, and this game does it correctly.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a short and sweet platformer with honestly some of the best sprite work and music I've experience in an indie title.Instead of a sword or a gun Taro wields a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ electric whip and its just the one button and that's it.Really had me feeling like the games i grew up with, super simple but extremely hard to master.You can't really hold right and attack and run you gotta learn enemy patterns and spawns tons of trial and error ESPECIALLY the bosses. Other than tight controls and a double jump what sets this apart is the inclusion of a zip line you can deploy whenever you want in any direction as long as the two ends latch on to a surface. Felt like Bionic Commando + Contra in all the good ways possible. Lots of death pits and stage hazards that force you to start thinking how to approach situations while using the zip line, its a ton of fun really makes the platforming challenging.If there's any issues i have with it, other than feeling a little -too- short, the second level is a painful difficulty spike. Feels like something that should have been saved for stage 4 or 5.What makes it all the more painful is the two hardest achievements involve beating each stage with no checkpoints - and the whole game on a single life. If the second stage wasn't such a massive pain in the ass id try for these more but the memorization on the little enemies on this stage really don't compare to anything else. Maybe if i feel like hurting ill try them some more but for now ill be happy with having everything but those lmao.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!Pure arcade goodness! Nonstop action, with very precise controls and tight gameplay backed by a frantic soundtrack!The graphics are gorgeous pixelated.The game consists of 5 stages with very platforming/action sections and various bosses. Each boss plays completely different from the previous ones.The last stage is a banger all around.Great game! Hghly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Only 2 hours in and ive had so many "WOW" moments. this game feels like the final boss of side scrollers. Everything i've learned from metroidvanias and side scrollers like megaman zero used flawlessly. Crazy enough while this game feels like home it adds a new grapple mechanic that makes movement feel amazing. The graphics are jaw dropping. Reminding me of some older ds games but modernized. I always loved that aesthetic. Only draw back could be the controls could take some people awhile to understand. Its a shame this game is not talked about. Must buy 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, short arcade-style game. Feels mostly like a mix of Castlevania and a side-scrolling shmup. Kinda like if a shmup was designed with mid-ranged combat in mind instead of their usual long-ranged player projectile fire.The music goes crazy, and the visuals are really nice, impressive bits of polish and personality were all over the presentation. There were some things I'd have designed differently maybe, but ultimately they didn't hurt the game that much for me. Things like the slide maneuver used for i-frames being really short, I feel like that could've been longer. Or the kinda awkward system of using melees to keep your whip powerup for longer, otherwise it just gets spent up and goes away.Regardless of some minor gripes, Steel Assault was a pretty enjoyable game and worth beating at least once. Lots of care clearly went into this and it shows!Oh and a tip: definitely recommend rebinding the grapple move to R1 or something besides circle/right face button. Makes it a lot easier to use at a moment's notice, and the game frequently asks you to platform off (i.e. jump) or attack while on your grapple rope. The R1 mapping makes it a lot easier to deal with those scenarios imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Over all I liked this game. If I had any real complaints, it's that it's sometimes a bit hard to see some bullets, and the default controls are kinda clunky. I rebound the grapple hook to R, jump to A, and attack to X. As well as, in Steam Controller options, bound Down+Jump to the L button. Because I am so annoyed by games not just giving slide its own button.It's much easier to get used to the grapple hook when you don't have to take your thumb off the very critical jump button do use it.As for the rest of the game, the level design is solid, the visuals are drop dead gorgeous, and both versions of the soundtrack are killer. I especially loved the FM versions.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic fast paced action platformer with a banger soundtrack! I first watched General Andrews run this game on stream and was a lucky recipient of a free copy from that stream. I absolutely fell in love with the action and music, and this is one of the very few games that I wanted to speedrun just from watching it with no prep work. There's some unexplained tech - Punch attacks don't use your energy bar if you have the electric power-up and on a successful punch kill, you'll get an orb to recharge 2 of the electric energy bar. The only major downside for the game isn't one that most people will be concerned with, or know about. It has to do with the difficulty levels. From somewhere between now and launch, there was a change in the amount of damage taken during normal mode, so now 5 hits, restart the screen. This is not really a big issue aside from 4 screens, primarily the waterjet section in stage 2.  Once you get into Expert difficulty, take that same 5 hits, and now it's through the whole level, making the heart pickups actually valid, but if you die, back to the beginning of the level you go. Arcade... same scenario without the pickups. Extremely unforgiving, and practically impossible to speedrun in a <20 minute run.On the flipside, Very Easy is literally that, very easy and if you die, you fell off the screen most likely. Easy is almost of the same caliber, but you might die if you don't dodge some of the attacks.Outside of the lackluster difficulty approach, the game feels and plays crazy well and I'll still be playing this gem for quite some time in the future.And for those who are curious, I did hold the VE and E speedrun records at the time of this comment (15:12 and 15:10 respectively) and a Normal mode run (17:49) on
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Although it is only 5 stages long, the game is amazing. Beautiful, tight controls and challenging AF! Playing on Normal was hard enough, final boss was great. My only complaint is the lack of a dedicated button for the "dash/slide" command, would make so much sense to me.I know the game is already cheap, but you can find it 50% off in any sale, so heads up.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on Normal difficulty (warning: it is tough.)This is a good game after you get used to honing in your twitch reflexes (you will need it to make any progress in the game). My main complaint against this game is that the screen just gets too busy to know what is coming at you and what to avoid (and where to shoot your grappling hook). Progress is made through dying a lot in tough spots (and often without sufficient warning for you to react in time on first encounters). The unlimited continues help as well as the checkpoints. I also found the later level bosses a lot easier than the first 2 level bosses. I remember I stopped playing not knowing what to do with the first boss. I came back to the game many months later to take another crack at it before I started making good progress.If you are looking for a challenge and enjoy gorgeous retro style pixel art then definitely play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This was a nice gem. the combat is really nice but took some time to really get it all together. its a game I went through all in one sitting which was slightly over an hour. normally I'll play something for like 20-30ish minutes and jump off because I wanna do something else but this kept me in all of it which is amazing. The only bad part- It only took that long to beat- I remember when I first beat it a while ago I was so in awe I bought it for a friend cus I wanted them to go at it. Its been a little over a year now since I last played it and looking back to it. I really liked this and wanted more. The price is steep but this is something I look back on and can really say *This had so much passion put into it-* I hope for maybe some dlc or another project just like it down the line but I say support the devs behind this and just check the game out. Its not long, but the time you do get with it is just amazing. and I remember there being some extra modes behind it too so a little something to keep ya mind occupied! Gonna go at it one more time!

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are good, Mechanics are good, soundtrack is good, gameplay is...On normal difficulty enemies do a lot of damage, so bosses battles tends to last little, so they are not memorable or enjoyable.You have to die A LOT to get past a short stage checkpoint, and at the end is about repeating and remembering how the enemies and obstacles are staged, more than skill.On the jungle boss, I understood at the second time that I needed to grab from the spaceship bottom, but didn't know how.I retried a lot, and I got tired of seeing the same boss cinematic and same game over screen.Guys, this had a lot of potential...Really!The game is very well done, but you made it too old school in terms of gameplay, and we don't have only four NES titles to play nowadays as we did.I'll switch to another Steam game, to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely one of the greatest action games of all time, I put it right up there next to Shinobi III.The art is insanely gorgeous, riddled with flashing lights , ester eggs, and pixel art animations so smooth that you'll be thinking about Metal Slug or KoF.To round out the total package it has an insane pumping soundtrack that can hang with the very best of the MegaMan X series any day. It can feel a bit on the tougher side at first but give the game some time to teach you, it is well worth it.12/10 - Peace Forever!
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell this was the most fun I had with a platformer in a LOOOONG time!!! The 16-bit graphics, the chiptune soundtrack, the off-the-walls difficulty, everything just weaves into a such beautiful and challenging game that you truly swear was indeed a forgotten time cruncher from the Gameboy Advance era. The balancing could have used some tuning but that's what the difficulty options are for obviously. In that regard, I sort of half regret not starting from Easy, but going fast and hitting the ground with Normal was still worth it. I believe my biggest gripe with Steel Assault is that it is painfully short, and it just leaves you wanting for more! Here's to hoping for a kick-ass sequel!!
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game thinking it would be a casual walk in the park, something like Megaman or Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge and boy, how wrong I have been! Game's hard as t*ts! If you are up for a challenge go for it, otherwise cease and desist, it is not like you will be able to sit down for 10 minutes every now and again while working on anything else, relax and make some progress. It might stress you out as it did me, you really gotta plough through it! Giving it a positive rate because you can tell lots of effort was put into it and it really took me back in time with its classic 8-bit feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review by saying that I grew up playing the types of games that Steel Assault pays homage to. With that being said, this game wears it's inspiration on it's sleeve. There are elements of Contra, Castlevania and even Bionic Commando. So, if you are a fan of any or all of those games then you're in for a good time. Steel Assault does not take long to complete similar to the NES games of yore, I finished it twice in roughly two hours. Maybe pick it up on a sale as I did. In addition to solid gameplay which is fast and smooth, the pixel art is jaw droppingly goregeous and that soundtrack is a non-stop assault on your ears that really gets you into the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: A very short game, which is alright. It has this grappling hook gimmick that isn't too fun or intuitive to use. At first while playing on normal difficulty I had no idea of what I was supposed to do and kept dying, it was very trial and error so I just knocked it down to easy and while it still had some annoying parts it was over in under an hour.Steel Assault has this weirdness with its graphics where you never know where the grappling hook will stick or not, it's visually confusing. That's probably the worst part of the whole game. I'd recommend that anyone serious about finishing it on normal or harder difficulties to play it on easy first to get familiar with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundrack, decent visuals, obnoxious gameplay.Visuals are decent however at the same time a chunk of it is also really messy and doesn't convey background/foreground very well.Really poor difficulty wise with plenty of unfair traps that feel like they're purely just "ha gotcha" style requiring trial and repition to get through not to mention how easy it is to be hit from something off screen. Checkpoints are decently placed but the small cutscenes pre boss fight (and one level has you repeating the last segment of the level before you fight the boss for some reason) makes repeat attempts a chore.Sad thing is despite the poor gameplay making things harder than they should be it's still a pretty short game all the same with no real reason to go for another playthrough.

The artist and musician should be commended but the level designer should seek a new career. Truly awful game.Also its stupid short so be sure to wait until its in a cheap bundle. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault's heart is in the right place but there's just too many flaws for me to recommend buying it. Enemies frequently spawn on top of you, enemies have confusing hitboxes such as a giant chainsaw on a charging enemy not being able to hit you but the very edge of their buttcheek can, bullets are hard to see with incredibly busy environments which is made worse by the game defaulting to an optional blur filter turned on in video settings, the grappling mechanic is awkward and a bit of a throwaway, and boss health bars legitimately block your view of the playable area in 2 of the 5 boss fights in this game with the last boss fight blocking your view of the one safe place to stand in the very last phase. I was in such disbelief of the last boss health bar issue that I went to youtube and found a clip of someone else standing there safely to make sure that wasn't a glitch. I would skip this one or at least wait for a deep discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I have a few negative things to say, but ultimately I do recommend this game if you like demanding run-and-gun type games.  The art is great and the controls are tight, and each level and boss feels unique.  The controller support was great for this game (Switch, PS4, XBOX prompts).Touching on the theme this is like Contra, Metal Slug, and Castlevania adopted a baby, and is well executed for the most part.  It's linear level progression interspersed with boss battles at a very demanding pace.On the note of pacing, on Normal difficulty I find it almost too hard.  I would put Normal at arcade quarter-crunching Metal Slug levels of difficulty, in that you will find yourself dying a lot to barrages of unpredictable enemies.  I felt demanded to execute mechanics in a timing-perfect manor before I was able to even learn how to use those mechanics.  I found myself dying a lot while trying to even figure out how I was supposed to beat a challenge in front of me, which I found frustrating, and I'm not stranger to these types of games.Luckily, the game never sets you that far back from where you died, so I rarely felt like like I was loosing too much progress.  Despite my frustrations, I found myself progressing through the game, which all said and done is relatively short (less than 2 hours for my Normal play-through).And while there are so many intentional designs decisions for this game (like CRT modes, low-resolution settings, intentionally hard gameplay), one thing that really bugged me (probably because I spent the longest on this section), was why you would leave the boss health meter for the last boss cover up part of the area you are fighting him in.  With so much attention to detail paid, that seems like an odd thing to overlook, especially when there is so much empty real estate at the top of the screen.Despite all that, I still enjoyed the game.  It's not one I would want to come back to unfortunately because of how frustrated I got, but for the very hardcore of this genre I think you'll have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: The steam next fest introduce me to this game and I'm grateful. This game is short and sweet. The sprites are beautiful and the music is awesome. The gameplay is challenging, even on normal difficulty, but could be considered excessively difficult by people who are not used to the 'difficulty of retro games'. The zipline is a fun mechanic to play with. Being forced to watch intros every time you respawn gets annoying quickly, especially if you suck at this game. Attempting to jump over certain enemies without making contact and receiving damage is more difficult than it should be.7/10

Enemies attack too fast, too unpredictable for the controls given.Enemy fire spreads too wide to dodge, while attack range and jump power of our hero where too small.And devs know of these things.
