_childDocuments_.review: , “You are a dude with an electric whip that needs to defeat an evil mastermind, it’s so cool, you have powerups like a shield and electric attacks, you can also use a rope to grapple on walls”, if someone would describe this game you would swear you did once play it in an arcade a long time ago but you can’t really put your finger on it.It’s an arcade game, through and through, if it was released back then it would be both an incredibly successful title and a quartermuncher.With standard gameplay for a 2d action game it features a lot of unfair stuff, that is until realize enemy spawning and attacks aren’t random, so even if the controls feel clunky you still have a way to think ahead and try to execute it flawlessly.The story is a play on a lot of game of its inspiration era, there’s a big baddie that threatens the world, go alone to stop him battling your way through bosses with little to no personality.Visuals are great if a bit generic, there’s a lot going on the screen at any given time, music follows well the rush this game is in with cool 8bit tracks.It’s a good time even if it doesn’t last a lot, an arcade game that you are sure nobody you know played it before.

_childDocuments_.review: Short on content but high on butt-kicking, this is a gorgeous 2-D action game. It's got the pace and amazing pixel art of 16-bit Contra, or a game from Treasure. There's no shooting, but this feels more like a run and gun than anything else. Expect breezy levels and challenging boss fights. Get it on sale though. $15 is kinda steep for a game that's over in about an hour (minus all the times I died to a boss).

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a brutal and beautiful game.  I highly recommend it for those who like games like old-school Ninja Gaiden, Bionic Commando, Contra and Metal Slug.For a little background, my first console was an Atari 2600, but my first true love was the NES.  I was drawn to the more difficult games like Ninja Gaiden, Castlevania, Contra and Street Fighter 2010 and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link.This game is a little misunderstood, because it's the opposite of what many games are today.  Instead of holding your hand, it has a brief, optional tutorial mode.  It's not just "sort of" old-school hard.  It's old-school hard on steroids.  Steel Assault throws you right into the fire, and pummels you over the head the whole way through.  There are two types of players at this point - Those who say "forget this" and play something else, and those who also get their butts kicked but say "give me more, we'll see who wins".It's not for everyone.  In fact, I found my whole play-through on normal difficulty to be incredibly difficult.  I have seen some of the superhuman speed-runs on youtube, and I'm not one of those people.  I still like my games tough, and to be honest, this game is tough - but it's also fair the whole way through.  If I die, it's my fault.  If I fail to memorize an enemy pattern, or take advantage of an opening, it's still my fault - especially on the second or third try.Every little nook and cranny, every enemy and ability at your disposal is perfectly posed where there is a way to victory.  It's up to you to figure it out - whether to play offense, or defense, or find a new strategy altogether.  Upon my first try at the game, I felt winded by the time I made it to the second stage.After a few hours, I was speed-running my way to the final boss, and still finding new and more efficient ways to dispose of enemies who I never thought I could take out in the first place (sometimes just avoiding them will work).With all that said, there are four difficulty modes, including easy, and very easy, which are better-geared for gamers who just want to have a good time without sweating bullets and clenching their teeth.As far as the graphics and music, this game slams.  The music is some kind of melodic techno-metal with an 80's montage feel. The graphics are like some GBA game on overdrive.  Thematically, the game is awesome.   Short, animated cut-scenes are really cool, and made me root for Taro, whom I think is one of the coolest-looking game protagonists I've seen in a long time.  I also really liked the enemy characters, and I wanted to know more about them, even though the game mentions very little in detail.The controls are also very tight.  That said, the zipline system takes a lot of getting used to.  My first playthrough was very awkward....but this is the type of game that will reward you as you spend more time with it.  In fact, using the zipline to traverse through corridors and tops of buildings is an absolute joy, and the platforming parts are usually my favorite.The whip is downright nasty and fun to use.  One you learn the boss patterns, it's a lot of fun to spam the attack button and take out that op boss way earlier than expected.So, most importantly, the game-play is great.  It is awkward at first, but so is riding a bike or playing guitar.  You have to have a little patience and be wiling to take criticism from the game and improve.I give this game a solid 9/10.  The only reason I don't give it a 10/10, is that like some have argued, it is a little too short.  Some extra challenge stages, or maybe some later dlc, could fix that shortcoming.  Other than that, this game is perfect for what it is.  It has razor-sharp game-play that rewards commitment, and is overflowing with style and inspiration that I find lacking in many of the old-school throwback games out there today.Highly recommended to anyone who likes a little pain in their game, and want to feel a true sense of victory upon completion.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This game has unskippable cutscenes at the start of each chapter and before fighting every Boss that play every time you die and try again. On top of that the Final Boss has two phases that you have to beat in one try and an introduction for each of them.Terrible Design decisions aside this game is fun, all of the levels are short so death doesn't get too frustrating. It can be hard to keep track of the mechanics but they all have their uses

_childDocuments_.review: An gorgeous game with a rockin soundtrack, fully created with love of the unforgiving S/NES era. It may demand near perfection out of its arcade experience, but with multiple difficulty levels and unlimited lives on story mode; anyone can enjoy this tribute to an era i hope we never take for granted!
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool albeit short retro action-platformer (emphasis on short) with visuals straight out of a GBA and a banger soundtrack, which blends gameplay elements from classics like Castlevania, Bionic commando and even a touch of Contra.One remark though: difficulty settings are all over the place. You can go from a cakewalk on Normal, with health refills at the end of each screen and very generous checkpoints, to a true hard-as-nails retro arcade experience on Expert, with all the aforementionned advantages being-stripped out and ennemies hitting twice as hard. Something in between would probably have been much better for the overall longevity of the game.Fun game all things considered, I'd just wish it would go for a little longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a tad short, but it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.The framerate runs at 60, but the doesn't have widescreen. It's a stylistic choice to emulate arcade cabinets. What is nice, though, is that the game supports all controllers, with button prompts for Dualshock, Nintendo, and Xbox controllers. You can jump, attack in any direction, use a pulley to attach to fill gaps in any direction, and slide with i frames. But the environment around those mechanics make full use of them. The art style is top tier, and the pixel art is SNK/Darkstalkers level. I literally utter "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and "woah" at certain points just from the pixel fidelity.I guess I wish the characters would get more backstory/interactions, as well as a longer campaign. But that's how good it is. I wanted more. I wanted to hang out more in this game. And you will spend a lot of time, since on normal, this is hard. But you have endless continues, and four difficulties means four ways to play.Steel Assault is a steal (HEHE). Please consider buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

So thanks to him I got the chance to know and give it a try. :DIt feels like an original Mega Drive. The pixel art and cutscenes are stunning. It's special. Good level design and challending. _childDocuments_.review: The trailers for this one hooked me. That familiar high speed arcade action energy was clearly present, and that can be enough to set it apart from other indie platformers, that in my opinion, more often have a leisurely home console feel to them. It is short and kind of simple, with only the difficulty slider and arcade mode to variety things up for you, but in my mind that makes it all the more genuine to the arcade titles that inspired it.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: well... this is more of "i'd recommend, but..." steel assault has amazing pixel art, good music, proper old-school arcade gameplay... but it is incredibly short. it is so short that even the sentence you've just read is longer than the game. granted, there's some replay value, but i really hope there will be some dlc's later on. for now i wouldn't really recommend it for the full price. it is a beautiful and fun game, but it lacks content.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that the developers listened so much to our feedback from the demo already deserves praise. I'm not going to go into details, but basically, they improved on basically every aspect of the game by a lot and made the more frustrating parts less frustrating, or non-existent.While it's a joy to see all the differences and improvements in the game compared to the demo, the game itself is fantastic. It's a high adrenaline action platformer, where split second decisions will always demand your focus pretty much all the time. It really wears down your fingers, but this is exactly what we came for. Don't get me wrong, this isn't just for oldschool platformer veterans, since now they added difficulty levels which is a welcome addition. Don't EVER feel bad for playing it on Easy or Very Easy. Get familiar with the feel of the game, the different type of enemies, stages, etc. Then if you feel like you've mastered that difficulty level, you can always challenge yourself by playing it one difficulty level above. But it also pleases the more hardcore crowd. The Normal difficulty I feel like is just right, it offers a good challenge.The music and visuals are both great, I don't have any issues whatsoever.The only real con to this game is how short it is. You're going to die a lot, but even then, it's really really short, even shorter than some oldschool NES/SNES/Genesis action platformers. Even so, I do recommend this game due to its high replay value and how generally fun it is.

name: Astral Ascent
detailed_description: Updates Roadmap Join our community (link in the right column) About the Game Astral Ascent is a 2D platformer roguelite game set in a modern fantasy world. As one of 4 Heroes with very different personalities, you must escape from The Garden , an astral prison guarded by 12 powerful and vicious bosses, the Zodiacs. CREATE YOUR OWN PLAYSTYLE Unlock dozens of unique spells for each or your characters. Optimize your own build or try out new ones to face all the challenges you'll find on your journey for freedom. Get progressively stronger with time to match up with your foes. Each run will test your skills and your reactivity. TWELVE ALMIGHTY BOSSES TO FACE The Zodiacs are 12 experienced guardians dispatched over 4 gorgeous worlds. Each with their own unique attacks and combat styles, backstories to uncover and reasons to be fighting you, they'll pose as a big threat to anyone seeking a way out of the Garden . Get yourself warned! 4 PLAYABLE CHARACTERS Unique characters. Unique weapons. Unique ways to play. Ayla: A skilled assassin sent on a mission by her guild to prove her worth, she uses her sharp blades to eliminate targets before they can react. Her speed and proficiency are unmatched. Kiran: An orphan that has learned life the hard way. He uses his raw strength to deliver attacks powerful enough to create shockwaves. Brutal. Calie: This talented sculptor became a warrior to recover the freedom her people have lost. She will use her magical gemstones to pierce enemy defenses and shred them to bits. She is unforgiving. Octave: Trained by a powerful witch, this young fighter summons ethereal weapons to attack his foes. Big or small, short or long range, he has the right one for every occasion. Lethal in all cases. A STORY THAT OPENS UP, ONE PIECE AT A TIME Astral Ascent is a roguelite infused with narration. Replayability is part of a story that will be unraveled piece by piece. As you get stronger, you will discover more about the characters, their motivations and the secrets of the world they’re trapped in. LOCAL CO-OP The weight of destiny is too heavy to carry by yourself? Don’t worry and bring a friend to play with the two-player co-op mode. Fight and crush your enemies together in local co-op or online using the Steam's Remote Play Together feature. A VAST, COLORFUL FANTASY WORLD WAITING TO BE EXPLORED Dash across gigantic landscapes. Explore original and hand-crafted areas. Discover a fantastic universe loaded with gorgeous art and fluid frame-by-frame animation.

_childDocuments_.review: amazing gaming feels like it was made for the steam deck i take mine to work and during lunch i always get an hour or so of gamplay in. the story isnt something i really care about so i dont pay attention to it. the game play loop is amazing the art style and animations are smooth never had a bug a glitch happen game has never crashed on me i dont know why it says i only got 6 hours when i know i got more time then that but thats fine. 10/10 would recommend if you want to get into rogue lites. its easy to get started and slowly turns the difficulty up before you know u are on the modifiers having a good ole time.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for you if like beautiful and fluid Roguelite games. The environment and story rich  experience, along with the  voiceovers for all (Not all yet - early access) conversations with characters and the zodiac, creates an immersive-like experience. The game has good player, character, and meta progression (More to come too! - early access).Don't let early access stop you from trying this game, it's a great time already. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Watch out, looks like someone dropped their Hades all over my dead cells.. they also bumped into a Yale while awkwardly rushing out and spilled unique lore out the wazoo. This is a beautiful mess that I look forward to cleaning up for the coming weeks and a definite labor of love. the rnd, visuals, mechanics and flow are all a major chef's kiss. Worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Fun builds, stunning art, awesome bosses! Props to the really small team that made it :)Unfortunately, the game is held back by some questionable choices on player progression, which feel like the game's main design philosophy is to have you slog through multiple runs in order to get to the more juicy content:- The game really picks up gameplay-wise from destiny level 4 onwards, reaching peak at destiny level 6+, but getting there is kinda slow and Player expression is kinda dumbed down because you need to unlock each difficulty modifier one by one (took me around 15 hours to get to destiny level 6 and 2 more hours to beat it, I could have been faster if allowed to activate multiple modifiers from the start). This is especially annoying because right after destiny level 6 a world of possibilities opens up, but I am starting to feel a bit burnt-out from the game.- Beating the game allows you to watch only one ending of the multiple characters journeying with you, for some reason, leading to what would normally be some engaging choices for min-maxers ("I wanna end the game with Ayla and Capricorn, since I don't have their endings I can get two birds with one stone) to unexpected frustration after beating the final boss. For example, I missed on Ayla's ending (and on an achievement) because I wanted to see Capricorn's first and had NO IDEA that I would be missing out on Ayla's.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Each run is so different from the last, and the ART (the art is amazing, the flow of movement and shading done with just a few pixels is breathtaking) and dialogue are incredible. I have so much respect for the small team of people working on this title, they're doing such an amazing job. The level scaling is also really fun to experience, the monsters progress in power and abilities really well.The only cons for me would be unlimited time (not sure if there's a challenge mode later in the game to make this a thing yet, there might be :D), and monster density - sometimes there's just one or two, and sometimes there's 20. BUT - it's a working title and the release isn't for some time. I'm glad to have given them some cash to further this project, it's really well done even now in it's baby stages and fun to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this pretty 2-player co-op game, but I found many issues with it that led me to be frustrated and annoyed instead.- At times when you can power up, particularly auras, the game will sometimes offer you a choice between two auras that you do not have abilities for at all. You have very limited opportunities to affect this. Why? Is it supposed to be random chance that sometimes your build sucks for the run? What is the design goal for this?- At the beginning of a run, the game offers you power-ups that you have no way to have currency for and no way to interact with. I do not understand why the designers would do this. This game is not one that gives a whole lot of power-ups, so you will not be creating a customized build -- you will be making small changes to the character you are provided. Because chances to power up are limited and you will pretty much never feel "fully powered" by the time you hit a boss, this is extra challenging. Why?- Serious control problems. It is very easy to accidentally recycle a spell instead of taking it, because "hold" RB recycles it, and "push" RB takes it. Both myself and my partner struggled with this.- Some enemies (flowers) don't make sense -- they are invincible and there are no instructions about how to fight them. It does not make logical sense for an apparently alive thing like a plant to be an invincible obstacle that cannot be defeated. Can you please add some kind of explanation?The art's good, the music is good, the creation of this game was quite an accomplishment. It looks like the designers need to revisit "hard but fair" and consider that the systems they're adapting from different genres of game need to be tweaked to fit with a roguelite like this one. I have been disappointed by these issues! I think the developers would be able to make this game into a masterpiece with a little more polish.I will definitely be keeping an eye on this game, because it has such potential, and will adjust this review in the future if possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun, but I can't say I love it. It plays pretty well, and the idea of pitting the player against overpowered but sympathetic anime villains with insane attacks that cover the entire screen is appealing. But where it falls apart for me is the story, or the attempt at that. I almost wish there was no writing in this game at all. As far as I could tell, the game tries to emulate Hades with its fully voice acted, large roster of characters, but nothing that anyone had to say during my time with it was even remotely interesting and a lot of it was totally and painfully cringe inducing. It feels a bit weird to downvote a game for something that was clearly not the focus and could be easily ignored, but I feel like the game tried to present itself as having characters I could be even somewhat invested in and that just wasn't the case. If you're the type of player that only cares about gameplay you will find plenty to like here, but for me it didn't click.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that completely caught me off guard with how good it was.  The multiple characters, their weapon options, and the plethora of skills for each add great variety to each run.  The controls feel tight, the astrology elements and overall character designs were cool, and the visuals were pleasant to look at.  Sure the characters and story could have been more fleshed out, but they are mostly just a backdrop to what's otherwise a fun mildly addictive time.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: What's released is well polished, can't wait to see the rest of the game when it finishes. A blast to play, but certain Ascension tags are a bit annoying to play with in uninteractable ways. This game is a 10/10 for me!Edit: The game has been getting consistently updated with fearless changes that all move in the right direction. These developers have a great vision, and I cannot wait for the full release to finally come.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: With a vibrant aesthetic and really fluid sprite animation, Astral Ascent is a joy to look at and explore! If you're interested in a game that can pull you in with looks alone, look no further! There's also the gameplay loop which can have tons of variety between runs! With many different types of rooms, moves, move upgrades, and ways to synergize these factors give it tons to keep the experience alive! The writing and visual storytelling is also pretty high key, I enjoy learning more as I progress through the bosses! A great experience all around!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of games like Risk of Rain, Dead Cells, Wizard of Legend, etc. These pixel-y indie roguelites are probably my favorite genre of game, and Astral Ascent is a lovely addition to that collection. The difficulty is well-balanced, the graphics are beautiful (especially the animation!), and the combat is intense with a lot of complexity.Only complaint I have is that the dialogue is a bit cheesy. Honestly if that's the only actual criticism I have, that's a really good place for a game to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Drawing elements from several of the best RogueLites out there, Astral Ascent is one of the most exciting entrants to the genre! The art is beautiful, the Combat is intense, and the platforming is smooth as you glide through the levels. Fans of Dead Cells, Wizards of Legend, and Children of Morta will love this. At the time of posting, at least 10 hrs of fresh content, so well worth buying even at alpha!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! I've been playing since 2021, super exciting to see it now officially released! everything else is really nice, yet there is a problem that whenever i enter the forge or try to fight ophiuchus, the background effects lag my laptop real bad. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: So far really fun in coop! Nice art style (full voiceover and a lot of high quality animations and art) and fun combat! Also a lot of long term upgrades and a solid roguelite progression and fun characters! Will update review later on but the first few hours were enjoyable enough to already recommend it as is!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: For early access, this game is in great shape. The game play, graphics, music are all top notch. Excellent start for a tough genre to make an impact on these days. Still early access and missing some content, but the road map looks very exciting. One of the best rogue like games I've played. I can't wait for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun early access game. Picked it up as a result of a kickstarter backing.I enjoy the music and the visuals a lot, it definitely looks like the team put work into making a labor of love. The combat is fast and feels nice, and I like how it weaves between attacks and spells. It can feel a bit repetitive at times, but that's what happens when you play any game that has several inputs for attacks. The movement is quick and floaty, and you can really do a lot of fun things depending on how you progress.I'm not super on the up-and-up with roguelikes and repetitive recreation type games, but this one is fun and I've been enjoying what I've played so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Very fast and smooth combat that is reminiscent of Wizard of Legend but as a sidescroller with a crazy amount of mobility built in. So far the only negatives are some of the mid-run upgrades being very lame (choosing between 5% damage or 5% attack speed) though some of the spell modifiers are cool they don't usually change your gameplay much at all. There also isn't much content now, only 2 of the 4 zones, 2 of the 4 characters, and 4 of the 12 bosses are available. Still, the game is very fun now and will probably be a 10/10 in a year or two from now.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just amazing. I have been following and playing it for years. Frequent updates and amazing devs that listen to the fans (it is still updated to this day frequently!!"). Combat is fun, builds are diverse and entertaining to build. Co-op is also great.  You will never be done with it the content is almost endless, even after 120 hours i feel like i'm only at about 70%.If you like rogue-likes that are tough and need skill you need to buy the game now! 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous, I'd say it's the most beautiful pixel style game I've ever played! I'm also impressed with the sfx, they give the beautiful animations a badass extra push. The combat feels great, and I loved the progression feel, both the skill that you develop by practising and all the various progression roguelite elements that the game has, which are many! _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Building SpellsI had difficulty understanding how to build my spells, I couldn't, at first, understand why the second zodiac just absolutely bodied me. Turns out gambits scale your damage. I'm not sure if I missed a tutorial on building spells or what but knowing that matching spell scaling icons to the gambit spell type is a must to do any meaningful damage.What I mean by that is, when you pick up a spell. On the top left of every spell, there's a scaling shown, so tier 2 spells have 40% + gambit modifier. Leveling up with pavos feather increases the 40% and using gambits scales up the second number. I was only able to figure out how to scale elemental gambits. For example, a spell with fire scaling would have 40%+ a fire symbol. For every fire gambit you equip, your spell damage goes up. At 4 fire gambits, you have a +100% damage.As you progress, you get higher and higher tier spells, so the game boils down to minmaxing when to scrap a spell. You could have 4 gambit slot unlocked tier 1 spell with matching gambit bonuses but it gets outclassed by any tier 4 spell.I found that for each world, maxing out a single spell either with gambit bonuses or with pavos feathers resulted in better success. So after world 1 for example, I would have 1 spell that was either tier 4 or had all the matching bonuses. I would swap my other spells on the fly and just hoped for the best.I couldn't figure out how to scale the non-elemental spells to any meaningful degree. I think a spell building tutorial would be nice.Character StatsI think scaling health was the go to. Attack speed felt like a trap, at best you get mana to produce more spells with higher attack speed. But your auto attack damage is miniscule.Damage scaling felt like a trap, I'm bad at platformers and a glass cannon build never worked out for me.For my Octave run, I had 13hp, 4 damage and 3 attack speed buffs. Take that how you will.I think that the basic attack damage should be scaled up a little higher, I shouldn't always have to use spells to take down the most basic of enemies in exploration rooms with any sort of meaningful efficiency.GambitsI think there needs to be more gambits for each element. I think around 10 should be good. Reason being, with three electric spells, all of them had the exact same modifiers I think. Just electrify on hit. Albeit with different % of success. I think more unique gambits would be nice. Hell, even unique mythical gambits would be nice. Something like 10% chance to recast a spell or something like that.Non-elemental gambits, I couldn't figure out their scaling. So I thought they were useless. Having a gambit tutorial would be nice.PowersI lucked out with a 5% hp Regen power along with 3 powers that modified electric damage. So I geared my spells to scale with electric damage and it seemed to work. I did have trouble understanding/seeing with my powers did. I think either slightly changing the colors of the elemental effects or making them slightly larger might be helpful both for seeing and understanding the elemental effects of spells and powers.ProwessI picked bellator has: 5 seconds of increased duration, cool down is 20 seconds shorter but 5 seconds less duration, and electrify on hit.I think the signature spells were done well, I liked Octaves and Ayla's spells. The fire guy, I never played after I saw that his auto attack range was quite small.The modifiers for basic attacks were underwhelming. I picked up the +20% damage modifier and after a few rooms, it became redundant I thought. I think basic attacks need some work, to make them viable for damage along with giving mana back. Even adding a stagger to some enemies might be helpful, like they do in deadcells or hollow knight.AestheticsLoved what you guys did with the pixel art. Looked up how the game looked before, and I'm glad you made changes to character art in dialogue screens.MovementLove the movement of the game, just wish there were more I frames when dashing.POV while playingJust wish everything was slightly more zoomed in, just a little so I can better follow what my spell effects did. I had 3 electric spells, all with 4 matching gambits and I couldn't for the life of me tell what spark did. I could never see it on the screen before it vanished.Andromeda's ChallengesFun concept. Just would like to see different iterations of it. All of them currently are 'take no damage'. Something like 'clear room in 1 minute' or a 'survive 1 minute' might make it more interesting.Overall, great job on the game. Looking forward to the next update!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting much from the game when I bought it through a humble bundle, but I was enjoying myself. Then I got to the final boss, about 10 hours in, and on beating him for the first time I get given a ton of more progression options I didn't expect going in blind. Tons of passives for beating bosses and higher difficulties and every character getting 2 additional weapons to the ones they start with and each of those getting three passives. I had just beat the game for the first time, on my first run with Octave, and didn't even have Calie yet cus the cutscene for her didn't show up until after, so I was getting ready to play what I thought was the last character, and thus last way to play the game, before the game tells me nope have more content. So far almost the whole game has been throwing me content I didnt expect, in a good way. Legitimately thought I was buying a shovel ware bundle for a few bucks and ended up finding one of my new favorite games. Kinda wish I had payed full price for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Red Barrens trailer was so good that I didn't even need to check the gameplay which didn't disappoint anyways I wasn't expecting gameplay to be this fluid, you definitely feel like you have the sheer control of the character and what is happening around you, great work devs. I just hope this game gets the attention it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much to offer. Whether or not you're a roguelite fan.I'm not specifically, but its world is so welcoming, colorful, and peaceful that you actually enjoy the challenge instead of fearing it.Diving into each run feels like a chance to discover more, enjoy the awesome music and improve in skills, feeling more and more its juicy combos the more you play.On top of everything this game is doing so well, you'll also be able to play with a friend, a child or your loved one, making it even more enjoyable.Congrats to the entire team for delivering a game that feels finished while only being in early access
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is excellent, has a lot of personality and skill-based gameplay. Definitely worth getting!In contrast, I'm not a fan of pixelized graphics in 2024... 40-50 years ago that was okay but now.. could be so much more immersive if it had cartoon graphics instead. With the very simplified pixels, even distinguishing between the avatar, monsters, and background in this title can be difficult. Anyway I understand it's a stylistic choice but I feel like this title could be a worldwide hit like Hades if only they chose a similar type of graphics. Yes sometimes it's the graphics style/feel that determine the difference.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely positively amazing. Really unique and fun atmosphere, fun buildcrafting, and great amounts of unique dialogue. There's a lot of replayability available here, and you won't get bored for a long time. My only minor nitpick is that I wish the playable characters had more to say, as even around the 10hr mark the dialogue when moving around and going from floor to floor has run dry and you won't really see too much new dialogue on that part. But, there's still tons of unique dialogue in the boss fights and between runs, which is really neat and a nice touch to the world building.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY recommend for everyone who even remotely likes roguelikes to play it. The developers love the game and community, having listened constantly during early access and included community inspired changes each patch.Story is great as you piece things together, really fun in that aspect. Combat system is a 11/10 for me. The hundreds of spell modifying gambits, over 100 total spells and hundreds of build-defining auras intertwine with each other into a beautiful song of chaos and pure fun. Then there is Andromedas bar, the stone altars, spell level increases via pavo's feathers, the sun and moon, zodiac summons, echoes, eclipsed rooms, Andromedas challenges, fight room challenges, 4 unique areas each with three bosses before the event horizon, the element system with, of course, elemental and non-elemental status effects. The choice of one of 3 random daily buffs via the telluric telescope, near infinite replayability via the destiny level system and destiny fragments to buff yourself up as you keep exponentially increasing the games difficulty to get stronger yourself, if you so choose. Oh, did I mention the game has coop?! Granted it's either local or steam remote play together, but it's there!The roadmap for 2024 looks insane as well! We already have new spells and pvp in beta. There is another character named Yamat in the works. Currently there are 13 zodiacs and 4 characters (Ayla, Calie, Octave, Kiran), who each have an ending dedicated to them. The playable characters are going to get one or more other weapons to play with, which will of course change the playstyle and the ability system is going to get reworked as well! Last but not least, there is another world planned after which a new gamemode will follow.And there is a good chance there will be more to come after.Again, I urge you to play Astral Ascent! The game, developers, and especially you, deserve it!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of substantial content for an early access. Good variety of spells and add ons for build variety. Each character has good personality. The pixel art is just incredible. One of the best looking indie games in my opinion. Developer stays dialled into the community and takes their suggestions for balancing. Great roguelike.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Like some mentioned; after about ten hours the cracks start to show.Primarily its the fact that almost everything is some sort of passive improvement that does not change your playstyle between runs. You got an aura focused on Meteors? ok, add meteor gambits to all your spells and watch them  oblitorate the screen. Ok, today its Spark. Tomorrow its Fire Shield. The spells themselves, 4 spell rotation, do not change anything about the way you approach the game. Its hit, hit, hit, spell, hit, hit, spell, etc. It does not matter if its pillars, knives or lightning balls flopping from the sky. They are just a damage dealer with a different animation.The low variety is one thing, but the hitboxes and telegraphing are inconsistent and hurt the overall flow of the game. One enemy show its red hitbox and you need to dodge instantly, another has a windup and now you got hit. Another does not have any telegraphing hitboxes at all for some reason. Some windups show it by increasing the red colored gradient, others do not. There is no rhyme or reason to it and this inconsistency I do not understand, and makes dodges kind of confusing. Was this a windup or an instant? And sir, why don't you have any red hitbox and just throw your massive sword out of out nowhere?Speaking of dodges and hitboxes, that is assuming you can see them, There are enough explosions and Meteors and stuff flying about that often it's barely clear what is happening. Coupled that with the fact you do not have invincibility frames, You might just lose 50% hp in a single barrage of attacks in an eclipse room, where a lot of  glowing elite enemies and explosions do not make it easier to see what is going on.Having said all of that; the game is easier than you think. Life, regeneration, and echoes (more passives) with life bonuses fly around so often that all the random damage and unclear hitboxes are quickly healed back. It just takes a run or two to figure out you need auras focusing on a single mechanic; fire shield, poison, slime, spark or whatever and align all your gambits and passives to that same mechanic and everything dies within seconds. Also at DL5, where I called it a good day, sir.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, do recommend, but be aware there is 0 crash protection, if your game crashes you lose your run, it doesn't save at the start of each room like you would expect from a modern room based roguelite. Otherwise it's a lot of fun, the progression is neat, the skills are fun, there's a LOT to unlock and the movesets for characters, bosses, and enemies are all pretty interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Just played through my first two runs, wanted to try each of the characters out. Actually beat the first boss on the second go so I was able to see the second world. (Would love online co-op if there are any plans on that!)Bit slow or has a wee bit of lag at times. Had to play in windowed, but overall it is a great game. The story-line seems intriguing and the characters all feel pretty interesting so far. The few spells I got all were cool too, with good animations. I like the gambit system in that you can add effects to those spells, only got a few utility abilities though, will update after a few more runs. Can not wait for this to be polished off as it already has loads of potential. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game around 12-13 hours. By finished, I mean that I got to the end boss and beat him. There is an end game that extends the playtime, but I found that I had come to a nice stopping point by that time.The combat is nice and fun. Good varieties of different builds. Boss fights are pretty epic with all their attack patterns. And the levels never feel too long or sluggish to get through. I found that a typical run would last around 30-45 minutes.If you are a fan of games like dead cells, then I think you may enjoy this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I loved everything about it. Was it hard at the start? Yes. But it was fun getting better and better every time. I managed to beat the final boss around my 20th run. Assassin is my fav. character with a focus on building sword gambits (Ice and spirit) and getting my atk speed as high as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh and fun entry to the genre, Astral Ascent delivers on beautiful stylized visuals and fast free-flowing combat. The progression system is incredibly rewarding, and unlocking new spells gives a very enjoyable variety from run to run. The particles and enemy attacks/patterns are very polished and readable, as well as the intense boss fights that present themselves in visually flashy and viscerally satisfying ways. Movement in this game is an absolute treat and it feels amazing to hop from wall to wall in parkour segments and among enemies in combat scenarios. The cut scenes and soundtrack, not to undersell it, are fantastic. The themes for The Sun and The Moon inspire such a feeling of awe just to name an example. I have been keeping up with this game since the beginning of its early access run, and I believe here we have a truly fantastic game that is a hidden gem of its kind. Highly recommended, especially to play locally with a friend. My one and only gripe is the voice acting can be awkward, unfitting and limply delivered at times, but it is easily overlooked among all its other shining qualities.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, and only more to come. Each update refines an already good feature, or replaces one that didn't quite fit. The game play is satisfying and gets even better as the updates come in. Whether waiting to buy at full release or interested enough to join the early access, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, fun and addictive as much as Hades in terms of combat.The dodge movement gives you a perfect hit free frame of time, which lets even a bad player like me get it going.The story is there for the sake of having a story, basically all characters want to kill the final boss cus he is the bad guy. _childDocuments_.review: This is a first impressions sort of review:As someone who hasn't played many other games like this (pretty much Hades), I've got to say. I HIGHLY recommend this game! And I know I've barely scratched the surface.For those who don't want a score: Just buy the game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: For those on the fence:I think this game is definitely worth your money. The best thing about it is the gameplay. It has some of the most fun synergy building systems I've found in any roguelike and I think that out of any other roguelike I have played or seen it has the best moment to moment gameplay. It's not perfect but if you are looking for a roguelike of the highest quality at an indie game price point.A little more in-depth:Now this game (after my time in early access and after release) doesn't have any outright flaws but when I compare the game to other roguelikes, specifically Hades which in my mind is where the bar is at currently, it falls short in some areas. Personally I prefer the presentation of Hades. Art and music are very subjective elements but I really feel like Hades had more polish when it came to art (but the difference is relative enough that my feelings my come down to preference for a specific art style). This game has smooth animations and everything looks great, but I really felt like Hades art was just a step up. Still the pixel art is nice. The music I think might be one of the more consistent meh elements of the game. Composing music is insanely hard but as a player there was never a moment I wanted to look up a track or was wowed by the audio of this game.The narrative here is also definitely not why I'm playing. There are stories and lots of pieces of information to discover about all the different characters, but I don't think it's delivered in a very interesting way. I've been comparing this game to Hades a lot but honestly I would say that there are plenty of roguelikes that have stronger narratives. It doesn't take anything away from the game but it doesn't add much either in my opinion.Ultimately though the game is just pure distilled fun. So many insane options, a really fun flow state, and even the decision making both out of run and in run are exciting to make. You get tons of unlocks after every run which feels really rewarding (but does eventually run dry) and ultimately I think this game is amazing. Like I said I really think the gameplay is the best of any other action roguelike. I loved Hades but this game is actually more fun to play for me.Ultimately if you don't like this style of game, don't play it. If you aren't sure or you do like it however please pick it up and give it a try. It is insanely fun and this devs clearly put a lot of love and effort into making an incredible experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This review was made in a way to describe the things i really like about this game but also the things i hope are worked on before full release.First of the gameplay feels really good and the implementation of run progression can with some interface and generally more options probably be a contender for one of THE BEST ways to make the player progressivly stronger as the run progresses.The dialog reminds me of how hades implemented it where it actually is a big reason to keep playing since the way the charakters interact is really enjoyable, if you liked how hades did dialog you will like how they do it here.Then there are some bad stuff. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. It may take a few runs to "get" it but once you do it becomes addicting FAST. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, what a find. I wasn't sure about this game at first, until about 3 runs in I realized that feeling was only because Astral Ascent is genuinely doing its own thing that I needed to get comfy with. And it's doing it really bloody well. Exactly what I'm looking for, yet increasingly hard to achieve in this genre. "Wait a minute... this game is fantastic"Gamefeel is superb, run variety seems high especially with the multiple playable characters. I particularly like how gradual the progressive difficulty system is as you start winning, how generous the game is with unlocks, and how the systems seem easy to grok but hard to master - stuff you can kinda ignore at first will become more important to you as you keep playing. (E.g. one 'flaw' I have at the moment is I'm not super fussed what my spells actually do - whether they pound the ground or generate orbs etc - just the damage and effects they kick out. And I'm certainly not paying attention to which one is next in the queue. But I'm betting money I'll be watching those like a hawk in future as things keep getting tougher.)All these aspects make for a very smooth and rewarding uphill climb that's difficult to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A fast paced roguelike that may have pixel art, but doesn't prevent it from having gorgeous VFX.Feels a lot like wizard of legend, with more character and spell variety.Soundtrack feels like it was ripped of from dreamscaper though, maybe i'm wrong but there's many songs that i 100% feel i've heard from dreamscaper.Anyways. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: super solid game, really enjoyable combat with varied builds between characters/runs, the writing is enjoyable and interesting, the setting seems to be taking a lot of cues from Hades (bosses are not strictly antagonistic and some of them can even be recruited as summons in your runs, overarching story that explains both what you're trying to achieve and also how you keep repeating runs) but puts its own spin on it, and the updates have been very solid and have added some great QoL and lots of avenues for run variance and build variety.Incredibly worth your time even in early access, and full release comes next month so if it looks up your alley now is a perfect time to grab it before a full release price increase
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to really compliment this game on.  Beautiful artwork, music, and presentation.  But how about the game?  Play control that's smooth as butter and responsive as a coiled spring.  The difficulty start VERY easy, and slowly ramps up to a difficult boss that you might, or might not beat your first time.  Win or lose, its fine because the rogue like approach here is very similar to Hades.Unlocks are permanent stat buffs and potential new abilities to find during your trek through the levels and bosses.  New characters become unlocked in town, as well as new means of upgrading your character.  Its a really nice drip feed and doesn't make you feel like you wasted your time.  If I had to summon up the philosophy of this game it would be, "Challenge without frustration".  Its fun!  Update:  Have continued to play and this is an AMAZING game!  Don't miss out!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I would put this as third in this genre, right behind Hades and Dead Cells.Combat is incredibly smooth and satisfying, lots of interesting synergies that the devs continuously add/update/improve.The TL;DR of this game is - if you even remotely liked Hades, I don't see how you wouldn't enjoy this game. Whilst it isn't quite at Hades level of polish, thematically it's great, it has unique and super fun mechanics (I would argue the boss fights, for example, are more fun/challenging/mechanically complex than Hades) and has great meta progression with multiple characters. Much like Hades, once you 'beat' the game, the ascension/heat system comes into play, adding more challenges and depth to the game.Overall I highly recommend this game after 60+ hours and still playing to beat the ascension levels required for each character's 'true' ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Even at it's current state and with what little it has in it's early access content, this game is a blast to play, and I had no hesitation in playing it past the 2 hour refund mark. The game play is nice and fun. If you enjoy fluid combo style combat, this game is for you. The pixel art graphics, which is what brought me to this game in the first place, looks very nice and I enjoy it a lot (especially the boss intro cutscenes. I never get tired of those). This game has a unique kind of style in it's presentation that I rarely see in other games. It being early access, there are still a few rough edges. The game could use some optimizations to let it frame lag less, as I've had to set my graphics to very low to make it run smoothly, which is strange considering that this is a 2D game and I've had less stylized 3D games run smoother with higher settings.  and also I've had some issues with crashing (which seem to only happen in windowed mode). 10/10 would recommend. Probably going to be one of the next big rogue like titles
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like Hades, which I like, both story-wise and gameplay-wise! You unlock bits of dialogue and story with each run/death, and there's always something to upgrade when you go back to the hub area, and new mechanics are introduced at a steady pace.The boss fights are really neat, each having their own mechanics to dodge, and they're all really fun. The spell-system is neat and I like how they're upgraded, and there's a lot of passive bonuses you can stack via different mechanics available to you.I can see the game has a lot of updates coming in the future as well. With all of this said, I highly recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, massive replayability, beautiful art, well balanced, local and online coop, I can’t find one bad thing to say about it. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've played. Normally, when I 100% a roguelike I drop it for another one, but I keep coming back to this one. The combat in Astral Ascent feels so snappy; you never feel the game screws you over with any of the mechanics, knowing you can always improve. The voice acting is incredible with 99% of characters fully voiced.The Story isn't very complex, but it is there, with mostly characters interacting with each other. There are also collectible stories you can pick up in a run. The spell/aura/weapon systems bring in a very welcome complexity, that gives you a diverse build every run. The only negative thing I can really say about this game is the length of runs. If you aren't a speedrunner, I've found the average time of a run is just under an hour, which also depends on which difficulty you're on. I'd like to end this review to just plead with whomever may be reading this: This game is worth every penny and is a complete steal with a sale. The devs are excellent and update the game to this day regularly. Do yourself a favor and grab a copy (and even play some couch co-op or remote play co-op with some friends)
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr; 4/10 gameThe pixel graphic is decent and full of style, there is a boss design and systems are ok but the gemplay loop is a bit uninspired(small segments linked together add nauseam) and the character customization during runs push you to perform forced synergies for your builds. The gameplay is serviceable but nothing stellar. What I disliked the most is the rogue lite elements balance, there is too much power hidden behind them, so it creates arbitrary gates. When you're building a rogue lite, gameplay and mechanics discovery should always come fiirst, here mechanics are forced into you in a very dumbed down maneer and force you almost to play with upgrades.It is not that bad, but it is imho a bit below what I'd call a game worth playing. There are lots of games of the same genre flourishing, it is very far from dead cells but it is better than most of its clones. I expect the editor to do better in the future, there is definitely talent in this project.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing Hades, I remember thinking "I wish other studios will take a few pages from this game". And boy, did Astral Ascent developers  (Hibernian) pay attention!With a This game has the nervous & frantic combat from Dead Cells, the iterative storytelling from Hades, 4 different characters with distinctive personalities and gameplay, and, most outstandingly, a   as it's the best in the genre since Isaac and the Gungeon.A colorful, fast and furious game best enjoyed with a friend. If Hades and Dead Cells are the 9/10 of the genre, this is a solid 8.5+.(+) Excellent moveset,   rife with double jumps, dashes, wall climbs and plunging attacks(+) Surprisingly  . High ceiling to optimization(+) High replayability due to the way that Auras, Echos, Zodiac spells can significantly effect the play you play the game, even if obtained in the middle of a run.(+)  : combat is epic and the intro cinematics are badass(+) Path of Destinies (equivalent to Ascensions / NG+) level 6 reveal  , in the same way the "extreme measures" features in Hades did: just after you think you have the fights figured out, the enemies take the shackles off and remind you how much you still have to learn. Hats off to the devs for pulling this out successfully(+) Coming back to the garden and the bar, with its relaxing music in the background, is a welcome change of pace between 2 bouts of frenetic dashing.  (-) The  , which makes the Memory Fragment unlocking underwhelming. A lot of effort went into crafting backstories for the Zodiacs, but not much of it is compelling. Little character development in the dialogues with your characters and the zodiacs between first encounters and final runs. You'll quickly learn to click "redeem all" and ignore the text. (-) The screen can quickly turn into a  , especially in multiplayer. Even in a single 1 vs 1 with a Zodiac, it's not always clear where the safe spots are and how to dodge certain attacks, which, instead of encouraging the player to figure out the patterns to eventually play clean and perfect the encounter, results in  . (-) Invulnerability frames for bosses are an infuriating feature to waste your slow-loading summon on.(-)  , with a few special offenders that must be called out: - when replacing upgrades on your special ability or weapon, there is no way to first check what the offered 3 choices are before you decide if, yes or no, you want to replace one of your upgrades. - confusing color code which lets you think that you are picking the right gambits, but in reality there is no synergy between 2 abilities that have similar names and the exact same color. - some special effects from Astral Auras are not described at all(-) The tutorial manages to both hold your hand too much (start / stop / go talk with this person) and fail to provide important information you'll have to figure out later.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow manages to split the difference between Hades and Dead Cells, and do it well. Game is tuned on the harder side of things even by roguelike veteran standards, but combat is tight and well-designed, so you have only yourself to blame for losses. Naturally, you'll want to be sure to utilize and upgrade every part of a character's kit, as well as meta-game progression unlocks, to find success. Don't let the cheery aesthetic fool you, is what I guess I'm trying to say.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, the devs just keep on adding more and more stuff, for free!!! There's a DLC with a new character thats pretty interesting and fun, totally worth it. This is honestly one of the most fun rogues that I've played on a while. With a great variety of enemies, a fast-paced combat, dynamic boss fights and all the fun of getting powerful synergies that normally comes with the rogue genre, this game is definitely a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not normally one to leave a review for a game but this one really struck me. It's a solid platformer roguelike (lite?) with elements of deck building with how you model your spells. The game is challenging and the visuals are striking! I really love the animated pixel intro for every constellation. The voice acting is nice, it has good pacing and doesn't sound too hokey. I am super excited for the full release
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Great action platformer roguelite that goes heavy on build customization during a run. Plenty of spells to try out to build your own skill rotation, linear room to room map system where you choose from 3 different rooms to enter with different rewards. Plenty of animation cancelling and movement related stuff to make the gameplay fast feeling. You attack until you fill up your mana meter and start spellcasting relentlessly.Bosses are fun fights and have fun patterns on their normal and true forms, designed well around your cooldown-based iframe dodge and positioning.Nice metaprogression elements, first time clear happens pretty early and opens up more meta progression and story related elements. Best part about this is the amount of voice acting, so many lines said between characters and even deciding on what you get or what happened in the current room is nice to hear from the characters and shows their personality really well.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly easy to recommend. This is one of the best roguelikes out there. Probably the best co-op roguelike.+ Extremely satisfying, snappy controls+ Very good enemy design+ Steam remote play works like playing locally. Slightly finicky+ Never feels unfair, i just feel bad+ Does a great job of balancing flashy attacks and visual clarity. You can mostly see vital attack information over screen clutter+ Great progression inside as well as outside of a run+ Lots of fun build options+ Every Character is very unique+ I like the Art style+- Nitpick 1: The Skill system with 4 different skills in a chain is... strange. Its not the best system i have ever seen, but it is novel and works. I dont think there is anyone actually making a combo out of this. Everyone will just try to get the same skill 4 times. But it is an additional hurdle and thus still works fine as a roguelike system.+- Nitpick 2: I don't like shared rewards. _childDocuments_.review: extremely fun, extremely replayable game. If you're looking for a game with incredible artstyle, nice music, excellent voice-acting, action-packed & fun gameplay with some elements of classic rogue-like RNG progression, this is the game for you.  It was a serendipitous experience playing this game for the first time and watching it just exceed all expectations, highly recommend that more people give it a chance and try it, because I guarantee that it can get you hooked if you let it.The game also includes the ability to do steam remote play with a friend, or just local co-op if you have a controller on hand. I play it with some of my online friends and it's a very fun experience going through the levels together, and I am looking forward to the future of this game. _childDocuments_.review: - Game feels very fluid after rebinding Dash to a shoulder button - it always feels better for horizontal platformers.- Spells are fairly unique.- Audio is great.- Difficulty feels decent at the moment (Beating Stage 2 is very doable after a couple of runs).- Concept of rotating bosses is interesting and pretty well executed.- Interesting stages.- Pretty visuals if you like pixel art. If you're not really a pixel fan (like me), it's passable and inoffensive.- Is actually fairly charming.- Melee/Spell balance. Right now, Spells comprise of majority of your damage - melee attacks cannot compete. This is somewhat fine, but sometimes it feels bad chipping away at something for 20 or so hits.- Spell hitboxes can be strange and unintuitive. Ethereal Knives, for example, has a homing property, but only if it's cast in the right direction and within a range around your character. Despite that, once it's locked on, it has unlimited range, so it can feel a little weird.- Portrait Artstyle. The style on the Title screen fits the game much more, but the in-game portraits feel slightly mismatched (YMMV).- Mana not recovering when entering a new stage. I understand that Mana is supposed to be a resource on its own, but seeing as it's renewable from simply hitting things, it feels a bit odd that entering a new stage doesn't just set you at max Mana. As it is right now, it makes you want to finish off enemies with basic attacks... which would be fine, if the basic attacks didn't hit like peanuts. It would significantly speed up the game's pacing.- Percentage based Gambits. Nothing is more irritating than an unreliable effect. It feels like an utter waste of a slot if it doesn't proc, and borderline broken if you get several procs in a row (Infinite Mana, for example).- No way to customise the start of the run beyond character selection - at least, up to where I've played. Wizards of Legend, another spell-based roguelike, allowed ways to tweak your initial start via spell selection or starting relics, allowing for strategies before the run even starts.- Upgrades seem fairly linear at the moment.- Progression does not feel smooth - some things are unlocked even before features become unlocked.- Lack of visual clarity. Everything is so bright and vivid that it can be very easy to miss things when there are several enemies in the same location, mostly due to the game lacking outlines.- Luck plays a huge factor. You can get an Aura that has a Freeze effect... and have zero spells pop up that gives Freeze.- Customised starts to runs. The current system is similar to Dead Cells and Skul, but with 4 spells that you're forced to cycle through, this feels a lot less impactful than it should be.- Basic-Attack or Dash upgrades (not just Auras). Finding an upgrade to something you use 80% of the time would be very nice to have.- Mana Recovery on new stage (or on stage completion). See above.- Passive spells. Not only would they potentially reduce your cycle, they might open up interesting interactions. Maybe set a cap so it doesn't change too much.- Boss Relics, or really, something that can alter gameplay/playstyle significantly. (1 less spell, last spell in cycle does X, can dash twice, etc.)- Less percentage-based effects on Gambits. (Seriously, Hades only had Critical Hit mechanics as the only chance-based mechanic for a reason, and even then it was just a concept of 'more damage'. Stability is very important to curb frustration in skill-based games). Nearly all gambits in this game is percentage, from status effects to buffs to summons, and it is frustrating.- An alternative damage reading system. I would still like to see individual components of damage on-hits personally, but this is subjective to preference.Overall, Astral Ascent is out to a great start, but it's currently still missing elements of core design that makes me truly addicted/hooked. It can feel like a slog rather than a blitz at times, unfinished EA content aside. I'm looking forward to more content, polish, stabilisation/optimisation (game can stutter, slowdown, or take ages to load at the moment, but this is understandably the first build) and am planning to set the game aside until it's more fleshed out.To buyers, this game has a bunch of potential, depending on how well the devs listen to feedback. You're not buying the game for now, you're buying it to support it for the experience you might get later. I'd say it's worth it if you're a fan of the genre and are looking for something new and have already played the most well-known titles, and a few lesser known ones (like Blade Assault or Niigate Tale). But if you're new to the action-roguelike genre, I'd recommend playing the already completed gems first (Hades, Wizard of Legend, Skul, Dead Cells, Warm Snow). They'll give you far more bang for your buck at the moment and have sold like crazy for a reason. Come back to Astral Ascent later.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to Roguelites, bought a bunch and made my way here and to be honest I was pretty annoyed by Astral Ascent at first. From the jump I personally didn't like the music or the characters speaking in gameplay/writing so I muted all that and felt much better about it afterwards.The gameplay is good but not great, I think it would benefit from being simpler honestly. Coming off Skul which is very simple but effective in terms of building, I found too many options in builds for Astral Ascent to be not very meaningful. Not saying everything has to be broken but it should at least feel rewarding to lean into whatever elemental thing you got going for you in the run.Grunts are not fodder in this game, at higher difficulties you need to be very alert at all times because relaxing will definitely cost you from even the lowest enemies. Not necessarily a bad quality of the game but it can make for some extremely frustrating encounters.All that being said Kiran quickly became my main thanks to his counter and when it came to clearing all the runs up to Destiny 20, I leaned into exactly that to get them done. Took 4 runs to clear the game the first time with him and after that it definitely became more fun for me. I cleared the rest up to 6 without dying and then that's when I ofc hit the wall because that is basically when the true difficulty becomes evident.Acclimating to what the game rewards stylistically, in your choices and gameplay, is what really made this game stand out for me. When you got a nice build going and you get in the zone to finally get the clear it really does put you on cloud nine (but I guess that goes for most roguelites). Floors over Destiny 6 you get to customize the difficulty, increasing the Destiny level so after 6 I went almost immediately to level 20, figuring out what was most manageable difficulty wise was great and I ended up clearing it after around 8 or so runs.I had fun for what it is and what its worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is an extremely ambitious project, and the initial offering in this early access I think gives great reason to be optimistic that Hibernian Workshop will hit their mark and produce something extremely special.The art (both the art direction and the art assets themselves) are of extremely high quality and look drop dead gorgeous. The UI and core combat of the game are polished to the point that you can see clearly the vision the developers have for the game. Controls are tight and responsive; there is the nucleus of the same hypnotic, strike-and-weave flow as you would feel in something like Dead Cells.All that being said, the trade-off of releasing an early access game with this level of polish is the relatively sparse offering of content at this juncture. It needs to be clear that if you buy the game at this stage, you are doing so out of a desire to support the work on this game and to be able to come back and enjoy content updates when they drop.I firmly recommend Astral Ascent for any fans of this genre because the spark of true greatness is present here, and I can think of no better reason to get involved in an Early Access project.EDIT: I feel like I should update this review now that the game has reached it's full release. With the changes to how Auras and Prowess upgrades work, you can really get the insane synergies and screen-shaking god-like combos that rogue-likes are famous for. This is the best Rogue-like I've played this year, and stands alongside Dead Cells, Hades and Risk of Rain 2 as one of the best modern Rogue-likes in general. Get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must play for Roguelike fans. It really has infinite potential. I'm playing after the "Spells and Synergies Update" and I believe it addressed a lot of the concerns of those with middling reviews. I look forward to constantly checking up on this game for the next few years whenever a patch drops to see this game get even better. In short, it's a wild, sort of anime-style hi-rez 2D action platformer roguelike that's main unique traits are the champions that you choose to use on each run and the spells you'll equip them with. You have a rotation of four spells, starting off with four of the same spell and slotting in new spells as the run progresses. You go through your spells in order, like drawing cards, forcing you to think about what spell is coming up and how to use it. Spells can be slotted with gambits that modify the spells and synergize with the rest of your strategy. The best roguelikes feel meaningfully different from run to run and this game really checks that box with it's vast array of spells, auras, talents, and unique buffs. After finishing a run I just want to switch to a new character and dive back in. The moment-to-moment gameplay is the best of any roguelike I've ever played, Dead Cells included. The invincible dash is on a low cool down, letting you jet around the screen. You can (double) jump super high and doing damage resets your jump leading to insane control over movement. There are fights where I don't even touch the ground, jumping between enemies in the air and deploying screen filling spells and attacks. Combat is first in class, and that's really the most important thing, because the core game is so fantastic that the developers can continually add to it and take this really special game to even higher heights. If you're on the fence about this game. Don't be. If you like roguelikes, if you like super frantic, tight action games, and if you want to see where the devs go with gem then just get it now. It should only get better.

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is an action 2D-roguelite that has a satisfying gameplay loop, nails the feeling of progression and offers a lot of variety over the course of the many runs one can have.Only some small nitpicks add up that hold this game back from being an alltime classic. Okay, let's start at the very basics of what makes an action roguelite good:Engaging gameplay loop (you don’t want to zone out, it needs to be mechanically and theoretically engaging)Runs have to feel different (roguelites are supposed to be replayed, they have to differ)Steady feeling of progression (unlocking new stuff, options or possible opponents)Consistency (a good player should be able to win every run consistently)These I think are some of the main points, they are not exhaustive. Astral Ascent basically nails all of them.It is a skill based 2D action roguelike which has almost fully preventable damage, especially as Astral Ascent always shows danger zones of enemy attacks. The player can rely on mechanical skill, but does not need to. Absurd and strong combos are not only encouraged but also rewarded. I want to stress that despite some combinations being forceable, flexibility is very important as brute forcing is rarely as optimal as going with the flow.I don’t want to spoil the surprises, but there is a lot of variance, starting with the multiple playable characters even. My favorite part of the game is the progression:Astral Ascent offers permanent upgrades which are not necessarily just stat increases but often consistency boosters and new “gimmicks” that allow varied play.Sometimes I don’t want just more damage, but to abuse a new technique to then earn myself high damage. Just one spoiler for the challenge seekers: the game offers content even after unlocking most upgrade, as a system akin to the heat system in Hades exists (as in you pick disadvantages to spice runs up and get more rewards). And it is VERY hard. This is some sweet pixel art. Everything in Astral Ascent oozes lively energy. The sprites are very simple, but convey enough. While the playable characters are animated well, the bosses steal the show.They are energetic, fast-paced, but still very comprehensible. It is hard to create good and varied patterns for bosses that still feel intuitive and fitting for the character. An often used test is that a character should be recognizable by their silhouette. Astral Ascent passed that test with flying colors.Using this transition:Especially, I want to stress how well the game uses colors. Different elements use different key colors, but the game manages to make me understand what I am seeing despite dropping like 10 different colored projectiles because of my build. The color coding helps a lot, even in menus. Memorizing that poison symbol? Nah, I just memorize purple, easy. Through the use of a smart keyword system, everything gets explains fast and well, without having the player bored by superfluous tutorials. Long gone are the times I am ready to invest an hour or two for something that I could learn within 10 minutes. Astral Ascent actually keeps it at 10 minutes and technically makes most of the information completely optional. It is absolutely possible to win runs and finish the story without ever really understanding most of the keywords and basic interactions. The music of Astral Ascent is very competent, yet it lacks that certain oomph.Especially the relaxing pieces are very well done and can be listened to endlessly.The battle themes on the other hand are too short and loop a little too soon as a result.Everything that is in the game is good. The problem is that the tracks needed to be a little longer to fit in the mood, and listening to the same battle track three times in 10 minutes does get tiring. I do not dislike the music, far from it. This is one of the few times I did not only want, but actually needed more music. The lore of Astral Ascent is more than serviceable, despite being told in relatively short text segments. Especially, characters explicitly talking about what happened in the past and discussing their relations is very much interesting as relationships evolve over the course of the runs.The problem I am having is that the actual story is too simplistic, even for its own sake. I think that the developers wanted to reduce overhead and create something very coherent (at which they succeeded), but could not formulate a more ambitious goal for the story as a result. If you care about genuinely good stories and want to invest in something like that, Astral Ascent is the wrong game for you. I really liked my time playing Astral Ascent and I do see myself going for some more runs, despite being a person who hates having no concrete goals. The runs were fun, the gameplay is engaging, and the consistency is good enough. If the story and music were on par with the rest, I would call this a masterpiece. At this point, I will still wait, but if Astral Ascent gets even more updates and gets even better, this game becomes a no-brainer to pick up.If you are a gameplay first kinda guy, though, you can do nothing wrong with Astral Ascent.

_childDocuments_.review: I had about 37 hours during early access, now about 5 hours on full release. This game is incredibly fun, fast paced and fluid. The boss fights are super fun and you'll gradually master them to the point where you can beat them regardless of your build. The builds are really unique and each run will end up with you having multiple buffed elemental attacks. There is a pretty distinct lack of comboing and synergy between these elements. Your good runs will often feel like Risk of Rain with an absurd amount of action on screen with all kinds of effects damaging your opponents. Nailing down enemy attack patterns while learning the way to optimise builds offers a really satisfying progression. This game is a solid 9/10, and could easily be an 11/10 if they added proper co-op plus some minor adjustments. One thing that came to mind was having enemies have visual queues for when they are hit-stunned. Tons of replay-ability and difficulty extension. Can't wait to see the true ending for this, the final boss is beyond sick.
