_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the previous games in the Dark Pictures Anthology you've got a pretty good idea of what to expect when you play this.  The environments and story are easily the best Supermassive Games has put out so far.  For anyone that's been to Iraq during 2003 or after, keep in mind that this touches on some of the aspects of the conflict there at the time.  There's a lot that's frustratingly difficult to process, due to the portrayal of the characters.  There are some moments and actions that could trigger some bad memories.  The characters are the most irritating bunch I've spent a Thursday night with.  They have the personality of a wet sock and are just irritatingly annoying for much of the game.  That's problematic as the end goal is to keep as many of of them alive as possible.  Thankfully, Salim is a down-to earth guy and overall a pretty decent person.  Most everyone else feels designed to not be liked, and it probably isn't so bad if you let them all die.Voice acting is good, and is only thrown off by the valley of the dolls expressions of the characters.  Everyone looks so stiff and it was really off putting.  Aside from that, graphically the game looks fantastic.  Maybe it's because I'm a big fan of anything mythological and ancient civilizations blow my mind - but this game blew it out of the park on the environment.  Music is good but largely forgettable.I went in blind for this game but treated it a bit like the last 2.  Don't do that.  At least, don't treat it anything like the last 2.  Take everything you see as legit, and act accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure i'm going to get obliterated by some fans of this series since this game was my first experience with it so please take that into consideration whilst reading. This game absolutely fails everywhere where it should have been great. The gameplay presents itself in a similar way to the tearjerking, timeless, and incredible masterwork that was Detroit Become Human. It's a realtime choices matter game interspersed with some open world and quicktime events centered around a story. A game of this format has no business being set in the Iraq war. That being said, I like the way they portrayed and designed the NPCs as they look exactly like American troops and Iraqi soldiers respectively and I could tell the devs did their research on the Iraq war to portray it as realistic and inoffensive as possible.  So that is a major pro in my eyes. However, the bold step they took in putting a mythology centered horror game in the modern world just falls flat on it's face. They would have been better off setting this full in Ancient Iraq or even Ancient Egypt. An ancient mythology game set in an ancient setting is obviously formulaic but it would have worked better instead of forcing it on a modern setting. Also in Detroit Become Human, the main characters were all likable and easy to sympathize with while the villains had zero redeeming qualities, they at least had a personality and believable motivation. Here none of the characters are remotely likable and are just plain offensive. The setting and designs are great but the characters are just bad and completely forgetable. All and all, I respect the devs going for accuracy in how the world looked and felt but they failed to bring any magic regarding the characters and story to the table. It could have been a good game in a rarely explored setting but the lack of good characters and story completely not right for the setting is what kills it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: - Strong points : - Salim's character- An effective French version- Rhythm better controlled than its predecessors- Catchy atmosphere- An interesting plot- Visually successful- Weak points :- Decors less varied than before- Persistent moody tones (at the same time, underground...)- Some sound bugs- Uneven handwriting- Some annoying charactersSummary : House of Ashes does not distort the philosophy of Supermassive Games. While retaining the cinematic staging of The Dark Pictures saga, this third episode now offers a 360° camera and better integrated QTEs. Thanks to its controlled pace, its claustrophobic atmosphere and its interesting plot, it surpasses its predecessors despite its flaws (uneven writing, caricatural characters, frozen shooting phases, etc.). _childDocuments_.review: The problem with games like these is that you really can't say much in a review without spoiling it, so I'll try my best. I've only played Until Dawn and this game so far, so I'm hoping Medan and Little Hope will be a lot more enjoyable like Until Dawn. In this game, all the characters besides maybe Salim are just extremely cringy, and half of the dialogue doesn't even seem like real human interaction. I swear some of the options you can say to people would make 0 sense at all, and be the last thing on your mind to say. I honestly let some of them die because I was annoyed with their presence, which shouldn't be a factor in something like this. 90% of this game is a movie, which is good to some people, and bad to some people. Also, most of the collectibles are just along the main path now, leaving the player with no desire to look around. The endings in this are so dumb, leaving you not getting any of the achievements in 50% of playthroughs if you literally make 1 mistake at the beginning of the game. The only reason I was still playing was to get the achievements, and I didn't even get them because of a briefing choice. Until Dawn just had better characters, and a better story, with better gameplay. I don't even know how, because you'd think a scenario like the one they've painted in this game, would surmount some 20 year olds dying in the woods. The ideal player for this game would probably be a veteran, (thank you for your service) because all of these characters are so damn boring with only chatter for the army or for Rachel. Only one I liked and tried to keep the longest was Merwin. That guy to me was the only interesting character in the game, and they shafted the hell out of his character arc. I got gifted all of the Dark Picture games from a friend, but I'd say this game is maybe worth $10-$15 to be honest.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start of with saying that I absolutly loved the two previous games in this series. Man of Medan was really nice and kept you on your toes, while trying to figure out what's going on. Little hope was a really well blended mix of horror and story, although crashing alot. So expectations launching House of Ashes were high.Story wise, House of Ashes is Okay. There is a story, but it's a bit hard following along with, especially compared to the previous games. They also trew a couple of curve balls at you, making you have to change how to think a bit compared to the previous games and I love it! Unlike Little Hope there are no crashes or problems like that here.However, House of Ashes feels rushed. One character picks up a pipe and uses as his weapon. The animation however is that he just equip and unequip it by moving it over his shoulder. The weapon does not connect to anything at his back and more so just floats in the air there. The same character also has a lighter instead of a flashlight. A lighter, which shoots it light forward like a flashlight, instead of lighting up the general area around you.When you click to inspect something, it's not uncommon for your character to walk a circle around before stopping by the item again and slowly inspecting it.Finally, the camera angles in this games feels quite weird from time to time, with the camera looking one way, you moving another and the light shining in a 3rd directions.The game is okay, but it's not on level with the games before and it does feel rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than Man of Medan and Little hope. I liked 3/5 of the characters in the main cast and the story has a very hard left turn later on that I did not see coming at all, more importantly there is no "It was never spooky/super natural to start with" twist like the first two games which is a trope that I absolutely despise as it turns any horror story into an episode of Scooby-Doo real fast. The Animations are much better as well but I will say Rachel (the Ashley Tisdale character) looks really weird.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotta say, I didn't expect something of this caliber from Supermassive Games. I've played Until Dawn some years ago, and, while pretty looking and entertaining enough for an interactive movie, it was just a bit short from being a truly great game in my eyes. The characters just weren't that well written for you to truly root for them. And then Man of Medan came out and it was a step down in every direction, and I thought they've completely lost their touch. Boy, was I wrong.I gotta tell you, back in the first third of the game I wasn't really feeling the cookie cutter characters (even if they had the least amount of bullsh!t dialogue), and couldn't possibly imagine I'd be rooting this hard for them to survive. The chemistry between some of them really comes together towards the end of the game. A gameplay of simple QTE prompts became amplified by tension of real stakes - my homies making out of it alive. The plot, despite cliched beginnings, weaved and unfolded in new, truly unexpected ways, and had me way more engaged than previous escapades of teens at mountain resort and ghost ship.And visuals, man, that's gotta be one of the most good looking games out there right now. Supermassive Games perfected the faces, volumetric lighting and depth of field effect. The artistic direction is also worth commending - I couldn't keep my finger from screenshot button for five minutes, the environments and clever use of special effects is really something to behold. And for how great it all looks it also runs surprisingly well. I think I've had more framerate issues with rather drab looking ship of Man of Medan than I did with this game's spectacular looking caverns and tombs.A solid interactive movie that I'm not ashamed to recommend to any horror enthusiast. I'm looking forward for this studio's next and final Dark Pictures chapter now, and am also gonna check the Little Hope chapter soon.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is nothing really new, but it's okay. The character movement felt better than in Devil in Me because of the larger environments. _childDocuments_.review: 4/5. This is fantastic. It's an interactive movie where your choice matters. Great horror, intense, a story that you don't want to quit playing even though you need to log off for the night. The only quibbles I have is that there isn't an exit save - you have to wait til you get an autosave before you can quit; and the tutorial didn't let you try the heartbeat QTE more than once to understand how to do it. There are settings in this game to help you with the QTEs if you suck at them, like I do, and it made the game very enjoyable. There are other accessibility options available for people, too. I am definitely going to look at other games by this company. Worth playing.A word for trophy hunters: this is a hard game to get trophies, as you can't skip scenes. I would advise, after the first playthrough, to take a break before planning your next play and certain chapter replays.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game from Dark Pictures Anthology so far, at least for me. The first two games from the Anthology were not bad per se, sometimes scary/thrilling, but story/character wise not that strong. But this one is golden! I was actually invested in the story, the characters and the progress. I know a lot of people disliked the (final) twist in the first two games, and I can't blame them. Although I wasn't surprised by it at that time, this one did surprise me at each turn. Every time I thought I had pieced it together, another surprising detail made itself known. The threat in this game made the consequences of your choices/actions seem real. Again, although I definitely don't dislike the two previous games, this one is the strongest of them. Have fun playing it!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying that I genuinely don't mind whether these games are  good or bad. I absolutely love this genre, and I'll always buy and support them because I feel like there's something unique about Supermassive's games that other franchises fail to capture. With that out of the way, I think this game is pretty decent.Set in Iraq following the US invasion, it effectively portrays the impact of 9/11 on Americans. It's interesting to see the character arc development throughout the story; some characters change their views, while others don't. The story conveys commendable values and keeps you thoroughly engaged.The gameplay primarily consists of your standard QTEs and decision-making. I do wish they'd allow us to skip cutscenes, so I can 100% this game. There is also potential for a 2nd playthrough in the Curator's Cut, where you get to play the story from other perspectives and make different decisions. The performance is consistently solid, never dipping below 70 FPS. In terms of graphics, it's on par with previous Dark Pictures games.In my honest opinion, this game deserves a spot at the top of Supermassive's games. The jump scares are superior to those in previous installments and don't come across as cheap. With that and the tense QTEs, the game is sure to keep you on your toes.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous graphics with high quality models and textures. Ambient lighting and visual effects like particles, flairs and fogs give a push to the dark atmosphere.- Impressive world design with some massive blockbuster sceneries.- Nice direction and photography. Overall it's very cinematic with high quality cut scenes.- Good animations overall. Pretty convincing facial animations that reveal the emotional states of each character.- Nice sound design with convincing ambient, environmental and especially battles' sounds.- Cool music that seems to fit any given moment. Great heavy metal music during some parts.- It has some replayability value. You can try many playthroughs to watch some alternative endings and see what's gonna happen to the characters if you make different decisions.- It's a nice, smooth co-op experience. You can play it with friends either online or locally.- At last there are no annoying bugs of corrupted save files or infinite loading screens like the previous episodes of the series.The bad- It's awfully similar to its predecessors. Same pace, same gameplay mechanics, same well worn, boring QTEs, No innovations at all. I get it, it's the same series but you have to try to offer a new challenge.- There is almost no story. Its predecessors had flaws but at least they had a lot of mystery and you were wondering what's going on till the end. Here it reveals to you the monsters right from the beginning and you just run and fight in order to survive. it's a shallow action experience with weak atmosphere and no mystery at all.- Except of the last part, it is much less interactive than the previous games of the series. Cut scenes and just passively watching is way to much. Also, there is only a few of free exploration and most of the interactions happen via predefined animations during cut scenes. It's more of a big movie than an actual game and it becomes boring after a while.- Dull characters with flat personalities and shallow backstories. Dialogues and texts seem simplistic with a lot of cliché parts. It doesn't help you to love the protagonists so you end up not really caring who dies or lives.- There are some control mechanics issues. It's very slow and not responsive when picking up objects, characters tends to block the way of one another, while pathfinding and collisions aren't the best.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game like this before, so I wasn't sure exactly what to expect. It's mostly a cinematic-style adventure, in which you decide how characters respond to each other to shape the story. Interspersed with that are sections where you explore areas looking for clues and figuring out how to proceed, as well as action sections fill with Quick-Time Events and similar fast response mini-games.The strengths of this game are the way it builds the characters and their relationships over time, and the control you have in shaping both. By the end of the game, I really cared about these people. The story, which starts out as a simple war tale, also gets surprisingly big as you go, until the end had a few surprising reveals.My playtime is a little inflated, but I probably completed the entire thing in about ten hours. There were so many branching moments in the narrative that I can definitely see myself coming back to this game at some point and replaying it with different choices to see how that affects the story. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: At five hours and close to the finish mark on my first playthrough, I have to say that I'm really enjoying the game.This is definitely an 'interactive movie' more than some other games but it is well-acted, well-told, and constantly engaging.  There are moments of excitement and tension that really hit home and the pace is kept up well enough that I never grow bored.The only drawback is that, as an interactive movie, some of the characterization can be inconsistent when your decisions don't mesh up with what the writers wanted.  The worst example of this being the continued tension between two characters near the end, after they've saved one another's lives, and seemed to make a connection, over and over again.  That, and some of the 'choices' don't really mean anything as the outcome is the same either way.  Those things aside, the story is worth participating in and doing so has gone a long way to draw me into the experience. The short length (about 6-7 hours seems to be the norm on here) means that the usual price might feel a bit high, but definitely get this when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: A Gripping Thriller with Unforgettable Choices - House of Ashes House of Ashes is a masterpiece of interactive storytelling that seamlessly blends horror, suspense, and decision-making to deliver an unforgettable gaming experience. From the moment you step into the depths of the ancient Sumerian temple, you are gripped by a sense of impending dread that never lets up until the very end.The game's graphics are stunning, with detailed environments that draw you into the eerie world beneath the desert sands. The sound design is top-notch, creating a tense atmosphere that keeps you on edge as you navigate the dark corridors and underground chambers.One of the standout features of House of Ashes is its branching narrative, where your choices have real consequences on the fates of the characters. Every decision you make feels weighty and impactful, leading to multiple endings that encourage replayability.The characters are well-written and fleshed out, each with their own motivations and secrets that are slowly revealed as the story unfolds. The voice acting is superb, adding depth and emotion to the already engaging storyline.The gameplay is a perfect mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and intense action sequences that keep you engaged from start to finish. The tension is palpable during the game's heart-pounding moments, and you'll find yourself holding your breath as you make split-second decisions that can mean life or death for your characters.In conclusion, House of Ashes is a must-play for fans of horror games and interactive storytelling. With its gripping narrative, stunning visuals, and meaningful choices, it sets a new standard for the genre. Prepare yourself for a journey into darkness unlike any other – you won't be able to put this game down until you've uncovered all of its chilling secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm not a huge fan of the setting, this game has been the most enjoyable for me from the Dark Pictures Anthology so far. Controls are tight and it feels more stable in online coop than the games in the past when playing Man of Medan or Little Hope.Playing with a mate online, even keeping in contact with voice chat and deciding on what you want to do, making a slip on a QTE or having the game turn in a slightly different direction than you thought it would means it's not always super easy to 'plan' your outcome the first time through.. less so when your mate says that he's choosing one thing but actively chooses the other (I have never done this.. I swear :D).The story was engaging and we had played over four hours while thinking that we'd only played a couple. Looking forward to completing, and will update review when having done so, but at this stage it's definitely something I would recommend to friends or family that enjoy a cinematic adventure that tracks your choices and lets you do it together.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Until Dawn, this is definitely their strongest game since.The story is fine, doesn't quite hold up to UD but given this is around half as long that's probably to be expected - it's similarly as campy, but with a more serious overtone given the nature of the game (vs a bunch of teens in the mountains).On the whole, this definitely shows that Supermassive can take the Dark PIctures series and any future titles (The Quarry, hopefully) in an improved direction from Until Dawn. This game, despite being shorter, already features more 'branching' paths based on your decisions than UD did - you can end up with considerably different outcomes resulting from your previous decisions/indecisions to a level I never saw in UD, which definitely makes your choices feel much more weighty.If you blitz through, probably 5 hours, I explored a fair bit and likely ended up with some longer cinematic sequences on account of keeping everyone alive, which probably added a couple of hours on to the playtime total.Either way, I would definitely recommend it if you're a fan of UD, and if you liked the earlier Dark Pictures instalments then this is 100% the strongest of the 3 by a large margin.At full price I would only recommend it if you plan on using the Curator's mode or getting friends to play it as well, else wait til it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think that any review I write will be enough to describe just how amazing the game is. After I finished it I thought to myself; "this is everything a game should be". I'm a big fan of interactive choices genre games & this kind of immersive experience just can't be found anywhere else. Each choice ACTUALLY mattered and the relationships of the characters played a huge role as well. These games intrigue me so much because of the variant of pathing. Two endings or twenty endings are both fine, but it's seeing the way events can occur with different characters, the way conversations and decision points can unfold differently, that really intrigues me. I played many games from that same genre- but this is by far the best one.As I am also a huge history nerd, the lore of the game itself was so fascinating to me. I love that the dark pictures anthology actually do their research- keeping the player on edge with every 'secret' being found. Every note and entry were so interesting to read, and if you are a fan of such themes, you will be tempted to go back and re-read all of it even after the game is done like me.As for a multiplayer experience (movie night)- this game has the coolest features I have ever seen. The way it switches angles mid combat to the other player, the way you can actually assign characters to each player before the game begins- it was all so good. The action in the game only added to the overall experience, and me and my girlfriend had a blast playing this. We loved all the characters and actually wanted to do everything in our power to save them. There wasn't a single bad character, and as the story progressed; so did the characters. The realistic aspect of a group being stuck in such difficult situation is what got me. Each character handled the situation in their own way; and I found it very appealing to see.The graphics and character designs were incredible, there were absolutely no bugs or crashes (PC), the soundtrack was epic, the story is amazing and captivating in every aspect. I will definitely replay it and try to get all the different possibilities; something that didn't happen with the previous games in the anthology as I simply uninstalled them after I was done playing. But this game draws you in and leaving you with a taste for more. (Also, )As I mentioned at the start of the review, nothing I say will do this game justice or explain just how great it is. I will say, however, if you get all the four games in season 1 of the anthology- play them by order. That way, you will definitely appreciate House Of Ashes a lot more and understand why this game is by far the best one yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a 4/5. The story was interesting enough to keep the player interested in the roughly 5 hours of play time. The voice acting was pretty well done, but there were moments where the tone of the voice did not match the action happening on the screen (e.g. exasperated breath from climbing/running, Sadness/sobbing in times of fear/sorrow, etc.). Graphically, the character renders are beautiful with detail really showing through on the characters' clothing and facial expressions. However, the amount of detail in the characters made the quality of the foreground environments lacking; running up a playdough set of stairs often broke my immersion at times when I was meant to feel fear or tension.  The animation overall was decent, though I noticed moments where the characters moved and contorted like they had a stick up their...you know, and the movements of the mouth and eyes, while very rare, seemed buggy and unnatural. _childDocuments_.review: Overall: 85/100- Action is a fun change of pace compared to the others in the anthology. For reference, I prefer the more slow paced creepy style but this game was just as fun. I played 3/4 of the games back to back (HOA -> LH -> TDIM) and it was nice to have two slow burn creepy games and one be an action packed shooter. I found this ratio perfect, once I get through MOM maybe this opinion will change. - The relationship dynamic of this group is really interesting, there's some good heartfelt moments. I really enjoyed how the backstory was slowly built up for all the characters, this created a good emotional climax.- The decisions felt weak in this game. To me, felt like I had 5+ attempts to right a wrong. Oops messed up a quick time event, don't worry there's probably going to be a few more to save that character  they will just magically survive. Said something stupid and pissed someone off, well, they'll probably still save you. Maybe I walked some golden path and my decisions overall made this seem more outspoken than it is. There really is a lot of decisions to be made and I can't really pinpoint if it's my doing or the devs so I'm classifying this as meh rather than bad.- There's definitely some cringe voice lines and awkward delivery at a few parts. - N/AA little minor backstory, I have a pretty mentally taxing job and recently I've been a little burnt out on playing games where I actually have to do things but I still wanted to play games. I'm weird yes I know but I was in the mood for something that played like an interactive movie so I could sit back and enjoy the show but still participate. This game, and the whole anthology, is that to a tee. If you're like me and in those same shoes, I would highly recommend not only House of Ashes but the whole Dark Pictures Anthology.In my opinion, this wasn't my favorite of the anthology but it was a great addition. If you're looking for something that plays like an interactive action movie, this is probably the game for you. I felt like the action was done well and the relationships in this game contributed to a great overall story line that kept me invested. I had a few moments where I had to shake my head and grit my teeth at some questionable writing but because I was so invested in the underlying story of these characters, it didn't pull me out too far. If action isn't what you're looking for then I'd recommend checking out some of the other games in the anthology.I wasn't a huge fan of how the decision making mechanic felt in this game compared to some of the others but honestly, it really didn't phase me too much. I think somewhere between the action nature of this game and me being so invested in the characters, I was honestly happy the game coddled me in some situations. Overall I had a lot of fun playing this game. I played solo while my wife and a friend watched me play it over a discord stream and that was a fun dynamic being able to talk about the game and discuss it in real time. I would wager based on my experience that a co-op play through would also be a great way to enjoy the game. If you're just planning on playing completely solo, then you're also in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably the scariest of the Dark Pictures games thus far.   Not that these games are really "about" scares first and foremost - they're far more concerned with narrative and character than your usual horror fare - but it's a fact worth noting just the same. The often claustrophobically shallow field of view is partly responsible for this; at first, it felt like the "camera" was zoomed  too far in on the character's backs, but once I hit the caves/ancient ruins that are the setting for the majority of this game's action, I understood. It certainly helped ramp up the tension at times, making it feel like danger could be lurking around every fresh corner (something I hadn't really felt in the series prior to now).   Something this game unfortunately  a little, in comparison to earlier entries: the fruits of exploration. There's a bit less stuff to "examine" this time around, especially early on in the game; "secrets" being particularly scarce in the first few hours. This gradually picks up as the story progresses, but anyone who's a firm fan of Supermassive Games' tendency towards a very modern approach to "adventure" gaming may be slightly disappointed by this game's initial tendency toward plot momentum over meticulous exploration. Other players may, of course, warmly welcome this slight change of pace.   It's certainly the most action-packed of the Dark Pictures games to date, and should thereby delight fans of Until Dawn or Resident Evil-style games who've been feeling like this franchise hasn't been fast-paced or gun-happy enough for their liking. Clearly, the odds of this being your most or least favourite game in the series to date will depend somewhat on your own tastes. I'm personally going to proclaim this my fave so far, mostly due to the more sophisticated/profound choices you're forced to make (this one isn't just about "save as many characters as possible at all costs"), and the uniformly excellent acting throughout (even performers who were a bit so-so in earlier entries are perfectly effective here). It still falls a bit shy of the overall brilliance of Until Dawn...but at this rate, we might get there yet!   I'm still loving this series, any-which-way, and hope it remains an annual event for years to come. (The next one looks like more of a serial killer thriller, so you can't accuse Supermassive of skimping on the variety!)   Oh, and as a final bonus to those using keyboard and mouse: the default Quick-Time controls are just two buttons this time, rather than four, meaning you'll hopefully suffer fewer cheap deaths due to your shoddy reflexes! (Emphasis on "hopefully"!)   Verdict: 9.5/10.(PS If you enjoyed this review, feel free to check out my two Curator pages: Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: War is not the only horror you'll face.Story: Set during the Iraq war, you play as multiple characters. A task force is formed to attack a possible secret chemical weapons lab belonging to Saddam, but once you wide up there a massive sinkhole opens up which claims everyone into an underground ruin where enemies must become ally's to survive a new evil.The story of House of Ashes is incredibly awesome to say the least. Everything from the choices you make, character interactions and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane plot twist are just incredible. The game has a slightly slower pace than the other two, but once it picks up it just keeps getting more insane and I was just having a blast. Everything about the plot improves on the structure the first two games had. The characters are a lot more likable across the board from the start. The way you build friendships provide for some great moments of comedic relief after a tense moment or when things seem dire, actually drove me to try me to save everyone before I reached the ending and I felt devastated after I failed, something I can only say only happened in Man of Medan too.Graphics:House of Ashes graphics are just as good as the previous game in the series, however there are slight improvements. The cave is massive and some of the environments are massive in scale and look incredible. I actually really wanted to check out everything the environments had hidden and just seeing some of these places made my jaw hit the floor.Audio: The audio design is again rather on the weak side. Voice acting is again top notch, everyone across the board does amazing job with their roles, especially Ashely Tisdale as Rachel, who I was very surprised by, but everyone nails their parts super well.The music is again slightly on the weaker side, however I felt a little more positive about this one, the score is just okay. There's some great tracks when the game goes action mode, but there's still quite a lot of droning loud music that every horror game uses once in a while.Gameplay:House of Ashes has the same type of gameplay as the previous two titles in the Dark Picture series. It's a movie on rails, you walk around interact with stuff, do some QTE's and then make a choice which will impact what happens in the story. However unlike the other two games, it actually feels a lot more interactive.There's a lot more ways you impact the outcomes like items you can pick up (required or not) and they play into the story in different ways which was incredibly cool. Also there's a bit of a combat system, even though it's basically QTE"s you have to hit at the correct time, but it's still cool that it at least wasn't fully an on rails experience.Verdict:House of Ashes is the best game in The Dark Pictures series. After the huge disappointment of Little Hope I lost all hope in the series, but House of Ashes spun that ♥♥♥♥ right around and if the other entries are just as good then we're in for some good horror games. Can't wait to see how the first Season wraps up, so bring on The Devil in Me.Final Rating:8.5/10Pros:+ Story is great and incredibly off the walls+ Some truly jaw dropping environments + A lot more gameplay Cons:- Soundtrack is disappointing - Pacing of the story is pretty slow If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: You get to make decisions from two (or three) either stupid, similar, or obvious options. The obvious ones gives you the expected result. The similar ones will either improve or worsen your relationship with another character, and you have no clue which way it will go beforehand. And the stupid ones is where the characters don't do anything sensible - the complete opposite of what normal people would do.Other than that, you are supposed to react to prompts to press the mouse buttons. The game doesn't tell you that doing so is a decision in itself, and "failure" is an option. Now I've told you, and you are most welcome.So basically, you have no idea what you are doing (except when you get the obvious choices), but have to gamble. That kind of gameplay is completely pointless if you ask me. It's like watching a movie, getting asked to make some random decision, only for the movie to play out exactly like the director intended anyway. I wouldn't be able to tell the difference. The only way it has any value, is if you intend to replay it several times, trying different options. I have no plan to do so whatsoever.So think of the game as a movie, trying to keep you engaged by making "choices", while actual movies do so by being good instead. It's all about a bunch of soldiers falling down into a monster infested temple, where you are supposed to ♥♥♥♥ your pants. But you don't, because it isn't scary.

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is an absolute triumph in the Dark Pictures Anthology series, and it's not an exaggeration to say that it's the best installment yet. This game offers a gripping narrative, top-notch performances by the cast, and an unforgettable duo in Salim and Jason that's among the finest in gaming history.From the very start, House of Ashes pulls you in with its thrilling story and doesn't let go until the very end. The game's premise, set against the backdrop of the Iraqi war, is both unique and haunting. As you navigate the eerie, underground ruins of an ancient Sumerian temple, you'll be immersed in an atmosphere of constant tension, suspense, and spine-tingling horror.The standout feature of House of Ashes is undoubtedly its stellar cast. The characters are brought to life by phenomenal actors who deliver exceptional performances, making you genuinely care about their fates. The chemistry between Salim Othman and Jason Kolchek is nothing short of extraordinary. Their dynamic and evolving relationship, filled with tension, trust, and camaraderie, adds a layer of depth to the story that few games can match. The emotional journey these two characters go through is, in my opinion, one of the most compelling aspects of House of Ashes.The choices you make throughout the game significantly impact the outcome, and the consequences are as dire as they are rewarding. Each decision keeps you on your toes, second-guessing yourself, and questioning your moral compass. It's this interactive storytelling that sets the Dark Pictures series apart from other horror games, and House of Ashes perfects this formula.The visuals are stunning, the sound design is impeccable, and the game's attention to detail is remarkable. The oppressive darkness of the underground, the unsettling noises, and the lurking horrors create an immersive experience that will have you at the edge of your seat throughout.In summary, House of Ashes is a masterpiece that exemplifies what interactive horror storytelling should be. It's a gripping narrative with great actors and unforgettable characters, particularly Salim and Jason, who stand out as one of the best duos in the gaming world. If you're a fan of the Dark Pictures series or just appreciate a well-crafted horror experience, don't miss this game. House of Ashes is a shining gem in the world of interactive horror gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I wanted to reminiscence about the war crimes my country committed in this part of the world, instead what I got was a great freaking game.I adored House of Ashes because of its amalgamation of unique sub-genres and themes. An ancient temple based creature feature starring a military-based cast with a sci-fi twist is such an ambitious merging of ideas but it’s pulled off so well. Its themes of war bringing the downfall of everyone involved are pretty powerful in the context of the time period, and the characters are a reflection of that. A strained relationship becomes even more strained when a couple is torn apart by work, another’s trauma of killing an innocent woman is reminiscent of many true war horror stories, a soldier’s aimlessness pushes them into becoming a marine and having their racism nurtured into hate by conflict, and a man’s unfortunate fate of being dragged into a war he doesn’t want to fight in so he can support his son to have a life better than his.The game completely engrossed and drew me in from the first few minutes. This game has an amazing storyline, real feelings and mostly likable characters who you actually start to care about and desperately want to keep alive, just a super immersive gaming experience like no other. I’ve replayed it twice already getting different outcomes and always trying to keep everyone alive to the end.Other than the themes, the nature of the game having a real enemy is something that was new in this series when this came out, as we’d yet to see a real creature or otherworldly presence. The characters are probably the most solid in any Supermassive Game.  Each one is interesting and complex.  Not as scary as some of the other games, but very character driven and it works. Yes some of the characters are mean or irritating, and yes some scenes are pretty repetitive, but it’s a game that has a strong message that ties together its genre combinations brilliantly, on top of just being a fun journey.I’d say it’s the most worthy game that supermassive has made. For the relative cheap price of about $30 you get an exciting game with a good story, mostly good characters and acting, some cool kills if you’re into that, good graphics and an all around fun experience. It has flaws for sure, but not more than any other game. Fair warning that it’s not really horror, more like an action-thriller. Honest to god if you haven’t experienced this masterpiece I envy you because I wish I could go in blind again. Just please put aside a full night for this game.Did I also mention that there’s also a naked Eric mod available? I’m sure if you’re even remotely interested you’d never regret buying it. What the hell are you waiting for?10/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Detroid:become human or The Last of Us which are basicallly intereractive movies then this game may be for you.You play through the eyes of several protagonist altering the fate of both the love life and even if they live at all.Make too many wrong decisions or fail at the quick time clicks on the wrong parts and you may lose one or several of your team members.Sometimes clicking on what seems to be obvious (like what the game is hinting at) is the wrong choice. so follow your heart.The game plays like an interactive movie. graphics are really good. but they can go from uncanny realistic to a bit odd.The story is entretaining if a bit short. it took me 20 hours to get through the whole game. lost one member due to making a bit reckless decision and failing the quick time event. the game does not allow you to go back so you have to live with your errors which i fully support.if you do a second play through or third it may really shine in the replayability area.You can collect secrets but they don't seem to do much other than unlock some interviews and behind the scenes stuff.overall well worth the 30 bucks even better if you get it on discount. I mean. you pay 15 dollars for a movie ticket that last 2 hours so think about the value here. The librarian NPC that tells the story is great and serves great to set the atmosphere.Overall well worth the ticket if you like interactive movie-games.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to start with this game. The cinematography and visuals are beautiful and it has been edited very nicely. However, the voice acting, random glitches, green screen explosions, writing, and the awkward movements just aren't doing it for me. Watched an entire fight scene of a guy pretending to hold a gun. Funny part is he was shooting as well. There was no sound and he even had his finger on the imaginary trigger. Perhaps House of Ashes is introducing characters with mental illnesses. I find the relationship between Eric and Rachel almost insufferable and out of place. There's no backstory and they expect us pick a side in their relationship. Overall there is too much going on for me to care about some random characters love life. Thank God I killed Eric. Anyways, as far as other characters go they all seem to be missing half of their brains. They act more like they're in a fifth grade play rather than the military. A ton of character models have been reused, which is fine, but its really off putting when you've been shot to death by John in Little Hope. Dear God i swear if I see Angela I will delete the game. Please don't do that to me. This game just seems to be missing a lot and the writing is sloppy. I've loved the past games, but I've found this one insufferably hard to get into. On the bright side of all of this I have appreciated the graphics. I find the visuals very pleasing and they fit the setting very well. Along with this I appreciate the fact that I can used WASD and my mouse to move and look around. Outside of this, you won't be getting much more out of me. Waited months for this game and I've been met with nothing but a joke. Still going to play through the rest of the game with my best friend Todd. Perhaps I'll amend the review later. Anyways, if you're reading this just play Little Hope or Man of Medan.

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is a profound disappointment. The third installment to The Dark Pictures Anthology is so badly written and paced that the game feels like a chore that both insults and mocks multiple nations as well as the person playing the game. This game is the result of lazy development that did zero research before endeavoring the subject for their environment and attempt of immersion. The story is horrifically bad, and mocks the entire behavior or Iraqis and Americans. The story is only made worse by the abysmal dialogue, which seems to have been written by people who have never had a healthy conversation or person to person interaction in their life. The side plots that go along with this show further this problem. For example, the developers seem to think including a love triangle, that is more unbelievable than the story, is the way to keep things interesting. People being shot, blown up, sliced in badly graphical displays of gore and more around them dead as they are fighting to stay alive, but they have time to play this drama out. Two men are pawning for a chance of a sexual relationship with a woman in the middle of a war zone, during a life and death situation. This woman who is an expert in many field, needs no man, cheats on her husband, is the most athletic and capable of the bunch, speaks multiple languages, can throw heavy rocks further than Brett Farve and more. The graphics are a step down from the previous two. There is a clear display of filler and repeated textures, which is something that was not a problem with the previous games. I even complimented that they avoided that in the prior. In House of Ashes, the repetition is painfully obvious. Even the blood patterns on the uniform, which is applied to all of the character model, so it looks like the gear is bleeding, not the person. Very lazy and poorly done.The controls remain awkward as prior, but become more of a task in this game than the prior two iterations of the so far trilogy. There is a blur effect that seems to be with some desire to make things a focus or layered view. It causes issues, being that now many of the walls have break points, where at angles they do not show correctly. These are common graphical issues with independent games, but the first time it has been an issue with this series. The graphics overall are the same besides that.In all, this game is a hard pass for me. The developers did no research and took a very lazy approach to this game. It is by far a disappointment and a complete failure on the part of the developers. I do recommend the first two of The Dark Pictures Anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer:  Do you need to play Man of Medan or Little Hope to understand what is going on?  No.  Each of these stories are individually contained.  You can ignore the first two and play this one just fine. The story is about 5 military personnel on differing factions who fall into an underground temple.  Something lurks in the depths, stalking the group.  The group must try to put their personal beliefs and struggles aside and find a way out of their predicament and survive the horror beneath the desert.This review is based off of one play through, solo.  I don't personally enjoy the military theme at the beginning of this game.  I've just never been into that type of story line, especially in horror movies or stories.  It is too easy for military group to come in guns blazing and blast up what ever is in their way and for me, that is why it lost the horror element at the start.While the developer and story writers stated that they wanted the war element to not over shadow the developing plot line, it still stuck in the back of my mind.  I felt I was just playing Call of Duty: Side quest during act 1 and through the majority of act 2.  These characters were still just army people running around with guns and explosives.  There were a few similar scenes where they would some how drop the gun they were holding and have it slide just out of reach.  They would plain open fire on what ever they were mad at or fearful of.  I wish they would have taken the amount of guns / ammo / bombs out of the equation and focused on a minimalist survival story.  Might have been better as an archaeologist team, with differing views of the temple site. That would have probably increased the horror element for me.  Giving characters too many weapons and ammo at their disposal decreases any sense of survival horror and brings it into the realm of action horror.Similar movies it may remind you off:  Aliens, The Descent, Predator.I disliked most of the characters aside from Salim and Nick, the others were quite obnoxious.  It was ham-fisted military acting at best.  They might as well all yelled "You maggots" every second line.  Didn't really care much for the love interest story line, or the "I don't trust you cuz yur different than me and we're not on the same side" problems they faced or the "i'm a higher rank than you, so you need to do what I say" lines, or the "stay away from my man" "I'm not interested in him ThAnKz!" girl rivalry trope.  Salim and Nick seemed to be the only two reasonable characters in this story, at least for my play through.Without going into too much spoiler, the plot began to flesh out end of act 2 beginning of act 3 and turned into a decent ending.  Little Hope had me hooked in Act 1.   I believe I was startled twice or three times during house of ashes so beware, they still have them.  Not as much as Man of Medan though.  The horror is still present without them.The setting / atmosphere was good along with lighting effects. The soundscape has been top notch.  I do give credit to The Dark Pictures, they have nailed the sounds quite well in each story.They reuse the same character models through the stories.  Similar to how American Horror Story uses the same actors to play different roles each season.  Ashley Tisdales' model looked funny and she was just covered in blood the whole time. The game offers different difficulties, depending on how challenging you wish your QTE's to be.  You can also turn prompt prior to QTE's off or on depending if you need a warning before the game requires you to input something.  I did choose to use prompts as I tend to lose focus on these games in favour of watching the story line play out.  The aiming QTE's are slightly different, where there is no target circle to aim for.  You aim for what ever is coming at you and your cross hair turns red to know when to pull trigger.  You will face rhythm QTE's in stay calm events.  Aim and target QTE's.  Button mash QTE's and quick reaction QTE's.I fumbled a lot of  QTE's and still managed to save 3 out of the 5 characters.They added a flashlight system which you can toggle on and off.  It was interesting.  I did find that this game was quite dark given the suggested configuration when you first start the game.I had played this game in 3 sittings.  There are 3 acts and roughly full play through took me about 6.8 hours.  This play through was longer than what I put in for Man of Medan at about 4.5 to 5.5 hours and Little Hope which was about 4.5 - 5.5 hours.  So far, how do I rank each story.1.  Little Hope - The characters were great, I cared about each one. It had me hooked at the beginning with the story line and the creatures were disgusting.  The ending while still sad / personal horror and psychological damage, paranoia and trust, almost mirror'd Man of Medan's "twist".  It left the community divided on if this ending was actually good or not. 2.  House of Ashes - The characters were annoying, the story didn't start to get good until mid to end of the 2nd Act and I am just not a fan of characters in horror stories having access to an arsenal of weapons at their disposal.  With that said, it branched out to be something bigger towards the end and did end up with some interesting ideas.3. Man of Medan - While the story was cool, it got spoiled way too early. _childDocuments_.review: Another Supermassive game quality game!No spoilers here.Graphics: The graphics of their games are always top notch and one solid game to play visually.Audio: Atmosphere, sounds, music is all spot on with this game, like all Supermassive games.Controls: Easy keymap, harder to do quick times and get right.Gameplay and everything else after: So if you've played a Supermassive game or any of The Dark Pictures games, you know what to expect.There are twists, turns, jump scares, atmosphere setting, brain thinking, killing off people, choices to make that effect the game. It's all here and it's done amazingly with a great story along the way.It's like an interactive movie that you are along for the ride, that's the best way to explain these games. Your actions can kill off someone and affect the way it will end, the way the story is told, the different dialogue options and overal effect the general telling of what happens.You play a multiple amount of characters in the game, a lot goes on and it's up to you to solve and find out. You can "accidentally" kill of some people or make the wrong choice and someone dies off, can you keep them alive? Do you want to keep them alive? It's up to you what you want to do, but each choice decides actions with happy or bad choices, that's good fun!It has multiple play through's for different options to keep alive, kill etcWould I recommend? Yes, without a doubt an amazing experience like all their other games in the same series.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this interactive movie. Not sure about the quality of the previous titles of The Dark Pictures Anthology, since I didn´t have the pleasure, but I can wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking for a good story, good thriller(not really horror), or just a good action movie. I mentioned this is an interactive movie. But until now, I have never seen it so well executed - throughout the movie, you have hundreds(not exaggerating) of choices, that shape the course of the story. What characters will survive, what friendships and betrayals will happen, which ways the characters go...All of this and more is decided by you. By dialog choices, by succeeded(or failed) prompts, or just by foolish choices you make.Your freedom of choice is close to absolute. I was really surprised, when my two favorite characters died after several failed prompts, that the game continued with this outcome. There is no "Game Over" screen, the game counts with all eventualities and carries on. So to sum it up:+ your choices actually matter+ great acting, memorable characters+ interesting story+ good sound and graphical design of "bad guys"(no spoilers)+/- Game length. I finished it in 6 hours, but that was just one of myriads possible outcomes. Every playthrough is different, so the replayability is virtually infinite.Well, that´s that. Thank you for reading and give it try - this gem deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: This third entry into the Dark Pictures Anthology is without a doubt, the best entry in the anthology thus far. To the point that if you're new to the Dark Pictures Anthology series, this is the one I would recommend first; having played the other two chapters myself, I have to say, Man of Medan was 'okay' while Little Hope is a game I seem to dislike in further increments every time I think about the plot. I very much enjoyed a lot more fully in this one, and there were very few 'Oh, come ON' moments in this one, as compared to the previous two games, with Man of Medan being the most guilty on that front. One of the pluses of this being an anthology series, is that you can start on any of the three available games without needing to play the others, and if you want to spend money on the series, start on this one. It's a bit difficult to go into WHY this game is better than the other two in my opinion, without going into heavy spoilers for the other two, and it also depends on your taste in horror, and the different genres in horror. The other two entries in the series lean more into the psychological horror, and mystery, with Man of Medan being more realistic, and Little Hope (poorly attempting) to be more 'deep' about it (Little Hope's plot is like a back alley off brand attempt to do Silent Hill, and it fails hard).  This game, however, plays more into the action-horror genre, and I frequently found myself thinking of it as sort like a hybrid mix of Pitch Black, the Descent, and a light pinch of The Thing, and Ghosts of Mars. Whereas in the previous games in the series, you are playing as civilians, in this story, every character is a member of the military, quite tough, and very much armed. While you feel 'safer' in a sense because of this, the threat you face is more than enough to avoid making you feel overpowered. You will feel a lot more tense in this entry, at least in my opinion, compared to the previous two games. I found the characters in this one to be a step up from the others as well, with one in particular standing out as having a really nice character arc, where he starts the story as a standoffish, borderline douchebag, and can become one of the most heroic characters, who will do things for others that you wouldn't have imagined him doing at the start of the story, and you genuinely feel as if he's grown as a person. Plot-wise, I very much liked this one better than the other two; it's very much more straightforward with both, it's threat, and the situation they're stuck in, while still making it creepy and the tension fairly high. The story starts out far in the past, showing glimpses of an event that occurs, and then jumps far ahead to 2003, where that same threat is now encountered, buried far beneath the sands of Iraq, by a group of more modern soldiers. They are confused, disoriented, and have to try to escape said threat, while also dealing with an enemy general who doesn't seem to grasp the threat in the buried caves of the old civilization, and attempts to kill them several times. You also play as a reluctant soldier in the enemy army, who holds no ill will towards the other characters, and only wants to get out of the situation. There IS an underlying mystery, of what exactly the threat is, and a sub plot of an older archaeology team who found the ruins in the WW2 era, that's also decently handled, a fitting backdrop to paint the situation further, without feeling like it takes too much out of the tension. I will say, there ARE still a few of the almost trademarked 'Why can't I just do this' or 'Really?' sort of moments, where your characters, have the means to stop a threat in that moment, and just decide to NOT use it, for the sake of plot; without trying to give too much away, there is a part where two of your characters, both armed, are fleeing from a threat, and hide. It's the perfect opportunity to ambush this threat, as there are two of you, and only one of them, but it forces you to hide, and if you fail the 'heartbeat QTE' you will highly likely get one of the two characters you play as killed. It was one of the very few parts that actually had me irritated, but the game HAD warned me that there was a threat here, and I merely misinterpreted that warning. The QTEs are for the most part, fair, though I hate the 'heartbeat QTE' which is the one that you must play whenever your characters need to be quiet and stealthy. I feel like the game doesn't exactly explain the way it works very well, in ALL three of these games, and seeing as if you fail THESE particular QTEs, more often than not it will result in death or injury, I feel like they should be more clear on it. You have to time your button presses to a series of prompts that slide along a bar, and I assumed you had to hit the button RIGHT as the prompt touches your cursor, like a rhythm game, but that is incorrect, and got me hurt or killed or put into a worse situation each time. It wasn't until my partner I was playing with informed me you had to hit the button when your cursor is right in the MIDDLE of the prompt, that I started to be able to pass those QTEs. If not for that, I would have failed EVERY heartbeat QTE that I encountered, and lost more characters, which, I feel would have made the death unfair, as I misunderstood how that mechanic worked. Perhaps a safe 'practice' mode for the QTEs outside the story would help?Another thing regarding the QTEs; in this developer's early game, Until Dawn, the mechanic where you can decide to shoot/strike/throw an object or harm another person, it lets you know right away that sometimes NOT going through with the action, is a better choice. I don't know if I missed it here because I was already used to that mechanic and skimmed by the instructions, but I don't recall the game telling the player that they don't HAVE to shoot/stab/throw something when the prompt comes up in this one, so I could see someone accidentally killing or harming a character because they felt the game was forcing them to, when that isn't the case. Also, I feel as if they should change the icon they use for the 'button mash' QTE, where you must mash one button as fast as you can to fill up a meter to succeed a strength check. It looks a little similar to the regular one-tap button prompts, so sometimes it'll come up and you tap the button, and waste a second or two before you realize it's a mash prompt instead, and then have to scramble to start mashing. Even a game like RE4 handled it's mash prompts obviously, compared to it's one-taps, so I feel they could easily handle that in this game. Beyond the minor elements of plot railroad with the 'why didn't we just shoot that guy when we could' mentioned above, and honestly, that was one of the only points that happened, there are a lot less of the flaws of the previous two games here, and it feels a lot more polished and smooth compared to them. I played through (one time thus far) playing co-op online with a friend of mine all in one sitting, and I will say, I feel as though that's the premiere way to play the game, not to say the single player isn't good, it is, but going through with a buddy, who you can speak to and hear what's happening on their end (or not telling, if you want lol) can be a boon. I will also say that out of all the ending sequences in Supermassive Games series, this one has the best one, similar-ish to Until Dawn, which goes through all the surviving characters being interviewed by the police, this one runs through what happens after whoever is left (which could be NONE of them depending on how you play) manages to escape, and it's really cool. All in all, this is the best game in the Anthology so far, and I can only hope that they keep this up for the next chapter, which is previewed in the ending to this game, as looking like a serial killer story, sort of like SAW? I'll be replaying this one to see the variations of endings, and really enjoyed it!

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes succeeds at many things. With fantastic visuals, interesting characters and a claustrophobic atmosphere, it makes for a very fun game. Overall, I really enjoyed this and can't wait to replay it with the knowledge of how to save my characters. I think it is easily the best in the series, and I can't wait to see what the next game has in store. After a rough beginning to The Dark Pictures Anthology, I am confident that the developers are on the right track.

Animations are clunky and not consistent.The story is okay, nothing that made me go wow but I cared enough to finish the game and care for the characters. The sound design is good.With this out of the way, everything else is just disappointing.You could tell some choices didn't really matter and just led to a slight different course of action but with the same results.Usually in this game I always ♥♥♥♥ around with choices but this time I decided to save everyone and I did, effortlessly and not because I'm a god gamer but because the choices are so straight forward it hurts, you make all the good guy choices and that's it, there's no sudden, there's no character being suspicious of your innate kindness, zero.The game is supposed to be a horror yet it fails miserably to build up any type of suspense or tension and the fact that all the characters are armed it takes away any sense of being defenseless, just ends up feel like an action even tho you won't partake in any of it as a player.Quick time events have next to no impact on how things turn out most of the times because there's always some kind of failsafe that will lead the scene where its supposed to even if the player fails them, it's kinda lame.The tiny bits where you're actually moving around and have control over your character it turns into fetch quests or go from point A to point B and open a door, it just fills like filler instead of being a new opportunity to lead the story in different directions based on your actions.The controls are stiff and unresponsive, I don't know how many times I had to "re position" my character in order for the interaction with the object to work properly.In conclusion I don't think it's worth anyone's money, just buy it on sale for like 10 bucks and don't expect much.If you do play it do it with a friend at least.Honestly you're better off watching it on Youtube, lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: I love QTE games. I'm lazy and have a giant TV at the end of my bed, that's bigger than the bed itself. Problem is I can't aim very well with my mouse on the bed, nor can I aim particularly well on a controller. So games like this which have minimal aiming (and assist options for it too) are great fun for me. Plus with a giant a$$ 4K gaming TV, it helps me immerse better in a game that's designed to be super immersive.For the above reason, I own every game these guys make, twice in fact for a few of them (on PS4 too). and I have a blast every time. I still can't quite get my head around whatever the hell happened last year in Little Hope, so I'll have to go back to that one for a replay soon.But House of Ashes, I feel was truly the best in the series. It starts a little slow, a bit weak sauce, but once you get deeper into the chapters it starts to really get exciting. And the deeper you go, the crazier it gets. So whilst I definitely recommended buying the full Dark Pictures series, I'd say even if its your first one, this is the right one to pick. There are some Little Hope references in it so that might make you pick that one up too, just to see how it all connects.With this game series, one of the rewards for beating the game is it shows you the NEXT upcoming game. So next October, fans will get another game added to the series, and thats already looking pretty sick too. As I said earlier, I played this on the highest settings on my 4K TV, there was absolutely no lag or input issues, the game was smooth as a whistle with no issues stopping and starting. it played as you would expect it to on a console with perfect fluidity. My GPU is the 980ti, so it's getting on a bit in age now, but still performed perfect on this game.So if you want an immersive experience where you can distract yourself from the real world and engage in the plight of others - I say pay full price and go for it. I'll pre-order the next line up in the series as soon as it's available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: Just played Man of Medan, and this is much, much better, they have come a long way forward.  It is about (at least) 3x the length, there is no bs "you must finish the game first" so chapters can be immediately replayed if someone is drunk or tired and they screw up a QTE.  Story is much better, though this is subjective, the setting and characters were more interesting people.  It is a great game, well worth playing, and a good relaxing game because of the story-driven nature.  Only one problem is the quick transition between just relaxing through the story and some action happening that needs fast QTE.  Some warning would be good so can put hands on controller/mouse and concentrate first.  I think something like this was in a patch(?) though probably after I played.If anyone has trouble beating the heartbeat thing, if you can increase to 120fps, it is SIGNIFICANTLY easier than on the 60fps, I flubbed up my nvidia settings and played this locked to 60fps and only discovered my mistake when playing Man of Medan.  Just some advice if this kind of thing is annoying or inordinately difficult.  Graphics are mostly fantastic, animations are good, no complaints any way around it is a nice game that meets 2021 visual standards.Like all of these games, they are a 1-2 time playthrough experience.  There is a "curator's mode" where one can play as a different character in the scenes giving some replayability, which I have not tried yet, as it hadn't unlocked when I played, but at max game is 2 playthroughs.  Dont take it on a desert island if it is the only game you bring.So I do recommend it, nice game, no political correct woke bs being rammed down my throat which I really appreciate( a HUGE turn-off for me and I would not have played/finished the game if it was there).  Game deserves to be played if nothing else on the radar, it is just south of a "must play" but not by far.  Polish is very good also, bugs very minimal, annoying things very minimal.  Definitely put on wishlist and pick it up for a rainy day when on discount if not going to play today would be my advice.

_childDocuments_.review: A true spiritual successor to one of my favorite games of my childhood, Battle for Bikini Bottom, to say I was excited for this game is an understatement. After sinking 8 and a half hours and finishing the game, this game has exceeded every single one of my expectations. I'll start with the art. The character animation is expressive and fits the characters well (I did notice though that almost all of Spongebob's idle animations were reused from Battle for Bikini Bottom: Rehydrated, not saying this is a bad thing though), and each world is packed with detail and vibrancy, some more than others but still beautiful nonetheless. All of the character costumes are true to the show and serve as nostalgic fanservice for fans (Costumes have no gameplay effect other than cosmetic appearance).  Now onto Gameplay. One of the biggest changes I noticed from Battle for Bikini Bottom is a more open type of level design, which was a very welcome change personally considering the very linear nature of BFBB's level design. Combat feels responsive, with the new array of attacks at Spongebob's disposal being very fun to use. However i did notice a rather annoying inconsistency with hitboxes. Some attacks will not hit occasionally despite being right next to an enemy and some attacks will hit me despite being well outside of the hitbox. Platforming elements have a varied level of difficulty attached to them, with some areas being harder than others in every level. One of my favorite new platforming mechanics is when you have to jump on a boulder and roll down a hill while avoiding obstacles. Mechanics such as sliding also made a return in the game, however I did notice a weird issue when hitting tikis while sliding. There are certain times where I would jump to hit a tiki but the game would not break it, but instead bounce off of them, more often than not knocking me off the track and forcing me to restart from a checkpoint. Now onto writing and voice acting. The game follows Spongebob and Patrick (who gets turned into a balloon) as they try to bring their friends back to Bikini Bottom after meeting a fortune teller mermaid called Madame Kassandra, getting a magical bubble soap from her called Mermaid's Tears, which tears up the fabric of the universe, opening up Wishworlds that are takes on locations from the series with a theme behind them. The voice acting saw the return of the main cast from the show, including a well-awaited return of Clancy Brown as Mr. Krabs after being absent from Battle for Bikini Bottom. Other returning members include Tom Kenny as Spongebob and Gary, Bill Fagerbakke as Patrick, Rodger Bumpass as Squidward, Carolyn Lawrence as Sandy, Mr. Lawrence as Plankton, and many others. My biggest complaint with the voice acting is the delivery, it feels... weak, especially from Tom Kenny at certain times as Spongebob. Onto PC Performance. The game is powered by Unreal Engine 4 and was played on my Desktop Gaming PC, powered by a Ryzen 9 5900x, RTX 2080, and 32 GB of RAM, and installed on a SSD. Playing at 1440p wielded pretty satisfying results, with no changes to default settings (which is an issue, as the video options is pretty barebones, only offering window type and resolution options, and requires going into the game files to make setting adjustments). On default settings my game ran at a wide framerate range, anywhere from 90 FPS to 165 FPS (my monitor refresh). There was some stuttering here and there caused by what i can assume to be shader compilation, however it was much less frequent than other Unreal Engine games i've played on PC, and did not impact my experience much.   Overall the game is a fantastic sequel and successor to one of the best licensed 3D platformers available in the last 25 years, with faithful art direction, good voice acting, and fantastic level design. I highly recommend picking this game up, especially if you really liked Battle for Bikini Bottom. 9/10(My review will be updated after i finish the game with any additional thoughts or changes)

_childDocuments_.review: A very acceptable, honest successor to Battle for Bikini Bottom. Here are a list of my initial pros and cons. Will edit as I continue playing. Basically, this game is great and IGN is horrible.- Most aesthetic and gameplay elements return from BFBB, but many new ones are added to make the game feel more like an inspired love letter to BFBB rather than a soulless ripoff.- With that said, it plays almost exactly like BFBB. Relive your childhood.- Lots of unique objectives and minigames that revitalize the gameplay experience.- The graphics are very vibrant and cute.- The areas/zones/levels are very well designed and detailed and are incredibly creative.- The cutscenes are beautifully animated- The music is as great as BFBB's was.- The story is good for what it is.- The sound mixing is pretty bad at times. Voice lines with inconsistent volume, music clipping in and out harshly, etc.- The voice acting is below average in my opinion. The delivery of a lot of lines seem weak to me, and a lot of characters are either a little off or straight up sound like a bad impression of themselves.- The cutscenes can be very wonky/glitchy a lot of the time, even though they're usually animated very well.- Little nuanced, jarring details, like NPC's spawning right infront of your face, some voice lines glitching and playing twice, cutscenes being very awkwardly paced, and tikis floating in the air (not the ones that are supposed to).- The humor is definitely centered around the modern era of Spongebob, with lots of throwback references thrown in, which can be seen as a pro or a con depending on how you feel about modern Spongebob.I think I can honestly say that this game exceeded most people's expectations, and If you grew up playing Battle for Bikini Bottom, then you will most definitely enjoy playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a super fun, enjoyable experience for me. Personally, I liked it a little more than Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated. It seems like they took Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated and expanded upon it further. Although, instead of playing as different characters, you play as only Spongebob who gradually learns every single mechanic, new or old, as you progress further into the game. Several new enemy types get introduced throughout the story. You unlock more silly costumes over time. It sounds like they got most of the original voice actors to reprise their roles. There's a lot more charm and personality added into the animations too. But best of all, if you're like me who is a big fan of Spongebob and grew up watching the original seasons, you will definitely appreciate all the different memes and references they make throughout the game because they don't hold back on those. Overall, it's a very chill, basic 3D platformer. It isn't a difficult game by any means, so you can just casually play about, have some fun exploring the worlds, enjoying the dialogue, and everything! Very good game! A great addition into the franchise, and an improvement over Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated. Hope the dev team remaster more of the original Spongebob games later in the future.
