_childDocuments_.review: When SpongeBob and Patrick get their hands on wish-granting Mermaid Tears, the fabric of the entire universe starts to unravel. Now, our favorite sponge has to work with a balloon Patrick and travel across different worlds to put everything back in its place. Donning over 30 iconic costumes, The Cosmic Shake will send you on a 3D platforming adventure across 7 different lands. Traverse and defend yourself using classic skills, with many new ones you can unlock as you progress. Will SpongeBob be able to save the day?Even though I am older now, SpongeBob has always delighted me, and it's wonderful that this game captures that same delight. The art style is incredible, vibrant and simple, and the gameplay was very enjoyable. I had a blast going from world to world, seeking out the Bikini Bottom residents we have come to know and love, all voiced by their original cast! If you're a fan of SpongeBob, or looking for a great game to play after Battle for Bikini Bottom, this is going to be it. With that said, let me tell you a bit about how this will run on the Steam Deck.While The Cosmic Shake starts off on a great foot and decently well out of the box with 60 FPS, it does start to dip in certain areas. This is much less stable later on, with drops to the 40s, and battery drain rising to 24W+. Luckily, there are a couple things we can do to make this game significantly more enjoyable on the Steam Deck!The first thing I did when trying to optimize this one was see if upscaling would look alright. To my surprise, I actually noticed almost no change from native resolution! I even believed that it initially didn't work because it looked so close to native, yet it helped significantly with stability in most areas.From there, it was a matter of finding the right balance of framerate cap and TDP limit. For The Cosmic Shake, it seemed to dip to around 41-42 at the worst of times, so a 40 FPS cap worked out the best. This, along with the upscaling resolution, allowed a TDP limit of 9 that held up in all playable areas and still felt fantastic. I also put on a GPU Clock Speed Frequency of 1200 as this chilled out the framerate instability that occurred from time to time.I wanted to also find a 45 FPS build that I could be happy with, since 45 FPS felt fantastic. While there are still some areas that will dip to 41-42, even with TDP caps on at all, it held up beautifully with a TDP limit of 10. The times performance dipped the most were actually the cutscenes. These scenes tended to sometimes drop below 40 FPS and could be really hard on the system, but it ended up going right back up to normal as soon as the cutscene ended. They are more than likely real-time cutscenes that use extra filters to make it look much better and those could be taking a toll on the system. It's nowhere near a deal-breaker though!I also had no issue with any controls and didn't encounter any visual bugs, but I did find that the costume menu dropped performance by a significant amount. Going and selecting costumes went down to 27 FPS with a maxed out battery drain. I didn't mind it since I was just selecting my costume and it went right back to normal getting out of it, but it was still noteworthy.SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is just a joy to play. It has all the charm and beauty that SpongeBob is known for, but integrates some wonderful gameplay elements into it. Pair it up with the unique worlds it showcases and you've got yourself a good time! On top of that, this is fully enjoyable on the Steam Deck and those little tweaks really make a difference to stability and saving battery. The battery drain is a little high for my tastes, but overall, this will have no problem on your Deck!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as good as the best Spongebob games (BFBB, Movie Game, Creature from the Krusty Krab, etc) but still, a step above the generic ones that came out in the 2010's. There definitely was a very genuine attempt to create something fun for Spongebob fans and not just a corporate cash grab, and I appreciate that. For positives, it is a very nice looking game for the most part, and a step above BFBB Rehydrated. The humor is great and captures the vibe of classic Spongebob better than the TV show does currently. The hub world is fun and cool to see an expanded version of what we've seen before. I love that the game attempts to take some of the game design language of the previous Spongebob games and create something new with it. At the same time however, this is a bit of a double edge sword as it leads me to my biggest issues with the game. I think this attempt was largely unsuccessful and it's very frustrating.My biggest problems with the game are the level design and the combat, which makes up a bulk of the experience so it's hard to ignore. To start with the combat, the expanded arsenal of moves is a very welcome addition, but falters for me because of how deliberately limiting it is implemented. I don't like that a lot of the moves can only be used in certain times and only on certain enemies. Specifically the kick move would be way more fun to use if you could do it all the time and level design would encourage that. This is something that was very prominent in BFBB that I think this game missed out on. The platforming and combat abilities were one in the same, and the level design reflected this and was designed around it. Same goes for the bubble move which feels like a downgrade from the Bubble Bowl from BFBB. The closed in combat areas make this issue the most apparent with how operatic and empty they feel. In a better game, I don't think we'd need them at all.More on the level design now. One thing that made BFBB great is how the level design made the world feel much bigger and expansive than it actually was. Sure there is an obvious direction and flow to the levels, but you could make a mental map in your head of the environment and every nook and cranny was memorable. This maze like design is largely absent with the level design in this game is being mostly straight forward. The few times the levels opened up a bit was welcome. I just wish they went further in that direction. Best examples being the later levels such as Halloween Rock Bottom, Pirate Goo Lagoon and Medieval Sulfur Fields. The latter is probably the best level in the game in my opinion.A few other issues with game include it's shorter length, less engaging collectible system, and mediocre boss fights. These don't bother me as much but feel worth mentioning none the less as obvious downgrades. Now I've been very critical in this review, but I do still recommend the game. All these issues aside, there's a lot of glimpses of brilliance and capturing the magic of what made BFBB so great (at least to people like me who grew up with it). I did still enjoy it, and think if Purple Lamp where to make a sequel that addressed the issues with this game, it could be something really special. I don't know how well this game is selling, so it may be unlikely. If I had to give this game a score it would be a 6/10. Thank you for reading this way too long review. This may resonate with a very niche group of weird cartoon-game nerds like myself, who are getting to old to care about this sort of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, this review will inevitably feature several comparisons to Battle For Bikini Bottom (BFBB) and The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie game (TSSM) as the overall gameplay is pretty similar to those titles and I am pretty familiar with them. With that said, let's get into what I liked about the game.-The presentation is beautifulFrom the animations, to the lighting, to the various character and environmental models, this game looks fantastic. The more cinematic cutscenes are a treat to see and remind me very much of watching an episode of the show. In-game graphics are no slouch either and there were several times where I spent time looking around just to observe my surroundings-Gameplay overall is solidThe way that SpongeBob controls feels pretty good and he has a variety of moves that can be used for combat and platforming. To provide an example, SpongeBob gets access to a karate kick move early on in the game that homes in on enemies and certain obstacles and bounces you up into the air after you hit them to give you a second to decide what to do next and keep your momentum going. Occasionally, you will have sections in the levels where you're doing other stuff such as riding on a seahorse through a large stretch of land or (returning from BFBB) sliding down a slide that help keep the gameplay loop fresh.-Level design is goodIf I had to compare the levels to something, I would say that they're most similar to the levels in TSSM. What I mean by this is that levels are linear for the most part with some small side areas to explore or challenges to complete to obtain collectibles. Also similar to BFBB and TSSM, when you first go through each level, you won't have the necessary abilities or meet certain requirements to obtain everything. To add onto this, after completing the level for the first time, you will usually encounter a character in the HUB world with a quest that has you returning to past levels to collect stuff for them to obtain collectibles needed for 100% completion.As for the levels themselves, I found all of them to be pretty good. They're interesting to travel through and you're introduced to at least one new ability or mechanic that you'll use through out each level. The game is very good at telling you where you should go to complete the main objective and levels are designed in a way that it's difficult to get lost. You won't be seeing any BFBB Kelp Forest here.-Classic Spongebob songs and voice actors are usedNothing much to really say here, the voice actors that have been with the show since the beginning are here and sound exactly like you expect. If you like the music that's heard in the show, then I'm happy to say that they've likely used a familiar track in at least one part of the game somewhere. The game also features several original tracks (I think?) that fit with each level that they are in.-Only one playable characterThe only character you play as through the entire game is SpongeBob. It's a shame that previously playable characters like Patrick and Sandy aren't playable, but it makes sense when you consider that Spongebob has an expanded moveset that features moves very similar to the ones they had in BFBB, which would make them redundant.-Story is not all that interesting but serviceableThe story is mostly just here to give SpongeBob an excuse to go to each level. You can tell right away who the main antagonist is going to be within the first several minutes of the game and there's no kind of twist or anything to make it interesting. The story of each level can basically be summed up as: Find character or important building you want to save, figure out the conflict(s) of that level, solve the conflict(s), take character or building back with you at the end. The story isn't offensively stupid and there are some funny moments in the story and levels, which is why this is more neutral than outright negative.-Costumes aren't as important as they're made out to beIn the game and in promotional material, costumes were hyped up to be this thing that would allow you to complete levels using their powers. In reality, they are purely cosmetic and offer no gameplay changes. This is somewhat disappointing, but also understandable considering how many moves SpongeBob already has available to him. On a more positive note, you're able to change your costume at any time during the game through the pause menu and there are quite a lot of them to unlock, with the vast majority of them being references to stuff in the show.-Collectibles don't feel rewarding enoughThis might sound strange in a game like this, but the rewards you get for collecting stuff feel... underwhelming. When you're not collecting stuff to complete one of the quests, the main collectible is doubloons. As you collect doubloons, you'll fill a bar and eventually level up. What does leveling up do? It gives you access to more costumes you can purchase and then wear... and that's all it does. Unless you're going out of your way to get 100% completion or there's a costume you really like at a specific level, there's not much incentive to collect doubloons. The same thing applies to the jelly that you see everywhere in each level. Jelly is only used to purchase the costumes that you unlock through leveling up and nothing else. In this game, golden spatulas return from BFBB and there's 1 in each level. What do they do? They give you an achievement after you collect all of them and that's it. You don't even get to hear SpongeBob say any unique lines or do any kind of animation when you collect them, which makes them even more pointless than the previous collectibles if you're not going for 100% completion. Finally, in a few of the levels you can find the golden underwear from BFBB and it does increase your health like in that game, which makes them one of the only optional collectibles that affects gameplay in any way (still no unique lines or animations though rip).Finally, my last gripe with the collectibles has to do with 100% completion. After you finally get all the collectibles and complete all the in-game awards (achievements basically), what do you get for putting in the effort? Nothing but achievements and the satisfaction of completing the game entirely. I find this disappointing as in both BFBB and TSSM, you got an extra ending scene, got to view concept art, and other cool rewards to make collecting everything worthwhile. It just seems strange that the most notable rewards you get are costumes and a few health upgrades and it feels like something is missing.-The Final Boss is not very goodI won't say too much to avoid spoilers, but the final boss seems like they combined a few of the bosses you previously encountered and called it a day. The whole battle follows the pattern of: Dodge multiple shockwave attacks, pick up the power up you were introduced to in the final level, charge it up on basic enemies the boss summons, hit boss with charged up shot, repeat this cycle two more times and the boss is done. It sounds like I'm simplifying it, but it really is that easy, and for an enemy you encounter at the very end of the game, it shouldn't be.SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake was very fun for me to play through. I enjoyed all the silly references and memes from the show and previous games, and the entire game was captivating enough for me to want to 100% complete it, despite how underwhelming the process was. If you're a fan of both older and modern SpongeBob, have played BFBB or TSSM and enjoyed them, or just want an casual platformer and don't care about getting 100%, I can highly recommend this game. If you do not fall into any of those categories, I would wait for a sale if you still want to try it at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to give my honest review of this game starting sort of from the beginning, and giving comparisons to past SpongeBob games I played.As a kid, I grew up on BFBB (Battle for Bikini Bottom) and The SpongeBob Movie Game (both on the PS2). I also played a plug-and-play SpongeBob game, as well as PRR (Plankton's Robotic Revenge) on the Wii. I also purchased BFBB Rehydrated when it was released (PC and got it free on PS4).So OBVIOUSLY, I was STOKED to play The Cosmic Shake, as I had been waiting for its release since it was shown off at Sony's "State of Play" a while back. This is where my comparisons are gonna come in.BFBB/BFBB Rehydrated: To me these games remain the best SpongeBob games TO DATE, the original is timeless, and the remaster (although I had a few gripes) was spectacular as well. The Cosmic Shake definitely seems to take a pretty decent bit of inspiration from them, but In my opinion just isn't quite as good.PRR: Wasn't my favorite of the SpongeBob games, and although fun with a second player, felt dull in comparison to the other games I had played. The Cosmic Shake definitely tops PRR by a mile.The SpongeBob Movie Game: Really good game, but super long, and VERY grindy. Never beat it as a kid because the grindiness of the game couldn't keep my attention. I'd say personally that The Cosmic Shake, is a bit better than TSBMG.So now I'm going to go over the Pros and Cons of buying the game, what it did well, and what it didn't.PROS:1) The graphics are really good, maybe even slightly better than BFBBR.2) In comparison to TSBMG, it is a lot less grindy. I like that you can actually progress through the game and story without having to go get a bunch of bloody doubloons, unlike TSBMG and the Goober Tokens...3) THE FIGHTING OMG, I love love love the fighting mechanics in this game. I'd say it may have my favorite fighting mechanics out of all the games I have played. The Karate Kick is especially fun to use and made me feel super cool and like a total parkour master. The only thing I missed having, is the Bubble Bowl from BFBB. 4) THE VOICE ACTING!  It's pretty much all the original voice actors which makes it just that much better. Unlike BFBB where Mr. Krabs...well...sounds not quite right. The only thing I would complain about would actually be SpongeBob's voice, as it is a bit off. However, I know Tom Kenny is getting older, and SpongeBob isn't exactly the easiest voice to pull off, so I'll give it a pass.5) COSTUMES! I believe TSBMG did have them as well, but I really do like that they brought them back in this game.6) The callbacks and references made me smile.7) Smacking Anchovies, I rest my case.8) I do like that Patrick gives you Health/Underpants, I think that's a really nice addition, as it makes it a little bit less hectic when you're trying to fight a lot of enemies. Speaking of enemies...9) The new enemies are really neat, and I like how many different variants there are. Makes you have to actually have some form of strategy to how you play and fight.10) Level Designs: I think they did really well here, although I will say there are 2 that after a few times of running through, I started to not like as much. But, I didn't hate any of them, unlike another particular level from a particular game...(I'm looking at you Kelp Forest...)11) I will say it did pretty well on the achievements, the majority of them are fun and not super hard to get, but still fun and challenging enough to keep my attention and not make me wanna tear my head off in absolute frustration and rage.12) I like that you can use the Seahorses to get around Bikini Bottom, although I personally am quite partial to the legendary Sponge-Ball, they do indeed suffice for their intended purpose.Cons:1) The story...It's not bad, and it's a fun idea, but I personally just didn't feel like it was super engaging. A lot of the humor and dialogue fell flat for me. Sure, it had a few good jokes in there, but it just was all kinda bland/dry humor in my opinion. Also, the main plot line and villain were basically obvious from the beginning of the game. Although most of the SpongeBob games do follow that sort of rule of thumb to have it shown from the beginning, it just felt  Like perhaps it's just a bit too cliche for me, others may disagree though.2) As of now, there are bugs. I will give it the fact that the bugs I experienced were minimal, and I'm sure they'll fix them soon; but as of right now, the game does have some minor bugs (ie: Characters disappearing or becoming transparent in cut-scenes.).3) The length of the game: I managed to 100% the entire game in just shy of 22 hours. This means unless you play the game slowly, you'll be able to beat the entire story in 10 hours or less, and 100% it in under 24 hours.4) The price: I pre-ordered the game the day before release; and although I would say I did have a lot of fun with it, I feel like the game should have been only $20 and not $40 or more (for special editions). 5) The amount of content is lacking in my opinion. For as long as it took them to make the game, I would think that it would have a lot more content. And although I did enjoy the uniqueness of the levels and the new abilities/powers, after a while you get too used to everything and it starts to get a bit boring.6) The lack of levels: I actually wish there were more levels to play; the majority of them were really fun to play, and with all the new mechanics, I feel like they could have done so much more, especially with the expansive world that is Bikini Bottom.7) I know I said I like the Seahorses, but the controls do feel a bit wonky, and I don't like the fact that once you hop on it, you have no way of stopping them other than just dismounting them. 8) The boss's achievements in particular bothered me a LOT. Now it's not the achievements themselves that I have an issue with; overall, they weren't that bad and I actually had decent fun with them and found them challenging. The problem lies in having to restart, which normally I wouldn't fuss about...HOWEVER! In the case of these, any time you enter a boss fight, if you wanted to just commit die in order to restart the level, or you wanted to simply restart it by re-entering the level, that's not gonna work buckaroo. Every time you have to restart a boss level, you have to literally quit to the main menu, and then load up your game file...EVERY. SINGLE. BLOODY. TIME. And not gonna lie...it gets reallllly old quickly.9) The overall challenge of the game...wellllll it's just not exactly there. Sure it has a few moments where it could be a bit hard, but the majority of the game is really really easy, which in comparison to BFBB and TSBMG, makes this game like child's play. Even the bosses are so cut and dry and super easy, really only one of them did I have a minor struggle with. But the attack patterns were so easy to learn that it just felt almost a bit saddening. I was very disappointed by how easy the literal FINAL BOSS was.EDIT: I have two more things to add to this list.10) The repetitive voice lines get bothersome after a few times, I'm officially sick of The Krusty Krab Pizza song...11) Patrick pointing towards people and things that you just spoke to, or if you sit still for a moment he turns into an arrow and tries to point you somewhere, or even just wandering off to look for things he will do it then as well, which can get annoying. As well as audio cues telling you there's a secret nearby; it's not much of a secret, or gratifying when you find it if they literally tell you one's there.FINAL THOUGHTS:Overall, I'd say this is a good game. Although in my opinion, it is a bit lacking in content, I did still have fun with it. My advice is to wait for the game to go half-price, and then purchase it. But regardless of what you chose to do, full price or not, I do still recommend it, as it had a lot of charm to it.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in and i've roughly gotten to the start of the 4th main level, and while it is a good game, i feel a lot of it has been changed for worse.Good:- New movement combat options definitley improve gameplay! every new addition to the loop was a blast to gain in my arsenal.- Scenery is nice!- Dialogue, cutscenes and story are very good for what they are!- Gameplay is fluid just like the last titles.- Some minigames are added to the loop! some are pretty enjoyable!Bad:- Collectibles are kind of pointless in this game- Game is MUCH more linear, partially because of last point and just the design overall.- Some enemies and tasks/minigames are just mundane to be mundane. (button mashing, hit and wait for a few seconds then hit again) some can also be very simple (such as the final fight of the karate zone.)- levels do not feel very engaging. it's just go from one point, do a thing, do another, get to the end.- there can be a few dissapointments here and there. main standout is in the first level in the cave where a boss should be but isn't.effort was DEFINITLEY put into this title, they were the same devs who fixed up BFBB. however i do feel they chained themselves to the game and didnt improve the game enough. definitley is modernized, and it's not a bad game. however i would not say this game is worth 40$, maybe 20 at most. i do not believe we should hold it being a kids game as an excuse. BFBB was a good game for all. cosmic shake, i believe was crafted in a direction that does not suit the game well enough.Critics can be critics, but this didn't wow me. I can see where it is good but i can also see where they flunked out.EDIT AFTER COMPLETION:so! 5th level and onwards (except the final boss like holy cow did that suck) the game takes a huge improvement! i wouldn't say it changes my opinion on how much this game is worth but it does show me what COULD'VE been. i also wish there could've been more bonus/challenge content to help improve the mediocre levels and round out the experience for players who want a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this review off, let me just state that I  receive a key for this game from THQ Nordic, and while I am incredibly grateful, this will not influence my opinion in any way, shape, or form. I will always be honest, as I do not want to falsely sway anyone's opinion.Cosmic Shake felt so amazing to play, and I had so much fun with this game—even more fun than in . The atmosphere and voice acting just felt extremely polished in comparison to BFBB. For some reason, I feel like the BFBB voice acting was cheesy. But this was very well done. It features lighthearted humor for all ages, even if you haven't watched the TV show! I really enjoyed all the dialogue and found my adult self laughing. Playing through this game was like reliving my childhood with all the references to the show, and I loved every minute of it. In terms of graphics and soundtrack, visually and audio-wise, this game is so beautiful, and Purple Lamp/THQ Nordic did an excellent job.A lot of the worlds/levels are similar to BFBB: Rehydrated  they're more of an enhanced and better version of them, in my opinion. My favorite world was Halloween Rock Bottom! A lot of new enemies are introduced, some that I found super cool and others that I found so annoying (I'm talking to you, Baby Booms). Most enemies you can kill with a basic attack and have 1 HP but other enemies have 2-3 HP, and they can get a little irritating, like one of the enemies, Big Jelly. You can only hit him once he finishes his attack, and you can only hit him once. If you get hit during his attack, it won't allow you to hit him at all; even if you physically melee him, nothing will register. This annoyed me sometimes, but I just learned to get used to it. The boss fights are very easy and have very simple mechanics, but that's okay! Some of us don't like overly difficult games :P The only boss fight I kind of struggled with was the final boss, and it was more of the ADDs that were making the boss fight difficult for me. All in all, combat is extremely fun and mindless, which I adore in games like these. I don't want to get frustrated and angry. I just want to have fun, fight, and collect s**t.One of my favorite things about this was the amount of side quests available alongside your main objective to progress through the game. You can still work on these side quests after you finish the game, and I plan on finishing them in order to 100% the game. The side quests aren't too difficult to complete but give you a reason to go back and revisit the worlds, while also collecting any other collectibles you missed during the first run through. The collectibles are SO fun to collect without feeling too annoying. They don't require much thinking or puzzle-solving, but some will be "locked" in a way until you get a certain ability through progression of the game. The collectibles include: doubloons, golden spatulas, golden underwear, Spot locations, sticky notes, and so much more. If you love collectibles in games, this is a great one for you! Especially if you like 100%'ing games.In brief, do I recommend this game? Yes. Do I recommend it for the full retail price? It depends on the circumstances. I finished BFBB in 20~ hours. I finished Cosmic Shake in 11~ hours, but again, I do plan on going back and grabbing all the achievements. So, if you're a one-and-done kind of player, wait for a sale. If you love achievement hunting, the full retail price is worth it, in my opinion! I will easily get 20+ hours in this game through achievement hunting. Happy gaming!Thanks for reading my review and have a fantastic day!Rating: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this under two conditions. You're either a child or a big spongebob fan, otherwise this game is not worth it.I played the first one, both original and remake and that game was a blast, absolute fun level design, gameplay, etc. This game however.. it's not bad, if anything it's pretty fun. But it is kind of braindead. The game is incredibly easy, you're never once challenged, the levels feel smaller than they did in BFBB and this time you're playing just as spongebob. The collecting part here also feels a bit off. You don't really have a reason to do any sidestuff or collect things other than for completion, so it feels tedious to go back for things to levels you have completed already.The story is alright, again a little predictable but it works. The game also has lovely cutscenes and you're once again able to just run through different places from the show, which is always cool. The only issues I've had where that sometimes the hitboxes seem a bit bigger than they are which has let me to get hit when it looked like I should be fine, but that is a really minor issue, cause even if you do get hit or die, the game doesn't really punish you for it. You also fight the same 6-7 enemies all game over and over, and while every single one has their unique thing, most of them you can very easily kill, while there are two, that kind of require you to just wait around a bunch.That being said, the game really does feel like it was made for a much younger audience in mind. But if you can see past that, it would say it's still fun to run around Bikini Bottom and other familiar places with Spongebob and everyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know who the target audience is. The game has REALLY good reviews, while I couldn't get into it at all, and I adore SpongeBob. I also loved BFBB a lot and completed it several times as a kid and recently.The biggest (and almost the only plus) is that it looks visually good. I love the graphics and art style; it's super nice to look at. But that's kinda where it ends for me.The level design is kinda eh at best; it's just confusing, copy-n-pasted, and random in many areas. I absolutely hate the backtracking mechanic that makes you come back to levels hours after completing them just to get some collectible with a mechanic that you learned way later on. (That might be subjective; I know there are people who like it, but I find it severely unsatisfying.)And then the combat—it's absolutely horrendous and repetitive. (Except the jump-attack-thingy; that one is very satisfying.) You have to fight to progress, so you can't just skip it; you HAVE to engage with it. The bathtub mf is the worst offender; it's painfully boring to wait for him to attack you and lose his stamina/get his bathtub stuck three times in a row.I don't know, man. There are so many people that love it that I almost feel bad and weird for writing this, but I just really don't get the appeal. Except for nostalgia and graphics, the game doesn't offer much, especially for that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for September 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 1st, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A classic Collectathon SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is impressive. You can just tell someone to put in the extra effort in everything on this title. The cut scenes are well-animated with a style that is way above what I was expecting. The story is well told; the writing is quite funny. But with it being a collectathon it’s going to be about the levels, and Cosmic Shake has an impressive layout for the first area, and the first true level, as well as a funny concept. However, there are still some issues I have found. I saw three different times players rode a horse, and all three of them had rough transitions between the horse gameplay and the main gameplay, making me think I failed each time. I didn’t, it just wasn’t smooth. Also, sometimes players will be confused about what is expected of them, but not too often. The controls are smooth. It’s more of a question of what is possible. One thing I will bring up is the voice cast. The entire cast is back to my knowledge, and it brings me back to the original cartoon. I do want to call out Bill Fagerbakke. His line delivery as Patrick made me laugh so many times in the first hour. Pick this up if you’re a fan of Spongebob, or just like a good collectathon. The level design here is great. The characters are their classic self, and the story here is compelling. It feels like a large-scale episode, and that’s what you would want in a Spongebob game. This was a very pleasant surprise.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: look. i am probably the biggest 'casual fan' of the classic spongebob duo for the ps2/xbox/gamecube. BFBB and The Movie Game were my favorite games as a kid. Which makes me extremely sad to say how *agonizingly mediocre* this is. Which is sad! Because it was announced after favorable reviews of BFBB:Rehydrated, and it was by the same studio that brought us that (still good! but less good than the original in my eyes) game. So this is clearly intended to be a companion piece, a 'sequel' to battle for bikini bottom that wasn't associated with a (by now) classic movie.Unfortunately.. it's.. not great? They missed a lot of what made BFBB *good.* There were no 'quests,' no menu to track them, just the characters of bikini bottom telling you what needed to get done, and on occasion, meters to track collectibles. It was a true collect-a-thon. But this.. this is the World of Warcraft method of collecting. It's incessant backtracking and disappointing, unmemorable hiding places. The humor, also, leaves a lot to be desired. The few jokes that aren't "Hey, Remember the Show?" usually fall flat-- not to say there aren't a few ones that ushered a chuckle out of me, but most of them were mediocre. The enemies from Battle for Bikini Bottom all had a 'joke' associated with them (the Ham-Mer wielded a giant piece of ham, Slick was a bubble blowing baby, and the Tubelets were a bunch of rude little kids that you got a kick out of hitting.) but the classic environmental humor of The Cosmic Shake just seems to either be generic point-and-laugh "haha, look, it's a CUBE" style humor, or.. again.. "remember the show" vis a vis the Enemy Spawner (everybody run, it's the Appetizer!).This may all sound like it's failing to live up to the expectations set by the company's previous title, a remaster of a beloved cult-classic Nickelodeon title. But it's important to say, sadly, the game fails on it's own merit.The moveset, devoid of comparison to the original title, leaves a lot to be desired. It attempts greatly to be smooth, with moves leading into each other (or at least, that's what I take away from it). Unfortunately, the game seems to announce it's best moves (a flying kick that locks onto enemies, like Sonic's Homing Dash, and Grappling-- a stiff, clunky move that Sandy had in Rehydrated. They're so similar I'd wager the code was lifted straight from their previous project.) way too soon, leaving the rest of the game feeling uneventful amd gimmicky.The story, if you came to it for story, also leaves something to be desired. To summarize, Spongebob gets a magic bubble wand, and makes an inordinate amount of wishes, causing a multiversal-level catastrophe. In order to fix it, Spongebob teams up with the (clearly telegraphed villain) mysterious Madame Kassandra. We will get to her in a moment. Despite the ambitious more in-depth planned plot, it detracts from the gameplay of the moment, making every level seem dedicated to running through as fast as possible, beating the boss (which is usually the character you came here for. i don't know why they're fighting you, even after beating the game.) and then going back in to do a side quest or two (which is always 'collect 5 objects.') So mediocre.Now, back to the antagonist, Madame Kassandra. She appears to be one of the devs' Donut Steele level ocs, a disappointing villain on all fronts, and nowhere near as satisfying a villain as any of Heavy Iron's ps2/gamecube titles. Now.. this is where it gets disappointing, vis a vis the characterization. She appears to be heavily inspired by the stereotypes surrounding Romani people, or 'G*psy.' I am not at liberty to speak on issues on behalf of the Romani people-- because I do not know nearly enough about their culture. However! I can tell that "Caravan-Riding G*psy Mermaid who never displays anything but wanton lust for power and a propensity for stealing" is.. not a great look! But, again, I'm not at liberty to say.But, all in all, for every good thing this game does, there's at least two bad things sandwiching it. Really disappointing on all fronts, especially considering how ready I was to let Purple Lamp show off their game-development chops on a brand new, original title. Unfortunately, it seems Purple Lamp has very little originality to show for it, and what they do have I'd rather they'd keep.4/10. A passable experience.. in the sense of 'No thanks. I'll pass.'

_childDocuments_.review: I love the smell of bubbles in the morning. Smells like... victory.Pros:* Well crafted worlds, stories, and situations to play in. This game is nicely polished!* The game is always doing something new. I was never bored!* The move-set and game progression was greatly improved from the predecessor. * Most importantly, it pays honest tribute to SpongeBob! Cons: (Spoiler Free)* The final boss and ending was a letdown. It was too easy and short when compared to other battles. * Audio transition problems with music. This happened for most early game events. Sometimes music would even stop playing for boss battles, although I am sure this will be patched in the near future!* (Some) Empty promises. For example, one level constantly remarks about a certain character being a threat, and they build it up as you get closer, but we never see said character. It makes the game feel dishonest and cut short. As someone with a lifelong love for the franchise and videogame series, I wholeheartedly adored this experience. Never would I have expected Battle for Bikini Bottom to be remade, let alone a spiritual sequel. Adoration aside, this is a joyful experience that anyone can have nautical nonsense with under the sea.

Be careful when engaging boss fights and make sure to drop a HARD save often. While fighting Pom Pom (Pearl) at the end of the Prehistoric Kelp Forest level, I died at the exact same time that pearl was defeated. This caused my game to repeatedly spawn SpongeBob out of bounds infinitely dying. I tried teleporting away, however this froze the application and caused my PC to crash. Upon booting up the game there is no main objective, and I am unable to redo the bossfight, so it is impossible to progress. With no back up save, you essentially need to start the game over. Super niche bug but be warned, triggering this bug will end your play through. Other than this I have not experienced any other major bugs. I will change my review to recommended as soon as this issue is fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me feel so nostalgic. I remember playing SpongeBob on my old Xbox as a kid while visiting family in Bosnia. I would sit inside and play while it rained, or while the 40+ degree weather was hitting its peak around noon until I could go back outside with friends. To put it more simply, playing this game for me is kind of what the dish in Ratatouille is for the critic when he takes his first bite. I am instantly transported to simpler times, and my heart is happy.Everything runs extremely well and the game is graphically beautiful. The colours all pop and the new worlds you can explore are unique. Even the writing is great. I have found myself giggling quite a bit under my breath the past couple of hours while playing. The dialogue suits each character very well, and the voice acting is good, too, despite what some other reviews seem to think.While the game is "linear" in the sense that you have a primary quest to follow, I have been exploring around quite a bit to find gold items and the like. There is definitely a sense of freedom here that many platformers fail to have. Jumping is smooth and I have no complaints about any of the controls! I am currently playing with my keyboard and mouse but I will almost definitely play later on my Steam Deck with its controller. I have no doubts that it will run well there since I played the first game on Switch.This game is a fun, funny experience and it instantly has become one of my comfort go-tos. The world(s), characters, narrative design, music, everything... it works so well!  It was worth every penny in my opinion. Nostalgia, nostalgia, nostalgia! Now, if only I could get my hands on SpongeBob-shaped mac and cheese once again...

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a neutral option for reviews, if so I'd use it. Gonna go for Positive so the game doesn't get buried, I guess. For context, I got all achievements.The game starts nice, with good visuals, audio, and it controls well...but then it keeps going, and you reach later parts of the game; the later in the game you get, the more rushed the whole thing feels, along with increasing technical issues and lack of polish.Challenge-wise, it's alright for a kids game, but I was expecting more with the optional challenges, both in difficulty and variety.Collectible-wise, they have no real use besides getting you new costumes and for completion, which is fine I suppose; I have bigger issues with how they're handled: This game's levels are really linear, but it decides to scatter new collectibles along the way for you to get in future revisits. It could've worked better on sandbox-like levels, but adding some random collectibles to "force" you to basically redo the same linear sections of a level makes it feel repetitive.Also this may be just me, but SpongeBob's constant repeating of the same 4 quips every time he collects Jelly or glides gets old really fast. An option to disable them would be nice.I'd say to wait for a sale if you can. Game's fine overall, but can't say it's worth 40 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: The creative team at Purple Lamp have done it again with SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake! The game has players follow the yellow and lovable square sponge that we all know and love, in a quest to save his friends and his beloved underwater town of Bikini Bottom.In typical SpongeBob fashion, after acquiring a magic bubble blower from a mermaid named Kassandra, both SpongeBob and Patrick have some fun, causing the ensuing chaos that leads to the games story.The story is amusing; foremost, it is both interesting and humorous, leaving nods to the show all over its fantastically built levels. Dialogue is amazing, and on point. The story never made me feel bored, keeping me engaged the entire time. It felt as SpongeBob as SpongeBob could ever feel. Hats off to Purple Lamp for the creative and fun original story!Just as the remake to Battle for Bikini Bottom was stunning, Cosmic Shake takes it even more beyond that. The visuals are taken straight from the show and plastered all over the game. Each level is filled with details as well as gags that should not be missed. This has to be the most visually pleasing and stunning SpongeBob video game to date.The game is not super mechanical, however, there is a nice list of moves that you can do and mess around with, making it a very enjoyable experience! With newly added dodging, players can move out of the way of danger as well as use it for a slight boost in movement. You can double jump and now glide, allowing players to fall with style. There are others, but I won't spoil it. Attacking is just about the same as it was in the remake of Battle for Bikini Bottom, except with the added bonus of costumes (more on that below).THERE ARE COSTUMES, AND GOOD ONES TOO! Yes, that is right, costumes. I can now dress as a clown and defend my underwater home! The costume selection is great, with many costumes fans can enjoy playing in, most notably, a hard-hatted war hero. Seven costumes are locked behind a "DLC" paywall, which is quite sad, but there are 35 other costumes to enjoy if you so wish not to spend money on it.Costumes have another added feature that most might miss, while some costumes have changes and other don't, keen eyed players will notice that when attacking regularly, SpongeBob's weapon of choice changes just as well!Even though they don't serve much purpose other than being really, really cool. Players can have fun dressing up a sponge in this great addition to the game.They're fun, however, they aren't as challenging as I would have liked, and no, I don't want a Soulslike SpongeBob game (although that sounds kinda funny and I would probably play it). I just hoped that they wouldn't be as simple as dodging an attack, and within two minutes the battle would be over. I will say that some are different from others, but overall, are very easy to beat, making it feel as if there is little to no challenge in these fights.I felt that I should add this as I've seen reviews about people disliking them. They aren't all that bad. I mean, yes, they're kinda just there. Regardless, they are still enjoyable.Cosmic Shake has seven unique levels for the player to enjoy. They're each amazing and beautifully well made, leaving the player to want to explore as much as they possibly can.As aforementioned, the dialogue is amazing in this game; however, the lack of no auto-dialogue options/button is very much missing. Many times SpongeBob speaks and as he's cut off, the game requires the player to make an input causing a sort of weird stoppage to the pleasing dialogue that is expected to continue. The developers should take note of this and (hopefully) add it to their next game to come.The lack of extra/more phrases is very much apparent. I must have heard three phrases over and over throughout the seven levels the game possesses. One particular phrase, "sticky sweet", not only had me and my friend laughing, but had me just as annoyed for the 100th time.This may sound deranged, but, I wish there were more loading screens. This is the only game where I've wanted to see as many loading screens as possible. They are perfect nods to the show, directly ripped from those infamous time cards that appear in it.Finally, those pictures. If you know, you know.This is a great start to what is hopefully the beginning of new SpongeBob video games. I hope (more like pray) that Purple Lamp continues to create fun experiences for fans of the show and games alike!Gameplay mechanics are great and work well.Visually pleasing to look at, my eyes never hurt once, having me glued to my screen just as I did watching the show.Roughly 9 hours for main story.Roughly 12 hours for 100% completion.Personally, I would recommend purchasing at full price, but as always I have to say, wait for discount/sale.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Given the chance, I would do unholy things to SpongeBob if I could get into one of his holes… This is a game for kids, just like Dark Souls. Got this for my 8 year old autistic nephew and he has never been so quiet. I'm 35 years old, so naturally I loved this game too.One of the best adventure games ever made. Played it multiple times, and it never fails to get me all immersed. The lines, the visuals, the music, the costumes, they're all filled with SpongeBob nostalgia; I loved it! What an honorable love letter of a game.This game wasn't designed to be the next groundbreaking gaming experience. It was designed to be a SpongeBob experience for fans of the franchise. The average person isn't going in expecting it to change the industry, they're buying it to see the wacky sponge man cause mischief with the bloated pink balloon for a few hours.It's great, the levels are long but well designed and don't overstay their welcome, the story and humor are based on the early years of the series rather than the modern episodes, classic characters like King Neptune (who was retcon'd in Sponge On The Run) make a return and are all voiced by the original voice actors, the new characters like Kassandra are great and feel right at home in the SquarePants universe and my favorite part, THE SLAPPING SOUNDTRACK, every SpongeBob fan should play this!There’s many throwbacks to older episodes. Such as voiceline references, some pictures and level settings. The developers definitely have love for SpongeBob and it’s shown throughout the game. Also I loved using different costumes for SpongeBob. Despite you only playing as SpongeBob in this game, I didn’t mind it. I loved the constant SpongeBob and Patrick chemistry as he always follows you around in the game and it did make me laugh a good amount of times. Don’t go into this expecting it to play like Bikini bottom though, BFBB is a collectathon where you walk around and do tasks for golden spatulas, while this game is a lot more linear and you just go point A to point B with a lot less exploration. Games graphics are really nice looking and the gameplay is fun overall. If you’re a SpongeBob fan and have played previous games 100% pick it up

_childDocuments_.review: This review is coming from someone who really liked Battle for Bikini Bottom. As a BFBB lover, this game is only okay to me. It nails story, the platforming feels good and reminds you of the previous game and the characters and dialogue are all great, but to me it's a total miss in one very important category and that is the level design, which in my opinion is one of the most important aspects of a 3D platformer. They basically took BFBB and put it "on-rails" which I personally don't really like. The game points you to your next objective, you go to the objective and push a button - then you go to the next objective and push a button, and so on. It would be a stretch to call BFBB an "open-world" game, but it was certainly not on rails to this degree, and Cosmic Shake really doesn't encourage exploration or going off the path it is point you through at all. To me, it comes down to level design. B4BB took elements from open-world games and made them work on relatively small levels because the game was not forcing you to only go in one direction to get to the objective, and perhaps also because it was not telling you with arrows and objective markers exactly where to go and how to get there. It seems like Cosmic Shake has you run through the level once with no reason to return to any parts of the level you've already been to, whereas BFBB made full use of the levels by having your return to same areas to accomplish different goals or objectives and interacting with the same part of the level in different ways. It is still a decent game, so pick it up if you love SpongeBob and I'll give it the recommended thumbs up, but I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a bit disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake offers a nostalgic journey through the beloved cartoon's universe.The game features straightforward platforming mechanics reminiscent of early 2000s 3D platformers. While these abilities provide a solid foundation, some players may find the gameplay lacking in innovation. While the main campaign lasts around 10 hours, The Cosmic Shake offers some additional content for completionists, these extras provide some incentive for replay, though their appeal may vary depending on the player's interest in full completion.The Cosmic Shake takes players through seven distinct "Wishworlds," each themed after different SpongeBob episodes or concepts. These colorful and vibrant environments offer a visually appealing backdrop for the adventure. However, the platforming challenges are relatively simple during the game.One of the game's standout features is its soundtrack. The Cosmic Shake combines recognizable SpongeBob tracks with original video game tunes, creating a delightful audio experience that captures the essence of the show.  In addition, the voice acting is another highlight, featuring performances from the original SpongeBob cast. This attention to detail helps bring the characters to life and adds authenticity to the experience.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake delivers a solid, if somewhat dated, platforming experience wrapped in the charm and humor of the SpongeBob universe. You should try the game if you love 3D platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty worthy followup to Battle for Bikini Bottom and is definitely in Top 3 SpongeBob games for me. The levels are pretty straightforward and short if you're not going out of your way for the optional collectibles, and there aren't any other unlockable bonuses besides the costumes (and achievements, I suppose).As someone who hasn't really been following new episodes of the show that closely for about 10 years, I was pleasantly surprised by the charm and wit in the game's writing. Not every joke lands, and the cutscenes in particular are paced very strangely, but there's tons of references to the show's first 3 seasons and I got a laugh out of some of the game's original jokes as well.Cosmic Shake is just good, solid, simple fun, and kept me busy for a good week combing through every world to get all the costumes. _childDocuments_.review: Completed as of writing this review: 100%As one of the people who have completed Heavy Iron’s trilogy (BfBB, Movie and Tr.or Sq.), I think this is a great comeback of the old SpongeBob. Yes, I’ll admit that the charm of BfBB is still yet to be repeated, but it’s really close to it, with many cool references and how a cast of characters is being treated. The levels were very well constructed, even if they’re just a one road now (well like in a movie game basically), they’re still fun to play. The music is fine enough, though nothing special like in BfBB and Movie (the licensed songs comeback is amazing tho). The bosses were really well-designed (for the most part), except for the final boss, which was a huge letdown, most likely rushed for release. The gimmicks are also fun and SpongeBob’s moves are also satisfying to use. My only gripe with this game, is the replayability though. I’m not having any trouble with being told to collect things everywhere and replay the levels again and again. The problem was with guidance - there is none! My guidance was my friend, who googled everything to tell me the exact location, because I was tired of replaying the same level over and over. One of the doubloons in the first stage was a sick joke, because that’s the only time you use a mechanic (if you know, you know). Yes, I like the style of side-quests and how much they reference, but the quests themselves were so dull and tedious, because they were well hidden, but the game never tells in which part of the level you need to explore, which kinda defeats a whole point of exploration, because you’re empty-handed without any hints. Unfortunately there is no case of giving you a reward for 100% like was in BfBB and Movie game, instead you just get an achievement, like in many other generic games. I’m disappointed with 100% aspect of the game and it counts, because I was satisfied with all this in BfBB and the Movie game, which Cosmic Shake was trying to be a successor to. The other minor nitpick is the difficulty, but that’s a given for games for kids nowadays.Other than all that, I’m happy that SpongeBob is not in hands of that other publisher anymore, who didn’t care about SpongeBob for a whole decade. Now we got a real deal after like, what? 20 years almost? (Movie game came out in 2004) So yeah, it’s good to be a SpongeBob fan with this coming out and I can say that SpongeBob’s game series are in good hands once more!

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ∞/10Review:SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake catapults players into an intergalactic escapade that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. As a fervent follower of SpongeBob's ventures, diving into this cosmic journey was an experience unlike any other. Brace yourself for an odyssey that defies gravity, logic, and perhaps even Bikini Bottom itself.Visually stunning and bursting with creativity, The Cosmic Shake delivers a visual feast that rivals the most vibrant galaxies. From the neon-lit streets of New Kelp City to the surreal landscapes of Neptune's Moon, every location is a testament to the boundless imagination of the developers.But it's not just the visuals that dazzle; the gameplay is equally impressive. Seamlessly blending platforming, puzzles, and cosmic shenanigans, each level is a kaleidoscope of challenges and surprises waiting to be uncovered. Whether you're bouncing through zero-gravity environments or dodging asteroids in space, the gameplay mechanics are as diverse as they are delightful.What truly sets The Cosmic Shake apart, however, is its narrative depth and emotional resonance. Beneath the zany humor and whimsical charm lies a heartfelt story of friendship, courage, and the power of imagination. As SpongeBob and friends embark on their cosmic quest, they confront their fears, overcome obstacles, and discover the true meaning of teamwork.Moreover, the game's replay value is astronomical, with a plethora of collectibles, side quests, and hidden secrets scattered throughout the cosmos. With multiple endings and branching paths, every playthrough offers a fresh and exhilarating experience that begs to be explored time and time again.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake isn't just a game; it's a celestial odyssey that transcends the boundaries of imagination. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I'm a HUGE Spongebob fan - I've played and own most of the existing Spongebob games and I was able to notice almost every reference to the show in this game, which was very exciting! I appreciate how THQ Nordic took a lot of the existing elements from BFBB - Rehydrated, such as combat and art style, and went even further with it. The scenery in this game is beautiful, and every location is memorable! However, there are a few issues that hold this game back from being at the same level as BFBB - Rehydrated.As I mentioned earlier, this game is stunning. It's colorful, almost TOO colorful. Every location is a mix of older Spongebob references such as Prehistoric Bikini Bottom and Glove World with different overall concepts. I've seen others complain about this, but I LOVE the boss fights in this game. Each one is unique and well thought out. They're not overly difficult and vary from one another. The music is very fitting for each area and will likely be stuck in your head for a few days (I'm looking at you Wild West Jellyfish Fields). The new combat mechnics are pretty smooth, especially the new kick ability. I'm a bit sad that you can no longer use the Bubble Bash like in BFBB, but the new varitey of abilities more than makes up for it. I did encounter a few combat glitches, specifically the hitbox for certain enemies are a little wonky. There's a relatively long cooldown between Spongebob's primary attack that the game may not always recognize the next one.I'm so glad Clancy Brown reprised his role as Mr. Krabs. Clancy is notorious for being one of the only main cast members to not make an appeareance in many Spongebob games, so having him in this one was a treat.Enemy variety is pretty decent. I enjoyed almost all of the enemy types except for the Jelly Maker, that one was just downright annoying. They fall in line with the story pretty well, but honestly, I'm just glad we're not fighting robots anymore.THE COSTUMES are you kidding me??? There are SO many wonderful designs in this game that are well worth a 100% playthrough. I did pre-order the game to get the DLC skins, which were totally worth it, in my opinion. Coupled with the overall beauty of this game, the costumes make Spongebob stand out so well and serve as such cool callbacks to the show.I'm no audio expert, but this game seems to have weird sound mixing in most areas. Whenever the game transitions to a cutscene, an entirely different track plays for roughly 4-5 seconds, then cuts back to the theme of the world you're in. This happens A LOT and I don't really understand it. I'm also not a fan with how the cast memebers  in this game. I realize the voice actors for the cartoon have changed the way their characters sound in the last few years for the new, younger audience, coupled with the fact that the actors are getting older, but Spongebob's voice sounds much more... forced? He doesn't *sound* like Spongebob to me. Same goes for Sandy and Mrs. Puff. It's almost like the VA's are doing impressions of their own characters? As for the gameplay, The Cosmic Shake hides a lot of collectibles behind upgraded abilities for Spongebob that you'll have to go back and obtain later in the game. That's great and all, I really enjoy backtracking, but the menu doesn't really help you find the general area of where that collectible would be, unlike BFBB - Rehydrated. You're never sure what you're actually looking for in these levels once you eventually go back, which I'm really not a fan of. It's not a huge deal since the levels aren't that big, but since they're so linear it's not ideal to run through each level from start to finish all over again.Finally, the story, in my opinion, is not very strong. Which is fine... it's not a huge deal to me considering it's just a Spongebob game, and I wasn't expecting anything elaborate. Kassandra is... okay I guess? Her design is very cool, but I don't really understand why she's a villain, if that makes sense. The intro arc to this game () does not fall in line with how the story plays out at all, which I found very weird.As a fan of the original cartoon, I'm very impressed with all the references to the early (and some newer) seasons of the show. The costumes were a huge plus for me and made up for the fact that we can no longer swap characters like we could in BFBB. Level and boss variety is great but I wish there was an incentive to replay the game. The story took about 7-8 hours to complete and a little over 20 to 100%. I would say wait until it goes on sale, if you're interested, but don't sell this game too short! I hope to see more titles like this from THQ Nordic in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and worthy successor to the Battle for Bikini Bottom remaster. You can tell right away that the game is basically a sequel - the control scheme is the same, SpongeBob has most of the moves that were spread across him, Patrick, and Sandy in BfBB, and even with the change in general aesthetic, the graphics are just like BfBB. The big change is that SpongeBob is the only playable character, and that the stages are all linear in design with a clearly defined starting and ending point, though there are plenty of branching paths for side missions and hidden content, evoking the feeling of BfBB's wide open stages at times. I think this is a good change, given the scope of the game - it keeps it focused and rolling forward from start to finish, shifting your attention away from the extremely simple story and centering the pitch-perfect tone of the jokes and gags instead.I will say that for all the ways in which marketing focused on the costumes, I found the feature completely inessential, and it didn't feel satisfying to try and find the collectibles that would allow me to unlock the higher costume tiers. I also found myself drifting away from the game after a few hours, with a couple of bosses that were disproportionately difficult, especially compared to the overly-easy final boss. Though I was fine with the bare-bones story, it does leave you feeling like you're not especially sure why you're doing anything, aside from being told by the main villain to romp through the levels. on the whole, though, the critiques I have are no big deal - it's a well-made, fun platformer, so it's worth it if you like the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr A mediocre platformer wrapped in Spongebob assets.  This is not a proper successor to the previous BfBB Spongebob game. Spongebob's voice lines are also pretty repetitive.  I hope I pick it back up later and find a reason to delete this review.EDIT: Nope..  EDIT 2: After returning this game, I went back and replayed the entire previous title BfBB and loved it.  Here's why it's better: Multiple collectibles placed in fun places that reward exploration, multiple characters with unique playstyles, myriad references to the show from the collectibles to the levels to the dialog, proper level design that rewards returning to it later, more levels, better boss battles, better map fast travel system, I could go on..  Ultimately these developers ignored the entirety of what made BfBB such a great title, which is a shame because they had an excellent template for a successor.  Cosmic Shake is a lazy cash grab by comparison, and they have the audacity to charge for DLC like costume packs.  Brave new world..:(

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game on a sale if you can get it. Took me roughly 8.4 hours to complete the main game and I do plan on going back to 100%ing it, however.. I know it's not going to be that good going back to 100%.Overall, Spongebob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a 6.6 / 10. It's not a fantastic game, but it's not like it's a bad game either. It's a serviceable game that does its job of being a fun platformer with some challenges. Some of the pros of this game in terms of gameplay is pretty much the combat & fluidity of moves into each other. I think the combat can be a *little* stiff at times, but it's not terribly stiff and all the moves can flow well into each other. Landing combos from Karate Kick to Ground Pound followed by a dodge to bubble blow are very satisfying and I love the amount of variety to them. The story itself is also fine, leans more to classic Spongebob naivety mixed with his own emotions of discomfort and disdain at times. It's clear the writing is moreso modern Spognebob, but I do commend the team for working with the newer stuff. The worlds are also pretty cool and varied around with the amount of costumes that Spongebob can dawn on be plentiful. It's also cool to see citizens and other characters being portrayed in their said worlds differently too, just wish the enemies were like that akin to how you had the possessed Bikini Bottomites in Spongebob Squarepants The Movie: The Game.Now onto what makes the game very.. lackluster. The game tends to get pretty repetitive pretty quickly and while most Spongebob games tend to do this, I just wish there was some variety within the worlds. It's also clear that some things for doubloons or side objectives get little treatment since you're repeating the same abilities over and over again, which is a shame as I liked the areas where I had to chain together different techniques to get to different platforms. Like in the medieval world I remember having to chain together a Bubble Blow to open up a platform, use the Pizza Glide to get to said platform, and then jump towards and do a Lasso Swing. That was fun, that was cool. I wish this was in a good amount of the platforming. Also movement can be pretty stiff, but it's not terribly stiff. Going forward or backward wasn't terribly bad, felt a bit weird at times, but comparing it to Rehydrated Spongebob's turning was just god awful to perform and he seems to slow down when doing so? It's not a major turn off, but it definitely needed more tweaking and refinement. Also the final boss Overall just underwhelming fights & movement with some actual decent writing and great combat makes The Cosmic Shake get the grade of 6.6 / 10. For me personally, it means it's worth player so long as you're willing to get through some parts of slog.Edit: 12:43 EST @ 2/3/2023 - Just completed the 100%. No guides whatsoever, meaning if you want to go and find everything in the worlds, it's pretty simple to do so. There's a couple extra side things that go off, but that's about it. I'd say the hardest of the Achievements / Awards to get is the "No Get Hit" during the Royal Ballroom Boss. It's just making sure you don't bombrush each cake. Won't say much else.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy platformer games, love SpongeBob, or appreciate fun and whimsy, then GET THIS GAME! If you’ve played Battle for Bikini Bottom, you’ll find the mechanics in The Cosmic Shake quite similar. I played this right after completing the rehydrated edition of BFBB, and the transition in controls was incredibly smooth.The game is visually stunning—far more so than Battle for Bikini Bottom. The vibrant colours bring an overwhelming sense of joy as I play. The SpongeBob games embrace a delightful childlike charm, and while the difficulty is anything but childish (I found myself stuck numerous times), the whimsical gameplay ultimately brings a smile to my face. Growing up obsessed with SpongeBob certainly adds a layer of nostalgia that enhances my experience.During my entire play through, I encountered only one glitch early on that left me stuck for about an hour. Fortunately, I found a guide online, so it wasn't the end of the world.I spent around seven hours completing the main missions, but I still have side quests to tackle. It’s fun revisiting the maps to take on challenges again and hunt for hidden gems.If you’re on the fence about getting this game, I wholeheartedly recommend you go for it—you won’t regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where do I even begin with this one? SpongeBob Schwammkopf: The Cosmic Shake is a game that will leave you scratching your head in confusion, laughing out loud at its bizarre humor, and wondering what the developers were smoking when they came up with some of the levels.First things first, let's talk about the story. SpongeBob and his pals are on a mission to save the universe from destruction by collecting cosmic energy in the form of golden spatulas. Along the way, they encounter strange creatures and visit even stranger worlds, all while trying to avoid the clutches of the evil Plankton. The story is pretty standard for a SpongeBob game, but the levels are where things get really weird.In one level, you play as Patrick as he tries to avoid getting crushed by giant hamburgers falling from the sky. In another, you play as Sandy as she navigates a maze of cheese in outer space. And in perhaps the strangest level of all, you play as Squidward as he tries to escape a nightmare version of his own mind. The levels are all wildly different and keep the gameplay fresh and interesting.The controls are fairly simple and easy to pick up, but some of the levels can be quite challenging. The difficulty level ranges from easy to frustratingly difficult, so be prepared to die a lot if you're not careful. However, the game is forgiving enough that you won't get too frustrated, and the checkpoints are well-placed so you don't have to repeat too much if you mess up.The graphics are colorful and vibrant, just like the TV show. The character models are spot-on and the environments are imaginative and strange. The music is also great, with catchy tunes that will get stuck in your head long after you've turned off the game.But the real star of the show here is the humor. SpongeBob has always been a show that appeals to both kids and adults, and the game is no different. The jokes are clever and silly, and there are plenty of pop culture references to keep the adults entertained. One level even has a boss fight against a giant robot version of David Hasselhoff, which is just as ridiculous as it sounds.Overall, SpongeBob Schwammkopf: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and entertaining game that is sure to delight fans of the TV show. It's weird, it's strange, it's bizarre, and it's funny as hell. If you're looking for a game that's a little bit different and a lot of fun, give this one a try. Just be prepared for some weirdness along the way.
