_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake - A Fun, Nostalgic Adventure for FansRating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)“SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake” is a vibrant and nostalgic adventure that perfectly captures the spirit of the beloved animated series. Developed by Purple Lamp Studios, this 3D platformer sends SpongeBob and his best friend Patrick on a wacky, dimension-hopping journey to save their friends and Bikini Bottom from chaos. With colorful visuals, entertaining gameplay, and plenty of fan service, *The Cosmic Shake* is an engaging romp through the absurd yet charming world of SpongeBob.The premise is simple but effective: SpongeBob and Patrick come into possession of magical wish-granting bubbles, only to accidentally tear open the fabric of reality. The result is a multiverse of different “Wishworlds,” each filled with iconic SpongeBob characters, reimagined settings, and zany scenarios. Fans of the show will appreciate the many references to classic episodes, with each Wishworld capturing a unique vibe—from a wild west setting to a prehistoric land—all offering fun twists on familiar locations.Gameplay-wise, The Cosmic Shake features traditional platforming mechanics that are easy to pick up and play. SpongeBob’s moveset includes a range of fun abilities like bubble-blowing attacks, jellyfish-catching, and karate kicks, all while collecting shiny objects and solving light puzzles. The levels are packed with collectibles and secrets, which adds replayability for those who enjoy exploration. The controls are smooth, and the platforming feels solid, though the game sticks to a relatively simple formula, making it more accessible to younger or casual players.Visually, the game bursts with color and charm. Each level is filled with vibrant and faithful recreations of SpongeBob’s world, with cartoony textures and lively animations that bring Bikini Bottom to life. The voice acting, with the original cast reprising their roles, adds an authentic touch, and hearing Tom Kenny’s SpongeBob and Bill Fagerbakke’s Patrick deliver their trademark humor keeps the tone light and fun. The humor is in line with the show’s silly, whimsical style, and longtime fans will enjoy the quirky interactions between characters.While The Cosmic Shake is undeniably fun, it does have a few shortcomings. The level design, while visually diverse, can sometimes feel repetitive, and the platforming challenges may lack depth for players seeking more complexity. Additionally, some of the combat encounters can be a bit simplistic, with basic enemy patterns that don’t offer much variety as the game progresses. However, these minor drawbacks don’t detract too much from the overall experience, especially for younger audiences or those simply looking for a SpongeBob-themed adventure.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and nostalgic platformer that will especially resonate with fans of the show. It’s a lighthearted, colorful journey packed with references, humor, and classic SpongeBob moments. While it may not reinvent the platformer genre, it excels at delivering a fun, accessible experience that captures the magic of SpongeBob’s universe. If you’re looking for a breezy, feel-good adventure, The Cosmic Shake is worth diving into.

_childDocuments_.review: Like past Spongebob platformers, this game doesn't reinvent the wheel and won't do much to challenge veterans of the genre. Instead, it's the personality, charm, and wit that do the heavy lifting, much like Battle for Bikini Bottom. Cosmic Shake feels right at home within the show's continuity, with several references and nods to its source material's most memorable moments. The humor isn't solely reliant on callbacks though, as the writing itself didn't disappoint either (though slightly more hit-or-miss than BFBB). Even if this game isn't the most groundbreaking of its genre, it still manages to be consistently fun. There are lots of new additions to Spongebob's moveset that make traversal and combat all the more engaging, there are several set pieces and game play changes that spice up the levels, and there's lots to collect here that will certainly make for a fun 100% run.Cosmic Shake may be a 7/10 game, but its charm and fun factor make for an easygoing, enjoyable little package that might be worth picking up on a sale (like I did).

_childDocuments_.review: a fun little game in a similar vein to battle for bikini bottom, with maybe more of a "creature from the krusty krab" vibe. some really nice modernised bfbb-isms and a more structured level design (as opposed to the slightly freer, opener, meandering bfbb levels). i think overall bfbb is the better game, as this one does feel shorter and more rushed. it also feels like a game id have liked less if i was a kid, because bfbb lets you explore a semi-normal bikini bottom and do stupid kid roleplay stuff, whilst this games hub world is much more cramped and the levels are way more linear.still, some really pretty levels (even if performance dips sometimes) and an overall enjoyable experience even if you can feel yourself pushing against the constraints of the budget sometimes (like how in one level all the characters talk about an alaskan bull worm being nearby... and at no point do you run into an alaskan bull worm). if i was a kid this would have been an after school classic. just less than bfbb was.despite being deck verified, the game will drop 10 frames per lightning tiki explosion. idk how that performance is acceptable lol. game regularly struggled to run at 60fps, despite lowering settings. still, the game is not hard and this was more of a slight annoyance than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Yoink!SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a fantastic follow-up to BFBB, delivering a fresh, more linear adventure using the same engine. This game is a true love letter to fans, brimming with show humor, delightful references, and flashbacks from the classic seasons.The gameplay is engaging with new mechanics that make SpongeBob's moveset fun and dynamic. While it's more linear than its predecessor, this structure offers a consistent and thoroughly enjoyable experience throughout. I personally appreciate this approach as it kept the adventure focused and cohesive.However, be prepared for some repetitive lines, like SpongeBob's frequent exclamations or Patrick's quirky comments about jelly. Still, the game made me feel like a kid again for a few hours. That's worth the entry price for sure.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: A good spiritual successor to BFBB, the game can feel a little bit boring at first but it gets better the more you play, in my opinion it is well optimized and has a somewhat interesting story with decent gameplay, if you're not a spongebob fan you may or may not like this but I can still recommend this game, I'd give it a 6.3/10
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, surprisingly feels more linear than BFBB when both games are just linear. It feels like paths are very closed compared to BFBB, combat is an improvement but the jelly piles that spawn more jellies doing that shout move is annoying. Otherwise, good collectathon, presentation was great, not feeling super inclined to 100% this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed both this and Battle for Bikini Bottom and they are amazing games. Cosmic shake has better level design in my opinion but the game is definitely way easier than it's predecessor. Battle for Bikini Bottom is also more creative, this one gets pretty stale after a while. At first I thought the costumes will have some kind of a role but they are strictly cosmetic which is a shame considering BfBB had interesting idea with character swapping. Nevertheless I had a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmic Shake is good, that is true, but it does not amp up much like how Battle for Bikini Bottom did it. It feels shorter and lacking. It is certainly more challenging at least, especially on bosses, and the costumes and side quests were nice.Should you play it? Of course. Make sure to have a good platform at least, or you'll get frame drops.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: An very good spiritual successor to BFBB, combat and overall level design is quite linear as expected and I found them generally fun to visit the different worlds each with their own bosses that aren't too intimidating. Some fun iconic references from the show that I enjoyed hearing back from numerous episodes, is quite fun and enjoyable to sit back and relax on for all audiences, there is a few rough edges here and there with the combat and the camera controls (might've been day one bugs that are situated now, went back after a period of patches to 100% achievements) but overall I think this is a great step up from Battle for Bikini Bottom and well worth the money on sale :-)THQ Nordic & Purple Lamp, please rehydrate The Movie Game and Creature from the Krusty Krab, thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: The "Spiritual Sequel" to Battle for Bikini Bottom, Cosmic Shake is an enjoyable game.- A linear game, a collectathon, and a fun re-imagined version of the SpongeBob world.- Tons of costumes, both unique and references from the show.- Each world introduced a new setting and new mechanics that were fun.- The story has the typical goofiness a SpongeBob story would have!Tip: Finish the story before you go 100% the game. Makes it quicker.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure how to say this but it is definitely a modern spongebob platformer, cant help but compare it to the original bfbb. I do like the more important collectibles and their challenges, side quests (even though all the same), and costumes. Enemy design is meh but the new moves are very welcome, currency collecting is much more boring than shiny objects as well imo (luckily no grinding though). Where I run into real issues are the levels, they feel a little lifeless to me for some reason, they lack memorable music and the cosmic shake aspect makes their identity feel random and wacky like the current version of the show. Character models are used and reused with no name changes, plenty of weird visual glitches that just point to a certain lack of polish. Even post game (I 100%ed the game) there is less to do, you cannot go into houses or buildings, even the KK, it is a missed opportunity.  Don't know, if you like modern spongebib maybe you will have a better experience and I am very happy they made another spongebob platformer, just wanted a bit more from it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice little platformer.  If like me, you need a Sponge Bob fix, it hits the spots; but don't get fooled by it's cuteness, it's not for little kids.  Controls wise, usually very responsive.  Only minor problem, the trampoline jump is usually ok, exception for doing the long jump; requires pinpoint accuracy.  Can be frustrating; outside of that, just a lovely game that puts a smile on my face!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Spongebob and Spongebob games, this is a pretty good game. It feels like a true successor to battle for bikini bottom in every way.There's a good amount of gameplay, the levels are long and varied enough in environment to feel fresh and fun. having select able costumes is a nice fun touch as well. The boss fights felt unique to each one, and the story was good.The game can be very challenging at times, ever present when attempting all the award conditions for defeating the bosses, you will get mad at times trust me.The only issue i had with this game is the glide, that pissed me off quite a bit.I don't know if its an issue only to the Xbox controller, but half the time when you double jump the glide will activate when your not trying to, which after releasing has somewhat of a timed delay before you can use it. This can be very frustrating when either on the slides or trying to traverse some of the gliding portions of the levels.This is a fun game whether your a Spongebob fan or not, I only wish that it was longer.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Excelent game. Now, the big question, is it better than BFBB? Gameplay wise, level design and enemy design? nope, but on art direction and writting? Absolutely. There are some enemies that are very annoying to deal with and the abilities you unlock are plentiful but not as good as the limited kit you had in BFBB... though there are a lot of things that this game lifts up wholesale from BFBB, but if you're gonna ape someone ape the best.The love for the show is palpable in this game, the amount of references and call backs is amazing, the only glearing omission is Mermaidman and Barnackle boy. Think of it this way, BFBB is that great special for the show, This one is that one good movie from the show.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original games such as Battle for Bikini Bottom, The Spongebob Movie Video Game, and Creature from the Krusty Krab were all my top favorites but Cosmic Shake was something new that is similar to Battle for Bikini Bottom but expanded it even more and I enjoyed every minute of Cosmic Shake. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game!I very much enjoyed doing almost everything in this game. The collectibles, the areas, the characters, the visuals; all creative, bright and colorful!A minor nitpick is the much slower tutorial that takes you out of the action. I prefer BFBB's where Bubble Buddy would deliver you new abilities with silly dialogue between the two characters. Other than that, I can't really complain about much else. It's fairly short, with myself completing the game within 8 hours and going back to collect everything post-game within 13 hours. Some of the awards squeeze a little bit more fun out of each area, but some are just monotonous. The enemy variety is a breath of fresh air, instead of generic robots, we get silly jelly creatures with much more unique designs. The humor/writing is more on-par with modern SpongeBob with some referential jokes sprinkled in throughout. This isn't a problem, because I did find some original jokes to be funny. Same old silly SpongeBoy!Overall, it's worth the pickup when it goes on sale. I say that because of the game's length, wishing it had more to offer outside of revisiting many of the same areas for secondary missions. A definite buy for SpongeBob, BFBB, and 3D platforming game fans, in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this after playing several Spongebob platformers in the past including the PS2 era games and the remake of Battle For Bikini Bottom, and as fun as this game was with its fun visuals and smooth gameplay and even the dialogue which reminded me of the older episodes (which is a good thing), this game overall however felt a little bit underwhelming, short and at times feeling rushed for being priced at $40, so buying it on sale is a better value. The difficulty is also VERY low, a 5-year-old could most likely beat it. All in all, this game is good for people who grew up with Spongebob, platformer games like Spyro, and the combo of the two and just want something new to mess around with. BFBB is much better though.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: i would like to say i like this game however if you were expecting another game like bfbb than that's not the experience you will get here surprisingly this feels like a sequel to the movie game its very linear and the level design just feels smaller i like the new movement options though like being able to do that cartwheel move and jump mid air kinda reminds me of the trick you can do in dkc definitely encourages more creativity when platforming which is a good thing for a platformer to have
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome sequel to the beloved Battle for Bikini Bottom. I first bought this on Nintendo Switch when it came out and loved it so much that I decided to purchase it again on Steam to play it on my laptop. It's extremely fun for all ages. I'm in my early twenties and I find this game to be very enjoyable, and I think this would be fun for children and also adults older than me as well. If you love SpongeBob, you'll love this game. Please consider playing it, you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: This whole game felt like a victory lap for Battle of Bikini Bottom Remastered (which isn't the best thing to say tbh). The voice acting is good, and I appreciate there's at least video one cutscene per level, with gross-out freeze-frames being a thing while talking to key characters as well. At the beginning I wasn't terribly into the movement/platforming but later on with new skills unlocked the movement is fluid and the game scaffolds these skills nicely. The writing felt like a genuine "SpongeBob special" style episode, although there were definitely some gaps/parts near the end narratively that felt rushed. The final bossfight is also way easier than even some prior bossfights and overall just felt tacked on. The unnecessarily lame depiction of a Romani woman as a "villainous Gyp$y mermaid" caricature being the antagonist, and although the narrative/platforming had its moments didn't feel all that special and pretty run of the mill for a SpongeBob game (They seemed to play it safe a majority of the time, and geniune innovative "areas/levels" were usually only used in brief periods which was a bummer.) brings this to a strong 3/5 (in the context of spongebob games) or light 4/5 (in the context of contemporary platformers). I'd only pick this up if you finished Battle for Bikini Bottom Remastered and wanted an original story within the remastered style. Otherwise just play Battle for Bikini Bottom which had better execution, because this game won't wow you otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: not bad platforming, good new mechanics (including the sonic's homing attack reference), interesting visuals, weird boss fights (most of them aren't even "boss fights") and a strange good timing to make a story about multiverse (since kamp koral and patrick show are canonically seperated dimensions according to the tidal zone).either way it's still the closest thing we get to a spiritual sequel to battle for bikini bottom. and it also feels like psychonauts 2 with spongebob in it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: i enjoyed multiple things about this game however i will say that the best thing this game has going for it is the graphics. the story is entertaining enough but it doesn't feel as captivating or rich as it could be. also like previous games in this developer's franchise, most of the gameplay does not feel modernized; i feel like the complexity and variety of tasks i'm completing feel just as linear and one-dimensional as they always have been. although this may be intentional so they can continue to cater to younger audiences, i still feel with how many spongebob titles they've released, they should at least be trying to introduce more newer mechanics rather than reusing the same ones in different ways, I just personally feel that the least they could do is put more effort into expanding this franchise beyond the visual elements and use newer mechanics to expand gameplay dynamics. i plan to 100% this game eventually, but afterwards, i cant see myself coming back to it. i will be looking forward to more titles from Purple Lamp & THQ Nordic in the future. (:
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very very charming and is pure eye candy the whole way through, you can tell there was a lot of passion put into this game and it isn't just a cash grab. Though its a more linear experience than Battle for Bikini Bottom, I still think its worth its 1 playthrough and achievement hunting, I can see myself coming back to this in 10 years for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes several improvements above Battle for Bikini Bottom: Rehydrated, the combat has several new moves that are fun to play around with, the boss fights can be difficult from time to time, and the challenges add more fun content to complete. My only complain about this game is the length, I was able to complete all challenges and collect all outfits in less than 15 hours. I wish this game was longer so that I am able to play it more, a good problem to have.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: A very good, if occasionally slow spiritual sequel to Battle for Bikini Bottom - platforming is decent enough, though some of the abilities could be used more often in levels rather than for simple backtracking of collectibles. Would have been nice to have a final challenge or level that uses everything in your moveset at once, or to get all the powers earlier on. Then again, it's a childrens game from a childrens show so there isn't really much to expect. Charming to the gills.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: although this game might not be as good as battle for bikini bottom, it tries really hard, and gets very close. i appreciate the effort put into this, even thought it might be a cash grab after the popularity of BFBB rehydrated. gameplay was similar to BFBB, but unique enough to stand out. the collectibles were a nice touch but one or two types would have been enough. the final boss was a bit underwhelming but overall a fun experience
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: "SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake" is an absolute delight for fans of the iconic yellow sponge and anyone who loves a fun-filled gaming adventure! From the moment you dive into Bikini Bottom, the game immerses you in a vibrant world filled with humor, charm, and nostalgic references that capture the essence of the beloved TV show.One of the standout features of "The Cosmic Shake" is its engaging storyline. The plot takes you on an intergalactic journey alongside SpongeBob and his friends, exploring diverse and quirky environments while encountering familiar faces and new characters. The game's narrative is witty and engaging, perfectly mirroring the show's signature humor.Gameplay-wise, "The Cosmic Shake" offers a variety of entertaining challenges and activities. Whether it's navigating through imaginative levels, solving puzzles, or engaging in hilarious shenanigans, there's never a dull moment. The controls are intuitive, making it accessible for players of all ages and skill levels.Visually, the game is a treat. The colorful graphics are beautifully designed, staying true to the whimsical art style of the SpongeBob universe. Each location is intricately crafted, capturing the essence of the show's distinct charm and bringing it to life in a way that feels fresh and captivating.Furthermore, the game's soundtrack deserves applause. The catchy tunes and sound effects add an extra layer of enjoyment, perfectly complementing the gameplay and enhancing the overall experience.What truly makes "The Cosmic Shake" shine is its ability to evoke a sense of joy and nostalgia. It's a fantastic homage to the SpongeBob series, incorporating elements that will resonate with long-time fans while also welcoming newcomers into its imaginative world.Overall, "SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake" is a delightful gaming experience that successfully captures the essence of the beloved show. With its engaging storyline, entertaining gameplay, charming visuals, and nostalgic appeal, it's a game that brings smiles and laughter, making it a must-play for fans of all ages.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake, is one of the most entertaining and fun games i have played in YEARS! First off, who doesn't liek spongebob and his sidekick patrick?!?!?! The levels become increasingly "difficult" and challenging as you go. The story is fun and VERY funny. I don't want to ruin it, but i highly recommend it for any fans of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect sequel to the classic 3D Spongebob platformers. Single Player only, but provides you with the most attention to detail that most modern-day titles would highly benefit from. With the incredible references, accurate voice acting, beautiful art style, and addicting gameplay, you will not regret your experience playing this game. If you enjoyed Battle For Bikini Bottom (which you're already wrong if you didn't) and actually had a decent childhood, this game is a MUST PURCHASE! And for only $40, that's an absolute steal, especially with today's gaming market. Do yourself a favor, and play it.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game quite refreshing.I had played and 100% completed the original Battle for Bikini Bottom, Rehydrated, and the Movie Game. I had little hope for this game after seeing what happened with BFBB Rehydrated, but I believed the game was still worth a shot, so I got it.First impressions were great! The graphics are super clean, and still capture that BFBB vibe. I enjoyed the plot of the game and thought it was a clever twist.I was expecting lots of glitches and bugs from how games have been now-a-days, but was relieved when continuing into the game with no issues.Playing the game was super fun and refreshing. I was always looking forward to getting to the next time zone, the next objective, and the next collectible to get.I am glad to have played this game, and will likely play it again after some time as it does lack in replayability. The music was great, the voice acting sounds good and was funny, and I overall enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend, but not at full price. _childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for kids and Spongebob fans. However, it does feel like a step back from Battle for Bikini Bottom. Putting nostalgia aside, BFBB has a little more depth than this one, with multiple missions & really cool environments. Cosmic Blast does have the environments down pat, but every level is very linear. BFBB was somewhat like that but had levels that broke from the norm, so it doesn't feel repetitive. There's some collectibles in Cosmic Blast but they feel like an after thought. I overall enjoyed my time with Cosmic Blast as a small distraction and recommend it on sale, but don't expect BFBB 2.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Decent enough for a child's first 3D platformer, but otherwise an unfinished, unpolished UE5 cash grab most likely crammed out the door after the relative success of the Battle for Bikini Bottom remaster, which I enjoyed! But the sequel's bugginess, enemy repeating, and totally uninspired platforming mechanics just serve to make the eyes glaze over.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of spongebob for a long time, and I can't begin to explain my excitement going into The Cosmic Shake.Unfortunately my excitement was short lived.For a long time fan this can be a very fun Easter egg hunt throughout the entirety of the game, but if you're looking for something with the same challenge, difficulty, and playability as prior spongebob games, I would look elsewhere...Let's start with the Pros, because not everything about this gane is bad!Pros:-Beautiful cutting edge graphics-smooth gameplay-pretty decent story-a finite amount of Easter eggs and references that any fan will enjoy spotting-costumes are a big highlight for spongebob, the amount you can unlock is amazing.-voice acting is spot on for 90% of the characters.-funny dialogue that'll make you chuckle as you play-fun moves and abilities that make the game unique compared to other spongebob games-fun little side quests to obtain collectibles.Cons:-The game battle locks you in zones to defeat enemies that really aren't all that difficult and honestly just feels like a poor excuse to extend an otherwise fairly short game. -Great ideas, Awful execution.Ex. In the first world you have the opportunity to play as everyone's favorite seahorse, Mystery, unfortunately you only get to play her a handful of times throughout the story, and you can only move left and right with a Dash attack while the game moves you forward, taking away the freedom of this open world and ultimately the fun out of such a wonderful idea.-Not very useful abilities. The enemies are slow enough 90% of the time that you won't ever need to really use any of the bonus abilities given to you, in small doses will you ever really need to use them.-They say all original voice actors but the News Ancor Fish sounds digitized. Also spongebob audio quality is fair at best, it doesn't sound quite like Tom Kenny even though it is.-the side quests are hard to find, which could be seen as a pro for added difficulty, but in this case for something that is a "side quest" they aren't exactly something I would go put of my way to not only find, but complete, unless your a completionist.-No difficulty setting. The game is way too easy and a bit dull overall when it comes to game play. Like I mentioned before great ideas, poor execution.You can really tell this was targeted towards a younger audience which there's nothing wrong with that, but long time fans (such as myself) feel like an afterthought.-you're stuck as playing only spongebob unlike prior games.-the main villain is not all that menacing and quite frankly she's boring.Not worth the full price I paid in my personal opinion.it's worth the play through, but I would never personally recommend this to someone unless I knew they had kids who enjoyed spongebob.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the Cosmic Shake is an alright game. It's mostly fun, and if you're a big fan of Spongebob there's enough here to like. What starts out as a relatively decent story, ends up being a little bland and short. It's still fun but they definitely missed a few beats. The art style is awesome (IMO) and vibrant, may not be everyone's cup of tea but I thought it was a big highlight of the game.The gameplay while short gets repetitive and can be frustrating at times, not hard, but some of those moments where you thought you made the simple jump but didn't. These moments only pop up every so often but they're enough to be a tad bit annoying. It's also just too short and not varied enough from Battle for Bikini Bottom. There are a few new elements but nothing majorly noteworthy which is disappointing. There also feels to be a "tighter" world, it just feels very cramped and not open enough for my liking. I don't need anything massive, but it feels like a supremely disjointed and tightly compact Bikini Bottom, unlike the show.Voice acting is solid, it seems like they got a good amount of the actors from the show in here which I always personally love. It's not a bad game, it just isn't too great either. If you're a fan of Spongebob and you liked Battle for Bikini bottom, you'll probably enjoy this as well, but maybe keep the expectations a bit lower as it definitely doesn't live up to it's predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: A follow-up to the Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated from the same dev team. Compared to that game, graphics and art style are much more animated and lively, as here the team were not constrained by the rules or design choices of any previous game which they had to be faithful to. In addition, it feels like a collection of different memorable moments of the TV show, recreated in 3D with certain variations, blended together and spread across 7 zones/levels. which is great if you're a fan of the show. The story is quite simple and only serves as a way to explain different multiversal zones of the game. In gameplay, it fundamentally follows Battle for Bikini Bottom, but only uses 1 character for the whole game, even though you still basically get most of the abilities of other characters as the game goes on and much more, especially in combat. Combat feels great and fluid, compared to Battle, but hitboxes and some i-frames are quite confusing at times, especially with certain big enemies and bosses mid-game. Overall, the game is also quite linear in its direction, but you can still go around and collect additional stuff, which unlocks new costumes, and it's easy to get around and not get bored, because the idea for each level and gimmicks change somewhat quite often. In conclusion, a solid 3D platformer with a lot of good moments and some bad moments, which lasts for about 6 hours of mostly fun nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Actual Good game, a great follow up after playing battle for bikini bottom. Its a bit weird at first coming from Battle for bikini bottom. _childDocuments_.review: I have completed the game 100% and gotten all achievements for this game just to write a review for it.Cosmic shake, made by the same devs as the BFBB Rehydrated, feels very similar to other spongebob game. This is not a bad thing, as it feels very nice. There are some new things added to this game though, like the pizza glide (more on that in a second) that make the game different enough to still need to learn things. The levels are well themed and nothing in them seems out of place for what they are trying to do, each being a reference to a spongebob episode (as far as I can tell). The art styles all mesh very well and have that cartoon feel to them.The downsides are the Pizza glide, limited voice acting, and the ENDLESS invisible walls. The Pizza glide, though helpful, needed to be tweaked more. It activates if you hold the jump button, which goes against most platforming instincts. If this could be the "3rd jump" like most game do I would let it slide; but is isn't. The voice acting over all is very nice; but the constant repeating of the same phrases gets aggravating and had me taking off my headphones just to not hear them again. Every level has invisible walls or instant deaths that make no sense, like an invisible wall on top of a wall that has something next to it that (in other games) would help you jump it. If they did not want us jumping over things or gliding past portions of levels, they should have closed them off. Overall I am happy that I played the game and own it as part of my spongebob collection; but it has flaws that could have been prevented in the development fairly easily.4 potatoes

_childDocuments_.review: 🌟 Pros:• Beautiful graphics that make the game visually appealing.• The addition of Patrick as a companion adds a pleasant feel to the gameplay.• The story becomes more engaging and entertaining after the second teleporter.• The game captures the authentic SpongeBob feel, especially during the "Karate Master" segment.• There are great tidbits of humor that can genuinely make you laugh.• The unexpected close-up pictures during dialogues add a classic SpongeBob touch.🌟 Cons:• Accidentally skipping cutscenes or dialogues is way too easy and becomes inconvenient and annoying.• The game feels boring and less developed before the second teleporter.• The story and dialogue in the first part of the game could be improved and feel somewhat unfinished.• I encountered a game-breaking glitch during the Stone Age Pearl fight where you save Squidward. I somehow died taking out the last leg of Pearl's platform, which soft-locked me. When I restarted the game, I had to redo the entire dimension.• The price🌟 Overall Review:The Cosmic Shake is a visually stunning platform game that captures the essence of the beloved Nickelodeon series. While the game has some advantages, such as beautiful graphics and the addition of Patrick as a companion, it also has some disadvantages. Accidentally skipping cutscenes and dialogues can be frustrating, and the initial gameplay feels lackluster. However, the story and entertainment value pick up significantly after the second teleporter, with authentic SpongeBob moments and humor that can genuinely make you laugh. Despite some shortcomings, The Cosmic Shake delivers a fun and enjoyable experience for fans of the series.💭💦 SpongeBob would be proud of this game, but maybe it needs a little more jellyfish jelly to perfect its formula! Give it a go and dive into the zany world of Bikini Bottom. Who knows, you might just find yourself giggling like SpongeBob himself! 😄🌊

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very passionate about the heavy iron spongebob games. Battle for bikini bottom and the movie game. The cosmic shake is a good game but I'd rank it third best in the spongebob game realm. Battle for bikini bottom best, movie game 2nd best and cosmic shake 3rd best. Don't get me wrong the cosmic shake is a good solid game but it's not great like the heavy iron games. The cosmic shake is too damn short and once you're done with it there's no much more to do besides collect coins to unlock purely cosmetic outfits. I also think it would have been cool if there were more side missions based around doing stuff other than getting coins. Also in battle for bikini bottom you could go into characters houses. I mean it was somewhat limited but at least you could do it. In cosmic shake you can't go into any buildings really. The platforming in this game is top notch and very addictive but again I felt like this game could have added more power ups like the ones you get in the movie game.Despite saying all of this I still enjoyed the game a lot and it certainly reminded me of the 6th gen era of platformers. I still think its a solid game but battle for bikini bottom will always be the magnum opus of spongebob games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a huge improvement to Battle for Bikini Bottom in nearly every way, especially in its art style, expressive animation, music and sound, graphics, world design, tons of nods to the show (especially in all the variety of costumes you can wear - and there are a LOT of fun costumes, some that even I didn't see coming) and tons of variety in Spongebob's move-set. I actually don't mind not being able to play as other characters because Spongebob himself is just so much fun to control. I find myself trying to skip sections of the level combining Spongebob's moves and the fact that I can pull that off in certain areas only proves there's so much freedom in how you can combine his different moves to either go faster or reach farther distances. It's not Mario levels of variety by any means, but you can still pull off some different stuff. The game doesn't directly tell you any of this either, so there's a lot for the player to figure out just by getting the hang of the moves. That being said, as much as I love the improved move-set to the game, there just isn't a whole lot of platforming sections where these different moves can be utilized to their fullest potential. There's a handful of these like in the end of the Karate Downtown level, or some of the scattered time challenges, but the levels itself focus purely on open spaces getting from point A to point B and lots of stops for combat. The combat is quite fun, especially after unlocking the Karate Kick, but there's this one particular enemy you see a lot that really takes the pacing to a screeching halt because you spend a good chunk of time waiting for a weakness to open up before hitting him, like a mini-boss, but you see too much of him to my liking. As far as the lack of platforming is concerned, a simple fix for this would be to include DLC Challenge Levels that are more intense and platform-focused, where the move-set is fully utilized. Offer it as DLC so players who want more a challenge have that option, verses kids who came here from the show or more casual players that just want an easier time.And I think this is where the majority of the game's complaints comes from: that it's too short or too linear. BFBB was linear in its levels, too, but because they were less story focused and you could mostly tackle those levels in any order, plus they always naturally cycled back to the start at the end, those levels felt like they were more open when technically speaking, this game has much bigger, more open levels. But you can only tackle them in one order and because this game is so story driven (not saying that in itself is a bad thing) there really is only one focused objective per level, so the way this in itself is presented is most likely why people say it's "more linear" when it really isn't.Overall this game is a really solid experience. It's like a Spongebob episode pulled directly from the TV show. The moves are fun, the presentation is top notch, (much better than BFBB Rehydrated's presentation) and it grabs your attention long enough for its entire 10-hour runtime. Try out the game if you're a Spongebob fan, it doesn't take much of your time and it's an extremely fun experience from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I might just be nostalgia tripping, it felt like Battle for Bikini Bottom played better, while this one was a better crafted experience.Gameplaywise, they removed a lot of player agency, Spongebob only has 4 moves in this game (2 of them variants of a ground pound, and 1 is a parachuting mechanic, so really it's 2 attacks) versus the 5 in BFBB that don't rely on objects placed within the map outside of the player. While the levels were crafted in a fun way, it still definitely feels like a step down from its predecessor, but I guess lowering player agency scales with how much life they can give to the world.And the show references were definitely on point, it seemed like there was always a reference I was noticing between the environment art, the voice lines, and the skins. Was very impressed the amount of care that obviously went into this game, despite having grown up and becoming the jaded cynic that I am. A fun buy for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to its predecessor. While not as good as the original, it comes pretty close. (Gotta admit though, that nostalgia might influence me.)Pros:+ Gameplay: typical Spongebob Jump'n'Run Gameplay+ Good soundtrack: not reinventing the wheel but way better than expected+/- Story: well there is one. But neither does it really matter, nor do these games need one. Spongebob opend up different alternate realities, you gotta fix it. That's it.+ Voice acting: original (german) voice actors, who do a great job. Only downside: some lines get repetetive quickly+ Many funny costumes with nice references to older episodes+ Difficulty is quite easy/ achievements are fair (got 100% in around 12 hours)+ Many easter eggs/references to the show in general It's a freakin gold mine with pretty much every major meme. The studio knew what it was doing+ Every level offers up something different gameplay/world wise. While sticking to BFBB strengths, this game tries new things.+/- Humor is a hit and miss. Many parts feel like the good old first few seasons, some jokes on the other hand remind you of the current mess. It's a question of personal taste, though.Cons:- Small amount of enemy types, who are very generic- The boss battles, while not bad, can't keep up with BFBB at all- You only play as Spongebob himself. I'd love to play as Patrick and Sandy again :(- Bugs do appear quite often- rather short (12 hours to complete)If you love Spongebob and BFBB, this is a must. If not, it's still a fun enjoyable platformer reminiscent of the early 2000s Jump'n'Run era.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays as much more of a kid's game than the older ones - easier (and not just because I'm older now), more linear... For example, the tongue slide sequences are usually just following the single path down, with very little to no jumping onto alternate paths / finding secrets / etc. Answers to "puzzles" are often right there next to the puzzle. You have to complete the main quests in levels before being able to go back for side quests.I have a lot of nostalgia for SpongeBob, so I'm still enjoying this game. There are a lot of references / jokes / memes. Overall it's a decent game... just doesn't quite hit like BFBB or the movie game in terms of design, complexity, and challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER FREE REVIEW:As someone who grew up with Spongebob Battle for Bikini Bottom, this is the sequel we needed. Other than minor complaints, I really can't fault this game for anything. It's obvious the people who worked on this either A.) Included fans of the original B.) included members of what was once Heavy Iron Studios.The biggest critique I have of this game is that the soundtrack is definitely missing the iconic touch of the soundtrack BfBB had. They play it disappointingly safe with the OST for this one and mostly just include music from the shower and rather generic thematically-appropriate music. I did enjoy the occasional inclusion of sea shanties though.My other complaint is they are sometimes those detailed cutaway shots the later seasons of the show uses. I won't fault it too much since it never gets as graphic or gross as some of the more infamous examples, but I thought it's something I should point out in case that's a deciding factor in the buy for somebody.Outside of that though, the writing has all the heart and charm of BfBB and there's jokes that both younger and older fans will probably enjoy. So if you're a pessimistic 20-something like I am, you'll still find some of the comedy genuinely charming. The gameplay is smooth as ever and really recaptures the magic of BfBB's combat system. The enemies here, too, each focus on a sort of "gimmick", with the way encounters combine enemy types making for interesting and fun gameplay.I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob Squarepants The Cosmic Shake is a good game, however it totally doesn't worth 40 bucks due to its length. It took me 7,5 hours to complete the game and 13 to 100% it (all achievements) and it could take less if I had taken some kill related achievements on my first playthrough.Pros:-Amazing art style and graphics-Outstanding environment design-Great level design-Fun story-Good boss design-Spongebob's Series references-Great music-Cool skins-Satisfying sound design-Funny dialoguesIn between/Tolerable things:-Enemy design isn't terrible but not good either-New mechanics are okay but they are just copies from Spyro and Crash gamesCons:-Like I already mentioned, the game is too short even if you go for 100%-Ridiculous price-No replay value-You only control Spongebob-The game is full of bugs, they are not game breaking, but it can get tedious if you want to 100% -Karate kick doesn't register every time -I think there are missing sound effects at some parts (when you ride a rock for example)-Riding control is terribleAll in all the game is good, it has its problems but most of them aren't that important and can get fixed with some updates.Battle for bikini bottom is still a better game.Overall: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The design and looks are as good as it could ever get for a spongebob game.But the gameplay is as soul-less as it can get. You took many of the great ideas from Battle for Bikini Bottom, and threw them together in one character. Then made the gameplay cycle incredibly same and repetitive. Each level was beatiful and well designed and unique making the platforming aspect exciting and exploring fun. Then you make every bit of combat and fetch questing the same thing every stage. Unlike bbbr there is no attempt for weird zany more difficult levels like the dream worlds. The game is very oddly disconnected from the show overall with rare aspects to remind you this wasnt a cookie cutter drop in theme.If you enjoy Battle for Bikini Bottom, you will enjoy the Lite and not as fun version that is this game.btw  100% is broken very easily and bricks your ability to achieve it easily in saves. Achievo hunters beware

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I really enjoyed this game. Aside from achievements, I've finished the game 100%. It's very short/easy and I don't necessarily care to go play it again. Now that that's out of the way, I'm going to compare to BFBB.*TLDR: TCS is a good spongebob game but it's missing the charm BFBB had. It's a few steps down from BFBB in terms of story/gameplay/exploration/collecting, but they did a pretty good job. It's short, easy, and you do get mostly handheld through the game but it is still a fun one. For $40, I got my enjoyment out of it but have zero desire to replay it whereas I've replayed BFBB probably 5-6 times and now have an itch to go back and play it again. Overall I give TCS an 8/10 compared to BFBB at 10/10.*Collectibles:BFBB - The Golden Spatula system was fantastic (along with Patrick's socks). Some were hard, some were easy, some were part of the story, and some were secret. The socks from BFBB basically feel like the gold tokens in TCS as far as collectibles go.TCS - You collect gold tokens/coins on each map but they don't really equate to what golden spatulas were in BFBB. When you find one, it's more like finding a sock from BFBB. Not very difficult and certainly not very rewarding.*Story:BFBB - Great story. Detailed. Drawn out. Not rushed.TCS - Good story. Unique. Short & seemed slightly rushed.*Maps/levelsBFBB - We had a ton of variety and in most cases if you could see it, you could explore it. Tons of locations.TCS - Fun maps, but not enough of them. Also missing small details that made BFBB killer. An example of details in direct comparison are the sand slides and vine slide from BFBB. There were shortcuts, races, cool spatula challenges, etc. In TCS you get huge, easy slides that if you're lucky have 1 shortcut/branch to the slide that really isn't anything special. How about a boulder busting a hole in a mountain and we get to slide through a cave? I just miss these little details they added to BFBB throughout the maps.*Graphics:BFBB - Rehydrated was killer.TCS - Even Better.*AbilitiesBFBB - The abilities in BFBB were fairly simple but to me were more challenging to use. That made them a bit more fun IMO.TCS - New abilities but they really hold your hand in this game. Everything has a lock-on and requires zero skill to use.*CombatBFBB & TCS - Pretty much the same combat minus different enemies and aimbot jump kicks. Really cheesy dodge roll mechanic basically ripped from dark souls that lets you avoid damage in about any situation including boss fights.*BossesBFBB - Very unique and had some really well designed fights. Of course my favorite is robot spongebob. Completely unique and fun.TCS - INSANELY EASY boss fights in this one. Most battles were basically the same thing and didn't feel too unique. As I write this, I'm trying to remember the bosses as well as I remember BFBB bosses and they just aren't memorable. The final boss is a total scam of satisfaction or difficulty*Game TimeBFBB - Depending on how you play, BFBB can take much longer than TCS to complete if you want 100% completion with no youtube to aid you. This makes for a more fulfilling experience.TCS - With 100% completion done in 7 hours, this game was just too quick and I did it in 1 day. BFBB took me about a month when I first played it on ps2 with zero outside help. This one just felt a bit rushed.I truly believe had they added more regions/maps and a collectible system like the golden spatulas, this game would have been a 10/10. They needed to charge $60 and put another year of content development into it to butter my bread.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Battle for Bikini Bottom that finally gives us a great Spongebob game after so long (not including the Rehydrated which was awesome). This time around you only play as Spongebob but he seems to have several of the abilities that the others had in the last game. You get even more abilities as the game goes on, including a overpowered jump kick ability that trivializes nearly every fight after you get it. I think only 2 enemies are immune to it but it allows you to clear arenas in a flash. The Boss battles this time around are pretty good but nothing too difficult. The story is essentially a long episode of the show with a good amount of fan service if you know what you're looking at. Half the fun will be just going from stage to stage just to see it all. While I still hold BFBB higher this game still does a damn good job and I'm excited for the series gaming future for the first time in years. For me it was worth the full $40!
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels very similar to SpongeBob Battle for Bikini Bottom, but with an extra layer of polish. The levels are well designed and the soundtrack is top notch. The game also features a great selection of old SpongeBob episodes, which I found to be quite nostalgic.As a whole, I would give SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake a solid 10/10. It's a great game which captures the spirit of the classic SpongeBob series. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fun platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, solid 3D platformer that plays better than Rehydrated. Lots to collect and a couple post-game missions to do while collecting/backtracking for things you might have missed. The dialogue even changes when re-entering worlds post-game so that was neat. I did miss having golden spatulas rewarded to you as you progress but it's pretty much the same thing here without "you've earned a golden spatula!" I do wish the final boss was better. Pretty underwhelming since it wasn't anything special. Just an arena where you hit the boss a few times while dodging projectiles. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: After having played this game from start to finish, I can safely say that yes, the spunch has taken another W.+ The presentation is phenomenal, the graphics and animations are just wonderful+ It controls really well for the most part+ The abilities are nice and diverse+ A lot of love was clearly put in by true fans of Spongebob, feels satisfying as a fan myself+ The VAs all do a great job+ I wish Kassandra would sit on me+ Nice amount of collectables to find+ Great spins on old BfBB locations+ Most of the bosses are fun, each with their own unique and fun gimmick, which is nice- The health bar enemies are pretty tedious to deal with, especially the ones that either can't be hit or avoid you until they attack- The turning on the surfboard is a bit too sensitive for my taste- Frame drops!! Again. (probably my computer's fault anyway)- The final boss is kinda underwhelming. Not nearly as much spectacle or complexity as previous final bosses (ie: BfBB and Movie) ("That's it?")Is it as good as BfBB? I don't think so. But wow is it close, which is impressive for the first entirely original Spongebob game in a while.I recommend! (I'd say get it when it goes on sale, but I'd say that about any paid game)

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob Cosmis Shake is the spiritual successor to the beloved Battle for Bikini Bottom RehydratedPlaying as our absorbent sponge and balloon sidekick Patrick, it was a great twist on the creativity of the new worlds, the sliding levels could be changed a bit but overall it was a fun experience. Finding all the different easter eggs and references to Spongebob's new and gold ages was a treat to see. All the original voice actors reprise their roles and the costume pack DLC just made everything a lot better along with the new kinds of skills, my favorite being the karate kick and the pizza glider. I haven't encountered many problems with the mechanics such as the losing achievements or doubloons, wish there was a cutscene compilation on the main menu tho. Overall recommend it for the purpose of nostalgia, especially with the last world.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun levels, cute dialogue, lots of collectibles! I think we can all agree that the mermaid was a good addition to the game.However, I do find the boss battles to be a bit lacking compared to other spongebob games. I do like the concepts employed IN the boss battles, but felt the execution was a bit underwhelming, especially at the end. _childDocuments_.review: Rating Overall 7.5/10.0 // Booting up this game for the first time I greatly enjoyed the graphical quality and the game keeps that same standard all the way through. The dialogue was okay there were some clever zings and humorous dialogue. Game play feels as a spiritual successor to SBSP: BFBB though it contains a sort of flavor reminiscent of SBSP: CFTKK and not in the best light. Levels have a VERY fast pace to them as I could burn through them at a relatively fast pace. Level design is convoluted in places that don't always need to be and at times found myself lost in areas that felt relatively pointless.The enemies you face are very hollow and simple to defeat with a little basic dodging and the karate kick is a genuine hack against opposition. The overall enemies are gelatinous mongoloids of varying style and combat prowess though I found it very charming to see the jellyfish and cannonball puffer fish made a comeback from the early 2000's release. The cut scenes are amazing and well done, with quality dialogue between.Not a bad purchase by any means and you will enjoy this game, but having endulged in many of the prior titles released under the SBSS label, this has ALOT of minor elements featured from almost all of them in some way. I'm more than happy with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a comment stating that this game is a remix of BFBB. This is very true. Feels like BFBB with a different story. The gameplay is fun, though relatively easy. The dialogues are funny, graphics look neat and the soundtrack is alright. All in all it is a good game but just not as good as BFBB. I would recommend the game to everyone who likes SpongeBob and/or liked BFBB.But I have to criticize the game a bit.- In my opinion, the game feels a bit like it was rushed. The introduction to the story is relatively short and not really intersting.- I have encountered a few minor bugs like NPCs stuck at invisible walls or music disappearing after tabbing out and back in again.- When enemies are relatively far away, their animation framerate is lowered which looks a bit unnatural, especially since for other NPCs this does not seem to happen.- At some times, the gameplay is very slow. If you really want to see all corners of a place, destroy all tikis etc, you will have to spend a lot of time just running around. Bikini Bottom is especially large and there is a lot of empty space to just walk through and do nothing really.- The dialogues are very long sometimes. Also, I get the feeling that there is more dialogue than in BFBB but not really more information packed into it. Just more... jokes?- The combat system is a bit frustrating at times, as there are actions you can only do when looking more or less directly at an enemy. In fights with many enemies, this might have you hit the "wrong" enemy. Also, you will have to turn your camera a lot when there are enemies all around you because you cannot do any special attacks to enemies behind you.But other than that, the game turns out to be really enjoyable. I also like that there are some classic memes built into the game and some easter eggs that refer to BFBB.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but I feel like there could have been improvements, as it also feels incredibly easy. There's no option to change your analog sensitivity, and Balloon Patrick makes the game much easier if you ever, for some reason, drop down to one pair of underwear, as he gives you an extra. Spongebob, while fitting, is also too chatty when you collect the bubbles in the game, and I wish I could make him say those lines less frequently. But, besides the minor flaws, it's a pretty good game.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly average, if linear, 3D platformer. It isn't really a collect-a-thon, having more of a straight forward "get to the goal" level design (think more in the vein of a Spark the Electric Jester 2/3 or a 3D Sonic game over something like Mario 64, A Hat in Time, or Battle for Bikini Bottom). Sure there are things to collect, but they aren't really necessary or of consequence. Everything you collect with the exception of two health upgrades is purely for cosmetic (costume) or achievement reasons. You could walk past every collectable and not miss out on anything at all. You don't get to skip levels or go out of order if you get a bunch of side objectives and hidden collectables, you go firmly on the path the game sets for you. This is fine by itself but if you, like a lot of people, were hoping that it will be BfBB 2 or fill that nostalgia for it you may be slightly be disappointed. If you are fine with it not being BfBB it is a perfectly serviceable game on its own merits.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying what I've played so far, though I have to admit that I wouldn't consider this to be a true "successor" to BFBB, but rather, something to check out if you're a fan of simple platformers or just can't get enough of your favorite talking Sponge. The big takeaway here is that this game is linear, meaning there isn't much in the way of exploration; you go from one point to another, completing various tasks until you're told to move on. That itself isn't bad, though it *is* different from what you'll be used to if you're coming from BFBB.Pros:-Fantastic animations-Improved artstyle over BFBB-New ways to move (glide, roll dodge)-Frequent character interactions wreak of personality and charm-Great voice work as alwaysCons:-No graphics options-Linear (not necessarily an issue, but it may put off those who enjoyed BFBB's gameplay style)I really can't get over how well the cutscenes are animated, and seeing that cinematic camera angle when talking to NPCs is jarring (yet fully welcome) for a Spongebob game. The art team has really perfected their craft, as I felt that BFBB: Rehydrated's art direction was far too saturated just for the sake of standing out from the original BFBB's art style.It also doesn't have a lot in the way of graphics options for PC, which is a bit of a disappointment (it runs great on my Steam Deck @ 720p, but falls under 60fps @ 1080p).Again, I'd recommend this if you like simple linear platformers, but if you're looking for a real challenge, or a collect-a-thon like BFBB, this one might be too simple for you.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as BFBB, but I didn't expect it to be. It's more comparable to games like SBSP: Movie game or Creature from the Krusty Krab. Puzzles and level designs are simplified to the point where messing up is just a mere inconvenience. It's *kinda* open world but levels unlock linearly and it's less focused on being a collect-athon like BFBB. Instead you collect things for separate side quests that NPCs will give you. They do take a lot of assets from previous games so you'll feel right at home, but the game does lack polish in some places. For example, golden spatulas are in this game, BUT I have NO IDEA what they're for... That's kind of a big problem don't you think.?With all of the being said, there's almost NO REASON to collect anything. And I do mean anything.. Gold coins will eventually unlock different skins for Spongebob which can be purchased using jelly. (Jelly is equivalent to the shiny things in BFBB) That's basically it..If I were to rank it I'd put this game just above the Movie game and below Creature from the Krusty Krab.The biggest thing I miss from the older games is the writing style and the old type of humor it had. It's NEW Spongebob humor/writing, so don't expect it to feel like BFBB, otherwise you'll be severely disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, I don’t know if it is better than SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom – Rehydrated but it is definitely worth the money is you like SpongeBob. The platforming is great and the combat isn’t too bad (there are quite a few different enemies) except for one enemy which you can only hit after it does it’s attack. I thought that the boss fights were good too, not hard though (the whole game is easy but that is to be expected from a SpongeBob game).I really like the levels, the locations are interesting and they all introduce a new enemy and/or movement mechanic. There are also quite a couple different “game modes” so it isn’t always normal platforming.Graphically I think it is better than BfBB – Rehydrated but there are no graphics settings except for resolution and ultrawide doesn’t work properly (it cuts parts of the screen off to make it fit on an ultrawide screen so you lose part of the image as opposed to getting more). Another thing that annoyed me a bit is that the animations of enemies that are more than 20 meters away from you are very low fps, it is especially noticeable with the bathtub guys. It ran great though, I never had a stutter or fps drop.The last thing that I think they should implement in the settings besides graphical options is a sensitivity slider, the default sensitivity is quite slow and when you want to look around it feels sluggish.Besides that it is a good game that plays similar to BfBB – Rehydrated but more linear so if you liked that game, you will definitely like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Our review of this game will contain no spoilers. I’ll cover a brief synopsis of the characters and plot presented in the first half hour of the game and any screenshots shown herein will be spoiler-free.Spongebob is a cartoon that has lasted over a generation. When I watched the original episodes that aired back in 1999 I was a child, but now I’m well into my 30’s and I could show modern episodes of Spongebob to my kids. You’ll be happy to know that The Cosmic Shake would be a great game for audiences of all ages. It’s a very light-hearted and colorful platformer that never gets too difficult and has all the great mainstays of Spongebob, from its silly characters to the countless memes that have been created over the years.There have been many Spongebob games released, from Revenge of the Flying Dutchman that released in 2002 (which my first Spongebob game) as well as Battle for Bikini Bottom in 2003 and the Spongebob Squarepants Movie (the game) released in 2004 just to name a few. The Cosmic Shake is more of a successor to Battle for Bikini Bottom speaking strictly in terms of the gameplay – it’s a platformer in the same vein but it also improves upon Battle for Bikini Bottom’s original formula with different abilities and many modern quality of life improvements.The Cosmic Shake has a completely original storyline and you don’t need to have played any of the Spongebob games or have even watched the show to understand the plot, but I guarantee that you’d definitely will find the game much funnier if you catch the references.The premise of the plot is that Spongebob and Patrick meet a travelling saleswoman named Madame Kassandra who sells them a mysterious jar of gooey fluid. Spongebob uses this liquid to blow bubbles, but it somehow ends up covering the entire town with goo and also creates alternate dimensions that trap his friends, as well as turn Patrick into a bubble.It’s up to the duo to explore these realms and save their friends. The story is quite basic but very child-friendly and the game has plenty of funny dialogue from classic Spongebob characters, such as Mr. Krabs being cheap, Squidward wanting peace and quiet and Plankton not putting any effort into his restaurant.The game features a hub area, Bikini Bottom, as well as seven other dimensions to explore. As you progress the story you unlock more dimensions and more areas of Bikini Bottom are unlocked for you to explore.This game is not quite a “collect-a-thon” like Battle for Bikini Bottom. Rather, this game is much more linear with a few branching paths for collectibles. You progress the story by continuing forward and you’re never blocked by gates requiring you to collect a certain number of collectibles, but you do need to complete earlier worlds to unlock later worlds. In fact, you could progress the entire story without completing any secondary missions if you wanted to. You can’t also choose to go in the levels in any order, you have to progress through them linearly in this title. Thankfully a marker shows where you need to go to progress the story if you get lost.Collectibles in this title include globs of jelly, which is used to purchase outfits for Spongebob. Spongebob is the only playable character in this game. To unlock the outfits for purchase, however, you actually need to collect doubloons, which will unlock sets of outfits for Spongebob in sets of ranks. These outfits are purely cosmetic and don’t affect the gameplay in any way, but they are a neat throwback to the show, with many funny costumes such as Spongebob’s maid outfit from the episode “Can you spare a dime?"There are other upgrades such as Spongebob’s golden underwear, found sparingly throughout the levels. Spongebob’s health meter is represented by the number of clean underwear he is wearing (how many hits he can take), and you can get more of them as health pickups. In terms of difficulty, this game is really easy, with checkpoints almost everywhere and if you fall into a pit you’ll respawn on the ledge you just came from. One great addition is that Spongebob can even grab ledges if you were about to barely miss a jump, not present in Battle for Bikini Bottom.As you progress through the story you get new abilities for Spongebob which makes the game more fun and they are very different to his abilities in Battle for Bikini Bottom. His regular moveset is very basic such as swinging his jellyfishing net to attack enemies. You will eventually unlock the ability to karate kick enemies which is basically a homing attack to close the distance between you and the enemy quickly and is extremely useful. As you progress you see a wider variety of enemy types, all themed around cosmic jelly. One annoying enemy type was the glob of enemies wearing an anchor hat that spawned other enemies because anytime you’d hit it it would stun you and I couldn’t find a workaround to avoid getting stunned. This was annoying because while being stunned I’d get attacked by other enemies. But overall the game was easy including the combat as well.Other new abilities include riding a seahorse, which can be done in the hub world to travel around quickly as well as certain story areas. The controls are not the best and it’s tricky to collect all the cosmic jelly on the seahorse, but it gets the job done and mixes up the gameplay loop. Another new ability is being able to roll on a spherical rock, which is very fun – usually you roll on the rock over a hazard such as lava, and you avoid enemies and pick up collectibles. You can also use hook swingshots and glide, making platforming easy.The worlds are also very colorful and distinct. Rather than just visiting different areas in Bikini Bottom, they’re also set in varying time periods, including a Wild West Jellyfish Fields, a karate film set version of Downtown Bikini Bottom, pirate Goo Lagoon, Rock Bottom during Halloween, a prehistoric Kelp Forest, and a medieval Sulfur Fields just to name some examples.The only other gameplay mechanic I found annoying was that if you wanted to do a lot of the secondary objectives you have to revisit the levels. There are many collectibles you can get on your first run through a level, but there are also many collectibles that require powerups from later levels to get them. The problem is that this game isn’t quite open world. After completing each world you can warp to any checkpoint in the level, but it still feels annoying having to replay a portion of the level to get to the secret areas.Battle for Bikini Bottom was slightly better in this regard because you collected spatulas in a nonlinear world and you could warp back to any spatula you wanted to if you didn’t have the correct abilities at the time. But in Cosmic Shake, you somewhat have to progress through the linear levels again a bit to get to the secondary objectives. The checkpoint warps certainly make it easier but it does feel like backtracking. It’s never mandatory to do secondary objectives though. The game took us 10 hours to complete, but if you go for more secondary objectives it’s possible to spend 15-20 hours on it.Despite just a few missteps, the game is really fun whether you’re an adult who grew up with the show or if you want to purchase it for your kids or children in your family. It’s never a tricky game and the visuals and distinct worlds look bright and amazing with today’s technology compared to older Spongebob games. I really recommend you to pick up this game and give it a shot, it’s a very fun game and it was great to immerse my self in the world of Spongebob again.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with SpongeBob and obviously the video games, so when Battle For Bikini Bottom Rehydrated came out I got excited and inevitably bought the game, but once I finished I wanted more and had to wait. 2021 rolls around and the lovely lads at THQ Nordic shot me up with nostalgia by announcing The Cosmic Shake and of course I got excited, and pre-ordered once I got the chance. The story is obviously pretty good. I don't really have a lot to say about it, it just feels like another movie or special, an extension if you will. SpongeBob and Patrick get some magic bubbles for free and start willy nilly blowing them making wishes without thinking of any repercussions. In doing this they open up THE F***ING MULTIVERSE as they also destroy Bikini Bottom and send their friends away in the process, having to go through multiple universes to save them. The gameplay is pretty good. Everything controls as smoothly as you want, combat and platforming. Combat might get a little repetitive, you do face mostly the same enemies, but at least for me it wasn't too big of an issue because the levels look really great and immerse you into the world of the show especially with spreading easter eggs around, but any who might be a concern to somebody. Also wasn't a big concern as enemies don't take much to defeat. The way levels are done might be a thing that gets people divisive as they are linear compared to BFBB, I didn't really mind, but this might be a thing to take into account. 1 more thing to add are bosses, I mean let's be clear they are pretty easy, but most of them are fun, I just felt like the last boss was too short, probably the easiest of the entire game and once you beat it, it just abruptly ends.Length of the game might also be a concern to some players, the game can be beaten in about 4 hours or so if you rush without getting any of the collectibles. I beat it in about 9 almost 10 hours, but I was also gathering other collectibles, it took me about 15 to 100% everything. So the collectibles do feel kinda meaningless, just there for a couple achievements, gathering costumes, and to just to play a couple challenges. No real replayability besides this.Graphically the game looks amazing, I mean I thought Rehydrated looked really good when that came out, but The Cosmic Shake just adds and improves upon that. Cutscenes also look really good. Dialogue is really good in this game as well, it is just good, funny, and doesn't miss a beat, feels like the actual writers. The soundtrack is good, it is, but I have seen a couple other people say it's "Forgettable" and that's probably true for the most part, but these songs do fit all of the atmospheres really well, they do fit in, and it definitely is sad, but you also gotta remember there are almost 50 songs, what 46 for the main game and the 2 (Sweet Victory and Jellyfish Jam) in the credits, so it is understandable why most of the songs are gonna escape your mind.I think that is all I have to say about the game, so I am sorry for anyone who read this full thing haha. I just wanna say thank you to everyone at Purple Lamp and THQ Nordic for returning me to my nostalgic childhood, it's like I was living back when I was 8 with my Ps2 where I had no care in the world, was definitely needed for how s**t my life has been lately. So OBVIOUSLY I'm giving the game a thumbs up, for me I didn't regret paying the full price, and like I said it just sent me back to nostalgia town, but for anyone else hesitating I might say wait for a sale, it's a great game, but I also know not everyone is gonna want to 100% the game so you'll get a pretty short trip for the price. Ran 100% well on Linux, so for muh penguins out there, or just people playing on Deck, this should work perfectly fine. Let's also get the Movie Game Rehydrated as well, PLEASE!! PS. Can't wait for more SpongeBob games regardless. Thank you.

I'm not a fan of  completeing a game fully as it tends to get boring but if you like it, power to ya!My one gripe is that the final boss felt a bit anti climatic, only having three hit points and one phase compared to the Steelbob fight, but yeah it's kind of a love letter to BFBB with it actually having restored content in some way (even Truth or Squared did it better)- and meanwhile there was potential to have a second phase with the ending cutscene y'know?And maybe we get to see ports of the other older spongy platformers put on Steam, even the original Battle for Bikini bottom, as it had a style i remember more than the remakeI'll give it an 8/10
