_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing, I love it. While it dropped a few of my favorite things from Hard West 1 (such as the numeric luck system = no RNG in to hit, or the oppressive atmosphere and Death as the narrator), it is vastly improved in almost all other aspects and then there's new cool mechanics introduced to make it stand out more. I really like their resolve not to just follow blindly in the footsteps of XCOM. Bravado (kill an enemy = > your turn refreshes) might not be my favorite mechanic ever but I'm glad it was in this game. It felt pretty fresh.I like how it went for a single continuous campaign with a static cast of unique characters. I wasn't sure about some of them at first but eventually I ended up liking them all. The story was also pretty alright, while the plot itself didn't really stand out the writing was great with plenty of humor and badassery. Graphics are pretty, music is awesome, levels are quite varied, difficulty seems to be just about right (not a fan of timed missions though). As for negatives the achievements are a little bit uninspired, I hate how jokers are not only missable but outright made into secrets you have to stumble upon with no clues. Unity is a dumpster fire of an engine but luckily I've had no issues other than raging GPU/CPU usage and somewhat long loading times. All in all an excellent game. I sincerely hope there's gonna be Hard West 3 or something in that vein.Took me 19.5 h to finish on normal (called "Hard" ingame). There's some replayability potential as I'm tempted to go play hard ("Nightmare"), hunt for the missing achievements and use Cla'lish and Bill more than in my first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite understand the negative comments. 1) Difficulty:- If the game is too hard for you: play it on easy. That's what I'm doing to have an enjoyable casual first play-through.- there is actually a save and load function in the game. You can retry the mission and reload single engagements. Somthing I really like. If you complain about difficulty, try playing 'Into The Breach' - no save points, and ITB is brutally unforgiving. One mistake will ruin your entire run. This on the over hand is fun. You can do a mistake, figure out a better solution, reload and learn.2) Combat Mechanics:- Bravado: I find the 'bravado' style combat really refreshing. You feel incredibly powerful killing 5 enemies in a row with just one character.- Luck: I always disliked the chance based hit probability in X-COM. No matter how well you set up, in the end RNG always f***ed you over. To me that sucks all the fun out of a game. 'Luck' in this game acts like a battery you can fill up and use up to boost your hit probability. It greatly reduces the frustrations I had with X-COM and makes combat predictable and actually allows for actions to chain and to depend on each other. In X-COM every action can mess up your game plan due to RNG.3) Combat flow:You can't go into this game with an X-COM mentality. This is a new take on the same genre. There is no 'overwatch' here (tbh I found the overwatch system not that fun in the first place) and the pacing of combat is very different.Example of how I approach combat in this game:- I scout out the enemies (go in and out with a fast unit)- I get my characters into position- I wait for the enemies to move in- Finally: I release a chain of ('bravado') actions onto the enemyIt's less of trench warfare, where each party trades blows over several turns until there is a winner (as in X-COM). It's more about assessing the situation, making a plan, setting up the engagement and then crushing the enemies in one move. It feels really good.4) Upgrades and Progression:There are weapons, a loyalty system and cards. These are all ways to enhance your characters and customize their skill set to your liking.5) Story mechanics:I also find the way you engage with story line quite fun. You have a map you can explore, pick objectives, talk to NPCs, trade, etc. It feel more exploratory and less like you're just jumping from combat into combat. It's a nice break in between.I'm only 8 hours in so my opinion might change. But so far I'm enjoying myself.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. XCOM and Wasteland 2/3 lovers will likely enjoy this2. Typical turn based tactics strategies do apply - but with unique mechanics like trick shots and bravado, things get complicated real fast, so make sure you plan wisely and watch your angles!4. Loyalty and story based choices aren't new - but the way this game handles it is pretty interesting (shall not spoil too much)5. Unfortunately some quirks and tedium occasionally interrupt what would otherwise be an immersive and fun game - not to mention, I would really love to have more customization options for how my party members look!Would definitely recommend to lovers of turn based tactical games who also enjoy a solid linear story!

_childDocuments_.review: Xcom in the old west with zombies. What else do you need to know?---Followup after finishing the game:As an XCom fan, and recently replaying all the Xcom  games, and their DLCs, Hard West 2 (HW2)  filled the need for more Xcom type gaming. The combat mechanics are great. Yeah, you miss Xcom's Overwatch mechanic, for a while, but then realize how much fun (maybe better) the Bravado mechanic is in HW2. Ricochet shots also add a very fun twist to the shooting mechanic, but it works both ways. There's some darn hard maps late in the game where the enemy sharpshooters use ricochet shots on you to brutal effect.Cover is treated very similarly to XCom, and as in XCom flanking is important. I feel the hit percentages are treated more realistically in HW2 as opposed to the XCom games.While not a fan of cards used for skills in a game, the poker card mechanic works very well in HW2. I don't even play poker, so I had to refer to a wikipedia article to know what some hands were. But basically, each card gives some bonus skill (luck, health, weapon damage), plus each character has special abilities that are enabled or improved as you give them a better hand. By the end of the game you'll want to give each of the four of your final posse, a straight or flush to enable most of their abilities. You can change card hands around before each mission, and you should. Maybe you realize in order to complete a mission, Bill needs as much health as possible so give him all the health bonus cards.There is also at least one ability each character has that is only enabled by increasing their loyalty to you, and this comes from making 'Oregon Trail' style decisions during conversations or to resolve an argument. The tutorial feature is implemented very well. You actually get prompted what to do on the first mission, and whenever a new ability is revealed like the ricochet shot. It's not intrusive, and it can also be turned off at any time. Like XCom, the game makes auto saves, and you can do a manual save anytime. So save scum to your heart's content. I tend to do a save before each mission, and at key stages in a mission. You can type descriptive save game file names, so something like 'just before storming the barn'. I have often gone back to an earlier point in a mission to see if I can do it better with less losses, or to get a bonus for something I failed to do the first time (you get gold and item bonuses for optional goals listed for the mission, like 'kill all the sharpshooters in the first round'.There are main and optional missions. I chose to do all the optionals which led to around 34 total hours of gameplay. They are worth it for extra gold and items, and also lets you practice tactics for the harder main missions. Pro tip: Once you get Lazarus, always take him on a mission. He is essentially your medic. He is immune to effects (poison, drunk, crippled, bleeding, etc) as he can recover from them at the end of the round, and he can steal enemy's health and give it to members of your posse, while removing their effects. Once you figure out how to use Lazarus effectively, you will find seemingly impossible missions to be fairly straight forward, if challenging. Say a 20 hit point bad guy is coming and Bill has 2 health and is bleeding at the start of a turn? Steal the bad guy's 20 HP and give him Bill's 2 HP and his bleeding effect. Then have Laughing Deer race over and bonk him on the head, or just wait one more turn for him to bleed out. I plan on playing it through again in the future on a harder difficulty, and I would like to make better use of Cal’Lish and Laughing Deer. On my first game I preferred to stick mainly with the gunslingers with pistols and rifles. I didn't really appreciate how effective the shotgun is in the hands of Lazarus with the Shotgun skill enabled, until late in the game, and Laughing Deer's ability to run behind enemy lines and wreak havok with a melee weapon.Overall I would highly recommend the game to anyone who likes the turn based Xcom style shooter genre. If in doubt, try the demo first. It is the first few missions of the full game, and will give you a good idea if you will like it. Be aware that the demo save games do NOT carry over to the full game, so you'll have to start all over, but you will also have learned from your earlier mistakes.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard West II is one of the best tactical shooter I have ever played. Developers get what we like in these type of games: think and bloody action.Let me also try to explain why some of the reviews are mixed.The core of the gameplay is called "Bravado". When one of your characters kill an ennemy he passes into "Bravado mode". No special power there, your character simply regains all its action points. And if he kills another ennemy he keeps his Bravado mode. I let you now imagine the possibilities of such a mode. You must use all your characters to weak ennemies so you allow some of you characters to kill and kill more and more ennemies. You can litteraly kill all ennemies on the screen if you play it smart.Game is incredibly satisfying to play and bloody as hell. It fits to the cowboy theme.Now why this game disappointed some of gamers? Simply because in the game you can choose between three difficulties: easy, hard and nightmare. There is no proper normal mode. Well I would say that the easy mode is the normal mode (I started on hard but switched to easy, but you will have challenge don't worry). And in hard mode if you don't enter into "Bravado mode" all the time you will do nothing in the game. You will keep loosing and be frustrated. This mode is perfect if you are already very good at this type of games, if not go to the easy mode you will enjoy it more. There are many other good stuff about the game. There is a kind of open world between fights where you can do side quests, loot objects and weapons, speak with characters. Not incredible but very cool. You have many different ennemies and levels, the special powers of the characters are cool too.No but for real this game is worth your time, I had a blast with it. But once again: don't be ashamed to switch the difficulty.

Just more powerful versions of older guns.- The card mechanic as a level up tool is interesting. You basically use poker hands to power up your characters, this allows for variety and customisation early on. It gets less interesting in later stages. You just go and power up everybody, and when you get new cards you swap for more powerful versions. - It only crashed me once, in the final boss right when I killed him (super anti-climatic)- No support for controller is weird... this could be great in Steam Deck without having to use the track pads.If you like X-com / Wasteland type of games grab it on a sale and you are good.

_childDocuments_.review: Usual reviewing caveats: 1) I did not "git gud" (aka I'm a pretty casual player) and 2) I haven't beaten the game yet.As you've probably read in other reviews, Hard West 2 is almost a puzzle game wrapped in a squad combat game. At the harder levels, every move matters -- and you'll need to figure out how to best exploit your squad abilities / consumables / weapons to chain moves and kills using the new Bravado system if you're going to meet the extra objectives (or on higher levels, the turn counter).As I'm more interested in the story and quickly got tired of my incompetence resulting in needing to heal a lot (because presumably, I *wasn't* doing the optimal paths), I turned down the difficulty to Easy and restarted. Frankly, for a lot of us -- Easy is going to be Normal. The game even says "Normal" is *hard* (it ain't called Easy West 2 for a reason, I'm sure the devs are thinking!). Didn't try Nightmare, but knock yourselves out!On Easy (at the time of writing), you still do have to plan / may want to adjust your posse configuration, so it isn't as if you're entirely cake walking the game. Your posse does have higher stats (more health is noticable), and most missions lack turn limits -- so I found it a more enjoyable experience. Still stuck on one mission, but that's more than anything else because I'm trying to clear a bonus objective and am being stubborn about it. So all on me. Planning how you're going to take on enemies is still required -- and there's no shame in restarting a mission from the beginning once you realize what you're up against (first encounter with Blackhearts will doubtless trigger this response... until you understand what they do, you'll almost certainly fight them suboptimally).The voice acting is a little odd in that some lines have it, some don't... but overall it stays immersive enough that you can enjoy the story.TL;DR -- good story (at least so far), enjoyable in that you have to plan what you're doing even on Easy -- Hard/Nightmare mode if you want to *really* plan what you're doing and are much better than me. Overall point of the whole matter -- am I having fun when I play it? And since the answer is "Yes", I have to recommend it if you're at all interested in this type of game. Give it a shot, I think you'll find it is worth investing some time in.(Edited to remove stale load time / pending difficulty comments).

_childDocuments_.review: The first Hard West was an ambitious game. While I thoroughly enjoyed it, it lacked polish in many ways, and its characters weren't particularly fleshed out. _childDocuments_.review: I wrote a ludicrously long review for this game shortly after its release last year and received a very kind response from a developer. At the time I felt that the balance was way off, and I had severe gripes with the controls. The overall tone was very negative. I did not recommend Hard West II, although I liked a lot of what it did.I made it to the Act I finale and literally could not stand to finish it. The mission was excessively difficult and way, way, way too long--but more than that, I thought the enemy design was severely flawed on the most fundamental level. I decided I would put the game down and wait until patches were released.It's been eleven months, and two major patches have come. It looks like there won't be any more, which is disappointing, but I'm happy to report that I don't think HW2 needs them anymore. This is now a certifiably good strategy game, and I have no problem recommending it.Hard West II is still very flawed. Despite looking and feeling like XCOM, it does not want to be played like XCOM at all. Save scumming is encouraged, or even mandatory, and figuring out an optimal way to clean a level is very important. There are tons of great and unique ideas on display in the design, and the gameplay represents a big improvement over the first game IMO, but the lack of character progression mechanics and health recovery systems feel like gaping holes in the coherence of the mechanics. But as a puzzle-ish take on XCOM, adapted to a Western theme, it's still pretty good. Patches have massively reduced enemy HP and nerfed their skills, which were previously over-used (and are what ruined the game); and while these skills can still be frustrating, they're not even close to a dealbreaker anymore. Racking up kills with Bravado is great fun, and managing Luck is a great twist on this sort of game. I like the gameplay now. I like it a lot.The controls seem improved, but leave something to be desired. Shotguns still can't be aimed up or down, which is extremely frustrating. It's very easy to accidentally use special abilities when not desired, and the camera can be wonky. Like usual for these sorts of games, there's also a lot of annoying time-wasting stuff, from watching enemies take their turn to sitting around while buff alerts pop up before you take your turn, but unlike usual for these sorts of games, there's a fast-forward button. This is a good thing.I could sit here and gripe about the story, like I did in my previous review, but the overall verdict isn't complicated: the characters are decent, the narrative is good, the writing is better than average, and the story generally captures a Western feel--although the supernatural elements are too pronounced, in my opinion. I love the overworld and wish there was more to it. The prologue is amazingly good, while Act I stumbles a bit, and Acts II and III are both solid. Its biggest issues are in presentation, but many of these have been rectified through patches (typos especially). I still will point out that justifying all text on the right is insanity. There is no excuse for that. But it doesn't really matter.So, overall, I do recommend Hard West II now. It isn't perfect. There's a lot I wish they'd done differently. But I don't expect perfection from AA games; I just expect competence and fun. And HW2 is competent, and it is fun. If you're a Western fan like me and are starved for more games in that genre, it hits the spot fairly well. I hope there's a Hard West III, because I think it could be truly excellent. Especially if it has overwatch.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game that is sadly ruined by bad balancing and design.In the first few hour(s), during the portion of the game that was in the demo, the game was pretty solid. Good concept and gameplay that wasn't insanely difficult on normal but still a good enough challenge to be enjoyable. However, post-demo, the game difficulty quickly spirals out of control. Like others have said, if you don't have the perfect strategy first try, you're basically screwed. Your units getting completely focused fired by groups of enemies hidden in the fog and taken down to 1 health in one turn through some impossible through a wall angle (god forbid they were missing health before they got massacred by the very lore friendly AI hivemind). Even if you have the perfect strategy, you still have to jump through frustrating RNG checks again and again. There was one level with mandatory horses, which not only disable your character's unique skills, but also reduce accuracy by ~25%. This wouldn't have been too bad, as the luck mechanic makes it so that your failures from one round help improve your odds in the next. However, the challenge for this specific level was that you had to finish it in two turns, basically nullifying the mechanic, as if you miss on round one you pretty much are screwed since you don't have enough firepower to finish in the next round, plus you can still miss even with the luck boost.On top of all of this, metal objects which you need to ricochet shots become increasingly less frequent (in the levels before I got tired of playing, anyways). This takes a lot of the fun out of the game, especially since it was one of the main draws of the combat.To be honest, really wanted to like this game, and did for a while. However, post demo it quickly becomes frustrating to play IMHO. If you can power through it and don't mind resetting a few times, more power to you, it is a decent game. However, personally the bad design and jank really took me out of it and made it not enjoyable after a few battles.TL;DRSolid game in beginning but doesn't last. Playable if you are willing to get frustrated or are masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard West 2 is a unique take to the standard xcom combat style. Unique, in that it's both very easy to get 100% chances to hit, and each time any unit gets a kill they refill their entire AP pool and can take another full turn.  This leads to a good puzzle-like planning experience where you need to chain together kills so that you can wipe out a large number of enemies in a single turn.Sounds great right? Well not exactly..The enemy also gets access to easy 100% chances to hit, and while they don't reset their turns when getting a kill, they have numbers on their side instead.  By the 3rd combat mission your team of 4 is facing about 20 enemies (split into waves) that all get to run and gun just like you scoring constant guaranteed damage. (with no consistent way of healing)Another mechanic that doesn't feel very good is the cover system.  It has the full\half\none cover system commonly seen in similar titles, except % hit chance seems to only scale in multiples of 25%, meaning even if you're behind half cover and spend action points to hunker down, you have at least a 25% chance of taking damage that round, paired with 4:1 enemy ratios, typically means you're taking damage just about every turn.I've had characters get completely wiped in one turn by this mechanic, despite my best efforts to use the cover provided to me.  The only solution I've found is to kite enemies outside of weapon's range forcing them to spend AP moving up and allowing me to shoot while retreating, which is not particularly easy because weapon range limits aren't displayed during combat.My final gripe is that the user interface makes it too easy to accidentally spend action points.  I can't tell you how many times I'm trying to click on another character or deselect something, just to have my character sprint forward, or cancel the whole turn hunkering down because there is no way to have zero abilities selected while controlling a character.  Pressing number keys spends AP, clicking around the map spends AP, escape doesn't deselect anything, etc. It can get very frustrating when you accidentally move a unit wasting their turn, then have a horde of enemies guarantee a one-turn kill.Now, admittedly I didn't make it very far into the game, maybe it gets better later, but sheesh I couldn't make it through a single combat without feeling cheated on multiple times.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard West 2 was a fun, well-made game. I would recommend playing it. I think the game benefited very strongly from its good combat mechanics, a great art and narrative direction, and just generally solid construction. I never had any real bugs, and the game never crashed on me. I also enjoyed the use of the Poker Card mechanic to unlock abilities for characters. The ability to chain kills, and gain Bravado was a lot of fun too. Overall, it was an interesting game.My main critique is that the relatively small number of hand-made missions made the game feel somewhat more "puzzle"-oriented than outright strategy. This was especially true for many of the train heist missions, where in order to get equipment, or poker cards that you would never be able to find anywhere else, a lot of restarting was required to find the more-or-less "correct" method to clear the mission.My only other significant critique is that the game depicted Indigenous Peoples in a fairly negative light. The two Indigenous characters in your posse were (in my opinion) well-written, but the use of the Shadow Dancers as secondary antagonists left a bit of a sour taste. I don't think the developers SHOULDN'T have used the Shadow Dancers, but they were depicted as vicious killers dealing in dark/evil mystical powers. I think there was an excellent opportunity to write a much more sympathetic antagonist faction, especially given the real-world history of North America.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: X-COM combat plus Wasteland exploration, with some nice twists, on a much smaller scale.I'd recommend the game if you like the genre or westerns.The game offers a short campaign(under 18 hours on Hard) with lots of fun but fails to deliver the real potential of some mechanics(restrictive/limited inventory, brainless and linear cards management, simplistic rest mechanic).Story-wise, some characters are great, others aren't, the plot doesn't explain some important points and the ending feels underwhelming. Liked the art design.Performance isn't consistent but I managed to play the game on Linux through Proton.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed bag. Great art/visuals, good sound and music, good worldbuilding and lore, the main story is ok (minus the supernatural stuff, its a basic wild west revenge story). I enjoyed the side quests and exploration more than the main story. I do have problems with the mechanics and overall gameplay. I only played about half of Hard West 1 and never finished, but this is a standalone title and that had no effect on the story. I paid about $15 on sale. Around 24 hours to beat on Hard (the median difficulty).As other reviewers mention, the gameplay is very linear and one-directional. Every map follows a basic formula: Start in Area 1, move up, Spawn Enemy Pod 1. Clear to Area 2, move up, Spawn Enemy Pod 2. Etc. There's not a lot of room for tactical movement...some maps have maybe a tower you can put your rifleman on, buildings/traincars have two floors...but more often than not you are funneled straight down a street, or across a bridge, or through a church, etc. It feels like a chore that you have to work through a mob of enemies to get to your next objective. Before the final mission, I fully expected to write a recommended review. I've never had to restart and savescum so hard to beat a tactical game before. It was such an annoying chore to get through it kinda ruined the entire game for me. I would go as far to say it feels downright cheap and unfair. For example: the final mission starts right after a previous mission, with no chance to heal. So if you haven't played the level already, you start the hardest mission in the game with the final boss fight at reduced or 1 hp (if you character was knocked out the previous battle). This mechanic does appear a limited number of times in the game, but it feels cheap as hell to do it before the final mission.in addition, the final boss fight also includes another recurring feature: once you advance so far, you are locked into a cutscene and started in a new area. However, instead of the turn being reset and your action points reset, it just continues the turn...so if you have 1 move left on one character, guess what? The next turn is the entire enemy pod and boss wailing on your characters standing out in the open with no cover.In games like XCOM, save-scumming is always something you can do. Sometimes have to do, but through modes like Ironman its encourage that you try your best to survive and figure it out without resorting to it. From the way this game is set up, it honestly feels like....a puzzle the devs want you to figure out. Theres one way to advance through a level, one way to work a pod of enemies, and you have to figure it out through constant reloads and redos.I might play a little more to achievement hunt and find some side content I missed, but overall I would say I'm not interested in a second playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing in this game is really bad.  Mostly relies on cliche.  Laughing Deer is full of negative stereotypes, including allusions to alcoholism.  Combat is poorly tuned. Based on other reviews, it sounds like they overcompensate in the opposite direction later in the game.  Exploration and quests don't seem to be that well considered either.  I've already lost a side quest due to an area transition with no warning and no path back.  In short, there are so many better ways to spend thirty bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I just replayed Hard West 1 and comparatively, Hard West 2 is a game for a child with head trauma.   Hard west 2 takes all of the mechanics of 1 and just deletes them.  It is utter trash.  It is as if "Story Based" people made a tactical turn based game.   Luck, reloading, range, cover, concealment, hold ups, etc have all been removed from the game.       Aesthetically, Hard West 2 is Cutesie.  That is , it tries to be cute all the time.   Mind you, not well like Dungeons of Naheulbeuk, just annoyingly like Felicia Day.        You should not play this game if you liked Hard West 1.  It will not be fun for you.  It is torturous and dark in a  totally different way.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard West 2 is engaging but a bit different from the first one. Which is normal since it was made by a different studio. All in all, I enjoyed it and think it's a decent addition to any tactics games fan library. But I'd like to pinpoint what I didn't like about the game.My main gripe is the difficulty. The game is balanced around new mechanic Bravado - which replenishes the Action Points after a character kills someone. It's cool as a side mechanic but when everything centers around it the game turns to puzzle. If you want to play it as a tactical game pick Normal or Easy difficulty to avoid frustration.There are some annoying types of enemies which spam new enemies every turn or switch health with your characters when injured. But they're quite rare. Also, the train missions are pain in the ass. Otherwise, the game doesn't overstay it's welcome. The story and characters are okay. The missions rarely drag. There is some exploration. Some nice side quests appear here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: At this point I’m done with the game. As many people mentioned this game is a puzzle rather than a tactical game, and a puzzle game that relies on RNG. There are no real team interactions you’d expect from this type of combat system, your team members can’t heal other team members, they can’t buff or debuff, they can’t even use items on others. This becomes an issue when you are faced with hordes of enemies and really long levels, because you can heal each team member up to 2 times that is if a team member has two healing items in his loadout. So you must do everything perfectly to complete a mission.As I said, this game relies on RNG and I don’t know if it’s just my luck, but I noticed that this RNG is locked in your save during the combat. I can reload the same save 20 times and I still miss 75% shot every single time, unless I restart the mission.And the most annoying thing is the load time, it’s just ridiculous. So in order to do everything perfectly you will reload a lot, because there is no telling beforehand where the enemies are or how many of them there are, every time you sit through 2 minutes of loading and that’s on SSD.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I have played the beta versions a lot and I was really surprised by all the improvements. My highlight: the combat on horse while chasing a train. _childDocuments_.review: As a diehard XCom-like tactical games fan who really enjoys Westerns in any form, I absolutely loved this game. Don't be scared away by negative reviews and discussions - I finished the game on hard and can say that it's perfectly balanced for different team compositions and weapons. Be prepared to think out of the box though as Hard West 2 is build around different mechanics than your classical XCom-like - it requires a bolder approach, not playing defensively with overwatch crawl or waiting out stuff. Bravado mechanic isn't really hard to master when you get the hand of it, and it feels so rewarding and satisfying that whoever designed it should be a genious. Just keep in mind that this game is not only a turn-based strategy, but also a puzzle where you have to plan your moves to keep chain-killing enemies. The plot is also nice - a gritty Weird West story with companion relations and some dialogue options serves as a nice change from one combat after another - the first two locations are amazing, the third like could use some polish and additions - but all in all it's still pretty good. All in all, I can totally recommend this to all turn-based strategy and Old/Wild/Weird West fans out there - play risky and be rewarded for that.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first introduction into this style of game, and I really enjoyed the experience. A lot of reviewers comparing it to XCOM and that is a title I wanted to try but it seemed like a dumbed down version of XCOM so to see if I would enjoy the genre I gave it a shot. The story is great, the characters are fun, but I don't see myself getting a lot of replay value out of it. There is no incentive to beat the game again after I tried it on easy. I was hoping maybe some type of buff or even cards remaining and the opportunity to add onto cards. The actual content is maybe 15-20 hours on easy if you are a completionist you might 25-30 on easy. All in all if you are wanting to get into this type of game Hard West 2 is a great game at the price point. The only true "negative" I could find is the lack of info on buffs and debuffs, I had to join the discord to find out what "Bloodlust" did and even then the responses did not sound definite. 8.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:When I dove into Hard West 2, the first thing you notice is that there is voiceacting. Enemies talk, your posse talks, they grunt, they make comments in the battle, and roughly half of all the dialogue in the game is voiced. Something that drove me crazy about many early Firaxcom clones is how everybody silently murders eachother. Literally nobody talked in Hard West, where the addition of voiceacting ties everything together. The gameplay loop was completely overhauled, Luck is no longer a magic armor that protects characters. This is both a blessing and a curse, as the game now wants you to chain kill enemies to get a bunch of free turns. It's a fun mechanic, however as the enemies start getting higher and higher HP pools it becomes more of a curse; as you start to miss the Luck stat protecting you later in the game. The Bad:The game has put an arbitrary speed run clock on almost every single mission in the game, and in atleast one case you miss out on a playing card if you fail to do it correctly. So you get this feeling that the game is ALWAYS rushing you, and it kinda sucks. I don't like being rushed in strategy games, and it spits in the face of the "play your way" attitude of the game. You will definitely find yourself playing on easy mode to get all of the achievements since the higher difficulties give enemies more HP.Once you realize that there's an optimal choice for every event, you find yourself save-scumming literally every aspect of the game. Didn't get a crit? reload. Event with multiple choices? reload, there are hidden rewards for some events! The two strongest cards in the game, the jokers, are secret and pretty hard to find. Also, the speed that the game drip-feeds cards to you is pretty pathetic so you can only really start forming good hands in chapter 2. The 2-8 cards are missing, leaving 9's, 10's, jokers, and the face cards. Even when you have all the cards and make good hands, the level of power it gives you is extremely underwhelming. The Ugly:The gameplay loop simply falls apart near the end of the game as they start throwing enemies with 30+ health at you regularly who do extreme damage. Up until these enemies appear regularly, the game is actually really easy; as you can VERY QUICKLY tear through entire crowds of enemies even when they become their "veteran" versions. The last mission before the endgame is outright cruel as you have to face as many enemies as you usually do, but they have the same HP and equivalent powers that you have, and do INSANE damage. This is the only time we fight these things, thankfully, but it's a COMPLETE tonal shift from the rest of the game where the majority of enemies didn't have special abilities.Many of the levels have a three act structure with very noticeable boundaries; with the idea that the farther you go in the level, the more enemies you activate. This ties in with the general feeling of risk/reward and the speed run clock, but it also makes every level feel the exact same because there are not that many enemies in the game, and the only two abilities that you see are HP swap and summon. Even then, it's all just a weaker version of stuff you can use. So it's just lazy.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Don't listen to the naysayers, this game is excellent. No, this is not a puzzle game. It actually feels closer to pool, or billiards, in that you have to build momentum and maintain initiative to win.This is the first time I see an "Xcom formula taken in a new direction" done right. This game is built around aggressively moving forward, not hiding behind cover with overwatch on every turn.The action economy in Hard West 2 is based on killing enemies, so the more you kill, the more actions you get. This is the reasons people are complaining that Hard West 2 is a "puzzle game", where you have to "solve" the level by trial and error. That's objectively not true. Taking different actions changes the behavior of the enemies, which will just paint you into a different corner - if you're not playing aggressively and stepping out of cover. This game wants you to play like you're in an action movie, not in a tower defense game.Hard West 2 wants you to plan several moves ahead. Each character's turn has to include the set up the next turn, and the next, and the one after. When it all goes off as planned, it's a glorious chain of carnage - bullets, explosions, and bodies flying galore. If it backfires, then salvaging the run can be even more fun. Each mission also has optional objectives, some of which are pretty difficult. Indiscriminate application of explosives is often the answer to challenging situations, just like in real life.In Xcom, a stubbed toe can send your star soldier into a hospital for a week, but here, there is no real penalty for getting most of your squad KOed. The game just expects you to John Woo every mission, guns akimbo - and I'm all about it. Highly recommended.P.S. I think that once the new players learn to abandon their old Xcom mindset, and try a new approach, they will enjoy the game much more than the current review score indicates.

So if you like game series like divinity: Original sin, wasteland or xcom, then do not buy this, it is not like them. Those games are gold, this is just garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: (completed on hard difficulty, difficulties are: Normal, Hard and Nightmare) A really damn good game. Its enough of a mix of puzzle and freedom to solve said puzzle mechanics. I have more hours than usual as i was chasing all the optional objectives, but only failed the optional objective for one mission. There is a difficulty spike from chapter 1 to chapter 2, but it is not an insurmountable hill, it tests how you play along with your builds, like how you split your cards and each characters strengths with weaponsPros : Art and animations are great, atmosphere is pretty well done. A much simpler/less frustrating mechanic of taking shots, if your character misses, they gain luck equivalent to chance to hit (its simplified into 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% chance to hit) which adds up to your next attempt at shootingRicocheting shots feel really good and chaining math numbers in your head to achieve the objectives is greatYou cant fish rng by save scumming so there is less incentive to do so.complaints: there appears to be a memory leak/loading speed issue on longer play sessions at the moment, and the devs are tackling it.A bit weird/awkward to see when you have a skill active when first starting outAlso a bit awkward when you want to select a character but have the attack command on.This is more nitpicky if you run around a lot like i do, but the character dialogues do repeatThere is no post game, once you're done with the story you are done. While i wish there was more, though i appreciate what already is in the gameAs far as i can tell, the optional objectives feel very encouraged to make your life easier and i cannot tell at a first glance if they are mandatory to clear the game comfortably. If you are in it for the story on lowest difficulty, you may be able to finish it with no difficulty.Overall, if the memory issue is fixed i would put it at 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: You will find some negative reviews saying that this game is actually a puzzle game because you have to do perfect plays in order to succeed. This is blatantly false. It's perfectly possible to finish the game on the highest difficulty while doing some mistakes and still having spare turns at the end. You just have to know how to play. In other words, you have to master the Bravado system.After a first playthrough on Hard in order to learn the mechanics of the game, I had so much fun that I did another one on Nightmare and found that it was actually easier for me thanks to the experience of the first playthrough. Being a tactical turn-based games enthusiast, I found this game to be a lot of fun because it challenged me to learn new ways to play instead of simply reproducing what other great games of the genre like X com already did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm growing more frustrated with this game by the hour. The devs went way overboard with the Bravado idea. The player gets funneled into this one playstyle that's basically just "run in and use all your damage as fast as possible to deny the enemies their turn". If the enemy gets to have even one turn in this game, your chances of finishing the mission are in serious trouble.The overall problem is that all enemies are WAY too strong right now and all defensive options you have are essentially useless. If you go into half- or full cover and the AI estimates that its chances of hitting you have become too low, they can use cover ignoring spells or grenades that deal just as much damage as their guns and have additional status effects that are extremely annoying and unfun to play with.Every single time one of your character is in a good defensive position, enemies will just pull out a bs spell or grenade that has 100% hit chance and does somewhere between 6-16 damage when your party members only have 20 HP.On top of this all grenades that the enemies use seem to apply bleed every time they hit you which deals damage every time you take an action. It can be cleansed by using bandages but each character only gets to use one bandage per mission. If you run out of bandages and one of your party members has low HP it essentially removes them from the game entirely. If a party member has 2 HP, bleed does 2 damage per action, is active for 3 rounds and you have no bandages there is literally nothing you can do with that character for 3 full rounds. There is no way to apply bandages to other characters either which seems wrong for a squad of people trying to keep an eye out for one another. I have two characters with big med-kits but if the AI chooses to throw grenades at the other two it's gg.If the enemies spam their bs grenades at you it's very possible to have near constant bleed effects active on some members of your party.So the lesson is - try to not make enemies use their grenades on you. If you can't kill them in one turn, try to position your characters where the AI can shoot you so you'll only take their direct gun damage instead of 3+ rounds of additional bleed damage. Everysince I understood this, I have pretty much stopped using full cover to bait enemies into shooting me while in half cover to at least have a chance to negate their damage.  And it's working...what on earth is the design idea behind this?If that wasn't enough the duelist mechanic is also utterly stupid. If sharpshooters can't hit you, they will always just move into the open field activating the duelist ability. If you shoot them, they'll shoot back at you. It's VERY unintuitive and frankly broken to also have them do this if you kill them with your shot. The game wants you to chain kills with Bravado but then puts like 5-6 duelist sharpshooters all over the arena which means you'll take 3-6 damage for every enemy you kill, essentially killing your own party members for following the rules of the game and chaining kills together. Again, you can either shoot them but take damage, or let them live and have them take their turn...also dealing damage to your party. It is again smarter to go into half cover in their vision range and have them take their shot hoping they'll miss so you can kill them in the next round. The design decision behind this is frankly baffling. It's a non choice and has nothing to do with tactical gameplay.There are so many more things that feel not thought through properly in this game that it boils my blood sometimes when I play. All of these issues get exponentially worse later in the game where it throws tons of high tier enemies at you all equipped with unfun mechanics that screw your party over either way you decide to tackle them.

This game is so much less enjoyable than the first that I gave up midway through chapter two, even though I finished the first one three times and loved it.As others have stated, it feels less like a tactics game and more like a puzzle game. _childDocuments_.review: Caution: this is NOT like X-Com games, as many other reviewers have oddly compared it to. A better analogy would be Gears Tactics.Recently, there seems to be a trend of team TBS tactics games being more linear, fast-paced (by removal of critical decision making) and remove probabalistic hits, DMG, etc. Check, check, and check. If you, too, think this trend is in the wrong direction, read on - otherwise, this might be the game for you.Key Complaints:- Sid Meier defined strategy as a series of interesting decisions. Well, in both tactical and strategic layers, the decisions are not interesting - they are boring with a thin veiled story draped over them to appear more impactful than they actually are.- combat is completely on rails - maps are hand made, enemies spawn in pre-determined locations once you reach a checkpoint, you are forced thru corridors by conveniently placed collapsed buildings, etc- combat layer is confined to a very small area with very few tactical choices (i.e., flanking, sneaking)- strategic layer is a big map - but don't be deceived, it's mostly eye candy. You finish missions in a mostly linear fashion but with the option to skip a side mission or two - that's it.- Your most powerful character, not surprisingly, is a character who can teleport-swap positions with any enemy NPC. The ability refreshes EVERY OTHER TURN. What this effectively does is kill the need to consider the layout of the battlefield, consider the vector of attack for each of your soldiers, and plan exciting flanking maneuvers. Because you can just teleport the enemy into the open. How is this an interesting decision?- The trendy chain-kill ability exists for all of your characters for ANY kill, refreshing all your AP. This also removes the need to make another interesting decision - you no longer need to plot out the tactical advance of your soldiers since they can essentially move and attack infinitely. The decision becomes a simple addition problem of which character does how much damage and what sequence will allow you to do chain-kills. This diverges very far away from what "team tactics" is about - maneuvering your squad in-parallel to defeat an enemy.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: I will never understand why devs feel the need to make their games ridiculously challenging opposed to fun. Yes, you scale the difficult up for those that play on "hard" or "nightmare" modes, but can you please make a fair and balanced feeling game at normal? I lost interest in this game when I had a mission that put me up against a ton of enemies... I make it to my objective (weakened where my posse barely had any HP left)...and then, suddenly, they felt it necessary to have a surprise attack by FOUR enemies happen at once.This game is full of poor tactical combat, unbalanced gameplay, partial voice acting, glitchy controls, horrible mapping that makes it difficult to see where you're going unless you spin your camera around 50,000 times, cheesy dialogue, and a pretty boring story that did nothing original. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: I need a mixed option. I'm going with a thumbs down because after writing this out, I'm realizing I have much more negative to say than positive. HOWEVER, all my complaints could easily be fixed with a balance patch and I'd gladly change my no to a yes if I see an improvement.TLDR; good mechanics and gameplay, but iffy balance and frustrating enemies.This is a really solid xcom-like. Bravado is fun and allows you to extend your turn and finish off a bunch of weak or wounded enemies with one character. At first it feels almost overpowered, but as the difficulty increases it balances out. The ability to trick shot and bounce a bullet off 2 objects and hit an enemy across the map and behind cover is fantastic. The overworld map is fine, interesting to explore but it gets empty after you've seen everything in the area. I gotta say though, please reduce companion chatter. I really don't need to hear them whine about the cold every time I click the map. But as for the negative... I feel like it could use a lot of balancing. Difficulty scales up a bit too fast. You start off one-shotting enemies with 5 health which feels fun, if a bit easy, but that quickly changes. I was playing on Hard since its the middle difficulty between easy and Nightmare, and had to drop it to easy by the end of the first chapter. (I'm sure more goes into it, but it seemed to just double my health pools).  The undead enemies, Revenants, are such a nuisance and slow down every battle they are a part of. Which has felt like at least half so far. If a Revenant isn't fully killed during your turn, it heals all damage it took. Some of these Revenants have 15 or more health, meaning to have a chance to down them in one turn you have to focus fire with at least half your team, assuming you're using 2 people with rifles doing 8 dmg (and don't miss). If you take it down to 1, go ♥♥♥♥ yourself, its fully healed again, you wasted all that AP on  trying to kill it and you get nothing. No Overwatch either, more on that at the end since its personal opinion.Bleeding is insane. You take 2 damage per action you take for 3 turns. Yes it can be healed via bandage, but if you don't have one because you already patched up your bleeding from the last guy that spammed bleeds, then you have no choice but to end turn. Not even heads down, because guess what, that's an action. Just a hard end turn to avoid damage. You can't use items on team members either as far as I can tell.Cripple completely disables movement for a turn and you'll have 3 enemies in a single fight that will run over to you, cripple you, and run off literally ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ giggling and it makes me want to quit. Make cripple reduce movement distance by 50% so I can at least have an attempt at a turn with that character. This is personal opinion, but I like having overwatch of some kind. I know people think it's boring, but I'd so much rather set up an overwatch than use the heads down ability which boosts your dodge by 25%. At least then on the enemy turn I can hope to dish out damage as opposed to just hoping I don't take any.
_childDocuments_.name: Hard West 2

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant new take on turn-based strategy and in a really exciting and immersive setting. Navigate a world map (pretty linear but still) and go from fight to fight. In stead of the typical overwatch-function of the genre, you are encouraged AND rewarded for making aggressive play. Not only do you have gun, shotguns, rifles and grenade, you also gain supernatural skills. These are acquired by mixing cards that are earned on mission and placed in your hand poker style. Ie. equipping two jacks on a character will unlock a certain skill. The music is very well made and the sounds really suck you into the world. Sometimes the comments the characters make on the world map can get repetetive, but that is just a minor thing. All in all an excellent game and something I have been craving for a long time.BONUS: While it does not have fishing, there is mention of a guy called Black Fish or something like that.

The maps are small, with a limited number of things to do.  No random encounters, so you can't grind up money.  Overall I enjoyed it and would like to see some more adventures in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game so good, my main complaint is how short it is. The game seems like it was set up to be a bigger game, but just like the first game, there's 3 small maps to 'explore'. I went and did every side mission possible and the game kept feeling like I was just starting to get the game rolling and it was already ending. Like many games in this genre, the game spikes in difficulty in the beginning but get much easier as you unlock better weapons and skills.The game's bravado mechanic makes this game much more aggressive than similar games in the genre. It emphasizes setting up puzzle-like set pieces rather than having it feel like a realistic battle. A battle might be complete your first single turn if you set everything up properly. Again, this is highly satisfying to do as it makes every single turn significant, it pulls away from the battles from feeling like battles.The plot unfortunately was much weaker than Hard West 1. Hard West 1 had an absolutely memorable story with how dark it was and this game did not go in that direction. Instead, it follows the trend of modern games of wacky side characters that become pretty one dimensional. With how short this game is, it's hard to get really invested into the side characters.I'd like to mention one of the most important features in this game is the 4x speed. There's absolutely no reason for me to wait for horses to move slowly in the open world and for animations to take forever during battles. The fact that I cannot select or look at other characters while my character is moving, I am forced to watch the entire animation play out. This was excruciating and made me quit the game first time around before I discovered this.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a bad game? Not really. But it's not a good one either.Kudos to the team for a very stable release and a demo.But here is the list of small and medium things that stops Hard West from being something better:1) Story is meh. There is literally nothing interesting happens between the first and the last mission.2) Mission goals are meh. Not a single interesting level mechanic. Kill, get or run.3) Overworld feels like an afterthought. Why on earth do we need provisions if healing in town is cheaper and there is nothing stops you from going to town between missions?4) Companions backstory is not integrated into the game at all. It's just optional, missable flavour text.5) Writing is meh. Can recall a single interesting dialogue.6) Combat is ok-ish but as many other pointed it's more of a puzzle game than TBS. On top of that critical chance is absolutely useless since you can't rely on it and getting the bravado streak is way more important.7) I swear to god, the random seed for each turn is pre-calculated and your critical chance means almost nothing. Get on sale or play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast. Game length is about 35 hours. Definitely worth the buy when it's on sale. Up to you at full price.I have a few minor complaints and a hope for some tweaks. The game scaling feels very off; the early game is too easy, and the late game ramp up to the point you need to save scum. It would have been much more enjoyable if the scaling felt smoother, as monster health and how many there were scaled harder than player power.The Bravado system was unique and cool, especially with Laughing Deer, but made the game feel more like a puzzle with 1 answer, than the tactical game. If they ever make a HW3 or when we get expansions, I would wish that the Bravado system would different, maybe melee only, or absent entirely. While the bravado system made for some larger scale fights, and more enemies on the screen, I would rather have smaller scale fights with more drawn out gun fights, than using my pistols to poke them down, just to have either a rifleman or Laughing Deer run through and kill them all in one turn. That just didn't feel as compelling as the first game.I also missed reloading weapons from HW1. I liked the drawn out fights of shooting, missing and reloading. But this game felt more like if you didn't wipe the enemy in a single round, you were playing wrong, and I feel ammunition does that for these types of games. In the original, it also gave weapons more variety than range and damage. The chain gun is a good example. You sacrifice accuracy for more rounds. But in this game, I the same weapon felt like a waste of purchase.Character balance was a bit off as well. Flynn definitely felt the weakest of them all because her card bonuses didn't feel nearly as good as the others. I basically only found her useful for specific side tasks using her special skill.Also, the Duelist system felt very unreliable when I was using it. There were plenty of times when it was active and it didn't trigger, even when shot with single target skills, and in range to fire back. But maybe I overlooked something, I'm not sure.Level design was great, with two exceptions. When a player reaches a specific unmarked spot on the map, it triggers the next phase of enemies to spawn. These locations should either be marked, or reset your party's ability points, otherwise the player basically needs to reload the map so their entire team isn't a punching bag for an entire turn with a good 10-15 new enemies shooting at them. There were also very frustrating elevation issues that would not allow using skills, or shooting shotguns. It did not feel good to not be able to ever aim your shotgun down ever.The rest of the game is all positives. I feel there's enough there for another play through some time later. The music was really good. And the voice actors, especially Flynn, were great. I will play this again eventually, and I hope there is some DLC in the future, perhaps with some new mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid turn based strategy game. The Bravado mechanic makes it very fun to chain together those OP turns lategame snipers in XCOM would get but with every character almost every turn.Can feel a little bit linear/puzzley at times, but I found that aspect very fun to engage with. If you expect to play on the hardest difficulty your first playthrough you will be save scumming, but usually if i went through the level once and then retried it, I would get all the objectives. I like that the game encourages mastery and second playthroughs.Alternatively, Play on medium, be happy with not completing all objectives on your first run, and enjoy the story. You'll have a fun time blasting through mobs and chaining really fun combos and you won't miss out on much.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed Hard West. I like its theme, i like the xcom style game play. Theres a lot i like about it, so naturally i automatically liked hard west 2.among several compounding little things that i have a negative opinion on,( like the ridiculous difficulty, the near infinite way enemies can use devastating skills, the finite amount of money you can earn which has such a drastic affect on your ability to keep your team kitted out, the way that your skills and stats are 100% dependent on the cards you carry, the way that the weapons available to you dont scale up with you or the enemies, the way you will be consistently outnumbered by at least 5 to 1, the way that you are at such a massive disadvantage from turn 1 all the way the bitter end or until you frustratingly restart the fight just to make some modicum of progress, idk just to name a few) the major over arching issue i have are the oppressively long LOAD TIMES. omg its brutal. even with every setting put to low, every trick i know to try and get a game to run better, ever single load screen is at a minimum of 3 minutes. When there are back to back action scenes, or a level with a lot going on, the loading gets even longer. sometimes 5 minutes.i can forgive a lot in a game. even things that most would not be able to look past. but when you make a very difficult game, which by its very nature will ask you to retry things multiple times, and half of your gaming session is sitting in near total silence while you try to figure out if the game has frozen on a load screen, i cant get over that. out of 6 hours of play, im fairly confident a cumulative total of that was one solid hour of just loading times.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been loving this so far. The bravado Mechanic is probably one of the most fun and engaging systems I have played with in a game in awhile. Setting up a high luck shot and then having a character mow through the entire screen feels super rewarding. And thinking "Ok I can use this shot to get this guy to just enough to set it up" and it coming together feels good. The level design is great imo (I'll come back to this in a second) I wish there was a little more to explore/reward for exploring although not a deal breaker for me at all. I love scanning the environment and finding those trick shot spots and setting up wild kills. The one area I don't love the level design is a lot of the horseback missions. The top down plus the characters "moving" in place makes it a little hard to tell where units are. That being said its a super cool creative choice and makes the game feel a lot more alive, and a really interesting POVMissing that important shot feels bad (as it should) and having to make due is also really engaging, it feels like they got the worst part of other games like this  (missing with a 90%) and made it into a fun engaging STRESSFUL mechanic. All in all I have loved what I have played so far!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and if you love the first one you'll love this one even more. I'll just go through a quick pros and cons. Just keep in mind the cons are pretty minor, especially weighed against the pros. Graphics are improved and the stability/performance is perfect. The first game I was constantly chugging and having issues for no reason. Sound effects are great, voice acting is (mostly) great, music is great. The companions are pretty cool and they are unique enough from each other. The UI is fabulous looking, though has some quirks. I like the card system, though I don't like how much power derives purely from the Hand you are playing with each character. Even still, it's a cool way to build a team. I like the Weird West theme, even though I wish it went a little darker or let you use more of the Weird West stuff yourself. The game is much more fast paced and because of the Bravado system, every encounter kind of feels like a puzzle on how you can kill almost every enemy on the screen within one turn. This is kind of fun, especially when it's really working. RNG throws a wrench in it sometimes though. I would consider the Bravado system the main mechanic of the game, and understanding how to set up characters to get Bravado a bunch of times every turn is essential.  The late game (at least on Nightmare difficulty) was brutal and the RNG really started to ramp up, as enemies are sometimes randomly getting a Critical and just one shotting a character. Coupled with Gunslingers having Ricochet shots, on the final levels it feels like you almost have no actual usable cover because they can get around almost anything. This was really clear on the final level. Had to do a lot of restarting because of this, and was starting to frustrate me. Level design is a little strange, where it's more like set-pieces as opposed to a full map. You can tell each map is split up into 3~ clear encounter areas. There's a weird quirk of the UI where it is always using the last move you used, which can be pretty confusing and cause a lot of misclicks and plays you didn't mean to make until you get real used to it. Also there's a slight delay when cycling characters, which means if you play fast that will also sometimes have you move the wrong character. There's a lack of weapon variety this time, there's a good amount of weapons but most are direct upgrades and of the same type. I kind of liked having a Musket in the first game where you had to use an AP to reload, and handling that trade off. Most important thing of all, in all tactics games: enemies appearing out of nowhere because there's no clearly defined Fog of War or line of sight. Also, I am almost 100% positive that enemies have just SPAWNED in front of me, which can feel really cheap when you've used most of your Action Points already. This was a problem in the first game too and I feel like this has to be addressed, though I won't knock it too much because this is an issue in a lot of tactics games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has both fixable flaws, like missions you can break by doing things in the wrong order or not being able to choose where each posse member starts, to non-fixable flaws like a very lacking loyalty system, that might as well be completely scrapped, and general balance problems with the action economy that lead one of the characters to carry the whole team.Despite that the game is quite fun at times and I was struggling to decide whether to leave a positive or negative review, but the deciding factor was the fact that the gameplay simply becomes boring. There is minimal variety to the missions and most importantly challenges that you can do within those missions. The game starts to feel like a chore before you're even half way through your first playthrough, and since I question if I'll get the will to finish it, I don't recommend buying it, unless you need something mindless to play while doing something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm changing my review from positive to negative, because of the way the devs gutted their own game.HW2 was a challenging but manageable game that now got turned into a bland mush where everyone can be a winner, no thinking required. They have removed mission objectives and nerfed pretty much every enemy that required more finesse than "shoot at it with gun".Also, you can no longer play on the original difficulty settings, they just straight up lowered the difficulty across the board.Unless you already finished the game, you can never experience the original game again.This was my original review:"Hard West 2 is an excellent turn based tactics game with unique mechanics, a cool setting, great characters, an okay story and some annoying jankiness.Despite what every second negative review keeps parroting, this is not a "puzzle game" nor do you have to find out the perfect team/gear combo for every mission by trial and error and endless reloads. There are multiple ways to approach each fight and they will all work as long as you are smart and use the resources at hand.On the other hand, if your enjoyment for turn based tactics games comes from playing XCOM by overwatch creeping after disabling turn timers, you are going to have a bad time.The game rewards aggression, creative thinking and comboing your characters weapons, items and abilities to win against overwhelming odds. This fits with the narrative of the characters being cursed but powerful outcasts in pursuit of an impossible to attain goal.The setting is great and I liked the characters, although I liked the darker atmosphere and the crazier characters of the first one more. More enemy variety would be nice, but the focus is on killing everything before they could act anyways.Overall it's a very unique, very dynamic turn based tactics game which really makes you feel like a wild west action hero. I hope we get a third one, I will be there to buy it."

_childDocuments_.review: They took the best parts of Hard West (setting, luck system, presentation, cards) and made a much better game.  Bravo.  The 'puzzle tactics' debate is a non debate.  Every tactics game is a puzzle game in the sense that you are always looking for the most optimal way to win a fight.  The only question that matters is: is it a good tactics game?  Do you have lots of options?  How good is the difficulty curve?  The narrative?  Presentation?  World building?  The most important thing: the combat is great, fresh and fast.  I feel that the Bravado system and always moving forward regaining action points takes a page from the Gears Tactics book, which is fantastic.  Your posse of characters are tools more then anything else that you use in synergy to inflict devastating looses on the enemy.  And you will need all of them.  The game is hard and the enemy diverse and plentiful, which is great.  The story does a good job of keeping the game flowing.  Its weird west all the way and that is what we are here for.  Beautiful presentation, from the cards to the overworld to the event vignettes.  You move in the world map, encounter events, take on quests, fight battles, gain loot, all the while upgrading your posse and equipping better weapons, trinkllets and consumables, as you progress the story (getting your soul back from the devil Mamon) and fight ever more difficult battles against a plethora of otherwordly creatures, from Revenant to Wendigo.  Its an excellet tactis game in an unique setting with a beautiful presentation at only 20 bucks.  The math is clear.

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly recommend this game for anyone who enjoys tactical RPG's. Every level is a multitude of puzzles on "how to most efficiently win" yet can still be taken slower if you're not interested in the more strategic side of the game. The Bravado system (a character gets all action points back when they make a kill) is pretty unique in it's implementation and allows for you to take on large amounts of enemies without being overwhelmed or bogged down with lots of turns of smashing level 2 goblins.The "Card" system is an interesting and also unique way to juggle character abilities. Though some characters (Deer) benefit significantly more from their abilities than others. A bit more balancing here would make for more difficult decisions on who needs what abilities in the early game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: Save scum simulator but still funAll those people that are saying this is a "puzzle shooter" are kind of right. I completed the game in middle (in-game it's called hard) difficulty and I have had to save scum so much to be able to win these missions and complete at least some of the side objectives within them.The best things about this game:- Western setting? Yes please!- Pretty cool character design, though I mainly stuck with 4 characters out of the 6 available throughout most of my game time.- Voice acting is awesome. Flynn's voice actor killed it.- The gunplay is solid when you're not forced to save-load-die-load-die-load-die-load. It is comparable to XCOM but there is no permadeath, the % hit chance are better designed imo (Most of the time it's either 0, 25%, 50%, 75% or 100%) which allows you to (mostly) make informed decisions and risks without too many variables and complications (this is different at the hardest difficulty). You also get much fewer "buillshit" moments compared to XCOM. Much, much fewer. - The bravado system is awesome; every time you last hit an enemy, your action points are restored to full and you can take another turn. Allows for creative combos and cool sequences, especially towards the end game, where you can John Wick an entire section of a level in one turn. - The RPG elements and level-up system is unique and adds some very good flavour to non-combat gameplay. Your characters in the end-game feel much stronger than when you're first starting out, and it feels well-earned.- The weapons are, imo, so well designed. Some of them are very powerful at first glance but have drawbacks, and it becomes about balancing risk and reward. For example, you can shoot most weapons more than once per turn, and the average damage for a firearm is between 6-8. There is a rifle that shoots for 13 damage, but you can only use it once per turn, meaning that you cannot execute combos with it alone. - Similarly, the trinkets are pretty cool too. Many of give you more than just stats, but will force you to change your playstyle with the relevant character.- Although there are minor bugs here and there, I didn't encounter anything major or game-breaking. It sucks that this needs to be included as a pro, but in the age where 50% of indie and mid-sized games release in early access and AAA games are fully released in broken states, I thought this might inform any potential buyer's decision.The bad things about this game:- About 40% of the levels have time limits. This is quite subjective, but if I am playing a tactical shooter, I want to take my time, plan things out, and execute my plan methodically. On the flip-side, the bravado system does play into time limits in that it helps you beat them.- Save scumming is not optional. You have no way of anticipating where enemies will spawn (levels are divided into sections and enemies spawn in them when one of your characters crosses an invisible threshold in the map), and some main or side objectives will appear in the middle of the mission forcing you to change your focus and ruining your plan. Sometimes you'll need to restart a mission with a different loadout/characters or wait until you get better equipment. This could also be interpreted that levels keep you on your toes and gameplay is dynamic; it depends on how you like to enjoy your games. Personally, I don't like that. - I tried to follow the story but lost interest halfway through. Can be a bit text-heavy without the writing being good enough to justify that. Some sections of the writing are below average, though it was mostly average.- Though the contents of the game are solid, it is a little short. That being said, I'd much rather a functioning and fun short game over a long but boring one.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda mixed bag, but it's not 99% hit simulator, so it's a recommendation.Total gameplay length is kinda short, roughly 25h to clear normal in 1st try.Story wise, not too interesting, compare to hard west 1.For gameplay, bravedo system and reworked(?) hit chances/accuracy system adds a lot of choices to make in combat, which makes things even more interesting. Most of the time when you reload a save, you try a completely new approach on that turn, and not (really) trying to get that 50% chance to hit somehow.Equipment and inventory's kinda OK, there won't be enough "best" equipment of one kind for everyone, so rotating equipment types around characters still very decent.Map designs and enemies are OK, it gets more difficult and challenging later on, but with bravedo and ricochet mechanic, it's kinda fun to try out different approaches.Overall, it's still a good take from hard west 1. Not falls too short behind, but still really fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely surprise! Well done game for a somewhat different approach to turn based games. If you are a hard core x-com fan, you might have some problems playing this as this games rewards aggresion, tactical spread of kills and chaining everything between your characters. No overwatch, no defensive playstyle. I love this (as much as I love the x com series). There is also a significant reduction in luck based encounters, almost everything could be planned for so no luck is required (exceot for the hardest difficulty) - Lust is a resource in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Hard West II marries narrative and gameplay in a very accessible way. It’s not a by-the-numbers role playing game where you spend hours talking to non-player characters, exploring every nook-and-cranny of a huge open world. Instead, there’s more of an abstraction here, which suits the game perfectly. Most of what goes on outside of combat happens through text vignettes and dialogs, from character interactions to side-quests and exploration. To that end, there’s a lot of transparency here from a gameplay perspective. You always know what’s at stake; what supplies you’re gunning for, and what’s waiting at the end of the rainbow. You’re strategizing. You’re customizing your posse, getting them ready for action. It sort of feels like every other big role playing game you’ve ever played -- just distilled down to the important parts. Progress happens in big leaps, as opposed to a 200-hour churn where you need to meditate and write a backstory for every experience point you earn.Regardless, all of it is still in service of the real meat-and-potatoes of Hard West II: the tactical combat that takes place every time you cross paths with another set of ™. The design behind the combat is all about speed and succinctness. Like taking a warm machete through butter. The main attraction being that every time you finish off an enemy, you get to go again -- potentially turning a series of short exchanges into one long marathon of killing, where movement is as important as shooting. It’s basically the developers doubling down on their own principles -- giving you a game that tells its stories in big strides. I love it. Highly recommended, especially if you enjoyed the first game or think the occult western theme sounds exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Hard West 2 is technically a sequel, though you won’t see most of the characters from I mentioned here; however, the events did happen and are referenced. 2 revamps the gameplay, makes it more streamlined, adds more background to your posse and plays a lot with the abilities. It ends up being a fantastic game.   7.5/10Great western music with some fantastic soundtracks. Voice acting was really solid. Gunfire sounds were great. 8/10I honestly didn’t expect the game to look this good. Loading screens with the different weapons are simply amazing with the level of detail they have. The game has some amazing artwork which is explored during transitions or in cutscenes. 8/10Much better than Hard West 1. First, you have an actual posse with stories and motivations. You can develop their friendship to access new powers and learn more about them. Second, the card system was changed, now they add passive benefits and when combining certain cards, your team members gains access to their personal skills. Third, many more changes, but the game is a vast improvement.The only downside is near the end, where enemies can spawn around you just after you finished all your movements, and they get their free turn. So keep those saves in handy. 8/10I really enjoyed the story in Hard West 1 and how everything was connected. In this case, Hard West 2 follows one posse as they struggle to return their souls. It’s much more streamlined and linear, there isn’t much space for replayability unless you want to 100% everything and experience all dialogues with your companions. This however, works really well. It’s one connected story, flowing from heist to heist, with an ending that I did not see coming. And one that screams for Part 3 which I hope they make.
