_childDocuments_.review: Have you been looking for a throwback pixel art deck-building reverse-tower-defense rogue-like RPG with persistent old-school XCOM basebuilding elements and a grimdark story that feels inspired by the Dark Souls series and a totally awesome retro chiptune soundtrack?I wasn't either, but the game is really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously a rogue-lite, and it's a great one.I got bored of Slay the Spire after like 20 hours, and I'm already at like 60 hours now (was playing offline a while). Comparisons can probably be made, but everything about this is better than that snooze fest. It's styled like an old school RPG, except you don't have to think about each boring fight (it plays itself out based on your preparations), you just think about your next piece of armor or weapon to equip, and the loop is the map, which you build as you go. There are strategies on the map/cards you play, many hidden secrets and combinations to uncover, and a TON of things "back at camp" to upgrade, which keeps you involved and actually progresses/unlocks a fairly interesting and entertaining STORYLINE, which I think is what most rogue-lites lack. It's not a huge amount of dialogue, but enough to really make this game feel like more than other rogue-lites do, know what I mean?I have 25/50 achievements at about 60 hours so far (was playing offline). So it's probably at least 100 hours worth. THE MUSIC IS FRICKIN GREAT! AND THEY ARE ADDING MORE STUFF TOO??! So buy it, but maybe you should wait a minute before you start playing it to have, I'm not sure I'll return for updates once I finish this build. I think 100-150 hours is about right for this and then I'll probably be bored of it. At a certain point you can just let the loop play itself each time, at least for the Rogue character, so there can be some waiting, once you have the good equipment you like. You can still affect the game a little, and need to be mindful about the difficulty as it increases each loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop hero is a fairly unique game that does a good job introducing you to the concepts and then throws you in the deep end. Each level is increasingly harder but it keeps you coming back for more punishment. The classes all play differently and really have a nice feel to them. There only gameplay critique I have for the game is better explanations and tool tips on things to make figuring out what is going on in the town a little easier. For instance you can't hover over orbs in the build menu to see what they're called to look them up or anything. You just have to know what that icon is. You can tell the story is definitely written by a non-native English speaker or translated because some of the dialog seems a little odd in the phrasing. It doesn't really take away from the story but it has some interesting moments. Other than that the game is definitely worth the money and has a lot of replay value for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I've changed an initial negative to a positive, so that's something, but I will voice some strong reservations about this game and some of the choices the developers made in general and in the early game in particular.In short, the early game is not enjoyable. While the characters are, for story reasons, expected to have limited understanding of their situation and the rules of the new world, the same apparently applies to the player. Nothing is explained in game, and very little is documented. Everything important is discovered through trial and error and the interactions between different mechanics are not transparent in the slightest. Even after unlocking the encyclopedia and the library upgrade that allows me to spend items to unlock extra lore, the amount of information on stuff is woefully inadequate. This leads to an illusion of missing player agency. The biggest methods of interacting with the world, deck choices and tile placement, are not well introduced (and the obfuscation of one hinders understanding of the other) resulting in a feeling of randomness and helplessness that I get plenty of in my corporate wage-slavery day job.The first 6 hours of this game are bad, unquestionably, so why did I switch to positive? The feeling of progression is pretty compelling, and the mechanics are deep enough (once you begin to realize what they even are) to make you think despite the initial feeling of powerlessness and random cluelessness. I like the transformative possibilities of tiles that interact with each other, and I like the story so far.\The art and the music are horrendous. I play it muted and try to look at the screen as little as possible (preferring instead to look at NGU Idle, to give you an idea of how bad it is) during my play sessions. On the other hand, lots of people seem to eat up that pixelated crap because it reminds them of their childhood so YMMV on that. As for me, I had plenty of pixelated chiptunesy games back in the nineties, thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most novel rogue-lite games I've ever played. If you like the genre, get this one. It's got a cool twist too, so go in blind. Try lots of different combinations of cards, you never know what might happen when some are placed close to each other (pay close attention to flavor text). Source: Trust me, bro. It's good.

_childDocuments_.review: Loop hero is one heck of a game. I truly enjoy the dark fantasy vibe to it. The pixel graphics are extremely well done and the CRT filter is a nice touch, but can be turned off if you prefer. I like unlocking and reading the lore, and the music captures the feel of the game very well. Gameplay can sometimes get repetitive, and may try the patience of gamers who like to rush through things, (That's not a problem for me!) If you love strategy RPGs, or even just want to mess around with a new game then this is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Surprising game showing off indie developer ingenuity.Loop Hero is a novel strategy game where the player is tasked with weighing risk against reward, while also adding some spatial planning. It's unlike any game I've ever seen before, and even though it feels pretty far from perfect there is some really intelligent design going on here.Getting good at LH consists of knowing what cards do and how their downside is compensated for with reward. There are also a lot of gimmicks which I'm not too fond about in implementation, most notably tile combining. This mechanic adds to the game thoroughly (I would even go as far as to say I wish there was more of it), but is for some reason completely unexplained. Players have to run into these synergies by chance. Other issues primarily include UX issues and being somewhat needlessly repetitive.On top of being novel the game also sports a wonderful instantly recognizable art style and good, fitting music - with simple but fitting shading effects. This game is truly a pleasant surprise for me, and I hope the concept gets developed more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay  : 7/10You're a "hero" stuck in a loop, you'll let the autobattler do the thing, sometimes the AI can be very stupid by focusing tank or adds but It works, I'd like to have the speed on battle too. The item management is ok, I think there's some balances to do : some items are too strong for their level and others can be weaker than underlevel equipment. The build mechanic before boss is great and be able to continue after it to push a little more your run is a good idea. The story will follow your game experience after each "first discovery", pleasant maybe a little too "simple" but It's a rogue-like not a RPG Price and Lifespan : 7/10The price is fair, I'd say the game can be finished in 40h but I didn't finish it yet. I enjoyed most of my gametime, there is no wiki so you've to learn a lot from your mistakes. A lot of content for a game of that genre.Audio/Graphism : 9/10 As a old gamer, playing this game remember me the old arcade times, that retro feels pretty good. The pixel art is super neat. Soundtracks are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.Keep continue guys, hope you'll release more content or even DLC !

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of those games I was kinda on the fence about buying, but I was not at all disappointed. In fact, I don't think I've ever been disappointed by a Devolver game, they just seem to know how to pick em. I love how the developer made the "roguelike" elements as part of the story. The whole dungeon crawling that allows town building reminds me of an old Playstaion game called Dark Cloud, which I loved. I'm sure there are things to complain about, but I don't care, it's a unique take on deck buiding/roguelike genres and it's easy to get sucked in for hours, "one more run" style.

_childDocuments_.review: Im addicted now and on the hunt for 100% achivements love it perfect game to both play in the background while watching streams or focus on and try to get a super good run with a nice story and lovely art, the game feels a little slow but not as much that it actualy bothers you. Got 22 hours ingame time now since i had internet problems and played offline should actualy be around 40 and will soon be at a few hundred for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy Loop Hero.  I've put in 40+ hours on the Xbox.  I got it free on the Epic Games Store, and I just bought it again on Steam to support the devs (also for the achievements).  I didn't fully get the Groundhog Day vibe at first, but after a dozen or so runs something clicked.  That and a dopamine hit that made it impossible for me to not attempt to beat my previous run (my wife understands "one more run" means that I'll be in bed in about two hours).  I won't go into detail about the gameplay.  You should just take the plunge and try it for yourselves (especially when it's on sale).  What I will do is thank the devs profusely for creating an incredibly fun game that doesn't have microtransactions, doesn't require a persistent online connection, and most importantly, doesn't nerf my effing necromancer build with every patch.  Thank you, and may you live to be a thousand years old!

_childDocuments_.review: you don't just form your character, you form the world your character exists in. loop hero makes you thrive in a world that has nothing. you fight monsters to collect different types of items such as equipment to make you stronger or tile cards to change the world around you. loop hero is an extremely unique game in the rogue lite genre. it has the regular video game/ fantasy tropes but in a new fresh paint that does something interesting with said tropes. the writing tackles deep ideas but it doesn't take itself too seriously. everything you do in the game effects everything else. you build your deck of cards with the idea of shaping the world into the best case scenario for your character. for example, the warrior gains 2% damage for every second you're in battle. so you wouldn't want to use the beacon card to speed everyone's attack speed. finding the right synergies and getting rid of anything that doesn't work together is one of the goals in the game.  if you're looking for an interesting cast of characters, indepth strategy with multiple layers, and a little bit of sim city, then this game might just be for you.

_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The key word of this game is persistence. You are going to die a lot, you will lose a lot of resources, and you will resent it, which will make you eventually quit the game because you're full of it. However, the game rewards you when you learn its patterns and adapt to its environment, so much so, that it starts to take shape and soon enough the endless void of nothingness starts to be filled with creatures, people, things and places. But this process takes time and it needs change to occur, one step at a time, each day and each night something will change, and in each loop you will discover something new.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 5 hours... and probably slogged through 3 of those. This game just failed to sink its hooks into me like so many other steam reviews are saying.Loop Hero is a rogue-like with very minimal, but very RNG-heavy, gameplay elements. Your character walks on a small tower-defense style loop, and you as a player place different terrain modifiers than will either spawn enemies for your hero to face, or gives small buffs to the hero itself. Every time you complete a loop, enemies become more challenging. The "deckbuilding" element to this game is you can customize the group of tiles you'll have to place, but through 5 hours I only managed to unlock about 6 cards, 4 of which were only hindrances that weren't worth adding to your deck. This game really struggles at actually being a fun to play game. Your options as a player are extremely limited: Place tiles for your character, or change equipment. Placing the tiles often requires little to no strategy, the entire reason why TDS games are compelling. Changing your equipment is just a stat-stick. You have no participation in combat, and are forced to watch the same swinging animation against the same few enemies over and over. There's no fast-forward for combat, no skippable attack sequences. Even though clicker games are highly automated, they often still include some active elements like perks and bonuses for still actively playing. In my 5 hours I failed to encounter a single active combat option. As you complete loops, your reward between runs is the ability to build a town that'll grant you buffs to increase your survivability in future runs. Unfortunately, this town lacks any major impact on the future runs. Take for example the smithy: You now start each run with level 1 armor, things that you'd normally unlock after killing 5 enemies that have no chance of really hurting you. Is it an buff? Kinda, but in the same way that picking up a penny off the street makes you richer. Nothing feels rewarding or compelling. The townspeople that you're trying to save aren't really even interactable. Due to the inability to really effect your runs through the buffs in town, you're heavily reliant on getting dealt a good hand when building the layout of your loop. Even with a stellar layout, 90% of gear drops from enemies are absolutely useless. If you're fighting against level 10 enemies, it doesn't matter how good the synergy between your gear is if you're wearing all level 7-8 items. You're going to get bodied because RNG didn't drop any higher tier loot. This is completely outside of the players control, and is the main factor on the success of your run. Aptly, the achievement title for embarking on your 10th mission is entitled "Practically a job." I forced myself through about 3 more hours of content then I wanted to play, waiting for this game to grip me like the thousands of other steam reviews I read. This game felt like watching paint dry through and through. I'm glad to see that so many people are enjoying it, but this certainly wasn't the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Strangely compelling.  Difficult at first, but then you figure out what's going on (more or less) and come up with some combos that work and then it's off to the races.  It's an interesting mechanic; you don't control the guy, just pick his inventory and build the little world around the road path he loops around, thereby choosing the monsters that spawn for him to fight, and placing landscapes for stat boosts--but not too many or too quickly, as eventually tile placement spawns a boss, which can kill you if you're not ready.  After the boss, you can keep going until your inventory is full (or, in Act IV, forever), but each loop boosts enemy strength.  It's fun and a good value.  My only wish were that the inventory items be reflected in the sprites but that's asking too much from a small team.  And since the player is constantly switching items out it wouldn't really make much of a difference.  The retro text is hard to read, but there's a quick option to make it normal so no problems there.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Was on the fence, wondering if I could get into what I saw on the preview. I now have defeated the fence multiple times, scrapped it for wood and expanding my town with it.Deck builder meets tactical tile placement with town management which is a pseudo unlock tree for other classes to play and it's a rogue lite in the fact that you can craft items for your loops for a perma buff. The class / town unlocks and story are the carrot, risk vs reward. Bare minimum you'll keep 30% resources if you eat it, 60% is you bounce before making it to your camp, and 100% if you do.  13 hours within the first day and a half is a keeper in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Try this game it's a really good game. It's main purpose is to be fun, not perfect, and it shows in every aspect of it.Gameplay: It's an RPG first, an auto-battle second and to a much lesser degree a town builder and card game. It's not hands-off. You might not control the battles directly but your input is very much needed every step of the way.You loop around a path, killing enemies, placing building to spawn more enemies, get their loot, repeat until you kill the boss. Then you do it again Chapter by Chapter.In between you build your town, upgrade and equip your town, meet the people. There's also a town cat if you can spot it.Note:As noted above, the game was created to be fun and engaging. If you dig deep, you might find systems which are not perfect or things you might think you would have created differently, I did anyway, but it's all for the greater fun so to speak and for a small studio, an excellent accomplishment.Everything else: There's a neat story, nothing too flashy or ambition, it's just right and original enough to be engaging and want you to know more. It's stylish and well presented on the way there.There is also an immense amount of lore to be found in the in-game encyclopedia (once built and unlocked monster by monster, sub-story by sub-story). A whole book's worth.Replayability:It's not "modern/meta replayable" in the sense that there aren't (yet?) endgame unlocks, difficulties and in-game challenges except for achievement if you think of them in that term.It's "classic replayable" in that, if you love the game, you'll probably want to keep playing, getting stronger, collecting items and challenging yourself.More importantly, more is almost certain to come, in some form or shape. The game seem to have been quite successful and the Devs said they want to expand it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Loop Hero is a very fun, laid-back game with a lot of charm about rebuilding a world that has been destroyed. The gameplay is split into building your camp and allocating supplies, which functions as persistent upgrades between expeditions, and going on expeditions, which is where you will spend most of your time. During expeditions, your character walks around a circular road and fights the enemies they encounter automatically. Enemies will often drop gear and cards, with the gear being pretty obvious and the cards being used to place terrain that impacts the player and the world. The game is unique in that it places more focus on building the world you're playing in than your character. You can control which enemies spawn and usually where, as well as terrain hazards and the like. I've never seen a game quite like it, and would absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I'd really like to give this a good score. It really has a fun game loop (pun intended), but it feels like an unchanging grind really quick. I want this to have more complexity and depth, but it really doesn't have it.5/10, not terrible, fun for a while, but wouldn't suggest it for 14.99. Maybe 3.99.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A simple to understand game and concept mixed with a lot of little depths here and there and a genuine challenge.  Gameplay is more or less "Auto-Run", where your input is equipping new gear, laying down tiles, and occasionally interacting with the Map/Loop through special cards like Oblivion which can destroy monsters/Tiles in your path.   The bulk of the fun in this game is the strategy.  You don't want to overload the board early and end up dead from too many strong enemies, but at the same time you want to make sure you're fighting enough normal and unique enemies to get good armor and weapon upgrades so you're not overwhelmed in later stages. There are also different classes with different strong suits and weaknesses, some excel at early game but become risky late game, others have rocky starts but can become gods the more the Loops go on if you play your cards right, but it all comes down to how well you balance your gear stats and how you place your Loop cards.Its hard to explain how fun it is, but I do recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a fair share of rogue-lite games, but this one feels the freshest of them all. The main gameplay 'loop' may appear simplistic at the start, but every decision you make has a deeper effect on the growing difficulty you make for yourself in the long run. Other games have you try and fail and expect you to just hope RNG works better for you next time, this one allows you to actually ditch your run, but keep the loot you earned towards your camp. The world starts over, but anything you unlocked previously can now be added to your deck of map cards, which makes each new run slightly different.Graphically I like it, as well as the sound effects. While it may and look like something from an old Genesis game or older, it adds to the charm. Each tile has their own sound effect, each monster has their own grunt and growl. Musically, however, it is extremely catchy and well done. A few of them capture the mood of a dark, doomed medieval world...but there's a couple that get you into the action with a nice head bobbing beat.Highly recommended for anyone who likes rogue-lites, seeking something new in the genre if everything else is too samey, or wants to try something with a catchy hook. I keep coming back to play, and telling myself to do another round.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine an RPG which all you can do is to prepare the adventure passively and not actually engage in it. You set the scene and simply wait for things to happen. Nothing exciting happens and You grind for hours until the game progresses only to be rewarded by less than 5mins of dialogue. The only variety in the game is passive variety. Different enemies have different passive effect. Different tiles have different passive effects. Different hero class have different passive effects. Different equipment have different passive effects. Nothing in this game is exciting or rewarding. One of the most boring game I’ve ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Grinding is fun when you're still discovering a game and working towards a goal within reach, but once that stops, it just becomes a chore.  Loop Hero has some really cool ideas and a nice soundtrack, but it also has some balance issues that necessitate taking certain cards and hoping that RNG doesn't screw you over.  That's not to mention all the different resources that you have to grind for, which sometimes require subpar decks to acquire, doing run after run until you have enough orbs to finally be able to place river tiles.  The late game grind is even worse, where you're hoping for RNG drops of specific items to add to your supply so you actually have a chance against the final boss.I managed to make it pretty far, but the final chapter broke my interest.  I could just see the extra 10 hours of grinding ahead of me to finish the game (after already putting in 20) and realized that I would get no joy out of it, especially when I had already optimized my runs as much as possible.  There was nothing new except watching my little guy do his laps, unable to look away from my constantly shifting cards and items, hoping RNG would be kind.  If your tolerance for RNG and grind is higher than mine right now, then by all means, check this game out.  There are some really cool ideas here; they just need some more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It's really, really good. With its nostalgic, retro style, absolutely banging soundtrack and minimalistic gameplay, this game scratches the itch I never even knew I've had. Well worth playing, at it's current state it should provide you with around 40 hours of fun, figuring out combos with different classes, trying to pass multiple acts with significantly increasing difficulty. For a casual gamer, there isn't much to do after finishing last chapter, but devs have already confirmed adding new content. Buy it, and you won't regret it. A+ from me, loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun.It autobattles, so you don't need to click a bunch of junk for the frequent battles.  It has a speedup option, so it can run faster and can also be sped up more with cheat engine speed hack.After awhile, it gets pretty repetitive since it takes too many items to upgrade things which just makes the game go on long.  Luckily, they have a plain text config file that is easy to edit which can be used to modify many things.  Adjusting the resources to get a whole item is an easy way to speed things up without breaking the difficulty.The graphics are retro style. This is great for this type of game.  It makes it easy to run at fast speed even on an older computer.The music is really good and is implemented perfectly.  It keeps a consistent volume so you don't have to keep adjusting.  It also doesn't interrupt the music when battles start.  More games should use this approach.  It allows the player to listen to the full length of each song and goes to different song after one completes.  This is much better than other RPGs that do the dumb Square idea to boost the volume and interrupt the good game music with repetitive, terrible battle music.  Anyone making games should learn from this.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially an idle game that still requires your continuous involvement in order to equip new gear on the hero and place some buildings.The gameplay loop is that you've got a hero walking in a circle ("the loop") fighting monsters that spawn. He does the fighting himself, you don't control it. What you do control is what gear the hero should wear and what buildings to place on the map, which controls things like bonuses to fights and what fights will occur. You also decide at the start which buildings will be available. That's the game.Most of the interest of the game is figuring out what the game systems are like. It's mildly interesting, but not actually very fun, it just sort of pulls you forward because there's always the next thing you should do. There are ways of creating situations where you can leave the game to play by itself, but mostly you will be staring at the hero fighting and deciding what he should wear as the gear comes in. This isn't fun!The game isn't so difficult because most of what you do is gain permanent bonuses between runs. So even if something isn't working, it'll work after a while as you increase your hero's power. There's also a story, but there's not a lot of interest there, even if it seems at first there might be. It's an attempt to appear philosophical, but it's not.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Title doesn't lie, your hero will loop and its this physical and proverbial game loop that defines the fun. Loop Hero is the essence of a bare bones game that plays exponentially better than the sum of its parts in terms of fun and addictive gameplay. Does so much with so little of what makes most modern games good, an idea driven game. Very neat game that everyone should try once
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting to like this game. It bills itself as a deck building rogue like game and it was recommended because I really enjoy single player card games (Tainted Grail, Slay the Spire etc.). Do not sleep on this game. The mechanics are difficult in general, and a lot of the game is trial and error. I highly recommend this game for it's pixel art aesthetics, banger of a soundtrack, and solid repeatability.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

Then this is what you want. I literally only stopped play because I have to work... it's so soothing yet full of chaos. 10/10 everyone needs this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game.  Pros: Random item gaining system always has you swapping your gear hoping for better results. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

Really pleasant music, visuals make the intriguing gameplay systems even more fascinating to learn.Loop Hero also now features gamepad support. It's intuitive and works well. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and no its not an idle game, if you're not constantly managing loot and expansion you will die. Hard to explain what genre it even is - its both a completely new kind of gameplay while also being very accessible.My only complaint is that now that I've gotten a good strategy down and unlocked everything I have no more reason to play it - though this took 80 hours so it was well worth the price. Its just odd considering most other roguelikes/roguelites you can play almost indefinitely and get new experiences - with this one, you cannot. There is a *best* strategy and there are no "builds" other than more and better stats. Perhaps if the level up Traits were both more powerful and generated unique gameplay you could build around them and get tons of replayability, but as it is currently there is just enough replayability to beat the game and unlock everything before it becomes mundane.One of my favorite indie games of the last few years, big rec from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it an 8/10.Music, story plot, graphics were all good. It stood out to me with its interesting mechanic of letting the player choose the type of landmarks and enemies for each round. There is also a lot of character customization in between rounds.The one thing I did not like was how you still become stronger even when losing the round. And the game has almost no ceiling on how strong you can become. This means a brand new player can lose 100 rounds in a row and eventually become strong enough to just beat all the bosses including the final boss with very little input of their own.There is a currency that you naturally acquire that allows you to lose nothing (and not wasting any time) should you die in the later parts of the game. So there was no risk/reward decision to make.I would still recommend it since it is cheap and can entertain for ~20 hours or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like I was playing a cool RPG on my old Amiga. Graphics are decent. Music is great. Interface is unique and not hard to learn. I am glad there are multiple fonts to use and the CRT option adds some coolness to the screen.Game play is a mix of a self driving rouge game with throwing card mechanics and loot from the game of Munchkin. Once you start playing it it clicks. Items stack, your card you play modify how the game goes, and it is more about figuring out how to get your hero the best scenario to win. You don't have control of his actions, but you do have control of his environment and the tools you give him.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The games replay-ability is quite low. Once you get to a certain point of the game it's repetitiveness is no longer rewarding. I've only put 50 hours into it and I intend on unlocking all achievements and will update then. Have yet to pass area 4, but that's really the only reason i'm still playing as the difficulty curve is from like 10 to 90
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a mash-up of multiple different genres and with that it mind, it manages to stir everything together well.Loop Hero is part idler with some RPG elements, featuring deck-building and management - minor city building and resource, all mixed together in that rogue-lite format many have come to love.I normally do not enjoy 'idlers' so I was pleasantly surprised to find interaction is required frequently enough that I was not left overly staring at the screen while twiddling my thumbs. It has plenty of complexity and is balanced well too I thought.Overall, it's a great little indie game thus far and for $14.99 or the regional equivalent I think it's well worth the price. I'm quite addicted currently so I think it's a no-brainer this is getting my recommendation easy on the fun factor alone! I may or may not expand/revise this as I progress further but, the bits and bobs I've explored currently justify the early review.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Saw some guy with a girls name stream this game and it looked fun while I personally don't enjoy games like this since it gets repetitive and boring.BUT I was surprised this one is different there is this element of discovering when you combine cards on the field that keeps making me come back to try out new ways to loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Pay careful attention to the negative reviews, this is literally an idle clicker where all you do is micro-manage your characters load-out and the placement of the pieces on the board. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The first chapter is promising, and then almost immediately thereafter the game descends into grindy tedium. Periodically the game hints like it's going to ask you to make decisions and consider how to optimize, but generally the game just requires you to play. a. lot. in order to get anything done. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly addictive game and has some interesting strategic layers, plus is easy and relaxing to play without being boring. The rogue style elements are done well where even if things go poorly you are always making at least some forward progress on gathering materials for the base building portion. There is an inevitable degree of repetition especially when starting a new expedition again, but the speed sliders make this not really tedious. I wish there were a few more in-game cues about certain aspects of functionality but most aspects are intuitive and if you have questions there are plenty of online explanations. I got this very cheap on a sale and feel it was more than worth what I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game on Youtube shortly after it came out. After the first Video I was hooked. I bought the game and kind of played for a lot of hours. (Which I usually don't do that often anymore). It was extremely fun, trying to get all the stuff together, trying new builds and other classes. The Story is strange but also kind of cool. I'm now trying to get the last achievement. Wish me Luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is an instant classic to the rogue-like genre. There isn't anything groundbreaking here, just excellent design and simple mechanics that can become very interesting.Loop Hero looks like it was made in the late 20th century in style, but its core mechanic of building tiles you farm for gear and resources as you walk your path that loops makes it feel like a reverse tower defense where you are the threat, but you don't want to build too much too quickly or you can't handle it. Pairing this concept with permanent upgrades and multiple acts makes it satisfying as a rogue-like, but what kept me playing is all the new creations that can happen when combining certain tiles and the builds you can get creative with depending on abilities.There is a lot of randomization, but not enough to feel unfair. Upping your speed in the games config files is a  must and I hear the developers are working on implementing that in-game soon. The original animation and feel is very nice and quaint, but eventually it takes too long if you want to consider playing more seriously.I highly recommend this for those into any roguelikes, and also any fan of those late 1990s looks and sounds. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: For $15 this was worth it for me, but just barely. I've never played a game quite like this with the unique "passive" mechanics of controlling the world instead of the hero. I think after about 15-20 loops it started to feel like a grind and became less fun.So if you're really interested in this game, I'd say try it out! There's some neat stuff and it's a cool concept. But don't pay more than $15 for it, and if you can get on sale, even better.If you're on the fence about this game, probably don't get it unless you really don't have anything better to spend your time on.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun deck building strategy game. You have to set up the tiles as your main character follows a loop slaying monsters and looting for items until they get to beat the loop boss.Pretty basic concept but deep and well executed.There is a base building minigame that adds more cards, powerups and classes to start with.Also, a lot of the cards put in certain formations create new tiles that spawn new monsters or give different stats or mechanics.Overall, it is a fun semi-idler to play with.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: What an interesting game. I sunk alot of time into it, and I must say, it's one of the most addictive games on the market at the moment. That being said, it's weird.The difficulty requires experimentation to play around with, and at a certain point, one begins to figure out the builds they like. The obtaining of resources is time consuming, and serves as a grind, but the main game is fun enough where I never really had an issue with it. Easily the most interesting mechanic is deciding whether or not to loop again, and the general risk management, as resources to improve long term are on the line. The real customization comes in the deckbuilding, and figuring out the sort of setup the character is looking for. The pacing's interesting. Early on the game's quite fun, but after the first 13 hours it slows down. That being said, the lull is regrettable, as I think the second half of the game is quite strong. The game becomes far more fun once the warehouse is available, as it provides permanent buffs, allowing for an entertaining power snowballing. Four Quarters put a lot of effort in and it shows. The games brimming with polish, and the spriting/worldbuilding is fantastic. I love seeing unknown teams strike it big, and they're doing quite well via word of mouth.That being said, the gameplay's odd. Micromanaging the game is often boring, as the fighting is done for you, but you can rarely leave the hero looping and idle. It's in a weird crossroads between an idle game, and a standard game, and even after 60 hours, I couldn't tell which it wanted to be. I definitely recommend Loop Hero, unless you despise grinding in games. For me, it scratched an itch I love scratching, but I can understand why someone might be annoyed with the time it takes up.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique game with pretty pixel graphics! Planning out the environment around the 'loop' and finding new combinations is a really fun gameplay hook! The replay value is not very high though; the game is very easy at the end due to the vertical scaling, and there's not much endgame to explore. Despite that, I had a great time with this game. Very glad I picked it up (despite the hype being over).
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I do like a lot about it -  Artstyle is great, music is awesome, story seems super ineresting, but it's simply not for me.If it would be more idle or more involved then it could be more my thing but I can definitely recommend it, if that idle / non idle mix is your thing. And again - Music and Design is amazing <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I'd get this for the soundtrack alone.  Really fantastic job with the music, I found the songs stuck in my head all day after many many loops.Again, the music is good, especially if you're into older Chiptune sounding stuff.  I haven't played it in many months but now that it's on my mind, I think I just may again.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I've actually played longer than 10 hours. I pirated it, but v1.0 was bugged so I had to buy the game, unfortunately. It's just fun game to learn. Some people aren't going to like this game, so beware. It is somewhat of an idler game. You can play it by itself. I've been playing it on a second monitor though. A reason you may not like it is because a lot of it is going into the loop, getting as much resource as you can, then upgrading your stuff to do it again. I have a major criticism though and it's a lack of strategy. A lot of the cards you can't use in a run or they only work in certain scenarios. It's mostly about finding the strongest perks. There are some interesting things you can try with the deck building, but not a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it yesterday, I've already sunk 21 hours into it. Its extremely addictive (for people who appreciate repetition and optimization), the music is great, the art style is great, the font is headache inducing sometimes and I love every bit of it.Highly recommend to folks who like to mix/max, enjoy massive amounts of unfair and punishing RNG and for those who sometimes have limited time to really hard control a character in a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A fun blend of collecting loot upgrades, deck building, and strategy, all while at the mercy of RNG (random number generator, and in this case, randomly generated drops).  Games can be played at your pace, whether that is step-by-step slow or recklessly fast, with the ability to speed up both battles and trips around the loop.  As you equip your character and silently hope RNG is kind and gives you the stats you need to optimize your build, it's very satisfying to discover what all the cards are for, and how to best utilize them on the expedition loop.I found myself thinking, "One more loop," more than a few times while playing, and the achievements have been fun to work toward.A caution, this game does have a fair amount of grinding to unlock upgrades in your town, so that you can unlock all the cards, and other special upgrade perks, so be prepared for that if you want to maximize your chances of beating the game and completing the achievements.Overall a fun, slightly addictive game at the mercy of RNG and your own strategic thinking.  Looking forward to seeing if any updates are in the works!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to play a bite-sized, build-your-own-adventure rogue-lite in a decaying world, while experiencing full-blown existential dread of a lost amnesiac hero exploring the fragility of time-space continuum? Look no further, this game is for you!The game, like the name suggest, spawns your hero at a camp on a looping path lined with monsters. You slay monsters to get loot and the comes in form of Items, which boosts your character for that particular run, resources that you upgrade your base with, and Cards. Here comes the catch though: For every loop, monsters get harder, so you need the Cards and Items to survive as many full loops as possible. There are day and night cycles as well, which might provide situational benefits. A standard run typically takes between 15-30minutes depending on how well you perform.Items are gained and lost on a per-run basis, and scale depending on monster type and number of completed loops. This is purely RNG and can swing between easy run and complete disaster. Usually, the balancing makes sure that you should survive at least the first 5 loops or so without too much difficulty.Resources are used for upgrading your base camp. Depending on the outcome of your run you get rewarded accordingly. You keep various amounts of resources depending on if you end the run at camp, alive or dead. There is always a risk-reward calculation to be made and more often than not, you’ll gamble and get wrecked (or maybe that’s just me being ballsy). You use resources to build buildings, that unlocks new functions of the game and give passive bonuses. Some buildings also provides knowledge or ability to craft items that can further boost your character in a more situational-manner. This is the way you progress your character and improve your odds from run to run. You gain resources from killing monsters and placing cards. In camp you are free to build however you like, but if you’re a true person of culture (like myself) you’ll recognize that building aesthetics is the true end-game of this game. Fashion is always more important than stats #FashionWar4LyfFinally cards. Cards comes in three main formats: Tile cards, tile upgrading cards, and landscape cards. Tile cards alters the path directly changing the monsters there, increasing the difficulty through varying monster types and numbers, but also the rewards you get. Tile upgrading cards are placed next to the path to drastically alter the performance of the tiles. Finally, Landscape tiles are placed away from the path, primarily giving resources and passive bonuses to the player. For each card you place you progress the boss meter, and after placing a certain number of cards, it will spawn on your camp and you commit to a “do-or-die” scenario. The true beauty of the game ties to the card placement. There are synergies between cards! Placing landscape cards in certain shapes gives better bonuses, placing a certain number of a card type might spawn new enemies, certain tiles and upgrade cards will create cool synergies that will drastically alter…well…the entire run. You might accidentally do something that gives a tonne of resources, or you might completely f*ck yourself by accidentally create a immortal life-stealing Lovecraftian horror that suddenly end your entire run in less than 5 seconds.The story is pretty cool. Behind light-hearted and witty dialogue you have a deeper story that elegantly explores the concept of consciousness and memories, and how we experience time and space. I got to admit that I might have been too engaged in the gameplay and missed some parts. If I have any critique it would be that the story can be a bit confusing, but on the flip side, it is clearly intended to unless you really do a deep-dive in the lore. I've also not completed the game yet so that might be a contributing factor.To summarize: The world is yours to shape (literally) and no run is truly the same. Loop Hero really rewards an adventurous spirit that explores various cards and combinations, so don’t be afraid to try! Even in failed runs can be fun if you learn a new wacky combo to add into your arsenal. I really like the game. It is unique and have character, but can get grindy once you enter mid-game. I give this a solid 8.5/10, would definitely be death-threatened by a magical book after dropping a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pun again!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game that brings immense worldbuilding and innovation to the roguelike genre. It is similar to slay the spire or griftlands in that it demands strategic thinking and game knowledge to progress and is not restricted by time (you can pause the game whenever you want), as opposed to enter the gungeon and the binding of isaac which require in-the-moment execution. Loop hero's strongest facet is by far its atmosphere; the music, art, and mechanics all support its decent storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a time sink!Haven't played anything like it. It combines different systems from different games.* Reverse tower defence game, you place tiles that spawns monsters/resources for your hero to interact with* Idle mechanic, you don't control the hero, the battles plays themselves out* Roguelike and Base Building (meta progression), there is loot to be had and that can increase your hero's survivability* Deck Building, you build you deck with the cards(tiles) you want to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Greed is good, you say? Not for me - not for this game.It always gets me every single time I would die from being too greedy, thinking another loop won't hurt but I end up losing majority of those hard-earned resources...... I have to remind myself every single death and loss that greed is not. good. at. all. Anyway, I digress. I've been enjoying the gameplay so far; lore-wise, I've barely scratched the surface but the bits and pieces I've seen seem interesting so hopefully it would be just as enjoyable. It sort of gives me that "building a civilisation" vibe.Good game. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't say that I enjoy it. While the presentation, visuals and overall idea of Loop Hero, the game-play...Or, rather, the lack of it, didn't appeal to me. I can understand the appreciation people have for a sort of "Auto-fighting" game, but I came into Loop Hero expecting a puzzle-RPG game and what I found was, essentially, an idler game. Which I can't say I have anything against, I have one or two in my library gifted to me, but I still don't really enjoy it. Perhaps if I could have controlled the fights instead of watching them play out I'd have been more interested. It seems good, but its not for me.The strategy felt simple and simply a numbers game, while the core "Loop" was...extremely similar. I got up to the point of unlocking, and trying, a new class and when it really didn't change anything I figured it wasn't the game for me. The extremely positive reviews made me pretty excited, but I guess I must have weird taste compared to the normalcy.Can't say I personally recommend it unless you like an idler sort of game, where you increase numbers and watch the game play itself mostly. The tiles didn't seem to do much besides unlock more resources to get bigger numbers to unlock more cards for more resources...Also, this is a stupid and childish take on my half, but the game is absolutely nothing like Rogue and I'm finding myself hating the bastardized term "Rogue-like" more and more. It'd be nice if it was changed. DC:SS, ADOM, e.t.c are rogue-likes. They're like...Well, Rogue! Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A complete waste of time that doesn't require any skill or thinking.The graphics are on the Ultima IV level.The game lacks any internal logic. Building mountains or forests increases your character attributes.Should have called this game "Mud Hut Hero" instead. You just grind items thoughtlessly. I beat the final boss on my first try with a warrior, then did that again with a necromancer just to prove my point.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall.Also note that after hours of grind (collectiong/crafting supply items, upgrading buildings which gives you hp potions and revive options) game becomes so easy.You collect/craft supply items through your gameplay which I had 83 of them after almost 60 hours. Those items can synergise with other items. So for example, there is an item called "kitchen knife" which gives you +1% base hp for each food item in your camp. You can also use hp potions (there is a grind part for that too of course)In the end I had 7 kitchen knives and 57 food items so that makes ~+400% base hp. I also had 10 hp potions, each healing 10% hero hp on use. With this setup, I tried killing end game boss using all three heroes and had no problem.As a result, you have three options to beat the game1) Spend hours on grinding perks, items etc. then beat the boss using no brain at all.2) Play smart3) Get crazy RNG (which is very unlikely)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Creative gameplay combined with roguelite elements makes for a pixel game with an addicting replay value.I'm sure you could read a dozen reviews that go in-depth about the core mechanics and whatnot, so I'll spare you the details. Instead, I want to comment on how the LITTLE details just make this game go such a long way.Readable optional fonts. A dev team that stays on top of absolutely everything possible (even before the official release). And even some of the subtle humor lined throughout the story. All of this and more just makes for a much more enjoyable experience than you might think, and it's criminally underrated how these sorts of things are overlooked in a lot of indie games (or AAA titles for that matter really).Yes it's a sort of a niche game. Yes it's not for everyone. But judging by the majority of reviews thus far, I think if you're fan of pixel roguelites, give this a try. You might just be in for a surprise when you've sunk hours into this without even realizing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is terribly boring. I like rogue-lites, card games, resource management games, and even retro aesthetics but this game is way too grindy. Progression is slow during the middle section of the game and the RNG nature of what cards you get makes it so you don't even get much of what you were farming for on some of the runs. _childDocuments_.review: An extremely creative hybrid that somehow manages to combine "idle game" style dungeon crawling and world-building mechanics reminiscent of city-state management RTS games, and the result is far more than the sum of its parts.The goal is simple: slay monsters to collect landscape cards, which you use to put together the missing world.  The landmarks you place all affect your adventure, from stats to enemies to places of respite. Be careful, as the perpetrators of the apocalypse will attempt to stop you once you've restored enough, so you need to be well prepared for their arrival. You start out with one simple class, the Knight, and can unlock two others that significantly change your playstyle.  Furthermore, the landmarks that you choose to use can be switched to focus on different strategies.There is a little bit of "grinding" involved; it's unlikely that you're going to be able to beat each stage without some retries or revisiting earlier stages.  If that isn't a deal breaker for you, it offers opportunities to use classes you haven't tried much, experiment with different cards, and figure out advantageous landscape synergies.Oh, and the soundtrack is great to boot. This game is an immense value that I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty neat game, but I can't recommend it because it's simply too grindy. You will spend several runs in a row getting as far as you can, pulling out at the last second, and then after those 6 runs you  can't afford to upgrade any of your buildings even once.There's not enough progression in this game, and so they decided to pad the playtime by making it a huge grind to get anything. And in return you get very small and completely meaningless bonuses like +3% to some meaningless stat, or a building that gives you a slight amount of passive resource every run which isn't enough to even make back the investment that you put in.They should have sprinkled in more progression in-between to make gameplay feel more meaningful. Other than that, it's actually a decent idle game, but the lack of anything happening for long periods of time is painful.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: While Loop Hero looks good, sounds good, and has a number of interesting elements, the lack of meaningful choices and card combinations really lets it down after an initial good impression. The back half of the game is a terrible grind for resources, and it exposes a lot of small issues that keep it from being either an easy, time-wasting clicker or a meaty, deckbuilding roguelite. It's a passable enough game, but it pales in comparison to games like either Dicey Dungeons or Spaceplan.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 9 hours, but I finally figured out what this game reminds me of, and why I kept coming back to it for a long while. So, let me preface by saying that I've been playing the pokies a little these days to while away the evening hours, and I've put two and two together this way.In short, Loop Hero's mechanics aren't that much dissimilar from a slot machine; its only innovation is the way in which it presents the mechanics of this premise onscreen. If this doesn't sound appealing to you in the slightest, then read no further. If the concept doesn't make sense to you, keep reading.Slot machines have you press a limited amount of buttons - the main one being PLAY. Loop Hero has kind of turned this into a PLAY/PAUSE button, but it's essentially the same premise: play starts the game, pause has you manage your inventory, and essentially, you wait. You wait until something in your inventory is better than what it was previously by checking the stats of said something. Your chances of getting something good or something bad are entirely reliant upon RNJesus, and this is where the slots mechanic comes into the fray.In order to progress, you need better equipment that you can't guarantee you'll get each 'run' with the 'pokies'. Your currency is your time, in this sense, and the so-called 'strategy' which involves you simply placing the very 'best' of your equipment (which is a no-brainer in this sense, why wouldn't you wear the best equipment to prolong the game?) and letting things kind of idle closer to situations where you do this again. And again. And again. And you eventually reach a scripted 'boss' encounter which may or may not end positively. But if you keep pushing yourself, 'looping' more and more, the game gets harder, and you risk losing all of the 'resources' you've accumulated thus far. This is the essence of the slot machine - and playing again feeds into sunk cost fallacies of the highest order: chasing your losses.Now, Loop Hero really hides its gambling problem well, and I was almost fooled for a long time. The animations in this game are tight; it tickles the reptilian part of my brain in just the right way that gives me a quick bit of dopamine. And risking another loop for even more resources, or the promise of a better item, is constantly tempting you to play. one. more. loop. Things are so nice looking, in fact, that if they weren't, they still have another mechanic that I can't resist, either: cards. The cards you pick at the beginning of the game are your 'deck' that you play with, and that you get from watching monsters get killed (although the distribution of how many and when you get them is randomised), adding to the whole RNJesus mystique that Loop Hero has going on.That you can come back and play the game and 'progress', as it were, with different 'characters', with better 'stats', is simply waiting at the face of the slot machine to dispense out the winnings which you may or may not get this loop.And that is Loop Hero's mechanics; the story, on the other hand, is all about a world that has been 'lost' and you need to rebuild it through 'looping' and acquiring memories of the past.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to be a downer amongst all this hype, but the reviews do not seem balanced to me, as in offering different points of views. My main concern why i can't recommend is this: The mechanics lack depth, there are too many of them, they interact badly, there is nearly no variance in runs and it drags.Maybe i did get it all wrong - if someone explains it to me, i'll happily change this review if it makes sense to me.While a nice idea, i am doing the same thing since my first run. Especially with the grass+mountains. Lay out a block of mountains and get some grass in there. I don't have room for a tactical decision, i just do the same thing.What's the difference between placing a grove and placing some spiders, or a skeleton? They are slightly different enemies, but does it really change my run? I end up placing a manageable amount of some monsters each run, that's it.I also don't see anything interesting in the question, where i place those monsters. In a way so they don't overlap heavily - but if its at the start or end of the loop doesn't matter.Besides not being explained properly (how does magic damage differ from regular damage? How does defense work?), just equipping the item with the highest level and nicest colors works way too well. I don't feel like i'm doing a build at all, it doesn't matter if i have a lot of regen or a lot of magic damage. Sure the stats do different things, but the result is mostly the same. Also, regen + magic damage seems to work perfectly, always.It seemed like there are 9 perks that are rather uninteresting and don't go hand in hand with the items. A good combination of both could let me do something akin to a build, but it's all weak and doesn't matter.It doesn't really matter where i build what. Did it really need a placing mechanic here too? It's no interesting decision where to place a smelter. Sure there are farms, but this is boring too: place it on the edge, done.Again i don't see any way of building something like a deck. The cards hardly interact and some seem just plain bad. I don't know why i should ever play with a swamp. The individual monsters are always trivial to beat, only the intensity of the loop counts.I can finish runs nicely by setting everything for 20 seconds and the going away for several minutes (depending on the loop count). I have nothing to do - sure i could place that mountain as soon as i get it, but why? It hardly matters if i place it 2 minutes later. The thief only intesifies this, as he collects and stores his loot.I can understand why some people feel like it's addicting. It's the same quality many good idle games have: They seem busy with progress and there are many small things to do (that have nearly no impact). And there's a lot of  loot.Music and sound is top, i also like the story and characters.So overall, i don't know what i'm missing since everyone else seems to have a lot of fun. I only see a bloat of mechanics that don't work well together and are very shallow in themself, which leads to an overall shallow experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive, and Extremely fun to play. Fantastic retro style (and the CRT filter is one of the best I've ever seen)  You will have to do a bit of grinding but you'll enjoy it so much it will hardly feel like it. _childDocuments_.review: Addicting and unique roguelite that combines idle games, deck building, strategy, loot, and RPG mechanics into  something really special.
