_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly imperfect.I bought this game due to its recent popularity. I've not heard a bad word about this game; cool, sign me up. But when the systems, after such a painfully gradual unveiling, finally gave me access to the core gameplay loop, I was rather disappointed with what was inside.First off. The pacing. Or lack there-of.The content is drip-fed to you so painfully slowly. Even some of the basic buildings are build with 18 iron; for which you need 13 basic iron pieces; of which you get 1 per discarded item and a few other scraps laying around the run. That's 234 discarded items; and keep in mind, you can only carry 10 iron before you're arbitrarily given a cap. So even in the best case, this'll take you two runs to buy one building; worst case, much more. There are artificial scarcities like that throughout the entire game.Then, there's the design.Many of the descriptions, especially of expensive and immovable town buildings and certain per-run perks, are significantly lacking in description. It's either a translation error or a rush-job. Example: The lumberjack gives you one stick per "the amount of tiles around it". Okay? What kind of tiles? There are 8 tiles around everything, that's how tiles work, WHICH tiles? Vacant tiles? Other buildings? Wood tiles? If you are thinking "Wood, obviously", then that's dumb; wood tiles can only occupy the top row of the screen, so you would only ever get 2, maximum. And, in the circumstance where I am wrong here, I wouldn't know because the building is so expensive and permanent that I didn't have the ability to experiment.On your first few runs, you will find that placing rock tiles in a 3x3 creates an evolved, combined tile of all of the individual rock pieces by turning into a mountain peak. Cool! Then when you try to do it with meadows and the ennui sets in. No, it is not actually common for tiles to evolve; there's only about 10 in the game and you'll get about 4 without Googling the rest. Mountains encourage grouping by buffing adjacent mountains; but why would I place vampires near villages, (vampire manors add a vampire to fights in tiles around it) because villages do not have fights for the vampires to spawn in on! This information is NOWHERE in the game DESPITE THERE BEING AN ENCYCLOPEDIA and TWO DIFFERENT BUILDINGS implying further knowledge into the available cards. Literally just flavour text. And it's expensive too!! So yeah, enjoy googling how to get all the combinations like you're trying to make Minecraft pants. What the hell.Then, even the gameplay is at fault...Even the core gameplay loop of using cards to place down enemy spawns is lacking in its explanation and falls short from what it SHOULD be. You are told in the tutorial to place a forest spawner down. But why? Surely placing enemies is bad? It even takes like, 4 to 6 runs before this system finally makes sense, because they drip-feed the content to you, before you buy the Gymnasium yopu can't level up (which is a poor fit thematically, just saying), so the only point to fight is for loot, 90% of which is worse than what you have, and to get cards, 60% of which only spawn more enemies to give you bad loot.There's letting me discover strategies for myself, and then there's putting no explanation into systems that you've intentionally drip-fed me in order to keep my attention for longer than the implemented content would be able to without the intentional gating.Speaking of gating. The second level is significantly, almost bafflingly, intensely more difficult than the first level. The balance here is insane, but they knew what they were doing. This is a "One more run", game, but it's not because "Next time I will be able to do it!" but because "I still need 10 more iron before I can afford the basic town ♥♥♥♥."If you like grinding games.... More power to ya. But this is not the kind of game you can win with skill. You chip away at it til the game decides you are done.Anyway.I recommend, instead, that everyone check out The Last Spell; a turn-based town defense roguelite with a similar progression system but more comprehensive core gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're drunk and can't pay close attention to your gaming sessions, this is a great game to play. The music is bangers, the graphics are reminiscent of the original Final Fantasy 8-bit style, and it is strangely addicting. And the price is right. Solid recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I love rogue likes, imo goode rogue like > AAA games. But as for this game.....This game starts off really good. It is a game that you need to take hours on hours to learn. The nyace and synergy in placing different tiles next to eachother suprices me still after 27 hours, but there is a few problems. After you used hours learn the tweaks and kinks about how to boost your chance to get progress, you will find out, it does not matter. No matter how much you tweak your gameplay, you will fail or succeed depending on RNG loot and "lvl up skills". The problem is that a round takes too long to play when you loos so much. One round will last yhou 30 min - 45 min, and if you do not get the right RNG gear and skills you will lose no matter what. When I say 30-45 min it is at 2x game speed and that is the fastes the game will run.. And when you die you will lose almost all of your so called loot to improve your "starte area".  The problem with this game is two fold.1.) A round take way too long. There should be a 3x and a 4x, and the player should them self deside how comfortable they are at this speeds.2.) The RNG balance is way out of wack. The game if fun for a few hours, but when the RNG kicks you down 9 out of 10 times, then there game is no longer fun. Can't recomand this game as it is today.

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero turns the RPG loop on its head with elements from other genres in there too.The graphics are great. The music is surprisingly good - very memorable. The story is also surprisingly interesting, I didn't play it for the story, but I quite liked it. The way they tied in the nature of the game (the player building the loop and repeating it) into the narrative was clever.But this is not a game for everyone. It's strategy heavy as you have to basically decide how difficult or easy you want it to be in order to strike a balance and be able to move forwards at a pace you can handle. It's a good game to nerd out to and I enjoyed figuring out my favourite strategies and card combinations. The 3 classes provided good variety in gameplay.This is definitely a game for people who like to be in control of everything. If you prefer a more traditional experience then you might get bored of it as the focus of the game becomes more about your build strategy. I would have liked the game to have some kind of infinite mode or something. Now that I've completed it, I feel very little motivation to play it again. However, as I've played it for over 100 hours, there is no question I have gotten my money's worth. It would also have been nice to have some kind of glossary or explanation for certain things. I've completed the game, but I'm still not 100% sure of the exact mechanics of 'pure damage'.I wish it was longer - but that's as much a compliment as it is a criticism.Loop Hero is a very well made game, and I recommend it to players who are into hardcore gaming and enjoy min-maxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The game is small and exquisite, and I indulge in it for hours without knowing it, and the cycle can't stop. You can see how the game is evaluated by looking at the number of people online now. I like it very much and recommend it to you. Maybe you were playing a game and suddenly found that it was dawn.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is amazing, i have not eaten time this quickly without realising it in a long long time. The games mechanical brilliance is only matched by the mind boggling complexity that must have been employed in making this true gem. This is not a card or clicker game, its a world building ARPG, think of it like poe where instead of you playing the character in maps, you play at making the map from scratch, adding monsters and managing your loot, finding synergies between them all, loops are tiers of maps....honestly just play it, highly recommended!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This little game that people couldn't quite classify when it released is one of the most cathartic little RPG's I've ever played. I loved slowly building and uncovering the world, managing my equipment, delving into the story, and fighting, loop after loop, for the right to exist, despite my flaws and perhaps against better judgement. Challenge God, do not accept the fate you have been handed. Rise up. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Cow Clicker with an RPG skin. Slow, boring, and no sense of accomplishment. I beat the first boss on my first expedition just by playing all my cards as soon as I got them.Victory grants you generic resources to power up your character, but you also get some resources when you die. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting little game; you might see some of the tags of "roguelike", "deckbuilding", etc and roll your eyes but this isn't just another dime-a-dozen indie game. It's a bit of an incremental game where you repeat the gameplay loop and see small progress in the form of upgrades and camp buildings (which in turn make your future loops that much easier). To try and explain it, you are essentially playing the Dungeon Master to your hero, and you need to attempt to place tiles and enemies in a way that will allow your hero to grow and gather the necessary materials, but NOT kill them :). You build the world around your hero as they automatically traverse it, fighting everything in their path. The combat is completely hands-off, and there's nothing you can do to change the outcome once its begun. You are in charge of outfitting your hero and giving them perks when they level up, but after that they're on their own and will ideally survive and take all that sweet loot back to camp.It's a nice little game to play when you have a few spare minutes. Most of the time I'll even put it on while watching something in the background. Just buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the first act within an hour. It's all about trial and error. The second act is a little less forgiving.It's not a bad game. You only get to keep 30% of your materials when you die or run away while not near a camp fire, which is better than nothing. If the game took everything, I'd just shut it off.The material gathering to build a better home base and the chance of making it to the boss are the games only progression. I find myself just playing so I can gather more materials just to build a better base.The soundtrack sounds like it was made on FamiTracker software which is very nice along side the 8-bit graphics. The aesthetics and mood are spot on. I get kind of board constantly dragging mountains, rocks and meadows to the sides of the screen. It'd be nice to be able to just "one-click" armor and weapons instead of having the drag everything. It just slows the game down.Over all, time flies when you play this. If something isn't working and you keep dying, try a different  approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, this thumb down hurts me but I can't lie to myself.But let's start from the beginning. Loop hero is an idle style roguelite game, where you place environment/ structure cards to alter the world during expedition that you are looping around and change hero character's equipment to make him stronger while on the run. During combat only thing you can do is just watch as hero does the fighting (and change equipment/ loot if you want or escape if needed). Once you are done with expedition you return to village where you can build (upgrade), making next run slightly easier. Where village building part falls short however, in my mind is at the endgame. Once you build (and upgraded) one (1) piece of every available buildings, there's no reason but only to build remaining spaces with more mud hut's. This honestly felt missed opportunity to make village building filled with more strategic choices, where one would choose if he/ she would want to invest getting more than one golden card available during expedition or maybe have another resurrection available during expedition and so on.But that's not why I'm giving this thumb down. To avoid going too much into spoilers I'll speak here shortly and state how I feel Chapter 3 required amount of building you must do during expedition in order to summon boss is 10 - 25 % too high. And also the boss itself buff mechanic during the battle is too rough. I've spent 40hrs in total of this game, last 20 within Chapter 3 and only managed to fight the boss twice, getting killed both times despite looking through many guides how to beat Ch3 boss.Despite small shortcomings in village building side, Loop hero is great roguelite with great mechanics, but difficulty spike too high for me to cross. Whether I'm alone with this feeling or not is hard to say, as only 1/4th of players have managed to defeat that boss based on Steam achievement stats (and only 13% have even beaten final boss which I didn't even get to fight yet).In short, if you are into turn-based roguelite games and feel that you are really good at strategy/ turn-based games Loop hero is an excellent pick for 15 bucks. But if you are not good at strategy/ turn-based games I'd rather recommend games with lower difficulty options like XCOM-franchise game's.

_childDocuments_.review: is an interesting take on the roguelike genre with a dash of not-quite-idle.  However, the endless grind has gotten to me and my enthusiasm has dropped.  Your experience may be different, of course.The story boils down to your hero rebuilding an obliterated world.  Somehow, bits and pieces of the hero's memories are able to stick around.  People and monsters slowly reappear, thus populating the world.The three classes for your hero are Warrior, Rogue, and Necromancer, with the latter two unlocked in early gameplay.  Each plays differently and finds different equipment.  The Warrior is balanced with no inherent advantage or disadvantage beyond extra durability.  The Rogue accumulates trophies that are turned in for resources and equipment.  The Necromancer summons skeletons that do most of the fighting.Gameplay is sort of a reverse of procedural generation.  A twisty loop of about 35 tiles is created, and the only thing in this world are your hero and this path of wasteland.Fighting and traveling make the days pass.  Each day or every so many days, tile cards along the path spawn enemies.  With each loop, the enemies grow stronger, and drop better loot.Slimes appear in the road, and, when killed, drop cards representing tiles that the player can place.  These tiles then unlock bonuses such as a resource for your inventory or a little more HP.  Or, they might spawn a battle encounter.  Tile cards drop randomly, and the tiles they represent usually have limited placement options, such as on the path itself, along it, or elsewhere on the map.One tile is a Treasury.  Its placement is annoyingly limited to any space that does NOT already have a tile next to it.   Once placed, you are then free to place tiles around the Treasury.  The game has a light deck builder aspect.  You can choose which tile cards you can take into a run.  However, your choices are constrained by a min/max in four categories, and an overall deck min/max.Some tiles that you unlock don't feel worth adding to your deck.  Why place a tile that spawns an enemy that can join battles next door when all enemies and their equipment drops level up with each loop?On the other hand, tiles and their spawns can drop useful resources, or equipment.  The resources are what you use to build a settlement that grants you various bonuses.A tech tree guides your settlement build.  You have to build certain buildings before others.  New buildings unlock new tile cards and new classes to play.  They also unlock slots to "equip" supplies you find on your journeys.  Those "supplies" are really stuff like furniture and jewelry, but they give you some small bonuses.Kill enough enemies in a run, and you will gain the ability to choose a Trait from three randomly chosen ones.  Traits grant bonuses for  the rest of the run.  Some are universal, and some are based on your current class.  The Necromancer's for instance, involve the skeleton summons.Your enjoyment of the game may well depend on how much you like the inherent challenge of irretrievably losing everything at death.  Loop Hero is not  that bad, but almost.Befitting the "fragments of memory" story but annoying to the player, resource drops usually represent small bits, such as pebbles and twigs.  About 10 or a dozen of those mini resources combine to make one far more usable resource; that is, a block of stone or plank of wood.The only time you can turn in those resources are when you reach the campfire tile, or perish.  Dying means you drop all your equipment and 70% of your accumulated resources, and apparently, all of the camp supplies you found that run.  A successful retreat means you still need to start over with fresh new equipment on your next run.This is where the grind comes in.  You are slowly building up strength via the settlement and need those resources and supplies.  It becomes frustrating if you perish a few too many times in a row and therefore do not have much to show for it.You are, of course, building strength to fight a boss at the end of the chapter.  The boss battle is ONLY triggered IF you have filled up enough of the map AND reach the campfire tile.  It becomes clear in later chapters that you will need to fill in more and more of the map to trigger the boss, and presumably the entire map for the final one.Thus, a player in the late stages will often find themselves deep on a long run pressing to the chapter's boss, only to find their hero dead and most of that work lost.If you can stand that sort of frustration, great.  If not, you might want to take a pass on this game.Another annoyance is that it takes to about the start of Chapter 2 to unlock an encyclopedia consisting of tile cards and enemy info and other useful bits of information you've found along the way.  It would have been nice to have this sort of thing unlocked soon after the tutorial.Not that what you are given is all that useful.  Tiles have various synergies that are  hinted at in the limited space granted for text on the cards.Graphics are decidedly retro, with pixelated art and a half-grey palette.  This combination fits the story, mists of memory and all, but sometimes makes it difficult to tell what map tile is which and which enemies are on the map.Music is equally retro and chiptune-ish.  However, as my enthusiasm for the whole game dropped, I decided to mute the music and listen to my backlog of podcasts while playing.  That added a few hours of gameplay, but not enough to sustain my attention with this game long enough to finish it.One excellent quality of life feature as of January 2022 is a game speed slider up to 4x.  This only affects travel, not the battles themselves (which are mercifully quick, anyway), but does help lessen the tedium a little.This is another game that makes me wish Steam had a "meh" or "neutral" review flag.  Loop Hero is definitely an unique take on an RNG-based game, but it also has a lot of potential for frustrating the player.  If you do buy this, try to last long enough to explore the second and third hero classes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game to play while listening to an audiobook or podcast. Simply playing would feel like a waste of time, but combining it with something else works great. The game is pretty grindy and stat-based so in order to progress you have to go through multiple farming loops to upgrade your character. Knowing the deck and the effects of each card, as well as how to place them to get the most out of them does help, but there still seems to be a purely stat-based threshold that you need to reach to overcome the next boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that gives back just as much as you put in.If you want an idle game to play while you're in a discord vc, it can serve as that quite nicely. If you want to meticulously plan out every action and combat, it'll reward you for doing so. It's surprisingly complex, but careful enough to not appear overwhelming at first. Very easy to fall into not unlike a late night wiki dive.Simply lovely art style and visual design, very much enjoyed the crunchy CRT filter. The soundtrack is an absolute bop. The dyslexia friendly fonts are extremely appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game that is meant for people who like stats.If you're not a fan of trying to figure out how to arrange tiles to maximize resources, keep your health up; and max out any stat buffs. While checking out gear and building your hero to how you think will benefit them most for each loop. This won't be for you.It's a rogue styled game so it's repetitive by nature. You'll unlock new heroes and tiles that'll spice up later runs; but not by a ton. The things have kept me interested and playing is that I love to figure out new ways to arrange the tiles to aide my play style. I like to mess with new builds to see which ones are more effective. And how each tile interacts with other tiles and the world is so cool!Placing tiles near others and watching a reaction happen is by far the most fun.This game is designed for a specific kind of person, so look through other reviews and see if you like the sound of what everyone is saying. If you're iffy on it wait for a sale, watch gameplay online, ask a friend if they have it so you can try; or just don't buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most addicting game I've ever played. At first it feels like it shouldn't be engaging at all as the game at it's just a auto-runner with a D&D skin over it but the thing is, that's not what the actual game play truly is. The real game is you doing everything you can to make sure your little adventurer endlessly running the loop stays alive and gets as many resources as possible. You dictate the world itself through cards in a deck built before a run which means YOU decide how hard a run gets. You can't just let this game run in the background, you have to be paying attention to everything happening on screen. This game is so addicting because you can easily see every mistake you make, every time a run fails it feels like your fault because you have a massive amount of control over how things play out. This isn't even getting into the camp you slowly build up between runs were you can unlock new classes for the adventurer and new cards to put into your deck. This is all wrapped in a good premise about a litch who basically erases the entire world and now you have to find a way to restore it and kill him. If I gave this title a score I would give it a easy 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I Like Loop Hero!I've played a bit of the demo, and liked it. And got the game, and I Like it! And a nice little perk of playing the demo: You Keep the Progress you make in it! Awesome!Note: I Recorded my Progress if you prefer a more Visual/Audio format, please watch if you like: And I will update this review as I make my merry way around the Loops of Loop Hero. 👍Loop Hero is a 2D RogueLite Strategy game where you play the guiding spirit of the hero trying to save the world. That's right, you have no Direct Control over the hero, instead, you guide them towards victory. Think placing obstacles in their path to toughen them up and train them, equipping them with found new loot, and placing places on the battlemap to boost your stats. This is a Realtime with pause strategy game, with the 'Loop' being both the path your hero will travel on their way through the Dark Fantasy, Ruined World, on their quest to restore what once was, and the Battlemap where you will place locations to 'help' your Hero. The card game aspect are the locations cards you place on the map to 'help' your hero, as you toughen them up by having them fight battles they can win, getting them stronger and stronger to be able to handle the Dread Lich that has literally Devoured the World.Loop Hero is an auto-battler, and I normally shy away from those, but this one is different.And the Pixel Art Graphics and Incredible Soundtrack really nails the Dark Fantasy Vibe the game is rocking. This game drips with Style; Absolute Shivers.  Compared to the demo, in the full Loop Hero Experience you have more Items, more Cards, more Equipment slots, a Full Roster of Heroes, More Incredible Music and More! Just More! It's More Loop Hero! Come on, Be a Loot Hero, In Loop Hero! 💪In short, If you liked the demo, you'll probably Love this. Give the video a Glance to be Sure?
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: dont waste your time or money. theres alot of poeple shilling the game JUST because its made by devolver. there is not enough content to make this worth more than $5, and the level of quality of the content is so low that it should be free. the game is not long, its just artificially extended by having enemies ALWAYS heavily outscale your character.  you have virtually no interaction with the "game", and are very heavily limited on how many materials you can gather each loop. worst of all, you need 20 of every drop, to make an ACTUAL crafting material. didnt get 20 of something this run? then the 19 of the precursor gets trashed and you get NOTHING. GOOD DAY SIR.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Cool idea, great art, neat integration of story and mechanics. But the gameplay loop itself is too long and boring for me. It's an semi-idle RPG where you choose a pool of tiles and can place tiles that give you minor buffs or spawn certain enemies. There is some depth to choosing tiles to bring and tile placement, but honestly not a lot.You will be gated by your current meta progression and the meta progression is very slow, too slow to keep the midgame interesting. I'm at 10 hours and I feel like there's nothing interesting left for me to unlock, just stat buffs or tiles I don't want. I've heard a first playthrough is 30+ hours. This game may be for you but it really was not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is an AFK Battle Game which has interaction only when picking building placement, cards, and items for the camp. You start off with a generated map that has a road which loops, and you go around and around until you either die, retreat, or beat the boss then you can still keep going or retreat. Each loop increases the power of the enemies as well. Equiping items during a loop is more about RNG and picking the best out of the batch that you get. You'll be able to play as a Warrior, Rogue, and Necromancer, each with their own builds. Cards are used to shape the world during the loop, and items will help you but you'll need to find a synergy and get enough of them. Over all this game was worth the few dollars I payed for the 33 Hours. I'm still on the final chapter but not willing to grind more for my camp to keep going on.I wouldn't suggest playing the game if you're looking for anything with real substance. This game is indeed a grind feast with a lot of RNG on top so be prepared.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: What was a genuinely fun game for awhile has turned into pure unadulterated. I was able to push through Act 1, 2, and 3. But 4? No. That is where I draw the line. Omega is truly the stupidest bit of game design I have EVER experienced. Is it doable? Definitely. Will I be grinding and continuing to try to beat him? Maybe. Is he well designed? For the love of RNGesus hell no!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is not only a magnificent game that rewards careful planning and creative building, but a work of art that gives you a whimsically extravagant experience while learning and adapting to this strange yet fantastic world. While the start might be a bit of a stretch at first, the game alongside you quickly picks up and becomes a fun sim builder that relies on quick wit, risk, and unlocking strategies that fit your style. Furthermore, the graphics, style, music, and story all help you get fully immersed in a world of fading existence. Each step reaches you to a higher form of understanding and an absolutely fun way to spend your time when you are feeling for a little more relaxed game, or when you want to ponder and devise.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Very grindy but very fun. Kind of a rogue lite, where you can overprep for bosses as much as you want by farming resources and upgrading your camp.There are many customization you can make which make this game very strategic. From the road tiles which you can select before embarking on your journey, to the special items which give you bonus hp, hp regeneration of all sorts and bonus damage.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Great retro graphics and even better retro soundtrack. Game mechanics are simple but clever. Game itself needs a lot of strategy (You must count twice before equiping something. You must think about if it's good for early game, if it's good for late game, if it's good combo with something else etc.). Plus points for interesting theme/story of the game, for ability to changing fonts for better readability, and it's great game, when you can use just one hand. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A boring idler pretending to be a good roguelikeFirst, let's talk about the good things: graphics and pixel art are great, the story is intriguing, and the game presentation is well done.Everything else falls apart completely. Let me explain this:Every good roguelike game needs to have three qualities1) short to medium runs2) different runs every time3) progress through knowledgeLoop Hero doesn't tick any of these three. The runs are very long to the extent that playing this game on 5x speed would be more fun. Even worse, all the runs are the same because you are doing exactly the same things every single time - and the very limited and boring cards that you have do not change the runs at all. Finally, here the progress is made not through knowledge, but through mindless grind. Grind more resources -> unlock a building -> get ONE more card into the deck -> back to the grind. This game is essentially an idler because while you do a lot of things mechanically, 99% of them are not strategic decisions that make you win or lose the game, but filler gameplay mechanics to artificially inflate the length of the game.Overall, I abandoned the game after 7 or so hours because I couldn't be bothered to suffer through another mindless loop

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about this game briefly yesterday without much hopes for it. I have played about 3 hours of the demo and almost 5 of the actual game. I am highly addicted to the game-play loop (literally) of this game. While there doesn't seem to be that much content in terms of replay-ability at the moment the potential is through the roof. Some easy criticism or automatic turn offs are words like "idle game" or "grindy". Yes this game does have a grind element to it but at the moment its not to the point of having to do multiple 30 minute runs to acquire one building. After a solid run I can build 1-2 towers. There is also an insane amount of depth to this game that even if you cannot build a tower you can still edit your cards or upgrade a tower or craft an item that will still give you a benefit in the next run. You can effectively min-max and play half paying attention at the same time. Every build will get you somewhere as long as you dedicate a little bit of thought into placements and strategies. THIS GAME HOWEVER IS NOT AN IDLE GAME. You do not sit and afk for much of the game as every tile you place or card you use or item you equip will have a bigger effect the sooner you place it. At the surface Loop Hero seems to be a typical grindy roguelite with minimal effort put into it but as you go deeper into the world of the loop you will learn the insane amount of depth and creativity gone into it. The only cons it has can be fixed easily with future updates. More classes, cards and expeditions are a must aswell as extending an expedition a little bit more. Perhaps a second boss or a new map after the boss or the boss meter resetting would be a good addition to an already great gameplay loop. I look forward to see where this game goes and I look forward to dumping a lot of my free time into it. Loop Hero is a MUST BUY!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts great and is very enjoyable, but also quickly becomes very grindy. You have to figure out everything by yourself, the game explains nothing. It doesn't even tell you what the name of the resources are you need for buildings you can't build until you build the encyclopedia, and I wasn't aware that I needed different cards to gain different ressources. The game does nothing to encourage you to switch to different cards in your deck, so when I realized that I don't like certain cards, I just stopped using them. The game could learn a lot in that regard from "Hades" by Supergiant. After 13 hours of playtime, I feel like I'm doing the same thing over and over again, and I don't feel like I'm progressing in any way. I also don't know if I'm good or bad at the game, and there is zero feedback on what you could improve. It's definitly not a bad game, as you can see from all the positive reviews, but I was left unsatisfied and can't motivate myself to defeat the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Simple rouguelike game. All you need to do is placing titles on the map and your character automatically walk around the road and fight enemies. it's simple and addictive.During the run, you can bring back resources anytime to your base to upgrade and unlock items that gives you benefits for the next run. Every time unlocking items and skills that makes the game so different and gives you new experiences. I don't recommend checking the wiki on the internet, because this game has own wiki pages that will be unlocked by using resources and you can understand how each materials of the map work little by little. It's very enjoyable to understand the mechanics and how to beat the area easier than before.Only later game you need lots of grinding which is super boring as much as other rougueike games have. However, before the situation you might already spent more than 15 hours to enjoy playing this game without heavy grinding so it wouldn't be problematic since the game sold cheap price(sometimes around $5 on sale). Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A deck building game? A strategy game? A little of both and a lot of .It's a game in which you place changes in an environment that your hero grinds for resources in until either you recall them or they die.For me, the thing that keeps me coming back to this game is wanting to see . Uncovering new content and reading new flavour text is the one major thing I would recommend this game . Clever descriptions, subtle hints and hidden combinations are the "Good Stuff" of this game from my perspective; the "Bad Stuff" is how slow, empty and cynical the process of getting to interesting new things is.That depends on your preferences in games.If you like Unfolding games, indirect management, and the slow and gradual process of figuring out and mastering a confusing and obfuscated system, this may be a game you like.If you want a fast pace or challenging action, stay far, far away. The core gameplay loop is inherently grindy. It's a slow roll of monster corpses and resource collection. The amount of loot you lose if you let the monsters take you down is outright bitterness inducing and will leave you wanting to go back out and get a better run before you put it down... but it's also unsatisfying to quit while you're ahead and you feel like you . This is one of those games that will keep pulling you in like a slot machine in ways that are driven less by fun than bitterness and greed. This is half way an idle game. You sit back and tweak things, and it often seems like the game actually goes  if I do that , and just leave the little adventurer to do their thing. Placing cards aggressively can easily overwhelm them. It leaves it kind of frustrating how little there is to actually do from moment to moment, because the adventure isn't yours, you just vaguely oversee it and then base-build with the spoils. The voice of the hero and the narration leans heavily on the snark and cynicism, to the point of being self-deprecating and toxic at times. While it's intriguing that we begin at the end of the world, the pointlessness with which the hero's journey is portrayed seems to mock the player's own decision to waste their time trying to save a world that never existed. Overall the narrative tone is more a weakness than a strength, and winds up sagging under a sense of fatigue with its own clichés. The music is pretty sweet, for one thing, and the pixel art is stylish, in a retro sort of way. It's not going to blow you away, but the game looks and sounds decent in a way that reaches up into the UI. Despite the cynicism of the narrative, there are snippets of writing throughout various dialogues (especially the chats you have with special monsters the first time you encounter them) which transcend its fatigue and are genuinely quite interesting. The flavour of the short descriptions of resources, buildings and tiles on expeditions is also consistently fascinating and supports a sense of setting and tone far better than the narrative segments do. My favourite thing about the game so far is the way placing tiles in combination will sometimes do something different, changing the type and effects and description of tiles in play. Finding those secrets in play feels awesome, and offers new and more interesting game elements to work into your understanding and your strategy. I look forward to discovering more combinations that do things. If the game devs continue to update the game, I hope they will add more of these interactions. A few of the interactions between tiles are hinted at subtly enough in dialogues or elsewhere that it feels very satisfying to figure them out. Sometimes the game's own descriptions will also offer tantalising hints, such as the "something horrible" associated with the Blood Grove, that leave me burning with curiosity to see what they will actually do.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME. It is a game you will sink a tone of hours, seriously this could actually be a negative if youve got other stuff to do. With that in mind after youve played a few runs or a few hours and gotten used to the game i highly highly recommend editing the "variables.ini" in the root of the game directory. Search for "game_speed=60" and change 60 to 240 or anything you like. This will speed up the game drastically. Have the space bar ready or set the auto pauses in the game options as you need. FYI i have alot more hours than what steam says as i played the gog version originally and then transferred my save across. Doing this also prompted me to get all the achievements i had already earnt on steam when i loaded the game Props to them for good coding.

_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Nice incremental game. It has several distinct styles of play possible. I completed the game easily within 28 hours, so I think expecting somewhere between 20-30 hours of playtime is reasonable. Pixel art and sound are both well done.If I had to nitpick, having equipment slots for which you can *never* get equipment for is a bit frustrating (it is speculated that these slots will become usable in future dlc?) and the final challenge didn't actually feel that challenging. Some kind of new game+ would be nice. However those are all nitpicks, if you like grindy, incremental games, then this is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I have been putting off reviewing this game, because I have so much to say about it. But instead, at least for now, I'll keep it short and sweet.+ The visuals are a treat+ The story got me wanting to keep playing until the very end (which is rare in my case)+ The dialogue is extremely well written+ Lore isn't thrown into your face and force fed to you+ The mechanics are interesting, feel new and unique, and don't lock you into one playstyle+ Even after almost 60 hours of game time, the game still has more for me to discover+ QoL updates- The music eventually got a little repetitive for me (though good music)- Hoping for a DLC with more content (let me throw more money at you, please), not really a con, I just loved this game so much- Felt a bit grindy at times, but then again I was still getting used to the gameOverall, this game was definitely worth the full price, and I really hope to see a DLC, or maybe a new entry to this series by the same devs! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. Lot of systems to consider and optimize, but they get introduced at a gradual enough pace that you can avoid getting overwhelmed. I'd recommend avoiding the wiki until you find your way to some things organically, but you do you. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive game with some unique mechanics. Ultimately I found my self skipping most of the dialogue as the story feels low effort and it can't decide if it should be taken seriously or is just tongue in cheek. _childDocuments_.review: Again this is a balancing review. This game is good. It's fun and has unique mechanics. However, it is not a 95% game. So what is wrong about it? The pixel art isn't overly amazing. The story rich tag is a joke. The story delivered during gameplay is pretty much the bare minimum. Hundreds of unlockable ingame wiki pages with background info just doesn't make a game story rich. The game mechanics are inventive and fun and there is some depth to the mechanics but you'll still get to the lategame somewhat fast. Unfortunately said lategame is pretty much all repetitive grinding with infinite loop builds. There is literally zero replayability as in there is no reason whatsoever to start a new game. You can see everything the game has to offer in one playthrough. Not a 95% game.Overall a solid 85%-90% game with some weaknesses but that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively simple, drenched in pixel-art and sound design delicacy, Loop Hero is a game of pure ~stonks go up~ you can play while listening to longform podcasts, though to be honest, when those podcasts ended, I often found myself too involved in aggressive % micromanagement to bother to put on another one. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game, grinded it for a good amount. While it's fun and all, this game lacks in giving its players a bigger chance to explore different strategies and combos. It's extremely linear in what kind of combos work and what will send you back to the beginning.I do like the aspect of choosing your own tiles, etc. However, to beat some bosses and farm effectively, you need to have either 1-2 specific combos to really succeed. Sure, I believe you could defeat all bosses with different characters, but all characters have only 1-2 viable combos. I would also like to see items with different combinations. They could have made unique items. In general, the game is fun but becomes grindy after a while.Did not read the story.The sound was on mute.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's got a bit of everything I like. It's got deck building. It's got RPG stats to min-max. It's got rogue-lite progression. It's got a little base layout planning. It's got awesome 8-bit (might have my bit amount wrong here) tunes. It's got a dark and distinct art style. And it's a perfect game to chill out after a long day of work. I find such peace endlessly walking circles in the abyssal void-space and fighting monsters.This title has become such a 'comfort food' kind of game for me. I'm sad to hear that it's not currently being worked on, but that shouldn't dissuade you from picking it up if you like all that I have said here.Tons of strategy. Great pick-up and play. Can't say enough about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: "Overwhelmingly Positive.""Early GOTY candidate.""I've put 35 hours into the demo."Saw the Steam store rating and these quotes in reviews, and thought this would be a no-brainer buy - after all, I love both roguelikes and idles.2 hours in: it's pretty fun.4 hours: ok, it seems addicting.6 hours: wait, that's it? maybe it's a good game to just leave on while I watch videos.8 hours: i'm bored but there's got to be something i'm missing...it's rated so high on Steam. Let me give it a chance.10 hours: yeah, I don't think I'm missing anything. I'm probably never opening up this game again.To sum it up: your character walks around a loop. Enemies spawn on the loop, and you kill the enemies. With each battle, you get either equipment, resources, or cards. When you complete a loop, the enemies scale up 1 level. You don't control any of this - it just happens. That is the extent of the "idle" component in the game. Equipment is standard RPG style equipment. You need to keep the best equipment on your character, or they will scale to be strong enough to kill you. You can never leave this game *truly* idle.Cards let you place enemy spawns on the map, or other terrain. All have different effects (akin to tower defense games).If you die, you lose 70% of the resources you find, and revive back at your home base. You can also choose to go back to the base when near it on the loop, and you will keep 100% of your resources. Everything else (equipment, cards), you lose. This is the "rougelike" component.The resources you manage to bring back to your base allow you to buy permanent upgrades. However, this is very, very, VERY grindy. Expect to go through several loops without being able to obtain a single permanent upgrade. The upgrades themselves seem very lackluster, as well. 10 hours and several upgrades in and I don't seem to be doing much better on the loop than when I first started. I have access to 2 new classes, but that's pretty much all I have to show for it.Not to mention, the highest speed in game is 2x which is still PAINFULLY slow. You can edit the .ini file for more speed, but honestly, I don't find the game worth it. It's a mediocre idle game, mediocre roguelike, mediocre deck builder, and mediocre tower-defense, all mashed into mediocre package.Walking away from this game has only made me realize that "Overwhelmingly Positive" doesn't mean what it used to in my head.  I would have expected this game to have *maybe* an 80% positive rating. Not anywhere near Hades (ACTUAL GOTY.)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I have played. Gameplay is simple to understand and learn but has a lot of depth. Unlocking new tiles and tile combos feels rewarding and changes how you can approach loops. You can tailor your deck to farming resorces, fighting the boss or just to test new strategies. Give this game a serius try and you will not regret. Things that would be nice to have:- Increase battle speed ( in late loops while you have lots of fights it takes very long time to complete a loop)- game is good and if something is good what you wand is more: more buildings and their upgrades, more classes, supplies, cards and tiles.- more ways to impact item quality level Things tochange/fix- Seccondary atribues are often locked and don't increase with item lvl ( skeleton level is often lockedon 0.27, regeneration is locked on 0.6 tetc. )- forest and river meta gets boring after many loops
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: An idle game that keeps you intrigued the whole time.+ Good music. Boss bangers. Sound design has an aesthetic that pleases the ears.+ Art style is very old-school in a good way. It's made in a way that will never get old. This game could come out any year and be just as charming.+ Gameplay loop is fun. Figuring out how tiles interact is a huge draw. Building your character and testing tons of different builds is engaging, especially since building your deck of place-able terrain can decide how well your builds do.- Can be a bit grindy. Not sure if it's a difficulty wall, or a lack of my own skill as a player, but it feels like progression is a bit difficult at a certain point, and requires a lot of grinding, which won't be everyone's cup of tea.All in all its a great game to play on the side of listening to a twitch streamer, or to flex your mental muscles with decisions. The rogue-like aspects aren't too punishing, and instead add flavor in any element that they can. 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addictive in the best way possible. It's clever, engaging and challenging in a way that never feels frustrating. Whenever I die or am forced to end an expedition earlier that I had hoped, I always feel like I have learnt a little something to make my life easier the next time, or found out a new combination of tile, or had a new idea for a better build. I couldn't recommend this game enough to anyone who enjoys deckbuilders, strategy and this sweet sweet soulslike atmosphere.Bonus: the artwork is lovely and the designs of characters and enemies alike are an absolute delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about the game is great. They way they presented the game on the store page, over the art of the game (sound, music and graphics) to the gameplay elements.Watching your character do everything on it's own, manually checking new gear every few seconds and placing new tiles on the ground now and then, is the main thing you will do. It reminds me of Tower Defense game types and gameplay-wise, I had a great time with it. The story (so far) is intriguing and makes me want to know more. But I'm exhausted. I want to get to the end of the game, but I have to grind my way to it. Dying is easy, and the penalty is losing 70% of your gained resources is a very harsh. I don't mind the difficulty but the time I have to invest to get to new story elements is crazy. I gave the game a bad review due to this but now changed it because the game is too good for a negative review. Still... the grinding ripped a big hole into the fun I had before.Without sale the price is reasonable good for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It's an 8-bit auto-Monopoly Solitaire World Builder RPG with elements of Magic TCG, Settler of Catan and Tower Defense. What's not to get and love? It always amazes me when there is a new, must-play 8-bit game like this. It's like it could have existed 40 years ago, but uses all that time of game ideas and design to make something truly fresh and unique. Additional specific comment: I LOVE how this game handles looting. There are only 12 inventory slots, but they rotate out like a stack, first in, first out. Anything that falls out of the bag due to having too many items is converted into a more permanent and less restricted resource. It's such a wonderful feeling to loot your ass off and not have to worry about the space limit.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a first review at 4h saying i did like it but the game had flaws. I'm 12h in and it's a shame there isn't a neutral button. The game clearly has some good ideas but everything about the mechanics feels like they don't connect well together. First it's extremely repetitive, since it's not a real deck builder there isn't that much variety to make each run different. It takes a long time to unlock building so it means you're gonna have to grind loops again and again without much change to your strategy since when you find one that works you'll just to that.I feel like it could have been better if we had more chance to be strategic and not be at the mercy of the rng that much. I would have loved more cards when actually fighting, could have been fun to micro-manage more cards.It's asking to much attention for an idle game but not enough to be actually ingaging all the time. And for the love of god add x4, x8 or even x16 speed, after 10h everything is frustratingly long.I love cryptic games, i love finding stuff by myself but Loop Hero takes it to another level where it's just frustrating and some stuff is just impossible to understand by yourself or it's pure luck/accident. The encyclopedia helps a bit but not that much.There is to much fluff around the game that doesn't add much to the game, the "city builder" aspect is a bit boring, when you finally unlock a building, you don't feel like anything has changed that much.It's not a bad game per say but even thought i loved it at first i'm growing more and more frustrated with it and in the end the "gameplay" loop isn't that engaging and that what matters to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great throwback game to simpler times. The concept is simple but its very addicting. You are saving civilization from a witch who set a time loop, and after each day, the worlds reset. If you enjoy oldschool never ending rpgs, then you should get this game. You follow a loop and upgrade your character by auto-killing mobs and getting loot and slowly upgrading your gear, eventually fighting bosses, and moving onto your camp and upgrading the needed things to survive, such as farms, blacksmith, housing, kitchens, and much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Once you figure the game out in the first third or in the first half, there's very little of anything meaningful left to do. The initial phase of discovery isn't particularly complex, but it's still enjoyable. But it's over very fast. Once you figure out the handful of good cards there's no real decisions left to make. Your influence over the game boils down to choosing bigger and better numbers on gear. Upon finishing the game the first time I still had 3-4 buildings left to unlock in the "progress tree". Subsequent finishes were only easier. I literally AFK'd half an hour making food once I had decent enough gear and traits, having the game just play itself.The concept is good, but the implementation is deeply flawed. It's already an autobattler, so it should at least include making decisions that vary from loop to loop depending on the circumstances. Different coefficients for different decisions made at different points. FTL and Slay the Spire are far better examples of how to make decision making interesting. Maybe Loop Hero is a veiled critique of the autobattler genre itself, automating the player to do the most obvious things thinking they're actually playing something?As it stands the game is quite flawed, but with plenty of good things thrown in. It just needs a deep balance pass and changes to the underlying mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I suspect that this unique game might not be for everyone, as it is perhaps a little too passive. Although if you are trying to play optimally, you still need to be aware of when you get a rare card before it gets discarded. But realistically the pause after each loop tends do work well enough where you can play your cards and inspect any equipment you found during the loop.The gameplay loop (heh) is placing cards/locations which generate monsters which you can kill for loot. Place too many monsters and you'll die, but place too few monster and you'll fail to outpace the monsters leveling up each loop and be too weak to defeat the boss. Thus you try to weave a tight line between these extremes. Win or lose, you spend resources on upgrading your camp to help make your next attempt easier or unlock new classes to play with.The game does have a few flaws that mar it, perhaps not doing a great job at trying to teach you some of the deeper strategy of the game as you learn trial and error what cards to bring into each run. Or if you are trying to get more of a specific resource for the camp, it might become a little grindy.But ultimately I found the game to be quite compelling and I enjoyed playing through it until the end. Also the soundtrack does have a few nice tracks to be worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like an Early Access title, missing something to do to make the gameplay loop better & tie it all together.There are loads of better games in this genre, even from the same studio. Your time is worth more than this game.The pace of the game is too slow to be an action roguelike, & too fast to be a chill / relaxing / clicker game. You play the game by pausing the game every 5 to 20 seconds to place tiles & equipment. Combat is fully automated & you just sit there and watch it helplessly.That's it! That's the whole game. Start to finish. Never gets better or worse. Never does anything. It's boring. It's pointless. _childDocuments_.review: As addictive as crack, I couldn't stop playing it every 15 minutes!   Seriously though, there's something about this game that perfectly captures the charms of rogue lite gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: 60h+ 4/10 1 and a little bit No Yes, there are several including a lot of youtube tutorials. I mostly used . The official wiki was also of great use, you find it  48 on Astats No No Defeating the last boss 6 times felt a little bit like grinding but isn't real grinding No No Yes, for some you need a bit of luck No difficulty option NoBefore starting to play this I wasn't sure what to think of this game. The artwork looks ugly but interesting. I don't like roguelites/roguelikes that much but it seems to do something interesting and I like auto battlers. I ended up being intrigued by this game before playing it, doubting if it would be the game for me. How wrong could I be, it took an hour or so but after that I was hooked. A key component was to have a plan, what are you working toward. Most of the time this will be a building in your camp and when you know what you want to build you can figure out which enemies you need to beat for the resources. I died a lot in the beginning by pushing too hard, thinking I can do another loop before returning back to the camp, but when doing so you only keep 30% of the resources. It is better to be safe and return earlier so your work doesn't feel worthless and building up your camp goes quicker. You'll unlock 2 other classes in this game except for the warrior you begin with. I loved the rogue and have beaten the last 3 bosses by just using the rogue. The necromancer is very interesting but I never mastered his game style and always died before even reaching the boss. The warrior felt too plain to really enjoy, but it is a good start when you learn the game.In this game it is very important which type of cards you take with you in a run and even more important is what you place on the board, because how more you place the sooner the boss is coming. Sometimes you want that, but other times you mostly want quality cards. As an example, forest cards are great with +1% attack speed but thicket cards are better with +2%, so I never placed a forest card except for when I'm ready for a boss and wanted to summon it now, but that situation didn't happen that much. The achievements for this game are a nice combination of normal progression (beating bosses, unlocking all camp buildings, and fighting all different types of enemies) and specific requirements (Having 10 skeletons in combat, Getting resurrected 3 times in one run). You need to beat every boss multiple times (The first 3 bosses 3 times, the last one 6 times). This will also unlock all the possible traits if you always choose to unlock a trait.  None of the achievements is missable and only for 1 achievement you need to start a new game, because you need to beat the first boss on the first run. Gladly the game has 3 different save slots. Here some tips I have for some of the achievements:- You need to unlock all encyclopedia pages, this only counts for the first 3 tabs (Tiles, Enemies, Ingredients), you don't have to use "Book of Memories" on the supply items. Don't use them for that, if you have enough of them, use the alchemy option to get other resources. - To resurrect 3 times in one run you need the "Omnicron Technique" trait. I saw some guides saying you get it from the first boss, but this isn't always the case. It seems that the traits are randomly distributed through the bosses and for me, the last boss had this trait. Make sure to keep an eye out for this trait and don't try to get this achievement before you are sure you got the trait. I spend hours trying to get it because I thought I had this trait since I got all the traits from the first boss. Don't worry about the achievements while playing this game, enjoy the progress and give yourself short-term goals like unlocking new camp buildings or getting resources to craft specific supply items. None of the achievements are missable and you can get them all with time and hard work.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100% worth the price. Heck in all honesty the game would still be worth it at like $30. You would think "All you do is go in a circle?" _childDocuments_.review: If you like grindy games, this is definitely worth your money. The choices you make before the run by picking the right cards, the camp ugrades you prioritise and smart placement of your tiles can steer this autobattler quite well in the direction you want it to go. The tile placement system is really neat, and allows you to decide which enemies are spawning, what your stats are (e.g. max hp, regen, attack speed). Many tiles transform into other tiles when placed in an adjacent manner, spawning stronger or different enemy types, which each drop their specific resources.So you pick a number of cards for your deck, which decides whichg tiles you will get to place from enemies. Enemies also drop loot, so you can steer your character to a specific build which usits your chosen cards. If you pick the right cards, you can get a very strong run, or farm the exact resources efficiently in order to upgrade your camp. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to really enjoy games with a dark, very detailed pixel-art atmosphere and this is exactly that. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Fun semi-idler that has a decent amount of customization to keep the action from getting too monotonous.  Good nostalgic 16-bit music and graphics will take you back to the snes days.  While the challenge does get pretty steep when you get into a new chapter it tends to level out once you get your camp and collectibles sorted out.  Takes a little while to learn which gear mods you want and how they interact with each other but, overall, the game isn't too hard to pick up.My only major complaints are the game's randomness can sometimes be frustrating and it really ends too soon...  Sometimes you just don't get the right weapons to enable you to keep up with the loops but, the penalty for dying is really just a loss of potential loot and of course your time.  The game also doesn't have much replay value.  It's a linear story that, once completed, is pretty much over.Overall it's worth the small asking price and, while short, will not leave you feeling like you didn't get enough fun for your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This one's just not for me. Don't get me wrong, it's a very unique experience, that I'd argue is worth playing purely for it's incredible audio, visuals and an actually interesting story as long as you at least tolerate the gameplay, which I unfortunately don't. The gameplay for me falls into this very rough spot with it being too complex to play as an idle game, while at the same time being too shallow and offering too little agency to make for a satisfying experience, which in turn, makes the game boring really fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly interesting and fun! I thought I'd be doing a run now and then, for a tranquil moment far from more intense games. Then I found myself playing over and over again. The number of interesting interactions between placeable parts of the world in every run make for regular surprises and small puzzle times. There are many different ways to play and the best way to find out about them is to test things in different ways. It may take a bit of time to unlock some game changing tiles though. For example the rogue class seems very weak when you first unlock it but quite a few hours and new foundings later it can actually be very refreshing. I like this game a lot and am already awaiting an eventual expansion!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Solid!Seriously, a really solid experience. I wasn't expecting there to be an actual story, but even though most of it is exposition it builds up the world quite nicely.You can unlock another class pretty quickly, so that's gonna be nice, and the buildup of the town will let you start without too much risk each run.The fact that you can manage your deck so that you know what you'll encounter is also fantiastic, and likely will allow you to have different setups for different classes.So far I've only killed one boss, but it's very much a game to get hooked on.The RNG is fair and the risk/reward isn't toooooo difficult to measure. Though I wish there was a bit more to do during the boss fights, it's really just a butt clienching experience as you trade blows to see who will be the first to die.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great *With some caviats!!!*I enjoyed the unique atmosphere of Loop Hero quite a lot, and the story always left me wanting more. The premise is excellent and I can't wait to see more games of this genre. I say pick up this game to continue supporting the developers and encourage more games of this genre, it's worth its price.Now here are my spoiler free gripes:1. The game gets pretty procedural and grindy as it gets into the mid-late game. The later buildings which are practically required for progression to the later levels are locked behind a lot of specific loot.2. There are really only two or three reliable builds to beat the later levels, making your choices practically worthless and the deck variations nonexistent. Gold cards could have been made to be more useful, but really there's only one that's worth it, and deck customization is only really to achieve certain grind loot.3. The plot starts off very strong but gets fairly uninspired with the later levels. I was left wanting more at the end, and while there seems to be dialogue that's capable of being unlocked that might explain a little more, there doesn't seem to be another standard ending and the dialogue seems to be locked behind more grind.

I have nostalgia for Loop Hero even though it's new.I love the village progression, the deck/map building, the sprite work and music... Just, everything. I can easily see myself placing this in my top 10 games.

_childDocuments_.review: Odd little game. Will probably play it more when I get a Steam Deck to play on the couch.The permanent upgrade system is usually not something I like in rogue like games...and this one isn't much different. You get random ass resources, then spend those on "camp upgrades" or something to get buffs and whatnot. The reason I don't like those, is because their levels are usually factored into the progression of the game. So if you aren't as far as the developer wants, then you have a pretty zero percent chance to beat the first boss or first whatever arbitrary obstacle there is in front of you. It turns it into a grinding game, less about skill. Especially this style of game where you can't strategize getting past the first boss, or out shoot it or what have you.Honestly, still a great game. Devolver usually has some great games with some awful mechanic I hate, and this one is no different. Except it's not bad enough for me to never play this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: Very new game, but it's hitting a lot of the ol' obsessive-compulsive trigger points. Grind and farm! Plan your city! Take your time! Grow ever more incrementally powerful! Your gameplay consists entirely of planning; all the combat and fighting is left to the AI to automate. Instead, you literally pave your own way to victory by placing the tiles on, near, and far from the looping path your hero walks. Then take what little you can find back to your camp to re-assemble your world, piece by painstaking piece. Promises to be a real time sink. Multi-task friendly, when you're good at it!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most addictive game of the year. It looks great, it sounds great, it plays great. It's every enjoyable element of deckbuilders, idle games, and roguelites smashed together into a one-of-a-kind soup that tastes great. Almost every aspect of the game that seems weak eventually gets supported by later developments and unlocks, making it feel perfectly balanced. The amount of strategy involved in character builds, tile placement, and deck composition is enormous. Even with exactly the same deck, no two expeditions are the same. And despite the metaprogression giving you progressively greater advantages, you will never make an inch of progress without a combination of long-term planning, good luck, and meticulous equipment tweaking. Oh, and the plot, which it doesn't need at all, is fantastic. This game could've gotten by with an opening cutscene and nary a word after the fact, and instead there's a unique and surprisingly philosophical narrative that unfolds throughout the experience. It's not as character-rich as Hades, but, then again, what is? In a related pleasant surprise, there's also lore entries for everything in the game. I've only got a couple complaints. It'd be really nice to be able to pull up the encyclopedia during an expedition and learn about the world during downtime, although this might not be entirely coherent with the narrative, so I can forgive it. The difficulty spikes between chapters are unbelievably sharp -- if you're not at Light Yagami levels of strategy, you're gonna be grinding earlier chapters a lot to give you an edge. Overall, a strong early contender for game of the year, and one of the best curiosity purchases I've made on Steam since Hotline Miami released. 10/10, would painstakingly reconstruct a broken reality from my memories again
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This was honestly and surprisingly a neat idle game that I got on sale for $9. Well worth the price for this indie game. What I originally expected for it to be a chill game of letting your hero repetitively walking around in a loop slaying monsters, was instead a hero repetitively walking around a loop of your own making with quality of life adjustments. In a way the game feels fairly addicting in its own right. I give this a generous 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've experienced most of what the game has to offer:Since release, I have completed all the acts, got all the dialogue, completed the encyclopedia, filled most of my town with huts, to min max supplies. (Still haven't done any secret battles, but I know they exist.)Speed of Expeditions:I've only had a problem with the speed of expeditions as they begin. The first ~4 loops or so. Then the pace tends to pick up, as the monsters start spawning all over the loop, I found it quite enjoyable to swap out loot as it comes in, and just sit there watching the battles.Expeditions:Right now I've reached the point where there's nothing to do, and the challenge doesn't really scale well. I would like a 5th boss or maybe even a Challenge boss to fight after the first 4, as the game gets very repetitive on endless. (continuing the expedition after completing an act)Town:I hate the Supply feature, even though that's part of what makes this game Rouge>>lite<<, at first it felt like the game expected me to have supplies to get the full experience, but after filling it out, my hero just one-shots most of the enemies with 450% damage to all.I think the worst part of this game was pressing Decompose, and Synthesize 78328 times. (combined), and the craft button 1851 times.

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive gameplay loop (heh), huge variety of playstyles available, every loop feels worthwhile, diverse classes, charming dialogue with an interesting story, hard but not obnoxious, plenty to discover, simple but functional controls (two mouse buttons) Many facets of the game you are left to just figure out (eg. the Camp) and could do with a little more explanation, music is good but can get repetitiveAll in all it's a fantastic game, especially at this price
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Strangely compelling. Figuring out good character builds, functional board layouts and all the tile interactions is interesting, and the base building introduces appealing long-term goals. The story is engaging and well thought-out - a clever tie-in to game design concepts (core loop, progress mechanics). Just when the loop is losing me, the goals, dialogue and story pick things up again. I keep wanting to see one more thing!The minimal graphics and sounds feel like points in the game's favour. The nostalgia is one thing (for some), but more than that, it's simply a fresh kind of fun and more tolerable for me over long periods of time. The soundtrack kicks ass.Recommended if you like stories and board games, maybe even pen-and-paper roleplay? You will know in two hours if you're in the loop or looking for a refund.PS Think I even had some Carcassone and HeroQuest vibes while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game because of great reviews and played this game for nearly 10 hours straight. Incredible gameplay loop (no pun intended) A great amount of mystery, self discovery, and depth of game play. Really like how the game play if shaped overtime where new users aren't overwhelmed, but depth is added overtime. On the third boss now, but really satisfied with what I have experienced.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim and while this isn't necessarily my favorite type of came, I thoroughly enjoyed it for the most part. If you want a cheap throwaway game that will blow some time, this is it. I especially recommend it to people who like to micromanage and test out different strategies,etc..Things I like-Simple gameplay loop with lots of room for strategy and synergy-Amazing aesthetic that feels with excellent visuals and music-Pretty interesting premise and decently written dialogue.Things I didn't love-Even with all the different strategies and elements, it started to feel grindy after several hours and the lack of progression slow compared to many other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: great game, retro games are really rare these days and even tough i'm not that fond of repetitive gameplay, the game is still addictive, choosing between 3 classes with different types of biomes and enemy cards can make you spend a lot of free time.Overall the game is awesome, for its cost and its repetitiveness it can be a time consumer if you have a steam deck.

_childDocuments_.review: A pausable RPG where you you play a hero walking in a loop, while playing tiles that change the monsters that you encounter. It's a really novel idea, and the gameplay is interesting, but you need to grind to get access to the better cards and character improvements needed to win the game, and the grind ends up becoming too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is an absolute must if you are into rogue-likes. The game has an amazing soundtrack, very unique animation style, and the gameplay is innovative and keeps you thinking "how could I have done that better" after you finish every run. About 40 hours in and I still haven't beaten the final boss, so plenty of replayability for all the achievements and unlocks there are to be found. BUY THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: More like LOO Hero HAHAHAHA! Hahaha... hah. No but it's a good game though, actually. No gameplay video and no reviewer managed to explain that the game isn't boring nonsense, and I think the only way to do that is to describe it. I'm gonna, because if you know nothing about the game one look at it will make you wanna never give it a chance.So, the game is a guy walking on circular roads forever, you pause time to manipulate challenges/benefits (random cards from a deck you build, which can create combos on the board) he encounters for rewards by building the land around the road. Outside of gear for that particular road, you also unlock cards for your deck (and therefore combos), and story advancement (you're using memories of things in new ways, to rebuild the world that was basically erased).There's not that much to unlock, it's a relatively simple game. But so was FTL :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a "Maybe" rating, this would be it. The game is enjoyable for a very brief time, until you hit the wall that's called "heavy grinding". Roguelites should not be AS GRINDY as this it. Some grind is fine, specially for Skills and some "unlockable" items, but the thing is that this is not that much of a Roguelite (You don't even have control over your character) and the amount of resources needed for the many, MANY upgrades and buildings are just too ridiculous to be acceptable. If there weren't very useful guides (made by community, mind you, because the game gives you ZERO hint of anything, including the secret tile combinations to get some nifty spots to grind) I would've dropped this faster.Music is good, the art is too. The rest is a 50/50 toss between losing your mind or liking CBT.Also, Devolver sucks, don't support that publisher.

_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great example of how to create something fresh by expertly combining elements of different genres. It gets a bit repetitive and very grindy, but it's honestly surprising how the developers managed to keep the experience interesting and stimulating enough as you keep playing. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sound-track, fits the game very well. Art style is creative and pleasing to look at, I enjoy the feel of the menus as well; they're bold yet tasteful.
