_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, but after much reflection, I can’t.*minor spoilers ahead*The game was slow to progress, but overall it operated pretty smoothly with the exception of some minor mechanical flaws, like interaction indicators appearing through objects or walls, and one section in Chapter 4 where Ripley tells us there’s a letter on the desk... what letter? Nothing to be found. Prior to this, Ripley was at his desk when he apparently wasn’t supposed to be, and then later when he was “sleeping” he was sitting there with his eyes wide-open.It was also very amusing that the camera angles and props were conveniently placed to hide the character’s faces during dialogue so they didn’t have to be animated.The autopsy sections hold your hand a tremendous amount. I thought after the prologue that this would ease up a bit and we would be left to our own devices with our notes to refer to, but it continued to be the same throughout. There is a LOT of monologue and analysis from the protagonist which can drone on, but at least the option to skip is there. I do hope that the upcoming Autopsy Only Mode pulls back on these aspects.It was also unusually irritating that there was no “clean-up” after an autopsy and Jack would walk around doing other things with his gloves still on.As far as being a “horror-hybrid”, the game simply wasn’t scary. There was no tension at parts where a jump-scare was attempted, and it was lacking in comparison to the effort poured into making an accurate autopsy experience (at least for those unfamiliar with the process). The monologue and constant need for Jack to talk was a large factor in removing any tension build-up and uneasiness when the protagonist had a psychological break. The sound design overall was disappointing. Lots of squishy noises while you’re playing around with organs, but not much ambient noise (or lack of) to increase the immersion and spook factor. There were also parts where Foley was noticeably missing as well, like the whisky glass not making a sound when thrown on the desk.Contrary to other reviews I feel like having ‘simulator’ in the name is suitable, as it didn’t feel much like a gaming experience, but more like a semi-educational virtual task list.The lacklustre story definitely made it feel like the budget and time was dedicated to making the autopsies accurate, so corners had to be cut in other areas to try and finish it. With that said, the ending was VERY disappointing. Its rare that a game can render me confused and speechless by the end of it, but man, what the actual hell was that? I was left wondering how the devs decided it would be a fitting conclusion.I also went back in to get the second “secret” ending in hopes that it would be worth the extra effort and give me a more satisfying conclusion, but it was somehow even more disappointing than the primary ending.While I’m aware that there is more to come for in-game content, in its current state I would not recommend purchasing this game, especially considering its given price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Disappointing Journey Through Autopsy Simulator: A Nurse's ReviewAs a nurse with firsthand experience in the medical field, including shadowing a pathology PA, I was eager to delve into the world of Autopsy Simulator. However, what awaited me was a journey more akin to a frustrating labyrinth of disappointment rather than an immersive exploration of forensic medicine.The game play of Autopsy Simulator felt more like a convoluted attempt at weaving a lackluster story rather than delivering the promised thrill of a truly terrifying experience. As someone familiar with the intricacies of the medical profession, I found the portrayal of pathology and autopsies to be grossly exaggerated and lacking in authenticity.While the graphics were undoubtedly a standout feature, with meticulous attention to detail, they failed to salvage the overall experience. The voice acting, rather than adding depth to the narrative, felt like an overly dramatic distraction, pulling me further away from any semblance of immersion.One would hope that amidst the chaos of the game, the medical information provided would serve as a beacon of accuracy. However, this was not the case. While some aspects were commendably precise, others were egregiously inaccurate, leaving me questioning the integrity of the entire experience.What truly disappointed me was the game's failure to capitalize on its potential. As someone anticipating a hands-on approach to diagnosing cases through autopsies, I was left sorely disappointed. Instead of being challenged to apply medical knowledge and critical thinking skills, I was subjected to a series of disjointed tasks that bore little resemblance to the reality of forensic medicine.It's evident that considerable time and effort were invested in the creation of Autopsy Simulator, yet the end result falls short of its intended mark. The mixed reviews it has garnered are a testament to the widespread sentiment of disappointment among players, and I wholeheartedly share in their dissatisfaction.In conclusion, Autopsy Simulator is a regrettable waste of both time and money. Its failure to deliver on its promises leaves players with a bitter taste of unfulfilled potential. As someone with a genuine interest in the field of pathology, I can only hope that future endeavors in this genre will strive for authenticity and substance rather than opting for cheap thrills and superficial storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many negative reviews about this simulator slash game and unfortunately for good reason the criticism is deserved.I waited the three to four years for this simulator being a trainee mortician myself (In real life) and knowing I would enjoy it.First there is only five levels, and replay-ability is boring for many reasons, they way is made makes you not wan to sit through the endless stream of ummss and moans and groans from the main character. The  main characters voice narration is highly annoying full of over the top swearing coughing sighing and very irritating vocal tones. You get to the stage were you say to the character 'Just shut up I am fed up with hearing you'.Then there is the problem of the fact that you cannot manually save instead having to rely on automatic save which is so infrequent that if you stop halfway through..... when you return you have to play the entire scene again.The interactions are very very narrative driven and there is far too much talking from the main character when all you want to do is get on with the "simulator".The story is boring and the ending is such a cliff hanger that is is annoying, not very well planned feels rather rushed.The constant highlighting of "the next step" or item/object to pick-up is over the top, there is no ability to pick up equipment at free will you HAVE to pick up what you are told to at a certain time.Had the developers stated that there would never be an autopsy only mode them I am afraid I would be asking for my money back at this point, indeed the only thing stopping from requesting my money back and deleting this is the fact that there is supposed to be an autopsy only mode in development..... though I suspect that just like everything else the developers have done it will be a year plus before the autopsy only mode is even ready. _childDocuments_.review: The things I wanted to love about Autopsy Simulator felt more like a footnote to an odd narrative that took center stage. I was genuinely hoping that this game would be, more or less, a "simulator" for what it's like to be an autopsy technician, perhaps on the fringes of a true crime mystery you're helping to solve. Some of the jobs were that, but were overshadowed by what felt like a shoehorned main plot about the autopsy technician's real life, and what happened to his wife. The two concepts would have been better as separate games, but clashed as a combined concept. In the end, there was little to like about what was here. I can only hope the "autopsy only mode" that is advertised as coming soon will provide the experience I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- The autopsies themselves were very fun! I really enjoyed the medical accuracy and the in depth explanations for what we were seeing on the bodies.- I personally really liked the mechanics for the autopsies- The model design on the bodies was very, very well done, and the overall anatomy was excellent. - Autopsy only mode is on the way! Yippee!Everything else (minor spoilers):- I think I would best describe this game as an attempted horror. The atmosphere itself seemed to lean too much on eerie music on repeat and the protagonist coming unglued rather than subtleties that would have done it more favors- infrasound (the natural creepiness of mortuary labs and perceived silence would have done wonders for this game, I swear), strange noises, more discreet hallucinations (did you see that body just move out of the corner of your eye?)- The protagonist's descent into madness felt rushed, while everything else moved at an oddly slow pace until the very end when everything suddenly slams on the gas pedal, leading to a discordant flow of story.- Character animation for everything but the protagonist's hands felt like a lot of corners were cut. The only other character we see consistently is the office's clerk/security man, and we only ever see him sitting static in his chair holding a newspaper up to cover his face. Outside of a handful of brief hallucinations, the only time we have a character on screen for an extended period of time is the final scene, in which the character's face is conveniently out of frame as to not show him speaking to us. His movements are otherwise lackluster, feeling more like a standard conversation NPC than an aggressor in a heated conflict.- I'm not sure you could pay me to care about the protagonist's story, if I'm honest. There was a LOT of monologuing that was such an impressive mix of drivel and exposition that didn't hint to the right things and laid out a lot of stuff that could have just been left to context clues, while a lot of very interesting potential plot hooks were left to the wayside.- The fetch quests for items outside of the lab got on my nerves, I won't lie. Why is the notebook with the centrifuge information not in the lab, with the centrifuge? Why is the saw in the cellar after being cleaned? Why do you not have pump tubing in the lab?- This is just me being picky, but there were a few good lab safety things that drove me nuts; dirty tools, organs not being cleaned up, the protag taking his medicine with his dirty lab gloves (just... handling everything with his dirty lab gloves, actually), bodies being left on carts in the administrative hallway, and things like unbalanced centrifuge use.Would I recommend this game for the story? Definitely not. For the autopsies though, definitely yes!

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to this game and purchased day one thanks to it's relatively cheap price, I can agree the game probably had £12 worth of work per copy put into it, however I do not feel I got that level of enjoyment out of this game.The game is a hand-holding 'Simon Says' where your character does not. stop. talking. Meaning if you want to enjoy the surface level story there is you must stop and wait after almost every mouse click. There is complete tonal whiplash if you don't stand completely still too, where your character will hallucinate something horrifying then remark about how messy his work space is :p Too many times I would enter a room, hear an audio stinger to suggest something scary was happening, only to click on the main objective 1 second later and my character couldn't have a care in the world.The story is also unfortunately very predictable if you have ever played a game in this rough genre before, any game where the protagonists wife has died before the game begins due to mysterious circumstances. There are two endings, the more 'secret' of which to obtain is not an ending, the game just stops halfway through the final chapter instead.The only active engagement you can have is with very brief mouse-maze mini games when cutting open organs 2-3 times a chapter. There are no punishments should you fail these mini games as well. I enjoyed chapter 1 and was looking forward to them taking the training wheels off an adding in some challenges, risks, times I may actually have to think for myself or secrets to uncover. The game contains none of these, as an example, there is one achievement for reaching the previously locked off top floor of your apartment using the elevator, there is an audio stinger but literally nothing up there, you must then walk back down.I am sad to say after collecting 100% achievements I feel as though this could have been a great comparison game to Mortuary Assistant, doing it's own things but the killer is really the hand holding nature telling me where to go, what to do, and the music and environmental queues telling me how to feel. Watch a YouTube walk through of chapter 1 and make your decision based on that, that's the game.Hopefully the developer makes some kind of sequel, this game would require a major overhaul to too much for me to recommend at the moment and I find that unrealistic.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. That's probably the only way to describe this game...not good, not bad, just, Meh. I won't spoil anything that happens for the story, however my thoughts for the game are.The game took me just over 5 hours to complete, not a vast amount of time considering the price. In essence you are a pathologist tasked with looking at bodies, performing autopsies and deciding on the cause of death. In theory this is a great idea, and a great game, however in practice the game tells you exactly what to do, at every opportunity. After your first body, you should be allowed to turn help off, but no, its "Get the scalpel, check this, cut that, drain those over there"..over and over on every body, which is a huge shame. I wouldn't mind if you were working on lots of bodies, but you aren't, just a handful then the ending.Graphics are great, with floppy internal organs that you cut and remove, jiggle in your hand a bit, slice and dice, then repeat on the next part. Luckily the naughty bits are censored so you will be able to stream and not get into trouble. The atmosphere is good, flickering lights and sound effects popping up now and then, building the games scariness levels but I found that they were too little and too ineffective.Jump scare wise, there are events happening that you miss a lot. You see something out of the corner of your eye and its gone, or the main character will make a scared sound "what was that?" and that's it. So much potential in a game like this, and failed to deliver (Check out "The Mortuary Assistant" for how Jump scares should be)The story line is fine, but gets grating after a while, going on and on about it, and how he is. The main character...man oh man does he annoy me. The voice acting of the main character is very much Keanu Reeves from Wish. I just found him really annoying.As for the ending. Without giving any spoilers away ll I can think of is the dev's had a strict timescale of when the project was be to finished and spent 99% of that time on the main story, graphics and sound, and 20 minutes before completion they realised they hadn't done the ending so rushed one quickly, because it was terrible. No thought into it at all, simply "Yea, that will do...pub now?" Disappointing.My suggestion for the devs, remove the story (or add a new game play mode) and just make this an Autopsy simulator, with random bodies and stories behind the bodies, allow people to work on them and come up with their own ideas on them.As I said, for me its just a Meh rating. I am in the middle of Yes and No rating, squarely in the maybe option that isn't there. If this drops below £10 then I would take a go at it knowing you are getting around 6 hours gameplay, but for more than that I would be hard pushed to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first negative review I have ever given a game so I will just jump right into it.The name of the game is very misleading.  This is not a "simulator" game.  It is a realistic game, but not a simulation.  It is very on rails and offers the player an extremely limited range of agency.  It tells you what to do, when to do it and you have a very narrow window of deviation.  It is a story driven game.This might be a hot take but I think calling this a "game" is kind of a stretch.  It has no fail state.  You mess up any of the interactions and nothing much happens.  You can screw up the cutting mini-games all day and you will never see a game over screen.  In fact, I am confident in saying there is no game over screen.There is no reason to learn how the autopsy works because not only does the game tell you what to do the whole way, it won't allow you to do anything else other than what it says.  To say it bluntly, the game starts with the tutorial and the tutorial never ends till the credits roll.My final complaint, is the story.  It needed more time to cook.  It feels like the second, maybe third draft of the story.  Lots of red herrings, lots of spooky stuff added for no other reason than "spooky", some conflicting information, and an ending that is not an actual resolution.  There are also a lot of moments of weird stuff that I could not tell was done on purpose of if they are bugs.  My guess would be bugs but they left them in because no one else could tell the difference either.My impression is that the writer(s) did not fully know what the theme is.  Theme, in story writing, reveals itself through the interaction of character arcs and the plot.  This is why multiple drafts are important, so you can dial that in better.  Jack has no character arc, he is just "sad medical examiner" the whole time.  Mr. Ridley has no character arc and Steven, Jack's friend/wife's brother, has no character arc.  I am harping on this in detail cause the game leans heavily into it's story and this is why it fails to engage and why a lot of people are calling it a "yapping simulator".By far the most compelling part of the game is the actual autopsies.  Each one is different, with a fleshed out backstory and the process of examining bodies, as guided as it is, is cool and really feels like you are trying to solve a mystery.  It does a wonderful job of putting you into the Medical Examiner mindset and very quickly you stop seeing them as corpses and seeing them as a collection of potential clues for solving the mystery of how they died.  A lot of care and planning went into this part of the game and it shows.Over all I don't recommend this game simply because the list of negative stuff is a hair longer than the positive.  Technically it ran fine, didn't encounter any game breaking bugs, but the half cooked story and the lack of player agency really did it in.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave myself some time. I gave myself some time to actually compose myself... compile my thoughts... and bounce around in conversations with other "like-minded" gamers/content creators such as myself. The verdict however... remains the same. This game is boring. It literally has the right word in the title... "simulator". Because that's exactly what it feels like you're clicking through here. Everything... every mouse click... every movement... is preplanned by the protagonist. Like there isn't any "openness" to this game at all. The autopsy's that you perform... are all scripted... and the parts that you get to participate in feel like some upgraded digital game of "Operation" the board game. Not to mention you can't even take a liking to the main character here... because all he does is complain the entire time. He literally talks down about every single cadaver that arrives before him. His addictions... are on the lowest part of the totem pole as far as "reasons you won't like him" go. Then the end... or what they "called" an ending. It just cuts off. No finality whatsoever. I won't go into any details about how it ends... because I'd never want to ruin a game for someone else. However... the way it ends is likely going to garner the same reaction for you as it did for me... pure anger. I was so pissed when it just ended... with nothing. It was like "revelations... then retreat" is how they played it. Like maybe they lost ideas... felt crunched for time since the game had been delayed time and time again... and just said "that'll do". This is far from the game that was shown so many years ago... the "horror" aspect is missing entirely from this game. The only thing "in game" that scared me was a coffin falling in the basement... and that only scared me because the game had almost basically lulled me to sleep and the sudden loud noise startled me back. I would've swallowed another "year" delay... rather than have to swallow the $25 I spent on this lackluster unfinished game. We now refer to this game as "Autopsy S**tulator"... which to me and my community is a much more fitting title. Had this game never listed itself as a "horror" game... it wouldn't have garnered so much hate and negativity. Because as it stands as a "thriller" game... the only thing it's missing is an absolute ending. But as a horror game... it's missing SO MUCH more. So three of the games I've been patiently waiting on... "Stray Souls", "Pine Harbor", and "Autopsy Simulator" have been absolute busts in the horror genre. Much cheaper games from other devs have done much much more for the horror genre than all three of these games combined. You want a good suggestion that'll cost you $15 less?? Go pick up "Baisu"... I had an absolute blast with that game... and it did something in a game that I'd never experienced before (and it truly startled me). As for this game it was the worst experience out of the three that I had been waiting for. I am almost to the point now where I'm going in with not so optimistic expectations with the other games that I've had on my wishlist for a while now. Honest take... if I were you I'd save the money on this game and buy so many other games that you'll actually enjoy (because it's Steam and $25 can get you a couple different games). But if you insist on playing it... DO NOT expect anything even close to the caliber of "Mortuary Assistant" here. MA STILL reigns as king of the cadaver horror business.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been waiting for this game since its first demo. I bought it on the first day itself, and find myself disappointed. First, I'd say that the game has potential, but not yet achieve its potential just yet. The fact that it's not EA game, and come with the price relatively match the fully ready game, made me rate it "Not Recommend", at least, for now. Story 3/10Voice 8/10Playthrough 4/10Replayability 2/10[If you wish to buy, at least wait until they add more contents, add the autopsy (non-story) mode, and maybe wait for some discounts.]In this review, I'll separate it into 2 parts, Story, and Autopsy part:Story: I'd say that the story is hell damm short. It's like you perform autopsy with 5 bodies and you get to ending. It's supposed to be way longer, make the story for rich and add more details to the story.The endings are, I'd say, half-baked. Not show us any answer, aside of those that we could've guess ourselves. At the end, we got only a fraction of the revelation which are unfulfilled and disappointingThe horror jumpscares are more annoying than adding the flavor or relevance to the story, as if it's there because of it's horror game, with less to no connection with the story and being there just to scare you.Voice lines, however, is awesome. I tell you how MC feels and enhance psychological aspect of the game.-------------------------------------Autopsy:+ I'd say that it's not bad, but I expect more detailed action, more degree of freedom of dissection, and of course, the autopsy only mode -- which the latter is now under development.------------------------------My wish,I hope that the game could add the court system where our autopsy report could be used in the case, or anything that actually solve the mystery. This should include the prologue of each bodies, what case was there, what's their backstory.I may change my verdict in the future, depends on the state of the game at that point of time.

_childDocuments_.review: So i went through the story (havent unlocked all endings or achievements yet)I would like to preface: PLEASE DO YOUR RESEARCH BEFORE BUYING A GAME!The tremendous amount of people complaining this is not a simulator per se, even tho apart from the name it never claimed to be is hilarious and terrifying at the same time.That being out of the way. its a nice little game that puts you in the role of a mentally unstable person working on autopsies. You play through pre-scripted Autopsies and the story of the protagonist unravels more and more with every chapter.- Nice Graphics- Detailed Bodies and Organs- Thorough Explanation of alot of medical stuff- This is maybe personal: I didnt encounter any Bugs in my Playthrough. Not even a visual glitch or anything small of that sort. - The Game is very linear without giving you much options to think outside the box. This obviously isnt for everyone.- There is no way to do something inherently wrong. You get walked through everything. Again this is not everyones cup of tea so be aware that you get hold by the hand through basically the entire game.- its a very short game. Depending on how you play, you will get through the story in about 4-6 hours probably.- There is ONLY the Story Mode right now. A Sandbox Mode is being worked on.- The Jumpscares and Scary Moments are... okay at best. Im happy i didnt get my Ears Blown out by what we normally get for Jumpscares in other Games, i just wish there was more creative and well placed scare moments.- While i do like the Voice Acting itself (the voice of the protagonist), im sorry devs but the script is really bad. Its overexaggerating for what it is supposed to portrait which gets to a point where its either hilarious or just plain annoying to listen to. (The tremendous amounts of sighing could potentially be a Meme at this point)- The story had a strong start but it kinda fell flat and uninteresting the more you progress. With a Story driven game like this i expected a bit more polish. It gave me the feeling of someone having a really good idea about a story, and then just tried to exaggerate it more and more over the course of progress.- Even though the Game holds your hand throughout the whole game, there have been 2 parts where i was just plain stuck for 30 minutes because i just couldnt figure out how to do these 2 things. I only finished them by randomly doing stuff till it somehow worked. And yeah i listened to what im supposed to do, but that didnt really help ^^All in all i enjoyed the experience still to an degree where i think a thumbs up is agreeable because i knew what i was buying into as i informed myself. There is definitly stuff that could have been better. Im kind of excited what the Sandbox Mode will bring to the table and will update the Review accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't perfect, but it's an interesting glimpse into the world of pathology.The autopsies are essentially on rails, where you follow instructions and play basically the same minigames as Bully/Canis Canem Edit. Mostly follow the dots/line, and a few quick time events. The anatomy (though not 100%), is fine, and the organs look ok. I didn't expect the lungs and heart to look like flat roast-beef slices when I cut them open, I kind of expected them to be hollow. the stomach and trachea are made hollow with a different cutting game to "check the contents". Also some of the notes have minor mistakes, like confusing left and right.Aside from the autopsies, you follow the story of the Pathologist, who has psychological issues, and who's wife passed away recently.The whole game is voice acted, and the pc is commenting on everything relating to both the autopsies and the story.The sighs can get a bit much at times, and even if he's hallucinating and having a panic attack, he's back to normal 2 seconds later.Overall I enjoy the game, though I feel the horror aspect and side story is unnecessary. The devs have mentioned an upcoming sandbox mode that will allow us to focus on autopsies without the side story and less handholding. I'm looking forward to see what they will make of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Some spoilers if you haven't played already. Or if you don't wanna you can just go ahead and read this <3I knew going into this that it was going to be story driven despite others not doing so. Granted, the name of the game is misleading.. I've only gotten one ending so if I missed something vital that I complained about here, lemme know. There's a few things I want to go over and i'm going to be brutally honest.I played this game with a friend watching. We were very invested in Jack's story (although I know it's not for everyone). We felt bad for him MOST of the time. Other times we were very confused by his behaviour. Sometimes he'd just do the most absurd things in reaction to events going on around him, leaving us awkward and confused. We also found him to be really empty minded most of the time, him taking forever to deduce things we found clear as day.There were a lot of times I was really confused by the atmosphere because there were a lot of plot holes in the actual environments themselves. Tables fixed, windows fixed, things that should have been missing were back where they were before. It threw me off. Jack having to go home during an autopsy and says he'd come back later, only to never come back and the body being gone the next day?? Not to mention some other autopsies that didn't feel complete at all. The burn victim?? Like despite all the clear evidence that the victim couldn't have bound himself like that, it was still deemed an accident?? like how? There was also a letter that was mentioned by Ridley that I never managed to find on Jack's desk. Where it went? Got no clue but apparently it wasn't important. There was also a lot of things I did that I thought would change the outcome of the end: Closing windows and doors constantly, not taking the pills unless I absolutely had to, checking every intractable. I don't think that changed the outcome.There was a lot of audio and visual bugs, things floating, locker noises repeating when nothing was there, doors randomly closing in front of me. I'm sure that all can be patched up, just mentioning it anyways.Last thing was the ending. It was hella abrupt and confusing. Whether Jack actually killed his wife or not- I had no idea. Ridley got shot and it stopped at that, leaving me super unimpressed. No explanation, nothing more. Me and my friend were super bummed out.All in all, not all that impressed with the game. Between the voice acting, the confusing story and the lack of freedom with the autopsies. It wasn't really worth the 40 bucks canadian I had to pay for it. Maybe a 20 dollar game at best.

_childDocuments_.review: You fire up Autopsy Simulator and you're immediately struck by the visuals - the attention to detail in the rendering of the bodies, the organs, they're all depicted with a striking realism. But, you quickly realize, this isn't a game that coasts on its graphics alone. Let's take a step back and go beneath the surface, because that's where we start to encounter some hiccups. The UI system? It could use a revamp. Moving during dialog has the potential to crash the game or even skip the dialog entirely. The story, however, has its hooks in you. It's like a good book - even when the pace slows down and the dialogues run a bit long, you can't help but stay engaged.Then there's the voice acting - it's like a song that's slightly off-key. The performances are frustrating, the sighing is just a bit too much. Now, the game bills itself as a horror-sim hybrid, but let me tell you, it doesn't quite hit the mark on either front. As a simulation, it's more of a miss than a hit. But, you've got to give props to Team 17 - they've been listening. They're working on an 'Autopsy Only' mod, a response to feedback from the community, that they promise is coming soon.And the horror? It doesn't quite land either. There are intriguing plot threads that start to unravel, threads that could have added some depth left hanging - like an unfinished symphony to a crime drama enthusiast. Disappointing weak jump scares and disproportionately loud cut scene. The ending, coupled with nauseating camera movement, was a big letdown. So here's the bottom line - Autopsy Simulator isn't perfect. Would I tell you to shell out $25 for it? Probably not. But if you've got a chance to play it, I'd say give it a go. It's like an indie movie that's been marketed wrong. Don't go in expecting a horror-sim, think of it as a Crime Drama-suspense and psychological game. Look at it that way, ignore the minor nuisances, and you've got a pretty fun 5-hour playthrough. I'm personally interested to see where Team 17 takes the game next, they seem to be really dedicated to their community.

_childDocuments_.review: Had to refund. I Thought the game was going to be me performing autopsies and looking for clues as to cause of death and solving crimes. But this is nothing like that. The game isn't bad necessarily, but it's not in any way a simulator. It's an interactive story, not even a "choose your own adventure type, just a story that plays out with you in it. Everything is on rails, I spent two hours in the game and wasn't allowed to make a single decision. At any given time, there is one thing and one thing only you can click on to further the story sequence. There are some other things around you can click on, but they are purely decorative. Even during the autopsies, you are told what to do, when to do it and what tool to use, step by step. Then the character tells you what conclusion he has come to. The only actual game play is you using WASD to move around the building you work at or you apartment, and some "mini-games" where you follow a pattern with your mouse to perform certain tasks that is akin to something you'd see in a mobile game. As for the story, I didn't get too far and I don't want to ruin things, but it seems a little melodramatic and the acting seems a little hammy. The character does things that doesn't make much sense, like leaving the pills that apparently keep him sane on the sink in a communal work restroom. When he's done with an autopsy, he just goes home and leaves organs sitting out on the table. (I guess the janitor takes them home for leftovers or something, who knows) and the building he works in looks like a dilapidated New Jersey truck-stop that should have been condemned years ago. There may be a story element down the road that explains all this, but nothing I saw in the first few hours.If a horror story is what you are looking for, than maybe give it a shot, but understand you are little more that a passenger. There are no decisions to make, and no skill is necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions:I'm enjoying the game; it incorporates many tropes not typically seen in video games, blending them into a narrative-driven walking simulator. The autopsy section is particularly impressive; the developers have paid great attention to detail. However, it's important to note that not every aspect of an autopsy is covered. The gameplay largely consists of various minigames that you interact with. For those seeking a creepy, horror-infused psychological drama similar to Killer Frequency or Gone Home, this game will likely meet your expectations. Keep in mind, it does not precisely depict the process of performing an autopsy.Second impression:Pros:- Detailed Environment- Some of the voice acting is solid if a bit too theatrical - The general vibe and tone - Story is interesting Cons:- Lots of minor bugs       - Fx: game voice audio either overlapping or cutting each other off, leading to constant missed info about a case or other. - I've had numerous scrripting issues that have resulted in repeating voice audio, or that i have gone further than the game intended- There's a general lack of visual and audio feedback to the player:       -  Fx: There's rarely any audio (missing?) when you are doing autopsy task. Fx no audio when cutting through an organ.- I've had music looping through one chapter to another, resulting in two tracks playing at the same the same time.Overall i think the concept for the game is really interesting, but i felt the game is fumbling around in how it want's to present that concept in a meaninfull way. The constant chatter from the main protagonist is either something you will like or dislike, where i fall somewhere in the middle. The voice acting from John Hanman, to me, is just way too much and overacted in large parts or just do not sound like something an American person would say or act. Maybe this is a result of the team not being from the States, some of the language and line delivery feels more closely resembling how European TV/films are put together. I just sticks out a bit too much, to the point of me going “please just be quiet for 2 seconds”. But. I think there is something special about the game, maybe some patches can fix a lot the problems. And I hope the devs will implement some more audiovisual feedback, cause it just feels empty at times. It's a fairly messy put together game, so do not go in expecting to much.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave negative reviews until it is solidified that no improvements will be done to what seems to be an issue. I've seen games have terrible launches and switch it around to masterpieces many times before.Sadly, reading the other negative reviews and seeing how many had the same experience, it's sadly clear that this game had a specific idea and direction when it started but somewhere along the way it seems to have lost that due to something probably happening with the vision for the game during the development. Not only that, even without reading reviews it felt like the game was released before it was done, with no communication about it being in this state either. My main example is the end cutscene that suddenly and extremely abruptly cuts off in what seemed like the middle of it and starts rolling credits, which I've never experienced before in a game.The results is a game that (currently) has zero simulator elements and no freedom to do anything but follow the objectives from beginning to end, which is usually OK for a game but this one claims to be a SIMULATOR even in the name. There are some great mechanics in this game, none of which actually gets a chance to shine due to this current state of the game. While I'd love to give the devs time to add more stuff and leave a positive review of encouregement, in this particular case I feel a negative review is required to give potential buyers a better idea of its current state, and a stronger motivator to fix the game fast.Will switch to positive if a (good) simulator mode gets added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game quite a bit. Took me a little over 6 hours to finish which I think is fine for £20. For every one else I think you will enjoy the game play and the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to encourage medical sims as I believe they're woefully scarce and dangerously overlooked, so I'm recommending it --BUT-- it's very flawed. 6.5/10 - lots of potential, but trying too hard; think "Jack of all, Master of none", but if Jack was a promising beginner without enough material.This game feels like it's trying to do too much. It's trying to be a psychological horror with a deep story, and a medical simulator, but this just means it can't do any of them well. The devs really REALLY should've prioritised 1, then tacked on the other.- The horror falls flat because it's just generic jump scares, unstable camera, and "zombie horror" tropes (e.g: dead = scary = profit).- The story falls flat due to the bad delivery, chalkboard dry protagonist, and generally uninspired line.- The autopsy is good, but it falls flat because you're unsure of when the "horror" aspects will interrupt with either a jump scare, or it'll be randomly interrupted.The autopsy is the best aspect and it's pretty good overall, but as mentioned, it's weighed down by the rest of it. Maybe it's an engine issue, but a lot of it feels clunky. Fades to black, being forced to do things in a very specific manner, and tedious minigames (there's no need for different minigames for the same action, e.g: cutting).This could be easily solved if they completely wiped the horror aspect, made the building more presentable (like an actual morgue), and put the focus on the autopsy side. It is after all "Autopsy Simulator",  not "Generic horror with slab-ready character and campy jumpscare Simulator".Devs: keep at it, there's a lot that could come of this, but pick a lane and stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is unfair to the game that many negative reviews stem from players expecting something different based solely on the title. The game's description clearly states that it is a horror game with simulator elements, so it is not purely a simulator. Next time, please check what you're buying.I enjoyed playing the game. The educational content was a highlight for me; the autopsies were informative, offering a lot of interesting knowledge while providing fun through minigames. Personally, I enjoyed the tooth-matching game the most.The story is engaging and intriguing. Most things are explained throughout the gameplay, but paying close attention allows you to sooner figure out some aspects on your own, adding to the game's appeal.I did miss having more decision-making during the autopsies. The protagonist often performed most actions for us and explained everything, which prevented us from making mistakes—a missed opportunity, in my opinion. However, I’ve heard that a mode incorporating the features I missed will be added soon, which I’m eagerly anticipating.In summary, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, especially considering its reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: There is very little simulation to this so called simulator. I got this game expecting, as was advertised, a medically accurate autopsy simulator, but the gameplay is extremely bound to the mediocre story, leading to a very on-rails experience. You are directed step-by-step on what to do next and there is no ability to deviate from the set path beyond rummaging around in drawers or examining inconsequential props. With the autopsies, you are not graded and you can't really make mistakes that have any impact or effect other than make your character's mental health go a bit wobbly. The scares are predictable and pretty meh, regardless of how much the main voice actor insists in their scariness by overacting every. single. line. I played just over 3 hours hoping that the terrible story was mostly tutorial for the autopsies until it became painfully apparent this was the whole game, and given I got 16 out of 24 (as of time of writing) achievements makes me suspect there's very little game left to play after the 3 hour mark. All in all, I wouldn't recommend this game in its current form and feel regretful about purchasing it, but I am hopeful the devs listen to feedback to offer an autopsy-only mode in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I think anyone who has followed this game knows the use of the word 'simulator' is a bit misleading. It's a horror narrative. I've played a couple of hours and I've enjoyed it so far. The tension is building nicely and whilst I think the voice acting of the protagonist is good, he is a bit annoying at times. I haven't found it quite as scary as the mortuary assistant (which will draw obvious comparisons) but there have been a couple of nervy moments, particularly when you notice something in the background that could be easy to miss, even in the prologue. Would have liked a little less hand holding for the actual autopsy but can understand why that isn't the case as the cases are varied enough that you would likely get stuck not knowing exactly which squishy thing to stick the syringe in to get a sample. Overall if you take the game for what it is and you aren't expecting a tutorial on how to conduct an actual autopsy then you should find it an enjoyable game and good value for money (£20).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed the graphics and the initial concept of the game but it's just not what I expected based on the description. For the price-tag, I simply cannot recommend the game at this stag as it is nothing short of a point and click with an abrupt and confusing ending.  There are some pros but also some strong cons:The PROS:-Nice graphics and mechanics -Cool/creepy ambiance -Love the amount of research they've done on medical/pathology stuff (adds realism) The CONS:-Writing is pretty bad for general dialogue (though well written for autopsy scenes and explanations)-Voice acting was atrocious (some fault goes to the writing), which made the main character insufferable. Only good one in my opinion was Ridley who (ironically) was supposed to be the unpleasant one.-Story is bland and as others have stated the whole thing is very "hand-holdy". I wish there was a way for the player to actually get the autopsy wrong and deal with the consequences, or at least let you get to the conclusions on your own based on the info acquired. -Kind of a minor con, but the pixelated censorship really puts a damp on the realism. I understand it needs to be there for now and if I read correctly, eventually players will be able to remove it via settings.However, I still want to give props to the creator and devs. The idea is there and it's a good one. Graphics are cool and I am sure that the game will get  much better as the updates roll out, that's the only reason I am not asking for a refund. I trust they will prove mine and the other negative reviews wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Graphics }---Pretty average.  Some noticeably low res textures scattered throughout.---{ Game play }---Very easy to get into, and then very repetitive.  There is no real choice in the game. Everything is presented to you as-is and you’re pretty much railroaded to the end.---{ Audio }---It’s OK.  The music can be overbearing at times, typical “suspense’ music.---{ Audience }---Anyone who likes horror games, walking simulators, and basic “simulator’ type game play. ---{ Difficulty }---Extremely easy. Not much to say about it as there aren’t really many mechanics to it.---{ Replay-ability }---There seems to be an alternative ending which, I hope so. The normal ending is pretty terrible.---{ Story }---Very basic horror tropes.  No supernatural stuff and instead goes the mental horror route where the character wonder what’s real.  The normal ending is pretty bad so hopefully the alternative ending makes up for it.---{ Game Time }---Very short.  Could probably be completed first time in less than 4 hours.  If you do decide to replay, could probably do it in less than 2.Hopefully there will be new content added because the game just feels like it’s lacking/unfinished story-wise. ---{ Price }---Wait for a sale.  Even at $30 I don’t believe it’s worth it. ---{ Bugs }---Some minor bugs but nothing that affected gameplay, such as a drawer getting stuck open. ---{ Score Summary }---4/10It’s obvious that the developers worked hard on this. You can see where effort was put in.  However, it really needed more time in the oven and more review of the story.  Right now it just feels like it’s lacking in story, content, and pacing.  Very similar to Mortuary Simulator in direction but with it's own take but not as much polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Having been a placement student in a forensic morgue I have to admit I was impressed with the level of detail of the procedures and equipment that is used in this game. From the dissection of the organs to the collection of evidence photographs etc was brilliant. That said however to call this a simulator is wrong as it is story led. I would have liked a kinda L.A Noire kind of game where it allows the player to reach their own conclusions and have the story line change based on the consequences of your actions and decisions. While i enjoyed the story line I just wished that it was a bit more simulation and a bit less story. I've been playing this on the steam deck docked and with keyboard and controller and with a few graphic changes it runs flawlessly with a stable 40 fps and still looks good. The issue is that most of the time I spend trying to find the mouse cursor which is tiny and impossible to see at times and sometimes the cursor is not even there. _childDocuments_.review: So I was really hyped for this game, I want to do this profession as an actual career. I love solving puzzles and helping families of deceased get closure. I beat and got every achievement in Mortuary Assistant and was really looking forward to a game where I could zone out and perform more realistic autopsies. This is NOT that.There is a scripted, narrated story, which is all great and fine, HOWEVER, you cannot deviate from courses of action that seem pretty obvious. You have to click where the game wants, when it wants. How this leads to multiple endings, I have no idea. Its scares also are pretty lackluster and few and far between. There were a couple times it "got," me, but overall it's pretty boring. On top of all of that, the actual ending (without any spoilers) is far too simple and leaves the player wanting more out of the game.The gameplay is buggy and overall the game feels largely rushed and unfinished. There are things you can grab through walls, double dialogue if you skip narration, and a multitude of other issues. It certainly feels like they should have done more polishing before full release. They also should have had the actual autopsy simulator portion included with release, in my opinion, rather than a to-be-determined free DLC. I mean, why call it a "Simulator" if it doesn't actually have a simulator portion? The parts in the story do not count to most people. When we think "simulator" we think endless, non-stop cases that we finish ourselves without any hand-holding. Again, this all feels very sloppy. The one positive I WILL say that the game is very well optimized and runs smoothly on my outdated PC.In conclusion, I feel players should just wait to get this game until it's on sale and the issues have been sorted out. It won't fix the story or its boring nature, however, so if you're here for that, skip it. Maybe I will change this review upon the release of the actual simulator part, but I doubt it.Edit 1: I am trying to play through to at least get the achievements (which most feel not really like accomplishments due to the hand-holding, but I digress) and now I am currently stuck on (Spoilers) Harper's case because I took the pills before the scare was finished, and now the game is telling me to take my pills...when I already did, and I cannot continue the autopsy because the game thinks I need to take pills. I cannot take them again because the narrator says he doesn't want to overdose. So I am stuck here. If I quit out of the game, I will lose all the progress I've made so far because the save points are at the start of the day. (And if you know this case, you know how much work there is in this particular one by the time you need to go to the bathroom for your pills).

_childDocuments_.review: For someone like me, who's always been interested in anatomy, this game is really interesting. You can clearly see there has been spent a lot of attention to detail. I wanted to find out what happened. But if you're looking for a scare, this might not be your cup of tea. I wouldn't necessarily call it horror, but it definitely adds to the storytelling. I'm glad I bought this game and I would recommend it to anyone who likes realism, mild scares, and a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: People are horribly misinterpreting this game. It's really good; not only are the mechanics super fun, but the game itself is really creative and interesting. It's not a game for everyone, that's for sure, but if you liked the trailer and psychological horror is your cup of tea, you will enjoy Autopsy Simulator. As of right now, autopsy-only mode is in progress, and it will be released according to the developers, so don't listen to butthurt people saying that it's not enough of a simulator—it is, and it will be even more in the future. It's story-driven, the story is interesting, and our main character is extremely likeable and well written. It's definitely worth checking out, and all the negative reviews honestly surprise me. Give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Autopsy Simulator was a very enjoyable game start to finish for me. ive been waiting on the release of this game for 2+ years, is the game perfect. Absolutely Not, i never expected it to be upon release. Did i enjoy everything the game had to offer. Yes. AS i was closely following dev-logs and information i knew this wasn't going to be a full Simulator game, I was excited about the Horror Simulator Hybrid, and it met expectations for a new-ish genre of game play.The story was enjoyable and the voice acting was really good especially for our main character Jack. I understand the autopsies not being fully in depth in a story mode, there are plot points that need to be met and are closely involved with key points in the story. Only story complaint is we still got very little information about main characters wife Alice as we really only know that shes been dead for about a year, we dont have a reason why even after beating the game her death is still incredibly vague. The story genuinely had me unsettled at times and scared me on more than a few occasions, which was super enjoyable as i love horror. My only complaint gameplay wise was some tasks are inherently vague, examining the victims clothes stumped me as there was nothing to thoroughly investigate to plain eye once all the main things were noticed.I think sandbox mode will be a fun thing to add, with a variety of bodies and causes of death. and the price of the game was surprising as i genuinely expected it to cost far more.TLDRPros:Game met expectations if you followed the devlogsgame-play was enjoyable for the most part with only a few minor hiccupsI like the real professional terminology usedvoice acting was great for an indie gamethe game was unsettling and scarygame was decently priced for the content includedCons:Some tasks were unnecessarily vague and hard to figure outsome of the mini-games for cutting organs open were needlessly complex and time-consumingstory was good but we still got very little information about main characters wife Alice maybe it is intentional but id like to learn more in the future if they decide to add more.Overall i recommend this game i loved it and will definitely play it again. I only say dont go into the game expecting it to be  a simulator Its not one, its a horror sim hybrid.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has so much potential but barely did anything with it. The autopsy mechanics can be buggy at times, but they're very in-depth while also being simplified enough to function within a game setting. The story, however, leaves much to be desired.The player feels no attachment to the main character, and it's difficult to get that connection when the game is titled "Autopsy Simulator." In my opinion, such a naming convention would drive the player to focus on simply the gameplay since that's what's expected of games within the Simulator genre. The story itself feels like it's trying to do so much while giving us absolutely nothing. Everything outside of the autopsy mechanics was hastily thrown together; especially during the last scene. The dialogue felt melodramatic, the character animations were weird, and audio cues would play at inappropriate times.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : Was all that edgy millennial melodrama really necessary? Could we not have simply performed some autopsies, briefly considered becoming a mortician and called it a night?  3/10.The autopsy simulation? It’s okay, I would have liked more freedom to explore but it wasn’t bad, and the graphics were fine. What ruined it for me was the character and storyline. The actual character and/or whoever wrote this gives me the impression that the only media they have ever consumed is dubbed shounen anime, and Joe Rogan podcasts. The kind of guy to unironically use The Dark Knight’s Joker as a status update on Facebook describing himself as “a lone wolf, but fiercely loyal” , before arguing on Reddit about Marvel Cinematic Universe lore. You get the idea.Then there’s this hamfisted attempt at portraying what I assume is supposed to be PTSD, which basically involves him Malcolm-In-The-Monologuing about his dead wife, and tweaking until you actively make him take his “pills, I can’t do it without the pills!” He will quip about his alcoholism, poor diet and other things he thinks makes him “bad-ass”. He wants you to laugh and think “Wow, this guy is so edgy and cool.” Instead, I cringed for the final time and logged out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dropping a review before I've even finished the game mainly to show support for the devs.A lot of people held certain expectations and just because they misunderstood the game and what it would be, they instantly try to tear it down along with the devs. No game should be blamed because the player was the one who misinterpreted what a game was presenting itself as. Also, AFAIK, the devs never promoted this as a true and genuine simulator. They specifically stated it's a horror-sim HYBRID. Again, players with poor reading comprehension have resorted to negative reviews over THEIR mistake.People are also saying the game is "too short" when it's obvious they were rushing through it. I'm almost 4 hours in and I expect to finish the game in another hour or so. I saw someone took 7 hours to finish it. $16 for 4-5 hours is a fair price IMO. They'll also be adding a sandbox mode so you'll get even more hours of playtime eventually. Again, this is why you take these negative reviews with a heaping serving of salt.If you end up not enjoying the game either, then simply refund it. Some players are acting like Steam doesn't have an easy refunding process. Get your money back in 24 hours (which I always do) and spend it on another game. No one is holding you at gun point and telling you to keep the game in your library.In short, I highly recommend the game, especially as a fan of the horror genre in general. Story-wise, it's not the best, and the dialogue could use some work, but I still recommend it wholeheartedly.

I like how there are different options for motion blur- off, low, and high. I usually turn off motion blur because it hurts my head but kept it on low and felt fine. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy *Autopsy Simulator*. A game centered around performing autopsies in a dark, realistic environment? That sounds amazing! Unfortunately, it just doesn’t deliver on so many levels.The main voice actor  It feels like they were just as bored with the script as I was, which is a letdown because good voice acting could have really enhanced the experience. There’s something "off" about how they deliver their lines that just sucks the tension out of the scenes instead of adding to it. It seems like the actor is  for this part.The autopsy tasks are pretty cool—they're definitely the highlight of the game. But here’s the catch: . You’re not really engaging your brain or investigating; you’re just ticking off boxes without any chance to make mistakes. It feels more like a simple checklist than an actual challenge or puzzle., and they do a fair job of creating the right atmosphere. But the story?  It’s really shallow, lacking any real depth or conclusion to keep you hooked.In the end, *Autopsy Simulator* feels like a missed opportunity. There was so much promise, but the lack of immersion, weak narrative, and overly simplistic gameplay turn it into more of a chore than an exciting experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Autopsy Simulator is an intriguing experience with the potential to be great but falls short in a few areas. The atmosphere is immersive and gripping, leaning heavily into the horror and psychological thriller genre. However, it feels more like a thriller movie than an interactive game due to the imbalance between story and gameplay. The narrative is compelling but cuts off abruptly, leaving loose ends that make it feel unfinished. Despite these downsides, the game does a fantastic job of incorporating realistic post-mortem details—I actually learned a few fascinating and accurate facts. If you're looking for an atmospheric experience with some interesting forensic insights, Autopsy Simulator is worth a look, but don't expect a fully fleshed-out game.

_childDocuments_.review: While still in its Early Access stage, I'm having a great time with Autopsy Simulator!The good:- The experience is visceral and unsettling.- The environment is dank and appropriately disturbing. It's uncomfortable, just as one would expect. - The design is tight, and the voice acting is fantastic!- The story is rich and engaging. The mysterious supernatural elements mingle well with the criminology aspects of gameplay.The criticisms:- I think I may be missing out on some of the scares - I have experienced my character having tense reactions to happenings in the autopsy room, but whatever it is he is experiencing seems occasionally lost on me. I would truly hate to miss any of the horror, but I sometimes feel as if I'm looking in the wrong place at the wrong moment...- The following criticism is a double-edged sword (scalpel?): It's hard to mess up. The game guides you through your tasks like a first year med student shadowing an instructor. I'm grateful for the opportunity to engage in the autopsy tasks with minimal room for error (it helps me focus on the story and soak up the visceral gore - the very reason the game has been on my watchlist for the past few years), but I can't help but wonder if the tension would be higher with something other than my character's delicate sanity at stake.- I've noticed a small handful of misspellings in the dialog captions.The pros far outweigh the cons for this horror sim. This is an early access title with a lot to offer, and I look forward to "Autopsy Only" mode. I'd say this game has certainly been worth the wait, and I am eager to watch it thrive as it blossoms to full maturity. It's definitely worthy of a recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 2/10"Autopsy Simulator" is a game that promises an immersive and educational experience but, unfortunately, falls flat on almost every front. Despite its intriguing title, it quickly becomes apparent that this game is anything but a simulator.The gameplay is disappointingly mundane. Rather than engaging in a realistic autopsy process, players are merely told what to click next, removing any sense of autonomy or challenge. This repetitive click-and-drag mechanic strips the game of any potential excitement or educational value. The controls are simplistic to the point of insult; it hardly matters how you keep the left mouse button down and move it across the screen.The story, a potential saving grace, fails to deliver. It is poorly written and does little to engage the player or add depth to the gameplay. The narrative seems like an afterthought, hastily slapped together and utterly forgettable.One of the biggest disappointments is the price. At 22 EUR for just 5 hours of play, this game is grossly overpriced. The content and quality offered here feel more like a demo or a prologue than a full-fledged game. A price point of 5 EUR would be more appropriate and easier to swallow, given the lackluster experience provided.In conclusion, "Autopsy Simulator" is a misnomer and a missed opportunity. It lacks the complexity and realism that one would expect from a simulation game. The poor storytelling and monotonous gameplay only serve to make the experience boring and frustrating. This is one autopsy you’ll want to avoid at all costs, especially at its current price.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve always been a huge fan of the studio behind Autopsy Simulator. Most of the time, their games are of exceptional quality and provide immersive experiences. Unfortunately, Autopsy Simulator did not live up to my expectations, primarily because it isn’t truly a simulator as the name suggests.First off, I want to make it clear that I only played the game for one hour. In that time, I felt I got a good enough sense of the game to provide a fair review, but I don't intend to continue playing a narrative game of this nature.From the get-go, it’s evident that the game leans heavily towards being a narrative experience rather than a genuine autopsy simulator. Everything is designed in a way that restricts your freedom to perform autopsies. Instead, you’re guided through a story, which can be a decent experience for those looking for a dark, narrative-driven game. However, for those expecting a true simulator experience, the title is misleading.The game is visually stunning, and the atmosphere is appropriately eerie, capturing the dark tone it aims for. But again, it falls short in delivering the hands-on autopsy experience one might expect from a simulator.If you’re into narrative games with a dark twist, this might be worth your time. But if you’re looking for a real autopsy simulation, this isn’t it. A more fitting title for the game would be something like "Autopsy Chronicles" or "The Autopsy Diaries." Just about anything but "simulator," as it doesn't accurately reflect the gameplay experience.In summary, while it’s a beautiful game with a captivating story, it’s not what it claims to be. If you’re looking for a true autopsy simulation, you might want to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review:
Autopsy Simulator is a first-person horror-sim hybrid where players take on the role of a practice pathologist and study case files, created in collaboration with real-world forensic doctors, to help guide their dissection of anatomically accurate bodies to determine each subject's cause of death.

Autopsy Simulator features a free play 'Autopsy Only' mode and 'Autopsy Simulator: Dead Memories', a self-contained, narrative-driven psychological horror experience set in 1990s New Orleans.

In Autopsy Simulator: Dead Memories, you play a middle-aged pathologist whose life has taken a turn for the worse. After a career downfall and the loss of your beloved wife, you live each day shattered and exhausted. One day during a routine post-mortem, you find a relic of your past hidden inside a body. Now, it feels like something just won't let go...

name: Steelrising
detailed_description: Bastille Edition About the Game The city burns and bleeds as it suffers the madness of King Louis XVI and his violent legions of automatons. Aegis, a mechanical masterpiece created by the engineer Vaucanson to be the queen's bodyguard, must save the French Revolution in this challenging action-RPG. CHALLENGING COMBAT BETWEEN AUTOMATONS Up against the king's mechanical soldiers, deadly accuracy will be needed. String together dodges, parries, jumps and devastating attacks to fight your way through Paris. Every fight will test your nerve and requires excellent discipline, while the huge relentless machine bosses demand patience and skill. AEGIS: A CHARACTER WITH EXTRAORDINARY SKILLS Define your own style and upgrade your abilities as you progress through the game. You can play as a ruthless warrior, a hard-hitting bodyguard, a deadly dancer or a virtuoso of the elemental arts. Take advantage of a wide variety of weapons and skills to approach each fight in your own unique way. REVOLUTIONARY PARIS IS YOUR PLAYGROUND Using carriages, grapples, secret passages, a detailed map, and other methods and tools you find along the way, explore a city experiencing its darkest days. Your grappling hook adds a new dimension to exploration and Paris's verticality. Combined with your dash ability, it will provide access to all the city's secrets across multiple levels you can explore over and over again. CHANGE THE COURSE OF HISTORY You are one of the main characters of an alternative history where Paris is being choked by a tyrant king. Allies and enemies with unclear motives will cross your path, such as Marie-Antoinette, Lafayette and Robespierre. It's up to you to cut a path through all the plotting and put an end to one man's madness so that the French Revolution succeeds.

_childDocuments_.review: Stop reading this and go play that first – it garners an overwhelming recommendation from me (which you can read ), whereas Steelrising is far more tepid. Anyway, on with the show.Steelrising is what you reach for when you run out of Elden Ring & Dark Souls 3. It’s the game I’ve come across that feels closest to these From Software legends, however unfortunately it falls short in a number of aspects. All in all, it feels like trying to manage an opiates addiction with cigarettes.Why is Steelrising the next best thing to Elden Ring & Dark Souls 3? It has a healing flask you can only refill at ‘bonfires’, no map to aid exploration, you instead have to learn the environment yourself. There’s a lot of ‘the door doesn’t open from this side’ and as you explore a level you unlock more shortcuts to get back to where you were more easily if you die. The flow/pace of combat is very similar, though Steelrising doesn’t have i-frame dodge rolls, just a backstep. Steelrising also has some interesting and creative weapon designs (though the secondary abilities tend to be pretty bland,) which have distinct move sets and are fun to use.The above similarities to From Software Souls-like games and the awesome choice of setting for Steelrising was enough for me to want to play through the whole game, even though by the end I wasn’t really enjoying it much. That was because…The story is boring and hard to follow. There are a lot of very similar looking & sounding characters, and a lot of convoluted names for people & places to try and keep track of. Steelrising tries to take players through the story where From Software instead let the player decide if they want to try and find the story, but it’s not an improvement here. By the middle of the game, I’d given up caring for the characters’ backstories, and by the end I was scarcely following the main plot line.The enemy variety is a joke. There are probably about seven original non-boss enemy types in the game, and if you include the bosses that get recycled as enemies, there’s maybe a dozen enemies you see on a regular basis. Some enemy variety padding is done by changing an enemy’s elemental damage type, and some enemies get slightly souped-up versions later into the game, but the lack of variety becomes noticeable worryingly quickly into a fifteen hour game. There are a lot of ‘official’ boss fights which are either a bigger version of a regular enemy, or a bigger version of what’s about to be the most commonly occurring regular enemy for the next 30 minutes.Enemy move sets are simple. This applies to bosses also, which appear to have approximately the same number of moves as regular enemies. This makes a lot of bosses easy to kill in one or two tries, since learning their move set is trivial and only the final boss has a second phase.Encounters with multiple enemies at once, in a word, suck. As the game progresses, because it has so few enemies to make encounters with, it chooses to ramp up the difficulty by making you fight enemies in pairs, eventually groups of three or four. Their AI clearly doesn’t have any special programming for this to make the situation manageable for the player, so you often either have to kite and poke until there’s one enemy left, or try and kill one before the rest of the gang catches up. When your camera is unlocked however, landing attacks on enemies becomes a legitimate challenge, because the game gives you little-no magnetism for your attacks like From Software games do, and most skills (parry, critical hit from a stagger, and the two combat abilities you unlock) can’t be used without being locked on. Switching between lock-on targets with keyboard & mouse uses the scroll wheel and is incredibly inconsistent. Your camera can also whirl around jarringly when locking or unlocking the camera, making for an all-around awful gank fight experience.There isn’t a huge amount of environment variety. You’ve got city, garden, sewer (very small), and underground mine.The metroidvania-style abilities unlocking new paths that you couldn’t previously go down are... okay. The platforming is super inconsistent though, which is a shame because a lot of it is compulsory. You can use these abilities in combat, but I rarely saw a reason to.Keyboard & mouse controls are a second-class citizen. If you’re used to playing Dark Souls 3 and Elden Ring with them, you’ll feel right at home in this game. Yay. This is especially annoying here because your oil burette (estus flask) does not have a dedicated hotkey, it shares the active item slot hotkey which you have to also use for other consumables (or the compass for quest markers). Cycling through a hotbar in a fight is tedious, risky, and completely unnecessary with I have the full row of number keys completely unused.The game gives you a “point of no return” warning while there is still roughly three hours of gameplay left! Upon being told that I was about to cross this threshold, I expected just a walk up to a final boss fight, some cutscenes and story clean-up, and I’d be done. Nope! Two new boss fights, each in their own respective new area you have to explore. Ordinarily I wouldn’t be mad about a game having more content than expected, but my aforementioned gripes meant my patience was wearing thin, leaving me excited to be able to finish the game soon. The fact that there was so much still to do thus quickly became a negative as I just wanted to find the ending, only to find myself going through more garden mazes, more platforming, more three-at-a-time encounters, etc.. This definitely could have been communicated better, e.g. “By proceeding beyond this point the following side quests cannot be completed: blah blah blah”.I think those are all my major gripes. The other aspects of the game range of decent to okay. This review is largely a critique, but I do genuinely recommend the game for people who want more Dark Souls 3 / Elden Ring but in a different game. Just go in with managed expectations :)

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately the game has its strong points, but in reality this would be a mixed thumb.PROS:The SoundtrackThe ConceptThe GraphicsCONs:The FightsThe Obnoxious SubquestsSteelrising is an ambitious project, and while the Concept is original and the Graphics more or less gorgeous, it fails in delivering convincing fights, one of the actual cores of any Soulslike.Since you're forced to battle your way throughout most levels, you eventually feel like moving in circles, since you're forced doing something that requires the same moves with little to no risk all the time.As a result, you want to finish the game as quickly as possible, as the rest (Plot, voice acting, customization) is not enough to keep you there.The plot is taken too seriously by the developers: they added a lot of obnoxious dialogues as useful as the ones from the NPC of Horizon: Zero Dawn, which also had a lot of silly lines of dialogues.The Bosses are actually quite fine, but in the end you can defeat them all with ranged frost attacks of your secondary weapon, then once they froze solid you charge your heavy attack for massive damage.That's really all.About the sidequests, well, it's not like I disliked them, but this particular episode annoyed me a bit:I was in the Bastille, close to the last part of the game, then I realised I had two choices:1. Move away from the main road and do that sidequest that was purposedly put still next to the Bastille but totally far away from your path.2. Continuing on.I chose 2., I was tired of fighting the same enemies most of the times, and I felt the developers wanted to lure the player away from the main path only to prolong that pain.In the end I can see the passion the developers put into this, and the cons while not many, are enough to be a nuisance to veteran players, but IMHO not to the point to give a thumb down (generally meaning you regretted the purchase).I must say one thing, though: the game is not completely worth its price tag.Take it as discounted and you'll do yourself a favour. :)
