_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying it's a good game. Overall, very good, solid world, decent characters, decent gameplay, and good length. Most importantly, I was enjoying it most of the time I was playing it, to a fairly decent level. If you like dark souls or blooborne, then you may like this.Now, to some downsides. Combat... it's not bad, but not great, the pacing of the players attacks, range, enemy speeds, attack types... overall they don't always mesh so while sometimes it works, sometimes it kind of doesn't.Jumping... they added jumping but it feels almost like they only added it part way through development, so some assets/areas were made without it in mind. By this I mean, it doesn't really affect combat for the most part. And for world exploration, lots of areas have no use for it at all, though as the game goes on more places do make use of it so it's less forgettable than i first found it in the begining. The biggest issue here is how the game teaches you not to use it to explore. You see some place you could jump up to? Too bad, invisible wall. You see something you want to jump onto? Too bad, the collisions for that are not accurate, so it's a giant invisible cube going up a ways. You see that surface that's one of the specificly conveyed climable surfaces with the sllight white paint they tend to draw your attention towards to know what you can climb (that only sometimes applies)? Well this one will let you climb it... but instantly push you back because there's an invisible wall on it, someone just used those assets as is in  place they shouldn't be used in... Overall, 90% of the time I tried exploring using jumping the game just punished me for it with an invisible wall or glitchiness. The levels are designed so visually there are tons of places you could jump to get around, or navigate or explore... but they just plug almost all of it with invisible walls. More seriously, they can force a restart sometimes. Multiple times I jumped onto something, or off something, and landed on rocks or objects they set you to not stand on (forced sliding down), but they don't force you to slide off reliably, and you just get stuck in a crevace or gap or something and can't do anything but restart, or if you are lucky within a minute might randomly pop out of the area if close to an edge (try flicking menus open/closed and alt tabbing to alter frame rate, helps you glitch past the edges of some of these).So, overall while when used properly the jumping and verticality was great, much more often it was not used well and seemed counter the the level and world design, clashing rather badly.Not a dealbreaker for the game, but be warned going in, don't try to explore everything jumping, you will get worn out trying and probably die and lose some valuable anima on more than a few cases purely because of invisible walls/questionable surface properties you couldn't intuit just by looking.A number of general bugs, while very much present, overall not too bad. My game only froze and crashed once, though I got stuck and had to restart/load on multiple occasions do to issue in how the world was designed, lots of places you can jump or get into, but not out of... and a few bugs in combat, inputs, etc... Parry is... well you'll find some combat things don't have consistent seeming queue behavior, or rules on when they can be triggered during other animations. Also plenty of cases of enemy attacks just going right through my character and doing nothing, or going right through my parry and hitting me, not the most common, but still happened several times over the game. Still, again, not enough to ruin the overall experience, just put a bit of a damper on what could have been a great game, to just being pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising takes place in steampunk alternate history of the French Revolution. The King is gathering power and has replaced his forces with an army of loyal automatons. Has he gone mad or are his motives darker? The Queen has her suspicions, but she is a prisoner in her own home, blind to what's going on.You are the Queen's personal bodyguard, a sophisticated automaton loyal only to her. Perhaps peace is still possible if you can gather the right information on her behalf. You slip out into a hostile courtyard to find automatons patrolling everywhere. They are stronger and they have numbers, but you can use your cunning and skill to investigate the situation. Or that's what would make sense anyway. Your actual job is to individually smash each one into tiny bits with a giant hammer.What is this  supposed to be?I don't know what the original plan for this game was, but it seems like it was hastily re-designed to be a souls game to keep up with trends or something. It makes basically no sense otherwise.Some reviews have praised the unique setting - which, to be fair is very cool - but it's fundamentally at odds with the gameplay. The combat is non-optional because you need to destroy enemies to level up your character. Cleverness and stealth aren't really an option.I've also seen some reviews saying that the combat is great, but takes some getting used to. This is a nice way of saying that it's functional but bad. The best way I can describe it is by comparing it to Dishonored. In those games you're supposed to use stealth, but if you mess up the game punishes you by making you slog through endless boring combat. This is basically that: punishment combat.If you're really hungry for one more meh souls game, maybe pick this up. Personally, I can hear the people sing, singing a song of "don't buy this bad game"

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully detailed game, with fascinating designs and an interesting story. The combat is definitely challenging, but the Assist Mode settings allow you to make it much more forgiving, even turning off enemy damage altogether if you're truly struggling. I really appreciate this, as someone who needs accessibility in games in order to be able to play something more difficult, such as a souls-like. Adjusting the settings has allowed me to enjoy the game with challenge that doesn't keep me from progressing.The enemies are fascinating, both in design and the lore that comes with them, and Aegis is absolutely stunning. I've completely fallen in love with this character, and definitely want to play through trying all the different options. I enjoy reading through the Codex, and learning about the different automats, with each one having a well thought-out background as to their prior place in society before the uprising. Story wise, I'm enjoying this alternate-history, and how well a rather accurate period piece has been intertwined with this fantastical, steampunk tale. The visual details of the costumes has really brought me joy, as someone who is fascinated with the history of fashion, and it really brings the characters and their time to life. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone interested in soulslike games that struggles with difficulty settings, as well as to people who enjoy period pieces, steampunk aesthetics, and gorgeous character design.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun souls-like with an alternate historical setting, Louis XVI uses alchemy and an army of clockwork automatons in an attempt to fend off the French Revolution. Steelrising makes decent use of its themes and setting, it's basically Parisian Bloodborne. The weapons in particular stand out as being pretty creative, unique and fun to use. Ice projectile shooting muskets, maces with several rifle barrels, a short sword and rapier combo that deals fire and ice damage, fans weapons, claws, maces on chain whips, weird alchemical melee disc thing-y's. While initially challenging it felt like Steelrising got easier and easier after the first major boss. It isn't Dark Souls hard, it won't kick you in the balls and have a boss one or two shot you. In fact it's pretty easy to over-level but that's kind of fun in its own right. You're sort of a wrecking ball by the end of the game.Worth noting, it's possible to soft-lock yourself out of completing certain side-quests. You can untie the knot, but the game does a poor job of conveying how at times. If you miss a quest objective, backtracking can be kind of nightmare-ish. The game doesn't have an actual map, just a stylised overworld drawing of Paris. Four of the major zones are pretty labyrinthine. If you forget to unlock a short cut, you have to figure your way through some mazes.As for performance, I have a 3080, 5600x, 32gb of ram. I played the game in 1440p with settings on high except textures, which were set to medium so the game only ate up 5-6gb of vram. The game hovered between 120-90fps. There weren't any noticeable stutters or performance issues, but for some people those drops alone might be issue enough.Bought this for 30$, expected a scuffed but fun budget souls-like, that's exactly what I got.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Fun! But does not feel like a souls-like or like controlling a robot. Also janky issues about how much mass she feels to have.Play wise. This feels like Monster Hunter. My character does not (usually) get interrupted by enemy attacks, but it depends on the weapon.Graphics. Still look luscious even on a steam deck at minimum settings. In fact they look a bit too luscious, several times branches and stuff got in the way of the camera, distracting.Animation. the good: it feels clunky. *Perfect* feeling for clockwork. The bad: a lot is arcade-like does not feel human, does not feel robot.If you love robots: This robot is essentially a human with fancy descriptors, that occasionally remembers being a robot, equipping her is not like fine tuning a machine.Long version:I'm not a "pro gamer", never used a controller since the Super Nintendo.I now own a steam deck, i usually play with keyboard and mouse.Sneer all you want.I'm not changing controller config until i know what effect it has in/outside combat.But i do keep trying to "okay"/"cancel" enemies instead of attacking them, because i am not used to attacking with shoulder buttons.Tutorial level is very good and very well designed, but the popups are a serious issue, they tell you what is obvious, not what is not.I was shown i had an inventory but was not told how to bring it up.I was not told different weapons may or may not have different combos.If you like robots: outside of combat or with certain weapons feels *too* human and weightless.It also feels like a magical girl with "hammerspace".Most of the stuff that comes out of her would have no space to be inside of her.She has a movement with each equipment swap which implies she pops the stuff out... but out of nowhere.She has the habit of doing lots of preparation do deliver a blow and then waste that preparation to put everything back in.I started with the first option, the bodyguard, so she is going around lugging an "hammer" of music sheets for an automatic piano, but made of metal:• Light: telescopic arm and then swing the mass of the metal sheets and your arms at the enemies in a very wide arc and lounge.• Heavy: same as above but extends arm first and starts winding up a flywheel with sparks and all (for... reason? Does she need oil?) and then she engages the gears (now THAT would have caused sparks, but nothing happens) and slams the hammer. Enemies get flung around. Satisfyingly clunky.• Special: parry, she picks the 3 music sheets and opens them, Whipple Shield style.The graphics convey that perfectly. The movements look and feel good.But: There is no readying for the action that i want to do, you just push a button watch the robot prepare, attack, and finally, most annoyingly, un-prepare.A lot of work wasted. It ends up looking like one of those wushu movie duels, unsheathe sword, attack re-sheathe sword.The combat does not feel like i am stacking programs, i push, i watch and wait, i push again. The program is stacking in my head, not in the robot that i am commanding. When she stops attacking and starts moving around and interacting with people she becomes super-light, that's very jarring.It's like she suddenly gains mass only when attacking, and different weapons give her different mass.Light weapons have enemies stop her, massive weapons go through loads of enemies and are quite hard to stop the preparation of.The character is shown constantly running (dashing just makes you run faster), stops immediately, can turn without skidding.But those weapons are part of her body mass, that feels weird.But then you run into perfectly fine and sturdy boxes or benches and destroy them with a light touch.Does my character have or not have mass?! Those do not look like rotten crates and benches kept together by sawdust.You never lose grip because (example:) you have not yet bought the correct shoes for the environment you are traversing or (different example:) because you packed too much mass in your robot. You just run turn and stop on a dime.The equipment itself references emotions, not your robot's capabilities. Which is jarring.They used mocap so she moves like a human, not like a robot. Just look at that wiggling spine.The discus was also available due to being pre-bought, its animations feel completely human, not how a robot would use it.The monsters come at you with a given speed only if they spot you and you can pretty much time when they will reach you and plan your attacks accordingly.But, just like you, enemies have a very long range it's hard to tell when you are being attacked from behind which is the whole point of playing in 3rd person.Do the animation convey what she does? Yes. It is the un-preparation after each attack that feels out of place, it is how they mesh with each other that does not work with me.So while each animation looks good and perfect, the character gains and loses mass at the touch of a button.Story wise, the whole presentation you got in the trailer is skipped in the game itself, we start with the queen tasking her to save her, not how she was gifted to the queen and what is their relationship or how the kind went mad. You are just told those things happened, go figure it out.She is presented as an unknown thing and therefore everything about her is jarring when you start playing.Initial character motivations are barebone, but to a point where having less would have been actually better.On the character aesthetics: You can change the aesthetics of your robot, but:For some reasons the body and the head are handled in a different way, so you can end up with an effect which is ... cringe at best due to face and body color clashing.There are several different interesting options for the body (some have a full wooden look, or fully metallic) that are not available for the head.Vice versa there is no way to give your robot an head that does not feel like "a human being, but mechanical".For the head you have about 4 "racial tropes" with their skin tones and a harder or a slimmer face.The base clothing are white and very masculine for the era, a white frilly thing, but you can put on a more feminine black dress. Fittingly the initial masculine clothing makes you more agile, women's clothing make you more armored. It's in your inventory, which, as i mentioned, you are not told how to reach.I guess the idea is that she is more feminine or more masculine based on face and dress style, but she always moves in a very feminine way (and *not* like a robot).As i said face and body can have clashing tones which can look really problematic in some case, what surprised me is that darker face tones wear no makeup and the face is very close to real skin tones, this feels out of place.The European and Oriental face uses white varnish with black/red/gold decors (which is as inhuman as it gets and therefore my go-to choice) i'd have used a similarly inhuman "lacquered wood" or "polished onyx" looks for the other two face options and also still used bright paint that would stand out on eyeshade and lips like it happens with the white varnish faces. Instead they look just plain.If this is a problem with low graphics setting or a glitch that did not load the textures, i do not know. Could be, game has been out only for 24 hours.Other things that are not an option:• "the face has the same skin tone options as the body, including chrome and gold", not an option.• "the face is just a painted mask and does not move", not an option.• "the face is a simple rounded surface without eyes nose mouth", not an option.• "the face is a giant eye/camera", not an option.• "the face is a glass dome with tourbillon behind"......forget about it, your robot "has to look human", even though it can only open the mouth and blink.I'm not exactly buying a game about playing a robot because i wanted to play a human.Also: no "no hair" option.Still. I very much like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the most tepid thumbs up I've ever given a game...There's a lot to like in this game. The moment to moment gameplay is fun and responsive, the art design is very fitting and believable for the setting, the soundtrack is EXCELLENT, the sound design and voice acting are good, and the bosses are a highlight even though there are only a handful. This game is a very competently designed rpg, and presents a good number of builds and build variety for the player to enjoy. The game is not very grindy and generally respects player time, and overall I think the game does a decent job of balance (but it is on the slightly too easy side of it).There's a lot I did not like in this game however. Chiefly, is the level design. It is very maze-like, and the maps are small but VERY dense. You can jump in this game and the maps do make use of the z-axis for movement and navigation, but not too much. I overall found the maze-like map design to be very frustrating considering we are not given an accessible map, or mini-map to help us navigate. There were several invisible walls in places I feel like there shouldn't have been any to block off your navigation which was disappointing. The gameplay was fun, but became repetitive and boring after about 8 hours in. Main reason for this was a severe lack of enemy variety. The maps all looked similar as well. and even in visually distinct layers, there were several objects and textures that you had seen before, giving the game a very samey feel all throughout. Exploration felt tedious and not very rewarding. The last thing I'd complain about is the DLC. It is $12+ for a mere 4-5 hours of content, and even that's stretching it. The DLC doesn't add much to the rest of the game, with only a couple of new weapons (one of which is good), and one disappointing armor set. No new abilities, mechanics or otherwise content that affects the main story line.I don't feel like this game delivered in terms of value. I personally enjoyed the game for the moderately fun combat, great boss fights, and voice acting, as well as the carefully researched likenesses of real historical figures during the French Revolution. I have zero desire to play this game again though. Again, a very weak and tepid thumbs up. Overall, I'd give this game a 5.1/10. Worth picking up on a sale. I hope the developers pay attention to user feedback on what they did well, and make those key elements in their future games. They are a talented studio, but I know they can do better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a close call here because what was presented here had so much potential and at a few moments nearly reached it. But after completing the game, and enjoying it mind you, I simply cant recommend it, at least at its current price point. I got it on sale for 10$ and I think if it were anywhere from 10-20 dollars permanently moving forward I would recommend it. Since I cant recommend this title at its current price point I will start with the bad and then at the end of my review go into things this game did well or even exceeded at. I'll be honest after completing this game I was left with frustration and disappointment because The setting, story, game play, really every aspect of the game is so compelling and I think if it would have been made with a little bit more care that this really could have been an amazing title. Unfortunately what we got was a painfully easy souls like clone with less depth then even the earliest titles from From Software. The starting weapon was literally the best weapon I could find throughout my entire play through I would find myself experimenting with other weapons in hopes of finding something awesome and compelling but every single time I found a new weapon or armor set it was always lack luster and underwhelming and I just found myself returning to my original setup. Making sure your newly acquired loot has a significant enough impact on game play to make it worthwhile and fun to use is critical in these types of titles. Unfortunately for us they significantly under delivered in this department. Not only in quantity but also in quality of weapons and armor sets. Having an actual story in these types of games as a concept is a breath of fresh air and one of the things that compelled me most to this title. As most souls likes have little to no story at all. But again unfortunately in this department they also severely under delivered. There is no character development here, nothing that makes you care. I don't want to spoil anything but even at the end you just cant even find a reason to care about the main protagonist, let alone any of the other npcs you come into contact with. Even some of the big decisions in the game that determine what ending you get just have no weight. You don't even know enough about the characters to care. Also there were some minor bugs such as getting stuck on stair sets for no reason. Or picking up items but then there orbs that signify there location not disappearing after doing so. Normally I would say its no big deal but the fact they released DLC for the game as a cash grab rather than addressing these bugs beforehand is just predatory and I think were better off not supporting this type of behavior from developers. In my first couple of hours I was having a great time and was frequently discovering new enemy types at a good pace and was excited to see what I would encounter later in the game. But about 3 hours into my game-play I painfully started to realize that from then on I would be fighting the same enemies for the remainder of my 54 hour play through. This was a massive disappointment to me and probably the biggest problem with this game. Theirs maybe 8-10 different enemies you will encounter and they are all PAINFULLY and I mean PAINFULLY easy to kill. This problem also isn't just with the basic enemies but with bosses as well. These were by far the easiest boss fights iv ever encountered in a souls like title. Like to the point where most of them I didn't even have to heal my character once let alone die. Not to mention there is really only 4-5 true boss fights in this game and unfortunately not a single one of them breaks this narrative. I will say on a positive note that the creative design and concept of the few bosses and enemy types here is phenomenal which is why as I came to be so frustrated. There is no way to travel to other way points like in other souls like games which results in you having to backtrack so often that I almost gave up my play-through simply due to the fact. You will constantly get lost and even with the compass activated have no idea where to go due to terrible quest pathfinding. There really was so much potential here and they just completely dropped the ball. I will now list all of the pros and cons with this title for those of you who just want the meat of this review.PROS:1. Amazing enemy and boss design (strictly cosmetic).2. Amazing setting and concept that is truly intriguing3. First 2-4 hours feel really great4. An actual story in a souls like game5. Nice level of verticality in this game6. A few decently cool environments that gave me strong bloodborne vibesCONS:1. while the concept of a story is awesome unfortunately here it is delivered very poorly.2. PAINFULLY easy for a souls like game across world enemies and bosses alike. I died twice in my entire play through and only due to my own mistakes navigating the world never because of enemies.3. Loot feels bland I was never excited to find hidden loot because it was never good.4. Easy to fix bugs still remain 2 years past launch and after DLC has been released for a cash grab5. Significantly less content as far as loot, bosses, and enemy types compared to even the earliest titles from From Software6. Poor character development7. Janky, ugly cut scenes that are far below the standard for this generation of game8. Terrible map 9. Very easy to get lost with no sense of direction (you can literally wander around trying to find the exit of an area for hours) even using the compass as the pathing for it is atrocious to say the least.10. No ability to teleport between way points like other souls like titles which results in you running around in the same areas for way more time than necessary.I want to clarify that I don't want to bash the developers here. At its core there is an amazing concept and really cool unique idea in this space. I'm not sure ultimately what happened behind the scenes that allowed this game to release in its current state. But I can say for certain that something did indeed go terribly wrong. I hope the studio learns from there mistakes and is able to take there good ideas in the future and make an actual fun game I can see the potential here. I can confidently give this game a rating of 5.8/10 if you can get it for under 20 dollars I think theirs enough here to get your moneys worth. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a gift in physical form for PC. To be honest i have not even heard of this game until sometime this year. Even though i am a souls fan and played all the Fromsoftware titles, this  Soulslike must have slipped my attention. Once i loaded the game up and heard the amazing main theme in the menu i was instantly in love with the game and that feeling continued as soon as i played the first hour. What an amazing idea and take on the French Revolution. I had some performance issues during my playthrough and texture pop in that sadly could not be fixed but it was still a very enjoyable journey. The enemy and boss designs are very cool and the soundtrack was also outstanding. It has the typical souls "things" you would expect to find in a game like Steelrising and it even has a assist mode for newer players unfamiliar with the genre, which honestly is not needed in any way because the game is not that hard to begin with. Most of the bosses could easily be spammed with grenades and they sometimes would die before even hitting you once. The developers call the style of the game "Clockpunk" and you feel it all the way through.Definitely worth checking out if you are looking for your next Soulslike to play or wait until it goes on sale. Not Fromsoftware level of great but still very good. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a soulslike fan and I didn't like any of them except elden ring. However, this Steelrising is brilliant and I really like it. If it is too difficult in the beginning, the assist mode will help you until you get used to it. But this can be turned off later if the game becomes too easy. I would make this a standard in other similar games because it is very useful and you don't have to risk buying a game that you might not be able to enjoy.I really like this kind of story approach, namely that there is a direct story and you don't have to imagine it or piece it together from different object descriptions. I like the characters and how you can talk to them and the whole side quest system that is connected to them is a very good idea and a nice addition on top of the main quest.I really like Aegis as a female automaton and that she is not only beautiful and graceful, but her look can also be changed to suit our taste during character generation. The fact that the moves and attacks are tied to the weapons gives the character additional depth and adds variety and replayability to the game. The combat system is very well thought out, it doesn't fall into the mistake of being too unfair, but it also doesn't fall into the mistake of beating down everyone with closed eyes after two hours.Artistically, the game is outstanding, the locations reflect what happened in a great way, so the environmental storytelling is also great. The locations are interesting and diverse, I enjoyed exploring the various hidden corners and the newly opened places connected to the side quests.IMO it is not one of the better soulslikes but one of the best, very nice work Spiders!I can't complain about performance and quality. I bought the game on November 6th 2022 and I don't know what it was like before a couple of patches, but it runs flawlessly for me and doesn't crash as others have complained about performance. 5600X, 32GB DDR4 RAM (2666 CL19, average slow) and a 3080 FE 10GB RAM with Windows 11. All graphics are ultra, except for the texture, which is high, ray tracing on, 4K native resolution without DLSS and in 18 hours of playing time, the fps once dropped to the 50s for 2-3 seconds, but apart from that it is always a fixed 60. No lag, no crash whatsoever. My processor runs between 3 and 10% load, the card has not been modified for cooling, it spins between 90-100% all the time.Long story short, I wholeheartedly recommend this great game to everyone, and if you have technical difficulties, I hope you can solve it, because it's really worth playing this game. Looking forward to the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: A while back, I made a review of this developer and was pretty harsh towards them. I would like to apologize to the developer for this. Recently, I discovered that the DirectX 12 Ultimate Software has been implemented, and because of new DirectX and Shader compilation issues with newer forms of Shader compilation in video games, graphics cards like my Radeon 7 are no longer compatible. Because of this, my card will not still run. Rising cannot compile the shaders the way it's supposed to; there is no software patch or update that could make this game run on my GPU. I have had to update the graphics card I currently have to a Red Devil 6800. I'm currently waiting on the water block; once I've updated my graphics card, I will then update this review with more information. I just wanted to put this out there that the developer was not at fault; the fault was mine in that I did not update my GPU appropriately, not realizing that my graphics card hardware could not be updated through a software patch. I have realized it lately with Dead Space Remake this game and Hi-Fi Rush, as well as Alan Wake 2: As I've stated before, I will update my review of the game as soon as my PC has a new GPU in it again. My apologies to the developer; this was my fault. This is an update for the still-rising I am currently running the Ryzen 9 5950x, and my graphics card is a RX 6800 XT. I'm running 64 GB of RAM as well as using SSD M. 2  4 TB each can, and I cannot keep the EDC under control. The EDC is the frequency of power draw to the CPU, and I was running the game at 60 PS, and it went up all the way to 135 That's enough to cause my mother board to explode, and I immediately put all the settings down to as low as they could go, but my EDC frequency was still hitting 80, so I put the game on the 30th PS, and immediately my EDC dropped to 40 and 35 on further inspection. This game is not optimized very well. I took my time, went through every setting, went into the Exe, and messed with operating systems, but nothing seemed to help. I'm running the latest drivers, and I made sure to update my bios for my computer. Nothing helps. I've currently played every game I've had trouble with lately, when I was using my old graphics card, and all those games run perfectly, but still, Rising does not. This is a game that is not well optimized for PC. If you're going to force the EDC frequency to go up to 138, that's a big no. Seriously, if I did not stop it, you guys would be buying me a new computer. This is nothing more than a console port; it needs serious optimizations. With my monster of a CPU that it is obviously not optimized for, I should not be getting these problems, plus the fact that it runs better at 30 tells me they never intended for this to be a 60 fps game. In less than a few changes, I'm going to have to give the port of this game a one out of five. This is unplayable to the point of causing your computer to explode. Seriously, guys, get to work on optimization. We'll update if anything changes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just ok. It's not particularly great, but it's not bad either. I only recommend it if you're out of Souls-likes or its on big discount.I am not really a fan of the art or world. I don't know who thought it was a good idea to make a robot souls-like in the French Revolution. I just think its a bad idea. And the story is also very mediocre and has a stupid plothole ending. The villains literally could have stopped you at any time, but they're just retarded and let you beat them instead.The gameplay is decent, but easy. I don't think its even fair to call this a souls-like because of how easy it is. They give you way too many consumable healing items and I rarely used the recharging heals. There are a bunch of minibosses and like eight actual bosses. I think I only died three times while fighting bosses across the entire game. Don't get me wrong, you can't play stupid. But if you have any kind of experience with soulslikes, it won't be much of a challenge.The weapon design seemed to be pretty creative. You dont have standard swords and shields, but wackier weapons like a constitution scroll hammer, fans, chain blades, and ice pistols.You unlock abilities that allow you to inflict status effects and they can be useful to deal with the different types of enemies.The robot designs were also pretty good mechanically and visually, but there were too few types. By the end of the game I was getting fed up fighting the same robots over and over and over.The level design is not very good. They make layouts needlessly over-complicated and a pain to traverse even when you've unlocked every gate. And if you want to do the sidequests, you will have to backtrack a lot. You will wander around looking for the specific passage way that leads into a different passageway that maybe will eventually lead to the objective marker you're trying to reach. They spam invisible walls everywhere because they wanted platforming, but didn't do the work to make the visuals match what you should be able to do. There are a bunch of places that feel like you ought to be able to turn into shortcuts but you can't. This might be the most frustrating thing about the game.As for the map art, most feel the same and are hard to even tell apart. Other souls-likes actually make each area feel unique by having different themes, lighting, colors, enemy types, etc. There are a few iconic parts of levels, but they are mostly forgettable.Oh and probably the most important part of the game. They made sure to take the only black man in French history, have him deliver a speech on how slavery needs to be abolished, and have every other npc chime in and agree with him. I'm sorry, but I just don't believe ending slavery was the highest priority of the French Revolutionaries. It just comes across as modern people projecting their views onto people in the past. Everyone knows slavery is evil. We don't need to rewrite history to virtue signal.Anyway, I enjoyed this game more than Dark Souls 2 but I only recommend this game if you're out of souls-likes and/or this game is massively on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not without its fair share of shortcomings, however, I can't help but think this is an incredibly underrated game and easily one of the better soulslikes!The game can look quite great at times and the attention to detail in the various automat designs and animations is impressive. Pretty cool and unique in both story and theme with a great, but not necessarily the most memorable soundtrack, this is a fairly appealing package all in all.The biggest problems, I feel, lie in its overall combat balance, lack of exciting exploration due to most items being consumables and a lack of visual distinctiveness between the various areas. Moreover, the performance seemed to be all over the place, even though it doesn't feel like it should be a very hardware demanding game.These issues did not stop me from thoroughly enjoying the game overall, as the combat is still very fun with a unique blend of mechanics seen in other titles of its genre and a fantastic arsenal of weapons. Enemy variety, while not the greatest, is still better than in many games and fits thematically, with different automat templates being modified for different purposes.With everything being said, I had a lot of fun with this one and I think it's easily Spiders' best game to date!

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand the mixed reviews for this game. Is it the hardest souls-like ever? No. Is it perfect? No. But visually, I thought it looked great, even when I didn't play at maxed settings. The world they designed in 18th Century France was truly a delight to explore, and the characters felt like they jumped straight out of history. A lot of people complain about the combat being clunky, which for the first few hours might be true, but once you defeat the first boss, the combat becomes way smoother, and by the end, I felt like every fight was truly a dance, even with some of the more difficult enemies. The bosses, while not the most difficult boss fights in gaming, are all incredibly well-designed both visually and in their movesets, and I genuinely enjoyed fighting all of them. I love the variety of weapons and play styles that are available in the game, and the story is way better than people give it credit for, especially once you start getting into the side content. As far as being a souls-like goes, there was never a point during the game where I felt like I died to things out of my control. Every death I had was a learning experience for me, and by the end, I felt like I was truly better than the enemies I was facing, even in groups. Sure, it doesn't have quite the depth that Elden Ring has, but for a 20+ hour experience, it is very enjoyable.I love the Spiders artstyle, and as a history nerd, this alternate take on the French Revolution was truly an enjoyable experience, even for someone who is not well-versed in the souls-like genre. So don't let the reviews dissuade you: this game is absolutely worth a play, especially if you want to wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I have waited and we haven't had even any attempts at fixing for the poor performance and for this asking price that this game starts at, this is just completely unacceptable.Check this game only on a very good sale, or when they actually fix this stuff and it's Fixed Proper, ie, barely noticeable. I don't recommend buying it until then.Original review:Pretty good game, not the most mind blowing one, but a decent double A game. One big downside are the performance issues, they are pretty bad.The game's main strength are the concept it goes for, this Clockwork army of automatons, it's honestly its biggest selling point imo, with Aegis and the enemies' animations, especially the enemies, because those mechanical jerky movements are very spot on, top notch quality in that regard..This might seem like a moot point to some, but I think with souls-likes animation is integral to the experience, having great animations is something players might be taking for granted without knowing how much polish they add to the overall gameplay experience.For some negatives on the gameplay, some of the bosses specifically Titans feel just a bit too much like pushovers, I think it might be because their attack patterns could've been a bit more aggressive. This is mostly a problem because, it's a bit strange that regular enemies can be much more threatening and difficult than the big bad Titans.Likewise, the combat is decent and serviceable, but it could be further reiterated and improved in future games, some ideas are very nice such as the cooling mechanic, as well as building around it, but I think for a game of this much action, there needs to be just a bit more in terms of moveset.. Not an insane amount of additions, but just a few more moves and uses intended for them, because the amount of moves weapons have feels at home with say an old game like Dark Souls 1, which was slower and more methodical, but this game would benefit a lot more from getting closer to the Bloodborne model when it comes to weapons' movesets.For the story? I would say that it's serviceable. Not bad, but nothing to write home about.At some parts it gets a bit interesting, but I don't think it holds up that well, specifically many quest pieces feel like more subpar side quests in a game like Witcher and that can involve main quests too, not just side ones of this game.Still, the one part I actually felt involved by the story was during the main quest of La Cite and the slow build up to the titan of that place, that I would say was well done and that it's a bit of a shame how other titans didn't get the same type of a caricature as that one did, because this one's whole identity felt like it served a purpose in sending a twisted message from its creator towards the people, which is why I feel as though more was realized with this titan specifically.Lastly, the Performance hits seem to have nothing to do with the specs of the user, as they occur in very strange ways, such as angling the camera a certain way, whether it's into certain angles focusing on the distance, or if it's related to having water effects focused on your screen in a certain way, for instance, focusing slightly above your pov's middle position negates all those water related performance hits, which is despite the water still being in focus of the camera, as it's angled to focus only slightly above the middle most position of your camera..

_childDocuments_.review: Over the years the impression that formed in me around Spiders games is "quintessential AA".It's not a diss tho, I find their games endearing. It's just that going into them you can always expect a significant case of "Eurojank" in the form of dated animations (facial especially), performance instability and balance issues. But it's never a terminal case with Spiders games. I get over those quickly and the pros are good enough to get me invested very early.Steelrising is no different in that regard. Souls-like is a new formula for this developer, but more or less it follows the same set of pros and cons.Pros:+Interesting story+Good sound design and voice acting+Great art direction that extends to world and character designs+At the core combat can be fun and challenging, but the balance... more on that in a moment+On my midrange rig with most settings set to low the performance is stable. High-end users report issues, but with my low expectations performance is satisfactory.Cons:-My biggest and probably only gripe with this game is combat balancing:   1. Power weapons are too slow, leave you vulnerable for too long, and don't even provide good enough damage and poise break in return. Most enemies just tank through your heaviest attacks  2. Just 10 points in Vigor and Engineering is enough to turn you into a tank as long as you wear a good set of armor. By the end of the game instead of being MORE challenged and forced to learn enemy attack patters, I mostly gave up and just abused my fat stack of 100+ Heal-over-time items and most armored outfit while nuking the enemy with Claws. And that's with corresponding stats only half-way to max.This balancing ruins build variety, because there's just an objectively better way to build your MC, which affects replayability.Still, the first playthrough is excellent on the merits of world design, enemy design and story alone. Make your own conclusions if that makes this game worth a purchase never, whenever, or on sale.I'm satisfied with my day 2 purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, here we go. Steelrising is not a bad game, in fact it can be quite enjoyable. That being said: They want you to pay 50 bucks for it. Plus another 15 for the only Story DLC. That's 65 dollars if you're not getting this on sale. What you will get for that will be roughly 25 to 30 hours, I assume. I'm 20 hours in, and I'm confident I can finish this up in around 5 hours (1 more zone, 1 DLC zone). Honestly, the most time is spent travelling back and forth to finish the moronic side quests, most of which are rather dull and pointless and don't even give you any real reward it seems. Main story is just as uninteresting. I'm really trying to watch the cutscenes and dialogue, but my god, is it drab, so at some point I just quick-read, then skip. The character faces, interactions, animations are nothing to write home about. Remember that this game came out AFTER Elden Ring. A game that costs less than this game plus it's "DLC". I know it is unfair to compare a AA developer to a AAA one, but if you're selling a game at premium price it better deliver. And Steelrising simply doesn't (enough).Core gameplay is ... okay, but very floaty. It's weird to describe, it doesn't feel like a souls-like, but more like the Arkham games. Your character lunges and jumps toward the enemies all the time with every attack, the dodge feels like Bloodborn on steroids, the parry is the most satisfying mechanic though.The loop is either "dodge > attack" or "parry > punish". My recommendation would be the latter, since most parry windows are very forgivable and parrying gives you a lot of benefits if you equip the right modules (passive abilities you can have 4 of). Couple that with high "stance" damage and you can stun enemies and crit them repeatedly, especially with fast weapons. I personally love "Ice and Fire", since every parry also applies elemental damage and you can easily set enemies on fire and freeze them this way, givine you even more damage and chances to punish them.Combat generally works well enough after you've acclimated, the bigger issue is that after 10 hours or so you will have seen most of what the game seems to have on offer. This is when you've been to every area, but the final one. I don't know whether the Bastille will have a lot of new things in store, but I sincerely doubt it. Enemy types get really repetitive really quickly. While, TECHNICALLY, there's quite a few in the game, PRACTICALLY, most of them are the same. Fighting a fire snake or a lightning snake or a frost snake doesn't make a big difference. Same for the other enemy types. Each class basically has a few subtypes that all do the same thing, just a bit differently, and the biggest difference is the elemental factor. Enemies using frost attacks are resistant to frost, for instance. There is also a lightning effect I think is mostly useless, since it's just worse than fire or frost. You simply deal more damage to an enemy, but you have to apply the effect first. Most enemies are dead by that point anyway. And bosses are better frozen and burnt and stunned.The same lack of variety is encountered in the weapons department as well. Again, technically, there are a ton of weapons in the game, practically, you get 6 different claw weapons, etc. All the weapons come in different varieties. There's claws that deal lightning damage, claws that parry, claws that shoot projectiles, claws that have a shield, etc.It's just bloat. It would have made more sense to actually limit the amount of weapons you can find, and instead make your basic weapons (claw, chain, fan, etc.) be modifiable with different effects. For instance: Maybe I like the gameplay style of claws, and like parrying, but want to use the alchemy affinity, instead of the agility one, because I like my alchemy effects. And on top of that you could have actually added fun unique weapons you can't modify, instead of having the same weapon several times with different effects.The levels themselves are also a bit hit or miss. They look gorgeous at times, but more often than not they also kinda look the same, which was to be expected if your entire game is set basically in Paris, in a city-scape. Tons of intraversible barriers and your typical "shortcuts" that wouldn't be shortcuts, if the game didn't want you to backtrack constantly for side quests. Seriously, you open up a short cut to your last "bonfire", called Vestal here, only to find the next bonfire right around the corner. Most of these shortcuts serve no real purpose. If you're giving me a shortcut after I've already beaten the entire section what's the point? Not to mention that you can ignore every enemy in the game anyway, and maybe you should, because the enemy placement is often obnoxious as well. The game isn't designed to fight more than 1, at MOST 2 enemies, at least with normal weapons. And the leash range is huge. You also can't really surprise most enemies with backstabs. Sometimes it's possible, but whenever there's more than 1 enemy no way. And later on that's what they do. There's a level where most of the enemies are the same combination of "big lumbering ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and "small little spider buffing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". Every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ encounter. At least you can practice parry timings, I guess. But how about you come up with something different every once in a while?Luckily there is a "compass" item in the game that shows you where your main and side objecties are, otherwise you'd be hopelessly lost in this game. They took a lot of inspiration from Bloodborne, and one of my biggest criticisms of that game is that Yharnam was very difficult to parse compared to any other Souls game I've played. And even that was easier than Steelrising in that regard. And had a lot more variety by the way.Levelling feels insignificant. There's 3 damage stats, health, stamina and "armor" for some reason, which also gives a bonus to the loot you find... I mostly just invested into the latter one, and enemies don't really hurt me all that much anymore with the heaviest armor on. Do I need to increase my damage? Not really. When an enemy has 1,500 HPs, does it really matter all that much that I deal 10 more damage each swing? With fast weapons you can maybe kill them a few seconds faster, but the most damage comes from stuns and counters anyway. Alchemy doesn't really seem to increase your elemental application rate, health peters off after only a few levels (I have like 5), and endurance as well (I've got 4), while armor just seems to scale so much better (am at 15). Lastly, bosses: They look ... nice? But they're really basic. I think I died a couple of times against the first proper boss, but after getting used to the game and getting my build together the rest just fell like flies. At this point I actually have 80+ "slow healing" items (think Dark Souls 2) and 4 regular ones, but I rarely touch them. Every boss is designed to be parriable and stunnable, while many are resistant to elemental effects, because I guess, even the devs realized how broken it is to perma-freeze an enemy. Instead you can almost perma stun them. ;)There's even bombs to help with that from range. Bosses usually have 3 phases, getting more elemental damage with each phase, as well as 1 new move or so. They're not bad, they're not really challenging, either. Honestly, they're the easiest part of the game. And they're not even that much of a spectacle.TL;DR: Steelrising is a competent if flawed entry into the Souls formula, taking a lot of inspiration from Bloodborne when it comes to the core gameplay, at least. It's also got quite a few bugs still, and gets stale quickly, after the devs ran out of ideas, which is about halfway through the game. For 25 bucks WITH the DLC I could recommend it. I don't regret playing it, but I'm happy I got it via Humble Bundle, and only paid 10 bucks for the DLC. Keep at it Spiders, I'm sure SOME day you're actually going to create something special.

_childDocuments_.review: After the latest patch, my horrible performance was fixed. I now play at High/Ultra with RT on and DLSS on performance on a RTX 3070 and i7-10th gen. I still get some minor drops but nothing noticeable or bothersome.Even before this patch, I eventually pushed through the game and the stuttering fps, since my fascination with the art of this game. The environments and the animation really outshined everything else and deemed the game worth my time. I loved the atmosphere and the landscape of a somewhat credible 18th century clockwork-punk France. I felt almost like a tourist in a fantasy world. Second to that, the animations are lovely, clunky on purpose to capture the feel of a clockwork automat and on point with the art direction, but still challenging enough to give a interesting gameplay to soulslike, or ARPG, veterans.Something worth noticing is the great variety of weapons according to different playstyles. There's something for everyone, but unfortunately, I didn't notice the same variety regarding enemies. Still cool designs and good soundtracks.Plus, a big plus for me, EVERYTHING is parriable, even explosions or "dangerous" attacks, it made the game way more fun for me.The difficulty was alright. It definitely depends on what weapons you choose to main and how much you are willing to overlevel yourself. If you like variety in your build, it'll eventually balance it out and it'll become more challenging, surely not frustrating, but I've enjoyed this game also because it wasn't sweaty all the time.The story is interesting, nothing absurd, but it's good; and it's fun to see real historical figures in alternative universes.The time that takes to complete it is fair given its price, and I would recommend the game to everyone. Just be mindful of the performance. The very first area tanks a bit of fps (somewhat like the very first steps in Limegrave in Elden Ring). Glad that the devs are still giving their attention after release. Hope there's more to come!

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was developed in some-what of a vacuum. There are a couple problems that Demon Souls and all the proceeding souls-like figured out that this game hasn't.I will say, the setting is intriguing and the "rapid cool" mechanic is a neat addition (basically active-reloading but for your stamina bar) but that's about it. The combat doesn't feel great. This may be just the weapon I chose (ice batons) but feels more like an action rpg than a souls like. The first boss didn't give off a good impression either and the fight felt visually dirty so I couldn't read what was happening as well. Can't speak much for the environments since I didn't get very far.Here's some incredibly nitpicky and maybe less nitpicky things to just demonstrate my point on how this seems to be developed in a vacuum. This can demonstrate how the developers can fall into pitfalls within the souls-like genre that have been solved, but they are unaware.- Auto-save is awful. Instead of auto-saving practically every single second like a souls-like game should (and games such as Darkest Dungeon), this game auto-saves at random times. I loaded up the game twice from a save and I got placed probably about a minute before I actually quit the game. What's even worse is I did things within the game which should trigger an auto-save then and there. The first time I quit is after "resting at a bonfire" and the second time I quit is after dying. Both of those should trigger an auto-save. Not a fan of a game not forcing you to play through a mistake, especially for a souls-like. This can be akin to save-scumming.- No statistics description, pretty self explanatory- You can't preview a level up. This means you can't tell how much more exp you need to level up 2 levels rather than one. This goes for both cost and the actual statistic. You can't tell if the amount of exp you have is enough for 2 level ups and you also can't tell if 2 stat bumps in, say, alchemy, is actually going to bump up the stat you're planning on bumping up. - Why are there aggro-able mobs in the first boss arena. I'm fine with mobs in the boss arena but one that you can secretly aggro but walking within their aggro range is ridiculous. Imagine almost defeating a boss, backing into a sleeping enemy you weren't aware is inside the boss arena (because why would there be), and it killing you from behind. - The tutorial is kind of awful. Self-explanatory.- I'm not sure why this game slows down your move speed when you lock onto an enemy, whether the enemy is aware of you or not. The game also tells you to slow down your walking to assassinate the enemy but I was able to assassinate the enemy just fine going by the walking speed you get to when you lock on. The assassination range is also larger than the game's UI actually indicates which is just incredibly sloppy. You can press the attack button even when there is no visual indicator that you're going to assassinate the enemy but it'll still do it.- Why do I need to pick up alchemical capsules? Alchemical capsules drop from almost half the enemies, just let me auto pick it up like exp. - A very particular nitpick but I hate it when games, especially when games where the UI is important (such as a souls like for health and stamina management) anchor the UI to the corner of your display (without an option to adjust it) rather than a fixed 16:9. Your game may visually support 21:9 or 32:9 but it's not at all an aspect ratio I would consider playing at. - Shortly after you need to jump to grab onto a ledge to progress, the game puts another ledge that you are unable to grab onto to climb up for no reason other than "they coded it that way". It's at your character's height at the peak of their jump but no, you're supposed to drop down from there, not jump up onto it. - Yeah there's performance issues. It's pretty well-known. Minimum and recommended specs may be too weak for your preferred resolution/graphics setting.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a game I bought knowing it will be bad in many regards. I knew it will be AA at best, I knew the combat will be pretty vanilla souls-like and I knew it will not push any barriers regarding graphic fidelity. I was fine with all of this.However, the game looks pretty bad even by early PS4 standards and the artstyle doesn't help. It has ray tracing implementation but you can hardly tell. With it on, it's still ugly. Normally I would've joked that you can tell only by tanked fps, but that's not the case either. The game runs incredibly bad and turning it off and turning the graphics lower in general doesn't seem to matter in the slightest. This game has the Gollum problem that it has no excuse for not running perfectly on a high end machine. The combat is as vanilla as they come, but it is incredibly easy. I appreciate, however that it's the souls-like in which I relied the most on ranged weapons and usable items. Being easy it's not a bad thing, for me but it might be for you. However the selling point for me was the interesting setting, but, sadly, it's not taken advantage of too much. The characters are horribly designed and stiff and it's so distracting that it takes away a lot from the voice actors effort, which is ...let's say "adequate" at the best of times. The story is basically non-existent. This again, is a non-deal-breaker on its own but combined with everything else, is annoying. When everything is said and done I have played and enjoyed mediocre games before but one thing it had to do was run smoothly, and it doesn't. Far from it. And having this performance 2 years after the release, it's clear to me that this will not get addressed in the future. So, you won't be missing out if you don't play it. However you should check out Greedfall, if you haven't, this devs' other game which it's actually good and pretty optimized. Ah, I can attest to the bug-lessness of the game, but the game is pretty restrictive and "stiff", for lack of a better word. So it's not buggy but you can't really do too many stuff at any one time either, so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking about getting this game you should be aware of one thing first: the first level of this game runs considerably well. I had to put everything on Low to get a stable 60fps, mind you, but since the game doesn't look that good anyway, you're not losing too much graphical fidelity if you're on low. I can run the game on Medium but some FPS drops will occur from time to time.However, things take a turn for the worse when you reach Les Invalides - the 2nd level. This is where my framerate dropped to 48fps and never reached 60fps again. Doesn't matter what i did, even lowering my resolution to 720p didn't make a difference. I don't have the most powerful system out there, I'm just using a RTX 2060+ i7 9750h with 32gb of RAM, but you'd think this would be enough to reach 60fps at 1080p with most settings on low, but nope. I really recommend that you play the 1st level really fast so you can get to the 2nd one and check performance there. If you're under 60fps there, then you might as well asking for a refund if you're bothered by bad performance, because i can assure you one thing: after you're done with this level you can choose where to go next, and both levels that you can choose have similar performance as the 2nd level. Don't even bother. Just ask for a refundThe reason why i still kept the game is that it's fun, even though it isn't as good as The Surge or Nioh, for example. If it wasn't by that, i would never keep this game.The devs don't care about our complains, by the way. They keep posting the same copy-paste response but they'll never fix this game's issues. They made a FAQ regarding the performance issues and they pretty much pinned the blame on us for not having the right hardware to run this game. Thing is, PC is all about flexibility and playing X game in a different numbers of PCs. If you're setting the bar too high you'll not have a lot of people buying your game. Also, I'm pretty sure that people with better GPUs than mine are also having issues running this game. It's a shame that this game is so bad in terms of performance and this is the sole thing that sticks out for me. I could talk about gameplay, exploration, level design...but why should i do that if the most important thing isn't working properly?

_childDocuments_.review: THroughout the start of the game i was unimpressed with the setting and story but continued to give it a chance, the characters are mostly french men who are horrifically bland and exist purely as exposition, which is funny because they keep introducing characters that you have to rescue from area bosses that join the revolution. After some point I skipped every cutscene to get to the gameplay which also happens to be incredibly bland. you do get to pick between several playstyles with interesting looking weapons but why would you do that when you can stun lock the enemies with a charge attack from a large weapon.  Their slow AI that sometimes just stops for 10 seconds straight really doesn't help either. Every fight falls into the same patternof avoid one attack, and loop heavy until death because the amount of groups in the game is woefully lacking and kiting is so unbelievably easy that there is no issue with the few groups that do exist.The locations I saw didn't have enough distinction between them rather than "french countryside" and "french city." the colours used throughout the game for environments blend together into this blue and grey soup with fire sometimes just ultimately makes everything visually uninteresting. _childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I personally never liked souls games, never been able to get into them until I absolutely loved Lies Of P. I got this as part of the Humble Choice for May 2024 and I liked the setting so gave it a go.Never played a Spiders game before, and you can tell they're a small studio as this game is a bit rough around the edges in places, namely character movements/overall graphics.I found the world compelling enough to stay interested, plot isn't particularly deep but the setting makes it. It plays like your standard soulslike, with various weapons and playstyles to suit. I personally went for a Dancer/Agility build so I could break poise on most enemies easily, every enemy has poise, I know some people don't like that but you don't HAVE to play like that, you can play it more dodge/DS style if you want.Map design is cool, sometime's it's not very clear where you have to go, but it has a lot of looping and opening gates like Lies Of P.Comes in about 14 hours (I was idling for a little bit), probably quicker if you're more accustomed to these types of game. I found that just about perfect for my time constraints.]Overall I'd recommend giving this a play, and would say it's a solid 7.5/10. _childDocuments_.review: Scratches that Souls itch very nicely. Most of the time it looks quite stunning (I have no performance problems, but it does take almost all the 11G VRAM I have on 1080p) and plays smoothly.Exploration is a lot of fun. The bosses are somewhat easier than From's, but that's something I like, to be honest. The handful of 'major' bosses are somewhat tedious, though, as they take a long time to whittle down. I hate attrition wars because I tend to get bored in the middle which may lead to making mistakes.As I said in my previous reviews of Spider's games, I find it great to watch this studio claw its way up to the top. They had a nice idea on how to circumvent massively blowing up the animation department, and I think it worked. Some of the animations are really uncanny :) The downside of that is that I sometimes have problems understanding where the front and back of an enemy are, which can occasionally lead to wrong positioning.The sound department also did a marvelous job in creating a rich atmospheric layer that really supports the immersion. It's actually so good that Aegis' cues (when something recharges or the like) are sometimes totally lost to me, which is a shame as it would ease up the gameplay :)The game also features three 'traversal' features that are unlocked during the campain. In my opinion they don't integrate too well into the game, especially since the controls on the gamepad are somewhat awkward (you need to use L1 as sort of a 'shift' modifier - always a bad thing). I got used to them, though. It's used to gate you from accessing side content early on, so basically Metroidvania-style - I'm ok with that.The one thing I really hate is that it occasionally follows the originals a bit too closely in upping up difficulty by having groups of enemies team up against the player (like shielding, healing or, in the DLC, even resurrecting each other) - something the fighting system is not really made for.All in all very pleasant experience worth doing NG+ for me. (Update: NG+ was fun)

_childDocuments_.review: The performance was bad in the tutorial area no matter which settings I use. But then as soon as I left the tutorial area (after the first boss), the game has been running significantly better.The devs should definitely work on the performance issues of this game though, cause that first 30 minutes does not give any good impressions. I was not having a good time.I'm recommending the game cause it's a good one regardless of any technical issues.Update:I have beaten the game once before the NG+ patch, and here is my review of it:The Good:1- Aegis is a very interesting character, she's well-designed, well-animated, and well voice-acted.2- The setting and the atmosphere are on point.3- The graphics are great.4- The enemy design is great.5- The main menu theme.6- The level design is the best in a non-fromsoft souls-like game.7- The combat is fun and feels good.8- There is enough weapon choices for what the game is.9- It is a good mix of souls and souls-like mechanics + new things.10- All the dialogues are voice-acted.The Bad:1- The game has a lot of jank.2- The enemy variety is non-existent.3- Bosses are way too passive and predictable.4- There should be fast travelling between checkpoints and not just regions if the game is going to have a lot of side quest grind.5- The exploration is not very rewarding.6- This game needs a flashlight of some kind. The proper lighting of the game which is presumably 50% brightness shouldn't make the game look washed out. I have a high contrast monitor and I prefer 25%-30% of in-game brightness because that makes it feel authentic and look incredible. The problem is that I won't see anything when I'm in a dark spot.7- The game misses some key PC features.8- The cutscenes put you off sometimes as the facial animations aren't as good looking as the rest of the game. I didn't mind it much but it was an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about giving this a negative review so early, but there is one piece of this game that ruins what is otherwise an enjoyable experience. The movement feels good, visuals are fine for the budget, the UI and general systems of progress look good, but the combat is just too clunky.In most souls-like games, your hits either produce some form of stagger, or you're allowed to dodge/parry at a moments notice so that you can perform quick attack combos without being locked into getting hit. Not here. The ideal form of combat appears to be approach, backup/block immediately, and after they swing, get 2 hits in and back up again. If you go for a combo, you will be hit with no way to cancel the animation. Unfortunately there's no amount of good design elsewhere that can compensate for this flaw.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big time souls-like enjoyer and player. Wouldn't say I am an expert, but I have multiple no hit boss runs in many souls-like games. The following is my review of Steelrising:Pros:Decent graphicsBeautiful environmentSimplified level, weapon, and equipment systemsMostly functional UIObjective markers (most souls-like games don't have)Cons:Poor optimization, especially fps relatedDodge-sprint separate buttons (this one is personal)Rather clunky and un-fluid combat. There are weird pauses in-between actions and the animation doesn't look very fluid. Gives out a slow and unresponsive feeling to your input. This is a major blunder for me. Poor stamina system. The stamina system made it very hard to output damage. The only way to recover is to take health damage by using cool down or wait a year for it to naturally recover.  At its current state, I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few hours ago, I finished the game, and...Although it appears too easy, I really enjoy the ambience of the game. If you could increase the level of difficulty in the future, that would be fantastic!It has some bugs, which I experienced frequently, such as climbing up walls or becoming stuck in the "slide" animation. Fortunately, I was able to load my save, but there are some invisible walls that aren't placed well to areas we shouldn't be on early. For example, the path to a particular character behind a fog; you need a key to unlock his area, but if you jump over the wall you'll be able to get there, and the character won't even load.The optimization also worked great for me most of the time, although in other areas, the FPS felt incredibly low.Nevertheless, some complain that it is even worse for them, so perhaps it will be addressed soon!The protagonist's past was also incredibly fascinating to learn about. The story was incredible; witnessing the French Revolution from a different perspective and direction truly made the game engaging.The battle is alright; at first I felt strange because I wasn't used to it, but as I became more accustomed to the mechanics, it felt fantastic! I can't image how it is with assist mode because, once more, the difficulty didn't really help much because it felt too easy. One thing I didn't enjoy was the slow-motion while parrying or getting parried by an adversary. That actually makes the challenge a little less interesting since you know you have time to get out of there, but that's just a minor thing. The animation of the enemies looks wonderful, and the effects as well.That's all for now, I hope you guys keep making games and learn from what this one did. I highly recommend the game if you don't mind minor glitches or bugs and are patient while waiting for patches; it's a game for everyone. I didn't even know I could use the compass, but I didn't because I prefer using the levels for that. And yes, some achievements don't appear when you complete some tasks.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the 4 hours of the game so far, my first impressions of the gameplay and story have been pretty positive. There are still some level of jank as expected from a game made by Spiders, but the game is more polished than their previous titles gameplay wise. The character and weapon design is excellent and the animations of Aegis is very fitting, still mostly human-like but just inhuman enough to remind you that she is still a robot. The rest of the automats are very nicely designed as well. The locations all look rather historically accurate which can be a problem cause the levels set in Paris looks pretty repetitive. However, I cannot recommend this game right now cause the performance is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Ultra requires over 10GB of VRAM, which is more that what most modern GPUs have, and even with a 3070 I have to use performance DLSS and bring down most of the sliders to high and some even to medium and I still can't hit 60fps in some places. The game also reloads all textures if you tab out while on fullscreen, and watching all the textures streaming back in when you tab back in is really disorientating. When they fix the performance issues I will recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the easiest souls-like I've played, even without using the accessibility options that allow you to tune the difficulty. This also means that it's one of the few games in the genre that I've actually completed without the help of co-op or summons. I think it's a great entry point for games in the genre, especially when deeply discounted. However, if you are a veteran of the genre, you may find this game underwhelming. Things I liked:1. I could easily learn to parry most attacks, which is fun since parrying is a very satisfying mechanic in the genre.2. Revisiting old maps to unlock new passages, complete side quests, and get new equipment and upgrade materials.3. Having a strong and rechargeable-at-checkpoints healing consumable, but also having heal-over-time consumables, that you could loot or buy, that make exploration less punishing.4. Good enemy variety, with upgraded versions of older enemies that have new moves.Things I didn't like:1. Some zones being too maze-like, with fewer shortcuts than there should be. 2. Not being able to fast-travel to checkpoints within a zone. However, you can use a cheap consumable to return to the start of the zone, from which you can travel to another zone.3. The only agility weapon type that didn't feel sluggish is the claws, which made my gameplay options limited. I still got to learn how to best use the weapon against new enemy types, and how to parry them, so it didn't get too stale.4. Armor sets were strangely balanced. There were few with high armor rating, which made most obsolete, at least to me.5. The story and dialogue can drag on a bit6. The environments can get repetitive. They mostly consist of destroyed city streets, with a few unique areas, that are sadly not revisited much.7. No respec, so couldn't give a fair chance to heavy and elemental weapons
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: This game is art and Aegis (the main character) is the artist. The enemies are dancers in this performance and the other characters are the audience. There is a lot of politics here for my liking but if that's your thing, you'll be interested in the story. I was interested in Aegis and anything she had to say. And what a journey it was with her.The voice acting is very good for all the characters. There is a lot of emotions involved but you most probably won't be invested in any character except Aegis herself. There is also a lot of choices to make that alter the story and the ending which is a big plus. Now onto the negatives. Bugs and optimization are a big problem. Mission markers get stuck sometimes, (happened to me twice). It only happened in side missions but you won't be able to progress a mission sometimes without following a guide since the marker is stuck. The game also crashes if your screen turns off if you pause for too long for example, so it's best to not set your screen to go off when idle. I had the game crash at the ending's cutscene and I was incredibly frustrated coz I had to do the final fight again to see the whole scene. No biggie to beat the boss but annoying AF to have the game crash last 2 min like that. The game also ran incredibly poorly regardless of settings used. But perhaps it'll run better for you. It seems random at this point. Another negative is the lack of a map. Steelrising is definitely inspired by Bloodborne but over there every place looked unique and traversing it was easy. Here, most places looked exactly the same so you'll end up lost in certain areas if you try to go around and collect everything like me. Bloodborne and Souls games didn't need a map, but Steelrising would have really benefited from one. Combat in this game was incredibly satisfying and the weapons were really super cool to use. Not enough variety though for each build so that's a little negative. Boss battles consist of main bosses and mini bosses. The mini bosses are usually the same as the normal enemies but with some extra juice and moves. The main bosses were unique and fun. Funny thing though, I died a lot at the first boss but not many times at the others, if at all, including the final one. The difficulty is easier than souls games but it's not easy until mid game. After that, you are basically a Goddess. You'll die at the hands of normal enemies more than bosses in general though. The game has multiple endings and lots of side quests. Lots of stuff to find like weapons and costumes with different stats just like the Souls games. It's a lovely mini Souls game that is incredibly fun for the most part, although I admit it starts to get tiring towards the end because the enemy variety isn't great. TLDR : An almost great Soulslike or Soulslite game with a protagonist who keeps growing on you as the game goes by. And I say almost great because the bugs, optimization, variety of enemies and weapons for each build and repetitive locations are negatives I can't ignore even when I really, really love the game and the main character. If you love Souls games, I don't see why you wouldn't at least like this one. It's really a piece of art. Final Score : 7.5/10 Devs, if you ever read this, thank you for this game and I am looking forward to a sequel!
