_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Recommended. Reasonably priced, visually attractive, easiest soulslike game on the market. Perfect for those who are intrested in the souls genre but too scared of the "impossibly hard, for masochists only" genre's reputation. Rare french revolution alternative history setting is a nice bonus as well. The only questionable part is the performance – use the 2 hour refund timer to figure out if your PC can run the game with an acceptable framerate. I've finished the game and as promised I'm fully reworking and updating this review. First of all – the initial good impression stands and I still recommend the game, albeit with some minor nuances. Further on i'm going to whine and critique some aspects, but despite some flaws as a whole the game does deliver a pleasant expirience and that's what matters the most imo. Now let's explore Steelrising aspects: Graphics – Character and enemy models are very nice and detailed, most background props (statues, vases, paintings, etc) are decent as well, but you will find some murky and unimpressive textures here and there as well, foliage being the most "meh" one. Animation is a bit mechanical and stiff, but since 95% of characters are automatons it fits well with the game's theme. Particle effects... well lets say I've seen better and I'v seen worse, at least they are there.  Still in overall I'm willing to give 8/10 for graphics. Sound and music – sound design is ok, you will get your audiotips just fine and it's not annoying. Can't say the same about the music though – it's probably the most uninspired, bland and forgettable aspect of the whole game. The only composition I can barely (barely!) remember is the Versailles theme. Devs could have used a whole bunch of epic classical compositions by Bach, Mozart, Grieg,  Beethoven – with a bit of remixing they would fall right in place with the game's theme and narrative, but no – they either did not bother or had no funds to license them. 4/10 Story – clean, linear and easy to understand storyline. Basically you are the personified “one man” french revolution. Intresting fact – if you find the human characters of Steelrising looking a bit strange – don't blame the devs for it, blame the painters of the XVIII century. The devs actually tried to recreate the historical figures of the game by referencing the old paintings. Just google 'em up and you will find that they look quite alike. The downside of trying to stick as close to the actual history as they could – is that the side quests are not too impressive, educational – yes, a bit, but not impressive. But i'm willing to add a pont for the rare and not overabused setting so... 7/10 Level design – it's not a “From Software” game, can we lave it at this? No? Sigh. First of all the level design is very flat. If you have read the line about the “hook, new dimension and Paris's verticality” - just forget about it right now. There are a few ledges and balconies that you can reach with a hook and that is all. You will spend the whole game on a very flat city streets. There are shortcuts and metroidvania elements with some areas that you can access only after getting the certain tools, but as a whole this is not even remotely close to the structural complexity of the Anor Londo, Stormveil castle or even Blighttown. But again – the main reason for such a design was a fact that the devs tried to stick close to the actual late XVIII century Paris's city plan. And it was not know for an outlandish architecture. On the bright side historical buildings like Bastille, Louvre, Versailles and an overall city feel and layout – do resemble the actual prototypes. But I still think that the level design could be better even under such conditions, so... 6/10 Weapons and enemy variety – in the first few hours the game creates an impression that both of them are great. Player gets constantly introduced to the new weapons and new enemy types. But after about a 4 hours in you will start to notice that the new enemies are just the slightly beefier versions of the previous automatons only buffed with a different element (fire, ice, electro). And as for weapons – there are basically just 8 of 'em. Wheel, hammer, musket, fans, dual-wield, halberd, claws, chains. Movesets are the same inside the category, but each weapon does have a unique skill  like blocking, buffing attacks with a certain element, counter-striking, shooting, etc. Personally I think that both could be increased further, especially when we talk about the automatons – we could have got some very crazy ones – for example devs could animate the big torsos that protect some gates or make the partially animated death rooms with sticking automated limbs and weapons, make a few more “selfpropelled” carriages and let them loose on the streets of Paris, etc, etc. But we have what we have. On the bright side there is one weapon-related decision made by the devs, that I wholeheartedly support and approve of – namely weaponising all of the “metroidvania” skills. Hook, dash and wall break all double as a corresponding elemental attack, so even if you use non-elemental weapons you will still retain an access to the elemental status effects. All in all 7/10 Gameplay – I've played a ton of souls and soulslike games. Let me say with a 100% confidence that this is THE easiest soulslike game I've ever seen. It's overall difficulty is at about 10% of an average souls game. I am by no means an exceptional or “pro” gamer, I've wiped for hours or even days in some cases on some of the “FromSoftware” bosses, but I have literally steamrolled all of the Steelrising bosses with a single try (technically I did die a few times on some of them but only because i've been experimenting with creative strategies, instead of simply beating them into a pulp).  All you need to do is just occasionally side-strafe from the enemy attacks and poke 'em from the back and voila you are “the storm that is approaching”. And if you are counting in the elemental attacks – enemies do not have any chances at all. You can use any weapon that you like, including the starting ones, and you will beat the game without breaking a sweat. And if you want to make bosses look even more miserable, than they already are – don't use granades on the trash-mobs, save 'em for bosses. You can literally blow ANY boss into the oblivion with grenades alone and it won't even take that many of 'em. Just FYI – i'm talking about the non-assisted mode here. Unless you are a game journalist or an actually medically impaired person – if you use the assisted mode you should be stripped of the gamer title. The game is so easy, that even calling it a soulslike is a misattribution – it should be called an action-adventure instead. Performance – probably the most controversial thing about the game. I have a rather powerful PC, but playing on an ultra settings even at 1080p was out of the question – I had sudden fps drops and stutters. After a bit of playing with settings i'v managed to run the game on mostly high settings at a fixed 60 fps. For the most part I had zero performance issues, unless I've got into the last location – the Versailles. Oh boii. Despite running the same settings as before – there were a ton of places on that map where the fps suddenly and for no reason at all dropped to 30 or even 15 at times and the videocard tried to become a mix of a pan and a spaceship, getting to almost 95-99C while fans propelled fast enough to break off and fly to the moon. If this is what other gamers with less powerful rigs expirience from the start – I totally understand their dissatisfaction with the game's optimisation. Hence the advice – use the 2 hour grace period to figure out if the game runs fine on your PC. And if the performance is not too great – refund the game and wait until the devs will fix it.Apparently I'm hitting the review word limit, so I will have to stop now. The game is not perfect but it was fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: At it's core, Steelrising is an intriguing concept. A souls-like game where you play an automaton in an alternate versions French Revolution. However, TL;DR, despite some cool design features the game fell flat for me. One of the sticking points for me was the setting and design. I like the liberties that were taken with the French Revolution's historical elements and the design elements were top notch. Environments and character design being standouts. While I did experience some frame rate issues at times, I will chalk this up to launch week issues and my ageing hardware.I played this having just come off Elden Ring and was itching for more souls-like experiences...that weren't Souls games. I found that Steelrising takes many of the souls staples and watered them down into their simplest forms. Which isn't a negative, but it isn't a plus either. "Bonfires", "Estus Flasks", shortcuts by opening locked doors later on, and the rest of the family are all here. It just didn't scratch that itch though. There wasn't the weapon and armour customization that I had hoped for. There wasn't much point to mixing X piece of armour with Y weapon to max out your stats. Once you found something that worked, that was just your set up for the rest of the journey. Side note, along the Fashion Souls line, hats were hideous. I almost always shut off those from displaying. The story, while interesting in concept, fell flat for me about halfway through. Exploring the world and collecting items didn't really add anything to the lore. It was people talking about unrelated things in letters, while the story didn't really flesh out much aside from telling you "looks like you need to go this way now". This is what killed the game for me. At the halfway point, I just stopped caring. I couldn't bring myself to finish the game. Sure, I could do it to say I did it. But I wasn't going to happy about it.I think that the ideas are there, I just think its poorly executed. If you are looking for a souls-like game, you will kind-of-sort-of find it here but honestly you would probably be better off just diving into a title in the Souls series you have yet to play. This isn't terrible, but its not great either. If you super set on playing this and can get it on the cheap, maybe consider buying? For me though it was pretty "meh" and is a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: What seemed to be a competent Souls-Like turned out to be more unique and interesting. While the combat takes some getting used-to, it is competent and has various mechanics that sets it apart from just 'copying' From Software. The story is fully voiced, somewhat interesting, the level design is surprisingly good in an interesting way, and the biggest surprise was that it was a .  Overall, I am enjoying the game more than I thought I would and look forward to completing it.There is a good variety of weapons that you can acquire as rewards for exploring thoroughly. The combat itself is fairly loaded as well, you have the classic dodge with iframes, stamina management with a quick recovery akin to Nioh, stance breaking similar to Sekiro, special and heavy attacks, mana, aerial and sneak attacks, enemies have friendly fire, there is a lot more going on than I had expected. I had been on the fence about this game for a while and since it was on sale, I decided it'd be a nice ride before Wo Long released, but I was pleasantly surprised and honestly impressed by what I played so far. The devs did a great job on this and I hope they continue making good, unique, and interesting games.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a game where a lot of things are done to near perfection but also have some kind of annoyance or weird decision that stops it from achieving its great potential.The level design is absolutely amazing. Maybe I will get some hate for this but I will say, the level design is so good that it gives FromSoftware a run for its money. When I noticed that you can't travel from checkpoints, but instead it has some special wagon checkpoints that allow fast travel but are way fewer I said to myself "oh boy, it's gonna be one of those games". I was wrong. There are so many clever shortcuts you don't need fast travel, this game is truly a masterclass in level design. After playing for a while I had to go back for a side-quest in the beginning areas. Due to me unlocking some cool traversal options I found myself revisting an area that I was traversing completely different than the first time. New shortcuts unlocked and new abilities made the same area feel fresh. The level design was so intricate that I think a map would really have benefited the game (no, the map in the game is not a real map). I had to use the compass for some side quests because I really couldn't remember so many paths after some time and it doesn't help that the environments look kinda the same and they all have french street names that I will never remember. Speaking of environments, everything is so beautiful with amazing architecture, but the color palette was a weird choise, lots of areas are full of just shades of brown or grey, it's a shame because the details are amazing but the colors make them look dull.The story was interesting, a bit hard to follow with a bit too much dialogue for my taste. Many times my gameplay was interrupted to show me a cutscene I didn't really care about. There were a lot of NPCs that look pretty much the same. I can't remember who is who because they dress the same, they all have that same french wig, they all have a French name which sounds the same to me I can't remember them.Be careful, the game has a lot of jank. There were some jumps that I did that were so janky I don't even know if I was supposed to make those jumps or the game was just buggy. I could jump over some locked gates which I wasn't supposed to. Multiple times I did a jump and got stuck in the environment and I had to reset the game. There were also some jumps that required pixel perfect precision which were annoying. So pixel perfect that I can't tell if I was even supposed to make those jumps.There are some bugs too. Item pickup is weird, sometime the item effect stays on the ground.The bosses suck. They have cool design but I beat almost all of them 1st try. They were not a real challenge at all. One boss forced me into an NPC dialogue right away and I had an option to tell the NPC about an location but I didn't know it will actually teleport me there right away so then I had to go back where I beat the boss to get my reward, it was annoying that it didn't made it clear that I will be moved to another location.The combat is pretty good. It was a bit weird how sometimes I ran out of stamina just when I staggered an enemy, but the game really wants you to use this system where you can instantly regain your stamina but using this mechanic too much will punish you by freezing you. Some people complained that there is not enough enemy variety, honestly I don't really agree. More enemy types are always welcomed but I enjoyed the variety that was offered, the enemies were pretty different and were fun to fight.The player character is a robot so it speaks with a robotic emotionless voice which makes sense and I did like, but it was so bad how almost to the end they totally forgot the main character is a robot and it started speaking full of emotion and gasping/almost crying. It was really jarring to go from one extreme to the other so fast.The abilities you unlock are really cool, you use them to traverse the environment and also to fight.Steelrising is a game that truly deserves a sequel, the devs should really do another game in this style, it does so many things so good but then it has some annoyances or jank, I think if they would get another chance they can make something truly amazing. You can tell the devs really put a lot of love into this game and the only issues are maybe due to lack of experience in the genre.Overall I very much enjoyed the game and I hope they will make another and improve on the original.

_childDocuments_.review: got a Spiders biasyes, they are more AA, their budgets often rather A studio niveau, but despite the jank i love em allBound by Flame, Mars Wars Logs, Technomancer and especialy Greedfallin the same vain i played pretty much every soulslike (3rd person) out there.yes, even the terrible ones like Dolmeni'm pretty much done with the genre, the only thing i can still boot up is Elden Ring.but i do like Steelrisingthe most important thing in the genre is the feel of the combatand tbh. when starting i realy didn't like how the character feltuntil it clicked.once you get the more agressive style, the quick switching between running, jumping dodging attacksmixing in charged heavies or specials the combat gets realy good. is it From-level-good? certainly not, but i realy enjoy my time with the game.the next thing on the menu is build-options and character progression. you got standart "leveling", but basic stats. again first i was not impressed, but the stats and the way scaling, special effects (like critical hits, or status ailments) work synergieses alot. it's not an overly complex system, but offers easy access to quite some build-options. full on ranged worked perfectly, a more status-effect centered quick burst (dual-tonfa) worked especialy well and tbh. my favorite is pretty much the gun-halberd where you can mix in shots, do heavy charged chains and build around charged (crazy damage) via modules.itemization is okay. there's quite some weapon-variety, from guns, to chained weapons, heavy hammers to claws. each offering unique movesets and a special option (like parry for the claws, a shield for the hammer, or a gun shot for the halberd for example). there's quite a lot of armor to be found (coat, hat, boots'n breeches) coming all with their unique skins stats (and some lore fluff). then there's the usual grenades, stat-potions, and a HoT-potion-supplement for when you run out of os estus charges...stones to be tossed (to pull individual mobs), etc. . it's very competent, very enjoyable and once you understand the mechanics and core-concepts quite different to the usual soulsborne stuff. plays more like a mix between Bloodborne and The Surge. it's not overly fast like Sekiro, still not as slow as The Surge. i think the gameplay got it's own little niche..which is great in such an overflowing genre.then there's the technical side of things. running this game on pretty beefy rig (i9, 3070/3080, 64, Win10) i had wonderfull performance on ultra, with RTX enabled. however there are situations, specific areas where you see a short framedrop. it's not as chuggy as The Witcher 3 was on launch, but there's some optemization still needed. now it's a Spiders game, this ain't an Activision or Ubisoft backed engine-work. yet, the game looks incredible. which comes down to a) the detail (especialy on character models) and b) colors, design and general art-direction. from a pure technical point of view it's a mixed bag. character models can look great, yet human faces are an abomination. enviroments can look downright stunning, especialy on Ultra, yet you fill find many a texture (not in your face, but when rest to look you gonna find em) that looks more akin to PS3 area style grafics. the voice-over is great, but don't expect a narrative driven cutscene fest like The Last of Us. soundeffects are great, the music however is a bit hit'n miss, often just backround-noise-level (easy to forget), but sometimes hauntingly beautifull.realy happy how this game turned out (but i probably had the right expectations looking at the publisher and dev)only complaints:Aegis needs a lightsource...c'monand the game shouldn't have been set in an alternate steampunk history, but rather within the Greedfall universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's evident to me that there's a lot of love put in certain aspects of the game - the way you upgrade the main protagonist is interesting, the plethora of interesting weapons and armor sets is fun but the real downfall is how stale and bland the game gets, quite early on.I'm currently 3 hours in, and I have to say that defeating enemies or bosses in this game, simply doesn't hit the same way as it did with Dark Souls/Demons Soul's/Bloodborne/Lies of P/Lords of the Fallen or Sekiro. I've wanted to try this game for a while, and now I see why it's not a beloved souls-like game amongst the genre fans. Beautiful game, that is sadly 95% empty (kiss goodbye opening any doors) and has extremely repetitive and predictable enemies. At times, they tried a bit too much to be like Bloodborne with the NPCs talking behind locked doors, amongst other things. Perhaps it doesn't help that the protagonist Aegis sadly is, very dull. A game that, in my opinion, had a really strong premise and has beautiful environmental and period design, but has absolutely no identity of its own.------Boy oh boy. Perhaps this could be a case study on how they wasted such a potential for a game. It seems that the last part of the game is made of revisiting all the areas with the most annoying jump + dash combos you can think of. The first three Titans give you special abilities, after that, don't expect anything exciting to happen. I finished the game out of principal, but it stands true what I said - it feels like an empty shell, a game with no identity nor direction. And the storytelling is terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: I am playing this game non-stop. I think I'm about 25% of the way through it, at the moment. I love souls games, but I suck at them. I appreciated the developers adding an "easy" mode. I have been playing it on normal and it's challenging for me, but still fun. The art design, setting, etc. is all great. If you've played a Spiders (developer) game recently, you've probably come to expect things to be a little more organized, written, voice acted, etc. This doesn't disappoint. I've heard this title described as "AA" as opposed to "AAA". Given the recent debacles of many "AAA" games I think we may need to collectively re-think what these terms mean. Nowadays "AAA" seems to be something like "over monetized, over produced, over thought, over hyped". If Steelrising is what modern "AA" means, then I prefer it. Reasonably hyped, reasonably produced, well written, fun, a nod to the humanity of the players (looking at you From, give me a stinkin' easy mode please). Bottom line, if you play any souls game, this is a walking simulator for you, but I think you'll enjoy it. For anybody who is usually put off or intimidated by the difficulty, this game will not enrage you, and you'll enjoy the story and art.

_childDocuments_.review: They need a star rating on these review pages. This game is good for people who like the Elden Ring, and Dark Souls games. I am not a fan of those series so grinding through the same mobs of bad guys just to level up enough to move forward a few inches, then do it all over again, is not my idea of a good time, or an escape from reality. Even with the advanced options added in with quick cooling, which doesn't work all the time, and can freeze you from what it says, it's still a grueling grind to get through it. I spent 3.5 hours on it, and didn't even beat the first boss in the courtyard. I literally started falling asleep while playing it because it was the same thing over, and over again.  There are some people who enjoy that style of game play. Not me. Now, I DO love the story, and character design. The female protagonist looks amazing, even with the limited looks you can give her. I think they did an excellent job on the idea for the game, and the design of the main protagonist. The bad guys couldn've been done a bit better than looking like walking alcohol stills, but it's not a big complaint. Again, I would really, really, like this game if it made you feel like a strong "automat" that is super deadly, but in the beginning I felt just as vulnerable as a human fighting against metal monsters. This is a game for a particulare type of gamer, and I think it's perfect for them, but It's not good for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Souls-like game with beautiful, unique weapons, clothes, and environments, not to mention spectacular level designs. The game excels in these areas and is complemented by a well-told story that seamlessly waves together real history with its imaginative fictional alternate reality. It's a period I don't see represented in games all too often, and it was a pleasure to watch famous historical figures come to life in this creative way. Where the game has room to improve is perhaps most notably in enemy difficulty (it could really benefit from a hard mode) and the limited variety of consumable items. There are also some areas where even the best graphics cards struggle to cope with the demands, but it hardly makes the game unplayable. A little bit of fiddling will fix most issues. Definitely would recommend to people who already enjoy Souls-like games, but especially to those who are intimidated by them and would like a way to ease into it before trying some of the really punishing games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this feels like an AAA developer saw that "Souls-like" is in and tried to make a budget souls game, got halfway through early access and then dropped it once they made bank on early-access sales.Visually the world was fairly empty. Not much to interact with and in most cases you were given 2 paths: 1 obviously dead-end and one that continues the story. I mean that in a literal sense, there wasnt much in the way of exploration. There was a lack of setting and it felt very empty. There were very few enemies and it honestly felt like an Early Access game where you have to accept assets aren't all in and polished. The gameplay itself is subpar at best. Trying to "chain" or "combo" attack patterns results in very janky animations and things not quite working, plus being punished by your own stamina system. Enemy attack patterns are very predictable and everything feels so sluggish. You get into a routine of: Bait attack, dodge past them, attack a few times but not too many. Unlike the Souls trilogy, rather than enemies punishing you by retaliating in a smart/clever way, you are instead countered by your own ridiculous stamina system, whereby draining all of your stamina doubles the time it takes to restore. This doesnt make fights the fun kind of difficult, it makes them the tedious kind of difficult. Woo, I need to remember to attack twice, but not three times, when dodging an attack else I will overheat and get hit by virtue of enemies not having any kind of stamina system. I feel like a large part of the Souls trilogy and souls-like games are clean, responsive, difficult combat. The combat should feel responsive, your actions mattering and your enemies clever in how they fight you. In souls games enemies use heavy attacks, leap attacks, running attacks etc. In this, they might running attack. They will never leap or heavy as far as I ended up seeing, and the rare one would randomly use alchemic (read flamethrower) stuff, but again, it was less difficult and more tedious. I also very much dislike the lack of backstabbing/countering/riposting...  Such a cool and interactive Souls mechanic completely absent in this game. The maker of this needs to sit down and play the souls trilogy before referring to a game as souls like, this is more a souls-ripoff, and a bad one at that. One word tl;dr: Disappointing

_childDocuments_.review: I've had no optimization issues outside of a few frame drops very rarely, and I'm running this on a 1080.The game is enjoyable enough. The enemy variety feels like just enough to keep you interested but nothing beyond that. Level design gets a bit monotonous and same-y, but it's not the worst I've seen. The biggest issue I have is the difficulty, or rather, the lack thereof. Basically all the enemies and especially the bosses need more aggression. The damage feels like it's in a good place, but with how much the enemies just stand around waiting for  you to beat them down, it really doesn't come close to providing an adequate challenge. There are issues with balance as well, the most egregious one being that the very first ranged weapon you get causes freeze buildup on enemies, costs almost nothing to use, and has no diminishing returns, even on bosses. There's an assist mode, apparently, but I feel like the normal game is already on assist mode.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I cannot recommend this game enough. The devs took the absolute best lessons from Dark Souls, and improved pretty much every category. I cannot name one team in the devs' office that did not do its job above and beyond. Graphics, story, level design, music, enemy design, etc.(played this game more than 0.2 hours by far, but was offline playing it)Here is the list of good and bad things:+ GORGEOUS environments, stylized, but beautiful, atmospheric, and fitting.+ AMAZING enemy designs - large number of enemy types, each with a clear purpose (cook, gardener, lumberjack, etc.) and VERY creative designs which look beautiful and have unique attack patterns that fit the automatons' purpose and require different tactics. Special mention to the bosses which have these qualities up to 11. Another special mention to the protagonist herself - she's very detailed, well-made, and her weapons (usually hidden in her wrists) are a cool detail when you swap them. Clothes (armors) you can find and equip are also beautiful, I was considering the appearances as well as stats when choosing what to wear.+ GREAT level design - I cannot praise this enough. Dark Souls tried to recreate the maze-like feel of Firelink Shrine for 3 straight games now and failed. This game's levels are made just right, with creative shortcuts and rewarding exploration, which can result in nice loot or new paths. Each level revels in incredible verticality. Side quests require you to revisit locations and unlock new paths through previously explored levels, which is great and works well with level design and the Metroidvania-type abilities to break walls or use grappling hook that you unlock throughout the game. All locations are beautifully implemented real Parisian locales, each faithful to its atmosphere and unique. Aegis' extreme mobility allows for easy retracing steps and avoiding enemies when on corpse run or doing side quests. Familiarity with complex levels is rewarding.+ FANTASTIC story - the story is very good, believable, gripping, tragic, grounded. The characters are likewise multidimensional and interesting. You'll get to meet all the famous people of revolutionary France. Several side quests can affect the ending. Dialogues and voice acting are both great, with the scripts in particular being VERY well-thought-through, and I'm a harsh judge of that usually.+ good music - I'm not an expert, but both ambient and dynamic/battle music was beautiful, appropriate, and fitting.+ good combat - definitely an improvement on Dark Souls, with verticality, cool weapon concepts with light, heavy, and special attacks, with you and the enemy both being able to inflict elemental effects of fire, frost, and fulmination. Unlike DS, fire resistance or ice resistance isn't just a damage modifier - it helps prevent freezing or catching fire. There is a cool novel mechanic of cooling, which allows you to instantly regain some stamina when at 0 using a timed button press, at the cost of some freezing effect.+ game length - just right, IMO.+/- Story is not as cryptic as Dark Souls, nor is it told through environments and vague hints, but through quests, cutscenes and dialogue. I like this, some might not.+/- Arguably kinda easy. I beat most bosses on first try, and after a while, died rarely. Though this could be due to my experience with similar games. For me personally, the difficulty was just right - I did not care to be killed over and over at each "bonfire". Game features "Estus Flask"-like system, but also "Life Gems" from DS2 - which makes healing system more forgiving.+/- features a "compass" which tells you where the main and side objectives are on each sprawling level. I generally liked this, especially considering it's an optional item, but exploration is not as open-ended as in the first half of Dark Souls. I do not consider this a failing.- Saw some low-res textures on the ground in like one place, but it's well-hidden and the art style is stylized anyway so you probably won't notice. One small area is super dark for some reason, but it's really just a couple of corridors. - As beautiful as everything else is, the surprisingly large number of human characters are a step below graphically - but still very much serviceable.

_childDocuments_.review: If you to develop a soulslike, you gotta make sure it actually works right.Under no circumstances should you do any of the following:- Make all your weapons identical in every way except stats (picked up 7? fans, all with identical movesets)- Have no proper map- Have different healing items to make sure the player needs to waste a maximum amount of time going through items- Make enemy moves deal absurd amounts of damage (e.g. the last seconds of a rotating whip attack animation when the whip moves super slowly on the ground and shouldn't hurt you at all, but does the exact same amount of damage as the peak of the attack animation)- Have some truly unfair enemy encounter setups (like two melee enemies with two ranged ones pelting you while you try to fight)- The big one: MAKE YOUR DODGE BUGGY / CLUNKY AF SO THAT IT WILL SOMETIMES DODGE RIGHT INTO OR WEIRDLY AROUND THE ENEMY INSTEAD OF THE DIRECTION YOU PRESSED OR AWAY FROM THE ENEMYUnder absolutely no circumstance whatsoever should you develop a game THAT DOES ALL OF THE ABOVE.Unfortunately, Spiders did.This game is borderline unplayable unless you want to play on easy mode so the game's many control shortcomings don't get you killed all the time.

I mean, I am being very picky, but that is what bothered me the MOST about this game. It could be SO MUCH better, with a LITTLE more care on the surrounding of its development. The devil really is on the details.Game crashed 3 times for me. No error or reason. While exploring, I got soft locked about a dozen times. As this was before I got to have any carriage tokens, I lost quite a bit of essence like this. Later in the game, I was exploring and fell through the ground. I tried absolutely everything, every time I loaded the game I was still falling. When I tried using the Carriage token, It just did not work, but the disassemble worked fine. These build up essence lost made for a really poor experience, since it was all because of small bugs. I could find some really shallow sequence breaks in my normal playthrough, just triyng to find my way around and exploring, not actively TRYING to break the game. Sometimes the game forgets what your equiped modules are, and you have to remind him of it by opening and closing the menu. This is beyond ridiculous.You are thought by the game on how to open suspended sacks and get some items: in the late game, there are some suspended sacks that you simply cant open. The New Game Plus is nice, with new modules and levels, but it ends after the first cycle. And menuing through all the doubled equipment is boring as hell. The correspondence mechanic is GROSSLY missused in this. You barely send 4 letters and when you talk to the person you sent them, is like they did not read it at all. I could keep going with this for more time and more issues I guess, but this is not the space to do so.TL;DR:I enjoyed the game, but some silly minor bugs are really discouraging, and sometimes game breaking.Being really honest, the ending sequence changed my thumbs down to up, I LOVED the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an easy game for a "Souls-like," but I found it enjoyable anyway.  The game doesn't have many enemy types and only 7 weapon classes (though there are a few weapons within each class which vary by special ability and/or status effect), so there aren't many moves to learn, either for enemies or the player.  My favorite parts were the setting and exploration.  Because of the tools you unlock as you play, you don't just explore the streets of Paris, but rooftops, balconies, sewers and catacombs as well.  Beyond that, I thought the voice acting was excellent and there were plenty of little details that left me wanting to learn more about the French revolution and the people involved.I did have a few crashes and a few areas where the game just didn't run very smoothly, but fortunately they were not frequent enough to ruin the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Good take on souls genre, but sadly very wonky performance. Guess my RX 580 isn't listed as recommended (or even minimum) think latest before just recently released GPUs were o.o', but honestly played more detailed games with stable performance and looking through comments/reviews, people even with latest gears have problems, so it's instantly optimization problem. AMD software did show average of 80+fps, but had to throw all on lowest, except anisotropic 16x and never putting fsr/dlss or resolution scale options on. So far every game had with bit fiddling to med/high. Also there was setting for terrain displacement, as the terrain totally glitching around without it and even with it there were some to see, mainly towards late end of the game. This setting fixed worst of it, but needed to put it off and on back sometimes, as it did blur out textures for whatever reason. Good thing is that even at lowest setting game still looked pretty good for the most part, but had some fairly rough looking parts too due terrain glitch. Lowest fps was around bit under 40fps and highest under 100fps.So to the game itself, nice little story and theme around it. French revolution or so and devs being from there from what do know it's probably solid ground to start built on. Queen sends you the robot bodyguard off to find what is going on and then you get to choose class among four of them which don't really matter, as can upgrade in the end freely your stats and change weapons later on. Went with alchemist and freezing was exceptionally good, but batons were garbage to use due range limitation, sabre and falchion carried till the end of the game. Weapons can be upgraded to level 5 with variety of materials and basically all weapons follow same amount of materials used. Armors or more like fine lady clothing have different stats raisers that are also affected by build stats.Level design was overall very nice and think this is the one of the most souls "this door opens from other side" experience there is, this time they however are (b)locked. Main quest carries on quite a while and few places and you meet good bit of revolutionary fellows on the way before they start dishing out side quest in fairly late on to go even deeper to these levels which have bit of an metroidvania style block instead of (b)locked doors (also keys are sometimes found from these revolutionary fellows deep pockets).Enemy designs are pretty solid and there are good lot of them in several different categories, more animal like robos, entertainer robos, cooking robos, military robos, clerical robos and so on. Then there are the more of mini boss style Unstable versions some of these said ones and on top of there are the real heavy hitters.Gameplay side gives option for defense/offense/ranged and some upgrades from heavy hitters that make the metroidvania approach to level design as well give extra sauce to combat with adding option making some strong hits with alchemical affinity on top while using alchemical capsules which are used with some weapons special attacks and so on. Special attacks for weapons can be defensive or offensive and usually from these 9 types of weapons everyone has different types, so it gives variety and possibilities to play around. Steelrising isn't that hard as souls type, but it has some moments it can kick butt, but gladly there isn't too many of the gank squad moments. Also stamina system is built behind overheating and overcooling system. If you overheat there is timed event that if pushed right it cools Aegis (main character) systems down and keeps her in the battle, but pushed too fast it will take longer to cooldown and too late and you miss that nice extra stamina and if done too many times in short while Aegis will overcool and freeze solid which one need to struggle fast out. This was very nice implementation and idea and it worked very well.Overall would love to recommend this title, but honestly this unoptimized and broken product for full price or almost is starting to become bit too common trend these days. Fix and finish your stuff before putting it out, otherwise honestly people might become very strict their wallets and start the trend again which was fairly usual back in the day. Gameplay and core things very otherwise very well done, but performance and visual glitches were straining. Big points on some of these ideas and level design, nice to see how Spiders has evolved through the years and games. Though haven't yet played Greedfall as just got it as gift, but they older stuff was neat though tad janky.

_childDocuments_.review: A good Souls-like, albeit on the easier side. If you're itching to play a fresh entry in the genre, this game is an easy recommend on sale.Try not to compare this to other prominent titles in the genre, because this game has its own unique offerings. It has its share of problems, in-game and with performance/optimisation, but it's fun to play and is an enjoyable experience. I went in with low expectations and was pleasantly surprised; at the discounted price I paid, I had no regrets and felt like my money was well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising a pleasant suprise for me, i didn´t even know the game was planned i simply saw it on launch day an gave it a go. I really did enjoy my time with it, everyone who likes games like Elden Ring or any Souls game will be right at home. The Combat was very nice an interesting, many cool features and weapons to play around with. In general many possible builds, i testet agility and alchemy and liked both. While agility is rather squishy with high dps and crits, Alchemy does somewhat less dmg but inflictes all kind of status affects on enemys. In the end agility was my favorite thou Like any souls game Steelrising is rather difficult in the beginning, but as soon as you have somewhat a plan what you want to play and get familiar with some weapons the game gets really easy fast. The last few Bosses didn´t even hit me, i entered the fight threw some stun grenades and stun locked the bosses. In combination with a agility build that stunned every 5 hits with insane crit dmg, it even was a bit too easy in the end. Or maybe stun is simple op xD Also i saw some people talk about Assist mode, IDK as sayed the game is really not that hard after some time so i dont see a reason for that mode since souls games do profit from there difficutly, because only then winning a Bossfight and mastering a weapons class feels even more rewarding. But if some people think they need it IDC, i didnt even realise it existed until i saw it in the comments xD  The Story was really interesting with cool character and engaging storytelling, on top of that some Sidequest to thicken the plot around the main story and its Characters. I did finish every sidequest and must say even thou some are simple fetch quests i did enjoy all of them, because in the end u always get a nice reward or secret for your time. My personal highlight of the game, i really liked the Medival France with some Fantasy aspect. The world building in general was very good, the maps where somewhat complex with many parts only accessible with the right tool. i enjoy exploring any of the maps and in the end always found something to reward the extra time i invested looking around. Well i did like the Background music but for me personaly music is not really that important, but from what i heard it was ok Another highlight in combination with the great world the really good graphic of the game shines even more, i played on a decent gaming pc on high and the game did look stunning.  Many people complained about performace issues, i personally dont have an high end gaming pc but i dindn't encounter any problem whatsoever, the frames where stable the entire time and the game dind't crash once in my entire playtrouh so idk was fine for me.In the End i only can recommend Steelrising to everybody even non souls like fans can easely give it a try, if the game really is to hard for some people u have assist mode so there a no excuses, it really is a cool game with a beatiful world and great story. Sure 50 bucks for 15-20h playtime do seem much, but honestly the game is easy worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: How to beat this game:1. Get as much Power and Endurance as you can.2. Use the Fire Chain as your main weapon until you come across the Claw that gives you Blade Storm skill.3. When you get THAT claw, get as much armor as you can in your Modules and clothes.4. Blade Storm your way to ending.Honestly, I thought this game would be like Elden Ring where you need to kinda read the enemy's moveset in order to land a hit. _childDocuments_.review: No, no, no. Do not buy this game in it's current state.I played through the game once right after release (30 hours), actually wanted to give a negative review, but waited for the first patch to be fair. Unfortunately, the first patch does not change the main problems of the game.Gameplay:The player should be given a sense of freedom through jumping, climbing, air dashing and the grapling hook. However, this feeling is very much affected by limitations of the level design. There are fences for example, over which you can actually jump, but this is prevented by invisible walls.Towards the end of the game you realize that there was no time left for development. This is also made clear by the "subsequently added" New Game + mode, which at least appeared on the announced date.Performance:Without understating, I have never played a game with such poor performance. The game is simply unoptimized. With DLLS disabled and all graphics settings set to "low", the game runs at under 40 FPS (5k ulrawide monitor, resolution set to 3440x1440@60hz).The only way to get stable 60 FPS, with DLLS enabled on automatic. The first patch unfortunately doesn't fix any performance problems, but at least there is a justification on the part of the developers, in the form of a FAQ. Even when the game runs stable 60 FPS, it feels not fluent and the character movement feels melancholic.Price:The price is way too high for an "AA" game (is it an AA game?). However, if the performance was bearable, the price would be OK.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soul-like game with great art and concept.I personally like this concept of "french renaissance meets androids" concept. I only find it sad that it's not an actual open world and there is a lack of local map.Gameplay wise, the character movements feel a bit too wide and stiff, but it plays pretty ok most of the time. The variety of weapons and associated attack patterns lets you find a game style that suits you, though I find Elden Ring to be more varied in that regard.The story is ok, though not overly complex and is worth collecting the lore elements and side-quests.The difficulty is high as expected of a souls-type game, but is not as crazy as some other titles of this category.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a 4/10. gameplay is very chunky and there is like 5-6 different enemies in the game. So combat gets extreme repetitive. Also the game was very easy, so for me it was just dull button mashing. Didnt die to any of the main bosses. I think there is a lack of weapons diversity in the games as well. 4-5 types of weapons and 3 different weapon abilities. So claws with buff, or claws with shield or claws with counter etc etc. Also there are some brights ideas with elemental dmg, but it doesnt get utilized in the game. The story is decent, but again the gameplay kinda ruins it for you, so much running back and fourth and re-re-re-exploring areas after the questgiver has said "ok, now you can get the item for me". takes 5 mins to run there and 30 secs to solve and 5 mins of running back. Ok ideas for a soulslike but imo poorly executed for 50 moneys. At the current state the game feels like an indie and should only be worth about 25 moneys.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with a really interesting setting and a wonderful art design---{ Graphics }---Graphics are beautiful. Sometimes they could have used a little bit more variety, but all in all I really loved the atmosphere.---{ Gameplay }---It is a souls-like (kinda on the easier side). It is not perfect by all means (some difficulty spikes, especially if you go straight for the main quest, and some mechanics feel a little bit overpowered), but it is not at all disappointing. There is a good variety of weapons and armours available and you can build your character with the combat style you prefer.---{ Audio }---Nothing to complain about. Good voice acting, good sound effects and beautiful atmospheric soundtrack.---{ Audience }---It is for everyone, except kids and really sensitive persons. Keep in mind that there is a lot of violence depicted.---{ PC Requirements }---You need to have a decent computer to run it properly. I played it on a laptop with i7 11th gen processor and RTX 3070 and it was smooth sailing with very high settings.---{ Difficulty }---As I said it is a souls-like, even though a little bit easier. I am not really good at them so I found some difficulty spikes here and there but if you do all the side quests and level up properly it is manageable and enjoyable.---{ Grind }---You do not need to grind, but I would really recommend to complete all the side quests because they make your life easier, by discovering more powerful weapons and items.---{ Story }---I am biased because I love the French Revolution period, but I found the story to be enjoyable. Aegis, the main character, is a surprisingly lovely heroine, and she will be accompanied by some real historical figures like Robespierre and Queen Marie Antoinette. The ending is influenced to a degree by some choices you make during the main and the side quests, so again I strongly recommend doing them all. Besides, some of them are quite good and make you know better the different characters.---{ Game Time }---I think it is not too long and not too short. About 20 hours only for the main story line, 30 to 40 hours if you want to explore everything.---{ Price }---I have taken it with a 50% discount (€ 24.99) and I could not recommend enough for that price. For the full price maybe if you are really a fan of this kind of game.---{ Bugs }---I have encountered only a few really forgettable bugs.---{ 8 / 10 }---In conclusion I really enjoyed Steelrising and I would give a solid 8/10: good story, really good atmosphere/graphics/sound design, nice gameplay, very few bugs. Do keep in mind that if you do not like souls-like games you could subtract at least 1 point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review. There is an enjoyable game underneath the jank, but there's so much jank. SR is one of the worse optimised games I've ever played and definitely has the worse texture pop. It fundamentally fails as a soulslike because it's too janky to be precise with.The best way to play the game is to turn off the souslike aspects in the options and play it as an action game. The mechanics don't add anything to the game except artificially inflate its runtime. Spiders would have done better to spend more time playtesting it instead.That said, the design of aegis and the weapons have a gorgeous aesthetic, and hitting things with the flame chain is a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: The girl-next-door of souls-likes.Pros:1. the game is fun! The enemies are fun, the levels are fun to explore and the loot is also really good.2. the art is awesome, as usual for Spiders. The costumes, the environments, the enemies. I especially liked how they created jerky movements for clockwork automatons. I thought it was a neat little detail.3. music is also nice. Especially the main theme.4. I liked the weapon design and variety5. the bosses were not too difficult and not too easy. Ok, a little easy maybe, but very fun nonetheless! :)Cons:1. some minor bugs with textures. 2. reaching some places required trick jumps and this game is not made for trick jumps :)Overall, I enjoyed the game very much. I had fun, which is important, and the game did not overstay its welcome. The combat is easy to understand and I enjoyed it. There`s also a story, but since I am not overly familiar with the French revolution, I did not understand much. Last time I had anything to do with the history of France was at school about 20 years ago, so some names are familiar, but not enough to evaluate what the difference between the game and reality is. I did ALL the side quests and a lot of the stories were delivered via text notes (come on, this design element is way overused and needs to go), which I did not read. Anyway, I liked the enemy design, I thought it had artistic flair to it with the musical automatons among your standard knights, infantry, and dogs. I did not use alchemy much because you need bottles and of course if there`s a finite resource - I will hoard ALL of it. But I was ok with the physical weapons.EDIT: I noticed a lot of reviewers mention that it required advanced HW. That is true - I usually play on my MSI GP Leopard laptop (GF RTX 3060 laptop GPU) and I had to use the LOW quality settings. I moved to the desktop I have, which has GF RTX 3080Ti. So yeah, the game is not well optimised.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you meet the following requirements:-You have already bought and played all the mainline FromSoft Souls games. If not buy those.-You have already played, soulslike B titles like The Surge, Lords of the Fallen, Remnant and the upcoming Lies of P-You enjoyed those games and were not too bothered by the B quality-You have jank tolerance and can handle lack of polish and a smaller scale gameplay depth than real souls games-You have spare cash and want to play a new soulslike game-You can handle last gen graphics unless you have a top tier pc with 15+ GB of VRAM to put the textures above mediumIf all those requirements are met, you can get a pretty enjoyable 10-20 hours out of the game.On one hand I want to recommend the game even at it's full pricepoint because the foundation is solid and the gameplay is great. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, where do I begin. Let's start with the cons. Platforming and traversal around debris strewn on the maps can be hit or miss at times. A little more polish and this could have been fixed but overall, it does not take away from the rest of the game. The difficulty is definitely on the easier side for a Souls-like which is more subjective than a major con. Tutorial pop ups occur at the most inconvenient times. This could have been implemented a bit better. Some of the stats aren't explained very well.Now, onto the good. Literally everything else is amazing. The graphics, the maps, the art, the combat and the music, but MOST OF ALL the storytelling and voice acting! This has to be one of the most well written stories I've come across in any game I've ever played, PERIOD! This makes it stand out 10 times more in the Souls-like genre. The reuse of the maps to complete various side stories is top notch and well executed. Very interesting lore! I love that this story was told via in game events, cutscenes, conversations and text. This is how it should be! Also the weapon variety is amazing. I enjoyed every minute of Steelrising and I HIGHLY recommend it! This game is nothing short of a masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 45 extra hours, until I've finished the game and the DLC. First the good things: the robots designs, the Paris recreation is really really awesome, for me the best feature of all. There are some "copy and paste" stuff (same designs used over and over through the game) but is ok.  The fighting is also great, Aegis is easy to maneuver, every enemy has its unique power and weak point, and you'll have to learn to fight each one. Aegis' arsenal is massive, lots of impressive weapons. The history is also very good, several characters and I really like the dystopian France idea with robots in 1789.  The music of the entire game is fascinating, so well composed for the era and location.Regarding the things I did not like: during the fights there are moments when the camera falls behind trees, bushes, leaves, walls, and block your vision. This should be corrected: the objects should go invisible during these times, to avoid vision block.The mission "selection" could be better. Another annoying thing: is incredible the amount of tiny places where Aegis gets jammed. Just a small step or ledge and the character gets trapped there and cannot move forward. Regarding the graphics, they are good, but the requirements are too high. The system optimization is bad and the high loading times for textures should be corrected. The graphics are not that impressive in these days, even the faces of characters in the dialogues are graphically really poor. I think that the game is amusing, almost 2 months playing it but  it was launched too soon. There were still things and details to solve before launch. Still too green.There are tons of bad reviews claiming for an update for this game, and the developers just launched a FAQ.  Sorry, but until you don't came out with a patch, I cannot recommend. I can recommend it only to the one that want to play a Dark Soul's type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Having just now finished it, I can say it's an incredible game that excites with wicked combat, absorbs you in its dark atmosphere and carries you through an amazing story that builds up to one emotional climax. Bon travail Spiders! Definitely a game well done!To go into more details: Staring with the game as a whole. It really is done well. It has certain Greedfall qualities - so many of the same voice actors, it was lovely to hear! They did an outstanding performance again. The story is basically the French Revolution - I know, surprise, surprise. They tossed in decent variety of automates. So the range of enemies is not bad. It did have moments were it began to feel very grindy, I won't lie. I had times where I was left sighing over the countless assaults. (And getting lost, a LOT, I can't remember quite where... Louxembourg? Or La Cite? But uff.. a few streets just look a tad too much alike) BUT, it certainly keeps you engaged, albeit a bit monotonous at times. That said, I did play with Assist Mode, perhaps I could have tried turning that off at some point. However, I'll always be a firm believer that games should be challenging AND fun, not just the former. So, they certainly gave you a good option to gauge how you like to play. Back to automates, Aegis is the outstanding one, of course. While I wondered at some point in the story, what really sets her apart, her character develops nicely and naturally. I don't wanna spoil anything here but I promise, if you feel a bit stuck, perhaps even a bit tired of it - hang in there. It gets better. The story picks up and the ending was phenomenal! I also did all the side-quests which I found to be quite well fleshed out. They played into the main plot and even affect the ending. So, whoever finishes this game in supposedly 15 hours.. I have no clue how, nor why anyone would want to rush through a game in the first place. Do all the side-quests, engross yourself in the experience and Steelrising will definitely leave you satisfied at the end of it. As for bugs - I had no framerate problems whatsoever. Not in the Beta and not now. A few hiccups. Like the E button prompt would sometimes disappear. Along with the enemy health bars. I had one instance where the voices cut out during a cutscene, too. Luckily I had the subtitles on.Other than that, nothing major.From atmosphere to the soundtrack, the combat and the story I would give it a strong 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice soulslike that wears its inspiration like bow for all to see.The movement takes a bit to get used to, but it fits seeing as it's a robot you controlReally well designed levels with shortcuts and details, and the Bloodborne inspiration easy to see, especially how you interact with the NPCs through the windows and such.An interesting plot that keeps you engaged.Lots of interesting weapons. However, those weapons also becomes the focal point of one of the weirdest design decisions I have experienced in a long time. So many weapons to try, but no respeccs. So I ended up equipping weapons, trying them out, thinking: this seems cool, too bad there's no point since my stats won't work with it. Then putting it away again.I cannot fathom how they landed on giving us no respecs with that array of weapons available, just mindbogling.But I do hope the team takes their experience and creates a sequel, or something in the same genre. There's a lot of brilliant ideas here, but a lot of polish would be needed and experience to make this a stellar experience to play.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s obvious what  was going for, and while it succeeds in some aspects it ultimately is a Neoclassic-style victim of its own ambition.You take the role of a clockwork girl in service of the queen of France as she’s set to stop the madness of the king who seeks to raise a metal army to crush all who oppose him.You’ll meet various historical figures who will help you to achieve this plot to overthrow the monarchy in this alternate history setting.Equip your weapons, attacking and dodging your way to victory, it’s a very simple formula but one that works well thanks in no small part to the smooth controls, making dodges feel snappy and precise while other upgrades let you personalize your experience further.Levels themselves are a simple go from point A to point B while having some little side paths you can take to explore a bit and looping on themselves so you can open shortcuts near savespots.Another thing it features is traversal upgrades to make warded off areas explorable, so you’ll run in the various locales multiple times with different paths depending how far you’re into the story.Relatively to the game it tries to mimic it lacks depth, polish, aesthetics, and a characteristic sense of style many smash hits seem to have.Here’s some major complaints:Now this wouldn’t be a problem unless we consider what this game is priced at 50$, landing it in the same ballpark as the best of the best in its genre while being not only inferior but clearly a copy to them.I still had my fun and the game still does something interesting with its mechanics, hence why I recommend it, however is absolutely not worth the admission price, wait for a VERY generous discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is incredibly clunky.- If you don't mash the attack button your combo starts over, so everything feels choppy.- You need to hit the dodge button at least three times before you'll actually dodge, and even then the enemy attacks track you and hit you during the dodge.- Every enemy has high poise, so every fight becomes "attack, attack, dodge, wait for your incredibly slow stamina to come back, attack, get hit, attack."It feels like an incredibly cheap knockoff with a cool setting. Play Lies of P instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising was at first a positive surprise to me, despite me disliking Souls likes and combat centric games. It's because it's pretty easy in every way. At least the first parts. But since combat is everything in this game, it gets repetitive and boring in the long run. In fact, there's too much of the boring and annoying stuff. The genre is apparently not for me.Combat... Yeah, it's the same over and over and you have to either spend lots of time to avoid taking damage, or play it like I tried to do - agressively, with lots of power to finish the enemies off as fast as possible. But my build was obviously not good enough from the boss in the mines and onwards. At that point I had no patience left and was fed up with the same challenge in repeat. So I started up WeMod. God bless one hit kills. Because grinding isn't fun. Neither is "gitting gud".Then there are close to impossible jumps... Trying to reach that ledge that you have to reach to get to your objective? Well, try and try again, only to fall down and take damage or die, because it's too far. Finally succeed by glitching onto an invisible ledge just below the one you wanted to reach, and jump up. Annoying.It was one jump in particular that I just couldn't make that made me turn to Youtube. It turns out I was expected to use one of the special attacks to make the jump - one of those attacks to you believed only works when you have a lock on an enemy. Jeez.Navigating the city... OMG. There are walls, blockades and fences everywhere. Going from one side of a building to the other can require a detour around the whole city. You can spend a good amount of time only to figure out how to reach the objective marker. Annoying.However, I enjoy the story and love the atmosphere and the music. It's an amazing game in that regard. But the gameplay... No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the gameplay and aesthetic, enough to recommend to anyone who enjoys action RPGs, however if you're here for the story, characters, or history you'll likely be disappointed. The story is fine as a premise, but the way it is told is incredibly stilted and shoddy. I couldn't play the developer's other game Greedfall due to the poor lip sync, and while this game is just good enough the animations overall are quite lacking, both in cutscenes and combat. The main twist of the game is incredibly obvious, the main characters are largely unlikable people you are meant to care about helping as well as all looking very similar. As for the history it is less an exploration of the period and events and more like wax dolls of historical figures quoting textbooks about the French Revolution at each other. The combat is generally fun though it is hampered by a lack of clean animations on some enemies, most enemies taking a bit too long to kill, and performance issues that crop up every once in awhile. TL;DR Gameplay is pretty good but the story and historical elements are poorly done.

_childDocuments_.review: It has an interesting take on the soulslike genre. The combat is a bit slower paced, but has a rhythm to it that fits very well with the aesthetic and theme of being clockwork machines. It does some things I don't like (no i-frames on dodge) but does a number of things I DO like (don't mind the haters, heavy weapons are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SATISFYING to land, I've not seen many soulslikes that actually give heavy weapons the feeling of ACTUALLY slapping someone in the face with a fat penis. If you can't get HRT, just play Steelrising with a halberd on max strength. It's the same feeling. If your erection lasts for longer than 4 hours, call a doctor).There is a surprising viable build diversity as well. My personal build was a str-based heavy weapons build that was very fun, while the 'meta' is a medium weapon agility build based on stance breaking and ripostes. Status ailments aren't broken, but are effective enough that an elemental build is just as (if not more, in some cases) viable. Though, a part of this is also a function of the game's difficulty - it's a bit on the easy side. So easy that there is an achievement for not using heal flasks, and it's surprisingly attainable even for mid-range players.The story is actually pretty solid as well.  There is something to be said about how the sidequests softlock you out of one of the endings if you do them, which I found a bit annoying. Without spoilering too much, I really enjoyed how Aegis starts off as a blank-slate droid and develops into a distinct personality complete with her own political opinions by the end, and I at least think it had a very satisfying payoff.At casual pacing, expect a good 30-40 hours, depending on how much side content you do, with an easy 10ish hours extra if you go completionist with it. The worst string of collectibles to find runs about 18 pieces, and they aren't just random ticks on a counter, they are all actual intractable pieces of the game with little pieces of worldbuilding that can actually make them somewhat worthwhile if you really get into the setting.The art design is amazing all throughout, though the level design doesn't quite touch the level where you can avoid getting lost without a map. It's not bad-bad, but there are a couple of points in the game where you'll feel it (especially if you're going completionist with it).There are a couple of minor threads that are a bit annoyingly lose (like too small to be an actual plot hole, but big enough to ask 'what happened with that'), but the narrative wraps up nicely with a definitive conclusion that would make a narrative sequel a bit hard to pull off. There is a sense that there is more meat to this game than it's story allows you to really chew on. I hope to see the devs do more with this framework in the future.Overall, the price point is solid for what you're getting (I'd say it's worth it without waiting for a sale - but the DLC, definitely wait on, it is nowhere near enough content for full price there).

_childDocuments_.review: i'm on a 5800X3d and 6950XT 16gb with 32gb Ripjaw pc4000 and have the game installed on my SK Hynix P41 m2 ssd. In 1440p max settings, I get 55-60fps. That's absolutely terrible, considering this game doesn't look any better than Thymesia. The character models certainly don't, they're reminiscent of Xbox 360 or PS3 character models. If you notice the screenshots they chose for their Steam store page, you'll notice most of them are filled with bricks/gravel/rocky surfaces or surfaces with baroque looking artwork. That's because they can pump up the tesselation and ambient occlusion which give these specific types of polygons softshadows and other fidelity enhancements, and at a low resolution it does an excellent job of tricking your eye into thinking everything on screen is of equivalent quality. They just slapped a lot of bloom all over everything like they did in Greedfall.I don't mean to sound like a complete hater, but the negative reviews are absolutely correct. Spiders really screwed the pooch and jumped the shark with optimization here, it's absolutely ridiculous. My machine should only be getting framerates like this @ 2160p with Ultra quality and extensive raytracing enabled, ie. Cyberpunk 2077.It's too bad the framerates and 1% averages are so awful. After you've gotten acclimated to 120fps/240fps+ gaming for an extended period of time, anything below ~85fps starts to look really choppy and can even feel unplayable if it dips further. It's amazing how much a good machine spoils you.As is usual with Spiders titles, however, the setting is immersive and absolutely fantastic. I love Greedfall on my Series S, the Rennaisance-era/Early Spanish fusion for the aesthetic is unique and gorgeous despite the mediocre player models. Steelrising is the same exact way, this French Revolutionary era aesthetic is uniquely beautiful as well and despite some (once again) mediocre player models, still manages to create a distinctly original setpiece for the game's environment and backdrop. Spiders really does know how to create realistically immersive locales and ingame worlds, it's easily their strong suit next to combat mechanics.After playing Thymesia, Combat in Steelrising just feels kinda -meh-, like an average Soulslike game if you will. The atrocious stamina limitation is the main culprit here, you can barely string together a combo and a dodge before your character starts to overheat. If you can spam alchemical effect resistance potions to prevent getting frozen from instantly recharging your stamina bar (pressing E during overheating), than it doesn't feel that bad. But that of course isn't really feasible, especially early game, since they're rare. This jilted level of early game stamina leads to some really boring encounters, like the unstable automaton in the early garden level. Talk about a snore fest.I can't recommend Steelrising until they fix the game's performance. The quality of the game does not warrant the 9 gigabytes of used VRAM when you consider how poorly it performs. RDR2 on Ultra everything uses 2-3 less gigabytes of VRAM and looks much better than Steelrising. And I average 120+ fps in 1440p in RDR2 with everything maxed out and raytraced.PS. In fact you can tell for sure optimization is broken, because using 1080p->1440p FSR/enhanced scaling gives identical performance as just playing in 1440p direct scale regardless of the profile you've selected (ie. ultra/quality,balanced,performance,etc). Spiders needs to address and fix this issue immediately.. the longevity of this game is going to be a literal blink of an eye if they don't, I almost gauarantee you.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10If you're looking for a game that is a Souls-like, and takes a chance, Steel Rising works. There are pros and cons, but overall, I enjoyed it. Taking place during the French Revolution, you play Aegis, an Automaton loyal to the Queen, Marie-Antoinette. You embark on a mission to uncover the truth behind the automaton invasion, and how to stop it. At one point in the story I felt the pace ground to a halt, with the Black Frenchman, Julien. I personally didn't care if there was a black man in Paris, during the Revolution, who hailed from the Colonies abroad, but the lecture about slavery being bad wasn't necessary. We all know it's bad. It kinda tainted the story for a bit, and bothered me way more than it should, as I felt the writers were trying to justify Julien being there. The lecture about slavery came off as a virtue signal to me, and left me rolling my eyes, wondering if I were going to see a BLM Banner somewhere in the game. It's a Steampunk fantasy about the French Revolution, so anything goes. As for the rest of the story, it needed A LOT of focus. While I get wanting to write a complex story within this setting, sometimes just focusing on one or two elements is all that is needed. Too many different names to remember and what they were doing bogged the story down.I went with a very powerful Alchemy/Engineering/Power Build, with the Fire Bayonet and the Fire and Ice weapon, and with that combo the damage was insane, as are many other builds. But add in the Ordinary vials that dropped like crazy and you really didn't need to use the Burette. Modules made the combat and boss fights too easy. Level 3 Fortifying Counter essentially healed you for quite a bit when you successfully used a Counter. I LOVED the visuals of this game. The city of Paris was burning, smoldering, destroyed. It was fun to find different areas and explore them. I can't remember the name of the coat I had for Aegis, but I stopped and took a look at the embroidery on it and was really impressed by the level of detail there. Automats were really lovely as well. However there were some performance issues, and I have a pretty good rig(i7 10th gen, 2070 RTX Super), and the FPS sometimes dropped significantly for no reason. As I said above, if you're looking to scratch that Souls-like itch, STEELRISING is a decent game. I'd love to give it higher marks, but the cons and the story and game pace got in the way. I got my money's worth out of it(I saw that some folks beat it in 8 hours. Guess they just needed to speed run it), and even purchased a copy for a friend to enjoy. Pros:*Visually gorgeous.*Combat can be fun(but there are some caveats to that)*Character models are really interesting*Movement is nice, most of the time.*Spiders and Nacon are taking big chances with their games, offering something new and unique.*Aegis, and the Automats were beautifully designed.*If you like Sekiro you'll like this and how Aegis moves*Interesting fantastical take on the French Revolution, and those involved.*Weapons were fun to play with, but once you get into a rhythm with what you liked, the others weren't necessary.*Really awesome outfits for Aegis. Spiders and Nacon knew that Fashion is a priority with alot of folks.Cons:*Unstable performance issues*Combat can be easy(get enough "Echoes" and you can buy grenades, and just throw them at your enemies from a distance. Boss fights are too easy).*Assist Mode. Wasn't necessary. *Too many tools for you to use for survivability(the grenades and immobilizations should have been EXTREMELY RARE, not easily purchasable at the Boutique)

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is one of the most difficult games to review. On a scale from super frustrating to maximum fun, this game hits every single note.My initial impression was not great. I jumped into the game expecting another Spiders RPG and seemingly only got a linear combat simulator. Not being experienced in Souls-like games it took me an hour to familiarize myself with the controls and concept. Also the first map is probably the weakest graphically. After I finished the map and wanted to travel to Paris, the game crashed and reloading didn't help. After an hour of research and fix I was finally able to continue the story. This kind of crash still happened randomly later in the game, which unfortunately still has a lot of bugs.The first half of the game is pretty much just combat after combat. The gameplay is very simple: you try to reach the next save point and open all the shortcuts, so in case of death you can avoid excess combat. Apart from the enemies, there are no other NPCs on the streets at all, it feels empty and you also don't have a companion this time. Understandable from a story perspective, I just don't like running around in empty spaces with the sole main character. The combat itself is one of the highlights of the game, at least until you've seen and tried everything. There are no ordinary weapons and enemies, everything feels pretty unique and crazy. The design and animation of the automatons are awesome. Huge kudos to the designers, artists and programmers here.Once you start meeting human characters, another aspect of the game opens up. It turns out that there's a decent underlying story. If you skipped history class, and names like Robespierre don't mean anything to you, it might not be such a relevation. I had a lot of fun meeting these historical characters in a wildly fictional setting. The cutscenes (especially the echoes) are a joy to watch. I have to commend the melancholic, orchestral soundtrack that boosts the mood in these scenes. Still, it's not a proper role-playing game, all your skills are for combat, and the story doesn't really branch out (although there are several endings, but only with subtle differences).Unfortunately, after a while the core gameplay becomes tedious, there's a lot of backtracking, even with the shortcuts and fast travel coins. By the end, I wished there was a movie or series based on this alternate setting instead of the game. So is it a bad game then? Not at all. But don't expect it to be a masterpiece either. The story kept me going, but I totally understand those, who dumped it after a few hours.
