_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would give this a 7.5/10Pros: Amazing story, I was entirely invested in the world, its characters, and cried at the true ending. To get the full story side quests are imperative, but they weren't a slog. Really loved it, it was my favorite part.Atmosphere was really great, the burning city, the massacres, the feeling of despair in almost every map. It was really nice and felt authentic. It really got you into the mood for the game and really set the tone while doing the quests.Combat was relatively easy, but wasn't baby-mode. I'm not the best at souls games so I liked that, even without assist-mode, normal difficulty was exactly as described. Major bosses took one to two tries, had mechanics and patterns. Normal enemies annoyed the hell out of me but what is a souls game without dogs.Voice acting was extremely solid. A lot of them are from previous Spider Games, or were VA's who i could easily identify and did a great job as always. The voice of Aegis was amazing and made it super easy to connect and get invested in her.CONS:Not like other Spider games. For me the companions, the romances, and the friendships you build along the way are imperative to a good game and narrative. While I still enjoyed the characters, and connected with a lot of them, I'm sad they abandoned their normal design. I do accept this is what normally gets left out in souls games, but I think it would have added a special feel to the game.Bugs made the game a bit jank. I've played almost all Spider games and without fail they are always jank. For me it wasn't much of an issue, I could run everything fine, but now and then I got drops in frames as well as audio issues. A single cutscene wasn't voiced or animated as well. But Spiders isn't AAA so it really wasn't much of a problem/surprise, but I put it under cons as some people are mad about it. Other Comments: I really loved this game. I liked it a lot. I think, if they blended their usual stuff with this souls-like it could have been closer to a 9/10 but the lack of companions and romances really bothered me, even though I was still invested. The True Ending made me cry, and I really liked Aegis. Even though I missed these, however, I think the narrative is one of the better ones I have played through in a while. I also appreciate that it was straightforward. The sidequests were fun, it easily expanded the lore without being super long, and I think the game has a good length as well as decently fun combat. I think for most people searching for a chill game that is a good time, has good characters, a cool story, and decent gameplay will be pleased with this game. There are some bugs, but most games that come out these days have them, and for me they weren't much of an issue.I see a lot of people harping on the fact there are black people, or that its non historically accurate, among other things. Don't listen to them, they are idiots. It's a steampunk game about Robots fighting other Robots. It's fantasy, and if you can't get over a black person in it or they fact they added some random person or event for drama sake, don't play it. That is just my opinion, but I felt the need to put it here. It's a fun fantasy world and bigots need to go cry a river elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: For the first few hours of playing this game, I was battling the feeling of what a mistake I was making. The awful performance (more on that later) was so atrocious that I was barely able to run the game at a playable framerate. Jankiness is there, getting stuck on the terrain while running is there, bugs, getting soft-locked, characters freezing in dialogues, or completely bugging out are all there. The bosses are laughable, if you are competent or semi-competent even, they cannot kill you. Design-wise, yes, some bosses are intriguing but gameplay and challenge-wise? shamefully, not a single boss is memorable from this entire game. And regular mobs and enemies, once you understand how the game works you will rarely die even when outnumbered, it's just disappointingly easy.However, underneath that pile of issues, there's a game about friendship, heroism, serving God and Nation, about a political struggle on a national scale that will either sink or explode France. For those reasons, the game is worth playing. Assuming you really, really like soul-like games and are addicted to them (like me), then you can play and enjoy Steelrising. Here is where this game suffers the most:Steelrising has a Metroidvania-like aspect; you start out missing some abilities that you need to progress to other parts of the map and for combat, like every other MD except here: 1) This game isn't optimized whatsoever. I don't understand what their intention was here, the game needs so much VRAM on your GPU, and to do what? the game doesn't look revolutionary at all or special. Since the performance is so bad, almost everyone will have to lower the settings so much that the game will look like a mess so their work on the graphical part was in vain...2) The early levels are so uninspired and bland that it might just kill off your interest before you even get to the fun parts. 3) You have no special abilities at the start, you cannot interact with things you see in the world. Your combat options are limited and you care not about anyone in the story because you know nobody just yet.Now, if you can suffer through the first few hours and accept the bad performance, you will discover how this game grows on you. I believe, or at least that what happened to me is the game slowly got better or I understood it better. I still had to restart the game because I got stuck in the terrain or a quest got bugged out, but despite all that, those political characters that you meet, Ageis herself, slow and bulky elemental combat, and exploration make it all worth it. Especially more so when you finally unlock abilities that allow you to fight in more fun ways and more importantly, progress further in each region so you can start doing the interesting and fun side quests that help you understand the world and its people, foes, and allies, those who lived in the past and the future generations. The way people spoke in France back then, according to this game, and their traditions and clothes, haircuts, and culture, the artistic nature of life back then, it was a special thing to witness too.Maybe Aegis' heroism and dedication to her task aren't really things to admire about her because she isn't a self-conscious being, she cannot make an active decision against fulfilling her duty or looking the other way. If one cannot refuse to do something, then doing it isn't worth the praise. I wouldn't blame you for thinking that way, but at the end of the game, you will realize that even a rising steel can be conscious, and can make active decisions.Aegis says: "I cannot escape my obligations. It is in my very nature to honor them." But what about the player? Who made an active decision to play and suffer through this game's shortcomings as Aegis suffered through the game's events?Just you and her both, aiming to reach the same end goal: Pour La Nation...  Pour La Nation.

_childDocuments_.review: It is probably one of the worst optimized games of all time, its performance is absolute trash.Running on 12900k, 32 GB Ram, 3080 Ti at 1440p, and regardless of the visual settings, there are constant fps drops, stuttering and bad frame pacing. Disabling E-cores makes it run better, but there are still constant fps drops. It seems that the game utilizes only a few cores, and hence the stutters when the main thread is locked.And it actually looks like a 5-10 year old game, especially the janky animations, horrible particle effects and human characters right from the uncanny valley.Gameplay wise, it's also nothing special, just another Soulsborne clone with really bad level design (the locations are mostly linear and have no memorable areas), the only interesting thing about it is its setting. But this only plus is utterly destroyed by all the cons: horrible performance, janky animations and clunky controls. Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that throws a lot at you but lacks any depth. There are better Soulslikes that are much, much cheaper. It's linear, punishes exploring or any attempt to break the set path, and has no fun upgrades to look forward to. Visual design is an enticing point, but once gameplay kicks in that falls dead on the floor. Severe lack of enemy or weapon variety combined with armour and upgrades only increasing stats instead of changing the way you play means you'll be fighting the same enemies the same way for a dozen hours long. Some design choices are excessively lazy, with you being able to kick a robot to death but needing an upgrade to kick open a door or crumbling wall, every citizen dialogue being virtually the same and every locale being the exact same (Burning French city with exclusively dead people around).The story starts decent, is a slow mess for most of the rest of the game but ends strong, with multiple options to unlock. A replay is in my opinion not even remotely worth it.Combine this all with the many other complains people have such as performance issues and you got a game that doesn't even remotely hold up to the first Dark Souls, has worse systems, but a higher price tag. Get a different game.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you to the developer Spiders and Publisher Nacon for providing a new fun action game for me to escape, explore and enjoy. *This review also includes the DLC. My steam review rating: PositiveA couple of things first, this is not a souls like game. Second, performance is still weird even 6 months from launch. I tried to lower each option in the graphics setting(low or off) one at a time and nothing would ever change. My solution was to set everything to low and it fixed the problem. The strangest part of that decision, I couldn't tell the difference between max and low settings(besides FPS), none. Steelrising is a reimagining of the French revolution where King Louis and his advisor Caligistro have assembled a robot(called automats) army and declared martial law against all who oppose his rule. In the game you will play as Aegis, a automaton who has been assigned by the King to be the personal guard of his wife Maria Antoinette. Maria and her helper have been exiled by the King to a nearby city as they watch flames and smoke of Paris from afar. Maria worries the King has gone mad from the loss of their young son and is being led astray by others. She orders you to seek out those who understand the automatons' function and to help stop the King. A strong story set up and setting makes for a really great adventure, and it is, but the story is…Ok. There are two major issues that I couldn't ignore. The first is once the King and Caligistro are aware that you(Aegis) are causing all the havoc they could simply have pulled the plug, to avoid some story spoilers. The other major issue is the total lack of any amazement(there is a little) that an automaton has free will of their speech, actions, and thoughts. So much so, Aegis will be asked her opinion on certain political issues multiple times which have consequences to multiple endings the game provides. The story is not the worst ever and with good voice acting, tons of lore, and actually a story that I did find interesting, I think it was just a missed opportunity. This is also magnified by the DLC which feels like a stripped away chapter of the game and would have given some more insight into the real enemy of the game, Caligistro. After receiving your orders to go to Paris you have the ability to customize your look which is minimal and choose between 4 classes: The Alchemist, Bodyguard, Soldier and Dancer. This choice really only affects your starting equipment but keeping an eye on stats and how you distribute points as you go will determine how you want to play. I chose Dancer due to it being the class with fast mobility and agility which is how I like to play these games. Aegis would use light/medium class weapons and be able to dodge(dash) and strike quickly. You of course have a light and heavy attack and if you hold in for the heavy it will give even more damage. As I played through the game multiple times, I tried almost everything and found any class to be fun. As a third person action game, not too much is different from what we have seen the past 10+ yrs in the genre. There is a stamina bar, a very good parry window,  if you die, experience points you have gained will drop at that spot and enemies will respawn. You will be distributing points into 6 categories(I never added any into health on first playthrough) which consist of Power, Vigor, Engineering, Elemental Alchemy, Agility and Durability. There are plenty of weapons to enjoy from dual wield, two handed, guns and others which are all perfect for the steampunk like setting that has been created. Each weapon also will come with unique and different animations for each attack variation. All are very cool and the integration of Aegis' dance moves is pretty awesome. My favorite is probably using the morning star as Aegis will do a ballerina spin move and then kicking it at the enemy.   All combat will be against other automats who come in all shapes, sizes and wielding all sorts of weapons and even musical instruments. The creativity that went into the automats is definitely one of the highlights of the game. The enemy variation however is slim as they all will be used multiple times. As an example, the first enemy may only wield a ball and chain but later the same enemy and weapon will have elemental attacks like electricity, fire or ice included. Also when entering an area you will have a mini boss fight and once you have defeated that enemy they will become part of the rotation you will encounter while exploring. As the game is not the long slog like other titles in the genre, it didn't bother me but a few additional enemy types or just some different animations would have propelled the experience. I was disappointed the dlc did not include new enemies, but just more reskins with a few new tricks. One being a necromancer to raise fallen enemies and one to heal their friends during encounters, yea I'm sure to not be anyone's favorites….ever..As I stated earlier graphically the game looks gorgeous even on the lowest settings but I just have no idea how your system will react. The created world of Paris and surrounding bureaus are fantastic to explore and while a majority are just cobblestone streets, housing complexes and large gov. buildings you will also explore the sewers, a mining operation and grounds of large estates all in a very destructive state. One thing that I did not expect was the verticality and hidden pathways. Some bosses will drop equipment that will allow you to unlock doors, break walls and reach higher areas you encounter on the journey(avoiding spoilers). The DLC does offer a more countryside setting and definitely breaks up the confined city look of the main campaign.  A brief talk on bosses, unlike the common enemies you will engage with the bosses here are all well thought out, unique and fun. There are 8 major must beat bosses with an additional 10 that are tied to side missions. If you are either new or veteran of the genre nothing is really too difficult and unlike others most save locations are seconds away from retrying if you fail. I may have died only a few times until encountering the 2 last bosses(and the DLC) which definitely requires more patience compared to the others.There are actually two ways you can play SteelRising and one is sticking to the main story(no side missions) which will probably take around 15hrs max but if you go down the rabbit hole of exploring and doing all the side missions and DLC it will equate to around 30+hrs. After around 21/2 playthroughs to complete one of my favorite achievement lists, I never was bored or felt like any of my time was wasted. That my friends is what i like to call a good game. PositivesFun, cool action gameUnique story and setting Excellent enemy and weapon creativityFun RPGvaniaSolid combat DLC UI is simple and informativeOne of my favorite achievement lists to 100%Not a 100hr boring slogNegativesWeird graphical performanceSome story elements Enemy varietyNo area maps

_childDocuments_.review: Is Steelrising a good game in the Soulslike genre?No! Unfortunately it isn't. The game has some good approaches and has areas with great attention to detail. But the negative aspects simply took over! Here is a small list.Positive points from my point of view:- the game doesn't have too long of a playing time- beautiful graphics of the clothes and the design of the doll itself- the main bosses were nice- a few options for weapon selectionNegative points from my point of view:- controls are very terrible and clunky, especially at the beginning- combat controls are implemented quite poorly (when dodging you always had to press the button twice, otherwise you would always get 100% hit)- the wayfinding is a joke in this game (you're just running around and searching, unfortunately very confusing)- a Soulslike lives from its opponents, but not from the masses of enemies (there were too many enemies in one place in some places - not that great with the combat system)- the bosses were recycled and then turned into normal mobs, but they were incredible HP sponges- the story was conveyed quite poorly- the cutscenes for the story conversations were far too long and, to be honest, boring- there were NPC conversations in the city that seemed to be secondary tasks - I couldn't solve any of them because it wasn't clear where I could find something to solve them... so much for finding the waySo here is my conclusion:I played through the game - so it's not that bad. But at times I was so annoyed by the pathfinding and the associated jumping mechanics that I won't play this Soulslike game again. On the other hand, it was too “easy”. The main bosses were cool but also quick to kill. So the challenge isn't there and that's a shame.It would be presumptuous to compare this game with big titles like Dark Souls, because that's simply not fair. But I can only say this much, I enjoy playing the other Soulslikes every now and then - but not this one and that actually says it all.Of course, if you want to form your own opinion - then definitely wait for a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: The souls genre has become oversaturated. As with any fattened fandom, this has resulted in widespread subversion, due to the relatively simple concept. People want to give out hot takes and so they will get as subjectively faux-pedantic as possible.  Steel rising is a good game but, you can tell that it's affected by the shifting discourse in the genre. If I had to relate it to a game, it wouldn't be dark souls. It would be Soul Reaver, which is the ancient great grandaddy of darksouls that no one cares to give credit to.  I wouldn't have even marketed this game as a souls-like or even used the out of place 'bonfire' mechanic to pander to 'souls-like fans'. The combat isn't worth dissecting the Spiders classic combat system for. The animations were better and more unique when it launched but they weren't dark soulsy enough for a loud minority of players.  The weapon availability and styles were better when it launched but people cheesed the mechanics and then loudly blamed the game for it. I despise 'souls-like' fans. They don't actually care about gaming or games. They care about sublimating their masochism, rooted in low self esteem, into negativity in online talk spaces. They ruin games, like this one.  It's a single player game. No one cares about your steam 'achievements'.

_childDocuments_.review: The Soulslike genre has created an entry that is incredibly difficult to follow. I put hundreds of hours into Elden Ring while avoiding the rest of the Dark Souls franchise like the plague as intense amount of challenge and difficulty do not generally appeal to me. I don't like the idea of spending six hours on the same boss until I can dodge the right amount of times and kill the thing. No thanks, I have things to do.This game brings in the wondrous "assist mode", which I haven't seen in the likes of Surge or otherwise. You can customize damage reduction and stamina regeneration, both things that are incredibly useful in making the game a lot more playable for casuals like myself. I put it at the middling 50%. I still get punished for not timing dodges while not being killed in two shots, so it's a nice middle ground.So if you know anything about the Soulslike genre you know the deal, here. Challenging and difficult with enemies that pop out of boxes and corners, don't get their attack animations cancelled (while cancelling yours), and large boss setpieces that are most certainly designed with the sense that it will take more than one attempt to figure out. Block, dodge, maybe even parry if that's a thing you can do. I certainly never can, in any game really. Beyond that, there's no need to get detailed with the mechanics as it's all pretty standard fair. Limited potions, refreshes at save points (which also respawn all enemies), and so on.Generally what this genre has to do to set itself apart from others is theme and aesthetic. We're placed in Alternate History Paris where a mechanist invented automatons. You play as Aegis, a feminine Automato special for its ability to speak and think on its own. The intro scene doesn't explain why or how, just that the Queen's aide just says it is so. You're sent off to fix all the things.I don't yet know the full breadth of the story, whether they are actively on the fritz and sacking the city or if they're just doing what they're told... by sacking the city. Much like Bloodbourne (which I only know from Let's Plays), much of the civilian populace is unseen behind boarded up windows that occasionally yell things as you get near. So like most of the genre, a lot of the game feels fairly lonely. It mostly makes up for that with the general aesthetic, spades of Steam or Clockpunk are abound, and if you like the general clicking and whirring of gears you'll be plenty happy here. You can hear every step Aegis makes and patrolling Automat can be heard beyond various walls.Overall, I'm enjoying the game but there are issues.Elden Ring this is not. While you can return to previous areas to farm out experience, this is not an open world rife with activities. There are some side quests spread around for you to look into but it's really just a railroad of a game. A fancier corridor slasher in its own right (like the classic, older Souls games). So don't come in expecting a lot to "do" in general, as it's mostly a game of clearing all the hallways until you stop finding glowy bits to pick up.I have problems with this style of exploration. It's not always clear on which fences are mountable or not. Sometimes you see some messy white paint that denotes a grab-able ledge but it's not universal. Sometimes you just see a broken fence with some greenery all over it but there's nothing distinct about it to tell me that it's an explorable segment. Some ledges and fences look perfectly jumpable but there's a ton of invisible walls because they couldn't figure out any other way to say "there's nothing back there". Much of the city is in ruins so a broken fence just looks like a broken fence to me. Early on you learn about keys and gates and it just made me run into every gated door in the game only to find that there's not even a prompt on most of them so a lot of the times I spend exploring I'm just kissing the perimeter until I see a prompt for... anything.Notably, the game is badly optimized. I tried to record for my youtube but it came out as an unwatchable slideshow. The VRAM useage in-game is not representative of what the game actually uses. While the game itself runs fine on medium settings, it still bogs down my computer to the point where my podcasts on the second monitor start to hiccup and skip, and alt-tabbing makes my computer have a small seizure. At one point, I got a Crash To Desktop by changing some of the settings so even the game itself doesn't like you fiddling around with its inner workings.It's basically a task, the very first thing any player should do is lower the settings.I have this on "Yes" but honestly I would respect anyone waiting for a sale or putting it on follow to let this one cook in the oven for a few more months. There's some merit here, but a lot of calling out in the reviews saying the Devs are being inactive... for two month old game. Maybe they're not communicating as much as they should but let's cross our fingers and hope they work on the optimization. That's the biggest problem here so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from someone who has 300+ hours in Souls games, Sekiro and Elden Ring, TL;DR below.Where to begin with Steelrising? I am conflicted because I am inclined to recommend this game for all Souls players to experience what can be done better in the genre, but the lack of consistency when it comes to quality does put me on the fence. I have thought really hard on how to write this review, and maybe it is best I present some of the dualities in game quality first:On the one hand, the diegetic inclusion of cutscenes pulls me into the story and increases my involvement; on the other hand the outdated facial animations and abrupt story pacing is further exasperated by said cutscenes. (I have to note here the numerous amount of unexpected story twists that actually surprised me)On the one hand, your character is as mobile as it can be with sprints, dodges, dashes, air attacks and grappling hooks; on the other hand the abysmal enemy variety delimits any experimentation with any gameplay styles.On the one hand, the game surprises the player at every turn with how its world is interconnected and how shortcuts are everywhere; on the other hand every single area can be described as "Urban streets in Revolutionary France" and assets get old quickly.On the one hand, the weapon variety and the levelling system provides a customisable engagement; on the other hand it is both very easy to overlevel which makes the already very easy game, quite very easy (For my run I used a weapon with high attack speed and the ability to deflect, and wanted to mirror my now 4-time-finished Sekiro experience)The game starts out slow and rather boring. You quickly meet with many NPCs and start doing side quests for them, and the momentum of the intrigue and main quest escalates quickly and pulls the player in as they try to navigate the interconnected streets of Paris. During the peak times of the game you are having solid fun with combat-map design-story as the stakes are raised with every quest and new area. You've made mindmaps and can quickly navigate between environments. You try to piece together information that will allow you to deduce what will happen in the next cutscene. Afterwards it slows down to a series of quests that involves a lot, a lot of backtracking through previous areas to just talk to people. Regardless of its shortcomings, Steelrising is encouraging when it comes to experiencing Soulslike variants, and especially puts forth new methods to expand upon the gameplay, at least theoretically. I would not hesitate to buy a potential Steelrising 2, or other Soulslike releases from the same dev. The game would have been an instant buy only if, instead of an "Assisted Difficulty" option that decreases the difficulty, it had a "Hardcore" mode with bigger and better enemies. TL;DR: Buy this game if you are not a Soulslike player. Buy this game if you are a Souls player and are curious about viable advancements for the genre when it comes to story and game design and don't mind the fact that like out of 15 bosses in total only 3 of them are really unique.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm enjoying this, great visuals, decent performance and interesting story. Sometimes the camera and controls feel a bit sloppy but it's not terrible and certainly not game breaking, just requires some getting used to. Once you learn the cadence and rhythm of combat getting into a flow comes fairly naturally. It follows the souls formula well but is far less challenging, consider it a casual souls like. This is a good thing as I think more players will find it more accessible, it's a decent entry into the souls-like genre. It could use some polishing, which I'm sure will come with future patches. All settings at high or ultra except for shadows and shadow distance, ray tracing enabled. Getting 60-80fps on a 3080 10gb with DLSS set to balanced at 4k. Without DLSS I get mid 30's.Overall I'm having fun with this so far and would recommend it, but I'm only 3hrs in so you decide what thats worth.

_childDocuments_.review: My first review, yay.I just finished my second playthrough, the first being regular and the second with NG+. Some pros and cons to my experiences regarding both.Pros:I picked this game for a few reasons, being the beautiful character model of Aegis, the premise, and the fact that it looked like a less intense Soulslike game. I've been wanting to try the genre, and I felt like this would have enough going for it to keep me playing while learning the ropes, which it did.During my first playthrough, I eventually decided to turn on the Assist Mode because I felt like I wasn't having a good time learning the Soulslike mechanics without dying constantly. Roast me if you want. I really appreciated the Assist Mode because it did let me learn the mechanics of attack timing, stamina, and better resource management, which I'm frankly not as used to in most other games I've played.I unknowingly picked what's been deemed as the most difficult class to start for new Soulslike players, being Alchemist. I've had a good time with that class, and the batons that are associated with the class are right up my alley for a faster attacking play style. I'm going to use a third playthrough to try out the heavier weapons.I do feel like the game is scaled pretty well as you go through.I think the story is pretty good.Cons:I don't know the specs of my computer, and I know there are known optimization issues with the game, dropping frames, sudden closing of the game, etc. I'm pretty understanding that this is both because my computer isn't the most optimized, and that issues can occur unknowingly after publishing a game.Some of the achievements are still locked for me, notably the  and  achievements. I'm pretty sure I should've also gotten  and  achievements as well, but maybe I missed something in those achievements.While your main character is really well made (just the velvet on the armor pieces is immaculate to look at), I can't say the same for most of the human characters. There's some janky facial animation during the cutscenes that are in that uncanny valley spectrum. Monseigneur de Le Fare barely opens his mouth, even during high energy dialogue, for example.I do wish the world (well at least this context, this region including Paris), was more open world with each of the areas connected and there was a more proper mount to travel with. Imagine, an automaton horse to ride on and attack with.One more con that contains spoilersAnd with both the pros and cons, I don't think currently it's worth what I payed for it, but I do believe it could be if these aspects were tightened up.Overall, a solid 7/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Overall a decent Souls-inspired game. On the positive side, the graphics are amazing, the setting and locations are interesting (the first 5 hours at least), and the combat, while at times clunky, is quite fun. On the negative side, France and the French, the side quests are unnecessarily confusing to get to, the level design is extremely linear (and yet confusing), and the enemy variety is quite limited, which adds to the fact that the whole game is set in basically the same city, makes the experience repetitive after the first 5 hours or so. Having said that, the gameplay is compelling enough to finish the game without getting too fatigued. I wouldn't say this is a Souls-like game as it lacks the combat depth, the open-ended and interconnected level design, the challenging difficulty, memorable boss fights, and environmental storytelling. nevertheless, it is a fun, lighthearted experience with a pinch of Souls flavor with substance and a lot of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I want to preface my review with the fact that I've enjoyed every minute I've played. I'm running on a gaming laptop from 2016 and still capable of playing on custom graphics on a mixture of ultra, medium and low config settings. That being said, this games optimisation for PC is very lacklustre. The gameplay itself is quite fun and rewarding, if not just a touch shallow. The latter boss unlocks allowing for alchemical attacks provide a good way to open up for elemental damage for non alchemist starting profiles. I've enjoyed the setting, the atmosphere, the story and the characterisation of the historical figures; and I appreciate the accentuation of the Voice acting. All in all, the game itself has been quite a fun experience overall for me since my purchase; and I have been lucky enough to skip a lot of the problems a lot of other people in the reviews have had to experience. All of this being said, my experience with the title has been utterly ruined by a single glitch that has completely stalled my progress through the campaign. In MontMatre, after defeating the Centaur; there is a Lift. After doing some of the side quests and going to find the final echo for the coffin before said lift, I decided to be a derp and leave aegis under the descending Lift. This proceeded to kill Aegis. I expected this. What I did Not Expect was upon returning to the lift, it was fully recalled to the top of it's ascent path; and the lift lever that calls it down to descend is completely inoperable. This completely has forestalled my progress in the campaign. I've reloaded the save, restarted the game. tried fast travelling to other areas in the game and coming back. None of these have made the lift lever operable. For this reason alone I am giving the game a negative review, as the devs have clearly not even been bothered to think that their players might try to stand under lifts, and seeing as this specific lift is the single route to one of the final areas of the game; it completely halts all progress of a campaign. A major oversight of the design phase and truly unforgivable in my own opinion.

Still a good Souls-like set in French-Revolution Paris, with a few interesting mechanics and traversal capacities.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing, beating, and doing some side stuff, i can say that Steelrising is a great soulslike with some bad gameplay designs and decisions.First the positives. It looks fantastic! The detail in the world, the designs, the animations, everything is great to look at. Weapon animations in particular are downright gorgeous, even if the weapon variety is a little baron. Controls are tight, allowing for great movement in fights, and with the gameplay being more attuned to Bloodborne, speed is your best friend. Weapons feel top tier, hitting enemies is satisfying regardless of the weapon you choose, and with the addition of more modern features introduced in Sekiro and Elden Ring, jump attacks, critical hits, staggering, charge attacks, are all here and all great. Lets get to the juicy part, the bad. As mentioned, Steelrising is visually a very good looking game, but this comes at the cost of system requirements and performance across the board. I own a 3080ti, and the performance is decent, but seeing videos on people playing with even the 1080ti, i can see why people are complaining about performance. The story is so damn boring, that i rush through the dialogue at every opportunity, and thank god i do since some of these conversations can go on, and on, and on. Difficulty is either easy... Or incredibly easy. This all depends on whether or not you use the most broken thing i have ever seen in a soulslike. Steelrising's frost mechanic. Its insanely overpowered from the start, and only gets better when you level up weapons and find heavy weapons to synergize its effect. Freeze an enemy, swap to a another weapon, charge attack, profit. Even when not using this broken combo, the enemies have some tracking issues when it comes to dashing around them. None of these are honestly bad, but after hitting max level with my heavy and ice weapons, the game's bosses are literal jokes.One last thing to note is the price and how people are up in arms about it. $50 is steep, yes, but this isn't a unity asset flip. Its not a retro game with a minimalism style. Its a full fledged game that took alot of time and effort from an indie company to make look and feel Triple A as they possibly could with what they had. Its not fair for people to assume $1=1 hour or some nonsense like that. Is the game Elden Ring good? Of course not! Elden Ring had 100+ people working 5+ years, its safe to say Steelrising does not. the company needs money to fuel future projects of equal or greater scale, and i think $50 is fair considering most soulslikes are honestly pretty damn bad or lesser copies of the original inspiration. I really liked Steelrising, a few issues, but i would 100% recommend this if you're looking for a Bloodborne-like.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice and unique addition to souls-like genre by Spiders (their first). I enjoyed the game a lot: atmosphere, overall design and setting, but the best part in my opinion is a really fun gameplay. It is not hard or challenging once I understand how it works, but it is always immensely satisfying. So much so that I overlooked repetitive combat encounters and lack of enemy variety. The story is set in alternative version of Paris during French revolution, except, robots are everywhere. Historical is mixed with fantastical in interesting way and it all fit together nicely as I was uncovering what was happening bit by bit from conversations with many characters and doing some side quests. Yes, game has many well written side quests that have effect on ending of the game.The world of the game, mostly city of Paris, is separated to multiple enclosed levels. Each of them is vast and interconnected with a lot of hidden and not yet accessible areas and also visually unique (some more than others considering its mostly one city).There are a lot of small, but interesting features that enhanced my experience, like game pausing automatically after cinematic ends if I switched to second monitor in meantime or unique ways of dealing with elemental damage (except electricity for some reason). And many others I'm sure, that just don't come to mind.Overall I had a great time with the game, it is not super polished AAA experience, but that is not to be expected. The biggest issue I had was questionable optimization and really uneven performance, where I had  60+ fps in one level and barely 40 in other.

_childDocuments_.review: Just don't. This is not worth your time, money or attention.Performance is terrible and textures look so low-res that they rival the PS1 for fidelity if they even load properly at all, Gameplay feels awful and far too stiff, There's absolutely no variety whatsoever once you've finished the tutorial as almost every single weapon type and enemy type is found in the tutorial, Armour (clothing) is literally pointless as none of them actually appear to do anything of actual valueLight (agility in-game) weapons are the only ones of value due to the "immobilisation" mechanic demanding repeating hits to get "critical" hits (backstabs, basically), making the entire heavy category pointlessRanged attacks are worse than useless,Only the frost elemental damage serves a function as fire and lightning appear to do literally nothing, where frost damage locks enemies in place for big hits and the majority of enemies are vulnerable to it AND you get a reliable way to deal frost damage in the tutorial and another after the first major boss which puts you into melee range,There's only 8 bosses in the entire game. Only 8, and with each district only taking about 30 minutes to get through even while looking for pickups (most of which are useless items which give you currency), you'll fight the first three (which give you the mobility upgrades) within about three hours,The story is a mess and has absolutely ZERO catharsis since it's so unbelievably predictable that it could genuinely be a Dora the Explorer episode for how simplistic everything is. The plot thread regarding who/what Aegis is is literally resolved as soon as you achieve the second major objective of the game if you have two braincells to rub together and can do enough critical thinking to make a prediction.Every historical character you meet in the game is weirdly off-kilter. Somehow at one point, famous abolitionist Lafayette is talking about how he owns slaves and how much profit they make directly to Julien Raimond, a black slave owner who justifies his own ownership of slaves in the same conversation, and the game entirely unironically paints Robespierre as an incorruptible (a laughably bad take) figure of truth, justice and liberty. For a game made by French people, they absolutely do not appear to have any pride for French history if they're getting things THAT wrong. And yeah, yeah, it's an AU where robots exist, but beyond that they're all real people being portrayed, and yet here Spiders are portraying Marie Antoinette as a good person and fully justified in their dismissal of the peasantry rather than a flighty gambling addict so detached from reality that she was LITERALLY a traitor to France.TLDR: Don't buy this. Even on sale it's not worth your money. I finished it in just over 10 hours, and even THAT was too long for such a waste of developer time and my money. The DLC isn't worth your money either, as it's literally two reskin bosses, two reskin weapons and ONE new gimmick weapon and boss in an area that looks like every other area of the game and STILL doesn't have any catharsis as the bad guy STILL gets away.

However Steams review system is too binary, and I can't in good heart sign this game positively when it drops the ball so hard in the gameplay department.If you like story driven games that have a bunch of cutscenes and even more dialogs, then Steelrising might hit the spot. _childDocuments_.review: The game play and visuals of this game are amazing.The story is filled with plot holes, way too much exposition, and is incredibly anticlimactic.There is also a fair amount of backtracking and what feels like filler. you get two ways to transverse the landscape but are still very limited to where you can actually go, and considering there is no map it can get kinda confusing. I really liked the combat, its souls like Victorian clockwork, but the story and the end of the game feel very rushed. The voice lines are really well done, there is just so much of it. I heavily dislike that stores have a finite amount of ammo for sale per area. I did have a surplus for most of the game, but it means if you where to stick around to grind, you could go through all of them. I also did not have to grind, other then a few times where i wanted to level up new gear I just found. otherwise most bosses where killed on first try. I really loved the automate styles and different units. in reality there are only a handful of robot types but each have sub groups with different ascetics and varied attacks. Gear is varied and has a bunch of different styles and speeds. the modals work like rings from a souls like, and clothing changes your stats and armor (but lack a weight system). There is also a New Game Plus that introduces new enemy's and gear.Get it on sale if your interested, but do not expect a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of things about this game that greatly frustrated me when first starting, like accidentally skipping tutorials multiple times because they pop up while starting combat when you are already pressing the buttons that dismiss the pop-ups. This made it hard to learn the game because I could not find a way to see the tutorials again without restarting the game & after REPEATEDLY accidentally skipping them, I was very frustrated & was ready to write this off as a bad game with a horrible intro sequence with bad facial animations. So glad I didn't, this is a great game, I'm glad I stuck with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could put a neutral score. It's a "ok" soulslike with some interesting boss fights and story. The game is about 20h long to beat (it took me almost 19h with some side quests). Level design is mediocre for a soulslike, but I have played way worse than than (Code Vein). But, movement is clunky, enemy design is inexistent as you fight the same enemies over and over again and the facial animations are attrocious. It's a narrative driven story with plenty of cut scenes and the human faces look like creepy dolls. It's an almost full priced AA+ game with lots of movement bugs and glitches and animations from the '90s. If someone wants to play this game they should only buy it at 1/5 of it's current price.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting combination of Bloodborne and Vampyr formulas, making a unique take on the souls genre. Game looks good when looked upon from far away, but a lot of texture and lighting problems come to light when going through dark areas, or areas that are close to a very bright light source, making quite a lot textures and lighting look out of place.Story is very mild. Nothing interesting happens, and after a certain point of the game you get a lot of unnecessary exposition and downright uninteresting comments. The same goes with citizens around the map, where almost all of them act the same way towards you. Voice acting is not bad at all, but the animation during talking cutscenes is subpar at best. However, I did not like the way they portrayed important choices throughout the game, and sometimes picking one of them can happen by mistake in the midst of combat/progression.I did dislike the limit of weapon and armor choices. Very limited, and most of them (weapons) play the same if they are from the same class. For example, I played the bodyguard class, where heavy slow weapons are the thing, but there are only 4 of them in game, and all of them have the same moveset and attacks, just different damage values and specials. As for the armor sets, only two armor sets are made for the heavy class, one that I used for around 80% of the playthrough until I found the other one a lot later in the game, near the end. Standard enemies feel fine, but I really disliked the bosses. Game has two version of bosses, the mini and the real ones. Mini ones are just corrupted versions of the regular enemies that have increased stats and that block your next checkpoint until defeated...and to be honest, they don't deserve to be called bosses at all in my opinion. The real bosses are rare, and only a few of them exist in the game (around 7). They are interesting, but only one of them is great, the others are almost on-paar with some of the more dangerous mini-bosses.In the end, I cannot really recommend this game, but also cannot say that I did not like it. It had it's moments, good and bad, but in the end it was not really dull nor did it have amazing moments at any point. It could have used a lot more work and polish.Overall, it is a solid 7.5/10I would like to see a similar project from the devs, but I would also want to see the above mentions improved, especially the weapon/armor selection.

_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Not only this is a great souls like, it's a great game overall. The combat is good with some tweaks to the system with interesting weapons. I didn't use all of them, but the halberds had cool animations with nice combos even being medium/heavy weapons. There are no, of at least very few invincibility frames during dodges so it took a bit of time to get used to it, but not a big deal for the way enemies act. The maps are super detailed, big and intricate with several shortcuts. It's not one huge map like the souls games, more like huge areas you can travel to, but they are so big that I didn't mind.The game is absolutely gorgeous, but optimization is its achiles' heels. I managed to run it on high on my 3060 and even then it wasn't quite enough, while I can play heavier and newer games on max quality with no problems unless I turn on raytracing. One of its top points though is the story. It actually grabbed my attention and I was curious to see how they would fit it in the French Revolution context. It was a nice mix of history and fiction with known characters but with a puppet plot very similar to Lies of P. If you consider the optimization problems that got the game its mixed reviews, consider buying it on Sale. I bought it very cheap on a steam sale and I had a blast with it. I finished the game near the 22h mark, but if I try to go for the platinum I extimate easily another 10h or even more, the game has multiple endings and a new game plus so it actually incentivize you to have another run with different weapons.Overall a very solid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not had any performance issues, there were a couple texture loading issues that I experienced but nothing bad, and the game was easily playable for me. I have a Ryzen 5800, RTX 3070, 16 gigs of ram, running the game off of an SSD.First off, I understand what the devs were trying to do with the mechanical feel in trying to make you feel like an automaton. Unfortunately, it doesn't feel GOOD. I don't think it's more important to feel like a robot than it is for the game to be fluid and fun. Something about just moving around feels kind of glitchy and stiff. When you're designing the feel/look of a heavy machine, you need to think about POWER rather than stiffness. Again, I understand the stiff feel they're going for, but in my opinion, it is not executed very well. Machines might be a bit stiffer, but they're also REALLY HEAVY and POWERFUL. I think it would be better to shift the focus away from a stiff feel and more into a powerful, weighty, feel. Longer charge ups, bigger slams.This made the game feel a bit unfun to play at a base level.The reason I'm refunding is because of the hitboxes. After upon reaching the first boss (the tall robot that summoned normal enemies as minions) I realized that, at least that boss, has really bad hitboxes. I was getting hit a lot when I wasn't anywhere near the robots attacks, and even after dodging through some of them. It could be that I was just not timing dodges properly, I was playing with muscle memory from my experience with Dark Souls and other souls-like games, and it did me no good here. I simply can't play without feeling like I'm getting hit when I'm not supposed to. Maybe Dark Souls is such a huge part of how I see video games these days that it makes me unable to appreciate other forms of combat and their small differences, but unfortunately, unless this issue is fixed, I don't see myself enjoying this game.Aside from that, atmosphere, graphics, it all seemed pretty good. Some of the animations were smooth too, I like the feeling of injecting the oil vial (estus flask) and the ledge grab/jump up animation you do when grabbing ledges is smooth. I'm sure theres a lot to appreciate in this game, but you have to be able to play enough to get there and see them, and I can't play the way it is now.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say what Steelrising is not: it is *not* Nioh.  That anyone is making that comparison is baffling.  I realize we can only draw points of reference from what we've played, but If I had to pick a game this is most adjacent to I'd say Bloodborne.  I also think it does *just* enough to be it's own thing.  So, if you are a fan of action RPGs such as Dark Souls will you like Steelrising? I think so.  Spiders has done maybe some of their best work yet, gameplay wise, and I'll admit it's nice to get out of generic fantasy.  If you wanted Bloodborne but with a French Steampunk aesthetic, here you go.I think it's worth noting who it *won't* appeal to: if you just finished Elden Ring and want another 120 hour, poorly balanced epic with hundreds of choices to make for your character build: this ain't it.  Steelrising as a game is fine, but if your expectations are that it's going to rival the top dog in terms of content and presentation then save yourself the heartache and pass it up.  If, however, you like the genre and you could go for more?  You'll find that here.  If you are usually put off by these games for those very reasons, this also might just be the one to ease you into the genre.  I'll go ahead and say it as well: I'm fine when games don't need hundreds of hours to beat.  Sometimes you just want to play a game you like and finish it.  The content here is solid.As for what sets it apart from a basic Bloodborne clone?  Well, it's source inspiration is pretty bald faced, but you can chain attacks, jumps and dodges more easily and you have a more generous stamina bar.  There are other small tweaks but in general it just feels a lot "softer" than Souls-likes usually do.  Your movements are still very deliberate, it's *nowhere* as fast paced as Team Ninja's offerings, but they are less restrictive.  You unlock traversal abilities that also open up some options in combat.  You have equipment choices, but you aren't going to agonize over it.  That's not to say it isn't challenging, just that it lets you get away with a bit more and asks for a bit less.  Fans of the genre will feel right at home with *just* enough tweaks to help it have its own identity and, personally, it's challenge is just right.  If you let your guard down, you'll get your teeth kicked in, but rely on those old instincts and you'll find it very manageable.  Now if you'll excuse me, I have a game to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a medium rating to this, but I will give this a thumbs up in good faith. There is a lot to love in this game fighting with a lot to dislike.FIRST OFF TO ALL THE PEOPLE WITH PERFORMANCE ISSUES:If you move the setting to ultra, Ray Tracing will be turned on which will TANK you FPS. If you are 100+FPS on 1440p on high, going to Ultra may drop you to 60FPS and less on busy battles.You can still play on ultra, but once you change the setting, go to advance graphics and turn Ray Tracing back off. If you have an RTX card, you can play with DLSS to see if you can do some balance if you, for some reason, want the Ray Tracing feature on. CP2077 does this too, but they give you a setting of Ultra + Ray Tracing to avoid the mega drop in FPS.I am playing on 4k, Ultra settings, no Ray Tracing, DLSS on balanced and I maintain a steady 60 FPS. My GPU is a 3080ti combined with Ryzen 5900x...so your mileage may vary.That part out of the way, the game is overall solid. This game shares a lot of DNA with Bloodborne (sans the hit back to heal mechanic), so if that is your jam, you make like this. I will give some quick points on what I enjoyed and what I really think can be improved in the game:POSITIVE:-Aegis mechanical model is beautiful. The way her plates are rendered is very natural, you can FEEL she is a machine made of gold, or steel, or marble depending on the character creation. A+ on this...you can tell the devs put a lot of love into her design.-Combat animations are interesting and varied, and they kick-ass making you FEEL strong. Several weapon types have moves that pierce, slash, or smash enemies, and the devs really spend time making you feel like a badass at it. Most charge attacks make Aegis do some additional animations that are just down right cool. It's like, ballet that can kill. Solid A here.-Environments are rich and well artistically developed, which makes the immersion grip you. Deep green forest and gardens, muddy streets, graveyards, and everything is designed to be natural and realistic with god rays peeking in different places. The whole design is congruous to the game's aesthetics and it really sucks you in. Another Solid A.NEGATIVE:-The cooling system is a good idea, but it doesn't add much to combat. I think the mentality here was to give the game something like "Active Time Reload" in other games like Gears of War or Guardians of the Galaxy. If Aegis runs out of stamina, she overheats and needs to cool down, and you can do a "minigame" to get the cooling down at the right time. Problem is in the heat of battle, it's hard to pay attention to it. While you are managing enemies, weapons, healing, stamina, and countless other things, the last thing the player need is "oh damn, now I gotta add ONE more mechanic." I think they wanted this mechanic to make the game have a key point to say "HEY! We do something real different than other soulslikes with combat!"I think the idea was good, but like other games that have a mechanic like this (reload/regain stamina with proper timing), I think the cool down could have an icon in the center of the screen, so when it pops, the players eyes do not deviate from the action. Games like this can kill you if you are not paying attention, so don't add a mechanic that introduces distractions the players cannot always predict. I think if it gets a bit more of a revamp, it can moved to a positive (it would have been cool to see Aegis body really heat and vent steam as the overheat approaches).-Yanky hit boxes. I HATE THIS ONE. In the first miniboss, there are piles of body's on the ground and sometimes you can walk on top of them (like you scaling a small mountain) and sometimes you get STUCK on them (like if they were a wall). I also randomly get stuck on the environmental features (like logs or tress) even when Aegis' model is clearly out of the way. This makes some encounters frustrating as I died to being stuck on nothing...and that is incredibly frustrating in these types of games since precision is key. It feels bad when you are dodging an enemy and then get randomly stuck and die. You didn't make a mistake, but you are punished for it.-The voice acting (minor issue). The voices are mostly okay, and the models are mostly okay, but put them together is awkward to watch. Just the intro scene, characters sound calm but their models are agitated like there is a sense of urgency, and sometimes it's the other way around.-Aegis' movement is awkward when traversing, and she doesn't have physical impact in the world (minor issue). When you walk slow, Aegis' model looks great, when you sprint, it looks fine, but when you just run and you turn left and right, Aegis' looks like a top moving left and right on it's axis. It makes you feel like you are turning more than you really are. Also, when Aegis moves through bushes, she doesn't move anything in the foliage. when she walks on mud, or dirt, her feet do not cause any dirt or anything to kick up. It almost make her seem like she is flying.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear god, I was in despair after almost 5 hours of playing. But then I remembered watching a streamer fight Malenia with a RL1, I even watch (not entirely) Kai's 100+ hour Elden Ring. They kept losing and trying again and again, and I realized I need to play with patience. So yeah, it works for me (in this game).My first play took about 12 hours, including several side quests, reading a bit of lore, and unlocking the 1st ending. 2nd play was NG+ took 11 hours, it was for unlocking some achievements, learning more about the lore, collecting all echoes, and somehow got 3rd ending. I wasn't sure how I did it, but it showed that your choices do matter. There are three endings in total.I agree that Steelrising is not too difficult (after my first 5 hours, of course), but it does have some very challenging moments. The game features Immobilisation, which the enemies get stunned when the diamond is filled, allowing you to hit a critical attack. You can use throwable bombs like flame to ignite, frost to freeze, and explosive goes explode. I chose the Dancer class and my favorite weapons are Armoured Fans and Requiem Mallet.There are Unstable bosses and main bosses. The Unstable bosses weren't very hard for me, though I died 2-4 times. However, the two main bosses, The Selenite and The Bishop gave me motion sickness. The rest were a mix, some 1st try, others took 2-5 runs. If the game is too hard, you can always turn on assist mode, but I decided not to use it to see how far I could go on my own.Overall, I enjoyed the story, the combat, the character design, and the world. The only issue was the performance. But if the game were more polished, it would be amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it! A fun, engaging experience that was not too difficult, but did require some attention and focus. I had a great time with the game, and while I probably wouldn't want a direct sequel, as the story is already self-contained, I'd absolutely check out the studio's next iteration on their ideas.What I loved: Boss designs! These bosses were extremely creative, absolutely marvelous, amazing spectacles. I really cannot properly phrase just how incredible the main bosses were. They were also all very well balanced, providing a reasonable challenge but not halting your progress for 30 hours.  Atmosphere and world design! Steampunk Paris looks truly fantastic. I often stopped to admire the detailed buildings, fountains, all sorts of decorations and miscellaneous objects. It's clear a lot of love went into the graphical presentation, and it's a great experience to go through it. The idea of combining robots with French revolution politics is a surprisingly well working combination. Not only does it add a unique style to the whole game, it also provides enough room for all sorts of stories and mini-tales weaved into the game. I really like the overall creativity that is behind every corner, every important mechanic, and every design decision. What I didn't really like: Some parts of the level design were a bit troublesome to go through. I do like to explore and find my way through a world, but some paths were really not apparent at all, and sadly, are absolutely crucial for progression, as all levels are made as little labyrinths, with only one correct way through them. I missed a certain small story-related part of the game near the start, and this snowballed beyond my imagination. Me missing this one thing maybe 1/8th into the playthrough eventually resulted in a certain NPC not appearing where he was needed for an important side-quest. I went back and finally got the NPC to move to the right spot, but by that point the side-quest broke and I couldn't progress. Note this was the only side-quest I managed to break, so it's not some huge issue, on the other hand I wanted to finish all side-quests and got blocked because of some small thing I missed out on 15 hours earlier, which is never fun. It's also true that enemies start to repeat about mid-way through the game. Although it's not a big deal, it does get somewhat repetitive at times, especially when coupled with the level design which always makes sure to drag you through every location in the longest route possible. But I totally understand the reasoning behind why that ended up being the way it is.I can't comment much on the technical state of the game. I experienced 2 crashes and 1 minor visual (repeating) bug throughout the whole game, so I can't complain. It was a fun game, and I was surprised by just how well made it was! Definitely a good experience!

Also, the highly emphsised riposte mechanism was surprisingly niche, since lots of enemies has (delayed) attacks with extended or multiple hit-boxes (+the hyper-armour that will just blunt force through your counter-attack).2. _childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a much better game than you'd think.You start to realize roughly an hour in, after you've wrestled with the jank a bit and begun familiarizing yourself with both how and why this game is *different*. Sure, there are a few systems that present themselves rather immediately as throwing a wrench in some of the established works; an impromptu way to regain stamina after you run out -- with just the right amount of risk-reward play -- stands out. Then there's a story, with, y'know, cutscenes, which flies right in the face of the established norm. These games normally obfuscate their lore, don't they? But then it really hits you: you're having fun. And that's weird because, generally, these types of games are so hard that they're frustrating at times, but for whatever reason, that never happens here. Why?Well, it's because Steelrising is an easier Souls-like. It's easier for a lot of reasons: for one, it's fair. You don't feel like whoever designed this game is constantly out to get you: enemies present themselves in reasonable combat encounters. The game gives you just the right amount of heals, items and weapon options to make it through to the next shortcut with just a *little* bit of patience and time. But also, none of these enemies are poorly designed: they all have really great tells and animations, hinting at when and how they'll attack. And when they do, it doesn't kill you in one hit. Hell, it doesn't even knock you off that edge because, in *this* game, there's a grapple. That's right. You heard it here first. And the hits keep coming because as you get stronger in this game, you actually feel yourself getting stronger. What a revelation.And you DO get stronger. Every traversal option you unlock in a metroidvania-esque fashion (an in-air dash/doge, and a grappling hook among them!) can also be used in battle, endowing you with additional contextual abilities. It's a great change of pace from just having your weapons only dictate what you can do. Factor it all in with ample build options through weapon variety, stats, and armor to wear, and you've got yourself some replay value. Then there's the level design folks, and let me tell you: Steelrising doesn't disappoint here. Levels are large, layered, with repeat visits for side-quests allowing you to travel further and further in, unlocking tons of shortcuts and new paths as you go. The way the levels weave in on themselves is great, and while the game isn't fully connected (there are discrete levels that you eventually can choose to go to in differing order), I always felt there was a great sense of exploration. Exploration that ends, as it should, in a fun boss fight. No difficult bosses, mind you -- something that may seem strange because, again, isn't this a Souls-like? It is, and don't worry, some of the bosses probably will kill you. Once, maybe even twice. But never that third time: this game is just too fair; bosses, like yourself, stagger, and not a one of them comes equipped with a one-shot or a stunlock. It just isn't that kind of thing. You'll feel like a boss when you one-and-done them, and y'know what? That's okay. It's especially okay because these bosses are really cool to look at, and really cool to fight. But there has to be something wrong, doesn't there? And there is. At the time of this writing, Steelrising's performance is rough. Certainly playable, mind you; toggle on DLSS in the menu and you'll squeeze out the performance you need to keep the game moving along with you, but it's still a bit sad to see Spiders swing and miss here. If they release a patch addressing this issue (and some visual bugs), I'll try and update my thoughts accordingly. So, who is this game for? If you've never played a Souls game, and you want to, start here. It's incredibly approachable, and that's not to even mention the accessibility menu the game has for adjusting things to your liking -- but I don't think you'll need it. As I said, this game is more fun than it is difficult, and for someone who plays almost every Souls-like game whether I like it or not, it's a breath of fresh air to play one that isn't constantly trying to waste my time with cheap deaths or unreasonable demands. I also recommend this for even seasoned players who want the equivalent of a breather; you'll sink your teeth into this game and bite right through it, but I think you'll still have a ton of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is undeniably janky, and I've not completed it yet, but what I've seen in the 5 or so hours I've played so far i've found enjoyable. I would call myself a souls veteran but this game has been a nice change to be honest. After the honestly frustrating slog that was the last third of elden ring, and the constant need for perfection in sekiro, a slower and more easy/forgiving soulslike has been welcome.- The game's optimization is probably poor, but with my relatively mid rig its been running quite well (ryzen 7 3700x, rtx 4060).- The dialogue sounds honestly janky, and Aegis especially feels very strange, but for her at least it kind of adds to the doll charm for me. - Some enemy attacks feel pretty unfair, with damage hitboxes appearing practically instantly to deal damage without windup, and some attacks where it really feels like i was outside the attack range but took damage.Overall i've very much enjoyed what i've seen, and i've been wishing for a game where you get to play as a doll (actual doll, instead of the completely human P from lies of P). So yeah I really hope we'll get more like this in the future, hopefully with more bloodborne style worldbuilding perhaps?

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, especially as a Lies of P followup, though not as polished and satisfying. Gorgeous main character who looks like an actual puppet as a bonus, great weapon options and beautiful souls fashion. Difficulty level is easy if you've played other soulslikes. Many bosses including the final one can be first-tried, summons are not available, or needed, many cheese options like bombs can be ignored for the entirety of the game. It has an open world feel since you can, and must, revisit some areas because they can only be unlocked once you find a certain weapon/tool. There are some amusing glitches, like picking up loot 15x without clearing the prompt, enemies getting stuck in doors, and less amusing ones like an unholy amount of rubble for Aegis to get stuck on during combat, or the game crashing while she twitches on a fence. Also didn't enjoy having her auto-access the boss areas once she came close enough, or the autostarting of some cutscenes which prevented exploring and even finishing a certain quest during the ending.  The larger areas are rather badly and thoughtlessly interconnected with many unlockable doors and barriers, and can be lengthy to navigate, sometimes I didn't find my way back to the vestal or to the place I was looking for, and had to run in circles while fighting the same monsters over and over. Some rooms/corners feel too samey and like added fluff without contributing much to the worldbuilding. History lovers will enjoy meeting French Revolution celebrities and get to know them a little. Kudos to the La Fayette voice actor for the nice voice and flawless pronounciation in both English and French. Players who dont care about the story might skip everything, but they will miss out on a lot of cool details and getting  different endings.In summary: combat is easy, maybe too easy, map is too convoluted, the game should have been optimised more before release. But I would play a part 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a fun game despite it's flaws.You are playing as robot girl, you can customize the face, hair, and skin tone. Then you will get to choose starting class, although it doesn't really matter mid-late game because you have plenty time to change your playstyle.The combat is okay, just like dark souls game. The stamina bar runs out really quickly at the beginning of the game and you can do rapid cooling to restore it momentarily while in combat (need timing). The combat pace is slow, giving you plenty time to react. Block & counter is only available when using certain weapons. Dodge is always an option. You also have alchemy bullet to use alchemical skills. Bomb is also very good.The area is dominated in the city of France, so you are going to spend most of your time in the ruined city. The architecture is interesting enough, and the feel of each area is distinct enough, so not really a problem.You can upgrade weapon, potion, status. You also have some skills but you need to progress further in the game, it can help you traverse the map and fight. The story is slow at the beginning, you don't know anyone or where the story is going. But it picks up mid game when you finally get the sense of the situation and the people. It's interesting enough when you are invested in it.Now the negatives based on my opinion,1. The GPU load is high, even using RTX 4050 6GB, i can only play on 1920p low to get consistent 60-70 FPS with DLSS Ultra Performance :) and you don't want low frame in games like this...so that's a bummer. It doesn't make sense why the GPU load so high, the visual isn't that revolutionary...2. Bugs and lot's of them, stuck when running, the pop up menu disappearing, drop item visual cues not disappearing, freezed animation at cutscene, etc.3. Side quest, you don't know when you are supposed to do certain side quest, because certain side quest is actually locked before you progress the main quest, so good luck wasting time trying to complete it because you are not supposed to yet...4. The combat feels weird until you get used to it, i think this is also because of the GPU load, making the game feel sluggish if you don't have adequate GPU (6 GB is REALLY the minimum).I recommend trying it if it's on sale, and make sure your GPU at the very minimum have 6GB or it's unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: If the game stayed as good as it is at the start, I'd recommend it. Unfortunately the longer it goes on the worse it gets. It's a beautiful game with decent combat, although heavy weapons feel terrible here and fast weapons are king (bizarrely all weapons are classed as either heavy or medium, there's no light class for some reason), and a lot of effort went into the mechanical designs being both fun to fight and interesting to look at.Unfortunately by the time you're 1/3 through the game you will have already seen all but one or two of the standard enemies it has to offer. Even though it's only about 20 hours long it feels like an utter slog after a point because of the horrible lack of enemy variety leaving you fighting the same things over and over regardless of locale, and the player is able to quickly become so strong that enemies don't even pose a challenge, especially since there are so few movesets to familiarise yourself with.The few abilities you have to move around the environment aren't really that special; you can only use the grapple at a handful of select points in each level so it's basically a non-factor, while the wall break is even less useful, but I do appreciate that they all have uses in combat with distinct ailment effects tied to them so I was making use of all of them in combat towards the end of the game.The story is undoubtedly the worst part here, being a dull mess of cardboard characters that talk too much and say too little. Cutscenes frequently interrupt exploration and rarely offer anything interesting to make them worth sitting through. The ending of the game is laughably bad,  The game having quests that see you constantly running back and forth across environments that aren't particularly designed for speedy traversal and various locations being locked behind keys that only appear through such quests doesn't help the exploration feel rewarding, nor does the fact that 99% of items you find throughout the game are just consumables and ammo, with actual gear being relegated to only sparse chests.There was definitely a good core here and I was impressed by the visual design of the game, and the combat certainly isn't bad, particularly as far as Souls-likes go, but there just isn't enough meat here. Oh and it isn't very well optimised either; the frame pacing is awful and swapping from high settings to low made effectively no difference to performance.
