_childDocuments_.review: Edit after completing it:This game is like the film Tenet. A silly, but fun concept that looks pretty good until it sticks around way too long and dies huffing it's own farts. It was fun for a while, but became painfully repetitive, the mazelike levels are utterly painful to have to constantly backtrack through, what you can and can't pass through/ jump over is awfully janky, quests can bug and become impossible to complete for no reasons, and the story is embarrassing, boring, and utterly misguided. Credits rolled and I said, "thanks, I hate it" and unistalled it. I no longer recommend this game. Original Review:My feelings towards this game are powerfully ambivalent with a positive leaning simply because the gameplay is so much fun.The Good:The concept and aesthetics of steampunk regency France is undeniably brilliant and is largely pulled off. The classic Soulslike elements, Souls, bonfires, respawning enemies, enemies that hit like trucks, and bosses that are even bigger than said trucks, are all there and work well, actually integrated into the world and story in ways that surpass some others in the genre  The addition of the more fluid movement and combat from more traditional action adventure games is a fun addition.The art design, at least for Aegis, weapons, outfits, and enemies, is genuinely wonderful and works beautifully with the steampunk nightmare regency era France.The elemental mechanics are fun (though it's easy to lean into ice and paralysis and not have to really think about the rest or use any of the protective fluids). The Bad:The story is actually offensive in a number of ways. The actual writing of the narrative and dialogue is just interminably dull and longwinded without saying anything at all. The easiest thing to compare it to is all the politics and trade embargo discussion from The Phantom Menace. It also just slows everything down without actually adding anything to it because, ultimately they are just saying go here, do this, king bad, automats scary, with the occasional bit of French and waving a frilly collar at the idea of the French Revolution. I wish I wasn't so neurodivergent that it is impossible for me to watch every cutscene and choose every dialogue option (less options, rather a checklist of things to cover with no actual choice, outside of don't say all the things), but you truly do not have to. This really is an extension of the last, but it is so egregious it needs its own point. The handling of politics, discussion of slavery, plantations, capitalism, and the French Revolution itself are embarrassing and offensive. There's no other way to describe it. It's milquetoast liberal sanitised state education word vomit with no understanding of the history and motivations for the revolution, and absolutely no intention of sticking its head above the political parapet beyond easily agreed statements like slavery bad and maybe people shouldn't be starved and murdered. The mind truly boggles. If you can't stomach the politics and history, don't set your game in it. Using it as a fun aesthetic and setting is utterly morbid. It absolutely could have just been fantasy regency Europe (ignoring all the difficult colonialism) without losing anything. The hero of the revolution in this game is Marie Antoinette's bloody bodyguard!??? The NPCs look very iffy and sound OK. It's kinda repetitive (but that's the whole genre and I'm not complaining having played many other titles a ridiculous number of times). I feel like I wrote a lot more for the bad, but this is just because it's so ridiculous and got my goat. Ultimately, it's a lot of fun and something absolutely worth playing if you need a break from From Software and/ or want to imagine you are the Dancer of the Boulangerie Valley. Gameplay 4Visual Design 4Everything Else 1.5

_childDocuments_.review: Just for context before my review, I have 100%ed Bloodborne, Dark Souls 1, Dark Souls 2, Dark Souls 3, Sekiro, Elden Ring, Nioh 1, Nioh 2, Surge, Surge 2,  Thymesia, Mortal Shell, Remnant From the Ashes, Code Vein, The Lords of the Fallen, Ashen, Tails of Iron.*** Difficulty *** - Pro/Con - 1. General DifficultyEasy and relaxing compared to all other souls games. Died less than 10 total times in the game all from being lazy. 2. BossesAll but 2 bosses were 1 shots. All bosses could have easily have been 1 shots, but I was just being lazy/greedy. 3. Items/HealsThere are tons of heal/buff/damage items throughout the game that make the game even easier. I ended the game with hundreds and never even needed them.4. EnemiesEnemies move sets are simple and there are probably less than 15 total enemy types in the entire game. Most bosses are just buffed health bars of existing trash mobs with increased health pools. The game has dodge and parry mechanics and I completed the game only using dodge mechanic and it is extremely forgiving compared to other souls/souls-like games.Difficulty summary: Con. In my opinion it should have been more difficult*** Story *** - Pro/ConThe story wasn't bad. It had a few cool twists. It may just be me, but I had a hard time getting into the story or caring for the characters other than the main character you play. All names are in French and difficult to follow who its referring to and I think that makes it harder to follow to fall in love with all the side characters.Story summary: Con. I did not really enjoy the story.*** Visuals *** ProI really enjoyed the visuals. Very similar to Thymesia which I enjoyed*** Game stability/Glitches **** ConHonestly I was surprised by the amount of glitches and crashes. I have a new pc (built in last 18 months). Ran graphics on normal to make sure I was way under threshold my pc could handle and I still had 15-20 complete crashes during my playthrough. 2 times I got stuck in between trees or fell through the floor on the boss fight. Bot times I had to summon back to a bonfire and lose all souls just to fix it (shutting down game and reloading didn't work)*** Value *** Pro/ConIf you enjoy souls and souls-like games, its not a "must play". However, if you are like me and love souls games and want to play every souls/souls-like game ever created, this is one I would suggest buying for less than $20. It is not worth anywhere close to $49.99 in my opinion. I purchased for $29.99 on sale and feel like I overpaid.*** Game Length ***I completed this game and all side quests in 40 hours. If you didn't care about side quests or exploration it could be completed in 20 hours.Overall Summary - I would not pay more than $20 for this game. If you enjoy souls-like games and you're bored, then this is a fun relief from the typical punishing souls-like experienceOverall Rating - 6 out of 10passe une bonne journée

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the campaign, I would say if you have been eyeing up this game, wait until a sale or find it cheaper elsewhere.Things I liked; the setting, beautiful and detailed from the weapons. to the world, and even aegis herself all look beautiful and you can tell they have done their research.The satisfaction of taking down a titan boss; these beasts will test you and the feeling of accomplishment at taking them down was always great.The story itself; I wont lie, the ending did make me slightly teary which means they made a great story work. You feel as you progress through the game, you want to uncover the truth.The cons; OK, anyone who has seen any reviews will know this already, its a game plagued with mechanics that are not very well polished from the fact that enemies attack without little to no warning over and over again, to the locking system just going from one enemy to another, to frame rate drops that literally will mean the death of you, yet again.Oh, and there is ZERO indication of how what weapon you use, you need to make sure you level up the correct attribute. I did not realise this until a few hours in, and had to restart as you cannot reset your stats. Ever. So for example I chose the dancer class, and her weapon the fan needed two specific attributes to be upgraded so she was actually levelling up properly.Overall, I still do say YES get this game as its great to see a AA studio improve with each game, and I feel even with its flaws, this is still a gem of a game worthy of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Dark Souls if it was made by EA: Approachable difficulty, tons of bugs, and an ending so painfully stupid I want a refund.Actual review:If you're wanting a Souls-like game that isn't too difficult to dip your toes into the genre, SteelRising is a decent enough choice. The game is very forgiving with enemy placement, attack patterns, health items, and anima essence/souls, so even new players shouldn't find it too frustrating to advance through the game and upgrade their character. However, be aware that the game is also very buggy, has some very confusing level design in several areas, and has an ending so painfully stupid that I'm annoyed that I'm outside the refund window. Pros:Cool setting of revolutionary FranceAutomatons are awesomeInteresting boss designsLots of weapons to choose fromForgiving for those new to Souls-likesSome enemies blend into terrain making them almost impossible to counter or dodge attacks fromCons:So many bugsPainfully stupid endingThere's actually only 5 or 6 weapons, they've just been reskinned to pad-out the contentBugs I ran into in my 47 hour playthrough:-Getting stuck on terrain while trying to walk in the middle of a clear street-Item pick ups not picking up -Item pick ups allowing multiple duplicates before actually being picked up-That time I clipped through an entire apartment building to be trapped between two invisible walls-Bosses aggroing before you even enter the arena (One even insta-klilling me out of the air as I was falling into the arena)-Enemy AI not activating-Crash to desktop entering the final boss arena (only happened once in the entire playthrough though)

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game tentatively on the basis that if you want to play a competent souls-like, but don't care *too much* about good bosses or story, you could have a good time with this game. I think it's gameplay is a solid 8/10 - satisfying combat and a number high-mobility options for navigating levels quickly, interesting enemy design, sometimes interesting boss design. However the bosses do not feel particularly menacing or like an event. /minor spoilers/ The final boss was particularly lackluster and there was virtually no build up to it and no fanfare for defeating it. Environments are visually neat but sometimes blend together in ways that make it easy to get lost. That can make doing side quests quite tedious, even with the optional objective marker the game gives you in the form of a compass item.Story is meh, alternate history french revolution stuff. Interesting concept but it's delivered with such soulless character-to-character dialogue and cutscenes that I never felt particularly engaged. Things certainly could have been pulled off better. It doesn't help that all of the human character designs are quite boring and they're rendered fairly ugly. Their rough motion-capture animations paired with overly poeticized period dialogue made the whole thing feel rather goofy. The game does have its jank. I didn't experience many glitches or bugs in my play through and it ran fine, with one or two moments of stuttering throughout the whole thing. However the quest system and progression itself seems kind of precarious. I accidentally sequence broke a few events, but were able to return to them later and they triggered correctly after I fulfilled other prerequisites for the quests. But it sounds like I may have gotten lucky based on some other reviews. And one of the side quests never left my objective marker or location quest indicator, even though I had completed the criteria for it and it was added to my finished quest list in the journal. The game allows you to move freely between areas, however I'd be wary of picking up items when exploring areas you're not sure you're supposed to be in. It's very easy to get over certain obstacles that aren't obviously meant to keep you out of areas you're not meant for yet.

_childDocuments_.review: France? Rebellion? Mechanical clockwork maids that can dance and inflict death? I've never knew I needed all of these so much and here in Steelrising they are everywhere.After roughly 32hrs I've finished my first play through with the majority spent trying to wrap up the side quests and find all the weapons I could without looking online for hints - but I still did need help for one of the side-quests. What does this game have going for it? 1. Voice Acting. I hate people, and I hate people talking even more, and the way games try to make a plot mean something can either be great or so cringeworthy it stops you playing. Thankfully, this game is in the first category; the delivery of the dialogue was very well done. The lead, Cassie Layton, appeared in Greedfall by the same studio, delivered a believable performance which I think is especially commendable given that she's a clockwork robot in revolutionary France.The in-game animations do make the game feel a bit clunky in places and there are some uncomfortable moments where NPCs would be staring into my soul without a single word coming from them - but this I was able to ignore because I cared about the story. Everyone's French was commendably interwoven to remind me that we were in France and although I cannot speak French, I should expect it to be spoken in France - even clockwork France. The council of assembled learned and clergy each delivered similarly commendable performances, although spending all of my time with Aegis makes me bias to her contribution. 2. It's Different. I mean... as I said before it's historically accurate France during the assembly of the third estate the point of revolution but catapults expectations into The Bastille’s dry moat and takes us on a totally weird and wonderful adventure. 3. The Environment. It isn't perfect, as an addict for breakable objects I have found many a suspiciously floating book or candle in the middle of nothing but once again I wanted to find every street, every villager voice segment, and be shown just how brutally the people of this world tried to fight for their freedom but never had a single hope of accomplishing it. I also tried to jump on rocks and ended up sliding into eternal falling pits of sadness more than once - with a lot of menu pausing and using the camera to nudge myself in the direction of "not this Hell" I escaped. I consider the faults to be minor and not sufficient to ruin my enjoyment of all the death, disease, and dancing.4. The Music.I enjoyed it very much and found it to be impactful when needed and pleasant when in the background – the ending credits was a really beautiful piece that I enjoyed listening to especially.The Bad: 1. Performance.It's something that is very, very noticeable and will have you sitting on loading screens for 2-3 minutes when travelling. I cannot be sure why but I think the lighting in the game is possibly too good and everything else suffers because of it - coupled with the highly detailed environment I can see that it would be a very expensive process to get it performing to a 2022 standard. However, I think it would be worth the investment even if it were just to optimise the travelling between zones - I played Bloodborne on release and I consider my debt paid to loading screens.2. Character Models. I found the mechanical robot to be more emotive and expressive than the flesh and blood comrades found throughout the game. I can't even call it poor implementation or bad artistry; I believe it is a lack of resources to match the vocal performance to the visual - a limitation I believe can be better focused going forward. 3. So many streets. I loved running around and breaking everything, but when I realised, I had missed a collectable behind some random gate or fence I was suddenly wishing the game had some kind of map. I don't even want a full top-down Google Maps, I would love a scrap of paper that Aegis can draw on to remember where we went and where we didn't just so the spirit of adventure can have a direction to visit without handing it to you. 4. Wrapping Up.The game has volumes of text, dialogue, quests, and descriptions - I found items that by the end of the game I had no use for or never found to whom they belonged. I also found a prisoner in Le Bastille begging for food with no idea where or how to help him, I checked what I could but only found books, straw, and some questionable HR policies. I think the voice talent is so well assembled that on finding the memories a full cut-scene to bring the player up to the moment they find them would engage better. 5. Cost. For the dialogue I think it's worth the price, but for the action and execution of the graphics I feel the game is reaching for a price-point it doesn't belong in. What others do with their money is their own business, but I would fully believe that this game thrive in a lower price-point and be enjoyed more for it. However, I do understand that everything costs money and it isn't easy to "just do it" - of course they developers want to release the best game they can, but they also want to eat and have a dependable income. 6. I Want to Dance WIth Athénaïs de Vaucanson.Just let me dance with her and be happy... for like... 5-minutes, okay? She's been through a lot and so have I... we need this.... Finally the music box enemies need a mute button because sometimes I was hearing it when I wasn't at my PC and that's not okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Complex, interconnected and confusing maps. Fun and fast paced combat against too few unique enemy types. Cool and unique bosses with healthbars so small that you will get them on your first or second attempt. Good and satisfying progression, haltered by outright wacky balancing.I feel conflicted about this game but the positives far outway the negatives. I went in expecting a soulslike and was somewhat disappointed, but after simply accepting the game for what it is I found an enjoyable single player action game. The story was an unexpected highlight and a lot of love went into the levels and atmosphere. Honestly, this game could've done with around three to five hours less playtime, since its weaknesses really started to show in the last third.If you go in blind and try to have an open mind you might just find around 15 hours of familiar feeling singleplayer fun. This game, however, will not scratch your fromsoft itch.If nothing else, I believe Steelrising shows enormous potential for a possible successor, the groundwork for an incredible soulslike is 90% there.This is good game, though I would hesitate to call it a good soulslike. Well worth the money when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed, but fun! Imagine if Skynet became aware and Judgement Day happened in the 1800s...This is a janky but enjoyable title-not so much Soulslike as Souls-esque, or say...Souls-adjacent.  It apes the mechanics in a beautifully rendered setting, but misses the heart of what makes those games compelling on their own merit.  I found the game ran fine on my own machine, fearing the worst from reviews but very pleasantly surprised.  The flavour of the game being set in an alternative steampunk French Revolution is wonderfully different, and the sumptuous background is one of the game's strengths.  I cannot count how many times I marveled at the dust within god-rays breaking into an interior environment.  There is a lot to praise in the variety of asset you encounter in an area too.  There are exceptions of course-NPC faces contort with more muscles than I suspect exist in real people during dialogue, and the jitter of inaccessible space is severe at times.  Controls-wise, this game is more DMC than DS3 - there is a slippy overstep that occurs that while undetected in combat does tend to make itself known in more careful play.  At times, I felt like my character was balancing on a unicycle at the end of a walk, but ultimately it is not a game that depends on finesse to overly matter.  The draw for me was the more action-orientated focus of the title.  There is a confusing map layout that slows it down, but this is ultimately a linear game whereby you gather the resources you need most near where you will want them.  It is hard to miss a secret, and Steelrising provides enough brief side-missions in level to merit taking your time as you explore.  The enemies are varied, but do repeat quite a bit.  The tactics of my agility-based robo-dancing-ninja-bot never really varied no matter the weapon it employed; save for when there were multiple enemies on screen and it becomes a chaotic fight and dash away strategy.But I do love it.The game has so much it does right, that in a world without Dark Souls, it shines brightly.  With so many Soulslike titles out there, I would describe this more like a far more accessible, period-based version of The Surge 2.  It has that one-more try appeal crucial to this genre and varies itself just enough to push through the jank.  I love unpolished gems, and this more than qualifies.  I also root for smaller developers to make their mark on the market, and while this is just about a niche interest; it is a promising sign from the Spiders software team.  I recommend it in a sale for now; but it certainly merits the attention of both Soulslike aficionado and newcomer alike.

You will spend more time getting knocked down than anything else in the game. You can travel from region to region but you will have to navigate the maze of the maps every single time to get to your objectives. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Steelrising. However the game isn't without its flaws. Detailed notes below for those considering buying the game who have a few minutes to spare. Want to make the game harder?  .Worried the game will be too difficult? .  : So much care was given to the model of the player character, Aegis. From the cogs which are constantly spinning in your back to the rapid changes to your arms as you swap or use your weapons, it really added to my experience of the game.  : Clocking in around 20 hours for a run where I did a ton of exploring / completed the side-quests. This is very subjective, but I found it to be perfect. I don't feel burnt out from Steelrising's content. In fact I want to dive back in and see how I can affect the story through choices made during the game.  : I'm going to wrap these two into a single point, because I think most souls-likes often suffer from doing too little in these departments. The weapons are grouped into various "types", which are refreshingly creative. Some move sets are obviously more inspired than others, but the fact that each weapon has a "special" ability adds variety, and gives the best-designed weapons a unique identity. Armour design is gorgeous, but be warned that some suffer from poor cloth physics. I ended up finding a set of armour ("Diana") which I used throughout the majority of the campaign. The variety of weapons and armour was pleasant enough and, importantly, rewards your exploration of the game world, particularly in the first half.  : The clockwork enemies in the game are beautiful, and can be quite creative. The musicians were favourites of mine, playing their instruments like good bots until they try to kill you with them. Some enemy types which are genre tropes suffer from the same weakness fans will have grown accustomed to, such as dogs remaining the most predictable. However, Spiders did innovate on those tropes in fun ways due to the setting and themes. : This really should be mixed, but I want to give recognition to Spiders for the first three locations you visit in-game after Saint-Cloud. The levels are well-crafted, and serpentine, in a way that genre fans should enjoy. The abundance of shortcuts are complimented by a clear dedication to verticality, particularly within set-piece buildings. The last third of the game's level design does suffer from third-act-let's-wrap-this-up-boys-idis (what the medical community also refers to as Lost Izalith), which is a shame (especially because  is so beautifully recreated). To the developer's credit, the fact that this portion of the game is gated behind a point of no return indicates that they knew you'd be somewhat railroaded until the end of the game, which is appreciated and leaves you less surprised when it happens.   : This is something which has already been addressed by many reviewers, but the game is not particularly difficult. Difficulty is something I seek out in games like these, so it left me feeling ambivalent. Keep in mind that difficulty could later be affected by balancing changes and can be affected by your choices as a player (see the two spoiler tags at the top of this review). : I found the game's environments beautiful, but they can become quite repetitive, particularly in the last third of the game. Being grounded in realism, they are often too concerned with remaining true to life. This is obviously intentional on the part of the developers, but it left me a little disappointed, especially given the more supernatural elements in parts of the game. The last level you visit,  was by far my favourite from an environments-perspective. While several concessions affect the realism of the location in order to make it fun to play through, a lot of attention was given to it's recreation and it shows .  : The mileage you get out of the game's story will really depend on how seriously you take it, and how much you appreciate its subject matter. It is focused on a few key players of the french revolution, which won't be everyone's cup of tea. I thought the more engaging elements were those involving the fiction which the developers crafted themselves, and not the multiple conversations where Lafayette and Robespierre bicker. The story also suffers from some side-quest bloating as you near the first point of no return , with those same quests often asking you to retrace your steps. However, the developers were kind enough to ramp the difficulty / vary the type of enemies in the zones you revisit, which was appreciated.   : This is obviously very subjective, but I found the game's bosses really suffer from a lack of appropriate balancing, and are far too easy for more experienced players. Their vulnerability to critical hits, status elements, and bombs creates an unfortunate disconnect between their beautiful design and their actual difficulty / how long you end up fighting them. I found it a shame that an effective build could lead you to ignore some of their mechanics, especially since so much care was obviously put into their animations / design.   : Buyer beware, this game is quite demanding / taxing on a PC! My build below, for comparison:Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz || 48.0 GB RAM || NVIDIA RTX 3070I ended up having to pay attention to what settings I put on high, and opted to turn many of them down to medium so I could run the game over 60 fps in 1440p. I recommend reading up on optimisation guides / graphical requirements and seeing if your computer can run the game comfortably before diving in, as choppiness can affect your appreciation of the game. As Nacon has been kind enough to comment however, this is something that they are currently working on improving, so if your computer isn't as high-end, you may wish to wait until they've had a chance to make some changes. Ted talk over,thanks for the great game Spiders![Edit: some typos, small changes made to the content per developer comment]. -

_childDocuments_.review: The lack of real factions and fact that enemies are only robots makes what should have been a large and interesting world feel flat and one dimensional. The cinematics are done well, but with such a superficial world its difficult for the plot to be much deeper than a generic escalator moving the character onward. Gameplay feels a bit linear; in the way that a really good game for playstation 2 might. In a way it is a nostalgic callback, but in 2022 it mostly just removes the "open world" feeling of most truly great modern RPGs. Combat, true to the "Souls" style, is difficult to the point of being tedious. There is an assist mode to tailor the challenge level to something more along each person's individual preference. Animations and weapons are done in a way that is both unique and clear quality; these are redeeming factors to an otherwise let down. Though the weapons are easy to pass by and can only be found in one specific area of each linear map. I find myself watching location videos to make sure I don't miss anything. It is not my preferred method to play games, but little alternative is offered except to wander aimlessly through a world populated only by the same generic enemies.Overall this time period offers a unique and refreshing change of weapons and scenery from most traditional fantasy rpgs, and the steampunk element is done well. The worldbuilding and linear story progression lack depth, and I hope that future DLCs remedy this with additional enemy factions and better character customization.  TLDR: Worldbuilding: 2/5. Story/Progression: 3/5. Combat: 4/5. Graphics: 5/5. Overall: 3.5/5. Hope for future: High.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of "a diamond in the rough".I am only recommending it due to having a lot of fun and being very tolerant of the flaws.The combat, the aesthetic, the characters, the setting and the bosses are all absolutely fantastic and well worth experiencing, especially once the gem is polished.In its current state however, the performance complaints are the least of your worries I would say. I have a fairly old rig and had to play at 70% resolution to make it not overheat my poor i5-4690k CPU and RTX 2060 into force restarting my PC.The main concerns are what plagues many recent bigger games - enemy variety, lackluster exploration rewards and NPC dialogue animations. There is also the difficulty being a bit too low, especially on bosses, and the shortcuts for the sake of shortcuts, but those are minor comparatively.The Enemies - technically, there is a lot of variety, however this is achieved by simply having an enemy type have 3 different elements or wielding 3-ish different weapons, normally giving it an extra attack or different element, with the rest of the moveset remaining the same. You will witness the entire roster of enemies about half way through, at which point you'll beg for a boss, but will get a mini-boss that's just a powered up version of one of those enemies.Just having more fodder enemies can help with this, simple ones with a single attack even. I get that each enemies needs a lot of time with the model and animation production, which is why just having throwaway enemies is completely fine, simply for variety's sake.The Exploration - the levels are designed very well, good pacing, decent enemy placement, and good loot spots, however this gets tarnished by the fact that the enemies placed are ones you've killed hundreds of already and the items are consumables or extra upgrade materials which, if you already have selected your weapon of choice, won't give you much after you get your weapon to max level (which is again achieved about half way through the game).Having more miscellaneous consumables can help here, like random self buffs, apart from the resistance ones, mines or knives or something completely passive like a +1 to specific stat on use even, anything more interesting than yet another explosive or healing item.The Dialogue Animations - overall the animations are great, some can look floaty, some janky, but overall it's great. However the dialogue scenes focus heavily on the speaking character, this makes the animation a priority to deliver the emotion, importance or nuance of the lines being delivered. I could forgive it during the side quests as I simply appreciated this being a well voice acted dialogue instead of just reading a note, but when heavy story beats are being delivered it stands out a lot. This especially hits hard during a very emotional moment, which the story built up to, but fell flat when the good voice acting and dialogue is delivered by dead-eyed face models or animations not matching the tone at all.This just needs a bit of polish, easily fixed in a patch or two as the story, dialogue and voice acting itself is already there and good, just needs the animation to match.Well worth during a sale, might want to avoid the side content to make it feel less repetitive, but otherwise waiting for performance improvements is a must for most.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising has all the ingredients of a great souls-like.  The setting of the French revolution with machines is beautifully realized.  Weapon, enemy, and level design are standout.  Combat is mechanically satisfying, albeit a bit clunky, but once you get the hang of it, it’s fun.  It’s not too difficult either, so any deficiencies with the combat don’t become frustrations. Unfortunately, boss fights are the simplest and easiest battles in the game though.  Performance could be better.  The game is regularly on sale too, well worth it at a low price.

_childDocuments_.review: After a wave of underwhelming souls-bourne-like games, I finally found one that pleased me, it is Steelrising. I was skeptical about this one, the marketing was not very convincing and the gameplays shown didn't comunicate very well too.But after 20+ hours of game (finished) I can say the developers managed to deliver, a game that is structured similarly to souls-bourne, with great level design, full of secrets, well placed shortcuts and checkpoints.Enemy variety could be better and bosses could be challenging( this is on the easier souls side). The combat might not please everyone, even though they managed to make convicing automat with animations that are very realistic, if can feel clunky and rigid depending on the enemy, heavier enemies are more stiff and slow. The protogonist however is fast and slick conveying the idea of what it represents.Story is well done and very interesting, it kept my attention from beginning to end. Narrative is similar to Greedfall with slightly better animations, but well executed mostly.Now the elephant in the room.... the performance, yeah if you have seen system requirements you realize that a beafy gpu an cpu are a must. For me the biggest issue is the CPU, my ryzen 2600x clocked at 4ghz couldn't maintain a locked 60 fps all the time, there are areas of the game which brings framerate down to low 40s with sustenained mid 50s in some places.... and there is nothing you can do to alleviate this, and aparently this is not justified either, game doesn't have NPCs walking around nor there are so many enemies... the developers need to improve this that is for sure. On the GPU side things is not so bad, my rtx 3070 is able to maintain almost locked 4k60 with tweaked settings, but I used DLSS to give it more room for busier moments.I  didn't test all the weapons and builds, in fact I sticked to the one I found worked better for me right at the beginning until the end. So, I can't say much about re-playability but it seems to have potential.Some side quests feel like fetch quests, but they may have important implications on the story and ending.Finally, I recomend this game and hope it will be improved over time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a prime example of why games should have demos. Instead you have to buy and refund a game to see that it has massive performance problems on your system. Game consistently fluctuates between around 20-30 to 60 FPS while standing completely still, even with FSR enabled at 1080P with medium settings. I don't have a high end gaming PC by any means (Ryzen 5 5600x, RX 6600, 16GB RAM, PCIE4 NVMe) but when the FPS drops the game slows down too so it's unplayable. It's a shame because it looks interesting. Please PC devs, GIVE US GAME DEMOS.EDIT: I appreciate the response, and I did submit the dxdiag before this review based on your response to another user's review. Best of luck to you guys.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. A hack-n-slash with light RPG elements. Minimal Souls element that provide a nice sense of urgency and direction, without a focus on challenge. The story is interesting, and there is a sense of adventure and mystery in this game that fits in nicely with the atmosphere. The animations are great and help make the controls feel responsive. The art direction and setting in the game is great. Overall, an excellent experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game without any expectations for 60€ and was still disappointed, after 3 restarts, I finally could play the game with more than 30 FPS. (rtx 3070/i7 7700K/ 32GB RAM). The story is very meager and also boring, if you would like to read pages of notes every 20 meters to catch the „story”, you can buy the "soul's like" for 50 €.Since the story is very uninteresting and the combat system very sluggish ,nothing actually remains, except the graphics, which we can enjoy at a nice 40 FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: In a market becoming saturated with souls-like games, this one definitely stood out to me. To keep things relatively short and simple; the gameplay was very fun and smooth albeit it wasn't exactly the hardest souls-like game I've ever played and I've played a LOT. The weapons are AWESOME and definitely warrant multiple playthroughs to try different builds and the armors are all beautifully designed with clear inspirations. The story, setting and protagonist, Aegis, were also all beautifully designed and written. As for performance, I've had a completely smooth playthrough from start to finish. I know people seem to be having trouble but I've had no framerate or graphical issues during my entire time playing the game, and in that time I think I encountered only 1 or 2 noticeable bugs. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game and I'm definitely gonna give it another playthrough to try out an alchemy build this time. Worth every penny ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: I think Steelrising is one of the best 'souls-like' out there.The combat is very fun, there's variety of weapons, upgrades and specific items that better suits different play styles.The enemies and bosses have interesting move sets (specially the bosses), even though some of them tend to get quite repetitive sometimes.The story is good, the art direction is beautiful and the music is amazing.Overall a solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game. Definitely one of the better soulslike, and I have played a bunch. - It's too easy for my taste, that makes combat a bit boring sometimes. Though u can vary weapons and combatstyles (e.g. playing with parry or block). - The story is nice. I like the protagonist. Setting is also nice and interesting. - No bugs so far. Runs smooth with rtx3070 and ryzen3600, 70-90 fps on high/ultra. Never under 60fps. - levels are a bit flat. Exploration has it's limits but there is some.- itemization and character progression is limited bit its enough. Recommended. I never finished greedfall since gameplay was too repetitive and the story not catchy enough. Steelrising proves better here. It still has this tendency sometimes but it delivers enough to keep on going and have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: The optimization is bad, but I don't think nearly as bad as many other reviews let on. Plays 1080 low/med with ultra character models and pretty steady 60 fps on a 3060. I hope for better optimization with updates though. Otherwise, this is probably the best non-From souls like I've played in awhile. Has really fun combat, the world is winding and twisting and exploration is decently rewarded for the most part, the story is interesting. If you're on the fence, wait for a price drop, but I think it's a good buy if you enjoy the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Believe it. I have a 30 series and listened to one reviewer who said, "It wasn't that bad"..... Yes it is. I have a 3070, the game recommends I play on normal settings. First game to ever do that. AA at that! (SCROLL TO BOTTOM FOR UPDATE)Look.Look cool? YesCombat fun? Yes (imo)Interesting story? Got my attentionDo I want to play more? YES! But! I am more tired of people rushing out the product because quarters are about up, or holiday is around the corner. I do not know and I do not care. This game, ONE HUNDRED PERCENT, needs a patch / fixing. To give an example, the camera doesn't feel like it is transitioning up and down as you move. It feels like it is bouncing up and down. I never truly understood people when they said they felt motion sick (never had it before). I am not getting sick, but I have had to blink my eyes because it felt like they started bouncing up and down (weird feeling by the way). WAIT TO BUY. I listened to the thumbs up on a mixed game. I also listened to someone saying, "not that bad".. I am here with a spent 60. You? Not yet. So prove to devs and pubs why quality is key and NEVER trust the "not that bad" guy.. UPDATEI read another comment... and admittedly forgot DLSS is a thing. Did it fix it 100%? No. Stutters, frame drops (These two are by far the WORST offenders. Makes fighting a frustration in a SoulsBourne), rendering taking awhile to kick in. Everything detailed except a rug or wall, or even the road itself. Looking like a muddy mess. Pausing the game to continue. EVERYTHING continues, EXCEPT Aegis (your character). She stays locked in for another 2/3 seconds. Getting mauled in the process if a fight is taking place. Turn off Depth of Field, it continues to persist. Muted dialogue. Turn in a side mission item, awkward silence for a good 10/15 seconds. Then mission over. I have NO clue the resolution and no pop up from received items (if I got one). Then what lead me here to update my review, a crash. First one to be fair, but one none the less. Outside the technicalRarely, but some enemies have terrible attack animations. Where their blade WILL go through you, but does not count damage. It is not a bug, just not the hit to register damage. This is terrible design. Especially if you parry like me. Because the actual hit comes in, in the time I am stuck in the parry animation. Texture Quality at HIGH means blurry (looking at her armor). Only EPIC is clean looking. No joke. Higher the settings, more prone to the issues above. Now mix all this together. And for the ones not having these issues, congrats! However, this IS the gaming world and I know some are just dealing with it. If it was one of the these issues and not all, maybe. This is too much for it be just me / a few of us. I cannot wait to see what a patch does. I want to really like this game. IMO, they went all out. I can see what they were going for. I can see the craft. But it seems either PC was left behind due to negligence, or the engine cannot hang. Either way, we pay full price. End Game UpdateI beat the game. I am saddened because I kept playing thinking today would be the day the patch came. That turned into the day the devs would announce a patch would be coming soon.. I got to see neither. I usually rate Soulsbourne from beginner, intermediate to SoulsBourne. I would say this is a beginner level. There is NO limit to items. So once you find yourself rolling around with 187 heals and your estus (reusable heals) you have to make a decision. I decided to not allow myself to heal outside of parrying (item required) which kept the game interesting. Grenades are STRONG. Like, "I may die. Oh wait! I have grenades. I'll be fine" kind of strong. I guess the limit is 999 when factoring in how many healing I had because by the time credits rolled I acquired 40/60 per nade type. When it came to the upgraded variant, I had maybe 20/30 of those too, and I never used them. Didn't need to honestly. The normal nades where more then enough for enemies. IMO, I would do what Bloodbourne did. Have a max of 2/3 items, anything more is put away. Stored at the lanterns/carriage. Re-upping when you visit. HOWEVER! If I were the devs I would work on enemies with staff like weapons. Their reach is too far/wide. I would i-frame through as needed, but the range was so far to the left, right, center (whichever way they swung) the only real option was to run, or get far enough away, which in turn would take me out of the fight. If Aegis is within a foot of that weapon, you still get popped. So side stepping was a pain but BB is my favorite SoulsBourne to date. Side stepping/parrying is what I do. So I suggest fixing their hit boxes or shortening their weapon. Maybe both. I say this because at the end of the game, last map, you find yourself going against two staff wielding enemies at once. SO MANY GANK HITS!! This resulted in grenades. Tossing them like Aegis was trying out for the local baseball team. Fast balling like an auto turret. Worked. But it felt like I was cheating. Right then I thought of going into the final boss fight and seeing if my 30 or 40 level 2 explosive grenades could take the win (for closure, I didn't do this but I guarantee you, nades would win). Another review said this, but I have to agree. Normal enemies gave me more trouble then any boss. Shield barer, the one using a log and the one dual wielding two chains (sadly I cannot remember the names). Granted this was to do with the hitboxes more then the moves themselves but still. There isn't much to say here besides I hope they add a Added Difficulty section in the menu if some want (kind of joking). Also, between bosses and enemies, after they do some combos, or a few attacks, they would just stop. They just stand still, no movement what so ever. No joke for a quarter of the game, I thought this was a trick to reel me in like a trap. It isn't though. I moved in and hit them 2/3 times before they moved again. Not sure if this is a bug or not. My suggestion. Get rid of this and speed up some enemies. I love when my heart rate goes up in these games.  All in all, I like the game. I think it is gorgeous, fun, and I appreciate actually giving us a story. IMO, you HAVE to do the side content. It is half the game and fills in half the lore. However, to save you time, you will get side mission pretty early on, but it is not until you have the special abilities (obtained through the titan, main boss, fights). There are three abilities. Once you have those, most side content is good to go. However! Some will still be locked until certain story beats (need a key for example). As long as you keep talking to the NPCs, you'll get them all. Still. until the patch addressing the technical side drops and cleans up that side of things, I have to stay with a thumbs down. This has to stop. It is crazy to me something as SteelRising, which you can SEE the craft, releases in this state. UPDATE 9/28/22Patch came and what a massive difference it made. I played until the workshop (beating the first two areas). Running with Aegis never felt better. Only stutter I noticed was moving while the game was loading a new area, or auto save. There where a few muddy objects. However, we're talking a box, instead of the actual roads. Again, much better!  UPDATE 11/12/22Sadly this latest "DLC" deleted my saves. I had a end game save to load to instantly play the "DLC" at release. However, that is now gone. All that is left is my NG+ save. Which only has the first boss on it. I am HOURS away from the "DLC". Not in the mood to play that much again. I put parenthesis around DLC because apparently it has been in the game the whole time. Wow. Sorry to give a roller coaster of a review. I hope this proves I tried giving Nacon the benefit of the doubt. At this point, months after release, still having constant issues and the introduction of even more, a thumbs down is deserved in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this was my first soulslike, So I lack genre context. but I can provide some basic notesSetting: marvelous, the plot and atmosphere is refreshing and interesting. characters feel lifelike and plausible.Gameplay: Tough but rewarding. No doubt a veteran souls player will find it easy, but there are a number of difficulty settings to elevate the challengeLength: Just right, the game neither dragged on nor felt rushed at any point, the pacing was smooth and the challenge level rose consistently.Combat: Very good, combos and dodges were satisfying to use,  enemies telegraphed well, without feeling stilted, aided by the whole mechanical theme. Enemy variety was good, and sensibly typed out without being too redundant.Weapons and builds: Good, while i didnt experiment with too many builds I found a nice mix of weapons for various playstyles and experimented with  a few even though I wasnt ideally statted for them.Aegis recieves a number of interesting armor sets that suit her very well and many therein have differing focuses.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves 90%+ rating like it has on Metacritic on all platforms. My personal Game of the Year.Breathtaking art and soundtrack in a unique setting (reminds me of Syberia games) with kinda janky gameplay but more satisfying than Souls games because it isn't made for online play and thus doesn't have the annoying input delay, plus a lot less trial and error overall. Lots of secrets as well if you want to explore.Yes it has perfomance issues and needs a patch or two but nothing that FSR and DLSS cannot fix. On my 2060 with quality DLSS on all high settings except textures (because of 6 GB ram) runs most of the times at 60 fps. Oh and disable Indirect Illumination, it kills perfomance for some reason.And Spiders if you read this...get a proper marketing team for once.You are one of the few studios in the world that still have that old Bioware's touch in character and world building. It is a CRIME that your games do not get the recognition that they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: My first soulslike, which I mainly bought and played in anticipation of Lies of P to see if I could even enjoy this sort of game and the answer is: yes, absolutely. I mean, I ate dirt for the first hour or so but once I got used to the mechanics, it was smooth sailing. There's a large variety of weapons throughout the game so you can really customize your playstyle. I believe the main story is 15 hours but doing the side quests will extend it to 20, maybe 25 and I highly recommend that you do because I personally found them much more interesting than the main quest. Your enjoyment will partially depend on how much you care about the French revolution with automatons setting, so don't be surprised when you start encountering major historical figures from that time period. If you're a history nerd like me, that might even be a big draw for you and I think in that aspect, the game does deliver. In fact, I had so much fun with it that I ended up double dipping with new game+ to get some more achievements I missed the first time around, which I hardly ever do. Got the game when it was on sale for $20 or so and I think it's well worth that price.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a soulslike that has a few key QOL and design features that make it a good game for me personally. 1. It has pretty good voice acting and the story is actually comprehensible and good. 2. Quest design actually tells you where to go while not being too obvious or intrusive. 3. Combat is fast and there is a large variety of builds to try out. 4. The checkpoints (bonfires) are well placed and you will never lose a ton of progress from dying, or have to do a ridiculously long run to a boss room. If you are a fan of soulslike games and the above appeals to you, you will enjoy this. There are some bugs and I had to lower shadows for performance but they weren't a big deal. The movement animations look stiff in videos because you are an atuomaton in the revolutionary france era, the actual combat feels smooth and responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's do good/bad  reviewer, shall we?+ Gorgeous character models and architecture, excellent animations.- But very copy-pastey, sometimes disorienting, overuse of invisible walls.+ A soulsborne game with quests, decent story and extensive cutscenes. Awesome voice acting.- At times nonsensical scenes, overall more on the predictable side.+ Although  a bit clanky combat, way more responsive than The Surge for example. Creative weapons fitting in for the setting.- Very 'flat' progression system. (Attributes have almost no effect) Not much sense in experimentation.+ Unique Bosses. Base mobs that gain 'twists' the farther you go.- No real encounter variation because of not enough meat on the base mechanics.+ I like the decision of including metroidvania elements, but not overuse it.- Mind-boggling rule-changing of aspects regarding navigation for no apparent reason.+ Fresh and interesting setting. Doesn't shy to show violence.- Wouldn't mind if they included a spark of humor. (in addition to the hilarious music automatons)I can recommend the main game and story DLC. Could have finished it ~3h early if I used the damn compass earlier and not running around aimlessly for side-quests.As others said, not the best on the technical side. Around 15 crashes on Linux with Proton/GE.

_childDocuments_.review: I ran the game with a stable 80 FPS and had no problems in this aspect. The combat is severely lacking in this game. Often times I can visually see the AI breaking down. They would just stand there while taking hits. The enemy variety is not there and there's a lot of re-skins. They're trying to be innovative and create unique combat systems that work okay. They still need to do a lot of number tuning as stats make too much of an impact on your play style. I started as an alchemist and played with lack luster damage until I just decided to go full strength starting at level 25 or so. I went from doing no damage to practically one combo everything to death. There's a huge disparity of damage between the different weapons. Elemental abilities are extremely lack luster, however, frost is probably too overpowered as freezing an enemy allows you to do a full charged attack. There's no diminishing returns, so most BOSS fights can be won by freezing and spamming charge attacks. The story is okay. The rewards for side quests are atrocious. They reward you with story and achievements and one mobs worth of souls. They don't give you anything else such as cosmetics or equipment or even modules. I cleared the game while freeing everyone and doing all the side quests in my play through.They really messed up by having no free roam after beating the final boss. My file is now bricked and unplayable. There also doesn't appear to be a respec option for the characters, So my character was utterly trash for the first twenty five levels. The terrain is also super buggy and can bug out a lot. The levels are not as platformable as they might appear. Overall, I'd give this a 5/10 for being mostly bug free and innovative combat systems that need numbers tuning.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat starts great, unfortunately you never get new weapons after the first couple hours, so it gets a little bit samey by the end.They do give you alternate versions of the weapons with one of the elements attached, but since I wasn't spect for Alchemy I wasn't interested in those.Sound is great, all the Enemies sound great, the hit sounds in combat are good and the songs, when they do come in, are good too. Nice overall package soundwise.Setting and Story are interessting, optional Quests for the most part are worth doing, no complaints here.Looks great, ruined Paris gets a bit old after a while. But the other areas do make up for it.Performance isn't great, but I could still run it at 60fps most of the time (on medium), and my pc is over 6 years old at this point. Overall Good Soulslike, not exactly Nioh2 but better than average.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game, if you want some French infusion in your blood.[+]1) FRENCHSet in France, characters are French, there is even some French in English. Perfect.2) UNIQUE WEAPONSEach type is unique and with a different special ability.3) PRETTY GRAPHICSIt is not Elden Ring, but some Paris scenery is really beautiful.4) GOOD VOICE ACTINGVoice acting was pretty good, but bad facial expressions ruined the immersion.5) GOOD STORYSurprisingly, the game has a good story, with some mystery and a predictable, but still sad conclusion.[-]1) CLUNKY MOVEMENTMovement is clunky and annoying, especially rotational movement.If that was done intentionally to show the character's Automat nature, then it was a bad idea, which somewhat ruined the experience.2) UNBALANCEDAction RPG - yes, Souls-like - no.By the third of the game, you become overpowered, and the gameplay just collapses.3) BAD FACIAL ANIMATIONAnimation is so bad, it ruins a good voice acting.4) STUCKINGCharacter gets stuck on a small brick, or sometimes even on nothing at all.5) BOSSES ARE A JOKEThis game bosses are a joke. _childDocuments_.review: You'll enjoy it, if you you know what to expect. This game is definitely not a AAA title and worth 50€ but I got it for less than 30€ and that is alright.How difficult is it?I completely spikes in the first few hours and in a few boss fights. But once you get grenades/potions and learn how to use them, most enemies are easy going. IMO this is completely imbalanced because you can carry an infinite amount of grenades and potions and they are not very expensive.   Where it shines:- Combat and upgrades: Huge variety of different weapons that have completely different attack styles. Very Bloodborne-like, and you can combine two different weapons and several types of throwing weapons to develop your own approach to combat. -Art style and environment: Very unique and atmospheric. Next best thing until Lies of P. get released. Where it sucks:Cutscenes and overall story: In typical Spiders-fashion, this is early 2000s story telling. Looks like these guys don't have one single decent writer on their payrole or someone who knows the basics of camera work for dialogue scenes. Absolutely dreadful facial animations, no dramatic development and very little suspense whatsoever. This is a major problem in basically all of their games. Some boss entrances are souls-like but still sub-par. Performance: It doesn't run well and you need to lower most setting even on high end machines to get a stable framerate. Considering the resulting visuals, this is technically pretty weak. Watch a few gameplay videos first and decide for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: For me it was a surprisingly good game. For sure no AAA-souls like. But if you lower your expectations, you can have quite a good time for your money. (If you buy it in a sale)I would recommend it especially for people who are new to the genre, as it is quite easy, when you are progressing to the endgame. Positive:- Setting (French revolution with robots?)- Combat System and Upgrade SystemMeh:- Story could be better. But if you are trying to complete all the sidequests, it can be okay to say the least- Performance- Graphics. For me the graphics are okay. But with time the assets are getting quite repetetive.Bad:- Balancing. I think that this is definitely the weak point of the game. I ignored the whole alchemist-aspect, because i never needet it. And after like 10 hours or so, i killed all major bosses with my first try. - Enemy AI. There are always situations, where you can cheese the fights. And the enemies tend to be very passive, which can result in you benefiting from heavy weapons and heavy attacks very much.So if you think that the cons and mehs are no problem for you, and you are looking for a more "relaxing" souls-like experience -> Give it a try

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 from me.Music is really good when there is music, mostly it is just ambience.The Story is rather deep I think but I skipped a lot of it, bc. I play it for the gameplay not the story.The Game is really, really easy compared to DarkSouls, did the final boss first try without even needing 3 healing items.The worlds are beautiful BUT, and this is a giant BUT, it is basically impossible to not get lost in all the mazes there are, the levels are very linear yet there are many, many places to get lost, everything kind of looks the same, there is few landmarks to get a feeling of where you are, after a while it felt tedious to just search for where it continues to the point where I watched walkthroughs to find out where I needed to go. I would absolutely play the game again on New Game Plus but the simple fact that the maps are so confusing to navigate, I think I will not replay it any time soon.I did hop into NG+ though and it seems to get a bit better difficulty-wise but they also allow you to level up even higher than in the normal game.Almost everywhere is loot yet basically none of it really is interesting or fun, every now and then you find grenades but I didn't find a need to use them because the bosses were so easy. The best loot and the most interesting loot to find is upgrade materials, modules and weapons.With a heavy weapon you can stunlock almost everything from normal enemies to main bosses.The side missions are basically go there and there and so on, not really interesting nor was it interesting enough for me to do them all.Finding keys is a good feeling until you remember that you saw at least 3 doors, let me give an example. I was in the Bastille and I saw a bunch of locked doors, every time I found a key it seemed the door is less than a minute away, the fun thing was that I always was unsure if this was finally the key for the locked door I was at a while ago, the answer was always no, might be because of me skipping a bunch of the story cutscenes but yeah.I didn't feel as rewarding to beat bosses as it does in other games, probably because, just as said, none of the bosses really pose any challenge, the most I've died to a boss was likely 7-8 times, not more.You start just running past all enemies if you die just searching for the right way.Many parts of the game are unbalanced and there are some bugs, like items still being there after picking them up (makes it fun to guess if you've been to somewhere or not) or getting stuck and using the return to the last checkpoint item until you notice that the game just said, no and you lost all cash you had.I got it on preorder with the DLC included with a discount, the DLC took me about 2 hours or so at most, it was a beautiful level and actually one of the better ones.If you want to play it, buy it on sale, I don't think I'd buy it at full price after having played it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of my favorite games I have played in a while. I am really into historic games. While yes, it is clearly not meant to be an accurate retelling of the french revolution, it still pulled into that time era. I love the design of Aegis, the clothes were also a lot of fun to see. I do have some complaints about the game. One, sometimes its hard to find the certain tools that will help you unlock doors. For example, it was very hard for me to open the last door in the game. I also wish there was no auto lock switching because when I was fighting the enemies, it kept switching which enemy that I was locked on. Now that could be the weapon I used or the setup I had, but it was a real big issue for me. I still feel like this is a fantastic game for anyone that likes historic games and a fun kinda dark soulish game.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who aren't veteran souls players, this is a great introduction to the genre. The trainer option gives you ways to make the experience of learning the combat more pleasant and less punishing while still keeping the game a challenge. No, it's not the most original game, and as usual with Spiders, it's just a little off, but there's a lot to like about what they've done here and the French steampunk aesthetic is appealingly different than most of these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about purchasing this game, I've been in a souls-like binge and I've loved a lot of the games I've played but this one... It reminded me of Lies of P, to find out it came out BEFORE LoP, I really truly wanted to like this but a combination of the buggy textures / physics, the abundance of french words spoken by people who predominantly speak English (that's on my part I am aware, but I can't help but struggle to follow with what's going on or care if I can't understand half the words used) ALSO there are so many cutscenes and so much talking its practically a visual novel with some fighting.This game is so poorly optimised that it takes my 3070 to 99% usage on MEDIUM settings, not to mention the 80gb game size, it's NOT that big I promise you, three locations use pretty much the exact same assets, enemies are either piss easy or tanky as all hell. Bosses have like 4 moves and that's it, The story was just really not interesting and I've managed to softlock myself in multiple places quite easily...However! This game does quite well with the movement, in the beginning it was clunky making it really awful to move around with but after a few hours of playing I started to understand the movement and got into the flow with it. The game does an awful job at a sense of direction, you're given a compass quite early on but it doesn't tell you that you can use it to make way marks to guide you where to go. This would be good IF the game showed you a clear path, a lot of the time the ares you are told to go just take you to clearly locked gates.In conclusion, I would highly recommend against this game, full price, UNLESS you know for a fact you can either speak french or are able to understand the words with ease (again that part is on me entirely) or can accept that it's less of a souls like and just an easy Sekiro??? Just get this game with a key or on sale, if you want to play a good souls-like game with this as a base, I'd definitely recommend Lies of P.Not the worst game I've played but sadly one of the worst Souls-like I've played, I really wanted to like it but they just needed to keep this in the oven for a few more months.EDIT : My first review was after 19 hours which was to beat the game, not including the DLC, I didn't discover you can easily be locked out of the DLC if you're not careful until my NG+I'm now over 50 hours and 6 times playing through to get these final achievements and I want to just again say how INSANELY BAD THIS GAME IS. I cannot stress how annoyed I am by the bugged game, bugged areas and more importantly bugged achievements. I've followed countless guides to assure I don't miss any of the side quests or citizen stories. I've sucessfully spoken and interacted with all the NPCs for the citizen stories and the game just decides to not give me the achievement. This game is beyond atrocious. The voices are too quiet even at 100%, whenever the game wants it'll flip my camera 180 degrees which have led to me dying countless times. The enemies are harder than the bosses 9 times out of 10, the DLC is underwhelming and useless, the game crashes whenever it deems fit and I cannot tell you how much I hate this game. I'm still playing this long because I'm craving this last achievement and I'm expecting to have to replay it three more times before this piece of ♥♥♥♥ decides to give it to me. Look at the r/PlaySteelrising subreddit and a lot of the posts there talk about how bad this game is and how buggy it is on console and on PC. I have absolutely found the worst game I have ever played in my entire life. This couldn't have even been close to a passion project or anything that the devs loved, it felt like they tried to cash in on a Souls-Like experience without trying to make it enjoyable. 2/10(Don't even attempt to 100% it, you'll bald in minutes)

_childDocuments_.review: So it is definitely a Souls-lite. The character customization is very bare-bones but I understand. The combat is solid but slow and calculated focusing more on elemental damage. The enemies and unstable versions are quite slow and easy to dodge around. The leveling system is quite good and clear on what you are leveling. The weapon upgrading however very expensive but makes little difference (stat ups boost damage more early on). The item descriptions are a bit too detailed  (IE sometimes having a few paragraphs to just say its an elemental bomb). Story is OK but the cut scenes are very frequent and I have a hard time getting over that you are in 1800's France yet all the voice actors have almost 0 accent and when they do speak french, its only 1 or 2 words similar to broken french.All in all 7/10 decent game
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: A steampunk souls-like with excellent art direction and story. Don't be misguided by the average score, it is a good game that offers its own view on the souls-like combat system, and for that has found some disappointed detractors. It is hard to say whether the game is easier simply because, unlike dark souls, you're not fighting the controls, or because the difficulty is actually lower. One thing that is true is that I enjoyed the gameplay much more than I did the one dark souls game i played (dark souls 1) and that is simply because it is much more refined, mouse+keyboard friendly (you absolutely do not need a controller to play this), and the platforming side is actually intuitive and rewarding.The game itself is somewhat on the shorter side, even if you take your time I doubt you'll be sinking more than 30 hours into your first playthrough, with subsequent ones being much faster.

_childDocuments_.review: Mon Dieu!Steelrising is a "Soulslike" from developer Spiders and initially offers pretty much exactly what you expect: lots of action-heavy fights, loss of your currency when you die, leveling up at rest points. If you're looking for a Soulslike with a very cool, crazy setting , which is comparatively easy and can be child's play if desired thanks to its freely configurable level of difficulty, the game is definitely worth a look. And the French have not only copied the powerful and varied combat system, but also added a few interesting ideas of their own. The different and numerous weapons in particular invite you to experiment with their various extra abilities. Very good for getting a taste of the genre.Easy 100%!

_childDocuments_.review: I am not intending to shield Spiders, but I believe this game got bad rep for free.The game is not perfect (I am yet to find a Zelda levels of polish in another game, so I would argue that actually no game is perfect) but I don't find it to be particularly bad.I'll start with the problems:Inconsistency:Do You think Aegis (the character) will climb that ledge? Well, think twice, because it might not work... Or does it?Do You think a command will stay consistent along the menu? Well, not alwaysDo You think "she" can traverse that area... Well, it depends...And so on and so forth.The game is easy: The combat is DS1 levels of simple, which I don't find to be wrong, in fact, I am enjoying the experience so far, amend the inconsistencies... Yet, the AI is far from smartThe systems are highly exploitable... But We should be familiar with that at this point. Are We going to ignore That in every Fromsoftware title enemies can attack through the walls? Or the infinite amount of healing in DS2 (don't make me talk about the bosses in that game, please... What a joke)?The good parts: This is going to be my GF's first souls, since is like a light version of one. I'd call this a souls-light. So, if You only came for the dificulty, this one is not for You.The ambient, world design and narrative are pretty good. They do the same as Assassin's Creed regarding the storytelling (fantastic history) and it works wellThe combat is simple, but clean. I have something to say regarding terrible animations, high tracking and terrible bad telegraphed move sets... But it is not regarding this game but Lies of P. I believe that this game is better polished (combat wise) than LoP.The systems are easy to understand, which also plays well with my GF's play through this game planAre You lost? Do You have no Idea of What You are doing? Ok, They can add some markers for You if You decide to equip and use the compassAre You lacking skills? No worries, They offer guns (similar to magic builds in ER) that can and will Your life easier... And don't worry about resources, they support Your play style by providing enough and more of what You need All and all, I haven't experience weird deaths like in the DS games or ER? (I died of infinite falling from a meter and a half ledge in DS1, DS3 and ER. Annoying).I haven't experience any game breaking bug yet... Damn! SOTE (ER DLC) has (d?) a missing collision in a wall inside a catacomb and nobody is talking about that.So, it is my believe, that people is throwing ♥♥♥♥ to this game for free.I bought this game like 2 years ago and I am playing it now, because I was expecting Lords of the Fallen levels of bad, but it is not the case. In fact, I bought the first cosmetic pack of my whole life, just to support this guys.Keep up the good work and get better at what You are missing.7/10 It is not a game to throw a party for (even if people is celebrating another crab's treasure, notwithstanding the buggy mess it gets to be, only because the game is cute) but it is an acceptable game with a bad reputation, coming from people expecting to play DS4.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the beta and I'm enjoying the full release - optimization is better (significantly higher FPS and faster ultra texture loading) and the new areas I've seen are highly atmospheric and fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: It is enjoyable and could infact be an excellent entry point to someone new to soulsborne likes.  The gameplay is a little too easy for a Dark Souls veteran however.  Some negatives:-There are still occasional crashes-The stat scaling is not great; you either feel weak or way way too over powered-The graphics are not great either; the water on the street cobblestones looks MUCH better than most people's faces and those eyelashes of Laclos... dear god why do they go INSIDE his eyelids?!-Side missions have a bad habit of displaying waypoints you are not able to reach without progressing the story further-Be warned that points of no return ARE advertised in-game as such, the only one you can come back from is the DLC point of no return which takes you to the Bastille area (that one you can come back from and revisit later)If you can look past the flaws, there is a fun game here tho.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this one. It has excellent weighty combat - I went for a parry based build and found it incredibly satisfying to turn the machines' attacks back against them. The visuals are great and I had experienced no problems with performance; the game ran fine with highest setting and ray tracing on my 3080 with no stutter and not a single crash. The only things I'd change is the side missions which drag you back through familiar setting with extremely sketchy navigation (the compass often fails to chart the correct path). These are optional but I felt compelled to complete them even though they were not as rewarding as the main story bits. The difficulty could do with some balancing as well. I chose the dancer class and started out quite weak which meant each encounter was exciting as I could be killed in one or two hits. By the end the enemies has not scaled with me and I found I could charge in and absorb a lot more damage. Perhaps I was getting better at the game but even the bosses posed little challenge and the sense of achievement for killing than was slightly diminished.All that said it's still really fun to play and worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I usually have a very hard time with "soulslike" games but I try to persevere and do get some enjoyment out of them.  I LOVE Steel Rising!  The story is cool, the characters are interesting and relevant, and the way they weave history into the narrative is a lot of fun!  I think that most of the negative reviews are just nitpicking and once you figure out Aegis' rhythm you will find that the fights are satisfying and fair.  I think the only thing that makes this a souls like is because there's an endurance meter.  It's not as hard as Dark Souls or Nioh or anything, it's good for people that want to enjoy souls like but, like me, are terrible at video games!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying this game quite a lot. I was expecting one thing, and was honestly surprised to find another. The game setting is wonderful, the history is nothing to write home about, but its very enjoyable and concise. Graphics wise, there is indeed a few FPS drops, but I am playing on Steam Deck, only, so its understandable.Now, to my biggest praise to the game: this is is a Soulslike game. Its meant to be punishable, and hard. But, Spiders, in what I will consider one of the best decisions I ever seen a game developer make, decided to add an assist mode: were, if anything becomes too difficult, you'll be able to use it, and at least, be able to experience the game you paid for.The addiction of this caused a lot of backlash, and a lot of anger, unfortunately...The addiction of this mode caused so much backlash that, upon seeing it, I genuinely started to question my taste for video games, (a media that brought me so much happiness until now). I, for myself. will, once again, praise Spiders for this. Many players, like me, love Soulslike games, but, cannot, for varied reasons, either skill or time, spend 10 hours in one single boss, and this mode will help and not alienate anyone. Enjoy the game. It is an awesome game, and an awesome developer.
