_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 4th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Dark Souls with Marie AntionetteSteelrising has some interesting thoughts. Marie Antoinette is decrying the French Revolution. Though in this universe King Louie has created automats, basically clockwork robots. Marie has her own loyal version, Aeris, controlled by the player. Steelrising starts with this interesting concept, however, once you choose your archetype and start the game there are French influences, but so far it’s another Dark Souls Game. There are great choices for the Art Design and the combat feels fluid. Well mostly, the dodge is more of a side step that never feels as good as a full tumble. Overall this is a game trying to not be like other Souls-Likes so you have stuff like a massive jump but lack the weight and feeling of a Souls-like Combat, it’s being different but different isn’t exactly better in this case. Pick this up if you’re a fan of Souls-like and want a B-Tier entry. You can also look at the other games Spiders, the studio behind this, has made. That includes games like Greedfall and Of Orcs and Men. They’re interesting concepts but overall I don’t think they are the top-tier games people will be raving about. Still, it’s a Souls-like. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointed with the game.I just finished the game, and man was it a trainwreck. I rarely give games negative reviews, but this one deserves it.The main bosses are well made, but between them you have the worlds worst map design + a ton of "powered up trash mobs" in the form of unstable enemies.The zones look the same. There is no difference between a functional door, and a cosmetic door. Tons of invisible walls. Even with the compass, exploring the zones is just unfun and tedious. Combat mechanics as a whole are ok. The developers where going for a weird system where you felt like you where controlling a robot vs a human; which worked for some weapons -- but felt floaty for many.Weapons lack impact, unless you own a duelsense. The game features full adaptative trigger support, and that alone make it feel like you hit something. Get the game on sale, not worth the 50$ in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre attempt at a pared down Bloodborne clone. It does nothing unique or interesting in terms of gameplay, and the story does not make up for it in any way. You play as a living machine, yet they completely fail to take advantage of this. It is a cookie-cutter game with some style and little substance, and the style wears very thin once you get used to the recycled assets and backtracking. I think that there were a lot of very easy ways they could have taken advantage of the admittedly interesting world they created to make a better game. It is a solid attempt, but when Souls games already exist and do 100 times more than this, this just isn't enough. Just play one of those games again, you'll have more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the more accessible Souls-like games. Arguably the best one to recommend people who wish to get started with the Souls-like experience thanks to the assist mode. There is such a unique style to the character designs and animations and steampunk setting, I just wish performance was better.On an RTX 3090 I barely manage 60fps at 1080p (upscaled to 4K via DLSS) with Raytracing on and all other settings maxed out. I can't recommend using Raytracing at this time as it offers little visual improvement at the expense of a lot of performance. I can tolerate the 60fps if the frame times were better, I was getting a projected 60fps most of the time with 1% lows of sub 30fps at times which made for a really jarring experience. Otherwise turn off Raytracing to stabilize performance.Otherwise, based on the first hour and a half, performance could be better and enemy designs could be more varied, but that could change the more I play. It's still a mostly solid and unique experience despite how much it borrows from other Souls games. So far I give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite average soulslike, overstays a bit its welcome towards the end since the progression stops at level 20 for each skills and at level 5 for weapons (there are 7 types and all types have the same animation, only the special is changing) so you hit a wall really quickly if you invested in one type of weapon or skill.Also environments lack a bit of diversity for the most part and there are maybe only 6 enemy types that are reused through the whole game, only sometimes with different weapons, and bosses, although quite cool looking and with nice mechanics, are just really easy.Still the gameplay is ok and (mostly) responsive and actually quite fun since Aegis is very mobile and the level design is actually good, full of shortcuts and some vertical stuff. Also some of the environments are actually really beautiful and the whole design work on Aegis, the enemies and bosses is pretty cool.Story is meh though (and as a French it was just too cringy to listen to this weird Frenglish dub, I know they probably didn't have the budget for both French and English dub but it sounds just awful...)Some bugs here and there, optimization ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks at the moment and it took me only 20h to finish with almost every side quests.Overall wouldn't recommend at full price but would still recommend to souls-fans hungry for more eldendemonsekirobloodsouls-like games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably worth it on a sale, I'd really like to give a neutral review but steam does not and likely will never allow that.Let's talk about the elephant in the room. Technical issues. This game runs *really badly*, the recommended specs are a joke relative to how the game looks. On top of that it does not allow inverted camera, or rather it only allows it on the Y (up/down) axis, want inverted X? No you don't, not according to the devs at least.The devs clearly lack confidence in their level design abilities since they decided to spam invisible walls around quite literally every corner, the game feels extremely constrained and railroaded because of this.The combat is nothing to write home about either, the weapons are pretty haphazardly balanced with some being orders of magnitude better than others, not that it matters overmuch. The general design philosophy seems to be relatively sparsely populated (read: empty) levels with the occasional mook ambush, these are not a threat. Then there's the inevitable "mini-boss" room which is one or more (usually more) very strong enemies that hit like a firetruck and have enough poise to just ignore your attacks. If you randomly get shot by an enemy far off in the distance you've likely stumbled upon such a room, oh and the ranged type enemies have absurd aggro range (realistic, perhaps, but it's not very engaging to just get slammed with a shot from an enemy you didn't even get a chance to see).The stamina management feels, for lack of a better word, 'bad'. There's nothing obviously wrong with it at a technical level but it feels weirdly punishing, this might just be because your bars are in the bottom left corner so it's harder to see them when playing, but it's harder to get a feel for your stamina use than in... let's say dark souls 3. Additionally the stamina recharge delay is extremely punishing, likely to incentivise using the self-harm effect to recharge faster.Speaking of stamina, the dodge does not feel very good to use due to a combination of having practically no i-frames combined with some rather intense tracking on some attacks (that probably shouldn't have anywhere near as much) as well as some pretty suspect attack timings from certain enemies. That, and some rather strange hitbox choices frequently leads to getting hit by attacks you should have cleared. The best strategy for dodging seems to be dodging away, which is counter to wanting to actually hit the enemy with your attacks, this further reduces your practical attack window. You could, of course, also just use the block feature if your weapon has it but this trivialises combat if you play slow and methodical.Now we've already discussed weapon balancing, but armour balancing stands to mention as well. Armour balancing is practically nonexistent. Every new armour set you get is, more or less, a strict upgrade from what you had before. Do you like what your current armour looks like? Sucks to be you, it doesn't help that the game tends to dump armour with resistances suitable to the level you're in as well. If you're in a level with a lot of fire damage it's going to give you fire resist armour and fire resist consumables.For what its worth I do like the modules system, it's a compromise between power and progress gating in a way that traditional ring slots cannot realistically achieve.I don't... hate this game. I also can't recommend it outside of a very steep sale either. It has too many problems and doesn't run well on current hardware, let alone hardware from when the game was released. Future hardware may alleviate this but that's beside the point (and my machine is more than overkill sporting an Rx 7900 XTX and a Ryzen 7 5800X3D).

_childDocuments_.review: If it works on your PC it is okay so far.I won't say this is a must have for souls-like fans. It is very much your standard souls feeling situation but with as nice coat of paint. My only issue so far is that it falls into the trap of punishing certain actions without much recourse from the player.For example it feels punishing to use your attack chain past one or two hits. I can not say that feels good even on the basic enemies. My experiences with bosses is that they also force me to do one or two hits, defend and continue. Normal enemies feel like the just poise through my hits pretty quickly resulting in this stilted feeling play. It's mostly a shame because the attack chains look cool! I get it though. That's a very souls thing. My other issue so far is the lack of respecting mechanics some enemies seem to do. Each weapon has a special move attached to it. I had one that was a parry and one that was a full shield.The shield was pretty great on the first boss. Though it made the fight cheesy. The boss would rebound off the block, and I would try to time it to be close to a parry just in case that helped. It ate stamina but it gave me an opening. It felt reasonable enough. The next boss just could punch through my shield in a hit, and do damage to my health! Okay so maybe shields just suck and im supposed to dodge more? Keep in mind i've played for only 2 or so hours and I didn't do rigorous testing. Just sharing initial impressions and experience.I like to experiment though so I tried to use a weapon with parry. For some reason that worked on the heavy hits! No damage, no stamina loss of note, and a free counter hit. This felt weird. But even worse was later I fought an elite enemy which had two wrecking ball hands. Obviously it was going to be a heavy hitter. I figured that heavy hitters shatter shields. I tested it just in case and yep, shielding was not the way to go. It would burst through it and do damage like the boss. I could parry some hits with my other weapon. The timing isn't too tight so that's okay, but some attacks would not get interrupted by the parry. So i'd parry and get hit by followup damage. So this meant a parry wasn't the perfect solution either even if I timed it right.Which made melee against this thing annoying. So draw out hits and dodge, and maybe parry certain things. That or spam some ammunition on a frost gun to freeze it. Which is total cheese, but limited by ammo. Right now it feels kind of cool but i'm kind of annoyed by the inconsistency. Maybe if it was better telegraphed that certain hits were unblockable/unparryable it could elevate the gameplay better. As it stands I am guessing mostly. This is especially an issue because a block or parry is a weapon special. It's supposed to help define the weapon. Not all weapons can do it. Though the attack skills, so far, seem to drain a ton of stamina and leave you at the mercy of a stronger enemy. So it's kind of hard to say any specials feel too great.Still I found it fun and I am going to keep going through. I would wait to buy this until more people have reviewed it and maybe for some optimization fixes. It's a nice idea overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially had a negative review due to performance issues and a lack of universal block/parry. I still think those are issues but I think the game is HALF decent. I am returning the game, though, because it's not for me. Performance issues: Running 2k screen with medium graphics on a 2080 super and watercooled 10 series and constantly fluctuating down to 50 fps with really basic surroundings. I can usually run max graphics at 2k on any game with a crisp 60fps.Why I don't like the game: There is no universal block or parry move. Instead those moves are individually tied to specific weapons. Meaning some weapons can block, some can parry, and many can't do either. What's more is that dodging doesn't seem to have i-frames (maybe it does but didn't really feel like it when I played). So it seems that you're left with - pick a thin selection of weapons with defensive abilities or stay far away from attacks and get in little pot shots where you can. You can block attacks for 5% of your stamina and cause enemies to recoil, or get hit for 30% of your health bar. Sort of a weird balance.After about an hour with a defensive setup, I realized that the block and parry moves aren't even relevant because the enemy movesets are very limited. Just let them do an attack sequence, then punish them. It's just way too easy. They don't close the gap on you, they don't attack in groups, they don't surprise you, they just solo patrol. It's like a Steven Seagal movie.The art and animations and atmosphere all look great. Marionette automatons in the French revolution. Very cool character and concepts. But after playing so many good/unique souls-like games, I just can't get into an easy/slow one. Beyond the art, there is nothing uniquely alluring here.

_childDocuments_.review: Great soulslike with all the known features of the genre, but with few interesting twists.Fantastic maze-like level design with both horizontal and vertical paths, plenty of nooks and crannies to explore, ambushes to detect and shortcuts to unlock. After unlocking new traversal tools, there are reasons to come back to previous areas. One issue with levels is that some ledges look climbable, but really arent and if you manage to get on them, invisible wall will be waiting for you. Though problems like that are few and far between.Decent weapon selection, though some are clearly more powerful than others (if not straight up overpowered) - particularly guns, chain weapons and frost alchemy, turn the game into a cakewalk.Solid combat mechanics. Feels a bit slow at first but once it 'clicks', it becomes really satisfying. Especially when playing aggressively and utilizing cooldown mechanic.Graphics and performance are decent. No framedrops, stable 70+ on rtx 6900/ryzen 9. High-res textures take a moment to appear after first loading of the level, so the ground looks like soup, but after few seconds everything's fine. Animation of human characters in cutscenes is pretty bad for 2022, but outside of that everything is smooth.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried pretty hard to like this game but a few elements just sucked the fun out of it for me.Pros-Visually looks nice, some pretty unique looking enemies.- Special attacks are cool, felt different needing certain weapons to have access to parries or shielding but I think that cancels out the positive in a sense.- Customisation of the character is okay, since you are a robot after all.- The later plot related skills are pretty amusing to use, great utility and I won't spoil how they can also be used in combat (they are really strong). Cons- Felt a bit too easy? With the access to health regen relatively regularly and less aggressive enemy types I never felt like I had to go all out to clear an area or defeat a boss, with the other part of it being that the attacks are a little too telegraphed and having enemies parry your attack and still not hit you is very funny. I was expecting to be dying constantly  but the challenge simply wasn't there aside from one boss in particular.- Armour types don't seem to matter outside of stats. I just picked the heaviest armour and left it at that. Sure some of the resistances might be nice but better armour overall just felt more consistent.- Attack patterns per weapon are very uninteresting or rather it's just a difference in stats and your basic spear has the same moveset as the later ones, could have been nice to have something special per weapon even if it's something small.- Mild visual jank from time to time, for example enemies getting stuck on boxes or being too dumb to walk around- Level Design is pretty weak. Even with the extra help thanks to the compass there was several times I got stuck because it wasn't clear where I was supposed to go next. Part of this problem is that at times some chests or ledge look like they are accessible when they actually are not.tl;dr A French made and themed "souls-like" with a pretty unique plot that falls short despite trying some new things. Pick it up on sale, I've heard it's short to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Greedfall, and when this was announced, the setting interested me, so sign me up! After finishing my first playthrough, I can say this game probably won't stick with me quite as long, but I still definitely enjoyed it. I only wonder what could have been if they had a larger team or budget.The character-focused story/sidestory is a solidly entertaining experience, and the main draw of the game for me. The facial animations leave a lot to be desired, but the voice acting is solid. Most of the stories are interesting and unique, and seem to have multiple endings that I believe have an impact on how the game ends, though I could be wrong as I've only completed it once at the moment. On top of that, I appreciate that it's easy to follow the side stories in this game. Some people may like the cryptic, almost definitely missed on first playthrough experience of a Souls-game, but personally, I'm thankful that wasn't the case here as it makes it easier to appreciate the story of the game.The level design and world building is very well made, with a labyrinth-like map with plentiful exploration and shortcuts to reduce the amount of mindless backtracking to get where you need to go. For the vast majority of the game, I was fully immersed in running around this downtrodden city. Chests are always exciting as they are nearly exclusively filled with stuff that I wouldn't consider 'filler' items. I do wish there was a slight bit more variance in the way the world looked, 2-3 of the areas had a very 'samey' look. It led to a bit of confusion as to which map I was on. On top of that, a frustrating feature of this game is some paths being locked behind quests, without being obvious in that feature. It does slightly disincentivize exploration to a small extent as it can be frustrating reaching an interesting looking area to run into a gate that you cannot open and have no idea why you cannot open it.Combat and general gameplay feels super good in my opinion. There's a good variety of weapons and they all feel fun to use; despite having less weapon types than a game like Dark Souls, I ended up using more weapons overall as more of them just felt interesting and fun to use. On top of that, it's much harder to 'mess up' your build and gives you more freedom to explore all your items. On the flipside, this simplification of the character progression does mean it's not as exciting, as there are less choices to be made and stuff like stat-locked weapons are not a thing. Also, some of the unique features of combat are quite fun. Fast-cooldown took some time to get used to, but once I did, it was very fun to use and significantly impacted the way I playedAlong with combat, enemies are solid but leave a bit to be wanted. There were no enemies that left me frustrated, they all had a solid place in the game. That being said, variety does lack compared to the more mainstream games of this genre. My main criticism in this regard is the bosses, or lack of. There's a relatively small amount of bosses, and an even smaller amount of bosses that actually stood out to me as interesting fights. It left me wondering if this game being in the 'Soulslike' genre was the right option, or if it should have been in the same realm as Greedfall.I probably have a lot more to say but this review is kind of dragging on, so to TL;DR some of my views of this gameThe good-Very interesting story/world, side-stories in particular-Voice acting is solid-Very satisfying minute-to-minute gameplay-An accessibility mode for those that need it (sorely lacking in this genre)-Pretty environments, enemies, outfits, basically everything has great artstyle/aesthetics-It stands out as a unique experience in gaming-Level design is solidNot so good-System requirements are way too high for the technical quality of the game-Enemy variety leaves a bit to be desired-Boss fights are a weaker aspect of the game, which is disappointing considering the genre-Facial animations can be jarring-No french dub? :(-Story-locked areas can leave you confused-It leaves you wanting more from itAll in all, if you want to get the best bang for your buck, this might not hold up to something like Elden Ring. That being said, it's still a solidly fun ~20 hour experience and I enjoyed it the entire way through; it's one of those games that I just lost track of time playing it. At the end of the day, that's what I tend to desire from games, so I would say this game is worth playing to me.(as a sidenote, Spiders seems like a cool smaller dev and I enjoy supporting groups like them, which makes this an even easier buy)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some limitations, but I found myself continuing to come back to it. I completed the entire story, explored every level, and did every side quest I could find, so I would recommend it!The difficulty curve of this game is actually the hardest in the very beginning. However, once I found a weapon that I really liked and started to optimize my character around using it, I found the game getting easier and easier until by the final level I don't think I died once. You can also see where the designers had to deal with a limited budget. Most of the levels are either sewers, various types of palaces, or wartorn city streets, and the decorative objects used to make the levels are repeated again and again. The developers also did essentially no action animations on the human characters, so all parts of the story that involve dynamic movement of humans are told in flashbacks with large amounts of cutaways and darkness, or recounted in conversations while the human characters stand still. I get it - this game isn't made by a major studio, so they have to stick to a realistic budget. That said, even with the limited storytelling tools, I found the story pretty interesting. I liked both the high concept and the twists as you discover who you are and how the automatons work. And once again, the true test of whether a game is good or not is whether or not you keep playing it and enjoying it, and I found that I kept playing and enjoying this game for quite a few hours. I would recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I will be reviewing Steelrising as a souls-like, comparing it to other similar games that I have played.I enjoyed the game, and I think the devs executed a lot of elements very well:- to my surprise, I really enjoyed the idea of 'What if French revolution but robots?'- Ludia and Automats look really cool, model designs are amazing- side characters and quests are well written, but are lacking in terms of actual game design (it is 90% just running around betweeen compass marks). That said, I was so invested in the story that I completed all of them- combat system is good but not great. I enjoyed itThere are some things which I would expect in a souls-like but they were not there:- The level design is almost entirely linear. You almost never have to choose which way to go and you never get lost. This is something that I missed a lot compared to Souls games- Build variety is lacking. First of all, I don't think there is a perk reset system. Second of all, weapon upgrades are quite rare (so there is little incentive to switch your old upgraded weapon for a new, unupgraded one). Third, some weapons are so OP that they make the others obsolete. I almost ran through the entire game with the weapon I found in the first location, and I enjoyed it.- Bosses are ridiculously easy, I killed all of them, including the optional ones, in 3 attempts or less (and I am not THAT good). But they make up for it with their looks, at least for me- Enemy variety is also not really there. Near the end of the game I just got bored and ran past everyone, skipping entire huge areas. Something which again would not be possible in Souls games because you would get lost, trapped, jumped on, staggered to death, etc.Still, I wanna say that I drop games immediately if I see that they are boring or generic. This one I completed, and I really think it deserves attention of other souls-like enjoyers, despite its shortcomings.P.S. OBVIOUSLY with a huge discount

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you're a huge Souls fanboy like me, Steelrising is well worth your time. If you're new to the genre, or you only played FROM Software games, I recommend you play Lies of P, Nioh 2, Salt & Sanctuary, The Surge 2, Mortal Shell, and Grime before you spend money on this. PROS:- art design is awesome, the enemy and weapon designs are very cool and thematic, especially bosses- gameplay is great- music, sound design, and graphics are okay- level design is superb, with LOTS of hidden paths, shortcuts, and areas you can find and explore- lots of main and side quests, so plenty of stuff to do. I could've easily played for another few hours if I wanted- story is okay. the villain's speech in the final cinematic actually tugged at my heartstrings- I guess the difficulty settings can be a good thing if you're new to the genre and scared to play FROM's games? Still, I'd say Dark Souls 1 with a knight build is easier than this and a better entry point into the genre.CONS:- needs a lot more enemy variety- loot is extremely underwhelming and mostly limited to consumables, so the awesome level design is somewhat wasted as you will rarely find anything useful- game is too easy even without assist mode, you basically get infinite healing potions, and you fight the same enemies so much you fully learn their patterns, so the game gets even easier as you progress- despite looking cool, bosses are way too easy, which completely kills the epicness of the fights- minibosses are just regular enemies with a big healthbar- you can easily enter areas you're not supposed to enter yet and get softlocked as a result, forcing you to commit suicide and lose your souls in order to get back to the game proper- optimization could be better, but the game was comfortably playable on Asus Rog Ally, and stayed in 60+ fps on a GTX 1070 on 1080p, so most people should be able to run it without issues- you can't respec, so if you wanted to try out different builds and weapon types on your first playthrough, tough luck. Conclusion:Longtime Soulslike fans should definitely check this out. It's probably not worth the full price, though. Get it on a huge sale. The DLC is pretty short, but it's worth it on a discount.

name: Tails of Iron
detailed_description: Bright Fir Forest - Free Expansion Tails of Iron now includes ‘ Bright Fir Forest ’, a second free expansion that continues Redgi’s regal journey. Featuring 13 new quests (four story quests and nine side quests) this end-game expansion takes the young Rat King to the Squirrels’ renowned Festival of Leaf Fall, adds three new challengers in the Mole Arena, further broadens character customisation with new weapons and armour, includes eight cosmetic upgrades for the Crimson Keep, and more. King of Frogkind, the maniacal Greenwart has been vanquished, but despite the joyous celebrations in the forest, a new amphibious menace may be about to bubble through the pond scum… can Redgi overcome the emerging threat and be back in time to enjoy an acorn cup of Bright Sap under the luscious green canopies of Bright Fir? Your tail continues… Bloody Whiskers - Free Expansion Tails of Iron now includes ‘ Bloody Whiskers ’: a free expansion which introduces a new post-game questline, two additional difficulty modes, five new bosses, a selection of special armours and weapons, and a secret that was perhaps better left forgotten… With the tyrannical Greenwart now defeated, King Redgi’s vast lands chime with celebration. But the recently crowned saviour isn’t free to rest easy on his throne just yet. As decreed by an ancient Rat tradition, the new King must prove his worth… in a deadly trial of combat. Defeat the most lethal warriors from across the land to claim the key to the old King’s room. But what heinous secret lurks within? Your tail continues… About the Game Set in a grim land plagued by war, Tails of Iron is a hand-drawn RPG Adventure with punishingly brutal combat. As Redgi, heir to the Rat Throne, you must restore your broken Kingdom by banishing the merciless Frog Clan and their ferocious leader, Greenwart. As you explore the deceivingly charming world, you’ll encounter a cast of unique companions, ready to aid you in your adventure. And you’ll need all the help you can get, whether that’s new meal recipes, blueprints to forge deadly weapons and armour, or even a land-chugging, armour-plated mole mobile! Overcome your fears. Rescue your brothers. Restore Your Kingdom. Your tail has begun… Explore a Treacherous Kingdom Fully accompanied by the deep, raspy narrations of the legendary Doug Cockle (celebrated within the world of RPGs), prepare to embark on an epic adventure across the mediaeval-fantasy Rat Kingdom. Complete side quests and faction hunts for some additional gold-on-the-side, or join forces with a sharp-eyed companion to help even the playing field. Master Brutal Combat From frog zombies to gargantuan grubs - and everything in-between - the Kingdom is awash with danger. To overcome each perilous encounter, you’ll need to study your opponent’s attacks and react accordingly! Thankfully, there’s a range of deadly abilities at your disposal, including parry bashes and fatal executions, not to mention ranged attacks with your nifty bow and arrow. Customise your Attack Adapt Redgi’s combat style to the task at hand. Heavy armour may provide better protection but can you really afford to slow down your dodge-roll? And then there’s the question of weapon; axes pack a punch, while spears are quick and nimble. Perhaps you’d prefer the all-round performance of a trusty broadsword? Overcome Savage Boss Fights While danger lurks around every toadstool, you’ll need to keep your wits sharp and your blade sharper when it comes to the devastating boss fights. Cold-blooded in every sense of the word, these oversized amphibians each present their own unique combat challenge, and you’ll need more than a good set of armour to come out on top. Brew Recipes, Craft Weapons, Forge Armour Redgi’s keep is also home to his brothers, Rem-Rem, Bam-Bam and Dug. Rem can cook up a health-boosting feast with ingredients found throughout the world, while Bam can craft new weapons and armors from special blueprints you’ll uncover… if you look hard enough. And then there’s Dug, who’ll update you about new quests available throughout the Kingdom. Features: Master brutal combat, inspired by the souls-like genre, featuring dodge-rolls, parry bashes, and fatal executions! Explore a vast and treacherous Kingdom, comprising six distinct biomes, each with its own hidden paths and secrets Immerse yourself in a compelling story, narrated by the deep, raspy vocals of the legendary Doug Cockle Customise your attack style with a vast array of distinct weapons and armour Assemble a band of brave companions, ready to aid you on select missions Complete side quests to earn additional gold-on-the-side Unearth special blueprints to forge new and powerful weapons Collect rare ingredients to cook up health-boosting feasts Overcome savage boss fights against the Frog Clan’s deadly, oversized generals Lose yourself in the gorgeous and lovingly-crafted 2D hand-drawn art style.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this "not very hard" game has an interesting game mode that's available even for a first playthrough called "Bloody Whiskers". While playing this mode is definitely not recommended for most players, I consider it a suitable challenge for Souls veterans. With this single mode, the combat system of the game is transformed into one of the most punishing and intricate puzzle I've come across.Despite my extensive experience with Souls titles, I must say that the "Bloody Whiskers" mode is one of the most challenging gaming experiences I ever come across. While the regular base game may be finished in 10 hours or so, this mode took me over 20 hours to beat - it definitely earned its price.It's essential to unlearn some of the Souls habits (e.g. i-frames). The boss fights are more akin to fighting games, where spacing, positioning and planning are everything. There are attacks that cannot be avoided if you are in the wrong place at the wrong time, but with enough attention and practice, you can practically avoid getting hit even on the toughest of bosses. The game has a fair number of bosses, and they typically have some interesting designs and multiple phases.While the base game may be a chill story with passable combat, "Bloody Whiskers" is when the game is transformed into a SL1 Wretch challenge. If this difficulty mode had not been available from the start, I doubt that I would have enjoyed the game as much, nor discovered nearly as much tricks and nuances in the combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an awesome metroidvania type game about heroic rats fighting off invading frogs. It's more combat oriented than something like Hollow Knight, and so the combat is proportionally more involved and challenging. It plays really well though and manages a fine balance of being challenging without being super annoying and unfair feeling. What's really great is the attention to detail and the world building. Every backdrop of every stage has multiple layers of stuff going on in it, relevant to the specific quest you're on and how far through the story you are. It's great to see how the kingdom is being restored by your actions little by little, and hints to what enemies and challenges will be coming up. There's just a huge amount of detail and care put into every screen in the game and the rats themselves are extremely cute and charming. I've not finished it yet but I think I'm entering the third (and possibly final?) act of the main story, but I know a big update just happened to add more post-game stuff. There's also some secret side stuff i've found but not yet completed. My one and only complaint so far, apart from wishing there was infinite story, is that the jumping controls have some quirks it takes a while to get used to, but again it's pretty minor and easy to get the hang of, and there is less jumping than in something like hollow knight. 10/10 would help rats defeat frogs and harvest bug juice again

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a wonderful little game. From start to finish it has a gripping story, filled with charming characters and beautiful visuals. The gameplay is fun and is often rewarding. I highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of games like Hollow Knight. Now it's time for the longer review. Spoilers as always. I’ll have them marked. (Inspirations)Tails of Iron wears its inspirations on its sleeves. A lot of the little references it has are recognizable yet natural. Adapted wonderfully into the game without issue. Things like the quest board have been seen in many games, though this one seems to be inspired by The Witcher. Other things like the benches are very remnant of Hollow Knight. This one felt a bit more out of place, but quickly became alright with me as the game went on. Not every reference was adapted well. There were a few lines of dialogue that were more or less just direct references changed into rat puns. These were still nice but felt a little less earned than other ones. (Gameplay)The gameplay of Tails of Iron is a tricky fish to review. While I really like it, there are some glaring issues that crop up here and there. The primary gameplay lies in the game’s combat. Almost every enemy encounter was very fun. A challenge to overcome but not one that was poorly put together. These encounters felt rewarding as with bugs, you not only got currencies from looting them, but you regain healing juice as well. It helped me feel like I didn’t need to backtrack to a barrel in order to heal. There were a few encounters however that didn’t feel so pleasant or rewarding. The way the enemy AI is programmed can result in some pretty messy fights where your actions aren’t related to you being hit. Sometimes a gank fight can result in one or two enemies lining something up that is completely unavoidable given the situation. These are more at the end of the game but are still a downer when you encounter them. (Weapons/Gear)There is a plethora of gear that you use throughout the game. I love the options the game gives you for taking on your challenges. You get swords, axes, spears, bows and more. Along with that, you have your shield and armor to help keep you defended. These pieces of gear all have their uses, the armor being the most useful with their specified defenses against certain enemy types. These defense values are imperative to the combat as they do block A LOT of damage. Your armor is also split up by weight. Heavier armor being slower to move in but allows you to take more hits. Honestly, when it came down to weight, I barely noticed much of a difference between light and heavy loads. Some actions like dodging particular attacks were more noticeable in difference, but really weren’t huge. So you can use whatever you like if it suits you. The enemy specific defenses will matter more than your base defense. Weapons are a tricky fish. These things feel just fine as they are, but also feel lackluster with what they provide. It isn’t clear whether or not the different weapon types have different effects on different enemies. The game never tells you anything about it, so I just assumed it was all the same. Really it does feel the same. The weapons have great design, and all feel good to use. There wasn’t a single one which I felt personally offended to wield. Though there is one huge issue with them. I never felt overpowered or underpowered. I only ever felt adequate during my playthrough. I feel like a lot of this has to do with the weapons. No matter how high your one handed or two-handed attack is, you will always spend a fair amount of time with each enemy or boss. Not as much time as with lower attack weapons, but you won’t be breezing through them.  I don’t want to feel like I’m absolutely destroying an enemy, but I’d at least like to feel like I’m strong. Even with this though, the combat is fun enough to excuse this issue. (Story)The story of Tails of Iron is brief but bold. It’s a classic tale of a scorned hero on a journey for revenge. It’s something we’ve seen before, but it’s rat themed now. I may be biased, but that’s a pretty cool take on the formula. Even though the story theme is something we’ve seen before, how it’s told is what makes it stand out. Each character is lively and has a good sense of individuality. Some rats feel samey, but not so much that they fall out of being unique. Each one comes together to build up a kingdom that is exhilarating to explore. Seeing all the small details etched into each scene. These things all come together to provide an excellent setting for our story. Throughout the game, we are made to feel bad for poor Redgi as he battles the frogs. Tring to rebuild his fallen kingdom. We get to see the effects of Redgi’s efforts as we go along. Slowly watching life return to the war-torn streets of the kingdom. The losses Redgi faces aren’t small, and each goes a long way in making the player feel for Redgi. It’s a great motivator for seeing the journey through to completion. And what a journey it is. Taking us all throughout this kingdom of rats. From the forests surrounding the Long Tail Village to the depths of the rotten swamp the frogs call home. Each having it’s own challenges that must be overcome so that Redgi can fulfill his duty of rebuilding his kingdom and avenging his family. It’s a tale told in few parts, but with lots of significance in each part. The whole thing is pleasantly narrated by Doug Cockle as well which is just a treat. (Conclusion)Tails of Iron is a short but sweet title featuring plenty of action and entertainment. It’s flawed in places like all games are, but these flaws aren’t too bad that they ruin the experience. I recommend this to anyone who is a fan of games like Hollow Knight or The Witcher. I’ll throw in some bonuses for people who love rat or frog related puns. Well, animal puns in general. And good ones too.

_childDocuments_.review: Time to 100% - 7hrs 33 minsQuick review:  This is a really good game.  Here's the negatives first:  The combat is infuriating until you get into the swing of it (took me about an hour and a half to get a decent grip on it but you might take to it better than I did).  Many of the items are filler, you can balance things out somewhat choosing one over another but it doesn't make sense for the game to have this many pointless variants.  They do look really cool though.  A couple of the bosses are a tad too unfair, but for the most part they are all good.  Sometimes you get spammed in between enemies both using different things you can't counter at the same time.  A couple of bugs, nothing major.  No replayability.Positives:  It looks fantastic.  Seriously, you guys absolutely nailed it graphically.  From the designs to the rendering, and the animation style to the brutal / cute nature of it.  Audio was mainly nailed, but some issues were there.  I don't think the audio dampening effect works as well as it could.  It sounds like the speakers are getting quiet every now and again.  If you added in some kind of drone that was subtly drowning out the sound it would be more effective.  Also, the Clangers noises were infuriating.The gameplay is solid.  There's a good variety of enemies, and they all seem to build from one another in a way which I think helps guide you to get better as you go.  The fairy tale squeaks with narrator is a thing I've seen done horribly this year with Biomutant (it was so bad it ruined the game for me completely).  In Tails of Iron though, it works a lot better.  I think it is because of the storybook aesthetic, accompanied by the wonderful vocals of the guy that played Geralt in the Witcher games, that it succeeds.  I do think the Clanger noises are a detriment though, as they are horrible.  Horrible.It is a shame that you still lose out on feeling for the characters due to the presentation style, but I don't think it matters in this case as it further makes it play out like a proper fairy tale.  I'm really glad to have seen this handled so well after Biomutant failed so badly.  I strongly recommend Tails of Iron.PS - Hint for new players below (No Spoilers):It doesn't matter if you are using a shield or the 2 handed weapon, blocking still fully blocks.  Doesn't matter what way you are facing either.  Parry works with both, and I think has different timings depending on shield / weapon used.  I think you need to be facing the right way to parry.Get past the first jumpy stompy boss and the game gets a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: Adventure-focused souls-lite game in forest-critter setting.✔ dedication to the setting - lots of background details, especially with the rat-folk and how some locations change as time progresses✔ rough, bloody style✔ extra post-game boss encounters❔ lots of bosses with small number of other encounters (compared to other souls-like games), but at the same time it feels like you fight minibosses instead of having big, meaningful encounters✘ I wished for some interesting boss encounters with (relatively) huge animals, but it's all based on humanoids and some insects✘ unnecessary padding in the early-mid game when you have to do a series of quests, each forcing you to go to the underground and then back for another quest, instead of letting you do them all in one visit✘ on top of that annoying respawning blockades and vines, so that each time you have to cut them to go through...✘ disincentivises exploration (do not go anywhere you are not lead by a quest - there won't be anything there and another quest will make you go there later)Overall it's good, but not great. Doesn't excel in any of it's component parts like combat or worldbuilding, but it was a positive experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely looking platformer with a bit of soulslike sauce (was rather easy on normal mode, one boss was somehow more challenging but still nothing to get frustrated with). We are controlling a young noble rat, who can wield up to three different arms (one handed, two handed and ranged), there are many different weapons/armor types but we use them in pretty much the same way. Plot exists only, so the game can send us somewhere else, to find usually one of many bosses. The world and it's inhabitants are quite interesting, even though they communicate without words. Game is not long took me about 10 hours to 100% it - was playing normal mode. Anyway enjoyed it, so I recommend it, especially when you get bored with your usual games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: It's short, it's beautiful, it's sweet! Difficulty is just right - challenging, but not tormenting. It took me about 9 hours to finish on normal difficulty with all achievements (minus Hardcore completion). Game was fun almost all the time. Only downside is it tends to be a bit repetitive from time to time. In one part of the game I felt like I'm going back & forth between one location and quest givers.Visuals and music are truly amazing, atmosphere was great.I bought it on a discount for around 10€ and it was definitely worth it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay mechanics are just plain annoying: only specific attacks can be parried and you gotta wait for 'em, same for attacks that can only be dodged. This means that any other attack it's there just to annoy you, you can either block it or dodge it but there's no reward for timing a parry against it (btw parries are really easy to do). Enemies have a ton of health and fights are long and tedious. Animations are awful. Gotta say that both story and narrator sound pretty good but I won't give anymore of my time to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you like souls-like you will enjoy this. I liked it more than Hallow Knight. Shorter in length. Took me 19.5 hours to get majority of achievements and complete the game. I bought it on sale for $10ish. Excellent music, story, game play. Its a breath of fresh air for someone addicted to souls games. Its pretty linear and by the end of the game if you have OCD about finishing all side quests this game will satisfy. Bosses are difficult, but none I spent more than 20ish attempts on. There are some amazing characters and by the end you will be in love with many of them.Great job Odd Bug!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Geralt?! Is that you? :) There is nothing complex about the story, but the narration is phenomenal. One might say that enemies are inconsistent, It may be hard or easy regardless of the game phase. Nevertheless, it was enjoyable. Using a game pad and looking for a 2D platform that challenges you with arena-style combats, just give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: While this game does have positives to it the lack of polish is unbearable. While I did try to enjoy this game it quickly became clear that near the end of development the developers found they were running out of time and just threw some things together. About a third of the game is spent running back and fourth doing side quests through the same rooms killing the same grubs and mozis. Additionally many of the attacks seem to not be prepared for anyone dodging or blocking any other way than the intended way resulting in weird hitboxes sitting around attacks that they decided you should block (even ones without the block indicator). Hitboxes in general needed a lot of work. Enemies were spammed even in boss fights. Many attacks seemed untested. And then there is bloody whisker mode, it is the hard mode of the game required for 1 achievement of beating the final boss (yes you have to replay the entire game for 1 achievement) and to make it harder they just made you take more damage and made hitboxes worse. this is the first and I hope the last time I see a game try to make itself harder by making the hitboxes more obtuse, they also just spammed more enemies in bloody whisker mode.

_childDocuments_.review: The Secret of NIMH meets Dark Souls in this rodentine tale of war against the Amphibian Horde. First, let me just point this out to all potential buyers:That doesn't make it a bad game, though. I just want to warn you that this isn't a game where you float around the world on clouds, crushing all in your path. This game is meant to be hard. But it isn't terribly frustrating. Most of the time, there are checkpoints that allow you to spawn near where you died. In short, Difficult yet Forgiving.The artwork is superb, the story is a classic without it being too cliche. The combat feels amazing when you do it right. Just keep in mind that fighting is a rhythm in this game, as it should be. It's a lot like a dance: don't do it to get it over with. They aren't meant to be quickly done and over with. It takes strategy, timing, and knowledge. If you push through the difficulty, you are rewarded. It is so satisfying to finally beat that incredibly difficult boss after the fifth or so death. So far, not really a lot of bugs (except the Mozi and Grubs, of course). But the game doesn't explain a lot about the stats. For example, I had to physically look up the difference between Defense and Resistance, and I'm still torn about which is better or what to prioritize. Both help, but I'm finding defense better than resistance as far as fights go. You also won't be told that swords are faster than axes, but axes do more damage, and that spears are a bit of a combination of both. My only gripe is on the weapons. When you pick up a cool looking sword, it's soon replaced by the next tier weapon, forcing you to quickly forget about that cool looking sword you just found. You go through weapons and gear like water in this game. It seems like a missed opportunity with the Iron (I'm assuming it's Iron) that you find throughout the game. I was half-expecting the game to include upgrading your equipment to get better stats, but nope. So far, other than buying blueprints, and even that comes and goes quickly, I'm finding a hard time trying to figure out what to actually DO with Iron.Still, I love the story, I love the combat, I love the artwork, and I believe you will too.Just don't rush into it. It's a difficult game, but it's an extremely fun difficult game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour or two is good, then the game offers little but a ton of mandatory boring side quests that involve walking to the same areas for 5 minutes, killing 2-4 monsters, then walking back to pick up another uninteresting sidequest. It's a shame, because the game starts off really well with an interesting story, good narration, nice combat mechanics. But then that's all there is, the next 5 hours feel exactly like the first and not in a good way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: As beautiful as it is brutal- I'm only 4 hours in, and I was actually dreading that a) the combat would feel too simple and b) that the story and lore would slow down the action. Boy, was I wrong!! The combat is fiendishly hard, but with the save points being so frequent, it's forgiveable and so rewarding when you finally get to spray some frog blood! But I'm most surprised at how the lore and story works so well hand-in-hand with the combat. Graphics and audio are absolutely top notch, and having a respite walking through the villages before another onslaught is a lovely balance.That being said, I think I'm gonna restart the game and play on easy -something I never do- just because some of the later bosses are too much of a grind. But again in compliment to the game, I don't feel any beef about starting over because the worldbuilding is so rich.You can run the game on integrated intel graphics btw, you will just need to lower the resolution to something very low.

_childDocuments_.review: This is in many ways, an excellent game. It looks gorgeous, sounds good (narrated by Doug Cockle), and plays well.The combat is superb, with parries, blocks, and dodges turning the game far more strategic, even methodical in many places. Once you understand how a boss moves, you will engage with them in an elaborate dance, and it feels fantastic! Except for one thing: the total lack of i-frames. The game makes a point about some attacks requiring dodging, but since there are no i-frames, the timing (and direction) of these dodges becomes very strict, with sometimes bad luck being the only reason you get hit. In some ways this isn't necessarily a bad thing, as it forces you to think about not only the move the enemy is doing, but also your positioning on the battlefield. And when it works, it makes for amazing combat.It's also quite short, with ten hours getting me through the story with completing the majority of content available, while also not trying to beeline it. The locations in game are also quite small (but look absolutely amazing), meaning there isn't much to explore. Exploration is tied mainly to quest completion, meaning there really aren't any new interesting places for you to check once you've been through an area for the first time.Lastly, the story suffers from somewhat odd pacing, where in some situations you are expected to hurry, only to be redirected somewhere else to do sidequests just when you think things are heating up. This odd pacing lends itself to the game's sidequests as well. There are some locations in the game that you will spend a lot of time moving through, and some areas that you only visit once.I highly recommend the game, with the caveat that combat can feel very annoying in some situations. It's most certainly worth it to buy during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Man do I love this game! Only  a couple of things though. 1st thing is that dodge & roll don't actually make you invincible like in Dark Souls, which make the game quite unfair at times. You have to guess the hit boxes through trial & error in order to dodge successfully which makes the game a bit more frustrating than it needs to. 2nd thing is about defense vs. weight tradeoff. I find heavy build/ high defense so useless since you can't roll/ dodge effectively and that's 50% of how you survive in this game. And high defense build only gives you marginal difference in taken damage though. So it's more like an illusion of choice and in order to enjoy the game the 1st time you'd have to pick the most optimal build: either go full light gear or balanced & invest weight points in decent weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Not easy, but certainly not that hard and the fights are pretty easy to learn since it telegraphs what is coming via yellow/red symbols. I don't see the souls-like comparison really; it is kind of hard, but nothing respawns when you save, and there are no souls/XP to collect and lose. The art style is take it or leave it, but I really liked the pop-up story book feel of the whole thing.  The yellow blood/gore and dead bodies really contrasts the generally storybook look of the rest of the game. Overall a fun 2D kinda-souls-like game but there is really nothing new here. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could leave a Neutral Review honestly.I 100%ed the game in 7 hours which was pretty disappointing.It's not very difficult and you're forced to do most of the side quests as you progress through the main story, after beating the game there were two extra side quests added, however these were just fighting enemies I'd already fought throughout the game.That being said, the game is fun to play and is very pretty to look at, It's just not worth £20, I'd wait for a sale for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the best indie games of 2021.The art style is exceptional, the story is narrated by The Witcher's Geralt's voice actor and the combat is, at the same time, challenging and easy, after you master the enemies movement and the weapons and doge timing it is very satisfying, but knce you meet new enemies this loop of knowledge and mastery basically restarts. It is basically a Metroidvania-esque mixed with Dark Souls style of combat in a 2D style.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to like, like the art, and story and even the combat, which has its own kind of twist to it.For me personally, that twist took the fun out of comabat, at least for me. Some people describe it as souls like, but i feel it dictates your actions at any given moment with too little margin for creativity.I did't actually mind the combat after getting used to it, as it is a vital part of the game, and even if it's not my preferred style, it is incredibly well implemented.What actually made me stop playing/caring was the utterly unnecessary running back and forth to complete side quests, that needed completing to avoid farming. It felt like longer, but AT LEAST a third of the time playing was just running back and forth from the exact spot I was at back to some quest giver location. The running around parts are NOT fun. They are boring as can be, and annoying as well. By annoying I mean: Once you gain the ability to destroy an obstacle to reach a specific place, the obstacle is respawned the next time you get there, so you need to destroy it again, and again and again...This is fine, if you need to pass this obstacle once or twice, but due to the nature of the quests you will need to destroy the obstacle again and again, and its already annoying after the first time.All in all:OK game. Could be way more fun, if someone didn't try to strech the time needed to complete it, regardless if that time was actually fun.Note: According to Steam I spent about 8 hours in game (before writing this review), which is surprising, as I thought it must have been at least 12.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really frustrating to me. On one hand, the artstyle, the soundtrack, the narration, and the atmosphere are all really amazing, and to be honest, among the best of the genre. Most of the time the combat is really enjoyable, the new areas are exciting to see, the late game bosses have really fun movesets, etc. Except, the game is an unpolished mess. I was met with constant bugs. Over 16 hours, I had to forcefully quit and reload the game around 10 times from getting softlocked, and had to completely restart the game once to fix an audio issue. You can get stuck on the terrain, sometimes enemy attacks randomly don't show an indicator, multiple gameplay systems are never explained (the main offender being weight, with poison to a lesser degree), sitting at a bench doesn't heal you, the game kind of wants you to buy arrows and poison charges but you can just waste 3 minutes backtracking and get them for free at any point in the game, the only real collectables tend to be new gear but 95% of the time it's just objectively garbage compared to your current gear. And the backtracking is horrendous. Probably only about 50% of the content in the game is story relevant or unique, almost half of it in the direct middle of the game is backtracking doing tedious extermination missions for no real reward.I played on the hardest difficulty, and it was clearly not a focus making sure all the encounters are still fun and balanced on it. Especially with multiple enemies, you constantly get truly stunlocked from 100 to 0, stuck against a wall, etc. The vast majority of the solo boss fights have a satisfying amount of challenge, but many of the most difficult encounters are just a bunch of random enemies at once, and I doubt that was intentional. The game is good, really. There's just so much to complain about. All of the issues really nickel and dime the game down from being one of the best in the genre, to merely good with a bunch of caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positive things I have to say about the game, the presentation of the game is really good. I really ejoy this whole world of animal kingdoms. The graphics and the whole art direction is really good, the characters look very cute and the environnements are beautiful too.Now this is why this review isn't positive. The whole game basically only rely on it's combat system, it tries to be a "2d Soulslike" with a dodgeroll/guard/parry mechanics. But in my opinion it does a pretty  mediocre job. The combat doesn't feel good at all, you basically have attacks being color coded to know what action you have to do to evade that attack, wether it's a small dodge, a big dodge or a parry. I also felt like the dodge mechanic basically worked half of the time. I know it tries to be dark-soulsish but in dark souls as soon as you press the button your character rolles and is invincible for a small time. Here either the invulnerabilty frames are very wierd or the dodge has basically none. The movement feels very weird to, you character takes a little while before getting his running speed wich feels so weird and there are a lot of other small stuff that really doesn't feel good (like picking up items playing a slow animation every single item you pickup).You basically have to comlpete little missions to gather resources to rebuild your castle, wich basically mean the whole game is very tedious and has a lot of meaningless backtracking with no real upgrade or fast travel (at least for the 2hrs i've played).I can tell a lot of love has been put into this game, but I can't recommand it for all it's shortcomings. The devs are working on a sequel Tails of Iron 2: Whiskers of Winter, and i really hope they revamp the structure of the game and improve the combat system because I really love everything about the game's presentation and visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of an awkward learning curve for the combat system, but once you get the hang of it there's fun to be had.Most of the fun is in the storytelling (amazing pick on the narrator, guys) and the art and exploration. Not the most mind blowing amazing experience I've had, but I went in with lowered expectations and got more than I had assumed I was going to. Got it on sale for 10$ and am so far quite happy with my purchase.Edit: Beat the game. Rather short, unless I were to go 100% it to beat the final boss on the hardest difficulty. There's a large amount of back-tracking for both side and mandatory quests, but it was only a bit of a drag for a couple of them. There's also an optional boss you can beat a little early that gives a reward that ENTIRELY negates most every other weapon in the game, making many quest rewards later on completely pointless. Still, I fully recommend picking it up and trying it out. If you can get over the initial hurdle of learning the semi-awkward combat system, and temper your expectations, you're going to have a really good time. It's not Hollow Knight or Salt & Sanctuary, but that doesn't mean it isn't worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: is a 2D action-adventure with very light Metroidvania elements (1 item allowing to traverse a new area, and 3 health upgrades to find). The setting is low fantasy with anthropomorphic animals. The story follows a young vaguely-European rat king whose kingdom was invaded and father killed by vaguely-Afrikan frog raiders. The game is not an RPG by any measure - the story and the character development (health upgrades) are completely linear. There are no choices and no roleplay. The other critical issues are the narration - while the protagonist is as genocidal as an average action game main character, the narration brings attention to it (“he [the MC] would not be satisfied until every frog in his kingdom had croaked their last”), but not any reflection. The other “dialogues” are communicated via symbols above the speakers’ heads (e.g. an arrow, a thumbs-up), so the only spoken lines are from the narrator. It is possible to disable in the settings, but it is on by default.The pacing is slow - at every other main story point, it is necessary to complete 3 mandatory side quests to earn gold and purchase the next quest item, be it the materials for castle repairs or a piece of cake. Only one side quest (per board) can be active at the same time, which leads to 3 delves in the nearest dungeon and back to the board. Fast travel is possible, but limited to a few specific points. There are only 2 large areas, 1 final area, and 1 additional post-game area. In general, the post-game offers several actually optional side quests in different locations, with the Bright Forest ones having significantly less backtracking and all uncollected equipment becomes visible on the map. Finally, the combat encounters. On the Normal difficulty, everything is a hard-hitting damage sponge, with the game regularly locking the arena to one screen and the enemies walking in for about 20% from the border while being invulnerable. The combat itself sounds good enough in theory, but the quirks make it unsatisfying - there are blockable (indicated by white lines), parryable (yellow lightning), and dodgeable (red lines) attacks. Then there are no-dodgeable attacks (pink circles), with the enemy’s hitbox being far from their weapons or even bodies and the rolling i-frames being ignored. Some attacks, which are possible to block, do not have any indicators. Additionally, the enemies can stand on the same spot and visually block each other, so it becomes harder to tell when to act. On a positive note, the protagonist also can stand in enemies without contact damage, looting the insect type enemies refills the healing flask, which lore-wise is filled with bug bodily fluids, and the bosses’ movesets and appearances change as the battle progresses. The equipment is reasonably diverse - there are 1- and 2-handed melee weapons, several types of ranged weapons, and light, medium, and heavy armour, consisting of helmets and body armour. The issue is that within a type, the moveset is the same and the lightest item with the highest damage/protection is the best one. For the armour sets, the later light ones outperform the medium and heavy armour in terms of protection and weight. This is the only way to customise one’s build, with the ranged builds being less convenient due to the ammunition refilling mostly from the barrels next to some checkpoints. The NPC companions join and leave as the story dictates and it is not possible to choose them. They deal some damage and cannot die or be targeted. Some of them also provide soundtrack. The controls are as comfortable as they can be and rebindable, with 5-button mice supported. The game uses generously-placed checkpoints to save progress into one overwriting save slot (3 slots total), so if one wants multiple save states, using Windows Explorer is necessary. There are difficulty options and the difficulty cannot be changed after starting the game. The only bugs I have encountered are the odd hitboxes and one of the bosses had attack indictors covered by the arena architecture. Lastly, the visual design. It is delightful and reminds of old illustrated books. The locations change as the story progresses, most notably, the castle. The map is detailed and helpful, and matches the locations. Overall, while the game is visually appealing and does not outstay its welcome (I was able to finish it below 6 hours, including the post-game), with the lower difficulty and disabling the narration removing the more irritating issues, nothing can fix the poor pacing, the amount of filler content, and the complete linearity of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Took roughly 17 hours to beat the game but man what a fun ride! Beautiful art direction, beautiful sound design and music, I absolutely adored this world! Very well done, very fun, very entertaining. Whiles some of the fights felt very cheap at times, giving very little room for reaction even when you memorize what each boss ability does, it was still a good kind of challenging. Oh, and oh my gosh the audio and art style in this game are so amazing! I was not a big fan of the whistling noises to represent characters speaking, that was slightly grating, but everything else was truly amazing! The music was great and I still love Jay's little radio and the music it would play when running around with them. The world and theme were great, and it's the kind of world where I just wanted to explore and see more and more and more! Every setting was vibrant and beautiful, thematic music and sound design, interesting storytelling. Fantastic stuff!Would absolutely recommend if you are looking for a good Souls Like Side-Scrolling Platformer and can not way for Tails of Iron 2!Below this contain's spoilers so read more at your own discretion.I think the hardest fight I experienced was either Croakhis Khan or Double Trouble in the Mole Arena for me. They may not have been the most mechanically difficult fights but I think I had the most deaths to them and were some of the more annoying. Double Trouble would have been easier probably had I remembered to switch back to the Mole Arena armor instead of wearing my Frog defense armor still. Croakhis Khan on the other hand, until you get him off his mount, just was not fun in my opinion and even then this game really comes down to "Memorize the Fights and Patterns" and "Play Defensively". Once you learn the patterns and play on the defense you can easily take down most the bosses with only a few having just plain rough to counter moves.Game also has some really strange bugs that didn't ruin it per say but were unfortunate. Often times you would have to switch from 1h to 2h because something would bug out and you wouldn't be able to swing the currently drawn weapon. Graphical bugs like weapons being invisible or the poor Turtle when you get to the frog swamp only existing as a disembodied hand holding a pipe were minor (Probably should patch that one?) Had one bug where I was drinking when I died but revived stuck on a bench in the drinking animation and unable to get off so I had to quit and re-load the save. Just strange stuff.All in all though it's honestly a really charming and great game.I think the only major things I didn't like was the way equipment was handled. Often times I got a piece of armor that is like "Man, that would have been useful to have earlier and now I don't have a chance to make use of it..." like the extra mole armors I got well after fully finishing the Arenas in parts of the post game. I had no idea I would be getting other Mole Defense armors otherwise I would have held off on doing the Arena's until the other content was completed.Lots of stats had no real obvious information. For example, I still have no idea what weight does. Does it affect your dodge roll? I always went for a large amount of armor and enemy resist based on the scenario due to just how nasty some of the mechanics could be so I felt the only way to counter some of them was bulk up. Even then, it's not clear what defense and what resistances even do as there is no visible values like "Reduces Damage by X%" or anything to give an idea of the benefits of focusing general armor or focusing resistance values. A bit more transparency there would have been nice. Same with Weapons given the lack of damage numbers. I usually went for the spears because of their speed but there was no real way to tell if there was that much of a benefit to slower weapons like Axes/Maces over Spears.Some of the attacks also could have been telegraphed better. The training dummy at the start of the game does an AMAZING job at explaining the different attack prompts and what they mean, honestly really well done there! Block White, Parry Yellow, Roll away for red, double roll away for pink... until the line between pink and red becomes so skewed in the actual game that what was taught for those doesn't really matter and Pink and Red basically become "Well, you need to dodge but good luck figuring out what kind of dodge, which direction, etc. to do until after you have seen the animations and learned the fight a bit!" Some times its a simple straight forward attack, some times they rocket half way across the map, some times they home in on you, it's never clear until you have actually seen the moves. So the tutorial's explanation's of Red and Pink quickly become pointless and Red and Pink basically become the same thing, the boss is going to do something unblockable somewhere some way some how.Mind you all of this is super minor nitpicking on my part. Tails of Iron 2 looks even more crazy and fast paced from the trailer, curious to see what has changed in terms of the game feel based on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this Tails of Iron, but ultimately I cannot recommend it as a 2D souls-like. It's very cute and I was genuinely enjoying it until , but then the pacing really hits the breaks.You're tasked with performing underwhelming side quests that the game even lampshades with a line from the narrator, observing how normally kings send their subjects to run these errands. Questing is made all the worse by the baffling limitation of only being allowed to accept 1 at a time. You'll be running in circles between the same bounty board and dungeon until you have enough currency to progress the story. Shortcuts, a beloved feature of better souls-like games, are absent from Tails of Iron.The above wouldn't necessarily be bad if the gameplay loop was fun, but I grew to dislike combat after the admittedly strong beginning. You're frequently trapped in arenas, forced to clear an entire horde of damage sponge enemies (usually only 2 at a time) with your single-target attacks as they enter from both sides of the screen. This sometimes happens in places you've previously explored. Enemies are invincible until they've finished walking into the arena and some of their attacks have no telegraph. Even telegraphs can be so short that you might not have time to respond if you've already committed your own attack and have to wait to recover. Also, dodging doesn't have i frames that I could notice; instead, its purpose is to preemptively flee incoming damage zones.I'm not thrilled about leaving this negative review, but I can't help but think how much better Tails of Iron would be if it were a 2.5D hack-n-slash/beat-em-up, fully embracing linear levels, fast pacing, and interesting set-pieces to stop and fight in. Instead, we're left with a fundamentally flawed 2D metroidvania that feels almost ashamed of being a souls-like. I truly wish Odd Bug Studio luck going forward, but this game has soured me, so I'm taking my leave from this series.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game by a quite small studio. Tails of Iron definetly shines in environment and character design. It absolutely kills the pacing and makes you not want to play the game in certain sections.Another issue I have is coming in towards the end. The frogs have been established as "vicious tribals" which is quite problematic in of itself but towards the end you see frog farmers just going about their business and even Regi (The MC) says that the frog field seem just like home. You expect there to be a "we misunderstood them" or an "they were misled by their power hungry leader" moment but that just never comes.  Like, please pick a lane devs. I'm not gonna hold that against them too much, not even AAA games get that right (looking at you Jedi: Fallen Order)But all in all, can recommend at a discount. I think 20€ is a fair price for the game, 25€ is a little much.
