_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. The aesthetics are charming and so is the narration/story, but as a souls-like, I cannot recommend the game to be played on anything other then the Story difficulty as it's worth experiencing for a few dollars on a great sale. As far as Souls-like go though, I'd probably look elsewhere to be honest. I'm fueled off spite, and so I'm determined to finish the game and try and get my money worth which reflects my playtime (along with a healthy dose of afk time too) at the time of writing this review, but I'd probably steer clear. -The enemies have very inconsistent hitboxes with their attacks which feel improperly classified and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from a player's experience (which becomes more noticeable as you further progress and start reaching mid-late game bosses/enemies). The game lays out for the player the following expected indications of attack from enemies "Block (no indicator), Parry (yellow), Unblockable (red), or Double-Dodge Roll to Evade (red circle)".  As you'll often find in the later stages of the game, a lot of Unblockable (red) attacks get the properties of huge AoE Double-Dodge Roll (red circle) attacks which makes fighting a mid-late stage boss less a match-up of skill and rewarding the player for learning the mechanics of the game.... but rather a situation of beefing through attacks with overly-tuned Armor a frustrating endeavor when the game cannot adhere to it's own laid out formula, and you're getting punished for making the right decision based of the enemy attack indicator just for it to have additional properties associated to it. Throw on top of this frustration the lack of invulnerability-frames associated with the character's dodge-roll and some of these boss fights can be downright cringe-worthy and painful to slog-through, especially when unblockable attacks seem to be the go-to method for enemies/bosses to spam. I'm normally able to stomach a one-sided ass-whooping until I get down the boss's attack patterns/moveset, and I'm able to persevere, but some of the boss fights in this game just weren't it Chief. -The gear "upgrades" you get along the way feel inconsistently scattered across the game along with too much meaningless bloat of poorly paced gear replacements, with a lot of the more powerful weapons/armors being obtained early-mid/mid game which makes the slew of gear obtained later on feel meaningless and gives off the illusion of choice. But since the gear is very simple with no special effects/enhancements, it gives the player no reason to experiment with worse obtained gear as it'll perform worse then your current set of equipment albeit look different, so maybe it's fine if you're playing on Story difficulty and hunting for looks instead? In conclusion:If I could, I'd give this game more of a mixed review then a hard "no". It can have its moments of fun, and if you're able to pick it up for $3 USD like I did and none of the above pain points scare you off, you can expect an "okay" amount of fun to be had. Hope the review helps

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game. Gameplay is a combination of Redwall and Hollow Knight, art is Redwall and Darkest Dungeon, music slaps (though I wish there was more in the boss battles, as they can get weirdly silent compared to just walking through the village), sound design and the way of doing narration vs dialogue is clever and cute, all in all I have loved this game. I wish it was longer (with my first playthrough on the normal difficulty taking around 15 hours, though I know I've missed some things and there's apparently some DLC bosses I haven't found), with enough variability in play styles that I know I'll do another play through at some point. If Hollow Knight was a bit too vague about where to go and what to do, you're not great at keeping track of places to go back to later in traditional Metroidvania style games, then this is a good spot for you. There's enough exploration to be fun and interesting, with rewards that make it feel worth your time, but you're not going to get madly lost and have no clue where to go. Overall, rate it 8.5/10, thoroughly enjoyed my time, with very minor gripes that are really more wishlist items rather than negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: ------------------------------------------Tails Of Iron is a diamond in the rough. There a number of good things here but it is hampered by more than a few issues that prevent it from being a truly great game. The art and graphics of this game is it’s standout. The story is good but has bad pacing. The music is good but sparse. The combat is interesting but is mired with control issues. And the controls here is frankly speaking, not good – not bad, but not good either. If you can live with control and movement issues, there is certainly much enjoyment to find here. Tails Of Iron has a potential to be a cult classic – not good enough to be mainstream, but good enough to have gain key core fans over time. I look forward to seeing a sequel from Odd Bug Studio and improving from a certainly good foundation they’ve established here. Partial Recommendation. ------------------------------------------ The setting and the style reminds me of the brother’s Grimm fairy tales, and not the Disney kind, I mean the old-school 18th century German kind that has horror, blood and gore. The background is busy with parallax scrolling and  animation which adds to the atmosphere of the game.------------------------------------------ You play as Redgi, the newly crown king of the rats who has to save his ratfolk from an invading frog army. As cute as this sounds (and it does sound cute) the story gets dark very quick. War after all is pretty ugly and death comes often in this game but each character's death feel significant despite them having no dialogue or in-depth backstory.  The middle part is quite removed from the main plot, effectively being a collection of side-quests that do not add very much to Redgi’s arc. They're not bad, just not very good. It would’ve been better if side-quests somehow tie-in with the 3rd and final act and in any case, this is something that Odd Bug Studio could improve on in the future.  There are parts of the game where there’s only ambient environmental sounds rather than an actual background music. Some times this is warranted for atmosphere, but too often I find myself thinking that certain stages could’ve use more music. Shoutout to the sick Hard Bass track in Mole kingdom. ------------------------------------------In any side-scrolling action game, the most important aspects to nail down without exception are the movement and control, and  There is a drag and floatiness to Redgi’s movement. It is more noticeable during combat, where even if you equip Redgi with the lightest of gear, his attacks and movement are still sluggish compared to the enemies specifically bosses.  You can only jump, run/walk and dodge. And you can’t even do a jump attack.  seems wasted to me. Combat even though interesting, isn’t executed quite as well as I’d hoped.  While the combat move-set is slightly more robust than his regular movement, there’s only a limited number of things that you can accomplished with them, leaving no room for player creativity. The sluggishness in controls also compound an already stifling combat. For example, dodge doesn’t actually dodge, let me explain. Any dodge should have invincibility frames included throughout the entirety of the animation so that you can effectively escape from taking a hit. Dodge in Tails Of Iron works differently, where the invincibility frame is not applied through the entire dodge animation.  You can and you still have to use dodge (because it’s an integral part of combat) but timing your dodge now becomes even more difficult since the timing window to dodge is effectively cut by half.  Once you press an attack, you have to wait until the attack animation is finish before you’re able to input the next move, and yes, even when equipping light gear with little weight. This gets really frustrating especially when  While your enemies and bosses attacks and movement are quick and instantaneous, as if they operate on different physics engine. Even with color-coded icons telegraphing enemies’ attacks, there is barely enough time for you react to them given the unresponsive controls and sluggish animation, making the combat feels crippling and unrewarding.  Attack isn’t on X or Y (on Xbox Controller), rather they are bound to RB and RT. Why? And why can’t I have the option to rebind the keys? Having attack bound to RB and RT is just weird and simply shouldn’t exist on a 2D side-scrolling action game. ------------------------------------------Despite the issues, the game skirts by well enough for it to be mostly enjoyable. I am optimistic for an improved sequel from Odd Bug Studio. Partial recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is different from others in the genre but that's a welcome change.  It is very much a linear adventure compared to the Metroidvania style found in Hollow Knight or the Ori series. The gameplay is also unique in that it's very chunky as opposed to being quick and nimble - even with a light build.  Combine all this with the adorable story and you get a really fun game experience.  It's best to remember that this is an indie title so it can feel lacking in some areas but that's expected from a smaller studio.My only real complaint is forced side missions which is unfortunately something we're seeing in more and more games these days.  This is when the main story abruptly stops to quite literally force you to go do redundant and inconsequential side missions before you can progress. It's done as a way to stretch the main story playtime and it's a trend that really needs to die.  Beyond that, this is definitely worth a playthrough.  Fun story with challenging gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing first, this is not a terrible game, it has good things going for it like the very nice and climatic art style, Geralt doing a comfy narration, and overall a fine story if a bit bland at times.However, as much as I would want to like and recommend it, I can't because the most important thing which is gameplay is just off.It starts fine, but the more you play it the more you can see the cracks coming out. The hitboxes on some of enemies attacks are atrocious, the dodge is very poor and the fact that most places were you fight are extremely small makes it even worse to use.As for parry, while the window for it is quite big, parriable attacks are the least common attacks and often they throw enemy so far away that you'd be lucky to get a single hit in after it.Weapons don't really feel all that distinct, which is a shame as you only have three categories (swords, axes, and spears, for both one-handed and two-handed), and so basically you'll just use whatever has best stats at the moment.Armors overall look good, but the idea of them giving resistance against enemy type (not type of damage, but just the type of enemy) is a bit weird but not really damaging to the game when compared to the other flaws.But even besides all that, there are two things that gameplay wise are just sinful. For one, there is no invulnerability period when you're hit or knocked down, which means that you can get hit by two, three, or even four attacks in the row and you wouldn't be able to do anything about it.In some cases it means going from full health too almost dead or fully dead, and this gets worse the further you progress through the game as they throw more numerous groups more often.The second thing is the grey tint that happens when you're low on life. It supposed to be climatic and all that, but in the game with colored signals regarding what kind of attack is coming this is just absurd - especially since it happens when you're close to dying and every hit counts.To sum it up, the game has problems when it comes to gameplay, for me it was more annoying than fun. I would recommend it only for people that really like the art style and are not to much bothered by the subpar mechanics.Also get it on sale because it's rather short for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a fun little 2D souls like RPG adventure game. You are Redgi, prince and heir to the throne of the Rat Kingdom. Your kingdom is invaded by the evil Frog Clans and your father, The King is killed. Embark on a quest to reclaim your Kingdom, defeat the champions of the Frog Clan and banish them from your lands.Pros- Charming colourful 2D art and good music.- Difficult but rewarding combat with lots of weapons to suit your playstyle.- Decent length campaign (10-12 hours at least if you don't get stuck on any particular boss).- Narrated by Doug Cockle (the voice of Geralt of Rivia from the Witcher games).Cons- Honestly nothing I can think of.A very enjoyable little game that I streamed all the way through over a weekend soon after the game's release. It has a very fun feel to it and made by a small team of passionate devs who even dropped by during my streams.Lots of little easter eggs thrown in as well. If you like fun indie games with challenging but fair combat give this a try when you see it on sale next time.Here is a video I compiled of all the named bosses in the game (in case you get stuck on any particular one) :

_childDocuments_.review: I could tell you about how much I love this game, but instead I'm going to tell you what I know about it's journey.Matt White was a simple gamer, just like us. He liked Super Metroid, he liked Dark Souls, he even liked fighting games. It had been years since Nintendo had touched the Metroid franchise. So, he thought to himself, why don't I make one?It was 2012. Matt had already been toying around with Flash sidescrollers. Having fun dipping his toes into making stuff, just for fun. Matt was also an excellent artist already; he drew comic book art, in a style similar to those old 80s sci-fi anime's. He didn't really know anything about programming, but after conversations with a mutual, they agreed to partner up and try to make something special. Try and make a Metroid-like that was somber, yet lively, and hauntingly beautiful.So a Kickstarter was made. Matt didn't really know anything about making games. Few people outside of the industry really talked about it back then. They did some math, guessed about how long it would take them, and a goal was set - mere $15,000. A measly amount compared to even most indie games of today. It seemed like enough back then. And the Kickstarter was a rousing success, funding waaay above goal. Not quite enough to reach the oft-joked about Wii U stretch, but a windfall nonetheless. The money was divided evenly between the two bright-eyed and idea-filled partners. This was it. It was time to hunker down and get started.But then the programmer's work started to slow. He would miss calls, skip out on meetings. He stopped returning messages. Slowly, he himself became a ghost of the project. He had taken the money, but wasn't producing the work. There was so much to do! But only Matt remained. And only Matt would continue the project.Stencyl is a good engine to work with visually, especially if you are new to making games. Although shaken by the silent departure of his once-partner, he soldiered on; dutifully creating all the artwork, pulling from sound libraries and implementing his ideas into the game engine. It was rough going, for a single man. But it was going. And that was all that mattered, with the weight of the fully funded Kickstarter behind him, and the growing coverage of his dark, yet vibrant take on the (for the time) neglected genre.However, Stencyl just couldn't keep up with Matt. Fixing bugs was a struggle for this new developer. And the more content and artwork and ideas he shoveled into the engine, the longer and longer it would take to compile, sometimes up to 45 minutes for each change! Instead of smoothly moving forward, working on the game was becoming frustrating. This couldn't go on. A change had to be made.So Matt makes the tough decision to switch engines, communicating this to all the Kickstarter backers. It is an understandable, if regrettable choice. The game was already at least halfway done! But it was also necessary. The engine was pushed as far as it could go, and Matt, burning the candle at both ends to make his dream a reality, had no choice but to start over.The next years are spent learning to code. Unity has plugins to work visually, like Stencyl. But so much MORE could be done by directly coding it. Ideas exploded forth. The animations could now be expanded upon. Even more options for including melee and different weapons were now a possibility. Matt hadn't stopped playing other games during these years, and they all helped to shape and grow this new vision of Ghost Song.A vision I hope you will enjoy in its completion as much as I have.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing!Reminds me so much of Mouseguard or the Chronicles of Redwall... I simply love the concept!The art-style is gorgeous (hand-drawn but the animations flow very naturally and not at all "stick-figure-y", if you get what I mean?) and everything looks like it jumped right out of a fable book.The gameplay is very solid too! Movement feels fluid already 5 minutes in and combat can be hectic and... well, sometimes pretty hard too, to be honest, but never really unfair. One time you're rolling and jumping all over the battlefield like a one-man-army and the other you decided on tanking with higher defense and clever shield-play and just steamrolling everything that stand before you, calmly and methodically. 100%-ed normal mode and just restarted in hard mode, might say that combat is even better (feels like the stakes are higher). Difficult? At times, sure. Never exasperating or discouraging though.Weaponry is not very varied outside of the 3 weapon types for every category, but it never feels too little. There are indeed lots of different weapons per se, but other than a couple outliers (one very, VERY powerful as well... you'll see :D ) it's mostly reskins of the same weapon types with the same animations but different stats - still pretty cool, nothing missing there.There's also a plethora of references to history, other franchises and general nerd-culture: found myself chuckling quite a bunch of times after seeing names of enemies or locations - or even recognizing parallels in certain situations.The "instrumental" voices and the comic-like speech bubbles are adorable, of course, but what about the narrator? None other than DOUG COCKLE... THAT'S GERALT OF RIVIA, YA'LL! Dayum, stellar casting! Makes the whole story that much more epic and enjoyable - at times witty, but still always heroic and grand.Not much more to add, other than: play it.Odd Bug Studio, chapeau to you. You made an amazing game and a folk tale for the ages.Can't wait for other chronicles from the Tails of Iron world.......... I guess I'm a fan now.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know who is classifying this as a souls like but they must be smoking something. Don't go into this game expecting one at all.Even without that expectation, the combat falls flat and other decisions are confusing. There's very little impact from your weapon and enemies seem unnecessarily damage spongey on normal difficulty. You can have either or but both makes the combat feeling more flat imo. With how damage spongey the enemies are, you'd want to focus on one rather than spreading your damage but it's almost impossible when the enemies are the same appearance. The devs have "frog blood" which may be able to help you tell which one has lower health but the blood is green on a green frog body, making it useless. It's much easier to lose track of the enemy you are trying to single out in 2d than 3d. The block/parry is pretty great but the dodging in this game feels like absolute rubbish. This is an excruciating problem when there are two different types of attacks that must be dodged, red and red circle. The bosses typically do unblockable attacks and must be dodged. The combination of the separate red and red circle, boss mostly doing these, and dodging feeling rubbish makes the conbat feel awful.And then you have the save system, copying hollow knight's benches but terribly. You enter a room with something dreadful happening in eyeshot but there's a bench right before that. That makes the best gameplan to sit at the bench and get off to deal with the dreadful thing happening to a person that sees you just sit on a bench for a second. Don't think there's an autosave, not when going past a bench. You have to sit which is such a waste of time. Healing and enemies also don't respawn so there are times when you need to backtrack to a healing station to refill. For some reason you can't exit to another area at the start without getting a carpenter to create a "fast travel" billboard. Which in universe seems like just a map. The wagon to take you to a named location that the driver would be familiar with couldn't have driven you to that said location without the billboard obviously. LIGHT SPOILERS but there are side quests from citizens of your destroyed and ransacked kingdom for a cash reward. Feels super game-y and out of place for the situation everyone is in currently. They got the Geralt of Rivia to be the narrator for this game as well which is awesome. But then the "dialogue" between the mice is so awful and confusing. The mice just make noises but it sounds so shrill and is painful to listen to. The accompanying graphics are also not the most clear on what they are conveying. What is said is clarified by the narrator which is good but having that "dialogue" is just awful and useless then.These weird decisions aren't a huge deal since you're here for the combat but the combat, imo, sucks. The weird decisions just feel like examples on the devs not putting enough thought into the game (namely combat) as necessary or its just things that annoyed me further when the combat wasn't cutting it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I would thoroughly recommend Tails of Iron. It's a very simple, but excellently executed game. The premise is simple too. You play Redgi, whose world is turned upside down right from the start. Redgi is tasked with reclaiming his inheritance, clearing his lands of the threats that besiege it and becoming the hero of the hour. There's nothing new here, but the way it's done is what matters. There's a theme to the game, simple but rich in detail and immersion.The art and animation style is fresh and different from anything else I've experienced. Sure, there are similarities with some other titles out there that have a comic book style, but this game has cohesion that immerses you in the charming world the developers have created. The ambient sounds, the voice acting by Doug Cockle, the iconic voice of Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher games and the music all add to the sense that you're a part of Redgi's kingdom. There's a lovely touch later in the game where you encounter some dangerous animals out for blood and I swear they call Redgi's name in a guttural death rattle as you disturb them on your quest.Completing tasks and quests is what drives you forward in the game, always leading you into combat. That combat system is what gels the game's visuals, sounds and brilliant narration together. The developers could have wedged in a lazy, button mashing combat system here but they didn't and that in my eyes is what makes this game interesting, just long enough to complete it without petering out. The combat requires some thought and learning from the inevitable mistakes you'll make. There are times you have to figure out a pattern to the combat before you can win. Choosing the right equipment for the fight is important too. So what, you might ask? Well, you can't just rock up to any fight and blindly click the attack button to win. In my opinion, that kind of carelessness has made many games boring and ultimately unplayable for me. Not in Tails of Iron though. You have to plan a little and 'git gud' before you can progress. Some younger or impatient players may find this difficulty a step too far though and I didn't notice a difficulty setting, which may have been helpful for progression if the combat is proving too steep a challenge. There are however, handy save points throughout the game, which reduces the grind quite nicely, so before any challenging fight, you don't have to beat through several other combat's before you're back at the hard part.Overall, there's just enough of everything in this game, they never over do it or make you stay beyond your welcome. Combat in interesting and challenging, but rarely a grind. The world is beautiful, charming and gritty and changes in front of your eyes as you progress through the story. The sounds and music pull you in and immerse you. To give an idea of value for money, I completed the main quest line in about 11 hours and achieved 100% in about 14 hours. I did spend too long looking for one item that I missed during play, so that's one small gripe I had. Check the poison zones once you unlock them! Ultimately it didn't matter too much. I loved every minute of this game and some time wasted on searching for one item wasn't too much of a chore. So there we have it, I hope this is useful if you're considering buying Tails of Iron. Go for it, it's great fun.Well done Odd Bug Studio. I hope there's more from Redgi's kingdom in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is an action RPG that borrows elements from the Souls genre. The gear system might feel familiar to you if you've played Souls games before. There are a few different weapon and armor types. Depending on what you equip, your damage output will change, but weight is also something you need to consider, as the bigger the load you carry, the slower your dodges will be.In this game, you've got light weapons on your primary attack button. These are usually a bit more swift, and can be charged up if you hold the button down.On your secondary attack button, you carry your two-handed weapons. Usually a bit heavier. Throughout combat, you can alternate attacks seamlessly between the two. On top of that, you have a ranged weapon that can be fired at enemies.As for defence, you've got a shield, that can additionally parry if you time it right, as well as a short evade, and a dodge roll for further distance coverage.I found the combat to be exhilarating. You are very often caught in between two enemies. You'll have to shield arrows flying at you from one side, while you fend off enemies on the other.Enemies also all have special attacks, that are either undodgeable or unblockable. Depending on the warning above them, you will have to use the corresponding defensive manouver. I loved the combat system, as I always felt like I had to be alert, and aggressive. It is quite unforgiving, and you can die quite quickly, but I never found the game to be that daunting.Similarly to Dark Souls, you can heal combat damage by drinking from your flask. However, in this case, it heals gradually as you hold the button. I think this is a lot more of an interesting and tense way to do it.To save at a checkpoint, you sit down to rest at certain benches. These do not replenish your flask. You will have to look for specific tankards for that. As for the story, the frogs have invaded your rat kingdom. You must take it back. Although simple, the story is quite compelling. You actually do end up caring for NPCs that you meet briefly throughout the game, despite the fact that there's no voice acting. Instead, they squeek and grunt with speech bubbles to get the point across. It's effective, and keeps the appropriate tone of the game. The game's overarching story is narrated. By Geralt of Rivia, in fact. It startled me at first, but I felt his voice was perfect for it. Every now and again, he will comment on what your character's next goal might be, or what they are thinking. It isn't constant commentary.I really enjoy the world the game is set in, and it manages to always feel alive. Characters come and sweep rubbel from areas you've already cleared, and you can see enemies patrolling in the background. There's so much nice attention to detail.The aesthetic speaks for itself, and I personally love the art style. It reminds me of Darkest Dungeon, but not as terrifying. More along the lines of a dark fairytale book. This accompanied with the beautiful lighting effects and parallax, it's just a joy to look at.To conclude, I am in love with the game. It feels so great and everything about it feels thought out and polished. The only real complaint I have, is that at a certain point, the game has you run back and forth between the same areas doing similar quests. It gets a bit tedious, but overcomes that after a while. Most of the game is refreshing. Overall, I highly recommend it! I think it's my favourite game I've played this year!

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, short, casual adventure game that delivers a short story about a rat prince restoring his kingdom by personally exterminating all of its enemies all by himself.The art and enviroments look great, sound design is pretty alright.The game is incredibly short however and there are surprisingly few areas to explore, they try to extend the gameplay by adding "side quests" (in a million quotation marks) which are actually mandatory that require you to backtrack to certain areas several times, you are also encouraged to revisit every area after every progression in the main quest (sometimes this is as insiduous as one of the traders suddenly having one extra blueprint for sale, I have no idea why this is).There is tons of weapons and armors to collect, but there is no reason to use 90% of them? A lot that you come across minutes later is objectively better than the previous thing you were using, you also collect bug shells and iron as currency? But you don't really spend it on anything so you cap out at 99/99 really quickly. Not sure if they meant for the game to be longer or if they added this stuff because other similar games have it. Pretty strange.While the game isn't hard per se, the combat is absolute dogshyte garbage with certain enemy prompts either blatantly lying to you or being weirdly deceptive, especially for the larger bosses. The hitbox for some of the enemy attacks, again, especially for large bosses, is incredibly hit and miss sometimes resulting in these sometimes incredibly frustrating and cheap hits and deaths. A big chunk of attacks are also badly telegraphed, not in the sense that you don't see that the boss is about to do an attack, but rather where the attack will land. So you get these situations where you are given say, a red circle signal (signifying an area of effect attack that cannot be dodged or blocked), making you stay clear of the boss, only for the boss to then do some steroid and cocaine induced olympic quadruple summersault launch across the entire room - but only sometimes - sometimes the same attack doesn't do this at all. I wish I could name one boss or enemy that I enjoyed but if I'm gonna be completely honest here all the trash mob enemies along the way were a chore and the bosses were all varying degrees of violently brutally unfun and annoying.The hardest boss in the entire game (for me) was actually just the tag team in the arena, one guy with a spear and one big guy with a shield, the spear guy is all over the place and the shield guy has a heavy hitting shield bash that you have ½ seconds to react to and dodge, also they both frequently attack at the same time or just slightly out of synch, leading to you getting wombo combo'd to death. Bosses that dodge attacks or that jump from one end of the arena to the other are also just terrible. I get that its a 2d game so there is really only so much you can do while trying to vary bosses, but damn is it ♥♥♥♥♥.Bunch of people say the combat n such is good or okay though, so I don't know, maybe it's just not for me.Anyway this being said I liked it, mostly, but wish it was longer.25 bucks for what amounts to a 7-12 hour one time experience (there isn't really replayability here) that you can finish in one or two sittings seems kinda steep to me, so maybe get it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining game. The playtime is a bit short I beat it in seven hours and eight minutes at 100%. And the near end of it finishing the side quests felt like they were just tacked on instead of having an interesting boss fight. Don't get me wrong, there are two really entertaining extra bosses, but one of them gives an item that basically ruins the need to ever use another weapon in its slot ever again. Another draw back is that while the game has a very wide variety of arms and armor, the majority of it is useless besides the looks it gives. The items in the game have resists to them, but they didn't feel like they effected anything at all. Including what you'd expect with general defense. Most enemies when you have maximum health upgrades will kill you in four hits regardless.There's also a very huge jump in difficulty around the time you go to the mines. Everything up until that point felt fair, if you screwed up. You pay for it hard. But once you reach that point the enemies are, so erratic and have such quick reactions needed to not get you Sh*t slapped it feels a bit much way too quickly. Especially near the very end. The last boss, while fittingly difficult was downright infuriating with how small of reaction time you have to have to dodge or parry his attack.Another problem is that the enemies themselves, especially the larger enemies and especially boss monsters feel like their hitbox is twice the radius of what you expect. Many times I would dodge three feet behind them and still get hit, other times I'd f*ck up and swing my weapon and they'd glide right passed me.Finally the story. I was all for it, until you got to a certain point in the game and then suddenly you're introduced to this new faction in the game that is extremely out of place. I believe its a nod to a certain book or a mixture of a book and a completely different movie. As well I believe the developers are Slavs, which is fine it's just it might be a cultural thing I'm not understanding. It's just that such a tonal shift is very jarring where it just feels like it comes out of left field. The quests there are entertaining and the atmosphere is very nice, but it feels like you stepped out of this game and into another game entirely for a moment. As well you get a certain weapon that makes the non-damage sponge enemies almost trivial. Now, the ending is very disappointing. The last boss is very difficult compared to the rest of the game and it gives you all sorts of new armors and weapons, that while useless compared to the others you will have gotten if you were exploring, are neat looking. The problem is that it feels like it wants to continue from there and either the budget ran out or the developers wanted to work on a different game. For what is here though, it's fine, it's fun, and it's difficult when it wants to be. I hope you folks add some DLC or a sequel to continue the story. TL:DRPros:Good game playLooks very goodAtmosphere is amazingThe puns, oh god the punsDifficultCons:Most of the arms and armor is completely useless. It's busy work for skins.The hit detection; Hit boxes of larger enemies are all over the placeStory is short and ends on a semi-cliffhanger with how the narrator ends it.Jarring tonal shift about half way through the game

_childDocuments_.review: I've missed you, Geralt :')But on a more serious note, initial impressions are fantastic! _childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out, this games art work is truly amazing.  But what sets it apart from most games (at least for me) is its simple story and gameplay.  Unlike most other games where the minions you fight are basically cannon fodder and easily dispatched, the frog enemies in Tails of Iron are/ can be formidable.  But as long as you keep your wits about you and properly attack, block and parry at the right moments, you will be victorious. _childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun action RPG. Gorgeous visuals, wonderful music. The world has a great mix of darkness and charm that is done really well. Combat is very tight - fast paced and not extremely punishing. The game gives you adequate feedback to know how and why you took a hit. Frequent save points so even if you do die, you can get right back into the game without any tedious backtracking or exp-collecting mechancis that are just in games for the sake of "darksouls did it so now i have to".The game doesn't over extend itself, and in my time so far, it maintains its high quality of visual style and game design - it is consistent and fun. I feel like it would be really easy for a game like this to have unimportant gameplay mechanics that dilute the overall experience, but it has a laser focus on the core gameplay, and the small diversions the game offers are solely to push the story and atmosphere along.Very cool rats, love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. 10/10. It's tough as nails, but I never once felt like I died for a "that's not what I told it to do" reason: I knew the mistake I had made and did better next time. The save points are a fair frequency, and thoughtfully/mercifully placed right before bosses.I went through on KB + mouse, but my xbox controller worked fine. I'd normally go with a controller on a side-scroller like this but it just felt off in this case strangely enough. Not being able to remap controller buttons didn't help (you CAN now remap kb + mouse controls).I went through with light armor + spears and enjoyed that a lot. Heavier armor (with higher defense stat) reduces damage in a big way, but I preferred being nimbler. I can't put my finger on exactly what carrying higher weight actually does, but there's definitely a difference that made me prefer going the lighter route. I read a dev comment that higher weight slows down your dodgeroll but I'd have never pinned that down from gameplay, the effect is very subtle in my experience. Subjectively, weight really seems to slow down attack animations but I can't be sure.I think the story did a GREAT job of driving forward the action, and you even get a chance to keep playing after completing the main story which was a nice touch if you forgot something.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, there are several things that added together made this game one of my favorites and the first game I have 100%'ed (technically as of writing this there are three hidden achievements but they will not be achievable until the next update which I am waiting eagerly for.) Firstly there is the combat, the combat is solid and as to be expected for this type of game it has the basics of dodge, roll, and parry all of them seem to connect well with the enemy models and there has only been a rare occasion where an enemies (or my own) attack would connect when it shouldn't, which for an indie developer team like this is really great to see. Then there is the art direction, the medieval feel is captured beautifully and they are really able to capture these dark tones and moments that completely suck you into the setting along with the background actually feeling alive and not just some static shot. After that is the story, its solid for what it is a simple story of a newly crowned king trying to fix his kingdom and defeat his enemies that caused this. All of this wrapped up into one game forms something that I have honestly not seen from many Triple A developers in a while, but I mean hey if the game is completed then its already further along then most triple A companies now, and all of them make up for a game worth its price, but the last thing that just added the perfect bow onto this already incredible present is the music and sound design. Both of these not only supplied the feeling of impact from each swing that connected from both the enemies and my own swings but also added perfectly to the setting with the choices of music, where while your inside your kingdom  you'll hear a bard (or Thee Bard) playing a song or when you are facing off against the Toads you'll hear more percussion or tribal sounding music and you'll even have a small character in the background at times justifying the music by being either the bard with the strings or the little drummer boy for the bosses.TL:DR Great game a ton of things were done right and the game is well worth the price it is sold for, I am very excited to see what comes next from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. Art is great, characters are neat, mechanics are simple. BUT:Battles are just bad and give no joy. Hitboxes of enemies attacks are unpredictable. Fights with more then one opponent and helping NPC are a mess. Everybody moves in the same 2D plane and CPU always attacks player. Often you'll be attacked from outside your field of view. Player attacks never do stagger (except when parrying) or even won't break enemy attacks. Reggie moves slow as turtle, and because of this often there is no way to run/roll away from unblockable enemy attacks.  Enemies are flying and jumping all over the scene and you cant even attack them! Range weapons are weak and don't stagger enemies too. Poison seems to be a placebo rather then doing anything. And worst thing for me - you cannot redefine gamepad controls. WHY? Generally game worthy of buying and playing, but becuse of its length, fights are done in very frustrating way.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit mixed on this one. On one hand, I love the artstyle, the story, the naration. It's just very.. redwall. I don't mind the repeating quests and the backtracking. The main problem here is the combat system. I've played a lot of souls games. When you get killed, it's usually "fair". Here that's not quite the case:* The knockback attacks can be very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. No windup, they knock you back, and then hit you multiple times when you're down. You need to know when a boss can do knockback, and avoid those situations entirely. The final bosses second phase is especially ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in phase 2.* The hitboxes can be quite inconsistent* Some attacks are just very hard/impossible to block if you're badly positioned* The lack of i-framing does hurt hereTo beat some bosses, you have to "play" their AI. Invite certain attacks, position yourself so other attack types are rarer. This is just.. tedious. This might be coloured by me playing on the highest difficulty. Everything is beatable, sometimes it just takes a long time. I suspect higher difficulty levels just magnify the issues the combat system has.The game is fun. The expansion bosses feel fairer. _childDocuments_.review: I'll try to keep this short.  I didn't find the combat to be "brutally punishing" so much as just not impossible to lose at. I suppose if you aren't somewhat used to games that require timing, patience and a bit of grit to overcome, this game will seem quite hard, but for everyone who's played games that let you fail, this should feel comfortable enough. It isn't incredibly deep, though, and both lenient in some ways (while you are shown how to redirect your shield while it's up, for instance, you will automatically block and parry attacks from any direction if the button input is there, and parrying isn't very tight for a soulslike), and unfair in others (regis sometimes seemingly doesn't grab ledges, and iframes, while there, aren't generous).  It's also rather short. I spent about 10 hours playing, and have completed everything except for the last hidden boss and the final arena round, both of which are post-game activities (and are a fair bit harder than everything that precedes it). What's there, though, is wonderfully executed. Pacing, showing the player the ropes, the world-building, sound, music and voice acting (mainly being that of geralt of rivia's VA), art direction and story all culminate in an engaging and simply GOOD game. It's a bit linear, in that sidequests aren't usually optional and there isn't much to discover once you've cleared an area, but I finished the game feeling very satisfied. The setup of quite cute woodland critters brutally slaying each other is very emotive, and reminds me a lot of watership down, albeit with much lighter themes.I dearly would've liked to have explored more of the world, but that's my only real qualm here; the game's short lifespan.I hear many people lauding it as GOTY contender, but as much as I'd grant the makers their accolades, it is simply too short to qualify imho.  Still, this is a game and studio worthy of your time, attention, and, insofar as this kind of game appeals to you, your money. Yes, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: So, following Redgi through medieveal rat kingdom. With Ratatouille as his brother cooking up fancy dishes. The artstyle was on point that was the first thing I noticed, and the visual storytelling allows anyone to pick it up and play through it independent of language barriers. There is a narrator which helps progress the story, but to progress and finish what the narrator says would be completely optional. This game was a blast. Simple to learn, mediocre to master. There were definitely some good boss fights, and combat segments in the game. Some that had me retrying more than I'd like to, after dying before getting in my finishing blows. The RPG Elements felt nice. I  played a light/medium build up untill the end, when I got all the pieces for the top-tier gear. Then I equipped it all and became a heavy tank who could deal much damage, while also surviving most hits. Combat felt nice. It was nice to see different colored icons which alerted you of the next move your opponent were going to make. As I struggle with color blindness I was happy to see that they also made distinct icons for each attack your opponent were making, as to not leave people suffering from lack of color in their vision. The game felt like a normal lenght game with a few retries, and doing all the side quests. Landed at about 7-8 hours of playtime. Spent some time in game AFK, so not completely sure exactly how long I spent. Regardless would definitely get the game if its on sale for at least 30% of the standard 20€ price tag. Replayability is the reason for this. There is an achievement for finishing the game on the highest difficulty which would be the only reason to go for a replay. Other than that, everything can be done in one playthrough, from the start till after the ending credits, as the game allows for open world exploration once done.

All the while you go through the same mundane sidequests again-and-again to get enough gold to upgrade your keep.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid beat 'em up with souls inspired combat. It's not a full/traditional soulslike though - there's no XP to lose, enemies don't respawn after you use a checkpoint, no stamina system, no metroidvania-esque exploration. The game's not interested in punishing or stressing the player out at all.The combat never gets too big for its boots, so you'll usually be fighting one or two enemies at once, 3 or 4 in rare cases. The encounters always fit the combat systems.The animation work has character, but isn't very detailed, so the game relies a lot on visual indicators for the type of attack the enemy will do. It's not as boring as it might sound - one enemy can have several attacks of one type, and to properly react to them you'll need to anticipate them even before the indicator appears.The problem with the game is in the time wasting - you'll be sitting through hundreds of slow, pointless animations and running around the map following quest markers, back and forth between two places at times.If you do decide to play it, don't explore areas that don't have any quests set in them. The game is extremely linear despite being set in an open map, so just wait until a quest takes you somewhere before you waste time running around a new area prior to all the events meant to take place there being set up by the game.You also can't change the difficulty partway through the game, and it takes a long time before the intro gets out of the way and lets you see whether the option you chose actually fits you. Even if you're confident in this style of game, I'd stick with normal difficulty, because the combat just isn't tight enough to dive right into the instadeath mode that is the alternative.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I really wish I could slap a "maybe" on. It looks and sounds great, and combat against basic enemies is rather satisfying. It's a matter of figuring out what the developers expected you to do, and doing it  as they expect you to do it, or else you'll probably eat multiple hits and be either on the verge of death or already dead from a single mistake.There are points in the latter half of the game where your only option is to fight several bosses in a row, and so you'll keep bashing your head against them until you win, or until you give up. I did end up completing the game, but I feel like I have to slap warnings about the frustrating back half of the game before I can recommend this to someone. Consider this review as a "maybe" and not an outright "no," but given there's only two options, I'll have to slap a "no" on it.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game were 10$, I'd have given it a thumbs up despite it's flaws.As far as pros go, the game oozes charm.  The art style, the character design, and the sound design come together to make a very charming little game.  I enjoyed walking through the fort, town, and ranger station through various stages of the game as it did a very good job of showing a kingdom in despair turning itself around and prospering.  Add in narration from Doug Cockle (voice of Geralt from the Witcher series) and there's little to complain about on that front.Unfortunately, as easy as the combat was to get into, it did have it's problems.  Dodging was a bit wonky at times (even with a light build) and hitboxes were outright busted on some enemies.  The game telegraphs where an AoE attack is about to happen, and there will be times when you will be hit despite not being within that boundary.My biggest gripe is ultimately the length of the game itself.  I'm not a speedrunner by any stretch of the word, and I still reached the end boss in less than 9 hours.  If the game were 10 or 15 bucks that wouldn't be a bad deal at all, but 25$ for something so short that doesn't really have any replay value?  Eh...Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an awesome little gem of a metrovania. If you are a fan of Hollow Knight or metrovanias in general, I think you will really enjoy this! Gorgeous artwork, world and character design. Sound design is fantastic. It has a lot of similarities to Hollow Knight. The characters don't speak, they just make noises and little emotes. Very cute and effective. You drink bug juice to refill HP (similar kind of mechanic to essence in Hollow Knight). The combat is punishing but fair, once you learn the enemy attack patterns it makes bosses much easier (again very similar to Hollow Knight). I 100% completed this game with all achievements on the medium difficulty in roughly 13 hours (including all secret areas etc..).There is a fair bit of back tracking.. that was the only thing I didn't really enjoy about this game. Also I wish there was some variety with the weapons/armor.. maybe some special traits like lifesteal or elemental damage or something to make it interesting. Currently every weapon/armor you find has only damage/weight or defence/weight. Would have been nice to see maybe some of the gold tier items have something special (like the hammer).All in all this is a solid game with a brutal/rewarding combat, incredible world design and a nice story. Would love to see more content in this world in the future. Buy at full price or on sale, you can't go wrong with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: beat the base game in 9 hours, taking my time. as everyone said, it's very short. It's clear there were unmet ambitions, as there are a few loose threads in the writing that feel pretty important. Fun overall, though.Combat is fine. I see a few reviews saying the combat is like a qte, that's.... really not the case. Enemies telegraph their moves. Some moves can't be dodged. Some moves can be blocked. Some can be dashed from. You fight, die, learn the timing, fight again. Does this sound familiar? If you've ever played almost any modern game, it should. I think some people went into it expecting something where you just mindlessly mash the attack button and tank all enemy attacks? Or something? Fun, but short. Exploration is very linear. Side quests aren't entirely optional, you have to complete a good chunk to progress the main story, but not all. After the beginning, they mostly lead to unique bosses, so I don't mind that. It does get a little backtracky, though.As for equipment balance, it's not very depthy. A lot of people comparing this game to dark souls/Salt and Sanctuary, but there's no stamina management. Unlike DS or Salt and Sanctuary, similar games, there's not really an attempt to create weapons that are all lateral upgrades to one another. A sword that has a little less reach but swings faster, or does more damage--you won't be weighing these options and deciding how you're going to build your character. Swords have the sword moveset, axes have the axe moveset, spears have the spear moveset. Many are straight upgrades, both weighing less and doing more damage than the previous weapon in the set. At first enemies feel very tanky, but once you get better gear you cut through them easily enough. It's a short and simplistic but fun game, with engaging combat. I found the bosses to be fair. The save system is a manual system similar to hollow knight--you save at benches. I saw a recent review complaining that this means you have to trek a long way between bosses and save points, but the guy must not have been very observational, because every time you find a boss, the save bench is in the previous room. I don't have any idea how somebody could miss such obvious design, but it is what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I'm kinda bored of this now and probably won't finish it. The combat is great, but the progression and exploration is sooooo linear and disappointing. The game just gives you everything as it is needed, like bottleneck items suddenly appearing in shops. There's no sense of freedom and adventure, currency and items are kinda pointless, the health upgrades are pointless given how the health system works in battle. It honestly may as well just been a boss rush game / arena battler.The game is also padded to high heaven that it's not even funny. It's like they think backtracking in Metroidvanias is good simply because you backtrack, and that's not how it works. The moment they started bottlenecking progress by having to do sidequests in the exact same locations just to upgrade your throne room, I had to wonder where on earth this game was going. And they repeat the exact same thing when you get to the 4th map with the arena battles. I really hope on the next game they employ a narrative and level designer that knows how the flow of these types of games should work, because there is a great idea here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game on the hardest difficulty is not for the faint of heart - achievement hunters beware!This game has charm and a nice aesthetic but it will piss you off. Hitboxes are bad and there's no invincibility frames on dodges. Most boss arena claustrophobic, oftentimes making getting hit by attacks inevitable, especially when bosses or groups of common enemies start mixing up between unblockable attacks (red flash sign) where you can just dodge to escape and the slam attacks (red circles) where you have to double roll away from in order to not get hit.There's also unparriable attacks (yellow flash sign) often executed by enemies capable of thrust attacks, similar to Sekiro's Mikiri Counter mechanic. Not to mention the fact that whenever your health gets low enough, your screen starts to grey out to indicate that you're near death. You cannot turn this option off and it sucks because it interferes with your ability to read enemy attacks as the type of attacks the enemy throw are indicated by different colored icons. In theory the contrast between grey and solid colors would help, but the grey screen effect also makes it harder to read ordinary enemy attacks that have no special characteristics as it darkens the game screen.The flaws of the core combat mechanics shows itself when you play this game on Bloody Whiskers mode as enemy attacks are sped up and damage is increased even more to the point where you get stuck positive feedback loops in which the enemies or bosses combo you back to back until you die.Regardless of its flaws, I beat the game on mouse and keyboard on Bloody Whiskers my first playthrough and am about to finish up the new update's content thus beating the game 100% and getting all achievements. I enjoyed the aesthetic and the narration done by Geralt of Rivia and even the puns. There's charm to the game but that charm might not be enough to win you over if you find the combat mechanics overwhelmingly frustrating/unfair/janky. I was debating between recommending this game or not, I'd say it's worth playing on the lower difficulty. Here's hoping the sequel has better fleshed out combat mechanics and hitboxes and i-frames on dodges/rolls.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: An utterly gorgeous and viscerally satisfying game held back by the lack of variety and re-use of old areas. The games art style is absolutely beautiful, drawing you into the environment and characters like few other 2D games manage. Every item you can equip has a unique model which is visible when displayed on your character, making collecting them all very satisfying, by far not a standard for 2D games of this nature.Something that I would have loved to see more are themed/silly items (cheese shields, tail swords, etc) and objects to signify that this is indeed a rat kingdom. As it stands it's just a wonderfully realized medieval world that happens to be inhabited by rats. Very few items/areas have enough of a distinctive tone and style to remind you that it is indeed a rat society. I understand this is a personal preference and the art direction team shouldn't be swayed from their vision for the game.The story is very basic and doesn't need to be more complex for what it is. It manages a good balance of dire and dark atmosphere with occasional lighthearted moments. (Also having Geralt of Rivia narrate the story doesn't hurt.)The music is good across the board, so far I haven't encountered a track that really burned itself into my mind but everything fits the atmosphere and environments.The combat system is good for the most part. Attacks, parries and dodges all feel incredibly satisfying and the auto-aiming ranged weapons are a great implementation as an aid in combat that doesn't interrupt the flow. However some of the attacks are poorly/incorrectly telegraphed and can feel misleading. Certain bosses will flash the icon to perform a double evasion roll only to then jump to a completely random point in the arena and proceed to do an attack you would have evaded just by standing still, or dogding normally. If you want to have sekiro-style markers for attacks, they have to be perfectly consistent and predictable.The item system seems a bit unbalanced as there rarely a reason to equip heavier weapons/armour since their bonus defense/attack is neglible and not worth the weight penalty. You can always wait a few minutes to find a weapon which is both lighter and stronger. Also the point of having different weapon classes escapes me if they all work basically the same, the slight differences in attack patterns don't matter for 99% of the enemies and otherwise they all perform the same functions.The game is linear by design but presents itself as an open-ish world where you discover new areas and go back to them later in order to find new quests/items. This seems counterintuitive and can throw people off. Either have a tightly designed linear experience or allow for player exploration and experimentation. Here's it's a weird amalgam that doesn't really work either way.I'm still greatly enjoying my time with the game and will most likely finish it. It's a great first project and I can't wait to see what the developers make next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great example of laziness. Yes, the the visuals are good, and suddenly hearing the VA of Geralt from the witcher series was nice, but that's it. Once you get past the looks and into the gameplay, you start noticing all the corner-cutting and lack of thought in the design (I will give my examples for this at the end of this review).Boss fights - Lazy. Bosses and their attacks have ridiculous hitboxes. Many times you'd be sure you dodged but still get hit. This is made worse through the 'Bloody Whiskers' mode, since almost every boss chains their attacks and their attacks knock you down. This means that if get caught once, you can't escape and will probably die, even if you had max health. Gameplay itself - Lazy. The are no combos and there isn't any real difference between different weapon types(different attack speeds at best). You can try to use both 1st and 2nd weapon and maybe that allows for faster attacks, but that's it.Most of the time you're running back and forth between quests. Also you get a bow, then a crossbow and then a pistol, but they all feel the same. It's just another button to push when you need to wear down a boss. Regarding the lore and writing - There isn't much of it and the little there is doesn't make any sense. Frogs are your biggest enemy but you'll spend most of the game fighting bugs and walking back and forth through the sewers. The developers tried to add some humor by giving the moles faction a soviet vibe, but it just feels too random and uninspired. Exploration - There is none. The game is linear and the map is small. Most areas are only unlocked through the main quest and 'side-quests' are just running back and forth to kill something in the same general area. Finally, my examples for laziness- Lets say you saved at a bench and you died. Once you are revived, you can't hop off the bench instantly because the game was design in a way that technically your character 'teleports' back to the bench, sits, on it, and that's when the game fades back in. This makes it so it's better to save at an inventory box(Which are almost always next to a bench) and so what's even the point of the bench then.Obstacles re-appear when you re-enter a map, which is the dumbest thing I've encountered in a game. Why do I have to not only run back and forth for some side-quest, but to also have to destroy the same weeds 5 times just to get through the map.All ranged weapons are the same, and their only purpose is to be spammed at bosses.All fall damage is the same, no matter the height. This isn't the big deal but rather the reason for finding this- you have to go through so many ladders in this game, at some point you just start hopping down rather than climbing down endlessly. TL;DR:Game is semi-decent. If you get it at 5-10$ and just play it casually on a low difficulty, it could be worth its time. I'm going to assume it's priced at 25$ since most of the budgest went on Geralt's VA.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I adore the visuals, the actual gameplay is very clunky. _childDocuments_.review: This game would have been amazing for the gameplay and the graphics but there are two things that infuriate me and warrant this negative review.1. The save system. It is a manual save system where you need to sit down on a bench to trigger a save. What is means is that after each encounter I WOULD SPRINT BACK TO THE NEAREST BENCH, SAVE AND THEN SPRINT BACK TO FACE THE NEXT ENEMY. There's no save system just before a fight! You are losing a lot of time going back and forth.2.  The inability to skip the cartoon dialogue. What happens is that the rats talk in cartoons drawn in speech bubbles and it would be fine EXCEPT THE NARRATOR STARTS TALKING ABOUT THE EXACT SAME THING WE JUST SAW IN THE BUBBLES just after the rats finish their bubbles! So what's the point of waiting for the characters to talk to have the narrator sum it up in the next 10 seconds? At least give me the possibility to skip or speed up the balloons.3. There are plenty of places where there are vines growing and you need to slash them to move forward. And they regrow after like 2 minutes or so! So if you have to come back to the same area a second (or third or fourth) time, you will have to slash these vines again and again. It's just a very stupid mechanic to slow you down and make the game longer.

What truly sets this game apart is the storytelling. The narrative is outstandingly developed (and narrated <3), and as you progress through the game, you will fnd yourself deeply invested in the fate of the main character and his kingdom. Also a good point goes to the unique art style.Overall I highly reccommend this gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Awful attack animations leave you wondering what exactly each enemy will do next. You have to hard learn what each of their code will do based on your position to them and their position in the room. Many enemies have the same symbol for a number of their attacks, and each of them will hit you at different areas if you're not positioning correctly.The story is charming and the narrator is great. The art in this game is amazing and I loved admiring the detail of each of the different areas. The gameplay unfortunately is the meat of the game though, and that, became quickly more irritating than fun, worsening as the "difficulty" of the areas went up.Don't play this game for the challenge, as the design of it is simply a memory test of learning every single enemy. I'd recommend playing it on easy, not sure how much of a difference that makes as I played on normal. The game was reasonably fun on normal, but the hardest difficulty "bloody whiskers" was a nightmare and incredibly frustrating. The difficulty cannot be changed once you start the game and you're required to play the whole game through on "bloody whiskers" for an achievement. I'd recommend you avoid playing this game if your a completionist and avoiding the hardest difficulty altogether if not. But, the story is decent enough if you can stomach the irritations of combat and mandatory side quests that have you walking back and forth between long treks, some of which will make you go back that very same area you just came from, and you can't grab all of the quests in one go.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I read the Redwall books when I was a kid, so when I first saw the store page that was immediately what I thought, and I couldn't believe it. The series does not get a lot of exposure, but here is Tails of Iron to carry on the legacy. I started to play and the influence of the books is present, which is awesome, yet it does a great job of standing on its own.The game itself is extremely well done IMO. Beautiful settings, great audio, characters that are aptly named and fit right in to the world, an archetypal story, and combat that plays very well. One can only hope Tails of Iron ends up as prolific as the material that influenced it! Big thanks to the developers for giving us this. A true prince of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: It is important to note, that you shouldn't expect any metroidvania-style exploration from Tails of Iron, which is something that a quick look on the screenshots may imply. The game is strictly linear, and I was able to find every secret - and there is not many of them - without even specifically looking for them. With that out of the way, anything else about the game is great. Visuals are simply astounding, narrative is enjoyable, combat system is great - don't get discouraged by many reviews calling it frustrating in the later portion of the game, I was able to breeze through every fight relatively quickly on normal difficulty - and the enemy variety is good enough to keep you entertained through the whole playthrough. Even with the limited exploration, the game will take you about 10 hours to complete, which is solid. You can pick it up for full price if you are 2D action platformer enthusiast, but personally, 50% off was an ideal price range for me. Either way, the game is definitely worth your time.

The first thing I hear, when I pressed play was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Geralt of Rivia as narrator and jaw fell to the ground. His voice suits narrator very well, since his voice very smooth and calm. _childDocuments_.review: My review system works with a 10 point score. 0 = bad and 10 = good.I have 5 criteria on which I decide. Each can give 0 - 2 points.Below that I will explain my decisions.Tails of Iron is a very unique approach to the souls like genre.Just like any souls game, its combat system is very focused on learning an enemies attack pattern and adapting to overcome it. But this time in a 2D world. And honestly, this worked better than I expected. The fights are challenging, and every boss has its own fighting style. On the flip side, there is one thing about the gameplay that was very dull. Backtracking...Being someone who played lots of RPG games, it is kind of a natural habit to explore everything BUT the main objective first. As a friendly advice: Don't do that. If you follow the plot, you will get everywhere you need to, even for side missions. Considering I didn't know that, I did a lot of unnecessary walking.But once I noticed my mistake, there wasn't much else that bothered me.The story combined with a very talented voice actor was quite enjoyable, the art style I found beautiful and overall, there was very much attention to detail. I'm just not sure about certain voice "effects". If you play it, you will see what I mean. I appreciate the idea, though.To summarize: Tails of Iron is a very well-made 2D souls like, and I had very much fun playing it. So, I can only recommend it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on bloody whiskers mode. Cool game although frustrating at times. You can fight a boss, reach the next one, play other games for a week and come back without feeling lost. The story is simple yet it can surprise you every now and then.I have no idea where reviews complaining about this not being a metroidvania are coming from since there is nothing in promo materials saying the game attempts to have a non-linear gameplay. You should also take the souls-like tag as "hard game" because weapon differences are minimal so you are in reality locked into one fight style and exploration is limited to a handful of side bosses and areas.There are almost no i frames and there are no recovery frames. I.e. if you don't get up immediately after getting hit you are going to get hit again.There are some problems i don't know if are intentional or just lack of polish:Bosses will input read/have instant reaction to your movementsSome bosses will chain an unavoidable combo if you get hit once and delete your entire life bar even with almost max armor and racial resistanceHitboxes can be a lot larger than the animation makes you believe they areThere is some degree of randomness in some attacks. I.e. an aerial attack consistently lands right in front of you if you don't move but every now and then you get hitSome attacks are not dodgeable unless you have a millisecond reaction time or is lucky to be in the correct position before it startsAgainst multiple enemies you will sometimes be in a position where getting hit is unavoidable because two enemies are attacking at the same timeThe only thing i've found straight up unfun were battles against more than one boss at once.I wouldn't say there is replayability once you finish it aside from doing harder modes or speedrunning.If you get frustrated easily, don't recommend buying because you will die and there will be nothing you could have done differently to avoid it. If you like the art style and like difficult action rpgs this game is aight. Wait for a sale if unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so much, but the gameplay is just not fun. Not difficult, it's more like Simon Says rather than actual combat at times, just incredibly slow, clunky and repetitive. You just wait until the enemy telegraphs what kind of attack he is going to do (which is very easy to tell thanks to the colored symbols over their heads) and then you either block, dodge or parry followed by an attack. Rinse and repeat until the enemy goes down. The "difficulty" comes from the lack of invincibilty frames and the slow movement from your character, which can lead to you getting bounced around like a pinball if you have to deal with more than one enemy at a time. And considering the high amount of save points, they knew how annoying that would be. I guess they just didn't know how to fix the problem.Overall: very nice Style over sleep inducing substance.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted 2D-soulslike with lots of charm and an intriguing world, which kept me hooked till the very end. As i am still very alien and new to games which offer similar combat styles, i cannot account to other reviews by fellow gamers complaining about flaws in the fighting mechanics. Well... the game is not easy and as i have played the whole thing in Bloody Whiskers mode i cannot deny saying that i experienced points where i chewed on the armrests of my chair xD more experienced players and Souls veterans may find a hidden gem in this game for themselves.A few points that i noticed (or were too stupid to understand xD), that could maybe be improved: - i totally get some people complaining about backtracking and having to run back and forth just to accept a new quest from a questboard. Personally, i had no problem with this as i always enjoyed the artistic backgrounds and lovely music while traversing through the different game sections. Maybe this could be solved by adding more fast-travel boards, items or companions that allow faster travelling (a mole that could dig you and himself to another level would be awesome, for example in the crypt - the moles also had pretty impressive vehicles which would be awesome to use for yourself at some point ;D ) or allowing players to jump to different areas in one section (if i remember correctly, there are two fast-travel boards in the mines but you cannot travel between them)- the currency system (iron and monster parts) and the option to exchange became obsolete for me towards the end of the game as i gained everything by defeating enemies. Its a nice idea but could maybe be elaborated upon in the second game :D- several times i encountered a bug were i was stuck in the flask-drinking animation when re-spawning at a save point. A quick reload fixed the problem but maybe a small bug fix can remove it :D- the depth of the armor system could maybe be extended upon as well as the idea of having certain armor with perks and attributes against certain monster types is nice but fell short for me at the end of the main game and the Fir-forest DLC as new monsters appeared and stats of new acquired armor parts cannot be changed. (being able to upgrade your favourite amor/weapon and changing its attributes would be neat)I really enjoyed my journey with ToI and would always recommend everyone to check it out for themselves. Really looking forward for the second part (hopefully Geralt of Rivia is still narrating the story!!!? :D)Cheers, OLF

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever worked on the art-style of this game deserves double whatever they are being paid currently. The backgrounds and locations, although few, are absolutely gorgeously designed and teeming with detail. It is clear that the principle of quality over quantity was applied here, and the overall package is better for it. Same applies to gameplay. Little fodder and a lot of bosses and mini-bosses. Sure, it may make the game seem shorter as a result, but it's absolutely worth it, especially because...yeah, I can definitely see the combat becoming stale after a while. It works as intended ( despite what some that don't want to learn to how time dodges, parries or interrupts may claim. not everything has to play exactly like dark souls. git gud ), however design-wise I can definitely see it going stale if the game kept going after the most recent DLC. _childDocuments_.review: This game is PERFECT! ...If you ignore the combat.TL;DR: Buy on sale, play easy mode. Otherwise it's not worth it unless you're a masochist. Just finished the main story on the normal difficulty, I cannot recommend easy mode enough. The visuals, music, sound design, story, character design, and exploration are all brilliantly handled. The issue is that the combat feels horrible. The enemy hitboxes had me exclaiming in frustration at least once each combat, to the point upon defeating a boss I wouldn't feel accomplished as much as I was just thankful that it was finally over. So when you're at the final boss gauntlet of the game it's a slog. Repeating the same janky-feeling fight over and over until by what feels like luck you're able to guess what the game wanted you to do and survive with next to zero health left. I really wish there were invincibility frames on the dash or dodge-roll, most of the times where I'd die and felt frustrated would have been avoided. Now what I'm absolutely astounded wasn't included were invincibility frames upon taking DAMAGE. Holy god how the hell is it fair to take a hit from an enemy, get staggered, take damage from a second, stagger again, then take damage from the first again and die?  I really really want to like this game but I wish I just watched someone else play through it instead of playing it myself! Last note: The attack indicators were also a joke, especially when they show up for half a second before the enemy smacks you with an attack that covers 70% of the battlefield. If the sequel adds I-frames after taking damage that's good enough reason to play the sequel. If it adds I-frames to the roll & dash, they have the perfect game in their little rat paws.
