_childDocuments_.review: Basically Salt & Sanctuary or Hollow Knight, but now with rats. It is nowhere as open-ended or long as the two, but still offers high quality gameplay from start to finish. I completed the base game and free dlc on the normal difficulty just under 12 hours.Highlights:- Awesome art style, character and world design.- Great attention to detail, for example whenever there is a soundtrack playing, usually you can find a bard or musician somewhere in the map who is playing an instrument.- Levels are all visually distinct and immersive, if only there was more to explore.- Plenty armor and weapons to find, some designs of which clearly inspired by The Witcher.- Engaging combat for a 2D Soulslike, but has one pretty big flaw (explained below).Criticism- Mostly linear progression, yes there is some side content off the beaten which is VERY worth to tackle, but the general storyline is quite strict in terms of where you can go.- Lack of i-frames on dodge. I understand this was to make positioning important, but enemies' pink / area of effect attacks often cover too wide of an area and happen to fast to reliably dodge AND can be spammed. Many of such attacks are outright undodgeable if you are too near the borders of the combat area.- Finnicky flying enemies. Sometimes, hitting a flying enemy (especially the mozis) does not register despite them clearly being in the hitbox.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 hours might not seem like a lot, but for this little indie game it's finishing everything there is to do minus the hardest achievement (beat game on hardest difficulty). I played on the easiest for one reason only, the combat.Combat/Gameplay - this is not this games strongest point. It does the job, but it does become very tedious even on easy difficulty. If you like the challenge it gives on normal or hard (Bloody Whiskers is hard) then you may enjoy it. Essentially it boils down to 3-4 types of attacks your enemy can do. Blockable (let's call them white attacks as sometimes they are colored with white markings), Parry-able which are marked with yellow markings, normal dodging which are red claw marks, and full dodging which you do a roll of and the enemy marks are red circles. You are very punished for adding in any attacks inside the latter 3. If those markings come up, you basically can only do the respective ability to negate damage. Otherwise you are trampled and punished. There are a lot more intricacies like weapon weights, armor weights, resistances to certain types of enemies, etc but from what I've noticed you don't even need to pay attention to those if you become a master of what the game wants you to do during combat.Story - reminds me a lot of when I read the old Brian Jacques series Redwall. You're a rat. Living in a world of other animals. Some are mean, some are allies, some are just regular bugs with no real cognitive thinking abilities other than survival. I enjoyed it but there are some who may say it's rather....generic. Obviously no spoilers but if you've read the old Redwall series, enjoy a good "revenge" story, and like the art style of 2D hand drawn, this is for you.Art style and performance - speaking of art style, this game is gorgeous to me. Doesn't take much to run it either(I completed the game entirely on the Steam Deck with zero issues). A LOT of detail was put into this game and it shows. Absolutely no glitches I ran into, no stutters, no crashes, etc. It played flawlessly to the end. Again, I ran it on the Steam Deck so YMMV.Price point - I got this game on sale for $12.50. For 10 hours of gameplay plus the amount of enjoyment I got out of it I'd say was worth every penny. If you do not play on easy, you may die more and therefore have more playtime but during my easy-mode playthrough I never died once, and just kept making progress so if you buy this game at MSRP, depending on your idea of price point versus hours played versus enjoyment it may be worth considering a sale. However, what is here in that 10 hours is quite enjoyable as mentioned before in the Story section.Overall - I recommend this game to anyone who likes and loves the 2D metroidvania souls-like genre looking to also enjoy a fun story with rats, frogs, bunnies, bugs, etc. There is a ton I did not get into for fear of making this review way too long and frankly, it's cheap enough that if you read this and still want to play it, just do it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: It's a delicate short game. All the art, music and story are good. And the rats are so cuuuute! ♥But the game mechanics is just awful. It's totally torture when it comes to the fight. Nothing is explicit. You can't tell if you could get hit on your position when the enemy deals AoE attacks. You can't tell whether you're standing behind or in front of your enemy when your models stack together. Most of time, you will die from this kind of misjudgment, which is very frustrating.The control is very rigid. You can't do anything until the animation of your last action is finished. That means your enemy can suddenly make an unpredictable attack but you can't dodge or block, because you have to wait for whatever you last action to be done. This is stupid. Bossfight is therefore very terrible. You die a million times just to figure out the pattern of the behavior of the boss. Even so, you still need to try a million times to beat the boss, because you still have to fight control. There is literally no joy of beating a boss, only relief that you know you can finally move on and don't need to do it again.As for the map design, some reuse of the map is clever but most of it is not. You spend a lot of time walking between places you've been before. There're only fast-travels among the main scenes. No shortcut ways in the map. You walk through a maze, the next time you have to walk through it again.The default keyboard bindings is kinda anti-human but still acceptable and you can change it.Overall, the gameplay is not that bad though, especially when you don't pursue to beat the game in hard mode. Those flaws won't bother you so much if you play the easy mode just for the story and aesthetics. But if you want to challenge yourself with higher difficulties, well, *enjoy* it.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Game took me about 11 hours to 100% on hard difficulty (excluding the achievement for beating the game on the highest difficulty)Overall, the story and combat are very good in this game. The story is fairly short, you could probably complete it in like 7-8 hours if you did absolutely none of the side content. Sadly, there are no permanent companions which I thought would be the case when I first bought the game, there are only 3 temporary companions that accompany you during certain missions.The combat in this game is very simplistic in design yet works perfectly. Combat revolves around your arsenal of weapons, of which you have the following: one handed and shield, 2 handed, and ranged. All three of these weapons can be swapped around and combo'd together. For example you can charge an attack with your 2-handed weapon and then immediately follow up with a flurry with your sword and board and then shoot an enemy on the other side of them. As for defensive abilities, the player can block, parry, dodge, and roll. Which one you use depends on the scenario and each has their uses. Now the main draw of the game are the bosses. The difficulty of he bosses varies wildly but there are some bosses where you should definitely prepare for some torture. I never really found myself getting bored in boss fights because each of them have multiple different attacks and most have multiple phases. Most bosses would take me 2-3 attempts to beat on hard difficulty but a certain marvel wannabe took me about 10-15 attempts to be able to beat.Overall, the game is very good, there weren't very many issues that I noticed during play. The only problem I had was that it seemed as if attack canceling didn't work in combat as I would try to dodge an unblockable attack but my character would continue their shield bash anyway. I didn't encounter any bugs whatsoever during my playthrough.

They are required to progress the story.If these were removed entirely and the game length cut down, it would be amazing.But it is just terrible pacing and I can not find it in myself to finish the game

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is one of those rogue-likes that grow on you. Beautiful graphics, fun soundtrack, and a main character you care about. The story is nothing to write home about. (Save the kingdom) But you care enough to want to finish game! So any problems? Well, most rogue-likes have main character who move FLUIDLY and carries an array of moves and techniques that add some flavor and strategy to the overall experience. But in TOI your character moves well like a mini-tank. Sure he can roll, (slowly) and has a very quick little scamper but mostly you roll, block, roll, attack. That's how you beat most enemies. The enemy bosses all have an unblockable move that makes game play very difficult and becomes more of a rock, scissors and paper strategy instead of the fluid combat that I expect from most rogue-likes. Do I still recommend the game? Yes, I finished it! Amazingly. Just be prepared for one tough game. Also Part two is on it's way and it looks tougher! Hopefully part two will have more game play depth and strategy than part one. Now go avenge your daddy and save the kingdom!

_childDocuments_.review: "Tails of Iron" stands out as an engaging action RPG that impresses with its smoothly executed combat system. Unlike many games where frantic button mashing leads to victory, "Tails of Iron" demands a more strategic approach, especially on harder difficulty levels. Each battle is a calculated affair, requiring thoughtful engagement and quick reflexes. This is complemented by a straightforward inventory management system, allowing players to focus on enjoying the game rather than micromanaging items. Keeping gear light enhances agility in combat. Additionally, the game’s narration by Doug Cockle, famous for his role as Geralt in "The Witcher" series, adds an unmistakably charming layer, enriching the experience, especially for fans of the series.However, the game isn't without its quirks. Side quests tend to encourage extensive map exploration, which initially seems rewarding but can lead to time-consuming backtracking as players often need to revisit previously explored areas. Furthermore, while enemies do not constantly respawn, their occasional reappearance requires either re-engagement or strategic avoidance. The game’s duration might also be a drawback for some, as it can be completed within 5-6 hours; despite this, the side quests are well-integrated, offering valuable rewards that justify the required back and forth.Overall, "Tails of Iron" is a delightfully crafted game that combines simple yet deep combat mechanics with an immersive narrative experience. The arena battles introduce a humorous element, with clever nods to various video game icons and sports celebrities, each bringing unique combat styles into the fray. With its balanced mix of action, strategy, and storytelling, "Tails of Iron" is recommended for both seasoned gamers and newcomers alike. Fans should be excited for the upcoming sequel, which promises to build on this solid foundation.

_childDocuments_.review: Over all, I do have to say, this game is great. Does LOTS of things right. Especially the visuals and the music, and for a 2D action adventure, combat is done quite well too.However, there are several complaints I think the devs should hear:- early game spoiler. Any player that is mildly paying attention when they play this game, will likely notice very quickly that 4 species of opponents are labelled immediately. Perhaps, like with weapon types and ammo, question mark cover them, until the player first encounters an armour for it? I noticed pretty much immediately, and the existence of moles was therefore not a surprise.- "Get off the bench" I'm not sure what the problem is, but whenever I save, or have just died, it takes a lot of effort to get off the bench, and I find myself saying this line near constantly. Suggestion: spawn Regie off the bench, when you respawn? It would help flow a lot.- I can't remember quite how far spread a problem this was, but at least in "The Village Sewers", there were at least 2 barricade fortifications you need a 2 handed weapon to demolish. And several vines. If they weren't constantly self resurrecting, it would be far less annoying and flow breaking.- Side quests, are not side quests, if they are mandatory. Most, if not all the missions labelled as "Side Quest" are non-negotiable to complete. Therefore the game looks like it should be slightly open, but really is quite linear. Maybe just label them all as "Board missions" and "Arena bounties" or something.- There's not much that can really be done about it, but in the middle-ish section of the game, there's a LARGE potion of you just fast travelling back and forth, "Hi I've finally returned home... you want me to go where? Okay, off I go. Hi I'm back, did that thing! ... You've got another one? Okay fine, catch you later. Woo finally got that one... you're kidding me, another one? And you can't do this yourself because. . ? I am the king, you know? I have slightly more important things to do"- Poison. Um, does it do anything? Or is it just a placebo? It definitely doesn't do any significant DOT to enemies, that I've noticed (many tests occurred, but not rigorous ones, just visual). Does it just boost the actual damage you deal? If so, why bother colouring the health bar of bosses?- Oh... and Jey should have their music box playing a lot more often.But yeah, as said before, good game, lots of content, lots of fairly well made mechanics, the constant mini arenas through some areas were a little tiring, but fairly fun, certain battles were really well crafted, music in certain places is stella, art style superb, continuity of what you select to wear: EVERYTHING is visually shown, and I love that, quality of life is very little, story all lines up, so no immersion breaking points. _childDocuments_.review: The game itself is decent. Despite not recommending the game, I would not say I have a negative impression of it. It has a good story with a level of self-awarness, Redwall-esque, reminiscent of the book series I'd read in my childhood. There are a few nods to other franchises here and there, but I won't spoil those. Clearly, the game is designed around a controller, and it tells you as much, but I got by ok using KBM, if a bit awkwardly at points even with custom mapping. For the most part it is not too difficult, albeit punishing of your mistakes. Even the tougher bosses will go down with a bit of persistence on the part of the player as you learn their patterns. Most bosses are fairly unique, and certain species have certain styles that they emulate. It's one of the more forgiving Souls-like games, as the game provides you plenty of supplies, and you can backtrack easily. Bosses will not one-hit you from full health or even half health, as there is usually a sliver of health that the player keeps, often allowing them to recover. These anti-frustration features prevent the game from getting too aggravating with the more tenacious fights.There aren't any skill points: your main progression is through access to equipment, as well as increasing your health. This is a neutral point. A few minor gripes that I have is that tracking certain things like finding ingredients which you need for your health, can be confusing at times, as you don't always remember who you talked to. If you forget a bit of dialogue for it, that part is not tracked, unlike the main quests and side quests. Fortunately, there are straightforward players guides about this unintuitive situation.So, why do I not recommend it? For the price it asks, I feel as though the lack of replayability does not give much of a reason to play this beyond clearing the main story, and perhaps a tiny bit of exploration and a side quest or two, depending on how much you took your time before finishing it. I bought this at a slight discount, and I still feel as though it is asking a bit much. Where the game is strong - the narrative, it falters outside of it. You gather a whole bunch of equipment by the end of the game, even some of the high-tier ones near the end, that you'll hardly end up using, if at all. You can redo certain side quests if you want, but there is not much reason to aside from a meagre reward of materials which you are likely already stacked up on, and some of them disappear later anyway. The boss fights themselves are not replayable unless you start a new game; there is not a NG+ mode, as far as I am aware. There are multiple save slots, but you can only use different ones from the main menu. The quicksaving method in game, which involves sitting on a bench does not let you use a different save slot, overwriting the one you are playing on now. You can't save from the pause menu, so you can't go back to an older save to play a certain situation over and over down the road.One of the thumbnails of the videos on the Steam page says "animated story" and I would say it's accurate as to what the game is. It almost seems like a visual novel at certain points. If you want to play something you don't really intend on playing again after you finish it, or once in a blue moon, maybe you will not mind this. The story is decent enough, but not so gripping that I'd want to sink replay it over and over again. The story is fairly short, and I am sure if you rushed it and did not take your time or explore much, you could do it in under 10 hours, and a good chunk of it would be spent in cutscenes. It is not too difficult to keep a low weight, which hinders your movement if it becomes too high: you will likely have gathered enough equipment early on that you will have suitable build for almost any situation early on. I only reached the heaviest weight intentionally at one point, when I did not have high-tier equipment and wanted to fight an optional boss. Otherwise, there is little incentive to have a high weight and it is avoidable, as you can have a high armour value without becoming very slow.I am not sure if the devs would add more replayability in the future, but it would help the longevity of this game. For what the game is worth, which is not a bad game, it does not entirely deliver.

Also learn to sheath your weapon, you move way faster.The story is compelling for the style. You actually have one, which is rare for a soulslike. Like you must already know, the narrator is Geralt from the Witcher video games, so that's great.You kinda lack customisation for your character. Yes you have a lot of piece of equipment, but it really doesn't change much. 3 style of weapon pretty much + light/heavy/ranged. I still have no idea what the weight threshold do. Seems to roll the same and move the same, maybe attack speed is a bit slower, still have no idea.It is very story driven, not like a standard soulslike, you have bar instead of numbers, so you don't really have any real of the change you get when you upgrade to a better weapon, except at one point you start killing enemies quite faster.All in all, a very good game if you have like me a Salt and Sanctuary itch.I would probably wait for a big discount to get more for your money, but you will enjoy the time you play with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming game I just came across! For sure, one of the best I've played this year. For starters, the art is gorgeous, giving you a lush and vibrant world that can look beautiful or bleak at times - you know it's good when you decide to walk slower. Combat is tight and tense, with a good rythm most of the times and the story is really the best part for me: a strong presentation that takes you into a narrative that is great in its simplicity and wonderfully narrated by the White Wolf himself, Doug Cockle, who's up there with the narrator for Darkest Dungeon, Bastion and Disco Elysium. Lastly, the only issues I had with this game, that did not spoil the experience at all, were in a very small number of boss encounters that felt like they had a hitbox that was slightly off and some of the postboard side quests that pop up after you're finished with the storyline - they felt rushed or lazy in comparison. The amount of available weapons and armor also feel a bit scattered and unecessary for my taste, especially if you do pay attention to your surroundings but, again, ultimately do not hinder the game.If you enjoy a charming fable filled with challenging and varied creatures to combat, please do give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: i really wanted this to be a good game, because it looks soo good! every screen has wallpaper quality and with the different layers you get a feel of depth wich i really liked!but thats were the pros end for me. the first hour was fun but the further you explore the map, the more you realize that the combat mechanics just dont work! combat on paper is super simple:normal attacks: dodge or blockcharge attacks: dodgestomp attack: double dodgeheavy attack: parryso far so easy. but stomp attacks will hit you almost always even though you double dodge, charge attacks have sometimes such a low window that if you pressed attack before the attack of your foe was telegraphed, it is impossible to dodge. sometimes enemies will chain attack after attack that can kill you instantly especially if there are more than one big enemy. if you are unlucky, they play ping pong with you because there are no invincibility frames. that was so rage inducing for me that i often alt f4 the game. its not just challanging but sometimes just unfair. i finished dark souls 3 and sekiro more than once so i like challanging combat, but this is just bad.some QOL improvements should have been made. if your flask is empty and you are low hp, you have to fill your flask, heal and then fill up you flask again. why not fill health and flask at the same time? but thats just a small detail. dealbreaker for me was the bad combat, no progression and backtracking straight out of hell. you can tell that the developer put a lot of love in this game and thats why it hurts me to not recommend it but it was just no fun in the end.

Combat was fun to learn, though initially clunky, especially the parry mechanic which I frankly didn't fully pick up until I was on the last area. There are a three types of light/heavy/ranged weapons that all have their inherent pros/cons, i.e. rate of attack, damage output, ect...The art design was amazing/unique, and the world design was interesting in that .The story started off fast and you get caught up initially but there are a few areas where there is no full explanation like . At the end the game left me wondering if this was all it had to give me, with the ending not really all that fulfilling. Catch this one on a sale if you like games like Hollow Knight/Dark Souls.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much that makes me  to like this game. The art is great, the world and story so far are intriguing, and the item system has potential.But the  of this game is just kind of awful. It feels like you're trudging through molasses, everything feels the opposite of fluid, even when prioritizing lightweight gear. _childDocuments_.review: Good game, but filled with small minor disappointments. Just little bits here & there where it could have been amazing but isn't.Pros:* amazing character. The story isn't anything to write home about but it's well told & has a great sense of atmosphere* interesting core combat system* haven't encountered too many bugsNeutral:* the game features somewhat slow & methodical combat, where you need to respond precisely to enemy signals to parry, dodge, block, etc. That is not everyone's cup of tea.Cons (or rather disappointments) - in order from least to most aggravating:* combat is good, nicely hits that souls-like vibe of you know you screwed up & you know how you screwed up so you keep trying again... but some of the hit boxes feel a little whack. One thing might be is the dodge doesn't actually give you invincibility frames, which can feel a little off. Alternatively, I just need to git gud :D.* economy is a bit busted, it's too easy to get grub-shells & iron, & not enough to spend it on. May have been advisable to go MUCH lighter on the various refill stations, forcing players to have to think more about how to spend their resources.* put the game down for about a week because of IRL... came back & couldn't remember what the enemy signalling meant. An easily accessible tutorial from the menu would be appreciated just as a reminder.* world feels small. I'm just about to do the mine quest... and have spent most of my time bouncing between the sewers, ranger headquarters & their damned tower, & the castle which serves as a hub. Looking thru steam guides, it seems there is maybe about another 2, maybe 3 locations to explore? It's starting to feel a bit repetitive* Weapon & armor variety - this is where the game is at it's worst... while it gives you a whole slew of weapons most of them feel the same, & even worse there just isn't a good reason to use most of them. The only stats are weight & attack; and the difference between spears, swords, & axes is rather negligible. An affix system would help a ton... but even better would be for the weapons to FEEL different, ala dark souls or bloodstained. In those games you might use a less statsy weapon just because it's something ridiculous like a floppy gargoyle tail... here not so much. Armor is a *bit* better with resistances but ultimately has the same problem... most of the equipment I find is at best a side-grade from what I'm already using.Best advice to the devs - take the same formula, give it a bigger world,  don't be as generous with consumables & for gods-sakes make the weapons & armor have bigger tradeoffs in terms of feel & playstyle. Those 3 factors take this from a great game to just very good, which is a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with Redwall you'd have a sudden moment of excitement at the idea that these guys could easily pull off a game that is fitting to the narrative of the book series.  Of course, this game has nothing to do with any of the Redwall books.  And that's fine.At it's core, it's a revenge story.  The bad guys, which are some Frogs, decimate your kingdom.  There's been an ongoing war between the two of your kingdoms so it almost feels like it's the turn of the Rats to be taken down a notch.  But, of course that's a silly notion.  You're the newfound king due to both your father's demise and winning a trial by combat against your brother.  Your job now is to restore your kingdom, and it's a blast.Combat is probably one of the biggest highlights in the game.  There are some questionable hit boxes, and some incredibly frustrating moments in the game where things just don't seem to go your way.  One wrong roll and you're pinned in a corner and subsequently dead.  Sometimes the block/parry combo doesn't work like it's supposed to and that might leave you a bit on the hurt side.  However those moments were all few and far between, minus the last boss battle where I often seemed to be fighting a boss who liked to attack from off-screen.  It's a lot of rolling, blocking, heavy attack and light attack, and some occasional ranged fighting.  Combat is like you'd expect from most games really.  Figure out how  your enemies attack, and then get into the motion of things to combat that.  Enemies are not particularly varied, but the pacing is good enough to where it feels like you're seeing a nice range of them.  Travel is what you'd expect from a game that's Metroidvania like.  You've got a large overall map and you move to different areas with the occasional fast travel.  I wish there'd of been more fast travel to some locations simply because the Side Quests(basically mandatory for gold) would often have me going through areas I'd already visited just to do a quest that was very similar to one I just finished.The environment is great, every area you visit is full of detail and keeps enough variety that each room feels just a bit different from the last.  Enemies look great as well.  If you're a fan of seeing your armor and weapons change based on what you actually have equipped you'll likely be happy with seeing that aspect here.  There are multiple weapons, sword, axe, spear, shields, ranged, and two handed weapons as well.  You also have light, medium, and heavy armors that will all change on your character depending on what you're wearing.Overall you've got a great experience with very satisfying combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect much from this game when I first saw it but boy was I wrong!This game is in one word "Fantastic" probably one of my favorite games of this year, it follows the formula of a Metroidvania / Souls-Like 2d game and it is fantastic, the controls are tight and responsive and the variety of enemies will keep you on your toes, every fight will give you a challenge and will leave you satisfied after you manage to beat it. There are multiple types of weapons and armor for you to find and collect over the course of the game and every type of weapon will have a different "glory kill" that will make you satisfied as you slay your foes. The story will provide you with a compelling tale of a rat's road from prince to king and hero of ratdom, although the rats do not speak the entire game is fantastically narrated by Doug Cockle the voice actor for none other than Geralt Of Rivia from the Witcher game series.The only complaint that I have of this game is that there isn't more of it for me to play, I have loved every second that I have played of it and can't recommend it more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about half way into the gamePros:Lovely artstyleokay gameplayConsSometimes the character just won't climb if you stand too close to the ladder, you have to jump on itProgression system is all over the place, meaning you find 1 weapon then the next 20 will be useless because they are weak.Poorly explained/ indicated mechanics. At first you learn that there are 3 different attacks. Yellow which you can parry, red which you dodge and red circle which you must double dodge most of the time. Now it's all good when indicated but later in many boss fights the indicator is missing and you are left with you've seen the attack once and now you must know how to handle it. While yes this would be nice but not on the 1st encounters because this isn't making the game challenging it just makes it annoying and poorly made.I got no explanation of what toxin does or why should I use it. So I'm guessing it's just extra damage. While it is nice it would be nice if someone explained it that it does nothing but bonus dmg so you are not there waiting for it to do any extra effect. In 6 hours I've found 2 pages of med and light armor and only found 4 heavy armors, which again is a poor progression since every med armor is better than any light and at this point any heavy armor. There is again no explanation of why should I use Sword over axe or spear since they are pretty much the same with very very little variety in moveset. (Some maces are categorized as axes and some hammer as axes for some reason.) The game gave me an explanation about the axe being able to tear down wood baricades, but then again so can the spear or sword so there is nothing special about them.Barricades respawning for no reason except to annoy you and to make it take longer to get from A to B even after you destroyed those. Sidequests, are not sidequests but mandatory quests. They are needed to progress the main story.Currency, it seems like I'm capped at 99 and can't earn more but I can't spend them as there is nothing to spend them on. Lastly while it was fun first, the annoying random instument sounds for rats. It makes no sense. At the very first scene it was funny when we joked about someone probably made the bard eat his whole set of instruments because of how he wakes us up, it got annoying as we progressed. From random balloon or whatever sounds to a whole washing machine effects. It just progressively got worse.I like the game but there are so many problems that I haven't seen anyone mention is strange. But even with this I recommend because it's a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A cool game that I had a ton of fun playing and completing to 100% after coming back for it's update.If you like to get beat up over and over again, you'll enjoy this.The art is nice and I very much liked looking in the backgrounds a lot, Combat is great in my opinion, and the story is being a rat exterminating a whole frog race.Weapons and equipment have a scale to them, as well as weight, armor can defend better against certain enemies better then others do but you'll mostly be fighting against frogs so you don't have to switch it up a ton.Weird quirk about weapons, only stat shown is their damage scale. However some can attack faster or slower then normal, not obvious for all of them but it's there.You will die, a lot, even on it's normal difficulty. And I first played it on it's hardest, which sure was challenging, but learning the combat took some time. Then I was smooth sailing with some bumps along the way.Only issues I ever had were attacks from certain bosses being cheap and almost unavoidable, but if you got a iron will, you'll end up making it.The gameplay itself is good but the way some enemies attack can be hard to predict since they are telegraphed in a weird way.There is some repetitiveness to the game such as some quests going over the same path 3 times over and overall backtracking quite a bit. I have an aggressive play style so perhaps a more passive one will suit others better. the game is a solid 6/10 If you can overlook it's flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron has it's moments for those who enjoy challenging combat, indie art and dark settings. It's a bit like Salt and Sanctuary meets Red Wall. While enjoyed the combat mechanics and over arching story, the game falls a bit short with the questing mechanics. Rather than playing directly into the plot the quest delivery format feels more like fetch quests that have you retreading the same few zones over and over. If you could pick up a few quests at once this could be greatly improved, even better would be integrating the quests in as part of the story and not a bulletin board quest grab. That said there is a lot more good than bad here, particularly the weapon and armor variety. I'm a sucker for equipment changes reflected on your avatar. For people who like a mix of  soulslike and metroidvania this will do. But I'd recommend grabbing it after you finish Ender Lillies and Vigil.  Overall its a unique take on the genre and solid way to keel 15 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Before the larger, brutal Skaven from Warhammer: Vermintide came to be, there was a slim sliver of hope for the rats of this world in the form of King Rattus and his band of rodents. His untimely death led many to believe the rats would fall once again into morbid disarray and it is at this pivotal period that Tails of Iron takes place.You take control of Redgi, smallest son of King Rattus but the feistiest of the lot… also the one who witnessed his brutal murder by the frog clan and their ferocious leader, Greenwart. It is you then, bruised and battered hero, who must rise and restore this bleeding, burning kingdom and fight its many foes for its survival. The game provides quite the difficult journey and defending the bosses planned attacks will be your main form of offence. Watching the Crimson Fort, the Ranger’s lodge and Long Tail village in ruins but slowly being rebuilt in the background as you run your errands to fund the next expedition gives a nice sense of progression. The hand-drawn art is top notch and ends up give a pass to the fetch quests that ultimately plague the story. It is unfortunate then - as a self-proclaimed rat chronicler, to tell you that even when you succeed in the war against the frog clan and declare yourself King Redgi of the rats, peace will not last… for soon after your death many moons after the events of this game, the acts committed by your revered father in the attic of the Crimson Fort would show its devastating effects, leading to the fall of rat culture and the rise of the despised Skaven. More mutant than rats, more deadly than frog kin.The humans who witnessed the period of peace from King Rattus to King Redgi speak highly of its cultural achievements, but could never take off the shackles of discrimination against the rats rooted in the vicious waves of killings during the Hundred Years war, examined in detail in A Plague Tale: Innocence. Almost the entirety of France was swallowed by plague and vermin and the humans tried (and failed) to exterminated the rats for it.I do not think the pests of A Plague Tale nor the Skaven from Warhammer truly represent the might of the rat species but this game, at least, shows its peak and true potential. Who knows if we’ll ever see another as noble as King Redgi; who knows if we’ll ever see rats not be vilified... but this is a start.This game shows the middle period of rat history. Play it to learn more.

_childDocuments_.review: played this and tried to like it ... but the game made it impossible.It really looks gorgeous and Doug's the voice acting (Geralt of Rivia) is really good...so what are the problems?Combat & movement!There are so many issues here, so let's start simple:- When you jump, you lose all your momentum, so jumping is incredibly undesired as a movement option since it stops the flow of movement.- When you start to move in any direction, there is a ~0,1-second delay before your character starts moving... why?- In combat, you have three options to deal with an attack, which is indicated with a colored icon above the enemies head: block, dodge or parry (shield charge). Every enemy has red (dodge), yellow (parry) or white (block) attacks. The first issue I encountered was that some enemies do not show any indicators when they attack. They just do a white attack but do not indicate so. So you have to know what it looks like when an enemy prepares an attack and block it. Bosses also have multiple red attacks, and since you have no iframes (dodging only makes you move faster), you have to know which attack it is. As an example, the first boss you fight is a giant toad that can either do a lead in the direction it is looking or jump up and land on the same spot. One requires you do doge through the boss before the attack, and the other requires you dodge away from the boss. If you get this wrong, you take a big chunk of damage. Which attack it is, is often not telegraphed well as its movements look very similar.- Building on the previous point, the problem with the game is also that it feels extremely repetitive since it uses its colored (especially red) attacks constantly! You are more focused on the icon popping up than on the actual movements of the enemy. Games like SEKIRO have the same mechanic, but it's sparingly used in comparison, since the intention is for you to look at the enemy, not the symbol. Here I felt like doing a paint by number game, as in some fights I had enemies spam their colored attacks in a row.- Enemies are reused and spammed at you. When a fight starts, the area you can move in is limited and enemies usually come in from the sides. Once you kill one, another comes in. Usually you will fight 2 maybe 3 at the same time. It's extreme annoying when you have to kill wave after wave of enemies. This is especially the case when you have enemies that can block or dodge roll around and evade your attacks... fights then drag on even more so since you cannot just spam attacks as enemies can then start a counter attack, which of course is not indicated. So you do X attacks and see how many you can land before the enemy strikes back and have to learn the timings.- (intended difficulty) Difficulty is all over the place .... some bosses are so easy that you can defeat them on the first try while starting with half health, others might need a few tries. None of that seems balanced, every fight is like a dice role. There is no progression of complexity or mechanics. - Hitboxes are wonky: Some of the attacks land when you are standing far away from the enemy when it lands. A good example is the vertical leap of bosses. They jump up and land on the same spot. The hitbox for that is larger than it visually indicates.- My worst gripe: EVERYTHING is a proverbial bullet sponge! Even if you spam heavy attacks, you need 10 hits to kill a regular mob?! Bosses are even worse, it feels like the only reason anything is this game is remotely difficult is because you need to hit it so often, that you get annoyed. And the worst part is that you cannot do anything about it. You cannot upgrade your weapon or find weapons that are especially effective against certain types. You cannot buff your weapon (except for applying poison, which feels barely noticeable). - Gear is also a pain. You have a quick melee weapon and a string melee weapon and a ranged weapon. The weapons only distinguish themselves by weight and damage. The more the weight, the slower you move and dodge. While the game offers a solid amount of weapons, those are meaningless since none of them have defining characteristics. You probably can find over 20 spears, but they all are just variations of damage and weight. There is nothing special about them, no lore to read, nothing. They are visually different, though. For me, that is meaningless, and I would argue that fewer weapons with more defining characteristics would have been a) more rewarding to find them and b) allow for more significant choices when it comes to selecting a weapon. The same goes for armor, though here you can have special resist stats (e.g. against Frogs -the main enemy of the story), so here at least you have a little to consider and can use different armors to adapt to enemies you will fight. The world, quests & travel!- There are side quests ... 99% seem none optional except for the ones that can be repeated.- The quests send you to the same spots AGAIN and AGAIN! "Kill insects in the sewers", "Kill mosquitos in the sewers", "kill another insect infestation in the sewers". You cannot accept all quests at once, you HAVE to do all of them in sequence... This feels like doing dailies in an MMO!Dialogues!- They are not skippable and are really slow. Whenever you interact with an NPC you get a flute sound and images pop up over the people talking indicating what is discussed. That works, but it all takes sooo long. If they showed the images for half the time it would be enough, or make them skippable (like dialogue lines in other games).- The flute sound stared to grind my mind since it is so shrill and since the game is otherwise rather muted in sound, it stands out by being so high pitch.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank A- (85-88%)Great game - play this if you can!!See my profile for more details about my reviews.What a great little game! Tails of Iron really took me by surprise, and like a slow burn. I had not much expectation for it, although the trailers and images made me probably think that it would be more of an adventure RPG than anything. Not at all! This is a huge tribute to Dark Souls (tough fighting gameplay, basic enemies can kill you quickly, painful bosses, light/medium/heavy weight gear with rolling and parrying, drinking potions etc etc...). The game is also mixed with a bit of metroidvania ala Hollow Knight but with barely any platforming, a bit of Witcher for its medieval fantasy atmosphere (and Geralt as a voiceover!), and a bit of references here and there like Metro 2033 etc.The first couple of hours, I was really underwhelmed, not only by the heavy gameplay (it FEELS clunky at first), but also by the odd choice of making the characters do annoying little sounds, and by the repetitiveness of it (you will backtrack DOZENS of times, and the overall map is not really big, this is NOT a metroidvania for that). The only thing that captivated me... was the visuals. MY GOD this game is BEAUTIFUL. The art is FANTASTIC. So I kept on because of that... well, served me well, because that little game is GREAT. The gameplay ends up being very pleasant to handle, the story, atmosphere and writing are all quite good, and the game just oozes of love in its craft. I really believe the guys who did this game did it with their HEART and SWEAT. Congratulations for that. _childDocuments_.review: A charming, unique, and immersive aRPG. It takes the best from some of the genre's classics and delivers a riveting adventure, with both challenging combat and witty writing.. The creator's sincere and passionate love for their game is palpable and drips across detail of every screen. There is level of quality reminiscent of Stardew Valley and Hollow Knight in that regard.In all fairness I'm still early on in the game, but I'm hopeful it will continue to deliver this experience as I continue this charming adventure,EDIT: Having completed the game (13 hours IGT) I can highly recommend it to any 2D souls-like arpg player. My only really complaint is I wish that there was just more content, as it's simply that good. but also a bit short. I hope this game's success begets more content, be it DLC or new game +.Constructive feedback to devs:You have a great base combat system, it deserves to be expanded on. -Perhaps create a 4th melee weapon type (duel daggers).-Range weapons could be balanced (too strong or ammo is too easy to get), perhaps make crossbow/bullets only purchasable by shop-Expand the number of utility items vis a vis dark souls, bombs, resins, maybe/pets or summons,Per the previous points, the currency system feel unfinished, give us more items to spend currency on (potions, maps, teleport stones, etc)-Expand the social aspect of the game - give a away to increase/develop/progress our relationships with certain characters, this could be one method of better utilizing currency.Fantastic game, potentially on the same level as Hollow Knight and if continued to be developed it stands to be truly an all time classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Tails of Iron just isn't fun. Gameplay revolves entirely around combat and combat is clunky and irrational. Parries only work if you press the button nearly half a second before the attack. Some attacks are telegraphed with the colored red/yellow indicators (indicating that you should dodge/parry), and others aren't, with no discernable rhyme or reason as to why. Dodging doesn't appear to have invincibility frames, so it's not actually about timing them, it's purely about avoiding the attack, and totally possible to dodge through/into the attacks area of effect, taking the full hit. It all feels very unsatisfying and arbitrary. And that's it. That's combat. Attacking, dodging, blocking (arrows exclusively), and parrying. It's extremely basic. Three of your actions are defensive, and poorly implemented. Attacking is a simple combo string followed by a delay. That's it. Skill and choices don't exist here. It's just all so mindless.Progression is standard gear collection, but without any meaningful depth. Every decision is just damage/defence vs weight, and honestly there's nothing interesting to it and never ever a reason to not always choose the higher damage/defence item. Worse, the "upgrades" all feel incredibly incidental and nothing feels satisfying. I quickly stopped caring about new gear, and after that, nothing else matters. It's just stuff that you pick up because it's there. Refunded

_childDocuments_.review: Such a nice game. The gameplay borrows the best aspects from other Souls-/Metroidlikes that have been sprouting everywhere during the last years. The atmosphere is phantastic and the gloomy-catoony world design is top notch. Combat is fluid and progression paths are quite well-telegraphed.BUT, the game also has some noticeable downsides: In my opionion, there was too much backtracking, which made the world feel smaller than it should've felt. Going back to places you have already visited for bounty hunting, which rewards you with currency that unlocks new paths is just a lazy concept that stretches playtime unnecessarily. Also, the difficulty curve (apart from the endgame arena and some good bossfights) is quite weird. The game becomes very easy in the second half when you will have mastered and found new gear. Furthermore, there are currently 6 new achievements in the game for content that can't be played yet. This is misleading, don't bother trying to 100% this game but save your time for a hard mode run when the free expansion is released or get the game at some later date.All in all, I still had a blast playing this and would rate this a very solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little game oozing with style and visual aesthetic.  The sound design excels (think  meets ).Having seen a number of reviews criticizing the game for backtracking tedium and rather simple combat, I played the game on the easiest difficulty.  I enjoyed it, and while I probably would've wrung more hours out of this game had I chosen a harder difficulty, I doubt I would've adored those hours.  Combat was challenging enough at some points even on the easy mode.  If I'd really yearned for more challenge, I could've picked worse equipment options.Music's pretty good.  The story hits the same sort of beats as any fairy tale.  The rats speak to you in pictures and whistles.  The only human voice is apparently the voice actor for Geralt from ; however, having not played that game yet, this was not much of a selling point for me, although the in-game references to  series did not escape my notice.  The guy's narration isn't bad, but I wouldn't write home about it; he did seem to put more feeling into it as the story went on, though.A fairly recent review points out that this game is, indeed, not an RPG aside from the dress-up you can play with the equipment.  It does retain a fantasy setting one would expect.I appreciate the game's length.  For me, it did not overstay its welcome and told enough story to satisfy.  Still, if you valuate games based on entertainment hours, perhaps consider picking this up on sale like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extraordinary game with great detail put into every aspect of it. The first thing that strikes is, of course, the visuals, which are very unique. The playable environment is 2-dimensional but visually, there is incredible scope to how these places are rendered. The various buildings, vegetation, and NPCs going about their business remind me of flat set pieces like you would see in a stage play, except these go on forever in the distance and create the sense of being immersed in an actual place. This is totally fitting because a lot of what this game is doing is telling a story. The story itself is pretty simple: the evil frog tribes come, mess things up, and the heir-apparent of the victimized rat kingdom must take up his father's sword and rebuild. It's a universal sort of "hero's quest" story, but what makes this instance of it particularly engaging is the pacing of it, which is realized through a very consistent balance of combat, exploration, and narrative exposition. There is arguably a sparseness to the combat compared to what one might expect in other 2-D games. But every encounter is a very deliberate one which the player character is not allowed to avoid. The fights are also not easy. Imagine playing a heavyweight character in a fighting game; you cannot simply slash through everything, moves have to be well-timed and thoughtful. But this isn't to say that the combat is slow. And there's quite a bit of variety to it in terms of dodging, blocking, counter-attacks, secondary vs primary weapons, and projectiles. Additionally, there's all kind of different items you can equip in terms of armor and weapons, that can be bought, found, or forged. In this way, you can give your character different balances of speed versus power, and of course, make him look super cool. The shear amount of gear really surprised me, and I found myself getting excited and backtracking to various places just in case I missed some hidden spear or shield.  But back to the pacing of how and when combat is encountered: because there are not waves of low-tier enemies to scatter on every screen, each fight feels significant. And each fight usually coincides with some revelation by the player character. Such as "I see there is a band of frogs hiding here, I should find and defeat the leader", or "This new skill I just learned will certainly prove useful moving forward". Those are obviously not literal things the character says, but you get the idea. Each fight is meaningful and serves to move the story along. No jumping on goombas three at a time here. The narrative is not simply a dressing which we are reminded of after a boss fight, it is interwoven with the game play throughout the whole thing. To me, this is the shining aspect of the game. You are not simply pressing buttons, you are enacting a story, a story that has stakes, as silly as that might feel considering you're an anthropomorphic rat with a sword.All in all, this game is such a well-balanced experience and an interesting example of what games have the potential to do. I really hope these people make more of them.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I don't hate this game. It's not a bad game but it is by no means a great one. If you liked Salt and Sanctuary this is basically that but trimmed down and a lot less varied. Story's good, art style is... well you can see it in the screenshots, if you like the style you'll like it all the way through. Gear is utterly boring and literally all feels the same, it's a bit pointless to have it in the game even.THE GOOD: - THE ARTSTYLE: If you like what you see in the screenshots, it looks like that, it just does, some of the best work in this game is on the artstyle and I tip my hat to the wonderful art team who pulled it all together wonderfully.- THE STORY: Whilst nothing extremely interesting has happened so far as of writing this review, it's a good story, the way it's told through the (excellent) narrator is a fresh spin on a formula that normally uses item descriptions for storytelling.THE BAD: - THE COMBAT is... very one-dimensional. Every attack is foreshadowed meaning every boss so far has been just timing and I really hope I'm proven wrong. Even with that, the combat isn't half bad, it feels clunky sometimes sure. Are some of the enemies uninterruptible and stupid? Yeah they are, but it's very much bearable. - THE GEAR: Why in hell are there only 3 different weapons that feel exactly the same. First of all that sucks, because I was expecting weapons to feel varied, when I first opened the chest and saw 3 weapon types I was SO excited to try axes and spears because the sword felt pretty good but not great. Turns out they all do the same thing, they have small light combos and a lunge attack. That's the entirety of the weapons. Sure there's a bow in there but you need arrows for it so it's not reliable to make it your main weapon. You get a heavy axe later but what does it matter it's only useable on really big openings meaning you can't feel like a badass all the time with it because some bosses or enemies just attack too fast for you to get a hit in. AND WHY ON EARTH ARE WEAPONS JUST STRAIGHT STAT UPGRADES? It's so unfun, they all feel exactly the same except slower or faster depending on how heavy they are (usually the heavier the more damage they deal). Even armors aren't cosmetics they're stat upgrades. So armor serves no purpose except to make you wanna explore for easier bosses, which I'm not sure is even worth doing.I'm not through with the game yet, but it sure isn't making tempted to go all the way through with it's somewhat boring combat and absolute lack of variety in gear.

_childDocuments_.review: , revolving around brave rats, immediately caught my interest due to its beautiful hand-drawn visuals that reminded me of some of the childhood’s books I used to read years ago, so I naturally wanted to try it out. Even though audiovisuals are not usually on my priority list when playing games, the incredible amount of details that please your senses from start to finish made me adore this title.Because of that,  managed to hook me from the beginning. Yet, that was not the only surprise! A familiar voice greeted me— one, whom you might know as  from  trilogy.  lovely voice is the only one that will bless your ears, as he narrates the whole story while all of the animals only make incomprehensible noises. Then, the catchy soundtrack only underlines the audiovisual qualities, forming a charming, atmospheric experience.However, is that enough? Or is this just another eye-candy game without much else to offer?Let us start with the premise; your peaceful rat kingdom flourished until it got invaded by villainous frogs who left their scummy pond to plunder your homeland. Unfortunately, they succeeded and left it in ruins. Yet, there is a last light of hope, as our protagonist, prince Redgi, intends to claim the crown, restore the glory of his lands and seek that sweet vengeance.That is about it, as it is the classic tale of a hero gathering their strength and, along with friends, standing up to the greater evil. Sure, that is not a unique nor complex narrative, but I would say that it is just enough in this case. While there are few interesting twists here and there, I rather enjoyed the story because some of its parts were pretty wholesome, and  delivers them amazingly.How does it play, though? I would describe it as a simplistic take on the  subgenre, as you have to travel through several diverse maps, search for various items and then backtrack to use them to get rid of the obstacle that forbade you from progressing further. I said “simplistic” because the world of  is not exactly interconnected, as there is fast travel between the main areas. I am okay with that; however, the issue is that the game forces you to revisit the previous regions often and participate in fetch quests required for finishing the storyline. As  only lasts about ten hours, such an approach is a bit disappointing, as I would prefer a new additional area for those quests. At the very least, the visual representation of those locations change as you progress through the narrative, so there was at least an attempt to make it a tad bit better.On this journey of yours, you will get ambushed by numerous types of animals, whether it would be those barbaric frogs, aggressive insects or other wicked beings. The combat system is simple; you only have light and heavy attacks, plus parrying, dodging and rolling. Despite the abovementioned fairy-tale vibes, the animations are brutal yet delightful to watch, as Redgi performs various finishers on those vicious frogs or dissects the corpses of bugs for their fluid to fill up his health flask.Thus, participating in encounters is enjoyable, especially when you fight with numerous enemy types at once, as it feels fairly challenging and satisfying to play. However, the combat system becomes problematic with some of the later boss fights, as the hitboxes related to their attacks are wonky; once you roll through them safely, while the other time you get hit. Moreover, some bosses tend to spam one type of attack, which can stunlock you, resulting in your immediate death. Even though I overall had a good time with it, these instances were annoying enough and might prove even more challenging for the newcomers to this subgenre.You can influence the combat a bit by choosing from multiple weapons, like swords, hammers and spears; each has its own attack pattern that can prove useful in different situations. My favourite one would be the spear, as it is fast enough to deliver continuous hits before the enemy reacts properly. Additionally, ranged weapons allow you to deal with the annoying flying insect, or you can put a bit of poison on your blades. While both have their use, they are not really a competent part of the weaponry, which is a bit of shame.Apart from that, you can choose from a variety of armours and helmets: light, medium and heavy ones. Each can provide additional defence bonuses against certain enemy types, so it is worth changing them often. They also add to your weight bar, but I honestly never noticed much of a difference nor felt any disadvantage for wearing heavier armour, so I ignored it completely and used whatever I wanted. This whole system is not necessarily bad—it is just way too simple.I guess that would be all, as there is not much else to say.  nails it with its amazing audiovisual presentation and a simple yet wholesome story, but the gameplay drags it down, as it could have been much better. However, I cannot say I was bored at any time, so I do not mind recommending this title for what it is; perhaps it would be better to wait for a sale, though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trash... hitboxes don't make sense, controls are clunky, there are no iframes for the player but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ENEMIES AND BOSSES get iframes. The audio bugs out constantly forcing you to restart the game to fix it. Damage is inconsistent, half the game mechanics aren't explained anywhere, nearly every boss has a 4-5 hit true combos that will 100 to 0 you no matter what, and worst of all, 100% completion is locked behind the hardest difficulty where these problems are increased ten-fold. This game does not deserve any of the praise it gets. Dark Souls 2 is a better game than this mess.Overall this game gets a 3.5/10. The game is ass, but the graphics are unique and it has an interesting soundtrack. The story is fairly neat so if you must play it, don't bother playing on anything other than the easy mode since the game isn't challenging, it's unfair. If you are a completionist, don't play this game, it is not fun to get 100% in and I'm debating if I even want to finish off the last few achievements I need since I did not enjoy this game enough to care.I said it once and I'll say it again: This game is not Hard, Challenging, or Difficult. This game is Cheap, Unfair, and Frustrating. Your skill means nothing to the game and your success is not determined by your abilities.Update: I decided to grind out the 100% and my opinion still stands. The game sucks ass for most of it. The post game content is a little bit better than the base game but some of the bosses still have the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes with inconsistent hit detection. With the Bright Fir Forest expansion this game is a 4/10 (0.5 points up from before) which is still bad. This game does not respect your time, it does not respect you as a player and it is not designed to challenge you. This game is designed to kill you and frustrate you. There is nothing fun or enjoyable about that. Ya sure, it only took me 16 hours to get 100%, but that's due to the extremely limited amount of content available. It's also due to the fact that the game is, once again, not hard or challenging. I played the entire thing on Bloody Whiskers and every single fight was either pathetically easy or cheap and unfair. There was no challenge to the game just rolling the dice and hopping for a favourable outcome. Against enemies where 5 out of 6 of their attacks have no openings for counter attacks, you could be waiting for upwards of 2-3 minutes to get a SINGLE attack before going back to waiting around again. And it's not just mindless waiting, you have to be playing near perfectly dodging everything you can just in case the boss decides to chain together a set of moves that is guaranteed to deal some damage to you with nothing you can do about it. And trust me, that will happen in almost every attempt.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully made game. The game is styled after a story book, with striking visual and a well-spoken (at times quite funny) narrator.  The combat is simple and straightforward, but has very clean movement making the battle still looks very engaging. Lots of customizable options that tend to be just cosmetic difference (which can be a good thing, in a way). The game is quite short, with a decently sized map that offers a few exploration opportunities. Although it would be better if you just stick to the area that your quests lead you to, else you would have to backtrack quite often. Progression can be a bit repetitive because of that, quests often make you go back through the same area as there is only a few fast travel spots. It can be quite a drag because of that, especially in the early game, when you mostly have to tackle quests that make you go underground and kill some bugs than go up get new quest, go back underground, kill some bugs, to gather some measly coins (man, isnt our rat boy supposed to be royalty). Platforming is quite simple so all the backtrack is simply time wasting. Aside from that the gameplay is very fun. You have an one hand weapon to stab your enemy, a two hand weapon to break their shield or sometimes stun them, a shield to block and parry, and your quick rat paws to dodge around. Combat is mostly recognizing your enemy attack type and hitbox, make use of your appropriate tools to deal with them. Personally I find it the most fun to fight a group of enemies, as there is many factors at play, requiring you to swap between your tools constantly. And the devs did a good job creating quite a variety of enemy encounter with this simple combat. Despite the gorey and blood gameplay, the game is really, very silly. Full of rat and frog and mole and many other animal puns. The silliness clashes with the quite serious premier of the game, which honestly make it very charming. Just earlier I saw my ratfolk getting brutally slaughtered by the maurauding frogs (look more like toads tho), and now Im fighting a dude called Molehammad Ali in the arena. 10/10 narrative. Seriously tho, if you havent, you should try the game out. It is quite short, you can easily beat it in under 15 hours. If you just want to enjoy the beautifully crafted world and the silliness, you can also select the easier difficulty. The game also received a bunch of free updates since launch, which basically double the playtime of the main story. The devs are clearly very passionate, so if you want to see more beautiful games like this, go support them.

_childDocuments_.review: I got it on sale for 3 bucks so I can't really complain. I fell in love with the art style and characters as well as the music, all incredible. The combat fell a little flat for me. There are a handful of fights in the game that just feel out of sync. That no matter how perfect your dodge or parry is, you are guaranteed to get hit. Any encounter with 2 or more mobs is also kind of a joke. You're on a 2d plane, this isn't Elden Ring. You basically just get knocked around left and right, sometimes in an infinite chain of stomps and staggers that is, well, supremely stupid. This left me incredibly frustrated on a few fights that should have been easy but I was getting knocked around unlike all previous fights. Its like the animation and the 'alert' are off or so incredibly short (im talking sub-ms) that unless you're a robot, it ain't happening. Nowhere in the game was 'weight' ever covered either, or it's impact on your character though I presume it affects your dodge roll and recovery time but I can't confirm. Seems like a big miss in a game that requires perfect timing. Despite this I'd still recommend it. It's quite short but an enjoyable fairytale romp.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough, during which I found everything and went everywhere, including the expansion. While I don't think this game is really a souls-like, and it's not really a metroidvania, it kinda fits in both categories without going too deep into either. First, the pros:-The narration is awesome. I didn't look up the voice actor for the narrator, but it sounds like the same actor that voices Geralt in Witcher 3 (and there are a couple of nods to the Witcher in the narration), so I'm going to just keep working under the assumption that they're the same. In any case, excellent narration. -The animation style, environments, characters, everything you see, are really pretty. It's just kinda delightful to look at the game.-The boss designs are pretty awesome, and their movesets are pretty unique to the boss (with a couple of minor exceptions), so each battle feels fresh, even if a couple of similarities in combat style arise. -The progressive story and map investigation lends to not missing anything, and the game offers zero missable equipment items, just in case you want to finish off your armory.Some cons:-This game has A LOT of running back and forth. There are moments where you will need to travel back to a point where you received a quest just to have one line of dialogue, and then you need to run back to basically where you had been before to continue the quest. It feels like an artificial inflation of playtime, and it can get tedious.-The boss fight mechanics can be infuriating sometimes. Due to how small your play arena is, and the limitation of a 2D field, there is opportunity for late game bosses to trap you in a combo that basically auto-kills you. This isn't a game-breaker, by any means. But there are moments where it feels like your positioning, dodging, or blocking simply doesn't matter, and that's a bit meh.-You heal using a flask mechanic, but it's VERY slow. There is no way to upgrade your flask to hold more juice, nor a way to drink it faster, so the higher your health (which you can progressively raise throughout the game in a 4-tier upgrade chain), the longer it takes. Late game, this matters, when bosses and creep waves can get into ability spam moments. Not insurmountable, just a bit annoying at times.I guess it all boils down to how much tedium and annoyance you feel like moving through. The game was fun. It was pretty. There were moments where I legitimately felt annoyed at it, but I kept playing to completion. It took me about 6.5 hours to beat my first playthrough. A lot of that time was simply travelling back and forth, it feels like. Was it worth the play? Yeah, I think so.Would I recommend this game? Not to everyone, for sure. And probably not for full price. I got it on a discount, and I'm not sad that I jumped in and played it, since it had been wishlisted forever. This game isn't Hollow Knight. Right now, it isn't even close. But it feels like if the devs keep working at this universe, there is real potential that they could make a spiritual twin to it. And that's why I'll keep my eyes open for the next installment they put out.Be well, all.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. There is a nice charm to Tails of Iron. From the art style, to the characters, the music and the wonderful narration; you can tell a lot of love went into this game. The premise is straight forward. Your kingdom is being overrun by nasty Frog-folk and as the newly crowned King, you must defend it. This means setting off on a grand adventure that takes through farm lands, underground tunnels, mines, and a few other surprising places I'd rather not spoil. There's a few adventure game tropes here in terms of locations and a few that break the mole to deliver a nice change of pace. The great art style does a lot to bring these places and characters to life too. As simple as it is, my main draw to keep playing was the story and seeing where our Hero ends up next. Your adventure is wonderfully narrated by none other than the voice of Geralt of Rivia, Doug Cockle and the whole game feels like you're unraveling a storybook. A violent story book, because combat can get very bloody, with over the top kill animations and the plot alludes to a lot of sinister things. If you had to compare, Tails of Iron is less Hollow Knight and more Salt and sanctuary in terms of gameplay, but with a focus on narrative.Combat is challenging, but never frustrating. The bad guys telegraph their attacks with visual ques, letting you know when to block, dodge or roll out of the way and failure to do the right move is very punishing. Once you get the hang of it though, there's a ice flow to the combat that I loved till the end. Boss fights crank this up to 11 and again, some fights can be difficult or tricky, but I never felt that any of them were unfair. Weapons come in a few flavors, such as axes, swords and hammers, offering different swing speeds and animations, but I often just went with whatever had the better damage stats. They don't really change much in play style. Armor sets give better defense the better quality armor you pick up and some offer resistance to specific baddy types, so you'll end up switching these out for certain fights a lot. I am also a huge fan of things like Mouse Guard and Redwall, so that added another layer of enjoyment to Tails of Iron for me.All in all, I think Tails of Iron is a great game that I highly recommend to anyone who's up to a fun, but challenging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all-time, period.  Bloody Whisker difficulty was perfectly balanced and fair, which is very important for a soulslike.  The parry system is brilliant.  I usually don't like parrying in soulslikes, but it's satisfying and rewarding here.  I like how there's a short window to hold the parry, yet it's not OP feeling.  Excellent variety of armor, weapons, grunt enemies, and bosses.  Not one boss fight was too easy nor too hard on the max difficulty, which I applaud the devs for.  It's hard to fine tune a game's difficulty that precisely and meticulously.  Your character's movement is very well designed and never a hindrance.  I like how you gain a slight speed boost when sheathing your weapon.  Once you master the movement you'll feel like a little ninja.  Excellent sound design, art design, PC performance (no stutter or frame pacing issues), etc. Will buy the sequel on day one.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is extremely compelling. It's challenging enough to be satisfying when you finish a fight but not so difficult as to be frustrating. Most of the tougher bosses only took me 2 or 3 tries to beat on Normal difficulty. The only criticisms of the combat I have are that each sub-class within each class of weapon (one-handed, two-handed and ranged) all feel the same. Swords vs axes vs spears, bows vs crossbows etc, you just pick whichever has the best stats because there's very little difference between them otherwise. Two-handed weapons also seemed almost completely useless outside of breaking the guard of shielded enemies, and even then most of those don't keep their shields up all the time anyway and by the time you've very slowly charged your shield break attack, the enemy has probably already hit you. Those are minor quibbles though. The combat is fun, the art is a great mix of cute and grim, the story is a standard revenge tale but those are almost always compelling and that's certainly true here. I finished the 10-hour main story within a day of purchase. Definite thumbs up from me.One last caveat: there are some slight tones of racism in there - certainly understandable that the protagonist would hate the frogs that did all that stuff, but the script definitely has him hating all of frog-kind, particularly repeating about how they smell. It didn't bother me too much but I did find it a bit on the nose (no pun intended).

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game this is. The art style is great. There's a consistent theme going on, down to the smallest details. How the background and areas around you change depending on the state of the story is very cool. Music is spot on, especially in one of the later areas. You strangely get somewhat connected to these little rats and friends, even when there is no direct voice acting. Very nice to hear Doug Cockle as the narrator, a distinct and soothing voice to accompany you through your travels. I think the length of the game is fine, and I think it's 100% worth its price. A lot of games overstay their welcome these days, and you end up being tired of them when they come to a conclusion. Tails of Iron has pretty good pacing and keeps changing it up without ever getting stale (maybe apart from a small section in the sewers in the first half of the game) Controls are good, but a little bit clunky in the beginning. You get over it quickly though, and the fighting is a lot of fun throughout the whole game. Sometimes challenging but not frustratingly so.Overall a 10/10 experience, looking forward to what these devs end up doing in the future... Would love to see more of my buddy Redgi!
