_childDocuments_.review: An early access indie game which is surprisingly polished.  It is a first person game that doesn't have aliens or zombies to kill which may disappoint some people.  The game is about you landing on a planet with very little and having a mission to terraform it.   Its all about crafting, exploration, researching, gathering, base building and watching you planet develop. There is also some resource management involved (food, water. oxygen).  No gruesome deaths, but should you run out oxygen you will respawn at your original drop pod having dropped a few items. I don't know how much replay value it will have once you have finished it (until it is updated) but I have 10 hours on the game already so definitely worth the money. There is something satisfying watching your barren planet turning into a green oasis.  I recommend you try the free demo as it gives a generous amount of gameplay to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wish I could recommend this game.Pros: Great soundtrack, exploration, discovery, base building, engineering unlock. GREAT idle game, for putting in minimal effort for minimal results over time.Cons: If you get stuck on terrain, you will have to restart from nothing. If you get yourself stuck in a box you built, you have to restart from nothing. If you get stuck far enough from a base, you have to restart with nothing. If you ♥♥♥♥ up your building options, you have to restart from nothing. Super slow progress. FIghting the environment even when it seems silly.All in all, I feel more could have been done to avoid inevitable losses. There should always be an out, even if it is just /unstuck.TLDR: Feels rushed and unfinished. Good music, good environment but bad mechanics. Don't expect anything easy or unbuggy. HOWEVER if you enjoy grind... this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been a huge fan of open world survival ever since I first discovered videogames. I have played through a variety of different titles, but this game totally blew me away. I don’t mean visually, but the way the game is structured is exceedingly satisfying. It feels like the game I have been searching for without even realizing it. I absolutely adore the idea of being able to transform an entire planet and make the world your own. Another thing that makes this experience so much more enjoyable is that there is absolutely zero hostile creatures! It still is able to capture the eerie mystery of the unknown without anything actually hunting after you. It gives the game a relaxed but also a sort of liminal feeling.  Although sometimes I do wish that I could have a companion to hang around every now and then. But my overall experience has been delightful. I will definitely continue to follow along as the game continues to grow and improve. Even in early stages of development I am very impressed! Cannot wait to see what the future holds for this absolute gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is a great game for those that like Satisfactory and Space Engineers - if they had a love child, this is what that would be. The premise is simple enough, look for materials and terraform the planet. While some may find it a bit 'grindey' at first (collecting resources at the start can be quite annoying), it's worth it. Progress is visable and you can see the world change and develop as you go along. As for other aspects of the game:- Exploration is always interesting - 8/10- Strategic base making is something to be aware of (I like a challenge) - 9/10- Storyline is basically non-existent but you're also not on this planet wondering why the heck you're there - 8/10- Bugs, next to none - 10/10- Graphics aren't amazing but good enough to thoroughly enjoy - 9/10- No Multiplayer but the game is very enjoyable regardless. For a lot of games that's difficult to do so - 9/10All in all, I very much recommend this game if you're questioning whether or not it's worth it. 9/10 overall i'd say!Thank you devs for making a game such as this, with only a small team of 2. Massive creds to you both!

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.As a singleplayer experience it is relaxing and captivating. The visual transformation of your environment as you progress is stunning, the different biomes are interesting and the "plot" giving good context, but you won't miss anything essential if following all the small bits and stories scattered around is not your thing. You can decorate as little or much as you want, with the progression always opening new options. Or you can optimize every little detail on your way to fully terraforming the planet. The difficulty settings offer reasonable choices for different play styles. I haven't tried multiplayer yet.Over all, if you like this type of game, you can't really go wrong with this one.Small tip for people with maybe not the strongest PCs: Don't spam fifty butterfly farms all next to each other. Yes, it will be very colorful and pretty, but your GPU will hate you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Just want to get out a review before early access ends, because this game deserves the support. This game is a perfect example of a small team executing on a very specific vision and refining their core appeal while being realistic about other aspects. The Planet Crafter takes heavy inspiration from Subnautica and other games in the survival genre, but differentiates itself with the terraforming mechanic, which is genuinely impressive to watch as you play. Having a noticeable impact on the entire planet is satisfying in a way that constructing a base isn't, even though base building is fun as well. However, this is a very ambitious game from a very small developer, so some aspects like character movement and interaction lack a satisfying feedback, and graphically the game looks modest. Go into it with these limitations in mind, however, and you'll have a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: My gods, this game has had me hooked for ages. I've been playing it every single day for the last like, 5 days. I gained an interest in it after seeing Aavaak and Drae (Both youtubers) play a good little bit of it. I must say, it's so satisfying, working hard for hours and watching the barren planet slowly come to life. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with Planet Crafter; it's a very zen game that really helped me relax. Watching your planet evolve over time is very satisfying, and the transformation from the beginning to the end of the game is remarkable. There are also many little secrets to discover through exploration. The game is stable, though I encountered a few minor graphical bugs—nothing major. In Planet Crafter, you have to build everything yourself. Initially, you don’t have a map or a compass, so you must rely on your sense of direction for part of the game. If you prefer having quest markers, this game may not be for you. There is very little guidance in the game. Your main objective is to terraform the planet and make it habitable, but there is much more to do in Planet Crafter (I won’t spoil anything further). The soundtrack is subtle and fits the game perfectly, enhancing the zen-like atmosphere. The graphics are good—not spectacular—but they are more than sufficient for a game like Planet Crafter.: The story is minimal, but what matters is the story of the planet itself. I won’t say more to avoid spoilers.Planet Crafter can be compared to No Man's Sky, but the two games are quite different. No Man's Sky uses procedural generation and its story unfolds on a universal scale, whereas Planet Crafter focuses on terraforming a single planet. The environments and various secrets in Planet Crafter are handcrafted, unlike in No Man's Sky.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical about this game, but I was bored and I like terraforming games so I gave it a shot and oboy was I hooked.The gameplay loop is rather simple:Build stuff, explore and gather, come back unlock new blueprints and build new stuff from the gathered resources. New buildings and machines are unlocked during exploration thanks to your terraforming efforts. The frequent unlocks and the slow change of barren world to a thriving lush plant is very rewarding.Pacing was great. Up until the last tier of terraforming there was no idling or grinding. I am at the end of my playthrough and I still quite a few areas of the map to explore. A few thing I would change, prio ascending. Allow drones to collect all item types even though you can not craft them.Allow autocrafting of all resources such as larva, seeds, genes, fish/frog eggs. Mainly to improve the speed of the last tier of terraforming.Encourage biodiversity. Covering ½ of the starting area with Shreox trees is unsightly. Display player position on the map.Frog eggs in the wild should respawn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: For me it was totally worth the price.The game is not finished yet. If you rush the game, you can easily beat it around 30h. I was exploring everything and used the rocket very late, which slowed progression down.Apropos slowing down. When you develop your base and build more structures, it's possible that the fps will go down. I have a PC from 2016 and I have no problem playing something in FUll HD. When the stages with trees began it really dropped and began to stutter. My solution was that I used the teleporter from the endgame and moved all my industrial objects far away that it won't render when I'm in my base. The same with flower and treespreader.To clarify this is a game with terraforming aspects, a little bit of survival elements and base building aspects. At this point ( Ver 0.4.015) there is no automation like in other games. That means you have to get the ressources all by yourself. It will get easier later on, but in the beginning and midgame that means a lot of travelling by foot or jetpack.I hope that there will be some kind of optimization. Otherwise I'm afraid the performance with upcoming updates and later stages will become more and more poor.Do not forget to use the rockets as early as possible. It will boost your Terraforming index a lot. I was nearly ready to quit, cause there was no progression, before I used it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Subnautica without the combat.  Lots of exploration and resource gathering.There are obviously places in the world for the dev(s) to expand with more content, so I'm excited to see where this game goes!Edit - well over 100 hours and at least 3 full playthroughs and I'm still loving this game! _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The doctors tell me as I get older, I need to exercise my brain.  They suggest crossword puzzles, sudoku, that sort of thing.  Me personally, I think this is the game to exercise my brain.  No stress of getting to certain levels within time limits. No other characters or players shooting at me.  Nothing jumping out and killing me.   I absolutely love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this one.  The best way I can think to describe it is if you combined Subnautica and one of those clicker games.Pros:It has the exploration, survival, and building similar to Subnautica.  You start in a crashed escape pod and have to build bases to survive and eventually terraform the planet.  So far the only enemy I have found is the planet and environment.It has progression like a clicker game.   You build machines to increase various terraforming metrics.  As the metrics increase, you unlock additional, better machines to speed up the terraforming process.I really like how the planet changes around you as it is terraformed. Cons:Some people may not like the graphics.   I tend to prefer gameplay over graphics, so this doesn't bother me.Controls are a bit clunky at times.  Jumping and falling doesn't feel natural.  It's like there is no gravity and you kind of just follow the terrain.  I found this really noticeable when I got the jetpack.  This doesn't really bother me that much and it may improve over time since it's in Early Access.I've noticed a few small bugs here and there, but that's expected in Early Access and nothing so far as been game breaking.I don't yet know how "complete"the game is since I'm only about 8 hours in, but so far I would say it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I got so hooked to this game it was ridiculous and I'm a bit sad now because I've run out of things to do. Even though the game is early access it felt like a finished game to me and I've encountered 0 bugs. I think the game will only get better as they keep adding stuff to it, as it is now the late game doesn't really feel complete as there is no ending, you kinda just stop when you get bored. After you spend hours collecting fishes and frogs you kind of start to question if there's any other purpose to your existence and you don't feel that sense of accomplishment that you did in the beginning when you were in the process of making a planet viable. Still though I've enjoyed every minute of it and I'll be looking forward to future updates.P.S. if you play the demo and you purchase the game afterwards you can continue your demo save file all the way to the late game without any problems.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A moderately challenging (especially early game) and fun space survival game with a truly unique story-line. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a highly recommend.  The world is beautiful (even in the early red sky desert mode) and they gui is simple and intuitive.  It is very satisfying watching the terrain and sky change around you and opening new areas to explore by raising the heat to melt ice that is blocking the path. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I do not go through the effort of writing a review on games in general, so here we go. This game is absolute brilliance. You start out with nothing, on a barren wasteland, the game has a brilliant way of portraying what sort of struggle humankind would go through living on another planet. There are just the right number of hints to push you in the right direction. If you play this game, take the time to immerse yourself in the gameplay and draft your own story. As you discover more areas on the planet, untapped resources become available which in turn brings innovative technology. Start out with humble beginnings struggling to survive and work your way to a planet that slowly but surely comes alive. The progress system highlights what you need to do to unlock new tech and through the process, your surroundings start changing. This is a true Terraformer at heart and the devs seem to have a wild but realistic imagination. Right up my alley. If you are a space enthusiast, enjoyed Subnautica and/or satisfactory this game is for you. While the game is in early access, the story is comes in second best to Subnautica, not sure if the developers want to go there, but I reckon this would add extra flare to it, in my opinion. The logistics system is less complicated than satisfactory (A big plus for me). Brilliant 10/10 would play again, but not sure if I want to start again after sinking 29 hours into a base that I have already established. The replay ability could use some work, hopefully new planets/moons will come along later on, like terraforming a moon of a thriving planet, another idea would be to reverse the terraforming of a planet, basically a planet that went too far a long and now needs to be saved would be a nice touch, this would add to the replay ability of the game, however I think the devs should continue doing what they are doing. After 29 Hours of gameplay, every hour was worth it. I think the devs should continue doing what they are doing. As you reach late game (29 hours in) there is a lack of things to do but 29 hours? I’m not complaining, it was a brilliant experience and I would encourage you to buy the game and support the developers. I would love to see how far this game can go… One last thing,, DEVS PLEASE HAVE MULTIPLAYER in the pipelines, excuse the caps xD

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so first off: i had a ton of fun playing this game. It's amazing to see how you craft the planet, and everything evolves. I want to give it a positive review just for that. It also has some great story elements, and the explore / build / explore / build cycle is really addictive. Again, I want to rate it positively for that.But theeeeen. In the very late game, it feels super grindy. Watch the number go up, upgrade production capacities so number goes up faster. Even if you have nothing else to do.Minor spoilers ahead:the portal with the different exploration sites is a great idea, but they are bland ,empty, have no story and get repetitive really fast.And then there are the three endings. They.... are all ♥♥♥♥. I really really did not enjoy any of them. If you enjoyed the game, take this advice: stay. Don't leave. Just.... stay. End the game on your own terms. No flying back into space. Thank me later.So, sadly, its not a recommendation from me for this game. The last 1/3rd of it were just painful. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: At standard difficulty the initial oxygen depletion rate in the game is absurd as the starting oxygen tank lasts for a shorter time than an average person can hold their breath. Additionally, the rates at which food and water are consumed are similarly unrealistic. It feels as though the player character has the metabolic rate of a hummingbird. This method of adding difficulty is not only lazy but worse than that immersion breaking. Choosing an extraterrestrial threat as a gameplay element would have been a superior design choice. Furthermore, it is puzzling that the player character is not provided with a compass at the onset of the game, given that constructing a functional compass does not necessitate a microchip and is considered basic survival knowledge.Constructing a base is straightforward and uncomplicated. However, the graphics are rudimentary and require further optimization. Playing this on a laptop with an NVIDIA 1050 at low settings and 720 resolution is quite challenging.Despite these issues, I am willing to continue playing for a while longer to see if things improve. However, at this point, I am not impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked it. It has a sense of urgency to it because of the food/water/air-gauges without stressing you out, which I love. Overall it's just a really nice resource management/base building game. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Still working on my first play through and I am enjoying the game. Has no multiplayer, which it would benefit from for replayability (games like this are more fun with others in my opinion). A single play through is really all you need to get everything out of the game. Best way to describe the gameplay in my opinion is to compare it to an idle clicker game almost. You build machines that add to one of a few different stats. As you advance, you get more efficient and powerful machines and need to source material to build them and the electric generators to power them. You never have to worry about losing anything to recycling machines and machines don't break on their on so its only about advancing forward in resources.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obviously an obsession.   The person who wrote this game really loves it.   You can feel it everywhere in the way the game was crafted, and it really brings some emotional relevance to the playthrough.  That said, they could use some help.  The ambition is too big for two people and it shows in general lack of polish everywhere. The star of the game is the way the world changes as you terraform it.   I've never seen this done elsewhere, and I think it's a wonderful core idea.   As a hard sci-fi lover, I'd like to see it much more science based and less hand wavy.   I’d also love a little help buying into how the tiny scale of the changes we’re making could affect the whole planet.  Later in the game, I really think the introduction of things like plants, fish, and frogs should always be directly tied to player activities.  In my playthrough, for example, I saw fish in a cenote before I had done anything at all with fish.  I've played through the game twice now.  I think the game is too fast in the beginning and too slow later.   It is a great idea to get the player to first "world change" pretty quickly so they can see what the game has to offer, but we could slow down some of the early progression after that, and give the player a chance to dig in.The automation comes way too late.   It basically just shows up for the final in game push, and doesn’t feel fully integrated into the experience.   The endings need a lot of work.  None of them feel good.  Not saying a sad ending can't be a great ending, but that takes a lot of art, and these endings are just depressing.   I think it would be fine for the default corpo ending to remain depressing, but the people who want to work harder for the space socialist or criminal endings should get something a little brighter imo.   In particular, I think for the criminal ending you should think like a heist movie.   I'd love to see the player stick it to the corpo's.  Steal the planet, or at least some non-insignificant amount of it’s resources.Also, what about the explorers who came before us?  The ones we meet through their text logs. The ones who undoubtedly died on this rock.   I think we should get a little catharsis, we should find their final resting place.  A couple skeletons and some environmental storytelling (As is exemplified in fallout) could really wrap those stories up well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Working on a barren planet and watching it go from a complete wasteland to a tropical paradise is so satisfying. Yes, it requires a lot of work and this game is definitely a slow-burn (especially if you play solo), but putting in the hours is so worth it.Not to mention the fact that there's no enemies in the game, no real dangers aside from the usual survival dangers and the occasional meteor hitting you or your base. It's very relaxing and exactly what I need after a long day of work.Give this game a go if you like survival games, or if you're looking for a chill game to play with a friend or even just solo. You can even play it with a podcast or a YouTube video in the background, like I do. It's such a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty relaxing game to play where you can build a new earth during a time our real earth is slowly catching on fire and dying. I love blasting off rockets and watching the greenery take over and even discovering new secret areas when trees start forming. The fact this game is fairly time gated and can be sped up by crafting and making a good base makes it feel like there is always something to do and more than one way to play it. The subtle implication of the planet being "haunted" is also a pretty neat angle and I wonder where it will go. If you like running around in open world games just for the sake of exploration - this is a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: While it's only truly good for one play-through, it's an amazing experience to see a deserted red rock become something far more than what it started as. It's absolutely spectacular and the world grows, develops, and changes with you. It's absolutely worth the money, and with multiplayer you can share the awe-inspiring moments with others.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This will be the first time I write a review but the game deserves it. It is AMAZING. I was really looking into something like this for a while. Downloaded the demos, played for an hour and I had to buy it. While it is relaxing you will constantly keep an eye on your resources, oxygen and whatnot. I've seen some people asking for some sort of enemies attacking the base but I hope this is not the case. I really like the goal of terraforming the planet without feeling paranoid as other survival games. Maybe add something like dungeons or an "alien" spaceship that crashes and the monsters are in there or something like that for players who really want to fight something.If you are looking for the next same formula of having to kill stuff to continue advancing, being paranoid all the time because of creatures attacking, this is not for you but it is a really fun and amazing experience and I can't wait to see what is next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Its gameplay loop hits the spot for me. Exploration is fun, biomes are unique, resources are diverse, automation is satisfying and progression is tangible. It feels wonderful to watch the terraforming numbers go up and the planet slowly transform before your eyes. It is also quite relaxing, as no creatures are out to get you, you are free to roam the planet within the limits of your oxygen, food and water needs. Despite some rough edges and bugs, this game is well worth the price and the time. Multiplayer is functional and fun. Hardcore mode and several game customisation options add replayability value. The devs are also constantly working on the game, releasing free updates, and expanding their dev team. Good for them. I'm a fan <3

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 44 hours at this point - probably should have done things like sleeping during that time, but, well, just one more blueprint unlock... I love this game so much - it feels like when I first discovered Subnautica (admittedly, more of a bleak and desolate hellscape when you arrive, rather then a stunning tropical reef, but hey, that's what you're there to fix).Firstly, it runs smoothly, the controls are intuitive and I haven't discovered any major bugs or glitches. There are occasional bits of scenery which are a bit clunky, but then it's a small, early access game with a two-person dev team, the quality is amazing considering that.It irons out all the gripes I've had with other space survival/crafing games - awkward UI. impossible survival, boring maps, ugly buildings, stressful conditions, lack of heart etc.It is an incredibly feel-good game. For once, you come to a planet, not to strip-mine it for resources and slaughter all the indiginous species, but peacefully, to bring it to life and make it thrive and be beautiful. There is no combat, a decision I applaud, and it's so refreshing to play a game where you can really do some good and see the difference you're making. (The only other game I've played with this 'Johnny Appleseed' theme is Green Project, a little pixel graphics indie game which I also recommend - it has heart!). After playing games like Satisfactory where it's beautiful but you're forced to commit ecological vandalism, this is a breath of fresh air. (Well, not actual fresh air, maybe you can create a breathable atmosphere eventually?).It's also a really good message - there's nothing like carefully nurturing a barren world until you start seeing plants trying to take hold, to make you appreciate living, growing things. I hope it goes far!There is also an intriguing story lurking here - I understand it's still in progress, but I'm excited to see where it leads!Back to practicalities - in terms of balance and progression, the game works well, but it pays to give attention to all the aspects of terraforming to avoid reaching milestones with, say, O2 levels, and then having to wait ages for your heat or pressure to catch up because the blueprints you just unlocked requires a component you can't make yet. In my case, I didn't send up any rockets for ages, and they make a huge difference!It also pays to explore the map thoroughly, and pay attention to detail. It's an amazingly rich and interesting map, full of secrets and hidden corners, and you can find some precious resources tucked away if you look carefully. There are also a lot of beautiful sites to place your base, some of which only become accessible later. All in all, it's still in early access and the devs are working on more content, but I'm already hooked, and excited to see where it leads.

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very chill and relaxing game. Nothing to fight except the oxygen/food/water meters. If you're looking for something fairly stress-free to play that isn't going to give you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ aneurysm out of sheer frustration, this is a good one. The visuals are nice, and the atmosphere is nonexistent until you create it... You literally turn the planet from a barren wasteland into a lush alien world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I can sense this game has a lot of good potential! I enjoy the way your curiosity is rewarded.Progression is quite slow, and generally a bit grindy here and there. But there's more good than bad in this one, for sure! So far it's my favorite terraformation game, after not having my terraformation itch scratched by purely strategic games. I like being in the middle of the action and seeing the planet change live as you progress.Has the early access hiccups here and there, naturally, but I still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of the survival genre I can't recommend this game.  The concept is good, but it needs serious work.  And I don't just mean the code, I mean the core gameplay concept needs to be tweaked because what is here atm is a game where you build machines to make a number go up.  The more machines you build, the faster the number goes up.  When the number reaches a certain limit you win the game.  That's IT.  No environmental threats except occasional meteors you can largely ignore or exploit for extra resources.  The environment is bland, and I get that it's supposed to get better as the game goes on and be bland to start, but not *this* bland.  And when it does get more colorful it's still pretty basic.  There's just no real game here.  Wish I'd bought Satisfactory instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The game kinda just throws you into the world and lets you figure things out for yourself, it can feel rather boring at first, as you aimlessly build machines that seem to do nothing at all. That is, until you start visually seeing the world change around you, and all of that building sorta contextualizes itself in a way that very few other games manage to do. The direct impact you have on the world makes this game equally addictive and endearing, and I have a blast with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Sorta 50/50 on this one.Overall, I enjoy the game and what it has to offer, but there are some things that bug me like the building mechanics, the endings and some other quality of life issues. Planet Crafter (PC) is a neat little time passer and seeing the effect you as the PC are having on your planet is awesome which I have to give credit for, so you can tell this was certainly done from a committed, caring team. Kudos to you all.However, the buildings crashing into each other and weird floating issues/artifacts with some buildings caused displeasure on the eyes and I know that given a few more months, PC will put out another patch or two to fix it. My biggest gripe however is the endings which is spoilered below for obvious reason.Overall, a solid game and pretty nice, but certainly needs some QoL fixes and some changes to the endings.3/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The Planet Crafter is a one in a million type of game. It throws you into a wasteland on Mars from space for you to get rid of your prison sentence by terraforming the planet into a Utpoia of sorts. You start by making low tier equipment then eventually you can explore deeper and further on the planet to discover more minerals to help you terraform and in doing so it helps you by giving you the ability to make better equipment. 9/10. The reason why its not 10/10 is because once you have completed the game nothing comes at a challenge anymore but thats way after you finish whats available in the game right now.Updates roll on on a couple month interval basis.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most amazing Early access games i've played thoughout last yesrs-  There's exactly enough time to enjoy current terraformation level. Before you get bored of grinding to next stage, you get to where you wanted to be and enjoy new stage of terraforming. Same with automation-  For some reason if feels extremely good to see conversion of your labor into how the planet transforms into something beautiful step by step. For me it is best and most enjoyable part of the game-  All bioms are quite beautiful and stunning first time you see them.-  Building is quite good except having no snapping outside and inability to build few certain buildings on platform structures, which logically could be built on it All machines look realitic and have steam and other stuff.-  Great thanks to devs for updating game each 2 months. it is amazing to come back to game so soon to enjoy updated content-  Graphics a little bit outdated, also you see abrupt mountains from time to time. still it doesn't disturb from enjoying the game and it's still early access-  There's bunch of hidden shacks with computer diaries. The info is interesting, but maybe audio logs would help to delve into the story more-  The only threat here is a gravity and low 02, but even falling from high plarform won't kill you. it can be good for ones who just want to enjoy the game, but would be nice to have more threats (maybe would be added with animal terraformation stage).Even with the cons it is one of the most enhoyable games for 5-10 evening. Terraforming the unknown planet and seeing it transform is very very fun. 100% recommend to buy and play it
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: BE WARNED: NOT AN ACTION GAME!! this is a beautifully crafted terraphoming simulator  you get to ecplore a hand made made map and work to bring this barren lifeless planet to life turning it from a tomb to a garden it wont be easy it wont be done over night but youll be right there on the ground level seeing it happen i still remember giggling myself silly when i crested the hill to see water actualy filling up the lake beds if you want to enjoy your time and relax highly recomend this game and be sure to show the devs some love as well to thank them for this absolute gem
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Cool peaceful survival game where you need to watch your hunger, thirst and oxygen level.It's all about exploring, finding minerals, farming for food/water/oxygen, and crafting. Build and improve your base. Terraform the planet and watch it change from a barren lifeless rock to an earth-like planet with blue sky, lakes, nature, insects, fish and other animals. Research gives you a lot of cool improvements and is unlocked as you progress with terraforming your planet.This is NOT a shooter survival game with hostile creatures. There are no weapons or anything that want to kill you  - except for thirst, hunger or you running out of air.You start your game as a prisoner with a life sentence, but have been given a chance to terraform a planet and get your freedom.While exploring the planet you find shipwrecks with new technology and useful materials.Your main mission is to terraform the planet and find the story behind the planet and why there are so many crashed shipwrecks. What happened to the people before you?You will find hidden underground bases, ancient cities and an interresting lore.I highly recommend this game if you like the idea of terraforming a planet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I think the main aspect of this game is one of the features No Man's Sky is missing. You start with very little resources that allow you making short trips around your base and step by step increase certain parameters of the planet's atmosphere. 4 Parameters at first, later a 5th one is added. You unlock new stuff just by increasing these numbers and this new stuff usually makes the old stuff obsolete.However, seeing the world change around you is a really nice touch and the occasional asteroids raining down on you really are exactly how they should be. The changes aren't just visually though. The way you play the game evolves over time as well, which keeps the game fresh the whole time. During late game I miss options for being creative within the game (like creating all the housing for people starting the colony). Since the game is early access it's possible that stuff will be added during the development process.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game, despite being a survival/crafting game, is actually pretty relaxed.  Once you get past a certain point, the only thing that can really kill you is your own stupidity...there are no aliens or creatures to fight, just a world that requires your work and a certain amount of planning and attention.It's not without its quirks...building can be a bit fiddly at times, and things don't always (or easily) snap together the way you'd like them to.  It doesn't even pretend to be scientifically accurate. And it's not complete, as of this writing; there are stages and features and areas to find and explore that are still in the works.  But it IS satisfying, if you're willing to take it at its own pace and can remember that it's not a Satisfactory clone...you don't have to build a gazillion machines and hoard up piles of raw materials.  You can watch the world slowly change (note, some changes will catch you by surprise if you don't think ahead).  And it actually FEELS like a game...something you're doing for fun...and not a second job.If you want a game that'll let you play at your own pace, and gives you a healthy dose of being able to build to your own tastes instead of having to follow some kind of strict optimization regimen, it's worth taking a look.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A game in the same vein as some of my favorites, astroneer, minecraft, Conan Exiles, etc.  It's survival crafting, but with a focus on eventually terraforming a dead planet into a lush livable world.  While the science isn't hard, the flexible nature of it allows for great game play and easy to pick up concepts.It's not perfect, but it's still in early access.  Some resource bottlenecks feel very arbitrary, and I wish there was a way to generate some resources that are finite  (seeds, white crystal, etc)  I very much enjoyed the time I spent with the game and will check it out again at a later date for certain.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very impressed. If you like survival crafting and pretty butterflies make you giggle, this is the game for you. I'm a 22 y/o male and I was having a couple rough days while playing this game and it was such a nice reprieve from life. I giggled like a little girl when I made some good progress into insect stage and finally had bees and butterflies flying around my base. It's incredibly satisfying to slowly turn a planet from a cold, dead wasteland into a beautiful paradise filled with life. Only caveats are that I am NOT a fan of the inventory system and had to get an item stacking mod to make it less painful (stacks of 10 items felt fairly balanced), and also that the late LATE game right before full terraformation takes AGES. It's an insane slog and I think they literally expect you to just leave the game running for several hours to get to the end. I had to get another mod that let me multiply resource generation when I was just waiting to escape and it still took several minutes of waiting with EVERY resource multiplied 100 times (yes, I had 10+ of every rocket as well long before this and 5-10+ of every highest tier machine). Mammal stage wasn't super intriguing to me, but I could see how it could be fun for the right person. Everything else was fantastic though. I was blown away by some of the exploration once I got into mid game. Worth full price, absolutely worth it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now the building controls are very bad; the only things you can place that will link up are living quarters and these can't have any overlap with the ground so they usually end up floating in mid air - ladders end short of the ground and don't align properly, some machines can be placed on structures others can't (with no explicable reason) and worst of all, foundations don't line up with anything. Considering the game is about grinding (with little survival threat) and building I'd have expected the building aspect to be solid even if there were only a few things to build... but it isn't. I'm about 90% of the way through. It's been fairly enjoyable in places but I can't be bothered to keep doing the same thing over and over to get to the end. Additionally - and maybe the worst thing about the game - I can't see how there would be any replay value unless the world was completely randomly generated and there was more jeopardy.Overall: not bad for a single play-through but grindy with very janky base building. Deserves a positive review but only just.

Game balance and pacing are just fancy words. 4. _childDocuments_.review: NOT READY YET!Not even sure how I managed to sink 40 hours into this.  It speaks to the utter level of addiction this game can muster from a player.  Unfortunatly the game loop at current development level flattens out by 15 hours mark to just building the same 3 things and launching rockets.  Basically as soon as you finish tree's unlock it lacks anything really after that.  i powered through and unlocked insects but it didn't appear to make any difference aside from changing the next unlock to Fish. Aside from choosing what type of tree's to plant;  you have little individual effect on the biomes.  Really got the feeling that there was nothing to do at the tree's unlock stage.  Game has promise but really needs some more interactive story, environmental or mission elements to give it some flavor before I can really recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: The game is nice and chill, with quite a lot to explore and build. It's very satisfying to see the impact of your terraformation on the planet. The surival elements(besides Oxygen) are relevant only in the early game, the game is more about resource collection, base building and later automisation than anything else-Earlygame is really engaging with all of the unlocks to build, wrecks to discover and caves to explore. -Midgame is full of setting up productions and early automatisation and ucovering blocked paths from early exploration. -Sadly by the lategame the game becomes quite sluggish and slow. Eventho I feel like we had a pretty well setup base(almost everything automised/endless resources) and high terraforming output(it felt high, I didn't compare it to anything), we found ourselves quite often just not knowing what to do besides waiting for next unlock(and half of the time they were useless in the end)Overall, I'd say it's an ok game and worth the price. _childDocuments_.review: Lovely game! Absolutely recommended :)The gameplay resembles "Subnautica on land" because you need to explore the game world with its different biomes, you'll gather and grow ressources, craft and build (equipment, bases and different types of machinery). Later on you can even dive into large lakes, (albeit currently without underwater plants), plus just like Subnautica, the game is not providing you with actual quests other than the tutorial tasks (no rewards for those) and is not really telling any story to follow (so far), instead you'll find messages that others (NPCs) have left here and there with a bit of a background story.Your task of terraforming a planet is really unique though, and that's why I'm in love with Planet Crafter :) It's awesome to behold how the look of the barren desert game-world changes into a beautiful green scenery with blue sky, all caused by the work of your own hands. It's really cool to watch how the lakes fill up, how the ice melts, the water level rises (and rises, rises, and then rises even more!), how the yellow-orange sand slowly turns into green "moss", how grass tufts start to sprout, how algaes start to form around your growers on the water, grass and beautiful flowers grow anywhere you want them to, then even unique looking types of trees... And I totally love the (new) different kinds of meteor showers!Another unique task of this game is building "base camps" along your way to provide yourself with oxygen and water at first, also storage, later on with food etc. This is something that I always loved to do (like in GRAV for example), but no other game than Planet Crafter actually requires. Plus: plundering the wrecked space-ships and underground hideaways is a real fun activity too :DThe game is very well made, I didn't find any game-breaking bugs found so far even though the game is still in EA :) Just beware of saving and reloading inside of wrecks ;) FYI: I've currently only just reached "insect stage" and a "fish stage" will be up next. It's a nice thought that we can bring the initially "dead" planet to life this way :)Can't believe these amazing graphics were made by only two people! Love the large space-ship-wrecks so much ^_^ Their different shapes look really cool. And the bunks even come with small toilets - so cute :D Actually, everything else is awesomely designed too: the many things we can craft and build, the lovely sky, the meteors that come crashing down, the falling sand from the cliffs - it all looks very beautiful and makes your stay on this planet enjoyable :)Story-wise there's still work to do though I guess... Well, it's EA after all, so let's see how this will evolve :)Also in terms of game balance, I'm not 100% happy (yet) - while being aware that everyone has their own ideas and taste of course.Here's some additional thoughts:1. We're a convict with the task of terraforming a cold desert planet and bringing it to (green) life. Someone (presumely the "Sentinel Corps" that left the message on the screen in our capsule) must have invested a lot of money: we were brought to this planet, were dropped down in a sturdy capsule, we got a fine space suit and a sophisticated multitool.On the other hand we aren't provided with much food in order to survive, and we brought no seeds to grow?! Even worse: our food grower blueprint is not available from the start? This significantly reduces our chance to survive and by that our chance to fulfill our task. If we fail, all the investments for this project will have been for naught... This does not make much sense to me.* Possible solution: just let the food grower blueprint unlock very early in the game or even be unlocked from the start, and provide us with at least one pack of seeds. We'll need to find aluminium in order to craft the food grower anyways and then we will also have to wait for the food to grow.** I'd like it if the different game modes could come with different starting options - relaxed game mode with more and better seeds for example, while hardcore mode could come with accidentally spoiled seeds so that we'll have to find seed packs first.2. (Randomly) filled chests are lying around all over the place. Also: you'll find better and rarer stuff depending on your terraforming progress. Why? Who dropped those in the middle of nowhere - and why would chests in your starting area contain much rarer stuff if you only open them later in the game?* Possible solution: wouldn't it make more sense if we found backpacks next to spacefarer's remains (empty spacesuits or something) instead of chests?** Wouldn't it be better to have fixed findings in all those storage containers - but differently depending on the chosen difficulty mode? The current randomness will just make players save the most chests for later, and also will lead them to saving their game progress just before opening any storage container, then reloading until the randomly generated content will satisfy them...3. So we can deconstruct chests, a few solar panels, heaters and specific iron girders, but nothing else in those really large wrecks? I would love it if we could gain cloth by deconstructing bunk beds in spaceships rather than randomly collecting cloth from chests. Actually: the more we could deconstruct and re-use/recycle or even fix in order to make it work again, the better in my opinion ;)4. How believable is it to build a whole building module that also procudes oxygen (!) out of nothing but iron and titanium? And we don't even have to craft semi-manufactured products beforehand for such large multifunctional objects? Not even to speak of Biodomes T2 with several tree types inside even though we don't use any tree seeds for their construction...* Possible solution: how about adding oxygen-producing algae or slime or so to the buildings? Basically an organic substance that our capsule should have integrated somewhere, since it too produces oxygen? We could take part of this substance from the capsule and when erecting a building, this substance would be put either in tanks next to the door in order to produce oxygen, or maybe even into a whole layer of the building. After it multiplies with the help of sunlight, we could then again gather a part of it in order to erect more buidings that will produce oxygen as well ... and so on.5. I'm also a bit irritated by message screens left by former crash-survivors, while our crafted "signs" are much smaller and we cannot write and leave behind message screens ourselves. * Possible solution: it would be nice to read different messages - those that were sent to the now-wrecked ships or abandoned bases (so that they could provide bits of the game world's background-story) rather than "last words" left by the castaways themselves...** Alternatively, I'd actually also be happy enough if we could "write" our own message screens ourselves too just like the shipwrecked ones did ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. The graphics are pretty good, not amazing. The soundtrack does not annoy you, and is good to listen to. This is repetitive like other crafting and survival games. I am glad I didn't see any "beginner's videos" because I might have been upset when I found out the map will not change.Again, I don't have to worry about something killing me. It's a strategy of using finite resources to build something that moves me along. I will play this any day of the week.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow.I didn't complete the game yet (but hey, I have lakes already), but I can tell you: I absolutely love it.It's not your typical "build a base on Mars". I cannot put into words how much I appreciate devs' choices.1. Changing world. You're not just doing bigger numbers, you can visually see how it affects the world around you, slowly. Not "congrats you achieved 100 points, now there's water everywhere". It gives so much satisfaction, and because map is huge, you can visit far-away points once in a while and be suprised how much they changed.2. No fighting, no fear. If you're a pro gamer like me, you will appreciate there's no jump-scare, no "oh god it's dark, something will attack me", you're going into wrecks without fear.3. Easy mode and keep equipment. Again, as a pro gamer I very much appreciate when I can just chill my beans and wander around without fearing for my life. Especially when you get lost.Game still needs some adjustments, there are some bugs sometimes, and please give us stacking, but overall I expected a lot from this game, and I got even more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game since the alpha version, (at least I think it was the alpha version) and it has come a long way. If you enjoy being able to leisurely build at your own pace, then I implore you to think about getting this game. Yes, it did just come to early access, but you will have the best chance to watch a fantastic game come to life right in front of your eyes, almost literally! I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys any Open-World Survival Craft games. 10/10. I can't wait to see what they do next for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is truly an amazing game! From the moment I first entered the world of Planet Crafter, I was fascinated by its immense variety and endless possibilities. The graphics are breathtaking, and the environments of the planets feel so realistic that I felt like a real space explorer.One of the best aspects of this game is the freedom it gives players to create their own worlds. From crafting ecosystems to building cities and exploring different planetary landscapes, the possibilities are truly limitless. Every detail can be customized according to one's imagination, providing a sense of absolute creative expression.The gameplay is also great. The controls are intuitive and easy to learn, allowing players to quickly immerse themselves in adventures and explore new worlds without unnecessary delays. Exploration is rewarding, and every corner of the planet holds something new and exciting.The community around the game is fantastic as well. Forums and social media are full of inspirational stories and ideas from other players, adding another dimension to the game and encouraging collaboration and sharing among fans.Overall, Planet Crafter is a great choice for anyone who loves exploration, creation, and imagination. It's a unique experience that's worth trying out and exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is two things I love: survival-crafting, and a world that changes according to the player's progress. As you terraform the planet, some places will open that weren't accessible before, new resources will appear, and of course everything will  a lot different. It feels great.Add to that a world that is beautiful before and after you change it, lots of places (and secrets) to explore, some pretty fun tech, and lots of room for future development, and you get something you definitely should try, at least if those things are to your taste.When I originally posted this review, I wrote:  That is of course now obsolete. 2 years and a bit later, the game is now past 1.0, pretty mature, and expanded a lot since that original review. Of course, it remains a strong recommendation from me. I beta-tested this game, and got a free key on account of that. But I was planning to buy it anyway, and of course I wouldn't have volunteered to beta-test if I didn't think the game was worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game after watching ImKibitz play on YouTube.  Understanding it's early access I assumed it would be a buggy mess.  However, I got far more than I paid for.  The game immediately sucked me in for an 18 hour play session.  The game provides a massive scale that seems small at first, but you can find a small crack in a rock wall that leads you to a massive area.  I'm now in the "late game" and I'm still finding massive areas with secrets.  I'm also finding areas that I assume will be added later in the game.   There is only one "edge of the world" (sand wall) indicating the games "early access" status.   Everything else is so expansive with only the ore-generation being your guide to where the content ends.  Progression continues as you explore reducing the "grind".  My only complaint is the sound track doesn't match with the overall "relaxing" feel of the game.  It has the undertones of the deep water portions of Subnautica.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I took time away from the game to post this. I've been searching for a couple weeks to find a new game on my steam deck. Unlimited budget, and I kept refunding game after game just unsatisfied. Then I came across this gem.At first, it felt like a low budget survival Sim and nearly dismissed it. But then I started noticing the sky slowly change into a tint of blue... and then I saw clouds for the first time... Then it started raining... And then my base started to flood because it turned out I had built at the bottom of a basin that was destined to be a lake!This is an incredible game with a strong sense of achievement. I doubt it has replayability but for the price you get a good number of hours of playtime before you're done.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very addictive open world survival game where it is mostly you versus the environment. If you ever felt Subnautica didn't let you build enough and upgrade more and you got tired of all the creatures in the way ... well, this is your game. It's an addictive loop of terraforming a planet so that you can eventually leave. That sounds so simple, but there will be tons of collecting, near death experiences from food/water/air loss, wreck explorations, hidden cave and mine reveals, and lots of building and upgrading as you unlock more crafting recipes and gear. The game has solid play, based in the Unity engine. Graphics and effects are quite good for this title based on its sale price. Sounds are decent, with a very light smattering of eerie and atmospheric music along with tool and machine sounds as you build. But this game has, "just one more thing," pull in spades.  You'll be returning to it quite a bit to go through the entire story.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long-time player and fan of survival games. I love Subnautica, The Long Dark, The Forest, Green Hell, Valheim, you name it and I'll play it.Now with that out of the way, this game is not at all worth your money. It's barely a game. Yeah sure it's in early access, but the fundamentals are awful and won't be improved.What this "game" is, is a Unity asset store-driven Subnautica wannabe knockoff. They literally bought most assets straight from the Unity store - you can find the minerals they used here for cobalt, "super alloy" and so on:There are clipping issues all over the place. Rocks float above the ground. My character has no legs and is a floating mass. The environment / ground is barren. The environment looks like Mechwarrior 2 from the 1990s and that's not a compliment.Bottom line: the developers slapped some Unity store assets together to make a quick buck with a very half-baked "game" and it appears that's working for them. I cannot recommend spending money on it.If you crave this kind of game, grab Subnautica or No Man's Sky. Miles and miles better and more polished for similar prices.

Tasked with terraforming a planet, you gather ores (strewn around the landscape, later you can mine for ores) to build machines and habitats. _childDocuments_.review: Within the first few minutes I felt the hooks sink in. This game is special. It actually feels like you are terraforming the planet. This game focuses on base building, exploration, and moderate survival. There are no enemies other than the lack of air, water, and food.I recommend going in blind if you can. You can easily spoil the discovery aspects which pull you into the setting and makes it not just a game where you are increasing some numbers.I would compare this to Subnautica. However It is in no way the same game in practice. Although I would guess that if you like Subnautica, you'll like Planet Crafter. Finally, while this game does have some bugs, none of them are major. Some machine UI is confusing. You can clip into terrain or go out of bounds fairly easily if you try. It is extremely stable though. I experienced zero crashes or freezes. That is almost unheard of today. For $20 this is a must buy if you like the concept. You won't be disappointed.  Oh, you also can rebind the keybinds. Something EVERY game should have but enough games don't allow that it must be mentioned.

It's very low-key as well, where you don't have to worry about an enemy walking up and killing you (you just have to worry about accidentally causing your own death by forgetting to eat or drink before you leave!). The storyline is on the simpler side, but I think the gameplay itself is built for that. The only suggestion I would give would be to mmmmmaybe improve some of the textures (I've glitched into mountains a lot, and definitely found areas I wasn't supposed to access yet just because I was like oh, what's over there I wonder!) and ui interactions (specifically for base customizing, because I've gotten stuck under my base and had to use the unstuck key multiple times when I've tried to add in glass floors). That being said, anywhere I've gotten into I can also get out of fairly simply. The game never feels too slow, unless you actively want it to slow down. And then you can speed it back up again by restructuring or building the next tier of unlocks. It's like the highest quality clicker game, and I mean that in the best way it could be taken lol

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Subnautica, then you will most likely find this game's tone and gameplay very familiar. However, unlike Subnautica, many of the things you construct will gradually change the look of the planet and open up new areas for your to explore and exploit.The other game I would compare it to is Surviving Mars, which is a colony management game whose end game is similarly to gradually change the atmosphere, temperature, moisture, and biomass until it becomes habitable.This game creates a neat fusion of the survival, exploration, and crafting loop of Subnautica with the industrial resource and power management of Surviving Mars's terraforming, and it really works to be satisfying and interesting. I personally always felt a rush of pride and hope the first time I harvested an eggplant I grew, or the first time it rained, and the very subtle way that the ground turned green over time really distracted me from my tasks as I was constantly revisiting areas to see what else might be changing. I really felt like a pioneer.From a general standpoint, the game hardly feels like Early Access. Most of the game's models and textures look quite final and polished. And the core explore, gather, craft, and survive loop is satisfying and respects your time. Beyond that, the environments look great, full of areas that look very unique, ambient, and even awe-inspiring. And based on the developer's roadmap, it sounds like they have very reasonable goals that aren't too ambitious but show a solid understanding of what the game still needs.That said, there are some things that disappointed me or could be improved. The first is that power-management is not very interesting. You have wind turbines, solar panels, and nuclear generators, with upgraded version of each. But they all behave the same; generating a set amount of power no matter the condition. And each type generates more power than the previous, so once you have the more powerful generator, there's no need for the others. It would be more interesting if each type of power generator behaved differently. Wind turbines should be more powerful at higher ground, far away from other turbines, and more powerful during windy storms and as atmosphere pressure increases. Solar panels should produce more power depending on orientation to the sun, visibility, daytime, and should suffer from dust that you must clean off. I think that in this way, you could create some more interesting challenges that require more complex setups than just clustering everything together and expecting power to stay constant.Similarly, the actual terraforming mechanics suffer from a lack of interesting mechanics. Different machines increase the rate of change of several variables: pressure, heat, oxygen, and biomass. However, aside from some choices about filling items with certain plants, or limitations in where you can place these machines, there's little to do in terms of optimization. As with power-generation, more is better and that's the only concern. And the actual process by which the planet changes is scripted based on how far you have pushed the overall value along, so the sense of satisfaction from all the progress decays quickly once you realize that and instead it becomes far more a routine of building more of whatever you need and just building them anywhere.I think Surviving Mars does this much better. As an example, you want moisture, but the more you get, the more frequently you get acid rain. And acid rain will kill your biomass. The more atmosphere you generate, the more often meteor storms burn up before hitting the surface, but the more often you get dust storms. And if you want to generate biomass, you need to make the soil fertile by planting certain flora before planting others.I think Planet Crafter would be immediately more fun if the terraforming process was far more involved. I should be making decisions about where best to place my machines and the game should reward me by changing the terrain more locally depending on my placementFinally, I think the game needs a bit more of risk and challenge. Early on you really do feel like you are surviving on an inhospitable world with the oppressive haze, aggressive red light, and frequent dust storms, all while living one oxygen-tank to another. And on the whole, it feels nice to gradually improve your equipment to stay out longer, travel faster, and carry more. But I think there needs to still be some late-game hazards like quicksand, rockslides, solar flares, equipment damage, and so on.But listen, if you think you'll like this game, you're probably right. And if you're like me, you'll have gotten well-worth your money before you begin to see the limitations, and there's hope that we might see them addressed before final release.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Subnautica survival on the surface of Mars, except without combat. There's fully-functional optional multiplayer here as well. My wife and I have put about 23 hours into it so far, terraforming the red deserts into lush environments, while slowly uncovering some background story.I can't speak for having more than two players, or how well chat works, but we've been pleasantly surprised with how well the game and multiplayer runs. No perfomance issues or really any major bugs. Good for casual exploration and building (once you get past the early struggle to unlock food growers ASAP). I imagine that some quality of life improvements will be coming to take care of a few minor annoyances.+Tons to do+New schematics unlock or are discovered at regular intervals+Considerable customization of difficulty/duration+Decent graphics and music+Multiplayer works very well+Save anywhere+Saves and loads rapidly+No splash screens~Menus could use some touching up~A few items aren't explained well~You need to progress to food growers ASAP (should have been an early goal)~No combat or any real threats other than running out of food early on~No autosaves?~Needs some quality of life updates~Some environments lack variety or detail~Lacking/late on story compared to even first Subnautica game-Really needs an item to display your location to other players-Map is difficult to traverse and could use coordinate compass-Beacons can't be selectively turned off w/o a mod, causing clutter-Compass could use a marker for exact location you're looking at-Inviting Steam friend sometimes takes multiple attempts-Some objects can be difficult to place or snap-Meteors create temporary debris that clips into rooms/gets you stuck-Not always obvious when you've taken damage-A number of terrain features you can clip into-Frequent bug where you can't do much besides jump straight up when you load the game. Have to close entirely and restart to fix.Played on:Win11, i7-14700, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080using KB&M on a slightly modified Standard difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good although after 12 hrs straight I stumbled upon a plateau where progress went a lot slower. Problem is there are no vehicles so far to explore the planet so going on foot can take some time, feels like a walking simulator. There are occasional non-dangerous meteor showers, I would love to see some more of this and more dangerous. After you managed to have a water supply and grow your own food you're basecally set. Until this point surviving is a challenge if you play on intense. TBH I think the game is overrated right now...the review percentages look like those from top games such as Rimworld but this truely cannot be for real. Hope the devs put more depth and time into this game. Until then I put my efforts more into Satisfactory which by comparison is more polished and has more potential for a long time challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating, challenging, Subnautica-esque survival game. An absolute must for Subnautica divers looking for something just a little... drier. The unique focus of this game *just* on survival and development - totally violence-free - makes it particularly special, welcoming and rewarding. Build a base. Develop your world. Bigger base, more development. One, the other, both. Safe and cosy or sprawling industry. A landscape of comforting bolt-holes, or a frantic sprint for survival between heavy-duty bases. The additional play modes and starting points give the game replayability value, even in this early stage of development: I'm very excited to see what comes in the future. I've never bought an early-access game so soon in its emergence, and I'm very glad I did.

And you need to keep keys 'w' and 'space' held down the entire time. Fun.Grand ideas, but jarring in many aspects. The gameplay hasn't been polished at all.

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, honestly rivals Subnautica however I think it would've been cool to have a rover/vehicle thing to get around and to require bases to be powered, that way it's slightly harder to just build a simple block base with a door to replenish oxygen while exploring. And having hostile mobs would have definitely added a slightly more dangerous feel to exploring and going into unknown territories. However, with all that being said, I still really enjoy the game for many reasons. The music is great and the way the game feels is incredible, it gives you an "at home" feel in your base while forcing you to explore further into the world to get materials. And the way the planet slowly shapes into a habitable world is such a cool feature and really made it feel like your choices had an impact. All in All, solid 9/10 game, definitely pick it up while it's still on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Planning your base, figuring out a teraforming strategy, then stocking up for an adventure on the planet's surface is such a perfect mix of gameplay elements. Watching your efforts impact the environment is extremely satisfying. Love this game, haven't had so much fun with a space sim since the Outpost series as a kid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is an easily lovable game that allows you to play to your preferences when it comes to simplicity.While there is absolutely opportunity to grow and progress in a straight forward manner, there are easily enough resources to create complex and organized structures, even from the earlier stages. The modular building system is easy to use and everything snaps together very nicely with very little effort and the build size only seems to be limited by your resources and stage of progression.Some of the environments do still include visual glitching around the outer edges and the cliffs at the highest elevation of the map do still seem to be inconsistent in their map mesh placement, despite the fact that they can be reached and traversed.Overall, watching the planet progress from a barren wasteland into a lush, customizable paradise is an incredibly satisfying experience and the addition of multiplayer solved the only glaring problem, which was emptiness. Though the maps have a ton of places to explore and plenty of flora and fauna to fill them, the experience of terraforming a planet devoid of all sentient life but your own still felt a bit empty somehow. Having the ability to bring friends onboard completely changed the game and added an entirely new level of replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is a fun "numbers go up" game. It plays like an addictive idle game with an exploration-based active play aspect. For the most part, it is balanced quite well, with each point where you feel like you're running out of things to do, something new will unlock or you'll discover a new resource you should go out exploring for.That being said, there are a few things to keep in mind. This game CRANKS your GPU, and I cannot recommend it for any laptop play; even gaming laptops will get very hot very quickly. The meshing is... great for a first-time game in Unity. I would have loved to see this game made in Unreal for its efficiency of textures and meshing, but that is a bit of a nitpick. As long as you go in expecting some rough edges that I wouldn't expect to be cleaned up, you're going to be in for a great and addicting 50-ish hours of your life.Ending on a few of the highlights for me is the light touch of Metroidvania-style biome unlocking, where as you progress, you'll get tools to access areas that were very difficult to enter otherwise. Additionally, the map itself shifts as you progress, allowing for new pathways.8/10 I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: My only issue with this game is there is only one, pre-determined planet for you to terraform. It's not an infinitely re-playable proceduraly generated map. Other than that though the game is fantastic and I would recommend it at full price if you enjoy these Survival Crafter type games.
