_childDocuments_.review: Space survival crafting games,  if you love them, you probably played most of it, Games, like. No Man's Sky,  Empyrion Galactic Survival,  Planet Nomads, Space Engineers, and perhaps you do like to try Early access indie games.  well what all of those space games might have in common, one thing was missing from them, something you might fondly remember when you played Spore back in the days? So. no exploring lush planets full of flora and fauna, no crafting your own ship and fly away,  nope.. you are there on a god forsaken planet with one goal: "Terraforming"  Sound dull?  well maybe, if you dont like the grind, to get better Tier backpacks , jetpack , oxygen, yeah..this game is A LOT of grinding at the start, until you might have enough power to power automatic mining machines. But all that gathering, and crafting, and building,  its not the rewards in this game, The real reward is to see this Dune like planet, slowly change by the things you do. Slowly the dead skies turn blue,  slowly clouds form, then rain, then rivers, lakes, grass trees! And there it is, you see your dead planet change from a Caterpillar into a Butterfly. So you feel like working hard to then relax under the shadows of trees your created?Get this game,  you wont regret it, if you take it for what it is, an Early access game, with a potential to grow bigger.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I don't say that very often, but this is literally the game of my dreams. I love Terraforming Games, but good ones are very rare (naming "Terraformers" as a good example, which approaches the genre from a TBS/rogue-lite angle).Planet Crafter does everything right and I immediately purchased it as it went to Early Access, but waiting patiently until it's full release. Imho it was the best decision, because the game is so deep and complex now with all it's updates. It wouldn't have been fun to make progress only every few months.You land on a barren planet with no air to breath, no water to drink and only a small landing capsule for shelter. You slowly, but steadily increase the first few planet parameters, like pressure, temperature and then oxygen. When you think you are nearly done and how fast and easy that was, the game opens wider and you notice it just started, because now you have to spread the many levels of life on the planet.The game gets never boring, because it motivates you to explore the barren planet, which is full of caves, wrecks and other stuff to discover and more importantly: It is always very rewarding, because the loot is super worth and every expedition brings you closer to your goal.The Planet changes a lot, while you terraform it. New passages open, plants grow, animals spread. The work you do has a real impact on the world and helps you to explore it even more.The user interface is super easy and user friendly. The base building and crafting system as well. As you progress you get useful upgrades, that help you manage with the new and bigger tasks, which never get too complex, but still challenging.The game itself looks also very nice and the music is atmospheric, but never annoying or repetitive.I don't know what else to say, except please buy this game and enjoy it, as much as I do!Thank you, dear devs, for this treat, which is already one of my favorite games of the last years.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I usually can't be bothered to write reviews (good or bad) but I just wanted to help bump this game because I love it so much, esp with the new update that dropped today. If you wanted a cozy version of subnautica or raft, this is it. You're alone on an alien planet and have to rebuild/terraform it. Best part is actually seeing the changes in the climate from your hard work. Seeing grass cover the barren lands and the dusty smoggy skies clear up is really wonderful. The one annoying thing in this game is: each piece of ore is one slot in your bag and you can't stack it. Solution: throw everything on the floor :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: An early access title to look out for, which is Planet Crafter.So what is this game about?You are stranded on a hostile planet with one task. To make this planet habitable. But you are alone in a planet with no sign of life. There is no water, no breathable air, no food, no contact with anyone, there are sandstorms, there are meteor showers which makes you think “can one person do this?”But from picking up the first ore, everything in the game moves you in a path to shape this planet. To create a blue sky, to create cloud, to form rain, to create lake, to make an ecosystem.As you are better equipped, you slowly try to expand and explore this barren planet, to find what secrets it holds all the while finding more and more things, unlocking more and more base building, biomass, machine to produce oxygen, food, heat, pressure; everything you require to bring a change to this planet.This might make you think how this is stress free, this seems complex. But as I said, the motto is do it simple. The game takes inspiration from science but it doesn’t want to make it too complex that you won’t enjoy it. This has been said by the devs in their official roadmap.Everything the game does or provides is good, and it gets better and better the more you play it. You simply run to every location at first. Well, now you get t1 gear, which makes you faster. Then you get t2 gear, which makes you faster. Then t3. But what now? Now you get a different gear which makes you better at traversing. The game teaches so well and you rapidly become efficient at doing what needs to be done and you can see a visible change in the environment because of your action.But you may wish to play it with a friend. And good news for those wishing that because the devs have announced co-op mode for 2024. The game is also getting 1.0 release in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely beautiful game. Mind you, the graphics are nothing special but as you progress through the stages of terraforming, the environment changes and as barren wastelands turn into lush landscapes you will sense a(n admittedly irrational) feeling of accomplishment you likely won't get from any other game.On a more technical side, the pacing is well done, the world feels big without being tediously so. Even towards the end, it never truly felt like a grind which is a miracle with these kinds of games.The endings are a bit lackluster and the non-standard endings require some work. As it's not really a story driven game, I don't mind the endings because the journey there is what mattered.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed building bases in Subnautica and didn't appreciate monsters screaming in my ear while I was collecting materials to make glorious, differently-themed bases throughout the land.  I was attracted to Planet Crafter because I could build bases in peace without monsters terrorizing me.  Planet Crafter successfully scratched that itch.  I spent so long building multiple bases in different zones that I didn't notice the supposed grind between terraforming phases.  If anything, I felt the game was too short because I hit 100% achievements including the 100,000 terra tokens after only finishing four small bases in different zones within 49 hours.  This game essentially felt like Subnautica base building with minor, end-game automation elements to make life easier (automating farming, food, water, and terra token generation).The downsides to this game include:1) a lack of story (Subnautica has a significantly better story and better introduces easter eggs), 2) there is no incentive to build more than one base (which you will probably put in the most optimal, obvious, and centralized location on the map), 3) there are no vehicles to traverse terrain in fun or interesting ways, 4) the base building blocks are not very customizable (base blocks don't combine in predictable ways and glass paneling isn't compatible with several wall configurations), 5) the map is flat and small (Mushroom river barely counts as another level), and the map is too easy to explore from your single base, and 6) I feel like there's a lot of wasted potential on tech progression (aside from T3 extractors, drones, and teleporters, there are not really big tech upgrades that meaningfully change the way the player interacts with the planet and significantly affect QoL to provide a sense of progression - there are many fun ideas to dramatically improve QoL or change the way the player interacts with the world to steal from other games that hopefully get implemented in this one).Overall, I still enjoyed the game and maybe some of these issues will be addressed in future updates!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A great solo survival experience for those that don't play with friends. You'll experience the highs of terraforming a planet a planet in real time while you work through a progression of better equipment to help you explore and survive .I've only played up to unlocking the first rockets but I enjoyed every moment I played and only put it down to play my favourite MMO for a while.Finally, a game worth its overwhelming positive reviews. _childDocuments_.review: Addictive!  Even with the expected glitches from an Early Access title in its first days, I'm finding it challenging enough to keep my interest, but not so much that I feel the urge to fling my mouse into the nearest wall.For me the game has been very stable overall.  I've experienced no crashes, though I have begun to notice a few framerate drops becoming more pronounced as I have progressed in the game.  Some erratic jetpack behavior over certain areas and the absence of a few basic construction items are my only 'complaints', if you can call them that since both could hardly be considered unexpected from a days-old Early Access title.  Refinements and polish all usually come with time if game devs keep their finger on the pulse of the community and are diligent in considering feedback, all of which at this stage, these particular developers seem to be.Overall, I'm finding Planet Crafter very enjoyable and definitely recommend it!  I look forward to seeing how the experience evolves and expands as development continues!

_childDocuments_.review: I last started the game over a month ago, so I think I am ready to call it quits.Overall,  was a fun time waster, a fun exploration and crafting game while catching up on podcasts and audio dramas while always getting just enough motivation and progress to continue playing for a bit longer. Once my (second) base was up and running, the world was mostly green and blue after terraforming and I had found the alien secrets in the world, the once enormous map metaphorically grew smaller and smaller. With little outposts dotted around and a high-level jetpack, traversal was no longer laborious, but just half a minute or so of flying around. The amount of resources required to reach the next level of terraforming exploded again, thus I felt more and more like a pack mule than anything else. I am not very good (or interested in) automating the fabrication capabilities of my base, so I more or less just stopped playing. And now, a few weeks later, I uninstalled it.BUT, nevertheless, I think this was a worthwhile experience. Not nearly as motivating as the two Subnauticas for me as the story was just meh, but it had a similar charm and scratched the same itch for over 20 hours, so I definitely had a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a joy to watch this game grow and develop over EA.  Whilst not sporting the most UHD graphics that is quickly forgotten exploring the world and watching it subtly change as terraformation gathers pace.  Starting with a world at home in the Martian you transform it into a vibrant green and blue one. Resource gathering can be a bit clunky at times and less refined than factory focused similar games but later on this is somewhat streamlined.  Terraformation is slow at certain points but this is largely as I forge to massively spam certain buildings before I go off exploring more of the world.During EA most of the rough edges have been smoothed but a few kinks remain however having played it though a good chunk of development these are despite a lot of love and attention from the devs rather than due to a lack of the same. The devs have a good track record of listening o the community and acting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: 0. Disclaimer:Most modern titles are vast as an ocean and deep as a puddle. This one is vice versa and definitely deserves your money and attention. Do not hesitate to buy it. Some day it will stand among the giants of interactive worlds like 7D2D and TLD, probably.Not today. Today this game has met a sophisticated player.1. At first you criticize this technical demo of a game for:— Pushing out a DLC before polishing out the initial product.Features-first Google approach has always been an epitome to the commercialization of entertainment. Meanwhile video games are art (sic!) above anything else, and imperfections which break the Player’s immersion are nearly unacceptable, now and forever.Low budget, humble team size or Early Access badge are not an excuse for the lack of quality, thorough game mechanics design, sanity checks, or extensive usability testing.— Poor clipping.There are plenty of places on the Prime map where your character floats above ground with no actual feeling of traversing the terrain, while camera clips through it. And although the invisible walls can be justified at map borders; having those in the middle of the map, especially in a game where you can literally build a stairway to heaven with zero regards to physics or common sense, — are mildly irritating, even though you do get the dungeon master’s incentive to limit your shortcuts.— W-syndrome.Long time ago Hinterland gave up to the community demands of introducing a toggled auto-walk button. Constant middle-finger spasm on the W-key is pretty common among first-person action gamers, and the Planet Crafter is no exception. In fact here it pushes the problem to a new level: you prefer NOT having a mining speed upgrade chip installed because it invokes minimal gameplay relevance, but secures a much needed rest for your left hand. Tool distance upgrade would have been a much more relevant option indeed, reducing the excessive movement of the Player. How come this hasn’t been resolved yet with built-in game feedback feature, eludes me.Same goes for shift-running. Auto-run outside and auto-switch to walking indoors would do the trick, but toggled shift would have worked even better.— Partial SFX.Game has only three types of footsteps: over metal, wood, and common. There are entirely no walking sounds in some areas (and no flying too for no apparent reason), and limited variability of existing ones eventually end up quite stale, especially the common ones. Doesn’t matter if you traverse snow, sand or stone, they are one and the same. Footprints are also above this game menu.— Lack of effects.Be it a sandstorm, rain or whatever, there are no environmental visor effects, and therefore you can’t help but feel you’re not actually a character in a dire situation, but simply a controllable movie camera. On top of this — such impression is also enforced by barely animated hands. I bet everyone smiles sadly when they see how protagonist lovingly dusts his multi-tool every once in a while.Moreover weather impact on your activities is utter zero, except for the meteor shower which brings in free resources. You don’t even need the compass not to get lost in a fog with all the beacons. And there’s no point in weathering the storm in a shelter, since it is of no danger; just go around your business like an iron man.— Physics.Or the lack of it to be precise. Believe it or not you actually fall faster on slopes and in water!Unless you intentionally go full-in on aesthetics as a rule — your builds end up cluttered with all parts overlapping each other at no sanity or repercussion. Solar panels will work just fine underground, interlaced wind turbines will perform perfectly, everything’s cool under any angle, and both weather and object placement has zero effect whatsoever. You can literally build anyhow anywhere, it just works, and is connected by ether. Power lines? Never heard of’em.In fact, the more you think of it, the more ludicrous it becomes. A couple of indoor heat generators and a few gas drills break the camel’s back on a planet that has open lava pools? Snow plains near the desert? Everything goes.— PEGI rating. It’s 18 in case you had no idea.The pretext of a male convict doing his sentence of terraforming a planet for an unspeakable transgression, doing weird dances each time he puts on a new space suit, is quite telling. He can die of hunger, thirst, suffocation and fall fractures. Some really ♥♥♥♥♥♥-up psychological ♥♥♥♥ can be found in the logs of hidden bunkers and spaceship debris. There’s even a cemetery of almost a full crew in one of the caves. And I can’t help but wonder why oh why this severe foundation was not built upon. Instead of dismembered corpses, frozen in ice, littering the trap-planet, and telling a story, you get a Disneyland vacation music and a cartoon palette. Yay!How about we progress from the existential dread to a loony toon instead of mixing it together from the very beginning?2. Then you start to kinda like it:— Once you dig a bit into the game, settle-in and understand what it is and is not by all measure, you decide to give it a chance.After all it respects your time by not making you hold your left mouse button or die of old age while you gather the resources like in No Man Sky, right? I mean you still doubt the game design decision to allow building structures without foundations, and can’t understand why containers need them, while living compartments absolutely do not. But you start getting somewhere.— Custom settings are always a fine choice.On my first run I’ve set both my vitals drain, weather and terraformation speed to 0.3 to compensate for difficulty, and began to actually enjoy the exploration. Without an impression I have to hold my breath in a jerrycan every time I go outside — the underground mushroom river, the crater, the moonlit veins field, the innards of space ships became a reflective sightseeing experience.Letting players do their thing is always awesome, but more settings are definitely on demand.— Although some stuff still made no sense.Why running does not double your vitals drain? Why dehydration causes your sight go blank and die outright instead of gradually draining health? Who needs a bed? That kind of stuff, insomnia induced no doubt.3. Then you begin to enjoy it:— Immediately when you build yourself a basic jetpack.I mean your left hand still hurts from no auto-walk key, but holding space instead of shift helps. Using it first time — really felt like reality. You jump, and then you thrust. Huh, this will never get old! Now the terrain turned out to be passable, walking sounds no longer get on your nerves, and going down a cliff no longer a cringe. Now that’s how it’s actually supposed to be played, huh?!Cool stuff.4. Finally you are astonished by it:— First Biodome and then Biolab finally show you what’s in store.Woah, this game is huge! Unlike the map it’s played upon. The environment starts to change, and if you keep the terraformation speed low enough, every aspects unfolds like a charm: puddles, lakes, rivers, waterfalls... Melting ice opens hidden caverns making re-exploration viable. Satellites turn out to be a disappointment, but you start building bases in breathtaking places to watch it all evolve...5. And then you make a rover...Wait, wat?Blueprint progression, darling.Clunky, bulky, slow, constantly stucking 3rd-person viewed vehicle with inventory that brings minimal advantage in comparison to the blazing exosuit capable of crossing the map in 5 minutes?No thanks.Air is not a problem anywhere, since you can build micro-bases, like, every ten paces. It’s not Subnautica for it to be ever feasible.I’ve bought Planet Humble, to support the devs if nothing else, and tried it too.But I will hold on for a year or so before getting back to this game.Let’s hope it terraforms.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I have always said that games must be made with love and patience for details. That, along with very good mechanics and logic.In addition, they must be monitored and corrected as soon as possible, taking care of the players.Planet Crafter has everything above.In addition, it is a very fun game full of adventures. I've been playing for almost 80 hours and I still haven't finished discovering new places and things.I love the game. I would play it again from scratch and I hope they release the new DLC soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Early Access Review.It's like a cross between a survival crafting game and an idle game. The survival crafting part should be familiar: you explore the environment, gather resources, keep an eye on hunger and thirst meters, build a base and crafting stations. The idle game comes in as your research tech tree. You build machines to slowly terraform the planet, each contributing a rate over time to both a certain category and to the overall progress. There are milestones along each category and for the overall progress that unlock new technologies. The new techs then contribute to speeding up the terraforming process, or allowing you to do more. So the gameplay loop largely goes that you'll build some set of machines to speed up progress, then wander off to go explore, or build your base, or mine resources. While you're off doing that, the progress hits some milestone, unlocks new technologies, giving you new toys to play with and goals to achieve. It's also pretty satisfying seeing the world change around you due to your efforts. Overall I found this game nicely addictive, scratching that "having a world to myself to build and explore in" itch.It's still in early access, and there's still some rough edges to it. Things like the collision on the mountains can be wonky. However, in the entire time I played it I never had a crash or freeze. The demo's save game carries over into the full version, so that makes it a good way to see if you'll like the game without losing time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: There's something odd with this game. Like a good book you start playing then don't want to put it down. I do hope the Devs stay the course and add to the game as there is so much that could be done. It's nice to be able to play something that you don't necessarily die in. If there had to be a criticism it would be maybe a number of planets could be added to give some more replay and diversity value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing and fun imprisonment on a planet, while being forced to terraform it.  Small learning curve followed by hours of exploration and building while watching the lakes form and planet turn green.  Its a builders dream.  The main two things i could see adding is Co-op play and procedurally generated maps giving it more and more replayability.  Wonderful game guys.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like numbers going up? Do you like stockpiling dozens of chests of a single resource? Do you like the idea of hardcore drugs but think they're too expensive? Then Planet Crafter is the game for you!At first you will want just a little more food, water, and oxygen to refill the constantly depleting survival meters but very soon you will solve that problem only to realize you are just a few hours into your shiny new scifi addiction. You will dash around snatching up every ore you can find lying around literally everywhere, sometimes coming across dopamine in a box aka chests. These chests will dangle goodies in front of you like seeds for your garden or flowers for your oxygen producers. Did I forget to mention you are an interstellar convict whose sentence will be commuted once you completely terraform a planet and watch it's ecosystem come to life before your very eyes? The Terraformation Index, helpfully abbreviated to TI in the UI so your brain can focus on finding just one more uranium to build another nuclear reactor which will seemlessly power your ever expanding terraformation operation.Anyway, back to the flowers. So you use flowers to produce more oxygen while using food seeds to make snacks to keep you alive while exploring this gloriously desolate yet nubile wasteland. All the while your drills will increase pressure and your heaters will, get this, increase heat. I know, an amazing concept. As the TI goes up so does the cost for the next level which means you need T2 then T3 and then T4 of everything to keep advancing. Discover brand new resource types and blueprints scattered around the world before you launch rockets into space to help you map out this now gargantuan play area. Seed life in the freshly melted lakes then mutate that life to serve your own needs. Drive a truck to add additional storage capacity to your inventory as you frantically trek from outpost to outpost looking for more and more stuff. And partake in every homosapiens' favorite past time, exploding natural rock formations to lay claim to the resources the soil dared to hide from you. TLDR: It's Satisfactory without the math getting in the way. HOOK. IT. TO. MY. VEINS!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game in the Subnautica vein. A few design choices make it a bit on the grindy side - particularly the lack of item stacking - but the game offers mod support so you can head over to Nexus and change that and lots of other mechanics to suit your preferences. Really satisfying to watch the planet transform over time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Planet Crafter is a great beginning. All the most of the basic gameplay is here.  It is a terrific little casual survival builder, and I hope the developer fleshes it out, and makes it more scientifically realistic :) My ThoughtsBut it is challenging to see where it evolves to. With the game itself being humans terraforming a planet the stage progression is more of a race than a real change to the conditions of the planet. I hope to see the developers make the terraforming stage progression less abstract and somewhat more realistic. I dont mean making it take millenia to change the planet but basic things like your planet doesnt start off at 0K (for those who dont know -273C (-459F) and then have rain and liquid water at a temperature around 1mK (-272C).Having the start conditions being something closer to say Mars ( NASA among others has lots of great info that could be used to set this up ). Then tieing the progression to actually meeting somewhat realistic requirements for the stages the developer has defined, such as liquid water at 273K (1C) and lets say 50,000Pa (about half Earths atmospheric pressure at seal level). The building gameplay is good for the development stage it is at, and from my experience surprisingly few bugs, The story attached to the planet and the players being there are basic but a solid platform to expand on. Definitely a game worth supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Some parts of the game get very slow, and there's not a lot of story at the moment(Or the story that's there isn't easy to find), but I love this game so much. Seeing the slow change of the world as it becomes more habitable gets me pretty emotional. I'm excited to see more stuff get added in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: While this game feels a little like a Subnautica rip-off, that's not necessarily a bad thing. The way things stand now, there is plenty to do for 25 hours and it's great fun. After that, you've probably already explored everything, unlocked most things (but not all) and then it becomes a bit of a drill, and all you can do it build, expand, make things pretty, etc. It's definitely already worth the money and it's very playable, there is enough story to add interest and none of the rare bugs are game-breaking. (I've encountered some glitching through terrain and some loot mysteriously respawned, otherwise everything works as it should.) The game will likely be amazing when it's finished. Even now, once I terraform everything fully, I will be curious to try the different starting locations for a new challenge. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow only 17 hours? Feels like a lot more!This game definitely has some Subnautica vibes, and that's a very good thing. Maybe even sprinkle in a little bit of Forager on top.So, not as refined as Subnautica or Satisfactory, but if you love those you should ABSOLUTELY get this one as well.Edit: pretty much finished with the game now at 34 hours. The original assessment held. I hope they don't add too much stuff now, but refine what's already there. Very much worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 47 hours, I found it hard to decide whether to recommend or not.Overall, I will reward the creative concept and the sheer potential, but I will advise against fully purchasing it just yet.Not much to spoil but I will describe the current end game. There isn't one. You play for a satisfying 10 - 13 hours, exploring the map, shipwrecks and outposts, eventually accessing blocked caves, unlocking and implementing better technologies, building up your base. It was great at first. But head my warning. Once you unlock trees, there's not much point in pushing through to insects and the final unlocks just yet. That is unless you just love grinding. Basically nothing happens. And according to the developers updates, the game apparently doesn't have much further to expand, other than some map additions, spawning in some basic animals, maybe some new tech and a tiny bit more story. They have fully admitted that their development capabilities are limited and they intend for this to be a pretty basic experience even by the end. So with that info, I will declare that the price point is frankly a stretch, and will likely remain so. This seems like maybe a 12 dollar game at most. So my final thoughts. Great concept. Check out the demo. Keep an eye out for updates on final game progress.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I love crafting game and this one is the best I ever played right next to Subnotica, It is basically the same game except there is no monsters after you and no jump scares. I love the exploration aspect of it, and seeing the planet changing as you are progressing throughout the game, and as the planet evolves you get more items to create so it is an endless supply of dopamine!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. As someone who fell in love with Subnautica as soon as I started playing it, this is just another game that strikes my fancy in a similar way. With little of the stress I might add :D But The Planet Crafter is still challenging in its own unique way. I really like the timing balance in the game; you never feel like you're just hanging around for terraforming conditions to improve, there's always something to explore or something to improve. The biomes are great and you just get this sense of grandeur and scale, much like with Subnautica. I like how calming it is, but with the added excitement of what's around the next corner. I've started the game 3 times over with every new big update, but I'm super excited for v1.0 and all the amazing things it has to offer. I really hope they delve deep into the lore and have a bit of a twist waiting to surprise us and I can't wait for the day where I have a flourishing planet after all the glorious time I've spent in this magnificent game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Play the demo first! You can continue the save if you decide to buy the game. Big thumbs up for the developers to offering a playable demo that you can continue in the actual game. You don't see this often these days and it's really worth it. It was the number one reason why I decided to try this game, fell in love with it and then bought the real deal. This game is just a perfect combination of space survival, casual gardening, exploration and building. I love the idea that you don't have twenty different processing steps and thousands of resources to gather in order to make one window. I really don't have time for things like that or the mental capacity to remember s*t like that, so this game is challenging enough but doesn't require you to sell your soul for it. One thing that I really like with this game is the feeling of progress you get. Things are changing slowly and you can see the change around you as you progress with terraformation. Resource gathering is basic grinding but there's always that little twist of making sure you have enough oxygen to still get back to your base. I also love the little suprises of grounded spaceships every now and then and the intense wreck search with your tiny flashlight. The wrecks actually look like they've come down crashing and getting over the debree and trying to remember your way out feels nerve wrecking but the goodies are worth it. Overall I say this is an excellent game already and it offers a lot of playtime as it is, but I can't wait to see the progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best "early access" game I've ever played.  Even if they stopped now and never did another thing there is still 20-40 hours of pure fun. _childDocuments_.review: (My 44.6 hrs play time is a playthrough: Didn't rush anything, but didn't AFK in-game either, played in slow pace, yet I googled about 5-6 annoying things -finding stuff very well hidden- for a shortcut)This game has a lot of negatives & downsides. Huge amount, from the small inventory and far too long walks, via the forced and hardcoded way of development, i.e. lack of freedom of choice (the game is unlocking stuff automatically, in order) to the meh-meh gfx / L&F and a million more things, and I have one and only one thing on the positive side:.Very small studio (if I remember right it's wife & husband and that's it), so forget the negatives and play on. Also, look on the bright side: If this was a AAA studio's game, would have better visuals indeed, however, it would be unoptimized, unfinished, unpolished, ultra-buggy, no issues ever fixed, and 29 pay DLCs already out, if not microtransactions, as we learned from Dragon's Dogma 2, even a SP game might have such BS (/spit Capcom).This game instead didn't try to be more than what was fundable & achievable for the creators, so it actually IS finished(!), in a good quality, again, can't emphasize engouh, fun to play, very well coded & optimized so it doesn't try to kill the PC (against the odds as it's running on Unity Cr@pgine), so it's just good, absolutely worths the price - I can only recommend it!Can't wait to see Planet Crafter II, hopefully without all the negatives (I'm not listing here, as for this game, it doesn't matter).

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is an amazing concept with excellent implementation. The ability to see this barren planet gradually come to life with water, vegetation, trees and eventually life forms is absolutely incredible. There are also views into the lives of people who came before and contact via satellite with Riley, a living being.You explore the region finding boxes, flowers and minerals that you can mine to make better machines to improve the atmosphere quicker. There are quite a few golden boxes for you to find that have above average loot. You build a base and keep updating it with new information screens and bio-labs to grow cultures and create items that allow you to make food. You need enough power to run things and it's good fun.Edit: There have been several updates since my original review and every one was excellent. Nice to see the input, better to see that they are moving forward with the story and a finale. This is without doubt one of my favour games of all time. Laid back and smooth. Well done Devs. I am in awe!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up after 1.0 launch, so I can't speak what the game was like in early access or how it improved since then. Also can't vouch for coop features since I played pure solo.The Planet Crafter is, at its core, an incremental game masquerading as an open world survival craft game. You are a convict sentenced to terraform the planet you land on, and to do this, you are to raise the oxygen, heat, and pressure levels of the planet. As you do, you unlock more things to craft, many of which help you terraform faster. Repeat until you unlock everything, at which point you have the opportunity to choose one of three endings for your run, provided you've met the prerequisites.Seeing the planet change and new paths open (and some old ones submerge) as you reach different terraforming levels is super satisfying, and this happens a few times over the course of a playthrough.The biggest complaints I have about TPC is that pop-in is noticeably bad, base building feels finicky at times, random events are super annoying (i.e. meteors targeting the player and the subsequent debris taking forever to despawn, torch chip being useless during night cycles), the lategame gameplay loop is extremely repetitive with lategame wrecks being particularly bad offenders... but despite all that, TPC is incredibly fun and chill (on standard difficulty, at least) for the majority of the game.Finally, at the time of writing, there is not much reason to replay the game (the planet's topography is the same between playthroughs), but I still felt like I got my money's worth from a single playthrough. Would look forward to a sequel or any content DLC with great interest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Even in Early Access, this game is completely enthralling. Left alone to build and collect and organize and explore, with just enough story and puzzling and mystery to keep it from getting same-y. This is a game for crafting and resource management junkies. Have you (like me) gone deep into Valheim console code to shut off all the monsters so you could just build? Then this is for you. You do have to survive the elements, but there are no stupid zombies or monsters or dudes with guns or annoying teenage MMO griefers to get in the way of just losing yourself for hours and hours, making a miserable dustball into a beautiful planet. I can't wait to see how it grows.

_childDocuments_.review: For the price you can get a lot of content out of this game. I have 74 hours but 30 were playing then quitting as it built up to full release. That said, after a certain amount of time it turns into a waiting game. For example I am at a stage where I can build drone controllers. I'm super excited about that but to build drones I need circuit boards which I cannot craft until more stuff can be unlocked so I don't know what certain things are in these kind of orders? Great I got the controller. No. Actually I got the recipe. Now I have to wait until I can create the key ingredient to build it. In some cases that wait is a really really long time. Other than that though I really like idea of rewards being given steadily as you progress towards terraforming, just not the order some are in. When you get to oxygen the whole planet really opens up to exploring and the journey to get there is also really fun. I definitely recommend this game and if it ever comes to console I'll get it there too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, and good for 12 to 15 hours of gameplay.  Runs well, and hasn't crashed once.  A few bug, mostly due to clipping with terrain, but nothing game breaking.  The only downside is that once you max out your tech trees that game is pretty much finished.  You just chase bigger numbers by launching more satellites and increasing the heat/pressure/temp of the atmosphere to get to the next plateau of terraforming.  But there really isn't anything to do, and once you hit trees level the game slows down drastically.  You are left with collecting more resources to build more of the same stuff you have already built on to build more and more and more without end.Worth the money for a few hours of fun gameplay, but doesn't really hold up in the long haul.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I am normally wary of paying for early access games, but as this one offered a free demo version, I gave it a go.  Right away there is a Minecraft/Space Engineers feel to it, and while there is a little bit of a learning curve in how to survive the first few minutes, long enough to start building anything of use, it was picked up quickly and mostly intuitive in how the game works.  The survival elements are there enough to remind you that you are on an inhospitable alien planet, but are not so prohibitive that a little time and resource management wouldn't let you keep going, which I feel gives it an enjoyable immersive quality.  The building habitat pieces and equipment, and unlocking of technology as you progress in terraforming, is also fairly straight forward and reasonable.  Most things will cost between 2-6 resources, and the progression of technology is well balanced in terms of what you need to continue.  There are other things that I liked, such as being able to enter and salvage resources from various space wrecks, finding certain areas with rare resources, the different filters for various biomes, meteor showers that strike nearby, often with additional minerals, and of course, watching the planet gradually change as you terraform it and giving you a sense of a reachable but not too quick achievement.All that being said, the game is definitely not finished, as it is an early access and still in the process of being created.  Clipping and there's some disconnect between rocky formations creating some "floating" rocks after meteors land.  Progression technically continues up to a certain point, but the effects stop well short of that.  The way buildings link together, or don't, needs some fine-tuning and the habitat build options are somewhat limited so far.  There's elements of a story that can be discovered (no spoilers about that, but they are there), and I'd love to see more of that.  Most, if not all, of these issues are directly attributed to the fact that the game is still being made, and are indicated to be resolved as updates from the developer are uploaded.If you're just looking for a quick, relaxing building game, the demo will probably be enough to fill that niche.  For myself, I liked what I saw enough to pay for the game in the hopes that it will continue to build on what is already a solid foundation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a recommend to support the studio as they continue to work on completing the game. I've put ~10 hours in and I really want to keep going. Terraforming a planet is such a great concept for this style of game (first person builder/survival)and I look forward to diving into it when it's ready.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter was a departure for me in my gaming library.  I am not a survival game enthusiast, but I gave it a try on a friend's recommendation.  650 hours in I'm a fan.  This game has provided much enjoyment over 2 years of early access and now in its 1.0 release. It's not perfect by any stretch, but for what it is, it's a unique kind of animal for an indie game.The good:  The graphics are more than adequate if not cutting edge.  By the time you are finished with your world, if you have developed well and put some effort into it, you will have a thriving planet teaming with diverse life.   The real satisfaction from this game lies in A) living long enough to get to the point where you have enough food to survive and a breathable atmosphere and B) watching a barren rock turn slowly into a lush green planet designed solely by your choices.   There is also ample opportunity to indulge in elaborate base building, pushing your terraformation numbers ever higher, and engaging in exploration throughout the various biomes as well as through a portal which generates random space wrecks ripe for looting.  You will launch rockets, participate in space trading, investigate alien sites, and fly around your planet like Superman or zap between locations via teleporters.  There is a good deal of fun to be had, and I won't spoil it all.  The not-so-good:   I have a few issues with the final version as it stands.  There are still some bugs to fix, which is typical in a new release.  You will find construction a bit tricky or restrictive in some ways. There is still some clipping, meteors coming through the walls of buildings, ladders that sometimes get you stuck (although there is an escape key) and things of this nature that need to be addressed.  Some of this is the fault of the game engine itself.  There is an upper limit on just how much you can add to the world without causing frame rates to plummet, but I have found that my planet can be quite lush and full without having problems as long as you have a decent GPU.  Hiding a lot of machinery inside caves helps with frame rate.  Overall, these issues have not detracted from my enjoyment of the game.  My one real complaint about Planet Crafter is the various endings the developers have provided.  There are 3 in all, and each one, in my opinion, is quite depressing.   Just not what I would have hoped for after successfully "beating" the game and fulfilling your conditions as a convict abandoned on a barren world and tasked with its terraformation.  I have personally chosen not to act on any of the endings.  I find that remaining on my pristine paradise, lonely as it might be, is far preferable than "rescue" given the circumstances.  I am quite comfortable at this point...and now I have pets.  :)  In summation: The developers, I must add, have been very responsive to player feedback and apparently plan to continue to support the game and perhaps add to it in the future.  I look forward to what they may have planned.  I also hope they add another "ending" involving remaining on our planet, but that remains to be seen.  Overall, I would definitely recommend Planet Crafter to someone looking for a chill, relaxing survival/world development game.  You can also choose more difficult or random settings if you desire a higher level of challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: "Embark on an awe-inspiring cosmic odyssey with 'The Planet Crafter,' where ingenuity meets the infinite in a mesmerizing adventure. 🌌 Stranded amidst the vast expanse of a desolate planet, your quest intertwines with the celestial dance of transformation and the imminent threat of cosmic calamity, weaving a tapestry of thrilling narrative depth.Navigate a seamless blend of exploration, base construction, and strategic ingenuity as you navigate the vibrant tapestry of this interstellar canvas. 🚀 The visual tableau, replete with dynamic environments and a harmonious symphony of color, draws you into a realm where every pixel pulsates with life and possibility.Immerse yourself in a melodic saga, from tranquil harmonies that echo the serenity of cosmic tranquility to heart-pounding crescendos that herald the pulse of imminent danger. 🎶 The auditory landscape, punctuated by the thunderous reverberations of cosmic forces, amplifies the immersive experience to celestial heights.Uncover hidden mysteries, unlock coveted achievements, and master the intricacies of planetary alchemy in this captivating escapade. While the challenge may beckon for seasoned voyagers seeking greater complexity, 'The Planet Crafter' stands as a testament to the boundless realms of creativity and cosmic exploration, earning a resounding 9 out of 10 in the cosmic lexicon of gaming excellence.In summary, 'The Planet Crafter' beckons you to embark on a voyage of cosmic proportions, where the boundaries between reality and imagination blur, and the universe becomes your canvas of endless possibilities."
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The base building, for the most part, is solid.  Can build bases almost anywhere.  They can get very big, very fast.  Not too many decorations, but the bases themselves have a decent look.The exploration is decent fun.  Finding boxes, finding new materials, etc.  Typical setup for these types of games.Terraforming is obviously the highlight of the game.  Taking a dead rock and turning it into a planet with life.  it was great to see the changes as the game progressed.What got to me, as I am sure got to a lot of folks, is the mid-game grind.  The exploration stopped, the base building (for the most part) stopped, the fun stopped.  Instead, I was just grinding out materials to build stuff to make numbers go higher.Storage was also a pain.  Half of my base was dedicated to storage.  I finally logged off when I realized all I was doing was juggling storage around to make room for, you guessed it, more storage!  There are things that help - like teleporters and autocrafters, but it's still a bit of a slog.Base building can be a bit bugger.  I accidentally built a corridor on top of another corridor, causing problems in my base.  That's when the base building started to unravel for me.I was tired of inventory management.  The game is good, no doubt, and unique.  But I got my time out of it and decided to move on.  Still, it was a blast up until that point.I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things. _childDocuments_.review: Nice survival/exploration game.It starts highly focused on surviving mechanics, pushing you slightly towards exploration to help you progress, and as the game evolves the survival part gets less pressing and you can really focus and enjoy the exploration part.Graphics are good, UI is intuitive and easy to work with, music matches well the themes of the game.My only concern while playing has been the game progression pace: I had the impression sometimes that some of the rewards or unlocks, for exploration or progressing the main objective, were coming at times where they were not really needed, or didn't felt as rewarding.More on a personal note dislike: The actual values of the different variables that you have to increase during the game to complete the terraforming process make no sense at all, from a physical point of view, for the different effects they are supposed to cause. They feel like just a lazy counter lacking any real background documenting work on their physical significance. But, whatever, I get the objective of the game is not to focus on the accuracy of the terraforming physics and just have a fun time, which it achieves.The co-op gameplay was straightforward and worked fine most of the time. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter provides the somewhat unique experience of trying to survive on a planet you are terraforming. I also haven't 100% beaten the game yet, but the enjoyment I have received from it was great regardless. This is one of those games I enjoyed, but it is a bit of a strange game, it doesn't fall easily into categories, so it is hard for me to know who else would enjoy this type of game. _childDocuments_.review: 9/10.Took me 59 hours to 100% this game (has 3 endings, but you can save before you start any of them and then reload to do the others, which is what I did).  Had a lot of fun, and definitely plan to revisit for more, especially when new content is released.  For a first-time playthrough I would expect the game will probably take most people almost as long to finish any of the endings.  They all require complete terraformation, and if you've never played before you probably won't have the most optimized progression.  Longer, if you really take your time.Would recommend for teens and above.  Preteens might enjoy it, but much younger than that and the tech "tree" would likely be too confusing.  Lots of calculations, resource management and figuring out how to increase your terraformation levels without running out of power.Pros:+Amazing techno-esque music.+Played great in multiplayer.+Gameplay loop is variable enough (especially with custom options) to allow for repeat playthroughs.+Similar to Subnautica in some ways, enough to scratch that itch a tiny bit.+Lots of recipes to learn and craft.+Several different terraforming categories to vary your activities.+Lots of different species of plants, animals, etc. that make the world come alive around you.Cons:-Some bugs, mostly due to terrain clipping, but nothing game-breaking.-Too much like Subnautica in other ways, enough that it felt less original (story).-Several times unlocked stuff that couldn't be used due to slower progression in other parts of tech tree.-The procedural generated content (mostly late game, as most of the world is hand-crafted) could use some work.  This is where we encountered most of the bugs, and in trying to avoid spoilers, "difficulty" of the procedural gen content mostly just translates to annoyingly complicated and confusing.  Needs to be less like an endless maze, with fewer loops.  We did this content less than a dozen times or so and then quit because it was too monotonous.Already thinking about where I want to base for my next playthrough.  Might try the random spawn option and look at some other options.

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to review the game in the state it is in right now, but it's definitely got potential, so thumbs-up from me.+ Very good early-to-mid game progression. There's sense of danger (from environment), and sense of progressing through the tech tree, and things seem to be pretty balanced overall.+ Pretty much no bugs, minimal visual glitches here and there, great performance.+ Nice visuals, the terraformation of the planet is very satisfying.- Graphic quality is on the level of year 2010 games. This does not impact the gameplay, but just good to know if you are into graphics. Hopefully the devs will improve this aspect later on, as this shouldn't be difficult to change on the engine they are using.- The late-game progression is horribly boring and grindy. While at the beginning everything is interesting and cool to do, later on it's just a meaningless grind of "go to point X, grab a bunch of iridium, go to point Y, grab a bunch of uranium, repeat for 100 times until your planet is fully terraformed. Again, probably a early-access-game issue as it seems there is an actual storyline planned, so probably end-game will be improved as well.- The terraformation starts as sandboxy, but ends with feeling very linear. The tech tree is designed in such a way, that it's very difficult to progress on one branch without progressing on the other. At the beginning it's not as noticeable, but when the grind begins - you actually start to understand that the tech-progression is pretty much meaningless, and you can just build whatever the new technology has unlocked without thinking much about it. In other words, there's only one way to play the game (build the latest technology unlocked) and the progression does not matter at all, making tech-tree pretty much time-locked and giving you no real choice on where do you want to progress.IMO - some sort of "research" system would help with this. Instead of time-locking everything, just let the person get some rare resource into "researcher" and unlock the tech this way.- I was not a fan of some locations being time-walled away. Don't think this counts as spoilers, but for some caves need you to reach a specific temperature to be unlocked. And reaching that temperature is pretty much a function of gameplay time (see previous point). Again, IMO it would be better to lock that behind some sort of research, like a "Drill T1" and "Drill T2", etc. Time-based access just feels fake.Overall, I think the devs got the general formula right, it's just a LOT of polishing that's needed in the gameplay loop. Still, the game is currently very playable and very satisfying, at least for the first 10 hours or so.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something I've wanted for so many years.No hostile mobs or other distractions, just surviving and slowlythrough incrementsbreathing life into a dark, dead rust coloured world.The changes are gradual, but you really notice them, after a little bit of messing around..Is that dark orange at the apex of the sky slowly turning into a golden corona?. Slowly getting stronger until the atmosphere breaks into a vibrant blue. Weather patterns slowly form, as the greenhouse gasses heat the planet ice wells melt and precipitation lashes dusty soil for the very first time.  Soon, puddles form and grow into lakes and rivers in the lower parts of the map (R.I.P first base) Eventually, after much exploring and gathering you can finally start to turn the planet green, low, primordial mosses and plants start to grow, you can adapt and plant flowers and trees.  Take a screenshot, on your first few minutes of playing, then look back at it once you have reached the end game. It's genuinely very moving.Absolutely recommend, and I look forward to checking back in a few years when it is finished and playing again, since the animal life is being worked on now, I cant wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Good day to all users of this game. My use of this game started with free early access, so I think all the same users have something to tell about this game. In addition, I would like to note that after the appearance of the map, it became much more comfortable to play , but I would like to see the display of the player himself on the map . I think many users started trying to create automated production systems for some items and faced the problem of drones, the developers added drones version 2, differing in only one speed parameter. I would like to see drones version 2 not only with a speed bonus, but also the capacity of their inventory in at least 4 slots, this would allow us to optimize production to a new level. Due to the appearance of amphibians, we are faced with 4 species of frogs, plus or minus, it is worth developing this direction in the right direction because if you plan to introduce the game towards mammals, you need to create a more general branch of the previous animals because everything looks as if everything is limited to 4-5 species and is not moving anywhere. As for resources , you continue to introduce new , rarer and more valuable resources , but you forgot about the old ones. I would like to optimize the use of resources such as ( silicon , magnesium , cobalt ) in some way in crafting , because after advancing technologically , we simply forget about them and do not use them so often , and there is almost no correction at all we use it with some exceptions. Personally, I would like to see something like large greenhouse complexes because putting small incubators for vegetables is something of a torment for them you have to allocate very large areas , you added a large number of seeds , but their use for production is not optimized. From the category of swords, there would be production facilities for the production of one or two products with related items to create, this would advance us in the study of technologically production vetoes (if you add them, of course). It dragged many users into the game for long hours and laid the foundation for the possibility of automaking many items and opened up a lot of opportunities, this is of course a pain in the ass in terms of optimizing production (personally, I sat down with this idea for 12 hours and did not leave the game yet, and everything worked out) I'm sure I'm not the only one who got to this point and many could give detailed instructions on production automation if the developers wanted to develop in this direction. _childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo for an hour or two and then uninstalled it … and immediately purchased the game!It really is a nice game to play. No hostile AI, players or monsters that attack you and ruin your day.  You can still die in it from lack of food, water or oxygen, the latter of which will more than likely get you a few times when you first start playing until you craft better longer lasting oxygen tanks.The tutorial is rather basic, with a guide that only takes you part of the way.  After that you are left to your own devices.  However, it’s quite easy to work out what you need to be building once the tutorial finishes by simply looking in the blueprint screen and seeing what is available, or what is to come.I play with an RTX 4090 and have no performance issues in game whatsoever.  However, the game does need optimising more as it does run my graphics card quite warm, and the fans work harder than they do with other games.  However, I am sure the devs will address this as the development of the game progresses.I play using a wireless Xbox controller and this works well, though I do find that when I start a new game, the right stick (camera) doesn’t work.  I simply go into settings/controls and save and close, without making any changes.  This seems to rectify the issue, and all is well.  Sometimes I find that I enter my inventory and cannot navigate it with the controller, but coming out of the inventory and going back into it rectifies the issue.As many others have pointed out it is quite Subnauticaesque in the way it’s played, and I like that!Gameplay is smooth and relaxing.  Many of the basic ingredients you need, such as ice, iron, titanium and cobalt are in plentiful supply around you.  Other more advanced ingredients will need to be looked for.A real gem of a game that plays very well, considering it’s early access.  I am hoping that as the development progresses, we may be able to travel to other planets and terraform them too.  Perhaps with varying degrees of difficulty.If you’re unsure if you’d like the game, try the free demo first.  I am not sure how far you can play with it, but it certainly is long enough for you to get a feel of the game.This game has plenty of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great steam ratings but for me is a Subnautica clone that substitutes wonder and discovery with grind.  The crafting, base building, food, oxygen and watering systems are all directly lifted from Subnautica and play at similar levels of difficulty (from chilll to moderately difficult).  Where the games differ is the playing experience.  In Subnautica the world is handcrafted with distinctly different bases to discover, technology scraps to find and a mystery to solve.  In Planet Crafter there is no discovery or suspense.  Your goal is clear from the start - to terraform the planet.  The tech tree is laid out in full from the beginning and progress is made by grinding out production machines that will build a terraforming score.  When the score gets high enough there will be a change (e.g. clouds form) and then its back to the grind.  When the score gets high enough a technology will also unlock for no apparent reason.   The points of interest  on the map use duplicated assets, meaning no place is actually that interesting or different.   If you turned the need to eat and drink off in the settings then you could literally leave the game for a day and come back and your production machines will have terraformed the planet for you.  I can't recommend this game, when Subnautica handles the same themes so much better. I definetely can't recommend a game that doesn't need your involvement to win.  If you like social grind games on mobile phones, then you may like this - otherwise I would save your pennies.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: My friends are a bit surprised that I am playing this game as I don't typically like "space games", but this one is absolutely amazing. The story is haunting and beautiful. You have to find the story pieces because they're not all given to you, but once you find them, <chef's kiss>. I actually am paused here in (no spoilers), and I am feeling the emotions of knowing the events that happened here that the story just revealed, and I actually am having to take a moment to emotionally process what I just learned. Story: A+The gameplay is smooth, and while there are a few graphical glitches that happen on occasion, I have not encountered any game-breaking bugs, and the glitches pass quickly. This game is rather enjoyable, and the tiers (as you meet them) feel like accomplishments. So far everything runs very smoothly, and there is an incredible amount of polish for the game being in early access. You can also control how quickly the terraformation occurs, so if you want to just kick back, and slowly work your way through it, you can. You also get the means to speed up the terraformation if you want, so the pacing is enjoyable as well because you decide the pacing.Gameplay: APacing: A+I cannot say enough positive things about this game. Definitely try it out. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game... until the final stage.I had not played this game in any of it's Early Access states.Throughout the game the pacing was great, all different stats to progress felt rewarding with the next building or craftable item. The exploration on the planet was also very well paced, you can only go so far with limited oxygen. The little stories hidden within are intriguing enough to want to follow them and discover more. The biggest issue this game has is the endgame. Nothing new is added to the table. Going from Mammals to Complete Terraformation is a chore. No new items, no new buildings. Just keep pumping those numbers. I think it would be much better if:-There are more buildings or craftable items to unlock (maybe a T6 Drill and Heater)-More creature variety-Reduce the target from 5TTi to 3TTiThen we come to the endings. One of the endings is even more huge grind and I found myself carrying on just to get the achievement and wishing the game to end, which is a real shame as the vast majority of the experience was really great. There are a few bugs here and there, which you can report in game, that need ironing out. The fact that only 2 people (I think) made this game is incredible and they have done a fantastic job.I recommend this game game to any who are interested, but if you hate a bit of grind then maybe give this one a miss (or play the demo and see how you feel!). If you hate a lot of grind there are 2 other endings to do instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A good sandbox crafting game. If you like the satisfaction of watching numbers go up, you'll enjoy it. The early parts of the game play a bit more like a survival sim, with finding food, water and oxygen being your main concern. You have to make your way around the planet gathering resources and terraforming the planet, laying down small bases to serve as refueling points. I enjoyed the survival aspect of this, and the strategy of stocking up my inventory to go on exploratory runs. Once you have your three basic needs sorted, the game becomes more of an efficiency simulator. I liked exploring the different biomes and discovering bits of story here and there. There was definitely more game here than I was expecting for a title only recently out of EA. That said, once you hit the 'animals' level of terrformation, the rest of the path to the ending is a bit of a grind. I gotta recognise that the devs did put some work into making sure that a lot of the slog (mainly travelling around) is cut down by then but essentially yeah, you'll be placing more and more of what you already have to try and boost your terraforming percentage.I found the game most enjoyable as something to play on one monitor while I had livestreams or music going on the other. There being no enemies means you can just relax and focus on making your planet look nice and advancing. There is some story, which encourages exploration and kept me interested in playing to the end, but it's not a narrative-driven game.Some of the UI could use tweaking (it can be confusing to tell what object you have highlighted in the crafting menu) and some of the tech advancements seem to come in a less-than-ideal order: e.g. I was already jetting around with a backpack way before I unlocked limited-time running boosts from food.Recommended if you want something to scratch the Subnautica itch but without the fear of the deep.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love and recommend this game to anyone who loves survival or crafting simulations. its unique in my experience as the planet and environment actually change as you reach new terraforming milestones. The collectionist in me spent a lot of time trying to get every tree, insect, frog and fish so with the new animals update, I am thrilled at the possibilities of so many configurations. And I love that once you place a type of flora or fauna in the area around your base or bases, they start appearing in other places on the planet.  I also really like that you don't need to have power and other items right next to your main base, because you can have bases all over, any power item you put down anywhere powers everywhere. I think the only thing you need to have in a specific radius is a communications tower and the communications screen.While there are only a few base building pieces this still gives you the freedom to imagine a ton of different configurations, even building in the sky! I hope in the future they allow for underwater and underground builds and additional or more types of building pieces for those who want true building customization. I am hoping to get other people I know interested to try out the multiplayer aspects as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is a game that does so much with so little.The graphics aren't anything to write home about.The gameplay is basic: get resources, build things, survive, repeat.The story is almost non-existent (it's there, you just have to look for it and it doesn't *really* matter)So... Why is it good?Every little thing that it does that's been done before, it does it well.The graphics get across exactly what the game is trying to do; transitioning a planet from a desolate wasteland to a verdant resource. And it does so incredibly well and incrementally.The gameplay loop is perfect for throwing you into an environment, pointing you in a direction, letting you go without holding your hand. And each step you take towards a goal gives you a substantial reward that can be immediately useful. NOTHING in this game is useless in the gameplay loop.The environments, while basic, are each unique and well executed even if they aren't mind-blowing or breathtaking by today's graphical standards.The best part? The actual, visible, tangible change to the planet. I don't think there's ever been a game I've played where progress is so.... rewarding and interesting.There are flaws, obviously. But I think this game did what a lot of other games with better graphics and bigger budgets failed to do... It was interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea for a game, terrible execution beyond the Prologue. This is probably why the reviews are so biased, as players are prompted for a review way too early into the game. Beyond the Prologue was extremely tedious and boring. I honestly spent half of my time AFK cooking dinner, napping, out at the bar, etc while letting my character die & respawn in the base just to keep the terraforming meter moving (and yes, I know about the amplifiers in the game and had dozens & dozens active of each variety and it still moved at a snail's pace).No enemies, repetitive loot (some of which would still spawn even after their sole purpose was already used to unlock items in game), menus with overlayed items outside of the menu's borders, clipping through walls & floors - including falling through the entire playable map into the game engine's abyss, major FPS drops in several regions (I meet recommended system requirements by a long shot), items disappearing, items floating in mid air, items stuck in walls, audio glitches, graphical glitches, sunlight randomly in underground caves with no access to a light source, items unlocking in the wrong order, game controls randomly stopping from working...All of this, and you get only ONE map -- and it's not even random, so no replay value. Want to play again? Buy the DLC map (which is smaller and simplified, but hey -- cool colored planet, right?). This is just insulting to players, and it's becoming common place on Steam. This is an Early Access game at best, but I recommend sticking with the free Prologue for the experience. I was surprised how far into the game it allowed me considering it froze the terraforming progress early on, so you're really only missing graphical changes beyond that point. Save your time & money, folks!PS - I really wanted to complete all 3 endings & get my 100% achievements before submitting this review, but after looking up their requirements it was clear that I would need to spend another 50+ hours playing in order to do so, and I would rather dig lint out of my belly button than play another minute of this drool-inducing game. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: "Do something simple, do it well."This was the goal stated by the game devs in a news update back when I first reviewed this game in version 0.4.008. Back then, I said the game lived up to it, but needed some polishing. Now, coming back to the full release version, I can safely say that it's received all that polish and then some.I love the concept of terraforming games in general, and I especially love when they're done well. This game is all about the terraforming, and it doesn't waste time getting bogged down in combat, economics, or other distractions. And it's BRILLIANT.What we have here is a planetary terraforming game that starts as a base building survival game that requires you to explore and gather food and water to stay alive, while maintaining your oxygen levels while away from your base. Eventually, you gain the ability to produce your own food and water, at which point it transitions from survival to the most perfectly chill game I have ever seen.Once you've reached the chill stage, it's basically a giant sandbox where you just gather, build, grow, and explore... and then explore again, once your terraforming level goes up and the environment changes. While you can technically make the game "harder" by altering game settings, all that tends to do is lengthen the timeline of a given save file. It doesn't really make the game more difficult, especially after you've gotten familiar with the gameplay loop, but honestly, that doesn't matter. This isn't the sort of game you play for a challenge. It's the kind of game you play to just relax and build your bases as you watch craters turn into lakes, barren fields into grasslands, and valleys into jungles.If you don't like that concept, this one probably isn't for you. If you do, this is gaming perfection.10/10. Legitimately one of my favorite games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for both survival-sandbox and terraforming games, so when I saw this was finally out of Early Access I grabbed the demo and gave it a whirl. Enjoyed it enough to buy the full game and play it through to the end. is clearly inspired by ; then again, that one was such a genre-definer that it's hard not to be.  But  does manage to mostly find its own path.  As with , you start out crash-landing with nothing but a few emergency rations and a very basic synthesizer. From there you have to hold your breath long enough to scavenge some resources, improve your gear, build a simple base, and eventually reach the point of self-sufficiency.  Then the game really starts as you head down the long, slow road of bringing a planet to life.The most noticeable difference from , aside from, y'know, not being underwater, is that there's very little danger.  The only living thing on the entire planet is you, so your only enemies are your oxygen and water bars (and the occasional meteor to the face).  This makes the game actually rather chill, and it's quite satisfying to see the planet change right before your eyes.As with most terraforming games, the endgame can be a real slog.  Once you've explored all the places and found all the things, there's really nothing left to do but sit and watch the counters tick up.  For me it really stalled out in the amphibian stage. Felt like I was stuck there for ages as the planet was slowly taken over by frogs and butterflies.  Things picked up again once I hit the mammal stage, though; none of the animals eat grass, apparently, and building up enough of a production line to keep them fed and happy turned out to be quite the endeavor, which was distracting enough to get most of the way through to the end.  The genetic splicing bit was fun, too - even got my daughter to design one of the animals.And if you run out of stuff to do, you can always spend some time crawling the procedurally-generated shipwrecks to find rare resources that you can't produce yourself.  But even that gets tedious after a while.  (Hint: you'll need more money than you think if you want to see all of the endings).Overall, it's a solid, if slow-paced, game. Not quite in the same league as  but enjoyable nonetheless.
