_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR? Yes I highly recommend trying this game if it aligns with your preferred genre.Guild Wars 2 - A World of Endless Adventure and Engaging Game playBefore diving into my detailed review of Guild Wars 2, it's important to note that it is a massive multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) cherished by millions of dedicated players worldwide. This review is based on my personal experience with the game, supplemented by the overwhelmingly positive reviews expressed by the Guild Wars 2 community on the store page.1. Dynamic and Beautiful World:GW2 offers one of the most captivating and visually stunning game worlds in the MMORPG genre. From lush forests to desolate wastelands, each area is crafted with meticulous detail, breathing life into the game world. The developers' commitment to continuously adding new regions and expanding the lore ensures that there is always something exciting to explore.2. Engaging Story line and Quests:The game boasts an immersive and evolving story line, masterfully woven with intricate plot twists and memorable characters. Players will be drawn into a narrative that adapts based on their decisions, emphasizing the significance of their choices. Coupled with hundreds of quests that are far from repetitive, GW2 ensures that players always have a purpose and a sense of adventure.3. Class and Race Diversity:GW2's character creation offers an impressive level of customization. With nine diverse playable races and a wide range of classes, players can create a character that aligns with their preferred play-style seamlessly. This diversity encourages multiple playthroughs, adding replayability and extending the game's longevity.4. Dynamic Events and World vs. World:Dynamic events breathe life into the world of Tyria, ensuring that even mundane tasks are transformed into thrilling adventures. These events frequently occur in various corners of the map, creating a dynamic and immersive experience. Additionally, the World vs. World mode allows players to compete in large-scale battles, conquering fortresses and fighting alongside their comrades for global dominance.5. Strong and Supportive Community:GW2 stands out for fostering a uniquely inclusive and supportive community. Players are always willing to lend a helping hand, guide newcomers, and participate in cooperative game play. Whether through guilds, organized events, or the game's built-in social features, players can easily find a sense of belonging within the passionate GW2 community.6. No Subscription and Fair Micro-transactions:GW2 has a "Buy to Play" payment model, meaning no monthly subscription is required. The developers' commitment to players is further demonstrated through micro-transactions that concentrate primarily on cosmetic items, convenience, and quality-of-life improvements. This approach ensures a fair playing field for all players, regardless of their payment choices.7. Constant Updates and Expansions:GW2 is consistently refreshed with abundant free updates and expansions, keeping the game exciting and providing players with new content to explore. The developers' dedication to consistently improving the game based on player feedback underscores their commitment to delivering an exceptional gaming experience.In conclusion, GW2 is an exceptional MMORPG that captivates players with its breathtaking world, engaging storytelling, diverse character options, and dynamic game-play. The overwhelmingly positive reviews on the Steam store page reflect the game's enduring popularity and the immense enjoyment it brings to its dedicated community. Whether you're a veteran MMO player or new to the genre, Guild Wars 2 is an adventure you won't want to miss!

_childDocuments_.review: I have 3,380 hours in this game. I have many things to say, but the crux of it is: Try the game for yourself and see if you like it. There's a mountain of good content without buying expansions. You don't need them to have fun, but they add endless hours of content. Whether you enjoy playing alone or with friends, if you prefer the levelling experience or the endgame, if you like challenging content or just taking it easy, if you enjoy fashion or just want to grind our raids, this game has a little something for everyone.Guild Wars 2 isn't exaggerating when it advertises itself as the MMORPG that literally changed the MMORPG industry. You can draw a sharp line between "old"-style and "new"-style MMOs, and Guild Wars 2 is that line. SWTOR started to tiptoe away from the classic way that games like WoW and LotRO were designed, but Guild Wars 2 completely did its own thing as though no other MMORPG had ever existed. Since then, every MMORPG has in some way been inspired by GW2 (and even a certain older MMORPG that's trying to hold its sub base).My only major gripes are with the way it was integrated into Steam. I can't link my existing account to Steam, and that launching through Steam brings up the game's launcher, but doesn't let me log into my own account.With over 3k hours played, I have plenty of nitpicks and some major issues, but ultimately, the game is fun and I strongly recommend it. It's not the greatest game ever made, but I would say it's one of the best MMORPGs ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably one of the most hardcore players on this game. I have been playing for 10 years and I have around 25k hours count on my account so this is not a new player review.With this being said I'm not going to lie and sell you the game as a perfect game.I'm realistic it have a lot of issues, but most of these (if not all of them) are only relevant for a really long time veteran player, because we somehow demand more stuff and faster than the developers can deliver, so don't take that too seriously,it's just a very passionate group of people that just want more and more. Arenanet management has been a huge problem for years mostly by choosing the wrong priorities. But things seems better now and the release here on Steam is proof of that.For you if you are starting now, damn I envy you. You are blessed, you have YEARS of content ahead, there is legit so much stuff to do, FUN stuff and actually always relevant because veterans like me are everywhere around still enjoying the same stuff because its FUN.I make guides and content to help people because me and many other people in the community actually love to help each other. The community is nice but you still can find some bad apples, like everywhere, it's not perfect so don't believe that.The game offers a lot of things to do but sadly it fails on communicating these to the player and due to how immense the variety of stuff to do is, most players get lost or don't even have the chance to experiment the different options, so make sure to not underestimate the game by your very first experience.This is mainly because the game have horizontal progression, you can do stuff when you want and how you want, so you have to set your own goals.The game values your time and your freedom, you aren't being told or forced to do something. And while this sounds nice and It's actually very good in my opinion, some people just dislike this and they actually NEED that the game set the goals for them. So this is why in the end many people choose to follow my guides because I help them to sort the goals.I like to compare it like a sandbox, especially that is why I enjoy the World vs World game mode in GW2, which is like a semi "open world pvp" mode, the freedom to do what you want and the unexpected things.So my recommendation is: Play it long enough to discover the different things, if you don't have patience for the start use a lvl 80 booster and just experience the huge variety of things to do in the endgame. You can always backtrack stuff or create alts.You might find some modes and activities more interesting than others and you might want to stick to those, but you need to experience it yourself, and still if you need guidance make sure to check out all the awesome Guild Wars 2 content creators (like me :D) around who make guides, videos, streams, etc. Arenanet could do a better job supporting them though.

_childDocuments_.review: The best MMO, and especially the best MMO for those of us who have lives outside of video games. A minimal amount of grind, amazing combat, huge world bosses and map meta events where you and 60 of your best friends work together to save the world, great story, cool lore, fun endgame content, horizontal rather than vertical progression (no gear grind!!!), etc etc.The biggest draw for this game in my opinion is how much it rewards cooperation. If you're used to an MMO which forces you to share XP and loot, this game doesn't do that. As long as you participated, you get experience, and there is NO loot sharing or stealing. This being the case, the community is one of the best in any online game, because there is absolutely no downside to helping people out, and that truly has fostered an amazing group of people to play with.I recommend it. And I have now played 900 hours only running it through steam and I still think this is all true.

_childDocuments_.review: The product of what happens when game devs actually listen to their community. I have personally never been a fan of MMOs, or I would give them a try and drop them in a few days. With bad recent experiences with Bless Unleashed and New World I was skeptical to try anything else in the genre. However, 2 months ago I got the itch again and didn't know what to do. I spent hours researching to try to find a good fit for me and I really only had a few boxes I wanted checked. I needed a game that was not extremely grindy, valued my time as a player, was still decently populated, and had fun combat mechanics. Guild Wars 2 stood out and checked all of those boxes and them some. It is amazing what can happen when game devs like these actually listen to their player base and put them first. The game is just SO good in so many different ways. It offers a vast amount and variety of content, the nicest and most helpful player base, regular events and updates, and so much more. I will say, Guild Wars 2 is not easy to get into, but that should not sway you from giving it a try. The classes, player builds, gear ladder, and mastery system are quite complex but there is always someone willing to answer your questions. Grab the game, hop in, join a guild, and mess around. The real beauty of this game is exploring and finding things out on your own. I am, again, someone who doesn't like MMOs. However, I am still playing Guild Wars 2 daily and it is close to being my most played steam game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played countless MMOs, but GW2 is the only one that I keep coming back to. It is one of the few MMOs with a horizontal progression system. This means that the level cap has stayed at 80 and ascended/legendary gear is still the best after 10+ years. I played heavily when GW2 launched in 2012 and then took a 6 year break. When I returned, my level 80 characters were still geared for most content in the game. GW2 is the only MMO where taking an extended break doesn't punish you and invalidate your progress.So what is the point of playing? First of all, fully gearing a character still takes time, especially when playing multiple builds and classes. Secondly, there is no shortage of goals to grind for (it is an MMORPG after all). The goals simply aren't all tied to character power like vertical progression games. Lastly, the answer depends on the player because GW2 caters to so many different audiences. Some of my favorites are listed below.With 5 playable races, 5 Living World seasons, 4 expansions, and more to come, GW2 truly has a decade of content. Almost all of it is fully voice acted including minor NPCs. The quality of the story varies but is good overall. The Personal Story (base game) and Icebrood Saga (LW season 5) are lackluster in my opinion. Everything else ranges from good to amazing. LW season 4 in particular was an absolute joy to experience for the first time.Each race has a wealth of history to discover. The Sylvari (plant people) are my favorite. Their aesthetics are very creative, and they have the curious perspective of only existing for ~35 years in the game's timeline. Every race has a dedicated male and female voice actor which keeps things fresh when playing through the story as a different race or gender. There are also plenty of non-playable races with their own lore and culture such as the Tengu (bird people), Kodan (polar bear people), Choya (cactus rascals), Skritt (rat-like hivemind), etc.GW2 makes exploration feel natural. It is very fun to explore a zone for the first time. Every zone is filled with discoverable points of interest and dynamic events. Many zones also have jumping puzzles and meta events that can span the entire map. Transitioning between these activities is seamless and usually lead to undiscovered portions of the map. Level scaling, achievements, and meta events mean that zones stay populated beyond leveling.The dynamic/meta events are top notch game design. If there are players doing an event, you can simply follow them. You don't have to worry about picking up a quest, backtracking to turn it in, or forming parties (though you can if you want). All you have to do is participate to receive credit. This makes it incredibly easy to aid other players you come across, and has helped foster GW2's notoriously friendly community. One example of this is world bosses. These are massive bosses that spawn in specific zones on a timer. There are usually a few Commanders ready and waiting to lead 50+ people to kill the boss, and anyone in the area can join in. Stumbling across a swarm of players attacking a world boss while leveling really captures the "massively multiplayer" in MMO.How will you show off to your friends without an endless supply of equipment with bigger numbers? By styling on them with superior fashion sense of course! GW2 has an insane amount of skins to collect. Once unlocked, skins are available in the account-wide wardrobe forever. The only cost to reskin an item is a Transmutation Charge which can be obtained in game or bought with real money. I've never bought a single one and have more than I can use. If you're up for the grind, one of the perks of legendary items is that they can be reskinned for free. Unfortunately, many cosmetics are gem store exclusive (real money), but that is a trade off of a non-subscription MMO. However, you can farm gold and exchange it for gems in-game, and many skins are tradable on the auction house. Additionally, there are lots of cool skins that can only be acquired through gameplay.But wait, there's more! There are also account-wide unlockable dyes. Changing dyes is unlimited and completely free, so swap colors as much as you like. There are currently 636 dyes in the game that range from basic colors to dyes with special effects such as a vibrant glow or metallic finish. With the exception of weapons, most skins are dyeable including mounts. Many skins have multiple dye channels which greatly expands customization. To my knowledge, every dye is purchasable on the auction house, even ones bought from the gem store (although those can get pricey). Dyes can also be obtained through gameplay, crafting, and birthday gifts.The community has created some excellent "cosplays". Whether you want to be a cute, pink princess, a battle-hardened war veteran, or a gloomy goth, it's all possible. I've even seen a shockingly accurate Optimus Prime out in the wild.The main format of "Structured PvP" is Conquest, a 5v5 capture point mode. Shorter 2v2 and 3v3 deathmatch leagues are run between Conquest leagues. All equipment is standardized and skills are balanced separately to PvE and WvW. Characters are set to level 80 which means a new character can jump straight into PvP! The only exception is elite specializations which are locked behind expansions.The combat in GW2 is so satisfying. It is action combat oriented with dodging and a little tab targeting thrown in. What makes it work so well is that there aren't any global cooldowns and most skills can be used while moving. Every class has its own identity and multiple playstyles. All of this results in fast paced, fluid combat that is engaging and fun to learn.Unfortunately, PvP has been neglected and only receives balance patches every few months. It desperately needs new content or refreshed rewards. I and many others continue to play PvP because we genuinely find it fun. The combat is just that good.WvW combines the best parts of GW2. It is a 24/7 territorial siege between three "worlds" (3 gigantic teams) with PvE and PvP objectives across multiple maps. There can be hundreds of players battling over control of a keep, roaming groups looking for skirmishes, and even solo players sneaking around flipping camps. Playing WvW with a good Commander is some of the most fun I've ever had in any game. There are plenty of Commanders who lead public groups as well as dedicated WvW guilds. It's also great to play casually with friends. Even getting steamrolled by a massive enemy zerg can be fun. To top it off, WvW has good rewards and loot drops like candy in battles. The only downside is that maps fill up quickly during peak hours and can feel dead other times since WvW never ends. GW2 has the BEST mounts of any game. They aren't just designed to get from point A to B. Each mount feels like a living animal and behaves differently. There's nothing quite like sky diving on a Griffon or drifting on a Roller Beetle. ArenaNet lumps anything from small easter eggs to epic quest lines in the achievements. Many of GW2's best goals and rewards are buried here. If you're unsure of what to do next, make sure to dig through the achievements. A guild hall is a huge time and gold sink, but it has many benefits and can be decorated. It is even possible to make Roller Beetle racing tracks. Gradually upgrading a guild is perfect for a group of friends. There are 6 annual festivals for various occasions. They have special rewards and are an easy way to farm gold. These instanced encounters are the hardest PvE content in GW2. The tiered progression of fractals is simple to get started with.

_childDocuments_.review: Guild Wars 2 is a stunningly looking, somewhat unconventional MMO with an incredibly detailed and dynamic world and one of the best action combat systems, held back by a chronically underfunded studio and different leads making, at times, erratic decisions that create new systems only to abandon them before they are fully baked. The game features PvE, PvP (which is rather dead at the moment) and World vs World vs World, a weekly large scale PvP match between 3 different teams / servers, a very unique and engaging gameplay mode if you band together with other players. Unlike any other online game I ever played, the servers are never down for maintenance. You can keep playing, patch within the 2 hour window and hop right back in into a patched server.As someone who has played the game since release for over 10000 hours I can safely say that now is the best time to start as a new player (when it comes to PVE, which is the main meat of the game). Systems have been reworked and streamlined, content has been added over the years and there's a boatload of things to do to keep you engaged. Even the very old maps are still well populated thanks to collections and world events funneling people to them and due to Megaservers which create instances as required. So your server choice at the beginning has zero impact on PVE and only matters for World vs World vs World.PvE works with the idea that "it's never bad to see another player" - people cannot steal your XP, loot or resource nodes, everything is shared or clientside, random players can heal, buff and revive you without being in your party.PvP allows you to choose and pick gear right off the bat (however the Elite Specializations of the corresponding expansions are locked until you buy those, and they are generally more powerful than the base "Core" classes).WvW uses your PvE gear and build with tweaked numbers and offers everything from 1v1 dueling, roaming in small parties to large scale assaults on towers and keeps or threeway battles between three huge groups (where lag might become an issue).You will find GW2 players loving to complain about the cash shop (Gem Store), because it offers a lot of high quality skins that you cannot get ingame directly (see below about gold). Or that a mount skin costs roughly 20€ (in Central Europe). I think most of these people have not played other MMOs that squeeze more money for less out of you. The GW2 Gem Store has a lot of skins, but it is a cosmetics focused game. The skins offer zero gameplay benefit or advantage. Mounts need to be unlocked ingame via quests or story and otherwise the store offers convenience items but never an unfair advantage.It is a game of great ideas bound to an inevitable BUT that makes the experience less straightforward and maybe jarring to some players:* the combat is amazing and one of the most fun ones in any online game I have played, BUT the early game (base game, before expansions) does nothing to encourage you to try it. Mobs in Core Tyria (base game maps) are so braindead, slow and deal so little damage that you can finish all of it just autoattacking and standing still, more or less* this leads to people jumping into expansions that actually require you to understand the combat system basics and utterly failing because the game did not prepare them for it, causing them to hit a brick wall* the possible builds are rather staggering, with Attribute combinations on gear, weapon bonuses from Sigils and armor bonuses on Runes, Traits for each class, BUT most of the time the same 3-4 attribute combinations are relevant, because mixing and matching is a lot less useful* there is no vertical gear grind - the BiS gear quality from 8 years ago is still the best, except Attributes needed might have changed. You can play the game casually and you'll never find that you are losing in effective power. BUT this means all grind is purely for cosmetics, so bear that in mind* the world is rich in detail and lovingly crafted and one of the most immersive open worlds I have seen in an MMO, BUT you can completely ignore all of it just trying to complete map points for the reward, or tagging events and moving on once it's done without ever seeing all the rich follow-ups that enhance the world and your experience* you can make decent gold (which can be used to buy the premium currency, so technically you can be fully F2P in this game and still get everything from the cash shop) if you know what to do, BUT 99% of the loot you get in the game will feel unrewarding because the gold comes from crafting it, breaking it down or selling it in bulk on the trading post* there are a lot of very well made systems in place (like the Legendary Weapon Precursor scavenger hunts) that took a lot of time to be introduced and enhanced the game tremendously, BUT a lot of them are abandoned halfway through because "they cost too much time to make"* there are currently 27 specs to choose from (9 base classes plus 1 Elite Specialization per class that expands their abilities per expansion with 3 expansions currently), BUT balancing those is an ongoing struggle and they are not classic DPS, Tank Heal. So understanding what each class or spec can do based on the build you choose for them might be overwhelming at first. It is however aided by the community and third party sites* the game touts itself as having "the nicest community", BUT this is based on much content being in the open world where it does not really matter to you what others do most of the time. When it comes to instanced content (Dungeons, Fractals, Strike Missions, Raids) and the individual performance makes or breaks the group's success, people will naturally be less forgiving and friendlyAnd more I probably forgot about. None of this is a gamebreaker but the more you play the more you'll notice these things, which is a shame, because it is a lot of potential unused.Which is the main downside. The developer studio ArenaNet has always seemed like they are struggling with budget and given the size of the studio what they have achieved is quite impressive. However this also means new content is coming out at a slower pace, bugs and QoL fixes are taking more time and desperately needed overhauls are on the backburner or implemented halfway before being abandoned because there is "no time". As a new (or casual) player this will not affect you at all, but as a "hardcore" player spending the majority of your time in the game this will become more and more apparent.The other major downside is the lack of concrete vision. The leading heads of the studio have changed, people were laid off and the focus seems to shift between things every now and then, as if different teams are in the lead that period. But you don't feel much of a coherent overarching design vision. This will make feel some content, especially when you play it in one path start to finish, rather disjointed and shifting in tone. The game starts off as medieval / magitech / steampunk fantasy world with the base game, by the third expansion we are looking at the internet, long range transmissions and holograms in a futuristic looking city, all in the span of roughly 10 years of ingame time.Which segues into the last point - the story. The presentation jumps between base game, living world and expansions, characters behave inconsistently depending on who wrote them and the overall impact of the story is not as great as in most other MMOs.Guild Wars 2 is world building, lore, combat and immersion first and story second.To anyone trying it, you will have many people helping you no questions asked. It's definitely worth it to take a look, immerse yourself in the world and learn the ins and outs of the combat system - just don't get discouraged by the abysmal first 20 levels or by the braindead easy open world in the core game (which is sadly what you will see as F2P).

_childDocuments_.review: There's an endgame quest in which you defend a city against angry chickens. 10/10Jokes aside this MMO really is something else.The story in the base game is pretty good and immersive. There are fully voice acted cutscenes and even some personal choice-elements in certain missions.There are no typical "fetch quests" in this game, instead you have to help NPCs within the zones with a variety of things in order to get experience and level up. All the zones are also relevant despite which level you are since ArenaNet decided that horizontal progression is the way to go.There are also dynamic events that occur in almost all zones that make max level players return and that in turn makes the world feel alive.The story really picks up in the expansions and also other content such as; Raids, Fractals (Basically dungeons), Strikes (One hard boss encounters) among other stuff.Overall a great game to try out and immerse yourself into. It really scratches that MMO itch as well as the single player experience.What are you waiting for?

_childDocuments_.review: I am 134 hours in, so I've basically only scratched the surface of the game so far, but I am having fun. I am an old school WoW player, been burning that game between 2008 and 2016, I've seen it all and done it all pretty much, and here I am 8 years later giving this a go.Pros; The game is really looking good despite a tad older graphics (still far more advanced than WoW), it works flawlessly and I have had no issues so far. I love the mechanics of switching weapons and using both weapon skills and class skills, its very interactive, there are more ways than in WoW to make a unique character build, you can experiment a lot and see what suits you the best. With a few guides online I really got a grip of the game and I am not lost anymore. The content is huuuge, there is so much to do and I often get sidetracked over a possible jumping puzzle, or jumping in to help others with events, world bosses and such. The auction house is amazing to me, I was pleasantly surprised when I found out that once get your bags full you can sell most of the stuff via AH without going to the actual auction, which saved me a lot time. The combat itself is so much fun, I feel like I can just kill trash mobs the entire day and still have fun and have a feeling of an epic battle. I still haven't played wPvP which I intend to as soon as I get some masteries done, from what I've seen it will likely be my favorite part of the game.Cons; I know a lot of people love some characters and NPCs, they love the lore and the vast amount of conversations you can have. As someone who used to read all the quests in WoW and learn about the lore and important NPCs, I am quite disappointed with some of the characters I feel 'forced' to play with in story modes. I will not name any, but some characters really lack a good voice actor and sensible conversation. I know this game is for younger audiences but I cringe way to often at some inconsistencies in some characters, the oblivious and senseless chitchat during something that should be really important and big just turns off the feeling of epicness and makes me roll eyes. It sometimes feels like work rather than entertainment to wait for a couple of minutes while you're being forced to listen to some unskippable conversations that include some of the characters that feel annoying, in those moments I just feel like quitting the story quest and switching to other quests or events, but I need to do the story for mastery points. Due that reason I often play on mute when I do story and I have some playlist in the background killing the silence, which is a shame because the soundtracks in GW2 are amazing. There are some really epic characters that I like quite a lot, the writing and voices are top notch, so I am really surprised that some characters might vary so much in quality. I also feel the game can use some upgrades in LFG sector for easier dungeon access, but thats really not a big bother, I still managed to do a number of dungeons as I leveled up.Also, I wanted to single out one of pros at the end,I was baffled by how nice and welcoming the community is. I did not engage into any conversations yet because I feel like doing the game solo until I get a complete grip on it, but I often see other people conversing with zero toxicity, they're all very willing to help and I know if I asked some random dumb question out loud there would be at least three people giving me an honest answer. People help each other out, they will always ressurect you or give you a helping hand. I also haven't engaged myself in any guild so far, but I know the game will just get better once I do.In conclusion, I don't feel like it would make sense for me to give this game a grade, like I said I have only some 130ish hours in, I still have to try wPvP and raiding which is an endgame content and matters a lot. But from what I've seen so far, I would recommend this game to anyone who likes mmorpgs. Vanilla part of the game is free, and you don't really need all the DLCs at the beginning, and they're often in bundles and there sales often. I'd say its worth the money

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, try it and give it some time. This is coming from me with a day one account and also played wow for 10 years  mythic raiding.There are pro and con of both game, but i won't be talking about wow here as this is a GW2 review. All i Ask you gamer give this a fresh pair of eyes and do not compare this game with other MMO.1. The game is totally free to play, you  do not need to pay any anything, and you can buy GEM with your in game gold to buy anything from the in game gem store. Gem store item will not effect your equipment stats, most of them are for game play convenience, cosmetic items, toys. if people ask me: Is this game pay to win? I 'd say no. I will explain more in the gearing down below.2. No Subs, you can pick it up and leave the game for while any time, but there are 3 expansion pack you will need to pay for, which can also buy from in game gem store with gold (in game currency), remember everything in the gem store you can pay for with in game gold, that is in including those extra bank slot, character slot, extra bag slot, There are one thing to be noted: if you want to raid, wing 1 to wing 4, you must have HOT expac, if you want to have mounts and raid wing 5 to 7, you must have POF expac, fractal, does not need any of them to do, but the there are few elite specialisation are locked behind each of the expac, so if you do not have them, you may not have the strongest build you can get. Ask yourself how much you pay for a AAA game which will last you maybe 100 hours vs this game has been around and keep on updating content for 10 years. the 3 expansion are not expensive. (do not buy just yet, finish the review before you take out your credit card)3. At end game, There are a lot of things you can work on, if you like pvp, go swim in it, if you like WVW (world vs world), and some people only do that too, and if you into pve only? there are end game Fractal ( in other game they call it dungeons), Raids, open world event going all the time, each game mode will have their own LEGENDARY ARMOR you can work towards. Also achievements, for those achievement hunters out  there, there are too many achievement in this game. Lastly, there is legendary crafting, this is a huge part for GW2 community at end game, you will see people with flashy weapon/armour with great looking foot prints and aura while they are running around, they are from legendary equipment, your hard work won't be unnoticed once you crafted them.4 Gearing equipment and gears stats: one thing unique about GW2, each equipment Tier, it will give you extra stats, there are basic (white), Fine (blue)+25% stats, masterwork(green)+8% stats, rare (yellow) +7% stats, Exortic(orange)+14% stats, lastly, we have the ascended and legendary armour and weapons, they both have the same stats number, which is +6% stats from exotic gears, The different between ascended and legendary armour are: ascended armour and weapons are easier and way cheaper to craft, but you can not change the stats of them on the go, but you can change the stats of the ascended armour once you back in town with mystic forge with the cost of some materials. On the other hand, Legendary armour and weapons, they usually cost a lot of gold materials and also require you to do some achievements, to craft, but once you have done the hard work, you can change your equipment stats on the go as long as you are out of combat, that become hugely beneficial if you are playing a class can do dps support and healing, and once you crafted for example legendary light armour all your classes with light armour will have legendary light armour available for them as long as they are level 80, you have crafted all light medium and heavy legendary armour, you will never need to craft another piece of armour again in your GW2 life. unlike other MMO, you do not need to farm equipment again if you have ascended armour or legendary amour when there is a new raid or expac.put it this way, people running around with the ascended/legendary gears 5 years ago, will be still running around with the same ascended/legendary gears 5 years later.Is the game play to win:I'd say no, but in reality, you kinda can pay for legendary weapons with real life cash if you are really rich. we talked about you can exchange gold into gem, but you can also do it other way around, turn gem into gold.Let's pick latest legendary AXE Aurene's Rending, it cost 2889 gold in trading post (this is the action house in GW2),  in game gem store you can exchange  1 gold with 6 gems, so that 1 weapon converts into 17334 gems, in gem store top up, i think the cheapest way you can buy gem is $100 for 8000 gems, which will make it $1 per 80 gems, so that will make up the cost of that 1 weapon $216 USD and most classes require either 2 two handed weapon or 4 one handed weapons, so you will be looking at either paying $432 for 2 two handed weapon, or $864 for 4 one handed weapons, but can just craft ascended weapon with 30 to 40 gold each, and there are ascended weapons from story line and achievement you can get them for free.(remember ascended equipment and legendary equipment have the same total stats on them.)Buying this 1 item does not complete your build, and you can not buy your way into legendary armour and trinket, so you still having to farm them. but can you win against other players in pvp and wvw once you have full set of ascended/ legendary gears? That is a NO, at end game of GW2 players at top level  share the same number total stats, so it is really depending on your the stats you pick on your gears and also traits on your character. I love the game, and I have been playing this game for many years, and will be playing this game for more years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore steam hours, I have four max level characters on my main account. This review might be a bit long, but GW2 does things differently from most others.Though it's not as populated as other MMO's, the community is still going strong. People will happily help new comers (myself included) and toxicity is pretty rare. You can find it occasionally in PvP, but that can be safely ignored if that's not your thing. Guilds are here of course and most of them are pretty tight knit. So if you go looking for a guild, your best bet is the GW2 forums. The story is quite good! Story quests play out as an instanced quest chain. The first two quest chains are determined by the background you choose when you make your character. The next two chains by choices you make in the story itself than goes to a set path. It can be skipped pretty easily if you want, but I suggest giving it a try for your first time around!GW2 does quests a bit differently than most others in this genre. Instead of picking up a quest from a quest giver and killing x number of enemies, you have hearts which activate when you enter it's area. These hearts can fill from a variety of activities. One heart has you clear pests, play with puppies, help lost dogs, and knock down weeds for example. GW2 also places a focus on exploration. discovering points of interest on the map gives you xp and contributes to map completion. There's also vistas to be discovered that give you panning shots of the games more beautiful locals. Reaching 100 map completion for an area grants you a random reward, and is necessary if you want to craft certain legendary weapons.There are nine classes. Three each of heavy armor, medium armor, and light armor. Each class can equip a range of weapons that change the abilities they can use. For example, Mesmer can equip daggers, scepters, wands, focus's and great sword. Each weapon has unique abilities that can drastically change how you play your character! Most classes can also equip a second set of weapons that you can switch to on the fly, granting you even more flexibility. Aside from weapons, you have also skills. Skills are different. They can be freely switched out and are available no matter what weapon you're using. There are a ton of different skills for each class and even some racial skills! Though these tend to be weaker than class skills.Crafting also works a bit differently, but can still be grindy like others. You can learn two crafting skills. the usual weapon and armor crafting, as well as cooking. Crafting materials are find out in the wild and can be stored in a completely separate crafting storage so it's not flooding your inventory. Crafting is focused on discovery. You combine different components to discover a recipe, which adds it to your crafting list and gives a burst of xp and crafting skill. Higher crafting skill unlocks more recipes. Crafting is the only way to make legendary weapons, but legendary weapons are mostly cosmetic, adding cosmetic visual affects to class abilities and is more of a way to reward players that do a ton of different things more than a necessary thing.Aside from the purchaseable expansions, you have an in game shop with mostly cosmetic options. There are a few utility type things like unlimited harvesting tools, additional character slots, more bank space, the ability to learn more crafting skills and keys for loot boxes. The in game shop isn't the most egregious i've seen in an mmo, but nothing there screams have to have. if you wanted to spend some money on this game, I suggest getting all the expansions first and foremost.You've probably noticed this already, but the game has a gorgeous watercolor aesthetic for none 3d assets. The graphics on the models are fine. pretty in line for an MMO really. The music in this game is above average with some real stand out tracks. Weapon hits are skills are appropriately weighty sounding and give good feedback. Example of a standout trackArena Net crafted a wonderful game here that most people overlook for more popular fair. GW2 respects your time more than most others, offers fresh takes on classes and customization, and offers a great and emotionally touching story. If you're reading this far, I implore you to give this game a try. The most it'll cost you is a bit of your time. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, worst MMO community in-game I've EVER encountered. I cannot tell you how many times I've stopped to clear out mobs and revive random players just to have them run off without saying a word AND 9 out of 10 times that I ask for simple help I get no response, YET offer one criticism of the game in map/zone chat and everyone starts screaming "SKILL ISSUE SKILL ISSUE SKILL ISSUE." It's like the community is made up primarily of AI drones.Second, the story/quest missions are horrendous. The number of bugs, drawn out and un-skippable dialogs, terrible "action" mechanics (spamming 1 button for a "epic" boss fight, attacks that cannot be dodge'd or blocked, long drawn out damage-sponge battles, etc) is incredible for one game. I know this game was made YEARS ago, but it's 2023 and there's DLC's still dropping so go back and patch your game.Third, the exploration and mini side quests are great. They give me the nostalgia of my first time playing classic WoW which is what I was looking for in a MMO. Sadly in order to get a "flying" mount (the two airborne mounts act more like gliders than flyers) and enhance your exploration potential, you basically need to sell your soul and go down a checklist of 100+ items along with sitting through 2 10-hour long campaigns just for ONE "flyer"... which isn't really even a flyer. The griffon is strictly a glider and the skyscale (dragon) requires rest (landing or downwards glide) to traverse upwards so you're basically just jumping with wings while looking bad ass. Give me a cow-sized bumble bee that actually flies to ride around on and I'll be happy.As I write this there's an in-game festival which has multiple events that I will admit are decently fun. One event is 6 bosses in a sectioned coliseum and as each boss is dropped it passes a unique power on to the remaining bosses... basically it's a massacre with about 200 players all trying to work together to spread out and take down the 6 as close to simultaneously as possible. Very cool concept and very nostalgic to raid mechanics from the early 2000sI haven't tried the raids/fractals/strikes and I haven't tried the PVP so I can't comment on that content, but after paying around 100$ for 3 of the 4 expansions there's enough issues with the game where I'm saying to steer clear of it. Play the free content if you're looking for a quick fix of PVE similar to classic WoW

_childDocuments_.review: The new player expecience:It is... strange, but in a positive manner. While being thrown into a vast world with some guidance, there is a constant feeling of... odd. Now, as a new player you'll have your hand held in a way, plus the "mentors", experianced players that spend time in the starting zones in order to offer extra help/guidance to new players. This is awesome! The issue is simple, as a new player, the game can be quite off putting. There is a lot to do, while also having nothing too fun to do. Dungeons are (somewhat) dead, due to players being... I don't know. In almost 20 hours of gameplay, I have not seen that many players to be honest. The game is massive, but it feels empty. If there would have not been NPCs around to do random events, it would have felt straigth up dead.The pvp aspect of the game is like in any other MMO, if you're new, you'll be cursed to oblivion and beyong.The crafting system is not that easy to get into, unless you spend time watching 20+ minute videos on youtube.The combat feels... it does not have much of any feeling, nothing special, just like melee skyrim. Click a button and DMG happents, nothing to feel, nothing to watch really. The level balance of zones is a wonderful idea, except when it is not. It is difficult to keep up if you're solo. Like dungeons... Doing a dungeon solo is in a way, close to impossible. And with very few players actually running dungeons, you're going to spend a decent chunk of time just waiting for other players.

_childDocuments_.review: Very strongly focused on respecting the player, their time, and their relation to others players' characters. Almost all progression, apart from your initial 80 levels, is horizontal - you get mounts that can make you more mobile and able of moving in more dimensions, you unlock new ways to interact with the environment like boating and gliding, you gain a subclass which mostly just makes your gameplay different, not much better, etc. Even the greatest goals of the game, Legendary equipment, are only as powerful as the tier below them - the only thing they actually add after that is the ability to fully re-spec the weapon at will, which is once again, incredibly useful but not a form of vertical progression. Everyone is equal, basically. This is even reflected in its truly free to play/buy to play nature - you can't even buy your way into more months of gameplay, making you more able to connect with the community than others. Everyone gets to participate exactly as much as they like.One could argue this comes with downsides, like any design decision - if everyone is equal and you aren't compelled to make good use of your playtime, maybe you'll feel aimless? But I'd rather be aimless than exploited.The story and gameplay is also still excellent. I highly recommend playing through Heart of Thorns at least, it's a ton of fun. Very soloable, if that matters to you, though the community is also very friendly and will gladly help.I have played many hundreds of hours of this, joined early. Luckily, you can play the Steam version even with your non-Steam account, you just need to input a launch command to let the client know.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out great - but - it's a trap!After level 80, it all falls apart.   Storyline (80+) issues...1) Horribly buggy, unclear, boring, and inconsistent.2) Babbling.  NPCs talk too much!  You can't hurry them up -- can't continue until they are done babbling.   Occasionally funny / important, but mostly just boring.  At lower levels, you can skip-to-end but later, you cannot.3) Wild goose chases.  Sometimes quests say "find the item" but means "talk to your team of NPCs" ... I'd run around searching,  then happen to get close enough to an NPC to trigger the dialog to continue.  Then *sigh* wait for them to babble about it.  4) Saving progress.  Sometimes progress is saved at certain points, so you can start near where you left off.  Not all storyolines have this.  I had to redo one area several times: Each time run all the way over here to listen to NPC's babble, then walk a bit, wait for NPCs to catch up, then babble some more, and more walking, finally a battle! ...and *sigh* more babbling...  not fun! x4!5) Lost XP.  At 80+ your XP goes to leveling masteries, which also need mastery points to complete.  If your selected mastery XP is at max, but you don't have enough mastery points to complete it,  all XP is lost while you try to get those points.  Some things have notifications, warnings -- THIS does NOT have any notifications.  Terrible design.6) Inconsistent.  There's one part that requires reading your in-game mail for a list of locations.  It's the ONLY mail you need to read for info.  EVERY other quest has indicators on the map or a list on the sidebar.  When trying to figure out how to proceed, reading that mail was the last thing I would have thought of.7) Discombobulated.  The wiki info on how to get to a farming area was vague and did NOT mention paying gems!  Some zones cost IRL cash->gems!   So, the farming zone portal did NOT open when completing the storyline!   The portal had no name on it, just a thing with a red X... the NPC nearby says "you are not ready" -- absolutely nothing leading the player back to the storyline info panel to pay up.  There's little need to open that panel and dig through the subsections... Total discombobulation.  This riddle was not fun and took way too long to figure out!   After all that,  I will NOT buy gems!  And I want my hours back!  Note: The babbling is fine - some people may enjoy the yuk -- but it NEEDS a fast-forward button - this is complete failure on the developers part.  How many 1000s of player requests have been ignored?Aside from storyline, and at all levels...1) Overpriced storage and boosts.2) Stingy on storage space = $$$$ for what should have been included.3) Too many currencies.  There's 30 or so in-game currencies!  Let's play find-the-right-vendor!4) Auto-targeting fails.  No options for combat vs friendly targeting.  It's wierd because it might target properly for 100 kills then decide to target a friendly.   Now and then it would have a fits of targeting wrong repeatedly for 10-20 minutes or so.5) Targeting indicator.  ArenaNet put your target way up at the top, but put health and shortcuts at the bottom!  I have a big monitor = TV!  I want them close, so I can see everything at a glance.6) Map icons.  When map icons are the same color as the map background, you can't see them.  Duh.7) Map quest indicators.  A green star shows on the map for where you need to go... but they used a too-similar green star for zone spots to get there.8) Swap-weapon has no indicator for which you're using.  Swap-weapon has *NO* indicator for which you're using.  Bleh.9) WvW requires much reading / video's to have any idea what is going on.  The in-game info is laughable.  My team color is red, the enemy's on the map are the SAME red... lolz.   In-game communication?  Nada?  I would run around a huge map looking for where stuff is going on.   You can't see your side (green dots) until you are close to them.  It's a big confusing mess.10) Wiki is a joke.  The maps are zoomed way in:  You can't tell where in the world!  "To get there use the portal at such and such"  OK... hrm that portal doesn't go there... Bleh!Conclusions:I don't expect perfection.  I do expect progress.  ArenaNet wont fix these (mostly old) issues, but makes new content?!  Not for me.The best parts are free -- I recommend NOT purchasing this game.I tried... I kept playing and playing, thinking it would get better, but it does not.It's a TRAP! (with no fast forward button)

_childDocuments_.review: Not a big review guy, but i'll try my best. So lets set the stage. I work 40 Hrs a week, exercise, cook, clean, and take care of my father by myself. My point? I am exhausted by the time I get to the 2 hours ( at most)  i get  to play a night. With that in mind,  I just want to have some fun and at the end of that 2 hours I want to feel like i did something other than farm acid *cough* Once Human  * cough.*  Guild Wars 2 provides an interesting take on things and it had me hooked ... at first.  Combat is fun simple and timers for skills are quick. No waiting 1-2 minutes for a damn skill...Looking at you Division 2 ! Fights are quick and as long as you brain it through what skills /equipment to use, you will def feel more and more powerful. Crafting does not seem to be necessary. All quest gave decent gear and i did not feel obligated to pick up a needle and hammer. Just run straight out and ... and find all the ... where the f*** are the quests?!? SO the game is not driven by quest with 'gather this' or 'kill that'... ish  You will run to an area and to accomplish the area requirement it is a combo of gather kill or other random thing like feed animal or taste ale! It was nice to have options.   There is a main story line, but that even has options, which is nice. I neither felt overwhelmed nor fatigued in the 31 hours I played.... SO why did I stop.2 ugly, one of which lazy, reasons...maybe both lazy.  As i said I dont have much time for my fun but in that time I like to feel ike i accomplished and have been rewarded. My first gripe, the gear up to level 40 was all ugly! like basic chain mail for hvy armor.  It all looked the same. I dug into it, and it is because of the games transmog system.  Which is total fine! every single piece of equipement as you get it, gets added to your wardrobe library,  but you dont have to pay real money to use them Right????....right?? the answer is ... sort of?  You have to clear an entire map and you can get 1 one 1!!! transmog!! To put that in perspective that's 1 of 5 armor and up to 4 additional land weapons and 2 additional water weapons ( oh, this game has swimming fights). You dont get the Transmog thing back, and its 1 per one piece.  The majority of weapon skins come from dungeons or the CASH SHOP! Same for skins for mounts, but the game is quick to give you a mount that does feel useful.  Other things like Dyes are also pretty heavily reliant on the cash shop as well. I know, I know its all cosmetic, but when you are wearing the same gear at 80 as you were at 10..... And how sweet is that BMW with a Kia DOOR.... (armor skins for everything but pants). 2nd thing is simpel.   IMHO destiny failed at one thing. Raids and no random group finder.  So what if it never worked and raids need some level of coordination.  My point  “Let them eat cake,” - Marie Antoinette. In other words, So what if it does not solve the problem, at least they will be satisfied. Guild Wars 2  DOES NOT HAVE A DUNGEON FINDER OF ANY KIND!?!?!?! There is no system that rewards high level characters for joining low level dungeons. There is nothing for raids, pvp or anything! Oh but they tell you when events start!  Instead of a simple system like every they have LFG build in? It does not ping the masses, it just sits in the LFG area. I hard stopped at this. I  dont  have time to meet new people (of my 2 hours of gaming i spent some of it writing this.)Guild Wars 2 has some pretty inovative ideas such as how it does quests and approaches combat. That said, it has some greedy and archaic ideas such as asthetics through real cash, and NO DUNGEON finder.  So my verdict ? As we sit there are only 3500 people playing the game according to STEAM (which, fun fact, was created by Valve).  If you have all day to play games and some cash to spare, yah...hell ya, plat this game. If you are and old ...person and dont have a ton of time for games because, well, life... no, not in hell. oh but for Steam i have to go with my needs so thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Installed this game to try out the PVP game modes I hear good things about. You gain access to the Structured PVP lobby at level 3, which is fine because you leave the tutorial at level 2 with progress on the exp bar. A few events take care of that. There doesn't seem to be a shortcut bound to the sPVP lobby like the other menu panels in the game. You have to find the crossed-sword icon on the top left of the screen to gain access to it.In sPVP they have an amulet system that provides stats of a specific prefix of gear which can be accessed even in the PVE world by going into the equipment tab on the hero panel, and clicking on the 'Helmet' button to the right of the headgear slot to switch between pvp and pve equipment. In the lobby, it seems you can access this too if you look at the top center of your screen and click on the helmet that represents gear or crossed swords to que matches and set rewards. The amulet system is interesting. On its own. you can basically set yourself as a pure damage dealer or with some level of damage mitigation with just the stat distribution.All skills and trait lines are unlocked in pvp as far as the expansion you own. I only have the core game for now so I do not yet have access to the advanced elite specialization sub-classes. Still, I am able to keep up with the elite classes with intelligent use of the core professions. Skills are divided into weapon skills, ahealing skill, utility skills, and an elite skill. Weapon skills change with what you have equipped and each class has some sort of 'swap' mechanics that allow them to expand their offensive and defensive options during combat. For example, the warrior is able to swap between 2 weapon sets giving them 10 skills to cycle through. Elementalists on the other hand look to have an element attunement system between fire, water, wind, earth, giving them 5 different skills each for a total of 25 skills to cycle between on just the weapon skills alone.Trait lines were a bit tricky because they look like they unlock later in the pve game mode and jumping straight into pvp unlocks all of them. Trait lines enhance your class with passive effects and additional mechanics that synergizes with your weapon and slot skills. These effects boost the ability of classes to dish out or soak damage. In pvp a total of 3 slots for trait lines are unlocked meaning you can slot in any combination of trait lines you have unlocked. The 3rd slot at the bottom is gilded in gold signifying that the elite specializations are swapped there. If you have the expansions swapping in an elite-trait-line in this slot changes you into the subclass they call elite specializations.Then there's the sPVP panel. In sPVP there's a pvp rank level you gain exp for and ranked matches are only available once you hit a certain level. At the moment I'm still rank 10 and can only que unranked matches. To the left of the sPVP panel are additional options. There's a segment there for pvp reward tracks. You can set which reward track you want active to adjust the rewards you will receive for playing pvp. I'm on the glorious armor track because it gives a choice armor piece at the end of each completion which will help my transmog game.As for the actual gameplay, there's a NODE System that is effectively like capture the flag and the match is a race to 500 POINTS. You start out as either Red or Blue and need to contest 3 NODES. There are three states to a node: UNCAPPED, CAPTURED, and CONTESTED. Turning a node to your color provides your team 1 point for every second it belongs to your color. It may not seem like much, but for context a single kill is only 5 points. If your team controls 3 NODES that's one kill of equivalent points every 2 seconds. In drawn-out fights you may feel like you are winning fights but will actually lose if you do not have control of sufficient NODES. I actually like this dynamic because the NODE factor means it's not just a brawl and forces players to be mindful of how their actions will move players around. For example, if I were a tanky spec and was able to capture the enemy NODE, I could draw a number of them to me leaving my allies free to fight with a numbers advantage assuming I could hold out against multiple assailants.That's also where my appreciation for the layers of build customization in this game mode comes from. You have:1) The Class mechanics, which are varied and suited for different roles.2) The Amulet, which provides everyone the same stats of different variations for an even playing field.3) The weapon and slot skills, that determine the feel of the play style.4) And the traits that enhance the effectiveness of your build.If you consider these 4 layers, you can go pretty deep into build crafting to prepare roles, which I think are important in sPVP. If your team is composed of all damage-focused builds you may wipe if you make one mistake. If you're too tanky there might not be enough damage to take out a target or you may end up to slow to capture nodes. With all the considerations to make it really gives the player freedom to build out different styles and expand on what they find enjoyable.I have yet to try the World vs World vs World game mode because it requires you to reach level 60. Which makes sense because unlike Structured PVP, this game mode relies on your PVE gear to determine your effectiveness. Going in with gimped gear is probably going to get you killed in small encounters. This shouldn't be a problem though since 'Tomes of Knowledge' are also given as a reward from time to time in sPVP. 'Tomes of Knowledge' boosts your character level by 1 for every use and I have since reached past level 10 just playing sPVP.All in all I'm enjoying the sPVP in this game and it feels almost like a MOBA. However, it's not all good news. It feels like a lot of the players I am qued with totally ignore mechanics. But this is not entirely their fault. At first, the NODE system might feel logical at a glance, but the game doesn't have any tutorials for the NODES in the sPVP lobby. In pve they teach you the dodge mechanic in the starter zones, but in sPVP they haven't provided a comparable interactive experience to introduce how the NODES work. As a result, you have allies running around like headless chickens not knowing where to go in actual matches or wondering why they lost even though they were dominating in kills. Even for me, it took a while to discover that it only takes one body on the NODE to initiate the capture, and adding more allies doesn't affect the speed at which it is captured.Hopefully, the developers will do something about this, but for now, I'm having fun even on the basic classes.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I haven't played every MMO out there, but I have been playing MMOs since 2001 starting with UO. The next game I spent a ton of time on was Guild Wars 1 and World of Warcraft since launch. I have tried many other 'next big things' that turned out to be failures within the first couple months. They either faltered due to poor launch, inexperience, or just lack of content. With Guild Wars 2, those are not concerns. ArenaNet is experienced and has plenty of content here at launch. I firmly believe this is 'the next big thing' since the juggernaut known as WoW has been around, I shall explain why. This list is in no particular order...This game is polished for release. There may be minor bugs here and there, but the game as a whole just works. I'm sure there will be more polish put on this with time. It can't compare to WoW here, but then again WoW has like an 8 year head start. Give it time.Depth of character: Open race and profession combinations. Anybody can be anything. The depth of how you can pick your utility skills and traits and have a real good chance of not running into anyone else with a cookie cutter build is very nice, especially since Blizzard killed off hybrids with Cataclysm and more so with Pandaria. 3 - Combat! Skills are determined by what you have in your hand more so than your profession. All buffs (boons) and debuffs (conditions) are of simple design. There is no dedicated Tank-Healer-DPS although there are some classes that excel at certain things more than others. Combat animations are done well and it seems to flow very smoothly. I am very critical on this as this is the exact thing that put me off of wanting in on The Secret World. There haven't been many MMOs to give you such an active mode of combat. Age of Conan tried and was very unbalanced between ranged and melee. Guild Wars 2 gets it right. You are able to fully Line of Sight some ones attacks or even actively dodge them!PvP at launch! This is a direct stab at Blizzard. They still haven't added it to Diablo 3 (still wouldn't make me want to play it again, heh) and WoW was going for months before it got it's first battleground. I give major props for Dynamic Level Adjustments up to level 80. There are no such things as lowbie twinks or leveling zone camping and gankfests. Racial abilities can't be used in Structured PvP also (no Human double trinket domination!)Robust crafting. This game has one of the most interesting crafting setups I've ever seen. It could use a bit more polish such as maybe showing you what you could make based upon components that you could make based upon your materials. I think there should be an option to consider your bank materials as well. I have only scratched the tip of this and am anxious to get more materials to craft more. Also, experience is gained for crafting and gathering!Dynamic questing system. You do have a main story line that gives you a clear direction on how to progress through the game, but a big chunk of your leveling will be done through dynamic quests kind of similar to Rift's rift system and Instant Adventures, but more dynamic. No forced grouping during leveling as the content adjusts to how many players are active and you automatically get heals or assists off whoever is killing the same target as you. The Dynamic Level Adjustment works opposite in PvE than PvP, if you go into a lower level zone, you get reduced to an appropriate level and rewarded as if you were higher level. It is impossible to out level the content and you also can't get a high level guy to just run you through something! Also, no looking for yellow ?s or !s on the map!The graphics are 2nd to none in MMOs. This is not a factor for many, but after spending thousands on PC hardware over the years, I appreciate being able to fully use it. This is the first game in years to have me taking screenshots because I am in awe of the design. A lot of MMOs don't put as much thought into design of the whole game as ArenaNet has done with just a single zone.I don't know what else to keep on about... You can join multiple guilds. You get nice rewards for 100% exploration of zones. You can 'fight for your life' instead of dying when you get downed. You can transmute gear for different looks. You can freely dye armor different colors. .... and quite a bit more than I have space or time to describe. Let's not forget about the sensational mount system and the great music.I spent over 30k hours in this game and 20k hours earlier in GW1, which should be the best advertisement for the series!I heartily recommend it with all my heart! <3

_childDocuments_.review: It was much time I wanted to play this game, and I'm glad I gave it a try: it's profesionally made, interesting, various, lot of options to choose with. I like mostly the artworks, their style, and the giant building all around one can see, wide places where to explore. 500+ hours and I've still seen 25% or even less.Like every other game, GW2 have to be taken by its own: sure previous experience, like WoW, FF and such, can help, but its mechanics are to be understood, to obtain a viable performance. Last but not least, I appreciated the free-to-play: not as is, as (many won't agree, nonetheless) it's really unviable to play it F2P after the first levels. Just to tell, F2P can't access mounts and Trading Post: if one may survive the mounts lack, it's terribly hard to stay without TP: can't trade anything, every item one can't use will be sold to NPCs, earning nearly nothing, can't also sell surplus materials... all non-core limitations, but enough to not making me comfortable in playing: just bought 1 DLC and all such things was unlocked, it worths the expense. As I told, tho, F2P is still nice to have, as one can try the game, find viable class/race/story to play, see if his/her machine can really bear with the game's requirements and such, all for free. Then, after the choice to go forth, to buy at least one DLC is "recommended", if you don't want to play against yourself too, while fighting the game's challenges.Also consider you'll get to level 80 in a very few, comparing to other games. Just to say: GW2 L80 seems the same as WoW L30: where the game begins: all which happens before is just "preparation". There are "rites of passage", e.g. at L60/70, and when your 1st storyline ends, around L80. Then it's a road forward, up to L80/mastery 455 (I may be wrong, on that: nowadays I'm just L80/12 on my 4 characters).Since I started playing, I tried some classes: starting by ranger (hunter in some other games), then necromancer (warlock elsewhere), but I tried mesmer (mage) and warrior too. I'm currently raising a thief (rogue) and I must say it worths the pain to bring it to L80: now I choosen Deadeye (sniper), which is one of my "natural roles" (together with ranger/hunter, and necromancer/warlock) and I feel good.One word about the community: it's vibrant and helpful for sure. Chat panel have the /map selector, where one can chat to the whole "map" (the zone where (s)he is exploring, not the whole /world): I found it helpful, if not keeping an eye too close to the constant map chatter (if one knows WoW, is the same as town's channels). That apart, it's only up to you, if to stay in cities to chill and chat, or to get around, chatting sometimes, mostly at need, like I do.Arenanet told they wasn't that much insisting, about to push people buying DLCs/expansions: I found that true and false at the same time. If the initial advertising was "heavy", at least to me, then, after buying at least 1 DLC, it relaxes a bit, allowing you to play without too much distractions (it's their job, after all, they're paid for). For sure, you'll see there are a lot of "little suggestions" which try to make you spending money: TP "bargains", the fact they give you far more than you can keep in your bank and inventory... one may think "ohhh... so much gifts", but it's to make you fill bank/inventory slots, so that you'll "unlock" more by spending money in gems, IMHO, kind of "poisoned apples".I'll keep going (in the meantime I bought all first expansions, up to the one before Secrets of the Obscure) and will see if to implement this review later. Have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better F2P  (B2P if you get the expansions) that I have seen on Steam.  I played it briefly a couple years ago off steam, but didn't stick to it because of other time commitments.   The main reason I like it is that the shop is not in my face. I can easily ignore it.  Unlike a lot of other F2P MMOs I don't feel gimped in the inventory department by ignoring the cash shop.  I had plenty of bags just dropping out in the world.Things I like 1.  Combat is easy to pick up and intuitive.  Being in water, you get a different set of attacks based on aquatic weapons.2,  Your attacks change based on the weapons you have equipped which makes for a variety of game play and similar to Elder Scrolls Online you can swap 2 weapon sets.    I play warriors so wont speak about casters.  I did Necromancer when I played the first time but I barely remember it.3.  Horizontal progression rather than the usual boring vertical where you keep growing in power.  Once you cap, the gear you have is the gear you have and rather than being like WoW where you are constantly chasing gear you work on completionism (playing the game rather than redundant game play loop of chasing gear through the same set of dungeons only to have said gear get obsolete next patch/expansion)4,  Character creator is decent, the races are interesting enough except for one but more on that later.5.  Everything you do gives XP and exploration is rewarded.6.  You have a personal storyline per starter zone/race and I enjoy it a lot more than FF14 because in GW2 they respect my time rather than force me to sit through long cut scenes for a story I do not really give a crap about.  The GW2 personal storyline is entertaining and gives you something to do rather than the FF14 style that basically treats you like a movie audience.7.  Free form enough where if you just want to go around murder hoboing you can.  The "quests" are really just suggestions and the main story quest can be done at your pace.  Unlike FF14 that forces you to progress in it to get to the content you actually want to play.8.  Cash shop is easy to ignore and never in your face the way Elderscrolls online is.  It's there for those who want to do that sort of thing, but for those of us not into such things it is as if it does not exist.Cons.1,  Race choice is limited.   There are two human races, regular humans and Norns who are basically giant nordic types.  Giant is meant literally.  A human female standing next to a Norn female she is like more than half my height. I play human, my first time playing I played Nord and Sylvari.   Sylvari are like "elves" more on them later.  There is also Charr, they are sort of like if you mixed a minotaur with a tiger.  Then there are the Asura.  Basically huge eared WoW gnomes.  So 5 races, 2 of which are really the same thing (humans and Norns).2.  Sylvari are cabbage people.  They are basically the "elves" but they are so heavily plant based in looks that  to me they are visually unappealing.  My take on it is if you are going to put in an Elf race, do it right.  Just take the page from Tolkien and do them right.  I like Elves, I want to play an elf, not a cabbage person with elf like qualities.  Even the name, Sylvari is elven.   I hate when game designers try to be fresh and original by ruining elves.  They are perfect as they are depicted in traditional fantasy media -- they are elves after all.  If you want to play an Elf and you like Elf stuff, this game wont deliver.  They should have just called the race something planty like Greenfolk or Leafae (get it leaf fae) and I would not have this petty complaint.3.  Dwarves are mentioned but there are no playable dwarves.   4.  When there are few players in your area the game spams you to let you know so you can move to a more crowded mapset.   Most mobs, and ALL trash mobs are easily soloable so having more players in your area while leveling just slows you down.  Let those of us who actually enjoy playing with few other players around enjoy the experience.  After all, Sigurd didn't have any friends killing Fafnir.  Yeah, yeah, I get that MMOs are Multiplayer.  But most people like to solo play them anyways.   Oh, and when they spam the message about few players, they give you an hour to accept moving to another world server instance with a buff.  If you decline it, they move you anyways after that hour.  Because waiting around for respawns is so fun, NOT.

_childDocuments_.review: Over 700 hours into this game and I'm...still not sure.The good:Very friendly player community IN SOME GAME MODES.Beautiful graphics.Multiple game modes that appeal to many different kinds of players.'Horizontal' progression (you can do pretty much any content to varying degrees of success with a small amount of grinding).A lot of content.The not so good:Not all game modes are treated equally, (Structured) PvP gets no love from the game developer, and class balance is awful.Rewards in structured PvP are awful unless you play a certain type of PvP (ranked) in which you will be unwelcome as a noob.World vs. World (kind of a PvP-uag mode) is well supported but nearly unplayable if you aren't on a top end gaming rig.PvE can become nearly unplayable if you're not on a top end gaming rig when trying to follow a large group of players doing   themeta.There are scads of in game currencies, and you won't know what to do with many of the ones you have or know how to acquire   the  ones you don't without endless googling.There are scads of different kinds of loot boxes.  You open loot boxes and get minor commodities and junk and more loot boxes.    You then salvage things from some of what came from loot boxes, and have more things to deal with.  Basically, it feels like an   endless flow of crap that you constantly have to deal with trying to manage your inventory and bank.  Crafting is a hot mess.  You can never seem to just go craft what you wanted to, you always need a some recipe you don't have  and don't know where to acquire, then you google where to get it and you don't have the right currency or the right vendor   unlocked...etc.The maybe good, maybe bad...depends on your preferences:While there are a lot of different game modes (Open World, Dungeons, Raids, Fractals, PvP, WvW, etc...) there is no synergy to   them, they aren't part of a cohesive game world experience.  Would I recommend this game?  Man, it's a tough call.  If you mainly want a MMORG with an active player base in which to explore with beautiful scenery...then YES!If you like doing crafting, then probably not.If you think it's fun to get a super cool item drop every once in awhile, then probably not.If you want PvP to feel baked into the game to some extent, where doing well at it has some ramification on the game world...then NO!
