_childDocuments_.review: If you value a ton of top-quality content, a fully voiced story-line built inside an immersive universe and the friendliest community you have ever seen in an MMORPG, Guild Wars 2 is probably the game for you. Guild Wars 2 takes place in the world of Tyria, the surface of which is home to numerous humanoid races and civilizations engaging with each other, but also where beneath all that, primordial beings known as the Elder Dragons are hibernating. Due to events taking place in the previous games of the series, five Elder Dragons have awaken from their slumber and are causing widespread destruction to Tyria and corrupting its inhabitants. The story is enormous, with many twists and external threats, but I guess this is the main take you should know before beginning your adventure. Everything else will be known in due time. GW2 differs from the usual MMORPG formula, there are no simple straightforward quests such "Kill 20 monsters" or "Gather 10 wood" to proceed. Instead of the traditional questing system, each area has its own unique dynamic events that bring each and every map to life, presenting you with its history by having players explore & interact with it. Each action has multiple outcomes that also result in new events, creating a cascade effect. In addition to that, you don't have to be in a party to participate and you can jump into the action at any moment, even if the event is at its peak. You can also join your friends anywhere, as levels don't really matter in this game. Your level and equipment are scaled to the map and the EXP reward is percentage based. If you have a friend who's ahead, or if your buddies are only beginning, you can play content together with no real restriction whatsoever. One of it's biggest selling points is that GW2 is NOT Pay to Win. However, it is not Free to Play either. While it advertises itself as such, it's more like a trial of the main game. Let me explain:GW2 has 3 major expansions, which I'll refer as HoT (Heart of Thorns), PoT (Path of Fire) and EoD (End of Dragons). The core game is essentially available to everyone, but some key game-play elements such as Gliding, Mounts, a bunch of different class specializations etc. are locked behind said expansions. Purchase them separately or as a bundle, once you do, you will not have to spend another dime in game, at least until a new expansion comes along. You can still top-up and buy cosmetics or quality of life stuff for your account, but everything in the shop is also purchasable with in-game currency. That includes Living World Seasons, which are lore based episodes of content that act as the ongoing story-line between expansions, giving access to numerous maps and features. You can think of them as mini-expansions.You want to experience PvP in this game? No fear. Structured instances of PvP in the forms of a few individuals or even worlds against each other are easily accessible with just the click of a button. Most of the stuff (including class specializations) in casual or competitive PvP is available to everyone, meaning trying out builds or different classes is quite easy, or even encouraged in some cases.Fashion; Hate it or love it, cosmetics are a huge part of Guild Wars 2. You’ll be frequently unlocking skins throughout your adventures, either by looting them, crafting them or by purchasing them from the trading post/cash shop (which you can do using in-game currency, as mentioned earlier). Once a skin is unlocked, it is usable account-wide. Now here's the big reveal; dyes. You are able to dye your equipment with hundreds of different obtainable colors, making fashion a complete headache. You want wings? Sure. You feel like being a walking fire hazard? Go ahead. There are so many different combinations that you will spend many hours creating your own outfit, or you can just copy someone else's if you don't feel like going through this process.End Game; There is no real end-game in Guild Wars 2. The game is enormous and it's always evolving. You can have thousands of hours put in game and still have stuff to do. You can craft Legendary equipment (which is a very long process), work towards account progression, dungeons, strikes, raids, fractals, you name it. You can even hunt for collections or aim to reach the top rankings in competitive. For a game that launched back in 2012, Guild Wars 2 has been very well maintained considering that most games of this genre die out after the initial hype is over. The constant release of new content over the years makes GW2 a game with hundred of hours of unique game-play, innovative ways to explore the MMORPG genre and a compelling story that starts out slow but ends becoming breath-taking. My recommendation is that you should simply play the game for the first dozens of hours without getting any expansion, test the waters (something like a trial period), and then if you feel like exploring what this game has to offer, which you probably will, go ahead and enrich your experience. I'll only say this: enjoy the ride.Edit: some minor spelling mistakes

Although most content is PvE anyways (aside from PvP arenas, GvG, WvW, etc), nothing in the gem store adds a pay-to-win element. _childDocuments_.review: This one's a gem. One of, if not the best multiplayer game out there with an amazing community. The community is incredibly friendly and eager to help out other players. The story line, even just core gameplay, is very enjoyable and you could put so much time into it without even realizing. There's a mountain of things you could spend your time doing. If you enjoy solo gameplay and want to roleplay with your character, you've got it. If you want to go through the story with a group or do dungeons and fractals with your friends, you've got it. If you're into completing insane amounts of achievements, then you've got it. Seriously, I'm still barely scratching the surface with achievements. If you dig a challenge and have a thing for intense boss fights then you've got it but if you're not and you just wanna chill with exploring the massive, beautiful map then you've got that too. This game deserves a 10/10. If you're not sure weather to get the expansion packs, there's really no rush and you can enjoy gw2 just the same regardless. There's a large number of benefits as a ftp player compared to... basically any other multiplayer game. In case you're choosing though and if you're especially interested in the story, Heart of Thorns comes before Path of Fire as far as storyline goes and it honestly has the best story of any storyline in the game. It's awesome. And the fact there are no subscriptions make it 10/10 all on its own. With that said, it still isn't overly confusing or overwhelming when you start out and they don't throw everything at you all at once. I definitely suggest giving gw2 a try, it's beyond worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put over 3000 hours each into both Guild Wars 1 and Guild Wars 2. They are both fantastic and unique, and nowhere near as popular as they deserve to be.Guild Wars 2 is brilliant from top to bottom - you can play as casually (story, guild activities, exploration, jumping puzzles) or as hard core (fractals, dungeons, raids, strikes) as you'd like, and you are never penalised for taking a break for months or years.The world is massive with tons to do, the lore is deep and endless, and the mount system introduced in the second expansion is the best in the industry. The game is vast, with countless weapon and armour skins, almost limitless character customisation, 5 very unique races to choose from, and tons of things to accomplish, such as crafting legendary weapons - it's almost impossible to be bored. The game is incredibly alt-friendly too.World vs World and Pvp, although not my cup of tea, also offer a lot of playtime and fun, especially as a team.The community of Guild Wars is equally fantastic. there is very little toxicity except occasionally in raids (which can't really be avoided in any mmo), but the 99% are friendly and patient. Joining a guild is simple, and well worth doing - I highly recommend this for new players, even if you aren't the most talkative, it's great to have a friendly community there to give advice.On top of that, aswell as your main gameplay, you will find tons of small features such as mini games, festivals and world events, which are always taking place and always fun to engage with.If you have time and fancy a new mmo experience, do not hesitate to try Guild Wars 2. Especially when it's free to play, and incredibly cheap to buy if you choose to (considering hours:price and no sub fee).How people can continue to pay monthly for a subscription when Guild Wars is sitting there offering such a fantastic experience still baffles me.5* Fantastic Game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great open world experience, minimal vertical progression, and a fluid combat system which puts you at the mercy of your own skill. the downside? stubborn devs chipping away at what makes the game great with bad decisions, one after another. Worth a play, but not worth the long term investment.Combat system: great at a lot of aspects from movement, positioning, and even timing. you'll get to choose to play 9 classes with each having their own specializations, which is a sort of an upgrade of your chosen class and greatly changes their gameplay, but to play those specializations you have to own any of the expansions they're released with and some of them are not even worth playing in some content due to certain problems that the developers doesn't address despite the playerbase already suggesting on solutions. If you're going in the game with the expectations of wanting to play a priest-like support whose main job is to support your group from the backline or want to play as a warrior who's just job is to just pummel the hell out of the enemy, then perish the thought, RP is lost in this game and more on on how fast you can pummel a boss in record time.Graphics: Maps in this game are beautiful, lots of places good for screenshot/wallpaper material but when it comes to gameplay, Tons and TONS of visual noise, everywhere. from players showing off their how glowy their armors are by stacking the items that emit it, to the skill visual effects covering important AoE circles on the ground and turning a large portion of your screen into an unreadable blot. hope you like keeping track of what your own skills and do some guesswork on what your enemy is doing because both will be drowned out by the sheer amount of visual effects that the other players will be crapping out on top of your enemies.Story: Nothing to write home about but somehow the devs are treating it like as an emmy award winning thing and highlighting it as the game's selling point. if you've decided to soldier through the other downsides, especially with that terribly underwhelming boss fight of the first arc of the gameplay which all boils down to pressing the 1 key for 3 minutes straight, and play the game further into its story, you'll tell at which point did the devs stopped caring about making an epic fantasy world and decided to go with real world "politics" and go extremely hard on the pointless melodrama.Content: There are over a hundred maps in this game, even with just the free to play version there's already a lot of maps to explore and play on with tons of places to explore about, There's also dungeons, raids, and their other variants because just sticking to "dungeons and raids" isn't enough, then there's PvP: Structured PvP (team matches with match format) and Large Scale PvP called WvW. lots of content to play with in the game, even when some of them are downright abandoned by the developers.The devs: Never had a good track record, from balance patches, content, and releases. never consistent and you'll have to guess when they're going to release content and there's content drought. despises and disrespects its playerbase to the point of arrogance and somehow has a grudge  against skilled players with their philosophy of "class complexity is bad", shaving off on what makes the game great, and because of this the recent changes to that lead up to steam release made a lot of old players leave. There's also the issue of developers who are in charge of the classes of not knowing their own game and base their decisions on the wiki while also showing blatant favoritism which affects the game as a whole.bloating player count by giving away account codes which only resulted in increased number of AFK farmers/bots which can be seen in some areas in the game, to not letting us link our own account to also bloat up steam player numbers. not the kind of people you'd give your money to or to put your trust on. Overall, great gameplay with lots of potential, lots of content to sink into, decent'ish story all hampered by stubborn devs driving the game down with their biases and easing it with empty words. 10 years worth of experience, but a decades worth of disappointment

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:*I like it*99% of the community is friendly and helpful*imo plays a lot like WoW*buying every expansion is 150$*unlocking every living world season (mini expansions) is another 50$~ (depending on sale)*LWS can be bought with in-game currency, just like everything else (even deluxe edition upgrades for every expansion)*end-game gear is easily obtained and will never get outdated*your dmg is less dependent on gear, and more dependent on knowing how buffs, debuffs, combo finishers, skill synergy, etc works*there is hard group content, but to me end-game is about fashion and QoL unlocks*coming back to the game after a long brake won't feel like you are behind.it's a nice game with a mostly friendly community.imo it does resemble WoW a lot with how it plays, but you don't have to constantly play to keep up with the content because reaching end-game gear is as easy as buying a set of exotics from other players which you can easily do after 2-3 days of playing. this doesn't mean that you are op after 3 days, because the main part of your damage comes from understanding how buffs and debuffs synergize (and this is something I still haven't rly taken the time to learn as it is a large system).the game has a lot to offer and thus, also a lot to set yourself into, it will be overwhelming and it is highly recommended to join an active guild or find ppl to play with (which isn't too hard considering how helpful 99% of the players are)I have taken 3 longer brakes from GW2 and I have never felt behind, the second I started playing again, my gear was as good as it was before my brake.there are raids, dungeons, harder group content, PvP, etc which competitive players can enjoy, but for me the aim of the game is to have fun and just hunt for fashion or QoL like a flying mount.the only things you rly are forced to spend money on, are the expansions (30$ each usually) everything else can be bought in-game and gold can be converted into gems, altho you rly need to grind and know what you are doing if you plan on using gold to unlock the expansions deluxe editions or any of the additional "Living World Seasons" (which are kinda like mini expansions).personally, I'd say playing this game will cost you about 200$ (all current expansions + living world season bundles which often go on sale for 46%), after you have this, the entire game is open to you. this might seem like a lot of money, and it is, but compare it to any other MMO RPG that's actively played nowadays, and then compare it to the hours of fun (not forced grinding, actual fun) you get out of this (still cheaper then a night out at the bar at least where I live).that said, even the base game which is free altho with some noticeable limitations, still has a lot of content, and you might not even care for all of the expansions.

_childDocuments_.review: I put 1000 hours into this game within 3 months of starting playing it, and it was nothing but pain and frustrations. I forced myself to play through it hoping it gets better but it never did.The new player experience is so bad. Players are bullying newbies into skipping straight to the last expansion just to get the flying mount - which happens to also be the biggest grind in the game. I thought this was just the community being bad but the game outright spoils the story for you anyways through things like cash shop item names and seasonal events dialogs.The game advertises itself as f2p but as you can expect from every f2p game, is also p2w. You can buy gold with a credit card and then use that gold to buy the best weapons in the game straight off the trade post. And players are pushing this line of toughts by telling newbies to forgo the grind and just "swipe" to get gear - and that flying mount i mentionned.Those arent deal breakers on their own, just play the game like you want, right? That's where it gets worse: LFG is completly dead so it's impossible to just tag along any kind of raid or dungeons, you HAVE to join a guild that does those. And then those guilds are all backseating you and telling you how to play the game, going as far as kicking you out of the guild for not wearing their guild tags 100% of the time. (the game lets you be a member of 7 guilds at the same time) I ended up leaving my first guild after i was snarked at for using non-glass-cannon gear.The thing is, i have to use gear with both offensive and defensive stats BECAUSE the game is so dead. Most things in the game can be bought with gold, and the best way to farm gold is to farm open world events like world bosses, map "metas" and pretty much any event you come across. Now there are two types of events: the solo ones with a Veteran rank enemy that is easy to kill on your own, and then the group events with Champion rank enemies that are legit impossible to solo. And of course the champions drop the real gold. Group events are timed, so you need to do enough dps on your own to beat the timer, but then that means being a glas cannon and getting one shot by a champion stomping on you...Which leads me to the true killer of this game: the "action combat" game play style. In theory what this means is you need to always be on your feet and dodge out of troubles. (the game has an actual dodge button like your typical single player RPG) But in practice all it does is take the controls out of your hands by knocking you around like a rag doll and stun locking you. Then kill you. Every boss in the game - yes even those Champions - has what's called a "Defiance Bar" that works like a shield. Unless you break that bar, bosses will knock you around and kill you. It's possible to break a defiance bar on your own with the right build, but that only makes the boss vulnerable for a single second before the defiance bar fills back up and the boss stuns lock you and kills you.There are abilities that make you immune to "control effects" like knockbacks and stuns, but those only last a few seconds and have long cooldowns. I even leveled 6 different classes to 80 hopelessly searching for a class that is "playable" and they all fall short.And that's the keyword here: "Playable". Because after putting 1000 hours and a few hundred dollars into this game, i was never able to make it playable.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing since launch in 2012 and it's still always a treat to boot up this game. It's my go-to chillout game these days and I love just hanging out in the various zones and doing whatever strikes my fancy.The main strength of the game is the open world design and the dynamic events that occur in the various zones (i.e. maps). Some events evolve into chains that alter the state of the zone, which is a nice touch.The best showcase of the game’s strengths are the map scale meta-events, which require lots of players and varying levels of coordination. Also, the world as a whole is gorgeous, with strong art direction that has aged well despite the slightly dated graphics. There's so many details to be found in every nook and cranny of the world, and it all feels alive because there's always something going on somewhere.The game doesn't force you into specific type of content to progress your account (although you'll have to dip into most types of content if you want to go for legendary gear) and there's no need to rush anything or play every day, as you'll never miss out on anything important because you didn't play when it was new.Most old content is kept relevant and populated because new events and long-term endgame goals keep bringing established players back to older zones. You're never completely alone and it's usually possible to bring some random players together for group content when needed.The second expansion, Path of Fire, introduced mounts to the game, and they’re probably the best feeling mounts in any game. They feel like real creatures and each of them have drastically different abilities and use cases.Every (paid) player gets a raptor now, but I would personally recommend playing without mounts the first time around, until you get to Path of Fire, because the maps before that expansion were not designed with mounts in mind. You’ll get a much better appreciation for the map design by going on foot. Of course, it’s not always that simple, as it’s impossible to keep up with other players when running with a group in certain cases, but do try it out when just roaming around. It’s comfy.This is not really a game for people who like grinding to become more and more powerful, as the level cap has never been raised from 80 and the most powerful gear in the game has the same power as in 2013, but if you like exploration and freedom to do whatever, this might just be the game for you.And it costs nothing to try, so give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long time non-steam guild wars 2 player with thousands of hours on the game. Overall account/character progressionGuild Wars 2 was born from developers that came from blizzard and worked on WoW. Guild wars 2 as an mmo has all the main features that mmo players will recognize, however the way the game is designed at it’s core makes it a much less stressful experience. Unlike other mmos GW2’s level cap is 80 and will always be 80. The end game build you made for a character years ago will still be viable today because there is not this endless progression of having to get new items for the new end game content as the level cap is unchanging. GW2’s content map, instead of an infinitely expanding arrow pointing upwards where that arrow is levels, looks more like a mushroom cloud where you get to level 80, and then the content expands out laterally. This means that the game doesn’t utilize FOMO (fear of missing out) to herd old and continuous players back to the game. This makes being involved in the game much less stressful and makes it more compatible with being played alongside other games. Much of the motivation that encourages you to unlock stuff like new weapons and such for your account comes from you simply wanting to have new builds for your characters or unlock prestigious cosmetics. This will make more sense as you learn about how stats and builds work. It is also important to note that almost everything you get that matters in gw2 is shared across your whole account, so making a new character because you want to try a new class doesn’t necessarily involve having to redo everything you’ve already done. This enables a healthy amount of gameplay variety as the game’s 9 classes have very unique feels to them.MonetizationThe complete original game that had a single up cost several years ago is now free to play. The expansions that bring new gameplay and quality of life changes now sort of occupy that new upfront cost, and make the core game feel somewhat like a demo, but it is important to keep in mind that the free portion of guild wars 2 is still a complete game with enough content to justify it being called a full game. There is the same type of premium currency store that we expect to see in live service games that has to exist to keep the hamsters fed that make the game work. The way Gw2 does this premium store is much better than the way other live service games do it. Gem store upgrades are all convenience and cosmetics and provide no combative gameplay edge. These upgrades are not unreasonably expensive and you feel as though you are getting good value in game for the real money that you are spending on gems. Gems can also be purchased to use in the gem store by trading in-game earned gold for them, meaning that all gem store upgrades can be acquired through gameplay. There is no subscription fee. As a long time player at no point in time have I felt like the game has been squeezing money out of me, and all worthwhile account unlocks are gotten through gameplay and are not purchasable with real money. CombatGw2 is an MMO ACTION RPG. Combat is deep and strategic, but also occurs in real time. There is no point and click gameplay. Fighting is dynamic and unpredictable. You move around while you are attacking and are not stationary while actions and spells are being used. You dodge and block attacks and projectiles in real time. You feel like you are actually in control of your character and are not just commanding it like in a moba or a traditional mmo. If I were to compare the combat to another game, something like kingdom hearts wouldn’t be so far off, but there are probably better comparisons. Even if you don’t like Mmos you might actually like this game just for the combat.Classes/CharactersThere are 5 races and 9 classes. The races are not entirely cosmetic and your choice of race affects your characters personal storyline and their voice actor (yes your character is voiced), but does not affect things like stats that matter in combat. In character creation there are various sliders and such for adjusting how your character’s face and body looks. Single player RPG players will feel very at home in Gw2 character creation process. The 9 classes all play very differently, but no single class dominates a single DPS or support role. Having each class be able to fulfill these traditional RPG roles such as DPS, support, tank, utility, etc is very important to the developers in how the go about balancing the classes in balance patches which happen frequently. You cannot change your character class but each account has many slots for new characters to be made so that you have options. Each class has different traits, skills and specializations that are unlocked as the character levels up and these have a major effect on how the class plays. There is a lot more that can be said about combat but its easier to just play the free game and see for yourself. Leveling up a character in guild wars 2 and unlocking skills is a very fun and rewarding process and does not feel like a chore. There is a level 80 boost available once you purchase a paid expansion but this deprives you of one of the games most rewarding processes. Game modes, pvp, etcThere are three major game modes. MMO vets will recognize the PVE and PVP game modes. There is a third major gamemode in Gw2 called World versus World. In this mode entire servers play against other servers in what I think would be best described as an RPG version of planetside 2 (also a game I play lot). This WvW mode is a unique experience that I haven't really found in any games other than ps2 lets you fight in large scale 30+ vs 30+ player conflicts where the objective is to take and hold fortresses. WvW could be a game by itself. PvP is 3 point capture type gameplay, it is deep and a lot of thought goes into strategy in the games pvp modes. Toxicity among pvp players is present but is comparatively low compared to other pvp games. PVE is pve, if you like the combat you will be happy just roaming around bustin caps in the open world. It is worth noting that in a low level zone your level will be scaled down to keep you challenged so that you aren't obliterating level 15 enemies as a level 80 guy. There is hardcore PvE content in the form of raids and fractals where you need coordinated group effort or at least need players that have practiced and know how the fights mechanics work. I wont go into detail but that higher tier of effort to reward type of PvE gameplay is present but isn’t mandatory to be successful or prestigious in the game. Maps/explorationThe previous paragraph about PvE brings us into what PvE actually looks like. There are a lot of maps in a lot of regions that each have their own unique feel and unique dynamic events. There are large-scale world bosses and events where you will be working with 40+ or however many players to do the big event or take down the big guy. These events usually run on a schedule and there are many and they are rewarding and there is a good reward to time investment balance that is maintained throughout the games open world PvE. Everyone gets rewarded by participating in the event, so no one is stealing loot from anyone by playing together. This encourages teamwork. As far as the maps go, you will always find new things in all the maps. There are jumping puzzles and minigames and all sorts of other stuff that adds depth to the game and contribute to making the game a worth second life. You can sit in the chairs and drink alcohol and do other stuff that helps bring your

Play it as if you were playing the witcher, do you remember that feeling that not knowing where to go, having immediate access to the whole first map, and at the same time the game saying “hey if you don't know what to do come here”.Also if you see an event near to you, don't be afraid to participate, if the zone says it's on your level that means that the event is for you, all high levels will be at an equal level as the zone (reward are set to your actual level, making all zones always fun to revisit since they are still relevant and challenging).Well, there is a lot to love about this game and there are some bad things as well, the hotkeys for skills can be a little bit awkward (don't be afraid to remap those), it has an amazing feature that is called action camera (great for melee characters), but you have to set it to a hotkey to go in and out of this mode, Now maybe the expansion are too expensive even if it a fair price it doesn't mean it's adorable for everyone. Maybe you have just enough to buy one and don't know which one, easy answer end of dragons, includes all quality of live of all previous expansion, and the only downside is that skips all previous story lines.The free version is a full game storyline with some quality of life locked, the expansion and living world are new maps, stories, and some mechanics that were released later, they are worth every penny and the most fun mechanics can be used from the beginning (mounts and glide) because of course why not. _childDocuments_.review: Guild Wars 2: A Fantastical Journey Through a Vibrant World of Adventure and CommunityGuild Wars 2, ArenaNet's masterpiece MMORPG, isn't just a game – it's an immersive journey through a stunning world filled with adventure, camaraderie, and endless possibilities. With its dynamic events, rich lore, and emphasis on player-driven storytelling, Guild Wars 2 sets the standard for what an MMORPG can be.Dynamic Events and Living World:One of the defining features of Guild Wars 2 is its dynamic event system, where the world reacts to player actions in real-time. Whether you're defending a village from marauding centaurs, escorting a caravan through dangerous territory, or battling a massive world boss alongside dozens of other players, every moment in Guild Wars 2 feels alive and full of possibility. And with the ever-changing Living World updates, there's always something new and exciting on the horizon.Rich Lore and Engaging Storytelling:From the towering spires of the human city of Divinity's Reach to the mystical forests of the sylvari, the world of Guild Wars 2 is steeped in rich lore and history. The game's main storyline, as well as its numerous side quests and personal storylines, offer compelling narratives that draw players deeper into the world and their characters' roles within it. And with branching dialogue options and meaningful choices, your decisions have real consequences that shape the world around you.Dynamic Combat and Skillful Gameplay:Guild Wars 2's combat system is fast-paced, fluid, and deeply satisfying. With a wide variety of classes, weapons, and skills to choose from, there's a playstyle to suit every preference. Whether you prefer to rain down destruction as a fire-wielding elementalist, support your allies as a protective guardian, or sneak through the shadows as a deadly thief, the combat in Guild Wars 2 rewards skillful play and strategic thinking.Beautiful Environments and Immersive Soundscapes:From the lush jungles of the Maguuma to the snowy peaks of the Shiverpeaks, the world of Guild Wars 2 is a feast for the eyes and ears. The game's stunning environments, combined with its immersive sound design and stirring musical score, create a sense of immersion and wonder that few other MMOs can match. Whether you're exploring hidden caves, battling fearsome dragons, or simply admiring the view from a mountaintop vista, every moment in Guild Wars 2 is a visual and auditory delight.Community and Collaboration:But perhaps the greatest strength of Guild Wars 2 lies in its vibrant and welcoming community. Whether you're teaming up with friends to tackle challenging dungeons, joining a guild to conquer massive world events, or simply chatting with fellow adventurers in the bustling cities, the sense of camaraderie and collaboration in Guild Wars 2 is second to none. With players from all walks of life coming together to explore, create, and celebrate their shared love of the game, Guild Wars 2 truly feels like a home away from home.Conclusion:Guild Wars 2 is more than just a game – it's an epic adventure through a vibrant world of fantasy and wonder, where every corner holds new surprises and every moment is filled with possibility. With its dynamic events, rich lore, engaging storytelling, and welcoming community, Guild Wars 2 is an MMO experience like no other. So grab your sword, summon your allies, and embark on an unforgettable journey through the world of Tyria – adventure awaits!Rating: 9.5/10 - A Fantastical Journey Through a Vibrant World of Adventure and Community

_childDocuments_.review: Made a new account after I lost my original that I had in 2015. As far as MMOs go, Guild Wars 2 provides extreme, bordering on ludicrous value. There is a TON to do in Guild Wars 2, from jumping puzzles, crafting, world events, dungeons, explorations, world quests (which might I add isn't just fetch quests, you have a lot of variety there to spice things up,) and more; mind you, I'm only talking about the base game here, I haven't even touched the expansions yet. As far as character creation goes, you have nine different classes with specializations you can take which unlock new weapons for that class to use and new abilities, so there's even more to do there. What kinda sucks is you don't have enough character slots starting out to have one of each class, you have to buy more, but I'll be honest I've barely touched my alts so that isn't as big a concern to me right now. In terms of skills and abilities they are all unique to your class, and you can even switch around your weapon skills by dual wielding, or you have a second weapon slot that allows you to swap from melee to ranged on the fly, which is pretty cool, and gives a ton of customization to your build. As far as character customization goes? It's pretty alright for the most part, you have some options that are locked behind the premium currency store which also sucks, but thankfully it's a small amount of stuff. Speaking of the premium currency store from what I can tell it doesn't really sell power as much as it does style and convenience, which take that as you will. Now of course depending on how much you like the game itself you can either outright buy the currency, or convert gold into it, which fluctuates based on the in game economy as far as I can tell which is neat. The in game auction store sells about everything you can think of, from weapons, armor, skins, sigils, dyes, you name it, you can buy it there, and make a decent amount if you level high enough into certain crafting skills. Lastly, the story for the main game was pretty good, nothing special but definitely serviceable and set up the game for it's expansions well. You have the living world stories which help give contexts to the expansions, but the older ones are for sale, and you can buy them individually if you want to experience the older ones. All in all if you like MMOs and especially ones that don't charge a monthly fee (looking at you, WoW) this is right up your alley and I definitely think you should give it a shot. Coming back I like it just as much now as I did almost 10 years ago in 2015.

_childDocuments_.review: ARENANET WILL SCREW YOU:If you are a player with an existing arenanet account, do NOT buy expansions on steam, these idiots cant even figure out how to the two accounts "shake hands" and they will not help you if you fail to see this. I purchased some expansions recently, but after 6 hours of play and (weeks past steam's return window) I went to access the expansion only to find it unavailable. While talking with support, I learned that, because I used steam to buy it (so I didnt have to enter card info on the arenanet website) I was now SOL because they only recognize products purchased directly through them. Customer support literally told me to "just buy it again"There is no reason to have an "inability" to share this information between accounts in the current year, screw these people.Original review:Really lame that when I come back to this game its gone f2p and because I paid full price for the core game I get less benefits than someone who buys an expansion for 15 bucks on sale.That said, Its not the worst.Combat does this irritating thing where it pretends its action but pretend is all it does...I understand netcode is going to cause trouble with anything else but at that point I think its time to just rethink your approach, Just don't fall for anyone trying to sell you on it as an "Action" game. Another weird feature is that weapons are your skills, and weapon switching allows you to have two "builds" at your disposal on command. There are a few additional skills that you have regardless, but your playstyle is mostly defined by each weapon. It works, but the variety in combat for individual weapons is limited and shallow - if you like four of the five skills for a weapon, you're just going to have to get used to using the fifth one, or ignore it. It also sucks that you cant work to improve individual skills, instead you can upgrade the weapon to add stats you like - but because you are going to use an optimal strategy, instead of wasting a slot to upgrade the skills you don't like, you'll just bolster the ones you do. This isn't terribly different than a game with set skills for a character, except that progression doesn't unlock opportunity and some weapons have skills that seem redundant to certain classes, making the freedom to choose a weapon seem more like an afterthought or a "wouldn't it be cool?" instead of a well designed mechanic.Of course, its simplicity is what makes it so easy to access and experiment with, you can level by doing anything, from killing monsters to filling out the map to pelting kids with snowballs, or all of the above. The game drip feeds you so you're never overwhelmed and because you can level up by passing out beer to thirsty soldiers in the desert, you'll never feel like you're wasting your time dong something. Its a great way to emphasize the best parts of an mmo while stomping out the worst....its just a shame that the levelcap throws all that out the window.Overall, If you like the idea of mmos but hate the grinding, loot mechanics, and 6 hotbars worth of skills that you may have built wrong and totally ruined your character - This may be the right game. Grind doesnt exist, the game seems to always find a way to give you something from a big fight, and simplicity is at its core, Its major flaws are just a lack of customization and a sometimes frustrating combat, especially against world bosses that are incredibly confusing if you dont read guides or ask.Really, The biggest thing holding it back is the very thing that makes it easy to get into, meaning the complaints exist mostly as a consequence of the praises. Give it a try, aim to fully explore one region before you decide to buy or uninstall.

_childDocuments_.review: Other than for competitive PvE/Raiding, this is my go-to MMO. _childDocuments_.review: Despite having made a second game, three expansions in and working on the same IP for nearly 20 years, devs still lack vision of what their game should be. Never ending idiotic decisions, feedback deafness, record breaking content droughts and general clownsmanship. Some highlights of incompetence and bad design; -Live service content patches as a substitute for expansions -6 years between expansions -4 years to release a new raid wing -Not allowed to have dps meter in PvP lobby because of reasons. -Not allowed to inspect anyone because its much more fun to roll the dice on randoms and hope they don’t lie about their stat allocation. -Not allowed to trade anyone directly and can’t send more than 500g in mail to others. So to trade valuable items without paying thousands in taxes it is meta to go to some discord server, find a middleman, hope to god you won’t be scammed while the buyer mails you dozens of mails with valuables. -10 years and Elementalist class still hasn’t been removed and its players banned.P2W.Convenience items? Paid by cashBag space? Bank Space? Character slots? Paid by cashChanging your hair colour? Paid by cashBuild templates? Paid by cashTransmog tokens can be obtained by playing quite rapidly however, pretending that they serve any gameplay function besides being cash shop bait is dishonest.Safe to say that 95% of non cash shop skins just look awful compared to the cheaper paid ones. While mounts are different here, sure, none of their skins can be obtained by playing the game, everything from the cash shop.Gold can be directly converted from cash, which then can be used to go from lvl 1 to 80 in an hour, or more importantly you buy crafting materials to level up your crafting skill, which can then be used to craft BiS gear, that will forever be BiS because more powerful gear hasn’t been added in almost 10 years.To be fair, it is also possible to convert gold into cash shop currency, so technically everything can be obtained by playing, but you will need absolute insane amounts of gold or getting lucky by some other means like infusion drop or my preferred method, gambling.No matter how you look at it, cash provides significant gameplay advantages not just cosmetic skins, by that definition it is p2w. Gameplay is trash.Great swords and hammers often attack just as fast as dual daggers or pistols making the combat feel floaty and weapons weightless. Absurd visual clutter due to stack meta in group content, combine that with ancient engine, dx9, 20+ people, and you get an absolute vomit of colour sounds and low fps even on high end machines.Extreme class imbalance in both PvE and PvP. You can play a class that requires you to memorize 60 step rotation and deal less damage than some brainlet that autoattacks with a mechapet.PvP hacking goes unpunished for months, soft-botting is pretty much allowed. Parking your character with 5 autoattacking pets or AoE autocasting and leaving him there for days is allowed. Server vs Server open world PvP mode has been completely abandoned for years.Rewards for doing content are pathetic.Nothing is rewarding. Developers put in obvious effort when making the interface and loot systems to shoehorn you into buying bag space. Adding no less than 30 different grey vendor trash items, hundreds of crafting materials and other junk. Every new map they release adds new currency and junk into the loot table, bit by bit they continue worsen an already bad and convoluted loot system.New, more powerful gear hasn’t been added since Nov 2012, so content rewards are usually just crafting mats and vendor trash. You killed the map boss? Trash items and matsYou finished a dungeon? Trash items and matsYou left your character afk farming? Trash items and matsIt is almost as the devs want you to do braindead afk farming instead of actually playing the game. I would argue it is more profitable to just set up an afk farm and go to bed than go raiding. Exploration rewards also, without fail, disappoint every single time. You found and completed a jumping puzzle and opened a giant golden chest at the end? Enjoy lvl 20 gem, two silvers, grey trash item, and an unsellable medallion that you have to manually destroy. It’s like that every single time.Because it doesn't matter what class you play, what gear you have, what content you're doing, I would only recommend the game to those that want to pretend like they're playing an MMORPG instead of playing one.Guild Wars 2 is a perfect example of a bad sequel and failed potential.

_childDocuments_.review: The game I spent the most hours in, Guild Wars 2 shaped my '10s life. Now it is held up by quality of life features, so that even though Secrets of the Obscure, the latest expansion, wasn't up to par... I can't imagine ever going back.Audio: 7/10Nothing special or outstanding outside of the main theme and some silly/funny jungle music in Heart of Thorns.Story: 8/10It's no JRPG or better yet a visual novel, but for an MMO it's the best story next to Final Fantasy XIV. Think of this as the American alternative to the latter. Some of the characters are abhorrable though, while Commander is often lampooned for saving the world from ending 10 too many times. Latest expansion promises to address this,  offering a return to day-to-day quests.Gameplay: 9/10The combat is stellar, probably the best in an MMO after Black Desert. Dodges allow for situational awareness and a high skill ceiling, while noobs can get by just auto-attacking. Some may complain there aren't enough skills, but that means fewer keybinds, and you're going to have to memorize all the alts as well, because this is a hugely alt-friendly game.Graphics: 6/10The modern, pretty version of WoW, basically... and yet, still old enough to look unplayable for some. Optimization is also poor, framerates should be better than what we get with these visuals.Overall:This is an A-Tier MMORPG. And since A-Tier MMORPGs are still B-Tier games overall, you'll want to play an A-Tier MMO, and nothing less. If you catch the MMO bug, then you can move on to the few other gems in this stagnating genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Downloaded the whole thing on Steam just so I could put in a review to support the game. Having logged over two thousand hours in playtime on the original client this is definitively the most impressive and enjoyable MMO I've ever played. It's simply more advanced than the older games of this genre, while being far more intricate than the newer games of this genre.The game almost immediately sets itself apart from many other MMOs by the way its world is structured. The environments are fully traversable, players being able to run and jump around all manner of dynamic settings like caves, hills, ruins and mountains. Numerous platforming challenges are hidden throughout the world for players to find and struggle with for rewards and achievements. While the absolutely pristine mount system gives players even greater options when travelling the world through the ability to zoom at high speeds across a map in seconds, jump to massive heights that can scale mountains and colossal ruins, or fly openly across the map and just avoid everything.Each map is filled with many random events that will periodically trigger on their own. This adding an extra layer of depth to the exploration and levelling process as players will constantly encounter random scenarios that they can join in on. There are also many absolutely astonishing large scale bosses that appear across the world at set intervals, which players are encouraged to continue fighting for rewards long after they surpass the level of that area. The game actively downscales the player to any lower level area they enter, allowing players to experience lower level content at any time without being completely overpowered.Even more distinct is the way this game handles fetch quests. Numerous MMOs force players to do a variety of arbitrary chores that string them across the world as they have to repetitiously talk with forgettable characters to acquire and finish tasks. In this game you automatically gain tasks by simply entering the area where they are active, while being given a variety of options on how to make progress towards that task. When you complete it, the task is automatically cashed in. Players have full control over where they travel and which tasks they perform, the only linear progression in this regard comes from the story missions. Which are also completely optional. The story of this game is decent for an MMO but not extremely compelling, however there are a select few powerful moments. In general most of the writing that really stands out comes from the overall world design and random character interactions, many of which tend to be fun and wholesome.The game features nine classes each with: four or more default weapon movesets, around two dozen selectable abilities, dozens of passive traits and three specializations that further expand the class. Although players cannot change their character's class, all other facets of their class can be customized on a whim; allowing players to set up and swap between multiple different builds when desired. The combat is quite unique in that its complexity largely depends on how much effort players want to put into being optimal. Many combat encounters can be survived by doing the bare minimum, but there is also a lot room for reactivity and memorization. Outside of more difficult encounters, players can choose how much effort they want to put into the combat based on their current mood. Many of the more difficult combat sequences in the game however do largely revolve around memorization of the mechanics and patterns. Which does make the latter end of the difficulty scale very inaccessible as players have no hope of survival until they memorize the encounter. This only applies to very specific portions of endgame content though, which can be completely ignored. The vast majority of content in this game can be beaten with decent reactions and a casual remembrance of the mechanics at play.There is a massive amount of endgame content between map bosses, dungeons, fractals, strike missions, raids, achievement hunting, mastery unlocks, crafting and holiday events. The game has an extremely expansive achievement system that hides all manner of special rewards, along with a multitude of daily tasks. Unfortunately the reward system in this game is not very structured, so discovering all the things you can actually unlock may be awkward as they aren't openly advertised to the player.The game does feature a large scale and small scale competitive mode. However both are extremely abrasive to new players as they require extensive knowledge of the classes, mechanics and most optimal builds in the game for survival to be very plausible. There are a multitude of balancing issues with the classes in competitive, and in general really, but that's not exactly unique for a game with this much variety. Outside of competitive the balancing issues are largely unnoticeable except in very specific types of content, or when using very specific builds. Neither competitive mode is being aggressively updated at the moment though. But it is all fleshed out content that players can dive into if they choose.The game is free to play by default but has multiple expansions and story sequences which can be bought. All of which add a multitude of new endgame content such as maps, story missions, mechanics and rewards. Each of the three aforementioned class specializations is unlocked via having the corresponding expansion. There is a cash shop but it's pretty much just full of cosmetics and niche convenience items sold to sustain the game between expansion releases. Players can convert their ingame currency into the cash shop currency so it is completely possible to buy things from the cash shop without actually paying with cash, as I have done multiple times. Unfortunately the game does have a lootbox system but fortunately it's extremely inconsequential. Somewhere around ninety five percent of the monetized cosmetics in the game are bought upfront from the cash shop, only a very small amount are lootbox exclusive; so the lootboxes are quite forgettable.From the exploration, to the class design, the combat, the general mechanics and the endgame there is a massive amount of variety and depth to this experience. Although some grinding is required for very specific achievements or rewards, much of the game revolves around highly varied activities that players can pick and choose as they please. The game offers a huge amount of content entirely for free, and a massive amount of expanded endgame content can be bought after the initial free campaign is finished. This is definitively the best MMO I've ever played, and I honestly do not expect any other MMO will ever supersede it.If you're interested in finding more games that I positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: [MMO that breaks the Holy Trinity]There are no clear roles like "Tank, Healer, DPS". All classes/specilizations can be many things, Healer, Bunker, Buffer, Roamer, Condition / Power Damage, and probably many more roles. Hell, you could even be all of these at the same time wih "All Stats" Celestial stats gear. You'll see max level people even in lvl1 areas, since the content will be ALWAYS relevant, in many cases the low level areas are even more relevant as max level rather than low level since the game has no traditional questing system,Many people are confused what do next due to lack of guidance, WIKI is your friend /Wiki Event Timer or ET, Chat CommandYou'll open up a wiki site where it shows upcoming events. You can also /wiki, then shift+click an item and it'll open up a site for that item.Instead of questing, you have (achievement) collections, hearts, world completion, world bosses, meta events, bounty hunts, open world events: where you'll get a notice.For example Hey theres an escort happening, go there and you'll almost always see other people doing it WITH you (everyone gets their own loot, so NO ninja loot in this game)I've played almost all of the big MMO's, and this is my favourite by far. I like how versatile all classes are. The "Fashion Wars 2" is GREAT, you have such an amazing depth to customizing how your armor look, multiple DYE slots for armor, the openworld is always alive with the MEGA-server system. EU / NA are different datacenters.For endgame there are Fractals, Raids, Strikes, Structured PvP (Fixed Stats), World vs World, and DungeonsIn the end, you set your own goals in the game, like creating a legendary, you'll do a collection which can include doing dungeons, jumping puzzles, openworld events, some have even their on "quest" collection line. You could have a 2 year break, and still hop on back and you won't have a huge gap in gear difference. Because there will be no better gear coming up, only different stat combinations.For returning players, you can enable Anet Launcher on steam by adding " -portal Provider" to launch options.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing GW2 on and off since prerelease, and it's always felt like my home game. Coming up on 4k hours played and I still feel like I've got bits to do (although that might be procrastination). Let's focus on what got me hooked in the first place. It largely boils down to two things:    1. No sub fee. Back in the day I couldn't afford it, and I know I wouldn't have kept coming back to this game if it had one.    2. The sense of exploration and community.GW2 has no sub fee. The closest thing to it are releases of "Living World" episodes, semi-regular patches that include new maps, story, cosmetics, and more. If you login even once while an episode is the most recent, you'll keep it for free forever. You only have to pay for them if you've taken a break from the game. (NB: The biggest bundle here gives you all current episodes upfront, and is fantastic value imo.)As for immersion, GW2 captured me like few other games have. The dynamic event system makes maps feel alive and flowing. Because hitting a mob once is enough to earn drops, there's no animosity towards other players at events, fostering a friendly, cooperative atmosphere. It also makes meeting players (future friends!) so much easier, as groups of players will naturally form around event chains. In later maps, event chains can span the length and breadth of the map. "Meta-events" such as these form the bulk of the open world experience at endgame, and vary from killing enormous dragons, laying siege to a series of forts, or gathering coins to summon a giant cactus pinata.I also want to mention exploration. I've touched on events, but equally important are the maps themselves. From the gentle rolling hills of starting zones, to dingy marshlands, vast deserts and towering cityscapes, each is full of interesting locations to discover. Hidden areas within each map make sure exploration can still feel fresh years later, and jumping puzzles exist across many maps to test your movement skill (which some people hate, but they're all optional).Final point I want to touch on is the community. Thanks to the structure of the openworld gameplay, finding friends isn't hard, and the community is very friendly. New players will likely find veterans in starter zones giving helpful advice and items to make your experience better. If you need someone specific to reach out to, feel free to PM me ingame and I'll be happy to help you out. My IGN is Zylarth.2807 - if you can't reach me I'm likely busy or you're on the free-to-play version, which prevents whispering to non-friends to avoid bots abusing it.I hope this review helped you to understand why I love this game, and hopefully I'll see you in Tyria! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Guild Wars 2 is a captivating MMORPG that sets itself apart with its dynamic world, engaging gameplay, and player-friendly approach. Here’s why it’s one of the best in its genre:Pros:1. Living World and Dynamic Events:Guild Wars 2 boasts a dynamic world where events unfold in real-time, responding to player actions. This creates a living, immersive environment that constantly evolves, keeping players engaged and invested in the game world.2. Unique Combat System:The game features an innovative action-oriented combat system that emphasizes skill over traditional MMO tab-targeting. Dodging, positioning, and combo abilities add depth and strategy to battles, making combat feel dynamic and rewarding.3. Extensive Character Customization:Players have extensive options for character customization, from choosing professions and skills to personalizing appearance and gear. This flexibility allows for diverse playstyles and ensures that no two characters are alike.4. Player-Friendly Monetization:Guild Wars 2 follows a buy-to-play model with cosmetic microtransactions. There are no subscription fees, and players can enjoy all core content without spending additional money. The monetization is fair and focuses on cosmetic enhancements rather than pay-to-win advantages.5. Rich Storytelling and Lore:The game features a rich lore and compelling storyline that unfolds through personal story quests, dynamic events, and Living World updates. Players’ choices have meaningful consequences, shaping the narrative and their character’s journey.6. Supportive Community and Developer Interaction:Guild Wars 2 has a welcoming and supportive community that enhances the multiplayer experience. Developers actively engage with players through forums, live streams, and updates, listening to feedback and continuously improving the game.Cons:1. Endgame Content Variety:While Guild Wars 2 offers a variety of content, including dungeons, fractals, and PvP, some players may find the endgame progression lacking in comparison to other MMOs. Additional high-level challenges and activities could enhance the longevity for dedicated players.2. Learning Curve for New Players:The game’s depth and complexity can be overwhelming for new players. Understanding the combat mechanics, character progression, and world events may require time and patience to fully grasp.3. Performance Issues in Crowded Areas:During peak times or in crowded areas, Guild Wars 2 may experience performance issues such as lag or frame rate drops. This can detract from the overall experience, especially during large-scale events or PvP battles.Conclusion:Guild Wars 2 stands out as a top-tier MMORPG with its dynamic world events, innovative combat system, and player-friendly approach to monetization. While it may have some minor drawbacks like endgame content variety and performance issues, its engaging storytelling, supportive community, and continuous updates make it a must-play for MMO enthusiasts.Would I Recommend It?Absolutely. Whether you’re new to MMOs or a seasoned player looking for a fresh experience, Guild Wars 2 offers a vibrant and immersive world filled with endless adventures and opportunities for exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: I often give MMORPGs a try (WoW, ESO, FFIV, etc.) and while I like aspects about them, the games ultimately feel repetitive and like a chore. After playing an MMO I'll ask myself, am I actually having fun doing this? That's where Guild Wars 2 blows me away. I've never played an MMO like this that feels fun and rewarding right out of the gate and doesn't get stale. Exploring genuinely feels fun and full of wonder. You're never pigeon holed into doing a specific task. You get experience for exploring, doing quests you want, random events popping up all over the place. It also has an active and welcoming community that enjoys exploring and teaming up like you do. There is no subscription fee. The game is almost too good to be true. Jump in and have fun. Don't rush to get to 80 because no matter what your level is or where you are in the world there is something to do.

_childDocuments_.review: 19 hours on steam, closer to a couple of hundred on the ANet launcher.Im a long time veteran of Guild Wars 1. bought this game day one. Played for a month, quit because it had an identity crisis of trying to be a sequel to Guild Wars while at the same time trying to be something entirely different. It just was not a cohesive or engaging experience. At all.I said I would wait a year until they had better fleshed out their overall design philosophy in terms of what exactly Guild Wars 2 was trying to be and who it was trying to appeal to.Instead, I waited an entire decade and came back to find out this game has aged better than any fine wine ever could. It feels like its own game, every facet has been polished to a shine and the game feels like it has come into its own, both creatively and mechanically, while still staying grounded in the source material it spiritually succeeds. It has gone from a 4/10 smashed up 1000-piece jigsaw puzzle of an MMO to one of the most gratifying, fair and engaging online gaming experiences you can currently have.9/10. Don't let anything stop you from giving this a shot. Even if it takes 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: BEFORE THE REVIEW: Please note this IS NOT truly Free to play. The BASE version of the game is free, which is the Core 2012 package us GW2 veterans have been playing back in the days (10 years ago). If you absolutely want the best experience ever, not only in the MMO scenario but in the online gaming, you should consider buying the full packages (all Expansion packs and Living World episodes).The game itself is FREE FROM ANY MONTHLY FEE, but it has to be said that playing the f2p version will gut you out from tons of content and functions.THAT BEING SAID:I have over 8000 hours of playtime on the Arenanet game version betwen more than 10 fully optimized characters and i've been on and off between years since 2012 and have been playing since the very first day.Let me tell you, this is something UNIQUE. A true gem like Guild Wars 2 is rarely found, especially in the MMO genre, as it caters to both casual players and to hardcore ones and i truly mean it.You could focus on the long term goals between each and every game mode and decide your very own pace. Do you wish to grind the game nonstop to reach your goal? Why not! Go ahead!On the opposite, do you find frustrating to grind and want to savour what the game offers when you want it, how you want it? Please do!You could "freeze" (MMO term which means taking a break from a game) for months, even years, and your account still remains relevant with the newest content released.Yes, the endgame content is horizontally shaped which means as soon as you've hit level 80 and are geared with the right equip for the job, you're good to go; and there is no amount of time that will invalidate that.There are several type of content to be done, an ocean of experiences to have and a plethora of side activities that will get you hooked in no time:- You can play it mostly solo, as some kind of online role playing game, while leaving the most demanding content for organized play;- Content is shared and doesn't require groups for the most part except for high end instanced content. You can gather from the same resource node and get kill participation on the same mob that somebody else is fighting!- No traditional quests, instead there's dynamic events which shapes the life of the world;- Instanced story missions with iconic characters and cool plots that will overarch in intense dramas and twists;- Thousands of skins to choose from for your equipment which you can also dye a huge spectrum of unlockable colors;- Everything gives you experience points so you can choose your preferred way of reaching the endgame: traditional world exploring, story missions, crafting, pvp or by other means;- Traditional dungeons, Fractals of the Mists (scaling infinite dungeons), Raids, Strikes (shortened, easier raids), Structured Arena PvP and a dedicated Pvp war zone with 3 servers fighting each other called "World vs World vs World";- Legendary quests to obtain legendary gear, crafting skills, collections, jumping puzzles, Guild missions, Achievements, side activities such as minigames, mount races, fishing and exploring secret zones;- Gorgeous open world pve maps with huge epic bosses, lenghty meta-events with hundreds of players that must collaborate to clear;- The item shop provides with loads of quality of life items and skins which can both be bought with real money and with earned ingame cash that can be converted.There is so much to do in this game that i'm sure i'm forgetting something. The thing that hooks me up and motivates me to play is that no matter how long i take a pause from it, i just come back whenever i choose so and i can jump back from where i've left it, with no power creep mechanics outplayingme or forcing me to catch up. I can be as performing for a raid group as i was if i'd take a 1 year break, no sweat and no tiers of gear to recuperate between me and my friends!All of the classes, called "professions", are fun to play and have their own unique flavor and class theme. There are many subclasses, or "Elite specializations" for each single profession which focus on different playstylesand are favoured through specific game modes. For example, a Warrior could specialize in the Berserker Elite spec to deal loads of damage in PVE or could pick the Spellbreaker Elite spec to bring utility and boons in the pvp battlefield.Fights are intense, action packed, full of reaction mechanics and encourages you to dodge and move around a lot to survive. Bosses all have their own mechanics to be beaten and the more progress you do in the game, the more unforgiving they are,culminating in the Raid scenario where organized of highly skilled players have to diligently follow mechanics and role, or perish. However, also WvWvW bosses are hard to deal with and they won't nudge if a powerful army of pvp players won't engage them.After you're done with high intensity activities for the day or you just want to take some relax time, i advise you go around the beautiful world of Tyria, uncover its misteries and unlockable secret achievements and collections. There are literally hundredsof tiny little secrets and collectibles for each and every zone in the game, being from the Core 2012 experience to the latest high end expansion zone. No region feels dead as many players are always looking for scaled, down levelled content in those regions as they still remain valid and provide a challenge.Or maybe you're a bit bored out of the look of your character and want to search for another style of your gear; i'm sure you will find plenty, even overwhelming choices for your look. And if you're bored of your character...why not try to level up and play another one? The game doesn't punish you for starting over again and have multiple toons to have fun with. It's absolutely not mandatory but it can be rewarding, such as having more crafting disciplines available, more characters for different game content and so on.Some times during the year there's timed events that bring all players together such as Dragonbash (the celebration of the death of the first Elder Dragon) or the Festival of the Four Winds, and each has their own achievements and meta rewards. They cycle all year long so no worries if you've missed some, they will always come back.The trading post and the open world are both shared features on all servers, so don't stress too much about which server to pick when creating your first characters. However, the only exception would be for the WvWvW PVP: if you want to conquer castles and fight with your friends you must create a character within the same realm.All the rest of the content of the game is shared between each and every player.As a last tip i'd suggest you a couple websites that will help you grasp and master this exceptional game: GW2wiki, Snowcrows, Lucky Noobs, GW2 Skills, GW2Spidy, Gw2 Efficency, Metabattle (they are all websites that provide help for building your characters and manage your resources in the game)Last but not least, i hope you will enjoy the wholesome community of this game, which always encourages and welcomes new players as the game itself doesn't care for how long you have played: it treates everyone on the same page!Guild Wars 2 shaped the modern way we play MMOs and it's still not popular enough for what i think it provided to the genre.Play it and have fun! :)Thank you for reading,Heretiko

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Positives:+Interesting action combat for a MMO+no monthly fee+gear treadmill is minimal/non-existent+casual and solo friendly+world vs world has fun 200 person battles (but can get stale)+build diversity exists for most content+mounts make getting around a pleasure+very little reliance on the trinity: dps/tank/healer+real money store is only for cosmetics and QOL improvements like bank spaceNegatives:-engine is extremely CPU dependent with strange frame drops-class balance isn’t strong, and updates are slow-story is very uneven, some great elements spaced out with some filler-ranked PvP is interesting but receives little dev attention-many skins available for purchase with games or real money, rather than earned in gameI’ve played this game for ten years and clocked several thousand hours, so I’m certainly a bit biased and rooting for continued success.  I find this game to be an excellent MMO, the combat is satisfying, the story is engaging, and there’s no sub-fee, so I simply put the game down and take a break if I get bored.Unlike many other MMO’s, there is a fair amount of build diversity.  Your equipped weapons will determine your main skills, with a few ‘utility’ slots available for player choice.  Swapping weapons will give you a whole different set of skills, and you can swap between 2 on the fly, adding some nice variety to combat.And luckily, the combat is the best part of the game for me.  Rather than stand in place and trade blows, you’ll be dodging, teleporting, weapon swapping, and swinging in real-time, meaning if you swing and contact 5 enemies, they’ll all take damage.  Add on top of this a variety of interesting classes, and you can put together some creative groups for open world exploration, raids, and dungeons.Further, the open world question is incredible – other games take note.  As you explore, you’ll come across ‘dynamic events’ such as a caravan in route to a new city.  Everyone who joins in gets credit for the events equally, encouraging spontaneous group play.  Best of all, succeeding or failing an event will often lead to further quest chains, creating a ‘choose your own adventure’ type decision tree.  Some end with massive fights against enormous bosses and 50-100 other players cooperating simultaneously.Finally, Guild Wars 2 also minimizes the gear treadmill.  Most of the content offered can be completed using cheap weapons/armor from the trading post, and even the higher level ‘ascended armor’ can be fully obtained by a couple weeks of farming various map currencies.Overall, I think a whether people enjoy Guild Wars 2 or not comes down to how they approach and play the game more than anything. The design favors players who go slow, read quest content, listen to the NPC's, explore high vistas, and admire all the work the developers put into the world.   If this sounds like you, give it a shot – the base game is free and will keep you busy for many hours.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of playing Guild Wars 2, I can confidently say that it’s one of the most rewarding and respectful MMORPGs out there. Whether you’re a casual adventurer, a competitive PvPer, or an endgame raider, the game lets you enjoy it on your terms without pressuring you to sink endless hours grinding.From the very start, Guild Wars 2 sets itself apart with its horizontal progression system. You’re not constantly chasing the next big gear tier—once you hit max level, the game shifts focus to skill mastery, exploration, and customization. This approach ensures that my time always feels well spent. Logging in for just an hour can result in meaningful progress, whether it's completing a map, earning achievements, or simply participating in dynamic world events.The living world updates and expansions are a testament to the developers’ commitment to creating rich and evolving content. The storylines are engaging, the open world feels alive, and every map is packed with secrets, events, and stunning visuals. It’s hard to believe a game this beautiful and expansive is free-to-play at its core.For someone who values their time, the convenience features are a dream. Fast travel is affordable and plentiful, inventory management tools are seamless, and systems like the trading post and account-wide unlocks make progression feel smooth and satisfying. And with the addition of mounts in Path of Fire, exploration is not only faster but also more fun and dynamic.What keeps me coming back after all these years is how the game makes every session feel worthwhile. Whether I’m exploring the breathtaking vistas of Tyria, tackling the challenging endgame content, or simply hanging out in Lion’s Arch, there’s always something meaningful to do.Guild Wars 2 is more than a game—it’s a world that respects your time, your playstyle, and your pace. For veterans and newcomers alike, it’s an MMO experience like no other.💎 10/10 – The perfect blend of freedom, fun, and respect for its players.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the only MMO that doesn't piss me off.They solved some really basic problems of the genre. For one, other people being around is generally always a positive. Remember old MMOs having "kill stealing"? Doesn't do that here. Everyone gets credit.They never raise the level cap. Once you get to max level you don't have to keep chasing new gear. My characters I've made years ago are still valid. There's new options and the meta shifts, but you don't have to get on a gear treadmill. You can chase legendary equipment if you like, but that's for prestige and some qol perks. One really basic thing that's so nice: you can deposit materials from your inventory to your bank from anywhere. You can sell stuff from anywhere. You can access your bank and more from anywhere (via the pvp lobby, so you suffer a loading screen). It's nice. The basic gameplay feels like a real video game. You can dodge attacks.You don't have to do inane quest chains. There are "hearts" in the world where you get credit for doing stuff in the area. Some of them are silly. Some are great. Most of them include "go kill some stuff" as an option. The main draw are the dynamic events. That's where stuff just happens in the world and anyone nearby can participate. Portals open and demons come out. The volcano erupts. Allied npc soldiers attempt to take new territory. You just hop in and play.There's also instanced content for organized (or disorganized) groups of 5 or 10 or more. The latest expansion added a big 50 person event where you have to fight a bunch of demon bosses in a big map without letting the NPC die. It's fun. There's world PVP for when you want to go knock down a keep's walls with catapults and kill everyone inside. Or just go seize supply camps on your lonesome. There's a long story. Lots of solo content there. There's mounts. They're great. Make it fun to move around the world. I could go on. I'm just rambling. I have like 3500 hours in the game on my main account.

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently nearing level 40 as a free-to-play Guardian and have yet to reach the third zone for my chosen race of Human.Following the achievement tracker in the game has given me a shallow introduction to the crafting system which I find tedious, but that experience would have been made better if I had not neglected to collect resources in the open world while pursuing other achievements.Like in the first game, Jeremy Soul's score is the perfect soundtrack.The graphic direction is an improvement from the first while remaining true to the style of the first.The decision to remove the ability to collect skills is in my opinion a poor one as hunting Elites to capture their skills was a large part of my satisfaction from the original, but I can understand their desire to make the game more accessible to more players, especially given that Guild Wars character builds overwhelmingly followed the meta, with fewer players experimenting with atypical builds.Regional events provide a welcome distraction from my goal to 100% each map before I move to the next.
