_childDocuments_.review: Unique seems like a word that doesn’t quite begin to capture the hypnotic chaos of Post-Void. The core game-loop is an engrossing blend of roguelikes and 90’s twitch shooters, where you feverishly battle your way through 11 stages and an epilogue of procedurally generated hallways whilst fending off a swarm of cursed monsters. As you push on through, the stages increase in their verticality, becoming more labyrinthian and the enemies - more numerous and challenging. At the end of every stage you get to choose from three randomised weapons or power-ups, allowing you to slightly tweak your playstyle and strategy on different runs. Once you reach the end of the nightmare, you’re greeted with a splash screen that tallies your score based on time, kills, accuracy and hits taken. Essentially that means you can finish the game in under five minutes if you possess the skill, but Post-Void’s tight gameplay and engaging presentation will keep you coming back over and over.So, presentation is one of Post-Void’s most captivating aspects. It features a dizzying blend of disorganised imagery and sound; psychedelic, vibrantly coloured visuals and an eclectic, synthy music track that all converges into a playable fever dream. The constant barrage of audible and visual noise can certainly feel off-putting at first, especially combined with the consistent intensity of the experience but sticking with it will treat you to a very carefully and purposefully crafted, high-octane thrill ride quite unlike anything else currently on the market. Juxtaposed with the previous 11 stages of bedlam, the epilogue treats the player to a darker, more understated stage. There are relatively few enemies and the soundtrack starts to fizzle out before leaving you with just the music of your guns and the death throes of the monsters. As the killing ends, the climax presents a quiet moment of reflection as you watch a flower bloom in front of you; a final moment of respite to catch your breath before receiving your leaderboard posting and diving back into the fray. In total, Post-Void is a strange, eccentric game - something best witnessed first-hand as words can barely express the one of a kind experience it offers and a testament to the strange creativity of indie gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fast paced game in every aspect of it's design.  A little frustrating at first, but after a few tries all the movement just becomes natural, and all thoughts meld into raw instinctual reflexes.  I don't think I'll be beating this game, but it nails down the feeling that it advertises. _childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic and how fast paced it is simply amazing. This game is definitely not for people sensitive to flashing lights but in general this game is extremely well made. I wish there were more modes and more of a story because the intro cut scene was very interesting to me. Other than that though, please give this game a try if you are not sensitive to flashing lights.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game because it feels like something that might rewire your brain if you play it enough. The first time I played it, it did feel like it could be the first game to ever give me a migraine (didn't do that, thankfully). It does have that factor that makes you want to try again right away after you've been defeated, to try to get just a little further.It also might be a better FPS shooting trainer than any app/game on Steam that's actually been designed to do that. Mostly in the sense that after playing it for a bit, everything else with shooting in a three-dimensional space feels slower and so easy to parse, as opposed to this, where you feel like just looking at a wall could give you a seizure. So, whilst anyone with any kind of issue with games making them sick, and especially those with epilepsy or something similar should absolutely avoid it, everyone else should try it. It's something to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, shooting feels amazing and both visual and sound design are unique and cool. It is a shooter based mostly on movement, basically, if you keep moving, you will be fine, since there are many upgrades that allow you to loosen up your aim a little (except the Uzi, i swear i never hit anything with the Uzi). My only complaint is that it is very short, it actually took me less than an hour to beat the game and i'm not very good at shooters. I could refund it and get my money back, but i had so much fun playing it that i won't. I really recommend it since it's very fun and very cheap, even without being on sale. I still hope that the Devs add more content, but i'm not sure about that. Even while lasting less than an hour, it is more than worthy of your time

_childDocuments_.review: Play fast (7-8 minutes total for a winning run)Win fast (30 minutes to beat the game originally)Die fast (often 2 minutes in a run and I'm dead, health is always draining)Kill fast (Things have barely any health and die instantly to headshots, you must kill to gain back health)Upgrade fast (beat a level? pick one of three simple perks, they're all fun)Headbang fast (music good, that's all)Score fast (beat the game? it's got arcade scores, beat the game but better, fool)It's like 2-3 bucks, play the game fast, learn the game fast, and just have a good time killing everything in your path before something kills you in a couple minutes.Then do it all again.Also visuals are WACKY man, I mean I like em.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the closest thing to taking cocaine and acid at the same time that ive experienced soberHere are some tips to not die as fast1) There are 4 weapons, but its a trick, the only thing you'll ever need is your starting pistol. The shotgun takes an eternity to reload, the machine gun pisses away your accuracy, and good luck surviving three seconds trying to get a hit with the knife. Just aim for the head on all of your opponents and theyll die instantly, sometimes before they can even see you, and even sometimes before you can even see them (Dont ask me how it happens it just happens)2) Try your best to get the explosive ammo before the second act, because thats when the Telephones show up and they are the worst thing to be created in this game. They dont attack but when they touch you they stop you pretty much dead i your tracks, letting everybody else come over and kick you while you're down. They're tricky to hit and like to swarm up, but with the explosive ammo you only need to hit one in the bunch and they'll go down like domino's3) Try not to get caught up and remember that the goal is about speed. Any more than two shots on an enemy is wasting time and bullets, if they aren't directly in your way than they aren't worth noticing unless you need more juice in your head. Its easy sometimes to get turned around in the chaos of exploding bodies, so if you feel like somethings taking too long just slide the hell out of there and don't look back, the compass also helps immensely with this

The overall aesthetic, hand drawn looking visuals and wild soundtrack all combine to make one of the best experiences I had playing a score chasing, wilding out game in a long time. This game is punk as f*ck.

And I'm glad I did. It's a great party game. It's a game where you get together with friends, and have a big WHODUNIT match, very much like an interactive board game, but better. It's a LOT of fun, when you have people to play with.However, you have to understand that Among Us is simply that. A casual, party game meant to be played with friends. It's not a game that requires a great amount of skill, just the ability to be a detective, and see through people's lies. Or, when you are the imposter, it requires you to be an excellent liar. It's definitely a game worth playing, but it isn't a game that you should take and replace your life with.The core gameplay loop does get boring relatively quickly, because there is nothing to work towards, nor does it have any real progression mechanics. It simply exists as a fun, round-by-round type game. Nothing more, and nothing less.Why do I recommend against buying it? Only because the mobile version exists. The PC version is just the mobile port, but while the mobile version is free-to-play, the PC version is $5 normally, or $4 on sale.I suggest that if you to play Among Us, that you save your money, download the BlueStacks Android emulator, and play it on there for free instead. That's what I wish I did.I hope you found this review helpful! _childDocuments_.review: Man, I love everything this game does. Never played anything like it; just inspired game design. I'm going to do my best to describe the fulfillment I'm feeling right now, because I just beat it and boy oh boy was that enjoyable.Post Void is a procedurally generated roguelike twitch FPS where you gain health by killing enemies. Your health depletes when you're idle so it's a speedrun game by nature; you want to make it to the end of the level as fast as possible, killing enemies to restore health along the way. It has the same purity in FPS game design that old school 90s skill-based single-player FPSes had: you die insanely fast (1-2 hits usually), and need to manage the delicate balance of attacking enemies and just rushing to the exit. Some enemies you can ignore, some you very much can't, and learning the ins-and-outs of what to prioritize and not is part of the joy of learning this game.The game is split into 3 main acts and 11 levels in total. To beat it is technically like a 8 minute run max (probably even less) but don't let that fool you: you'll die so often learning the game that it will take you much longer to actually beat it. Losing never feels that bad because run times are so low, but I definitely had a point where I was like "ayo can I actually beat this? This is so hard!" Turns out I just hadn't "figured it out" and once everything clicked, I was making it to the end or near the end pretty consistently. Depending on your experience with FPSes, and how long it takes you to understand what you're supposed to do, I expect most players will take somewhere along the lines of 3-10 hrs with this one. That's assuming they can beat it at all; only 17% of players beat this one even with its short runtime; it's a genuine challenge.  7 unique enemies, 4 weapons, 9 upgrades ... pretty good for $3; there's a lot more value here than it looks. Plus it's infinitely replayable; it's one of those games where you can just pop in at any time when you have a few minutes and want to click some heads. It's procedurally generated after all, so every run is slightly different. I've only won one run so far but I'm tempted to try to get wins with all the other weapons; that sounds fun.Obviously I should mention the aesthetic which is just 10/10 perfect. OK, maybe not if you have epilepsy, or a sensitivity to bright colors (I think there is an accessibility mode to make that better to be fair). For the rest of us though, it's got this awesome chaotic energy that encapsulates everything the game represents so well. The UI is beautifully simplistic; there's no numbers on scren whatsoever. You have infinite ammo and your health is represented by the liquid in this idol in your other hand. Not only does that look great, but it also makes it super easy to look in your periphery to get a quick gauge on your health (which you need to know in order to make decisions). There's only one music track, but like everything else, it's perfect. Sound effects are fantastic (love the end of run death animation and sound too); guns feel appropriately powerful. Sound is particularly important too; once you get some hours under you, you begin to recognize different enemy noises and that affects decision making. Hearing a Flamingo scuttling behind me and doing a quick 360 shot to save myself, or the whirring of telehands ... these things will save your life.I had a huge roadblock for a few hours in act 2 because it introduces some new enemies, and requires a bit more pathfinding. You have to jump to different elevations constantly, and getting lost even for a few seconds is a death sentence. Once I learned to always go in the direction of the enemies, that helped a lot, but honestly that wouldn't solve it completely. Sometimes I'd jump from one elevation to the next and get immediately ambushed by 2 enemies and die instantly. Learning to slow down between elevation changes helped enormously; the big thing that helped me finally be consistent is learning when to go fast and when to slow down. All this was a part of the learning process, and is by no means a criticism of the game, but there's a massive difficulty spike in act 2 that will take patience to get over.Learning the upgrades and what's important is huge. All the weapons are viable (though I find the knife very hard to use; apparently it's the best for speedrunning so I know it's good), even the starter pistol. The most important thing in this game is reloading. Time is your enemy and reloading is brutal. Learning when is a good time to reload, and also just getting every upgrade that improves reloading is huuuge. Everything is secondary to that; it's counterintuitive because you'd think things like "more health" or "slower enemy bullets" would be most important but no. Every time you reload you best case lose time (and time=health) or worst case have an enemy in front of you who you can't kill (which often means death). I know there are other ways to play the game but taking out most enemies, going slower, and tactically reloading were what got me over the hump.Anyway that is all to say it was a joyous learning experience. I highly, highly recommend this one. My only complaint is I want more. What a rush. Masterfully done.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is a surreal, randomly generated first-person shooter offering quick play sessions, leaderboards, frantic action, a sense of urgency, all awash in an 80s colour pallete with an uptempo soundtrack.  Post Void gives you a gun in your right hand, and a head in your left. Within that head is a white liquid. Should the liquid run out, you die. The liquid is ever-decreasing, granting you but a limited opportunity to push forward. Where are you going? To a flowery oasis at the end of a series of rooms filled with an assortment of foes, all bent on your demise. Killing an enemy grants you more liquid, but you can't stop moving. Reaching the oasis grants a temporary repreive, a rest-stop of sorts, allowing you to catch your breath and select one of three perks. Perks are either a weapon replacement, a one-off ability, or a stackable passive boost. There are a total of 11 randomly generated levels. Beating them all can take less than 10 minutes. It took me 4 hours.There are a limited number of perks to choose from. Some are more useful than others. For example, a compass which points an arrow towards the oasis offers less utility than a boost to your shots making enemies explode on death. Enemies range from close-range imps, to long-range shooters, to clusters of flying drones which cause your screen to look tie-dyed on contact. You don't have time to question what you see, only to shoot, jump, and slide your way to the exit. Or die. Over and over again. At the end of each run, you are given a score. Think you did well? Compare your score to others on the leaderboard and prepare to be humbled. The first three levels are straight sprints to the finish. The fourth introduces new foes and a more vertical, labrythine level structure.Do not play Post Void of you get motion sickness from 3D environments. Do not play Post Void if you are prone to seizures. If you experience neither, buy it immediately. This is a game whose ideas are only 5-10% original. This may not seem like much, but it is massive in terms of the oversaturation of generic shooters presently available. It takes the same basic concept of Wolfenstein 3D from 1991, placing you in a series of hallways with 2D enemy sprites, providing you a gun and tasking you with reaching an exit. Just like that title, not every enemy needs killing to win. Unlike that title, you can't stay still. The enemies are less of a threat than your own inaction.When your white liquid, head, timer, whatever you want to call it, gets low enough, you are given a 3 second countdown. Should you take damage or not kill anything by the time it runs out, you die. The trick to getting further is prioritizing headshots, at least for the first few levels. By the fourth, counterintiutively you'll want to slow down. The addition of rooms above rooms, the need to jump to reach them, a more roundabout level layout, and deadlier enemies, makes considered movements a higher priority. In particular, contact damage can kill you in seconds. Having your vision blurred by a flying drone only to jump on a ledge and be blasted by a rocket turret can be entirely avoided by backing up, killing the drones, jumping the ledge, and taking aim. Because the rounds are short, ranging from 1-8 minutes at a time, death is negligible with the desire to replay kept high. The game's visuals are not cutting edge. However, there is something entirely unique about them. The sprites for your arms and hands, the furniture and wallpaper, even the pixel artwork on the paintings dashed by amid the chaos, all add to a sense of an LCD drug-trip I have not felt since playing through Hotline Miami (bright colours, irregular shapes, warped vision, and a frantic pace). Not all of the perks are as useful as others. Regardless of what you get, the game is still challenging. When you finally get the perks you do want the satisfaction is unmatched. In terms of negatives, you probably won't be playing the game much after you beat it. Doing so took me 4 hours. The Steam Achievements are not annoying, but if you are easily discouraged you won't get far enough to earn them all (you aren't forced to be a masochist in performing a mundane task thousands of times, or to not take any damage in a playthrough or anything even remotely evil). Level 4 is the greatest gut-check in terms of difficulty. Levels 4-6 are arguably the hardest to get good at. Once I mastered those, beating the rest of the game wasn't so bad. Based on the name, you might think Post Void is about rebuilding democracy after the postal system is dismantled. While this is not the case, it offers an equally intriguing journey filled with bright colours, frantic action, and lots of headshots. When I reviewed Gato Roboto, I had a hard time recommending full price for a game with limited replayability and a short length. Post Void is similarly short and only mariginally more replayable, at least after you've beaten it once. The difference here is that the leaderboards, the smaller time-investment, and the lower base price of $3 as opposed to $5 (approximate cost in Canadian dollars) add up to a far more palletable fun to price ratio. It isn't necessarily better crafted, but it justifies full price, at least as far as I'm concerned. To the creators of Post Void: more please!

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the retro-FPS style shooters that have been coming out lately, this one definitely has a closer feeling to that of playing a rogue-like, repeating runs and improving until you actually manage to beat it.The gameplay basically comes down to: get from the start of the level to the end before the liquid from your idol (your health) drains down, killing enemies in the process to regain such liquid. To do so, you'll have a handgun, which you can switch for a uzi, a shotgun or a knife when getting upgrades, which you will get a selection of three at the end of every level.Something that I really have to appreciate is how well balanced this game is in terms of your tools and the perks you get: no matter what gun you choose, no matter what upgrade you pick at the end of a level, they're all viable options and there's none that could "hurt" your playthrough.This, in a way, is because even if the upgrades play a role in your runs, your possibilities on actually getting through the levels comes mostly from your own skill and not from getting good runs or generation, something that can happen a lot in most rogue-likes.There are two main problems tho: The first being the lack of options. I would have really liked to be able to choose whatever resolution I want or being able to play in windowed mode, maybe turn off the mouse acceleration, which, although not horrible, took a while to get a hold of...The second problem is that, for some reason, the more you play the game (in a single sitting) the slower it gets? It's not that it drops FPS, no, it literally starts slowing down for no apparent reason. At first I thought it might be something in the later levels, since that was when it started happening, but when I replayed it the problem was still there at the beginning of the new playthroughs. It doesn't ruin the fun at all, but it would be great if this could be fix so we can experience the game at it's full.TL;DR: Even if the game isn't very long (it only has 11 levels and a tutorial), it's really a lot of fun and even when you've already beaten it, you just keep coming for more, and since it has randomized level generation and upgrades, your runs will never be the same, making it really fun to play through repeatedly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sucks ass, but it's so cheap that it's worth recommending. It comes close to being great, but it ends up falling flat on it's face and just being ok.It has a pretty solid and fun gameplay loop, but the visual presentation takes a ♥♥♥♥ all over it.Let me ask you a question. Have you ever wanted to play Doom, but every time you pull the trigger, someone covers your screen with piss and ♥♥♥? Because that's how this plays. It's very fast, and puts heavy emphasis on constantly moving and hitting as many headshots as possible, since that's the fastest way to kill enemies, and, as previously mentioned, you want to keep moving. Sounds pretty straightforward, right? Yeah, that's because it is. None of the perks really change this core concept, so that's what you're coming for, and that's what you're getting.On the topic of the perks, they're actually terrible. Two thirds of them don't really do much, some of them are actually terrible (see: Shotgun). Honestly, you want faster reload, bigger clip and the uzi. You can get the other ones if you want, but they're not exactly optimal. As for the weapons other than the uzi, the knife is alright, but doesn't scale well into the later acts, and the shotgun is god-awful. In a game where you want to be constantly shooting, it has two shots and the longest reload time out of every weapon. To make up for it, it has higher damage, enough to one-shot every enemy. The problem is, even with that increased damage, it still loses to the starter pistol in raw dps, because hitting headshots also kills things instantly.The story was pretty vague, to the point that I'm convinced it's actually intentionally meaningless. I have nothing to say about it, because if it has anything to say, I didn't get it. The post-void is as empty and meaningless as the old void, it seems.To conclude, I'll put my main argument nice and short:It has pretty fun gameplay for the price tag, I wish I could have seen it.

_childDocuments_.review: I should like this game a lot more considering how pick up and play it is but I find the art to be garish, yet boring at the same time, I don't like the colors and how bright everything seems. walls and other still scenes are all animated with a few frames, so everything is wiggling and dripping. this might be cool if the attempted pixel look didn't turn into a miserable scaled artifact at any sort of distance. you will never not be holding the same exact thing forever in your left hand, while it's "neat" it serves no purpose beyond informing you how close you are until  a 3 second timer fills the center of the screen. I know this game is pretty anti-hud despite informing several things in a hud area briefly, a subtle hud timer would go a long way but this game lives and dies by its gimmick and style. the health system never feels like you have much control over the timing and risk. you could be half a second away from the timer starting and really have no idea so you make a split second decision to take some damage the moment after this next timer already started and you are dead.feels like a demo with the variety of potential powerups you get to choose from between each level, surrendering all future runs to the people that just dig the simplicity and I get that. I believe there are more than enough weapons, I would just like to do a lot more things with them via choices made instead of seeing "reload faster" every other run and other ultra basic, non-brainstormed or hyper-refined current implementations, I really can't tell the philosophy on display herethe other sin this game commits is introducing verticality, it falls absolutely flat here when the entire stage rushes right underneath you in a 2d setting where you cant look down all the way and are forced into a near endless series of faith jumps into hordes of enemies, clearly I am playing wrong but going fast, going slow, doesn't seem to change a whole lot in this regard. when I say verticality I mean minecraft block style up and down, we don't get gradual slopes or a series of quarter height steps to walk or jump up. just completely blind faith death pits. which to the games credit, these levels are generated on the fly so its the one part of this game that really has any legs.I would call it appropriately priced but go check out blood and bacon or something or the wealth of free games we have at this point in time, 50x-100x more impressive and interesting. it's not the same thing but theres so much more there on a way better engine with so many more agreeable decisions made, referring to blood and bacon.I could see this game getting better but I don't think the game engine or vision will ultimately allow for thatlives with jet set radio in the style over substance category

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void has some pretty interesting graphics, intentionally jarring visuals, and almost frustrating visual engagement. Every aspect of the game is designed to push you forward in a race against time. Monsters will get in your face and dare to backpedal and risk wasting time, shooters will flank you from every angle and tempt you to try and pick off every one of them, hands with flash bangs attached to their stump will ambush and blind you, sending you walking in the wrong direction as you stagger through the temporary blindness. The levels are void of any real intricacy, and are instead sprawling mazes of the same asset over and over, as you aren't meant to enjoy the scenery, but rush like hell to reach your goal. The game makes it very clear you here for one purpose alone, and that is to reach the end of the level. Post Void doesn't force you to slow down, there isn't any ham fisted story, not even a cliched minimalist one. It drops you in a level with an enemy in your face, and prods you to the end of it, and the result is a fast paced, fun, addictive, and highly rewarded. Post Void plays like a 3D Hotline Miami, and costs as much as it's development as well. TLDR; good game, would play

_childDocuments_.review: It looks and plays as if Hotline Miami injected pure Acid into your veins to shout at you with a Teletubby voice and your momma kicking you in the nuts while your neighbour smashes Cashews into your nose.They better call it Post Mortem with how i feel after only playing it for 5 minutes.Also i think my brain is severely damaged as im unable to see any colours after just looking at the screenshots.The game features one mode, 11 levels, after that your highscore is counted. If you make it this far.After every level, which takes about 2 dozen seconds if you are as bad as me, you get to choose an upgrade.There arent many upgrades, roughly like 6 or 7 only.Besides those you can also pick a weapon instead and replace your old one with it.Choices also limited here, with only 4 weapons.Levels become more and more complicated and loaded with more enemies.Main goal is to go fast, thats it. Shooting and killing is only there to fill your liquid, which acts as a timer and health. If it runs out, you are done.The principle is simple but the idea behind having a timer that acts as your health is quite intruiging.The appearance of the game is...i mean see the first sentence for that.It doesnt look good ofcourse, its stylized artsy trash.But thats ok, it serves the purpose.Honestly, i feel a bit like the artistic skill is a bit wasted. Not meant in a negative way, but i feel like YCJY Games could craft an astonishingly great retro inspired FPS like a new Heretic, Doom or whatever with more depth and complexity.Because of that, i hope their next game will be a more fleshed out game but following the general idea of post void, especially with the Idol idea.Its only 2.50€ for some good short fun. Def. worth it if you are ok with the appearance and speedrunning.If not, no shame to avoid it.I would also give a shoutout to Devil Daggers, as i felt a lot of similar vibes with what the game aims for, a short but tough, highly stylized shooting experience for a small pocket. If post void isnt for you because of its look, maybe hop over to Devil Daggers if you dont know it and give that game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good don't get me wrong. But it lacks of replay value. Once you see the pattern laying in front of you, you kinda get the whole idea and lose interest in moving on in the game.I didn't quite understand the point of the slide button since there is corners everywhere in the leveldesign, and you are stuck by enemies. Mobile move sets are perfect for vertical maps or big rooms, but this game is all about corridors. So why ?Eventually you figure speed isn't really needed. And if not for the unavoidable enemies waiting at corners, you just have to dodge projectiles and aim calmly. Playing this way get you a solid 4 seconds reserve at all time, you hardly get hit, and the levels are suddenly a walk in the park. The only difficulty it manages to introduce is increasing the damage sources by area (3 drones, then 2 guys in next room etc).I didn't reach the end of the game, but the formula was obvious.The crosshair is also lost in the pixels mess of this game. I'd probly enjoy it a tad more if I knew where am aiming.Then there are no difficulty selection. Which makes this game highly refundable if not in the right hands.Which brings me to this final point :It describes itself being about speed, but not about time. Which is different. When purchasing it I didn't expect to be pressured by a clock. I'd sincerely put this bad review on my shoulders only, but post void's marketing fooled me. I mistook this as some singleplayer roguelike arena shooter with various drug effect translated on screen at each chapter. But it's a racing game. And I didn't like that.On the cool side, the visuals and soundtracks are funny as well.My review wont change the game's overall reception fortunately and am actually glad the devs got credit for it from the crowd, I just don't see myself playing it anymore than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is a 2D retro pixel story/level driven action "difficult" retro FPS that's been slapped together with the godawful GameMaker Studio video game construction kit from Yoyogames.  Yeah, not only can GameMaker Studio pollute Steam with 2D retro pixel shovelware, it can make 3D DooM ripoff shovelware too.  The game has a vomit inducing psychadelic theme and is part speedrunner as your health drains over time and must be recharged by killing.  What an inventive gimmick, surely PC gaming is now saved.The visuals here are massively substandard, looking like badly phoned in blend of comic/MS-paint "art" and 2D retro pixel "art" slapped onto a DooM clone engine (which this basically is). The engine is also lacklustre, the developers couldn't even manage to work out variable resolution, so your screen resolution is locked and there's no way to change that or tweak the graphics to try improve the laughably terrible visuals here. GameMaker Studio is a very poor quality game construction kit, and unsurprisingly results in products that have little to no value as games, especially when compared to the work of professional developers who create genuine products for gamers.  Just like you can't make a silk purse from a sow's ear, you can't make a good game from a completely crap game engine.  Using a video game construction kit requires little to no talent or skill as a game developer.  Very often, GameMaker Studio is used to make shovelware and lazy cash grabs. Given that you can play older, better games like DooM and Quake 1/2 completely free, and they're infinitely superior to this in terms of art, theme, game engine, visuals, and everything else, it's impossible to recommend this GameMaker Studio shovelware/game bundle worsener to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really simple concept but it is designed in a way that makes it really engaging and fun to play. The combat is basically from an fps, but its really fast paced and simple, so you don't have to focus on things such as loadouts or running out of ammo. Instead, you need to advance through corridors while focusing on your health level and shooting enemies.Its simple gameplay in addition to the psycodelic graphics and its incredibly fitting soundtrack makes it so despite being a simple game, its fun to keep playing it and slowly progress through it. The only downside to the game is its lack of content, because once you manage to beat the game the only thing left to do is improve your highscore, as you will probably have gotten all the achievements.Overall it is an excellent game as it does what it wants to do in the simplest way without any clutter or unnecessary content or mechanics. If you find it on sale or even for the full price it is totally worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing but has alot of untapped potential!So, for one, this is now my second favorite game (nothing could top #1 so this is the best it possibly could have done!)Gameplay wise, while it does require fast reactions peed and decision making I wouldn't necessarily say it's "too hard" as others have. I'd actually say that it's difficulty curve is relatively flat. It gets harder with new enemies introduced, but honestly I think some enemies were meant to be more of a hindrance than they where. Specifically the hands and helicopters that mess with your vision, now this may just be me (I've never been bothered by the squid ink powerup in mariokart for example) but stuff that messes with your screen like a flashbang or splatter never really made that much of an issue for me. I absolutely love the fast paced gameplay that simultaneously make me feel powerful and frail. I always like games where mobility is a core part. There was a little bit of slowdown near the end of the game, however, as I think others have mentioned.I'd argue that this game could also be classified as horror, but in a very specific way. It reminds me of a nightmare, and alot of Danni Antonucci stuff visually, along with overall reminding me of the game Hylics. The endless mundane hallways definitely gives me that dream vibe, plus, if you play like I do you're being chased by half the enemies in the game by the end of the level. The aesthetics hit that perfect mixture of cool and unsettling to fit the vibe the game is going for (dudes with giant mouths for heads, and cool white suits is badass, but the dinosaurs with floppy titties is offputting, but together they work)People have complained about the bright flashing colors; I for one have no issue with it as that fits my favorite aesthetics quite well, but I will say that if it does cause you strain; THAT'S THEMATICALLY RELEVANT! If you payed attention in the tutorial, the main character himself is trying to do nothing more but end his own headache. The 'story', however much there can be said to have one, seems to imply that this is an endless cycle, make it to the void, grow this flower, momentary peace, and then more senseless violence. Interesting I guess, but considering the dream logic of most of this, I might be misinterpreting it. The compass upgrade I will say is basically useless. I only ever got mixed up A BIT in the big rooms near the end, and that was quickly resolved. The levels are set up in such a way that you're usually funneled in the right direction. This isn't a negative criticism, I actually enjoy that._____________________________________________As for untapped potential; this definitely feels like a "portal 1" to a potential "portal 2" as far as great game vs a masterpiece. The leader boards are a cool way of making it more of a competitive thing but I'd argue you could implement more gamemodes. My only real criticism with this game is that it's too short after all, often my high score is limited more by the length of the game than my ability to keep going (but I guess at that point I need to run past enemies less and shoot more) Anyway I'm gonna plop my ideas and suggestions for further game modes in a potential sequel here:-Weapon challenges (start with X weapon, you can only use it all the way through. The knife is objectively the worst weapon in the game so that'd be interesting)-No Upgrades challange-one-hit death (no head (In-universe the head would still be on the body) so you're not on a timer, but one hit from an enemy kills you. This would be especially hard since, at least for me, I'm taking most of the game, killing enemies to keep my health up.)-No enemies mode (Basically a giant procedural generated maze, like even more complicated than the last level, with no way to get your health back, basically on a timer. You might have the wall enemy just to make it harder to guess whwere to go, but ideally they'd give no health back)-Endless mode (And endless series of levels or a single endless level, up to you I suppose)-Multiplayer competition (Two players dropped into a level, with the same gameplay mechanics as the base game, meaning there's a limited number of enemies to get health from. whoever makes it to the end first wins)-Multiplayer vs (with the movement mechanics in this game that'd be interesting. You might run into the problem of the enemies in the game using projectiles and the players using hitscan though, as in games like this it seems sort of unfair to be hit with a hitscan weapon.)

_childDocuments_.review: not a bad game but not “good”+very fun gameplay albeit dragged down by the cons  +good soundtrack (although there’s only really ONE track…)/ Short. Can be beat in under an hour if you get a hang of things (was able to personally after less than 5 attempts). Not a lot of “content” in a sense.-Roguelike. On top of being a part of one of, it not the WORST game genre, it gets repetitive fairly quickly (after the first handful of runs or so).-Lack of any basic settings outside of volume, sens, and rebinding controls. No fov tweaks, no advanced display settings, nothing really helpful.-sens/volume settings are sliders instead of numbers, difficult to fine tune -60 FPS cap. An EXTREME issue when it comes to a rapid, twitch shooter such as this. -HORRENDOUSLY optimized when the game gets a bit busy. Dipping into the 40s is very common and even going as low as 30 FPS isn’t rare. Makes gameplay extremely annoying and hard to follow, especially with the visual style. -RNG upgrades that can straight up kill a run after just a few bad rolls IE: no gun upgrade, no ammo upgrade, no ghost-lots of flashing lights, can lead to headaches/eye sores and even epileptic attacks. -severe amount of camera sway + shake, can be dizzying and also just annoying-as levels are procedurally generated, you can have an unfair death due to long open spaces with no cover and swarms of enemies-crosshair that’s very easily lost in the visual clutter-uzi bloom/spread + recoil can be difficult to land accurate shots with especially with visual clutter4/10 – at the end of the day a fun little shooter severely bogged down by a multitude of things, with it’s saving grace being relatively addicting (for a short time) and quick to beat (so you don’t have to deal with it for long lolez). Would’ve rated neutral if I could, but despite being a somewhat fun game, it’s issues make it hard to recommend, especially with the FPS issues, lack of advanced settings, and psychedelic visual presentation that can be annoying and nauseating for some and straight up damaging for others.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 10 minutes I was like I'm getting refunded this game. You die every  10 to 15 seconds.  I'm not even joking either. In your left hand you hold a bottle which is draining fast which is you health/HP.   And the only way to live a little longer is to kill something.  And kill something fast before you die.  My problem with this game is sometimes as your just looking left to right for an enemy to kill.  And your dead only a few second in.  You need to go as fast as you can & kill stuff.  But there could be enemies behind you that you didn't see.  But you don't what to turn around because you could run out of time.  That's how fast your HP drains.  This game could be awesome.  Only if they gave you a little more time.  Or at least give us that option.  But the options menu....hmmmmmm?  Why even have an option's menu.  There's nothing you can really do in there.  It's crude as hell.  But just adding 5 seconds to your life drain would make should a HUGE difference in the gameplay.  I really don't know what the Dev's were thinking when they did this.  It's like every 10 or 15 seconds your dead.  Time to hit the restart button & try to go for 16 seconds.  I know I sound like I'm griping.  But the game is a lot of fun for a little.  And a steal for 2 bucks.  But after a few minutes this time thing gets old fast.  The game could be so much better with that simple change.  Like I said if some people like your health draining that fast.  Let them have there hardcore mode.  But for those of us that want to live a little longer & just have some fun blowing stuff up.  This could be a great little game.  I wish there was an option for that.  I just hope the devs are listening & try to make this a even better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: You can see my video review here: Think about all of the classic shooter format DOOM games. Then, mod them to ♥♥♥♥ and have them all have a struggle snuggle with Hotline Miami in an alleyway, and have the result of that come out addicted to PCP and looking somewhat like an episode of Rugrats. That’s essentially what Post Void is.On the bottom left of your screen is your idol. Think of it as a health bar. As soon as it runs out of this mysterious white liquid, you’re dead. You lose health not only through being damaged by enemies, but also by simply existing. The only way to recover health is through killing enemies. I’m sure you get the gameplay loop here. Go fast, live. Go slow, die. The game not only encourages you to use this playstyle through the ever present fear of death, but also throws mechanics like one shot headshots and sliding into the mix to not only encourage instant, mind-blowing erections but also the swift dispersal of enemies and their respective gray matter. There are eleven levels divided between three acts in Post Void, all of which are randomly generated but progressively add more and more challenge, along with new enemies. This might not seem like a lot of content, but considering the replayability of the game, that really isn’t a problem.After a while of playing Post Void, it starts to feel like the game is playing you rather than you playing it. It has that trancelike quality similar to Hotline Miami. The game is fast, brutal and addicting, and combined with the utterly asinine visuals, the game pretty much forces you to go into this state to cope with the sheer amount of pixels moving rapidly on-screen.One thing to mention is that Post Void is currently on sale for the low low price of 2.88 canadian bolivars, or approximately 1.2 million Runescape gold as of the time of this writing. Not that the original price point was really that massive, but seriously, give this game a go. You won’t regret it.Overall, I give this game a 10/10. It’s simple, fun, has a ridiculously low price point and a unique artstyle. What is there not to love?

_childDocuments_.review: It does what it sets out to do perfectly. If you watched the trailer, you already saw how most of the gameplay is. You run through psychedelic levels, shoot enemies as fast as you can while trying not to get hit and waste any time.Your health is tied to your kills, a twist that makes the game a lot more interesting. Precise aiming at the enemy's weak spot is heavily rewarded. It's pure, distilled shooting that is *almost* perfect.The art style is great and I love the music, however the flashing effects are just way too much for any sane human to endure. Even in accessibility mode (which is the only mode I'd ever recommend you play in) it's still quite tiring for the eyes after 20m+There's sensitivity options, but no way to change the crossair color (which is a very opaque gray, for some reason), FPS is locked to 60 (pretty puzzling given the game's frantic pace) and there's only one mode and leaderboards.If you can overlook these very minor shortcomings, it's an incredibly fun and refreshing FPS that is certainly worth the low asking price.

Overall it's a nice concept and a game, but I honestly dread the time when other devs catch up and overcomplicate the simplicity that this initial formula offers.

_childDocuments_.review: In simple terms:Its a fun, (VERY) flashy, fast paced, rooty-tooty-pont-n-shooty with a similar control set to the old DOOM games if you're into that sorta thing. The whole deal is to keep movin', kill the things, get to the end, do it real fast. Do recommend, very cheap, very replayable, very stimulating. Pros:- VERY replayable imo.- Kick-ass messy art style.- SFX cues are distinct and easy to memorise without having to solely rely on visual cues.- Takes literally 2 minutes to install for my impulsive homies.- One of the few games that ran on my old ♥♥♥♥♥♥ laptop from 2015 when my PC broke.Cons:- Experienced frame drops when recording with OBS on a weaker laptop.- Only runs on fullscreen (feels better playing on smaller screens imo would be nice to have windowed).- Fairly short experience once you get the hang of playing-  Audio can get repetitive after a while because of the limited music.- Is challenging to get the hang of first and probably will be frustrating, but pays off and end up being fun if you're looking for a challenge.Replay-ability:- (Optional) Speed-run timers.- Death screen stats.- Procedurally generated levels.- Tight variety of weapons/items = offers multiple different playstyles.- Offers a bunch of leader-boards for the stages that total up into another big leader-board with your whole score.Every stage introduces something new that changes the games dynamic and once you actually beat it for the first time makes it feel super rewarding. While Post Void only really takes a couple hours at most to 100% it's one of those fast paced 'keep moving forward or the whole run falls apart' games that takes a lot of dying and retrying to get the hang of, and I dig it big time. Alongside that it's also total stimulation overload in a way that tickles my brain right. In other words if ya got a touch of the tism and all the other games are feeling desaturated n slow, try giving this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: BUY POST VOID - It's ridiculously under priced. There's no excuse not to.This is an utterly amazing FPS and an amazing demonstration of a studio knowing how to work to scope and nail the game they're making. Post Void's FEEL is immaculate. Movement feels great. Headshots feel great. Life = Time. They are one and the same. Time ticks down one second at a time, however if you take damage, you lose a chunk of seconds. You pause(or reduce - there's a lot going on) the loss of time & life by powersliding along the ground. You gain life by killing enemies. Headshots are king. This is a corridor shooter, you need to get from one end of the level to the other. Levels are typically less than a minute long. Post Void is also a Rogue-like. There are 11 levels. If you die, you go right back to the start. At the end of each level, you get to chose a randomised upgrade. Speaking of randomisation, the level layouts are randomised each run, keeping the game interesting and fun to play even after your 20th death in the space of 30 seconds. Did I mention that restarting your run is instant? Everything about this game is designed to be fast. Love the art direction too, although that's very much down to personal preference. The music is pretty damn good too.BUY THIS GAME

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void has been one of my favourite games this yearIt was a random game I stumbled upon when browsing the newly released section and I was instantly hooked by its unique and psychedelic art style. As soon as I started playing I fell in love with the motion and art style.The way you have to reach the end of the level before the idol runs out of liquid or the liquid is forced out of it from the enemies shooting you adds a sense of urgency to the game play and with an intense song playing in your ears as you dart through brightly light corridors facing all sorts of enemies really makes this a special game. The rogue-like aspects of the game make the different playthroughs enjoyable. With each death making me want to try again just to get that little bit further. The game is hard due to its fast paced game play and may even be difficult for some to follow or enjoy. It also lacks proper replay ability, with the three acts of the game and the prologue being 12 levels in total. Despite this however, I still enjoyed the game a lot while I was working towards completing it.For those who decide to pick up this game, you will not be disappointed, it is one of a kind made by developers who had a vision and saw it through.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is a really short shooter, took me 45 minutes or so to finish. Mostly to understand the gunplay as a single playthrough is probably 10 minutes.  It’s a fast paced, roguelike, retro fps with an action-packed main theme that kept me really engaged. The gameplay is based around an Idol in your left hand, which slowly drips a fluid that will end your game if you run out of it. Damage reduces it, kills refill it partially.You can choose between 3 random upgrades after each level which you have 11 of them. The upgrades aren’t that interesting, basically either a different weapon, a stat upgrade like more idol fluid or reload speed and an effect which the game doesn’t have that many like exploding enemies or ricocheting bullets. There are 4 weapons, starting pistol, knife, double barrel shotgun and a smg which I used the latter mostly.It’s a real interesting concept due to the visual bastardization of the retro fps look. Everything is trippy, bright and violence is everywhere. Enemy design is crude, as are your leathery, solely skin and bones featured hands.Gunplay is fun, I really like the feedback enemies and your gun gives you as the recoil is heavy, so is the impact of the bullets you shoot.The game kinda says it has a story, but it doesnt. Its a real weird mix between offering substance but actually realizing it has none, or trying to intepretate the few snippets of text the game offers you, including those in the trading cards, to somehow picture lore in this game.It’s a short game concept that I take anytime over a long-fetched roguelike that takes me 50++ hours to complete. Although the rather limited abilities and it having basically only a single (although fantastic) theme song and not that much variety in the map design it feels like a demo or concept for a much greater game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something else. The art style is probably just about the most unique I’ve ever seen in a video game. It honestly is the main draw of the game.  Everything else is there to support it and continue the chaotic theming and mood. The gameplay is solid. It’s fast, frantic, challenging, and a boost of adrenaline. There is a constant threat of running out of time, and the only way to gain time back is to kill enemies. It encourages fast and risky gameplay, a perfect match for the insane looking visuals. When killed, enemies explode into bright flashes of pink blood and colorful explosions, simultaneously painting the walls with dripping blood. Lights flash around the screen when bullets are shot. The walls’ sprites are constantly shifting and vibrating. Enemies look mangled and otherworldly, they move around in animalistic and unnerving ways. The rooms feel as if they are moving around while the player is fighting through them, enhancing the sense of urgency and panic that this game establishes so well. The music blares in your headphones, the sharp sounds of electric guitars and drums shoot into your ears and heighten tension, the sound of gunshots push through the soundscape to accompany the violence that’s happening on screen, you can hear blood and guts splash onto the walls. The soundtrack and sounds of the game act in perfect synchronization with the completely out there art style. It's a constant attack on the players senses, and it's something that is impossible to forget, and that's what is at the core of Post Void's style as a game is its unpredictability and weirdness. It is such an intriguing and confusing game, it's one that begs the player to pick apart every stylistic choice it makes, to try and find symbolism hidden beneath its surface. The roguelike mechanics are there, but are very simple compared to contemporaries like hades, dead cells, and risk of rain 2. You start, get an item every time you finish a level, the run ends, start again. Runs can be completed within 10 minutes, seeing as there is a time limit, they have to be done quick. The upgrades that can be obtained usually add stat boosts to certain actions, not really that interesting but it gets the job done. Although some are borderline useless compared to the good ones, which limits the item pool to an extent, and there isn’t that many of them to begin with. New weapons can also be obtained and they change up the gameplay quite a bit. They all sound different, look very different, and play extremely different. They are all fun to use, except for the only melee weapon, a knife. Which is completely useless against enemies that surround you or only attack from a distance. It’s really hard to focus on anything other than the incredible aesthetic that post void manages to establish. It is a fun, brisk, and surreal game that just nails everything that it needs to. Seeing as it has pretty fun gameplay, one of the best art styles in all of video games, and is really cheap, I think this is a game that is very much worth experiencing, cause damn, it’s one hell of an experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "Post Void," a game that seems utterly nonsensical at first, much like Megatron's leadership! Initially, I thought this was the dumbest game—dying in mere seconds, over and over again. The frustration was palpable, and I couldn't fathom why the reviews were so overwhelmingly positive. But something compelled me to return, perhaps a masochistic desire to conquer this madness.As I delved deeper, it became clear: the key to survival is relentless, lightning-fast killing. You must KILL AS FAST AS POSSIBLE to stay alive. It's literally a forced speed run, a mental challenge that pushes your reflexes and decision-making to the limit. The adrenaline rush is akin to dodging Autobot attacks mid-flight, and I kind of love it."Post Void" is a chaotic, frenetic experience that rewards those who embrace its insanity. The constant need for speed, the ever-draining health idol, and the surreal visuals combine to create a game that is as addictive as it is challenging. If you thrive on high-octane action and can handle the pressure, this game is a must-play.Starscream's verdict: 9/10. Embrace the chaos, or be consumed by it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game sums up how it feels to live in our day to day "post void" society. There's always a hurry to get somewhere, the brain is constantly under stimulus and pressure due to stress, overwork and all other sorts of little annoyances. The game simulates this with its high speed combat, colorful visuals and with a brain worm inducing music. The game is one hell of a dopamine trip. I especially enjoy the simple yet addicting combat. The game forces you to be constantly on the move, with its mechanic of constantly depleting health, which can be regained by killing enemies. The artstyle compliments the action very well, giving satisfying enemy death animations and easily distinguishable enemy siluets. Sound also plays an important role of recognizing the threat before it gets to you. The best example that comes to mind is the fast and deadly melee enemy "flamingo" which can be easily heard due to its loud thumping sound once it starts its attack towards you. Overall Post Void is a very fun, high tempo and addicting arcade shooter, which I give the personal score of 9/10.

It's hard to say that the rest of the game is anything near polished, I suspect some elements may even be intended to inconvenience the player to purpose, but it's good enough for a $3 experience that's meant to be beaten in a couple of hours (or 5 if you are garbage at video games like me). _childDocuments_.review: Post Void is a franticly fast paced shooter, where you have to keep pushing forward or you die.My only gripe with this game: there is no multiple resolution support. The game renders in a fixed resolution and stretches to your screen. in 1440P at full screen the game looks horrible and is physically an eyesore. It was unplayable in full-screen mode for me. Thankfully with trusty alt+enter it can be windowed and resized slightly bigger and from there it mostly plays without issues, except the mouse cursor will leave the game window after most rounds.The gameplay pacing in this is fast. Much faster than the videos and gifs on the steam store show, in fact. You'll be rushing forward constantly blasting at enemies that you can barely register were there in the first place because you're so focused on trying to keep moving forward without getting cornered and killed.There is a fixed amount of levels you have to go through in a single life. Each level is generated fresh each time but has certain rules to them like new enemy types and such. In between each level your health refills and you can choose from 1 of 3 upgrades, some of which aren't as useful as others and could probably benefit from a better balancing pass.The movement and shooting feels great here, all the enemies have clear weaknesses and the player is rewarded for exploiting them efficiently. Mostly this game boils down to managing the timing of all actions. When to do a movement slide boost, when to reload and aiming and shooting all at the same time.All in all I'd say for people that like high skill ceiling shooters this would be worthy of a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasent little surprise this was!Post Void is a relentless, fast-paced retro-style shooter. While it only consists of 11 short and somewhat random-generated levels, it will be a hard and unforgiving way until you get to the end. Plus: You die, you start over. Roguelike principle. However after beating each level you get to choose one out of three random-picked weapons or power-ups (and some of them stack), which doesn't just add an element of "luck" but also allows for slightly experimenting with different playstyles and combinations.To me, the clear highlight of Post Void is definitely its psychedelic visuals and style, combined with the gameplay's pace and flow it makes for an awesome and satisfying but also "keep-you-on-the-edge" feeling. Some other review mentioned David Cronenberg and I myself had to think about his work the entire time while playing. The character design, body-horror elements and overall atmosphere just seem like somewhat in line with his movies, which I, personally, absolutely adore.A learning curve is definitely there but it will also stay challenging until the end. While reinventing the wheel is something Post Void doesn't, the feeling of it is unique nevertheless and it just works so well and smooth. It doesn't have that much content, as it took me about 90 minutes until I finally beat it (and picked up all of the achievements along the way), but if you wanna play for highscores you can probably get some more playtime out of it. Even if you don't, the price of 2,50€ is more than fair for this little gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Does that make sense in the year of (our lord) Doom Eternal? It's just that good. Post Void is  bite-sized in the best ways. Not stubbornly difficult, but not *not* at all dastardly, upon dying you'll realise you haven't taken a breath for the last thirty seconds. Void's roguelike upgrades break up the experience of a void of air into literal breathable portions in a five minute run. Void is exhausting.   Halo-esque overpowered pistol syndrome is here in earnest. It's overly accurate and can be almost endlessly fired, but why not? It let me complete a run. Whilst I'm not up to a knife run-level quite yet, the other weapons remain fun to play with. Consider them artificial difficulty! It could just be new PC magic, but dispatching foes with headshots whilst aiming backwards during a slide is... easy? Post Void makes this frantic scramble also feel effortless when you're on top of it. I just hope that unlocked frame rate update is possible for extra slickness. Post Void is actually a game of survival. You have to navigate a fine balance between killing to replenish your ever-depleting health reserves, avoiding enemies carving away yet more, and making a jumping/sliding beeline for the exit. This pace is uniquely married to its music. Its one track dovetails perfectly, but replace it with the official unofficial soundtrack  and Post Void becomes transcendent.  Winding corridors and nonsensical rooms of unholy sensory overload and visual noise. Stylish to the extreme. That's not my scene exactly. I'm just happy to survive a run. The determining equation revealed on the forums is sufficiently deep to support an interesting scene here, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because it showed up in my recommended, was cheap, and looked pretty interesting from the trailer.  Now I'm absolutely hooked.  I almost feel guilty only spending $3 for this.  In this little package is one of the most kinetically driven, visually distinctive FPS games I've played in a long time.  If I could describe the experience of playing Post Void, I would say it is like playing the OG Doom with the speed cranked up to 11 and grotesque Ralph Steadman-esque illustrations as enemies instead of pixelated demons, all whilst blasting a punk record at full volume in the background and tripping balls on your hallucinogen of choice.  Do *not* play this game if you are really sensitive to bright lights and fast-moving images or if you are prone to epileptic seizures.  At least the game warns you of that on the store page and within the game itself.  More than Cyberpunk 2077 did (ha ha, topical humor).  Anyway, if you want a truly unique retro-but-not-really FPS experience that goes faster than a hummingbird's heartbeat this is $3 well spent.  Keep running.  Keep killing.  Keep that idol full.  Get to the POST VOID.

_childDocuments_.review: No hidden secrets about this game. the store page images and short gameplay trailer show it all. You'll know exactly how you feel about this game before the "2 hour refund" mark so its a safe purchase worth checking out.It's fast, it's twitchy, its a little unforgiving and if the visuals seem to induce a headache maybe shy away(though it's short nature might make it tolerable in small sessions)Levels are visually busy and chaotic but you'll easily find your way since theres very little wiggle room on where to go. You just push forward as you maneuver around the turns and bends of the psychedelic corridors while capping dudes and strafing and sliding under their projectiles until you reach the end and move on to the next level. After a level or two the color scheme will change along with a new enemy type to keep things interesting but the overall aesthetic remains the same.There's 4 weapons total : The starting pistol (headshot machine), Double Barrel (boomstick), SMG (spray and pray with a kick) and the Knife. They're all distinct from one another, not necessarily balanced for equal viability (the knife is just to flex) but they're all more than competent, fun to use and have their own quirks and pros/cons to make their functionality different to one-another. I'm partial to the shotgun.There's 4 enemies in total that resemble archetypes you've seen in many other games before but are used effectively here. You got the glass cannon thugs with fast projectiles that go down quickly. Melee enemies that will punish you greatly when they close the gap. Turrets that are sitting targets but will constantly fire slower projectiles until dispatched and the "manhack" looking enemies that swarm you in packs but die to a single shot (or are obliterated in groups when bunched up by a single shotgun blast). They'll slowly introduce one after another after reaching a certain point in your run to escalate the action and keep things interesting. You'll find yourself in the later half avoiding different types of attacks simultaneously while prioritizing which enemies to take out first or outright run past.If you're fine with no overarching progression system of any kind and a successful run only taking about 10-15 minutes, with the only real incentive to replay it for the raw gameplay and chasing leaderboards scores you'll have a good time.The price is right as far as i'm concerned, though if you're not one to replay something unless you're given an in-game reason to then maybe snatch it at a discount.

There is an upgrading system that lets you pick between 3 things after each level that I really like that can be either weapon based or perk based. This creates freedom to have different play styles that suit you in the game and allowing for a variety in gameplay which I really love! The visual design is very interesting as there are lots of bright neon type of colours present in the levels and every time you fire your gun the muzzle flash flashes really intensely. Furthermore, when enemies die, they usually obscure your vision in some way such as bright explosions, a water-like substance or simply blood. Audio wise, there are lots of grunting and ear-ringing type of sounds. All of these elements contribute to the chaotic and frantic atmosphere that the game conveys with the ambiguous story. I absolutely love how it just breaks the rules in order to offer a great unique experience! For me I don't really get bothered with the continuous flashing lights and bright colours that some people may feel pain with. This is not your typical FPS game, it is just something else and it is meant to give you a sense of a headache but in the most fun way possible! I gotta talk about the designs of the enemies, they are incredibly unique and easily distinguishable from one another. I love how they have a strange horrific look to them which really makes them appear as dangerous threats that can ruin your run if you're not careful enough! Each of the enemies bring a good variety to the gameplay and make it fairly challenging!There is only one soundtrack in this game and you would think it would eventually get boring but it never does and it is always a blast listening to it while going through hell and insanity. There is something cool about it that screams action, adventure and badassery and I think it also serves a purpose in making players motivated and have a sense of high bursts of energy to get to the end! Overall, this game was a blast to play and it is in my list of my favourite FPS games! Very unique and psychedelic game with a huge feeling of adrenaline from the action and atmosphere that offers a varied experience! 10/10 game for sure!

Should I try to kill everyone or rush past sometimes? Am I just bad with the knife or am I just holding it wrong? _childDocuments_.review: Guess I gotta review it to say I like it, then.Post Void's a fast paced, fun, frenetic shooter that evokes the feeling of an old arcade game. It's simple on a surface level but it quickly evolves into a frenzied, complex acid trip simulator once you get the hang of it. Every weapon is satisfying, every headshot is impactful, every enemy looks like a piece of abstract artwork and every run is a good run, whether you finish all eleven stages or not.I'll be honest, I'm biased here because Post Void's become one of my favorite video games in general, more than just a favorite FPS or an interesting title, but legitimately one of my favorite games ever, because it's simple, it's violent, it's fast, and it brings me happiness to mow down hordes of telehands and crying eyes. The best part is that it's all three bucks, and it's cheaper if it goes on sale. I don't regret my purchase at all, as a matter of fact, no game I've purchased since Post Void has hit me the same way.TL;DR, Perfect game for listening to loud music to while you blow off steam and blow off the heads of your enemies. I'd highly recommend it if you like old school FPS titles, weird graphics, and breakneck arcade action.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable experience, I played it through to the end a few times with different weapons and each one was riveting. This game grabs you by the throat and doesn't let you go for the hour or two that you play, with only the time between levels giving you the slightest bit of respite. There you can choose abilities to go into the next stage with, wouldn't be a rougelike without it, but these upgrades seem very unbalanced with a few major ones being helpful and others doing basically nothing (backwards run speed increase and compass to be specific). This isn't the main draw of the game though...Really it's the running and gunning that makes this game so fun, and you should be running. The game incentivizes sliding and jumping as fast as possible, killing as much as you can so the skull in your hand doesn't run dry. Once you do, you have three seconds to kill an enemy before you're dead. The most satisfying part of this is how quickly enemies can go down if you play right, proper aiming at a weak spot can take down enemies with everything from the shotgun to the uzi in one tap. Naturally, this would bring challenges for anyone who doesn't play fast paced/twitchy shooters, but as someone who does I can really appreciate the pure and distilled high octane action this game provides. Not to mention the satisfying sound of getting a headshot and the pounding music urging you to take out just one more.The story is simple but minimalist and intriguing, the opening definitely sparked some curiosity from me to go look more into the game online. The art, too, is grotesque despite its simplicity, which is again pretty stunning considering the limitations of the pixel art style. This game looks like it was made in 2D (like the original DOOM and Wolfenstein) and honestly I wouldn't doubt if it was. It looks and feels amazing to play, and the controls feel spot-on even without fiddling with the settings.A word on accessibility though, this game simply isn't. If you're looking for a new indie to play as someone with epilepsy or motor coordination impairment, this isn't the one. It is headache inducing (that not necessarily being a bad thing), which is funny considering the story itself is about easing a headache. The developer has provided a nice FOV sliders and settings to make the experience as accessible as possible, which is a great step considering the difficult nature of this game. Normalizing this is important and I applaud the developer for taking this step even though they didn't have to.

name: VR Skater
detailed_description: VR Skater is designed from the ground up for VR to give you the most authentic, challenging, and immersive skating game ever. Picture the board under your feet, the rolling, clicking sound of rubber wheels against the tiled pavement before you pop that perfect ollie. Feel like you are really skating, with the most innovative input mechanics allowing you the board control you’ve always dreamed of. Moving your hands in the same motions you would follow with your feet gives a perspective and level of control never before seen and the sense of fulfilment experienced upon perfectly executing even the most basic tricks is something that never leaves you! To help you master the art of street skateboarding, you’ll will be guided through flip tricks, grab tricks, grinds, slides and manuals enabling you to conquer each of these skills to carve out skating lines and combos during game runs. All of which each helps you rack up those points for that all time high score run! You will skate across 7 stunning urban environments as well as the Mega Ramp. Test your mettle by launching yourself across the chasm. A truly amazing experience in VR. Enjoy XP, medals, trophies, leaderboards and the VR Skater shop, where you can exchange your hard earned XP and swap out your grip tape, trucks, wheels and of course, that all important board artwork!

_childDocuments_.review: After a few years of patience, there is now finally a worthy skater game for virtual reality.It feels fantastic, it plays very well and there are many tricks you can practice,VR Skater brings the promise of long-term fun with a very skater-friendly level design.Despite the fact that you will not have to use foot trackers to skate in this game, you will still have a convincing experience that almost makes you believe that you are on a skateboard.In the beginning of the game you will have to choose between a regular or goofy position and this body position is a striking detail in this VR skating experience.After determining your position you will very easily learn the basic movements of the game following with a step based tutorial where you'll learn all the different tricks step by step + you'll also be able to do each trick via an ollie, nollie AND also front & backside.Learning how to skate in VR Skater is fairly straightforward but certain tricks may need a little extra effort and attention,but once you get past that you'll be glad you know how to do them.After passing each part of the tutorial you can do a challenge for each part of the tutorial to make sure you can seperate the tricks from each other.VR Skater is currently not only unique in its genre but also pretty addictive,you will feel the urge to do your route or combos perfectly without any mistakes,this also requires a lot of practice, along with the countless mistakes & crashes.That is why, in addition to the tutorial, we can also choose a practice mode in the levels.During this mode you will be able to fall endlessly without harm, all for that perfect trick.The other mode you can choose in a level is a run, where you have a small limited number of bails that you can have in a single run in order to be able to finish the level.As you play for hours, your gameplay will also improve and you will experience less or no more bails and then you can also do longer or more difficult combos that also provide a lot of extra points.These points will, in addition to proving your skills for an online leaderboard, could possibly also be part of future required challenges in the levels of the game.You can make higher scores by doing longer and complicated combo's and also by jumping over an obstacle.It will take you a while to get out of the habit of repeating the tricks that don't make you fall but you will get higher and higher scores if you do as many different tricks as possible so it is important to memorize the required moves.Although the use of the feet is not required to skate in vr skater, this will hardly be noticeable in the gameplay, the game requires a lot of concentration to master everything and it certainly does not feel like some kind of fingerboard vr experience at all.Once you know your way around the game you will soon forget that you don't have to jump in your room to do an ollie.It's great, and the skater vibe is undoubtedly there. The game will only improve and I am very excited about the next updates.Speaking of updates, the dev team are very ambitious to expand the content of the game, when you take a look in the details on the store page on steam then you'll notice a list of upcoming promising content for the game.Early Access review:
