_childDocuments_.review: VR Skater is a gem, balancing nostalgia with cutting edge technology. Not everyone is or was a skater back in the day, not everyone has played irrecoverable hours in various Tony Hawk console games. A front side nose slide may be indistinguishable from a backside tail slide to you. None of that matters. If none of anything you just read chimes, you can and will still derive huge enjoyment from this game. This VR experience matches accessibility with challenge. There's an "easy to pick up hard to master" vibe. Such challenge may not be for everyone in the long-term, but it has me hooked here and now. Graphics are good. The scenery whizzes by to give that sensation of speed. The textures are high quality, and timing performance at 120fps on Valve Index is solid on Ampere. If you have the performance headroom there's a windowed mode especially for demos, live streamers and youtube recording. Sound design is great. Music is great. None of it has been muted on Twitch so far in my experience. And it can be turned off in-game, if you want your own tunes to accompany you.The feeling of street skating has been captured very well. Surprising then to learn that it only uses your hands, and wee bit of head tracking, to perform tricks otherwise unreachable to most of us in IRL. I was skater in my time, and loved it. The developer team has tried, tested and ruled out many other options for controls to get to where it is now, and it works.The environment doesn't give up its secrets easily. You can be creative. Looking for unusual lines, just because. It feels like real skating. You can practice again, and again. And when you're ready, go for new records.The study of IRL skating by the devs is evident, the hand motions required to make the board jump, spin and flip are as your feet would be required to move. I played on Vive controllers for each session (heed the warning on the store page about incompatible Windows Mixed Reality, HP Reverb G2 and VIVE Cosmos Controllers) . The mappings are great. It all flows so well to perform complex combos, once you get your head wrapped around where your thumbs and arms should move to.The tutorial is excellent at walking through the moves. And gives you some fun boxes, rails, and small ramps (no half-pipes or quarter pipes in the game).  There is much to commend the learning process that underpins the tutorials. I still go back to them even now. Even just to muck around in the warehouse.One of the negatives that might be perceived early on, is that you cannot free roam. The decision was taken to offer either a linear path (in a recorded run), or the ability to "hop" backwards to checkpoints in a practice run. Either way there is a linear feel to the level. That's not bad thing. I spent days skating at the same spots IRL in my home town. It brings back that feeling of sessioning a particular gap, rail, stairs, slab, wall or whatever part of the street you had until you got what you wanted from it (or janitor/security moved you on). If you like skating, VR and/or skill based VR games, then this is the one to pick up. It's kept me going for 28 hours, and it will easily keep me going for a lot more on top of that.  You fall off. You get back up again, quickly. No messing about. Adjust your posture, mentally rehearse the trick, eye up your path.... breath... relax and go again.   You'll get it this time. Just. One. More. Run.The game is still in early access. The developers have a clear idea of what to add. Including leader boards. Meanwhile, know that my best combo is a bit over 60k at time of writing. As a pro VR Skater said to me, manuals and nose manuals are the key! I'm sure it'll not be long until you beat it.  I hope the community will be generous in sharing footage from their runs. Just like the old days, when the stars of VR Skater rise, and VHS videos are delivered taped to the latest skate magazine... it will inspire others to follow, to learn, and to improve. But never be discouraged. As long as your next run is better than your last, you're doing it right!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an empty shell at the moment, a tutorial and one level that's like a minute long if you don't fall. there is no sandbox here, you go from one end to the other and that's it and that is after you master all the moves in the tutorial which is super frustrating. It also needs a quick turn physic and not just going in one direction all the time but it seems they are going for start to finish course which is cheap in my opinion, also the physics are very annoying, maybe some head gestures for moving left and right instead of having to hold the right controller and turn while trying to peddle with the left controller, maybe even an option to use the sticks to turn. _childDocuments_.review: I've clearly not put much time into the game yet, but in my short time so far the gameplay already feels incredibly refined. The developers have essentially nailed the feeling of skateboarding within VR using only your arms, and within 5 minutes of the tutorials it clicks and feels totally natural.I just did around 10 runs of the School level in practice and it's exhilarating to make split second decisions on direction and tricks. I do find myself leaning down to ollie, even though I haven't skateboarded in at least 10 years - that alone tells you how immersive the game feels and plays.The early access version comes with one level (as well as many tutorials to learn tricks), and it's designed in a linear way, however you can pick your lines and string together tricks. As another reviewer mentions, you can't simply turn around and head back to try again when you bail, but in practice mode you can hit down on the left analogue stick to go back by a checkpoint. Besides, the School level is designed to be a run from start to end with plenty of staircases, windows(!) and more.This approach is fun, but does make me wonder how many levels will need to be churned out to provide enough content for these kind of linear style levels.All of the game play systems feel in place for free-roam (you can change direction easily whilst stationary), so it would be great to see a flat skatepark style level with boxes, rails and ramps, maybe even using the warehouse from the tutorials. That alone would add many hours of gameplay for me.There's already so much promise in this game I have a lot of faith the developers will achieve their vision for VR skateboarding. Definite recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my gameplay & impressions here: This is the best skateboarding game in VR, bar none. It has no competition. However, it is not perfect and I did experience some bugs. Nothing game-breaking though and the game is very enjoyable even as is right now. I had a blast playing it and this is one of the best success stories of a VR Early Access Game.I bought this game back in 2021 and I'm very happy with my purchase and early support for the developers. This is how EA should work, but we all know it seldom works this way. The tricks are easy to learn as far as the basics, but it is quite the challenge to master them. I played this game for about 5 hours straight and I did not want to stop playing (my arm is hurting from all the swings though).I do want to talk about the negatives though. There's a bug in the freaking tutorial where the game asks you to pause, and then if you hit continue, it asks you again to repeat this task. You actually have to push up twice on your joystick. The game also stutters heavily at the start of each map. Not a big deal if you just wait a few seconds. Lastly, it is possible to land in an area and be totally stuck. There is a way to unstuck yourself (grab the board and teleport out), but unfortunately, that has caused my board to spin sometimes uncontrollably and for me not to be able to finish the map. Game is running on the Unreal Engine 5. On my RTX 3080, on high graphical settings, I was getting mostly 72 fps on my Q3 (default). I was able to play comfortably seated. Game looks beautiful. Soundtrack is fire. Gameplay is a lot of fun. I do wish the game had Steam workshop support as I'm sure fans of this game would love to be able to create their own maps & challenges. Multiplayer would be awesome as well. Maybe a replay system & a way to easily share your best tricks (video - which would be genius marketing for this game).
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has skated all his life I was looking forward to trying this game. Let me clarify first of all, I was not expecting a skateboarding simulation type of game but was just hoping for a fun skateboarding based experience in VR. This game has come very close but I think it just misses the mark. The game play is very much tunnel like in that you start one end and work your way down to the other. Although you can stop and go back in any direction this is slow and not intuitive, it is obviously not how the game was designed to be played. This ruins the free skating roaming experience we have all come to love in flat screen titles. Turning is slow and limited. You can't spin at all (probably for motion sickness and balance reasons) so a simple frontside kickflip is impossible. Maybe this just isn't possible in VR without major safety/sickness issues but still disappointing. being able to turn sharper would also be good.The hand controls are well thought out and work quite well. Easy to get the basics but very difficult to hit some bangers. and this is how it should be because when you nail that trick you were going for it actually takes skill and is quite satisfying. So that's a big plus for the game but for now  this early access version gets old very quick. I really enjoyed the first 30 mins but can tell I'll be over it very soon even when new levels and game modes are introduced. I think the only long term joy I would get out of this game is if I could set a marker at a spot and repeatedly try hit a particular trick on that spot, even a multiplayer game of SKATE in this manner would be fun.I can see where the devs are going with game and I'm not sure it's the right direction. It's fun because it's new and there's nothing out there like it but once the novelty wears off, The actually game play is a little one directional. I can't really recommend this game for more than $15 early access or not.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! If you have ever skateboarded in real life, played with tech decks or even just got down on some THPS you should definitely give this game a chance! There first level so far is beautifully done and has some fun lines you can run. No other skateboarding game gives you the same sense of achievement from landing tricks as this game. The controls may take some time to learn for a newbie, but if you have already put in the time learning how to skate in real life then everything feels super intuitive. The motions for a kick flip are the same for your hands as they would be for your feet in real life (close) and you almost forget it's your hands doing it. I'm always crouching down and "jumping" and leaning into turns. Turns took a sec to get used to but then I started leaning instead of pointing and it feels way more natural. (I hold my front elbow to my side) Anyway, can't wait for the devs to release some more levels and for there to be an official leader board.

_childDocuments_.review: VR Skater Has the king of VR skateboarding games arrived? Watch me break down this brand new early access VR skateboarding game and find out.Video Review here: Written Review VR Skater is the first skateboarding VR title that really scratches that itch good, and does it without over complicating stuff and ruining the experience in the process. The current early access build is limited to only one level so far and only 1/3rd of the music library (you can stop the music listen to anything you want through a separate program too).VR Skater uses a control scheme involving waving your arms in different ways to do the tricks. The motions your doing feel satisfying and aren't overly difficult to pull off. For grinds, and manuals your using a combination of face buttons  (axby on oculus) to do these things and admittedly when it comes to the manuals or more complex grinds like nose grinds it honestly will take time to get used but is all the more satisfying when mastered. Your movement is done by holding the left hand trigger down and and pointing in a direction, if your not moving you can basically turn in the spot with this but during movement it just shifts your weight in that direction so you might struggle a little to get used to how it works but you will master it very quickly.Visually the one level looks great in the headset with high quality textures. It also has a lot of great options for the second screen viewpoint if your playing the game with friends or creating content by allowing you to increase the fov. Audio wise the songs included sound great and like they were right out of a tony hawk game. And when it came to the sound effects, honestly everything was top notch and I have no complaints. To conclude I think VR Skater in its current state even with only 1 stage is worth getting. Its been in development for years you can see the early stages on the developers YouTube page. I have played tons of skateboarding games in the past and I completely agree that this doesn't have a lot of content and doesn't have any vert tricks. But if you really look at what's available for VR boarding experiences for me this is way more fun and works way better then any of those. I think it won't take long to start seeing more of the stages released and even as one stage its going to take you a lot of time to master it and I never felt bored of it when I played. I consider VR Skater the current king of VR boarding games and most definitely recommend it for those into that kind of experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Skater In Me Is RebornVR Skater is one of the best skateboarding games out hands down. This is a very immersive VR game, you will feel the ground under your board and move your body to moves. The world will suck you in.The game is a mix between arcade and simulation game play, little heaver on the sim side. The game is said to be easy to learn and hard to master. This is true the controls feel very natural and smooth. You will learn the basics in no time. Then there is the long list of tricks you can learn. These will take some time and practice to pull off flawlessly, just like in really life. Unlike other skateboarding games, where you just mash some buttons and skate like a pro. You will have to work on your skills to be a pro, which feel s really rewarding when you pull of a new trick.As someone how use to skateboard a lot back in the 90s, this game re-sparked the skater in me. It felt like being back on the board again. From the amazing controls to different sounds of the ground as I skate over them, the world is just very immersive. You will find yourself ducking down to do an ollie, or wanting to push with your leg time to time. The game just draws you in that much.With 4 fully designed and different maps and 2 Tutorial Maps, which includes an inside skate park, you will have plenty to skate on and explore. The road map also says we can expect more stages to come. The game is also packing a rocking sound track to skate to, or turn it off to add to the simulation of skating.This is by far one of the best skater games I have played, and one of the top immersive VR games I have played. The two mixed together makes for a must have VR title.Watch my preview here,

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I had a lot of fun with this game when it was in early access. As soon as the final release hit, the game just is just completely unplayable (at least for me.) The game ran perfectly with no issues whatsoever during the early access period. Now it runs about 2 frames per second and each action is delayed by at least one full second. Setting it to the lowest possible graphic settings didn't make a difference (in either the performance or the graphics, from what I could tell.)Early Access review:This is really impressive so far. My only complaint is that I wish the placement of your head in relation to the board would effect the gameplay much, much more. I think that if the game would make head positioning play a more central role, the game would feel much less dizzying and disorienting. It feels weird when leaning has no effect on your balance or position.At the very least, I think you should be able to turn by leaning your head. i.e. turn by moving your head frontside or backside relative to where the board is. That would allow the player to lean to turn in a way that would simulate real skateboarding more accurately. Some more advanced features could take head-positioning into account as well. It would be really cool if you had to adjust which way you lean to maintain balance on grinds and slides. That would make me feel much more like I am grinding a rail than simply having the board stay glued to the rail.It is really cool as is, but I think allowing for leaning with your head would make it much better.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible start to Early Access!TL:DR Pros/Cons list at the bottom of the review.This review will be subject to change as the product evolves and more content is added, but I wanted to share my initial thoughts on what's available right now. (Playing with Quest 2 via the official Oculus Link cable)VRSkater is what I would consider to be the first real VR Skateboarding game on the market. It captures the feeling of being on a board and is a thrilling experience! The trick list isn't huge at the moment, but it satisfies most of the street skating tricks I enjoy. On top of that the tricks are actually challenging when in motion. Something I immediately loved about this game was the precision required by the player to execute things properly. You'll definitely want to play through the tutorials to get a feeling for the mechanics.DEFICIT Games have, in my opinion, nailed it with their control scheme. Almost everything you do in the game is a combination of arm swings and button pushes which I think is brilliant! The triggers are utilized for braking and turning while the joystick serves as UI level input for menu access and re-spawning further back in the level when in Practice mode, or insta-bailing if you're doing a Run. Practice is a way for you to explore the level without consequence, while Run mode will penalize you for bailing. Run leaderboards are local only at the time of writing this, but they do plan to implement online ones as well!Currently there is only one map with six more planned to be released over the course of development. It's a more linear downhill jam type of flow, but there are diverging paths with different obstacles to skate on or around. I don't see myself getting bored of the initial offering anytime soon as I still have so many great trick and line ideas I've either yet to try or haven't been able to master.Even though the game is technically speaking a more "arcade" like experience, I can easily spend a half hour trying to dial in one very specific trick, combo, or line of tricks. That's been the main source of my enjoyment. VRSkater succeeds at making you work for the perfect landing, and it feels freaking awesome when you get it just right.Graphically it's a very clean looking and immersive game. Nothing looks too low detail or out of place, and I really dig the aesthetic. On top of that the soundtrack is full of some really great songs from up and coming artists who deserve more attention! They all feel in line with what I'd expect from a skateboarding game, and I look forward to them adding even more.If I had to be critical about anything at this point, it's that there isn't an input for body rotations. So you will have to physically rotate your body while in the air if you wanted to do something like a 180 or 360 body rotation. Not impossible, but definitely more work, and I don't think it counts towards score at all. Just for looks. That said I don't know a good way to add those kinds of rotations with an input that would make sense with the existing controls. So I do hope they have their own ideas of how they could do it.Overall as a long time lover of skateboarding in general, I'd say the game is totally worth it! Especially if you've been craving a VR skating experience like I have. Updates will come, and the game will grow as time goes by. What's offered here is the foundation of a great game, which even in it's current state is going to take up so much of my time.Pros:-Spectator Camera-Solid controls that make sense-Visuals are pleasing to look at-Soundtrack is great-Addictive gameplay-Polished for being in an Alpha state-It feels like you're actually skating-Map design is well doneCons:-Content/trick-list is limited at the moment (Not a con for me as I know it'll get more)-Physically exhausting (Again, not a con for me since VR is my morning cardio)If you love skateboarding or even have the slightest interest in the sport, I highly recommended picking it up and giving it a try for yourself! :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever liked "Skate" games this is fantastic VR version. Though very bare bones right now this game really stands apart from any other typical VR game as it uses motion controllers in an innovative way that should really be applauded. You essentially mimic the movements of street skating with your upper body only.  It translates very well.The game itself is primarily a street skating course that is a downhill run that you score based on trick combos and jumping obstacles. The satisfaction of landing tricks is addictive, not too hard to complete, but hard enough to make good flawless runs rare.  As it stands right now there are three modes not including training.  Freeplay for practice, Ranked where you get a set number of "bails" before your turn expires and, Sudden Death, where you can not fall or your turn is over.  The latter two having ranked leader-boards where your tricks/combos get calculated.  The training course is a kind of warehouse skate park that is only seen in training and really should be utilized for a small indoor free-roam skate park.  Instead it's a series of runs always going from point a. to b.  It works well, but I find myself using the tutorial as a way just to practice jumps off of ramps I like.  I don't have many complaints about this game other than it is missing a free roam style skate park. Also, sometimes getting the speed right can be janky.  Getting max speed before a ramp can be troublesome as if you are not "pushing" right before the ramp you lose momentum.  It can get physically tiring and frustrating.  I'd like to see the momentum stay longer to have better control for timing big jumps/rail slides.  All in all the games pros outweigh any cons and obviously this is a work in progress. For an early access game though I've already got a nice return for my enjoyment. I have high hopes for this game.  I've already requested a feature and the Devs responded within a day saying they are already working on something like I was requesting.  The fact that the devs are still working on it and are responsive to feedback is also a huge win that can not be understated.  Buy this game and buy a copy for a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dope. Cadence , speed , sounds  are dialed in quite tightly. Motion control in hands to affect feet/ flips etc comes natural / is satisfying . I wonder if the choice to make unidirectional runs was for accessibility in vr or if the scope of project was decidedly focused on mechanics...? . AND What a fantastic start with truly innovative mechanics and great physics.  Heck the graphics/performance is good too. I highly recommend this game and look forward to expansion of tricks/ maps. Please consider powerslides right away! Great job devs -thanks it really brings me back to my peak period skating and gets me really excited about where vr is going with such sports!

_childDocuments_.review: The "Skate." of VR, complete with an even higher level of satisfaction when you finally land that insane manual-chained grind combo. The implementation definitely plays much better than it shows off in videos, I held out on this game for quite awhile because I felt like waving my hands around just wouldn't do it, but man I was wrong. It feels somewhere between playing with tech-decks, actual skateboarding, and playing with the "Skate" control scheme using analog sticks. I find myself crouching IRL before big tricks and bracing for big falls off the rails. The maps feel heavily inspired by/reminiscent of Tony Hawk maps (4 at the time of writing this) and they each distinguish themselves really well. Game modes are currently limited to practice, "run" and "sudden death". Run is effectively a high score run until you finish - either arrive at the finish lines or bail enough to break your bones (~4-6 times). Sudden death is high score but first bail ends the run. I did encounter a few janky moments, i.e. suddenly coming to a complete stop without bailing on seemingly invisible/insignificant terrain, but in my ~6 hours playing I can count the occurrences on 1 hand. On the flip side, the tricks, landing, grinding, everything feels really satisfying/smooth. When I don't land a trick, I can pinpoint immediately what I did wrong. Definitely worth the full price tag of 20$.Pros:- Satisfying, unique, and intuitive controls- Smooth, well fleshed out base mechanics- Great map design- Fitting soundtrack- Runs great- It's skateboarding! In VR! Kickflips without the bruises!Cons- Limited game modes (2-3 ish)- Limited Maps (4)Would love to see a HORSE/SKATE gamemode, some more vert-oriented maps, maybe hippie jumping?

_childDocuments_.review: BETA TEST VERSION REVIEW:I have been following this title on socials for awhile now as someone who loves skateboarding, IRL. Then my interest turned to, 'Well how are they doing a sport which mostly requires your feet to be controlled by your hands...?'. Well, they've taken a very thoughtful approach to this by considering the relatively standard arm movements that each trick uses. Combined with some interesting button combinations, presses, and releases, which feel easy to remember and comfortable under your thumb (on Quest 2/Quest controllers), you are really able to replicate the feeling of really skating! Currently the game is in BETA at time of writing this review, so what it doesn't boast in QUANTITY it more than makes up for in QUALITY. The tutorial is very well done in a progressive manner, and even gives you the option to skip and go right into the pain, if you want to try and figure things out for yourself. I recommend doing the tutorials however, as it REALLY helps you build up the muscle memory to execute the tricks with little effort. There are also still a few things that aren't implemented (and I'm awaiting confirmation on a few questions I had with the devs) yet which I think would improve the gameplay such as:- Truck tension setting (so you can adjust your turn speed to preference)- Fakie/Switch stances (may be implemented and I'm just ignorant) - Body spins (like 180s, 360s, etc) - Body IK for spectator cam would be cool (in a 3rd person environment - not for FPV)- Multiplayer/Coop support (again, may be coming and have inquired about this)TLDR; if you have ever skateboarded, liked skateboarding, wished you could skateboard and didn't or were scared to get hurt trying it, THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU! I seriously think this is a GOLD MINE waiting to be tapped for these devs, and as long as they stay true to the sport and keep coming up with innovative ways to push our industry forward, they are going to succeed hand over foot.

_childDocuments_.review: - 15minutes of gameplay!It's about time we had a new skateboarding game right? How about returning to the glory days of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater & Skate whilst simultaneously creating a brand new VR skateboarding game that feels authentic & realistic? That's exactly what the team at Deficit games have accomplished here with VR Skater, a brand new Skateboarding VR game that teaches players the basics of skateboarding in a VR environment before challenging them to pull off the cleanest runs with the highest scores. To say it feels good is a huge understatement...VR Skater feels like it's been built from the ground up with a community focus, fantastic spectator modes and options mean you can capture smooth VR gameplay with a wide FOV and create your very own edits of your best runs and trick chains. Everything that feeds into the VR Skater gameplay loop feels perfectly thought out and planned, tricks are executed by swiping and swinging touch controllers in specific ways and at differing speeds, mimicking the movement of your feet in actual skateboard maneuvers.Don't hesitate, buy this game for one of the freshest VR experiences in years!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Great skating game that shows the usefulness of Early Access again! But now, two other large maps have been added, and also, a feature I had been asking for has made it in the game in a manner of days (The leaderboard is shown at the end of a run)! This is why Early Access is great, we can shape the games we want to some extent. Also, it's still super hard to make money in PCVR for most developers, and this way, the devs can afford to work longer on their games, making them bigger and better and ultimately even approach some AA-style quality. Because the graphics and music of this game are certainly top notch at this stage already! Now we just need more, and that's what we early adopters are making possible :D

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives:-No Free Roam. You can only skate straight and turn up to around 60 degree angle.-No hardcore mode with verts and ramps. The devs think we can't handle it. We can.Positives: - The feeling of skating feels natural and realistic in VR.- Has a high learning curve with tricks that are satisfying.- Burned 350 calories in an hour.Summary: The game feels great but lacks freedom. Skating in this game is all that you can imagine what it would feel like in VR. However, where it falls short is the ability to roam and Free Skate like you would see in games like True Skate, Tony Hawk. Hopefully one day we'll get an Ultimate skateboard game with Freedom. Right now this isn't that game. Buy the game and support the devs until we get a skateboard game that we truly desire, an Ultimate Skateboard Game. Suggestions: Monetize the game by selling more maps as DLC's or in-app purchases (line maps and hardcore Free Roam 360 maps) like they do in the game True Skate. The game worth the investment.Use this Environment:
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't leave many reviews of games but even with just 1 map this game was amazing in it's mechanics. Obviously it isn't exactly like skating (not that I am any good at it) but it feels natural and it can be exhilerating. I am excited for the update today which adds more maps totally increasing replayability. If you are on the fence about getting this game. Just get it. It's worth trying out
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: 7.8/10Amazing game, and actually pretty difficult. As others have said, it DEFINITELY feels like a demo. I wish visuals weren't compromised for obvious market gain on inferior headsets. The terrain and textures just look too dumbed-down and do not help immersion at all. Also, you MUST be in the center of your room no exceptions. There are NO options to re-center outside of the absolute-center of your play-space so be prepared to move furniture to accommodate.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Brought back tons of beautiful memories from middle and high school days :') takes effort to learn tricks...but OMG it gets addictive after that :D Totally recommended.Ideas to improve:1. Add support for modding maps2. Add multiplayer support, to host a server and let others join to hang out and play....however, enable hosts to permanently ban toxic users, lately VR social experiences have been infested with those who spew all their bigotry due to lack of penalties and punishment.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man what a fun game. Im a bit sad at the little content that it has in it currently, but heck, its an early access so, you get what you get. But, if this game had a few more maps, free roam mode that wasn't just a downhill map, some custom boards, heck give us a few parts in the warehouse and give us an editor and let us make our own silly little things to kill time. If your a stickler for content id say maaaybee hold off for just a little, but, honestly, it feels great, the controls are amazing, the game looks decent, the sound track from what I have heard so far feels on par with this type of game. Really my only complaint is the content, and, again, its early access so I can't even complain about that. TLDR, if you have a spare 20$ and are a fan of skating games, id say pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to pick up, hard to master, but feels great...plays really nicely, You can tell this has been lovingly and carefully  crafted over time to really try and get the feel of skating into Vr...and i think it works. Still a way to go as there is only one level...but that's why its early access..just means more goodness to come.Takes time to really nail the trick techniques , i think a bit of text on the tutorial info graphics could be quite useful. But its fun experimenting.Overall , fantastic..its all about the way it feels and is up there with games like stride in the way you use your body as a controller. Very satisfying...another VR classic in the making one i shall be playing for a long time to come :)edit: I was being a dumbass, there are text instructions, i just wasn't looking to my left
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: It's too difficult to control the skateboard and you end up looking straight down to see the board most of the time which isn't comfortable. And above all it makes me feel so nauseous playing, the movement and jumping just do not sit well with a VR game. Although it's a cool concept, I cannot recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game but I will request a refund.The game really appealed to me because I used to skate and the controls remind me of Skate. But after just one hour into the tutorial, I can tell that some of the controls are difficult to pull off and janky. Steering moving certain directions is very difficult, therefore straight sections work much better. There's a ton of well-time inputs that have to make their way into your muscle memory, some of which required minute inputs withing a second or two. This paired with the fact that I either have the choice to look at the obstacles or at the board (to check whether the trick is actually pulled off) makes the whole experience somewhat unsatisfactory. On a real skateboard it totally makes sense to not look at your feet that much, but here you kind of have to. With time I might get better at mastering all the inputs but I'd much rather hope for an update that improves on controls and then reconsider re-buying. Like, I want to be able to pull off tricks easily. This is a skating *game*. I don't want to practice hours to pull off more than a 50-50 or 5-0 grind.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun experience with LOADS of potential. Also the controls feel pretty intuitive once you learn the basics. But it is clearly Early Access (the devs said it is, so that's fine).At the time of writing there is only one map so not a whole load of content. I spend more time in the tutorials then the actual game. Personally I am refunding the game for now but will place it on my wishlist and rebuy if they flesh out the game a bit more.The following is my feedback and personally my reasons for refunding now:- The UI could use some work. It is often not clear where the 'okay' or 'start' button is. And sometimes you are looking for a button to start while you just have to start pushing your board.- The tutorials are good but still need some work. I got stuck on the 'shove it' tutorial because the video example didn't show how to 'catch' the trick. It was after a lot of frustration that I accedently pressed the jump button again at the end that made it succeed.- You don't need to put in a tutorial for every trick variation. We get that if you can do a front slide variation of a trick you can also do a backside variation after the first few tricks. - I think the player should be placed back a bit more on failure. I often wanted to try a trick, only to fail and not being able to try again because I got placed to close at the place of failure. Which was frustrating. Also nowhere was explained you could use the tumbstick to place yourself further back.- The way falling is handled made me kind of sick. If you are new you will fall a lot and the constant black flash was a horrible experience. I think the falling itself is good and it should make you have a small scare reaction. but the actual fade to black was upsetting. Maybe just let the player eat concrete for a few seconds.For now I do not recommend buying this game for the casual gamer. I do recommend it for skate enthausiast and people who don't mind a game that needs a polish and more content.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of promise but the physics for skating is not all there yet. For example if you go halfway up a ramp and stop you wont go backwards. . One thing that was not there that needs to be in all VR games is snap turn or some kind of direction reset so i'm not facing my desk. the price is right and it could be fun but it really needs some work. It would also be nice to be able to grab the board.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This games has the foundation to be a great game. In this day in age of ea vr devs I think 20 bucks is a bit much to ask for one map, and a promise. That makes it hard for me to recommend. The bone are really tight though. No real jank to speak of. Great graphics, and I am a snob about graphics. Cool soundtrack even though its really short. I was thinking it would be cool if the dev could tap into some late 90s early 2000s local punk / ska scenes to get cheap good tunes. If you have the money and want to skate in vr, this is the only reasonable option. Its very fun  to play, I just wish there was a lot more here.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT! i mean wtf man!? the hell kinda controls are you trying to sell? come on with this CRAP make it free if you don't know what your going in game making. more than half the tricks are so picky in the buttons you have to pressthe grinding buttons are absolute garbage...you have to release the jump button in order to prep for another jump after you land a jump BUT! you must press down that same jump button before you land or you will bail....... WHAT?there is NO TURNING don't let them BS you that is not turning. oh and if you mess up even in practice mode it puts you a few feet away where you will have to either somehow turn around and go back or turn and angle yourself to try again oh but wait for literally EVERY trick you need quite a lot of speed that you just don't have the time before the spot smacks the board out from under you.f*%^ manualing it doesn't happen. FIX YOUR S&#% !!! i mean damn man its ridiculous. its not hard to realize that its not good controls. that said the flip and shove tricks are nice but give us more levels better turning and better controls and fix the jump/land button. as for manuals have it like hold down a button or something not this jump and click both jump buttons again then release then hold 1 down crap. skating is supposed to be freeing and fun. not stressful annoying and ruin the desire to play vr.UGH and please fix the movement method... that swinging oh GOD THE SWINGING! good music tho
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Works on Reverb G2.It is a challenging and satisfying VR skateboarding game, that feels great once you master the controls. However, it is still riddled with bugs and performance issues after the release update. 1 out of 7 main levels (and 3 out of 5 in DLC!) is ruined by visual glitch, framerate is low, there are some infrequent crashes and screen freezes. The game is still playable and enjoyable, though, and the devs promised to fix launch issues eventually.Controls are simple for basic actions like accelerating and jumping, but advanced tricks will take some time to practice. The game mixes motion controller gestures with well timed button presses to create not very intuitive, but expressive and responsive control scheme. It makes pulling off a particularly difficult set of jumps feel absolutely amazing. Skill ceiling is so high, it might not even exist. Even after playing for 9+ hours I am still not entirely confident in my abilities to glide/grind and chain tricks with a manual.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Heck ya dude! I highly recommend this game.  I'd wait for a sale to pick it up (currently $45 CAD + $20 DLC) as I don't think it has quite enough content to justify the price tag, but definitely a really fun gaming experience! Not to mention the devs rewarded all early access buyers with the DLC for free!
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinly wish we had a map we could explore and skate around in freely kinda like skate, instead of the linear 1 run hallwaysBut the game is quite good, tricks feel nice and satisfying to pull off, so satisfying that i kept jeapardizing my street run to pull off a perfect manual ontop of the caravan  and triple kickflipping out of it...i did it eventuallyWith some work this game could become one of the greatest VR games.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: was great in early access. The full release is weird. Nothing telling you when to calibrate, and the animation during flip tricks and grinds lag now even on lowest settings. What once felt decently fluid now feels worse. I'll update if game gets betterUPDATE: The game now prompts you to calibrate. The stuttering seems to be alleviated as well. And for all my gripes with this game it's honestly really easy to sink an hour of my time over and over again and I notice I am getting better than i was even in early access. This is also due to the new maps they included and they are a ton of fun. Skate parks of varying design allow you to practice very fun and engaging lines.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun skateboarding game, translated so well into VR! Don't get me wrong, don't expect to get sponsored in real life if you are good at the game, but it is good enough to still let you gather a good "flow" on your runs. I look forward to future updates, maybe custom maps or at least new maps from the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly addictive game. gestural controls make it very satisfying to learn and land tricks and adds a real sense of accomplishment when you get the hang of it. Only issue i can find is with the linear level design, once you play on a map for a while it starts to feel a little repetitive but there are heaps of different ways to approach the level so its not too bad. a more open world type of level or big skate park where you are able to turn full 360 degrees freely and skate around however you want would be what really seals the deal for me.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I have tons of fun messing around in this game.  The controls are great and moves are clearly explained in the tutorials.  I had a lot of hope for this game as it reminded me of Tony Hawk back when it came out, trying to keep your combo going while grinding to get the highest score.  Unfortunately, it seems that it has been abandoned as there have not been any updates for quite some time.  It would have been great to have a few more maps and boards that you can customize more.  I think this game would benefit greatly from the Mod community here on Steam, I can only image what would be added!
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game had me dead for a while, I would go all out getting up to speed and trying to nail the perfect combo, it's so much harder than you think. Not due to any failure of the devs, the controls are tight and tricks are explained really well. It's all up to your brain to keep up with what's going on and communicate that to your hands and fingers! But once you nail it, you feel such a great sense of a accomplishment because you finally nailed it. The maps are great, once you start opening your mind to how you can do things it becomes a lot more crazier. Grind a ledge here, manual over there, do a sick trick over a gap into another manual to keep your multiplayer going it's endless and I love it. Buy the game, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: So I gave it 2 chances in an hour of gameplay time. I have to say as cool as a thing this is, it runs very poorly. Half of the tricks don't want to even function properly. Also the turning is very slow. IT only has 3 mediocre levels that are all force linear like THDHJ, and is over all boring to look at. I am very disappointed of this game. I love the ambition of the way it is however I feel like the devs who made this game made it so poorly optimized and it feels rushed. If you do get this game, beware as there isn't a lot of content. A few generic skateboard designs, and 3 lousy levels. All feels like it was rushed.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: if your against fun this is not for you. easy game to play just got it today and can't put it down. its about midnight now there was still light outside when i started.... but anyways the tutorial tells you all you need to do controls works great. so just gotta say compliments to the devs they have made a wonderfull game.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This is a blast to play! Move your hands like you would your feet! Booom Heel flip!Excited to see more of the levels and where/how(if) the game progresses.Some people might find the controls take a bit to figure out but its not an arcade skateboard game! You can also only go forward, but thats ok, there are lots of lines/spots to choose from or find!If you like to play skateboading games, get it!
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is truly skateboarding in VR! You really have to master the controls to be able to get this epicness!Taking your time and getting frustrated just like in real skateboarding is a part but a good one!Practice and you will make it! Its just so satisfying to land tricks you trained hard for!Game is challenging! Graphics are great and Devs taking ideas and critics to get the game as good as possible!If you love skateboarding or want a good skateboard challenge, you should give it a try :)
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: VR Skater is a skateboarding arcade/simulator. It's set up as an arcade game like the Tony Hawk games, but the controls are more for a simulator like Skater XL. There are 4 levels at the moment: a school, down a street, industrial, and on top of a construction site. Being a huge fan of Skater XL, I really enjoyed this, but it really needs a way of placing yourself into positions. The trick system makes sense with the motions used to do each trick. And the music really slaps. And I give this a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic VR Game! I was completely enamored with this game upon first playing it. The Graphics look great and the tricks are easy enough to learn but difficult to master. The biggest downside of the game is the lack of maps and a free roam type mode. If they could slowly incorporate more aspects of the Skate series, this will easily be one of my favorite VR titles.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played it much, but man was this cool. The only reason I didn't play longer is because the room and myself got really HOT! LOL! It's got a slight learning curve on the controls, but overall I'd say it feels pretty natural (for VR) and intuitive . I can not wait to see future updates for this. I played on a Quest 2 via Airlink. Hats off to the devs for bringing us as close as we're gonna get to a Tony Hawk VR experience. This is a lot of fun! This will be a regularly played game over here. Great job, and keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: 14 year old me would have ♥♥♥♥ myself.Seriously, to me this is what VR was made for. I just paid $10 at 50% off, but would happily pay twice that even though there's not a ton of content at the moment. It is clear that the devs have put a lot of careful thought into how the fundamental game mechanics should work, and I believe they have achieved a very convincing experience because of it. This is some of the most fun I've ever had in VR. Yes, the learning curve is steep, but it makes it that much more satisfying when you pull off tricks. The tutorial is very good. Even after doing the tutorial, you will need to practice quite a bit to pull off the harder tricks. Overall, I give this a 9/10 in its current state, only for the lack of content. Can't wait to see the finished product.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing once you get the movements down, the fact that the game has a skill ceiling is what makes it so good. Pulling off a nollie 360 flip into a grind feels so good the first time you land it. This beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of skate while in early access. I would love for a mulitplayer mode and a slow motion feature. (kinda like in tony hawks project 8 where you could slowly flip the board in bulltime to make custom tricks). overall for early access its worth the money and the time put in. PS. (if we could have a plugin for music via spotify/soundcloud/apple. that would make this game 10x more replayable!)
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing skating games since Skate or die. From Thrasher, to THPS, to Skate 1-3, and Skater XL. I love VR, I love skating games, and VR Skater reminds me of the "beginning" all over again. It feels like a definitive beginning to the evolution of all the skating games I played in the past. It's young, but it has an unexpected polish. The music, sound engineering, and best of all... the controls, all leave the impression that great care was taken to respect both skating culture and give a great product out of the gate. I love difficult but fair games. This was right up my alley. I'm a big fan of doing a very specific flip trick, into a very specific grind, and hearing the satisfying sound of landing on the board at the end of a line. I would definitely recommend this game to people who have a similar opinion when it comes to skating games. If you love VR and love skating games, this is a great place to start. You won't be pressing square to kickflip, you won't be unlocking moves, but you'll start with the ability to do every trick you have the patience to learn.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how what the bad reviews are talking about. This game is absolutely a gem when it comes to sport simulations. It nailed the mechanics perfectly. There are plenty of tricks, they are explained amazingly well using visual tutorials.Gameplay and first impressions: There is plenty of content in terms of the three maps that you can play, practice or just ride for fun. This game requires lots of practicing to remember the moves, and time it right. But PRACTICE MAKES PERFECT and progressing in this game rewards you with very satisfying gameplay experience when you are able to pull up some cool moves.I was skateboarding many years ago and I loved it. This is the thing that got me as close as possible to real-life skateboarding. It takes a talented developer to make something like that and designed it well for VR.I'm sure more updated will come and the game already shaping up to be a unique VR experience on Steam that you ahve to try out if you love what you see in the videos. Trust me, it's way better than in the videos in this case and one really have to experience to get the fill of it.I'm sure you'll just enjoy riding the skateboard even without doing tricks, but the tricks is where the most fun begins. Once you get it, give it time, try a few moves, then move to the others and enjoy the ones you have mastered so far.HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - Visuals look great on ultra BTW
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.  Just can't explain how satisfying it is to hit a ramp, ollie and land on a picnic table in a nose slide.  It is so smooth.  It took a little while to get the hang of it; but now I can almost always nail boardslides and nose/tail slides.  Can't wait to see new levels.  Also they use Blender.  I wonder if they will allow us to import/build objects or levels.  Does anyone know if you can do spins?
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most satisfying games to get good at in VR that I've played in a long time, my only real wish is that there was more tricks to do, they can be added later though. I'm really impressed this works so well, on paper this concept doesn't seem like it would work, but this works great, great job.I like the music player and the music included, but I was hoping that I could go into the game files and add my own somehow. If it's possible to do that that would be amazing, obviously don't give away the tracks in the game for free, but some secure way for us to add our own would be great. That would be my main requested feature, but I can get around it with OVR and Spotify.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Yup, its vr skateboarding. Now that it has more levels I intend to put a fair amount of hours in. Still only runs but I think they're planning to add a skatepark down the road. Performance wise it runs well on my index with a 3070 and a 3600x, no performance dips or anything. Looks quite good, the controls are really good (easy enough for a total non skater), overall pretty great.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Last update with the 3 maps and the other little changes (like different boards... different modes) is RAAAD! You can tell the devs are awesome and that this game is going to be THE reference in VR skateboarding. The only downsides that I'm seeing at the moment is how hard it is to gain speed by pushing. Sometimes it feels like you push like a sicko but it barely goes forward. Also, turning can be hard... like really hard. I know it's meant to be played as a "run" type of sessions but this affects the gameplay a lot. There is wrong feeling of being stuck which isnt great because it never occurs when you are on a real skateboard. I have plenty of suggestions to make actually. Would like to join the devs on Discord or wherever. That being said, it's a must. Click buy now before the servers are down haha.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so well made. It's a tiny bit complicated with the fact that a lot of the moves are similar and I end up not do the one I want to do. For the most part that doesn't affect the gameplay except in the academy. Other than that it is a fun game that you can really just hop into after doing some of the tutorials. The one map is a lot of fun but I bet in the future when theres more maps it will give us lots of options for different challenges. Its truly a lot of fun and I can't wait for more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential. It's only a month old and in early acces, but it still exceeded my expectations. Nice activity for skaters that can't go skate, and for people that don't know anything about the sport. There are still many tricks and modes that need to be added, but devs, please never ditch this project. I would love to see this game grow and become one of the most popular titles on the vr market. <3
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome stuff! Great controls and feel of skating .. I am a skater and I thought it would be weird using my hands instead of my feet but actually after a while I forgot my legs weren't doing anything and it feels pretty cool.It was quite easy to learn all the moves but executing them intentionally in a run is a lot more difficult .. but very rewarding when you get it right.// FOR THE DEVS - I would like to see proper free skate levels that we can just skate around rather than this kinda downhill run stuff .. you have something really good here.. just needs more freedom.. like real skating ;)Session markers and all that good stuff please.I like the runs as an extra challenge but I want to feel like I'm at a skate park :D
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: I was highly doubtful a good VR skatebording game could ever be made and boy was I wrong !While this is in early access and needs some more work (maps, grab mechanics, more flip and rail tricks, etc), the basics are there, and pretty well made ! The feeling is pretty good when you land a trick, and there are some pretty ingenuous designs to make tricks feel "realistic".I have two mains "complaints" or rather feedbacks for the devs :- Make more content ! The game is clearly in its early stages, and it's perfectly understandable why its content is limited to say the least, but I implore you to capitalize on the relative hype you mustered and produce content regularly ! Your game is worth the price for skateboarders, but give it more maps and modes and it can become a mainstream hit !- The "push" mechanic is extremely tiring for long sessions. My right shoulder is still sore from all the waving around. Maybe you should implement an "easy" push mechanic for more chill sessions and practices, or at least lower the required movement "intensity" to gain decent speed. I basically had to go all out to get enough speed for the academy's slide challenges !Good job, and I wish you the best on your dev adventure !
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the closest we are ever going to get to a good skating game in VR, and it is great! VR skater has easy to understand tutorials to get you started, and when you get the hang of the physics and how the tricks work, you can perform some sick trick lines. The soundtrack has some great music too. The game uses your hands to perform tricks and you press a button to ollie (similar to the Tony Hawk games) The game is overall really fun and immersing, I would totally recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a full experience yet, it's also not a tony hawk in vr kind of game, don't go in expecting that experience and you'll likely enjoy your time.At the moment there Is only one level and you cant freely skate around rather you are confined to moving forward through the level, i'd prefer a freeskate mode but this is only early access so this kind of stuff can still be added.The skateboarding is extreamly intuitive and fun, i dont really have any complaints in this regard except the steering beeing a little to weak, especially to the left it feels impossible to make any hard turns to the left.On a side note the sound design and music are great, especially the sound of going over tiled floor is incredibly satisfying and the music choice is great aswell.All in all: If you have a few bucks to spare and want to support a potentially great skateboading game, then this is the game for you, if you expected a tony hawk in vr game, or a fleshed out skating experience with hours of content, you'll likely be dissappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: OVERALL: very bare-bones at the moment with some flaws, I'm hoping more content/development gives me more of a reason to play more than an hour of this game in the future. There's a lot of potential here, the gameplay fundamentals are really solid and fun. I'm tentatively giving this a thumbs up with the expectation that this gets fleshed out a lot more in the coming months of early access.BAD:- there is no button mapping to go back to the menu with index vr controllers, so sometimes you can get stuck and have to exit the game just to get back to the main menu- there is only one fairly small map available- no board customization, overall very feature-bare (this is early access after all)GOOD:- the controls are mostly solid, except for the times where my first swing doesn't register as a push, but otherwise no complaints so far- grinds lock in very well, they're satisfying to pull off- flip controls, catching the board, manuals all work really well- combos are tricky but fair to pull off
_childDocuments_.name: VR Skater

_childDocuments_.review: keep in mind that i am writing this review with the fact that it is an early access game in mind, and that it *may* improve. my negative points are all things that can be fixed, should the developers see the need to do so. furthermore, i have never touched a skateboard in my life and so you'll have to forgive my miserable memory as i've forgotten the names of most tricks immediately after the academythis game is a really really fun, really really hard, and really really sweaty VR tony hawk pro skater. with enough maps (perhaps even workshop map support, or a nexus modding community like B&S), a custom radio, and a little more optimization, i'd play it for hours on end as-is. BUT, and this is a very big but, in it's current state there are only two maps. one of these maps is hugely modular, and only appears in the academy/challenges, and is a big warehouse with obstacle prefabs placed around. the second map has two modes, 'practice' and 'run', and is, as another reviewer has quite accurately put it, one big tunnel. middle school is this map, and it is 'fully designed and skatable' according to the developers, despite the fact that1. multiple railings that should be grindable (at least noseslide, or 50-50) will instantly bail you on contact, and usually end your run then and there. this includes the leftmost staircase railing towards the end of the middle school map which doesn't seem to support 50-50, whereas the rightmost railing does. either someone got their calculations wrong and installed that railing a bit to the side, or i managed to consistently mess it up on one end, where as i almost perfectly nailed it each time on the other. i was only ever able to 2. staircases will bail you when you touch the top step, even though the top step is perfectly level with the ground behind it/under you, usually ending a run or ruining a good start3. there seem to be a number of spots around the map where air is solid, and you'll impact nothing mid-grind to ollie/nollie near certain staircases, though i suspect this ties into issue 24. the map is extremely linear, essentially serving as one straight hallway with any forks having no real effect on where you go throughout the school. there is one path, and a number of obstacles to use. i feel as though adding more paths to the map, more methods to reach the final area (possibly more in line with a ramp towards the end) would make this map a whole lot more enjoyable.aside from this map itself, there are a number of issues that may just be me being out of shape or poorly coordinated.1. depending on your stance, you will either use your right or left arm swinging in a downwards arc from directly ahead of you to directly behind you or your left arm the same way in order to accelerate. constantly. every time you want to speed up. my right arm is aching as i type this, but it's the same sort of aching you get while you adjust to a new difficulty in beatsaber.2. some tricks are extremely difficult to pull off, simply because they require a very specific speed in a very specific direction to properly handle. i see a feasible solution to this problem being holograms in the tutorial instead of a screen, allowing the players to mimic the exact speed/direction of holographic controllers in front of them, making the tricks far easier.3. certain times, tricks just don't happen. mainly with grinds and manuals, you'll do the right button combination and it just won't activate. i tested this for about 20 minutes on the first ramp in school, and it seems to have to do with 'catching' a trick you do accidentally. if you're used to swinging your arms around and sort of 'acting' your role in a game, you'll need to unlearn this so as to avoid accidentally tricking during a manual or a grind, as it could end a really good run. 4. turning and braking are extremely ineffective, and it seems that sometimes you might accidentally press the trigger in a certain way when you didn't intend to, jeopardising a runhowever, with all of these negative aspects, there are a lot of positive aspects about the maps and the gameplay.1. the music is crazy good, and incredible nostalgic. i used to play tony hawk's pro skater on the xbox, and this threw me way back.2. pulling off a combo for upwards of 10k or 20k points is incredibly satisfying, and gives a huge thrill that no other vr game i've played can make me experience. from beating alyx to a stunt in boneworks or a fullcombo in beatsaber, this just tops it all, making it so much more worth it.3. with only 6 real buttons to work with, the developers have done well to make pulling off stunts really intuitive and fun. i feel this could be further improved with a game modifier at the start of a run (like switching between practice or run) to choose the speed the game runs at, allowing for more precise practice. alternatively, a bullet time mode which can be toggle on and off, with a similar method of selecting the speed it slows to (not unlike B&S's bullet time mode and modifier4. there's a huge amount of potential in this game. a more open world sandbox environment, improved turning, and more polish on the maps and mechanics and i'd gladly spend as much time on this as i have on h3vr or beatsaber, and a p2p co-op system with even very basic avatars like beatsaber multiplayer would make this so much more fun, racing in co-op to see who's the better skater. i'd argue that there's enough potential in the mechanics currently available to outweigh all of the negatives in the lack of variety, the bugs, etc.for any other early access game, i'd scoff and ignore a $28.95 AUD pricetag. this game managed to grab my attention well, and i can safely say was worth the investment. i look forward to seeing how the devs improve this game, not just in mechanics and the maps but also in the music and community interaction.TL;DRthere's a fair amount of issues, namely the map and bugs within that map, or inconsistent mechanics and unclear tutorials, but aside from those issues there is an endless potential with levels of satisfaction or difficulty way greater and more versatile than beatsaber or any rhythm game i can think of. there's a lot of love and care put into the map, (currently also the only map) and i hope that they'll only improve from here. if you liked tony hawk's pro skater, and you're rather skillful at vr rhythm games like beatsaber, you'll probably have a huge kick out of this game.edit: as a post-script for the tl;dr, i beg you devs to increase the rate at which players turn. seriously, never seen anything quite as frustrating as having a perfect combo and then getting stuck because you physically cannot turn fast enough to get back on track, as you usually cannot turn effectively with the stationary turning mechanic.

name: Exoprimal
detailed_description: Exoprimal Product Information - Exoprimal Exoprimal Deluxe Edition Product Information - Exoprimal - Head Start Kit - Vigilant Early Unlock Ticket - Murasame Early Unlock Ticket - Nimbus Early Unlock Ticket - Paladin exosuit skin (Vigilant) - White Guardian exosuit skin (Murasame) - Wonderland exosuit skin (Nimbus) Note: Early Unlock Tickets can be purchased even if you have already unlocked the corresponding exosuit, or if you already satisfy its unlock conditions. Be careful not to purchase an Early Unlock Ticket for an exosuit you have unlocked. Skins are cosmetic items that change the appearance of an exosuit and have no other effect. The Head Start Kit may be purchased separately. Be careful not to purchase this product if you already own it. Visit the official website for more details about the Head Start Kit. About the Game 【GAME DETAILS】 Exoprimal is an online, team-based action game that pits humanity's cutting-edge exosuit technology against history's most ferocious beasts – dinosaurs. Exosuits are grouped into different roles, and players will pilot these exosuits to hold firm against overwhelming dinosaur swarms in online-only, team-based action game modes. 【STORY】 The year is 2040… Sudden dinosaur outbreaks have engulfed the globe in a crisis that threatens humanity's very existence. Yet all hope is not lost. The corporation Aibius has developed a hyper-advanced AI called Leviathan that can predict the location of future outbreaks. This technology, along with Aibius's revolutionary powered suits, or exosuits, gives humanity a fighting chance to stem the tide of the saurian swarms. Exosuit pilots, otherwise known as exofighters, are in high demand. Take the exofighter aptitude test and join the ranks of Aibius's heroic pilots in their fight to stave off the extinction of the human race. 【EXOSUITS】 Exosuits are cutting-edge powered suits developed to combat the dinosaur threat. Based on their range of abilities, exosuits are primarily categorized into one of three roles: assault, tank, and support. Exofighters can change exosuits at any time, even during battle, by performing a suit change. Take advantage of this flexibility to alter your team composition on the fly and complete your objectives. ROLES ASSAULT Assault exosuits focus on dealing damage to enemies with close, medium, or long-range attacks. Although exact loadouts differ, each assault exosuit is equipped with weapons and abilities tailored to its effective combat range. Use the best weapon for the situation and eradicate whatever stands in your way. TANK Tank exosuits specialize in protecting their allies by drawing enemy attacks and absorbing damage. Whether they're holding back a massive horde or stopping relentless dinosaur attacks, tank exosuits will form your team's first line of defense. SUPPORT Support exosuits use a variety of abilities to ensure the team's survival. While the ability to repair allied exosuits is most common, support exosuits are also equipped with a range of buffing and debuffing abilities. Support exosuits use these abilities to improve a team's combat effectiveness and accomplish objectives even faster. RIGS Rigs are additional pieces of equipment for exosuits. Rigs grant exosuits additional abilities, but only one may be equipped at a time. For example, the Zephyr exosuit excels at close quarters combat but has trouble with foes that attack from long-distance. Equipping it with the Cannon rig will enable Zephyr to use a long-range laser. Or, equip Roadblock with the Aid rig to provide healing and create a formidable front line of defense. Players can experiment with different combinations of rigs and exosuits to find their ideal playstyle. Both rigs and exosuits can be changed at any time. 【DINO SURVIVAL】 In Dino Survival, two squads of five race to complete objectives. Teams must follow Leviathan's directives and complete the mission before their rivals to win. Some situations pit players against one another in direct combat, and others require players to band together with their rivals to take down a major foe. In Dino Survival, the missions change based on players' progression through the game. The experience will be different with each match, even in matches with familiar surroundings and objectives. Players can unlock story sequences by playing Dino Survival and also earn rewards such as experience points to increase player and exosuit levels. DINOSAURS Dinosaurs, once the most fearsome and powerful creatures in the animal kingdom, are no longer history. However, traveling through spacetime via the vortexes has mutated these beasts and ramped up their ferocity to all-new heights. Humanity must rely on its ingenuity and its most powerful weapons – exosuits – to respond to this crisis. NEOSAURS Neosaurs are mutated dinosaurs with unusual appearances and abilities. Dinosaurs are imbued with a highly unstable energy when they cross through the vortex barrier after passing through spacetime. This energy is responsible for the ferocious transformation many dinosaurs undergo. Neosaurs possess an extremely high concentration of this energy, granting them unusual appearances, abilities, and attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a "Play for 2 hours and you've played it all" game like I've seen some reviews seem to read or have playtime below 2 hours. There are 10-man activities, the objectives get harder, the dinosaurs get replaced with Neo-Saurs, or harder dinos, and MASSIVE 1000+ swarms. The story is done well so far, the characters are likeable. Now, monetization is a valid complaint, but I counter that with the premium pass being only cosmetic. The only DLC that provides tangible in-game benefit is the Headstart pack, and the Overdrive kit, which will unlock all of the Alpha suit variants, because you insta unlock suits. And the Alpha suits don't release for 3 months. I really like this game. Its alot of fun. Now, there is not pure PvE experience where there are no enemy players. The closest you have is PvE with one enemy player showing up as a high tier Dino one time to wreck your day. There is no pure PvP experience, there will always be dinos butting into your fights. Ignore anyone with a playtime under 3 hours. Understand that there are no loot boxes, and there are goofy skins you earn from the pass, or that you get from playing the game. This is a new IP from Capcom, give it some time, they are learning as they go.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't agree with the price, or the fact that it has a premium Bpass and the ability to insta buy heroes (exos) to unlock faster while at its current price (7/22/23 - $59.99). I'm warning you now, as this may very well end up a F2P game in the future. Unless this is the new norm with how things are shaping up in the AAA gaming industry. If there is one thing i dislike the most, it's the price (and some of these skins...jesus)  ...Exoprimal, simply due to the experience it gave me, the gameplay, even the story   - There is a lot to unpack in terms of those categories alone, but to sum the game up: The game includes overwatch like heroes and objectives which you will be required to accomplish with others. A dose of badass mechs (you, the exo) fighting waves of dinos  ...all while trying everything you can  to finish each objective faster then the opposing team. It's one of the reason you might see a review around here with  this is where that Destiny 'Gambit' mechanic comes into frame, teams get a chance to turn into a big Dino   to screw up (invade) the enemy, or you can walk there  The downside to leaving and going to harass the enemy however, would be abandoning your payload which is now not progressing, or you're not capturing point B, or you're not collecting enough cores...etc So yes, there are varied game modes . Additionally, due to story beats, you may end up playing WITH the enemy, rather then against to progress...Speaking of progression, everything becomes available to you by level 45-50  and will take about about 15-20 hours.I will say, the game design is a fresh take on the copy and paste of genres lately, i think alot of people would enjoy the spin of familiarity in Exoprimal. Again, for $60 (base game) + $10 (Bpass premium) + $15 (headstart pack, not required) it can almost justify itself due to the level of execution of the game - I think $29.99 would have been a better entry point.  100% completion of the story, and currently with over 60 PVP matches complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok game. I played the beta and I assumed that was only a part of the content that was still locked behind the release but nope its the entire thing. Maybe it will change in the future but not right now. Also micro transactions inside a paid game is a no.edit after playing for a lil:- cutscenes aint skipable (the ones that happen before every match and after a game ends)- ♥♥♥♥ looking human characters (at least the female ones)- sometimes the waypoint doesn't show when you first start the game so you are just left wandering and following your teammates or enemy players- sometimes you get the dino ult thing 30 seconds before the game ends cause you are the winning team while the other losing team (by like 5 seconds) gets it 3 minutes before the game ends which just causes luck based situationsMay add more stuff later if I find them buggy/annoyingDon't bother getting the game through steam by paying $60. Just play included xbox gamepass version.
