_childDocuments_.review: BLUF: Story is interesting, but not terribly compelling. Gameplay loop is mid - weapons have mediocre feedback at best, teammates are often poor quality, and the PvPvE modes don't feel great. If you're looking for PvE against dinosaurs, majority of the game is that but always ends in competition against an opposing team in some manner. If you want a solely PvE experience, you'll have to wait and see if they add such a mode. On the one hand; It's not a terrible game. On the other hand; I can't recommend it at it's current price. Wait for a sale, and then it might be worth it.Long version:PVP mode ends with you and the enemy team fighting one another at the end of the match as part of a data-cube escort mission. It's not very good. Suits are not balanced to be fighting one another, so once one team wins a fight it's pretty much game over. The PvE mode has you compete in objectives against the enemy team for the final segment, avoiding suit-on-suit warfare and has the possibility to end in a double victory (If one team finishes the final objective the other team has 20 seconds or so to finish their final objective. If they do, they also win - or so I've experienced.) Each suit unlocks upgrades that can affect each of it's abilities, but those abilities have to be unlocked and upgraded via bikcoin (yes, really) which you get through suit-progression or player account level and battle pass progression. There are also generic upgrades that apply to every suit in place of skill-specific upgrades, and they also need to be unlocked and upgraded with bikcoin. The "Survival Pass" and heavy monetization leaves a sour taste in my mouth, and I understand why any would not purchase this game because of it. I don't hate this game, and it has potential, but the current state of it is middling at best and not really worth the $60/70 USD, imo. We'll see what other game modes they add to help enhance the current experience, and what tweaks they make to suits/abilities/game modes down the line and see if it's really worth the current cost of the title.

The game is highly monetized with exo suits and skins behind paywalls along with paid battle pass for 10 bucks. Low player base and repetitive after 10 matches theirs nothing new.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal successfully pulls off what Brink & Titanfall set out to do with its narrative storytelling in a multiplayer framework.  It's not perfect, but it's made me rethink how one can structure a multiplayer experience. The gameplay that accompanies this is super tight, the exosuits are exceptionally diverse and add tons of variety, and there are a ton of different objectives and maps that get injected into matches are you progress through the story. I really do wonder what a game like Overwatch, Payday, or Mortal Kombat could do if they were to mimic the framework and narrative storytelling Capcom has accomplished here. It's a really nice blend, neither taking away the focus of the other, while providing a bunch of surprises a long the way.The first few hours do come across as a bit barren or lacking in content at first, but stick with it and you won't regret it. It's been a truly memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest people...You will read a lot of other reviews telling you that this game is too repetetive and is not worth the 60 bucks. Furthermore there is this misconception, that this game would have a PvE only Section, which was advertised nowhere and is completltey made up by the player's  wrong preconceptions.Yes the Battlepass and DLCs are little bit obnoxious, but all of those are just cosmetics. You will be able to play the game and have no disadvantage for not buying any of those. To be frank, i don't get the hate to the degree the game is currently getting for the paid stuff. Other Games like Call of Duty and League of Legends are selling skins to enormous prices and no one bats an eye.The progression so far feels fine. It will unlock personalized ways to play your favorite characters. Not much to say here.I also think the missions offer enough variations to be not too repetitive. A competitive game needs a little bit of predictability to be able to develop tactics and a meta.Just take a look and think before you buy, like any normal sane person. Overall you will just have to deecide for yourself if this game is worth your money or not.I hope a lot more people will give this game a chance, despite the overly negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface by saying I love ME3 multiplayer and that was what I was partially hoping for here.  TLDR, this game doesn't really scratch that itch for me, and feel like ME3 MP is just a superior product in comparison, by a decent margin.I also got excited, since most games like the premise of this one usually are FPS and I really am not a fan of FP perspective.  That isn't to say I don't or can't enjoy them, but given the option, I'll always prefer 3rd person to 1st 10 times out of 10.Having said that, the enemy types don't feel varied enough, there are too many fodder enemies not enough "hard" targets,  the pvp is just odd, not particularly interesting when I find myself in those portions.  Using ME3 mp as a comparison, there felt like  alot of opportunities for cool plays in ME3 and the gameplay by the different classes felt fresh and fun to explore from the infiltrator, to the biotic, to the geth to the turian variants etc....there just isn't that variation to Exoprimal comparatively imo and I've tried the support/tank/assault types and while they are different in how they play, to me it doesn't feel that exciting/different while playing any of the class types.This game is just not worth $60 and unfortunately by the time it hits a sale in two months the game will probably be close to dead.

There's literally THOUSANDS OF THEM POURING FROM THE SKY!NO? GOOD. You have blades, grenades, rockets, and bullets to MOW THEM DOWN WITHOUT PREJUDICE!DO YOU LIKE PVE?YES? GOOD. Merk dinosaurs until you die of glee.NO? GOOD. Harness YOUR OWN DINOSAUR and go ♥♥♥♥ UP OTHER PLAYERS. OR HELL, JUST SHOOT THEM YOURSELF.DO YOU LIKE PVP?SEE ABOVE.DO YOU LIKE PLOT AND CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT?YES? GOOD. This game has a surprising amount of it. I'm genuinely invested in where this story goes. I like these NPCs.NO? GOOD. EASILY SKIP THE CUT SCENES, AND STORY MISSIONS ARE JUST MORE DINO KILLING FUN.DO YOU LIKE A VARIETY OF CLASSES TO PLAY?YES? GOOD. _childDocuments_.review: Many People state this Game has not much Content and is on a F2P monetization despite being 60 bucks (Seasonpass) but i disagree. First of all you unlock more mission types as you Progress through the Story, which is never explained to you though. And the PvP complaint is stupid because on the 18th of July there is a coop only Mode coming(not even Racing against each other) and you dont ask of CS:GO to be a Coop focused Game. The Monetization is fine as well, Street Fighter has it as well, and you don't need to Pay2Win in this game because (almost) all Suits are Balanced and you can unlock them with enough Time spent in Game. _childDocuments_.review: Great fun shootin up some dino's and added challenge of doing a bit of PVP at the end of each round too if you fancy it, great fun and passes the time quite quickly, few different play styles in the terms of roles and the type of characters in those roles, for example aoe healers, single target healers splash healers,Burst dps, aoe dps, melee dps, plenty of characters to play around with for a fairly new game, with more to come im sure, has a fun overwatch feel without the massive amount of sweats that come with it, only flaw i would say is, theres not really a campaign just sorta a few cutsences after a few matches every so often till the storys been told, not actual quests or story missions.And the battles feel alittle samey they use same few maps far be it sometimes you're not always going the same routes and there's no many objectives, just run there kill these mobs, run there kill these mobs, Not at all saying it isn't fun as it is, just can be a fairly bit repetitive after a few match's but overall yeah id recommend this game for a good laugh with some friends or even solo, always fun when you see yourself at the MVP position at the end of the match!.

_childDocuments_.review: We wanted a new Dino Crisis, but what we got was Exoprimal, which is just Overwatch with dinos, the PvE is non-existent because it is essentially paired with PvP.The lack of maps variation affects replayability, and the game's aesthetics are the only saving grace. If you enjoy Dino Crisis, I feel for you. This is the game you didn't ask for or deserve. If it had more game types, separate pvp from pve, dropped the microtransactions, and added more maps, it could be worth a second look.The story and characters are absolutely stupid, most cutscenes haven't been dubbed, so if you want to hear the character in another language too bad, this is a AAA studio.There are no penalties for leaving in the middle of a game, and the reporting system is only for show. Keep your money and play Overwatch if you already own it!This game is just as awful as Capcom's other money-grab game Resident Evil Re:Verse.And they've added the "Exosuit Early Unlock Ticket Pack 1" which is not included in the Deluxe Edition, so be ready for the next ones.

_childDocuments_.review: Game states cross play but it's not cross party.I was denied a refund since I played 4.5 hours, assuming my friend who had it on Game Pass could party up with me when he got home. This was NOT the case.EDIT: I wanted to leave an actual review with this game to make it as fair as possible. The game is fun! Each exosuit has good variety, the roles are all fun to play, the combat is interesting, and the mob density can be surprisingly high. This is also one of the first games to launch in a state recently that isn't filled with bugs or performance issues.On the down side, it's a little repetitive, partly due to how long it takes to unlock access to new objectives, dinosaurs, and exosuits. There are new exosuit variants, game modes, maps, etc on the road map that the devs posted, so I'm excited to see where this game heads.I think that this game should have launched at $40, not $60. It's genuinely good for what it is, but it's pretty shallow all things considered. Conclusion: I think this game is worth it on sale for around $40 or through Game Pass. Once it receives ACTUAL cross play (meaning I can play on Steam with my Game Pass friends) I will update this to a positive review. Right now, I don't feel the value is there and it's borderline false advertising to call this crossplay when you can't actually play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good and here is why.(You can NOT buy LOOT-BOXES and only EARN THEM as you level up)(The Exoprimal community is super fun to play with and they are not toxic.)(After 50 hours the game is still extremely fun and I am still not even close to being done.)(After 80 hours of playing I finally hit lvl 100 on one character)-They will  update the game to add more game modes so people will stop crying about the whole pvp and competition.       The new game modes will add more life to the game and the seasons will add more modules (hopefully) and new skins, ect.       The boss fights that incorporate all 8 players are amazing and each one of the bosses have unique skills, they are not buggy, and it is super cool. ( This is definitely a taste of what is to come later)- When it comes to the game modes there is a lot that the developers can do with this game. I mean they have all the assets there to create numerous game modes. ( maybe even a team death match, rumble, dinos vs hunters, ect). There is a lot of modes that can be on their way.- When it comes to the progression of the game, it is slow at first till you get one character to lvl 16 and upgrade it modules to best in slot. After that, it is super fun to try to get achievements and play without worrying about how much gold you have in order to get the next upgrade. Here we can play for fun and not to progress our character even though our character can reach lvl 100.       Once you have a main that you really enjoy then the gold cost will never effect you again. You can always play with new characters or use your main to do whatever.      Once you hit lvl 50 every additional level you get 1000 gold and a loot chest which is super cool to unlock skins and stuff for characters you didn't use, so there is incentive to use and develop them.-The combat is really well put together in my experience. It just feels so good to get that ability head-shot on a large monster and you can feel it hit when the monster staggers. There are also such good mechanics on the effect system that lets you freeze, burn, and electrify monster. It feels good overall I would say.- CONTENT. I know that a lot of players complain about this one a lot and yes I can see that if you only have played for less than 2 or 3 hours because you don't know what you are talking about. There is a lot of unique missions and events that happen as you progress the campaign and near completion. I think in total, if you rush it, you can finish it all in 22 hours or so.      Once you complete the campaign all the missions are unlocked and you can play all of them so there is a lot of replay ability because it goes off of the 22 hours of missions.MY ONLY COMPLAINPLEASE MAKE A MOD TO FIGHT ONLY BOSSES!!!!They are so cool and are literately the best content when it comes to the game. I mean the last battle was so epic that I want to do I at least 50 more times. You did a great job, but I want the ability to replay it by selecting it and not by luck.-Overall, this game is so much fun and you win no matter if it says defeat at the end. The people that are hating on it have a right to because it did not live up to what they thought it would be , but this game is worth the money and it such a blast to play. I would 100 percent recommend this to anyone that wants to take a break from all the usual games that we all see and kill some dinos.THANK YOU DEVELOPERS FOR MAKING A GAME THAT IS NEW AND FUN TO PLAY.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game design ruined by monetization. Diagnosis: This is a free-to-play game with a $60 price tag.Exosuits must be leveled-up in game, then you spend currency to buy upgrade modules, then you spend more currency to upgrade those modules (up to 5 times each, getting more expensive with each upgrade). All of this requires you to play in matchmaking, against other players who already have everything unlocked, so you'll be at a significant disadvantage and drag your teammates down until you grind out several dozen matches. Unless, of course, you're willing to pay even more money on top of the $60 you already spent for the game. Also, there's a battle pass (of course there is), with a premium track, and loads of cosmetics, so expect to see exosuits running around in swimwear and giant teddy bear costumes.I love the design ideas behind this game. Competitive team-based PvE culminating in a final PvP showdown, or sometimes teaming up with the enemy against a massive PvE onslaught feels extremely novel. The way they deliver plot and meta progression in a competitive team game like this feels like an evolution, although an imperfect one.My understanding is that you unlock more mission types and objectives as you progress the plot. Once in matchmaking, the game decides on objectives depending on the least-progressed person in the lobby. So you might get stuck in simple dinosaur-culling missions over and over if the game decides to match you with noobs.The competitive PvE aspect doesn't feel very impactful. Maybe this changes at higher levels, but at the start it's just a race. Go here, kill the things, do it faster than the other team, that's it. Once one team gets a lead, it feels very unlikely that you'll make up the time difference, so the rest of the match becomes a formality. There's not much you can do to slow down the enemy team that they can't just throw back at you. There's very little decision-making besides spamming your abilities as often as possible.I know that all of these things can be improved and the game concepts are solid. But I don't feel comfortable paying retail price for a game that's going to ask for money again and again and then maybe get shut down in two years.

_childDocuments_.review: Up front, the concept of destroying large hordes of dinos with exo-suits sounds fun. I wish they just focused on that. This game feels like it's having an identity crisis. It wants to tell a story while having no actual campaign aside from a few events that feel like RNG things that just happen when the game starts. They give you these somewhat open areas but force you along a path. You only get 2 maps, City day/night and jungle cavern. Then they want it to be PVP but not PVP? Only in a few circumstances do you actually fight another team. The rest of the time you're just speed running along side them. Just separate the modes if you really want PVP. I came to detonate dinos with the boys in our fancy power armor. Why do we have to compete against another team when there is no real reason for it? The story reason is dumb and I'm going to completely ignore it. On top of that they throw in a battle pass, free and paid, and you don't even get all the suits. Well not without some grinding or paying for them outright. Something I could look past if they game itself was free but it's $60. I hope they can change it up. I like the game play and it looks good. I just wish they focused on the PVE, dinos vs power armor, over this weird MOBA but not a MOBA thing they're trying to do. Get it on a HEAVY sale if you really want it. Please don't pay full price for this, thing. You'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hard one to review because it's pretty weird and confusingthe first 4-6 hours is all repetitive, once you get to your first raid and you've picked your jaw up off the floor, then you realize wow this game has potential.  It seems to be set up like this in segments, so every like 4-6 hours depending on how fast you're progressing the story nodes, you'll do a really dope coop raid and then unlock a new multiplayer map and slightly diff objective game types.I love the exosuits and I love how the gameplay feels but overall I don't see how this game is going to lastI beat the game and leveled up the only exosuits I care about.  Apparently there is a new game mode coming out in August and also alpha variants which adds different playstyles to the existing exosuits, so we'll see how that goes but let's be honest there's currently so many good games out and so many good games coming within the next few months that this game will probably be swept under the rug which is why I bought it at release cause I wanted to play it while it had a nice healthy player base.I wish you could choose what game type/mode to play, the game chooses for you which I think is annoying.  Some nights I would love to jump into raids and help people with those but I don't get the option to do thatI would love to see just a PvP game mode as well or PvPvE but being able to PvP during the whole match, not just towards the end of the matchI'll be keeping an eye on this one, if you're interested in it I would recommend getting it now while the player base is still there but is it worth $60? no, it's worth $40 max.  If you have gamepass, it's free so just get it on there but just note if you want to play with your friends they have to be on the same device you're playing on.  Xbox game pass players cannot team up with steam players which I found really annoying cause I had a friend on game pass I wanted to play with but couldn't. 7/10 I had a good time and thought I got my money worth, I'll be back when the new content rolls out

_childDocuments_.review: So it's not a terrible game, the only real complaint I personally have (and I know a lot of people will disagree with me) I personally don't care for the PvP, escort the cube, end game comp, it feels highly unbalanced because at times where my team has had a 20% advantage, we still ended up losing in the end even when we weren't really dying all that much, maybe it has to do with how much damage the enemy team was doing to our cube VS. what we were doing to theirs, idk, none the less it feels unbalanced. I'm giving it a thumbs down because I think you need to fix the "random" option when selecting matchmaking because i have only chose "random" a total of 4 games and probably about 15-20 games without "random" and each game with it enabled they were ALL PvP, and I'm not the only one who has noticed this, I have a couple friends that play as well and they say PvP has come up about 90% of the time. I personally am not a hardcore gamer, especially when it comes to PC gaming, so comp gameplay I'm not a fan of and the 1.2x multiplier for "random" doesn't feel like it's worth it when I get a bad match up and lose every game. Playing the PvE mode though is awesome and at least my win loss ratio is much better there and I just feel like the "random" needs to be more 50/50 in the game modes and not so tilted on the PvP mode

_childDocuments_.review: Tried for the free weekend. Suit designs are gorgeous, sound design is excellent, cutscenes were cool from the jump, everything looks super pretty and the setting and story seem interesting. The game feels and sounds so good to play, to stomp around in big heavy suits or to float and prance gracefully in lighter ones.However, I don't especially care for how you have to unlock entire suits, variants, story progress and even dinosaur enemy types despite the game having a significant price tag. Content structuring like this is befitting of a free-to-play game, which this is not. If this game  F2P, it'd be fine in that respect, but when you paid forty to sixty dollars to get in the door, you really should have all the base suits, if nothing else.On a more personal note, I also don't much care for the primary game mode being 5v5 objective versus, but that's just because I have poor memories of Gambit. I'd probably enjoy this game more if it was like a spiritual sibling to Earth Defense Force, in all its desperate, campy survival glory.It has the bones of a very, very good game. But it's not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to start by saying: DON'T LISTEN TO MANY OF THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS!! Most of them aren't making very valid points.I just finished the main story of this game and can wholeheartedly say that this is a great game and i love itFirst I'll address the negative reviews, or at least the main points they've been making:- "There is no content." No, there is content, it's just that you dont start to unlock more until after a few hours. The first few hours are to get you accustomed to the basics before throwing more challenging things at you.- "The monetisation makes this game unplayable." No, far from it. Granted it's a payed game with a battle pass system, but the pass is completely optional and you can earn MANY cosmetics without it. If you aren't willing to pay the big price tag to play it, then wait for a sale, thats totally valid.- "The crossplay is trash." This is the only take i somewhat agree with, but then again, it doesnt make it unplayable, it just prevents partying up with people from other platforms. If youre friends all have the same platform for it then youre golden. Granted im a little biased since all my friends play on PC, but regardless.- "Theres only one gamemode." NO, THERES NOT. YOU UNLOCK MORE. You just need to play a bit to get them. Dino survival is a catch all term, once youre in, there are 11 game modes that can switch into one another. Area defence, Dinosaur cull, Omegacharge, Energy Collector, the list goes on. Plus they added the savage gauntlet mode for people who complete the main story, and from what i understand, its a lot like deep dives from DRG.Now that im through the negative stuff, i'll get the the praise.- The game is very well balanced. Aside from one suit i think that could use a buff (Vigilant), i think all of the exosuits are totally viable and i think so long as you dont flood your comp with one class then youll be fine with anything.- This game is a shining example of how to optimise a game. It runs like a dream, even when you have literally hundreds of individual dinos rushing at you at once, and up to 10 players doing their own things all on screen at once, it still runs amazingly. And before you say it, my PC isnt the strongest in the world, and it still runs fine.- The gameplay. In short it can be described as "Amazing dumb fun." I rarely had moments where i found it lacking. At the end of each match, i would always find myself raring for another. I even find myself having fun when i lose. The PvE is satisfying and you always feel like youre being helpful, even when playing tanks and supports. The PvP is far more fun (in my opinion) to PvP in games like Overwatch and CoD. It doesnt feel sweaty at all because unlike those games you dont get popped in less than a second if youre not the biggest tryhard alive.- The story is far better than i expected from a game about exosuits fighting dinosaurs. The characters are endearing, and there were multiple times where the plot developed in a way beyond what i was expecting.If youre wondering if it's worth it because of the somewhat mixed reviews, then listen to me when I tell you: YES. If youre short on cash, maybe wait for a sale, but just know that you will get your money's worth. Please get this game and show it the love it deserves,

_childDocuments_.review: Went into Exoprimal with zero expectations, and boy, was I pleasantly surprised. After 23 hours spent immersing myself in all roles, I finally finished the story - and it was an experience to remember.Let's address the elephant in the room: yes, it's a repetitive third-person hero shooter. But, does that detract from the experience? Absolutely not. The story was actually pretty damn good, the whole time it had me looking forward to any and all cinematic or story progression read outs. The characters are charming, likeable, and overall just unique plus the boss battles or 10 man fights were like fine wine. Now let's talk about combat. Though it may seem fundamentally repetitive, the variety provided by each exo and their respective roles makes it thrilling to play. Whether you're a hovering skywave support or a front-running zephyr, you'll enjoy blasting and slashing your way through swarms of dinos. The potential this game has for growth is impressive - perhaps even enough to evolve into a franchiseAll I'm saying is that this game is a real gem that had some real heart put into its design even if at its surface it seems pretty straight forward. I have high hopes for future content and more pve focused experiences, but it does really well with its PVPVE approach. I can't wait to see what the future holds for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll go over what I thought Exoprimal was, the monetization system, the gameplay structure, and my current rating.I'll be upfront that I had purchased Exoprimal hoping more for a pure PvE experience with PvP being available for those who wanted it. I'm a big fan of both Monster Hunter and Lost Planet and was hoping that this new Capcom IP would help satisfy that itch, however because of the confusion regarding the games launch and play structure that I was a little disappointed. I don't mind playing competitive games, but I was hoping that Exoprimal could have just been more similar to EDF or DRG style of game but with mutant dinosaurs fighting robots.There are currently two modes of play, Dino Survival and Savage Gauntlet (Savage Gauntlet is  accessible after completing the "story" which takes about 55 games of Dino Survival, which in my case took about 20 hours)Dino Survival: Players can queue PvP and PvE modes where they race to complete a number of missions against another team in two rounds. As other reviews have mentioned, when you first start out in the game, the missions are pretty simple, kill "x" raptors, kill a triceratops, etc. As you progress through the story, more variants of missions are thrown into the possible missions, now you have "Defend Checkpoint A", or "Escort the cube". Whether or not you win or lose Dino Survival will progress you through the story, so you'll always be introduced to these new variants, even on a losing streak. So long as you play more you increase the variety of missions you can experience. It is important to note that  in a race, and the difference is either indirectly (PvE) or directly (PvP). I'll try to describe the flow:Round 1:Complete missions racing against the other team, with the in-game narrator letting you know if you are matching or falling behind the enemy team's pace, teams do not directly interact.Round 2 (If you chose PvP):Towards the end of Round 2, you will compete directly against other teams in PvP combat while trying to complete the mission, This is hectic, this can be fun, this can be frustrating. Dominators are given to both teams in this mode, allowing a player to "play as" a dinosaur and fight the other team. Some gameplay missions will only be available in this mode.Round 2 (if you chose PvE):This mirrors round 1 where you continue to race against the other team, but the team that is slower is given a Dominator, in an attempt for the slower team to catch up. A little later the opposing team will get their own Dominator to use at their own discretion. Whichever team completes the final mission first is declared the "winner", and the other team then has 20 seconds to complete the final mission. I've played a fair number of games where we're on the "losing" team, but still manage to complete the final objective before the time runs out, and the narrator calls us winners as well, even netting the victory exp bonus as well, so it's actually possible for both teams to actually win here. Some of my favorite matches were where both teams had the dominator, but neither team ends up using it, either out of fear of a revenge invasion or want for both teams to do well.Dominators are present in both modes, so if you are looking at Dino Survival (or Exoprimal in general) know that you will always be competing, and if you were looking for something purely cooperative, that this game may not be for you.Savage Gauntlet: PvE only mode that has teams of 5 playing a set sequence of missions that records time scores. Replaying this mode during the same period allows for teams to polish their strategies and compete for better times. This mode was released today, and from my impressions of it, it seems underwhelming. Savage gauntlet was advertised as a cooperative mode that would build off of that level of skill level and engagement deserving of a mode that is only available post-game, but instead it's a short romp of a few missions. Savage Gauntlet is supposed to rotate weekly with new variations and mission challenges, and only time will tell in this regard how well this will be handled, but my first impression was not great.I think 60 USD is  too steep of a price tag for the game at the moment, given the content we've received so far. You may take my continued negative review with a grain of salt, since I've established that Exoprimal's structure is (disappointingly) not for me, but I think there is still not enough content to justify a 60 USD price tag, .What kept me playing until now was a combination of sunken cost fallacy, wanting to beat the story so I could try out the savage gauntlet mode, and surprisingly, I found myself playing to continue learning about the story. For a horde-type game, you would not typically advertise story as being one of the stronger parts of the experience, so I was very pleasantly surprised and entertained in this regard., but the game modes available are structured in a way that a player like myself (who was looking for a traditional PvE game) am not really satisfied and could not recommend to other players looking for that kind of experience.I want this game to do well and I think Capcom has had a good streak with its releases lately, so I hope that one day I can come back to this review and make appropriate changes. Again.

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter version: Solid co-op PvP/PvE game that gives you options before starting a match for how you want to finish out matches (PvP objective race or PvE race with enemy team) As you level up your suits you unlock modifications that amplify your suits that you can upgrade. Exosuits themselves are (imo) balanced very well, with one or two being better in certain scenarios but nothing too extreme. There's also sometimes a 10-player final mission at certain parts in the story where both teams work together to finish it and those are VERY fun. Comeback mechanics exist and you can definitely win when behind, with or without them, or even with a full squad of A.I. teammates against human players (sometimes they are way better than human players). Story is decent, and a nice addition, and as you progress the story you unlock more missions and more variety in the dinosaurs you are fighting which is a great way to ease newer players into the game. New stuff comin' soon, and plenty more planned beyond that.Stuff people might be annoyed by;There's loot boxes BUT they are completely free, you can't buy them at ALL, and earn them via leveling up your player level. Plus, as far as I've found, you cannot get repeat items/items you already own. There are plenty of in-game cosmetics too, that can also be obtained outside of loot boxes by purchasing them with in-game currency. In-game currency, dubbed BikCoins (Bikitoa Coins) is also used to upgrade mods as well as purchase cosmetics, so for a bit you'll have to decide what to use your coins on. There is a Battle Pass with a free tier but that 11 items, compared to Paid/Premium Tier 50 items. But it is all completely cosmetic and has nothing P2W. There is ONE paid non-cosmetic DLC that is a "Head Start Kit" that unlocks 3 suits as soon as you buy them, instead of leveling up your player level to unlock them (Nimbus at 20, Murasame at 30, Vigilant at 40) but hitting level 40 doesn't take very long (I'm level 41, almost 42 at just under 20 hours and you typically level up at least once after EVERY match). There are paid DLC for skins (currently 5) that are alternative colors/styles some of the battle pass skins and include some emotes and other cosmetic stuff.Now for the in-depth stuff;If you like team based PvP shooters, with an option of a final segment of direct combat with the enemy team or a race to finish objectives to win (or randomly chosen between the two, which will give you a bit more EXP for choosing), then you'll definitely enjoy this game. Also at certain points, after getting to certain story progress, you get to partake in 10-player PvE final missions which are very fun. The game also does a great job of not leaving out players who are behind in the story by regularly matching you into those story related 10 player missions so you get to replay them again. Players also unlock new "Modules"/Modifications for your Exosuits upon raising Exosuits or Player level. Some are for any suit and some are suit specific (suit specific you unlock for leveling suits, general you unlock for general player level ups) and modify abilities and/or increase damage for weapons/abilities. These can be upgraded with in-game currency from Level 1 to Level 5 and you can actually decrease or entirely remove downsides for modsGameplay itself is very good. I personally think all of the Exosuits are pretty well balanced compared to each other. Obviously DPS type suits do really good damage, Tanks are tanky but also do decent damage, and supports heal goodly but really only one does decent damage but the others have tons of utility. Don't count the tanks or supports out for PvP combat though, they have enough utility and damage to deal with DPS suits. One suit in particular, Barrage (Grenade/Fire DPS), does seem to be probably the best in terms of PvE, but any of the other DPS suits can do just as well but require a bit more from the player compared to playing Barrage. Also comeback mechanics exist, one being the "Dominator" and the other being a "Dinosaur Upgrade". Dominator lets you control a Dinosaur (so far you get randomly given a Carnotarus, a Triceratops, or a T.Rex) to directly attack the enemy team. Dinosaur Upgrade, which becomes more common the further you get in the story, is where a special variant Dinosaur appears and you need to kill it, and then your score during a certain amount of time (related to damage, dino kills, and support) increases the strength and will spawn higher difficulty variant dinosaurs for the opposing team. Even without these comeback mechanics you can definitely win when behind, even with an entire A.I. team (I literally have done this myself, 4 A.I. teammates vs a full team of players and I won.)There is supposed to be a PvE ONLY extreme difficulty mode called the "Savage Gauntlet", but it currently is not available until July 28th (currently writing this on July 21st, will update this with my personal take when the mode is available.) Savage Gauntlet is supposed to change weekly, and I'm personally interested about how hard it will be considering the difficulty of the base game can get pretty hard sometimes.As for the story, I wish there were more actual animated cutscenes for it. After finishing missions you unlock "lost data" which is collected in a menu that you can only access when not in a mission and most are a still image and sometimes text with the story characters talking or listening to audio logs. There are ACTUAL cutscenes that you have to play multiple missions to get to and they are actually very engaging and had some funny moments in them. Honestly this game's story does remind me a bit of how Monster Hunter's story progresses in those games. You kill a bunch of Dinosaurs, complete multiple missions/matches, and then you get story. Rinse and repeat. I'd give the story like...a 6 or 7 out of 10 so far. I'll change this when I finish the base story.There are loot boxes but they are COMPLETELY free and you get them from leveling up and you cannot purchase them with any real life money. There is a Battle Pass, called the "Survival Pass" and you do need to purchase it with real money, but it only gives you completely cosmetic items. There is a SINGLE "Head Start Kit" that lets you unlock 3 suits that are typically player level locked (Nimbus/Murasame/Vigilant) but as I said above not one suit is MILES above any others so I don't feel like it's very P2W, but you can totally disagree with me on that. Also it looks like there are going to be alternate colors/styles of Battle Pass/Surival Pass skins (currently there are 5) purchasable for real money, but again not P2W as these are completely cosmetic. Finally they have said that Battle Pass skins will EVENTUALLY become purchasable later, so if you pick up the game after a few seasons have passed you can purchase those skins that you may have missed (unsure if it will be with real currency, or in-game currency). I know microtransactions can be a huge turn-off for a lot of people, but there are PLENTY of base skins for each suit that can be unlocked completely free (9 Exosuit skins and 2 weapon skins for each suit) without putting a single extra penny into the game.There's also a roadmap already out for upcoming content, including new maps/modes/suit variants/ and rigs/modules (combat support tools/Exosuit Modification Items). Once the first set of Alpha variants drop on August 16th, the total cast of playable characters will go from 10 to 20. There's also already plans for Beta variants are set to be released whenever Season 3 drops, and if that's another 10 suits that will bring the total playable characters to 30. On top of those previous things, Season 2 is going to include a Crossover with Street Fighter 6, and Season 3 a crossover with Monster Hunter (typical Capcom titles collabing with other Capcom titles). So look forward to those things if you wanna try the game out and stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game. The gameplay loop is super fun, you bash dinosaurs, then either fight players or bosses or race other players for an objective or everything at once. This is a really creative competitive shooter. Optimization is actually insane. I can run the game maxed out with a 2080 super without a hitch on PC as well as a steady 60 fps with some dips to 45 during the worst of it on my steam deck.Decent optimization is rare these days and I do want to commend Capcom for it as all their releases recently have been very well optimized.The way the content is delivered is unique as well, like any competitive game you keep running the same mode repeatedly, yet as you progress new enemy types, new maps, new types of objectives all emerge along with a decent story.There are plenty of cosmetics to unlock just by playing the game which is great.I'm not a big fan of battle passes or early game monetization, but there's lots to unlock with the in game currency.The gameplay mechanics are clean they work well, each exo feels unique and suits a variety of different play styles. It's very reminiscent of overwatch and being able to swap characters on the fly.For consI think my biggest issue is one that's been addressed, it's the cross platform grouping, although you can play cross platform, you can't make a party with your friends if you are not on the same system. They did say they are working on it.Now for these reviews...I almost never write reviews, but in this case I had to because I see people reviewing after drinking bleach from a bottle labeled "bleach" and expecting Pepsi.The steam store says "online pvp" , the game was marketed and showcases as pvevp. It was never ever marketed as PvE exclusively. It was always meant to be a competitive game. Giving a negative review to a game for not being a PvE game when it never even pretended to be one is like going to a ramen restaurant and asking why they don't have any pizza and then literally flipping a table...Anyway, it's a great game, I'm looking forward to more content from it, hopefully monetization is controlled.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is a title that promises an immersive and engaging experience, but unfortunately, it fails to deliver on its lofty expectations. With a hefty price tag of $60, one would expect a game packed with content and replayability. However, after spending just five hours with the game, it becomes evident that it falls far short of its value proposition.Lack of Content and Value:One of the most glaring issues with Exoprimal is its lack of content. With a price point that suggests a robust and expansive experience, players are left feeling shortchanged. The game's content feels more suited for a 15$ price range, as there simply isn't enough to justify the higher cost. Within a mere five hours of gameplay, the game becomes monotonous and fails to hold the player's interest.Absence of Character Customization:Another disappointing aspect of Exoprimal is the absence of character customization. In a time where personalization and individuality are highly valued in gaming, the lack of options to tailor one's character to their liking is a significant oversight. This omission further contributes to the game's overall lack of depth and replayability.Repetitive Game Modes:The game modes in Exoprimal suffer from a lack of variety and innovation. Each match feels strikingly similar, with only minor changes to differentiate them. This repetition quickly becomes tiresome, leaving players craving more diverse and engaging experiences. The lack of fresh and exciting game modes greatly diminishes the game's longevity and replay value.Underwhelming Story Mode:The story mode in Exoprimal is a major letdown. It fails to captivate players and lacks the depth and narrative complexity that one would expect from a game of this caliber. The story mode feels rushed and poorly executed, leaving players feeling disconnected and uninvested in the game's overarching narrative.Unbalanced PvP Experience:One of the most frustrating aspects of Exoprimal is the unbalanced PvP experience. After spending a significant amount of time engaging in PvE activities, the PvP portion of the game lasts for a disappointingly short duration of 3-4 minutes. Additionally, the impact of completing objectives faster is rendered meaningless, as players can easily be steamrolled in PvP events. This lack of balance undermines the competitive aspect of the game and leaves players feeling frustrated and unfulfilled.Conclusion:In conclusion, Exoprimal is a title that falls far short of its price tag. With a lack of content, absence of character customization, repetitive game modes, underwhelming story mode, and unbalanced PvP experience, it fails to provide the immersive and engaging experience that players expect. It is advised to steer clear of this game, as there are far better options available that offer greater value for your money.﻿

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a couple of good things going for it, as well as a ton of awful things that prevent me from recommending it as it currently is. The best things about it imho are the graphics and the optimization, the animations are super smooth and clearly take A LOT from Monster Hunter, but I don't see that as a negative; the combat is fluid and I haven't encountered any game breaking bugs or crashes in the few hours I tried it. That's about all the praise I can give it.Now for the bad.. where do I start, it simply tries to achieve too much while delivering way too little. Let me explain in a little more detail what I mean:-From the very first moments, it tries to present itself as a story-driven game, but the story is as generic as it gets, and it's only "played out" in what seems like the tutorial. The rest of the story is just snippets of voicemail you have to access in a separate  menu, like, you know the diary pages and voicemails cassettes you find as environmental storytelling in a normal story-driven game? That's the main story in this game, and you access it through a separate menu section in between matches.-It tries to be a PVE third person shooter, but it offers so little variety that it doesn't encourage long term gameplay in the slightest. Also, it's a huge grindfest with slowcrawl progression and monetization in the form of battle passes, lootboxes, DLCs and whatnot. On a fully priced triple-A game. Also there's only like 1 mission type and it's hella repetitive after a while.-It tries to be a PVP hero shooter, but again, it lacks variety, not to mention balance.. honestly, the only good thing I found about the PVP part was the ability to turn into a dinosaur and fight the enemy team which kinda had some Evolve-esque vibes to it, but even then you only get to do that once per match, and only one person from your team gets to do it.I'm not saying this game is utter garbage, it shows potential but I don't think I'd buy it nor recommend it in its current state. Would I play it if it was free to play? Maybe, but even then, why would I play this over Warframe or something else?

_childDocuments_.review: THE GAME ADDS SIGNIFICANTLY MORE CONTENT AS YOU PROGRESS THE STORY.I DONT KNOW WHY CAPCOM DID IT LIKE THIS BUT ITS HOW IT IS.I've got ten hours in the game, so i think i'm entitled to review it.Exoprimal is a PvPvE hero shooter, where PvE takes form in objective-based, competition gameplay agaisnt the other team in two phases. The final mission being (at your choice, or at random) either a PvP-possible objective, or further, difficult PvE objectives.Catch on this wargame mode, is that during the final phase, you will be granted (or the enemy, depending on who's leading), a dominator. Using this lets you invade the enemy team's play area with a miniboss dinosaur likea t-rex  carnosaurus, etc, in order to hinder their progress. Think Destiny 2's gambit invasion if you need a direct reference, except you are a dinosaur.This will be the bread and butter most of the time. I do not yet know how the matchmaking choice on mission bases, but i suspect two factors may be involved: Average story progression% and the players' level average in the match. I've had times where i've had back to back, same type missions that you encounter at low playtime/progression, with a story-variant  mission or a 10-person pve megaboss event here and there.YES: the 10-person PVE mode exists. It's purely just progression and RNG whenever you get to play it or not. I find the way the missions are done somewhat confusing, if needlessly complicated, and capcom could have certainly done a better job with emGraphics are 'modern' to say. Nothing eye-gasmingly amazing, but nothing too horrible either. Enough to at least render two thousand raptors onto your screen with no problems.Game play, whilst repetitive, feels satisfying to myself at least. Certain Exoframes are more appealing to me, but there are many styles. My basic brain favors simple ones like Barrage, Deadeye or Funny Samurai man. When i played during the beta, Vigilant used to be my go-to due to sheer PvP damage it can dish out, but the frame has been turned into a pure glass cannon after the fact, everything kills her quite easily.As with all online games now days, or free-to-plays, the game has a battle pass system. Presumably 10$ being the standard price (i got the deluxe edition because of my beta impressions), i can say that if you plan to play the game, you will definitively get your money's worth, as it has been one of the most /generous/ battlepasses i've seen as of yet. The only way to progress it is..to play the game. No silly quests, no tracking 'bounties' to do specific games, you just play it, and the game dumps almost identical quantities of XP to both your Player level and the pass.As for the generosity remark: Far as i notice, you get an exoframe skin every three levels, with littered decals, emotes and weapon skins in between, and every ten levels or so, you get one of the many legendary skins available on the pass. Would i recommend it? Yes, BUT: If you got other games to play, or the patience to wait for a while, i recommend you do so definitively. If you got nothing else on your list, and are looking for a new game, not minding the light grindiness, then definitively give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I seriously love this game and everything it has to offer.  The characters, gameplay, story, visuals, and everything else is just fun.  Doesn't take itself to seriously and is a joy to experience.  All the exosuits are a blast to use and customize with some great looking cosmetics.  Unfortunately it seems a ton of the negativity surrounding this game seems to stem from misinformation, wishing that the game is something else entirely, issues from an abundance of micro transactions and some weird decisions how cross-play is represented in this game.  I agree with the latter two but almost all of the game was crystal clear from the developer streams and trailers.I love the way the game mixes PVP and PVE.  It's not the most balanced but this game isn't meant to be competitive past just playing the game like MP games of the olden days used to do.  There's no ranking system here, which makes it way more fun to just hop in and play both alone and with friends.Speaking of with friends, the one biggest flaw that this game has is a lack of cross-platform friends list features (and cross-save to some extent).  While the game does have cross-platform play, it does not allow you to form parties with your friends on other platforms (ex. Xbox App w/ Game Pass and Steam).  This sucks for me personally as that meant I did have to refund the game on steam just to play it on the Xbox App so I could play with the majority of my friends and will probably hamper the game in the future.  Even though I'm not the biggest fan of the micro transactions (Battle Pass, DLC Cosmetics packs and DLC Skip packs), they're at least priced much more fairly than a typical F2P title.  However this is not a F2P title but at least you can earn skins through gameplay without paying any extra pretty regularly.I highly recommend you try this game out for longer than a couple of matches (either via Game Pass or Steam).  Content is unlocked at a very steady rate and from what I've played in the betas and seen in the trailers, there's a ton more out there that early reviewers have not experienced yet.  Just be aware of the caveats that this game has, and don't be surprised if it isn't for you.  It's definitely gonna have a smaller than average player base but I hope this one can live on.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very obvious from reading a lot of the user reviews that most of them did not get far enough into the game, although I will admit this is likely due to the game's massive design flaws. It does at first seem like there is only one game mode; however, the more you play the game, the more modes you unlock, from takes on classics like escorting payloads and capturing control points, to more interesting fare, such as MMO-inspired raid battles where both teams set aside their differences and work together to take down one big, bad dinosaur using The Power of Friendship™ (my personal favorite missions). The issue is that the game does not make it immediately apparent that there IS more than one game mode, and while this appears to be done for very deliberate, story-related reasons that I will not spoil here but that are easily found online, I have to say, it really does the game a disservice. Personally, I enjoyed slowly unraveling the story and discovering why new game modes were being unlocked, but I can totally see why this would be a huge turnoff to some people, especially the casual crowd that is just wanting to jump in and out for some quick matches and/or those who are not interested in the story. And honestly, the story is a way bigger part of this game than it really advertises and I was pleasantly surprised to see a multiplayer game with such an interesting, albeit insanely cheesy, campaign - but it's completely understandable that some people don't even make it to this point since, on the surface, Exoprimal appears to be just another standard hero-based team shooter and those are typically very straightforward. The graphics are technically very impressive, although some of the environments are a little bland for my taste, and the sound design is great. Weapons feel good to use and a lot of the characters are insanely fun, but another huge ding against the game is that there just aren't enough characters. In combat, your customizable player character pilots giant mecha called "exosuits" to fight off the hoards of dinosaurs and/or the enemy team, and while each exosuit has their own unique play style, voice lines, cosmetics, etc., and the roster initially looks pretty large, in reality, there is a very small base roster of only 10 exosuits, with 4 DPS options and 3 each for tank and support. The remaining playable exosuits are α and β variants of each character, but there is great variability between how different the variants are from the base suit, so while some may feel almost like a different character entirely, others feel almost the same as the default exosuit, with only minor changes. This can feel disappointing and frustrating at times, and is made worse by the fact that you have to either buy the variants with real money, or grind for several hours to reach level 20 on what is essentially each character's "battle pass" that you level up by playing matches with that suit (battle passes that are free I might add, but don't you worry, there's paid seasonal passes too). So, depending on the number of variants you're interested in obtaining, you're looking at potentially hundreds of dollars spent buying each of them outright, or hours spent grinding to get each exosuit to rank 20.The rest of the game is largely fine. The story is extremely cheesy and tongue-in-cheek, often in a "so bad it's good" manner, reminiscent of straight-to-DVD B-movies playing on basic cable at 3 PM on a Saturday type of way. It's nothing groundbreaking, but I found it enjoyably dumb and interesting enough. The voice acting falls into the same category, being a hodgepodge of either perfectly adequate or laughably bad, as characters shriek at your sweet, dumb, doofy-looking silent protagonist in exaggerated Russian, Jamaican, and British accents. The progression system is unusual in that you unlock new cutscenes and story sequences by playing a certain number of matches; sometimes you may end up waiting in matchmaking for several minutes if you are being unknowingly queued into the next campaign mission, which can often lead to getting matched with bots or players who have already completed these missions. This can lead to some confusion, as you may occasionally get matched with a group doing a campaign mission you have already completed, and for some reason, every time you complete a campaign scenario, the same story-related cutscene plays when you exit the match. It took me a while to realize why I was occasionally finishing a match and seeing cutscenes I'd already seen before, and on more than one occasion I actually got matched with groups doing story missions I hadn't even unlocked in my own campaign, which led to me exiting a match and loading into a very confusing cutscene where the story had apparently jumped ahead with no explanation.Overall, I think Exoprimal is a great game, just one held back by some rather head-scratching decisions on CAPCOM's part. While I would say I definitely got more than my money's worth from Exoprimal, and I would argue the high production value warrants the $60 price tag, it is a paid entry in an over-saturated genre that has almost entirely pivoted to a F2P model, which is understandably off-putting to a number of players. Add to that the presence of paid DLC - and yes, the majority of it is obtainable with in-game currency, but there is some content locked behind four paid seasonal battle passes, as well as crossover content from other CAPCOM games - and the first impressions are, sadly, really not great. Even if one gets past these hurdles, the convoluted manner in which the story is told and locking alternative game modes and characters behind dozens of hours of playtime does little to help an already struggling game's reputation (to say nothing of the complete and utterly baffling lack of marketing). I have enjoyed my time with Exoprimal greatly, but I completely understand why it has the negative/mediocre word-of-mouth that it does, and as much as I would love to play with my friends, I can't fault them for not jumping into an exosuit to shoot up some dinos with me, especially now that it's been announced the game is "complete" and will not be receiving further content. Why it is obvious to thousands of average gamers the many reasons that Exoprimal failed to become the next big thing, but not to the million-dollar development company responsible for it floundering, is absolutely beyond me, but I sincerely hope that CAPCOM realizes how hard they dropped the ball on this game, how much potential it has, and revisit it in the future instead of letting it fade away into obscurity like so many other live service games these days. TL;DR - Great game held back by questionable choices, I'd get it on sale. Alternate game modes locked behind hours of progress. Small roster, 10 characters + 2 variants each & some variants are too similar to default. Paid DLC, including $40 worth of battle passes. Story is dumb fun, but told in a confusing way. Lack of fresh content going forward due to game being "complete."

_childDocuments_.review: I read a few reviews regarding Exoprimal having "rampant" or "excessive" monetization and wanted to comment because I was initially skeptical about that and what the nature of this game was as well. We've all found new titles or even old reboots that wind up being blatant cash grabs/soulless live services a plenty, theres no doubt. I find it disheartening every time.    One of the things I appreciate most about Exoprimal is the fact that you are rewarded for just playing the game. All the Exosuits and their variants are obtained by earning currency as a reward from finishing matches, leveling up your account/Exosuits. Everything is unlocked through in-game currency except the few, just IMO, mediocre season pass skins, stamps, and such. The many and arguably cooler skins otherwise aren't purchased with IRL money from an MTX store. There isn't even an MTX store in the game, nor is there a premium currency or subscription rewarding XP boosters or exclusive items. Just a season pass with silly emotes, dances, and skins, currently Security Guard Zephyr, Barrage in surf shorts and others...    Instead, all skins including legendary ones are thrown at you for playing via chests and credits when your account levels up every few matches. Leveling your Exosuit up earns you mods, credits to upgrade your suits and mods, and unlocks Exosuit variants which change that suits weapon. You don't pay a dollar for chests either, they are simply earned behind level ups. Thats it.    Rampant monetization is when a game launches a list of ads you spam close after every single match. Excessive monetization is releasing Exosuits and Mods that you have to pay IRL money for, or making the grind or power differential so steep that you can't reasonably afford the time to keep up with other players power without thinking about paying for catch ups or upgrades/xp, even to the point where they release arguably identical versions of characters or weapons with an extra arbitrary star or rank locked behind premium/paywall. To the point where you might be PvPing against or PvEing with people with gear you can't touch without paying $29 upfront or it being part of some payed pass. Or even instances where you can't even try a new character before paying for them. Games that hide behind EA with barely functioning systems, abundance of bugs save for the fully functioning MTX store from day 1. Its pricing your in game items for 1150 points when you can only buy  1100 points at a time without buying more than you want/need. BS gouging strategies straight out of a textbook.Exoprimal doesn't have any of that.     That was an unexpected surprise to me. Advertisement wise, Exoprimal has a small rectangular window on the bottom right of the home page that flicks through 4-5 ads about news, updates, season pass contents, new suits, emotes, etc, no MTX store, anything purchasable just links to the steam store. The UI is silent and unflagrant relative to other games that treat whatever your eyes can see like FOMO real estate.    To me, skins and emotes are totally besides the point, but I wanted to address that specifically. I tried the Exoprimal demo earlier this year, and was less interested while having my own reservations towards the quality of the game since then especially upon releasing as a full price title ($79.99 CAD). In the little I had heard and seen of this game recently, I was still genuinely suspicious of its prospect in seeming like it could just be another half-baked momentary live service.    So my expectations were not high to begin with, but they were definitely surpassed considering how much I enjoy the game play, team play, progression, and specifically how little incentive there is to pay for anything more when all of that is tied neatly together. At level 86 I'm still unlocking mods and variants through progression rewards every game and still seeing 10-30 second queue times every day and night on PC since the matches are cross platform. 10 new suits were released to unlock since the update went live this morning, unlocking them and slowly but surely upgrading them, learning their play styles and potentials with other suits is a big part of what I like about Exoprimal.    My experience has been this funny incidence of waivering a lot of my initial expectations in satisfaction of what was being presented. Some of the main things that I didn't initially realize or expect but enjoyed while progressing and trying out Exoprimal after playing it to this point were the following:    You unlock new maps and differing scenarios as you progress through the story. Your story progression is dependent on the amount of matches you have played, not apparent right away.After a certain point early on, you can choose to queue up for PvE only, Guaranteed PVP encounter, or Random Queue in the main game mode called Dino Survival which gives a slight bonus to match rewards.Sometimes the match will throw you and the enemy team together for a 10vZ raid encounter.Seeing players go way beyond the level 20 reward track with their favorite exosuits up to level 100, accounts level 350+ playing the Savage Gauntlet mode competitively for placement on the leader boards or just for fun.And switching suits mid match to accommodate more dangerous encounters you become familiar with over time (ie: PvP/Large Dinos)Relatively small but very active player base.    If you enjoy those aspects in other shooters like this, any and all of those activities are how you upgrade your Exosuits and mods over time, including earning the overwhelming majority of all that secondary stuff like skins and emotes like I keep reiterating. Its nothing fancy or incredible, and it does get repetitive (kinda like this review) due to a lack of game mode variety currently, but its certainly not egregiously trying to sell you skin upon skin. I don't understand why or how some of the reviews are complaining about how that ISN'T the case. I found the story to be totally generic and skippable, but thats OK with me, I wasn't under the impression that Exoprimal was the second coming of Regina and Gail. That all being said, even with today's content update, I would say Exoprimal is still now slightly overpriced without more than the two game modes currently offered. Over all though, the unexpected amount of fun and interest relative to my initial impression is in itself why I wanted to drop by and say this is far from what I would label soulless cash grab or anything like that at the very least. Time will tell if the next content update justifies the asking price for this game and whether or not it can earn more players. Adding 10 variants for 20 suits total now was sick. They call them Alpha Variants, and they plan to release 10 more Beta Variants in the future. Cool. Before then, I think Exoprimal still needs different game types and lacks features in terms of long term replay value. Its not currently lacking more new skins and juiced up season pass rewards. Maybe Capcom will indeed lean in that more monetized direction in the future, it would be classic of them, but so far it has been surprisingly the opposite with no expectation of it lasting nor changing.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is a lot of fun. The game play loop is fairly simple and the missions overall are a little repetitive. However they do have an ok variety of events during the missions. The game runs smooth on my computer rig of almost 8 years old on high settings and there are very few visual hiccups. Most of them happen on loading into the initial loading area and mission area. During game play is quite smooth. The game isn't pay to win, the few things you do buy with in game currency are things you can get enough of to buy in 2-3 missions. Especially in the beginning when you are constantly leveling up your player level, Exosuit level, and this version of a season pass. Overall the game is a lot of fun, you go around shooting and exploding dinosaurs for the first 4 parts of the mission, and then you get a final mission that may or may not be PVP depending on if you chose to include those missions or not. The only time the enemy team can mess with you other than the PVP specific last missions is when each team gets to summon a large dinosaur and control it while it gets teleported near the enemy team or sometimes you can complete an event that increases the difficulty on the enemy side.One of my favorite final missions I've seen so far would be the cooperative missions where both teams come together and essentially fight a Raid Boss ala MMORPG style. Complete with hiding behind large pillars during aoe party wipe attacks, and jumping or maneuvering away from targeted or sweeping attacks.The game is great, however the only thing that really holds it back is the gameplay loop. As I said it is pretty simple, and honestly not worth 60 bucks. Maybe they will add a bunch more free into the game that will make it worth that price, but right now, either wait for a sale, or until they add a content update or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Horde shooter, Hero shooter, exosuits, dinosaurs. This game has everything I could ask for in a 5 v 5 multiplayer game. It takes a few games to get the hang of it, but just when you do, the game starts throwing spicier twists at you. New dinos, new game modes, new mechanics. It doesn't stop, all the way to the end of the story.Oh yeah, they added *Story* to my Dino Punching game. It's really good, too. You always get a new piece of dialogue or a cutscene after a mission, and I'm glad you can binge all the cutscenes you've unlocked after you're done playing with your mates - no cutscene walls slowing down the evening of pub stomping (or being stomped). Yeah the characters feel like one-note caricatures or stereotypes, but they get fleshed out to a point where they feel more like the people those stereotypes were based on.The ability to switch suits mid game (hells, mid *fight* if you're daring enough) is huge as you can swap off a tank to a DPS if the situation calls for it, or swap to the counter class to an opponent's shopwrecker. Or even have one suit for PvE and another for the PvP section.Overall, i thoroughly recommend this game when it's on sale - $30-$40 for this game is a very reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game where you have to hunt dinos with and against other exosuit pilots.Story progression is necessary to unlock more dinos and more stages. This design is good because if you had to fight stealth dinos, sniper dinos and ability blocking dinos from the start; this game would have the Dark Souls of "X" meme all over it. Which I still wouldn't mind cause I like the game play loop. Pick a suit and start blasting some dinos.The story is entertaining and mainly serves a purpose as to why the game opens up slowly. The AI Leviathan is slowly collecting Exosuit data to further enhance development on it's pet project so, It overtime increases the variety of dinos you fight. As you play through the missions you'll get data packets that'll expand on the story, Just go to the database tab to view more. You'll still get cutscenes that progress the story; no need to to look at the database if you do not want to. You do get some really good battles where instead of competing for bonus existence you can fight together against whatever Leviathan has cooked up.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I'm not sure what people expected. This game was pretty transparent with what it was. PvEvP. You complete objectives (killing dinosaurs) while racing against the enemy team with the occasional ability to invade the enemy team as a dinosaur or straight up fight the team in certain game modes.The battlepass is not necessary, just gives you some cosmetics and occasionally more currency to customize your rigs loadout, but you get more than enough to get everything you want even without it.The suits are pretty well varied and they already have plans for alpha versions of them next month which appear to change the primary weapons. I'm fairly certain they plan on adding suits going into the future.They appear to plan on adding more and varied content as they move forward, but it's not super clear.The story model is a bit weird and tacked on. As you play the game, you get more lore unlocks and occasional cutscenes. At certain thresholds you reach "critical missions" where the stakes are raised and you will start experiencing more advanced missions.I haven't seen it yet, but at some point there are purely PvE missions where all 10 players fight a boss. They also plan on adding a horde mode in 2 weeks.The game has room to improve, sure. I think it should have started with significantly more content, but I'm greatly enjoying the core features.

_childDocuments_.review: OVERALL RATING FOR A FILTHY CASUAL 7.5/10WHY I LIKE IT SO FAR....I had to find which character worked for me because my first two games were no fun, but once I found one that worked for me its a GAME CHANGER. Also if you die in game you can change your exosuit MID-GAME which is PHENOMENAL.I swapped to a tank build which I normally don't enjoy but it has been great! I've been getting MVP a majority of the time and love it. The matches aren't painfully long either so its nice if you want to play a game with matches, but don't have hours at a time. or are awaiting something like Doordash, or are burning time till an appointment or phone call.The level up system feels rewarding. You can level up different pieces of your gear independently which I LOVE because it allows for VERY customized builds that you could tweak based on whether you are playing with friends who you know excel in different areas that allow you to focus in others, or a well rounded survival build for playing with randos. The rate at which you gain coins to buy skins and decals also isn't a PAINFUL grind like it is with most games (I don't mind a moderate grind but I have a full time job and chores so I cannot dedicate more than a few hours a day to a game. and if the grind is brutal I either resign myself to not ever buying anything, or it bothers me so much I just don't play the game)The UI is well thought out. I love how clear and concise everything I've looked for has been to find (so far). Nothing feels super hard to figure out. As someone who NEEDS subtitles I love all the options available to customize how you want to see them (color, size, background).The FPS mechanics feel very good, hit boxes don't feel brutal as a character that punches but it also isn't too hand-holdy when aiming a gun. The dino physics are HYSTERICAL when you YEET them across the map with a punch.Overall really like this game! COMPLAINTS....I do wish it was a little cheaper so more of my friends would be wiling to try it. or if it had a free trial of some kind?I'm a liiiitle disappointed that I picked the feminine and all I hear are male voice lines.And I'm more than a little bummed that none of the skins for my character are appealing (to me personally). I feel like if the game does well they likely have plan to add more skins down the line or at least that is my hope.I do worry that this game, while SUPER FUN is going to die out fairly quickly ( >6 months) if they don't add seasonal games, random events, etc. Something that will spice up the variety of the gameplay. Maybe more maps, weird dinos, capture the flag like events, timed events, character lock events, etc.If the Devs read this, I AM a filthy casual so don't take my complaints to heart, any dino game is better than no dino game. Also I freaking hate pterasaurs. Slippery bastards.

_childDocuments_.review: For now I am rating this a YES, simply because I am enjoying time played with friends, but here is a more realistic breakdown if it is to help anyone:***THE BAD***The game should be free to play or only cost $20, as day one the developers have shown they are gonna flood with micro transactions. A $10 season pass at release, a $15 head start bundle to instantly get characters locked by progression, & $5 cosmetics that are reskins of the battle pass skins.Early game play is EXTREMELY repetitive, but opens up as you level up and the more you play by providing new levels, new enemy types, new modes, etc. No sole PVE mode, no matter what you do, you are against an enemy team, even in the so called PVE game type.Main story seems...random at best. There are story cutscenes that are triggered by playing certain missions, but the missions seem to spawn randomly and can be repeated at any time.Loot boxes.***THE GOOD***Class type versatility is great and definitely provides needs for appropriate team comps to allow for a competitive drive against the enemy team.Each suit adapts to different play styles so it seems there is a fit for everyone's style of play.Loot boxes are free to open fortunately and don't need a key or grinding to access components to unlock.High octane action.The lore and story can be experienced on anyone's schedule as it is largely told through a database that is accessed in the main menu.Allows for 5 player teams so it is easy to grab friends and vibe in a squad while slaying dinosaurs.For now these are my biggest gripes and highlights, but we all seek something different in gaming. I will say, if you buy this and look to test it before the 2 hour mark for a refund, you won't even experience 1/4 of the overall game. It feels intentionally designed this way to reduce refund costs. If you manage to catch a sale on this game, I do highly recommend it as it is a great way to kill time and just have a blast.
