_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite what I was expecting or what was advertised...BUT....TLDRIf you're into horde shooters and coop, this game spins it in it's own way. While I've yet to see anything ground breaking or epic in terms of gameplay, it is a solid "s'hmup" and weirdly implemented pve or pvevp that has some interesting mechanics that are tried and true.Essentially, you are one member of a 5 man team of exosuit wearing characters sent into combat with each other at the benefit of an AI that seems to dump dinosaurs on you. It definitely has given me some Metal Gear Kojima type vibes with the weird story but I'm not playing it for the story, I'm here for the drip and the teamplay.PVP is "optional" and pits you against a team of similarly equipped players that are racing against you to make it to the end of a mission zone. Once you get there, the pvp is thrown in for a short period of time. I've really not experienced anything quite like it, but there is a handicap thrown into the mix wherein one of the opposing team members will be given an opportunity to wreck havoc against your team if you're outperforming them by transforming into a dinosaur. That part is legitimately fun and if you know what you're doing, you can easily stall the enemy team and watch your team progress past them. Past this, the aesthetics are nice, I do think it's intentionally over the top in terms of glitz and cosmetics, but that's part of what makes coop games interesting; giving a player a timesink that grants them the ability to make their in-game avatar customized to their liking. The reward system seems fair.Onto the bit that leaves a bad taste in my mouth. Microtransactions and season passes. I hate that ♥♥♥♥. It's thrown in your face right out of the gate. Full price for the game is enough and with the current world we live in as gamers, there are plenty of other options out there that don't make you feel unworthy of the same rewards as another player that handed over another chunk of change. In the end, it's your hard earned money, you get to decide. Anyways, this is long enough. What you see is not quite what you get and it's lacking polish and content imo. It's new though and perhaps that's just the beginning of their concept. I'm not thumbing it down for now, because I prefer games like these and have a soft spot for intense wave combat, which it does do well, even if it makes absolutely no damned sense the entire time. Best of luck and see you in game.

_childDocuments_.review: The one thing I can say about this game is that it was not what I was expecting at all. It just kept giving. I read a lot about people getting bored from this game but so much changes as you play more that I really don't see how. I just finished the game and have done two savage gauntlet runs when writing this. + Differing Game modes that occur at random+ PvPvE and can decide if you would rather have pvp or pve endings+ Dope Exosuits w/ way diff styles of playing (like MH weapons)+ Fun Dinos Appear Later ;)+ An Interesting Story+ Dope Skins+ Sick Emotes- Another Time Loop story o_o- When playing solo it is pretty tough to get into full games- No crossplay invites but is Crossplay?- Too many audio logs, even though I love listening it can be annoyingIt's another asymmetrical, team coordinated shooter, akin to Overwatch. But they throw in obstacles. PvE mixed in with your PvP. I love that. I need more of that. I am so tired of the trope of just being sent straight in me against people who are able to put in more time than me in a competitive game. Having the dinos kind of adds that complexity that can give anyone the edge in a moment. I saw a lot of people saying they got tired of Dino Survival after like 5 games, but those people must have very short attention spans and these types of games may not be for them. That's fine. But this game is anything but not exciting. Every so many missions they throw in cutscenes or wild events until later in the game you just start going into new maps entirely.Think Metal Gear Rising or DMC5. Heavy riffing guitar with digitized beats behind it. Very fun. Nothing that you get chills over but definitely entertaining to listen to. There were a few good tracks in moments of the story that made me go wow, but thinking back on them, nothing really stuck. But when you hear them, they're great.The story is another time loop head scratcher. I really liked the story. I REALLY liked it. It was funny when it needed to be. It was emotional when it needed it to be and the ending was satisfying. I would definitely like to see more story from it.The world is our world, but in 2040- after an apocalyptic event where vortexes opened everywhere and destroyed everyone. It's a fine trope. But the trope I really liked was the exosuit lore. <3 It goes deep.RE ENGINE GO BRRRRRRR. I love it.No crossplay invites, but crossplay? I hate that.It also has issues trying to find rooms when playing solo. There should also be a ranked added! Would be super fun for pvp'ers. Otherwise, it is very fun and the multiplayer had very little issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game's earlier beta--as well as its full release--very concerned about their PvEvP approach to the game flow. In practice, though, it's been incredibly fun, and I think it will help the game's longevity going forward to have that competition between the teams. There's a lot of depth to be found in both your character choices as well as your loadout and traits. I would like there to be more variety in which objectives are spawned on your way to the final mission, but I've found myself always enjoying that last fight--whether it's joining forces with the other team, racing to complete our objective first, or fighting them head-to-head in teamfights.I do want to say, however, that I think releasing the game at full-price with a battle pass and whatnot for this sort of experience may not be the right call. A PvP game like this that relies on a healthy population would benefit immensely from the base experience being f2p. While I don't regret my purchase, I know the price tag is going to be a hard pill to swallow.

_childDocuments_.review: i'm going to go through the misinformation because it has been insanely high for this game for some reason in particular.i doubt anyone will see this since the negative reviews with less than an hour played Took the top spot, people didn't research it at all and decided it was bad or not what they decided they wanted or thought it should be when they saw a handful of screenshots, it isn't. it runs beautifully the matchmaking works really well and it continues to be a blast here are some key things with now around 13 hours played.-Loot boxes- exist but you cannot buy them, you get them when you level your account and after lvl 50 you get one every single level.This is ACCOUNT LVL not battlepass level those are different. everyone gets these. These items can be got from earned coins in game and or you can wait and hope to get them out of the box. IT IS ALL COSMETIC. is Free and is included with every version of the game. They ARE NOT BOUGHT WITH REAL MONEY. its just a nice little free bit of stuff as you progress. i cant stress enough there is no paid Loot boxes. -Lack of Content- No this is not the case Its a slow burn for some but as you continue on and progress the story by just, you know playing the game, more and more maps open, more dinosaurs, more variations, more Combat scenarios, More 10 player raids, more variations on 10 people raids. Some of these 10 player sections are sick. They are some of the coolest parts of the game for sure and some of those scenarios created show so much potential for both pvp and pve its fantastic. the Idea is you are forced to compete by a rogue AI and he increasingly throws harder and weirder variants at you. i believe the game slowly introduces you to them because when these things come up you need to adapt. which brings me to my next point. -hero shooter. Yes there are classes and heroes in the game but the beauty of this game is the variation to each of them and the reason for the slow progression is teaching you not to stick with one and just only play that, the Adaptability of this game is the Strongest point of it. deciding to switch, when to switch, what rig to switch you can do all this practically on the fly and is necessary to win the games. Sticking to just one character is not a good idea and it really limits you for what is being offered. learning to play to the teams needs is important and incredibly fun if you can set yourself aside and do whats best for the group.-Pay to win/ Weak upgrades No again this is not how it works, you unlock upgrades as you level your account some of which are suite wide so you can put them on any suite as you play specific ones more often you get upgrades to different abilities of that suites abilities and those ones are super powerful if used properly but again YOU CANNOT Spend real money to buy these and are crucial to the late game but still with a good player are not extreme kill shots anything of that nature they allow you to spec each suite more varied to the abilities you prefer and variations to them, honestly think of the suite wide ones to something like monster hunter where if you Slot in high tier earplugs you can reduce or nullify the effects of roars here its similar to lower gems in that game like less knockback, faster recovery time quicker reloads. -PvP yes this is a pvp centered game at its core at the moment but it really isn't, from narrative you are being forced into it and it unfolds in some interesting ways. that said as you play the pvp becomes more and more fun the more you mess around with each class and again see what is needed in each situation. again adaptability. you can turn the tides of a match in this section or fumble it completely. but that is the nature of the game to start and i believe its done this way from the narrative In two weeks we are getting the PVE mode but i think all this helps to get acclimated with the game types and the suites to be prepared for it because i dot think it will be easy this is not a relaxed en-devour it gets really really intense and i imagine it only goes up from here which for people sticking with it i think were in for a real treat. -Paid Dlc on the store. This is the last thing ill touch on because it seems like people are super upset that there is dlc day one on the store, all the items you can pay for are in the battle pass just color swapped, if you want them and don't want to get the battle pass you can just buy the one you want albeit a different color but obviously none of this is needed. The Headstart is exactly what it says it is you can pay for the option to play suits earlier if you want to but all those suites are available in the game and you can get them as you play and level your account. to put it into perspective you get all these before level 50 and i'm at lvl 54 with right around 13 hours played which to be honest feels completely reasonable time frame. again making you try new suites as you get them because you should be swapping. none of them are over powered compared to another its really just situation dependent and the farther you get along you will see that. Another key note to mention is this was free on gamepass and even though there are deals set there for that they still need some way to gather revenue from people who did not buy the game outright and it makes sense to do it this way AGAIN none of this stuff is necessary you can get all of it in the game by playing a very reasonable amount of time. I like this game a lot, I liked the betas I enjoy what it’s offering and it could use improvement for sure but one thing I think people are missing when they say it lacks the content is that the matches get progressively harder the more you play it, you start to see more and different variations of dinosaurs and it gets more involved. The pvp aspect is not a huge setback the way it seems and I think the idea of racing to get to a completion with good teamwork is a good idea at its core. And if nothing else is something new and pretty different in this space. Is it perfect? No but they’ve listened already and done some quick turn around on some aspects which isn’t easy to do and I think as time goes on they’ll continue to make interesting changes. Honestly to me the biggest misstep they made is not having cross platform parties at launch, I also think that this isn’t entirely on capcom and more on the platform holders. I paid $55 for the deluxe edition through humble and I’m enjoying it quite a bit. But if nothing else try it on gamepass and see if you like what’s here.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun concept that was horribly mismanaged.60 Euro baseprice is not worth it at all. This should be priced 30 at most on release.most of the characters are locked if you only buy the base game and unlocks are horrificly slow. After 10 hours ive unlocked 3 new characters out of a roster of 12+ unlockable ones. Most of these barely change gameplaywise but some later ones do quite drastically.The PvP is awful. Enemies teleport frequently. Its super laggy and theres nothing you can do about it.The big dinosaurs have terrible hitboxes. If a T-Rex swings his head then everything in a huge CUBE in front of it dies. Most matches also feature PvP as a Dinosaur so now you got teleporting t-rexes with broken hitboxes.The characters themselves are poorly balanced. Some of them are borderline mandatory in certain situations like the taunt + shield. The game encourages an overwatch like character swap system in the middle of the match where youre supposed to change to optimize the time to kill. Nobody ever charnges. Even if you got a good comp you actually need people to do the thing theyre supposed to do. Most of the time they dont. Without a dedicated group youre kinda just screwed.The game does a terrible job at giving the player feedback in general. The only metric you get at the end of a round is "score". This "score" is completely arbitrary and for example blocking with the shield gives obscene amounts. But it doesnt matter if youre actually blocking relevant damage. You can legit press block in front of a horde of weak mobs and go afk and get top scores despite being completely worthless.No ingame text chat function. But voice chat exists (not sure why youd ever turn that on, guess if you dont like your ears you can).MehYou do get to beat up huge waves of dinosaurs with mechs. So yea.. amazing concept but just bad everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the story for Exoprimal. This game has a lot of potential story and gameplay wise! The new missions, maps, and dinosaurs you will encounter are a absolute blast to experience! You unlock new modes, maps, and dinosaurs to fight as the game progresses. Every 5 matches you will get a new cinematic that will involve a boss fight with all ten players, a new map, or gamemode! I really enjoyed how the progression in this game works and I encourage others to stick with it! The only micro transaction in the store is to buy the battlepass and cosmetics for suits for the suits. Loot boxes are in this game for cosmetics, however they are not obtainable by purchasing them. You can only earn them by leveling up.The gameplay is highly addictive with every new match being just as great as the last! I personally really enjoy the suit, "Kriegor." You can swap suits mid game while on the battlefield allowing you to switch your play style whenever you would like. The suit transferring animations and amazing to watch and I really enjoy being able to swap suits while in game. The beginning of the PVP matches goes as each team of five race in parallel universes to get their missions done the quickest. Once a team as completed all of their missions, they get transported to the same universe with the other team and it is now a race to complete what the objective might be. Such as, payload, zone control, energy pick up, etc. The team who gets their missions done the quickest will be at the shared universe before the other team giving them a slight advantage in whatever the gamemode is. Customizing your suits are fun. There are a lot more skins that are not shown available for purchase (only obtainable in loot boxes). You can give your suits augments they give them bonuses, such as faster reloading, faster movement, more health, less damage from dinosaurs, etc. They each have their own unique augments specific for that suit. None of them are game breaking to the point where you blame the enemy player for winning because they had said augment. They provide a unique change of playstyle that is not too impact full to be game breaking or a balance issue for PVP.Small rant to negative reviews, steam shows to not have a not-so active player base of under 5k. However this game is cross platform and a majority of players are on consoles. I get in matches in under seconds never having to wait long to play! I recommend this game for anyone who likes shooting a endless amount of dinosaurs with a fun pvpve gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: very addictive cycle of fun with dinosaurs. Ignore most of the negative reviews, they were from people who played the beta whom didn't want to pay for the videogame and wanted it to be a free to play trash minefield of players.Instead, we got a great game.. with easily playable multiplayer, just queue up and near instant grouped play, on any selection of dino survival. The game looks and plays like a dream, a mashup of several different formats all seamlessly put into one.I was skeptical when i preordered it, i never played the beta, since it was much much different then the final product. But this game is well worth the purchase, even without having the battlepass myself i have more then pleanty of mechs to play, and the rest are unlockable with levels anyways, there are like 4 locked till you hit certain player levels but this is for a reason: each mech you already has needs to be played repeated matches, so you can learn your mech and its strengths and weaknesses already to properly harness them, so the end mechs for each branch are locked up till you figure out how to "get gud"People complain about the battlepass, but hey.. they need to pay for the server, and sense none of us are forking up our hard earned cash to keep the servers online completely buying them out for capcom, i fully understand the need for one. Just paying the price of the game doesnt help with that as they do need to pay their employees who made this game for us and worked the long hours, then the rest goes to company to keep the lights on.. everyone here knows how finances work. and they arent slaves for our gaming pleasure, so those idiots can shut up and move along.graphics: top notch, fps: very VERY stable and fluid animations and no slowdowns. I'm using a i9-9900kf and a 2080ti, but im sure most recommended set rigs can get the same amazing graphics, and frames that I am easily, afterall it is using the same engine as resident evil village and re4 remake, so you had a great time with that which im sure most did you will with this.Have not noticed in over 30 or more matches any bit of latency issues, i have a 1gbit though with 50 or 60mbit uploads, so ymmvall in all its a refreshing approach to pvp and pve and pvevp gameplay, you can choose any of them you prefer to complete the main story, and after the story is done (which i havent even scratched the surface of so far) you still have fun short matches that keep the tension going and pleanty of stuff to progress on every single mech in your repritore as well as the next mechs they introduce into the game later on (which they are working on now) which wont cost a penny either.bravo capcom! a silent winner this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, i really do, it's very innovative and ambitional from Capcom to make a game like this.The dinosaurs are really cool, the mech suits which are litteral characters are fun (Nimbus is one of the best healers designed in a hero shooter i have ever seen, trust me i played a lot of healers on these type of games) the story is not that decent but who cares in a adrenaline-filled action shooter game like this.Once you start unlocking endgame contents, the game is just insanely good and is in my top 5 best video games moments of all time, especially the final boss.Sadly the game has suffered from many things at launch which resulted in players leaving or getting a refund.The story, that's where the problems began if we think about it, let me explain :all the content is locked behind players progression levels, you get matched with 9 others players everytime you start a game, all of these players need to have done certains key story quests in order to keep progressing your own story pace or else you will have to do older missions, and that's the main issue.You keep doing the same missions over and over for 6-7 hours straight without new dinosaurs or events just because someone has not progressed enough in the lobby. Simply put, this is what killed the game, the first impression that the games offers just suckass.A lot of players also didn't like the forced PvP, i personally enjoyed it but it's totally understandable that people disliked it, some 5v5 were just team dependent and you could be crushed to oblivion by good players on the enemy team.In my opinion, one way to help the game (not save) would be to put the game on Free2Play.It's important to note that the devs cares a lot about this game since they keep doing content that adds bosses, events, collabs, they doubled all the numbers of playable characters since launch for more diversity.I had a great time and was lucky enough to play this game (Story + some extras for 30 total hours with a friend) while it was at it's prime, thank you Capcom for this wild game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, I like robots.Exoprimal feels like a racing version of Destiny 2 Gambit and a warframe lite.I absolutely adore this game and worry for its longevity.(I know you can see on steam its a low player count)However it seems the player base for console as of current is still very healthy since cross platform carries this game for pc. Mix of PS5 and xbox players make matchmaking quite fast.Gameplay is always 4 or 5 small phases or round in 2 sets, first set is pve only and even with pve only selected for matchmaking(pvp if selected you fight over players while moving your objectives while contested in the second round.), thats where player invasions come in, on the second half. You get a chance in 1/4 of the phases in the second round to pickup an item to invade the other team as a T-rex or other large bipedal dinosaur. Point is to just kill your targets as fast as possible per phase and invasions are to halt the enemy team if you use it in fights that yield a bigger advantage to overwhelm them.The game has a bunch of characters and even added a new set that modifies their weapons to be different or change their playstyle slightly.I've been enjoying Nimbus and Nimbus alpha variants quite a lot. Hybrid dps/healers are always so versatile.If the price is driving you away from trying the game, just blame capcom and hope it goes on sale sometime soon. This game is very casual and enjoyable for me, I hope it lasts longer than gundam evolution did in terms of a live service.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I would have been SO mad if I'd paid $60 for this. SKIP IT.On paper, this should be a game I'd die for. It's got dinosaurs, it's got mechs, you could theoretically play it PvE... However none of that coalesces into a whole I'm willing to spend time playing. Not for free, and CERTAINLY not for "AAA" game price. The best XP rates are locked behind playing "random" matchmaking between PvE and PvP modes, the customization is non-existent unless you engage with the Overwatch/Fortnite/[insert Live Service Game here]-style shop mechanics, and the gameplay itself is... fine. It feels less like a game carried on the intrinsic fun of gameplay and more like a Minimum Viable Product shipped as a vehicle for the store. But then, the store is so bare-bones and M.V.P. itself that it feels tacked-on and careless. Am I "grinding" the game for terrible cosmetics dealt out via loot boxes, or am I playing dolly-dress up in the hangar so that I can show off in the trite 3rd person shooter? Capcom doesn't know the answer to that design question, and definitely doesn't care. They're the ones with -at the very least- hundreds of thousands of dollars invested in this project. If they don't care, why should I?I could barely finish the tutorial sequence, there was just no flow and so little driving me forward. Setting up my player avatar was both slow and lacking in options. Then getting introduced to the controls had like 3 cutscenes of my silent protagonist pantomiming at the camera followed by a very on-rails explanation of how to click on things. I got told once how to activate abilities, but not what they do or why I'd use them over simply holding down the 'fire' button. The ability selected for demonstration, and the enemies chosen as targets didn't seem like a sensible pairing, either. I know it's a weird complaint, but it's indicative of the lack of attention paid to the assembly of the game. For reference: you get this big railgun on your back, and that's the swappable ability they chose to demonstrate. The enemies selected are flying Pteranodons. They're very clearly chaff-style high-volume targets, easily killable with most suits' primary fire. Thus, using your huge railgun ability on them raises a number of issues: For one, it feels like using a battleship cannon to scare away seagulls. They'd have died anyway, so the ability use feels like "Overkill". The ability is a straight-line piercing projectile and the enemies are a cluster of highly mobile targets. It's not a good tactical use of your chosen weapon against this situation. If they split up, or hover around in clusters, your railgun won't hit everyone and you'll be waiting on a cooldown to try again. You don't want to use a precision weapon here, you want something like an airburst AOE attack or a shotgun/flak-style projectile weapon. You *could* make the case that precision weapons allow you to pick them off one-at-a-time from a distance, but you'd want to use a weapon or ability with lots of follow-up shots or fast recharge. Finally, I'm also at a loss as to how much damage the railgun actually deals. Chaff enemies can be killed by theoretically anything, so the fact that this weapon instant-kills them doesn't tell me much. I tried it out later on a larger target, and dealt X% damage to it. That can be very hard to quantify and especially so when this is a chaotic team-based horde shooter. Is it worth bringing the big cool railgun? I don't know. You can kill a big procession of bunched-up raptors (a situation the tutorial assembles for you elsewhere but DOES NOT combine with the Railgun explanation), but I can't tell you if its utility overall or its damage-dealing potential makes it any better or worse than the mobility tool or "health pack" items you could swap it for. They aren't teaching me a sensible use for this ability, so why demonstrate it at all? It checks the box in the Game Dev checklist that says "you must show a player how to do a thing", so they gave me something to use my ability on and told me which button to press. The only problem is that I'm not learning WHY I'd want to use this in a real combat situation, so the only useful information passed along is the button mapping.This kind of mindlessness is present EVERYWHERE in this title. The UI is functional, but conforms to every convention that comes to mind when I say "sci-fi HUD". The characters you meet are stock stereotypes, which again is fine in a vacuum (and even preferable/beloved in some instances, such as in the context of Street Fighter/Monster Hunter). The objectives of  every mission are THE oldest and most established shooter tropes: Push the Thing, Stand in the Area, Shoot All the Bad Guys Until They Stop Spawning. The spaces you explore are... I guess *technically* varied, but they don't really make a lot of sense. You're not defending hastily-evacuated city streets, it's all simulated recreations (or you're sent back in time to specific battles that all seem to take place on a single island at various points during an emergency, it can be hard to tell because you're likely not meant to think about it too much). So you might be "On The Docks" in one mission, shooting through warehouses and piers, and in another you might be in a "city block" map. Maybe if you sink more time in, you'll play the missions that play in the "digital dimension" or deep in the jungle or whatever, but it's all just set dressing for the "lanes" and "arenas" you'll be fighting through. It all just rolls off of your mind, you might as well be playing the 'Grey Box' renderings of these spaces.What I mean to point out is that it's hard to know or care about the stakes of the action, because these aren't the streets of anywhere in particular. You're not saving New York or Tokyo or Hong Kong or Amsterdam. I *genuinely* can't tell if you're even in The Real World *at all* during gameplay. You might be simulated entirely, or you might be time-traveled to a real place at a previous time. It's impossible to know, and that *would* be fun as a narrative bit, if it weren't for the fact that all the action I saw revolved around a completely isolated and made-up island. Everyone on it, every building there, it was all built FAR from regular human civilization with the express purpose of building, researching, and sustaining their own version of SkyNet. So we might be fighting before, during or after the moment that the AI 'went rogue'. We might be caught in its endless Wargames for some kind of test, for no reason, or for some legitimate purpose that the AI has simply "gameified" as a way to push human subjects to work their hardest averting some end-of-the-world scenario that the AI is genuinely trying to prevent. Who knows? The devs probably don't, and I'd be lying if I said they presented any of this well enough to care. You're never *really* going to find out; this is a live-service game that's going to sit in limbo for as long as Capcom deems them profitable and then the servers are going to shut down. The likelihood that any of the narrative questions matter beyond set dressing is slim already, and even slimmer that they can, will, or already have worked on any wrap-up content that ties up the game's story with a neat bow at the end. You'll play the intro to get acquainted, everyone sits in the static status-quo of "keep killing dinosaurs until something happens, I guess", and then the servers will go down. All we'd have to show for it is thousands upon thousands of hours wasted "grinding" matches, thousands of dollars spent on cosmetics that vanished into the ether and a mediocre story told badly.I'll waste my time elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: AAA games should not have such a vague beginning narrative in my opinion.Below is a description of 5 minutes into the game.Weirdest start of game ever. "Dinosaurs flood cities" or something in that regard, my character was making weird faces during the interview giving no prompt of what the heck is going on. I get assigned to "Hammerheads" my character doesn't look happy. ill be frank, it looks like someone released some "fart gas" in the room and he tasted it.Fast track to "Hammerheads" scene, I am introduced to some... random characters I know nothing about, a big guy called chief "I'm too fat and too old"... then a one armed man then a woman with an attitude problem... then BOOM I am in a scene where chief is like NA we not gonna fight after flipping a coin.Our ship is crashing from some random vortex in the air and then I'm on an Island, thrown back in time (3 years) being chased by some random dinosaurs that randomly appeared... and I just started some mission with dinosaurs pouring into a room, I Alt F4'd out of it and uninstalled.Its not worth its price just for the graphics and some of the game play. It lacks any real narrative telling you how this all started, you sort of start in the middle of a narrative and your wandering around killing dinos that spawn from some portal.

_childDocuments_.review: So been trying exoprimal for a couple hours. Its not what I thought it was going to be, but it occupies a unique place due to how its designed.At its core its a PvE game, but you do race the other team to complete the objectives first. So the games REALLY easy, like I honestly don't think you could fail if you tried to levels of easy. You're just a bunch of bad ass warframes basically, but while this might be a negative if the game wasn't a racing game (lol), since it is at its core a race, even if you technically aren't being challenged by the PVE element, you feel compelled to try your best because you can lose simply by doing it slower.This creates very weird situations that don't normally exist in a PvE or a PVP game. So someone like a genji/tracer can occupy a weird space of, we need you to race to the other objective as fast as possible so we can start the next PvE phase slightly faster the the other team. Than everyone gets there and you feel like badasses because of how fast you killed everything, but than you find out the other team is a bunch of badasses, so they're hot on your heels, so you're like damn, gotta do faster, better, stronger.Ultimately I think it gives the game the advantages of both and the disadvantages of both, its strong PvE because you feel awesome doing everything, but you don't feel like you are getting dominated like in a PvP game. While the PvE is easy and technically you can't lose, you still feel like you want to win against the other team, so you still try, even though its easy, but you lose, and it doesn't feel bad because you don't actually get dominated by them ever? Its something I think you ultimately need to experience to know how it feels exactly, but it occupys a pleasant place of being easy and fun, but still challenging and you lose due to the other team being faster at times, but it doesn't feel bad because you felt like a badass throughout? Its hard to explain.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly good time~ For the one-time asking price upfront, you can get almost ALL of the game's contents completely free very easily, including unlockable characters and skins. I much prefer this model to a ftp one. Besides that, the gameplay is phenominal and very well-balanced. I'd highly recommend giving it a go. At this point, I'm more than willing to say even full-price the game is worth it. Only thing to be aware of is that the game slowly unlocks more missions for you over time as you play. The first few hours will be the most repetitive , but you'll be rewarded with incredible bossfights and some truly insane missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is crazy, in a good way. Switching between a wide variety of exosuits while shooting dinosaurs in a crazy simulation whilst trying to find a way to escape an ai's wargame simulations? Count me in. The gameplay is fun, and hopefully the planned future gamemodes will only make the game even better.I know a lot of people are complaining about the game's price tag & the passes and purchasable content but to be fair the passes are purely cosmetic and it's always a good idea to wait for a sale (or just use GamePass, it's there too!). Secondly, the PvEvP stuff seems to be controversial. I don't have a problem with it, since it's what the game was marketed for. PvP segments aren't too shabby if you're into that kind of thing, and there will be dedicated PvE gamemodes in the future (The Savage Gauntlet) so when those release hopefully some of those worries will be put to rest. Anyways, the game is fun as hell. I say give it a try if you can, and thanks for reading this silly review all the way through.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell that a LiVe SeRVice game is good and successful when it's 50% off half a year after release.Exoprimal is awful. That is ignoring that this game is something that nobody ever wanted to begin with, which is the Gambit mode from Destiny 2 turned into a full game. It is a mortally boring grindfest with unsatisfying combat, boring music, a story that would have been better if it hadn't existed at all, disgusting monetization, and a developer team that is so desperate for gameplay ideas that they're resorting to the novelty of crossovers in their second content patch. A game that does not allow for skill expression, where matches are decided on the question of which team has more people AFK-farming playtime for battle pass XP to curb their FOMO in case that this game is ever not going to suck. A game that is so awful that I'm tempted to check the "check this box if you've received the game for free" box because I would love to trick myself into thinking that I only wasted 80 hours of my life on this trash, and not also $70.

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the generic presentation lies a great combat system: controls are tight and responsive and it's ludicrously cathartic to mow down raptors on mass with a samurai power suit. Though it is true the game is a bit light on content:  not that many playable characters and the various steps of any given match don't vary that much, perhaps it has to do with the player levels and their respective story progression. While I am a bit worried about the future of a multiplayer exclusive game with a population on steam that peaked at 1500 and it's now under 500, I must note that the game features crossplay and I've never waited more than a couple seconds for a match. Capcom might just support the game for a good while despite low player count.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is actually really good. At first, I only picked it up because a friend really wanted me to so I wasn't expecting much. However, the game play is immaculate, the emotes and skins are fire, and the big boss fights are pretty well designed. My main gripe is that it feels a little cash grabby. _childDocuments_.review: The different exosuits are real fun and unique to play, especially the sniper character (Widowmaker/Ana but bonkers) and the tank samurai Muramasa. Mindless dino clearing is especially satisfying when you nuke a bunch of them.Supposedly there's six maps total so far but you initially have access to two. Three hours in and I haven't seen one of the other four. These are story-gated and to progress story you just play X amount of games. There's also a lore wheel with I want to say there's 100 different nodes where characters discuss the specific discovery about the island. These are also progression-gated.The PvP queue feels like a ♥♥♥♥ show at the end when you start trying to kill off the enemy team and hinder their progress. Damage and abilities overload especially when people start blowing their ults like an Overwatch fight. As I mentioned before maps are story-gated but the only PvP final mission I've seen is a Payload mode ala Overwatch/Paladins.The PvE queue final missions you just have to compete against the enemy team to clear objectives faster. That's basically it.Apart from the Dino Horde mode there's also another which is pretty much a time trial? I haven't unlocked it yet. But yea there is pretty much only much two modes with maps that have rotating routes and objectives. According to one of the Steam News Posts for the game there's around five regular objectives and five final mission objectives but I've only seen one of each so far. Seems like it'll take a while till I find some variety.I never touched the Aliens horde shooter but I've been looking for something new and for once it feels like a game with "hero" characters did it right. Unlike other games that shoehorned "Overwatch heroes" into their game.You can argue that there's not enough content to make it worth full price but it does have that AAA Capcom quality to it. Even the story cutscenes are engaging and characters are witty although I'm barely interested in the overall plot. It was worth my purchase and don't regret just playing it for a couple days on Game Pass instead.There's cross-play but no cross-play parties at launch although Capcom said they're working to add it. Japanese companies...On a sidenote, this along with Street Fighter 6 and Re:Verse use the Capcom ID system yet there is ZERO cross-progression across platforms for all three games. PLEASE CAPCOM.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I've played this quite a bit since I got it and I will say it is a bit slow to get into the new stuff but I kept with it and just... Please give it a chance for a couple of hours. It's a game that changes and gives new things and experiences as you progress because this game leans into its lore with that. I play this with my husband and we LOVE IT.This game is Crossplatform but not CrossPARTY YET. They have a roadmap and so they plan to add more just in the next month alone! You can't buy progression so it's less predatory than some other games. Some skins are paid but most can be earned by literally just playing the game (what a concept with modern games I swear) I can have literally hundreds of dinos maybe even a thousand on my screen at once WHILE streaming and not experience a single framedrop (I use a 1080ti+Ryzen 5 and I did not turn down graphics at all.). I've also experienced minimal to no connection issues and some games do give me consistent trouble so this is a big plus for me! _childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie. I REALLY want to like this game. The core gameplay is pretty solid. The game is easy to pick up and can have a high skill ceiling. The problem is that this game is incredibly monotonous and cyclical, There's barely any customization options, AND the pretty much ripped off Anthem with this except they didn't bring in the verticality. The verticality of Anthem was made it actually really fun (for a small amount of time) . There's also the problem that this game is SEVERELY bare bones. Once you've played the first 2 missions, you've pretty much seen all the content you're going to see.If this game were say $20, it would be worth it. But I legit payed $60 for this game that feels like it was a high budget production from a 3 man dev team. The problem is that it wasn't a 3 man dev team.......I do not recommend this game until they add a lot more to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Update Title update 3: Since the latest update I feel like the game has become a lot better content variety wise. I don't get beginner maps as often, and I feel like the modes I get in general are different most of the time. There is also a bigger variety of weapon selection for exosuits. I wish they had more ability variety as well but oh well. It still isn't perfect but its a major step up. I still wish there was a bit more control over the modes/maps you play on, for example I played like 30 matches in the last 2 days but still haven't seen the new super raid fight. I wish I could skip cutscenes I have already seen. There is a lot more I wish was just better, but at this point id be comfortable to put this in the recommend range rather then just neutral. There is still a lot of work to be done but its absolutely going in the right direction.This is exactly the type of game I wish I could give a neutral review. Exoprimal is a great game with so much going for it. Yet the game is riddled with annoyances and things holding it back. Lets get into it.First what makes this game great. The core aspects of this game are fantastic. It looks fantastic and runs great. The game is fun to play and has a good amount of varied and fun content. The story is surprisingly strong with fun characters and an engaging plot, its nothing award winning but it adds a lot to the game. The game has high difficulty pve content and the chaos you feel as thousands of dinos swarm your team is something fresh, exciting and fun. There is also a challenge mode/speedrun mode that switches every week after you beat the story. The goal of that mode is to clear it or to get as fast as a time as possible beating it to compare yourself to others. The joy I had when I got a top 10 % time was insane, its incredibly fun to try and improve your time even by seconds, the game feels so rewarding in those moments. I seriously can't praise all of these parts of the game enough.So what is holding me back from just saying this is a recommend 100 %? Its that getting to actually play the game is an insane drag. To begin with the story is integrated in your early progression, every match you get a bunch of lore explaining what is going on, if you collect enough lore you can progress the story. Once you have progressed the story enough you start seeing the different modes the game has to offer, it took me about 10 hours to feel like the game was genuinely offering something more to me then the basic mode of slaying basic dinos, those 10 hours are a drag and don't feel fun. The difficulty at those 10 hours is so incredibly low and boring that you can almost do everything alone. During matches you race against opponents to see who can finish the PVE content first, but with the difficulty being so low I felt like both teams were always next to each other in terms of progress to finish the missions. It took me another 15 hours to finish the story and the game kept getting better during those 15 hours.So that makes about 25 hours to finish the ''turtorial''/story mode. If that was all the game asked it would be fine, but the problem is that the game gives you practically 0 control over what you are going to play, that cool boss you just faced, want to do it again? Well that sucks you can't. You can only hope the game offers it up on a limited time speedrun contest every week or for you to randomly get it when you queue for a match.Not only that but because other new players also need to play through those first 10 hours we now also have to deal with playing those low level easy missions even after completing the story. Imagine having to play the first level in a game over and over again without being able to decide if you want to play it, there isn't enough diversifying to make that first level feel interesting. To add salt to injury if you do get an interesting mission you usually have to watch a cutscene, those cutscenes are really fantastic the first time, around, but after seeing them for the 5th time you start to REALLY wish there was a skip button.The last topic I want to cover is the live service model. In general you can get everything in the game through gameplay relatively simply, it can be a bit time consuming but it is honestly quite nice to see a game offer nice cosmetics and progression that is very accessible. My only complaint is that the game recently added more exosuits variety that you can play as, the unlock requirement for these suits however is quite time consuming, being able to experiment more with those suits would help a lot with enjoying the grind through those first 10 hours.All in all Exoprimal is still something I would recommend. I see a massive amount of potential here, it has that capcom magic all over it and the roadmap already showed some exciting updates like a collab with Street fighter 6 as well as Monster hunter. That being said right now that potential isn't realized properly and there is a lot holding it back, are you willing to shelf over 60 bucks for a live service game when there are now a ridiclious amount of free to play games that offer even more content then this game? That is up to you to decide. What I will say is that when Exoprimal is at its best its a REALLY good game, something that will keep getting improved. If capcom doesn't decide to pull the plug on this game due to playercount then I think this game has a very bright future.

_childDocuments_.review: So let's get the negative out of the way.It's a full priced game.It released with a cosmetic bundle DLC.It has a battle pass.The "pve" mode you can queue up for is still basically a time-attack against another team.Now for the positives:The games free cosmetic options are frankly really good. There's the traditional recolors and then some off the wall stuff like dressing the samurai up as capcom's interpretation of robo-Benkei, a robo burger-kin. Stuff like that.The gameplay is pretty fun. It's pvevp and it scratches an itch and feels the void that was left when they axed Gambit Prime in Destiny 2 (and then soft abandoned gambit altogether afterwards).The story which I had initially written off is rather fun and well realized which is the biggest surprise to me. The presentation could use a bit of work at times but the mystery the game introduces and then slowly works the characters through is intriguing and unpredictable.The mission type is rather varied but I'm mostly looking forward to the 'end-game challenge content' they have prepared for later this month. Altogether the game is rather fun.The performance is pretty good. As is naturally what's expected from a game out of capcom, a toaster could run this game and get good fps.Now for the nitty gritty. The monetization is rather lean. You can't pay for the warchests, you can't pay for battle pass progress, you can't pay for any type of in game currency. The warchests the game gives you for leveling up your player rank seem to pull from all items at a relatively fair rate to the point that I'm more surprised if I don't get a 'legendary' skin.The only thing you can pay for are the few (rather mid) skins and the paid version of the battle pass. All in all. A pretty fun product.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Lets get the elephants in the room out of the way first.In my honest opinion, $60 is not a good price tag for this game. i honestly see it better priced at around $35 or $40 considering the content and the loop within.Yes, it is a fully priced game with a premium battlepass and lootboxes. BUT. You cannot purchase said lootboxes, they are drops as you level up and after lvl 50 you get them with every level up. Which is very generous. The in game currency, Bikcoin, is handed out very generously via player level ups and exosuit level ups. There is no premium currency and you cannot buy currency. And the premium battlepass does offer really good skins for some of the exosuits.So yes. Out the gate, not lookin great. Lets get into the game.To keep it short and sweet, you are a newcomer into the 'totally not evil corporation' Aibius who develops exosuits to fight dinosaurs. You're put on a team called the Hammerheads and not too long you meet the corrupted AI Leviathan. Who then traps you in a simulation with other exofighters from other dimensions in the means of gathering combat data. The story and lore are presented via mini cutscenes and a large amount of audio logs. Which isn't terrible. Voice acting isn't bad, isn't the greatest, but isn't bad. Honestly the characters have grown on me.Gameplay!Gameplay is veerrrry solid. Very solid, responsive and fun. Each exosuit brings a different kit to the table and no one exosuit is more overwhelming than another. The only case of this i have seen is in a lot of instance the Barrage suit, which is a grenadier style suit. oft performs better than the more basic Deadeye suit. Though it shines often as well. Gamemodes! Often see a few people complain there aren't a lot of modes. This is not the case. There are a good few modes in this. You just have to commit and push through the story a bit to see them. As well as special dino types. UNFORTUNATELY, it seems the way it is right now. If you get into a match with someone just starting, you will continue to get just the basic payload mode as the final mission. But when the stars align, there are matches in which Leviathan just goes "♥♥♥♥ it, this is now a 10 person raid" as the final mission.Graphics!This game is surprisingly super well optimized. I ain't got the greatest computer in the world and I rarely drop below 60 fps when there's a thousand raptors on my screen. The environments are decently pretty as well, some destructable environments like knocking down trees and blowing up abandoned cars. all in all pretty good.All in all i've been having loads of fun with this. One of the best PvEvP games to date. This is what I wanted Destiny 2's gambit to kinda be!Again. $60 is not a good price tag. If you have Gamepass on Xbox, I emplore you give it a shot there to save money. And again, YOU REALLY MUST COMMIT in order to see different things and modes. you won't see it all in the first 5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it.  It's a hero shooter but faster paced, has a pve element and with dinos to slaughter.  It has an overarching story with cutscenes and data to read.  It's actually pretty cool.  You kinda rush against another team to progress as fast as you can and then some missions devolve into pure pvp as you attack the other team to slow them down.  It also has a pve mode but you still race against the other team, only you don't fight them in the exosuit, you only fight them via the dominator(dino control and summon)  It starts super basic and it seems like there is no content but as you play, you unlock more and more game modes and stages and they just keep unlocking until you play a wide variety of missions.  There is actually a mode where you fight together with the other team that just unlocked for me which is pretty cool.  The dino waves get super crazy like world war z levels crazy which I just love cause it runs well as you ragdoll them around. For the most part, there is a competitive high score feeling to the game so if you don't like that you may be disappointed.  Personally, I don't usually like hero shooters but the blend of PVE and PVP does make me like it.  Plus slaughtering dinos in a robotic exosuit tickles that childish place in my mind that loves such things.  Having now beat the game, the story is fairly enjoyable.  I enjoyed reading the various data you acquire as you play.  I was pleased with it overall.  It has that format that Japanese games where the enemies and scenarios get harder and more insane the longer you go until you are fighting some God-Like thing.  I really enjoyed the 10 player pve scenarios with boss mechanics and everything, or just the 10 player pve scenarios with thousands of dinos running around going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: Its mechs vs dinosaurs, of course its a super fun game! Long review: Exoprimal has a  with multiple things levelling up, be it the player level, battle pass, or individual suits' levels, which constantly makes you feel like you are progressing. Even after a less-than-ideal round, you feel like you've at least achieved something. The  is impressively good. Dominators (big dinos you possess) and Dino Upgrades (makes the dinos fighting the enemy team harder), evening the playing field, leading to almost every match feeling like a close call. Every mech has a unique playstyle that compliments a large set of other exosuits and setups. Swapping between mechs at any time allows for a fun and un-punishing flow between different objectives for example switching from the close-ranged Roadblock for clearing out hordes of dinosaurs to a Krieger for more long-ranged payload defense. The same goes for Rigs which is basically bonus-abilities that any mech can equip. This leads to a large variety of gameplay variants which helps spice up the replay-ability. The  is surprisingly fun to follow with entertaining characters and good story beats. The characters are fun, quirky, and likeable. There interesting world building and lore as well as some cute character moments that help draw you into the story. The cutscenes are fun as well as some of the reveals. The beginning of the game is a bit slow, with . Since I beat the Season 1 story two days after the game's release (the story took me about 24 hours to complete) (I am unwell) a lot of late-game missions are still locked behind the newest member of whatever party I join. I still haven't encountered two of the Neosaurs listed on the exoprimal website. This will probably get fixed up once more people have played and beat the story proper.  On top of the $60+ ($70 for the deluxe version) there's also a battle pass ($9.99), head start kit ($14.99), and cosmetics dlc ($4.99 each). Personally if this is the direction this game wants to go, I think it should be a "free" to play game. It could help entice bring in new players to enjoy a new ip that they may be hesitant towards supporting/investing time into. There's  despite being able to match with them. I have friends who I want to play it with who are playing through xbox's gamepass. I really enjoyed playing in a 5 stack team during the free beta and I haven't been able to recreate that feeling because of this. I've had a lot of fun so far! think this game has a ton of potential and I'm excited to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated on Jul 5th:  So basically:- After season 4, comes season 1 again, and so it'll be until the servers are shut down ( "Time loop rebellion" revealed itself as a great title for the most recent game mode in many ways now)- No new battlepasses, game modes, thicc robot skins or collabs with Capcom IPs (They seriously gave us Megaman Collab before a DMC collab and I'll never forgive the Japanese for that)- Expect the same dumb Capcom dongle as reward for login bonus on every Capcom Anniversary until the end of time. That's it folks, pack it up, Kunitsu-Gami is right around the corner and I can't wait to be made a fool again.Original review:First and foremost:  . The game is great, actually one of the best multiplayer experiences I ever had in my miserable life, but the steam price is outrageous and it's really holding this game down. Capcom is out of their mind by not dropping this ridiculous price tag in order to open doors to new players on steam. 1- Comparisions to Helldivers 2 are constant and not only dumb, but criminal and should be a capital offense punished by making the offender take a shower. The only thing both games share is the "coop" tag. Exoprimal is about putting Iron Man in the Dino Crisis universe to see how many chicken-ancestors he can take before a rogue Chat-GPT says it's time to go to bed. It's an arcade experience not intended in any way to have you tactically moving to complete objectives. You pick your exosuit, and smash hordes of dinos while learning among dozens of hours on how to best make use of upgrades and skills, to do it better, faster, sexier (hope this is a word). Matches are short, and your class matter, as typical hero shooter. So, as I said: Nothing like Helldivers 2.2- The game is not dead, far from it. Matches start after 2 or 4 minutes in queue. And as long as Game Pass players keep being able to join with their mics permanently turned-on while they eat dorittos and scream at their moms, the game will be alive and well. Also, updates are slow, collabs are probably going to be mixmashes of Capcom franchises ultil these servers are unplugged, since let's be real, this game didn't take off at all. And in-house Capcom IPs are probably indeed the smartest option to keep things interesting here.

_childDocuments_.review: A meagre ten exosuits to play as, each with two unlockable variations with minor changes to pad out the roster. Free to play progress system with a full retail price tag. Pilot customisation is lacking to a point where everybody looks the same. I do like how the campaign progresses through the multiplayer but the story leaves a lot to be desired. AI running simulations for data is about as boring as you can make a story about dinosaurs falling from the sky.PvE consists of two back to back rounds shooting at dinosaurs. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, it's really that simple. A premise so straightforwardly dumb that I can't help but ask, "Why didn't this happen sooner." :DWith 3 classes for each role of Attacker, Defender, or Healer there are 9 unique playstyles to choose from. Each of them also has an Alpha variant that changes one thing about the class (e.g. Deadshot's weapon goes from an automatic rifle to a tri-burst/shotgun). At any point in a match, you can change your class and equipment so experimentation is encouraged.Matchmaking has always been fast. Even now with the hype of the launch died down I still find matches within 5 -10 sec.I could not care about the story in the slightest. I came to kill dinosaurs and the game doesn't get in the way of that since the story is played through multiplayer (there is no single-player mode). However, when an antagonist is introduced and established I did notice I was getting a little bit hyped with the dynamic it was creating. The more you go through the story the more maps are unlocked, more alterations of dinosaurs fought, and a couple of more game types are introduced. Even though I wasn't paying attention, I did enjoy how the story was delivered because when the end of the game came I actually understood what was going on. With that being said, the game types are no different than the ones you'd find in Team Fortress or Overwatch. I really wished there was a greater variety of dinosaurs in the game. I read a lot of dinosaur books as a kid and would love to fight Therizinosaurus or an Elasmosaurus that's able to be on land. They do have unique dinosaurs but it feels like such a small sample is currently available. As a second option for multiplayer, every weekend there is a Gauntlet Mode where your team has to take on a more difficult threat under tighter constraints than the main multiplayer. While I enjoy the challenge, it does feel creatively uninteresting.There are updates coming along. We have a collab with Street Fighter and Monster Hunter for the next two seasons. This is the most I've enjoyed an online shooter since Black Ops 2 and Overwatch so if those updates can bring more maps, more game modes, and (most importantly) MORE DINOSAURS, I think I'll be really happy because it's already a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rate it a solid 7.2/10 for its current state. It feels like the game was rushed-- and I don't mean that in the standard fashion. It feels more like the developers had more planned, but decided to keep the original release date vs holding off on it and releasing it with additional content.Don't get me wrong, the current game-play loop is incredibly satisfying. I haven't experienced any graphical, audio or any other glitches whatsoever, which is surprisingly rare on most games first launch week theses days. However, it does feel odd that additional enemy dinos, modes, and maps appear to be somewhat locked behind a progress log that has something to do with the total amount of matches you have played thus far, and the amount of Archive based content you have unlocked/watch/read.While that in and of itself might be fine, its very odd that I have yet to experience the purple-goo dinos shown in the trailers, or that lava lake like fight, but I assume it has something to do with the locked content behind a progression-like wall.I do think a sandbox like mode with a sea of dinos being thrown at you in a large map with two objectives; survive and kill some behemoth of a creature at the end, would go a long way in additional content for this game. Additionally, while the story is very interesting, its unfortunate that there isn't any single player mode to enjoy the story in. And while its an odd choice, it isn't necessarily a bad one.Regardless, more content such  additional modes-- particularly a true PvE mode where no 'invasions of player dinos' can happen and a single-player based mode would go a long way in retaining interested of all players alike. Even though I greatly enjoy the game and want it to do well and expend on whats currently here, I can't recommend it for its current price tag. Its got a value of around 25-30$ USD, not 60$. Definitely would tell any curious users to hold off until the game goes on sale. Or at the very least, for the next 3 months or so when the devs are more likely to release additional content.Still, that said, out of this years pre-ordered games, I don't regret this purchase one bit, despite its shortcomings, its still a very enjoyable game with fluid combat and relatively smart horde-like AI.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on a whim because I liked the sound of exosuits fighting dinosaurs and Capcom has been putting out banger after banger for over half a decade now. Fortunately, this continues the trend! Movement and shooting are super smooth. Designs for all of the exosuits and the dinosaurs are distinct and great. Most of the maps are visually fantastic, but at least one that I can think of is pretty visually samey with portions that are outright frustrating to navigate thanks to obnoxious natural hazards. Exoprimal shines the brightest during strict PvE, when you're fighting hordes of small dinos and a handful of larger ones. Every suit feels completely different and none of them are outright over or under-powered. You can also switch between any of them in the middle of matches which does a LOT to keep gameplay varied and I love that it's an option. Their abilities all feel powerful and worth using. Popping dinosaurs, getting chunky hits on weakpoints, and figuring out efficient strategies for killing the required number for each objective is a lot of fun. And when you manage to wipe out like 50 raptors with one big ability? That's the good ♥♥♥♥. Never gets old.There is a narrative present, and it uniquely progresses as you complete online matches rather than going through a campaign. The story is ridiculous and the progression can be slow at times, but it's so well-presented in its handling of the characters, voice performances, and the piecing together of a little mystery that I found myself liking it and even laughing a lot. The cast is very, very charming, and it culminates and resolves very satisfyingly.Its weakest aspect is PvP. It's not terrible, but there are a lot of ways to cheese other players and just be a huge unfun pain in the ass for the other team. Crowd control abilities (of which there are a lot, since the main focus of Exoprimal is being a horde shooter) are extremely effective at dealing a ton of damage to enemy players and robbing them of any chance at retaliation. Many times it's simply a contest of who sees who first which is just... not exciting. That said, if there's a big team fight and all of the exofighters in a match are all in one place then it's a riot.If I had to give it a letter grade I'd give it an A-! Great core gameplay, presentation, and overall quality with some very apparent smaller issues. Looking forward to see what else comes out of this project as Capcom continues with it. The recent additions of the Alpha suits are just wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is weird. It's a new live-service game from Capcom, acting as a child from the marriage of Dino Crisis and Lost Planet's corpses. It is hard to define because Exoprimal feels like a blender of many different ideas and that is reflected in the main game mode currently available: PvPvE.Getting down to the basics, most of your games will involve shooting dinosaurs with class-based exosuits (that have their own personality separate from your mute character) until the last round where you either race against the enemy team more or get into an objective-based PvP shootout with them. There are dynamic obstacles in play that help the losing team and hurt the winning team, but this assistance has to used carefully so that it's not used at an ineffective time. There is more to the main game mode Dino Survival's premise, but to say more I'd likely be spoiling some nicer aspects of the game.Talking about the gameplay leads me to reflect briefly in what I've seen in many early reviews that typically only have 2-5 hours of gametime. There is a misconception in these early reviews that once you've played this long, you've seen it all. YOU HAVE NOT. There is a lot more varied game content within, however the game chooses to gate this content in two ways: general matchmaking and story progression. Whenever you matchmake for a game, it will pool all currently unlocked (or the newest unlocked, as the priority mission for you) missions for you to play - there is no individual mission selection. In addition, you do NOT unlock story content unless you go through the Data Analysis section of the menu and listen to the conversations/presentations, which are completely skippable if you don't care, but you still need to actually do it.After about 20 hours, I've played to the credits and found out there's also going to be an extreme co-op mode in two weeks time, so it will satiate more co-op minded players. What is currently here is scratching my itch but a live-service game could always use more.What I don't agree with on this game is that it costs 60 dollars and they put a battle pass on top of it. I think they were betting massively on this being a Game Pass game, but they should have at least priced this instead at more like 40 bucks, or paired the battle pass with the game at 50-60 bucks. What IS present here sounds good, feels good and is fun. I personally believe people are already busy with their own live-service addiction and they need to defend it by crapping on a brand new IP one. A point in their favor though is that those games are usually free.

_childDocuments_.review: Do Not Buy This Game. First off, it is lacking content and the "content" that it has is gated behind hours of playtime. This usually isn't an issue unless the actual gameplay loop is not fun nor has any depth which is the case for Exoprimal. Gameplay consists of shooting hordes of dinosaurs which sounds like it could be fun, but this game feels like you have zero agency. When you're succeeding there is almost no reward and when you're failing you hardly get punished. Gameplay is just blah so you have no incentive to try or not try. Literally the kind of game that will rot your brain.The storyline is pretty bland and repetitive. It's clear there's some mystery going on, but they don't tell you anything interesting until you play for 5 or 10 hours. The story consists of bland cutscenes and reading data logs. You don't really get transported to different areas or unique maps. Think of a game like Titan Fall 2, The story is its own thing and the multiplayer is separate. This game combines the two, but completely fails to deliver any semblance of story. It would literally be like if TF2 removed the entire campaign and added a lore tab in the settings menu where you could read a few data logs that's the story.The icing on the cake is Exoprimal being a $40 game on sale and having a microtransaction, loot box, and battle pass system integrated. It's very clear this game is intended to push the limits to see what people are willing to buy. This borders on being a scam.Long story short your $40 will be much more valuable by Not buying this game. Go spend money on literally anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start...There's not much in terms of gamemode or map variety. There's an insulting amount of skins/battle pass/DLC greed on display. The story feels tacked on and it unconvincingly attempts to contextualize the game's obtuse premise. Story dialogue is almost always awful and the exosuits’ limited number of quips range from annoying to uninspired. The silent protagonist situation is super awkward and player character customization is surprisingly weak for an engine/company that brought us the character creator in SF6 and MHR.Queue times are long, matchmaking seems mostly random, and the gameplay is no replacement for many of the other co-op shooters. Close/back-and-forth games seem rare with momentum being hard to stop and no obvious tug-of-war system to keep the leading team on their toes. Team compositions aren't usually well-coordinated either. The number of synergies between exosuits that might've enhanced gameplay are slim to none. Abilities are usually single-purpose self/AoE buffs or defense stuff with the rest being individualistic attacks.Enemy variety is rough. Of all the games that could’ve taken fun creative liberties with dinosaurs, Exoprimal keeps the lizard diversity dry with basically two categories: small ones that are trivial and medium/large ones that charge at you.While Exoprimal comes across as largely derivative and has elements that bear a striking resemblance to various ongoing live service games, what's here isn't not fun to play. All the weapons/abilities have satisfying animations/sounds which makes the moment-to-moment dino-hunting haptically entertaining. The whole absurd  premise has my inner child pretty hyped. Plus, I've kind of been looking for a team-based shooter that's not exclusively PvP that also includes classes/support characters. So, against my better judgment, I've been mostly enjoying the core of Exoprimal.So, the game fills a random, temporary niche for me, but I can't bring myself to recommend it based on that. It also feels wrong to promote a game with such toxic monetization. But if you are interested in the game, don't buy it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm impressed by how well they created the story/lore about Dinos, AI, Mech, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ time travel. You would think this cluster♥♥♥♥ of themes would be a train-wreck but shockingly no lol, it all actually makes sense if your following along with the story. Sure there are a tad bit of rough areas in the story and  a bit of corny dialogue sometimes but you still have to give em credit for managing it overall plus the corny dialogue in some aspects are likely intentional given the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cheesy theme of game which personally for me, I find it charming. The time it took for me to finish the story progression took like 26 hours to finish though I was reading thoroughly reading/listening to the lore. Im guessing if you just skip the dialogues in the lore wheel thing it prob take you to finish like 19-23 hour maybe? which honestly isnt bad of a game time, not too long and neither too short.Even after finishing the story I find the gameplay aspect super addictive in like a arcade manner its just pure dumb fun to play. Sure theres like a competitive aspect to the game but dont let that distress you, this game isnt really too competitive. I've seen some certain comments flowing around of those who dont wanna get this game cause of the player vs player aspect of it but really I think this game doesnt really commit too hard on the competitiveness theres like comeback mechanic stuff if your really far behind on progress but generally you dont see them often cause imo you generally always finish about the same time more or less.Ive also seen people not wanting to get this game cause live service, which is understandable if your not into that, and "micro transaction". There are no micro transactions in this game except I guess the season pass but like every season pass they are not pay to win stuff. Everything else you can unlock by plying the game and the grind to get them is super quick in comparison to other live service games. There are jumpscare lootboxes but you cant buy them you unlock them by leveling up and the loot you get from them is always high rate like ive gotten 3 legendary skins from 2 lootboxes I unlocked by leveling up.1 level up in this game takes about like 2 random game mode matches all the time.Ive also seen complaints about its repetitiveness which is fair it can get be time to time at first but its not mind numbingly repetitive like how people perceive it to be. There are different variety of game modes and scenarios you can get when you are progressing the story. The people I see complain about it being repetitive are those how haven't actually progressed the story properly but once you do there are plenty amount of variety you can experience and there will be more to come cause of it being "live service". Also the EXO Suits of the game are drastically different from one and another so you get a refreshing kick out of all the different suits. You can also add 3 mods that modify and enhance the play style of the suit and you can create your own style or experiment for each suit if you want but you do have to level them up to get unique mods which can be a bit grindy if you dont like the suit your plying at the beginning. I hope capcom can expand further on the mods as I personally enjoy this aspect of it, which im sure many others do.Okay the price of the game, its up to you to decide if you want spend $60/£50 on this game. For me, I already love the concept of shredding mobs of dinos so it was an instant cop for me and I am thoroughly satisfied and surprised by how good the story was.If youre interested on the game but the price is scarey, like many others have said try it out on game pass or wait for sale.If youre unsure, try it out on game pass, or make the judgment call by reading/watching more reviews and check a look at more gameplay for it, especially the midway of the storyline so you can see more of the other variety game modes and levels and then its up to you to decide if you wanna try it on game pass or not.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It is a very fun game, but the amount of content is not worth the 60 euro (basically 70 euro...) price tag.The main gameplay loop consists of running through a map completing objectives, such as defeating a certain amount of dinosaurs or defending an area. When you're doing these objectives survival is rarely a major concern, the main focus is instead to complete them faster than the enemy team. The game features an interesting story and an expanding amount of gameplay content the further you go, on the flipside this means the game feels fairly barebone at the beginning. Overall the game is quite fun with a fairly interesting story and an okay amount of replayability, but it does only have the one speedrun gamemode with a limited amount of variability, which would make it a great 40 euro game, but in my opinion lacking content for a 60-70 euro game.Update: Now they added an new variation of each exosuit, but to play them you either need to grind each and every character or... pay money of course. The game was already lacking content for the price tag, and now they're just adding more paid content instead of making the game worth the price.
