_childDocuments_.review: Whoa, what a ride that was. Just finished the story and I will say I enjoyed every second playing this game. It brought me back to a feeling of nostalgia of playing Lost Planet 2 with friends on the Xbox 360. (BTW capcom please fix LP2 on steam). It truly feels like an Xbox 360 Capcom game, but in a good way. I didn't know it was a feeling I missed. I may be biased because I am a pvp gamer, but I do recommend this game. I enjoy the gameplay loop of racing the enemy team by  killing your hordes and completing your tasks faster than them. If you are not a fan of pvp, the pure PvE boss battles that you can eventually do are some of the best experiences I have had in a long time. Unfortunately you have to grind the PvP till you can reach them, and then you can queue for those battles specifically till a few weeks from now I believe. I know this game won't be for everyone, but I do suggest you try it. A few things to note:- The game drip feeds you content. The beginning might feel repetitive, but the new missions that come as you level up are what truly make the game shine. Once you get that first big boss battle, you crave more. It may suck, but keep going. It is WORTH IT.- The story is tied to your matches, you progress it by playing matches. There is no single player.- The story is given mostly given through dialogue with portraits of the characters that are speaking. The story itself isn't bad and is the main reason that I kept playing, because I NEEDED to know what happened next. I think the big battles that they plan to release are what will keep me playing, plus the game play itself is fun.- I have heard people say the game is heavily monetized, but I don't see it in its current state. Yes there is a battle pass with cosmetics, and most of the skins you can buy on steam are just recolored skins that are in the battle pass that you can earn. Plus so far the game has a generous loot system that has allowed me to unlock many skins for exos by just playing and leveling up. It doesn't stop, once you hit player level 50, every level afterwards is 1000 coins; then a loot box and 1000 coins the next level, repeat. The coins can buy most skins besides the current premium ones. All in all I do recommend this game. It isn't perfect, but damn is it fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom tried something new with this game and I really enjoy it. The first few hours are pretty repetitive and that's due to the fact that the story is tied to the "matchmaking" and unfolds as you queue up for matches. The missions are pretty straight forward with you and your team racing against the enemy team to follow a set path and eliminate all the dinos in a specific area as fast as possible and towards the end of the mission you will either be (depending on the mode type) fighting against the enemy team and/or their team controlled dinosaur and vice versa. Near the end of the matches depending on who is in the lead, the game will reward the losing team a controllable dinosaur first to attempt to gain an advantage. Matchmaking is also determined by whoever has the least story progression in the lobby which will have you playing the same story missions until the current player base is progressed enough through the story.Gameplay feels great in exoprimal as you are always on the move and the characters are very fluid and feel fun to play. The characters are separated into 3 classes being Damage, Tank, and Support. each character has a unique playstyle that can be modified with unlockable perks, and a secondary equipment weapon. There are also plenty of cosmetics and unlockables that don't require any real purchases and can be earned by playing and spending in game currency.The real MEAT of the game comes in a few hours into the story which is a shame because the missions become raid boss levels of insane at times and some missions just have both teams join together to fight a single large threat. There are more enemy types that begin to appear and they each have their own mutated variant that have their own unique abilities that can be very challenging at times as you can be swarmed with hundreds of dinos while you try to fight off the larger ones that are barrel rolling your team into the dirt.Coming into this with low expectations I have to say I am having a great time with Exoprimal, it definitely isn't your standard multiplayer experience but it offers something new and exciting that few other games have today.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like mechs and want to blast a bunch of dinos in different ways I highly reccomend this game, with a caveat of getting a key or game-pass as it's absolutely not worth the £50 price tag thats still listed nearly 12 months later.Exoprimal offers somewhat decent progression in the form of (character) mech-unlocks, which are the original mechs but with a twist. Your 3 mainstays of tank, damage dealer and support are on offer and each has their own way to keep things fun and getting you to try out ways to speedrun your way to the end of each level - outpacing other teams. The story is fine, what really shone for me were the combat/ raid style encounters that follow. They feel special, unique and really make you feel like there's a big bad AI to kill. However it's a shame you can't jump into these great moments easily, together with friends like you could in other Capcom greats like Monster Hunter.After racing to complete the first lot of objectives (commonly hordes of raptors, but different maps) you'll be thrown into another dimension to complete a different style of race either PVE or PVP.The gameplay loop is good, somewhat let-down by having you bash your head against the same 2 maps and Objective completing missions. PVP follows well-known modes, lending itself to either a payload push or king of the hill style brawl which I found to be a bit more adrenaline inducing. There may have been stellar marketing for this game on arrival however it doesn't seem to do much to keep you wanting more 12 months on. Right now there's a mega man raid and I've seen theres also a monster hunter raid, alongside the fact that upon completing the story you unlock 2 harder missions to jump into which I like the sound of. Considering it's a full priced game, the battle pass system is ridiculous and the fact you can pay real money to unlock free content is bizarre. I wish they kept that out of the game and introduced a novel progression track that enticed players to stick around instead of opening their wallet (again, this is a FULL PRICED GAME nearly 12 months on).All in all, give it a shot if it's on a big sale, give it 10-15 hours and work through the story content to really enjoy that raid-like content and fingers crossed you'll have as much fun as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 20 hours of gameplay, I managed to beat the story. The story is comprised of a series of audio-logs and cutscenes (most are skip-able) that you obtain randomly throughout playing the missions. The further you progress into this story, the more difficult missions become.I played a total of 56 matches to get to this point, and overall, I would recommend this game.As an aside, the game features [at time of review] 10 unique exosuits (basically heroes/characters/what have you) that you can choose from during a match, all fitting in 3 categories: Damage, Tank, and Support. 3 of them you have to level up in order to unlock, but all the suits I tried are fun.As you progress through the story, you will start to encounter boss fights, which feel a lot like raid bosses from your favorite RPG game. Instead of team V team, the entire lobby works together to defeat them. I think there are about 3 or 4 of these bosses in total, and every single one of them are both challenging and engaging. Overall, the bosses are fun.Mentioned previously, the farther you get into the story, the harder enemies appear during matches. I couldn't count the unique enemies, but there are plenty in my opinion. As far as the battlepass goes, I know its a hot topic of discussion. I had reached level 30 in the battlepass at time of review, which is a bit less than half. To purchase the battlepass, it is $10. KEEP IN MIND, the battlepass is purely optional. The only things you get from it are cosmetics. They dont lock new characters to play behind it (like some other hero PvP games that shall not be mentioned.) Do NOT let the fact that it has a battlepass deter you if you are interested in the game. Not having it wont affect your experience at all.There is [at time of review] only 1 queue-able game mode; however, after completing the story, the game reveals there is one gamemode being developed. _childDocuments_.review: Kino game but people are getting upset because they chose to make an uninformed purchase and thought it was EDF/Evolved/Anthem (which are all wildly different games by the way so you can really tell it's mostly people upset that a random game is not uniquely tailored to their individual tastes)All in all, very solid Team-based hero-shooter with some good mechanics, maps and solid gameplay.To be clear what you're getting is a PvP objective based game. This game is played over rounds, and there are a variety of objectives (typically payload and wave clear) with hopefully more to come (Exo culling rounds please). The structure is pretty neat, The first round is essentially a warm-up, where you're clearing waves while racing to one end of the map, whoever get's there first gets solid advantages and head start in the following round, but overall the PvE round slightly inconsequential and is focused on your teams ability to coordinate and wave clear. Round 2 is where both teams play a bit of tug of war via payload and PvP. The structure of the heroes is similar to what you would see in overwatch, however the big exception here is that it's not balanced in the same squishy and slow philosophy as overwatch. What you're getting here is great third person shooting, with well balanced abilities and a low (relatively) time to kill, that actually allows for some great tactics and individual mechanical skill to come through.It really is unfortunate so many people were either misinformed by someone or not willing to look up and follow any information about a game before getting upset and have chose to start looking to form a brigade against a thing that is really neat for the people who were looking forward to it. You don't have to like every game and that's fine, but c'mon don't kill this thing the rest of us enjoy over it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with lots of content on the horizon. They already have a new hardcore mode coming in about a week and numerous new exosuits, areas, and skins planned out for at least a year. Many people are complaining that you are forced to PvP and this just isn't true, in fact the PvE elements are WAY more enjoyable than fighting players, but the PvP feels fairly balanced with the ability to outplay anyone with anything as long as you know what you're doing. PvE-wise, not only is there a PvE-only queue, but some missions end in a 10-player coop showdown against a huge wave of enemies or a big baddie boss, which is TONS of fun, challenging, and completely cooperative. The gameplay itself is great at what it is: shooting/slashing dinos feels very sastisfying in both the visual and auditory feedback. A rogue AI constantly screams at you to do better. This does make you want to do better. However, Capcom are asking you to shell out a LOT of money just for the game (which is effectively Overwatch if it had a PvE mode before you did PvP with anyone), let alone the battlepass which is an additional $10. I don't have an issue with this because I love this game, but if you don't feel like paying $60 upfront for Dinosaur Overwatch, definitely get it on GamePass.It's not as microtransaction-heavy as other reviews want you to believe. I guess people put in like 30 minutes to get through the tutorial, see a few classes are level locked with an option to buy them, and want to cry about paywalls. Many things can be bought with ingame currency that the game loves to shove down your throat, including EVERY class and I would say 80% of the cosmetics.If you enjoy the repetitive grind of the average hero shooter, this game is worth the money and definitely does not lack for content in that regard. I'm not entirely sure that people who don't think this game has the content to at least be charging SOME money have ever played a hero shooter or any lobby-based cooperative game, because if they had, they would know MANY games charge this amount of money for what is ultimately a repetitive, grindy loop carried by playing it with your friends or competing against randoms. Sure, Overwatch is free, but Overwatch is also pvp-only and makes its money off the tons of skins sold by its immense reputation and history in the industry which obviously a new game trying to innovate on the formula doesn't have.Sixty bucks? Maybe not. Good thing it's on GamePass. Personally I don't mind if a game like this costs money. One, I KNOW this game will give me my money's worth and two, spending money generally deters cheaters (lets be honest, EAC doesn't do anything).The story gets completed in give or take 10 hours of running missions and spamming your way through the lore, probably significantly longer if you watch everything but honestly it's just barely good enough and is carried by the decently-written and well-acted characters. The best part of the story is honestly unlocking the big cooperative endings where you fight bosses because THAT is real good stuff.Very fun, sometimes frustrating, and a little overly expensive, but ultimately a quality, polished product that, while not likely to ever be as popular as its competition, definitely has staying power and potential to grow into an even better game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorta kinda highly recommendable robo dino action.If that is confusing, let me explain. Capcom definitely dropped the ball on a number of fronts with this game. The advertising and messaging is confusing, making many (myself included) think this was a pure cash grab platform given the full price, day 1 battle pass, and so much paid DLC. Buuuuuuuuut... it's actually not that bad at all. All of the different suits (the actual character classes) are unlockable with in game currency you get from playing, and there are loads of skins/tags/emotes/etc. you can unlock for free. The other area they really messed up was not having a completely offline mode. I get that they want to encourage multiplayer, but there's no real reason this game should require a connection since it has working bots.With all that said, I do recommend this game with some caveats. I bought the game on sale for about 23 euros. I won't be buying any battle passes or premium skins. For that price, it totally feels worth it to me. The in game unlockables are keeping me motivated and the progression doesn't feel drip fed. The always online factor is a bit worrying, but I figure if Capcom turns the servers off in 6 months without adding an offline mode, I'll still have gotten my moneys worth. Not everyone will share that sentiment though. If you want a guarantee that this game will be playable in 10 years, then stay away until Capcom decides to add an offline mode (or modders do it for them). Likewise, if you are the type of player that can't ignore premium or time limited content and needs to have absolutely everything, you might want to give it a pass too.So WHY do I recommend this game? Three words, "ROBOT DINOSAUR ACTION!"In some ways it's the most video game video game ever; It's the future, you play as mechs, you fight dinosaurs, and the bad guy is an evil AI. If that appeals to you, then this game has you covered. The different suits are satisfying to play, with various weapons and abilities to keep combat interesting. The hordes of dinosaurs are fun to fight, feeling like "sci-fi musou with guns". I've only tried 4 different suits so far, but they all feel unique and I'm looking forward to trying out their variants and the other completely different classes as I unlock them.PvP-vs-PvE-vs-PvPvE???Some of the criticism of this game has come from the confusion about whether it's actually a co-op or a versus game. I totally get it, I want a co-op experience, not a competitive one. The modes I have played so far are all a hybrid of the two. The key thing is that the PvP parts are very unobtrusive if you come looking for PvE. Generally you play the majority of the mission in a co-op setting, just killing dinos with your team. Towards the end of the mission, you will be given certain PvP options like trying to slow the enemy team down, or direct conflict. When matchmaking, you can specify you only want to play PvE and then the "PvP" sections are all indirect conflict, like just trying to beat the mission faster than the opposing team.Story? What story!? Seriously though, there is a story. It's a bit silly, somewhat intriguing, and not the main reason to play this game. I quite like the combination of story cut scenes and audio/video/text logs to fill in the blanks. They definitely should have made the story progression smoother and offered a fully offline option to play through it. The current implementation is that when you queue up for missions, you sometimes get the next slice of the story, before/after you play. It works well enough for what it is IMO.Pros: -ROBO DINO ACTION!!-Nice graphics.-Cool mech suit designs and skins.-Actual in game unlockable content.-No pay-to-win DLC/microtransactions.-Fun co-op experience, even with randoms and voice chat off.-Crossplay and bots and mean you can always get into matches quickly.-Works well on Steam Deck with some settings lowered.Cons:-Required online connection for no good reason...-...which also means Capcom could kill this game at any moment.-The default non-sale price.-Microtransaction temptation.Exoprimal has room for improvement, but it's a solid game that I would recommend to the right person. If the idea of "Co-op Robot Vs Dinosaur Musou" in a Saturday morning cartoon setting sounds enticing, then this might be the right game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Poor Exoprimal, constantly and overly berated and punched down on. I gave Exoprimal a shot half a year later after its prime despite all of this because I was excited by the premise of dinosaur Salmon Run. Salmon Run it is not, but I was overjoyed to find that it was a different-but-similar kind of addictive fun. Exoprimal has its problems, but I personally found them to be blown out of proportion and I’m going to try to explain why.Exoprimal’s “PvPvE” gameplay involves reaching one point of a sizeable map and killing a certain number of dinosaurs faster than your opponent. In between checkpoints, you’re told if you’re going slower or faster than the enemy team and you’re shown the enemy team’s outlines in the intermittent. The high of “You are completing objectives faster than the enemy team” still hasn’t worn off 30 hours in. While being told/shown I’m notably slower for most of a game is disheartening, a few games where we brought it back taught me nothing’s set in stone. The Dominator, an item that lets your team take control of a boss dinosaur, seems like a “blue shell” equalizer for the team behind to help with this. However, the team ahead also gets one near the end of the game, so it’s more of a tool to use at a more appropriate time than your enemies (like when you think the enemy team is fighting another boss dinosaur or about to finish their wave).Each round is split into two sections. The first is always the aforementioned PvE race. The second could be either another PvE race, a PVP mode, or a mode where you team up with the enemy team. While the game forces you to do a few PVP missions (like giving you one on your first mission for some reason), you have the option not to queue for them. However you go get a good EXP bonus for queuing Random, which my friends prefer. I personally don’t like PVP because it’s hard to see what’s happening, but switching to an exosuit that has an easier time in PVP like a sniper mitigates this somewhat.Speaking of exosuits, the “classes” in this game are great. They all looked fun when I watched an overview video of them, and the game itself did not disappoint. Each exosuit is grouped by whether they’re Offense, Defense, or Support-oriented and each suit has a unique playstyle in those types. For example, one tank focuses on keeping dinosaurs on them, another stuns swarms in their tracks, and another is based around countering. You can also switch suits on the fly. So if you happen to feel like playing a certain way or think another suit would fit your current scenario better, you have a lot of freedom. I think this is the best part of the game by far. You unlock alternate versions of the suits once you reach Level 20 with them, so that also gives you an incentive to focus suits in you want (which I enjoy).Now let’s get to the issues with the game. The biggest one is progression. You unlock a story beat every x missions you do, which unlocks a new mission that gets thrown in your random multiplayer pool. Then repeat. It is definitely a UNIQUE way of doing it… People say this is too slow and that the game gets repetitive before you unlock enough different missions. But honestly I didn’t feel that way. Maybe it’s because I started on a Double XP Weekend, but I think a lot of it came down to me switching up exosuits often (which made the same missions feel different enough).People complain about low dinosaur variety, but I think the variety comes from the context they (and you) are in. Different maps, modes, exosuits, and teams helped mitigate things feeling samey to me. I do believe missions are the same so it’s not entirely like Salmon Run where every run is truly different because different enemies and bosses spawn at different times/places, but only at around 30 hours in is this starting to become truly apparent to me.Exosuits get modules that upgrade them. The problem is they unlock as you level up a suit and some of these are very good, so the enemy team might just have better ones. Double XP Weekend mitigated this a lot for me for sure, but even without it and good modules, games haven’t felt one-sided. Still, I wish they would just make all modules available at the start.A complaint people have with this game that I can’t really refute is the repeated cutscenes. Each round starts with Leviathan talking and a notably long waiting room. While this does maybe give you a hint at what mission you’ll be doing based on what Leviathan says, it seems largely unnecessary. And while the waiting room is good for looking at your team’s comp and changing accordingly, it’s still too long. Plus, certain missions will always play certain cutscenes and sequences, too. This should be familiar to Final Fantasy 14 players. Personally this doesn’t bother me that much since it gives me an excuse to go on social media, but there should be a Vote To Skip option or something.This is a full-priced game with a battle pass and loot boxes. I’m not going to argue for it, but it also hasn’t been intrusive to me in Exoprimal. I don’t think you can even buy the lootboxes, skin drops have been common enough, and I’ve been entertained enough by the game itself. Because it’s a 3rd-person game, I think skins have more value (and there are a lot of really good skins actually), but to me the game doesn’t feel as monetized as you’d think. As someone who unfortunately buys cosmetics a lot, I only bought three skins on Steam and have just enjoyed random skins in the game. I was actually completely fine with not getting the battle pass and only got it to support the game; imagine that!Then of course there’s the playerbase issue. And, honest to god, even when only 100-200 players are on Steamcharts (which is most of the time I play)…I haven’t felt it. Maybe it’s because of the aforementioned social media thing, but I don’t think queues are nearly as long as you’d expect. As of this review, my friends and I have only gotten stomped by a team of level 1000s once, and there have been a noticeable amount of new players bringing us back to the first mission (and making me feel bad). Maybe the playerbase will dwindle into nothing as time goes on, but if you really are worried about the game dying then I’d hop on while it’s fine now. In only three weeks my friends and I have been obsessed and put in 30 hours, more than justifying the “steep” price tag. And we plan to play more! I think this is truly a really fun game worth experiencing, and I really hope it lasts or gets a second wind.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the reviews have stabilized, my thoughts:The game's pacing is way off. The first hour or two of the game I will freely admit makes it feel shallow, repetitive, samey, whatever you want to call it. But once you start to unlock additional game modes, special encounters, more rigs and modules, the game starts to shine. I'm now nearly 20 hours in and the game is still throwing curveballs at me. They just needed to make it more clear to consumers that there was much more to the game than what is initially presented.The graphics are also, while quite nice, a bit too flashy sometimes. Sometimes you just have to fire blindly through the visual clutter and trust in your hitmarkers to guide you. You can select what Exosuit you want to use before matchmaking starts, but there is no "role queue". One time I spawned in and literally everyone on my team was a Deadeye. There needs to be some effort on the game's part to make matches with balanced team compositions, or at least try to avoid repeaters. Not that there's anything inherently wrong about having two of the same suit on your side, that's fine. But having a team of all Deadeye is just silly (would be kinda funny though ngl). Additionally, it would be nice if there was a way to easily indicate to your teammates who you plan on switching to while you're standing there waiting with Mr. Leviathan. Maybe it calls out like "CONK KREET IS CHANGING TO KRIEG!" when you do the switch. This avoids several people swapping to fill out the team comp at the same time, all switching to the same class, and wasting time doing the class shuffle.Now that the negatives are out of the way, the positives.The graphics, while a bit much sometimes, are very impressive for how well the game runs. There can be hundreds of dinos on the screen all looking quite nice, and I don't notice a frame drop at all. Exosuits are designed with good attention to silhouettes, so they are easy to recognize from a distance (this is important in the PvP aspect).There are a wide variety of dinosaurs, even if they aren't used to their full potential most of the time. While you can just blindly mow down hundreds of raptors (and have a damn good time doing it), something like an anklyosaurus or a carnotaurus will force you to be smart about positioning, timing your attacks, coordination, etc. The gameplay is smooth, engaging, and fun. There's almost no downtime between waves of dinosaurs, just 10-20 seconds at most. Cooldowns for abilities are pretty reasonable across the board, exosuits are varied and customizable with rigs and modules. Things unlock at a pretty steady pace, and you get a decent amount of BikCoin just playing the game. I haven't felt the need to fork up any more money than the asking price.Sound design is great, love the combat noises and some of the music tracks are bangers for sure. Overall I would definitely recommend it, even at the steep asking price. II can't wait for the Monster Hunter colab to drop.

_childDocuments_.review: I am an extremely huge fan of the game and love the exosuits and the action and the overall feel. No bugs seemingly on launch and the characters all feel good to play. I'm a huge fan of the hordes of dinos that I get to murder with friends and randos'. However despite the really fun gameplay I am still not a fan or recommend picking it up UNTIl they fully commit to making a PVE mode. As it stands the game is really fun to play but the PVP feels tacked on and out of place and the speedrunning of levels just bums me out. I was really hoping to just kill LOTS of dinosaurs in a wave survival kind of setting with big bosses, we somewhat got that. I think if the game was developed around purely PVE it will do a whole lot better. Despite the criticisms I think the game would succeed better if they followed through instead of a purely live service PVP oriented shooter. I'm also not the biggest fan of bringing in a dinosaur to kill the enemy team. First off, The dinosaurs you can use have too much health and do too much damage, you can basically stun the enemy team into a corner for awhile until you die and while I understand it's to make things more tough for both sides at the end, it just comes off as unnecessary. There isn't much of a competitive edge either since you just have to be quicker. That's not skill. I really hope they add more PVE stuff cause I genuinely enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll redo the review after 30 hours in the game.The response to commands is fantastic, I have never noticed a slowdown or input lag.For the first 3-4 hours of the game I would have gladly returned it, but after getting the hang of it for a moment, understanding the various exosuits, understanding the types of dinosaurs, in the end this game is wonderful.after 30 hours can you already hear the repetition? Unfortunately yes, but it's not excessive, each mission can be different especially due to the PVP element in which at a certain point you have a carnotaur at your disposal with which to attack the opposing team. At the beginning this can be disturbing and for those who love PVE it can even be hateful, but in reality with that touch of randomness that never hurts, it's as if there was a more intelligent extra boss to fight, so it's not bad. (+10,000 points are always welcome)There are few Steam users, but cross-play and multiplatform is enabled so matches can be found rather quickly.Do you like exosuits and do you like killing dinosaurs? then this is the game for you.The thing I love most is blocking a triceratops' charge with the shield, really, you can feel the power of the triceratops impacting the shield and the exosuit using all its strength to contain it.Skins can be bought or unlocked with supply crates that you earn as you level up, from level 51 onwards, you get a supply crate for each level.Great community.No toxicity.Widely recommended.The dinosaurs are waiting for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Got to try out this game in a free-to-play weekend, on the first few matches I thought it seemed super fun and promising. The monetisation aspect of the game is a huge trash pile obv but I want to focus on the gameplay, and I will let people with no respect for their money waste it however they want, instead I want to focus on the gameplay. As I said the game looked like it'd be lots of fun at first, killing dinosaurs with huge mechsuits and explosions? Yes please! Then after you play a few matches the problems start showing up... Ridiculous amounts of cutscenes to watch, good in quality and acting but boring and obvious story overall so why make the game so focused around it? Did anyone really see this game concept and think "I hope the story is really good."? But what about the gameplay? Well both the PVE and PVP aspects have huge issues. First of all, the pve might as well not be there if you're playing pvp, the dinosaurs will NEVER manage to kill you, but you will either steamroll the enemy team or get steamrolled when you are able to fight each other. So the winner is decided strictly on the last few minutes of the match, making the rest of the match pretty much pointless. Oh and that's another thing, the "rest of the match" is you doing the same repetitive missions again and again and again and again and seeing the same 5 dinosaur types, mindlessly mowing them down with ease until pvp is enabled and a lvl 1000 player camps your lvl 3 party in spawn for 5 minutes. Major improvements needed, would not recommend, especially for that price.
_childDocuments_.name: Exoprimal

_childDocuments_.review: Sad this game isn't getting much love but also this game should have launched at a bit lower price.I had loads of fun making my way through the story mode which took me 30 hours to beat. Pretty much how the story mode in this works is you play a certain amount of games and special missions unlock which you fight a raid boss, but instead of also going against the enemy team you guys are working together in a 10 player raid which is really fun. Throughout your games you unlock different cut scenes and audio logs which progresses the story. The story wasn't anything crazy but it was enjoyable for me as it kept me wondering what will happen next and I actually liked the characters introduced throughout it.There are a total of 10 exo suits and 10 alpha variants of those exo suits, 4 DPS, 3 Tanks, and 3 Healers. The classes are well kitted so any of them can do their part to take down those dinos so you aren't just a Mercy main holding down left click and can actually play the game as a healer. The Alpha exo suit variants, which unlocks at level 20 for each character, changes up their kits, as changing up their weapons or how their abilities work. A small issue with them being a separate exo is that you can't use your skin from the base exo on the variant exo, but it's not that big of an issue.Now what exactly do we do? The game is 5v5 PvEvP but more weighted towards PvE where our main objective as an ExoFighter is to KILL KILL AND MURDER dinosaurs faster than the enemy team as you are both thrown the same objectives throughout the whole match. Objectives consist of things like Killing a specific amount of a specific dinosaur, capturing a point or multiple, killing Triceratops and/or a Tyrannosaurus, or even "pushing the payload" .You are fighting all types of dinosaurs small ones, big ones, and even ones that are controlled by a player on the enemy team, but it's not like they can keep invading you over and over as the tool (Dominators) drops only once or twice on the map per match.There is no in game store to buy skins or emotes and pretty much everything can be earned either through the the loot boxes (You can't buy them and only earn them through leveling) or by using the in game currency which you also can earn from the loot boxes or by leveling your account level and Exo suits, there are a few skin that are available as dlc through steam but they aren't heavily priced like most game prices their skins. The game does include a battle pass system which for the current season ( Season one) goes up to level 50, but can be avoided, as it is just Skins, emotes, and other cosmetics, no Exo suits locked behind the battlepass.I don't have an issue with how much I paid for this game as I had a lot of fun but I feel as most people will get turned off by having to pay $60 for it and it should have launched at $30-$40 price range, for me $40 seems about right. The game features crossplay so I find games within seconds so don't let the steam chart numbers fool you as the game is on game pass so a lot of players are over there. Disclaimer: If you do play on game pass and decide to buy it on steam you can't transfer your progress and another silly thing is that you can't party up with a game pass player if you are on steam, you can still match in matchmaking though

_childDocuments_.review: I truly don't think there's a game quite like Exoprimal. There's a lot of vitriol from either side regarding its design, but the truth is that whether or not it will be to your tastes is subjective. No one  to like the game for what it is, and that should be respected. But I also don't think it's fair to say the game is bad for being exactly what it was designed to be, especially not when Capcom has already discussed plans to expand the game's breadth of content in the future to accommodate those looking for a more co-operative experience, which I'll touch on later.Personally speaking, I adore the gameplay loop. Blow up dinosaurs as a team of cool robots in a PvEvP competitive speedrunning format. It's like if Tetris let you fill in the opponent's column with a T-Rex. The suits are all varied with interesting gimmicks, and leveling up is a steady process that rewards you with new ways to personalize those suits using various cosmetics and passive upgrades. If you're familiar with classic Call of Duty progression a la the original Modern Warfare titles, it's very similar in structure: level up your individual Exosuit and player levels to unlock new upgrade modules that provide boosts or even change the function of some abilities.The story isn't going to be what everyone is looking for, but I've enjoyed the way it's presented. It lets you focus on the meat of what you're here for—the multiplayer—and you can either skip it to get back into matches or enjoy the cork board web of mysteries. It's a totally absurd narrative with a wacky cast of diverse characters, and it's exactly what I'd expect from a game self aware about the fact that it looks like some ridiculous mock up you'd see on a gaming monitor advertisement.As for monetization, I don't  it, but it could be better. Cosmetic-only payments are ideal, especially if you're going to have the audacity of charging $60 as a base price. The monetization isn't what bothers me because I understand that profits need to be made, servers need to be maintained, and lights need to be on if the game is going to keep getting support and releasing free content updates. But to add multiple $5 cosmetic sets on top of a battle pass at launch with a $60 base price tag? That's a lot to ask of people when taking a risk on your new multiplayer title. If the base price was $30-40, I'd be a lot happier. That said, everything surrounding the entry price is fine. Yes, lootboxes exist. However, they only provide cosmetics, CANNOT be purchased for real money, and are handed out with considerable frequency alongside the in-game currency (that you also can't buy with real money), which can be used to bypass the lootboxes for the majority of cosmetic items. Think along the lines of Overwatch (NOT Overwatch 2) if it wasn't designed to try and pressure people into gambling. It's a fairly admirable system overall, but for a lot of people, the price of entry is going to be a tough pill to swallow.And regarding the aforementioned free title updates, Capcom has already given a roadmap for the game's future content. The first major title update will not only be adding alternate variations of  but also a strictly co-operative gamemode; a purely dedicated PvE mode for groups of five players. This is separate from the existing raid-style content of ten players that you can only get as a random event during Dino Survival. Given the demand there's been for this sort of content, I can only assume more like this will be coming in the future. I may love the competitive element of the game, but this can only be a good thing. More ways to enjoy a game I like, and new features to attract those looking for something different. My hope is that, by the time these things are added, it'll be possible to buy the game on a decent sale to attract more players understandably put off by the price tag.This has been a lot of words to say that I really do love this game. In a time where so many multiplayer games come out wanting to be a living, breathing ecosystem or whatever other buzzwords, it's been refreshing to have a game that hearkens back to the old philosophy of just making a game that's fun to play with other people. No, it's not perfect. I've already addressed the $60 price tag, and I have issues with the rubberbanding systems in place feeling questionably effective at times. But it's hard to care when I've had such a damn good time killing dinosaurs. No daily challenges, no toxic stat spread, no ranked competitive grind: just dead-simple fun rolling the mission objective slot machine and playing dress up with my little robots. If you're looking for a good drop-in, drop-out multiplayer experience then Exoprimal has delivered in spades with more variety to come in the near future. At worst, it's a game worth keeping on your radar to see what's new when the price goes down.

_childDocuments_.review: I think with a lot of reviews; good or bad, most people will go and throw an opinion out there and rate a game without helping viewers understand why besides "I found the game good/bad." I find myself looking for what are the Pros and Cons are of games and their game play so I can see if it's the right game for me. So, I'll go ahead and throw this list in here so people can get a good general idea. Hope this helps! :DGame Play:- Online VS Multiplayer- Match-based- PVP competitive game direction- Simple HUD set up- Fast-Paced FPS game play- 5 player teams- Cross-platformPros:- High resolution shooting Dinos- Easy to learn the game- Match based rounds make it easy to come and go- No penalty to player if you have to leave in the middle of the match- Easy to get back into if you've been away for long- Matches are not like HALO and other match based systems, it will find whatever players that are queued up in your data center whether the are starting out or higher level players. (Prevents burn outs and getting paired against sweats constantly)- Match queues are very quick when playing during live times on your server (If you're playing in early hours on a NA or JP data center, you'll likely find long queue times before the system either finds someone or puts you into a match by yourself)- No pay to win mechanics (Only thing is if you would like to buy the Season Pass for an additional $20 USD ea. season, it is all just cosmetic items)- No Fear of Missing Out (All seasonal pass items and in-game events rotate back and players will have another opportunity to earn those items)- It only takes 56 matches to get through the Story portion to unlock all game modes- You don't have to do any PVP (There is a mode that if you'd like to do just PVP of PVE competitive, you can equip that for less EXP gain to enjoy the game how you want to)- It's really easy to earn in game currency to unlock Mods for improving game play or Cosmetic items that do not drop from Loot boxes- Loot box earn system through player levels. (If you don't get an item, you still get coins for rewards that can be used to purchase them)- Any stickers/decals/pendants/emotes are player based, not Suit based- In matches, can communicate with players through stickers or Voice - Matches do not require any one to be a set "class" (You could play all Support or Damage dealing if you'd like)- If you don't want to play against those from Console you can make a selection to turn it off in Settings- There is a player block/report function (Just because it uses Anti-cheat, doesn't mean someone didn't find a way to get around it. You can report them without any issues)- If you don't want to hear a player, you can mute them (You can also turn Voice off completely in settings)- Is crazy fun- Great game to play with 4 of your friends after work on your downtimeCons:- The game is poorly optimized (While high resolution, it eats unnecessarily at resources)- Players can leave the match at anytime (Whether if you're in the middle or not, they can leave and hop back right into a different instance; but you can do the same)- Queue times differ depending on the time you're playing (There are high volume times and there are times no one is on, it will take a while for you to get placed in a match by yourself with just bots. Meaning you can't play at all in the wee hours of your region.)- If you do not remember to go to your "Analysis" tab between queuing matches if you're just starting to the game, you will not progress through story, which will not unlock new game modes- You HAVE to do the story to unlock more game modes- You can not choose what game mode you get (If you want just to play Area defense or protect the pay load, you're just going to have to keep playing till you rotate around)- There is no text chat communication function (You have to use stickers, emotes, or Voice)- The player block/report function can only be used in the match (if you get to the Player analysis screen at the end, there is still time to block/report players as there is a players tab. However, once you leave a match, you can't block/report problematic players)- In game player community can be quite toxic (I personal have voice chat turned off because if you do not, you will still be able to hear other players, even if you're not plugged in. More people from street fighter community than Monster Hunter community of Capcom came to play the game is seems.)- You can't actively friend or play with a buddy cross platform (The game uses the Console or Steam in-laid Friend system, you can't add a friend from PC to Console and vice versa. If you want to play together, you have to queue at the same time and hope you get into a match together)Sorry, it's long, but hopefully people can just take what they need.

_childDocuments_.review: Dinosaurs and PvP collide. I had a blast. I didn't mind that the story was tied to the PvPvE mode. You learn a lot about how to play competitively by doing all the PvP. The bad part about this game is actually the point system not the progression. You don't get rewarded very much for doing the objectives like staying inside the zone so a lot of players just run off and kill dinos or just spam heals the entire match. I would like to see a specific queue for certain story missions at least once you've unlocked them. The PvE mode seems pointless until you unlock more and more story which unlocks 10 man raids. I'm sure every FPS gamer would enjoy these modes but you'll have to randomly get them sometimes unless you were the one that progressed the story far enough to unlock them.I have no hard issues with the monetization in the game. All of it is skins with the exception of the early unlock pack which blocks 3 exosuits from being played at account level 1. If they removed this and let everyone play them from the start then I don't think there are much issues to really talk about. Maybe some QoL stuff like looking at abilities of every suit from the main menu. IDK what the deal is with cross play but luckily all my friends are on steam. From my understanding xbox and steam players cannot join each other's parties but are still thrown into the same matchmaking.I crashed one time over the course of 3 days but matchmaking was quick. Takes about 24 hours of playtime to reach the end of the campaign. There's tons of replay-ability but only if you want to get into a FPS game. Kill, respawn, repeat. That's how all FPS games are. I wouldn't get the game if PvE was your only desire from this game. If you are still on the fence about the game then wait for the next few updates and see where we are at. Savage mode (PvE only) unlocks but requires the campaign to be completed and then 11 more variant exosuits will be available within a month. I can't wait to see the monster hunter collab they got coming.

_childDocuments_.review: Give it a chance! Story is very good. Gameplay is fun and active. Its a somewhat competitive PvEvP shooter that pits you up against other players to complete all the objectives the fastest. With final objective being either a random choice between PvP or PvE interactions. You can choose between what kind of final objective there is after a recent update and it makes agency a lot better for preferences. One thing that does stay consistent is dominators, the ability to slow down the enemy team by taking control of a large dinosaur and attacking the enemy team.Story is good, it is highly integral to the game's progression and you would be missing out on a lot if you do skip it. Not gonna spoil it. Soundtrack is good, loved the credits song though. Progression is done through completing matches, just completing them. Around fifty-five matches is all the story progress done to get to final boss. I had fun in every one of the matches and it was truly a blast just playing and destroying dinosaurs. Some matches are special as they are story missions.There are ten different exosuits to choose from, each unique to their class with different abilities. Three of them you can unlock for free by just playing and leveling up every ten levels. Each suit can be outfitted with different chipsets that either enhances the capabilities of the suit or upgrading the abilities. Alongside the suits comes a rig, a utility slot that can be fitted with supporting weapons or defensive measures. Eventually, there will be variant suits to unlock that completely alters the playstyle of the suit to fit more needs. Those variant suits will come in future updates and they look promising. Overall, very good. Get it either full price or on sale. More updates will come along like monster hunter with its season to season content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Amongst all the loud murmurs of disinterest for this game, I was incredibly excited to play this game. I'm not usually one for team shooters, and modern ones with battle passes even less, but this game was truly magical. Trust Capcom to make me enjoy a genre of game i'd normally pass by without a look.Exoprimal is one of the most fun shooters i've ever played, in part because of Dinosaurs (dinosaurs will never be uncool to me), and partly because its almost entirely a PvE experience, playing as a team while you fight the hoardes of raptors and more that come your way. I was initially skeptical of the PvP aspects to the matches, as i felt there was no need for it when the PvE is so fun, but the way individual exosuits interact with one another in a PvP environment creates a wholly different type of fun! Some suits have entirely new uses when against other players, some are better against players than the AI! The flow of this game is something I feel isnt replicated anywhere else, working alongside teammates and synergising against both the computer and the enemy.Now, the story. It starts off with a super fun premise, and from there only gets better as it adds more and more mysteries and information, building to a climax where all the loose ends are tied up one by one, and one of the most fun final bosses in modern gaming, using all the mechanics you've been learning throughout your time playing. I can imagine the writing feeling cringy to some people, but I grew to find the characters incredibly endearing.At the time of writing this, the game has incredibly low numbers of players. since a match needs 5 people on each team, you can understand how asking for 10 people just to host a single match can be difficult. you can still find a game, and the game will place bots to fill the spots at worst, so theres no risk of not getting a game, but the chances of a full team of human players will be slim. Of course, the big kicker is that the story is entirely cutscenes and conversational logs, occasionally leading up to a unique mission type or boss fight, unlocking as you progress by playing online. To me this is the big blemish on this game, since no single player or even online co-op campaign means that once this game's server's go down, there will be no way to play it. For such a big budget project for Capcom, this feels incredibly shortsighted, like it was pushed simply to satiate current trends. Regardless, the devs worked with what they were given and created an experience I won't soon forget. There is so much more I wish i could talk about, going into each exosuit individually and the story in more detail, but to keep things brief and spoiler-free, I must relent.If people are still playing this in the future, I hope to play with you some day on Bikitoa Island.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm extremely disappointed by Exoprimal, mainly due to the PvE mode of the game.I'm a fan of PvE types of games. I only play Call of Duty for the Zombies mode, I LOVE Splatoon's Salmon Run, I played TF2 MVM a lot, basically I like PvE games. When I saw this game being revealed on the Capcom Showcase, it looked like it could be a fun PvE game. Well, it wasn't bad, but not what I expected.Let me specify this: Exoprimal is NOT a PvE game. Yes, it has a PvE mode, but you are ALWAYS competing against another team. Capcom's response to the criticism of PvE was not handled correctly. To describe it, the PvP mode is fighting AI dinosaurs, then you complete an objective while you can kill the enemy team. What is the PvE mode? It is literally PvP expect you don't fight the enemy team direcetly. Even in PvE, you can still fight the enemy team by capturing a dinosaur and control it to fight the enemy team. That isn't PvE, that's PvP with less conditions, or if you want, it is PvEvP.Alongside that, Exoprimal is a $60 game that feels like there's barely any content to represent the price. Don't get me wrong, it is a good looking game, but it's the typical shooter-type game with a battle pass and all of that. The gameplay is unique, but that doesn't mean it'll last. I honestly won't be surprised if the game ends up free or ends service in the coming months, because this game does not do enough to warrant the price.I seriously hope Capcom will listen to feedback, because they've at least shown that they know some of the criticisms. That said, they didn't solve the PvE issue people gave from the test, and it was that the PvE mode wasn't PvE, and it still isn't. I may have less than an hour on the game, and while I usually want to spend more time to review a game, I feel like this game is an exception from playing the PvE mode.If you're looking for a PvE game, you can pick up games like StarShip Troopers: Extermination which does the whole fight AI enemies while completing objectives far better, and at a lower price.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't pay for Exoprimal, but if I did, I would be pretty disappointed with what is currently available. Live service games tend to expand and fill in the gaps left from release, but it's hard to appreciate a game's future in the present. I guess that's why they made it about time travel.Abbreviated Review: My experience with Exoprimal was a distinctly parabolic journey. After the fairly basic tutorial, the game throws you into the story with very little exposition and has you suffering a traumatic crash landing and blasting dinosaurs within minutes. I appreciated the urgency, but the story and explanation of why you're even here in the first place take hours to finally come together. This makes it a little difficult to feel connected with what ultimately become some decent characters with fun personalities and a story that, while not interactive, is worth the journey once you get into it.However, this game is practically a clinic on bad pacing. You currently start with only one game mode which you repeat dozens of times to make your way through the game. While you can select "PvE" or "PvP" (or either with a small bonus), all of the missions are technically PvP since even in the PvE option, you're racing your mysterious competition and can still lose to them. The story and these missions are almost entirely separate – only crossing over for a handful of unique missions – so you can play a few rounds then head over to this 'wheel of progression' to unlock some narrative. As you reveal these little folders of knowledge miraculously ascertained from repeating the same tasks of shooting dinosaurs that fall out of wet-looking spheres, the story is presented in chunks varying from Metal Gear Solid-style picture conversations to full-blown cutscenes.As I settled into the monotony of missions, it eventually opened up more with more maps, more enemy variety, and an increase in difficulty that made it a lot more enjoyable to play. Here, the sporadic story missions and boss fights were a welcome dose of additional variety and made those first five hours of repetition fade away. However, when I started getting repeated story missions (sometimes conflicting with game-changing story events), the experience started to feel tedious again. My enjoyment level hit rock bottom when I went into the final mission and realized it required the coordination of 10 random people to do a multi-stage boss fight. This was made worse when failure meant relaunching the entire mission with potentially a squad of people new to it and always sitting through the cutscenes.The core gameplay of Exoprimal can be as enjoyable as any of the many live-service shooter games on the market. It's easy to compare this to Warframe and Destiny, but I didn't realize until I looked at an old review how much it feels like Anthem. Now, I know that's a scary thought, but Anthem's issues weren't so much in the feel of the combat. Exorpimal doesn't suffer from the scourge of loading screens and doesn't have any loot at all, so it can't mess up that system. In fact, Exoprimal has little downtime at all, and if you want, you can essentially ignore the story for mission after mission – though I believe that may have been a contributing factor for what had me stuck in the same handful of maps.The maps are one of the issues for the game though. They are already small but also rope you onto a path that has you looping around these tiny areas essentially just navigating to the combat areas. Sometimes you will literally loop in a circle and fight in a place you downed a hundred dinosaurs earlier. The speed at which you cycle through missions (15-30 minutes max) doesn't help in diminishing how often you see maps recycled either.It seems like a waste of time explaining what exosuits are available in great detail because they're all filling familiar roles – but are well-executed in their crafting. Tanks have more health and moderate damage, assaults have distinct attack styles like AOE grenades and assault rifles for more damage, and healers heal and stun – though in a way that's interactive enough to not be yet another 'boring healer' role. You can also swap between suits any time before or during the mission. This part of the game is mechanically sound and fun, for the most part, but it is held back by the lack of gameplay customizability you can perform with each of the suits. The Barrage you play at the start of the game is going to be (mostly) the same one you play 20 hours later.Going into the game, I thought the monetization was going to be a huge issue. It still is an issue, but it wasn't quite as bad as I assumed. There are loot boxes containing cosmetic items, a battle pass, and three locked characters when you start the game. However, you don't seem to be able to buy the loot boxes, they're only given as part of your account leveling up. It's still annoying to have RNG involved, but without a purchasing element, it's at least not gambling. The character unlocks that can be purchased with a "starter pack" weren't much of an issue either, though. They're mostly locked behind the leveling system since the amount of in-game currency required once you achieve that is negligible. That leaves only the battle pass, which is still another way to milk you for money but is comprised of your typical cosmetics and weird dance moves, so it's easy to ignore.Aside from the repetition issues and limited content, Exoprimal launched without an "endgame," so once you finish the story you can only do the same missions again. In a couple of days, the "Savage Gauntlet" mode will be available for "veteran players," which I assume is going to be the option for the endgame experience. However, without any kind of loot-based system and the very limited customization you can achieve through the Rigs and Modules (an interchangeable activated tool/weapon and three modules for buffs) I'm not sure what you'll be working toward with this.Exoprimal has a solid premise with fun characters and gameplay that is satisfying while in the action. However, the lack of content, maps, game modes, mechanical variety, and general monotony makes it lose its luster much faster than other live service games. With it being on Game Pass, it does have a chance to thrive through sheer persistence like Sea of Thieves or Fallout 76, but paying $60 for this, let alone $70 or more with the battle pass, is outright crazy. This feels like it was meant to be a free-to-play game and someone changed their mind just before launch. It can be fun at times, but the amount of mediocrity you have to wade through to get there diminishes its value well below the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and very fun time in this dinosaur starved gaming world.The price point is a tad high but I believe its worth it by virtue of the fact of how CAPCOM releases updates for their games via their Title Update system, with stuff already planned into the first quarter of 2024 I wholeheartedly believe this game to be a good purchase.Do note however in its current state the game is rather repetitive but it is varied enough to keep myself and a friend fully engaged finding weird ways to mess with the enemy team and start to memorize spawn locations/strategies/combos etc.The gameplay is essentially a mishmash of the following; Gambit from Destiny 2, Overwatch/TF2 Payload, Warframe waves of enemies and the corniness and campiness of CAPCOM Dino Crisis. _childDocuments_.review: I've honestly been looking forward to this game, not because I had any big expectations, simply because I knew it would be something to semi-mindlessly enjoy. This game has actually surprised me with the way the combat and progression systems are set up. Each Exo-suit is fun to use and the modules (upgrades) allow you to change your play-style and priorities according to what you think/feel is most beneficial to either yourself or (preferably) the team.The leveling is actually insanely fast and the 'story' progression is done in a unique way, It ties to the scaling difficulty of newer missions and game modes unlocked as player level increases. The game did feel repetitive for the first couple of hours, mainly because it felt easy, but as new modes and enemies are unlocked it definitely becomes more challenging and forced players to switch up the way they approach some tasks.As for the those that want a more PvE experience.. remember what the base concept of the game/lore is about.. creating the perfect.. using combat data. No matter what mode you play you will be going up against other Exo-fighters. The only difference with PvE is that you don't directly fight other humanoid players. As far as them using the dominator.. just think of it as an intelligent AI control dino.. Kite it, Kill it. (I personally don't get the complaints on that one sorry)I think this game is incredibly fun, but I get that not everyone can make that full commitment without the assurance of a refund, so I'd recommend checking out higher level game-play videos in order to make a more informed decision.Best of luck, and happy hunting.. "You are completing objectives faster than the enemy team" :)

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I started playing this game, I have been engrossed in almost everything about it--the story, the characters, the voice acting, the dinosaurs, the combat, the music--all of these things are fluent, smooth, and easy to digest. Granted, the story does start off slow, but after you do about a dozen matches of Dino Survival, things will pick up  and your missions will start being more varied in objectives, including escort missions, sabotaging machinery, defending VTOLs, even full-on boss fights where you have to cooperate with the enemy team.Regardless of whether you win or lose, you are rewarded with further story progression, worldbuilding and funny dialogue between your crew, and currency to either upgrade your exosuits via specifically-tailored modules for their skillset, or buy cosmetic items ranging from skins to emotes to show off your style.Capcom have given us a wonderful addition to their list of IPs, and it's criminal that it hasn't gotten more attention. If you have the money to spare, I implore you to try this game out and see for yourself how amazing it is. Or, if you don't have as much to spend on the Steam version, you can get it on Xbox Game Pass--just beware that your saves will not carry over if you make decent progress on a different version. I learned that the hard way, and that's really the only other negative I can think of.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too good. Monster Hunter feel andd quality, but third person shooter horde mode with objectives. The game's downfall is the menu just showing off one gamemode at the beginning (you get more later on) as I've completed the story, almost all suits at level 20 and player level 100+, but I'm still meeting new dinos and missions and maps. A new player might believe there's only like 5-10 missions if they only play a few hours or group up with a friend that's lower level as them since new missions get unlocked as you level up (no indication of this in-game either, you just have to experience it) and the lowest leveled player controls the pool of missions available (which makes sense as they do get harder). The season pass you can gladly skip unlike most games and it's cheaper aswell (no Blizzard greed). 90% of cosmetics are outside paywalls and progression doesn't feel grindy at all. It's a strange take on story presentation, but it's actually very well thought out for a multiplayer game you didn't expect to have such a great story. There's only worldbuilding intro and basic tutorial before you play multiplayer for the rest of the game, even story missions. However you cannot manually choose missions, so story progression can get very on/off depending on the friends you play with or even solo (less so solo) as you need to get enough progression before the next story mission is available, then you need to matchmake with people at the same place. This hasn't been a problem, just a note, but this is how friends can "halt" your progression somewhat, but there's no real downside to this as you won't powerlevel and just destroy the next mission. Solid 9/10 we need more of these highlights to this year. There's also more of this coming for free already this month.

_childDocuments_.review: After clocking my first ~100 hrs within the first few days of release I can confidently recommend this game to anyone on the fence. The reality is the game is everything they present in the trailers. You kill an assload of dinosaurs while progressing through a decent story (which you can do with friends) with a pretty sizable starting roster. The three locked mechs you can easily get through playing the game and unlocking them with currency (pocket change for all three) and play them. This variety of dinosaurs, maps, and stages come from playing the game and passing through cutscenes that adds a nice lore element to the game. When it comes to the multiplayer aspect they kinda shorted some people I felt with the inability to craft parties over multiple platforms. Because they used the Capcom ID system and recently made Street Fighter 6 cross-platform, folks figured they could do the same with this game. It didn't impact me personally because all of my friends were purchasing on Steam, but people adjacent to me who wanted the game with PS5 or Xbox Games Pass were disappointed and didn't buy the game because of it. I think it is an integration that they might implement in the future, but who knows honestly. Doesn't impact my recommendation TOO much.Talking about microtransactions is another thing. The game offers a pass that unlocks cosmetics in exchange for playing the game as you would normally. It was $15 from what I remember (don't quote me) and the cosmetics on there are pretty cool. Dances, emblems, skins, weapon skins, all super nice. Outside of that there are the loot chests that you frequently unlock (pre lvl 50) and then every level after lvl 50 you. That loot chest or "war chest" as its called has the other cosmetics like charms, skins, and so on. All that goes to say is the game is EXTREMELY generous with the access to cool cosmetics to apply to your mechs. I was shocked and quickly came to appreciate how fair the loot and unlocks were, so I'm super happy on that end.The mechs themselves are super cool all around. The storyline explains their importance as you go, but as you play with them you kinda start to appreciate their detail. The gameplay tweaks with modules and add-ons that give stat buffs or ability buffs are really cool, definitely gives each mech some gameplay variability. That shines in team fights and PVP modes in the form of a healer who heals more, or a DPS that has more CC. Super cool with the ultimate ability mechanic as well, personal favorite is Deadeye since its like an instant in button when placed properly. The Dominator is worth its own little section, just the little holobox that makes you turn into a badass dinosaur that you can control and use to do massive damage to objectives, enemies, or just clear the path for your team. There's a lot of room for skill expression with a giant barrel rolling triceratops (its broken ngl). The only funny thing is the controls which can be wonky your first few times using it, and then there's the occasional random who picks it up in a game and wastes it, but that can't be helped. Super fun mechanic, hoping to see more dino options in the future for controlling.Savage Gauntlet dropped a few days ago as per the time of me writing this, and I've played it a few times with a 3 man. I'm hoping to get a 5, but I think the mode is super fun despite not making it too far each time I ran it. I want to try and get a sweet record myself, just waves of objectives and enemies to keep us occupied. Also excited for August's update, should be sweet.That's about it for my review, specific questions can be asked and whatnot for anything I didn't directly cover. This is my first game review, little sorry about getting it out late but here it is! My article is strictly my opinion, so of course none of this is "objective fact" :)

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's basically the New Overwatch, but from Capcom with Apex combined with Gambit from Destiny 2.Basic game play comes down to team vs team. It's basically a race to complete as many points each one having an objective to kill x amount of dinosaurs. The last point having a boss dinosaur. Then round 2 starts at different times. The faster team gets a head start escorting a payload. Somewhere about 60% of the way the opponents team can invade the opposing team of they are behind with a dinosaur. Near the end of the payload escort about 80 to 90% of the way both teams are able to fight each other with their exo suits to see who can get the payload to the final point. After that the teams continue to fight to stop each other from staying on the payload to upload the data.Imho I like it but it feels sorta confused because it feels like a bunch of games all at one.1/3 of the cosmetics are real money. The rest you can purchase with ingame currency called bikcoin. The shop feels alot closer to what overwatch 1 was.Each exo suit has their own play styles ranging from your regular dps/tank/support roles. You can play different roles. You can switch roles when you die like in overwatch. The exo suits are separately leveled up and get their own rewards for each level they gain. You can equip your suits with different mods you unlock as your progress and you can level up those mods with bikcoin. The premium pass does have some cool stuff I'm not gonna lie. I kind of wish the game was advertised more. I found it by accident. It sucks that it's getting a lot of backlash because people are polarized to either playing pvp or pve but not both at once. Also the monetization does suck. In In way can be invasive especially after you come out of you first game and you are greeted with a bunch of ads for mtx. However since overwatch went free to play. I feel like you'd spend less money on this game then on overwatch having to buy the separate skins and season passes. Also Blizzard kind of sucks at the moment - but this game is from Capcom. So I want to believe in it. I would say try it. It's not bad. It's not the best. It does have flaws, however it still shows promise. There is apparently a road map of the next three seasons out there and they will apparently be collaborating with SF6 and Monster Hunter. So there is something to look forward to. I will admit though in the end its a wonky Mashup of several games but I am having fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR; Keep playing until about 15-20 matches played, that's when things get insane. This game is such dumb fun, it's you and others VS hordes upon hordes of dinosaurs. The exo suit power fantasy is real. One of the biggest complaints is how repetitive the game is. Do not listen to these reviews. The game's progression system in terms of unlocking new game modes is weird but if you stick with it, you'll be see a huge improvement in the game play and replay ability. It takes roughly 20 matches to start getting into the deep of things and the more story you unlock the more mission variety there is. I want to say roughly every 20% of the story progress adds in a handful of game mode variants and new enemies to fight and it gets really, really good. We're talking full on MMO boss mechanic fights where you stop fighting the enemy team just to team up to slay a huge enemy with a fulfilling victory for everyone with full on wipe and and limited respawn mechanics during these fights. I'm only 41% into the story and just hit a major event which feels like it changed my entire perspective on this game and took it from a 7/10 to a solid 9/10. The game makes you  powerful and as you slot in upgrades to your exo suit, you keep getting more and more powerful. It feels rewarding. If you're looking for a brain-off mass horde mode game with elements of PVPVE, this is it for you. And with the promise of PVE as a game mode shortly, this game will only be getting better.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about buying this game, read this review.All the people complaining about the DLC/Battlepass etc. Haven't taken the time to intelligently think about what these things are actually providing. All but one DLC are purely for cosmetics, and the premium battlepass is also purely cosmetics. The one DLC that is not cosmetic, simply helps you unlock 3 of the 10 Exosuits instantly. Those three suits can also be obtained from playing the game and getting to levels 20,30, and 40 respectively.Yes, there are lootboxes, no you don't pay for any of them. You earn lootboxes from level ups, and can even view your player level status to see when you will get a lootbox. Inside these lootboxes are, guess what? Cosmetics. Most cosmetics you can also buy with the in-game currency, which guess what? You earn that simply from playing the game and leveling up either your Exosuit or Player Level. There isn't any premium currency or premium account time either. All paid content is purely cosmetic.There is a story to the game, and the primary game mode(Dino Survival) relies on you playing it in order to progress the story, which also progresses the amount of content you get access to, that content being new dinosaurs to fight, new objectives to do, it doesn't toss everything it can at you from the beginning, it sets you down slowly.How Dino Survival works, is there are two missions with a set of 3 objectives. You compete with the enemy team to complete them the fastest. After those two missions are finished, you go into the final mission, which if you choose Random like I do, it's a coin-toss on whether that final Mission will be a PvP style mission where you will be able to directly fight the enemy team, or a PvE style mission that so far seems to be a third mission set of 3 objectives. Whoever beats all the missions first, wins.I highly suggest giving the game a try, it is quite fun and reminds me a little bit of Lost Planet 2 and Orion: Prelude having a baby.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:I played through the entire story, completing it in 58 games (the number of games required may vary depending on your rating). Even after unlocking everything, I continued to receive new missions, and I am now 128 games into the experience. As I played with higher level players, the missions became quite challenging.Summary:While there are some repetitions in the game, I don't really mind them because each playthrough feels significantly different. The queue times are relatively short, ranging from 5 to 30 seconds. Throughout my 52 hours of gameplay, I only experienced one disconnect, which is a rare occurrence for me in games.Now, the question of whether it's worth spending 60-70€ on the deluxe edition (compared to the basic edition priced at 60€) is a difficult one to answer. Personally, I found a lot of enjoyment in the game, particularly due to the engaging story and awesome boss fights. Though it may be a bit pricey, I would still consider buying it again.14.07.23TL;DR: nice game; nothing groundbreaking, but solid and fun!7 hours in. Here are some key points (which are partly missed by the negative reviews):More content (maps, enemies) is unlocked by progressing through the main story. You pick up notes while playing, which unlock new parts of the story.PVE: There are still two teams competing to clear the map quickly. Each team has a chance to spawn a player-controlled dinosaur (1 max 2 per match!) that invades the other team. Calling this PvP feels inaccurate because it's not really character vs. character engagement.PVEVP: Every mission consists of two parts. The first part includes about 3-6 objectives. After each objective, the narrator (AI) tells you if your team was faster or slower than the enemy team, giving you an impression of your team's efficiency. You can switch operators at any time, similar to Overwatch, making the sessions very flexible.So far: 0 bugs, 0 disconnects, 0 crashes; the game works flawlessly. Performance is nice (4k on ultra with a 3080 and ultrawide screen, although there is a really small black line on the left and right). Other developers should take this as an example.Pay-to-win: There is no advantage you can buy with cash. The only thing available in the deluxe edition is the ability to unlock 3 out of 10 exosuits (classes), which you would otherwise need to unlock. The other 7 exosuits are available from the start. You cannot purchase loot boxes containing skins for exosuits and weapons, as well as banners and player icons.The grind is relatively low compared to other live service games.The game can become very chaotic, which is a matter of personal preference (I like it - it gives the opportunity to get better).If you're expecting a relaxed dinosaur hunting experience, you will be disappointed. There is a certain level of pressure that fits the setting: you have to fight for your life and for an AI. If you cannot handle losing games or have problems relying on a good team composition and players who know what to do (defending an area means staying in the area), then this might not be for you. However, even if you lose, you still receive rewards.Steamcharts "only" represents PC players and doesn't include console players since crossplay is activated from the beginning. Current queue times in Europe are around 15-20 seconds.Personal note: this is not EDF, Destiny or something else.
