_childDocuments_.review: It's everything I could ever hope for in a game. I grew up on Taiko Drum Master for PS2 and, of course, GTA (lol), and have grown to love other shooters. So when I heard that this game was coming out, and a day before my birthday, I HAD to get it. And I think this game is the most fun I've had while dying every 2 minutes in years. As of writing this, I've completed all Valkyrie except Odr, and completed just one of the challenges (though admittedly, I haven't spent much time on those yet). I have also unlocked all loyalty with Huginn and only spent maybe 800 with Muninn. Below is what I think are some pros/cons about this game, for those who are on the fence:+ Variety of weapons that each have unique reloading and shooting patterns+ Loyalty system with shopkeepers (unlock more options/freebies as you spend more with them)+ Blessings that up your individual stats are added fun and can be the thing that changes the game for you, or means you can't afford an important item in Huginn's shop that you've been waiting for.+ Well rooms are an interesting concept that I'm glad to see.+ Challenges are a great way to quickly grind some coins if you're up for the risk.+ Can adjust rhythm sensitivity if you're new to rhythm games or if you've been playing them for a while+ Can change cursor to show/hide metronome (which personally I like not seeing it; makes it a bit harder for me)+ Can adjust saturation of the levels if that sort of stuff hurts your eyes (I love the high saturation but I don't have any eye problems lol)+ Variety of Valkyrie to choose from that each have their own unique starting abilities/weapons/traits (when you unlock them)+ "Easy" isn't actually that easy unless you've been playing rhythm games for a hot minute. And "Hard", well... it's hard.+ Boss fights beat me into the ground in the best way possible. Each boss has their own unique abilities and patterns to learn as you put more hours into the game.- Some of the descriptions for secondaries/ultimates are vague**- Some of the descriptions for equipment are vague**- Only 5 challenges so far. Fund the devs so they can make more stuff!- Blacksmith has sort of ridiculous pricing. It's always 5, 15, and 30 coins for the different tiered weapons, but sometimes a pistol ends up in the 15 or even 30 tier pedestal. Kind of wish each weapon had its own price point or was in a certain tier and only those within that tier can show up on the 5/15/30 coin pedestals respectively.- Mini bosses are kind of really easy. At least for me.- For a while, I didn't know that you could pull the Challenges lever multiple times (up to 3). I think this Con is just my own idiocy, but... it's not obvious. Usually you just pull a lever once to toggle between two settings, not flip it back and forth for 3 different functions! Maybe I'm just dull...- Blessings are kind of hard to see on certain levels where they blend in too much and there isn't much indication that they are there except for a quick sheen.**They are quite vague, but to me that also adds a bit of fun to the game, because "Ooh, what the hell does this do??" and then I lose 25 health. I personally like figuring things out hands-on, but some people don't. Take these two Cons as you will.This will be a game I'll keep coming back to for sure. If just to die by a dumb baby bat...

_childDocuments_.review: Background: I'm a big fan and a veteran of roguelike games, especially roguelike shooters. One of my favorite games ever is one such shooter, Ziggurat.This game, BPM, has a few good things going for it, such as secret rooms (which I love), fluid combat, good room variety, and a plethora of standard roguelike mechanics (donating excess money on this run for use on future runs, upgrading shops the more you buy from them, casino-like luck-based things you can gamble money on etc.) and its music-beat-based combat on the vein of Crypt of the Necrodancer.But it also has a lot of bad things going for it.1- Monochromatic oversaturated aesthetic looks bad (in my humble opinion) and makes it harder to spot enemies and make out boss attacks. I died to one of the bosses because I couldn't understand everything that was going on and how his attacks were telegraphed (or not) by flashes of the screen. Can be somewhat improved by reducing saturation in the options2- There is no tutorial or help at all, so you have to figure out EVERYTHING by yourself. I reckon this can actually be a plus to some. While I was able to figure out the beat-based mechanic quickly, less experienced players might not be able to.3- The game design is backwards for a roguelike. Normally in roguelikes, as you die often, you're able to spend on permanent upgrades so that you are automatically stronger next run. On this one, you only get extra powers if you beat the last boss (clear a run), since the aforementioned shop loyalty upgrades only increase the variety of items offered for purchase on them. So players who obviously don't need those extra powers (otherwise they wouldn't have completed a run) get them, while players who struggle and could use those extra powers to help them, don't get them.4- The beat-based mechanic can be really annoying, because if you miss the shot (shoot off the beat) there will be a cooldown period before you can shoot again as a sort of mini-punishment, but what's worse, if you try to shoot again within this period, the cooldown will reset, so clicking several times in sequence (i.e. when you're panicking) will lead to you being unable to shoot for a while. Constantly having to stop clicking and wait for the cooldown to subside during intense fights gets annoying really fast.5- Worst of all: the maximum range you can shoot enemies from is way too poor, so you're forced to constantly get near the enemies to be able to damage them. Normally that's OK, but this makes some rooms REALLY unfair, namely when there are a lot of fly enemies shooting super fast projectiles at you. If you were able to snipe them from afar, you could dodge the projectiles, but having to be near them means you WILL get hit a lot even if you're moving and dodging constantly, through no fault of your own. This is the most unfair aspect. Can be mitigated with "max range" upgrades you find during the runs, but you'll likely die before you enough of those. And that's on EASY difficulty.I have refunded this game mainly due to point 5, which I find unacceptable. Maybe I will try this game again if they get rid of the maximum range mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really frustrating because of how divisive the different parts of it are to me. I absolutely love the premise, the music, and the style it has. Beyond that, I love how Awe Interactive came up with a pretty unexplored idea and went hard on it. However, there are so many problems that hit me in the face every time I’m playing and having a good time that bring it all the way back down from an awesome experience to just an “OK” one.All in all, this is a game that I had a good time with for a few hours but sadly won’t be continuing with. I want so badly to love this game because of how cool the premise is and how good the gunplay is, but there are so many flaws (even more than what I mentioned) that bring the experience way down for me and drastically reduce the fun I can have with it. I don’t think this game is really worth full price for most people, but may be worth getting on sale. That said, I think the roguelite aspects of this game are basic at best and there are a lot of better options out there if you’re looking for a fun roguelite experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Sound design? Excellent. Everything falls short however.BPM is a rougelike just like many others, get powerups, find better weapons, kick ass, die, repeat.Gameplay honestly is not so bad, despite my 14 minutes of it... The charm is there and can feel great when you get a hang of it.But let me tell you, fellow rougelike enthusiast to another player, two biggest problems about this game.First and foremost, you definitelly  saw it right away... The visuals, right? Bunch of filters stuck on top and called it a style... Sure might work in some cases but not for a hecktic first person shooter. Not only you are forced to maintain a beat to every single movement you do, but also somehow keep a track of 8 different enemies and 10 projectiles heading your way. Not only it is already a lot of information to process, but you will NOT be able to see everything as well. It's not a blur, don't get me wrong - you just don't get a big, differently coloured warning to your brain that you are about to get hit and you should change your trajectory. Also you're surrounded, also you got thrown off-rythm, enjoy instant death!It's incredibly bad game design, some might say to make it harder for player but... Is it fair? Is it fun? You won't even know what killed you or what you were supposed to do, so learning this game is gonna be as equally bad. And there won't seem to be any plans towards fixing anything. All of this because of single visual choice.Secondly major issue, rougelike.But isn't that the core principle of the game? Yes! But they never took what makes rougelikes fun. They are not unique. Same song, same level, same enemies, same mechanic, your every single playthrough is going to be copy pasted for hours until the end. Looked game up quite a lot online before purchase, it's as bad as they say about this problem.Buy it, play for like an hour if you insist, but keep in mind that the game design team absolutely messed up with the foundations.Soundtrack mixed in with sound effects slaps tho. But please... For the love of god, double check with playtesters if a game you make is something that you could play for hours without switching to something more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty solid start for a game. I'm at 11 hours currently and only need three more winning runs to have all the achievements. The learning curve is low-moderate, but it's really more about the items you find than the characters or playstyle that really decides a run. I'd like to see them expand further on the idea. Maybe more randomized mini bosses for each stage, alternate music tracks(off 4/4 rhythm so the gameplay isn't the same besides gun choices[These could be tied to characters to give more purpose to rerunning after hard victories with said characters]), and better item variation. There are clear cut better items to look for that make runs a breeze, and I'm unsure why there are so many movement speed items when you're already super mobile with double jump and dashes to begin with.Overall a fun game for $20USD. If you're hesitant based on current reviews, then I'd wait for a $15 sale later on after more content is added to fill out the game a bit better. After release they updated the game with a bunch of fixes and a new gun, so hopefully they're funneling the money they're currently receiving into expanding the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, is now my go-to when I have a little spare time.Really, really Fun. If you like music or have ever played an instrument, then you are probably going to feel special satisfaction by the mechanics of the game. Just watching gameplays for me is ASMR.The "follow the beat" is not just a mechanic in this game, is the WHOLE theme. The Ai attacks and takes desicions on the beat, your character model moves to the beat when walking, the boss fatalities are the most satisfying thing ever, and Hugin and Munin are the most adorable vendors you will ever see (and Hugin's song, I love it).I don't recommend it if you have trouble following the beat though, yes there is a "no-beat" mode, but honestly you remove most of the reason for playing this game instead of any other shooter if you do this.

_childDocuments_.review: Flat out, Bullets per minute is one of the best games on steam if you can overlook the few flaws that it has. The two biggest pros are:The gameplay is this games biggest selling point, as it is by far one of the more cathartic games I have ever played. The satisfying feeling you get as you shoot, reload, jump, dodge, and use abilities to the music is absolutely amazing. The difficulty, while stiff, is not overbearing (WIth one note I will address later) after some sufficient practice.The music is phenomenal, I have been listening to the tracks in this game on and off for months now and any time they get stuck in my head, it’s always a welcome surprise as they are all very catchy without being monotonous.The two biggest cons are:The RNG in this game could really use some tuning. I understand this is a rouge like but there should be some weighting, but I have had many runs coming out of the first area with no keys, into a barren modifier on the second stage, its honestly not worth continuing at that point and generally resetHellish, the new difficulty released with the Overdrive update. I have completed Hellish, even a with Sanngriðr and I think this difficulty is a mistake. It would be one thing to make you take double damage, or another to remove all sources of healing outside of non-gaurenteed shops, but both of these together, along with also making enemies tankier and even spawning later enemies earlier into the run means a LOT of runs are going to take a nose dive in the first area unless you get some blessed RNG. Honestly I think they way the devs should fix this is by just adding the health drops back, but that’s just my 2 centsOh, and I HATE the fly enemies. There is no reason a tiny, evasive, fireball shooting Fly, that can and will spawn in bulk, should have as much HP as a slow giant spider who is melee only. Fly enemies are -way- overtuned for what they should be. I still enjoy the game, and it easily gets my game of the year in 2020

_childDocuments_.review: Bullets Per Minute is a fairly interesting game that tries to combine roguelike elements with fairly standard FPS mechanics. Whilst I personally played the game without the rhythm mechanics, I can see how this game could be rather big with the rhythm game community. My time with the game was fairly enjoyable, but I wouldn't say the game itself was anything more than your standard FPS when you get down to the core.Judging the game for what it is, I can say that I suggest it to anyone looking for a hybridized FPS which has more parts to it than just shooting; However for those coming to it looking for an FPS roguelike experience, there are other games out there which accomplish this task in a much better fashion, even though this game was fun whilst I played it.For this review and others like it, feel free to check out and follow my personal Steam Curator page if you'd like! The Good:- Great soundtrack. With the game being a hybrid FPS-Rhythm game one of the biggest hurdles to tackle is the soundtrack, and it's quite good. Everything fits well with each map, and even with the rhythm mechanics turned off I still felt like the sounds from everything fit perfectly with it.- Sound design. Weapons sound chunky, your footsteps sound heavy, and enemies make very satisfying sounds upon being hit or upon death. Everything fits well with the soundtrack as well, and only really adds to the experience.- Five characters to choose from. Each character has their own quirks and presents the player with a different challenge and weapon to learn and potentially master. There's a character with a humble starting pistol, and another with aggressive jazz hands.- A large selection of weaponry to choose from. There's everything from a starting pistol all the way to bazookas, an angry super-soaker, quad shotgun, etc. You'll have multiple options as you play through the game, allowing you to diversify your gameplay as much as you like.- Upgrades seem to be catered to your chosen character. Unlike most roguelikes your upgrades seem to be chosen and catered to your chosen character as you play through the campaign. Truly the game feels as though it's built around making you feel like a badass as you play through it.The Ok:- Fairly standard FPS mechanics. When you strip away the rhythm game mechanics the FPS combat feels bland and at times unintuitive offering almost nothing that we've not particularly seen before from other FPS-roguelike hybrids. Weapons have a maximum distance they can fire which overall takes away from the general flow of combat as there's NOTHING saying why you cannot fire your GUN more than 10 feet in front of yourself. You're allowed to carry only a singular weapon with you at a time, when having multiple guns in this instance just feels like the logical progression, as you'd be able to string together weapon switches and combos from each one to amass a higher score when done on the beat.- Very short without the rhythm mechanics. Most roguelikes are quite short, but they require more playthroughs and perseverance than BPM does. With the rhythm mechanics turned off a runthrough of the game could easily take as little as 30 or so minutes to complete, and whilst it's still enjoyable the game does feel as though the overall timesink is tied to the rhythm mechanics. I can see how the game would be much longer with them turned on. There's only 8 stages total, and whilst diverse at times they don't feel diverse enough to actually increase the games longevity.- A moderate level of diversity to the maps. With random-level generation I've typically come to expect more than what seems to be five templates for a games overworld layouts. Whilst the way the generation works is interesting, it just feels like there's some missed opportunities such as more than just a single sub-boss per level, trap rooms, etc. There's also only a singular boss per stage as well, and whilst they do have randomized effects tied to them such as having a clone of themselves, it feels as though they're overall very samey and not at all difficult after having defeated them once.- An interesting enough upgrade and item system. Whilst there are items and upgrades in this game they all feel fairly unintuitive. Upgrades and items are fairly unimpressive with some of them seeming to have absolutely no place in the game, whereas others just feel kind of overkill depending on the weapon that you're using. Upgrades come in your standard flavor of one upgrade for the stat listed upon the shrine, and this leads to there not really being anything particular such as builds, but more so just grabbing everything you can, which seems fairly counterintuitive when there's five characters with their own unique abilities.The Bad:- Tracking Projectiles. I've said this a few times in the past, but projectiles which track the player add absolutely nothing to the experience other than being a gigantic nuisance. With how you're supposed to play on the beat with the rhythm mode and can only fire at the enemies on the beat some fights turn into a gigantic mess where all you could feasibly focus on doing is dodging whilst only being able to fire back once or twice before moving once more.- Rhythm mechanics which feel too strict when it comes to the more densely packed areas. I'm not sure how most people would go about playing this with the rhythm mechanic turned on, as there are some rooms in later stages which are densely packed with both sub-bosses and previous stage bosses which devolve into a projectile spamming mess.- Difficulties feel lackluster without the rhythm mechanics. Upon trying both easy and hard I found the experience without the rhythm mechanics turned on to have no discernible difference, with the enemies doing the same amount of damage and the game seemingly having no differentiation between the two when it comes to the standard FPS part of the game. I can only assume this is tied strictly to the rhythm mechanics of the game.-Final Score: 6.5/10.Worth $17.99 ($19.99 standard)? Honestly, it's hard to say for me. If you're coming into the game looking for a roguelike FPS experience and have no interest in the rhythm mechanics I'd say the answer to this question is no. Looking at it as a standard FPS I'd say it's worth about $10 as there are other roguelike FPS's for less which accomplish the same things this game does and more from an FPS STANDPOINT.Closing Thoughts: My experience with this game is entirely based around the non-rhythm mechanics version, and whilst I definitely enjoyed my time with the game it feels like there's a lot of missed opportunities regarding both the standard FPS mechanics and rhythm mechanics. If you're looking for a fast-paced roguelike FPS this isn't the first game I'd suggest for you, but I'd say I definitely had enough fun for me to warrant recommending it overall. I suppose overall the feel I get from BPM is that it's an Early Access title which is still trying to polish itself, even though it's a fully released title.

_childDocuments_.review: For a time signature of 4/4 the music is incredibly sophisticated, so kudos to the team who was in charge of the sound track.People may ask if the game is "objectively good", but that's a silly question (only computers can be truly objective), since anything one deems "objectively good" has their own opinions and past experiences as the foundation of that "objectivity"But enough philosophizing, IF you were (or still are) a fan of bands like Avenged Sevenfold, Disturbed, Bullet For My Valentine, and others within that genre of music (minus the lyrics and all the beautiful sophistication alternative rock can bring to the table), and a fan of fps games.THEN you will thoroughly enjoy Bullets Per Minute (BPM)!p.s.It takes a bit to get used to, but don't let that discourage you, it's a looottt of fun while & when you get the hang of it! (Great game to do in quick cycles when you have the down time or need a break from what you're currently playing)

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay looks flashy and is really fun when it works. But 75% of the time the game total garbage. The "rogue-lite" elements are horribly implemented, leading to either god-runs or ♥♥♥♥ runs, there is no middle ground. The music is really good but after restarting for the nth time, hearing the first song over and over again just makes me hate the music. The bosses are all over the place. The hardest boss in the game is the first boss. THE FIRST BOSS. Everyone else is such a joke, I've never seen such unbalance before. And before you say "ItS A RoguE-LiTe Its NOt SUpPosSeD to bE BalaNCeD". Risk of Rain 2 is one of my favorite rogues and that had more balancing in the first stage than in this whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. The only redeeming factors are the rhythm mechanics and custom music. Despite my other gripes with this game the core mechanics are fun as hell, it just sucks that everything else is such a dumpster fire. The visuals are makes my eyes bleed, and when you turn the saturation off the game looks boring. Also half the game is reused assets from a cancelled EA game, so the enemy designs are all over the place. Overall, I really can't recommend this game, at least at price of $20. If you really want this game get it for $5. After some time it gets really stale and I'd rather play better rhythm games like osu! or Crypt of the Necrodancer.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine combining Isaac, Doom and Guitar Hero. That's it, this is the game. Although the game is hard to grasp at first since nothing is explained to you - no boss mechanics, items, weapons. Nothing. If you're not fine with that, and want the devs to hold your hand while you're slowly progressing then sorry, it's just not the game for you. You're thrown into the stage and all you know is that you have to kill. everything. to the beat. I loved the game since the very beginning (even though i died 10 times before progressing to the next stage), and i couldn't get out of my mind comparisons with Isaac. How the shop works, chests, arena, items, it's all very similar, and that's cool and all, but i just wish there were more details on how items work or show more clearly what you give up when buing one thing from the shop. But apart from that and (oh god why?) filters on levels, the game is great and I'll be having fun in it for many more hours. Just please, let me disable those filters, becouse some of them can give you serious seizure after playing the game for longer time.

_childDocuments_.review: Though a little rough around the edges, this game gets it right where it matters and provides an incredibly fun and unique blend of first person shooter and rhythm game.Having played and been a big fan of the MOBA Paragon before it shut down, i'm noticing alot of assets from that game being used, including all of the main characters you play as, many of the bosses and most of the enemy units. The developers have also utilized alot of other assets, and then given the game this somewhat ugly saturated filter to make all the assets mesh since i imagine without it the art styles of different assets might not match.That said, what matters most is the gameplay, and it does that very well. The assets from Paragon were released for free by Epic Games, so they've done nothing wrong in using them to save time. I do hope any sequels or future games by this studio utilize custom assets instead of store-bought ones, but this is a marvelous first attempt, and at $20 (or less on sale) it's really hard not to recommend giving this game a go. It was instantly addictive and i can see myself coming back to this game for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I know it's cliche and often inaccurate to claim games are a straight riff or mash-up of other existing games, but If you like rhythm games, and you like Doom Eternal, and maybe you like Binding of Isaac as well, this game is a pretty nice mashup of those concepts into something pretty cool.  I could spend all day just firing and reloading certain guns to the music. It is beyond satisfying and really fun. There are characters with different traits to unlock and choose from, a decent selection of guns and powerups and magic, and a handful of dungeon levels that switch it up just enough to keep it interesting during a playthrough.  I think overall the balance *kinda* works, but there are big flaws. Some items are overpowered, and some of the strongest strategies will seriously put a damper on the core experience of dodging and shooting to the rhythm, which is what makes the game actually fun.  So far I've found if I limit myself to certain guns, even if they are weaker, I will have much more fun, and combo'd with the right powerups you can still stay relevant depending on your difficulty selection.  It took me a long time to finally bite the bullet and grab this game, but my biggest takeaways are:  - If the visual design (color-wise mostly) bugs you, that's a valid reason to avoid. It's pretty harsh and IMO was a mistake. I can tolerate it most of the time.- If the core mechanic of shooting and reloading to the music sounds fun to you, it probably will be.  - There are indeed problems with certain aspects of the design but don't let that stop you from having fun.  - I got it on sale for $10. I'd probably pay $20, but only if I had really needed something new to play. (I didn't really.)  But honestly 10 was a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game works it's awesome but I'd guess that for the majority of the time you play you will not have a good time and it's probably better spent somewhere else.enemy attack patterns from basic enemies can feel very frustrating to go against, which is most notable against any small enemy which are very abundant in the game, it can feel unfair to have 10-8 flying enemies which are difficult to hit in addition to firing projectiles. Some attacks from enemies are very well telegraphed but unfortunately a large roster of enemies and bosses have hard to read attacks. Some of the hardest enemies in the game are difficult because the way to dodge an attack or the way to properly damage them is not immediately obvious leading to many game overs until you give in and just google how to do it.The upgrades in this game are half and half, they are either completely worthless or completely broken, this is probably why most players have beaten the game with the first character, having found a broken combo that sucks out any meaningful gameplay that could've been there. It feels like your reward is playing less of the game. There's nothing inherently wrong with a very good weapon or upgrade  but having such a low point of entry like on the first floor that trivializes the rest of the game isn't very fun. I should also mention that there aren't even any unique or innovative items in the first place, most are very easy inserts that you could find in any roguelike.Using the guns can feel awesome and it's the part of the game that keeps bringing me back to play it, but some of them just feel clunky and unresponsive, especially projectile weapons in addition to both the shotgun and marksman rifle feeling absolutely awful to use; that being said all of the characters I tried have very fun to use starting guns. Reloading can feel very satisfying as it breaks up the gunplay whilst you are moving away from enemies, I'm not sure why but having infinite ammo weapons also feels quite bad.I with there was more immediate variety between each of the four starting characters as the only difference between them is their weapon and health, it would have been nice to see some more passives to spice up play. Characters that do have passives are cool but they aren't explained at all to the player.One part of the game I like is the spells as it feels really good to use on top of all the gunplay taking place, I think it's a shame that the game locks them behind having to complete the whole game with that character, it would make the game way easier but I think the easy mode is far from easy in the first place.It goes without saying since it's a rhythm game but everything sounds really good, from the music to the chunky reloads, some absolute bangers in here.I think it's a shame because this game can be fun but I don't think it's going to get updated, and in it's current state many runs feel unfair and unsatisfying even if you win, mostly due to poor game design and balancing.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, BPM is a good game. Not a great game, but good and worth buying if you like roguelikes, Doom-style FPSs, or rythem games. There are a few problems that keep it from being great, however.First is inconsistency in movement. When strafing around, there are no issues. However, when you are attempting the jumping puzzles, sometimes your character will jump short distances, other times, you'll be catapulted across the map. When trying to access secret areas or just clear a lava-pit, this inconsistency becomes frustrating.The second is enemy design. Specifically, some of the flying enemies and their hit-points. More times than I care to remember, I've had runs come to an unceremonious ends due to one or more small, hyper mobile flying enemies bombarding me with projectiles while I desperately try to unload a full clip into each one. This wouldn't be so bad if these enemies were uncommon, but they aren't. The worst offender of this design choice are the innocuously named "Fly," which will be a massive thorn in your side from the first to the final level. Worse still, they are the only enemy that has spawner enemies, meaning that if you load into a room with seven or so spawners, your in a desperate rush to kill as many as you can before the room is flooded with over a dozen highly mobile, highly accurate flying enemies with HP equal to a large melee enemy.Aside from the aforementioned design issues, the game plays well. Weapon, item and spell variety is good, and high score chasing keeps things fresh and fun, as does trying to clear the game with the various playable characters, each of which has a distinctive play style.Moderate recommend. Just be prepared to be frustrated with some of the design choices. And develop a deep, abiding hatred of flies.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just doesn't click with me at all. It's supposed to be a fun rhythm shooter, but everything seems to conspire against that idea. The graphics are a mess, making the enemies and their attacks blend into the environment, leaving me constantly surprised by yellow orbs flying out of walls when they're actually enemies.I gave it a shot when it was first released, but the same issues plagued it back then, leading me to quickly refund it after completing a run in just two hours. However, when I got it again as part of a random bundle from Fanatical, I thought I'd give it another chance. But being older and more critical of games now, I couldn't help but see why I shouldn't waste my time on something like this.Sure, the concept has potential, but the execution is so lackluster that I can't bring myself to recommend it. The graphics implementation is downright frustrating, as I'd rather see the enemies clearly on my screen instead of being taken aback by random orbs coming out of nowhere.The soundtrack, supposedly the saving grace, turned out to be a letdown too. Despite being a metal fan, the repetitive and monotonous tunes lost their appeal within just a couple of minutes. I know they tried to vary it with different tracks for each floor, but it doesn't salvage the overall experience.In the end, there's not much that works well in this game – from the graphics and gameplay to the soundtrack and level design. As a result, I can't, in good conscience, recommend it to others. If you're hankering for a metal rhythmic shooter, perhaps you should consider looking into Metal Hellsinger; I haven't played it myself, but it seems like a much better option.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the most fun, broken game i have ever played.BPM is a mix between a Dungeoncrawler, First Person Shooter, Rhythm game, with Roguelite elements.Every map is randomly generated, consisting of mostly square rooms with enemies, loot, shops, and other things in it.Every floor is finished by defeating the boss and going through a portal to the next floor.You shoot, reload, and dash on the beat of the music.Most Rhythm games fail here, either having great music and bad gameplay, or bad music but a fun gameplay. This was one of my major concerns since i am realy picky of the music (quality) i listen to and enjoy. BPM has a rock/metal type of music that you play to, consisting of mainly electric guitar and drum, that has the perfect balance between complexity and simplicity.  The music does not get repetitive because of this, and its also unassuming enough where someone who is not a big fan of rock/metal still might enjoy it.It takes a bit getting used to doing everything on the beat, since you dont play to a single instrument. Rather the music has a certain beats per minute, and this corosponds mainly to the guitar.There is an indicator around the crosshair that helps a bit, but its not 100% accurate.The quality of the rooms are a lot better then pictures and videos tend to show. The floors all have a specific feel to them, and every room is crafted with enough detail to make them interesting and not feel empty. The color wash over every floor does not remove the details they have.There are parts of the game that are too dark to see, or dont have the right collor difference to make it work visualy.Sometimes dropoffs and hazards are invisible, corners of the map or other places in a room are 100% black where no detail shows. There are Altars in the game where you upgrade your main stats, like damage, range, and so on. But these Altars are the same color as the walls and often tucked away in corners. This results in searching every room over and over to make sure you have them all, since they are so important but also hard to see.You select one of a few characters (you start with one unlocked) each one starting with a different weapon, health/armor, and other starting items or abilities. The game spawns you in a starting room that is empty and leads to other rooms. You kill enemies that might drop gold and keys, and you have to find a balance between spending and saving them up.Enemies are a mix between melee ground units, flying and ground units that shoot, and special enemies that often have AOE attacks or attacks you cant dodge.If you try to shoot/reload/dash off the beat, you will get penalized in two ways; the action wont happen, and you cant shoot/reload/dash for half a beat.You have to keep moving to dodge enemies and attacks, and staying on the beat helps you play the game better.I have not seen anyone talk about this, and the game is tagged as ''Roguelike'', so lets shine some light on this.You start every run off ''fresh'' with the starting things your character gets, and everything you find is fully random.However you unlock new characters by playing the game, and every coin you spend in the 2 shops will unlock more items being sold.These unlocks stay, and make the next run easier. Since you have more chance to find the things you want in shops, or even guarantee some items.''Huginn's shop'' is a normal health and item shop, and starts with only 2 pedestals selling potions. Spending gold will unlock up to 5 additional pedestals. Selling max health increase, shield, keys, equipment, and stats increases.''Muninn's armory'' is a weapon shop that starts with a single pedestal containing 1 low tier weapon. Spending gold will unlock up to 5 more pedestals. The first 2 unlocking tier 2 and tier 3 weapons. and the 4th pedestal always contains a +1 ammo upgrade.As much as this game does right with the music and replayability, it also does a lot of things wrong. Most of the things that are bad about the game, make this feel like an unfinished early access game. And are all things that are very easly fixed, if the developers would have spend a little time to pollish the game (or finish it).Everything from map generation, loot, enemies, weapons and gear, is extremely broken and unballanced.If you do well in the game is hugely determined by what the game trows at you, and often you will lose the game even if you play flawlessly. Not every run can be won by just playing good unfortunally.Enemies that have the most hitpoints and smallest hitboxes, are the enemies that have ranged attacks and attacks that you cant dodge. Some enemies have attack animations where you always take damage and those wont disappear when they die.Enemies can spawn on top or in front of you when you go to a next room, forcing you to take damage.Weapons and gear is unballanced, and what you get, or even if you get anything at all, is random. You can get a fireball-rocketlauncher with huge AOE damage that kills everything in a single hit paired with items that give you infinite ammo and homing shots. Or you might be stuck with your starting pistol with no upgrades, no stat increases, and struggle to even kill a single enemy because you dont deal damage nor have range.Nothing in the game is ballanced, and it realy shows. Things as simple as a clip upgrade, gives the same +1 increase in a 2 shot rocket launcher, as well as +1 to a minigun. These are easly ballanced and are just overlooked by the developers.Add to this the limited content and no options to modify the game other than dificulty, and it makes the game feel like an unfinished product. The little contact the developers have over twitter, shows that they are working on an xbox and playstation version. And most likely wont come back to this game for updates and fixes.Aside from the game feeling incomplete, it runs mostly smootly with little bugs from what i have encountered.There is a glitch where the walls flash white as if they clip through something, or visual bugs on occasion with floating weapons and other loot.These are mostly not gamebreaking, but they can be an issue if you have problems with flashing lights.I have noticed a bug where there are no frames for a short moment and you cant do anything, while the game still runs, making you teleport for about 1 beat. This is mostly not gamebreaking and did not happen often. But can end up making you take damage and cut a run short.This game is a fully functional game, but feels like an incomplete product with missing content and no balance what so ever.If you dont mind playing early access games, and dont mind the game not getting ''finished''. This might be a game you enjoy if you like the genre(s), and can look past the flaws.If you dont like unfinished products, i would suggest stearing clear of this game, since you most likely wont enjoy it for what it does have to offer.When you are unsure or money is an issue, buying it on discount is suggested. 16-17 euros is a lot of money for a game with this little content that feels unfinished. Even if the game does a lot of things right.

_childDocuments_.review: this is the most likely game that anyone will bring up if you ask about a rhythm-based fps game. while the penalty for being off-time is incredibly annoying and keeps you out of the rhythm for longer than it should, the timings are quite on-point. on your first launch you calibrate the timing for your monitor and audio to make sure that the timings are not unfair for you. almost all deaths i've felt i was at fault for, because i messed up somehow, whether through timings or not dodging attacks. the game itself is difficult to get accustomed to and can take an hour or so to get the hang of it; it took me about an hour myself to start making progress, and ended up fluking from asgard somehow. there are certain parts of the game that definitely need some sort of fixing, because people are able to cheese achievements through a few methods. the hardest character cannot take a single hit or they die, but with an extra life you can save-buffer and re-enter at the start of the level without any penalty. similar to the binding of isaac and its toughest character, the lost(or moreso the tainted lost), it makes it a lot more encouraging for people to cheese completion. the rng in the game is mediocre, with some issues time to time with getting the same things repeatedly. it isn't like the binding of isaac or other roguelikes where there are a lot of weapons and abilities, there's around a dozen or so per category. regardless, it still makes for some fun builds and attempts that you'll inevitable have.movement is quite odd and unusual, with bunnyhopping similar to quake or old source engine that can accumulate ridiculous amounts of speed, nullifying the practical use of dashing(holding the shift key). i think the maximum velocity based on bunnyhopping should be adjusted based on your speed stats in each run, just to encourage the use of dashing for its purpose. i'm unaware of any abilities or items that give a buff for dashing, but even if there are any, it still doesn't justify the use of it because it's incredibly inferior to bunnyhopping.all in all, the game is quite smooth and nice to play, but there are some minor issues that haven't been fixed which definitely should be considered and adjusted. by issues, i don't mean bugs, because i have experienced zero bugs so far; balance, rng, and workarounds are the most important issues i think should be addressed and resolved, hopefully sooner than later. if you like rhythm games, fps, and roguelikes, this mixes all three together with a great, enjoyable experience

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't understand exactly the first time why I didn't like this game, it had ALL the correct checkboxes for me to like it: a fast-paced FPS rogue-lite with rock rhythm and valkyries.But after some thought, here are the points of dislike that may help you:- The guns aren't satisfying      Shotguns don't feel any stronger than the starting pistol. The range and bad accuracy at the start of the game makes    you wonder if you are really hitting something, and when you do, doesn't feel impactful.- You spend more time reloading than firing    You have to press the reload button EACH STEP of the reload animation to fully reload your weapon, with the revolver requiring 7 presses for 6 shots. With upgrades and more stats I spent about 50%+ of a fight trying to reload my weapon. This was the most annoying part of the game, so much that I refused using the revolver even if it was the only upgrade for my pistol.- The enemies are generic      You are a valkyrie and is fighting in places like Asgard, but your enemies are scorpions and wasps. The bosses are cool though.- This monochromic art is really tiring      I enjoyed the screenshots and the videos, but the oversaturated monochrome starts tiring the eyes really fast. Also, it's common for enemies to be hard to distinguish during the most intense battles.- The randomness is bad    I know this happens with any rogue-lite, but this one is pretty stiff, many times you don't get any keys at all, or sometimes don't get any coins, or any shrines. Or sometimes you just faceroll and kill bosses with 3 hits. Randomness can create memorable moments, but the randomness in this game many times ruins it, because you can't access part of the game (like upgrades) because the game won't let you.- Controls take a moment until you can properly play the game     This is more a warning than a bad thing, just remember that a rhythm fps game is indeed pretty hard to control in the beginning.- The music always sounds the same  Since you have to shoot and dash with the beat, ALL the stages have the same beat. Combined with the generic hard rock it gets old fast.I hope this helps someone, I recommend watching some runs first, before buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for those of you with no rhythm.I LOVE the music and appreciate the gameplay, style, and all the elements of it, I see how they should mesh together. I also see that there are some issues that are common in procedurally generated rogue-a-likes, If you are ok with those elsewhere, you won't mind them here. I am not unfamiliar with rhythm games (Guitar Hero, Rock Band, and Crypt of the Necrodancer as examples) but my apparent lack of rhythm makes me suck at this game because it is brutal even on easy, I find myself in a loop of missing beats, failing to load or fire, and then dead by weak enemy. I am frustrated because /I want to be good/ at it to get past the first level and get more content of the game. Practice difficulty helps, but I wish there was a training mode or some UI tweaks to help with the timing of everything.Final Say:I am RECOMMENDING this game even though I lack rhythm because it is FUN, and the music and concept are great. But perhaps SKIP IT if you are REALLY BAD at rhythm games as there is minimal hand holding in the game and it is brutal.Bonus: Having said all of that I HIGHLY recommend getting  the soundtrack, I've been humming the games music and playing it separately.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game full of wishes.... devs wished to go back to old-school FPS, they wished to mimic the greats of the genre like Enter the Gungeon and they wished to implement a music mechanic to tie it all together.Paradoxically enough they mostly achieved most of it but in in the end I'm also wishing for many things like...• music variety (I'm 7hs in the the repetition, as good as it was for the first 3, is getting on my nerves. Different soundtrack per character would be a dream come true or even better, let me put my own music!)• rounded up difficulty (easy is pathetic after an hour, hard doesn't feel like much of a step up and from what I hear the last one is plainly unfair)• BOOM weapons (maybe because of the rhythm mechanic, although I don`t buy that, quite a few weapons feel seriously underwhelming specially the ones that go BOOM… the rocket launcher in particular is pathetic)• graphics (seriously… where are they?! There are none and they covered it with the ugliest filter I`ve ever seen… it`s so so so ugly...)There are other things that I dislike but these are the ones that would make me not purchase this if I hadn`t already taken the blind leap and landed on things that I do like as the game-play flow, the music mechanic, a few of the weapons and the overall pace of the thing.Do buy it for cheap. Enter with low expectations. You might have a riff of a time then.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelite FPS, old-school feel (which is good). Your actions are restricted by the beat of the soundtrack to which you get used quickly (means you will learn not to click triplets). Soundtrack is nice but repetitive. Graphics are nothing to talk about and just suit the game. You can turn down saturation but it's not as irritating as I had thought initially.Controls are okay. I wish there were more alternate keybind options so I can put jumping on Mouse4 and such. Relatively fluid movement, fast-paced. Air control, dashes, rocket jumps, double jumps, as expected. Grenade jumps are a bit iffy.It's unpolished. Kinda feels like the devs ran out of time. The 4th and last world (Helheim) has invisible walls and doesn't feel as geometrically accurate as the rest, feels rushed. Some stuff just seems off, like not being able to click the button to quit the game (you have to press Enter). Framerate is stable for the most part but has hard drops for me when entering full rooms or using certain scatter abilities with lots of effects. Overall very playable and enjoyable with some caveats, short loading times.Length of games is short but it feels nice and I wanted to go for one more run a lot. Items, weapons and powers aren't balanced as you'd probably know from other roguelites. Most gunplay feels good but don't expect gun porn. Selection is alright.Not sure if balancing would be out of place in a genre like this but there's a lot of unused fun content because there are good items and trash items. Example: There are boots that create an explosion on landing, a shield that increases critical damage on weakpoint shots and a bracer that allows your shots to penetrate enemies, but there is also double damage and shield regeneration and infinite flying, so effectively, unless you restrain yourself, you'll always go with like octuple damage and invulnerability instead of gimmicky things.I'd give it a 7/10 because I like it, but it could use some attention to detail. It's a very fun shooter and definitely recommendable if you like faster-paced shooters. I'd say it's worth full price for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and addicting gameplay. For someone who has no sense of beat, the games can be a bit punishing at times but once the pattern is learned, the game opens up. Amazing music, great diversity of weapons. Not to say the game is without its flaws. For one, new weapons can be a bit iffy as you have to relearn the reloads. Second is the items you obtain. They give very short details. Without spoiling anything too much, It would be nice if there was a little more detail when it came to said armor. Third thing is, if you find a perfect set up, you cannot die and the game because very simple. But ive only ran into this super awesome combo once out of 60 something runs so chances are it might be hard to find, but would to see certain things nerfed. Last and final piece, saturation. The visuals of the games are nice, but one level is just nothing but orange. Would like to see some more visuals come by along with not a color change but more details added. Other then that, game is great and would high recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: With the release of , it seems like this game is the "lesser" version but I think both games are good for different reasons. While  has the better overall quality (especially in the music category), BPM has put more thought into its gameplay and replayability and is therefore superior in that regard.For those looking for a quick rundown of each games' merits, here are a few key points:- Better replayability thanks to its randomly generated levels, weapons variety and pickups- Better rhythm mechanics, especially in boss and mob design- More weapons and better gunplay (examples: reload is an actual rhythm mechanic; some weapons can shoot and reload on off-beats)- No "slaughter" mechanic- Significantly better music quality with lots of variation depending on level progression / performance (including vocals)- Better visuals and a generally more likable art style (compared to BPM)- Story and voiced cutscenes- Solid game balance due to linear natureAs I said, both games are great on their own and I recommend both if you like shooters and rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a jammer with issues. The overall flow of the game is great, the music mechanic feels clunky at first, but once you get schmoovin it feels really good. Enemies are tactical, causing you to always be moving or dodging based on what you're fighting.That said, woo boy there is also some big cons. The game is thin, there's not much to unlock, every boss is the same every time, once you've won once...you've kinda done it all. The visuals are harsh, seeing things can be difficult and some very large enemy attacks effectively blind you because there's no color. There's also no invulnerability frames so some instances you can feel like you get 1-shot because an enemy shot a series of small bullets meant to zone you but if you walk into it, woopsie-doopsie, that's 5 hits in a quarter second.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a while, but then you realise that this game is simply either trivially easy or impossible to beat depending on the modifiers, spawns, rooms, and drops you get. No inbetween, as in 9 levels one of the two will happen eventually. If you are unlucky enough to get a bad combo of boss+modifier the game is over. Likewise, if you get lucky with a good combo of weapon+equip you automatically win the game.The rithm gimmick is fun, but it's also flawed. Most enemy attacks are on beat, but so is your dash/jump, and you already know how this will be a problem... Because of this, most of the gameplay is running in circles.It also has to be said, that most enemies are simply boring to look at and fight. Rooms are brim full of slugs and flies or equivalent up to the later levels, and you're way more likely to die from the bullet spam from fodder enemies than from an actually interesting attack, or from a boss even. These enemies are also near impossible to distinguish from their corpses, and, even if the latter disappear very fast, you're still likely to waste bullets on a dead spider. The bosses and minibosses are really REALLY good, but you waste most of the game time on comically bad mobs.Also, the progression between runs is poorly implemented, as the only thing that is transferrable is gold you can deposit/withdraw at a "bank" room, IF/WHEN it spawns. Emphasis on the if/when, because it is first of all an actually pretty rare spawn, and second of all because the combination of having a bank and having something worth spending on AND not having enough gold already is simply a super rare occurrence. Pretty much the only real use for the bank is for unlocking a character after depositing 100 gold you will almost never use. Sure, you then get a chest with some gold and a key after you do so, but it's largely inconsequential. Don't count on it, for all intents and purposes, this game is permadeath and you restart from zero. Not a bad thing lets be clear, but still has to be said.Final nail in the coffin is that some modifiers, guns, and equips are simply unfun from a gameplay perspective (looking at you dark levels... well, actually, NOT looking at much then). No way around that.I actually like the visual artstyle and concept, just to be clear, but the hours you see in this review are the hours this game is worth playing to me, and the price does not match its worth.

_childDocuments_.review: BPM: Bullets Per Minute is one of the most fun and addicting games I've played in awhile. It combines several of my favorite genres as it is a rhythm based First Person Shooter Roguelike. And that sounds like a lot of genres in one game and you may be right, but that doesn’t stop this game from being insanely fun.In Bullets Per Minute you have to fire your guns to the beat, reload to the beat, dodge to the beat, and pretty much just do everything to the beat of this super awesome rock opera. And so not only are you, and all your actions tied to the beat of the music, all the enemies are as well. So they kind of like to attack to the beat and will do choreographed moves and attacks that make them look like they are almost dancing to the beat of the music while trying to kill you.At first getting used to having to fire on the beat was pretty hard and a little awkward but eventually you will start getting the hang of the game and you can start focusing on getting further and further in the dungeon.All the different guns not only act differently in terms of what they shoot and how many bullets they have, but they also have different ways you have to interact with them to the beat of the music. So while a normal default pistol you can shoot to the beat and half beat of the music when you reload you only have to make one or two hits on the beat to fully reload because you can put the whole mag in, and this makes each weapon feel completely unique and different from each other.You can find coins to use in shops and donate to shrines to increase your stats and there are a ton of items to find and these can be some insane things like allowing you to fly, doubling your damage, giving you auto aim and other crazy things. You can also find secondary abilities and ultimate abilities as well that are super powerful.So between all the cool new guns you can find, the items you can obtain, and the stat increases you can get, you can have some really awesome builds that make you feel super powerful and godlike. Some roguelikes have a hard time finding a good balance between allowing the player to feel a little overpowered sometimes but still staying grounded and not game breaking and BPM does it perfectly. There are definitely some runs that make you feel way more powerful then you should but it never was game breaking for me especially because of the rhythm mechanics. You could have the most overpowered build in the game but if you choke and mess up the firing and reloading to the beat you could start messing up and choking and then you die before you know it. The artsyle is really cool and the rock opera soundtrack is fire and really ties in great to the gameplay.So overall if you are a fan of either FPS games, especially older classic shooters like DOOM, roguelikes, or rhythm games this is a must buy. And it's pretty impressive that it combined so many different genres and yet it feels absolutely wonderful to play. This is easily already making it on my top 10 games of 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tough one to review...At first i hated it, after few hours i kinda liked it then i realized that it didn't lived up to it's potential.Still a fun game and well worth picking up if you like fps games mixed with some rogue lite elements.The main problem with this game is that the gameplay doesn't really feel in sync with the music, so the whole gameplay loop doesn't work (for me at least).In the end it just plays like another regular fps.It's a cool idea but far from being that much innovative.In fact IIRC this concept of fps mixed with rhythm elements was first seen in Chroma, a cancelled game by Harmonix.There was also another indie game, Music Killer with a similar gameplay, so yeah BPM: BULLETS PER MINUTE is far from being a pioneer or anything revolutionary.Don't get me wrong BPM: BULLETS PER MINUTE is not a bad game, it's just not polished enough to be a must have.Kinda sad because there was lot of potential here.I still recommend it because this was a passion project from a very small indie team (only two devs afaik).They worked as hard as they could with a low budget and still delivered a nice game.I really like the visual style of the game, well done Awe Interactive !The game is fun to play, graphics and filters looks cool, it's fast paced and satisfying, theres many different weapons to use.Unfortunately there are some balancing issues, mostly because of the rng.In some runs you will be an unstoppable killing machine while in others you will get overwhelmed by swarms of ennemies, getting almost insta killed by some very hard to dodge projectiles or bosses moves.The randomly generated dungeons are well designed most of the times but it start to become repetitive probably a bit too fast.I noticed getting the same seeds or same level layout after only 5 or so hours.Few words about the soundtrack, well it's alright, nothing memorable though, could have been better.Like i said above, in the end BPM: BULLETS PER MINUTE plays just like another regular fps with some rogue lite elements so the main selling point of the game is not really it's best part.Guess we'll have to wait for Metal Hellsinger then, we'll probably get better graphics, better gameplay and a better soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Shoot to the beat, roguelike elements where each run is randomized. Plenty of weapons, enemies, abilities, and upgrades that will keep you coming back for more. If you do not like the music the game comes with you can fiddle around with CUSTOM MUSIC and put what you want to jam to in game. Only gripe with this game is that some of the challenges and characters are a pain to beat. For example theres this challenge called "Boss Rush", where you do not get any upgrades, just kill most of the bosses with your starting pistol. I feel this challenge would be made more fun (because the bosses can still get up to 3 modifiers), if there was a random drop of something after every boss, to make it more manageable. Also the final character is a huge pain to play because you literally die in 1 to everything, and there are very limited items that can stop this. So you have to hope you dont get screwed with op bosses and get good drops in order to have a chance, or you can just dodge everything and anything like a dj on meth. The only bug ive encounteres is rarely, enemies may attack off beat, and yknow that is really bad if you CANNOT under any circumstance get hit.Overall 8/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: BPM is one of those games that is personified by a Boss with a glowing target weakspot on his body. The fight is fun, you're enjoying it as much as you can, but you can't help but wonder how better the fight would be if the common convention of the Achilles heel wasn't being used. That's BPM in a nutshell: only the weakness is so big, that some will struggle to enjoy the game even with the other games strengths.The game's unique take on FPS gameplay may just seem like a FPS stacked with a rhythm gimmick on the surface, but there's level of detail underneath. Each gun and how you face enemies changes based on your reloads, your abilities, so much so that you do have to unlearn somme of the basics of 90s FPSes to really take advantage of all the game has to bring you. It's a hard learn curve: you will die several times in the early going, sometimes to what seems like complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but over time you will get better if you have the frustration tolerance high enough to deal with it in the early goings.If you're looking for a balanced experience however, you may not want to look here. There's definitely problems with balance as the game can literally give you everything but what other parts of the game are giving you (like never giving you a single key except for in specific mini-boss fights), and the game's procedural generation will screw you at times. With that said, when you're ridculously overpowered with infinite ammo and a gun that can 3 shot bosses.....you sorta don't care about those other ones.Back to the Achilles heel: which in this game, is the visual presentation. Make no mistake, you can change all you want about the graphical settings here, mess around with the saturation levels per the options menu: nothing will make you happy. While this seems to have come from a limited budget, the problem is that it constantly gets in the way of gameplay. Whether it's enemies blending into the background or being blinded by large flashes of lights, you'll find yourself squinting even in the midst of battle, and wondering if you're missing something. The UI beat in the middle of the screen may be the worst offender, as specific actions to do can become Herculean tasks in the middle of the chaos of battle as you literally can't see what it's trying to tell you. You would think that you would eventually adjust, but even after 15 hours I've had problems and I never got used to it. This is especially troubling for those who have red-green colorblindness, as with the nature of several of the levels, you basically won't be able to play.Sure, the game has other weaknesses, but that one stands out as the one that will stop several people in their tracks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game confuses me greatly.I can't tell if it's more a rhythm game, roguelike, or an arcade game, but it doesn't hit any of them right?If it's supposed to be more of an arcade game:It is an absolute sin that you can finish a playthrough with 0 points. Easy mode point drain is way too fast, almost inaccessible fast. Like getting 90+ combos doesn't matter at all fast. Doesn't feel like killing anything is rewarding in that regard. Sure you killed a massive dragon and slayed many things, and did so without guidance. No points for you though. Killing enemies should be more incentivized. Like a kill combo that drops when you get hit rather than just a combo for rhythm combo. If it's supposed to be more of a rhythm game:Rhythm games is a genre that is incredible simple to gauge and understand fully. This game doesn't have a tutorial like any great rhythm game, but it isn't a fully-fledged rhythm game and it needs to explain what things mean. The rhythm cross hair/indicator is a bit misleading, not rhythm wise but more so indication wise. I had to rely on tips given in between runs to gauge how to play at all. Like what do half of the indicators even mean? The jump indicator looks exactly the same as the dash left and right indicator so what would intuition imply? Dash forward. Not jump. Practice mode was useless at teaching the fundamentals of the game. What are the hit windows? Are they adjustable? What does the 3 settings even imply? It's too vague to apply actual feel of timing from other games like Etterna, Osu, etc. What was my accuracy after the run? Why does dashing break combo but reloading doesn't? Why isn't it explained to begin with? If it's supposed to be more of a roguelike:All the good guns are in the same pool as the ♥♥♥♥ ones so it feels unbalanced. There should be implied risk involved with attaining these sorts of weapons. (Aka at the end of challenges instead of just sitting in shops). It's more satisfying for builds to come together during the mid-end game. Some upgrade pools don't even apply to guns you get. If you get a gun that has unlimited ammo in the clip, why do you get max clip upgrades? There's legitimately no benefit for playing the game with the array of weapons that could be offered because there's no incentive to. Give a score multiplier for less used weapons or something along those lines. Time spent in run usually doesn't punish people much in the genre due to the implications of risk = reward, the point drain really kills the idea of exploring thoroughly and finding secrets in the game and actually fighting sometimes. The upgrades are a bit misleading. A specific example is the upgrade that makes loadouts "permanent". This doesn't do that at all. It allows the player to stack items during a single run. It's a good concept for an upgrade just misleading.The score system overall is alright but it doesn't exactly line up with this mish-mash of genres as well as it could. What could be changed about it? Well here's my take.Arcade elements: there should be a pool of points that are able to be attained at a maximum without it slowly draining. This could be a kill combo based on kills attained during either during a timer based multiplier, or one based on not getting hit. Since it seems the rewards from the rooms worsen if you get hit the latter would be best. More importantly leave it out of the drain pool so people can actually get some sort of a score arcade wise. Add base point gains for finishing levels and getting upgrades (discluding repeats/swap outs). If you want to punish people for being slow make it a separate mode for the same drain as is or give a penalty for those who take ample time to complete levels and reward those who take less (think dead cells). Rhythm wise: the multiplier is great but what breaks combo should be made consistent across all shooting/movement elements, god please show an accuracy. Maybe even punish people for missing shots instead of draining it. Lots of arcade games punish people for not being accurate (like hitting sweets pots) and it'd tie in well with accuracy multipliers. Most importantly if you want a drain system keep it to the rhythm elements. It can be a higher amount but there should be static points that cannot be drained. At least not at hundreds/thousands per second on easy.Roguelike: most of the arcade elements are already in a lot of roguelike and scoring based of those I've provided here is suitable enough for it.Ultimately I wouldn't play this game if it wasn't a great concept, didn't have controller support, great quality sound elements, decent enough ui, or satisfying gameplay mechanics. It's all very great to play and quite enjoyable in all regards. It just lacks polish or help for new players and it's a big turn-off.Though none of the issues are gonna stop me from playing it so.Eat my ass this is a positive overall experience and i'mma rate it as such and put more time into playing it. :P

_childDocuments_.review: People are saying this game is just an asset flip. Without it's main mechanic it would be just a mundane dungeon crawler shoot-em-up. If these things are true then the devs of this game basically made something interesting and hyped up out of nothing, which is a feat in itself.The whole point of the game is that you're an angel going through mythic places with a goal to find and kill Nidhogg. However while in pursuit of this goal you're limited by one thing - you can only fire your weapon (and use abilities) to the rhytm of currently played music. This on itself makes game much trickier, but also much more rewarding when you start getting good at it.The complaint about game being overly saturated in bright red colour and it's varietes is valid, the intensity of it can be toned down in options but turning it to 0 just makes game grey scaled, which is kinda weird. My personal complaint is that by third stage difficulty curve ramps up extremely high by making rooms very open (a.k.a. with no covers to protect yourself with) while they're filled by 20+ ranged enemies pelting you with ranged attacks with various patterns you're just expected to predict and avoid and usually at least one or two fly nests that keeps endlessly spawning more ranged enemies that scatter across the place while you're already barely handling the initial spawns. I finished only one run so far and that was only because RNG granted me a weapon firing some latch-on mines that 3-shot every boss up to the Nidhogg (so I didn't have to try over and over again to get boss patterns down as they would die before second attack) and a "no longer reload your gun" item which carried me hard.Hopefully the devs keep working on the game to make it more interesting (like for example adding branching paths Dead Cells style or something) and smooth out the difficulty curve with enemy spawns, because the basis they've made so far is very good.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw BPM, I wrote it off. Boy am I glad I did!BPM just... hits right. I'm a big music person. I play a handful of instruments, did band all throughout my schooling and some of college, and write music as a hobby, and I almost immediately caught on to how you have to sync actions to the music. It creates a VERY satisfying gameplay loop that ends up working quite well in-tandem with shooter mechanics.Keeping on the beat while having to dodge, aim, and reload tactfully is a very unique gameplay style, and I find it really entertaining. Can't say whether it is worth $20 as I got it in Humble Choice, but its for sure worth the Humble Choice selection! Give her a shot if you're musically inclined or just like rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: Great rythm FPS with a very addictive gameplay. It's a must for metalheads. I clocked almost 20 hours into this game and enjoyed every second. I had to lower my saturation bar to 65% on every level, just to be able to play the game, and still it's far from perfect.2) There are almost no descriptions on items and abilities, making it impossible to actually understand what anything does exactly, so I had to Goolge everything.I saw a lot of people advising to rebind the reload key to right-click, because they find it easier to reload on the beat. _childDocuments_.review: Gun play feels good, soundtrack is good, enemies and characters are uninteresting and balancing is abysmal.Both the gun play and soundtrack are the strongest points of this game, also they kind of go together, as the main mechanic of the game is doing stuff on rhythm. Shooting, reloading and dodging on the rhythm are really interesting mechanics and are pretty fun overall, if they were accompanied by interesting and fun enemies to go against they would make for a pretty enjoyable game.However, the enemies are not fun to go against, most of them feel like the same thing but with a different skin, there are basically the ones who fly and the ones who don't, those who charge at you and those who throw stuff at you, that's it, they don't have any distinguishable characteristics from any other enemies in any other game. The bosses also aren't anything special, none of them are memorable nor have any distinguishable attack patterns as far as I remember, the only one that has one is the first boss, which has an attack where he damages one side and you have to dodge to the other size, other than that the bosses are just stronger normal enemies. The enemies design doesn't help them either, they're as bland as they get, we have a scorpion and a spider and dark_mage.jpeg and etc, not bad designs but you'll forget them after 2.5 seconds after closing the game because they're so generic. The same can be said about the characters you play as, none of them stand out with their design, and considering none of them have a personality (as far as I know) you'll also quickly forget them.What really got me out of this game was the balancing, I played with around 6 weapons before refunding the game and the difference in power between them was absurd. Some weapons just straight up one-shot every single thing in the game and made the bosses extremely easy, while other weapons are so under powered that I'd rather just stick up with the standard pistol, some are just equivalent to the standard pistol but with a longer reload time. There are also equipments which are also pretty damn unbalanced, some examples are the boots, while one grants you the ability to fly another one just makes you slightly faster, and the shields, one can just make the game extremely easy by giving you infinite ammo and another one buffs criticals or whatever. There are ultimates which are also unbalanced, such as throwing 4 coins at the ground, healing yourself a decent amount or losing HP for luck(?), there are also some side skills like freezing an enemy for some time, shooting some pallets that deal horrible damage and doing whatever to your enemy with the death mark (I honestly couldn't figure what it did, if it was a damage buff I didn't notice it). So yeah, eventually the game would boil down to "Restart until you get the good stuff". First thing I can compare it to is The Binding of Isaac, in both you can get pretty bad items at the start that might screw your run over, but I feel like this game doesn't give you as many opportunities to turn the tables as TBOI does, for me that's the biggest flaw of this game.The animations are great and the visuals are good, except for the dark variants of the arenas, they just look terrible. If the intent was to make the arenas more difficult by messing with your vision they did it, the dark arenas just give you headaches if you look at them for too long, for some reason the flashlight of the dark arenas is so damn bright, even reducing the gamma doesn't help.So overall it's just a bland game with some atrocious balancing, it's not terrible but there are so much better stuff to play out there, it really doesn't deserve your attention.
