_childDocuments_.review: Combines the best parts of Immortal Redneck with Crypt of the Necrodancer gameplay, with Doom sound and world design, however currently lacks little diversity and needs a little visual tidying up.The gameplay and music of this game are fantastic and make this game well worth trying out. It's fast paced and challenging to a degree and can be punishing if you aren't constantly moving and shooting. The overall world design, music, and enemies fits perfectly together to create a decent visual and audio harmony, however right now replayability is limited in my humble opinion. In terms of run variety, it is rather limited. Don't come into this game expecting Binding of Isaac, where every run is different and unique, levels of diversity. A fair portion of weapons feel rather similar, just slightly different (2 or 3 beats to reload, firing every other beat, for example), and lack a lot of creativity you'd find in games like Gunfire Reborn where weapons have various firing modes, hitscan/projectile, secondary effects, etc. On the plus side, weapons feel very balanced compared to other games, where almost all weapons, maybe with the exception of some starting pistols, being strong enough to take down the final boss. Similarly items are very generic, with effects such as double damage, fire twice as fast, never reload, the game really lacks items that makes runs feel unique and different. The one thing I do like though is only being able to equip one of a shield, boots, gloves, and helmet to prevent runs just using every item under the sun until you're an unstoppable force moving through very stoppable objects. The game could certainly do with more items and especially items that come with a cost, for example speeding up music 1.5x at a cost of losing hp for example. There's a lot of potential of what could be done to make runs fun and challenging, and making the gameplay feel unique. Right now though, it is far too easy to stack damage items with a shotgun, and beat the final boss before it even has a chance of killing you. It's also worth noting that whilst the world design is good with the music, on it's own it does feel lacklustre and repetitive, and there are some issues that should be addressed by the devs. Rooms do lack flare and creativity with them being generic box shaped areas, with minimal changes from room to room and floor to floor. Chests and shrines can be very hard to see as they often match the same colour as the environment around them and only give off light from a distance. It also doesn't help that they are very miss-able, with one shrine being a literal rock with a stone coloured bowl in front of it. There is also a filter on some of the later levels that does the game a disservice by pumping the saturation too much and causing the game to be a bit of an eyesore and makes the issues with chests being hard to see, even worse. I'm torn whether to give this game a positive or negative review. There is clearly a lot of potential that could come out of this game, and the gameplay and music alone make this an enjoyable experience, at least for a few hours. Unfortunately with the lacklustre visuals and disappointing amount of weapons, items, and character diversity, it makes the game feel stale rapidly. Right now, I would recommend this game, however that would be on the basis that the devs can continue to add content to the game and make some changes to the visuals. If this game doesn't receive any content updates in the coming months, then it will be a disappointing end to an otherwise interesting game that will fall into obscurity. tldr: Music and gameplay are great, however runs will lack diversity quickly and the visuals need some polishing and changing. The game is worth buying and checking out if you think this type game is up your alley, but in it's current state, don't be expecting a game that will keep you coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: You'll fight the learning curve more than the game for the first few attempts, but keep at it.  There's a pretty fun game in there once everything clicks into place.  If you love shooters and rhythm games it's a no brainer.  If ever there's custom soundtrack support it'll be even better.That said, a couple of critiques: - Items could use some balancing. I've completed the game each time I've found the Dragon Heart shield, for instance, because the later levels sling so many attacks at you once that, even if you're moderately good at dodging attacks, the regeneration feels expected.  At the same time, being even "moderately good" at dodging attacks will make that item's regen enough for you to rarely ever need to seek healing.  Nothing else in the game makes your mistakes so readily forgiven.  There are even multiple other shields I enjoy using (Battle Lion for instance), but if I find THAT one, that's it, no other shield for the rest of the run, it's that good. - Can we please get a colorblind mode, or the option for highlighting of enemies/shrines/pickups, or something. I appreciate the aesthetics but the game can be hard to look at sometimes, and dropping the saturation any amount doesn't feel like it helps because the contrast between anything on the screen remains as much of an issue.  A game with as much action as this really needs those enemies and attacks to POP in your vision, and sometimes they just don't. - Nitpick: Why do keys still spawn when you have the Skeleton Key, and guns still spawn when you're playing as Njord?Still love it, and still will probably keep coming back to it for quite some time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve never played any similar games, it can be a little daunting at first and it might feel like the game is not responding to your inputs, but once you get used to performing actions in rhythm with the music it becomes satisfying. The devs really nailed the main gameplay loop. There is no story in this game and it plays more like an arcade game, so it’s easy to pickup and replay. There are not many levels in total, but the randomization aspect makes it so you never play the same layouts.Unfortunately you have only one life per run and if you die you have to restart from the first level. You’ll restart a lot at first, but don’t let that discourage you, after some time you’ll get good enough to complete all levels with the easier characters. You can unlock new characters and their abilities with each completion. All the characters are unique and there’s a character for nearly all player types ranging from beginners to pros.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid 87/100The art style is brilliant and unique, gun play is also brilliant and unique and this offers a very fair chunk of content for its price. If you think you'll enjoy this game and its on sale you have no reason to not pick it up. Even if it means you dont eat for a day.Once you get over the learning curve of staying in rythm and being consistent this game becomes very satisfying and enjoyable. If you're having trouble sticking to the beat try putting the strict-ness scale on 'loose' until you pick up the vibe. In fact this game is so damn addicting I am typing this review to the beat of the soundtrack. Leaving the only real negative elements left to the strict randomness of this rougelike. Some events such as floor modifier are just too impactful for there not to be a way to at least toggle off certain ones (screw you shopless). Because they straight up ruin the flow of the game, preventing you from progressing as intended. Same can be applied to boss modifiers, there not too bad by themselves but are the reason behind a ruined run when they combine together, often seen in the harder difficulties.Feedback for the devs: Keep up the support, And it would be great to see more valks, zones, bosses, foes, weapons and armour. Potentially even a custom valk where you select the attributes, for those who make them game harder, maybe a better multiplier and a lower multiplier for those with decked out valks. Or mods for custom armour, weapons, rooms, bosses or foes.Time trials for specific dungeons, maybe a daily/weekly dungeon where you can compete with others to achieve the fastest time.I think multiplayer might even have some potential as well, maybe a horde based game style in a room with periodic boos fights and the occasional break where you have some time to gather your bearings and some equipment, spells, etc before the next wave. IF this were to be introduced some customisation would be really neat: select the starting gun, select an array of modifiers for the area and/or bosses, an option for shared or split funds, modify the coin drop rate, what shops appear, time of breaks and obviously difficulty (obviously a solo mode as well).I'm aware the chances of this being implemented are extremely low, and some would argue that this wouldn't capitalise on the gimmick of shooting to the rythm. But that gimmick is incorporated so well that its much closer to feeling natural rather than forced.Regardless of what happens, this game is a solid pick up- especially on sale, its an absolute steal. Great work devs, I'm looking forward to seeing the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: BPM is an amazing game. Starting off, a rhythm shooter game is a great idea, and it's a very, very small genre of games, and this one is definitely the best. The music itself, being rock, just really works with the game, and it develops as a run goes on. It gets heavier and harder sounding as the floors progress, which is a really nice touch. It's unique style also really helps add to the overall atmosphere and enjoyment of the game. It's also a simple game, in appearance and storyI only have one small issue:You can't map the controls of a controller, and the presets just felt backwards to me. I really don't recommend using a controller unless you really want to. Otherwise, 9/10. Aside from some other small personal issues, it's just a seriously fun, incredibly unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 20 minutes are difficult because the game lacks any kind of tutorial. Luckily, there's only a few things you need to understand to get started. It's amazing.The color scheme makes some things difficult to see, but I think that's part of the game - you have to look closely to find all the hidden secrets. Movement is fast and snappy and there's a lot of different enemies, semi-bosses and bosses. Weapons and upgrades for them are available. Absolutely no micro transactions and a playthrough takes roughly 45 minutes to an hour. While the soundtrack is great, it does get a bit repetetive after a few hours. There's one song for each level and I'd love it if the songs were also randomized, just like the amazing level generation (each level is unique). I'm having a ton of fun and I'd recommend this to everyone who enjoys shooters and music.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this with "you're probably going to love this game or hate it".   If you're like me you heard "oooh, rhythm-based FPS!  Roguelike elements!" and thought "I must have this!".  Read on, and if any of my complaints sound like the kind of thing that'd grind your gears, move along.  If not, maybe you'll like it.  Because, don't get me wrong, I really want to like this game.First of all, I had to play with my graphics vsync and other settings to get the audio to be enough in sync with the action timer such that I could actually play.  It burned a solid 20 minutes of messing around--FYI, if it helps, I had to do true fullscreen and an FPS lock that was something my monitor supported with Gsync, and then never alt-tab out.  YMMV.  I cannot use the visual indicators in a rhythm game, just the way I perceive things, so the audio sync MUST be perfect for me to enjoy it.  Plausibly adding a delay calibration like Rock Band etc. have is a good idea here.Also, the game lets you customize the cues around the crosshair, but only in a really weird linear way, where if you want to turn off the beat cues you must ALSO turn off the dodge cues.  This is obviously user-hostile.The game is honestly ugly as hell.   There's a minimalist aesthetic and limited palette, and then there's jsut muddy and yucky.  100% of visual information is conveyed by "ugly yellow-red bloom".Gun ranges feel absurdly short.Suffers from the all-too-common roguelike mistake of "I'm not going to give you the slightest bit of context for anything" because "the fun is the discovery"--that might be so for some people, but I just get cranky when I have to go to a wiki to look up the difference between "a shrine that takes 1-5 coins to give you a reward" and "a magical slot machine that may or may not reward you every time, but accepts some number of coins before jamming up".  Compare to something like Risk of Rain 2 where you know how much a shrine will cost, if it's a gamble, etc, up front just by pointing at it.Similarly, Draugr (the first boss) has an attack with vague glowy bits in half the room that sometimes I can dodge out of, sometimes I can walk out of, and sometimes it insta-kills me, and I just don't like the game enough to spend another several deaths figuring it out.I want to like the soundtrack.   But it's not varied enough if you've played through the first level and gotten stomped by Draugr 15 times and it's the same damn riff.Pros:- Soundtrack is okay for the first few minutes before it gets irritatingly repetitive.- Huginn as a dancing fatass cardinal is cute I guessCons:- It's ugly as ♥♥♥♥ - red muddy pseudo-monochrome feels like playing inside the brake light of a 76 Ford Pinto.- Pistol, at least, has an absurdly short range so if you like shooting things farther than 10 feet away you won't like the shooter aspectsWild card:- This game strikes me as the kind of thing one either loves or hates.  I cannot imagine anyone having a "meh" reaction to this game

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most satisfying games I have played in my life. I say that without any regret.In short terms, BPM: Bullets Per Minute is a short (but HEAVILY replayable) game with no dialogue, with a simple premise told only visually - You are a Valkyrie on a journey to Helheim. Your enemy is the fearsome dragon, Nidhogg. Almost every action is done to the rhythm of the amazing soundtrack in this place - from firing bullets, dashing, jumping, to reloading. And yes, non-magazine weapons must be reloaded cartridge by cartridge, but that's a good thing since that also contributes to your beat streak!The gameplay is much like a mix between Crypt of the Necrodancer and DOOM: Eternal, but it's mostly like DOOM: Eternal.- Everything in the game is beautifully modeled around the rhythm, from the first level's solo synchronizing with the mag size of your starting pistol, to the satisfying slap/click in every gun noise, to even your footstep noises and boss attacks.- Heavy inspiration from QUAKE movement torque, and DOOM2016/Eternal gunplay. Bunnyhop forever!- A hard, but easily learned difficulty.- You can feel yourself being absorbed into the music, and you get lost in it while playing perfectly. It's indescribable!- All boss attacks feel very fair.- There are no 'item rarities', you can get infinite ammo as your first item. Every weapon works, too. All that matters is how you use what you're given. You'll need to play well no matter what seemingly overpowered thing you have. This is a roguelike where the items don't 'make you.'- There are a LOT more weapons in this game than you'd expect. I like the Revolver, but all of them are good!- You can't lose your Streak when out of combat, so test weapons all you want.- You can stop and continue runs whenever you want.- The devs left the Saturation at maximum for some reason, leaving the game 'deep fried' in appearance and very hard to look at. Please don't let this turn you off from the game!  I use 65% for all levels.- The mixing for the first level's song is very bad, similar to most of the songs remixed in DOOM Eternal without Mick's permission, if you remember that. It does grow on you though! It just lacks in bass and is mostly riffing on a guitar. The other levels sound much better.- The ammo counter is too far away from the crosshair even at max UI scale. This means that instead of counting bullets visually, you're going to have to listen for the clicking sound which plays on your last two bullets. Since clip size can change, relying on the sound becomes much more viable later on.-Svartalfheim II and Helheim I can be laggy sometimes, but you might have a different experience.All in all, really loved this game, and I feel like I'm gonna play it a lot. Please give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from an avid rhythm game player, I feel this game does the "rhythm" part of rhythm games than standard ones do. In standard ones, it's more about remembering how many and which buttons to push at a certain time. But this game, if you're staring at the crosshair trying to click on beat, you'll be dead because there's so much going on. You actually have to remember the rhythm and play to it. And Im not saying that standard rhythm games are bad or anything; it's just at higher levels it becomes less about playing to the rhythm and remembering what to do. And I'm honestly ok with that. This game perfectly mixes together two genres of games that wouldn't seem like they'd go together.Another thing is I love shooters, and the guns in this game feel super satisfying to use. I read a review that talked about how "unsatisfying" they are but this game is upgrade reliant (like every other roguelike/lite out there).If you dont get at least 1 damage up by the time you make it past Asgard you won't have much luck getting to it. I haven't made it to higher levels yet, so I don't have much to comment in that regard (yet), but the game seems very promising.

_childDocuments_.review: tkae doom, binding of isaac, and crypt of the necrodancer, and you got this game.a rythm shooter dungeon crawler.it's amazing. it's addicting. i bought it and played it until my arm got numb, then kept playing regardless.why? let me explain:imagine yourself on your way home from work, with headphones on, listening to your favourite heavy metal album. you're a bit tired, dozing off, and just daydreaming to the music, imagining how you are slaying countless enemies to the rythm of the music.this is exactly that, but for real!you move to the heavy metal beats, the awesome soundtrack, laying waste to thousands of enemies, while dodging bullets and enemy attacks, and sometimes you get lucky and pick up an extremely overpowered item combo.but this game is super hard! it takes a bit of practice and experimentation to get the controls right, but once the muscle memory is there, you'll be shooting to the beat in no time! _childDocuments_.review: I read some people criticize the game on the assets used and the level design but that's not the pull of this game. First, if you close the game in chapter 2 for example, you can reset your progress in the chapter, health and loot and restart the chapter if you like. The rooms and enemies stay the same. Second, you can copy and store your save game files on desktop or something for easy access when you get to a new chapter, so that you can retry from that same chapter when you die. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but very shallow.  The developers clearly saw Tomb of the NecroDancer, Binding of Isaac, and DOOM and said "what if we combined all three of them?"  With that in mind, I've got some suggestions for updates to this game, or for the developers to use in a sequel.  There's clearly a lot of potential here, it's just not fully realized.  I'm very hopeful that the developers are able to make updates to the game or a sequel that's able to fully realize their ambitions.  Rooms are very samey because other than very specific tile sets, every room spawns with one special interaction: angel altar, devil altar, stat altar, chests, or sword (as far as I recall).  To add variety, make stat shrines cost 2 instead of 1, and reduce their chance to spawn.  Add a sword chest, where you have a 2/3 chance to get stabbed instead of getting the chest, but once you're stabbed both trapped chests open.  Make the tribute altar have a 33% chance to remove a stat instead of granting one, effectively making each stat point cost 3 coins instead of 1.  The game desperately needs equipment tiers.  Loki's Gauntlet grants +1 to each stat as a wrist-slot item.  Midgard Bracelet grants +1 to each stat, +25 to maximum HP, and +1 permanently to every stat for each level completed, also as a wrist-slot item.  Battle Lion Shield is broken and not fun to play with.  It makes it so that you can fire every gun twice as fast, and the downside is that you also can regenerate your abilities twice as fast. Sorry, did I say downside?  I meant upside.  The real downside of the item is the carpal tunnel that you'll get when you play with it.  Instead of doubling your attack rate, introduce triplets so that there's a tradeoff of skill and power.  I'd also recommend adding a second fire speed upgrade, probably in the wrist slot (secondary ability would be prrecision, not ability CDR).  If you've got both, introduce quintuplets and slow the game speed to 50% or so during combat.  The combination of items would present an interesting difference from the normal gameplay.  Muninn's Armory would benefit from stricter tiering.  30 coin buys (the same price as a prestige) should be guaranteed to be better than 5 coin buys, and this would also open up the possibility to adjust some of the damage numbers on weapons in the shop.  It'd also benefit the shop to have a chance at each tier; for example tier 1 weapons could have a 70% chance to spawn on each pedestal, tier 2 weapons a 20% chance, and tier 3 weapons a 5% chance.  For Huginn's shop. bring max health up to 10 coins to buy, reduce armor cost to 3 coins, key to 2 coins, and adjust the equipment cost by tier.  Tier 1 equips could be 5 coins, tier 2 8 coins, and tier 3 14 coins, for instance.  The clip-up upgrade has a different value depending on the weapon.  Perhaps adjust it so that it grants an additional +1 max ammo per 5 base rounds that the weapon carries?Stat upgrades aren't remotely balanced.  Damage up is the clear outlier, and should be adjusted down by a lot, maybe by 40%.  Precision is very hard to notice, perhaps a more noticeable visual cue on critical hits?  Healing abilities are much too strong.  Odin's Blessing, Elli's Touch, Steal Life, and Circlet of the Serpentine all make the game trivial, while Svalinn and Dragon's Skin both negate several mechanics.  It would be sensible to make the shields at least tier 2, with the rest at tier 3.  Weapons are confusing for early players.  Putting very short descriptions or even just names for each weapon would help a ton in knowing whether they're worth trying out.  Finally, a couple item suggestions.  A T2+ wrist slot that causes enemies to drop rapidly decaying chunks of healing meat when hit.  Possible name "Cannibal's Claws", but doesn't quite fit the theming.  T1+ Shield slot item called "Charge Shot" that requires 3 correct beats to fire a shot, with the charged shot dealing 5x damage.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I continue with this review I need to clarify that it comes with only 4 hours of gameplay, during which I only managed to get halfway. As per usual, here's my list of pros and cons:First of all let me say that I HAD A BLAST. The game was real fun for the first few hours and I will definitively continue playing it in the upcoming days to at least unlock the new characters and defeat hard mode. However I can see how neophytes of the genre might only get frustrated over this and decide to drop it early. The lack of tutorial would discourage most newcomers and even on easy the game destroys you fairly quick: this is NORMAL in any roguelike however. Roguelikes always take some time to get used to for most casual gamers and it usually takes me a fair amount of hours to finish at least one routing in any roguelike really, and in this case you also have the rhythm factor to keep track of that complicates things a fair bit. If you buy this game and you believe it's too hard, I beg of you to just be patient: you will see you will get better and better the more you play, it's just natural.I cannot really defend this game on any of the other cons I listed however: the biggest problem are certainly the over saturated colours, which I understand are a part of the style of the game itself and I can deal with them, however there's plenty of people out there who simply can't look at this kind of colours for too long. It would be nice to have something more toned down. Soundtrack is very good, but also quite limited and gets old really fast. I would like to clarify that so far I unlocked only the first two characters, so I might be jumping the gun on the lack of differences, but I would generally expect characters to be vastly different between each other, which is not the case at this point.I realize that I mostly listed cons and that overall my review may not sound the one of a happy customer, but I genuinely had a lot of fun and most likely will continue to have fun: I seriously hope that the game will sell good enough for developers to continue adding more and more, even with DLCs if needed.So if you are asking me if I recommend this game the answer is totally YES, you can get quite a few hours of entertainment for a very fair price (especially now that it's on sale): the only situation in which I do not recommend it, is in case you have sight issues or suffer from chronic migraines like me, as you will most likely have difficulties playing this game for long.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but beyond a cool soundtrack and core concept it's lacking anything special that would make it soar to the heights of Asgard, instead just making most of the experience a tedious slog through Helheim. The rewards are sparse, and the run to run loop lacks too little variation to keep you playing in hopes that a new run will be any more interesting than the last. I want a challenge, but I seem to be in the minority when it comes to thinking the game is a bit too punishing, especially in the mid to late game. A run with the best combination of equipment, weapon, and special attacks can be cut short by stepping into a room with enemies sitting immediately by the door. Hordes of hit scanning/projectile based monsters in a small arena can end you quickly when the margin of error is already slim because the damage you receive is immense and you have only a small amount of hit points. Chances to heal are few and far between, especially with the armoured character. Challenges or gambles reward little but frustration. Sacrificing a quarter of your precious health to a sword of Damocles for a few coins or potentially half your health through a chest door for a +1 to your ammo or some trivial stat boost makes you not want to bother. There's a lot of 'something' here, I think I'll just have to come back and see if that's turned into anything worthwhile at a later date.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while having a very cool concept and great execution, suffers very much from poor enemy design. There are many enemies in this game, which can be encountered early game, which are very large bullet sponges unless you happen to find a better gun before encountering them. There are also Boss Modifiers, which, while most of them are great and well implemented, depending on the boss and the modifier it gets, can be an immediate run ender. One of these being "Clone". More than one boss, if cloned, and you don't have a gun that can do a lot of damage in a short amount of time, will create situations that you cannot avoid taking damage from, very quickly and repetitively.  Overall, I enjoy the game and it's concept, however, due to the steep learning curve and the enemy flaws, I cannot enjoy this game for long periods of time like I would with other shooters.TL;DR: I hate cloned enemies and unavoidable attacks. _childDocuments_.review: - Shoot, reload, jump, dash n dance on the beat!- There are hidden secrets in some rooms, often up high which you only can reach with skill jumps.- Interesting movement: o Jumping off stairs uphill lets you jump higher o Jumping off stairs downhill lets you jump farther o Jumping height and length is dependant on your movement speed o You movement speed depends on different things. Basically you have a speed counter which can go from 0 up to 9 by spending coins on upgrades, if you find them, for each run. The weight of your gun influences your speed/jump height/length, but there is more to it. You can increase your current speed by bunny hopping and a smooth direction change à la Quake. With these tricks going fast and continuous you are able to reach optional secret heights unreachable from a standing position, which adds just the right amount of skill to spice it up.- High difficulty. Even easy is hard. But then again 'Hard' isn't much harder than 'Easy'. But both are definitely hard.- Different characters with different abilities and starting items can be unlocked to keep it fresh.- bosses don't require much rhythm. If you found the right items you can even kill them before any rhythm part is needed. On a regular run there is only a couple of timed dodges or jumps needed for the whole boss fight. Also those timed dodges/jumps are only once in about four 4/4 (four quarter) times. I would find it better if bosses would require much more rhythm to make it less like a usual FPS boss fight. E.g. make them invulnerable unless you do the rhythm part correct to open their guard up. And I would appreciate more rhythm combos like dodge right/jump/dodge left/shoot in rapid succesion and different combos randomized.- Sometimes enemies clip through walls and can't be hit, so you can't finish the room. The doors won't open, because that requires all enemies to be beaten, so you can not continue the level. In this case you have to quit to main menu and restart the chapter.- item descriptions are a bit vague. Most often you have to try it to understand what they do.- You can't drop an item once picked up. There is an item which enables you to shoot two projectiles with one shot. This doubles the damage, but halves the shots fired before you have to reload by inputting the gun's reload combo sequence. Now if my current weapon is already strong enough for most enemies, I prefer more shots instead of double damage. The first armour item I picked up was double shot and since it was the first one I had no other item hovering over the chest to change it back to. There should be an option to drop an item in case you don't want it.- You cannot unequip items. In some situations this would be good.- There is a character who cannot pick up certain items, but these items still spawn for him in randomized content chests for which you have to spend coins to open. So you invest into your run but are sometimes given nothing.This game is for tough FPS players who like a challenge and like some spice in their usual rogue-like FPS soup.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "meh" recommendation button, because it's what I'd give BPM Squared. It's not bad enough to say I wanna give it a bona fide thumbs-down, but it's behind most games that get my unreserved thumbs-up.BBP:PMM was my first experience of games that are technically rhythm games but don't involve much in the way of the arrows or other big body movement to the beat (I don't count Crypt of the Necrodancer, as that is literally played principally with the four cardinal directions, after all). Whether or not it was "the" first, it definitely took some liberties in cramming a metronome (and metal) into a roguelike, only some of which worked out well in the end.For starters, roguelikes, rhythmic or otherwise, are as a genre prone to rollercoaster-grade difficulty curves, based upon the procedural generation of each run. Bullets Per Bullets Minute Per: Minute suffers from this more than even most roguelikes I've played: get low-grade items generated, or not enough coins, and prepare yourself for a short and sad run that only Hobbes could be proud of. Alternatively, get unusually lucky, and cruise through the game largely unimpeded, splattering mythological creatures on the pasted-texture walls right and left, all the while unsure of how you've gotten so far so quickly. What was that level just now? Were you supposed to learn something? Oh well, best make hay while the sun shines!Bippem to the second power also has its characteristic sort of washed-out graphical "aesthetic," which is certainly a bold design choice, but frankly, I hate it. In a game about precision dodging (and even more precision aiming, depending on your weapon), being able to clearly read what enemies are doing and distinguish them from the background is key, so this strange and arbitrary infusion of grainy murk adds needless difficulty without any feeling of payoff (who feels rewarded for successfully squinting?). Certain random level modifiers make it even worse (I'm looking at you, "retro"). I would've been alright with the washout being one such modifier, such that it could only be that  something else, and even then only rarely, but having it as the continual baseline and then subjecting it to worse is just not fun.And while roguelikes are frequently skinny on the storyline (unless they're Hades or Children of Morta, apparently), B2P2M2 has, quite literally, none at all. Why are the Valkyries going on a metal rampage through the realms of Norse mythology? Beats me. I guess the end boss  is a big problem for somebody. Too bad he keeps coming back to life every run. I ultimately have zero investment in which Valkyrie I play, as they say nothing and have no introduction; each simply presents a different set of starting advantages and constraints, a la Binding of Isaac but with no particular flavor (or at least, none which I could tease out; perhaps if I'd read more of the Heroic Eddas I might have a different opinion of them). What's more, with how often you die, you will be hearing the first level theme , and it gets old quite quickly (my stream audience was complaining rather vociferously about this one). I usually turn the music off on roguelikes after a number of runs, due to this very kind of effect, but that is quite literally imprudent (if even possible in a game where  While there is apparently now a custom music mode, which I haven't tried, I wouldn't be able to get much use out of it, streaming as I do, due to copyright issues--unless I wanted to go to the trouble of porting generic, license-free music into the game, I guess. Ultimately, BPM: Bowels Pretty Moving was cast into the spotlight more for being new and different than for being pretty good... or even just being pretty. It's not utterly terrible--there's still plenty to learn and engage and feel dimly accomplished for figuring out--but if you hardly ever get to try out neat combinations if they're not the ones which magically give you a Get Out of Helheim Free card, any such sense tends to be fleeting at best. With the only form of cross-run upgrades being stocking up on banked coins and occasionally being able to afford upgrades to the (surprisingly delightful?) shops, along with unlocking the small number of Valkyries not initially available, you have even less reason to feel like you're getting anywhere with all those deaths.Good thing you're a Valkyrie, I guess. If you live in Valhalla, can you ever really stay dead?

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time. The game is challenging, there are random modifiers for runs (like slippery runs, anti-gravity runs, etc.), and the music is great. On top of that, there are unlockable characters who have very different play styles, upgradeable stores, secrets, and many different weapons to master (each with their own play style as well). I haven't tried the custom music option, but what an awesome update! It's currently $5, which is a borderline crime! This game is a must-play for anyone who likes rhythm games, FPS, or roguelikes (or roguelites idk). The developers took a chance with the art style and I love it, but for those who find the red coloring of the first area too much (or any other area), try turning down the saturation in the graphics settings. If I had a wishlist request for this game, it would be a mod or update that provided a more realistic lighting and color design. Regardless tho, a GOAT FPS roguelike!

_childDocuments_.review: BPM, at its core is a very fun, rhythm based fps; however, it has some glaring issues.I really enjoy cranking up music to the max and playing video games, and many times i find myself playing video games like they're a rhythm game, so I was really excited when I found out about BPM from a friend and bought it. However, after playing for a few hours I was pretty disappointed. While the gunplay being tied to the rhythm is fun, not much else in the game actually utilizes the rhythm mechanics, and I wish i had a little more agency. The game feels kind of unfinished, like the creators had this cool idea of like a rhythm game, a shooter and a dungeon crawler roguelike, and they put them together, but then they didn't really let the concepts work together well. The rooms before the final boss which don't have mini bosses are extremely tedious to clear. It feels like the smaller mobs are just thrown in as filler, and they don't really actually add anything as kiting them boils down to "run in circle, shoot them 1 by 1" which is completely different from the feel of the bosses and minibosses. The bosses and mini bosses actually somewhat utilize the rhythm mechanics of the game and really add skill and strategy. While it is a roguelike, and every run should vary based off of RNG, it's pretty rare that you come across a blacksmith with an weapon that's better than your starting gun. There are a few other things i could nitpick which are simple ui, perfomance, and QoL things, but i don't think they are a huge issue. That being said, I have enjoyed the time I've put into the game, and plan to sink some more time into it. I love the aesthetic and I enjoy the soundtrack (though I wish I could do some music of my choice). I don't recommend buying this game full price, but if its on sale for a good deal, not a bad pickup.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, fellow warriors, gather 'round as I recount the epic tale of "BPM: Bullets Per Minute," a game that thrusts you into the heart of a perilous dungeon, much like our own ancestors faced in their heroic quests.In this audacious blend of first-person shooter, rogue-lite, and rhythm game, you, brave adventurers, shall delve into the abyss with the valor of a Viking warrior preparing for glorious battle. The relentless beat of the game, like the pounding of war drums, guides your every step. It's a rhythmic symphony of chaos and strategy, akin to the tumultuous battles of yore.As you venture deeper into the labyrinthine dungeon, you face an unending tide of monstrous foes and cunning traps, reminiscent of the treacherous perils that await in the dark recesses of our Norse sagas. The rogue-lite elements ensure that no two excursions are alike, much like the ever-shifting challenges of our epic quests.Your arsenal, my fellow adventurers, is a testament to the diversity of our Viking armory. Guns, relics, and artifacts await discovery, each with its own rhythm and power. The strategic choice of equipment, much like selecting the right weapon for a dungeon delve, adds layers of depth to the gameplay.But what truly sets "BPM" apart is its fusion of music and combat. The soundtrack, like the ancient chants of our skalds, drives your actions with a relentless beat. It's a harmonious blend of rhythm and destruction, much like the battle cries of our forebears in the heat of combat.In conclusion, "BPM: Bullets Per Minute" is a symphony of violence and rhythm, a game that beckons you to embrace the spirit of a Viking adventurer. It's a glorious battle cry, a saga of courage and skill, and a reminder that in the heart of the dungeon, the rhythm of victory beats ever true. Valhalla awaits, my brave companions!

_childDocuments_.review: This feels very early access. The concept is good but the execution feels unfinished. Enemies don't lead shots or flank in any way, making it too easy to strafe in a single direction around the room (and try to peek shot through whatever cover is in it) and making any other strategy an instant death (changing strafing direction means you'll take a bullet you haven't seen).The music is okay but repetitive and will give you a headache before long. The bosses are the only interesting enemies (compared to spiders, worms, and flies...) and the satisfying end sequence, where each of your shot plays a note, feels like it should have been the whole game.I hope the game is developed further past this stage, or that it inspires further attempts at this concept. Pick up this game on sale if you are curious, the current price point just feels inadequate.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot, and I do recommend it. However, it's a little saddening to talk about this game at length because I know that my favorite game of all time is somewhere buried within BPM, but what's actually here is just an ok experience. The game occasionally feels completely incredible, with the music and gameplay and having-just-learned-a-gun's-bar-defying-shot-pattern all coming together, but it's weighed down by most of the rest of what's going on.I'm a lot more of a rhythm game guy than a shooter guy, so I'm coming from the opposite angle as I imagine most people are, but for either camp there seems to be a decently sized initial wall to get over to really get into the game. After that, though, it gets a lot more enjoyable.I think roguelikes are generally overdone, and if you're going to be one you ought to bring something new to the table. BPM does nort As far as greater dungeon organization, this game doesn't really do anything a BoI player doesn't already understand. It adds some things, like shrines to improve base stats (that are miserable to find), and adds limited slots for weapons/items, but there's a shop and item room on every floor (the latter requiring a key), a square grid of independent rooms that drop items on completion, key beggars, etc. (Room rewards are actually based on how well you performed in a room [i.e. not breaking the beat or getting hit]. This is cool but not very well telegraphed to the player.)The item system is theoretically interesting but pretty underwhelming overall. You have four slots for items, head/sheild/arm/boots, and each item can only exist in one of these slots. Many items are not terribly interesting (speed up, damage up, etc.), and they're not balanced at all. It makes total sense for a roguelike to have unbalanced items, but how well a run is going depends near-entirely on getting some of the literal or effective damage doubler items. I've have runs where I 4-shot the final boss, and runs where the fight just drags on. There are occasional interesting trade-offs to make but non-specific item descriptions make the decision more of a guess or whim than an actual thought-out choice. (There's also abilities that I literally forgot about until right now because they're hardly ever given the chance to be interesting.)The guns are cool but having to save up for an armory to maybe buy a better one is really not terribly fun. I feel this is another issue with the roguelike system, learning new guns' shot and reload patterns is one of the game's strong points, but you start new runs with the same weapons every time, and once you find a decent gun there's not a ton of incentive to change it.One thing I'd like to mention because it either isn't brought up in game or I just missed it, is that there's a lot of attacks that seem completely unfair until you realize that they're telegraphed on the beat indicator in the middle of the screen. I found myself tuning the GUI out completely because you don't really ever use it, except for for one specific enemy and parts of some boss fights, so I had to relearn to pay attention to it whenever there might be a led projectile or wall of damage incoming.There's also just some final polish missing in a lot of places. Hit-register on shield enemies is funny with some weapons. Items aren't always well explained, so it's definitely a tab-to-wiki-to-figure-out-what-this-thing-even-does type game at times, and sometimes it doesn't seem like the wiki even knows either.Art style is contentious. I like it overall, but there are definitely times where incoming projectiles are impossible to make out from windows or other enemies or your own projectiles. Shrines are essential, appear nearly every room, and are really annoying to find because everything is the same color and brightness.Progression is really weird, it mostly happens to line up so that you'll have unlocked most of the game once you've gotten a hang of the mechanics, but I've beaten the game on hard with most characters and I still don't have all of the armory or the bank unlocked, and either way it feels pretty cheap to only sell you a couple items a floor at the beginning and make you unlock a shop that actually sells a reasonable amount of items over time.This review ended up being more negative than I meant it it, I promise there's a incredible core gameplay loop in there, it's just dragging a ton of small issues behind it. I probably have more thoughts--this review is already much longer than I intended because I kept thinking of new things to say--but it boils down to what could be an incredible game just ending up as a fine game. I paid full price and it was definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: AGHHHHH, YES!!!  The soundtrack in general is as good as the trailer track, all of the action and a lot of subtle bits (footsteps, heartbeat, boss laughs, ..., but not item pickup sounds) are as satisfyingly rhythmic as the trailer action teases, the movement is surprisingly great (other than the jump-to-apex time not being exactly a beat long), the overall tone is great, ...  My face hurts from the smiling!Update:  My only real beef with it longer-term is that it's a roguelike/-lite/etc, which I was aware of going in, but *man* it'd be nice to have some options so I could just enjoy the game's seriously thoughtfully implemented beat-oriented mechanics without needing to rely on the item lottery and/or being amazing at boss fights.  Welp, at least I can still thoroughly enjoy the early stages and listen to the soundtrack on its own.  Genre resented but purchase not regretted.Update update:  I still give the whole item lottery + permadeath thing the hairy eyeball, but MAN.  When you win the lottery and have played the bosses enough to not die to them immediately, it is properly NICE again!  Stat upgrades are usually pretty generous throughout a given run, but being graced with the health steal ability at an early stage made my first victorious run (after 6 hours of play) possible and thoroughly enjoyable.  I love this game again.  Its dedication to the beat is like nothing else I've played in FPSes (except arguably Pistol Whip), and finally not dying was the proper homemade icing on that cake.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that this game is one of the funnest single player shooters I've played in a long damn time. - The rhythm aspect is great. It's challenging and makes you feel like a badass when you get it right.- The weaponry is fun. Each gun handles smoothly and differently.- The enemies are challenging. Each enemy presents a different threat, and that's neat.- The economy in the game is well made. I get excited any time I find a shop room, and that's exactly how it should feel in a game like this.- The music is SO good!- The easy difficulty feels almost no different from hard. I spent the first 2-3 hours of playing the game getting a little frustrated and feeling like there should have been a tutorial. Talked a friend into getting this game, and they refunded it because they got too frustrated with the learning curve. A game should be challenging, but it shouldn't be frustratingly hard for new players on the easiest difficulty.- As mentioned in the point above, the game should have a tutorial.- The weapons and armor could use some balancing. There are certain gear and weapon combinations you can get that make even the final boss stupidly easy. Land yourself with a minigun, infinite ammo, and lifesteal, and suddenly the game goes from very challenging to just clicking, holding, and aiming wildly. The rhythm aspect and the challenge can be completely lost with certain combos.- Item descriptions are vague in some cases. This may be intentional, but I don't really like when a game doesn't make it clear what items will do for me. This isn't the right genre to build mystery into your items. That just leaves your players having to google what items do what.- The final boss is simply not challenging. I've actually never died on the final boss, and I've cleared the game 4 times, now. In fact, I find myself most commonly dying on the first floor, regardless of what difficulty I choose. Once you manage to beat the first 2-3 floors and get a good roll going, the rest of the game is suddenly not as challenging because your weaponry and gear make you a bit too powerful. This could be balanced out through buffing later enemies or nerfing some items, and that would make this a 10/10 game.- Some of the character choices are considerably too weak, and others are very strong. Not sure if this was intentional to add variable challenges, but it feels a little wonky to me.- This game is fun as hell, but it needs some balancing to polish it into a 10/10- Please buff some later enemies- Please nerf some of the gear- Please add a tutorial- Please add the option to sub in your own music of the same tempo instead of the in-game music. The music in this game is amazing, but you can only listen to it so many times before it gets old.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to love about the game. It makes wonderful use of some of the abandoned Paragon assets.The soundtrack is actually lovely and fits the mood of the game precisely. The gunplay is some of the best I've ever encountered in an FPS, entirely by virtue of the mechanics of the game.That said, the combination of Rhythm and Shooter isn't fully realized here. You are rhythm locked for dodges, attacking, and reloading, while enemies (except bosses) do not seem to have that same limitation. It's often hard to 'find the rhythm' within a levelWhile I love the music there are moments where I wish more effort was spent on polishing the tracks to fit the expectations of the game itself. I do wish there was more variety in how the characters feel, and that their abilities were not locked behind playthroughs. _childDocuments_.review: A literal take on the 'ballad' of combat found in arena shooters and a brilliant premise that's been hidden in plain sight. The clicks and snaps of gunplay have always had a figurative rhythm to them and trailers that set weaponry to music have always caught my  ears. That said, the premise is about the only thing unique that BPM has to offer and, even then, its execution is distressing.Learning to play a ‘rhythm shooter’ is like trying to ride a bicycle backward. In BPM, a genre about patience and consistency while overseeing a set of static inputs fails to harmonize with the spontaneous decision-making and overstimulation of fast-paced gunplay. Timing is essential to flow in either case, but layering the two introduces a conflict of interest between reaction time and acting on someone else’s time. Even if forging the new habits required for BPM was simple, the game is still less than the sum of its parts. As a shooter, it’s awfully shallow and derivative. For a rhythm game, the animation often lacked impact and anticipation. The music is a highlight but is unavoidably repetitive due to its role as the metronome. It’s no help that the roguelike elements are bog-standard and share their own set of inadequacies. As an aside, It would be interesting to see how inverting the game's restriction from working  on the beat to  on the beat would change gameplay. For instance, performing actions on time could provide an essential buff to damage/I-frames/reloads. The player would grow into the tempo through incentivizing correct timing instead of demanding it. The end result would look the same. For that matter, what if a game let the player consciously compose their own ‘shotgun serenades’ as a motive for intrinsic arsenal experimentation? Digressing, red-light green-light doesn't easily suit a playstyle where unimpeded movement and split-second improvisation are the main course.Speaking of red-lights, the game's all-consuming shader is plain ugly. Red-on-orange is even less readable than the gameboy's shades of green. It’s like ten-year-old me considering that windows movie maker videos look more stylish with maximum contrast and sharpness. In terms of marketing, using the yawning valkyrie as a mascot for the steam store/nauseating menu screen if off-putting. The uncanniness of that offended grimace keeps burning into me, as if I spilled her Starbucks or something.The painful deconstructing of welded-in shooter habits while being given little opportunity to appreciate anything the game had to offer made for a generally unpleasant few hours. That said, there's certainly a market for BPM. The elevator pitch clearly got me. Those with the dedicated masochism to rip through the roughest games from BPM’s source genres may find the scrambling of their circuits delightfully exasperating. Chances are that you'll end up with another incompleted 'roguelike but with x' in your steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the foundation for this game could not be more solid, more fun, more addicting as a rogue like. It's fast paced, the music is awesome, and the Shooter + FPS mash works AMAZINGLY well, to the point that I'm surprised it has never really been done before. I'd go so far as to say the gameplay itself is funner, at least for me, than even Crypt of the Necrodancer. However strong a skeleton is though, a bare bones game is bare bones.I'd say it's definitely a great attempt, a good job, a well done game that you can get hours of playtime out of SIMPLY because of the gameplay itself. But after that... ehh? Let's take a look at Hades for instance, a Rogue-Like with Mythos Flavor, just like this one (Though this is norse). There is no flavor. There is no plot. There is no story. I don't feel like I'm fighting norse monsters; there's no dwarves, there's no giants, there's Nidhogg, but nothing else. The items are named, but there's no flavor text. There's NO text, NO story, NO background, JUST the bones. And there are cracks, even, with heavy reliance on luck and bullet sponge enemies, as you progress things might turn a bit sloggish or an absurd breeze.I really hope that from this game there's maybe, I dunno, story add-ons? DLC maybe? Preferably a free story update, which would probably get me to fall in love with this game as much as I did Hades.BPM does one thing, and it does it VERY well. But if you're looking for more than one thing, such as an engaging plot or a real good milking of the Norse mythos, you won't get it. If you're however looking for a no-nonsense heart pounding time waster, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, bad in executionThe core idea works great, FPS and rhytm game elements come together well. The rest is not so good.The visuals look very bad, they are oversaturated to the point of blurring into a mess and making telegraphed attacks very hard or impossible to see.Progress of any run is too dependent on RNG. In roguelikes some RNG is to be expected but in BPM your run will get decided almost solely on the loot you get. One run you will get a gamebreaking item combo in the first level taking all the fun out of finishing it and on the other you will get stomped by bad drops after another and have the run ended not by any mistake of your own but just bad luck. Not fun. I killed the end boss in 10 seconds on my second run, although on the easier of the two difficulty settings.Music is OK but very repetitive and will get boring after an hour or so. In a rhytm game and a game leaning much into replayability this is not acceptable.Artstyle is in conflict with itself. You play a norse mythological character of your choice, in locations that tie into norse mythology but you come up against scorpions and flies and have to swat them with a space-age shotgun that looks like it's straight out of doom? Confusing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite shooters of all time. It's a rhythm based shooter in which you're playing a first person shooter but you're dashing, shooting and reloading to the beat. There's a bit of strategy to it because you can't do two actions in the same beat so sometimes you're not shooting so you can focus on dodging. But let me boil down what makes this game so good.1. It's satisfying.The guns feel good to shoot. There's a nice clear sound to every gun shot and the reloads all sound great and it's further emphasized with how it blends to the music.. speaking of which.2. The music.The music is fantastic. I think some people in the forums want different music but I find myself able to listen and groove with the music in every playthrough. The Overdrive update added a new song and I hope that's added to the OST that I paid for.3. There's nothing like it. Yes its a roguelite. Yes its a first person shooter with a degree of nostalgia/retro to it but it's a niche that I keep seeming to keep coming back to.4. Every playthrough doesn't boil down to the same broken combination of weapons and items. Similarly there are some very fun combinations. I had a pistol shotgun and a bracelet that transformed all my bullets into explosives. So i was rocket jumping across maps and wiping bosses.So here are some cons.1. Roguelite quirksThere will be some runs with horrendous seeds and terrible rng. Idk if thats really a con since the game is  beatable without items or upgrades. Removes a lot of fun though.2. Balance. Certain combinations of items are a guaranteed full clear. Thats another quirk of procedurally generated and RNG items but you can game the system a bit to get an absolutely broken combination of weapon and perks. 3. Unfriendly introduction.What the hell does "mind flay" or "mark for death" mean? Often, items will only have a few words (or single line of text at best) to explain what an item does. The wiki is awful at explaining things. This also goes for weapons too. How do you know if a weapon is better than your current one? You'll often be looking up online for things that the game should have explained to you. 4. Nitpicks:Playing as a 0 hp character (odr and sanngrior) and still having health, armor and hp upgrades spawn could kill an early run because you can't use any of them. Also enemies should not spawn terribly close to you. This usually happens with the baby spiders who can often spawn right behind me next to the door. Though this only happens sometimes, it can be quite frustrating.Thats a lot of cons. And a lot of words for some guy whos only played this for about 20 hours. But think of it this way. This is a game where you can do an entire run in 30 minutes. I've beaten the game on hellish with Sanngrior and Odr (and lost a few years of lifespan because of it).  Please pick up the game and try it. If you hate it and saw this review. Comment and call me names. idk.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously underrated game, quickly became one of my all-time favorites. Imagine combining DOOM, Crypt of the Necrodancer, The Binding of Isaac, '80s hair metal, and it is all executed PERFECTLY. These known quantities combine into something truly unique, and once you have passed the admittedly steep learning curve, the game is extremely satisfying to play. The weapons are all very distinct from one another and so the player must master each one. This is also true to an extent with the roster of characters. You do have to devote quite a bit of time up front to begin internalizing the mechanics. Therefore, I think there will be likely be a significant number of people who will turn away frustrated. I imagine those who are musicians or proficient with other rhythm games will have a significantly easier time.My only complaint is that I wish there was more content, maybe branching paths and different endings a la Binding of Isaac, and this may materialize in time, as the devs have expressed interest in creating more content. But I highly recommend giving BPM: Bullets Per Minute a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: BPM is the kind of game that is great in theory but awkward in execution. There are moments when the combat and music gel and you get into a rhythm, but this is almost always followed by *something* that breaks the flow. On top of that, the visuals of the game while unique are very difficult to look at. Enemies blend together with the background and their own projectiles, making it difficult to actually even play. On top of that, the roguelike elements are barely present. All the items I picked up didn't seem to really change my runs, aside from the infinite ammo rocket launcher that basically *removed* half the point of the rhythm based gameplay.I wish I could recommend BPM. I really do. I've wanted a rhythm FPS ever since Crypt of the Necrodancer proved that rhythm games could be integrated into other genres. But BPM misses the mark both visually and gameplay-wise for me.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of both Doom and Rhythm Heaven, I have to say that this is the exact game I've always wanted.  The gameplay and music are both fantastic.  I love the fast based gameplay, and I love the feeling of slowly learning patterns and getting better at the game.  The oversaturated artstyle isn't my cup of tea, but thankfully it can be turned down in the options menu.  The only issue I have with the game is the map, there's no way (that I could find) to get a view of the full map.  Also, map symbols mark special rooms but nothing else.  In Binding of Isaac (for example) if you left a chest in a room, it would show up as a symbol on the map and if you opened the chest, then the symbol would disappear.  In BPM, on the other hand, locked chests only show up on the map if they are in a treasure room and don't if they show up in a different room, and opening the chest doesn't remove or change the symbol.  Basically, you can't tell from a glance how many locked chests remain, which makes it harder to decide on buying a key.One other minor issue that might get better once I play the game more, none of the weapons at the blacksmith have any sort of label or stats.  I can understand stats being hidden, due to this being a roguelike, but it's annoying because I have a hard time differentiating similar looking weapons.  Something simple, like giving every weapon a name, would both improve the gameplay and add an extra cool factor to each weapon.Other than those two QOL things, this game is INCREDIBLY fun!

The RNG either loves or hates you, no real in between, which leads to the game being way too easy, or very difficult because you didn't get anything good on the first level. I would've liked to see a bit more consistency and variation in the difficulty. However, this does not take away from the fun.Overall I recommend it if you have the money and want some time to burn. _childDocuments_.review: BPM: BULLETS PER MINUTE is what the gaming public never asked for, and never wanted.  At some point, someone got stupidly drunk and decided first person games like DooM just aren't cool.  Why not?  Because they aren't enough like Dance Dance Revolution.  They were wrong. First person shooters, when made properly with the right level of budget, quality, talent and effort applied to level design and storytelling, are the finest example that gaming can provide.  While the basic technical execution of BPM is acceptable, with 4K support, graphics tweaks and control customisation, poor decisions were made in terms of game concept.  The rhythm mechanic is, quite simply, an annoying distraction from an otherwise plausible concept for a game (because story driven FPS games have been done before, they are very successful when done right). The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content. So the result is an excellent premise for an FPS game with nice visuals and soundtrack, destroyed by poor design decisions.  Because FPS games don't need to be like Dance Dance Revolution or Guitar Hero, and because this game has no content, only soulless, repetitive algorithm "content", it's impossible to recommend. If you want a decent FPS game, try Halo: Infinite's campaign or DooM Eternal.  If you want to play Dance Dance Revolution, play Dance Dance Revolution.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, i really do. I tried every setting in the game, i tried following the cross hair rhythm, but i just dont think this game should have A. Varying rhythm that can change drastically and quickly mid song. B. Every single action be about rhythm, like dodging and reloading. C. Be a rhythm game with a rock soundtrack. I can follow beats fairly easily, but trying to juggle shooting, 2 step reloading, dodging projectiles and having to be within range, is a little much. Its a shame for me because i really like the effort and style of game here, the art style is awesome, the guns look and sound fantastic, and the music is top tier. I dont want to discredit the game for my own issues, but I would recommend people trying the game and figuring out if its right for them, this isnt just a roguelike afterall. For that reason, im going to recommend with a little *, theres nothing wrong with the game itself, but people should know its not just shooting to a rhythm for a damage buff, you literally cant shoot or dodge unless its on rhythm, so if you cant get that down to a T, you wont progress at all. I hope in a future game or sequel, they might try a different genre of music with easier to follow rhythm.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant example of how a strong, well tuned gameplay loop can carry an experience. Shoot shoot bang bang to the beat, and it never gets old. *The rouge-like elements are exactly what you've come to expect and keep each run fresh and different.*The different unlockable characters feel unique enough and working to unlock them is fun.*The various difficulties feel like they actually add challenge. Take note though, even this game's "easy" can be punishing if you're not prepared.*The art design and style are cool, but the super saturation may not be to everyone's liking. There's also a vague Norse mythology theme that adds a cool but admittedly shallow flavor to everything.*The music is AMAZING, but that should be a no-brainer. An experience like this would fall apart if the music weren't tuned to fit perfectly. Overall, it is exactly what it looks like: a cool, stylish rythm-shooter with a neat aesthetic and a 🔥FIRE🔥  soundtrack. The developer also just added a bunch of new stuff for free so it is well worth your money, sale or not. Get the soundtrack if you can afford it.And remember to Shoot Shoot Bang Bang to the beat

_childDocuments_.review: it takes a lot of Binding of Isaac and converts it perfectly into the FPS genre, which alone would be an amazing game already.But the heavy focus of music and playing to the rythm (in a vastly different approach than necrodancer) takes it to a  new level. At the start not being able to shoot when you want to, reloading for 8 seconds cause I couldn't hit the beat or getting hit by a projectile 5 times in a row since I didn't dodge on beat felt horrible. After playing a few games (and dying in my 3rd room) it becomes more and more satisfying once you start getting 10+ streaks and after playing for a few hours the beat is basically second nature and it just feels amazing shooting through hordes of enemies while listening to the dope soundtrack and adding your own gunshots, gun pumps, dashes and reloads to the music. Some actions are able to be on the off-beat (like pistol shots, or single cartridge reloads) while more grand actions (dashes, jumps, heavy weapon shots, abilities, magazine reloads) are only able to be on the full-beat.Because of that if you try to be efficient with your beats you will constantly change your button pattern making it never get boring.biggest downside is the quite limited variation of items and weapons. Although all the options currently available feel very unique with only a little to no overlap. it still hurts the game a lot since there are a few very broken combinations you can have and the low amount of stuff makes getting one not really unrealistic.You all might know some Isaac runs that are pretty much impossible to fail because you have full guppys or a full dmg brimstone+ludovico, which are maybe once in 500-1000 runs. Here similar OP levels are reached in I would say 10-20 runs.Its a fantastic game idea and what they have so far is a good foundation, it's tons of fun to learn, master and play with only missing more content. Which so far, is being delivered in a steady pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, great music, great everything! It is a rhythm game, which isn't bad at all; but the issue stems from a lack of options to adjust audio and video synchronization. In order to fire your weapon, you need to click the button with the rhythm of the song played in the current level, and if you miss the beat, your weapon would not fire. I seem to have an issue where either the video or the audio is out of sync with my inputs, and in order to fire, I would have to click earlier than the beat for it to register; and as stated earlier, there is no way to augment the timing window in any way. For the main appeal of the game to be rhythm based, it failed on that aspect- at least in my case- and the lack of options to fix that is upsetting. If something is added to fix this issue, i would immediately repurchase the game and change my review,  but the game is currently unplayable for me.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After beating the game the first time I've gotten better and better at beating the game.  I still really enjoy this game.  Once you kind of figure out the item progression it gets a lot easier.  This game is so damn good.Wow.  I finally beat the final boss in the game, after 107 failed runs on "easy".  This isn't a very easy game, at least for people like me with bad reflexes.  The music in this game is amazing, and I found it on Spotify and added it to my rock music playlist. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It is by far worth the price tag, maybe even a little more since they plan on continually updating the game. Odr is by far my favorite character even though he needs a little bit of balancing. This game just seems to absorb hours. There are a few flaws though:1. There are a small amount of characters (5)  and challenges (5 I think) compared to other rogue likes.2. With a lack of difficulties beyond hard, once you master the mechanics, the game becomes very easy. The only exception to this is Odr. Who dies in one hit, so you are never safe.3. There are a small amount of Items total in the game currently. I trust the developers though, and believe they will add more items, guns, characters, and challenges in time.4. THE MOUSE SENSE USES A SLIDER INSTEAD OF A DECIMAL SYSTEM! There is no way to go below .5 sensitivity which is like 1.4 source. The second lowest value is .6 so if you are worried about this game messing with your muscle memory, then BEWARE!Over all, this game is fantastic. The dev team has patched the game, and changed core aspects for the better. They really need to change the sense slider soon, but otherwise this game is definitely worth the money and the pros definitely out weigh the cons. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved Crypt of the Necrodancer for years, so this concept already had me sold. there's a little acclimation period at the beginning, but after you push through it becomes some of the most fun gameplay I've had in years. this game requires a fantastic mix of skill and luck, and it makes every playthrough cathartic and nail-biting. it feels awesome to get a build that feels just right. I really like how each playthrough builds onto the last in subtle ways. I may just be imagining it, but it feels like the game responds to your experience too. there's a big sense of risk and reward.this game does have a few bugs, though. the audio has this tendency to cut out altogether for seconds at a time and I tend to encounter crashes in the transitional period between maps (the game autosaves before this happens though, so it's not like I'm losing any progress). the visual style can also strain your eyes a bit - it's definitely unique in its own way. I think the game is well worth it despite these facts, but just be aware. I can tell I'm going to be playing this one for a while longer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect example of a diamond covered in ♥♥♥♥. The Core gameplay idea is good and very fun. Its fast paced shooting.However there are a lot of problems, that become apparent right away:1. The graphic design is questionable. Due to the extreme colors and saturation it is very difficult to see enemies or their attacks.2. The Loot and upgrades aren't explained anywhere. You are supposed to pick between gear and upgrades but the game doesn't tell you what they actually do most of the time. A lot of loot is also completely useless where as other loot is so op it breaks the game by making it a cakewalk. 3. The difficulty isn't worked out very well. At the beginning the first level on easy is incredibly hard. I am a fps and rythm game veteran and i could not get through the level on my first 5 tries and got very frustrated. Then i understood some mechanics that were not explained, got good loot and almost finished the whole game in the 6th run. For the next hours i kept dying on the first level until i got a good run and charged through very easily. Basically you die a lot in the first level till you get a good start, then its easy. Not a very good difficulty curve and made worse by the op and ♥♥♥♥ loot. For example the first run that i finished i had such dumb loot that i could literally facetank the final boss and heal against his dmg. It was impossible to die. 4. The rhythm part of the game is at best useless at worst actively hindering you. The soundtracks become repetitive and grinding veeeeryy fast as there is only one per level. The beat you have to hit doesn't really change much but the reward for doing so is barely there. But trying to hit the rhythm means you waste time between shots and reloads. If you instead just spam shoot and reload as fast as you can you are way more efficient. Which is very sad because now its just a shooter no longer a rhythm game. I think i had one or 2 more points but this is honestly enough...To summarize i did have fun playing it but it's just sad to see all these very obvious problems ignored. It makes the game equally fun and frustrating. If the core gameplay wasn't so simply fun, this game would get a 2/10 from me. But thanks to the shooty part it gets a 5/10.
