_childDocuments_.review: Was ship of fools a good game?I first tried the game out during next-fest when the demo was available and i liked the concept. Now having played the game i find the concept to be very well executed and its a blast to play with friends and it has the feeling of having replayability. this is sadly where it falls short.On my first run with a friend we obviously didn't beat the final boss and it felt like it had a serious difficulty to it and we were both super excited, finally a difficult game. On our second run we finished the run and were disappointed. The expectation was for there to be more areas to play with a steeper difficulty curve. what really happened was that we got strong on the first map and just auto won because the difficulty doesn't really increase at all. massive snooze. knowing that the content is lacking on this part, not to mention the super wonky balancing i wouldn't recommend this game for players looking for a traditional roguelite with difficulty. However, if you are looking for a party game to play with your only friend then its a great buy for an hour or two of fun every now and then.TLDR:Make the game 4 player coop and ill consider making it a positive review, this should be early access not full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is a 2 player co-op game that's well worth its $15 pricetag. Combat is made up of balancing keeping on the offensive with cannons and melee attacks with defending through melee combo knockback, melee to put out fires, and charged melee attacks to deflect projectiles while dodge-rolling through the occasional stun beam attack. There's a lot to juggle and it's a lot of fun. Between fights, you'll navigate a map for different loot and shops to beef up your characters and ship for upcoming fights.As far as cons, we hit a progress impeding bug about 10 minutes into a run where the camera got stuck not showing the fight currently happening and we found the cannon mount/dismount and the pick up/use controls to be unintuitive. I also have a strong preference to rogue-likes as opposed to rogue-lites and their gross permanent unlocks locking away boring but super practical unlocks like more health with the same currency as the fun but less practical unlocks like "a random swordfish trinket that I don't have a clue what it does".With all that said, it's still a very fun 6 hours or so playthrough to beat it once even if it doesn't hook you for extra hours of replay. Go grab a fellow fool and give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very easy recommendation. I personally think that people that find this game too short or want 4 player co-op are slightly missing the intention behind this game. Make no mistake, all of the design choices are very intentional, and in my opinion, combine to make one of the most special co-op roguelites I've ever played (and I've played quite a few). The game is relatively short but very replayable. 4 player co-op would be far too easy based on a game very finely balanced for 2 players. People have mentioned they want more cannons, but the point of 4 cannon pedestals is so you can move the two cannons around so you can have one each side or both to one side, depending on the encounter. I have nothing but praise for the devs who managed to keep a game this simple yet deep as well as a fun solo experience but even more fun with a friend! 100% recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a roguelike, meaning once you die, you reset your progression. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a rouge-lite that's also co-op, this is for you. Otherwise, it's passable. 7/10.Note that I previously reviewed this game on the Steam Deck and performance was all around not great, especially at key moments where enemies boarded your ship. This has been fixed and it should now run well on most hardware.This game is designed for co-op. The difficulty is much higher with a single person. You can get a sense of this when according to Steam Achievements, 40% of players have completed a run ("beat the game") vs 9% of players that have completed a run solo. It took me ~15 hours to complete my first run solo, grinding and leveling up things. The game provides you an auto turret to make up for a lost friend. However, it's unhelpful in more situations that I'd like. Swarmed by pufferfish? Too bad, it probably won't do enough damage to kill anything. Ran out of ammo in a key moment? Well it just won't be shooting then.Overall, there isn't much diversity in runs early on. Most of the diversity comes from buying or finding Trinkets, Ammo, or Artifacts during the run. This relies on you getting to enough spaces on the map to push your luck, but your ship probably sucks too much to visit too many of them. It took me about 3 hours to beat the first boss, 8 to beat the second, and then 5 to beat the third and fourth bosses. It was a grind. The lack of diversity can be really painful early on and likely leads to lots of people dropping this game if it's not their cup of tea.Now that I've leveled up most of my stuff, I'll likely try co-op again but otherwise don't think I'll loop around and see the other mechanics they built in. They don't seem like it will honor my time with anything too new or unique.

_childDocuments_.review: has great potential. is kind of funny. but way too often the game is frustrating due to simple inputs not working or being processed properly. it wouldve helped if the developers did a market check before starting their own mediocre project. game gets laggy if too much is happening on the screen (like with binding of isaac) with some particular item builds or in certain game situations - especially in 2-players mode.also occasionally weird and frustrating at approximately 10% of the time are: ranges, hitboxes, deflects, AI, enemies clipping in the rear part of the ship and being only half visible, animations (of the map, the ship driving) being too long which gets more annoying the more you play, game locking input sometimes. most of the casuals wont be bugged by those tiny things. but i like quality and got too many runs ruined and time wasted because people were lazy and/or incompetent. there is more to videogames than some funny phrases and cute artwork. some day people will understand that and deliver serious gameplay and functionality.i like and enjoy this game a lot and i would love to give it a thumbs up. still you get the thumbs down you deserve for the aforementioned factors which leave a bitter and annoying taste.80% of the encounters are so easy that you dont take the game seriously anymore and you just grind through the animations. then you get oneshot on a single encounter from full hp withing 10 seconds.i got just another 5 runs (easy wins with a strong setup and good syngergy) ruined because your difficulty is created due to pure RNG. one can have the best comp and still get oneshot in a single encounter, because it all comes together. 2-3 inputs on cannon reloads or item interactions not working, AI of the cannon focussing the wrong enemy because you couldnt implement a priority on enemies who already have a red alert symbol over their heads, 10 enemies spawning on deck with no way to prevent that from happening with superior firepower, 4 enemy shells getting lobbed at the ship at the same time - 2 of them being crits and therefore direct damage you need to deflect, the rest setting the ship on fire causing damage with a 3 sec delay. then ranges and timings on deflects and fire extinguishes being off again result in receiving even more damage.TLDR: funny, great potential, very frustrating gameplay being prone to time-wasting because developers chose cuteness, colours and other bs nobody cares about over proper, thought-through, consistent gameplay and balancing

_childDocuments_.review: A fun rogue-lite, great art style and gameplay, but there's almost nothing to it.It's an incredibly short game in terms of how much content there is as well as how long you actually play for between runs.I just cannot recommend it for what is available especially at this price considering it is a full release, and there isn't even a roadmap as far as I am aware.A few particularly annoying or bad things, mainly to do with solo play;Upgrading your cannons is 100% worth it, but you will almost certainly notice absolutely no change to the actual effectiveness of it. You also have no clue what the upgrade does without looking on the wiki, because there's no information at the upgrade shop.If you play solo, you can choose a cannon for yourself and then you also get a sentry cannon that is automatic, but extremely and disgustingly slow. If you want to move it to a different spot on the ship, you have to do that yourself while also keeping it and your own cannon loaded, and swatting away any enemies or projectiles that are on/approaching your ship. It also cannot be upgraded until you beat the very final boss, and even then I'm not entirely sure if it will actually affect the default solo sentry cannon or only if you pick it as your primary gun. It's ridiculously bad and only just worth even using.Pufferfish are stupidly deadly on a solo run. On levels where they are the main enemy, it is physically impossible to kill them all on both sides before they reach your ship, and it is impossible to swat them all away before they explode and damage you. The sentry gun is completely useless against them so you have to deal with them entirely alone.The final boss is a decent challenge, most of the enemies can be handled well enough in singleplayer (except the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pufferfish) by moving your cannon back and forth and just keeping the sentry loaded. But when you complete the wave and are fighting the actual boss again, it's almost not worth moving the cannon to the other side when it teleports there. By the time you acknowledge the boss has teleported to the opposite side, you pick up your cannon, and then place it on the other side, you are lucky to get even a few shots on it. If it happens to stay on the same side, great, you can shoot some more and if you have the precision or grapeshot cannon you can charge up and hit it hard. But chances are it will immediately teleport back to the other side and you will have to move the cannon . It's just a chore to try to fight it, and it doesn't get much better in the second part.19/01/23Latest update; sentry cannon can be upgraded from the start now, but they removed the ability to carry items in your hands to the next area - only things on pedestals stay, no matter what.29/12/23After playing a little bit more since I first did, I stand by what I said.It's just not a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concept, art style very cutesy (a bit too cutesy for my liking, but I guess it is well done). It would be nice to be able to fit out the ship at the start of each run with different ammo and/or artefacts to vary the play style a bit more.  As it stands each run is very groundhog day, rinse and repeat.  There are upgrades to cannons/ship health / storage etc, but these don't really change the game play much.  You can change ships but the different ships offer little variation in play style or strategy.My main gripe with this game though is that it is really not for solo play.  As it stands it seems intended for coop play, being poorly optimised for solo play as soon as it starts to get a bit harder.  You simply can't be in two places at once to stop simultaneous attacks (particularly once you have unlocked critical hits which then happen quite often) and/or reload cannons at same time. On that note, there is far too much time spent in a battle simply reloading cannons which makes battles a dull, repetitive scramble.There are also too many different types of ammunition, many of which seem very similar, many of which are pretty useless.  A run's success entirely depends on finding good trinkets, ammunition type matters much less.  And overall there are too many items, particularly ammo but trinkets too, that are a waste of time.  None of the items (even the good ones) really result in much difference in strategy - back to the dull, repetitive point.

_childDocuments_.review: Great roguelite if you like being TOTALLY BLIND about what goes on.the descriptions of all items are very limited and hardly explain anything at all. the game doesn't tell you a lot of things. One thing is "let's figure out what all these map icons mean by visiting them once" and another thing is feeling like a FOOL yourself because half the relics or weapons don't give you any helpful insight. I've spent half this game looking up info on the wiki or steam guides and there is no more info than what you can read in the game most of the time so you're just left wondering and guessing. it's good to not spoil too much of your game to players but this game feels like you either are a super veteran who knows already everything aftrer dumping many hours in it or you like to gamble your run. and on later runs it becomes frustrating, sacrificing an entire run just to find out if something is worth it because the game description prefers to be "fun" rather than informative :/Why the bad vote? despite the mechanic of the game being fun, I find out the lack of clarity frustrating, and at the end... you have to re-do it again? well duh! it's a roguelite, but like 20 times? and each time you increase the difficulty despite even maxing out all upgrades you don't get  that much help.. _childDocuments_.review: Two fools, a boat, a couple canons, and that's it : Ship of fools is about fighting in these mysterious oceans, discovering new equipment, boats, characters (fools) and using your paddle & canons to take on the biggest monsters of the sea. The slowly increasing difficulty allows you to play both in a relaxed manner, or in a more serious and planned approach whille still having fun. The art style and sound design are incredibly well done, and the game can easily take over 20 hours to complete. It took me somewhere around 25-30 hours with a friend to reach the end of the in-game lore, but there are still achievments that we still have to obtain and some strategy we still want to try out. TL;DR : Ship of fools is a great rogue-like in an ocean-themed world, that really shines when played with a friend.

So this probably won't change, and I'll never get my money back.Don't get me wrong this game IS still a great game but I wish a change would occur to fix this ONE issue, because I will never see that gold medal that I ABSOLUTELY deserve for getting all the achievements that aren't dlc related. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, and there are not enough people talking about this game. However, there are some problems. The main one is lack of variety. There are around 65-70 items in the game, but they all are basic increases to stats instead of interesting effects and thus all feel about the same. Also. you only start with about half of the items and unlock the rest later, thus leading to a feeling of even less variety in the early game. The other problem is the lack of equality in how hard certain enemies are. _childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is quite good if you have friends to play with.  The mechanics are fun.  The difficulty is tied reasonably between game knowledge and skill at the mechanics.  If you have a good grasp on either of them you can succeed, and if you want it harder you can just use a worse ship.  There are also a few different fun playstyles, with gunners, support, anti-boarding, and more.  You can also play it solo quite well, especially if you play as the axolotl whose ammo regenerates, but this playstyle is a little too slow for multiplayer (Unless you have a *very* patient friend.The main issue I'd say is balance, but the game is fun regardless.  Some artifacts and trinkets are almost never useful, and some are always basically OP if you get them (like the one that gives more damage depending on how much money you have).  If you do the "more money = more damage" trinket, and do endless mode, you can just replicate the trinket on whoever you have as the gunner, for instance.  But that's a pretty minor gripe.

_childDocuments_.review: Manning the cannons aboard a crumbling ship with a buddy in Ship of Fools is pure, chaotic fun. We fight off waves of fishy fiends with a delightful mix of frantic cannon fire and satisfying melee combos.The cartoony environment keeps things lighthearted even when the deck is overflowing with enemies. While the overarching story is minimal, the quirky characters and ever-changing sea throws new challenges and surprises our way.The best part is discovering insane item combos that turn the tide of battle. One minute we're launching firebombs, the next we're unleashing a wave-clearing laser beam. It's a constant scramble to keep the ship afloat, but the laughter and camaraderie make every defeat feel like a learning experience. Just be prepared for some friendly competition over who gets the shinier loot!

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is a fun, simple game with surprising depth and immense replayability. The element of randomness to the rewards you get means that once you unlock enough things, virtually all characters can be viable, even the ones with seemingly niche abilities. On top of this, the different ship types allow you to try different gameplay styles and pick the kind that you enjoy the most. And, crucially, you can play with a friend.The core gameplay loop is simple - keep your ship alive while fighting through "stages" of enemy waves and slowly upgrading your ammunition, hp, abilities etc. You can choose a path through each of the three main areas (which end in a boss fight) and the path determines what kinds of rewards you get, e.g. ammunition, but it doesn't determine exactly which one. Defeat the boss to move to the next area and repeat the process until you fight the "final boss" in a climactic showdown. As you progress, and as a reward for defeating the last boss, you earn "tendrils" which are basically the unlock currency for new stuff. As mentioned, there's a lot of replayability in the game. Aside from the random loot system, during a round you can unlock additional characters and ships to try on your next run. The game loop is short, usually taking about half an hour to win, which means you can try all sorts of combinations and upgrades quite quickly. It also means not having to commit too heavily to long gaming sessions to progress, which is always welcome. As you increase the difficulty you also unlock new features, keeping the game fresh and interesting as you go.All in all, a very fun, casual experience with more than enough playtime to justify the price. I have some minor gripes with the game's mechanics, but these are likely to get ironed-out before the early access period is over and it's already a lot of fun as-is, even if it were abandoned right now. Strongly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever dreamed of captaining a ship filled with eccentric characters, absurd situations, and more chaos than a seagull in a seafood market, then Ship of Fools is the game for you.In this comedic adventure on the high seas, you'll take command of a ragtag crew of misfits as they navigate through a series of bizarre encounters, questionable decisions, and the occasional sea monster or two.Visually, Ship of Fools is a delight, with colorful graphics that bring its quirky characters and zany situations to life. And the voice acting? It's so good, you'll swear you can smell the salty sea air and taste the stale grog.But don't let the laughs fool you – beneath the humor lies a challenging adventure game that will test your wits and resourcefulness. Whether you're navigating treacherous waters, fending off rivals, or trying to keep you from mutiny, you'll need to stay on your toes to survive.Despite its flaws, Ship of Fools is a hilarious and engaging experience that's perfect for anyone who enjoys a good laugh and a bit of swashbuckling adventure. So hoist the anchor, raise the sails, and prepare for a journey filled with laughter, danger, and more absurdity than you can shake a parrot at.Pros:-Hilarious humor and quirky characters make for a memorable adventure.-Challenging situations keep gameplay engaging.-Colorful graphics and top-notch voice acting bring the world of Ship of Fools to life.Cons:-Some may find the gameplay a bit repetitive, but the laughs make it worth it.-Occasional bugs and glitches may mar the experience, but they're as rare as a friendly kraken.Overall Rating: 8/10 – A comedic voyage that's as entertaining as it is absurd, perfect for anyone who's ever wanted to sail the seven seas with a crew of lovable lunatics. Just be sure to bring your sense of humor – and maybe a life jacket or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Played many more hours locally with my best friend, but recently finished Lighthouse 15. (Highest Difficulty Level)The game is super fun, even though it is ungodly imbalanced and a lot of runs require extreme teamwork, precision, and a lot of RNGesus blessings. Some runs, especially at high lighthouses can be come an insane battle of attrition. The game also runs horribly no matter what your build is or what OS you are on. _childDocuments_.review: While I have gotten a lot of enjoyment out of this game, I can't entirely recommend it to others. Having more difficult runs with the lighthouse is nice, but my main thing against the game is how it adds difficulty. Most of my runs are either so easy they are boring since I got good luck with encounters or nearly impossible. I can win almost every time but when I lose it isn't because I made a mistake but because multiple crit projectiles came zooming at 100 miles an hour to the other side of the ship before I could reflect them. While this may be easier to deal with in coop play it feels like absolute crap for solo runs. I also feel that in most runs some encounters are almost certain death while the BOSS battles are so easy I feel relieved when I fight enough to get to them. Another thing that I think is kind of rough and have seen other people say is that the controls aren't super intuitive. There were times after coming back from a break from playing the game I couldn't even remember what button prompted dialogue. Often it is a toss-up whether the game wants you to click space, e, or enter because it isn't always the same between different interactions. A final thing that is more just a personal issue I have is there isn't any way to save any runs. Often after completing various difficulties and runs you will be gifted an item but now you have to do another run. _childDocuments_.review: The art style is amazing but that's pretty much it.It takes an existing concept and makes it worst due to extremely poor game design decisions and poor balacing.Every run is too similar. The monsters are always the same, with the exact same attacks. There is a lack of boss and attack patterns.The items we found are lazy and uninspired. More often than not, you will retrieve new ammo that are worst than the starting ones. There is no info, no tooltip about their effect so be prepared to try new ammo and be extremely disappointed.The artifacts are simple and have too many restrictions. Some of them try to synergize but it's just not worth it.The trinkets are unfun, uninspired once again. They are the only items with cumulative effects that could have made a run unique but we don't get enough of them. They usually are a simple raw stat bonus.Accessing a merchant is frustrating since its position is just random. The game don't try to put it far enough on your path. It means you won't have enough money to buy things most of the time, and will just gain money for no reason.The worst part is the "game +" mechanic. It's like to "heat" in Hades but with *auto-censored* decisions from the game designers. For instance, at lighthouse level 3, slugs will appears every ~10 seconds. The issue is those slugs will spawn continually and can attack your ship, even when you are on a peacefull island (like a merchant) or even when you are locked in a map animation. This is one of the most baffling thing I have ever witnessed in a video game.There are currently some game breaking bugs. Some monsters will not spawn properly, locking your run. I also experimented audio issue where a sound never stops.The game is also too easy. You will finish it in just 3 to 5 hours before the lighthouse mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you enjoy rougelikes and are looking for a very unique take on combat encounters you should buy this game.Longer version:This game takes place on a ship and most combat is done through stationary turrets you aim,load, and fire, and through melee attacks for defending the ship. You take damage by enemies either approaching the ship slowly and melee attacking, or selecting a tile on this ship and launching a projectile. In general the combat is very fair, and you usually have a counter to anything an enemy can do. However with high enemy numbers it can feel a bit unfair.ITEMS: The items are highly variable in usefulness. some items do immensily useful effects and sometimes they do basically nothing.  If you get terrible rng the the bosses and random encounters can wreck you.However this game is very fun, and if you have a friend to play with it has a moderate amount of replayability. Once you unlock everything the game begins to get stale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ship of Fools! I'd rate it 8.5/10. As a game designer, I'm excited to share my thoughts.Pros: Amazing to play with friends for tens of hours and make memories (due to replayability, strategizing, improving synergized gameplay etc), hilarious text, discoverable synergies, great optional difficulty climb thanks to updates, tons of fun modifier items, lots of super individual experiences, etc. There are tons of characters that feel quite different when leaning into their unique perk (mixing and matching w ur duo is great!) and the ships feel unique too. There is consistently a workout-level challenge even after 40 hours if the difficulty is at least medium. The devs really care about getting making sure you can play as much of the content as possible--if your friend owns a dlc (theyre cheap!!) then you can use those characters too. You can push any one fantasy insanely in one direction and that's always funny and awesome.Cons: It's really difficulty to play alone, if not impossible at high difficulties. The bosses never change and enemies are consistent , the final boss , the replay grind is intense and LONG, the strats don't get super different and some are guaranteed to work if you wait long enough. It really feels like we need more different enemies--seeing ALL the SAME ones EVERY run is just doesn't feel special, even if it's a good marker against your power. There's a rare audiovisual bug that occurs only on one player's screen.I really highly recommend this game and it gets way better with every content drop!! IT'S PERFECT FOR NEW AND EXPERIENCED PLAYERS!!! It's silly and can be either generally relaxed or intense. And I'm so glad for this latest update with new ships and characters. But please, devs--decrease the downtime and increase the differentiation!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good, very good. Can recommend it, very good for co-op, especially with someone that isn't well-versed to video-games.-Fun, fast and offers variety, lots of weapons/builds without being too complex since you have a limit of 5 slots. Major decisions that can either make the game or break it, but without feeling too unfair.-Animations/sounds/effects are all satisfying. Some enemies are meh and just flat out uninteresting, but visually speaking the game looks and sounds nice.-Gameplay feels somewhat fresh, a few good "new" ideas are presented in a nice manner, the melee/ranged hussle is tough at first but once you get the hang of it, it feels very natural.HOWEVER, has a few problems that can be frustrating at some points, which you do need to mind before buying this.-Ever since the lighthouse update, minor lags will happen, that might just make you lose. Didn't happen before the lighthouse update, so no idea what's on that end. Also, whenever you go into a new area, it loads A LOT.-The lighthouse becomes insanely difficult too quick. I mean alright, you're replaying the game to get more spice, but at around level 6-7 it becomes very difficult unless you get a very good combination. Which leads to point 3-You get new items, but the old ones DON'T ROTATE OUT. This is a MAJOR PROBLEM, because you might be at the second zone and get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥-ass piercing shell while you're in desperate need of something that is actually good. Not a "balancing" issue, but please, lower the chance of older/more useless stuff appearing later in the game.Can recommend, game's worth its money, at a discount even more so. Given that this seems to be the studio's first release, it's good that they keep updating it, that they are interacting here and on the forums (not a lot, but enough to at least feel ALIVE), so can definitely recommend supporting the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a roguelite co-op game with quirky cute graphics that I received as a birthday gift.The controls could benefit from better logic, making the game harder than it should be. For example trying to grab a seagull as ammo may end up make you pick a nearby object instead, or reloading a canon or putting down a plank for repair can fail because of other objects close by. I would have liked the reloading and repairing being automatically performed just by having the object in hands and being close to the canon or to the hole in the hull. In stressful situations it only adds to the chaos and the frustration of losing.The game is not really balanced, as some ammo and trinkets are completely overpowered and will trivialize a run while others are just garbage and incentivize to "run again" for that dopamine rush when the RNG gives you the right combination of trinkets, artefacts and ammunition... but I guess there is some fun to be had in stomping everything after hours of painstakingly learning the monsters pattern.Another dubious design choice is that for a co op game, the characters stun each other when hitting too close and I have not found any way to disable it, which makes the game even more frustrating whereas playing with a friend is supposed to be "more" fun. Not sure about recommending the game but I guess I've seen worse?

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Ship of Fools is a great coop experience for 2 players with many hours of content! I definitely recommend it.In short: you're on a tiny little ship with two cannons, sea creatures are attacking you from both sides, and you've got to sail all the way to the Eye of the Storm to find out how to repel it and save the island you're from.Ship of Fools is a tight gameplay loop with surprising amounts of fun hidden behind the simple options you have: shoot cannons, carry items, dodge/roll, and strike at close range with your paddle.Each of these basic actions is complemented by in-game items that empower them uniquely, meaning you'll often find yourself deviating from your go-to build to make use of your new trinkets and baubles.RNG, while present at all stages of the game, leaves a lot of room for strategizing and skill expression. This means you should be able to complete most of your expeditions without sinking once you've learned the basics as a young Fool! While it's possible to try and force the same build each game, it would be wiser to adapt, so getting an idea of what items work best together becomes a big part of your learning experience.Ship of Fools is charming all around, with beautifully drawn characters that will immediately clue you into the tone of the game. It's full of humor, colorful, and unapologetically cartoonish. You could draw a lot of similarities to Cult of the Lamb! Minus the blood sacrifices. At least, that means Ship of Fools is accessible to younger players! Parents, this is a great way to have fun with your little gremlins.Ship of Fools is definitely built as a duo experience. While solo is possible thanks to automatic cannons that fire without your input, the hectic nature of the game will quickly test your priorities. Hordes of enemies will swarm you from either side, projectiles will fly above your head threatening to damage your hull - something easily repelled by two coordinated Fools can prove difficult for the lone sailor. My advice: only play Ship of Fools solo if you are looking for a challenge.I am writing this after the Great Lighthouse update was introduced to the game in May 2023. The game was initially lacking an endgame, as I was happy to put it down after getting all Steam achievements. This has changed with the introduction of a new system that tests your might by throwing in extra difficulty modifiers (projectiles can directly damage your ship if they aren't caught, enemies are smarter, tougher...) and I've already sunken hours into the new content with a smile.More is planned by the developers, but in its current state, It feels like Overcooked met Cult of the Lamb, and the result is very graceful. Props to the developers behind such a charming title - but I must return to the High Seas now. The Storm is coming back, and it calls for a Fool to repel it. Ciao!

_childDocuments_.review: I have 3 other friends that plays this but it only allows two players per boat. The only solution is to split us up in pairs and play separately.And we all still had a blast! Heck, melee only can even be broken!Plus, almost anything can be used as ammo!The issues the arises from this is that only two of the hosts have their progression saved, whereas the other two, me and my other friend, doesn't have their progression saved. _childDocuments_.review: A fun little rogue-like for you and a friend, would highly recommend controller over M and K but regardless you and a buddy can have a wild and enjoyable time. The game play loop is fun and due to the randomness somehow never feels repetitive, it's also definitely a memory maker in my opinion, especially if you use the local co-op option. The amount of struggling times we've had where we just barely make it through feels so rewarding and gives a real big hit of dopamine. Never once have I felt like a part of the game was an unfair difficulty and while some people complain about the lack of item descriptions on upgrades until you put them on the ship, I far prefer this as it's sort of the point of a rogue-like game. You get better at the game through experience rather than because it tells you something is good or bad. An item that seems like it's bad at first, might just be because you don't know how to use it yet. The only part that could improve is when you do get a description for an item, sometimes it is a bit confusing, as well as there isn't much clarity on what upgrading your cannons does. After playing fourteen hours I honestly don't know what it does, but it feels like they're stronger. Each Fool (Character) feels unique in their special abilities and design, not one feels like it would ever be useless and given the right combo's can be down right over powered. Betty being one of the most powerful offense and Todd, one of the first you have to use, being an insane defense machine.Without a doubt, you should buy this game, preferably at full price. But no matter how you pick it up, I'd just highly recommend you do.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5.Overall game is good, but there are a lot of improvements should be done.1. Single player experience for endgame is very difficult and need rebalancing comparing to coop.2. Sniper rifle cannon need rebalancing/reworking. It should increase damage with each success hit up to +100% (5% per hit). Miss should clear bonus.3. Bottle exchange artefacts must be not destroyable, as there many regular artefacts better or not much worse that these.4. Online coop usually lagging, many visaul bugs. When host leave session, person that have joined are stuck of screen and should restart the game.5. Many ammo types are simply auto skip.6. Freeze effect needs reworking. Frozen enemies must take much more damage. Frozen spiky ball boms enemies should explode. Often shooting owl freezes it and it drifts offscreen while staying alive alive.7. Add ability to break objects (ammo, artefacts, trinkets). For instance, breaked object may give 1,2,3 wood planks, etc.8. Harpoon build only viable for 1 character, which is not good.9. Few characters need rebalancing, as if may feel much weaker that others.10. Lighthouse artefacts mechanic should be reworked. Must allow to load many tentacles with diminishing return. For instance, 1 tentacle -> 1st storm tile, 2 tentackles -> 2nd storm tile. So if you peek 4 tentacles, you should be able to load all of them to artefact, allowing to overcome 2 shadow tiles and start progressing for 3rd tile. For now this artefacts is almost auto-drop.11. Two head boss spinning hypnos attack duration should be decreased. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun innovative rogue-like!Mechanics are engaging and fun to pull off like reflecting projectiles!Great Soundtrack!Responsive game play!Satisfying and easy to pick up learning curve!Cheap game!TLDR Fun, worth time, minor issues below first is quality of life change I think, second is Opinions:I highly recommend trying this game with a friend or solo either way is viable I've just beaten the final boss on a solo run and I only have 2 things I feel need a change. The first is a quick one, maybe an option to toggle this on or off, So many times I push down to get off a cannon then try to run left or right to quickly stop my ship from taking damage, but if you try to do it to quickly the game wont take you off the cannon like it has an input delay and you will be stuck thinking you've already told the game to get off the cannon and you are stuck in place which cannot happen in a solo game when you are responsible for everything, this happens to me multiple times a run and is very frustrating my solution is just make left and right take you off cannons as well, you don't aim with it so there should be no reason not to?This is more of a game design issue in my opinion, the final boss was the most disappointing thing when I realized it was just enemy spam and the boss doesn't even attack or pose a threat. Which I'm not really sure how video games have come this far and people still think enemy spam bosses are a good idea very rarely can they be pulled off and this is absolutely not one of those cases, this is not an interesting, new, or a fun experience. On top of it just being enemy spam its the longest fight in the game! 3rd Phase really?! For what?! in case you didn't see all the enemies that he spawned in the first 2 phases? It just doesn't make sense and feels like complete fluff which I hope isn't the case because the game doesn't have a huge amount of content to begin with only 4 bosses and one of them isn't really a boss has me worried but thats just my pessimism kicking in I really hope this game gets updates in the form of enemies and bosses the new ships sound interesting but this game desperately needs new adversaries.

_childDocuments_.review: After 36 hours of playing this game to full achievement and game completion I can say it's been fun, but missing a lot of features. It truly felt like an early-access game that got released too soon. Which felt like a huge disappointment when playing.This is written BEFORE the new spring release update 2023.The game starts of great, I love the rogue-like features and unlocking them at the shop and being able to bring them with is great.What's not great is that when you buy all three pearls from Briny; And they're artefacts or ammo, you have to walk back and forth 2 to 3 times to load them on the boat. Just have them loaded on immediately. It's less obnoxious. They also disappear if you close your game, which is quite sad.I wish there was a feature to randomly have already unlocked artefacts, ammo and trinkets be bought for slightly more expensive with tendrils at the start of a new run, this will make certain challenges like the no damage achievement a bit more do-able. There's enough market stalls, why put the only merchant on the far end? It will also solve the problem of not being interested in tendril tiles anymore. I got about 170-200 saved up after completion now, with no way to spend them.Trying for the no damage is so incredibly luck based rather than skill it cost me 4 days and a lot of frustration to get. Absolutely no fun in that. The common and 'bad' ammo is far too common for a fun run. It also feels like there is too much fire ammo compared to the other types. There's certain items I have only seen once, and others far too often. I have played most of the game solo, and gave up a lot after damage. If you play co-op you can't give up. You are forced to let the boat sink entirely or quit to menu. Can this feature please be implemented in co-op.An endless run would be a huge plus to this game, the three bosses and end boss does feel short after multiple completion.Another feature during the run which would be great is to be able to sell your items for a huge decreased sell rate. For example; Only 25% of the actual 100% price; Or to have the merchant re-roll it's products for a good penny. It makes the game a bit more fun, the amount of times I have seen the chicken statues without a chicken on my boat has cost me a lot of sighs.The sentry on solo play is great, but it'd be nice to have more sentry upgrades. Or be able to swap the sentry out for another gun and have that act like a sentry. I know this is hard to balance and motivates co-op, but it's not fast enough for the boss fights and makes them much harder than need be.Some of the damage you take feels very unfair. The Bully in area 1 sometimes are behind multiple enemies and hitting them is impossible. Being able to reflect their tongue would be a great last resort.The fire damage on area 3 is the most frustrating unbalanced experience I have had in this game. When the beakaneer appear or when multiple pecker die, its a lost cause. As experienced and skilled you may be. The beakaneer has been a run ender on many occasions because the fire damage just keeps coming and as a fool you can't keep up and get rid of a boat full of fire in time. Sometimes the fire doesn't immediately get extinguished when you finish the wave, resulting in losing HP anyway; And there is nothing you can do about it. Getting whacked around by your teammate might have a slight cooldown in my opinion. Sometimes it gets a bit too much when you have to focus on multiple things. But it's not too bothersome.Overall, the game has been fun to play co-op and solo. It can use some tweaks and extra features; Which I hope will appear in future updates. I have faith in this game's success and am looking forward to play future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Having now beat the game, I have a few notes. 1. The content is absolutely worth 15 dollars, however, once you've run through it there is little reason to return to runs. Things like run modifiers, "special events" across the sea board, and challenges would help give reason to continue playing.2. The gameplay loop is fun, I played with a buddy and co-op was very enjoyable. One small note, being able to be stunned by co-op partners seems like a nice addition of "difficulty" at first but after reaching further into the run, you'll find yourself in bad spots where it's very difficult to dodge your partner AND what is happening on the ship. It simply adds another layer of micromanaging, which for some may be fun, I just personally found it tedious.3. Stuns. some of the best runs we had were lost because we were stunned by an enemy attack and stuns are INCREDIBLY potent. Frankly, with how much you have to micromanage combat in this game, the stun feature just feels bad as even if you're playing well, there are simply scenarios where getting hit by a stun is inevitable unless you sacrifice ship health. Stuns last seconds and there is no way to fight a stun after you've been hit by it, leaving your crew immobilized and forced to watch the run end with no counterplay except simply not getting hit by them. With more content, this has the potential to be a longstanding roguelite. I look forward to it's future.

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is an extremely LITE coop roguelite with the unique gimmick that all encounters occur aboard your ship. All fights require cooperation and teamwork, there are around 100 combined upgrades for your characters, ships and ammo types, but most of them are flat upgrades or elemental types, there's room for build experimentation but not as much as I'd like to justify repeated runs after completing the game. Also, the game has only 4 zones with one boss each, therefore each subsequent run becomes incresingly similar to the previous ones. Pretty neat and clean coop experience, would totally recommend getting it on sale for a fun seafaring afternoon, but wouldn't buy if you are expecting infinite runs and/or replayability. Finished the game with most upgrades in 7 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good roguelite, with a few caveats.It looks good, and sounds good, and writing is great, and co-op actually requires both players to do something (you can't just have a more experienced player "carry" your session to success), which is rare for roguelites. Some encounters and boss fights gain you "currency" that persists between sessions and is used to unlock more items or slightly upgrade your initial stats. More on this later.Online multiplayer mostly works. It could use a little polish, and you'll almost definitely won't be getting back in the game if you drop out mid-session, but overall was usable - at least for us. The game also features the strangest multiplayer pause menu implementation that I've seen - the game  like it's paused on your end (a still image of the game is blurred in the background), but the battle goes on for the other player.You can also play this game in single-player, though I would highly recommend playing it in co-op instead - with only one player on board, some encounters and boss fights boil down to you dashing around ship in panic (torn between putting out fires, slapping intruders off the ship, and repelling the larger enemies from taking a bite out of it) while the auto-turret sure takes its time with shooting the enemies on its side of the ship. newer versions of the game have added additional challenges and ship types, which spice things up... a little.The game can be won with multiple kinds of builds, but most of them boil down to either maximizing damage or stun-locking enemies. Anything else risks long fights where you might take damage simply because you can't be everywhere at once.Some things (like birds laying ammo-eggs) look fun at first, but ultimately never win over regular setups as they require multiple chance items and equipment slots to be  viable and in the end you're better off using those slots for items that offer extra damage/fire rate/ammo capacity.Not sure what you'd do with this either - perhaps this is the point where the main potential for improvement is in adding game modifiers and daily challenges.This game is pretty resource-intensive, possibly  most resource-intensive game I've seen to date that doesn't feature exponentially increasing numbers of entities. On my machine (i9900K, 1660Ti) the game runs at 90..120fps@1080p while maxing out one of the CPU cores at 4.6GHz (and usually  maxing out the GPU), so you might need some pretty beefy hardware if you're hoping to run it at high fps in 2K or 4K.I have completed this game with a friend in some 15 hours (some of which the game sat idle as you can't save&quit mid-session) and then completed a few sessions in single-player to see what's that like. Unlocking the Cooler Items and upgrades would probably take another dozen hours, but also make the game easier on average, so that's a tricky one.In its current state it might not be the game that you would usually play for hundreds of hours, but still it's pretty neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give this game a Meh vote, other reviews are pretty accurate. It's SHORT. There's not a lot of content, three randomized floors where your path affects what loot you get, four bosses, and that's... apparently it. Buddy and I almost beat the game on our third run, and once we do I'm not sure we'll play much more. There's items that cost 50 meta-progression each to provide some pretty significant bonuses, but... when you get 8-10 per run, we might realistically beat the final boss before we've collected a sum total for those, much less saved up enough.That said, what is here is FUN. It's a goofy, lighthearted 2 player co-op adventure, the humor lands well, the gameplay is pretty great, but lacking any kind of newgame+ or ascension or difficulty modifiers... it just feels thin, for a 15$ price tag. The only real randomization is what loot drops for you, aside from that each run's pretty similar.

And the threats pile on quickly, the end of a run in particular demands full focus and attention.I don't think the game has quite the depth for hours and hours of constant play. _childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, Ship of Fools doesn't quite hit the mark when it comes to game-play longevity. With only three bosses to defeat, players could potentially complete the game in just a couple of hours. I would have expected a bit more content, like additional boss fights or dungeons to explore. It would have been nice to see some variation in the existing boss fights, with new mechanics added to increase the challenge. Additionally, while there are various characters to collect, I found many of them to be lacking in depth, with the default characters being the most effective in most scenarios. Overall, while Ship of Fools has its strengths, its brevity and lack of character development may be disappointing to some players. That being said...Ship of Fools is an excellent top-down rogue-like adventure game that offers an exciting journey of battling sea monsters while keeping your ship intact and improving your combat tactics. The game excels in its progression system, making it a captivating experience for solo players and an even more thrilling one with friends. The wide range of items available in the game adds to the overall experience, making each run distinct due to the randomly generated maps, and the player's choice of path dictates the game-play experience. The game's visuals, music, and sound effects blend together seamlessly, elevating the overall experience and making it an enjoyable way to pass the time. Overall, Ship of Fools is a great game that delivers a well-crafted and engaging adventure that can be enjoyed alone or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible Roguelike with a really fun gameplay loop and for $15 I think it's a great value.The devs recently added a huge content update that addresses the issue of low replayability. There's tons of stuff to do and the game gets pretty challenging with the new Lighthouse mechanic. I'm really happy to be able to report that the game has a lot of end-game content which was missing on launch. .. HOWEVER I still think that an Endless Survival mode and new bosses or variably changing bosses per storm area would be a much more productive way to get people to finish out multiple loops without getting bored. The way it stands there is 3 main area bosses and a final end game boss and they are all the same each run. I have mastered each of these bosses and there's nothing new to see in the core game in terms of areas or enemy variety within each boss zone. A looping mechanism similar to Risk of Rain would make it far easier to unlock tendrils (upgrade currency) for experienced players and give players a harder challenge for those seeking it. My only other wish is that the ship could accommodate more than 2 players but that might be an overly ambitious idea reserved for a sequel. It's not really a complaint but merely a suggestion. As the game is I think it's an extraordinary value and lots of fun with the new free update.

_childDocuments_.review: The debut game from Fika Productions, Ship of Fools is a 2D co-op roguelite naval combat game, where you have to move around cannons on your ship, the Stormstrider [cool name btw] in order to defeat enemies who're storming said ship. There's a lot of strategy involved, especially when it comes to the numerous different ammo types you can load your cannons with. Now, the game is intended to be played with another person, but I don't have friends so I've been playing it on my own for the most part. The game does actually compensate for the lack of a Player 2 by giving you an automatically-firing sentry cannon, but said cannon is significantly weaker than the cannons a hypothetical Player 2 would receive. Which brings me onto the difficulty of the game -I don't know if I'm playing on Easy or something, but Ship of Fools is disappointingly easy - even when playing solo. It was probably down to the ammo type I had during my victorious run [the stupidly overpowered Crystal Ball], but the final boss, who I expected to be very difficult, was quite honestly trivial. In future, I'll probably put self-imposed restrictions in place to manually pump up the game's difficulty.Final thing I wanted to talk about was post-game content, which Ship of Fools... lacks. I mean, obviously - considering the fact that it's a roguelite - you can just keep playing, and that's fine, but post-game content is something that really goes hand-in-hand with a lot of games in the roguelike/lite genres. Take Hades for example - once you've beaten the final boss once, you gain access to heaps of new content which you can use to change the difficulty of the game, giving you lots of incentive to keep playing. Or, Brutal Orchestra - beating the final bosses with different party members yield new rewards. In Ship of Fools, it's mainly just ''keep beating the final boss - oh, and you can try and get all the upgrades and stuff too if you want''. To be fair, though, it was released only recently, and I suspect the devs are working on more post-game content for future updates.I know this review has mainly been critical of Ship of Fools, but it really is a solid game - the amazing cartoonish graphics and incredible pirate-y soundtrack composed by Phillipe Grant are most definitely highlights - and despite the lack of post-game content, the game is fun enough that you'll be fine with going through and defeating the final boss a few more times. It's definitely a game that I'd recommend if you enjoy pirate games [like myself], roguelites and cool combat.EDIT:With all of the new updates that Fika has provided the game, Ship of Fools has been elevated high beyond its initial release form! "Lighthouse levels" introduce post-game challenges that get increasingly more difficult as time goes on, and "Endless mode" adds a fun new twist in your ability to create absolutely insane builds over time. There's a slew of new items, and the new ships add even more diversity! Overall, Fika has knocked it out of the park with all of the new post-game content!

name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands
detailed_description: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Chaotic Great Edition THE CHAOTIC GREAT EDITION INCLUDES: Full Game Season Pass (Includes the Butt Stallion Pack, Blightcaller class, and 4 dungeons with new bosses, loot, and environments) Dragon Lord Pack Bonus Content About the Game Party up with friends in cross-platform multiplayer! Embark on an epic adventure full of whimsy, wonder, and high-powered weaponry! Bullets, magic, and broadswords collide across this chaotic fantasy world brought to life by the unpredictable Tiny Tina. Roll your own multiclass hero and loot, shoot, slash, and cast your way through outlandish monsters and loot-filled dungeons on a quest to stop the tyrannical Dragon Lord. Everyone's welcome, so join the party, throw on your adventuring boots, and be Chaotic Great! AN UNPREDICTABLE FANTASY WORLD Tiny Tina is your disorderly guide through an extraordinary tabletop realm where rules rarely apply. Explore a vast overworld spanning majestic cities, dank mushroom forests, foreboding fortresses, and more! GUNS, SPELLS, AND MORE Blast baddies with powerful guns and devastating spells in frenetic first-person battles. Use your firepower to vanquish legions of enemies, including smack-talking skeletons, land-roaming sharks, and colossal bosses. Then delve deeper into dangerous dungeons for a shot at epic loot! PARTY UP TO DEFEAT EVIL Joining you at the table are headstrong captain Valentine and rule-obsessed robot Frette. During your quest to defeat the Dragon Lord, you'll meet a cast of lovable misfits like a lute-wielding Bardbarian and your very own Fairy Punchfather. PERSONALIZE YOUR HERO Create the perfect hero with deep customization, including a multiclass system that lets you mix and match six unique character skill trees, all with their own awesome abilities. Level up, refine your build, expand your arsenal, and become the ultimate adventurer. BAND TOGETHER IN CHAOTIC CO-OP Enjoy the story solo or start a party with up to three friends in seamless online multiplayer. Share the spoils or rush to get the shiniest loot—how you play is up to you!

_childDocuments_.review: You know how one of the synonyms to the Borderlands franchise is "Badass"? Well, this one is "half-assed".Fundamentally, this is a reskin of Borderlands 3 with fewer mechanics - the vehicles are gone completely, replaced with characters traversing an overworld map, getting into dungeons. If you played other Borderlands, you might say "Okay, so this is an extension of fast travel that used to be just a map, right? That sounds ok". But the problem is that the dungeons you go to are almost never unique! You have several fantasy-themed "Biomes" that you traverse, and the dungeons and random encounters on them will just be some combination of pre-generated arena maps with randomized waves of enemies attacking you and giving loot at the end. Only several locations have some thought put to them.Out of 7.4 hours clocked in the game, I spent about 4 in these boring sloggish encounters. The gunplay is inherited like-for-like from Borderlands 3 with all the idiotic scaling issues - the hard difficulty simply tweaks numbers on enemies, making them bullet sponges. So you just end up watching the same number pop up from the same enemy for hours on end.What exacerbates this problem is level gates - several times in the campaign, you encounter a banner saying something like "Oh, you were enjoying the story, you silly goose? You are level 10, and moving on, the enemies will be level 15! You can proceed of course, but they will be so bullet spongy your finger will get numb. So be a dear and go do side quests". Remember what I said about dungeons? Yeah, it asks you to grind same encounters in the same walls for hours.I suppose I still need to commend some of the whimsical guns and locations in the game, as well as Will Arnett's vocal performance as the Dragon Knight (though half of the time I felt like Bojack Horseman was narrating his dnd campaign to me), but Dragon Knight's presence in the game is criminally low because of above mentioned level gates. Just the second you start getting into the flow of the story, the game turns you around and makes you fight more mobs.What saddens me is the degradation of Borderlands franchise - with each passing game, you see less fun gunplay and more boring dialogues that lock you up in the same room for what feels like hours. Pass by this one. It's not worth your time and certainly wasn't worth mine.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game. However please read below for some clarifications.It follows the same Borderlands formula. If you have enjoyed previous games, you will probably enjoy this also.The story was alright, I'd say maybe better than the Borderlands 3 story.This is the shortest game of the Borderlands series so far. Just look at my playtime. 27hrs and I got 80%-90% of the achievements plus I completed the first two DLC's. I expected more of a "Pre-Sequel" length but this game was even shorter than that.The game has sort of the same atmosphere as the old Tiny Tina DLC has in Borderlands 2, so this was a big plus for me. I really enjoyed the Overworld mechanic and the Encounters. Some of the side quests were quite repetitive though.The loot was a bit disappointing though. You have to collect dice to increase your loot luck otherwise your loot will not be that good. I got the loot luck achievement and I had some good drops but I had to grind about 60-70 dices (which is maybe 50% of the whole game) to get 3000 loot luck.Through my playthrough I've been using only pistols and shotguns. In the endgame I have started using some assault rifles but that was about it. Sniper rifles, SMG's and launchers.. are not good.I would recommend purchasing together with all of the DLC's in one bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: A long time Borderlands fan, and Tiny Tina fan for sure.  You'll fit like a glove if you're used to playing the series. _childDocuments_.review: If you've liked any of the previous Borderlands franchise, and you're a fan of TTRPGs and/or fantasy in general, this is the game for you!It's shooty, it's looty, for better or worse it's sticking to the proven formula... well, for the most part.Create-your-own characters, armor, jewelry and spells, cross-classing, a tabletop-map Overworld... there's enough of a twist that it does still feel fresh. (and there continue to be some QoL improvements here and there)Plus, it's a full campaign run by Tiny Tina! and accompanied by some 'celebrity' voices that don't feel like stunt casting. If you enjoyed the BL2 DLC "one-shot" version, it's even better than that and a lot of the dialogue makes it clear that the writers have plenty of TTRPG experience (I know Ashly Burch, Tina's VA, does for sure)Anyway. Yeah. A D&D type game run by your favorite insane explosives expert girl. Guns and magic! Dice?

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina’s wonderlands is a borderlands spin-off game set in a dungeons and dragons realm. The story has you playing the “newbie” and you will go on various quests of defeating monsters, delivering items, and looting chests.While the story isn’t terrible it’s also not very memorable and I have forgotten most of it by the time I reached the end. The entire time playing the game I kept thinking how the borderlands 2 DLC Dragons Keep was far better than this game and I kept getting distracted wishing this game was more like it.The weapons were pretty much all the same from start to finish. I didn’t really come across anything that stood out other than a single shot gun that rained down a dozen arrows or so that would quickly melt enemies hp. Most other weapons were all the same from basic pistol style crossbows, underwhelming machine guns, sniper rifles, and rocket launchers. Almost all weapon drops were very underpowered and weren’t very good for full multiplayer sessions.The multiplayer wasn’t much more exciting than single player. It just didn’t have that borderlands charm to it like the other games. While I did play a lot of multiplayer, it was actually easier to play solo as enemies became increasingly more bullet sponges. There was one boss in particular that was so impossibly hard with 4 players it took over 30min to defeat it. I went back through that area in single player about an hour later and beat that boss in less than 5min.Once that story concluded I played some of the chaos rooms which are just small areas to battle enemies to try and get some of the better loot but again didn’t come across anything worthwhile. I was honestly hyped for this game as I wanted more of that borderlands 2 DLC but it just didn’t live up to it. 6.5/10Buy it on sale as it’s not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands builds on the Borderlands 2 DLC “Tony Tina’s Assault on Dragon Keep.” The levels are bigger, the loot pool is bigger, the gameplay is mostly copied from Borderlands 3. Sounds good, right? But no New Game + (wtf!), a terrible endgame and shortage of farmable bosses make Wonderlands worth buying only with a deep discount.7/10 for original ideas (but could have been higher)Total size on my hdd: 49 GB++ DOOM-inspired gameplay is back. Grenades have been replaced by magic spells.+ Even with other characters like Aloy (Horizon series) and Parvati (Outer Worlds) to her credit, Tiny Tina will forever be voice actress Ashley Burch’s signature role (for me, anyway). She’s as good as ever here.+ Wanda Sykes, Andy Samberg and Will Arnett all turn in great performances.+ Story doesn’t rival the Dragon Keep dlc of Borderlands 2, but is good.+ Replacing the space-ship and map travel of Borderlands 3 is a table-top-rpg-style “overworld,” where you move a miniature of your in-game character around a 3D game board. There are ambushes, chests of loot, and random encounters. Great addition to Wonderlands, adding to the feeling of playing a classic rpg.+ Legendaries are rare again!+ Fun side-quests. One of my favorites was “The Ditcher,” which features famous monster hunter Gerritt of Trivia…+ The best graphics of any Borderlands game.+ Lots of character customization options+ Most of the performance issues that plagued Borderlands 3 are not present in Wonderlands. Ran smooth and stutter free. + Still has a DX11 mode, so if you’re still running an older gpu Wonderlands should work.+/- Wonderlands is woke. There’s pronouns in the character creator, gay pirates, and Paladin Mike is Lorelei from Borderlands 3 (who has transitioned to Lor by the time New Tales from the Borderlands occurs, though Tiny Tina’s design indicates Wonderlands takes place before Borderlands 3). Whether any of that is a positive or negative is up to you.-- No New Game +  A core part of every main Borderlands game to date (including the Pre-Sequel) has been replaying the main campaign with tougher enemies and more specialized loot in NG+. Gearbox seriously missed the mark here. - Those “random encounters” in the Overworld are the same areas, used over and over. There are a good variety – more than a dozen - which minimizes the fatigue of the repeated encounters. I guess there had to be a way to create randomized encounters while keeping Wonderlands under-budget, but completionists will need some serious fortitude to do everything in the Overworld.- Endgame content features the “Chaos Chamber,” which repeats the levels from the “random encounters” of the Overworld with a few re-used bosses thrown in. It’s pathetic and borderline insulting ("just keep playing the same levels over and over, like a hamster running in a wheel").- Shortage of farmable bosses. You’ll get more consistent loot from vending machines.- Levels are too large. You’ll spend a ton of time running around (because you can’t fast-travel until you’ve visited an area at least once).- Default audio balance is terrible. Make sure to move some sliders around so you can actually hear the music.You’ve still got some great ideas, Gearbox. Just need to give us franchise old-timers the bosses and endgame content we’ve come to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on sale for $30 and it was the perfect price. This game isn't worth $60 but has enough value in it to be bought at $30. This is fantasy mixed with Borderlands. I personally enjoyed the main story line and the side quests were entertaining and enjoyable. The fantasy setting is engaging, the monsters are awesome, and the Overworld setting mixes well with the actual game. I beat the game in a good 20 hours and it was a blast!There are a few shortcomings with Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. The main one being the lack of legendary loot. I play these games for the thrill of seeing a legendary item drop and having the icon pop up on the map. In my 20 hours of beating the game, only TWO legendary items dropped before the final fight. I received two more from quests but still, only TWO legendary items dropping in 20 hours of game play is unacceptable. You can argue that this makes greens/blues/purples more balanced but I don't like having to sift through hundreds of weapons to find the right one. When I saw the trailer for this game and the dice rolls I thought they had so much potential to drop good loot but they feel so underwhelming. The loot is easily the biggest problem with the game but everything else is amazing. Another shortcoming is the credits. Why are there 20+ minutes of FORCED credits? I'm all for appreciating the developers for the game but when I'm having to sit there for 20-30 minutes and I can't get out that feels real bad. Other reviews mentioned LBGQT being forced down their throats during the game but I didn't notice it (probably because I didn't play with sound for most of it). There's some characters here and there that are LBGQT but overall it doesn't feel pushy. In conclusion, this game was a lot of fun for what it is - a Borderlands game mixed in a fantasy world. The story and side quests are at their best but the loot feeling so underwhelming is a clear issue. Also, the credits... WHYFinal Score: 8/10-1.5 for lackluster loot-0.5 for 20+ minutes of forced credits

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with some reservations. The good: the character creation is SUPER great and I really appreciated the inclusiveness and lack of gender-bound options. So many COOL options for classes, this is one of the few games where I spent nearly as much time agonizing over class choice as nailing the exact right slider for every single one of my cosmetic choices (mushroom bro! plague bringing! THE AGONY OF CHOICE). Loading up a co-op game was also very smooth with no problems. What little I've reached of the story and characters involved is hilarious and wonderful, and really loads up on the nostalgia for previous borderlands games. Having the different types of maps and game play is weird but cool, it breaks things up a little and makes the game unique, it's a plus for me but I can see why others might not like the overworld map when all they wanted was a shooter.Some bad: I don't usually have problems with motion sickness during games but after playing for just a few minutes it gave me a wicked bad headache that lasted for hours. After consulting the almighty google I changed a BUNCH of different settings and to its credit, I have no discomfort now. Half of these settings I never would've been able to find on my own, however (in case you need it, the big ones for me were in accessibility and concerned turning of ALL camera motion/bobbing and then in gameplay to center the reticule. Higher field of view nice, but not as impactful). Consulting google was a constant since encountering a game-hindering/breaking bug was a very common occurrence and fully half of the initial few hours of gameplay was just making it playable. Not ideal.In conclusion: at full price, especially for the chaotic edition, I would be pretty upset with how buggy it is. Having bought it at a significant discount, I'm feeling pretty good about things. In this context a few bugs don't bother me as much, especially knowing I've got the worst of them figured out and can more or less just sit back and enjoy Tiny Tina's particular brand of chaos and fun. YMMV.

_childDocuments_.review: For a "Looter Shooter" the loot system in this game feels bad. I'm level 25 and all my gear is "Purple - Epic". I've been playing for 2 hours and EVERY SINGLE chest I've opened has had Trash tier guns or gear in it. When you fight your way through a Zone or find a hidden room, and open the chest, and all the guns are "Blue or Green" tier - it feels bad. But yet, you go to a Vending Machine in the city, it has 3 or 4 EPIC level guns to buy. This game can be fun at times, but the Loot system needs a rework BADLY.Further, the enemies just become more Bullet Spongey as time goes on. Getting 200 "Critical Hits" on an enemy with "Fire Weakness" for example does not feel satisfying. Critical Hits should be special..Also, you can't track more than one quest at a time. So you'll often bypass necessary objectives, enemies, or areas - just because you're tracking a different quest. But it's all in the same Zone and area.Borderlands has fun gameplay and lots of cool guns, classes, and a neat world to inhabit. But it's really showing it's age from a Game Design perspective.Couple that with the TRY TOO HARD writing where EVERY LINE has to try and be a joke - You've got a game with no stakes, no emotional resonance. The inventory needs work. The enemies AI needs work. The quest system needs work.If you're a die-hard Borderlands fan- this may tickle your fancy. But for the rest of us, we deserve a bit more from the (5th?) entry in this series.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the worst game in the series.  Mechanically, sure, it plays almost the same as the others in the series, but this one lacks character and direction.  For me, BL2 is the pinnacle of the series.The world lacks cohesion.  The different zones are kind of just there as an obstacle to the end boss.  They don't tie into the story in any way.The weapons don't have any character.  Sure, the brands are there in an off-brand way, but all of the weapons can have elemental damage and they just blend into each other.  In the previous games Mailwan means elemental submachine guns.  Jacobs means high damage, low rate of fire sniper rifles, and so on.  They are all here, but then everything can have an element, and the styling is not very unique to each weapon.The character skill trees were not clearly understandable to me.  I picked some stuff and left it.  If equipment buffs any of my selected skills or not, I didn't really care because the names are meaningless to me, and the icons are hard to extract meaning from.The characters were fine.  I like their banter and Tiny Tina is Tiny Tina, but inside this fantasy world she's not quite the same.  As a story teller, she's not the best.The enemies are also not very memorable.  All I really remember is mushrooms, pirates, and land sharks.  Why am I fighting them?  Because they're hostile.  They don't have an agenda, they're just monsters.  The lamia/serpent ladies have something, but that's about it.The overworld is easily the part of the game I liked the least, especially with the random encounters.  It's very tiring and not interesting.  I'm playing a first person game, I kind of want to navigate the world in that way.  I'm aware that I'm supposed to be playing a tabletop game, but it doesn't feel like it, and I don't think it has to.I want to like it, and there are some interesting things in it, but I can't recommend it unless you want to play every game in the series.  I thought Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep was okay, but that  had some parts that were dragged out and grindy.  You won't miss anything by skipping this.

_childDocuments_.review: When the game is working as it is supposed to, it's some of the most fun I've had with a Borderlands game, when it functions the way it does the other 80-90% of the time, it is one of the worst gaming experiences I've ever had.*Bugs that make accessibility options not work or not work as intended*Regular crashing and freezing*1 out 10 of those crashes will give you an error that corrupts your character and deletes all of your progress*Connection issues that make it very difficult to play with others*The game does not allow you to cancel joining a game once it starts trying to connect you, even if it tells you in the top right corner of the screen that the connection failed, you will have to sit there for several minutes until the game releases you from its failed attempt, that you and it already know it has failed*It is very rare, but when enough effects are happening on screen, your frames will dip and you'll have a heart attack thinking that you're about to lose all of the hours you've put in to your character*Some side quest progression and overworld progression doesn't save properly when playing with others*Missing items or characters to quests, crashes causing you to have to restart quests*Some times the game will just decide to minimize itself, and when you bring it back up, it will go away after a second or two, and you repeat this multiple times until it randomly fixes itself*If you have other programs that like to update, or have any pop-up messengers, they will not just appear under the game like usual, they will pop up and the game will close entirely (This one probably won't effect most people)*Be very careful when adjusting things in your options, because some weird things can happen, and some times its hard to tell what issues are being caused by what.On top of that, there are also parts of the game that function as intended, but are downgrades from previous installments, or are straight up just missing quality of life features that existed before, making certain parts of the game that were fast and helpful, grind to a halt.*You will never use vending machines to purchase items because the equipment sold is worse then anything you'll find in the game, and the pricing is outrageous*Trying to compare equipment in the shop to your own equipment is tedious unlike other installments*Trying to go through your equipment to equip the best gear in your inventory is tedious, because the menus make sure you have to press several more buttons than needed (if using a controller)*The class abilities and skill trees are limited to 2, and the level maximum is unnecessarily low, especially when there are so many different combinations of two classes you could put togetherThis may not be everything me and my friends have experienced so far, but it is all I can remember at the moment of writing this. Some of you may have been lucky and not experienced any of this, or maybe you were having so much fun that you didn't notice some of the poor design choices, but all of the issues I've stated happened at least once to each of us, me and the two other players who purchased the game with me, and all of us have PCs that are able to run this game on its highest settings without issue, the problems are definitely coming from the game itself. We bought the game when it was on sale, which did include all the DLC.We have not yet interacted with all of the DLC yet, most of what we have played is really fun dungeons, but very short (a little under an hour to a little over, each)They are dungeons with about 5 to 6 rooms, per DLC (again, from what I've seen so far), you can play through them several times each, where the only difference seems to be the difficulty of the boss at the end of the dungeon. And again, these have been a lot of fun, but if you didn't get them in a deal like we did, they are not worth the $10 per. they are currently being sold for.This game has been a roller-coaster. If they were to fix all the issues, it could be my favorite of the franchise, but I believe the last time I checked the game came out 3 years ago, which means, if they aren't fixed yet, they never will be.I still plan to finish the game, and play through most of the optional content, as long as the game itself allows me.
