_childDocuments_.review: Well phock.  Whoever had the idea for this game should be let go and not allowed to work in the industry ever again.  When I read the reviews mentioning a "linear" plot, I expected something, you know, linear but this game is anything but.Let me specify, it also isn't open.  Imagine you are put into a baby crib with a couple of balls, cubes and a blanket and once in a while, someone walks up to the crib and drops a hamster which of course, won't stick around for much more than 1-2 minutes, then it's back to you, alone in that crib with your balls and cubes.  And this repeats over and over and over.Then, take all of this and slap "ADnD" on top of it so people buy it because nothing sells like painting a turd gold and pass it as a collectable right?So...I bought this game and I roll my character, which is about the only good thing this game has on the preceding chapters of this franchise, like you're not forced to play a pre-made character you don't identify with.I jump in, it's fun, the combat feels great and moving around is fluid, quick, precise, I love it.  So I run around the map a bit, you know, to try and find all the hidden things only to find out you are confined into a tiny space, with a bunch of monsters who want to kill you (the hamsters).  You kill everything, open a bunch of chests (they are all over the place and rarely drop anything useful (ammo out of the a-hole and health potions of course, 80% of which you will never need) and tons of chests "filled" with 1-15 bucks (stuff you get to buy usually costs 2000+) so you spend your time going after chests for that extra few bucks over and over and over and over.  You don't have to but hey, if you wanna speed up the upgrading, they help.  So instead of fewer chests with more money in them, you get 10s of them with pocket change...  Get tedious about 5 minutes in, not to mention that you have to stick around each chest for a couple of seconds so you get to suck in their contents, adding to the already boring tedium soup.And then, at one point, you're given this map where you have a mini figure of yourself with a big ass head, you know, to make it more ADnD-y where you get random encounters (only in tall grass mind you) and where you run from one place to another.  The map would have been a great idea if the random encounters had been worthwhile.Each random encounter is just a gauntlet.  You appear in a bowl shaped map, a tiny map, where mobs will spawn for some time.  You are given a few barrels, sometimes, there are traps and once you've killed a few mobs, you're given one stronger boss (which you can take down in a couple more hits than normal mobs) which will drop rarer stuff and then, a portal opens and you get out and that's it.  All encounters are the same.   The only random elements in them is when they appear, the rest is EXACTLY THE SAME.So you run around on the map, go from here to there, following the main quest, just like in the other games of the franchise, but with smaller, more limited and especially more boring maps with a very limited variety of mobs to fight (I have played 5 hours and so far, 90% of all mobs are skeletons, either gunners, archers or plain stupid melee skellies.They certainly outdid themselves on the graphics, they are beautiful.  The humor is bland, like a bowl of corn flakes... without the milk, or the flakes.  It's cheap and not funny, so not really humor after all but that would be ok if the game threw you something good to play, which it doesn't.It's repetitive, limited and well, just not that fun.  I played with a few people and got knocked down a couple of times, at first, legitimately, and didn't get "helped" back on my feet even though they were standing right next to me, then on purpose only to end up with the same result, no rez.  So the function is not working or people playing the game are so bored that this is what they do to spice it up.  Let their teammates die on purpose.Graphics : 10The rest : MehI am glad Epic players got phocked before I did.Edit : I hope you enjoy reloading.

_childDocuments_.review: Like running full speed on a hamster wheel going nowhere.POSITIVE STUFF:- Game is gorgeous; best arenas and puzzles across the BL games- Awesome gunplay; spells are really cool- Great audio designNEGATIVES:- The story stinks; even worse than BL3, which I didn't hate. Lots of story setup, the villain gets interesting but then the game ends with a fart. Zero payoff- The side-quests are bad. The fantasy world created here looks amazing, but its characters are all flat and boring. You'll get a few good sidequests here and there but most are just not interesting.- Loot is bad; This is what killed the game for me.- "Luck" mechanic forcing you to collect random dice around the game world in order to increase your chances at gaining good gear in every respect, but the system is WAY too harsh. Destroying a boss and getting showered with green loot never feels good. Felt like every chest I opened, every store visit I would find nothing useful. Literally all of my gear (that I would have to use for 5+ levels) came from SHIFT keys.- Inventory management is absolutely terrible and felt like busy-work, and you are alwasy having to be in the terrible menus.- Leveling is very slow and tedious; early on you level up at a good pace but the further you get the more it starts to just CRAWL. 1 hour per level, it seemed like.I can't recommend this one, especially to Borderlands fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Made during Covid, from the developers homes, when they couldn't go to work properly, for that i give them a bit of a free pass. The game though is absolutely boring, the gun play is rubbish, the gun variety is awful i mean like you will see the same 8 guns through out your play through, nothing like the previous Borderland games, the character skill trees are boring and not interesting they just feel tacked on to give the D&D feel, previous Borderland games did it better and the campaign is a slog to get through.  That's the negatives out the way,if it puts you off the game, don't worry, better games out their.As for the positives - The game is funny and quirky and hopefully that is enough to help you slog through the main game. Tina herself literally makes the game ( More ways then one, brilliant actor ). The world is interesting to look at and really appeals to those people who play board games. Plenty of content here to keep you occupied.If you can make it to the end of the game though, that's when it actually gets better, it becomes fun as you unlock a rogue like mode and you can earn really good weapons as well as an actual variety of weapons. It becomes a lot more challenging and engaging. At the end of the day i was not going to recommend that game, it was so bad me and my partner had to break it up into several sessions just to get through it, but when i reached the credits and i saw that the game was made during covid, at a low point of peoples lives, living in fear, unable to leave their homes, work was a struggle, people losing loved ones and each day full of anxiety and stress, for this game to come out like this, trying to make people happy and bringing a bit of enjoyment, how can i in good conscience give it a negative just because it is boring, when the performance is great and the world is interesting and is good to look at with awesome voice acting and great humour, i can't.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tedious. That's the best way I can put it. The classic Borderlands humor is there in bits and pieces; the Skelly-mens dialogue in fights is hilarious. But the overarching story falls flat. Plus, the Tiny Tina bit gets old FAST. In BL2, it was great to meet this quirky character who did funny voices, or called you Mamasita, etc. But an entire game of that - it got old quick. Dungeons are a slog. Most of the game is "encounters." Where you collect a shrine piece, or a side quest item. You hop into a closed arena with a pre-set amount of mobs to kill and at the end get your item. This, over and over and over again, gets tedious.Adding stats to your character - Strength = Crit Damage Buff, Dexterity = Crit Chance Buff - that was a nice touch, and you can pick an Archetype at creation that innately buffed your class choice, i.e. +Wisdon if you wanted a caster, etc.There's a heavy emphasis on melee attacks in this game. In fact, your melee weapon is now equippable with its own stats and damage like any other weapon. However, you still only have the default melee attack button as with any other BL game. No combos, no rolling or dodging, you just stand in front of an enemy and mash 'V' (for PC players) over and over. Tedious.Everything else about the game is boilerplate for a BL game. Weapon types, damage types, art style, it's all the same. This feels more like an up-jumped DLC than a full game on its own. Like the main BL team handed over all of its art assets and game engine to another studio to make something BL-adjacent.Lastly, for lack of a better term, the game as "Woke" as hell. Quests, NPCs, even audio-only lore narration - someone is gay, or trans, or asexual. That by itself isn't a bad thing, but the game just clobbers you over the head with it at every turn. It reminds me of a 12 year old, green-haired tween at Thanksgiving who's decided they have new pronouns, are Bi and everyone else there needs to know it *constantly.* It's obnoxious."We get it, Tina. You're on the right side of history. Now eat your carrots."

_childDocuments_.review: First of all i must warn you that this game has nothing to do with Borderlands lore (nearly). So consider this as a new game. The Borderlands universe welcomes you as a "newbie" and you are just you who plays bunkers and badasses with Tina. So that is why we do not have lore info in this gameI do not really know why they developed a game like this but as i said it before: if your approach to this game is having a new experience then this game fills your expectations. It has different item slots like rings and books and melee weapons, it has a very similar atmosphere with borderlands 3 which is nice, and it has a really smooth and chaotic gameplay that satisfies both new players to this universe and fans like me. I did not quit the game until finished every single side quest. So i can easily give 7.5 out of 10.There are 2 reasons behind why this wonderlands does not deserve 10. Firstly, this game might have better atmosphere with better musics but instead musics are just existing and you do not even recognize them. Second reason is lack of enemy types. There are just 3 maybe 4 different types of enemies and that's it. You are keeping fighting against same enemies around the world. Final point: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but after 14 hours of banging my head against it, I have to say that I don't.  Honestly, I don't think it's a bad game, but I don't think it's for me.  All of the enemies are entirely too tanky, soaking up bullets like sponges.  This stretches out combat encounters to the point where they become tedious, not fun.  And while I understand that the random rolled weapons are supposed to be part of the fun, they're so random that any kind of classification becomes useless. This means you have to equip (and use) almost every weapon you find in order to properly evaluate it.  Which again becomes tedious.There's a lot of things I do like, the art style, the writing, the acting (the main trio of Tina, Valentine and Frett are particularly enjoyable) and the shooting itself isn't bad (apart from the overly healthy enemies.)  I would just urge caution for folks heading into this game to evaluate it closely and be honest with the types of shooters they like.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. Definitely a weak entry in the franchise.There's some good of course :-The environments are really nice. They're colorful, varied, and detailed. Fantasy locations look quite good with the serie's cell-shaded style, and it's a welcome change of pace from the usual bleakness of the mainline games.-The game lets you pick any two classes (out of 7, one of which is DLC), allowing for a bunch of combinations.-The "fantasy" weapon variants are nice and an interesting twist on typical weapons (typical weapons are still there though, don't worry).-Story is alright. Nothing groundbreaking, but just alright. (Although after Borderlands 3 my standards are admittedly very, very low.)-Grenades have been replaced with cooldown based spells, which have a variety of cool effects and go a long way to sell the fantasy theme.-The bosses are cool and more interactive than just "stand there and shoot until the health bar is empty".-And overall the gunplay is nice and tight.But there's a lot more bad overall :-While you can multiclass, each class only has a single skill tree. So you'll only have two skill trees in the end, which may or may not synergize. You also can't reroll your secondary class until you finish the game, and you can never reroll your main class.-The level cap is very low (40). You get a bit more skillpoints than that (44 total), but it's still low. You can't even get both of your capstones. And unlike the other games in the serie, no DLC increases it.-To "compensate" the low cap, from level 40 onward you get "mythic levels" which are incredibly minor bonuses in lieu of proper skillpoints. Gain a level, get +1% reload speed! Can you FEEL the progression? It blows.-The game is short. My playtime upon finishing is at 37 hours, and that's with a lot of idling, doing nearly every side quest, and just generally taking my sweet time.-The humour is tired. Sure, a couple of jokes got me smiling, but when the entire game is a never ending avalanche of corny jokes, puns, and pop culture references, obviously one or two are going to land. But the vast majority did not.-Claptrap is there. Mercifully, his appearances are brief and limited to sidequests.-There are a few bugs. Nothing gamebreaking, but definitely some annoyances, like a pickup prompt not going away or menus not scrolling properly.-You can now loot and equip melee weapon. Which means instead of melee scaling automatically and increasing in effectiveness with some characters' skills, now it's yet another equipment that'll become obsolete after an hour and a half. Yet another category diluting the loot pool. Yet another chance to get a legendary you don't give a damn about (because no, melee combat isn't good enough to build a character around, so it remains a gimmick).-Most dungeons, "random encounters", and a majority of sidequests are just basic arena fights where the game plops you into a randomly selected map, throws a couple of small waves of enemies at you then calls it a day. It's a very lazy way to make content and blatant padding. It's boring (especially since the maps are somewhat big and enemies spawn sparsely and often far from you, so you regularly get gaps in the action), it's uninspired, the rewards are lousy, and you'll be sick of them by the time you've done your third one.-There is now a luck stat, which you increase by finding random dice hidden in the maps. Fitting in theory, but in practice it means you'll mostly drop worthless trash for a good half of the game, until you've found enough dice to prop up your luck - at which point you'll start dropping thing like a normal Borderlands game. It also means you are punished if you don't take the time to explore the map and find at least a good portion of the dice in each one.-Those arena fights I mentionned? That's THE ENTIRETY OF THE POST GAME CONTENT. Yep, instead of getting some new sidequests, raid boss, or even a harder new game+ like usual, you just get a bunch of lousy arena fights with some half-assed modifiers thrown on top. After completing a "chaos run" (that's what they call it), you get a bunch of loot, which you can then use to... do more chaos runs, I guess. Because there is NOTHING else to do.So... yeah. "Meh" indeed. Pick the game up on a deep sale, play a bit until you've had your fill, then just move on to something better and forget about this one.

The game play itself is also a bland, while you are able to multi-class in several classes and combine abilities in your build it doesn't add much to the game play.For a looter shooter you really have to search for the enemies as they are spread thin around the map which is really a hassle and breaking the flow of the game play.The normal game mode is so easy and it is boring even on the highest difficulty.The endgame is a boring repetitive grind which makes the game a tad harder every time you complete a special level as in... the enemies become bullet sponges so not much interesting there.There is no replay value in this game and you can't start a new game+ as you might be familiar with in the normal Borderlands games.If you want a fun game go play Borderlands 2, and try the Tina DLC there because that's just so much more fun than this boring and bland game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an 8/10. If you are a fan of Borderlands, or looter shooters in general, then this is worth a purchase. The story telling is an improvement from 3 along with some new features to the gameplay. The endgame might not be what typical Borderlands fans want, but I believe is serviceable for a spin off title developed during the pandemic. It is a DND-themed game so having the game play loop being a dungeon crawler mode I thought was fitting. If you are not sold on the chaos chamber endgame then the story, and its 40-some-odd side quests, will provide around 35-40 hrs of game play. Every side quest was very entertaining, and they may even be the best of the entire series. Lastly, I will note the T rating shows in this one. The jokes are definitely geared towards a younger audience, but that didn't harm my play through like it did with BL3.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start off that i recieved this as a gift when it was on a 50% sale, but i had this in my wishlist ever since the kickstarter.I would 100% recommend this game to borderlands fans. If you've just finished Borderlands 3, play this game, even if just for the campaign, which took me about 30 hours to complete, but i had fun, i like to rush the main story line, i still got almost all the sidequests untouched, bunch of challenges and what not. If you'd like an apology from the writing team after what happened in B3, go for this, especially if it's on sale. The cast is all different, there may be couple of recurring characters, like Tiny Tina (duh), cl4p-tr4p is there running around the world, but he won't be with you for the whole journey. There are few more, like MR. TORGUE, possibly couple others. However they do not take main stage, they are most of the time in sidequests and in the background. Otherwise it's a whole new cast of characters, giving the writers some freedom and ease of baggage from the past. They're lovely, colorful and i find to enjoy them.The plot is simple, with its own twists and turns, it's no Shyamalan, it all fits well. It's a D&D type of story, with lots of refferences and puns to go. But even still it has strong moments. There were times where i could relate cause these things happened at my tables as well. They know what they were doing in this department.The jokes are back, baby. The borderlands game have a distinct humour that can be a hit or miss for everyone. It's very in your face, sarcastic, no-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, punny, full of references like you love them. In B3 a lot of things felt forced, a huge vibe of "hello fellow kids". Not in this game, the jokes felt like the borderlands i know. Sure there were couple that had me eye rolling but otherwise i actually laughed out loud, or made me smile with a dumb grin. This of course is something that will differ from person to person, but in my perspective, it feels like the writers gave a ♥♥♥♥ this time around. The gameplay is awesome, it's basically the best thing from B3 ported over here, what else would you want. Of course this time it's more with a fantasy aesthetic, and it's design very well when it comes to glueing together space-cowboy guns and fantasy magic. Instead of grenades you got spells and there's but ton of them. It's like a secondary skill that you can pick and choose (of course, you can pick and choose your skill as well, especially later on when you unlock multiclassing and you will have a choice between 4 skills), with infinite use and cooldown on top. Plus there's the variations of each spell like damage type, some unique quirks like shooting it twice, the way you cast out the spell, charges, etc etc. With classes and fairly simple yet detailed character creation, you can truly make your own vault hunt- i mean fatemaker. There are issues of course, some people might not like the map is much smaller than previous titles and the "quirky" way you move between locations, but honestly, this (and it's just my oppinion) is one of the strengths of the game. It's smaller, but much more detailed and each location has its focus. The outworld, or gameboard you walk on gives it a unique charm and it sells you the feeling that you're sitting down with Tina to play some tabletop. But there are some actual issues like bugs, they are not gamebreaking, mostly annoying. For example, sometimes (and this happened like two times exactly in my 30 hours of gameplay) when i'd use my skill, after it ended, the camera would stay in this awkward first person wind up moment, where you had no access to guns, nor spells, or actions, as if i was stuck mid animation still, but just opening and closing the inventory, or the pause menu fixed this. Second bug i encountered was having a prompt still up on my screen, even though there was nothing to Use or Open, but again, quick pause/unpause fixed it just fine.Overall, wait for a nice sale and get the game if you love borderlands. I can't speak for the DLCs, i see a lot of negative reviews, but i might still get them, if i'll get to them. But either way, this is an enjoyable game, with a bonus rogue-like loop at the end, which might be the main focused what they intended, but to me it's just a nice bonus for after-campaign shenanigans.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers ahead...Several chapters in, and I can't recommend this game. I was a huge loyal fan of the BL franchise from the start, and consider BL2 the peak (the Tiny Tina DLC was top notch and super fun), but TTW has just been a chore to play. The guns aren't particularly fun to shoot, enemies aren't tuned very well, and even tho I understand they are going for the RPG references, all the extra rings, spells, necklaces, etc etc are a pain in the butt to manage. To much clutter affecting stats to balance comfortably. The amount of theory crafting needed to put builds together is way too much for a looter shooter.The humor is there, and the voice acting is good (except for Wanda Sykes, not sure why they put her in the game, her acting and character are terrible), but the playable characters are forgettable. And there just aren't enough significant core characters to latch on to. Just your two game 'friends' and Tina. Makes the game feel emptier than the past entries. Add on to that the over-the-top wokeness (gay pirate ghosts, the creepiest, cringiest trans whatever-the-hell Lorelei's created character is supposed to be, Brick turned into a foofy fairy, so much more I can't even list it all here....and rainbows... rainbows everywhere), and the game induces far more groans than laughs. There's so much of it and it's so over the top and in your face that it's impossible to ignore and work around. Their intended messaging is QUITE clear.The side quests are annoying. Waaaaaaaay too much time spent having to sit and wait for the NPCs to finish telling thier life story before I can get to shooting stuff. Not sure why they can't just start the mission and then chatter over the comm while I start running towards the objective, but the side quests feel like more of a time sink than an avenue for powerful red text weapons like in the past.There are some cool story moments, even tho it felt like they were there for shock value more than plot value. Those were entertaining at least. And I kind of like the overworld map idea, tho most locations aren't clearly labeled and it's easy to get stuck in the wrong areas if you aren't following the quest marker, and getting from one point to another takes a bit too long for my tastes. The 'dungeons' are just copy pasta and get old quickly.All in all, if the game didn't feel like a slog, and the guns were actually fun to shoot, then I could say the rest of the downsides are ignorable inconvieniences. (Well....mostly). But the core component of what makes looter shooters great (fun weapons with lots of variety) is simply missing. Its like they took away from the guns to put more into the spells, which I ended up not liking very much, since the spells are just a glorified grenade replacement system.I will try to actually finish the game at some point, and it breaks my heart that I dislike a Borderlands game. But I can't honestly recommend this game, and it will probably be the last Borderlands game I buy until Gearbox decided to shift their priorities back to what made BL1 & 2 so awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played all the borderlands. When the first borderlands came out it introduced many new mechanics combining shooter looter rpg elements. Now with this latest installment capitalising on its most interesting and likeable character, Tiny Tina, it tries to bring in more variety whilst sticking to its roots. It is a fun game I can recommend to any borderlands fan. New changes ive noted and welcomed - a dual class system for more experimenting with builds. More character customisation. The unpredictable usage of old fav characters from prev series. Things that were missing:I think a backdrop story relating to the main borderlands would have been helpful. I think a story where Tiny Tina discovers old DnD rulebooks and modifies it to her own rules because she is a lazy genius. She then kidnaps unwilling players to play her game. Thats where you the new player comes in, waking up strapped to a chair, answering basic questions as part of character customisation, as part of being interrogated by Tina to see if you are 'willing' to play her game and while she designs your character card/backstory. Rather than a tabletop and using imagination, she uses VR and tabletop. The game therefore switches back and forth between three 'worlds', VR (main game), tabletop (overworld), reality (cutscenes in the real world with dialog choices - these cutscenes can be short & initiated by the removal of the VR goggles to warn players, and then speaking to Tina and the other unwilling players in the reality. It can also sometimes be a small ingame window as per the older borderlands game). I think it would be cool where cutscenes showing what remains of previous players who refuse to voiceact for example or of Tina sometimes showing a mature side would really elevate the main story. In the end, the ultimate story of Tina really wanting to force finish this game as escapism for finding her parents and living happily ever after, but in the end settling for her friends instead and learning to form real relationships would be a more meaningful story but can also be as lighthearted/satirical as needed for a borderlands game. Sidequests will elude to various clues to tie in with the real world. It could have been a real gem of a story, with DLCs relating to backstories of the other characters in the real world. Also... claptrap didnt need to be the same old claptrap. A missed opportunity would have been to used him as the tutorial guide but in a different form, such as the hero he envisions himself as, as a throwback to earlier games. In fact, he could be the programmer for Tina's VR game, therefore funny glitches/malfunctions can happen in game. With a RPG focus, I think the inventory screen could be much better... its still the same sidebar even when within the inventory tab, there is so much wasted real estate on screen. Inability to switch spells on the fly like guns. If you are in a spell build, and your one equipped spell is ineffective against an enemy then its abit annoying. at least allowing players to equip 2 spells or quickswap would have been useful and easily implemented. Same for melee. Maybe could have made guns that double as melee weapons too.Certain guns have lost all advantage. I found myself just selling any snipers and most bazookas i had. They were pretty useless in dps and since crits seldom one hit an enemy... not even 2 hit... probably 10+ headshots to down one. Borderlands enemies are typically interesting & unique but this one felt uninteresting due to fantasy elements being very explored by other games. They could have gone really wild with the characters here since its a meld between postapocalypse, cyberpunk, steampunk and medieval with a satirical setting. Instead we see goblins, skeletons, imps and mushroom people... really? Eg. i really liked their play on magic missle and the bardbarian... Im not sure why they couldnt go a little more unique on their enemy designs... Eg. Tina loves bunnies, why not use that instead. Rather than help a town besieged by skeletons yawn... Maybe a town of unwilling playactors dressed in bunny costumes besieged by redneck zombie werewolves or something. Bad stuffI personally hate games that scatter hidden items that are crucial. Its ok if its just for fun to discover but items like the lucky dice which increases your loot luck makes it somewhat crucial to find. This game mechanic is there as a filler. It should be made 100pc optional. The game relies on gear discovery more than levelling up to progress as  a powerful character... so i think this is a huge oversight. As someone who works, I can only spend so much time playing a game. Thus to maximise efficiency, I found myself either scouring the edges of the map from the getgo, not being able to appreciate the handcrafted maps as it should, but instead looking out for the nooks and crannies. When NPCs start talking, Id wander off to stupid places like trying to climb roofs or jump ledges, where else in the past, Id pay more attention to the ingame scenes. The other option would be to check on the internet for the hidden locations and it becomes much more of a chore rather than a discovery. To all game designers please do not do this esp for AAA titles. Id say borderlands devolved abit when it became more reliant on such mechanics as a filler. There were other RPG elements they could have added instead such as dialogue choices, minigames, recruitable NPCs, skill checks, more fledging out of the melee combat. Instances in a grassfield akin to pokemon was annoying. I found myself running away whenever i could as they were so so meaningless.Overall, I think this installment has played it safe here and because of that it was uninteresting. However, it does deliver a solid borderlands experience. To a newcomer, I wouldnt recommend this game though as it would just seem like a mixmash of mechanics which fails to deliver on what seems like crucial aspects of combat like melee/spellcasting (which to the usual borderlands fan is totally acceptable)

_childDocuments_.review: Never before has my opinion of a game flipped so dramatically and so quickly. I started playing this game solo and was entirely expecting that it would be a fairly normal Borderlands romp, got treated to new and old concepts that were improved upon but what I felt was a fairly bland game for me to be playing solo, and was just drifting my way through sidequests thinking I could just get my multiclass by level up rather than quest progression.I went from being uninterested and thinking the game was going to be fun with friends but I wasn't gonna enjoy playing it solo. Then I start investigating on why I didn't get Multiclass at level 15, the level I thought it was gonna be at. Turns out, I had to complete the quest missions, and I was like a single mission away. I put my grinding on halt, take my Blightcaller to the end of Emotion on the Ocean and pick up Spore Warden. I fully respec my character because new skill tree and all that, and then.. it all clicks. I was enjoying myself with the elemental weapons, particularly frost, but it fell flat, it felt hollow. Part of it was because I was poorly specced and only had a 10 in Strength and Dex, meaning my Criticals were crap on a class that could abuse criticals to great effect.After the Respec, I started enjoying myself a lot more. I went from being frustrated to realizing the potential of the Sporewraith I had created. I actively went from being unimpressed and thinking that it wasn't going to be worth my time to finish it without my friends to running around and enjoy random encounters much more.The progressive leveling of the enemies makes the game constantly challenging, which at first I didn't quite enjoy because it also made certain bosses even more difficult, specifically the GTFO questline's end boss. Nothing like an on level boss that can block your screen with fire. However, now that I'm playing with Spore Warden, I have my companion who can revive me, and I've found weapons I quite enjoy? This game feels great. It has difficulty, but not to an extent where I feel frustrated. I feel pleased with my growing skills and encouraged to play more.My major complaints are basically as follows:Still have issues with the fact certain enemies (see the boss from before) can do an AOE attack that blinds you.I dislike that Blightcaller is not a standalone DLC character and I got it from the four DLC packs that are not worth the money from everyone else's point of view, I have yet to try them.Most major of all, the level cap, in my eyes being at 40 is a damn shame, simply because having a third Multiclass and up to level 60 would make some incredible builds and this game feels like having it at 40 is a waste of potential. I'd kill for the ability to be a Brr-Zerker/Spore Warden/Blight Caller, even if I couldn't afford two capstones, simply because there is so much combo potential for insane characters that I wanna experience but can't. If the DLCs were expansions and gave us more levels, I'd be satisfied in all counts aside from that damn boss blinding me when I go down.Overall, good game, buy it when on sale with your friends, avoid Chaotic Great Edition unless you feel like buying a bunch of poorly rated DLCs and a cool class.

_childDocuments_.review: Review is based off of an almost 100% solo playthrough and coop playthrough, first 3 Mirrors of Mystery completed and Chaos Chamber up to 30 as of writing this, but I feel like I've experienced everything the game has to offer, so I'll just list the pros and cons like Borderlands 3Pros:Spells are fun to use, pretty refreshing compared to how montonous BL3's grenades wereGame is more technically stable than BL3, less bugs, crashes and frame dropsMelee ravamps have some nice touches like having bonus effects when hitting enemiesEnvironments are nice looking, Fear-amid and the Necropolis were my favourite sectionsClass customisation is interesting, especially since the secondary class can be changedSidequests are unique in their design that rely off the RPG and fantasy settingCons:Gameplay has regressed in almost every single way when compared to BL3. Guns don't feel nearly as satisfying to use, melee has improved and downgraded since lunge is now unreliable and ground pound is still bad, UI is worseEnemy damage and balancing is absolutely bonkers, even without Chaos levels my health was constantly reaching healthgate threshold, it only gets worse on Chaos levels where death is almost guaranteed. Enemy density is also very miniscule resulting in being forced to wait for enemies to spawn just to fight encounters.Endgame is really boring, Chaos Chamber is not fun to grind and repeats issues I have with BL3 Mayhem Mode and BL2 OP Lvls, Myth Ranks only want me to invest in one tree but I have to invest in all fourPersonally I did not find the story very engaging and wasn't invested in, when the story finished I only had the, "thank goodness it's finally over" feelingEquipment loadouts is pretty boring as well and generally only functions as stat checks for your characterThe Mirrors of Mystery are way too overpriced for DLC, functioning only as a singular level that can be repeated three times with minimal changes, the lost souls currency is also not motivatingOverall traversal is neutered with minimal fast travel and Overworld doesn't change enough IMOCollectibles is incredibly irritating and forced, Lucky Dice are the worst to search for and are bugged if playing with coopPersonally this game is easily the worst entry in the Borderlands franchise, each game has an element that makes it superior against the other entries, however Wonderlands offers nothing for me that the other Borderlands games have already given and on top of that downgrades everything that I like about the series. It was a chore from start to finish. I understand that the game was made in lockdown and compromises have to be made, but that doesn't forgive the design decisions that went into this game. I cannot recommend this game to anyone, casual players or hardcore Borderlands fans.

_childDocuments_.review: According to Steam it's been almost exactly one year since I played Tina Tina's Wonderlands. In all that time I never even considered writing a review. You know why? Tina Tina's Wonderlands (TTW) is a looter shooter, like all of the Borderlands main series (a series that's now in its fifth iteration, and one that ran out of gas after the second). TTW, like most of its predecessors, features numerous fun guns; terrible, bland, skill-less, samey combat; "humorous" characters; and a story without meaning or impact. It is absolutely not worth your time.There is nothing to say about the gameplay. It is identical to all other Borderlands games. You kill mobs that spawn in areas, move on to new areas, and repeat forever. Occasionally you kill a boss. That boss might even have a weakspot you need to aim for, but you don't have to if you don't want to. There is nothing mechanically challenging or interesting in the moment-to-moment gameplay, although it  hilarious to note that sniper rifles have fallen into complete uselessness in Borderlands because actually aiming well and hitting a weakspot on an enemy is not just unnecessary but actively worthless.There is a new endgame gameplay mode that's just a Slay the Spire ripoff featuring an endless grind. I'm glad I played TTW after several patches, because it used to be even worse, apparently. You might find this mode fun if you aren't tired of games throwing random enemies into a room and then letting you pick a track with random boons and curses after you've cleared said room, but I've played that style of mechanic a dozen times now and I'm over it.Gearing, despite the plethora of interesting guns and an RPG-style multiclassing system, is the most simple and boring it's ever been in Borderlands. Rather than finding interesting synergies between guns and gear, like in previous games, TTW is mostly about just having the same enchantment on all of your weapons, which is only difficult becasue you need to grind the Slay the Spire mode to get the currency to reroll enchantments.Story is where TTW gets truly baffling. The conceit is that the player is sitting down to play a tabletop RPG session with Tina, an insane teenager. This should lead to quirky-fun storytelling, right? Wrong, it's mostly boring and nonsensical. The Big Bad literally makes no sense: he is Tina's former character who - as she's now Dungeon Master - she has turned into the antagonst of the tabletop game you, the player, is playing. But  the context of her game, the Big Bad has become self-aware that he's in a game and is talking to the player. Somehow. No one else at the table hears him, and Tina isn't directing him. The literal character in the tabletop game is talking to you. This isn't a 4th wall break or anything; it's just idiotic.But wait! This is a comedy game, right? Borderlands is famously irreverent. I'm sure there are plenty of great jokes about tabletop games and the way they're played and the people who play them that make up for all of this, aren't there? No, there are not. There is surprisingly little humor about TTRPGs at all, actually. Most of the jokes come in the form of banter between the people sitting at the table. I can only recall one quest, one single time, that was actually about the way players act when playing TTRPGs. And you know what? That quest was funny. That's why it's literally the only quest I can remember now, one year later.Also, special mention for a collection quest that runs through the entire game filling you in on the tragic backstory of an NPC that you .Well, I guess I lied at the start of this review. There was something to say, and it was the same thing I've said before: all told, this Borderlands game isn't worth your time. A bad story, uninteresting characters, boring combat, and braindead itemization make Tina Tina's Wonderlands just another Borderlands game for the garbage pile.P.S.: The DLC was once again horrible as well. Worst yet, actually. Four one-stage levels that you need to beat  to unlock the rewards from them you'd actually want. Just terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very sweet game, but buyer beware: there are some very key and glaring flaws in this game. Endgame feels awful and Don't bother with the PLC.Main Story: 7.5/10 - Worth it if you like Borderlands Characters and Style.Endgame: 3/10 - Boring, frustrating and repetitive.PLC: 1/10 - Just... dont.Story and Side Quests: 7/10Solid and engaging story, best enjoyed if you're a fan of TTRPG's and know the Borderlands universe & Characters, but not a necessity by any means.Gun play: 7/10Balance is very finely tuned and feels great, The weapons are amazing to use as always in borderlands games, new Melee weapons, Spells and gun types are fantastic additions.Overall aesthetic: 8/10The wonderlands are fantastic to explore with Beautiful visuals and areas ranging from Mountaintops, Forests, deserts, ruins and more*BUT*Areas, once played through, tend to get repetitive quickly, especially the endgameGameplay: 5/10The player classes feel great to play, and their skills really fit their themes, All have great features and all are fun to play.Good amount of enemy variety, each with their own characteristics.Some Quality of Life Additions: Melee Autoswing, Audio prompts for cooldowns*BUT*Lack of Endgame content, and what endgame there is, is deeply flawed. Mostly Spoilerless summary in 3 points:Repetitive Everything. Zero Variety. Game collectibles can become Monotonous to collect, 100%'ing the main game is not difficult for the most part, but it is tedious due to the sheer amount of collectibles in the world. Thankfully, Gearbox has taken steps to fix this issue, but I personally feel it needs further addressing.The Loot and Farming: 3/10While there are many great additions to the Wonderlands in regard to equipment, weapons and more. However, TT Wonderlands legendary weapons can feel lackluster, with some being outclassed by Purple and even some Blue items."Class mod"/Armor variety between the Character classes are lumped together, meaning you're dealing with RNG on Skill increases for specific skills you want on top of Secondary stats ON TOP OF it dropping for your specific class, meaning there's a lot of garbage farming.Many named enemies from quests and elsewhere are one-and-done fights that never re-spawn, leading to a Very empty feeling world after a first playthrough. There's little to no point in returning to previously completed areas except cleaning up side-quests or collectibles.----PLC ratings - Overpriced and less content than the small Headhunter pack DLC's from Borderlands 2, each require multiple Playthroughs to access the Legendary gear associated with them.PLC 1: 1/10Nothing of value beyond some specific legendaries that get added that are Borked with Cryo builds.Gameplay includes a MANDATORY 5 minute wait in an area with a insignificant trickle of enemies that killing is akin to wafting flies away from your face, just for them to loop round and pester you again half a minute later. The last boss is easy to farm for the aforementioned loot, thankfully.PLC 2: 1/10A small step up from DLC 1 going to bottom of the barrel from being buried 6 feet under the barrel, but still the same, garbage content but some good gear. Areas look interesting and the Boss is interesting but annoying to fight in a bad way.PLC 3: 3/10Actual Content!! (on par with a headhunter pack) Follows the same formula from previous PLC's but with actual effort to make it engaging and interesting. The boss fight is a challenge and interesting to fight for the first few times, *BUT*Fighting the boss becomes tedious when progressing in the Endgame, A tragic victim of TT Wonderlands awful endgame balancing with enemy damage and cheesing the healthgating mechanic is mandatory for victory.*BUT THAT'S NOT ALL*Completing fights VS PLC bosses adds them into the random boss rotation that act as a finale for the Endgame loop. PLC 1 and 2's bosses are manageable to frustrating. Running into PLC 3's boss means you might as well quit and start fresh, as it takes so long to fight and is incredibly punishing for the vast majority of viable builds.As good as PLC 3 is versus the others, which isn't that much, I can't recommend it as it makes an already bad endgame EVEN WORSE by adding a permanent random chance to ruin your progress for just playing the content.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't even know why this is sold as a full price AAA Borderlands game. This could ve just been a a smaller spin off game like Far Cry Blood Dragon. Launchers are super weak and i still dont know how they haven't buffed them at all in the entire games lifespan, not that it matters since there are no big hordes of enemies really. _childDocuments_.review: Put 10 hours into it and I can say that... I wish this was a DLC for Borderlands 2. On it's own, it stands fine, but I wouldn't buy it for 60+ bucks. It's Borderlands 2 with 3 and Presequel's mechanics, which I don't have a problem with. I've had a lot of fun with it, and it's likely because of the superb writing and art direction, I also appreciate the pronouns inclusion, be it limited. That being said, the Dragon Lord is such a good villain bc gearbox followed the Handsome Jack formula. He just never shuts up and his voice actor is hilarious and has great range (It's Bojack Horseman) so of course he feels thought out and has clear motivations, just like Handsome Jack did. The bosses have all been fun, and I mean that they are not only interesting mechanics wise, but also engaging. They all feel like they have a puzzle you have to solve while beating them to succeed, and even on normal I can say that the game is definitely challenging. The guns are cooler than ever and the gunplay is more engaging - I actually had to choose when I wanted to take cover or run, I built up melee not as a last resort but as the choice I wanted to use most of the time in close combat, and then the weapons, abilities, and classes compliment each other so you really feel like you're pulling off awesome DND combos on the spot. The characters aren't necessarily likable in this one, but they are entertaining and the themes of the main story and side quests are particularly progressive, though they do miss the mark often (Tiny Tina still talks with a little bit of blaccent, but one of the side quests told by her is all about communist revolution. IDK things like that show a disconnect between the game's goals and execution). Overall, no DLC, 10 hours in, I can say I'd buy this on sale for $30-$35 bucks, but not 60, and DO NOT BUY THE DLC THEY ARE AWFUL, YOU GET 6 CLASSES STARTING OFF AND THE DEVS ARENT INCREASING THE LEVEL CAPS, YOU DONT NEED THE DLC.Seen it done before, better, ab 6 years ago, and it feels much more like an extension to Borderlands 2's Tiny Tina DLC, but it is fun, the characters grow on you, and I'm loving how these new games look and feel to play. Would've been a 6 but the accessibility options and pronouns make it a 7 for me. Only the queer folks know how rare they are even now. I feel about this how I felt about Borderlands 3, it's fun, it's new, and it's engaging, but after I'm done with it, I'm done with it. 7/10.Edit: After 40 hours and 40+ levels, I can say that this is one of my favorite entries to the series. I thought the story would've been more meta, but it was just a feel good, simple, lighthearted adventure about the trials and tribulations of early Game Mastering, which is just up my alley. The guns and weapons keep getting cooler, and Chaos Mode makes it for me because the options to customize your RNG like a roguelike is something this series has never done before, and it works so incredibly well. The enemies get cooler in Chaos Mode, the bosses were all incredible, the characters are interesting and understandable, the set pieces and level designs were all outstanding, GIVE IT A PLAY!Yeah the DLC ♥♥♥♥ sucks, but it is COMPLETELY optional stuff, they even gave the DLC its own area way apart from the rest of the game, to the point that it's never even mentioned, you have to find the DLC to play it (DONT).40 hrs in, Im gonna keep playing. It's a lot more engaged than I thought. The Live Service model of all games has eaten at it a bit and saved the best until after the final boss, but hey, it's still a Borderlands title and works almost just as well.FInal Thoughts: BL1 was Skyrim with guns, hard as nails, and couldnt keep my attention, but the characters and story kept me playing. BL2 was a thrill ride where every story mattered and where I wanted to find every secret and play every side mission, and every reward contributed to the main quest. BLtPS was a fun ride across the main games' lore, a bit unbalanced and the setting was rather dreary and it took itself a bit seriously at times, but I had fun with it. BLtPS was the first attempt at a live service model, so you can imagine how that went. TFtBL was interesting and weird, and I liked that. BL3 was some of the best gameplay the series had at the time and I continue to come back to it despite its rushed and awful story direction. TTWL is a culmination of all of these games and the shadows that loom over them. Gearbox's heart and soul went into this one, they listened to the fans, and it seems like the new direction this world is going is about taking the time to give the players the most options possible while exploring a well thought out story, no matter what happened in previous games - and while this game still lives in the shadow of 2 and the presequel, it stands on its own regardless and I've thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. At the end of the game the devs put a thank you note to the players that details how and why TTWL is the way it is and what direction they are taking moving forward, and I'd just like to thank the devs for all their continued hard work and dedication to one of my favorite series of all time, and for taking the time to make their games the best they can. In conclusion, the real villain is corporate greed, crunch culture, and live service models. I hope one day we see more games like Tiny Tina's Wonderlands without the terrible DLC and maybe with the Chaos Mode before the end of the game, but until then, this is the best we got. 8.5/10. Needs more communism.

_childDocuments_.review: I have some complaints, but it's generally really good and a solid entry to the series.TTW takes a different approach to the theme of the Borderlands franchise, being set in a world of fantasy and magic controlled by the bunkermaster; Tiny Tina. This looter-shooter can be very satisfying but also feel a little off in a few ways: 1) Loot drops feel really lame, and there is a major reason for this. Your chance of getting rare loot has a lot to do with how many lucky dice you have found, and how far you are through the game. This can leave new players feeling like the loot pool isn't rewarding. But after getting into the mechanic it does play into my completionist mentality and does finally manage to win me over in the end.2) The soundtrack is designed with the theme in mind; it feels a little airy and mystical while previous entries felt energetic, mysterious and exciting. I also feel the volume in this game is really low and I cant hear dialogue clearly even at full volume. 3) There aren't really any main characters in this one, the idea is that you make a custom character to play with. And while this can open up some creativity it can feel devoid of the personality from previous entries.4) Being a mock DND session, there is a lot of story changes happening all around you as Tina dictates the action, sometimes it's really fun and exciting, while other times it feels like a cop-out to having the writers plan out the story better.5) Random encounters on the overworld map are a nod to more classic games but they make the smooth gameplay of the Borderlands series feel clunky. I am learning to be thankful for the traditional open world fighting the game still has to offer. The levels are fun, imaginative and well designed. The spells are interesting and unique, albeit a little weak. The classes are all really fun to play around with and feel powerful. The story telling is intentionally a little awkward but still plenty funny and interesting.

They are also a part of every Overworld quest, so they quickly become tedious.Paladin Mike is just like Lorelei from BL3 - useless and annoying, but this time you see him way more often.Loot - utter s**te. They aren't even a challenge like raid bosses from Borderlands 2/TPS, just a swarm of enemies with a couple of tanks.If you think "well, there sure are DLCs that add more to the story" - don't bother, they just add a couple of cosmetics and new... you guessed it. _childDocuments_.review: If you don't take this game seriously, its amazing, genuinely. Im a huge fan of the borderlands series, I put countless hours into every single game entry on my PS4 back when the handsome collection came out. Honestly this might be my favourite game since BL2. Let me explain. First I'll start with the setting, characters, story, etc. At first I wasn't really buying the whole D&D vibe of the game, but as I kept playing I found myself getting more and more sucked into the world; the RPG mechanics are surprisingly deep, and the developers are really in their element here with the "D&D parody" vibe of the game. To me the biggest draw of Borderlands was always how silly and fun it was, the characters that lost me with the bland story of Borderlands 3 have slowly showed me why I love this series to begin with over the course of the game. Seriously, I haven't laughed like this at a Borderlands game in forever. Borderlands 3 didn't make me crack a single smile (which was honestly my biggest complaint about BL3, it really lost the funny aspect for me). Also I gotta say the graphics are GORGEOUS. I haven't seen a Borderlands game look this good EVER. The environments are enchanting and beautiful, and the design of the enemies is believable yet creative (Again, another complaint about BL3, the enemies in that game were bland as hell). Also I gotta say, the sidequests in this game are the best. They are funny, creative, and challenging. Yet another big draw for me when it comes to Borderlands was the variety of sidequests that unlike other games; felt as if they actually impacted the world and absorbed you into the game more rather than just being random BS you have to do to get more experience or gold or whatever. You definitely will not get bored running around the world doing quests for the people of the Wonderlands and will run into a lot of things  that make you think "Did that really just happen?" while you're laughing your ass off.Now the gameplay. Like I said, the RPG mechanics in this game are pretty in depth, at the cost of less varieties in skill trees, you get the multiclass system and "hero points" (basically like badass rank but more inspired by D&D). The multiclass system adds a ton of variety to the game, I sat for 2 hours trying to decide what to make my second class lmao and I instantly knew I was gonna be coming right back for another playthrough to try more combinations. The hero points really help sell the whole "character sheet" idea to the progression system very well. Despite what many other people think, the biggest weakness this game has for me personally is the spell system. While yes, the spells are interesting in their own right and are very flashy and cool; a good amount of the spells feel very clunky to use and sometimes come with bugs and glitches. The gunplay is like any other Borderlands game really, you know what you're signing up for, Gearbox never really misses when it comes to this, you get some new stuff like crossbows which is cool but its pretty typical. The coolest addition is the new melee weapons; they are very flashy, have tons of cool abilities and stats and definitely add another layer of complexity to the game. I've always wanted to see something like this in the series and I hope it comes back in a future entry. Overall,  Id definitely recommend to anyone if its on sale, but thats just most games nowadays really. Pick this game up if you are willing to just turn your brain off and forget any expectations you have for a Borderlands game. If you've never played Borderlands before; great. Even better. This is a solid introduction to the series (though you will miss lots of funny references)

I just wanna play D&D borderlands dude, not be forced to sit through a poorly written Gearbox PSA that they support the gay movement now. They don't even try to fit it into the plot, they just found some way to make every single NPC interaction a sexuality check. Its all so exaggerated that it almost feels like its all just a bit that's making fun of how tolerant-pilled everything is now. Kinda sad that such an anticipated game just turned out to be yet another company trying to make a political statement to make money off of a progressive movement. As for gameplay, the combat is halfway decent, but disappointingly repetitive. There's shockingly little content, the campaign is short as hell, and the three separate DLC's they dropped are just repeatable boss-raid missions that have zero story or exploration. You can finish each DLC mission in 30 minutes or less, and all they do is serve as a pay-to-win raid you complete to gain a bunch of otherwise unobtainable in-game currency to roll for legendaries on the in-game gacha wheel. Honestly I am a diehard borderlands fan and this game feels like it was some unholy Activision and Ubisoft hellspawn thats sole purpose is to pander for your wallet and not even having the decency to give you a reach-around while they pipe you out.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an okay game and the reason I say that is because that they do a lot of things great and wrong. As the game goes it took me over a year to drag myself back to play it. I am glad I did go back to it but it was a hard time trying to pull myself to play something that wasn't grasping me to. Overall I enjoyed my time playing this game and going as far to 100 percent it.The game play of Wonderlands is very similar to any of the games in the Borderlands franchise but with some minor differences. There are no grenades but spells and the addition of the melee weapons which was a cool addition and a change of play style and skills that you play around. All the sliding and mantling from Borderlands 3 still feels great in the engine that the game is made on. Still the same old format of main quest / side quest grind with collectables in between and loading screens galore but what do you expect from a Gearbox game. Gearbox fixed the loot system making legendries rare again and adding the loot luck system which gives the game a better flow of power. Spells give the game a different approach to the usual utility of a grenade with a wider aspect of buffs, damage types and play styles.   I am still not a fan of the enchantments which are just a re-skin of the anointments from Borderlands 3. Speaking of similar features the Chaos Level is a more tedious version of the mayhem levels where you have to spend hours upon hours to reach level 100. Guardian rank has been replaced with myth rank which works similar but has minor differences and all it serves as is an end game content dump for those who want to keep playing after they have done everything.Character skills and classes are very diverse and the ability to multiclass is a very good feature and in theme for the Dungeons and Dragons. This does give the game a creative class composition where you can pick and choose what you want. The class skills in the game or for the class that I played, the Stabbomancer, felt like that there wasn't much going. The class felt slightly boring to play and if it wasn't for the fact that you could multiclass then I would have just deleted the character and started again. Attribute points where a new addition to the character's statistics these are some additional stats to boost your characters ability and creates architypes that change the way that you think about playing your character in the first place.Opposed to the old map and fast travel the player has a map and can fast travel from there or they could wander around the map and travel to different places that way.  In the overworld there are different challenges to do and collectables to get that can make you stronger such as the shrines, which offer a variety of buffs to the player. Camps and encounters are a new and unique way to utilise combat in the game and provides a different experience to bite sized content.The Aesthetics of Wonderlands is pretty much the same as Borderlands 3 where it's this cartoon like drawing with thick comic book outlines. Some differences are that there is not as much neon in this game due to the environment setting, but the colour pallet is a lot brighter to give the game the fairy tale feel to it.The Animations are smooth, with the different types of creatures that are in the game, they all have their own physics and ragdoll pretty responsibly. The new melee weapons add a new aspect of animation for this game especially for the continuous swinging in a fluid motion. With the setting being medieval fantasy there is a lot of magic that has some really nice animations with lots of different colours and particles which makes casting spells really satisfying. The environment of Wonderlands is good and bad in all places sometimes it feels like the environment is bare and could use some little touches but at other points it seems to be flourishing with interactable and props that really immerse the play in this medieval world. The difference zone that you go to have their own themes and they are done really well with keeping the atmosphere correct, where you have a dark evil forest there is mushrooms that look deadly and the enemies that are there are also fitting too. I am so sorry Tina but your story sucks... I feel that the antagonist of the game really sucks and it doesn't want me to go an progress through the game to defeat him. I think that the 4th wall breaking villain was the incorrect move. It's dungeons and dragons for crying out loud there are plenty of examples where you can create a more interesting story line and give more plot hooks to keep the player interesting. As a DM in real life, I couldn't play this game for the story anymore and looked toward the progression and game mechanics which weren't half bad.Although the main story was terrible some of the side quests where good and made me chuckle at times but I am not paying the triple A price tag for garbage.Progression in Wonderlands is okay, I prefer the lower level cap and the changes to how the myth rank works. There was something missing which was a new game plus or a way to reset quests for that little bit or replay ability. I guess the incentive it to create a different character to try out their skills but that shouldn't stop me from playing the game more. Overall I think that this game in the franchise was an experiment at best to see what works and what doesn't as there was a lot that change, some better some worse,  but I found the game fun. I think that it is worth playing only if you haven't got anything else better to play or crave a casual FPS. I do not think that it is worth the price tag that it wears and you can pick it up on sale for pretty cheap or if you don't really care about the developers you can get a key on different sites for even cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:* Funny writing.* Beyond-imaginative world.* By-the-book exploration.* Beautiful graphics and good sounds.Cons:* The whole frikking gunplay. I mean, what's even going on here. Normal difficulty: A 5th-level, absolutely lowly mob takes 2 headshots from a unique 5th-level sniper rifle with flat damage bigger than anything else. A 12th-level melee fighter with the biggest, rarest, two-handed weapon and all skill points invested in a melee tree still has to smash three times into a common mob to kill it. Submachine guns have generally 3-5x less flat damage than a pistol (!!). Okay, I get it. Supposedly, that should be balanced by the rate of fire. What a joke. What good is the rate of fire if I have to empty half a clip into one single mob.  Don't get me even started on tougher enemies. Weapons in general are either powerful but shoot in ways that are weird and cumbersome (whereas enemies move to and fro as if on cocaine) or are shooting straight but are "rightfully" much weaker. You might say this gets better later on, when you supplement the weapons with passives and abilities. No, it does not. Once in 5 hours you get a weapon that, by some miracle, operates on sane levels at least two more hours, before it becomes under-par, or an inventory mod that could technically make one more skill work wonders if only you had those other two mods that would complement it, and you would search for them another 5 hours, and once you get those, the mods are already outperformed, and... AAAAARRGGGH!This was most of my experience with Tiny Tina's. I am no stranger to FPSs; I've always done my successful builds in many ARPGs or FPS/RPG hybrids to satisfactory levels. I've played and mostly loved everything Borderlands with some exceptions of some weird choices in BIII. This... this is just no.I finished the game because of the scenery, humor, and imagination. But gameplay-wise it was a frikking chore to begin with and ended the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I was boycotting this wonderful looking game for 2 reasons. Epic exclusivity and release of DLC trailers a week before the release of the game. Wanting a game on a platform that actually works and isn't based on bad faith concepts like "not wanting monopolies" while they try to monopolize. And wanting a full game a company is charging $60, even tho the budget is smaller than other AAA titles... Like y'all got epic money and still couldn't give us a full game for $60?After finally getting this for my boyfriend and I, we found it to be the worst borderlands out of the bunch, including the pre-sequel. Short campaign they try to make longer by increasing the level of of each subsequent mission by 4-5, making you want to level from the (mostly) poorly designed side quest, just to experience the story. The story missions feel like side quests, and the side quests feel like content that shoulda been scrapped. A large chunk of the game is just horde mode they're calling "random encounters". If you walk near tall grass you might spawn an enemy who will take you to 2 waves of horde mode if you don't melee them. Most of the side quest force you to do a horde too. I found myself rushing the story missions hoping the next mission/area would be something I liked... That never came XD Final bosses wasn't even fun. Just a big chore with too many health bars and phases.Two things I loved about the game was spells now replace grenades which you can cast while shooting. And the character creator replacing the vault hunters you normally would select. This allows you to chose a class (a single skill tree). An hour or 2 of gameplay will net you a second skill tree you can select from the remaining classes. This system was great until you realize max level is 40 and you only get 2 skill trees. Every vault hunter got at least 3. Even borderlands 1 started with a level cap of 50 and the pre-sequal was 60.How does end game look? It's literally just horde mode or side quest you missed... The ability to redo the story missions or even just fight older bosses is removed. Oh, and there's 3 DLC bosses you can pay 10 bucks each to fight. Making this a $90 unfinished short game. I'm gonna remember this next time gearbox releases something. Like how did you make a game worst than 3? This game is in no way worth $59.99. Maybe $30 at most. It's crazy all the positive reviews I've seen before this game came to steam... And even on steam itself.

_childDocuments_.review: My friends and I had high hopes for this game starting out. It had a fun (though quite standard) fantasy atmosphere with a heaping serving of Borderlands style combat, which is really quite nice throughout the whole game. Plenty of interesting loadouts to be had here, though with a distinct D&D themed twist compared to the usual Borderlands formula: spells replace grenades, wards replace shields, and so on. Melee weapons are also much more prominent in Wonderlands. At first they seemed like a nice addition the Borderlands style of play, but they ended up being a bit redundant for me personally (why use sword when have shotgun?)Unfortunately the bland side quests, average dialogue, and the utterly repetitive and uninspired "encounters" that the game likes to throw at you slowly whittled away the fun. There were a few good moments for sure, but in the end it all just continued to wear us down to the point where we just wanted to get the silly main quest over with and be done with it (and even that was a complete let down).I would also recommend avoiding this game if you aren't at least a somewhat avid fan of D&D. Most of the jokes and character banter depend on scenarios and tropes that frequent the D&D meta (honestly the whole story could be seen as one giant commentary on the peculiar relationship that builds between players and the dungeon master.) Seriously, if you don't have experience playing D&D at a table with friends, all of that stuff will be lost on you. You will forfeit the narrative's one saving grace—the thing that was actually able to give me a chuckle sometimes—and you will have nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this game on sale for around $28 for the complete edition.I've been playing the Land's titles for quite some time now, and this is truly disappointing. The writing is absolute dog water, completely forgettable. It feels like it was ripped from some thirteen year old's Wattpad/Fan-Fiction. That checks out knowing stinky baby inc had their grubby fingers all up in this game (as they did in Borderlands 3).The Over-world seemed interesting at first, but quickly realised that the dungeons in each area are the same. And even when going to the different areas of the over-world the dungeons all feel similar to each other.The endgame is a joke and there is no reason to play through it. 100 levels in the same stale dungeons that you have already experienced through out the main game just isn't it. Sure there are stronger varieties of the same guns you are using if you slog through that mind numbing grind, but what are you going to use them on? The same content you've been doing for the past 25 hours? There is no TVHM or UVHM to re-run the story with your newly acquired gear. It is just pointless.The 4 "PLC" as they seem to want to call it are a joke. Each of the PLC's take about 15-20 minutes to complete and feel hollow and soulless. Id rather listen to Grandma Tourge tell me stories of her "good ol' days" than play this phoned in content. And Grandma Tourge's content in Borderlands 2 was the phoned in content of all phoned in content. The class system seems interesting but the fact that you can change out your second class later on in the story further negates an reason to play the game again.The highlight of the game was finishing it, knowing that I never need to come back to it again.This isn't another 'Lands' title, but a blatant cash grab riding its predecessors coat tails. Avoid it at all costs, and take your hard earned currency to game developers that care about the games they are making and the community that surrounds them. 2K/Gearbox is not one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a really, really long time since I played a Borderlands game, so honestly I don't remember what is special to this game, and what's usual for those, so please keep that in mind.I overall, really loved this game. It was by no means flawless, but the characters were fun, the gameplay entertaining, and it overall kept me engaged the whole time, which can be hard for me. I've always loved the art style for Borderlands, and Tiny Tina definitely kept it up nicely with fun character designs and even more fun characters themselves.The story was pretty basic, but I didn't find it boring to be honest. It was full of tropes, but it seemed intentional and fun, where I usually find them annoying.The Voice Acting really stepped the game up, in my opinion. It was really well done, and suited each character really well. While the dialogue itself may not have made me laugh at times, the way it was done by the VAs did. Especially Valentine and Frette.My biggest issues with the game absolutely come from the overworld. Overworld combat is… lame. It takes forever for the enemies to spawn some times in the encounters, so I'd just be running around waiting for them to come. And the encounter maps were kind of large, meaning the 1 or 2 enemies that spawn could be on the other end of the map as me and considering you need to kill a certain amount to END the encounter, it was just. Annoying. Plus, overworld movement speed is slowed down and just. A pain. You don't spend too much time in the overworld though, and most encounters are just for side quests, not main story, so not too bad.To 100% the game, there's definitely a lot of grinding. I had fun doing the story and all the side quests, but then I felt done. My copy came with all the DLC, but based on reviews, I felt no need to play it, as they don't seem like they really add much aside from an achievement checked off and maybe a small, tiny story.I really did have a great time with this game, and it's made me want to go back and finally play more Borderlands 2 for the first time in 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a 3 out of 10.  The PROS: Has a borderlands feel. CONS: 1)  kind of boring, the campaign is lame and dull.  2) The new characters are also cringey, lots of attempts at humor but it's flat af.  3) Borderlands at least had different segments of worlds you could fast travel to for a completely different setting, but in this spin off you only get one, so you get the sentiment of dull repetition real fast here.  4) The game also got rid of key characters in the BL series, I think that was a huge mistake because those characters made the game, but at least they kept Tina [obviously], Mr. Torgue and Claptrap.  Was hopeful when you finally reach the town saloon and the bar keep makes their entrance!....except it wasn't Moxxi, it's now Izzy - they had already made Moxxi the barkeep in the original bunkers and badasses so whose genius idea was it to replace her? Bad idea....5) The arch-enemy was poorly integrated, nothing but routine interjections in your comms and desperate attempts at being funny but are not.  6) Why in the bloody hell would you use wanda sykes as one of the 3 main narrators? She was HORRIBLE for this game and if you play it you'll understand exactly what that means, bad very bad choice. 7) I HAVE ALL BORDERLANDS GAMES and DLC, all of it, because it's fantastic and I couldn't stop playing it!....but this one, this was really really easy to stop playing anytime and a lot of times I would.  Ya know, before you settle in for a few hours of Borderlands and it's a blast and addicting -- this one I can only play about 30 minutes before it's just too boring to justify spending more time so I would shut it off.   Also the game gets into some weird stuff, like romantic attraction between npc's and frog looking trolls with innuendo and then going back to the npc's house....also what's with the woke stuff?  They took the Australian girl's voice from BL3, made it the voice of the male Mike Paladin in this one so he sounds like a chick....and then made him look like a girl with a moustahce...please get out of woke game we don't want that infection penetrating something we're about to stop paying for, it's bad enough you make what is pretty much a DLC, charge $60 for it - have it be completely boring and then make sure it's politically driven, complete with actually selecting pronouns as in your character creation....my god, please stop...there's more but I'll stop there.  Regret shelling out for this game, was waitinggggg for it to come to steam for awhile but wish I could get a refund instead. THIS IS THE FIRST EVER BORDERLANDS GAME THAT HAS BEEN A COMPLETE DISAPPOINTMENT....never thought I'd actually be saying that considering they had put out banger after banger every time until now.  This is a DLC game, not a justified $60 stand alone as it pretends to be.  If you want a true price point you can live with, spend no more than $20 at the most on it.  Even then I think that's a little high for what you're getting.  Really wanted to like this game :(  .....
