_childDocuments_.review: No game embodies tedium moreso than this, I cant honestly recommend it to anyone. I really enjoyed myself for the first chapter but everything after that was just dreck, filled with issues as follows-Bog area in chapter 2 can be difficult to navigate with the puddles looking like you can walk between or around-Key items should get their own inventory-Rat holes should show up on the map after you've interacted with them and not blown them up-Stamina should regenerate slightly between screen transitions. The fast travel truck should reset stamina to full, makes no sense you get out the other side still winded. Same with talking to characters, item box ect.-Honestly the slowdown on empty stam is more annoying than interesting, esp with so much back tracking and open areas-Bombed city areas are just annoying to navigate with too many blocked passages-The flashback scenes are just a bit boring-For some reason cant use flashlight batteries off the floor to reload flashlight, have to pick them up, unlike bandages or alcohol?-Blockages on the map show up in the first few chapters, but dont bother in a last few. Dont know why.-Enemies can sometimes hit you even if you're "above" them or weirdly around corners-Having to make sure the torch is equipped to put a battery in is pointless, torch could also do with being up-gradable.-Personal preference but locks ect, with randomized codes to prevent googling is just more tedium, people are just going to look up how to get the solution.The last chapter had so much faffing around I said "not worth it" and closed the game. Waste of 7 or 8 hours. A great idea, horribly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: A premise is in order here: I love history, I have a deep fascination with World War 1, and am kind of obsessed with the Battle of Verdun specifically. I've read a lot about it and went on a trip to France in order to visit the forts and battlefields, which was a profoundly meaningful experience. Some additional context: within WW1, one of the bloodiest and most brutal conflicts in history, Verdun has the infamy of being the battle with "most dead soldiers per square kilometer". Ever. It was an operation engineered from the very beginning to "bleed France white" and that is why it is sometimes referred to as a "meat grinder" that swallowed more than 300.000 sons of Europe. Total casualties amount to more than 600.000, with many young soldiers going completely insane after the trauma they experienced.Conscript is a top-down survival horror game by lone Australian developer Jordan Mochi. A Kickstarter project more than seven years in the making, I backed it from day one because it deals entirely with the Battle of Verdun. And what a special game it turned out to be. The premise is simple: André, a French soldier, must find his brother Pierre, missing in action during the Battle, by navigating through trenches, forts, ruined towns and the devastated countryside. The game's tone is the first element that could alienate players: survival horror is never the happiest genre of all, but Conscript has almost zero elements of levity. It understands its subject matter perfectly: it is about trench warfare, abysmal hygienic conditions and humanity's madness on full display. The cruellest conflict in history. Playing Conscript is facing massacres, mud, rats, blood, viscera, explosions and rot. It's a draining experience, with little personal triumphs that often ring hollow, and climaxes that feel nullifying instead of exciting. Soldiers in Verdun, French and German alike, cared little about winning the battle after witnessing the trenches and the front lines: most just wanted to get home. Conscript nails it, and it is so, so special for that. It nails the humanity of the conflict: the brief conversations you have with fellow soldiers, the mundane act of giving a smoke to a companion or finding a lost photograph for a prisoner of war feel so much more impactful when everything around you is screaming for complete annihilation of the very concept of humanity. There are no clear-cut good guys and bad guys, either: many times, you'll kill a German soldier just for him to drop a photo of a girl, or a baby. One time, I shot an armed enemy that was looking at an agonizing soldier on the ground. He was carrying the photograph of two young men. I had just killed two brothers just as I, André, was looking for mine. Their only fault was to be on the other side, as was decided by power-hungry generals who treated war as a personal stage and a ticket to further prestige and power. The soldiers, mere lambs to the slaughter.The gameplay skeleton is the early survival horror template set by Resident Evil, with inventory management, item boxes, resource conservation and puzzle solving. There are RE4-like elements, like a merchant to trade and upgrade weapons with, and he is pretty much the only solace from the constant grimness. Level design is complex and mostly really tight, with numerous shortcuts and nooks and crannies to explore. Many puzzles involve finding the right items, but there are also numerous combination locks which can be quite tricky and very satisfying to figure out. There are a good number of enemy types, all soldiers with different gear and roles, such as raiders armed with shovels, elite riflemen with deadly bayonets and armored, axe-wielding knights. You can kill or try to evade enemies with your speed and your clumsy dodge, each approach having its own benefits. But there is also the threat of rats to consider: they feed on fresh corpses and carry deadly diseases, so you'll have to evade them, dispose of them or burning the bodies of slain foes, saving you from potential headaches but costing some inventory space to do that. Combat is simple, and not entirely reliable. You are slow and must be very deliberate in aiming, shooting and reloading. Sometimes hitboxes are a bit janky, but the general feeling is brutal and impactful and I think it worked fantastic for the game, even if it made me feel horribly. The game is also quite long for the genre's standards, and never loses steam, which is a commendable feat.Artistically, Conscript is oppressing, with muted, dark colors capturing the atmosphere of utter horror and hopelessness. Some effects, like the explosions, look exceptional and intimidating. It feels authentic and effective. The audio is incredible, with foreboding, suffocating ambience that would rival Silent Hill, and some utterly beautiful, somber tracks that play in safe rooms and during pivotal moments to crushing emotional effect. I loved the SFX and what little voice acting there is.Conscript is a very special game that feels made for me specifically, and I can't thank Jordan Mochi enough for it. It won't be for everyone, but I think it must be experienced by those willing to confront our kind's darkest hour yet.

(it's not great war themed tho but has some german undertones)

_childDocuments_.review: The World War I trench warfare setting is the absolute perfect location for a survival horror/thriller game. Overrun by enemies, dealing with limited supplies, and feeling a general sense of bleakness was trench warfare in a nutshell. I took a chance on a day 1 purchase with Conscript because I want to reward developers who strive to make something unique, and I'm grateful that I did. I'm enjoying everything about the game. The sound design is haunting, the pixel art aesthetic leaves just enough to the imagination, and the combat, while a little rough around the edges, is completely serviceable. Put it all together, and you have a deeply immersive experience.

Some stuttering here and there)- Art style: Excellent (Pixeled art, World War I ambiance...I loved it) - Gameplay: Very Good (Old school survival. Glad to see difficulty options available, which will let you save with specific items, unlimited, or autosave)- Story: Very Good. (Different endings)- Sound, Music, Voice: Very Good.This definetly is an indie gem. I recommend this for fans of old-school survival genre such as Signalis, REs.

_childDocuments_.review: Brutal both in difficulty, and in the portrayal of trench warfare, Conscript offers quite a literal interpretation of the survival horror genre. The player is cast as a young French conscript who must survive through the Battle of Verdun and find his brother and bring him home safely to their mother. All the while he must face down all the horrors that war enables.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game. You will see a lot of similarities to resident evil game play and I say that in the best way possible. you're gonna have to make choices and they will change how you play the game. its probably my favorite WW1 game now as i think it dances the line well of having a fun and tense gaming experience, while still respecting the harsh and horrific reality of war and the loss of life and sanity. This isn't scary in a classic sense. but by having the horrors be realistic I think was the right choice. and If you have a hard time playing horror games but want to experience them? this is for you.I love this game and I hope it does well because it deserves it. and I'm excited to see what Jordan Mochi does next.

_childDocuments_.review: Bent double, like old beggars under sacks,Knock-kneed, coughing like hags, we cursed through sludge,Till on the haunting flares we turned our backs,And towards our distant rest began to trudge.Men marched asleep. Many had lost their bootsBut limped on, blood-shod. All went lame, all blind;Drunk with fatigue; deaf even to the hootsOf gas-shells dropping softly behind.GAS GAS GAS! Quick boys! - An ecstasy of fumblingFitting the clumsy helmets just in time, But someone still was yelling and stumblingAnd floundering like a man in fire or lime.--Dim through the misty panes of thick green light,As under a green sea, I saw him drowning.In all my dreams, before my helpless sight,He plunges at me, guttering, choking, drowning.If in some smothering dreams, you too could pace Behind the wagon that we flung him in,And watch the white eyes writing in his face,His hanging face, like a devil's sick of sin ;If you could hear, at every jolt, the bloodCome gargling from the froth-corrupted lungs,Obscene as cancer, bitter as the cudOf vile, incurable sores on innocent tongues, - My friend, you would not tell with such high zestTo children ardent for some desperate glory, The old lie: Dulce et decorum estPro patria moria

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just barely hitting a 6/10 for me, because when it's good it's pretty enjoyable, but the lows are just too significant to ignore.To start, this game's atmosphere and music is on point. I really dig the visuals, and the atmosphere in general does a lot of the narrative's heavy lifting.I love me some classic RE; RE1R, OG RE2 and 3, 7, and 2R are all really great survival horror games. This game's basic loop scratches that base itch for me. Getting thrown into an area, wandering, finding obstacles, finding Key Items, and seeing how everything fits together to get to your ultimate destination. The first area, Chapter 2, I think is a solid first area. Individual areas stick out well enough so it's not hard remembering where stuff is, the map gets the job done, and the pace is mostly pretty good. Backtracking is also not too bad My only main issue is that it's a little big for the first area and I think one more save room would've been nice, but it's not enough to sway my opinion much.It's this praise I have for Chapter 2 that makes Chapter 3 all the more painful. I won't sugarcoat it, Chapter 3 is the worst part of the game. The area is way too large and the individual screens are so incredibly long and winding. Your first run through the area has no enemies, it's about letting the atmosphere sink in (which is well done I should add, the music in this moment is also excellent. More on those later). This place is simply exhausting to travel through and not very interesting. Backtracking's the name of the game in RE, having to decide what rooms to clear of enemies for safe passage and when to conserve those resources, best managing your inventory to minimize said backtracking. But this area's backtracking is not interesting, it's tedious as ♥♥♥♥. The moment I noticed a Fast Travel system for this area, I knew it was a bad omen (I am aware this was added in an update. This is a band-aid fix at best, and frankly the area as a whole is so poor that I don't think there's much saving it). This chapter is also home to the infamous Minefield puzzle. I actually think this is a very neat puzzle in concept, and thematically fitting too. The issue comes down to the punishment, it's instant death. I was on the default difficulty with no saves nor checkpoints, and my last save was right before putting in the keys and the boulder section. Having to redo those menial tasks each time added up and just got on my nerves. The next major area is in Chapter 5 which really isn't much better, but it at least has better shortcuts. The same core issue lies here, the area is overly large. The individual areas are more interesting though.The final major area is in Chapter 6 and I actually thought this was a good final area, outside of its length.That really is the main issue with this game, it's just too long for its own good. One key thing all of the survival horror REs have is that they're short. This is important when resource management (even if the item drops are generous) is a major mechanic. Conscript fails in this regard for me, and I can't see myself replaying it anytime remotely soon because of this, which I see as a further problem since replaying most REs is also part of the fun. Using your existing knowledge to perfect your routing, nabbing higher ranks (even tho I'm not a big ranks person myself, but what I mentioned beforehand absolutely holds), all that. This game's length makes that really unappealing to me. My playtime was 12ish hours, maybe cut off one for this one moment I got lost.I suppose on that, I think the game is generally good at leading the player. As long as you check the map often enough to see what keys are needed where, I don't think you'll get lost. There also wasn't any puzzle I got stuck on for a long period of time. The one time I pulled up a guide was purely because of my own incompetence, and not because of something I felt the game poorly communicated.As for combat, well it's clunky and that's entirely the point. If you don't have to kill an enemy, don't. Save those resources when you can. I will say I think this game is really generous on resources, and once more I was on the default difficulty. I was pretty frequently killing most enemies I saw and I can maybe think of one instance where I had to play things cautiously. That being said on direct combat itself, I feel like hitboxes could be a bit off sometimes. I'd be a good distance away from an enemy and somehow their melee hit still connects. Sometimes I'd also fire a shot (with steady aim from Alcohol too I should add), reticle on an enemy, and it just wouldn't connect. It caused me to eat some unnecessary hits, never to the point of killing me but it was nonetheless annoying.Back on the topic of resources, part of why the game is so generous is because there's an RE4 Merchant system. If I had a nickel for every time an RE inspired survival horror indie game put an RE4 Merchant system in, I'd have two nickels, which isn't a lot but weird it's happened twice right? I'll just get straight to the point, I think this completely spits in the face of survival horror, which this game considers itself to be. The entire point, in my opinion, is making do with the resources scattered around the environment. Just being able to buy additional resources thoroughly kills that aspect of the game, having to best utilize what the environment gives you and no "just don't use it" is not the gotcha you think it is. If I have to ignore a major mechanic of the game to make it more interesting, then that is a major problem. There's no tension, because I can always just buy more ammo or healing items or whatever I need with the many cigarettes (the game currency) the game tosses me. Does this game want to be survival horror or action horror? Do you want me to avoid combat or not? Are my weapons tools or are they toys? There are forced combat sections, like in the intro and the game's climax and I realize this was inevitable for a game set in WW1, but it makes the game feel unfocused. Anytime RE tried to merge the two, it inevitably leaned far more into the action by the latter half of the given game (RE8 being my prime example). The only RE game I think managed a good balance of this was the original RE3. What compounds this lack of focus is the game's attempt at a Crimson Head system from RE1R, which would imply the game DOESN'T want you killing enemies.I should preface this by saying I played this game after the update that nerfed rats, and I had difficulties finding footage of what they looked like pre-update. I'm relying on what other reviews before this update said, but from what I played I can't help but think the developer overcompensated when nerfing them. According to other reviews, rats were incredibly fast and Poison would halve your max HP. In the version i played, rats were very easy to avoid and Poison barely even scratched my Max HP. It was never a reason for me to burn a full heal to replenish. Since they were so negligible, I had no qualms killing all the enemies in a room, never burning bodies or grenading holes. Why bother when they only ever occasionally got a hit on me. The Crimson Head mechanic is a lot more fragile then people seem to realize, and the reason it worked as well as it did in RE1R was because despite the additional backtracking, the map was still rather compact so returning to burn a body was mostly a matter of if you had the kerosene to do so. Scenarios where you had no choice but to deal with a Crimson Head meant meant putting one down for good or thinking up a different path to your destination, if possible. I should also mention RE1R was wholly dedicated to being a survival horror game, not some hybrid. Again, this all feeds back into a lack of focus.I wanna say more but gotta cut it short because text limits.All in all I don't regret buying this game at full price, and a lot of my grievances are ones a good sequel could address.

_childDocuments_.review: I adored CONSCRIPT. It's clearly taking inspiration from survival horror classics such as Resident Evil and Silent Hill, but CONSCRIPT stands distinct. Part of this is the top-down perspective, which reminds me of SIGNALIS - another modern classic. The top-down perspective (which makes aiming during combat significantly easier) is given a survival horror touch by having the player character manually eject shells from the barrel for strong weapons. This allows frantic moments where the player is desperately running away from enemy raiders, knowing that they cannot even shoot immediately, but have to participate in the slow process of ejecting and loading another bullet. Part of this is the tone, which never strays from subdued and mournful, punctuated with tense, almost overwhelming action. Killing brings rats, which bring disease, so upon seeing an enemy you're not immediately motivated to kill them. It works both on a gameplay level (stopping you from simply killing all enemies and then proceeding with puzzles, keeping levels tense) and a thematic level: you're a soldier, not a super soldier - combat is scary and should be avoided.A big part of it is the setting: WW1 and the Battle of Verdun is an inspired place to set a survival horror game. CONSCRIPT makes great use of it's locations: I particularly enjoyed the trenches and avoiding enemy raiders. Areas feel constantly bombarded and under attack, which is a unique feeling for this type of survival horror game. Storytelling is a light touch, which I think adds to the feeling of hopelessness shared by the characters.Overall, if you're a survival horror fan CONSCRIPT is incredible, and is highly recommended. Even if you're not, CONSCRIPT is a unique enough voice that I think it's worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Version:  Do you like WWI history and old-school survival horror and stealth games?  If so, buy it.  If those aren't always or even usually your bag, watch some streams or YouTube vids first.Full Version:So, a little over 12 hours in, I have to say I like it, maybe even love it.  It really does a good job of being what I would call "war horror."  There aren't any "monsters," just humans being horrible to each other, which is actually just as scary as zombies or what-have-you, if not more so.What a prospective buyer should know before diving in is that this is definitely old-school survival horror.  Foremost, you have a limited inventory.  In at least your first playthrough, expect to spend a good bit of time backtracking to your item boxes.  Not only is your inventory limited, but also your ammunition, healing items, etc.  Very often you will find yourself playing this much like a Metal Gear Solid clone, sneaking and hiding, planning ways to run past enemies rather than fight them, simply because the odds of defeat are too great, and even if you win the fight you know you'll waste too many resources.  In the normal difficulty setting and above, saves are also limited, so unless you're content to play on easy,  you'll find yourself agonizing over whether to use a save before something you think may be risky.  Do this too often, and you'll find yourself wasting precious currency (cigarettes; it's WWI, after all) to buy more ink for extra saves.Combat is actually some of the best I've seen in a pure or near-pure horror game.  You have to kite certain enemies more than I'd like, but that rings fairly true to how you'd fight as an outnumbered soldier in a trench in that conflict; one long fighting retreat.  The weapons are varied enough, far more than in most classic survival horror, actually, and surprisingly satisfying to use for the genre.  They are also upgradeable if you like that element in a game.Certain mechanics, such as having to work the rifle's bolt, ♥♥♥♥ the revolver, pump the shotgun, etc. via an additional control input, add quite a bit to the horror element.  A moment's panic, where you just try to keep "pulling the trigger" by clicking or hitting the fire button on your controller, can actually detract heavily from your chances to survive, or at least get you wounded, forcing you to expend more of your limited supply of healing items  (More on that later.)The dev has been very receptive to players asking for particular bug fixes and such, including most crucially the fact that the rats were a bigger threat than enemy soldiers, so this isn't a game where player concerns are going to be ignored by the dev.  That comes as a big relief in an age where a lot of indie titles basically become abandonware on launch.The music is excellent, very fitting to the setting, and even includes a great, old survival horror tradition in the form of a relaxing save room theme that makes you feel nice and safe for the couple of minutes you're rearranging your inventory and such.  Then you head back out into the darkened gloom of the trenches, and of tracks that do their best to convey that you are knee-deep in corpses with little chance to survive.Controls are responsive and effective.  I can't say that I've taken a death I didn't deserve due to a control flub.  I recommend playing on a controller if you have one; it feels more natural for this kind of game.  The only caveat is that you will have to learn the weapons, because you do have to manually chamber the next round.  That is by design, however.  Let yourself get panicky, fall out of the rhythm of the weapon you are using, and there is a price to be paid.  That reflects the atmosphere and setting of the game, so I consider it a strength rather than a weakness.I don't want to go on forever, but overall, the game takes a lot of the things old-school survival horror lovers have come to appreciate about the genre and very effectively wraps it all in a WWI skin with a simple premise:  No monsters, no ghosts, no pseudoscience or weird supernatural conspiracies.  You're alone in war, and that's horror enough.

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT reminds players that World War 1 is most faithfully adapted through the medium of horror games. _childDocuments_.review: Where to start ? Well, I guess with I would have to say that this is going to be a long review because I want to do an in- depth analysis.I am writing this because I care and I want to point out what the developer got right and what they got wrong.I will not spoil the story in any way but I will give my opinions on other stuff. I played this for 50 hrs so I explored almost everything this game has to offer.So, this whole thing where indie devs emulate the RE or any other formula isn't necessarily wrong, you can copy and make a good game.CONSCRIPT is a RE clone (set in the WWI) but not a good one. I would describe this game by -when it works it works- . The game has some sections that are good but the rest is ruined by huge portions of backtracking and poor resource balancing.This game has 6 chapters and if you play it without searching for key items and getting lost you are looking at 10 hrs + . It is a long game but when you spend so much time backtracking, managing your inventory, looking at the map and trying to remember where was that one room...it is frustrating. These things kill the horror in this game.The maps are quite big so it is really hard to remember everything and the constant going back for the item thing doesn't help. The other thing is that environments look similar. Let's take the original RE1, you had to do some backtracking but you always knew where you were and where you have to go. Look, I get it the trenches look the same but when you get to the indoor sections it gets very confusing.One thing that I regret is playing with limited saves. I wanted to play as the developers intended and realized in chapter 3 that I made a mistake. Use the checkpoint system to minimize frustrations.Ok, resource balancing is bad. This was a survival horror game for the first 2 chapters, I was low on resources and INK (saves). So repetition killed the horror element and poor resource balancing made this into an action game. By chapter 4 I had so many bullets that I could kill each enemy 3 times. I got to the last battle and I fully upgraded 2 weapons, I had so many healing items...chapters 4,5 and 6 Rambo mode.There are 4 or 5 types of enemies but the most annoying are the rats. So, when you kill a soldier the rats will come to eat of course. Now there are some methods in stopping the rats, you can burn the bodies using fuel but there is not enough gas to burn the bodies. The second method is to collapse the rat tunnels with a grenade but only in certain areas, if the area has no rat tunnels you can't stop them. Now, you can't shoot the rats, you can only use melee weapons to kill them but they will come back if you don't burn the bodies.I thought this rat problem would be present only in few chapters but no, you have to put up with this stupid method through out the whole game.I could go on and on about some other minor things but I don't want to.The game is at it's best when the things I listed above are reduced to a minimum. It is not a bad game. The combat is ok, the sound design is ok and the story serves the purpose.Would I recommend this game to fans of the genre ? Nope, I think the whole thing is a mess but it has potential.I hope the developers don't take this the wrong way. This review is more a constructive criticism. You can see that they understand the genre, I do not doubt the effort put into this game but the end product is not that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Survival horror fans are eating well with indie titles like Crow Country coming out earlier this year, and now CONSCRIPT. This passion project pays homage to titles like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, set against the haunting backdrop of World War I during the Battle of Verdun. It features all the genre's hallmarks: limited resources, inventory management, recursive unlocking, puzzles, and yes, plenty of backtracking.The horror in CONSCRIPT is psychological and atmospheric, with limited jump scares. The narrative makes you sympathize with the protagonist and the other soldiers who have been conscripted and forced to fight. Combat can feel clunky, especially the aiming, with a cursor that shakes violently at times, reflecting the protagonist's mental state. The giant rats are particularly hard to hit and often more dangerous than the German soldiers.A hallmark of good survival horror is its map design, and CONSCRIPT excels here. Each major area is well-crafted with interlocking routes, making exploration feel rewarding. Thorough players will find plenty of items scattered throughout the environment, leading to an abundance of ammo and healing items by the end of the game.The environments are horrifically detailed, with some late-game areas feeling like they’re straight out of Silent Hill. However, outdoor areas can sometimes look busy, making it hard to tell which objects you can pass through. Environmental puzzles make sense for the setting and are never too complicated, though some areas require tedious backtracking to find necessary items. The music and sound design are effective, with the heavy breathing of gas-masked soldiers adding to the tension. Limited vision when lacking a torch or wearing a gas mask also contributes to the unsettling ambience.Despite minor issues, I highly recommend CONSCRIPT for its classic survival horror gameplay and haunting atmosphere. The passion behind its creation is palpable, and supporting this title will surely encourage more great work from the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Set during the First World War, Conscript is a top-down survival horror game with old-school mechanics clearly inspired by the classics of the 90s genre. You will play as a young French soldier who is sent to Verdun with his brother to fight the Nazi invasion. After a brief introduction, you are separated from your brother and thrown into the trenches overrun by German soldiers. The Battle of Verdun is known to be one of the longest and bloodiest of the First World War, so you can expect a very dark and oppressive atmosphere right from the start. Solo developer Jordan Mochi has really done an impressive job of portraying war in a realistic way, not only visually, but also narratively through cutscenes, flashbacks, and interactions with other soldiers. The game doesn't rely on traditional jump scares to scare you, but deals with the horrors of war on a more psychological and human level.Conscript proves that you don’t need monsters to tell a horror story; humanity can be monstrous in many ways and war is one of them. Instead of fighting zombies and other mutated creatures, you kill German soldiers and… rats. The combat is intentionally clumsy to increase the sense of danger and vulnerability, especially with the slow aiming. You can use ranged weapons from a selection of WWI firearms, but also various melee weapons (such as a shovel). It is advisable to avoid enemies or kill them silently whenever possible because every bullet counts and even one-on-one encounters can be deadly, but it is when you are outnumbered that the game shows its full brutality. Of course, you can run away from any fight and leaving the area will reset the enemies’ position, but you will inevitably get blood on your hands. Dead enemies will attract rats, so it is very important to burn their corpses using the lighter and fuel. You can also use a grenade to seal off a rat hole and prevent any spawning in the area. Rats can be very annoying because they give you an infection that permanently reduces your health until it is treated with a medical kit or a disinfectant bandage, so it is very important to minimize their spawning.The game is obviously inspired by classic survival horrors like  and this is visible not only in the UI design but also in the scarcity of ammunition, resources, medical supplies and ink cartridges that must be used for manually saving the game inside safe rooms. Your inventory is very limited, and while it can be upgraded, you always have to decide what to carry and what to leave on the ground. Throughout the environments you will also find cigarettes that can be used to purchase supplies, ammo and even new weapons from a merchant. There are some decent environment puzzles that require you to look out for hidden objects and activate mechanisms that can unlock doors and make you progress.The level design is a claustrophobic maze with interconnected areas that rewards exploration but also hides risks and dangers. You can always open the map to check the area layout, but understanding where you are can be often confusing and time-consuming due to the lack of any positioning marker. There is also a significant amount of backtracking required to solve puzzles, with enemies and resources re-spawning, which can become quite tedious. Fortunately, there are some quality-of-life additions that make the game less tense, such as turning on autosave checkpoints or enabling unlimited saves in safe rooms. There are also four difficulty options (Training, Recruit, Soldier and Veteran) that affect the damage received, quantity of resources and the number of inventory slots.Visually speaking, the pixelated art style is beautiful, although simple, and the isometric view increases the tension since you don’t know what you might find in the next area. The sound design is also impressive: gunfires, screams, explosions and other metallic sounds are everywhere, but there are many moments of pure silence which can be really disturbing and keep you on edge.Conscript offers a phenomenal setting for a survival horror, focusing more on the brutal reality of war rather than zombies and outbreaks. The environments are filled with tension and the superb sound design always delivers a sense of danger and anxiety. I have found many similarities with another recent game that I loved, , and I would recommend both games to fans of the genre who are looking for that slow and classic survival horror feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: Uses classic survival horror mechanics to tell a narrative set during the Battle of Verdun. It's really unique & I had a ton of fun with it; if you like Resident Evil and the top-down style or the setting seems interesting, it's definitely worth checking out. My first casual play-through on normal was ~12 hours, and I've beaten it 4+ more times, I can now knock it out in around 2 hours and have a blast while doing it. I can see myself coming back to this in future, whether it gets additional content or not. RE1/2/3 style exploration and puzzles, the trenches in this game are a labyrinth of locked doors & some of them were sealed by very eccentric locksmiths. Item boxes, ink ribbon style save system (optional), multiple endings & ranks D-S+.REmake style corpse-disposal to prevent some nasty consequences from biting you in the future. RE4 style upgrade-able weapons/bag size, but you're a French WWI soldier so the traveling merchant uses cigarettes for currency. Instead of zombies trying to eat you, the German Imperial Army is trying to cudgel you. Big focus on melee combat, most enemies are melee only: there is a sprint meter & dodge roll to deal with the 1/3 or so enemies using firearms. They generally stand back trying to shoot you while their comrades run at you with shovels & clubs. Some tricky combat encounters, but not really any "boss battles" in the traditional sense. I wouldn't call it scary per se, there are a few "jumpscare" moments, but it lies firmly in the horror genre via the horrors of war & the survival mechanics. Personally I never felt a ton of pressure about ammo supplies, but on the hardest difficulty I was scrounging for healing items. This checks out for me due to the setting, but that would be my one nitpick about it, ammo could have been a bit more scarce on harder difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: I totally recommend this game, it's fantastic. Decent gameplay (has some drawbacks), great story, amazing visual style, music, sound design and so on. Also, If you have a steam deck, give this game a try on sd, its gonna be amazing.However. there are some details about this game that should be fixed:1-2 I've removed coz these issues were fixed3. 60 fps lock. That's my personal issue. I do not have a single device that has such an outdated refresh rate. Even my steamdeck is 90hz. Seeing 60 fps in a 2024 game is just frustrating. The game would greatly benefit from higher refresh rate.4. The combat is a little clunky. Sometimes you can't tell if you have a line of sight on an enemy that is close to some corner. Or unarmored enemies taking 3-4 rifle shots to die, but that's not really a problem, because the game rewards you with an immense amount of resources for exploring and puzzle solving.5. Also, the game clearly draws inspiration from late 90s - early 00s survival horror games. As I remember these games had an option to save after each chapter. That not really an issue, but I'd prefer that to be in the game.All these issues are either to be fixed in the nearest future or really not a big deal. So give this game a try, It's a very good game

_childDocuments_.review: Only reached Chapter 2 at the time of writing but so far, the visuals of the battle-torn trenches creates an unnerving atmosphere that keeps you on your guard and the music contributes to the dark, oppressive ambiance that is present, which fits wonderfully for a survival horror game.There are no zombies or genetically mutated monsters (a refreshing change imo), but enemy soldiers that can swarm you if you're not careful. You will need to be strategic on whether to fight or flee as ammo and healing supplies are limited, but not downright scarce (at least on Standard difficulty). Tips on how to solve puzzles or dispatch new enemies that appear are scattered throughout the game in the form of files that you pick up. You can also purchase items and upgrade your firearms at the merchant you meet early on or repair melee weapons/body armor with kits that you find.Overall, if you're a fan of Resident Evil-esque games (especially either the older ones or RE4 as it's quite inspired by those), I can personally say that this game has been satisfying to play so far!

_childDocuments_.review: My personal GOTY, Conscript is an unforgiving survival horror game in the vein of classic RE. Whereas in RE the survival mechanics like needing save items to record your progress or backtracking because of limited inventory space, etc., serve to increase tension in the moment-to-moment gameplay, I would argue that in Conscript the same mechanics also convey a sense of authenticity of the game's background, namely the gruesome trench warfare of The Great War, creating a perfect union of form and function. This is not to say that this is a must-play for every gamer. Far from it. Those who aren't familiar with this kind of games will probably find some design decisions frustrating or out-dated. However, if you know what you are getting into, Conscript will more than whet your appetite for a top-notch survival horror experience.

_childDocuments_.review: OUTDATED: Chapter 3 is horrible, it looks great, but the amount of backtracking is absolutely ridiculous! I found myself beginning to nitpick enemy placement and AI during the lengthy runs back to the minefield where the ONLY hint you get is a drawing. This'd be all fine and dandy if THE DRAWING WERE ACCURATE! Instead it takes you straight onto a mine, enjoy running unlocking the 3 locks, running through a mine shaft and dodging a bolder, then sprinting another mile only to die by a mine. I wouldn't be as upset if this was just a bonus area but it's required to progress the game. I've lost all interest in playing as the enemy variety and story just isn't worth sticking around for. **Maybe when the dev fixes Chapter 3 I'll change my review.**THEY DID!!! I'm leaving the old aspects of my review as the dev actually addressed and solved a ton of issues!***Conscript is both a great piece of art and a mediocre game. The art is gorgeous and expertly shows the man-made horrors of war. The gameplay however leaves a lot to be desired, RE style of aiming is fine, but the enemy variety is severely lacking with the armored enemies being nothing more than bullet sponges. Rats are insane as many have pointed out, hard to hit and inflict a poison debuff which lowers your max health and requires special medicine to cure. I spent most of act 2 poisoned til I finally bought alcohol from the trader. Act 3 really highlights poor map design. The farm in specific requires you to follow a path that snakes through the entire area making backtracking very tedious for no apparent reason. Act 3 also introduces a bunch of enemies that will ambush you. This doesn't necessarily sound like a bad thing, but the way its implemented is annoying. Dying to enemies that are scripted to spawn after finishing an area leads to repeating the same events multiple times because an ambush of 10 enemies came out of nowhere.*** Rats have been debuffed as to not be quite the menace. There are many more item boxes making backtracking and inventory management much more bearable! Seriously JD deserves kudos for their hard work!I'd argue that despite the game selling as a "survival horror" there isn't much horror to be had. The scariest enemy is a rat, and the soldiers you fight don't strike fear into the player. War is horrible, but as a player I'm not exactly terrified of my character dealing with nerve gas. Maybe in the later half of the game things ramp up, but so far its just not scary.I'm a big fan, if you're into WW1 or survival horror games this is worth picking up! It's not very scary, but the mood and atmosphere makeup for it in spades!

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT is an exhausting, miserable, depressing and draining survival horror game and it is those qualities that makes it work remarkably well. It might make it a struggle for some to see it through as a result, but the fierce conviction of its vision wins me over.Mechanically, it has a lot of similarities with classic resident evil, especially REMake, explore the environment, find keys, open new passageways, make decisions about how to spend health/ammo and all that stuff works pretty well, combat's not super complicated but mostly captures the positional emphasis of classic survival horror in a more modern control scheme, good stuff. But I think the main thing that sets Conscript apart is the crushing, suffocating atmosphere borne of its relentless dedication to depicting how desperately bad the conditions of WW1 were. It feels a little stupid to say that CONSCRIPT really makes you feel the horror of WW1 because how could I, some dork sitting here playing a video game, truly understand. But, yeah? I do think CONSCRIPT is successful in at least a small way in transporting you into that headspace, it bores down on you, it never seems to get any better, every new place sucks harder than the last and the tension it builds in some moments is incredible and it accomplishes all of this largely through pure gameplay. It doesn't need to tell you a whole lot, it's pretty confident that its depiction will get the point across and I believe this confidence is not misplaced.As a tone piece, roaring success. I think it's incredibly well executed. On a more nitty gritty I think the pace of exploration gets kind of unnecessarily bogged down at the midpoint by level design where save rooms/item boxes are spread kinda far apart? It's got a weird fixation on environments where the lone item box is located in exactly one corner of a given zone instead of being more evenly spread. CONSCRIPT's already a pretty long game by genre standards and you could argue some of the tedium is in service to vibes but I still think a better balance was possible here, especially since it encourages replays with a NG+ feature but it's honestly a bit long in the tooth and its depressing tone kinda works against that a bit. It's not a game where you could really give the protagonist a laser pistol as a fun joke extra to alleviate this which is one of the pitfalls of its historical setting which I nevertheless highly respect the commitment to.At the end of the day, I think CONSCRIPT is great and highly worth the time. It's a remarkable achievement to thread the needle on its subject matter in the form of an action game that doesn't feel tasteless or crude. It's a game I keep thinking about even when I'm not playing it, it sits with you long after credits roll, making me think about things I'd rather not, as it should, it is the game the era it depicts deserves, even if it isn't the one it necessarily wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Old school survival horror that makes excellent use of its bleak setting. As a solo-developed project, I think that conscript deserves heaps of praise for delivering a tense and often frightening experience. At times I was worried that the game might take a left turn into the supernatural but the horror remains grounded, and thus all the more unsettling, throughout the game's 8-12 hour runtime.The game is not without flaws, some of the puzzles are obtuse and some of the backtracking can feel frustrating, but this may have been intentional and isn't enough to detract from what is overall a very solid and very rewarding experience.P.S. the rats are not that hard to deal with. _childDocuments_.review: [Soldier difficulty][Unlimited saves][TLDR: Quality survival horror framework x WW1 realistic setting]+ The lo-fi visuals are surprisingly good at depicting the horrors of WW1, with the limited palette of browns and greys conveying the grimy, apocalyptic look of the trenches and front-lines. There's just the right amount of detail everywhere to build up an oppressive, immersive atmosphere that is one of the game's strongest selling points.+ Music is also fitting, ominous and oppressive and accompanied by appropriate sound effects, creating an ambience which sometimes verges on the surreal and hints at horrors beyond the game's realistic depiction of WW1. Taking a cue from the Resident Evil games, the safe rooms have a calmer, relaxed and melancholic theme to contrast strongly with the dangers that await outside.+ The framework of survival horror also extends to the level design, which I thought was excellent. Trenches, forts and barracks can support the kind of complex level design that's a puzzle in and of itself and a staple of the genre. It's surprisingly fitting and, for me, meshed very well with the game's historical setting, despite the obvious lack of mysterious keys, locks and door mechanisms in the actual battle of Verdun. Levels are fun to explore and learn, as you go from feeling lost to optimising your navigation while backtracking or advancing the objectives.+ Inventory and resource management are largely unchanged from something like Resident Evil and can be the source of quite a bit of backtracking. For me it's a sort of an optimisation mini-game, but I get how it can be tedious for others. A merchant is also present, selling items and gun upgrades, transplanted faithfully from other representatives of the genre.* Combat is definitely a bit clunky, revolving around taking space and standing still to aim which in the beginning, when low on resources, can result in some Benny Hill sketch moments with you running away from German soldiers to find an opportune moment to reload and shoot or smack them in the face. It definitely rewards positional awareness and tactical traversal (to avoid mud, use explosive barrels, etc.), but it can be a bit tedious when you're low on resources. Fortunately, as you stock up on weapons and ammo throughout the game's duration, it starts feeling more and more enjoyable.- Unfortunately, enemies have a habit of hitting you through walls with both melee and ranged attacks, and there are some moments when they catch your hit-box as you dodge when they really shouldn't have.+ The story is simple, but effective; the story of two brothers conscripted in the French army and thrown into the meat grinder of WW1. You'll have the choice of fighting or running (both of which influence the ending, of which there are four, each with two variants), you'll solve fun puzzles, navigate labyrinthine trenches and make your way across bloodied front-lines across six chapters to find your brother and bring him back home.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid entry in the genre with a fresh twist.  couple of rough balance bits at launch but that's been fixed. The combat is pretty satisfying and the atmosphere is great. Captures a kind of desolate feeling that few games have. _childDocuments_.review: War is hell, but this war.....  is the worst of them all.The visual and sound design of this game is perfect, hammering even more the depressing and brutal nature of WW1. The story itself is very simple: one brother trying to save his younger brother. There is not a lot of dialogue, but the journey is what makes this game great. Overall, there are 4 endings (excluding the A/B variation) and a new game plus mode, making this game highly replayable.As for gameplay, it's not a realistic one-shot kill kind of game, but that's okay. In turn, the combat is long, difficult (sometime clunky), and desperate, where enemies take many hits and always outnumber you. So, you need to plan each engagement carefully: either fight head-on, hit them in the back of the head, sneak past undetected, or just run. But god forbid, don't forget to burn the bodies of fallen foes, unless you want to deal with a pack of bloodthirsty rodden!As much as I like this game, I realize that it's not for everyone. If you hate backtracking, bullet sponges, searching every single room, or clunky combat, then this game is not for you..... But then again, the game is only 26 CAD$ with 8 to 12 hours for a first playthrough. It couldn't hurt to try, no?

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten the game and at the end of the game I just can't recommend it due to a number of different issues. Some of the issues I have seem to have been fixed by the 1.0.1.0 patch today. The patch made some of the more tedious areas better, but they should have been noticed before the game came out. I'm just going to make a list of issues I had with the game.-Inventory. At the start of the game you only have 8 inventory slots which sounds like a lot (can have 16 by the end of the game), but you learn very quickly that it's not enough. My inventory had a few items I always had on hand. I had my infinite durability knife (for breaking things, killing rats, and stealth kills), a random stronger melee weapon that had a durability (for when I had to actually fight), a pistol or rifle, and ammo for said weapon. This never changed through out the whole game. So that's 4 slots left, but that's a lie cause I also had a healing item on me at all times, a gas mask (when I got it), and at least one key item that was needed to get other items or progress the area. That leaves me with roughly 1-2 slots left depending if I had the key item with me or if it was consumed to get another item. There are a LOT of items in this game and I was constantly going back and forth to the storage chest to clear up the little inventory space I had. I never knew what I needed to have on me so I just had a well rounded inventory that would help me deal with anything. This isn't even counting all the items that take up slots in your inventory that just sit there and take up space. What if you wanted to burn the dead bodies? Well that would require you to have a lighter and fuel so there goes 2 slots. What if you wanted to wear body armor (which stops rats from poisoning you which you would only know because of the patch notes on launch day and is mentioned nowhere in game)? That's another slot. What bout the items that give you better healing, more speed, or better rolling? That's 3 slots right there. What about grenades to plug up rat holes? There are far too many items in this game for how little inventory space you have and it comes off like a sick joke.-Rats. I'm not sure how this made it out of the testing phase for the game, but they drag the experience down. Through out the game when you kill Germans and leave their bodies on the game, rats will come and eat at the bodies after a certain amount of time has passed based on the difficulty. At first they don't seem so bad. You just can just melee them and be on your way. However you come to realize how annoying them are.   a. You can melee rats, but you can only hit one at a time which makes no sense since you have hit multiple Germans in a single swing. I found this out the hard way and and got poisoned as punishment. (as of patch 1.0.1.0 you can hit up to two rats in a full swing)   b. Rats have the chance to poison you which permanently takes a chunk of you HP away and at the beginning of the game this is about half your overall health. The only way to fix this is from upgraded bandages or a med kit. At the end of the game I had plenty of these, but at the start I didn't and didn't want to waste my healing supplies on a bull mechanic so I just loaded my save up instead.   c. You can blow up holes with grenades (if the area has one) or burn bodies with a lighter and fuel to stop rats from spawning on a screen, but as mentioned in my inventory post this can be a pain to deal with since you don't have a lot of space to be just having grenades or a lighter/fuel just sitting in your inventory that just takes up space.  d. Rats never attack Germans and will only attack you. This makes no sense at all. It's mentioned that rats like to eat fresh bodies, but why are they even attacking you when you're still alive and running around? I understand it's a game and doesn't have to make sense, but come on.   e. If you kill an enemy and they fall behind the foreground, rats can be on them and you won't even know since you can't see things hiding behind the foreground.-Enemies. There are a number of different enemy types in the game. Some of them melee you and other shoot at you. Some even try to do both. Thankfully you can deal with enemies without much problem once you learn how the game works. You can stealth kill most enemies by hitting them from behind except when it comes to the bigger enemies that wear armor. There are a few issues that will need to be looked at and hopefully fixed.   a. Enemies can no hear the sound of your footsteps. You can run full speed up behind someone and they won't even know.   b. Enemies can see through the walls in the earlier trench areas of the game which ruins stealth. This really sucks cause the walls are obviously taller than all the humans, yet the enemies act like they are only waist high.   c. Enemies will never lose sight of you once they catch you unless you switch screen. That doesn't seem so bad, but the dev put in hiding spots in areas of the game no matter how many walls you put between you and the enemy, they will know you are hiding in those spots despite the fact that they couldn't see you at all.-Weapons. There are a lot of weapon in the game. Most of them are guns. It's a pretty cool selection. Pistols, rifles, shotguns, shovels, clubs, etc. Once again I have issues with the weapons in this game.   a. Guns are far too weak to even deal with the most basic enemies unless you upgrade them. You have to find gun parts around the map in order to upgrade your gun. The more you upgrade them the most it costs in gun parts. The only thing you should ever upgrade is the damage as more damage equals less ammo used to kill someone. Problem is you know your going to find better weapons for each type of weapon so it's pointless to upgrade unless you know what to upgrade as it will just lead to you wasting gun parts.   b. Dev locks weapon upgrades behind game progress. If you like a gun and want to max out it's damage well tough. You can only upgrade 1-2 times and if you want to get more you have to wait for the next chapter. New chapter means one more slot allowed to upgrade on each stat. Some weapons you can't even fully upgrade the damage until the last chapter of the game.   c. Melee weapons are a complete joke. You have a starting knife that does almost no damage, but had infinite durabilty so I always had it on me to do stealth kills. Every other melee weapon has a durability rating, but you can't really tell what it is since it's just a white bar. Weapons break far too fast and if you want to repair them you have to use a repair crate which is a precious resource. You would never waste these on weapon beginner melee weapons. Sad thing is the stronger melee weapon has less durability compared to weaker ones which just it feel pointless.   d. I killed most enemies with stealth. If I actually fought enemies like how they are programmed, I would have wasted all my ammo, melee weapons, and healing supplies just to deal with them. Best to either stealth kill or run past everyone to save resources.-Abusing game mechanics. Each room in the game is it's own thing with loading screens between each of them. You can abuse these loading screens to make enemies a joke which is what I did to save resources as explained above. If an enemy caught me while I was trying to stealth kill them, I would just run to another screen and come right back in to reset them and try again. I feel bad for doing it this way, but it felt like I had to do it. I played the game with limited saves so there could be 30-60 minutes between saves and since I never knew what the the next room was going to through at me I abused the load screens to manage resources.I have other things to complain about, but the Steam review has hit the text limit. At the end of the day I can't recommend this game. Just too many little things all adding up which made it feel like a slog to get through by the end.

_childDocuments_.review: The time played you can see above was all for naught. After playing this much I can tell you this game was not ready for a full release. You can't publish a game that's not been properly tested as this one, much less at a 20+ dollars price. For once I wish this was an Early Access game.This game contains lots of bugs; aiming works like hell, some guns don't work as they are described to or don't even work at all, fighting a freaking rat is way harder than fighting an elite human enemy and across the game you'll see more of the former, the layout of the items location makes it very easy to miss really necessary ones and even some KEY ITEMS can bug, preventing you from completing the game.Some of the issues mentioned before can be dismissed since it's a new game but game-breaking ones cannot be on the full release. I understand the "solo dev" background and for that this game does a lot, but that excuse goes only for so long.Wait for it to be on sale or a long time (solo dev...) for it to be fixed. If you are going to buy it try to keep various saves in case you stumble upon one of this bugs. I didn't and got hopelessly stuck on the very end of Chapter 5 from the total 6.Out of Steam this game costs a quarter of what it costs here, if you know what I mean. I wish I had knew that before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT somehow manages to feel completely fresh and unique while also scratching that classic survival horror itch. If you're a fan of RE1-3 you'll love this, no doubt about it. Even RE4 fans will probably enjoy this even though the overall structure adheres more to the original trilogy.+ WW1 setting+ Atmosphere is 10/10.+ Sound design is immersive.+ Soundtrack is great, understated but serves it's purpose well.+ Very cosy save rooms (I heard multiple save room themes throughout the game and they were all perfect).+ Map & level design overall is really good. Many "Ah-ha" moments when you loop around to an old area.+ Story leaves you alone for the most part and let's you figure it out on your own (lots of environmental storytelling as well).+ Combat is simple but satisfying overall.- Controls at time can feel slightly rough but if you're used to classic survival horror that's to be expected- Rats are annoying (but I know the dev is working on a balance patch now so this might be irrelevant when you read this).- Ran in to some small bugs but none of them ever really frustrated me.Is there some jank at times? Yeah, but none of it ever detracted from my experience. And I'm sure the dev will work on those minor refinements in time. tl:dr Buy this if you're a fan of classic survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent concept brought to life with time-tested mechanics, smooth control and a great visual style. And, while this shouldn't "matter" in terms of judging a game's quality, this was mostly the passion project of one guy. Damn. Caveat, I backed this on Kickstarter so of course I was inclined to like it. That being said, I never played any demos of it and waited until launch day.I usually prefer games that have fantastical aspects like magic or monsters. Conscript has no T-Virus, no radiation mutants, no supernatural creatures. But it does have monsters. It shows what it was like when techniques of warfare didn't keep pace with technology, so you had people in chainmail beating each other up with clubs in tunnels underneath wastelands with scores of bullets flying from machine guns. What I'm trying to say is, the atmosphere of the game is truly something to behold. The horror of being a soldier stuck in this is something else, something that touched me on a level that my "preferred" subject matter could not. Because, to an extent, this actually happened, the Great War is very real.Enough about that though. The gameplay is solid, you have excellent control of your character but they are heavy  and a little slow (think Darkwood) and so you must be deliberate with your movements or you'll be dead. Guns feel powerful but of course are pretty clunky. The soundscape is haunting, whether it's bullets and shells flying or the arguably even more terrifying silence. Mechanics with resource management that are in other survival horror games (mainly Resident Evil) are used here to great effect, and I won't spoil them. Ok, I can't resist, I have to spoil a little bit. So in this game, you're often incentivized to avoid combat so you don't use up your resources or get hurt. But you can fight. When you do fight, it's risky and brutal. And even when your enemies are dead, they don't stop posing a threat...so be careful.

_childDocuments_.review: To evoke stress and panic, horror games will typically conjure extreme, otherworldly elements to the player: for some it will be through corruption or sickness of the human body, others will use manifestations of the deepest fears in our souls, while others will summon terrifying cosmic creatures beyond imagination. CONSCRIPT, instead, gives you the role of a lone WW1 soldier. Isolated and surrounded, your character will have to escape pestilent trenches, while surviving constant gas attacks, enemy waves, the own folies of your commanders, and the simple horror of melee combat between two scared individuals fighting for their lives. The game gives a very effective portrayal of the brutality of war, and demonstrates the potency of this setting, both as a landscape for horrific atmosphere and as a way to denounce the senseless violence of it.Controller in hand, the game is a very effective, traditional survival horror game: enemies are plenty, dangerous, and you are low on ammo. The whole duration of my playthrough had me constantly contemplating the best way to deal with encounters, fleeing when possible, fighting effectively when necessary, killing everyone if unavoidable. If you have played the first Resident Evil games, expect a similar experience, albeit quite a bit longer and wider in scope.Playing the game, one feels that great care has been taken into the setting and the various environments the player explores: beyond trenches, you will walk through the front line, desolate no man's land, bombed villages, and the terrifying and deadly forts of Verdun. The developer is a history major, and it is then no surprise to see accurate details into a trench's organization, the guns used, the relationships in the trenches, and the overall geography and extent of destruction around the fields of WW1. As a point of criticism, the game has a very monochrome depiction of enemy soldiers, will all the enemies in the game being German soldiers attacking you relentlessly on sight. The horror of the war was shared on all sides of no man's land, and it's a bit of a shame that the game doesn't touch on that.Overall however, I can say that CONSCRIPT is the best survival horror I have played in years. The passion for the pillars of the genre is easy to feel, while the game builds its own identity, through interesting mechanics, many great pacing ideas, memorable encounters, and a gripping atmosphere in a setting one scarcely gets to experience in video games. If you are yearning to repeat the experience of Resident Evil 1 or want a challenging, original mix of horror, exploration and action, pick your controllers, put on your headphones, and let CONSCRIPT show you that we are well able to build our greatest horrors ourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been hyped for Conscript ever since I played the demo and the wait has been a long one. I usually end up getting disappointed in games when there is hype involved. Luckily that’s not the case here as Conscript delivers even if it’s not a 100% perfect game. It’s a game that’s classic Resident Evil in gameplay with a world war twist. There are 6 chapters of various lengths, the game will most likely take at least 10 hours with a first run for most people. My first run took around 17 hours with recruit difficulty (lowest of the 4 difficulties). It has a fleshed out new game plus mode, 4 endings, secrets & unlockable content that feel rewarding, different costumes and more. What’s mostly impressive about Conscript is how well thought out and fleshed out it is even with all of that content. All the endings are distinct, the game is designed to be played in different ways in mind and they all work. It’s impressive to keep all that balanced and enjoyable. The levels are really well designed and connected to one another. The story and endings are logical and to the point, no annoying or long notes/files that don’t make a lot of sense (I’m looking at you Signalis). The upgrade system with the weapons, health & stamina is addictive and there are lots of weapons you can find! The game succeeded at making you feel the horror/PTSD of war, it makes it personal and real. The game controls well and it feels like a joy to play. The achievements are fun, even the one where you have to beat it within 3 hours (I’m usually not a fan of those). NG+ with the upgrades, knowledge of repeated runs and some passcodes kept the same ensure a smoother transition than expected. The sound effects of footsteps, gunshots etc. were very satisfying to hear. I thought it was brilliant the way the memory/dream sequences were handled after every chapter along with joining the war with some of the chapters.The game has one main flaw along with 2 minor ones. The game has issues with backtracking, this is especially apparent with chapter 3, 4 and 5. Although 3 is much better with the recent patch, I’m not a fan of blocking shortcuts to force you to take a longer route. It’s especially annoying when you’ve been unlocking shortcuts in the first two chapters and having that taken away from you in 4 when you need it. The game has some weird aiming issues sometimes that I can’t explain. There are moments where I’m clearly aiming at a barrel or a soldier and it’s missing. You learn to get used to it but it didn’t seem natural. And lastly, while I love how much content the game has, you are forced to play a certain way if you want 100% for the achievements with the least amount of runs. You’re looking at playing the game at least 4 times, it can easily be more if you don’t have the runs well planned ahead. For instance, my third run was a combination of finishing the game within 3 hours, less than 6 saves, using melee only and get a specific ending. It’s not as difficult as it sounds but it’s not possible to pick a different ending if you want to get the melee achievement. The reason I also went with the lowest difficulty (recruit) is to ensure that I get the achievement to finish the game within 3 hours, not because I wanted to go for an easier difficulty. There is an achievement for S+ on the highest difficulty (veteran), so I got a taste of that and don’t need to feel guilty about recruit. But that’s what I mean with being limited and being forced to play a certain way.Regardless of all that I mentioned though, I absolutely loved the 45+ hours I spent to 100% the game. The one man developer clearly put all his heart and soul to create the ultimate experience. And it’s his first game with no background in game development! I PRAY we’ll get more games or DLC from this developer as his game is the real deal. Conscript is worth the full price and is a mandatory if you’re a classic Resident Evil fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is already great for not being a survival horror game that isn’t about zombies.This game was brutal at launch when I played it. The rats being so overpowered and being hard to hit, and doing so much damage made me panic and feel fear that so many horror games wish they could do. They did end up nerfing it two weeks after launch and made them no longer a threat, I might be the only person who felt that made the game less fun, but I am a masochist.Conscript has the normal stuff you do in a survival horror, backtrack to fetch items to unlock new areas, great puzzles using logic, and items you find. Combat with limited resources, managing rats by either blocking up holes to prevent spawns or burning dead bodies which was required at least until their nerf.The combat with humans can be a mixed bag as in some areas you can cheese them by leaving the room and resetting them, trivializing a good amount of encounters. There are more than enough times when it’s hard to do or can’t be done and this made those fights more intense. There are epic battles that are dreadful, at least until you become overpowered by upgrading and stockpiling every ammo because you min-max like a Chad.The story was not a draw for me, it has you needing to rescue your brother and you have these horrible flashbacks that are slow walking and no dialogue, and didn’t work to get me invested. It’s a classic mystery box that leads to nothing interesting. The ending with your brother fell flat to me because he was just a dude, I don’t care because I never learned anything to get me to care. You need to build a character to get me invested. But overall I would say this is the best depiction of trench warfare that I know of. The gas, the mud, the fear of charging up trenches, the ability to be a coward, and getting an ending that felt perfect for that. The theme sold me to get this and it did better than I expected and is gonna be another classic survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Conscript is a bit of an anomaly. It's a genuinely solid 2D Resident Evil with a consistent WWI theme. There's no supernatural dangers, no zombies, just the unremitting horrors of war.As a 2D Resident Evil, it's solidly fun. The environment is a jungle gym. You don't feel like you have enough control over your character, but it's the right amount of not enough. Guns are cumbersome and powerful. Melee works. Ambushes feel good. The merchant is great.As a WW1 game... I have slightly more criticism. Conscript is genuinely good at contrasting the war with normal life, and at digging into elements that made WW1 especially bad (rats, dying horses, mud everywhere, commanding officers shooting people having mental breakdowns as a short-term morale strategy made indefinite,) and overall it does a good job of bringing the horrors of war into Resident Evil... but I'm not sure I'd say it sticks the landing on those horrors overall.The German troops are depicted as these faceless killers, not as poor bastards stuck in the same mess you are. The gameplay tends to make you feel powerful when you're at your most patriotic, weak when you're just a person---and this feels like maybe the opposite lesson WW1 is supposed to teach. There are some notes that undercut this. You can find photographs on dead enemies. Enemy mobs are just as prone to shellshock as your troops are. But I was not left with the feeling that this game looked at WW1 and became anti-war---just that it thought this particular war was conducted badly.Obviously, I don't think the average player will have this issue, nor do I feel like it really disrupted my experience of the game. Just a little cognitive dissonance floating in the back of my head. The moment to moment gameplay is fun, the sound design reminded me of Fear And Hunger, and a lot of character is crammed into the low res art. There's one puzzle that feels like it requires a guide, but everything else is pretty intuitive---even if some spots like the minefield are wildly punishing.I think Conscript could've benefited from a You Will Die Here Tonight style approach, where you switch to a new character each time one dies, but that's a decision that would've needed to be made *way* upstream of the 1.0 release.Would I recommend Conscript? Yes. If you like survival horror and want to see a slight twist on the formula, and if you like historical wars, you should give this a go. I'd love to see more from the studio. It's also a pretty decently beefy game (my hours do not reflect the total length,) so if you grab it on even a small sale it's a very solid dollar/hour ratio.It isn't my personal favorite of the current survival horror renaissance, but it's towards the front of the pack, and that shows some serious muscle when you consider the pack includes You Will Die Here Tonight and Signalis.Edit: Weird softlock. I ran away from the flame trooper in the flame trench upon first encountering him, and while he was off screen he despawned or clipped into the geometry or something, permanently trapping me in the arena.2nd Edit: After further testing, fire trench man zips through walls if you scroll the screen away from him while he's walking into one. I think this means you can accidentally zip him through one of the perimeter walls, and I'd scrolled him out of bounds.3rd Edit: There's a lot of sequences that would land amazingly with just a nudge of supernatural horror. I can't help but contrast the chapter 5 town with, like, Fear & Hunger's Prehevil. And Prehevil feels weirdly more historical and more flavorful despite coming from an overtly fantasy setting. I definitely don't think Conscript is wrong for sticking to its premise, but it loses out a little in doing so.4th Edit: Hey, man. If you're going to make random pieces of forgettable art in an optional basement after each chapter necessary for the good ending, maybe when you read them they should get logged in your journal? Just a thought? I've done everything else, I have the other code, I visited the basement at the end of each chapter, I got all of the pronged keys, I have experienced all of the extremely missable content necessary to see the good ending, but I wasn't taking notes on random jpegs so screw me I guess. It's also fully randomized, so the only option here is to brute force it. This sucks gigantically. Guess i'm going to experience randomly turning a dial for the next hour.5th Edit: Hahahahaha. 10,000 possible combinations with a four digit lock.6th Edit: Spent half an hour brute-forcing it. Genuinely, this design sucks. If you want it to be so that the good ending is only accessible on new game plus when the player knows to look for the symbols on the pictures, make it that way. Don't expect the player to randomly draw every piece of artwork they see in case some of them might be used in a vague associative way to set the combination for an optional lock 10+ hours in. That's insane. And don't randomize that code so that people who want to see the good ending will realize 10+ hours in that they're screwed out of it, even if they explored every map and found every item and note. That's stupid and insane.7th Edit: Rolled credits. Apart from having to brute force a lock based on memorizing random pictures from 10+ hours of playtime, I think Conscript is stronger in its final act than in its opening one. Enemies never get super diverse or interesting to fight, but having the finale be a bunch of waves of goons makes narrative sense. There could also be maybe a bit more telegraphing on when you're supposed to release the pigeon. I had to guess blindly, and that feels pretty bad given how much time the finale takes to fight through. I also broke an enemy's AI during the final battle---it kind of ended up just standing in place, ignoring all action around it. No idea if this is replicable, but running all over the map seemed to mess it up. Overall, I'd describe this as a solid game with some VERY rough edges buried deep within, and I'm eager to check out whatever the designer does next.
