_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT - a throwback to classic RE (and RE4), featuring the exact type of gameplay I was craving after finishing SIGNALIS, provides some of the most intense gameplay of being a Frenchman I've experienced.This is a genuinely great game mostly made by *checks notes* one developer, and is worth a buy if you're into survival horror. I do have some caveats with the gameplay though, but I am keeping in mind that this was mostly a solo endeavor, so forgive me if I come off as overly critical (I'm playing post-rats patch, and also only at Chapter 4 at the time of this review, so I might be leaving out a few things that I've yet to experience). Spoilers ahead:While the clunky combat is true to form, I do question the use of one-hit backstabs which trivialize the game. It felt like both the developer and the game were trying to hammer the idea of  but the mechanics totally eschew this. For most of chapter 2 and 3, I stuck with just the basic knife, which deals a pittance of damage normally, since I could OHKO anything with patience. If I'd missed and alerted the guards? I'd just back out of the rooms and pop back in to reset the encounter.Enemies work much the same way in classic RE, which may be a good or bad thing depending on how conservative you like to play (I guess Germans haven't figured out how doors worked yet in 1916?). The only times you actually NEEDED firepower was the occasional gang rush out of nowhere and the door is further away, or when the big armored knights appear to properly introduce their fists to your prostate. Despite this, I still wasn't lacking in ammo or resources at all, which leads into the next issue:Too many items. While inventory storage is actually more generous than RE1 (I don't think you could upgrade bag sizes), the amount of  stuff you get is ridiculous. You'll easily be filled to the brim and have to trek to the item boxes again and again. I just played with the knife, pistol and rifle. holding only pistol ammo weapon-wise. I didn't see a point in bringing other guns because your inventory will not support it alongside the plethora of healing, key items and treasures you'll get. The "survival" in "survival horror" gets taken out when I have enough unused junk to be my own merchant. There's a reason Capcom circumvented this kind of tedium in their recent games.I'd love to see the dev address this as it is a major sticking point. Having key items like the  just be assigned to a separate "Key Items" category, and treasures be likewise relegated would  more than hinder it .I'm in the beginning stages of Chapter 4 and the game also starts to feel very samey. Chapter 2 was a strong start to your exploration of Fort Souville. It's much like my life - dank, hopeless and miserable. The map is almost labyrinthine in design and you have to puzzle out where to go next via text logs, rewarding the player's efforts of utilizing . Then Chapter 3 hits and it kinda falls flat. Chapter 4 then sees you The map design and layout (in Chapter 3) is, frankly, awful. I quite liked that  as it heightened the aftereffects of war while exploring, but the confusing scenery blocking your paths and the amount of collectibles just placed in random locations (these don't sparkle to indicate they're there, you just have to kind of stumble into them) were maddening.What's more egregious is that Fort Souville's map properly marked where obstructions were, whereas Chapter 3's doesn't. I was kind of just running into things figuring out where I could or couldn't walk for 3 hours. Not helping matters is that the map doesn't really indicate where the player is (your cursor is placed where you are when you open the map, but if you move it you quickly lose track of where you are). It just made me more frustrated and took me out of the game.Overall, I do recommend the game and enjoy it greatly. It's just the right amount of stressful and fun, but deterred by some design elements that we (as a society) had already decided were better to omit than preserve.

While it scratches that Resident Evil itch, the amount of backtracking is horrendous as ♥♥♥. You also get punished for literally not taking notes of the paintings in Pierre's journal - I got the Coward ending despite never abandoning my post in all battles and killing over 242 enemies because I did not know the code(paintings in Pierre's journal) to the locker that supposedly contains the item "Father's Watch" that is necessary for the true end. The Coward ending left a bad taste; it is like all my efforts to contribute to resisting the German aggression were for naught just because I do not have a specific item(Father's Watch) in my inventory. _childDocuments_.review: This game needs an insane amount of work to actually be good. The combat is truly awful. I get it: it's a horror game, so the combat needs to feel kind of unwieldy, unreliable, or used sparingly. But this game doesn't want that: it wants you to constantly be killing things to a point where it re-spawns enemies over and over. When those enemies die, it spawns gigantic rats in their place that you can only kill one at a time, and if they bite you you get poisoned which halves your HP. Given that you will be constantly backtracking through the game, you have to deal with this throughout. The game wants you to light bodies on fire, but nobody in their right mind playing this game will do this because you need to allocate 2 spots in your inventory for the lighter and fuel. It's like someone played The Evil Within and thought "that's cool, I want that" and then just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up completely. This game is really, genuinely, uniquely awful to play. I want to enjoy it, so I have spent, honestly, *way* too much time giving it chances, over and over, to get better. It doesn't get better, it just gets worse the longer you play. Chapter 4 is like the pulling finger nails equivalent of gaming. When you try to shoot things in this game, you'll magically miss shots because hit detection is not programmed correctly here. Enemies that run up on your character get these bizarre fast kicks which, in addition to locking you out of whatever you were doing, actually cause damage. It's death of 1000 cuts with this thing. Enemies can shoot around walls like it's Wanted and they're curving bullets, proving that the way in which combat was programmed here is completely incorrect. It's also not even a remotely scary game. It is what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying my time so far, it's a solid homage to its roots for better and for worse. If you're okay with the tediousness of early survival horror games then you'll be able to appreciate Conscript and I can highly recommend it to you. If you're looking for a straight up action or horror game, you might be let down. Conscript leans more into the survival and inventory management mechanics more than anything. The build up to parts of frantic action is well executed and the player truly feels like, well, a conscripted kid thrown into the hellscape of WWI. The combat feels as visceral as possible given the style and POV, but you do spend a lot of time just walking or digging around and sorting your inventory. I think that style of gameplay (e.g. Original Resident Evil) works and is a cool choice for a war story, honestly that alone is why I bought it and I'm not disappointed. Some things I love and want to give special recognition: -the combat, I love it and it's enjoyable enough to warrant repeating. It feels great in the context of the story and setting, it plays into the horror of the game.-the music and sound, I usually turn music off in games like this, but Conscript does an excellent job of knowing when to pull back and let the sound effects do the heavy lifting. The safe room music is great, I don't know why but that's important for me with games like this. The sound effects are solid, weapon sounds are jarring in a great way. -the art, I love it, it works. The cut scenes, enemy and world design, it's all great.-the story, I haven't completed it yet but thus far it's appropriately vague and striking enough for the genre. The big goal is laid out for you, but there's also a time spent in back story. Overall I think Conscript is an artistic, well designed ode to a classic and beloved era of survival horror. Games like this are why I love the indie scene.

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely great survival horror game that (for the most part) does not use any spiritual, occult, or any of the usual settings that are associated with the genre. This game is set during WW1 and some of the things you do in this game are downright harrowing. This was not a pleasant time, I really don't want to spoil the story but it is absolutely worth the playthrough for that alone. The gameplay is a bit hard to pin down. It's the classic Resident Evil item system with a unique aiming system that closes the aim the longer you aim like the newer Resi's but since its in a top down perspective it takes a bit more time to get used to but its well worth it since it gets the desperate feel down in tight quarters. There's a merchant and weapon upgrade system that works alright but there's one major flaw that kinda gimps it. You will pretty consistently be getting weapons but you use a finite amount of weapon upgrade parts that you cannot get back for new weapons and it takes more to upgrade higher tiers. This leads to an issue that the later weapons will rarely be able to outdo the earlier ones just on the sheer value that those upgrades are already spent. That's really my only gripe aside from maybe oppressively small inventory space. 1 playthrough for the average person would probably take about 15 hours but i was thorough so it took me 20. To me I'm happy at recommending it for a $20 price tag if you can get the DLC with it. That Golden Mauser is arguably my favorite pistol in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good classic survival horror with a few rough edges, but a fundamentally strong core.If you're a fan of classic Resident Evil gameplay, you'll definitely enjoy Conscript. Resources are limited, your inventory needs to be managed carefully, and enemies have the potential to remain a problem even after they're dead.Along with the wonderfully gritty low-res WW1 aesthetic, the thing I enjoyed most about Conscript was the combat. Much like all the other classic elements, it's intentionally cumbersome and awkward in the best possible way. Your aiming reticle will jump all over the place as you tremble in fear, enemies will shove you off balance while you try to aim at them, and you'll get overwhelmed and fumble your inputs as desperation mounts. It's the sort of combat that feels like a frantic trench warfare nightmare when you're panicking, but a satisfying strategic puzzle when you keep your cool.Everything is weighty and impactful, and the unique quirk of having to manually chamber many of your WW1-era guns between each shot adds a wonderful layer of tension that I grew to adore. It really does feel like a harrowing ordeal, managing to stay tense and satisfying from start to finish.With one exception (which I'll get to in a minute) the level design is also very good, the starting and ending chapters in particular. You'll find yourself looping around interconnected levels, unlocking shortcuts and collecting key items as you clear out segments of the map one at a time. If you manage your inventory well and only take what you need, progress is smooth, while overstocking on healing items or weapons will quickly leave you having to backtrack through areas where rats have started to chew on the corpses you left behind. The core survival horror loop is well executed, managing to cleverly adapt a lot of classic Resident Evil mechanics to a real-world setting.In terms of atmosphere, the game does a great job of treating its subject matter with respect while making room for some fun scares. Enemy soldiers will suddenly appear out of the darkness with the sound of hurried footsteps and breath huffing through a gas mask filter, and gloomy areas filled with gas, fire, and corpses make for some genuinely unsettling scenes. Yet when your enemies are dead, they'll sometimes drop photos of their loved ones or lie on the ground writhing in pain until you put them out of their misery. You can never feel good about yourself for too long before being reminded that there's nothing glorious about war. One thrilling set piece in particular really nails the terrified courage of a military charge, and there are several divergent points during which you have the opportunity to give in to fear and suffer the narrative consequences.One thing I wasn't initially that impressed with was the story; for most of the game, it's a very basic narrative about the main character trying to find his brother without much in the way of emotional investment beyond the basic horrors of war (which are admittedly effective). The endings, however, really struck an emotional chord with me and made up for it. I was fortunate enough to gather all the right clues for the “best” ending on my first playthrough, and it had my eyes watery when the credits rolled.There are a few minor complaints I have about the game, mostly just small things like the weapon upgrade system encouraging you to stick to a few guns rather than experimenting, a couple of scares being a little overused and predictable by the end, and the puzzles not being as prominent as I would've liked. Nothing major, but enough to shave off a point when compared to some other games that ooze polish in these areas.The only major issue is the mid part of the game, specifically the third chapter. The level design here is incredibly weak compared to the rest, consisting of lots of wide open areas and a long, tedious trek through the same unthreatening central path that makes backtracking a chore rather than a thrill. Walkable paths are also frustratingly indistinct from environmental obstacles here, resulting in a lot of rubbing your face against the scenery to figure out what you can access and what you can't. Besides a couple of cool setpieces, I honestly think the game would have been more enjoyable and better paced if chapter 3 were simply gone. It was a real blemish on the experience for me. I do respect that the developer experimented with something different here, but unfortunately it didn't work out.Overall, though, Conscript was a really enjoyable 8/10 classic survival horror for me. Not quite as tightly paced or thoroughly polished as some, and chapter 3 is an unfortunate low point, but everything else is great. The final level in particular was my favourite in the game, and the ending really stuck the landing. It starts strong, it ends strong, and the dip in the middle isn't big enough to sour the experience. A thoughtful and harrowing slog through the Great War with some lovely survival horror flavouring.

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT is a good game. The game mechanics are fun and intuitive. The story is interesting enough; you won't fall off your chair seeing it unravel, but I was curious to see where it was going. The graphics are pixelized, so it’s not about photorealism, but more of an art style, with that in mind, it’s a beautiful looking game. Really atmospheric! The sound design and music are excellent. I speak French, and we play as a French soldier among other French soldiers. I confirm, the French spoken in the game is good and realistic (French accent). Can’t say anything about the language of the Germans yelling at me though.  On the down side, even though I love multiple ending game stories, I don’t enjoy not having a clue what I’m supposed to do to trigger the events to get different endings. I ended up googling it and then I realized I’d have to replay since almost the beginning. So, Youtube it’s gonna be. Or may be a replay in a few years.Otherwise, some lock combinations are total mysteries. I’m talking about the one in Fort Vaux with the symbols on it… And one last thing. The inventory. A long rifle, a simple flashlight battery or even some bandages, they all take the same space in the backpack. I my case, I ended up doing A LOT of back and forth for equipment. That was kind of annoying. But I guarantee you, I know my way around the trenches of Fort Souville.I took me 20 hours for my first playthrough. Additional playthrough would only serve the purpose of getting different endings and achievements. So, even at full price, it’s worth it.In the end, I’d give it a good 8 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS] Conscript is a survival horror top-down game inspired by the classic Resident Evil. You play as André, a young French soldier fighting against the Germans in Verdun during WWI. However, your main objective is not really defeating the enemies, but rather bringing your brother Pierre (also fighting there) back home.The story is very interesting and emotional. It keeps you interested for the whole time and sometimes it can be heartbreaking. It definitely makes you think a lot about war and the atrocities of which humans are capable.The atmosphere is excellent: it doesn't need any supernatural elements, because the Great War was very scary by itself. The map is very well done and I love the art style.The narrative is great: telling the story of the characters indirectly with notes and memories, and alternating the trench warfare with flashbacks from before the war.The gunplay is a bit too simple: you simply aim, shoot and roll, being careful about the stamina and the ammunition. It's a bit clunky on purpose, which I think was a good choice to keep it realistic. The enemy types aren't too many, but after the first 2 chapters there are enough to keep it interesting. The guns are plenty, maybe even too much. You'll often run out of ammunition, but it won't be a huge deal. Overall it's fun.Outside of combat, your main activity consists of finding a way to go further and unlock more portions of the map, by finding keys to open doors or solving certain puzzles. This requires lots of backtracking, which is fun for a bit, but then starts to get very frustrating. Chapters 1 and 3 are very enjoyable, while 2 and 5 are probably the worst. Chapter 6 is also a pain in the butt, but I think that's appropriate for the last chapter.There are a two elements in particular that I found to be very annoying and bad for the gameplay: the field bag and the merchant.The field bag is you inventory, but for some reasons it has very few slots and even the things that you equip or wear (body armor, torch, guns...) fill the slots, making it very difficult and boring to manage the space. This element alone adds a ton of time to the already long backtracking experience, because you'll often have your bag full when you're about to pick up an important item, such as a key.The merchant is a guy that you can find in certain "safe rooms", where there are no enemies. You also find a chest to store your items and a table to save your game. While this is an interesting mechanic that adds variety and longevity, it simply makes no sense in this setting: why would a soldier fighting by your side sell you guns and other essential items instead of just giving them to you?! There is no explanation and it breaks the immersion. It might have made more sense to have certain civilians working as merchants that sold special guns and items, only in certain parts of the game (chapters 2 and 5 would be ideal). The whole "economy" of the game is boring and doesn't add much to the gameplay.I also didn't like the saving system and the score that the game gives you at the end of your run. I understand the elements I didn't like are a big part of the game and that they're inspired by other games that the developer probably loved, so I don't expect him to remove them. However, I feel like he should take notes for a future DLC or game: the same atmosphere and incredible story telling, without annoying elements and useless challenges would make a masterpiece.I loved playing this game and I keep thinking about it. However, after finishing it I watched a video to see all of the other endings (I got 3B I believe), and I was very disappointed in finding out that the "real" ending, which is beautiful and gives a lot more meaning to the whole experience, can only be unlocked only by solving a very difficult and hidden puzzle (pretty much impossible if you don't know about it before even starting to play the game). This is a shame and it should've just been the default, with a secondary ending being the "coward" one (which apparently gets triggered way too easily). Having 7 different endings is definitely too much and it can really be disappointing to play the whole game just to find out that a stupid mistake gave you a short and humiliating ending (the one I got was actually pretty good).There obviously are other small things that could be improved or implemented, such as the ability to place markers on the map. I think the developer should focus on polishing the experience and changing certain frustrating parts (remove some backtracking, add more space to the bag, keep fewer endings...), instead of completely changing the game by messing with bigger elements.Finally, the game right now is in a good state and I recommend playing it and supporting the developer (at least try the demo if it's still there). I really enjoyed it and I can't wait for a future DLC or something similar.

_childDocuments_.review: Speaking as someone who isn't super familiar with classic survival horror, I thoroughly enjoyed Conscript. The artwork is hauntingly beautiful. One of the stated inspirations for the environmental art is paintings about the war made by those who fought in it, and it certainly feels like I'm walking in one of them. It all contributes, with the sound design, to a particularly oppressive atmosphere, especially later in the game. So does the combat in my opinion; though perhaps cumbersome, which might be a turn-off for some, fights get messy and desperate, thematically appropriate for the setting. The game's horror begins to surface once it sinks in that everything you see really happened not too long ago in the grand scheme of things.I understand backtracking is a common issue people have with the game but I'm a sucker for exploration, taking in the world, and planning out routes, so this wasn't an issue for me. Certainly since the change to the rats, which happened before I played. I've still been meaning to replay, though haven't quite found the time yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the most unique World War I games I've ever played. I very much enjoy that this game offer a story with great historical immersion. I love that the game uses pixel, 32-bit graphics as its visual but with dark lighting and tones. I also find it very great that this game plays very similar in terms of puzzle solving and combat to be influence and inspired by Resident Evil. Some could call it Resident Evil Meets World War 2 but I call it CONSCRIPT. Overall I Highly recommend for any play to give this game a play, ESPECIALLY Resident Evil Fans. Overall I give this game a total of 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game.  The atmosphere is daunting with a sad and gruesome picture painted of what trench warfare during the battle of Verdun may have looked like from both a bird's eye view (that would be the player) but also gaining insight from the protagonist as well as other scraps of letters, diaries, propaganda pieces, characters, and even the weapons themselves.  Very few times have I actually felt terrible using a weapon against an enemy in a videogame of all places.  But seeing photos of families, brothers, wives, and children upon the bodies of the men I killed made me regret my choice to enjoy using weapons I acquired and upgraded.  If a man was injured rather than dead I felt no better but found myself in a psychological predicament.  Do I leave the man to suffer, calling for help and his mother, or finish the job and bring the rats out to feast?  The whole game really tripped me up like few games have but it was a very rewarding experience.The gameplay itself is very enjoyable with a surprisingly large array of weaponry to utilize from melee to range.  I don't even think I got every gun in the game and I had enough to fill up almost my whole inventory with weapons alone.  The puzzles were pretty mild with a couple that had me take a long time to think through.  Combat was mostly enjoyable minus the psychological repercussions.  The game does well to offer multiple ways to take on enemies from fire fights, stealth killing, or even pacifist runs.  It took me 15 hours to get through this game, being decently thorough about exploration and running back and forth through levels.  Some areas felt like they looped around pretty well while others were a bit of a slog given the limited stamina you have in the game.  I ended up getting ending 3A which was disappointing but expected given that it was my first try beating the game.  I may try a pacifist run in the future to see what I can get from that.  I played on normal difficulty with unlimited saves and checkpoints.  I understand it isn't how it was meant to be played and I found myself in situations where I was actually glad I had done this.The game caused my pc to blue screen on four play attempts just randomly while running from room to room.  IDK why or if anyone else has a similar issue but if not for my repeated saving I would have lost a lot of progress each time which probably wouldn't have kept me trying again.Aside from that the resource management felt good.  I never felt like I was low on anything so I think a harder difficulty is very possible to complete without much hassle,  I had more ammo and medkits than I knew what to do with.So overall it is a great game and I do recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Well, where do I even begin with this one?Conscript is a pixel survival horror game that takes place in WWI trenches and forts during the battle of Verdun. Scavenge for scarce supplies, bash Boche from behind on the head with a trench shovel or club, get eaten alive by rats, find a Chauchat that somehow doesn't get jammed from all the mud and then when you think it can't get any worse you come across a moldy baguette, causing you to break down and cry for an hour.Alright, alright enough let's get real now. The enemy variety and design are great, level design and atmosphere are perfect despite the reliance on frequent backtracking. Combat can be a little bit clunky and confusing at first, but it improves as you play. Also, the soundtrack is quite nice and fits its placement in the moments it is used. When it comes to the story, it is pretty decent and has multiple endings.Overall it is a great game that is worth its money and it shows that it was made with love and attention to detail.Ps: watch out for the German gorilla it really is a mad brute.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not really like or enjoy war games. But since it is a survival horror game, one of my favorite genres, I still wanted to give it a try. After playing, all I can say is this game knows how to create a tense atmosphere. It kept me going because I always wanted to know what happens next or for what I can use x item I've just found. I do understand the criticism about the bigness of the level. On the other hand: there is a fast travel option later on and well, it is set in WW1. It makes sense the world was created like this in my opinion. I personally did enjoy most of the riddles, some a bit more challenging than others, the ability to upgrade weapons and that exploration is rewarded most of the time. In the end, it is not only a survival horror title, it also showcases the true horror of war. This game does not glorify anything about it and it has my respect for it. War is not only a part of the past, it is still happening all over the world. It breaks my heart. So did the end of this game (it depicts war PTSD rather well, albeit briefly - for the ending I got at least, as there are several). It gives you information about the battle(s) in Verdun in the first World War and all the lives that were lost. It never ceases to amaze me what terrible things people can do to each other. I'm glad I played it because it not only kept me on edge, the visual design is spot on and it has a strong and important message. It depicts the humanity of soldiers, at the same time it doesn't shy away from the ugliness of it all. To me, it is a successful game.A small personal remark: Being able to understand both German and French was interesting as I could understand every word the soldiers said, either while attacking or once they were on the ground, wounded and helpless, crying out for someone to help them... was rough. As said, this game does not fool around (though it was sometimes funny how you can avoid enemies).

It's kinda more survival-dread or survival-despair than survival-horror though, so don't go into it expecting spooky scares.I don't really like combat or fighting enemies in games but found myself enjoying the weapons and tactics systems in place.I'll reiterate what everyone else finds to be a negative - the backtracking is uneccesarily convoluted. It didn't detract too much from the game for me, but it definitely didn't need to be like... that.I'd disagree with the what a lot are saying about the inventory management difficulty though - it's what you would expect with this type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: A really well  made game. Great mechanics, controls well, good enough enemy variety, and gets the atmosphere right that its going for. I'm really not into war stories, so that aspect didn't interest me much, but I do appreciate it for trying something new in the horror genre. It only really gets a bit typical horror vibe in the final few areas, other than that it's not really much horror.It keeps things fresh constantly with 5/6 chapters taking place somewhere new.I had to beat it over a long period, and I'm not eager to return for a good while, as like other reviews have stated it is very bloated and your purpose on what to do often isn't very clear.  It could use some more clever unlockable routes through areas to tone it down a bit as they are quite big, and not have so many mandatory things taking up inventory space.Overall a really great Survival Horror game that is worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great indie classic survival horror game set during WW1.If you're a fan of RE1-4 you'll probably really like this. Pros:- Standard classic survival horror gameplay with level design similar to RE1 and RE2.- Pretty lengthy for the price, 12-14 hours for a first playthrough with good environment variety (this took me by surprise).- Good replay value with NewGame+, multiple endings and the weapon upgrade system.- Very good sound design and soundtrack, as to be expected from this genre. - Merchant character!Cons:- A lot of backtracking - although I don't really think the individual level design is to blame here. I think because the game goes for twice as long as your average RE game it wears a bit thin by the end. It personally didn't bother me too much though. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Resident Evil and Metal Gear Solid from PS1 era, this game is a fantastic take on what I would Call War Survival. The Maps are large and detailed and there is alot of Puzzle Items and Keys, and well balanced Combat difficulty. Its not really a Horror game but the Enemies Cause a feeling of Dread like a Horror game. I won't tell you how to set the diffculty but with the Item management and planning required, I am glad to have unlimited saves enabled. On the standard difficulty, you will be challenged. I really like the camera style in these games because it is easy to learn your way around as the camera is always facing north. There are elements taken from Re2 Remake, for example you can replace damaged barbed wire to prevent enemies from re entering cleared areas. I highly reccomend this game, to me this is much better than what AAA games have become

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a great survival horror that doesn't rely on jumpscares or body horror to make the player feel unease. I recommend playing it on keyboard because using an analog stick for the 8-way movement of the character feels weird and more WASD intended.At first I didn't thought an horror game without monsters would scare me, so this game had already a big bar to surpass in order to make me recommend it. But I ended up enjoying more the whole experience this game provides (Exploration, Setting, Gunplay) instead of the horror side (But it still has crude or isolated scenarios!).First, I like that most of the guns require the player to manually eject spent rounds off the weapon in order to fire the next one, it makes the combat have more weight and stressful against the many enemies that will relentlessly pursue the player. Though I think the dodge mechanic is a bit overpowered for a Survival Horror game, if the player knows when to dodge, it can trivialize enemy encounters or make the game kind of silly. It's also amusing how all enemies are deaf to footsteps, like, I can get by past 2 or 3 soldiers running behind them and they would not turn around, but if I fire a single bullet every one and their mother will come to beat me to a pulp.Talking about sound, the SFX, the Soundtrack and the Ambience sounds are really really good, totally mandatory to play this game with a good headset.The game gives plenty of resources in the Standard difficulty, so the players are allowed to experiment most of the time with the resources they find around the trenches, but the Gun Parts used to upgrade weapons are really finite, so watch out not to spread too much of those on too many weapons. At the end in Standard difficulty I would end with much MUCH money that I don't have anything significant to spend on, if I could spend it on something, it would be more Gun Parts, but those are finite even in the shop, so the only way to spend this money would be in New Game+.Some nitpicks:-Ammo in the Storage Box won't stack automatically with the Sort button. One would have to grab the stacks of ammo from the Box, then put it inside again in one big stack.-The Torch Light, the Gas Mask and the Lighter are a chore to carry around (Specially in Veteran difficulty), at the end, the player either knows when to carry these items, or has to waste inventory space in them risking having to travel to the Storage Box multiple times. Like, okay, I have 100% Signalis before the QoL patch adressed the 6 slot inventory, and played RE1 Remake with Chris and it's pitiful inventory space multiple times. But Conscript has too many items that feel mandatory but aren't in many scenarios for a first time player, or someone that doesn't bother to write down which rooms need what. I am not asking to fix this right away, it's just a detail that bothered me a bit.Some bugs:-Playable character dissapeared one time in the safe room after interacting with the storage box, but would reappear after pressing the Aim button.-A couple of killed enemies ended up "T Posing" for the rest of the playthrough instead of laying on the ground.-One time a water SFX would stick for the rest of the gameplay between rooms in Fort Vaux, but resetting the game fixed this issue.This one scores an 8/10, great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've got probably less than an hour left before finishing, but I have a moment to leave a review and I don't really see my opinion changing as the experience has been fairly consistent from the start.It's kind of unbelievable that this game works for me. I love horror games, though I am sort of iffy on survival horror of yesteryear (I grew up with Resident Evil and Silent Hill, and I love their themes, but inventory management and overall difficulty with limited saving always kicked my butt). I'm a big fan of the genre, but many times I suffer some heartache while I'm struggling through the game.Conscript, on the normal difficulty, with limited saving turned OFF (glad this is an option) has been the perfect balance. It's challenging for a major portion of the game, and only begins to become a little easier (for me) around the final hours. It's also a horror game rooted entirely in reality, which is new for me. I'm a big fan of horror with monsters; here, the monsters are human. The atmosphere is stunning, and the gameplay is very satisfying despite not being particularly fresh. The game gives you plenty of space to move around, and I think that is a major difference in where it succeeds when others have failed. You'll find yourself in tight spots, but you'll always be able to move and find better positioning.I do have one major complaint, and that's that the game requires an unbelievable amount of retreading familiar ground. Large portions of the game are filled with backtracking, and sometimes you're getting a key to a room that just gets you a key to another room. This kind of design isn't fun (for me, anyway). It's become nearly a 10hr game for me, which is wild because the kind of gameplay involved really begs to be about 5-6hrs, I think. So much of the game is spent running from one spot to the next and checking the map 5x in between in order to make sure you're on track, or revisiting item boxes in order to make the most of your precious resources.It says a lot about the game that even with these fairly tedious issues, I'm still sucked in and drawn toward the ending. I -must- see how it ends. After such a harrowing journey for our character, I need closure just as much as they do. Conscript is a really tight experience, and it has multiple difficulty settings to make the game approachable for story fans and survival fanatics. I wish there was less trekking back and forth, as it really bloats the game more than it needs, but due to the sharpness of everything else around it, the good far outweighs the bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished "Conscript" a little while ago, with ending 3B.I'll start by saying that I appreciated the gameplay, the graphic style and above all the atmosphere that it manages to transmit to the player thanks to its beautiful story. It manages to make you identify with the protagonist and make you even remotely imagine what the people who actually lived through that terrible war had to face. Now let's talk about the flaws, I found "Conscript" really too much, I wouldn't say long, rather exhausting and in several points frustrating: an example being having to backtrack a lot of times, the difficulty in understanding just how to continue in the story... In some points I had to look at guides, because I really didn't know what I was missing to do, many times the reason was that I forgot some rooms or I forgot something in them, this was due to too many rooms, you have too many places to visit or visited and too many objects to collect and having to keep going to leave stuff in the trunks to be able to take them.Many times I WANTED to look at the guides to find the codes to unlock some chest or door or similar, this is because I was really too tired of having to go back and forth on the map, also with the problem of the stamina and slowness of the character. Honestly I would like to replay it because I would like to reach the ending 4 (obviously impossible to reach without looking at a guide, those codes to unlock it I have no idea where they are) not to mention the PRONGED KEYS to catch the pigeon at the end. I had recovered 2 out of 3 Pronged Keys and after hours of wandering around the map I decided to search on google where the last one was, well it was in one of the initial areas, now unreachable for me, this really bothered me honestly, making the best ending impossible without a guide is something that many games do and I never liked it. However, to conclude, I recommend the game and I rate it positively, despite all the problems encountered. I hope for a sequel, perhaps less punishing.P.S. Since I'm not the last of the idiots, before starting the game, I set the infinite saves and also the checkpoints, because the game smelled frustrating to me even before starting it. I made the right choice, without the Checkpoints and the Infinite Saves I don't think I would have reached the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The wait was worth it, I was very hyped for this game after playing the first demo back then and the updated demo a few months ago, and I wasn't disappointed by the full release at all. Conscript is a survival horror with a top-down perspective set in World War I and it follows the story of a French soldier looking for its brother in the trenches during the Battle of Verdun. I haven't seen this kind of setting in a horror game very often, as there are no monsters, ghosts, demons or anything like that, but it works tremendously well because having a real setting makes the horror much more poignant. The environments are absolutely fantastic, characters are well animated and the pixel art is top-notch, backgrounds have a lot of detail and perfectly convey the hopelessness, isolation and despair the soldiers who fought on that war must have felt. Some locations are based on real-life places, it might not be much but it was mind-blowing to me. The game also makes a fantastic job in making you believe you're fighting real human beings, forcing you to make hard choices and feeling terrible for it. There is little in the way of music, most of the time you will hear the sounds of distant warfare, but the sparse use of music makes it much more effective in key points in the game. The story of course is very emotional, and the several different endings (with somewhat cryptic conditions) provide much replayability.Gameplay-wise Conscript could easily be described as a top-down Resident Evil as the player must gather weapons, ammo and healing items while managing inventory space, solving puzzles, unlocking doors and trying to survive. In true Resident Evil fashion, some doors have multiple locks or require special thematic keys. This feels a little gimmicky and immersion-breaking but it works well and never becomes annoying or boring. The game is divided in chapters, each of which further expands the available locations and/or the existing maps, and the player can often return to previous regions looking for missing items. The game's UI is intuitive and easy to use, the maps are clear and helpful and previously collected notes can be accessed anytime. There is access to a shop providing ammo, items and weapons in exchange for cigarettes which are the game's currency. Some items can be combined with other items to craft more ammo or healing items. Valuables can be found throughout the game which can be sold in the shop in exchange for cigarettes.The player has access to melee weapons like axes or clubs that will break after repeated use and long-range weapons like pistols, rifles, shotguns and such, with the stronger weapons being available as the story progresses further. This results in a kind of progression in which the player becomes very powerful by end of the game, when facing many strong enemies at the same time becomes a necessity. There are several difficulty options available so Conscript could even be a good entry point into the genre. I played it in normal difficulty and I'd say the game is hardest at the beginning with few weapons and little ammo and gets easier the further you go, but it never becomes a cakewalk.Controls are good but might take a while to get used to as movement is very deliberate. There is a stamina bar that depletes while running or rolling to avoid enemy attacks, melee weapons have a winding animation, and guns need to be manually ♥♥♥♥♥♥ before firing again. All of this makes the combat very tense as the enemies are relentless and prone to corner the player if they can. There are lots of enemy types, some having melee weapons and some having guns, some being quick and agile and some being slow and heavily armored, so different weapons might be better suited to different encounters. Enemies do not respawn but corpses can attract the dreaded flesh-eating rats which can be far more dangerous as they are quick, pack quite a punch, and could even be poisonous reducing the player's max health. This can be prevented if the corpses are burnt using the limited oil the player has access to. NOTE: I heard the rats were nerfed a bit in a recent patch but I haven't tested it myself yet. The biggest hurdle for me was the inventory management, there are a lot of different items that can be combined in addition to the key items required to progress in the game, and the available space (which is quite large and can be further expanded) never feels enough, forcing me to backtrack a lot in order to find a magic trunk like in the Resident Evil games to swap items. Again, I heard this was addressed in a recent patch but I haven't tested it.Sometimes the main character will have to participate in large-scale battles against the German forces. These battles are incredibly epic and cathartic, often being quite difficult and requiring a lot of resources, and the actions taken by the player during these battles can greatly affect the ending. Even in these battles Conscript never stops being a horror game as these battles can be as stressful and scary as walking down a dark hallway with a couple of bullets left and hearing distant steps or grunts.In summary I strongly recommend Conscript to any survival-horror fan as its foundations are very solid and it is very engaging and gripping. Fans of war games might be drawn to it too but keep in mind that it is not an action game at its core, although it could be played like one, specially in the New Game+. A close comparison could be Signalis as both are top-down survival horrors strongly inspired by classics of the genre like Resident Evil and Silent Hill. Setting aside the obvious differences in aesthetic Conscript is more action-oriented and less puzzle-oriented than Signalis, enemies are harder to avoid, there are more weapons and ammo, and maps are bigger and can be revisited easily. The story and narrative are not nearly as complex and difficult but the general depressing and introspective tone is right there in both games, so Signalis fans might find Conscript interesting too. All in all Conscript is a fantastic game and anyone who finds its premise interesting should give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Just starting Chapter 2 as of this review, but already the game captivates me with its grim atmosphere and brutal combat. It really captures the horror of the First World War in a way other titles do not. The ever decaying corpses, the sounds of battle, the feeling of constant dread, soldiers having mental breakdowns while others wail out in pain from having lost their legs. As you find yourself lost in a network of trenches the Germans are ever ready to cleave you with a trench shovel, pierce you with bullets, or incinerate you with dreaded flamethrowers. If the Germans don't get you, then the rats will look to satiate their hunger with your flesh. You'll press on however, trying your best to survive as so many others did over 100 years ago during that gruesome conflict. You must, for the Germans shall not pass!(Here's to hoping for story DLC's with new weapons and costumes!)
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression is that its immediately apparent that this game was developed with a labor of love. The game is dripping with dread and desperation that the great war was known for. With a similar dark atmosphere to greats such as "Blasphemous" and other 'souls likes', it plays almost like an homage to "Resident Evil" as well as 'metroidvainia' style games, yet it manages to have it's own identity among the games that it draws inspiration from. It even includes some nice puzzles to solve (some optional), that reminds me of exploration games like "Myst", and all this while telling a unique and gripping, (if not somewhat interpreted) story that reminds me of Indie games like "Lone Survivor" or "Neo Scavenger".For the price (if you like these kinds of 'difficult' games that require you to plan your routes, read notes, and remember map/environment details), this is a must buy!
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a good little survival horror title, and definitely pays homage to the classics of the genre. I do entirely recommend the game, it is fun, has decent play time for the price and is interesting. I completed the game on Veteran (hardest dif iirc) with no checkpoints and limited saving, this definitely added a challenge to the game in addition to the genre. There were elements of back tracking, rats and combat that did irritate me at times. There was some tedium in elements of back tracking that felt unnecessary however I believe this has been addressed. The rats whilst slightly toned down and edited in ways to make them less of an issue, still just feel unnecessary to me and made for extra back tracking to deal with them. There was parts of combat where it felt like shots weren't hitting despite aiming to full accuracy, or dodge rolling wasn't dodging the attack properly unfortunately. These might have been fixed, but they also didn't stop me from playing as these were few and far between for the most part, I haven't played since fixes / updates were done. The game is well made, There are multiple endings (I watched the ones I didn't get after completing the game) which do hold a sentimental note to them. Not really sure what causes each ending, I got shellshock and whilst I know a little of what to do for each ending, I don't know everything and you're kind of on your own until you get the ending, I didn't realise until about halfway through that there might be a trigger for a different ending. Yes I recommend the game, yes I think its worth it, yes I believe its very well made and you should check it out if you're a fan of the genre and/or setting. I had been waiting since the first steam next fest demo for CONSCRIPT to release, and it didn't let me down.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I have been going back and forth on how to approach this review, as it is the first game to genuinely move me enough to want to write a review. As someone who has been playing survival horror since diapers, I can feel the love not only for the game itself, but for the genre as well. It has it's own unique gripes I'll get into, but for me personally, I can get past them. The atmosphere the game creates is haunting and the survival horror genre is a perfect fit for the setting. The art is, I think, the perfect style for this kind of game. Clear enough to get some slight details, but hazy enough for your mind to fill in the blanks. The audio design is also great in the context of survival horror as well. Being submerged in darkness and hearing metal jangling towards me was terrifying. I am worried about ever visiting germany now because I genuinely think I am conditioned to trigger fight or flight when I hear faint german yelling.  It does have some pacing issues, the mid-game kind of dragged a little bit, but the environment eased that for me personally. I would concede that the length could be cut down, but I also feel like all the areas could easily work and flow smooth if they had some adjustments. Some weapons only being accessible in the late game when it is sort of redundant to invest in a brand new weapon doesn't exactly feel the greatest, . However, the upgrade system as a whole is a major plus, the firepower upgrades specifically are very tangible and noticeable throughout a playthrough. I've noticed a lot of complaining about the backtracking, not sure if it is just people who aren't familiar with the integrated tedium associated with the classic survival horror it is inspired by. I did not mind it personally, there was only like one chapter was particularly bad with it, but overall I didn't think it subtracted from the experience with the correct expectations. Nothing really felt puzzle-ey though, which I think the game could have benefited from in terms of variety. The clunky combat is definitely a like it or you don't situation. I never had many problems with hit registration personally and the few misses I did have just added to the experience. I have pretty good aim but even I do not expect every shot to hit; I do think most of the criticism relating to the hit reg is just a skill issue tbh. The shakiness of the crosshair could be explained to some degree, I thought I had a bug when I first really noticed it. I don't really have anything to say about the enemies, as ironic as it is to say that about a survival horror game lmao. The rats were annoying. very annoying. They did serve their purpose and created good moments for me throughout the game though. Even in the later chapters when I didn't take care of them as much, I just rolled through them all. No biggie. The human enemy variety feels lacking I suppose; Then I think about RE7 (my beloved) and it only had like 3 molded types. Conscript overall is a notable, competent, and well-crafted addition to modern survival horror, even in a genre where you have to stand up to the likes of Signalis. I wholeheartedly believe that this game will age like a fine wine and stand the test of time.

_childDocuments_.review: While not perfect, I would still recommend playing through Conscript. _childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript, in my honest opinion, has to be one of the best survival horror games i’ve ever played, because not only does it succeed in emulating the classics it takes its inspiration from (Resident Evil and Silent Hill specifically), but also utilizing the sheer horror that comes with the WW1 setting to its fullest potential, which all makes for a grimy, horrifying and even borderline nightmarish depiction of the great war (and just war in general), without needing any zombies OR supernatural elements. But enough talk, let's actually get into what this game entails, eh poilu?
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Game was fantastic. I was constantly blown away by how well this achieved the classic survival horror feel while still being something wholly unique. The puzzles were smart and the combat is chunky. In the beginning I kept convincing myself some kind of monster was going to pop out and I had to keep remembering it’s genuinely just WW1.  I feel like something was lost when I realized there wasn’t going to be any supernatural horror, but the game more than justifies this as it goes on. The setting is unrelenting and its commitment to the horrors of war are admirable. Genuinely loved this game. It’s shockingly long for an indie solo game but I don’t feel like it ever overstayed its welcome. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a good game. The theme is strong, the combat is fun and the Resident Evil influences are everywhere. I would say this game is the child of RE1 (Item boxes, limited inventory, etc.) and RE4 (merchant, weapon upgrade system) and even tho that sounds weird it managed to pull that off just fine. But it's definitely more on the "kill enemies everywhere" than on the "save your resources as much as you can" side. Unfortunately it is plagued by some big flaws.The good:- Theme: This game manages to confront the big topic WW1 in a mostly mature way. The horrors of war are present in every second of this game. There are mostly no supernatural elements to this, which I liked a lot.- Combat: I think it has to be your cup of tea but it definitely was for me. Combat feels slow, somewhat clunky but also impactful and stressful, just like it should be in this setting.- Weapon variety: This really surprised me, there are so many weapons here with obvious upgrades. Shooting at guys never gets old.The bad:- Missing/weak puzzles: Maybe I'm a bit biased because I started this game right after Crow Country which has a lot and amazing puzzles. But Conscripts puzzles feel a bit weak compared to other survival horror games.- Backtracking (Chapters 3 and 5): Oh boy, the backtracking in this one is strong. A bit of backtracking is normal and expected in survival horror, but holy damn chapters 3 and 5 drag on forever because there is soo much damn backtracking. I've heard people complaining about chapter 3 being the worst one but for me it definitely was chapter 5. I almost gave up on playing in that chapter.- "Supernatural" stuff: I think the last chapter started to feel a bit off. All those chasms etc. were the first time in the game where I thought to myself "yeah no this is definitely not the intended realism the game tried to have all this time". Maybe it's supposed to be like that in a way like Andre is slowly imagining stuff but still I thought it's weird.- Playtime: Maybe I'm weird but I took ~ 12 hours to complete this game on "Soldier" (standard) difficulty. And for me for a survival horror game that is way too much. Combine that with all the backtracking and the result is a game which definitely overstays its welcome.The meh:- Difficulty: This one is very subjective because I played on standard and not on hard difficulty but even for standard there were wayyy too many resources everywhere. I basically drowned in stuff.- Terminator style: Again maybe this is a me problem with the chosen difficulty but I basically was the terminator in the last chapter. Invading an enemy base all by myself with a huge battle in the end in which I shoot like 30 guys? When I'm just a guy who went through hell at that point already? It starts to feel a bit silly at that point.Overall I think if the game would cut out the bad backtracking parts, shave off a bit of the runtime and maybe be grounded a bit more in realism when it comes to the endgame fights this game would have been amazing.For a first time project by mostly one guy this is very good already but I'm sure Conscript 2 would have the potential to not only be good but great.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is that kind of game that i would play again and again without problems.The story is quite simple, yet meaningful and touching. Multiple endings which is a great point and a lot of "old" Resident Evil games mechanics that i greatly appreciate. Overall, a great and refreshing experience, would recommend 100%!As a french who lives near Verdun, thank you for this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed my time with this. Captures the flow and feel of original resident evil games focusing on exploration, puzzles, and punchy and impactful combat. The trenches and forts of WWI provide an interesting twist on the survival "horror" genre. I wouldn't say this game is particularly frightening, but it does a good job of maintaining a tense atmosphere and dark tone.My only real criticism is that the intentional unreliability of gunplay can lead to some pretty frustrating moments, especially given the aggression and speed enemies have. The top down view sometimes conflicts with aiming in an awkward way where you miss shots that should be sure thing.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a monumental accomplishment for a single developer's first game. Conscript charts new ground for the survival horror genre by taking tried and true survival horror mechanics like inventory management, backtracking, puzzle solving, and route planning and seamlessly transplanting them to the WW1 setting. There's nothing supernatural, no horror-tropes, not a single zombie here, just raw horrors of war and it totally works. The scope of the game is impressive too with my first playthrough clocking in over 14 hours. And that was pretty much all gameplay with a great flow to it. I never really got stuck or had to repeat excessive amounts of playtime. There's replay value too with unique challenges, different endings, and harder difficulties to go with some cool unlocks. For $20, this is an easy recommendation for any survival horror fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I would definetly recommend the game and buy a sequel in heartbeat.  i rate it 8/10I really enjoyed my experience with "Conscript", it was a good survival horror, in a setting that is rarely used in a survival horror, do not  expect any supernatural concepts but only  the horror of war. The idea of having enemies dropping pictures that provide a window in their lives before the war or before action was an amazing idea. Also, the ambiance and mood the game creates is really great in a dark depressing war style. The game in summary is a combination of Resident evil 4 and Silent hill and a bit of metroidvania. Most of my grips are the combat which is mixed sometimes i felt like a direct hit would not register well. I also didn't like the whole Pierre story. I felt like the game didn't do a good job at making me care. An idea would have been to make us play as Pierre or maybe unlock a Pierre Scenario (Future DLC ?)  Also the camera in the game sometime felt like it was not helping especially between room. I would suggest inspiration from a game like "Signalis" for a sequel  with a angle view points maybe some first person switch here and there could be nice as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I try to always wait until I have finished the game before writing my review since it usually the ethical way of doing so but I feel like I should just get my thoughts out before I inevitably push this game further back into my back log. Conscript is a love child of 90s horror nostalgia with a twist, where instead of facing the unimaginable horrors of zombies or mutants, you're instead faced with the very real horror of WWI, a war that left a bloody mark in the history books as unforgiving and horrific, with enough causalities that would render a menial kill-streak from CoD as a joke. Young men sent to fight a grown-ups war, and Jordan Mochi capitalized on these themes with beautiful accuracy with all the hallmarks of old school survival horror in mind. Limited resources, puzzles, and enemies that you're better off avoiding. Hell the reason for me putting it off for long now was because I lost an hour and half of progress due to me trying to keep my ink pellets (ink ribbons from the OG Resident Evil) in stock. Conscript doesn't hold an punches, if you're familiar with the literary work "All Quiet on the Western Front" you will feel right at home, and for Jordan's first game it's a stand-out and welcomed surprise in the survival horror space, one that's original as well as paying homage to the classics that built the genre, I highly recommend it alone on those merits.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down the best game I have played on my Steam Deck. Runs and plays perfectly on the handheld. As for the game, I haven’t been this hooked on playing for years. 30 hours in and the campaign still keeps giving. The survival horror elements, complex puzzles, audio and story make this game one of the best of this style I’ve ever played. A sincere thankyou to the developer for the many years of hard work he put into this title. I hope he continues to support this game with additional content moving forward, I will buy whatever he puts out.

_childDocuments_.review: The developer has superseded mere gaming to create a masterful anti-war story. Few reviews mention the game's story, which is understandable because the story is sparse. Yet the environmental cues are unmistakable. Your slain enemies drop photos of family and intimate childhood memories. Your fallen foes writhe in pain and beg for mercy. You read journals from French mothers who send their boys off to die in the Great War. And there is, of course, the protagonist's own story--another war-torn family, imperiled brother, and brokenhearted mother.I ultimately ended up playing, and enjoying, Conscript much more for its environment-driven narrative than the actual gameplay. Indeed, there is much about the gameplay to dislike: linear, frustrating hit boxes, monotonous backtracking and map looping, lack of weapon and enemy variety, low replayability, and so on. But none of these flaws are severe enough to dilute this game's poignant and compelling lesson.

So I hope to see another game from this developer with a better balance of sadge and cheerfulness.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this on Standard Difficulty with limited saves. I enjoyed this game very much, I thought the story was gripping and the gameplay kept me on my feet. Not to mention I enjoyed the puzzles; this was the first time in a while I solved most if not all the puzzles on my own. I found that enough information was given for these puzzles let me figure out what the solution is or what I need to solve it. Except for 2 instances, 1 was a reminder that I had the solution with me the whole time. The last one being well the "secret".My only real complaints:- At the end of chapter 1, there was huge jump in difficulty. I understood what they were going for but it pushed me towards frustration. However, I played this area before the first patch. For all I know it may have been toned down.- Sometimes the geometry of the area, lighting and pixelated characters made it difficult to aim. Whether I used alcohol to steady my nerves or not in game. Few times the shots I missed surprised me. Didn’t happen enough to ruin my fun. If I had to guess maybe 5 times?- It would be nice if you could combine items while in the item box. I was a pack rat and hording as much as I could. _childDocuments_.review: Where to even begin, The art and atmosphere paint a fantastic portrait of the horror that this game is intrinsically trying show. the showing rather then telling pays off amazingly, with a feast for the eyes presented with every new area, the map and exploration is tight with small dark spaces and open areas providing a tremendous amount of dread.initially the inventory management has a bit of a steep curve.but by the mid and late game you'll find it much easier to navigate and have a good understanding of what you need and what you do not need.my only complaint is that back peddling and having to run back two or three times due to a lack of inventory space is more tedious then scary, rarely was I ever in an area i was worried about sneaking back threw as it was safe and remained safe, but recent patches seem to have fixed this problem, but i am yet to try for myself. with everything said, this game is a fantastic survival horror, i can see both the casual and hardcore fan enjoying this game and think in years to come this game will be considered the perfect fit for those wanting in on the genre. TLDR: a gem of game that has come polished and with a bow, you do yourself a disservice by not experiencing it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like this game was made for me!!This game in the amalgamation of all the best mechanics of the Resident Evil saga, it has aspects like -fight or fleee situations, -having to burn bodies to avoid another enemy, -maze-like map with backtracking, -vaults, -a merchant to buy, sell and upgrade, -treasures to be combine and sold-and some heavy action sections and they are mixed perfectly in a WWI setting, making the gameplay addicting.I used to hate 3rd person games with mouse aiming, especially with top down view, but the encounters are a little slow and methodical, you really have to think wether to kill or run, so the gameplay was very smooth for me.The setting and story are quite simple but effective, it shows the horrors of war and sometimes it makes you feel really bad after killing someone, it is a simple good message overall.However, the game being a love letter to Resident Evil also affects it in a negative way.What I mean is that the game sometimes looks and feels a little goofy, the rolling boulders are a nice reference but it doesn't match the setting, also the movement of trucks running looks a little cartoony and enemies being tanky AF it's a little ridiculous.But I wouldn't change that, just the trucks animation.I played this since day one so I got the glitched ending the dev mentioned, so I will have to play again to get different endings, I pretty much explored everything except in chapter 6 which I think they are for the different endings, I also encounted some glitches, like the flamethrower guys getting stuck in corners, the fire glitching visually when the flashlight is on and I aim to the fire.Hopefully the rest of the glitches will be fixed and I totally recommend this game, it's such a gem and I hope there's more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A top down 2-D survival horror. Mostly made by one guy set in WWI battle of Verdun. This game is masterfully made. Not because it's perfect and unblemished, but because it sets a game in WWI where there are no monsters, no supernatural elements, just war. This setting is so damn difficult because it's not something you can make a heroic story out of. It was the bloodiest and most catastrophic loss of life in human history. Even in game the 'enemy' are the Germans, but they aren't boogeymen, they're human beings that carry pictures of home and cry out for their mothers when you defend yourself against them. This game so accurately showcases the desperation, cruelty, and savagery of the conflict that by the time you end your 13 hour or so long run you won't say that the Germans are the villain. The war itself is the villain. Gameplay wise it's not perfect. The combat is a bit clunky, there's an absolute ♥♥♥♥ ton of backtracking (especially if you get lost), and many of the puzzles have very esoteric solutions to them that are more frustrating than clever. HOWEVER. for 20 dollars you can't do much better. I am so excited to see what Jordan does next, and I'm terrified to play it. Gods above help us if he makes a WWII game next... then we're ♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: It is weird how few horror games are based around world wars, isn't it? Conscript is an amazing horror game even for those who don't like horror. Even though the game plays like a survival horror game, it isn't scary. Instead, the atmosphere and the gameplay fits the setting perfectly.The only complaint I have about the game, which the dev hasn't fixed yet, is the targeting system. When you start aiming a weapon, the game displays a crosshair to show which direction you are facing. This is handy when you are aiming a gun, but if there is an enemy next to you, the game might target the enemy no matter where you try to shoot. This can be annoying when you want to shoot an explosive barrel instead. Aside from that issue, the only "complaints" are just nitpicks. There could be a bit more puzzles which require you think and a bit less ammo for the weapons. I wish the protagonist wasn't mute and commented a bit more when you interact with objects (just like with any other non-Parasite Eve 2 survival horror game). None of these nitpicks have been actual issues though and the game is 100 % worth playing despite them.

_childDocuments_.review: Bar none the best World War One Game ever made; an excellent example of edutainment; and as haunting as some of the great depression simulators like Ready or Not and spec ops the line. It honestly is one of the best explorations of violence in the medium I’ve seen in quite a while.   It can be a difficult beast to love at points; but the brilliant use of classic Resident Evil/Survival horror design and glorious PS1 art style really helps sell the sheer cruel barbarity of the historical event; with enough QOL changes and tight controls to make is work for a modern audience. Puzzles are legible, mostly diegetic and don't require 4th dimensional autism to beat and think the pacing is good for most of its run.  Highly recommend this; Can wait to see what this developer does next.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a retro stylized survival horror, in the vein of old school Resident Evil games, but played from the top-down camera perspective. Its also mostly one-man project, 7 years in the making. I am happy to say its a resounding triumph in the survival horror genre.Conscript is very dedicated to its retro roots, but thankfully it implements a wide variety of quality of life improvements for a smoother experience. You'll be upgrading your weapons, expanding your inventory space and extending health and stamina meters throughout the game. Best of all: it will discard keys that have no more uses, single greatest mechanic introduced in this genre.I recommend playing this game on controller since mouse and keyboard controls are a bit weird and stiff. Combat in Conscript is surprisingly good for a top-down perspective game. There is a wide variety of weapons at your disposal and many of them require manual control of the bolt action mechanism to load next bullet, I really liked it and it added to the pressure of combat. Using melee weapons is just as satisfying and you can even sneak up on the unaware enemies to hit them for increased damage. Combat feels brutal and intense, with agressive enemies that beeline for you while raspily shouting in German. Overall oppressive atmosphere is helped by strong sound design and grimy, pixelated visuals of the whole game.Its hard to describe why this game gets under your skin so much. Graphics are one thing, but the feeling of danger is ever present, the soundscape is never silent, you can always hear some screams or explosions in the background and it keeps you on your toes. Enemies can ambush you, filthy rats will fill the corridors if you leave the bodies of killed enemies without burning them or blowing up ratholes. You will explore pitch black corridors, filled with deadly gas, with only tiny lamp lighting the way and gas mask reducing your stamina.Conscript constantly hits you with the horrors of war. There is no real jumpscares or supernatural themes and still it manages to keep you tense. Sometimes when you kill enemies they drop photos of their loved ones, its bloody haunting. Your crosshair will get increasingly shaky the more people you kill and the more horror your character experiences.I managed to get a 'good' ending and to be honest, it struck a cord in me I didn't know I had. Theme of pointlessness of war is nothing new and has been done before, but the psychological grinder Conscript puts you through makes you so vulnerable by the end, that I got a 'bit' emotional when the credits rolled.Conscript is a must play game for any survival horror fan or just for anyone looking for a tightly designed experience that explores horrors of World War I. I can't begin to imagine the dedication this game's developer Jordan Mochi has and I truly hope it pays off for him. Congratulations and kudos to you sir.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best survival horror game I've played since signalis which is one of my favorite games period. And knowing that one guy did all of this is insane to me. _childDocuments_.review: excellently blends the tropes of classic survival horror with a gritty, gut-punching narrative. The way the game subverts your expectations in organic ways, such as  Or how I did find there were some pacing issues toward the middle-late game if you wanted to min-max and pick every item up and play cautiously, however, in the first major patch pretty much all my gripes were addressed. As with any game in the  style survival-horror genre, it is still down to the player with how slow/boring and cautious/tedious they play, but it is entirely beatable playing as reckless and/or pacifist as you want. Given the various endings and freedom of playstyle allowed by the structure of the game’s obstacles,  suits itself well to multiple playthroughs. There is a weird tonal balance with how much deference the game has towards its subject matter, with a narrative that, while simple, is one of the most effective video game stories I've seen, and the gamification of some elements. To at one point have an emphasis on the real nature of PTSD and the mental struggles veterans experience, and then to also have achievements like "War Criminal: Kill 2 enemy soldiers with one shotgun blast" or "Who Needs Artillery?: Kill 4 enemy soldiers at once with an explosive barrel", I wouldn't call it outright offensive but it definitely feels like an unearned dissonance. I can appreciate the need for levity, and there are humorous moments in the game directly, such as the propaganda or some of the dialogue, but it nonetheless feels too game-y. Such is also the case with the merchant and the borrowed exchange of treasure for upgrades and supplies. The  games got away with the suspension of disbelief surrounding so many of its more absurd mechanics because they were often ludicrous zombie games about evil mad scientists and cartoonishly corrupt mega-corporations, it's all so camp. Having the same framework applied to something which seems to want the player to take it more seriously, at least in a narrative context, begs for a consistent approach. Not to say the game isn't allowed to be fun, or take video game-y shortcuts, as an act of respect for its portrayal of the harshness of war (although you could make that argument if you want this to exist as more than a commercial product). I don't feel as though  is intending to make a political message in terms of the validity of the war itself, or at least the individual agency of any one soldier, let alone a conscript. People had to kill each other, for the most part you are expected to kill NPCs in the game. And the game goes to lengths to show the mental effects of such a scenario. However, letting the player revel in the slick game feel of some of the weapons, creating obstacles where enemies just happen to be having a chat right in front of a mounted gun, it’s a bit too indulgent. Creating longevity and replayability in the game with additional difficulty modes with extra challenge, with ranking at the end of the playthrough, where each subsequent playthrough would have less and less appreciation for the tender moments the game has to offer and is instead a problem to solve as fast and efficiently as possible. Its as though the game wants to have its cake and to eat it too. Which, to be fair, is par for the course for video games,  is one of the best examples of actually investigating this dissonance, but given it feels to only go halfway is what makes it particularly disappointing in that respect. Overall, I would definitely recommend  if you are looking for a fun twist on classic survival horror with a great narrative. If you liked this game and are looking for more new survival horror, I recommend , if you haven't played it already, for its intriguing sci-fi narrative and similar love of the genre.If you liked this game and are looking for more games that integrate the player-character's mental state with gameplay, I recommend  for its tender narrative surrounding depression and self-acceptance combined with an excellent 2D platformer.
