_childDocuments_.review: After playing this title since the very first game, I was extremely pleased to see it finally come to PC. Although not everyone's cup of tea, I'll provide some pointers to anyone less familiar than I;Graphics - 5/10 (Passable, not great, but fine for a lower-budget cycling sim, little to no change year on year)Gameplay - 8.5/10 (A few issues regarding difficulty I'll touch on after, but overall they have made significant improvements through the years to the point where it's very natural and very fun, with tutorials for those less experienced)Modes and in-game - 9/10 (There is genuinely so much to do, whether you want to create your own rider and get from a cycling noob to a Tourmalet king, or create a team from scratch, or use a real-life team, there are so many things to keep you wanting to play!)My main issue regarding this game in particular is the difficulty is either way too easy or way too hard at times. I struggle to get away from the peloton at the start of a stage to form a breakaway, as despite being over 20 minutes down on the General Classification, I am somehow a threat to them and they chase me down brutally. All this for them to run out of steam on the final climb and end up 3 minutes behind me. This hasn't been as noticeable in previous iterations on PS4 so I cannot say for 100% sure if this is a real issue or not, but for my hours of play it has persisted. (Will update review after I play more if this changes) I also believe that this game could do with some integration with Pro Cycling Manager, I can only dream of going from sitting back and managing the team, to hot-swapping into the saddle myself for the closing stages of the Tour!All in all, providing you get past the initial difficulty of learning the mechanics, and hitting the difficulty sweet-spot, this game provides an excellent strategic challenge, and can be one of the most tense and exciting sports games I have played as a result! The achievement of getting a rider from a 65 overall, to finally pulling away from the pack on Mont Ventoux 3 seasons later is a feeling that few games replicate as well as this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Tour de France 2020

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a cycling fan and like the Tour de France! This game will put you on the run to get ahead of the peloton. Even if you never participated in a Cycling race event the ordeal, the sweat the pain and tears and its details you will have fun and learn how difficult it is to be the champion of this incredible tournament. This game is just incredible in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: Tour de France 2020

_childDocuments_.review: Few things to say:- No energy management by AI - They either go full out until blow up, or basically stop riding so they can regain energy. Simply stupid to see on some mountain stages where peloton goes hard for like 15 km only to basically stop for final 3 km before summit.- Predictible - after riding like 3 TdF you can easily tell where breakaway is going to be caught, where breakaway can actually go away, what time will breakaway have at specific moment of stage(!)... (amazing "blockade" on some stages on 5 minutes mark, like 50 km of racing when time difference neither goes higher or lower than 5 minutes). Heck, on almost every single stage there is a certain "scenario" going on. And it repeats every single TdF. Fun, for sure...- Stupidity of AI - Yes, AI in this game is simply stupid. F.e: Direct Energie "chasing" breakaway for first flat 60 km on Colombier stage... with all 8 riders... not letting breakaway having more than 30 seconds. No matter how many riders are in it or what riders...  Only to have one of TDE riders to attack after it and join breakaway. Yep. Every. Single. Time.- Create your own rider - Yep, that's negative. If you want to do so, buy PCM, not this game. Stat increase is basically impossible at higher difficulty. And I mean only Champion by that. You pick climber for example. When you reach an amazing 68 in mountain, the only way for this stat to increase is by either winning mountain stages(!), or winning at least 2nd category climbs(!!). I want to ask anyone who was creating this game. How you are supposed to do so with rider with 68 MO? You can't increase your stats unless you're winning. Can't win having that low stat. And no, decreasing difficulty isn't an option. Unless you want to play on amateur and win Tour with... I don't know... Ben Hermans for example.- No crashes of riders. At all. I completed like 50 different TdF so far. I saw only one rider having crash. One. And it was most random crash I have ever seen in my life.- Real time weather (rain / wind) is basically non existent. Oh, you say there are some sectors with potential wind? If only it was possible to actually do something in those sectors... like splits for example. _childDocuments_.review: At it's best, Tour de France 2020 is actually a good game.  But as much as I'd like to sing it's praises, in it's more or less 'finished' state this year I cannot.  This series still feels more like a tech demo than a finished game.The main game modes (Pro Team/Leader) set you up for failure, because at first you have access to so few events that you can't achieve the ranking you need, unless you achieve unrealistically good results for your relative team strength.  Even then, you're still at the mercy of the simulation in races you can't compete in.  And in pro leader specifically, getting your rider into breakaways is a nightmare, especially when the peloton adamantly refuses to let a larger group dangle.If you get through the early game hell, what you're left with is still a game with less depth than Cyanide's other cycling game, PCM.  TDF does have an advantage in gameplay, as well as how it handles race day condition (seriously, what were they thinking with PCM 20?), but PCM is simply better when it comes to everything that happens between races.Even then, TDF wouldn't be getting a negative score from me if not for the fact that the developers recently gave the console versions of the game a major update... and failed to provide that update to PC players.  I don't understand why we were denied this update.  We're paying customers just like the console players, and maybe multiplayer was too hard to implement on PC this year, but surely they could've at least given us the rest of the update?Unfortunately, that lack of support sapped my interest in trying to overcome the pro team/leader early game and have fun with it.  If you still want this game, try to get the console version.

_childDocuments_.review: Tour de France 2020 is a unique and interesting experience, but falls in between two potential great ideas. The end result is a mediocre racing game and a mediocre team engagement game. I'm going to divide this into two parts, one for the concept and design aspects and one for the technical. - Design -The thing to be aware of going into Tour de France is that it is much more focused on energy conservation and long term strategy than it is on "racing".  The core strategies in the game are about drafting behind other racers to save energy, coasting down hills, eating snacks at key moments, holding the "Follow" button for long stretches and not wasting energy trying to lead the pack except where it'll score you points. (Racing at full speed or leading at the front of the pack will fully drain your energy in a matter of minutes)The game DOES shine on that front. There is a mental aspect to the racing that actually can feel really good.But, if you check my achievements, you'll notice I didn't even get the "Finish one race" achievement despite having played this for almost two hours. I currently have a middle-of-the-race save, 40 minutes into the first stage of a race.  The tour de france is 21 stages long. Awarding 10 XP per stage, I would need to play for almost 10 hours to reach level 2.This meant that I spent far more time using the "Simulate Race" option. But at this point, it lacks any meaningful interaction. You don't make any strategy decisions, no training, no race priorities, or really any decisions at all.  You just click through simulation menus and get insulted by the narrator for being a letdown.This is made worse by the simulation options being terribly user unfriendly. Even when my rider can compete in 2 races throughout the year I need to manually simulate through all 12. "You did not complete any goals this month... *press okay to continue* NO KIDDING... I couldn't race this month but you still made me click through this!  The end result leaves me craving either a competent racing game or a full-on simulation.  At the very least, when I'm holding the "Follow" button for an extended period it should speed up the game. Holding one button and watching the game for five to tend minutes straight kills any of the high points in the concept.- Techical - Long story short, It's crap. Long story long, It reminds me a lot of the ultra-low budget racing games.The constant bane to my fun was that driving into the grass immediately brings you to a stop. If you even get to close to the side of the road it acts like you hit a bus as you either pinball or stop entirely. You end up needing to stay near the middle of the road just to avoid the jank physics. I've also had major inconsistencies with performance.  - The first time I played, it would stutter every time a tree or NPC spawned in front of me.  - The second time I played it ran pretty smoothly and I realized the controls weren't as broken as they originally felt. - Every time I've played its been a gamble of whether it'll work smoothly or not. This is not a pretty enough game to perform as bad as it does.Finally, it's worth noting that you cannot play with a Keyboard or Mouse and there is no meaningful graphics settings. It's a bare minimum port at the very best and kindest review.  - - -There is probably an audience for this game and there isn't much competition in the cycling game field. But do yourself a favor and at least wait for a very deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd start this review by asking a question: "Do you enjoy cycling and following professional cycling?" - if, like myself, the answer is "Yes!" then you will probably enjoy this game. If not, it might not be for you because it isn't exactly an arcade game, in my opinion its more a simulation of cycling races (which are long and strategic), albeit one where you get the fun of controlling the riders.That aside, would I recommend this game? Yes, I would. To get them out of the way, negatives first (and this is minor for me):- all the riders look the same! C'mon devs, can we just have a few more faces!- downhill taking corners is a bit clunky; it's hard to take corners as you break and then lose speed after; if you hit the verge/barrier, your rider just stops. Onto positives and why I would recommend this game:-  scenery is beautiful, the landscapes do look really great when you cycle past and where they have recreated notable landmarks, you can tell its them. For example, the Ventoux stage mimics the climb, scenery and tower perfectly. - the individual stages/one day races and underlying gamepley feel like real-life cycling races. You get breakaways (albeit I've found the peloton seem overly keen to chase down at times), stages have your sprint sections or mountain classifications for points etc. AI respond to strategy - if you try to break with a possible winner (say Roglic), you will see responses from other favourites, for example. That said, this comes back to my first point... if you enjoy cycling, you will enjoy this. It's ultimately a strategic game - to stay in the peloton, go for the break etc... but a great one in that you can control the riders/manage your team/riders but with an exciting hands-on style (unlike pure management games where you just watch).  - game options: this is generally pretty good. You can play the full TDF or take part in other races; the team/career modes look good too. Some possible recommendations to enhance (IMO): more non-TDF races - it would be great to have some more races in the calendar (ideally likes of Vuelta or Giro!!); more customisation options (would be cool to design your own jerseys or be able to change bike colour). Overall, a great game if you are a cycling enthusiast!

_childDocuments_.review: There should be a 'meh'-button:The game is fun and addicting, but frustrating in its flaws (unless I'm doing everything wrong ofcourse)...- No graphics setting (except for resolution)- No real gameplay adjusting (only amateur and pro, the difference isn't that big)- ONLY 3 PERSONS in game: 1 cyclist, 1 female supporter and 1 male supporter. Some cosmetics try to hide that, but it's really silly to see 1 guy multiplide by 300 at the start...- The smart using of energy and energy loss is a great idea, but doesn't seem to really aply to pc-cyclists (even persons that are 30 minutes behind at 30km from the finish still appear at the front of the race for the sprint and have more energy than you for a long sprint)- The pc cyclists all play against you (when you follow them, they will always slow down to let the peleton get back, even your own teammates with instructions). The only time it does work, is when you fastforward...- Buttons do not always respond: attacking might make you completely stop, follow sometimes means ignore I'm asking anyting, ...- When you're to well placed on a crucial stage, in a mather of seconds you will be completely inclosed by 30 cyclists preventing you to move...- Taking corners going downhill is a pain in the ***. The brakes give you all or nothing, slowing down doesn't help you turning... All of this makes you park you're bike straigth ahead on the grass (while the pc cyclists take the corner at full speed)- There's no button to be used to slow down the tempo when you are driving first (expect if you park AGAIN)- If your energy is low, it will almost never come back (unless you fastforward and everybody passes)

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- It's the closest game you get to the real Tour de France- One for an insight into what different driving styles there are- You realize how much energy the cows use. The game is good to show that the riders use more energy the faster they drive, and that you can not drive full speed and be in the front throughout the raceCons:- The graphics are bad- If you are about to run off the field and into the grass you will be stopped. You can only drive on the road and if you try to drive on the grass it is like driving into a wall- A race easily takes an hour- The price. The game is by no means worth € 40- There is no multiplayer, not even in the 2021 version- The game only works with an xbox controller (Not a playstasion controller)Graphics:- There is not much else to say but bad- Menu: The menu looks old-fashioned and is by no means neat. It is a simple menu with some square boxes that you can press to enter the race or settings e.g.- Race: The graphics in race are not something to brag about either. It is almost reminiscent of the graphics in MotoGP 15 (a game released in 2015)Physics:- Physics is actually okay. It is clear that this is where the time is laid. That is not to say that it is perfect, because it is not. eg if you drive too close to another drive, you start driving inside the hindan and slow down a lot, but without tipping over or about to tip over as you see in games like MotoGP 21 etc.You need to know before buying:- A race takes a long time (1 hour +)- There's not really any cerrier modeConclusion:I wish I could recommend the Tour de france 2020, but I can not. The game is on almost all points the drawers and does not live up to the fact that it comes from Nacon and is from 2020. If you are a big Tour de france fan and that is the only thing you go up in it is an okay game. I would not think the game is worth 40 €. I got the game for 3 € and think I have overpriced the game. So if you're a big fan of the Tour de france and can find it for a deal of under € 10 it's okay, but if you are not you should not even think about buying the game

name: Disciples: Liberation
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Digital Deluxe Edition contains everything you need to take your journey even further. Within, you will find two unique sets of armor, two new weapons, an Emotion Shard for Avyanna, wallpapers, a digital compendium, the Soundtrack and two Packs: Yllian Resources Pack - get extra ressources to build up your hometown Pack with 5 Additional Skillpoints - get extra skillpoints for Avyanna Both Packs can be used once per new game session. About the Game Disciples: Liberation is a mature, dark fantasy strategy RPG with turn-based combat. Liberate the land of Nevendaar and uncover the endless stories hidden within this richly detailed world where every decision has a consequence, and every wrong move could be deadly. Explore a rich overworld and align with a variety of in-world factions: from a human empire tinged by religious extremism to the dark forces of the undead lead by a mad queen. Assemble a team to gather precious resources, sway political standing, and take on brutal beasts in intricate turn-based battles. Choice is everything in Disciples: Liberation and it is up to you how you write your story. 80+ hour single-player campaign: experience a sprawling dark fantasy epic over three acts, with more than 270 quests and objectives, and five unique endings to unlock. Explore a war-torn realm: journey through a sprawling world in ruin and work to unearth its endless secrets, hidden treasures, and bloody past. Write your own story: pick from four uniquely skilled classes and define your place in the world, recruiting others to your cause from an assortment of factions. Build a base: take on quests for precious resources and use your political savvy to build a place of planning and sanctuary. Fight for your life: recruit 50+ units and amass an army best suited to your play style; hone both steel and spell in intricate-turned based combat. Challenge deadly bosses: test your mettle and pit your party against horrific monsters and beasts, each requiring a unique strategy. Choice is everything: let your decisions guide your fate and directly influence what sort of leader you become. Fight your friends: put forth the ultimate challenge and battle for supremacy in 2-player online skirmishes.

_childDocuments_.review: I prefer turn-based CRPGs like Disciples: Liberation. It was pretty simple compared to games like Pathfinder or Divinity. Every "unit" or character gets just two moves, two abilities, and you don't have to worry about attacks of opportunity, allowing you to move freely around the battle field. There are obstacles, though, and some battles have a random "lightning strikes at the end of every turn" effect. What I didn't like is that you can only have 2 of your companions with you at a time, so the rest of your party is made up of "units" and these are essentially the same as enemies you'll fight throughout the game. They are weaker and completely disposable, but you actually can get special named/voiced units by taking certain actions in quests, etc. A few of them are worth picking up. I think it's important that companions in an RPG be given interesting back stories that affect their character, and Disciples: Liberation does that. The companions get special weapons and abilities if you do their quests, and these quests are actually pretty interesting. The world in Disciples: Liberation is pretty dark. Kind of Diablo-esque. I really liked the design of enemies, especially the undead and the demons. It has an interesting plot with a few twists, though it gets a little convoluted toward the end as so many new "gods" are showing up and no one seems to know why they're attacking you. I suppose this all makes sense when you get the true ending, but you can't get the true ending unless you play the game through a second time, and that's a big ask when you can't skip or auto-resolve many battles.

_childDocuments_.review: is a strategy RPG with turn-based battles. It combines a good story, plot progression among the many battles that are found within. The main character, Avyanna, is on a quest with her companion to kill an evil priest. When something goes terribly wrong during this quest, Avyanna accidentally creates a hole in the sky and both of them land on an ancient and abandoned city, Yillian. The game offers many quests, numerous battles, and story-progressing choices that matter.There is no classic tutorial, instead the game will explain new things to you as you encounter them. No difficulty options means that everyone plays at the same level. The game does give multiple saves as well as autosave function.The quests are many in this game. Aside from the main quest line you will encounter many side quests. As you make your responses to the choices presented to you during the story itself, they will also have positive and negative effects on the story. This involves the player directly in the progression of the story.The battles are turn-based and your unit are limited by your leader points that upgrade if you advance to another level. You will also have a passive backline of units that help you during the battle with buffs, but you do not control their actions.If there is a big discrepancy between the strengths of the sides, as in you are a lot stronger than the enemy, you can choose to conquer the opposition instead of fighting. This will save you a lot of time, especially given how long and slow-paced the battles can be.You can recruit and train new units in your town of Yillian, here you can also talk to your companions, build new places, among other upgrading options typically found in base building. You can warp to Yillian on the map at any time.The graphics are okay, though nothing groundbreaking.The music in this game is really good. Much of the main text is also in voice overs, and nicely done too.You can play either with a mouse and keyboard or with a controller. I have played with the mouse and keyboard.The price of €39.99 is a fair place for  The game offers a lot of gameplay. I am not through with it yet so I do not know exactly how long it is at this time. is a really good game that combines a nice storytelling RPG with its many battles. The battles themselves can be rather slow and you may need to use some strategic thinking to win them. On top of that, the base building is an nice addition to the game as well.The many choices to be made that influence the story involves the player more. Most of the choices seem like they really matter. It is impossible to always take on the "good" side because all decisions will have positive and negative impact throughout the game. The text within the story are fairly short and kept me interested with its heavily interactive component.I am really enjoying it so far, and I have not yet completed the game. The game looks and feels like an enormous project, and it's best devoured at first then enjoyed piecemeal for the complete experience.Score: 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent modernisation of the Disciples series gameplay. All the old units are still here and the maps you move around on are very reminiscent of the old ones. The music and graphics are pretty good. The only other drawback is that the battles are still quiet lengthy and very frequent. In Disciples II because there was no movement the frequent battles weren't as big an issue, but ever since that game they've added complex battlefields to move your units on which really isn't necessary. Look at Fire Emblem or Ogre Battle, having units in static positions doing quick skirmishes is still something that could be done today. Other than that it's a lot of fun, the plot is great, the different choices in dialogue are fun and most of the companions are really enjoyable to interact with and well written.

_childDocuments_.review: So Disciples managed to get a revival, good on them. Disciples 2 was a game I always felt didn't get as much attention as it deserved. The short version of this review is its a budget AA game made by a AA studio and its great for what it is. Its not trying to be a masterpiece its trying to be good fun and not charge you AAA pricing. It succeeds on that front. Solid 8 out of 10 with 5 being an average game. Some of the flaws I am willing to accept because I know this game doesn't have a $100 million budget but some of them are still baffling.Long Review: 8/10 with 5 being average gamePros:Do you like heroes of might and magic when it was good? I did, this game is heavily that.Interesting units with a wide varietyStory is simple but enjoyableNew Game+ is the right way to do New Game+ by adding extra dialogue and changing mechanics rather than letting you take an OP character to slaughter everyoneFairly low amount of bugs. One bug is egregious though and will be in the con section.Takes about 40 hours to complete first run giving great value for the costCons:One of the elven buildings is bugged so you can't produce those units, which makes up their front line units. This bug is so egregious awful it bears mentioning specifically because its happening to everyone and its so obvious that play-testing should have caught it.Legions of the damned continue their Disciples 3 design which is spiky with lava as oppose to their cool disciples 2 design which was beautiful Gothic structures, ominous Latin chanting background music and units who spoke Latin in their combat chatter making them feel like evil angel rather than generic demon of disciples 3 and now 4.Balance is awful. Protag is the only one who can cast spells so that automatically means you wont select 2 of the classes, then it double downs by making one caster class synergies with useless summons and the other ignore a portion of resistances. Gee which one should I select. Essentially witch is the only class that matters everything else is clearly inferior which is disappointing. This problem compounds with companions. Companions can only equip weapons and emotion shards in addition they are basically just a glorified unit having the same passives and abilities as one of the units you can recruit as a generic soldier. So this means tank companions are useless because they cant equip armors and such that really help tanks plus the units they replace aren't even the good tank units, it means primary spell casters are useless because they can't cast spells, it also means that 2 specific companions are mechanically the best by a wide margin because they are primary damage dealers so weapons are the most important thing for them and they are late game units and you can recruit them much much earlier than you can those units.Ultimate abilities are worthless, you can't use them until turn 5 and only 2 battles will last that long by the time you get them.The auto-battle option is inconsistent. The game says you can use it if you are stronger than the enemy and the fight doesn't relate to a quest. That's a lie there where several fights i outleveled my opponents by 4 or 5 levels and it was a generic random encounter that I couldn't skip even though they posed 0 threat to me.Tooltips need to be more descriptive there are several abilities in the skill tree that don't function the way you think based on how they are written but do technically do what they say from a certain perspective.

A great game for tactical turn based combat on the small scale and a fun open world to run around in. the story is a hybrid of both linear and choices matter. your choices do have an impact on what happens, but the heart of the story line stays true so what this really effects is companions, which factions back you (and which do not).  This is also not a game you can beat in a few hours. this is a long playtime game with decent replay factor as well. _childDocuments_.review: Never played Disciples (1).  Was a big fan of Disciples 2. Disciples 3 was a disappointment. I was grateful for the release of Reincarnation which allowed me to finally play the 3rd issue of the game, but I didn’t finish it. I truly thought that the Disciples series was over. So I was completely surprised in October of this year when I came across Disciples Liberation. The trailer looked interesting and there was a lengthy free demo being offered. I downloaded it, played it for some 30 hours, and was hooked. Later the full game was released and I just finished it after investing more than 120 hours.   Obviously, I like the new game. However, let me get this out of the way right up front. If you’re dying for a remake of Disciples 2, with its dark graphics, turn-based battles with stationary troops, units evolving from, say, acolytes to archmages as they gain experience, and where there is a heavy focus on territory expansion: THIS GAME IS NOT IT. Disciples Liberation is set in the world of Disciples, but that’s about it. As far as I could tell, all of the characters and their stories are unique to this game. There is no carryover from the previous iterations of the series. Disciples Liberation has overland maps for exploration and quests, and tactical screens where turn-based battles are fought. Here’s my take on the game.  First, the negatives:•	Convoluted story, not easy to follow or comprehend•	Outcome of storyline choices often difficult to predict (had to replay some battles)•	No difficulty settings and the game is pretty easy•	Horse stuttering on the overland map•	Too few interactive items •	Treasure chests full of mediocre items•	Some dialogue not audible•	A few game mechanics not well explained •	Not always able to flee from a tactical battle where your troops are vastly outclassedNow the positives:•	Very long story with many interesting characters•	Almost all dialogue fully voiced by good actors; Orion, a primary sidekick,  is especially good•	Beautifully detailed overland maps and tactical screens•	Nice array of troops, consisting of demons, undead, elves, and humans•	Can mix and match troops to your liking•	Can respect your character at any time; can even change from melee fighter to mage•	Can upgrade gear and dismantle it to recover materials•	Can save game at any time•	Wide variety of spells, which are all graphically interesting  •	Good sound effects•	Very stable; Over 120 hours played with only 1 crash  Again, it’s not a remake of Disciples 2. I would have loved that, but I truly enjoyed this. Think of it as an offshoot of Heroes of Might and Magic with some elements of King’s Bounty thrown in. If you enjoyed those games (which are favorites of mine) I believe that you’ll enjoy this one as well. Is it a perfect game? Absolutely not, but I certainly enjoyed my time with it and definitely got my money’s worth. (Something I can’t say about a number of games in my library.) It absolutely was a pleasant surprise and I’m grateful to the developers for resurrecting the Disciples series and making this game.  If anything that I said peaks your interest, just give the demo a shot. You’ve got nothing to lose, except some time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an RPG with turn-based combat. I really hoped there'd be a bit more to this than there appears to be on the surface. The game starts with you on an assassination mission, which you fail by design and then fall through a portal to another world that then acts as your base.Then it's a case of building an army for some unknown reason - I've no idea what the actual end goal is though.All the equipment icons look the same and at first, I thought there was no way of comparing equipped items to things in your inventory - there is, you have to hold a button down to show it (which I missed at first).The environments are functional but mostly non-interactive - you can open cages for example, but there's then an invisible wall preventing you from going inside, making most of it pretty pointless being there other than to get in your way.After an hour, the turn-based combat hadn't opened up at all strategy-wise, leaving you using the same attacks over and over, taking more damage than you're able to give out. So there isn't really that much strategy to be strategised about. Maybe this opens up as the skills and magic trees are climbed, but it's definitely slow going at first; without a particularly compelling story to drive you through the early game, it's difficult to get enthused about this one.So, not sure I really recommend this and it gets only 5 Stuffed Fables out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, not really worth it. Combat is extremely repetitive a ridiculously easy. Each unit has only two skills, that have absolutely no interactions with each other. Basically the whole combat system is based on using one ability, that is stronger and has a cooldown, and then spamming the other one for the rest of the combat. Even the companions are just simple reskins of basic units with slightly tweaked stats.The main character gets dumbly overpowered around mid game, being able to clear whole battlefield in the first round - including enemy tier 4 enemies. No need to even look at the ultimate ability - it's weaker by a mile and you get it much later than the spells.Sadly, this game offers the most disappointing bosses I have ever seen. They deal no damage, they offer no interesting mechanics, they're just big, annoying and boring damage sponges. You just stand there, not even dodging their attacks, spamming your abilities for 10 rounds. The whole game seems kind of lazy and really leaves a feeling, that noone really playtested the game.In the end there is really little to offer. Perhaps get it on 60-80% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, but not as great as it initially seemed. When opening up the game, one first gets a weird launcher of Kalypse, after which the game starts. The graphics are nice, and before the music starts repeating a lot, it's good music. Some of the voice actors are quite nice to listen to. However, I expected more of an RPG experience, as advertised, but instead the game is about 90 to 95% just fighting. It doesn't feel like there's a lot of freedom in the choices either: most of it is divided in 'yes I'll help you', 'no, I will kill you' and 'not now'... Story-wise, it just feels quite basic, lacking depth. It annoyed me that all factions seem evil. It doesn't feel like there's really much difference between which faction you choose,  as all of them will bring ruin if given the chance. Initially the fighting system was quite fun, but as the game throws a lot of back to back fights at you, the fun soon disappears. A lot of these battles are quite alike as well, so it often feels like you're just repeating what you just did, which is frustrating to me. There is a conquer function, but it doesn't function nearly well enough, as it often still makes me fight troops that are way under my level. There's also a bug (or feature, lol) in which the troops/amount of troops/placement (frontliners or backliners) that are shown for the enemy are inaccurate. So you've always got to keep that in mind when putting together your fighting party. It doesn't always happen, but it is very frustrating when it does. (Though, sometimes there's a hint about the bug, like the game stating that way too many enemy troops are backliners.)This game could do with a LOT of quality of life updates: a lot of things aren't explained and the UI isn't great either. It seems some of the keys can't be changed either, and if the enemy team's turns are going on, you can't seem to pause the fight. A lot of elements in this game are 'inspired' by mobile apps: 'hold mouse button' for travelling, for upgrading and such. It also has a weird resource management aspect, in which the game requires X resources to upgrade things and buy troops. The materials are gained by playtime and by finding them in the overworld, but it's a weird limitation in this type of game. The same odd time aspects are for the marketplace, in which you can buy gear and mercenary troops: every hour they refresh.. And as I mentioned mercenary troops: I can't seem to level them up either. Your average troops, which you hire per 'main faction' camp, you can easily level up. However, those that aren't able for hire in those faction camps can't be levelled there either, which leaves very frustrating situations.If you plan to play the game, keep an eye on the bottom left corner, as important warnings will be given there, as well as additional story background by the characters. They're not really explaining most things, so save a lot and be prepared to get angry the first few hours.All in all, the game had quite some potential, but it just doesn't do anything with it. If you get it, get it during a sale, and make sure you first play the demo. The demo offers quite some playtime, though I did not see a way to continue my progress from the demo. I wanted to love this game, but it gets a 'meh' from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  Out of nowhere with this.  Nothing like previous games in the series, and if that's what you want you'll be disappointed.  This game is more like King's Bounty....only a million times better.  The unnecessary unit stacking mechanic has been replaced by a better RPG leveling mechanic.  The leadership model has been made better and more strategic with units having different values based on their tier.  Oh...and easily won battles are auto-won if you choose, without any loses.  Which takes out the ridiculous redundancy Might and Magic and Kings Bounty have as you try not to take any loses in easy battles due to production scarcity.   This is probably the best turn-based tactics RPG to come out this year.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this is a surprisingly enjoyable game.I admit that I was initially skeptical about Disciples Liberation because I expected it to "return to its roots", and be more similar to earlier installments, especially to Disciples 2. I was intrigued and eventually persuaded by the good reviews that the game had received, and I purchased it out of curiosity. And what a pleasant surprise it was! So,Cons:- it doesn't have the grim aesthetics of Disciples 2. The overall atmosphere is not bad, but it certainly cannot compete with the one in Disc2.- the combat gets repetitive after a while- you can only quit combat when it's your turn, this is especially annoying if you're losing the combat- the city tutorial could be a bit more polished, I had to guess my way around it- in bossfights you cannot check the stats of the bosses. This is imo one of the game's biggest flaws. There's no way of finding out the stats/resistances of the most difficult enemies I'm facing, and for no apparent reason. Pls fix- good but repetitive soundtrackPros:- the game looks very beautiful- surprisingly well optimised, very big +- quite a long gameplay, it took me 70 hours to finish the main story on brutal difficulty- unit diversity- reputation system- customizable main character, including gear and three skill trees- immersive story- very pleasant companions, and the occasional jokes/comedic relief moments are a big plus- some of the units in disciples 2 are also present here, big +- quite a rich variety of spells- satisfying building capture/progression- the "conquer" mechanic is a blessing. you can avoid easy fights with one click, huge +- replayable game. after finishing the game, you can begin it again, but with a slightly different story (won't spoil it), big +- good combat mechanics, with a surprisingly capable AI. the fights are quite good, enemies don't make silly mistakes, and really try to kick your assSo, it's a really good game. Show yourself and the devs some love and try it out, you'll most probably like it.

_childDocuments_.review: For the record, Disciples: Liberation is not King's Bounty 2. However it is what King's Bounty 2 should have been, judging from many of the comments (incl. my own) on both forums.That being said, Disciples: Liberation is a good game, and a hybrid of both styles in fact which seem to blend nicely.Although there's one thing hardcore players (i'm not that hardcore, but i am an old-schooler) might notice early on, which is how simplified things actually are. I'm not pointing that out as "negative" criticism guys, it was no doubt decided to appeal console players alike so to me that makes perfect sense. Yet, by mentioning simplified i'm looking at combat mechanics, skill trees, questing and options given to reach or complete certain goals. (there's plenty to do, icluding crafting, building, exploring, expanding and improving)It's all pretty straight forward, and doesn't involve complex strategies or never seems to give the player bad outcome whatever choices he or she makes (even though it was advertised as "choices matter"). You'll get the gist a few hours in..Continuing upon that idea brings us the skill tree, which has seen a post béta rework which is fine tbh (the main protagonist will be OP soon enough without the changes anyway). However, and again this is where i'd recall myself saying the game is a bit simplified when you look into the "3" available skill trees. That's right, you can freely choose from those 'three skill trees' albeit the player will still have to decide which one to master. So you can either stick to one or mix it up depending on your preferred playstyle. There's no downside to this as well, if you don't feel comfortable spending points on skills you no longer have need of, the game provides an easy way out. (sometimes Less is Moar) Right, Alfred Pennyworth?For a 'fist full of coin' you can use a 'handy' redo option which will set the skill trees back towards the beginning, allowing you to re-distribute the points as you see fit. (simplified - choices matter?) Mhm..Now quickly looking over to the graphics and music department i can say this much, the devs did a decent job on that. Although the limited camera options often bother me. There's no 360° camera rotation available as of yet, and i expect it will not get implemented over time which is actually a small piece of criticism here.Anyways, now that's all been said i am quite happy having purchased Disciples: Liberation and i'll gladly recommend it to anyone who likes those classic Disciples & King's Bounty games (in a modern day twist mind you).Highly recommended score: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Do you know how annoying it is to have a "Leave a review!" on a game's starting splash screen?It's annoying enough that people like me will intentionally leave a bad review. Seriously, how dare you pander and ASK for reviews? If you want to know whether people like your game or not, look at the sales, social media, game forums, and reviews people take the time to leave. Take ALL of THAT feedback seriously.What I like about the game: It reminds me a lot of Heroes of Might and Magic, and that is a good thing.What I dislike about the game:There's a quicksave, but no quickload. WTF?Battle speedup is capped at 200%. This makes them drag on, and on, and on.....Playing on normal difficulty and things are typically 3-5 levels higher than me (I am clearing EVERYTHING I find, that I can reasonably clear) and in some instances the enemy has up to 5 more troops than I do. Something is horribly wrong here.I intentionally went out of my way to buy it on PC after seeing how beautiful it was on PS5. I have a super awesome TV with my PS5 and a great gaming rig/monitor, but despite cranking the graphics, things still look muddy. What gives? Was optimization for this given for PS5 but skipped on PC.....?Shortcuts. Some shortcuts are not intuitive. It took me forever to figure out what "tab" did (to end a unit turn). Further, these shortcuts CANNOT be edited. WHAT. THE. FK!?!? It's 2022, why can't I edit key bindings!? Why aren't they even LISTED?The game does a really crap job of suggesting what you may want to make for choices. I've been playing like a total arsehole - intentionally - and I regret nothing, but I am concerned it will make me miss something. IE, I'm dedicated to building rep with Demons/Undead, but....will it be at the cost of Humans/Elves? So far the answer seems to be yes? I cleared the first demon area, and now am on the first human area, and I've....lost some rep with Humans already......this is maybe more of a gripe about my own playstyle than anything I guess.Overall, do I recommend this game? Not for your average gamer. This is VERY MUCH a niche game from a bygone era. If you liked Heroes of Might and Magic, consider giving this a try - but in case you don't like it, watch that 2 hour time limit closely. The game's intricacies really doesn't start kicking in until well past that mark.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little game that doesn't quite reach the height of Disciples II, but gets most things right. Gameplay wise it's closer to Heroes of Might and Magic IV. Combat in the first half is terribly unbalanced, I was always overleveled and didn't build a single structure in my base, because combat is just that easy, if you pick your battles right. AI is very prone to abuse, you can manipulate the enemy into attacking your summoned creatures and keep the main force unharmed. Pathfinding is also a bit broken, since most AI units refuse to go over tiles with negative effects, which gives you plenty of opportunities to lock enemies down in one corner of the field and just bombard them with AoE spells and attacks. Dungeon crawling is terrible, they should've done that similarly to how HoMM III did it instead.Story wise, the game loses steam in the second half, that feels rushed as hell. A lot of choices boil down to losing reputation with one of the factions, but if you do all the side quests you'll end up being Honored by 3 out of the 4 factions. Regardless, Friendly was more than enough for me to wipe the first five maps clean with my Tier I units, because some of them are incredibly unbalanced.Still going to recommend DL, since I really liked some of the fights, it scratches that turn-based itch, but only if you're not a huge fan of Disciples II, which is a better game in all respects.

Like the other people said, dialogue is not this game's strong point and the companions are not really fleshed out enough for me to care about them or their opinions. Found it really surprising they have romance when there is no growth or lead up to it. I barely have a relationship with them, let alone be open to the idea of exploring it further. Companions' personal quests are not relevant nor were there special 'moments' or cutscenes, which makes it really awkward when it just HAPPENS after you press the heart option (but I completed it for achievement's sake). Most annoying part was the fixed movement when navigating the open world. Having to move by clicks in dungeons and not being able to fly across the screen using the mouse to view what's around makes the game go really slow.Story was ehhhh. Still, I enjoyed it for the most part but it lacks the replayability value for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put approximately 10 hours into the game at the time of writing this review. Apart from a few things that I have noticed, I have to tell this game feels solid. A blend of tactical turn-based strategy and RPG, great experience so far, only minor bugs.Issues and bugs:- Stuck on victory screen twice with no means to close it, had to alt+tab and restart the application.- The sounds sometimes goes either bad quality or repeats itself every 0.5-1 second for a few second interval and then carries on. This happens to both BGM and environmental sound effects.- The camera is terrible, sometimes it's set and the players have no control or only keyboard buttons can be used, and can't rotate the camera 360 degrees, plus can't rotate the camera with mouse buttons.- Can't change keybinds, but that's not a big deal.- Sometimes when the companions talk their message only gets shown for 2-3 seconds on the left side of the screen, not enough for the player to read them.- The mouse button has to be held for a few things, like upgrading building, training units and reseraching spells. I find this annoying and this could be gone altogether. A simple click should be enough, with a comfirmation message maybe.- The combat animation speed can be altered within a range of 100-200% by the increment of 50%. I think it's still to slow at 200%, I could imagine a 500% limit to this option, battles with many units start to get quite drawn out as the army gets bigger. I would also like an "no combat animation" option make all attacks instant.- There is no way to change difficulty, but it felt too easy from start, and whilst the game does get more complex as the story progresses, there is no challange.- There was a pile of corpses with a treasure chest on the undead lands and when I approached it I was forced to battle level 20 army with my level 4 army. There was no way of knowing or inspecting any army prior, perhaps it was a bug of not showing the enemy on the map.Keep in mind this is a spin-off title within the franchise, so it comes with it's own features and many different things from the base titles (Disciples 1-3). It's all set in the Disciples-verse, but many things are different, even the combat and the units. Great game, but this is not Disciples 4.Edit #1 (at 75 hours):The developers are listening to consumer feedback, difficulty options are about to be implemented with a patch. They seem to have an interest to make their product as good as they can and to learn how to develop better titles in the future. I would rate this game a solid 8/10 as of now with difficulty options, and if they implement the rest (like combat speed increase) then it will bnecome 8.5/10. Reviews average around 7.5/10 right now, but keep in mind that there are many reviews that come from consumers with biased perspective that expects the game to be disciples 2 style. This game is a successive trial to resurrect the franchise (that was killed by the abomination called Disciples III, a decade ago), and a good development ground for something better in the upcomming years (for the next disciples title). Ignore the ones who want a disciples 2 remake with new story, not being able to appreciate this franchise being resurrected by an actually good game, and not considering what a failure  Disciples III was, which was basically an inferior and terrible Disciples 2 clone with pointless added features.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples: Liberation is a Disciples game in name only. You got the same universe, the same name, the same gods. That's about it - everything else has nothing or close to nothing to do with Disciples. It's a quite weird tRPG with the bare minimum of tactic element and almost the whole difficulty coming from your semi-useless main character (just make her mage. Don't even try giving her a melee class for your own good). The game is rigged with the questionable gamedesign decisions (pretty much every aspect of the game has some): 1) The level design2) The mobile game design (hold this button, 5 IRL min CD on fountains, resources/IRL hour etc)3) Although the game claims to be an RPG, the only choices that have a real impact are mostly side-quest ones4) Some unit design 5) Progression 6) Add-your-own-thingThere are also quite a few bugs, but only a few would actually affect your gameplay (for example, crystals that would randomly appear during the battle state "Destroy this to get the massive benefits. Ignore it and it'll explode", however, no matter if you wait or destroy it, the effects would be the same - explosion that damages everyone).The voice acting.... is pretty bad. Especially during the battles, given that the units have about 2 voice lines for each move. It's pretty weird hearing Avianna screaming "DIE!" when she heals an ally or Orion screaming "You mess with Avy? You mess with me!", then "You mess with Avy?!" and finally the first one again. The speed... it's really something else. Anything other than 300% speed is unplayable. 100% is a slow motion for masochists. The starting Legion of the Damned location should be reworked. Honestly. It has some weird bug with the music and audio in general, the difficulty is just stupid compared to any other location due to everything outleveling you at any point in the game. Some quests are not intuitive at all because you are not given any real pointers on the condition. Some units are just copies of their counterpart units from a different faction. They just have a different model and a passive. The loot is a complete mess and so is the "conquer" button (sometimes it allows you to insta-defeat the squads stronger or equal to your army, sometimes you have to manually kick some underdog squads with a bunch of healers). While the side quests are good and have multiple outcomes, the main quest line feels really bad. Mainly, due to a reason that there are no real decisions and it's poorly written in general. For example, I had discovered that my quest is to "Liberate people" and "Save the world" completely at random, during the dialogue of a side-quest. Before that? - I had no clue what was the point of literally everything happening in this game.Honestly, I'm being held as a hostage here. The game isn't good or isn't bad. It's a mediocre among the mediocre games.    Gameplay is pretty relaxing, although if you'll have to abuse the inner mechanics (mainly the AI) if you set the game to anything other than "Easy".However, once again, the game isn't good. I don't want to leave a negative review only because I don't want the series to die. But if you want to play the actual Disciples game or support the series - Disciples 2 are both on GoG and Steam (I'd recommend the first platform, it works better for whatever reason), the third one is a much better game than Liberation after they made that Reincarnation edition (DO NOT mistake it for the original Renaissance. If you ever find Renaissance being sold anywhere in a physical edition - buy it and burn it in the purifying flames of salvation). To the devs: if the story part is likely not fixable, at least fix the gameplay part. Or do the workshop part, given that even Disciples 2 still has the modding scene, it is likely someone will fix the game for you. To the Kalypso: just make/remake Disciples 2 with HD models and the workshop.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this review by saying that I'm a long-time Disciples fan and Disciples I-II might be my favorite video games ever. But I went into this game with zero expectations, and tried not to let the idea of "ruined series" get into the way of enjoying it. In fact, when I first saw the trailer, I was excited because a Disciples RPG was something I dreamed of for a long time.Unfortunately, as it turns out the game is just not good on its own merits.The basic gameplay is this: you have a city where you can hire units and upgrade stuff, and adventure mode where you run around maps, do sidequests and fight battles using your companions and units hired in the city in order to earn resources to upgrade the city. Fairly similar to King's Bounty. You also have a main character who can level skill trees, equip items and such RPG staples.All the reviews that say Disciples: Liberation feels like a mobile game are unfortunately true. There are so many mechanics that reek of mobile, and the worst part is that they're there for no reason. For example, resource income is per hour and you have to click buttons to collect resources before they hit cap. Just like in a mobile city building game. (And no, resources don't trickle while the game is closed). Upgrading your city is also locked behind story progression. Why can't I just grind resources and upgrade it whenever I want? Because mobile games do it, that's why.Do the developers think these mechanics exist because they're good game design and players enjoy them? No, they exist to milk players for microtransactions. Now I'm not saying that D:L should've had microtransactions, but without them these mechanics serve LITERALLY NO PURPOSE. The game just wastes your time for no reason at all.Thanks to these mechanics, progression feels painfully slow. It took me the entirety of my 7+ hour playtime just to unlock the second tier of buildings. Before you do that, all you have available is crappy level 1 melee units and there's barely any reason to visit the city as it offers nothing to do. This is just bad game design. You should give the player a few options to play with right off the bat, so they can plan and look forward to new unlocks. D:L just gives you the bare minimum and then forces you to wait for hours on end before you can unlock anything meaningful. So, the city building part is bad. What about the writing and roleplaying? (I am holding off the combat for the last). The game was advertised with "your choices matter" (just like any RPG nowadays), so let's talk about that. There's a fair bit of dialogue in the game and you can usually choose one of the options: Good, Evil or Liberation (something a bit unique, somewhat similar to Chaotic Good in D&D games, basically you want to save everyone from the tyranny of the gods). Sometimes you can also lie. There are some dialogues where your choice leads to different outcomes (for example, I had a choice to either recruit a demon cultist into my party, or let her die and become a demon so she gets rid of an annoying combat encounter later). But most dialogue choices lead to the same outcomes, and even when they don’t, usually the only difference is that you get to choose between two slightly different combat encounters. The game never really made me feel like I’m choosing my own adventure or making hard choices.The writing is…meh. I liked some tidbits of lore it adds to the Disciples universe, but overall it feels bland and tryhard. The worst part are the dialogues between the main character and your first companion. They’re both mercenaries, and of course that means the only things they talk about is fighting and drinking. Seriously, they talk about drinking so much! Learn a new piece of information? “I remember hearing about it at the bar”. Unlock a new location? “I heard they make good booze here”. Beat a boss? “Let’s go home and have a celebratory drink”. Almost every single dialogue has your MC say something about booze. My god, we are playing as an alcoholic! Such a lazy way to characterize your fantasy mercenary.Oh yeah, and we play a fixed character, you can’t generate your own. She’s pretty much a tabula rasa. Her entire backstory is that she’s a mercenary with mysterious powers. There’s nothing unique or interesting about her that would justify not letting us make our own character. The only reason there’s no chargen is because the developers were too lazy to include it.There’s also no cutscenes at all, in-engine or otherwise. All dialogues are between two talking portraits. Another thing that feels very “mobile game”. The prologue just hands you a floating city of your own without a cutscene of any kind, and your characters don’t even act surprised about it. Very lazy, very mobile.But now it’s time to talk about combat. If this game had good combat, I could overlook all the other problems. Unfortunately, it doesn’t. The combat in this game is the worst thing it could be: it’s slow. You can adjust the speed of animations, but even at 200% it feels slow. 200% should’ve been the standard speed and let you go up to like 500%. Combine this with elaborate animations, weirdly damage spongy enemies and ranged enemies who just love to run away to the corner of the map, and you’re looking at random trash encounters that take up to 5-10 minutes. For a game that’s 90% combat, that’s just painful. There is also not nearly enough variety to make you want to suffer through the slog. All companions and units only have two active abilities, and there is very little enemy variety. Every map only has a few varieties of enemies from the same faction, and after 2-3 battles you’ve seen them all and everything they can do. Even the first Disciples game had dozens of different neutral creatures to mix things up, but the devs of D:L were too lazy to include more enemy varieties. “Strategy” barely matters, it’s mostly about making sure you’re flanking and using special abilities on CD, and “map hazards” are just glowing circles on the ground that do good stuff or bad stuff if you step on them. Exciting.The game does give you a button to auto-resolve fights, but it isn’t available nearly as often as you’d want it to since it needs the enemies to be much weaker than your party. I only got to use it once or twice.It gets seriously tedious. After about 5 hours I had to literally  myself to keep playing, avoiding all the optional encounters, just to see if the game gets better when you get to choose your class (yes, you can only do that about 6-7 hours into the game). Tip: it doesn’t.BONUS: The most baffling thing about the game is that you can rotate the camera in combat (where it’s pointless since every battle map is just a flat rectangle) but can’t do it on the adventure map (where you’d actually want to rotate the camera since your line of sight is sometimes obstructed).Unfortunately, D:L is a dud and a game that actively wastes your time. If you’re curious about the core gameplay mix of turn-based strategy and character-focused RPG, play King’s Bounty instead. If you want to play an RPG where choices matter and you can join the forces of good or the legions of the damned, play Wrath of the Righteous. There are very few redeeming features about Disciples: Liberation. There’s some kernel of a decent game buried in there, but it’s simply, fundamentally not fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignoring that, I wouldn't recommend paying anything above 20$ for a full Deluxe version of the game. It's fine, but it's not a 40-50$ game and feel VERY linear for what it is.This game has decent combat (against similar level opponents) and progression system that feel meaningful in scope of combat.Yes, there's a "BUT", and not just oneWhat I've listed above makes building a squad not feel as engaging as it should be. Everything leads to slow incremental progression, while making choices in building a squad mostly meaningless. The game allows skipping some fights if you're higher level than opponents(lovely feature), BUT story-adjacent fights aren't skippable (for some reason about 40-50%). If you explore, you're basically always higher level than story fights, which leads to slow, but guaranteed wins in most fights on starting 2nd map. I would REALLY like to skip animations in this game. You can speed up combat to 300% speed, but it's still slow when you're fighting large groups.Best way I can describe this "mode" is a completely new playthrough, which gives you access to post-game dungeon (and true ending). It's not a traditional New Game+.The only real difference in this playthrough is you can use all companions instead of normal units (regular playthrough limits you to 2 companions). Story is identical. Choice outcomes are identical. You just fight 1 extra boss at the end.Combat is your standard Tactical RPG, BUT with about half of tactical components removed. Almost everyone has the same amount of movement, covers(Line of sight) does not apply to magic and flanking(back attacks) only seem to work when attacking from 2 sides (with different units). It's not a very deep tactical combat system, as it doesn't allow you to boost your damage or evade enemy damage strategically.Crowd Control and Debuffs are the 2 things you can use to your advantage. In most fights you AoEs and CC with your opponent and then proceed towards trading 1 target attacks.Also, I have to mention "Ultimate" abilities. You get them towards the end of the game, and while they are good, You will never get to use them (unless you play on high difficulties), because they take 5 turns to charge. In my playthrough ONLY boss battles lasted long enough to charge an ultimate. Funny thing is, they don't have the same value against bosses as they do against normal enemies, because unlike normal fights, you only do damage and don't reduce damage intake by taking out priority targets.Different builds actually play differently. Available skills overlap across different classes and there's value in mixing skills from different trees (rare quality). I felt like magic builds are vastly superior to melee. To put it bluntly, AoE is king, and magic allows you to place your AoEs better.You take over resource generators in the world and they passively generate resources (only while the game is running). You use those resources to upgrade your city, equipment and buy troops. Despite collecting/conquering everything, I was always short on resources. Also, all upgrades are gated behind story progress.I feel like 80% of city aspect only slowed me down without adding anything to the game..Equipment is generic stat gear with hidden geargear score (equipment drops gradually gets better despite it always starting out at tier 1).  The stupid thing about equipment, is when you fight upgrades, you have to upgrade each item to whatever tier you're at (which ends up being a huge resource sink).Some story passable (generic "Whoa you're about to die. BOOM You're the chosen one"), but writing includes mediocre text sex(fanfic tier) and gore way too often. I am convinced some sections are written by a teen who just hit puberty.  No it's not romance, just sex. For example, you're on a quest to find spleens, you just come up to a pile of dead bodies and get a choice to have an orgy. Talk to a random rock demon for the first time ever? SEX TIME! Undead queen? LET'S GOOOO! It's optional, but feels really out of place.You're on a quest and then it goes "but what if this demon cook cooked ZOMBIE SOUP?!?!?!".Many side quests force you to sacrifice creatures for no real reason. I feel like you're forced to choose between kicking a puppy or eating boogers too often. I don't think a few of these would hurt the game, but I feel like this game overuses these.They have a bunch of nice time saving options (such as the auto-win when you outlevel the enemy), but then they make you do these completely useless things, like manually leveling up companions (required participants in some fights), which basically has to travel to city and spend a few pennies. Most of the named NPCs in this game look identical to generic units. This is not a huge problem, but for a 40$ game, they could at least put a mole/mustache on the dialogue images of NPCs so I know I'm talking to a different NPC without reading the name.There's more, and none of it is game breaking, but  I think this game being priced as it is could use a lot of polish in these things.I enjoyed the gameplay, but I wouldn't recommend it even if they didn't have that deluxe edition. It's okay, for UP TO 20$, but for 40.... I think you'll find similar gameplay with better features AND at a lower price.I would say it's great for a 20 hour game. Fine for up to 40. When you go into 100 hour territory (replaying entire game from scratch for true ending), I say it's tedious. There's barely enough variety to keep me engaged in 1st playthgrough. 2nd one feels like torture

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.  Highly recommend.  Has some issues, but overall a great experience. Pros:- Great Story- Great voice acting and dialogue (for the most part)- Good graphics and animations- Great unit and spell selectionsSlight Issues:- Racial reputation is poorly designed and poorly explained.  You unlock units by building reputation, but the game doesn't tell you that you basically have to go "all-in" on one (or maybe two) races if you actually want to make progress.  If you don't, and try to role-play answers based on how you think your character would handle a situation, you wont make any progress as your negatives will keep offsetting your positive gains.- The city management is not great.  You basically have 6 spots to build for 14 buildings.  Two of them are permanent (I feel) and the rest are racial buildings you are supposed to phase in and out. - Resources are balanced poorly.  By the end of the game I had hundreds of thousands of wood and iron, but was always waiting around for gold.  You can exchange and buy all currencies except gold.  This was a strange design decision.Big Issues:- Balance in this game is awful.  If I was starting the game over, I wouldn't have picked a Witch.  By the end of the game, using Fear of Darkness or Evenfall, you clear entire maps with one cast.  Units become irrelevant.  The game is reasonably easy as it is; playing a Witch breaks end game.- New Game + was strangely thought out in this game... basically "play it all over from scratch but this time with some different dialogue options".Overall I loved playing this game.  Especially the first 3/4 or so.  The ending quarter, based on the game breaking balance issues of the Witch, I was just reading the story as each combat only lasted until my Witch went.

_childDocuments_.review: Will give this a positive rating but not because I am personally convinced but because the game is somewhat playable and I assume it can be fun for some people.Note though, that if you are a fan of the previous Disciple games, this one is different! (which is the only reason I bought it in the first place, cause I disliked previous Disciple games).Anyway, I was 35 hours into the game (although it is more like 22 if you take away the AFK time) and I felt bored. Each map feels so similar... 50% fights you can auto-win, X amount of chests with crap loot, X amount of ressources randomly scattered around, a few quests that basically only ask you to kill certain enemies, usually 2-3 places that you cannot go yet. I do not quite understand the point of the story, guess it is average when you finish the game.This being a turn based strategy game, I feel like the game is way too easy though. I bought the deluxe edition: usually bonus items etc. you get somewhat blend into the game and give you a tiny little bit extra at the start. But here... 5 extra skill points?! Two usable items that last for half the game? ouch.Now about the fights... 50% is auto-win as mentioned above, with no penalty doing the auto-win. All other fights have the potential to be somewhat varying. However...SPOILER AHEAD... there is that one unit that costs the lowest amount of leadership (10), having a 2-hex AOE spell that both, heals your allies and damages your enemies. This is completely overpowered. You can see that the game wants you to grind down individual units but with those AOE healer/damager you kick 50-100% of all enemy creatures after putting your units on "wait" in the first round. Anything that is left can be taunted by your main hero from the third map onwards, which means you will never lose a single unit, not even against big dragons.

_childDocuments_.review: "A Disciples game? In the 2020s? This must be a wish come true!"And it was, but I didn't hear the creak of a finger on the monkey's paw curling.Disciples Liberation is a long, solidly written title that is held all the way back by its combat.Said combat is balanced, frequent, and sucks.Everything is just enough of a hitsponge to keep you from onetapping units, but also not enough of a hitsponge to keep the enemy force from converging on and killing one of your units if they spend their whole initiative pass doing it (and they often do.) The first phase of each fight is a big clash of armies where everything moves slow even on 300% speed, but at least there's a little bit of tension. After that single round you spend another 11 minutes hunting down all the foes that broke and ran after that big clash. Several of which have immobilization abilities, healing, self-resurrection, or stunlocking.Combat is on a hexgrid, not jrpg style like in earlier Disciples, and the game *suffers* for it. There are so many fights, they're basically all the same, and the game even gives you a tool for skipping ones you're overlevelled for---and then never lets you use it. You'll bumble into a random wandering pack of six skeletons you have ten levels on and the game will insist that you go through the motions of fighting them.There's also a lot of... let's call it mechanics with a whiff of live service to them. The game feels like it was maybe meant to be a gatcha and then got veered off into single player. Which, kudos to the dev team if so, but it explains the very grindy progression.Also it explains the boss that you fight about 30 hours in. The first boss, in fact. And it takes 45 minutes of uninteresting whacking with your whole team to kill it, at no point of which are you in any danger until right at the end, when it randomly non-telegraphs an attack that is field-wide and strong enough to oneshot your commander if you haven't been grinding those tedious fights.The writing is, again, quite good, and I think without any combat I could safely recommend the game. Choices are meaningful, the world is compelling, and the characters feel like they fit the tale.However, with the combat, I think you need a high tolerance for tedium to get all the way through this.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often give "No" review.. And I really did TRIED to like this game (I like strategy game, and look at my hours played), I went through the entire thing, and my final thought is: I felt like I've wasted my time here, which I shouldn't have.. (Writing this so you don't have to)The game started ok, but get boring and tedius soon at about mid game.. The moment you are able to recruit Tier 3, you've probably already checked the rest of the units and seen all the game has to offer. And if you know what you're doing, your team is probably already pretty OP too and most battles are just chores (I'm playing at Brutal difficulty). There aren't even much strategy involved, you could just use 1 same team and do every battle (occasionally swapping 1 back row maybe), it's just a click-fest.. My Avy can insta-kill 2-3 enemies with crits (easily maxed) in the first turn at late game.. Oh and the DLC is just adding even more OP units that you definitely don't need.. Really nothing to lose (except your time) without it.Exploration and items are also unrewarding and boring, almost all treasures are just randomized useless equipment or resources that you don't need more...  The city building part & resources management too felt like brain-dead filler to waste the player time... You just go there to click every level like playing a mobile game :/Dialogues and story is decent but not very exciting, some of those choices feel very out of place to me especially those that allow Avy to tried romance random stranger / monster lol... Then the main story, the true ending is locked at New Game+... I have a bit of interest in that but ultimately can't justify spending more days & hours on it just to grind through the same tedious stuffs, the game length should've been much shorter for that.The art and music are probably the only few things that are pretty well done here, environment and units looks fine. Some of the characters though.. Are reused model with added effects (which really cracked me lol, I don't care how the game try to phrase it, it's obviously due to laziness).. Man, the moment I saw Avy's mother model.. Am I playing a custom Warcraft 3 map or what..?Conclusion (4/10): Do yourself a favor and skip this one if you like challenging and satisfying gameplay, there are definitely better similar games out there (I have fonder memories of playing old King's Bounty than this). Unless if you prefer an easy game + time waster, you can consider giving it a try on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A good-ish turn based combat RPG,  that has some similarities with HOMM and Kings Bounty but not quite as good as either of those two.  It’s a bit Eurojanky, and the UI could use some work (way too many menus to wade through to do simple tasks), but it's fun nonetheless.  The difficulty isn't too bad as long as you play it smart, most of the time.  I loved the dark theme of it, there’s orgies, lots of murder and torture…even spleen collecting!  The characters that can join your party are engaging and their voice acting is quite good.  I especially liked Ejamar the necromancer:  “Death is close!”   It takes a while to understand the city building aspect and the four factions you’ll be interacting with the entire game.  Overall, it's a good game with challenging combat and interesting quests...definitely worth playing.
