_childDocuments_.review: This game is by no means perfect.  It has its flaws, some of them pretty chunky ones, but I've played this game for 68 hours, and most of that was enjoyable.Pros:- Story choices matter- Varied world and mobs- Plots short enough to keep you moving and interested- Good replay valueCons:- The combat is too slow.  300% speed is not fast enough- Bosses are terrible.  Uninteresting and tedious.  (but there aren't many of them)- Most gear is utterly useless (although you can dismantle them for gold etc)- Not enough combat encounters can be skipped when you are over-levelled for them- Ultimate skills seem very poorly tunedThe game I think can be improved greatly if you use a mod to speed up movement and combat.   Although that shouldn't be necessary to install mods to enjoy a game, the devs haven't added faster speeds than 300%, so we have to do what we can ourselves.  Combat won't feel so tedious at times with the faster speed.  The other Cons are small compared to this, so if you can work around it with a mod, I would advise you to.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent some considerable time with the demo and about 9 hours with the retail game so far. This is by no means a full/complete review as I have yet to see how the story will ultimately play out. With that being said here are my initial impressions of Liberation.So lets address the elephant in the room. While it carries the Disciples name it is very much unlike previous games in the series. In essence this is a reboot or different take for the series. It very much feels far more like a Heroes of Might and Magic or a Kings Bounty. This is sure to disappoint some who were expecting a game in the vein of Disciples II and I will touch on this a bit later. Combat now takes place on a hex based grid (like Disciples 3 before it) as opposed to the more static battles of the past. It has it's pros and cons. Flanking and unit placement do open up some strategic options. There is also a "backline" Where up to three units can provide passive benefits to your allies. The problem is with the amount of battles a certain degree of tedium can set in. The devs have to their credit listened to feedback and tried to alleviate this by allowing you to speed up enemy unit turns. It does help a lot but bear in mind that you are going to be fighting a lot of the same units over and over. The problems can be compounded when you fight a lot of ranged units that tend to hang out at the other end of the map. You typically end up in a protracted battle against melee units before finally making your way to the back where the healers and other ranged units keep running about until you all but box them in. The game does offer quite a lot of quests to complete and the maps you traverse can feel quite sprawling with a lot to see. And to it's credit there are nods/references to Disciples 2 Dark Prophecy for eagle eyed series vets. For instance references to Hubert De Layle and Yata Halli are among those I found. The game has a companion system where characters that you recruit feel like decent characters in their own right with their own motivations. Unfortunately these companions often share models with bog standard unit types. Take Corisandre for instance who is one of my favorites for her healing abilities. She looks virtually identical to other priestesses you face in battle. Speaking of characters, lets talk about the main character of Avyanna...I appreciate the attempt to craft an original hero and give them their own story within the world of Disciples. Avyanna herself is a likable character. However the dialogue and options presented can at times feel at odds within the context of the world. Being more of an RPG you are able to choose dialogue options but many times these options can feel like your pidgeonholed. Take an early quest where your tasked with siding with either the elves or the human over a 10 year old boy who had trespassed and was killed by said elves. The choice boils down to whether you justify said child or not. Witcher 3 for instance is all about choice and the "Lesser evil". But the choice as presented in the scenario I outlined above had no "lesser evil". These choices play into a "reputation" system for the various factions. Empire, Elven Alliance, Undead Hordes, Legions of the Damned. No dwarves again I am afraid though there is a story/lore reason and they do address it in the game. The problem I have with this reputation/faction system is that I've never really got the impression that humans would willingly seek out alliances with the legion or undead hordes. They have also written the empire to be quite a bit darker. It's a different take on the Empire and one that kind of lines up with the state the Empire is in in previous entries. The problem is if you really want access to certain units be it the empire's knights or some of the elven units? You need good standing and good standing with one faction affects standing with another. Further still, negative reputation gives your units a passive debuff that gets worse the worse your reputation is. In this sense the game kind of pidgeonholes you again regarding what units you may get access too. And these units never feel as precious as they did in the previous games where you promote them and change class via upgrades to your capital. Here the units feel more like disposable canon fodder and can easily be replaced should they fall by spending some resources like Gold, etc.Resources themselves are handled differently. In previous Disciples games you changed the terrain via planting rods to capture gold mines, or rune stones. The terrain based resource mechanic is gone here. Instead you capture buildings for things like lumber, or gold which generates over time. You then collect it at the capital. This can be a double edged sword because sooner or later you end up with so much that it feels inconceivable that you would ever run out. The capital upgrades are kind of like previous games where you "Phase in" new structures which determine what units you can recruit.Finally it has to be said that Liberation falls short in terms of aesthetic. This may be the first major release Frima handled. But part of what makes Disciples what it is; is the aesthetic/atmosphere. While the main maps you explore are quite nice looking with lots of environmental detail? This game at times can feel incredibly generic. The UI in particular feels pretty underwhelming and lacks the flair people expect from Disciples. Even DIsciples 3 I think had designs that felt more in line with Disciples. It's really quite apparent when your in menus, etc. and it at times feels like this could be any other mobile game. The music too is a crucial part of Disciples atmosphere. The title track is decent enough. But when you played DIsciples 2 you had a a lot of ambient tracks as well. I realize my review probably sounds incredibly negative, but that doesn't mean I hate the game. It's because I love the series and while there are some good things in Liberation? I feel at times it doesn't really feel like a Disciples game aside from an occasional wink or a nod to what came before. It feels every bit like the formula was changed to give it broader appeal. While I understand the desire to do so; it risks losing the series identity in translation. Does Disciples have to be another Heroes or Kings Bounty? Is Liberation worth checking out? Sure. If your looking for another Disciples 2 you won't find it here. At the same time it is perhaps unfair to criticize this game for what it isn't rather than what it is. Play the demo if you can (if it's still available). My opinion may change once I finish the game, but I still think there are some things they could improve if they look to do another installment. Perhaps Liberation's greatest test will be whether it can liberate itself from being compared to Disciples 2. Time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen so many "This game sucks because it's not Disciples 2..." comments when looking through various reviews for this game and tbh, I'm glad I gave it a shot and bought it.The major complaints I see are:"It looks too cartoony, not like Disciples 2!!" - Have you seen Disciples 2 recently?  The game was made in a time where cartoony style graphics was the way these games looked.  To be completely honest here, this complaint makes literally no sense as it looks less cartoony than previous games in the series..."The story and voice acting suck/This is nothing like the original Disciples stories" - Voice acting is largely above par, with occasional slip ups.  Better than some, not exactly on par with the likes of PoE2. but certainly not awful either.  As for the story, I'm around 2/3 through act 2.  So far it's felt very much like a Disciples story.  The story itself is a pretty convoluted, lengthy tale with various (potentially seen as convenient) plot devices to justify war.  Not sure what makes this one worse than any of the others lol.  I've been enjoying it so far personally and I come from a background of having loved Disciples 1 & 2.  Reincarnation, less so.I also tend to see most of these complaints come from people who have less than an hour in the game...  For a game that's 80+ hours..."The combat is boring" - Enemies are less bullet-sponges than Disciples 3.  The games combat also feels less brutally unfair than previous games. D2, getting started was always a pain as your casters would die almost any fight with archers.  D3. the fights often felt brutally one-sided to the enemy until you levelled up.Here, it's still much the same and they WILL focus fire your casters down, so that's still the same.  But the enemy die just as easily as you do rather than seeming to take 2-3x the hits of your guys.Otherwise it feels just like other disciples games.  Units have always had 1-2 attacks depending on level and iteration, no idea why people are complaining about that fact unless this is the first game they've ever played in the series.So TL;DR - Don't let the negative reviews put you off.  It's a good story, looks decent, combat is alright, but I find the story was always better than the combat in the series, this is no different.  Slightly easier, but feels less unfair against the player for BS reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent grimdark RPG with hex-based battles.  The story is also pretty good, the combat is fun, there's lots of choice in how you navigate the world and quests, the voice acting is good, there's a lot to like.But it's firmly in the 7 out of 10 territory, which is a shame as it had a lot of the elements of greatness.  But there's just too many rough edges.For starters, the game is way too padded.  This game takes 80 hours when it could easily have been 50.There is a Conquest feature which lets you autoresolve trivial fights but the problem is it isn't very well balanced, especially for play on the hard difficulty.  It forces you to always fight in quest battles regardless of how weak the enemy is and that's fair enough, but I was always going about with maximum number of units with maximum leadership, finding the weakest enemies I could find on the world map and there were still times I was forced to fight units of 5 levels below me which I end up breezing through.  Speaking of leadership, this is the amount and quality of units you can have in your army at any one time, with higher class units taking more of your leadership allowance.  And this figure ramps up so slowly, sometimes only for a value of 5 every few levels of XP (there are NO units in the game that have anything less than a round figure of 10,20,30 or 40 leadership cost, so the 5 point increase is pointless as far as I could tell), and you find that not only the fighting is a slog, but the evolution of your army is as well as most battles only give you about 50xp.  And with a XP threshold of 1000xp per level, it means you would potentially have to fight 20 battles per level up(!).  My advice is, do every quest you can find as soon as you can to speed up your leveling, to maximise your chances of being able to skip a few combats.The excessive battles are further hampered by the slow speed.  Every battle startup you have to wait for all starting abilities to trigger, again and again.  And the max combat speed is only 300%.  So every battle takes a minimum of 10 minutes when it's a foregone conclusion you're going to win from the start.And there's lots of other time wastes everywhere - once you enter the compare forces screen prior to a battle, if this particular battle doesn't let you retreat, you can't quick load or exit to menu - you have to proceed to battle, wait for the starting abilities to trigger, then EXIT TO MAIN MENU, and THEN reload.  It's bonkers that anyone thought this was a good  user experience.  And when you level up, you always want the rest of your army to be leveled up as well, so you go back to base and click level up.  But there's no mass level-up button, you have to click on every single unit in your army and hit level up.  This is incredibly tedious, to the point where you end up keeping absolutely no reserves to speed up the process of leveling, as then you're only leveling up your companions.  But then you inevitably get hit with a multi-battle scenario, with multiple battles are strung one after another without chance to return to base to replenish your army, so if you lose some units in the first battle you've no reserves to replace them and you're absolutely screwed.  It's beyond infuriating.Also there doesn't seem to be a point to the DLC if you're not playing in New Game +, as the enemies always scale to your level and in the first go around you're never going to reach the level cap, so those quests were always marked as hard in the game with enemies in those areas several levels above me.  Basically any quest that is medium is generally too hard, you have to level up until the quest is rated as easy or very easy before it becomes beatable generally speaking, as levels make a huge difference in this game.And there's other annoyances like you can't portal to homebase in a dungeon.  And some of those dungeons are huge.  And you're on foot in them so if you lose any units in a battle you have to slowly leave the dungeon, portal back home, recruit replacements, portal back and then walk all the way back through the dungeon.Honestly I wanted to love this game but it fought me at every step.Just a little bit more playtesting and a little more polish and you'd be looking at one of the best games of it's year of release.Instead it's just a mildly forgettable, decent RPG.  So if you can look past some of the above, and really enjoy RPGs and hex-based battle, then I would still recommend you pick it up, but only on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Disciples: Liberation

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this one a thumbs down, since it is my kind of game.Sadly, Liberations has many great ideas, but most are very poorly implemented, the game could have easily used another year of fine-tuning the gameplay mechanics / designs in development. It’s a looker, but has little to offer beyond that.In the end it made me appreciate the Kitauri made Kings Bounty games even more - they are a well-designed, smooth running gameplay machines in comparison.The most negative points for me are:- the deeper you are in the game the more of a repetitive drag it gets; progression gets slower and slower….- extreme poorly designed loot/item system; soon you learn to expect nothing when opening a treasure chest; it’s just trash you will disassemble- unit design lags hard in gameplay mechanics variations, there are about 60 different units, that share like <10 skills with different color variations (main reason the combat gets boring so quickly - the fancy tire 4 dragon does the same stuff as your tire 1 unit, just with bigger numbers and different animations)- UI/UX and especially mouse control on PC are horrible (as of V1.1); whoever approved this for release deserves to be fired (because he/she has obviously no idea how to do the job)

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few hours in, and about to uninstall. Some of my issues are nitpicky, but - to each their own.First - the main character is set - female. Call me what you want, but I wanna play a dude. Period. No customization (except for occasional clothing changes) doesn't help.Voice-acting; mediocre at best.Skill Trees - almost seem pointless. Battles - Long-winded, repetitive.Sound - repetitive. Sound effects in some places are plain over-the-top. i.e. the enemies that shoot that ice-arrow attack makes it sound like an entire mountain is crashing into the planet - way over the top.XP - I get the same amount of xp no matter what kind of battle I win: There could be two enemies or six - same EXP. Regardless of enemy level. Same XP. Super-lame here.The maps are borrrrrring. Almost nothing is interactable. And you can't 'spin' the map, which for me in an iso-game is simply a requirement in 2023.Gear - pointless. So many pieces give +1 this or +1 that - which is mathematically pointless. Also, limiting gear slots to the main character (yes, I know companions get two slots) is just silly. Theme - my elves and my undead, and my demons and my empire and.... nevermind. The 'theme' of being able to freely mix/build these is incredibly lame. Not to mention, so many of the units are either reskins or very close to reskins.Not sure where all these high-ratings come from. I just don't see it. I do see a game that could have been great, but really it's 2 out of 4 stars, at best.

name: Way of the Hunter
detailed_description: Way of the Hunter Elite Edition The Elite Edition includes the base game as well as the following extras items: Way of the Hunter: Hunter's Pack Way of the Hunter: Map Pack 1 About the Game This authentic hunting experience lets you explore and hunt in large open-world environments in the USA and Europe . Discover true to life animals in beautiful natural habitats and handle various detailed and highly realistic weapons. Way of the Hunter provides a highly immersive, completely integrated experience amongst stunning wildlife with true to live animal group behavior. Witness the changing of complex ecosystems that react and adapt to your input. Learn what it means to be a true hunter and put your skills to the test. _childDocuments_.review: Recent patches have fixed some of the bad decisions made on release. Updating to reflect that. The game is more of a realistic hunting simulator and, now that some of the release stuff has been fixed, I'd recommend it to those who have the patience to sit through the bad dialog in some of the missions who want a more realistic hunting sim.Cons (critiques, not bugs) I really hope there are more rifles and shotguns that unlock as you progress. The selection right now is kind of lame. I'm not expecting a pawn shop selection but the small amount of limited hunting gear is meh. Would be nice to see some AR-10/15 style weapons, some hand cannons, and some bow/crossbow action. You can only hunt waterfowl with shotguns. Kind of a weird design decision but whatever. The shotgun names are tied to the lore which I haven't cared enough to learn about and, I'm sure they're clever in someone's head, but $15k for a double barreled shotgun named after "who cares the jack" is a bit much. No sleeping bags (at least that I have found) or tents to camp out near a shooting house. There are some camps near some of the shooting houses but some of the shooting houses are quite a hike.The voice-overs are cringe and there's a sense you're being waterboarded when waiting on the radio dialog to end so you can actually do something. I tend to walk away because I really don't care if Timmy fell down the well or not. Would be nice if there was a skip button here because it sucks when you fast travel to the lodge and then have a 10 minute long radio conversation where you can't even open the door to the lodge. Really, really bad decision there. Missions are the number 1 way to unlock gear, so you're basically held hostage to a bad story trying to get better guns.The emails are pretty bad. Just accept the quests without reading them if you enjoy your sanity. It's basically Facebook grammar.Beginner scopes are garbage. Even medium-tier scopes are pretty bad. Save your money for the two highest end scopes and just use your basic starter scope.The perk system - level 3 of any perk includes penalties that make me want a way to lock the perk at level 2 so I don't get dinged for progress.Bugs:Getting stuck inside a tree when crouched beside almost every tree. Bypass is proning/jumpingBlood - This was buggy at first. Haven't had a chance to test if they fixed the meshes yet or not but pre-patch, blood would fall through the mesh and sometimes the animal you shot (heart insta-kills) would also fall through the mesh. Haven't seen this in a while. I'm assuming it's fixed.Pros - The game looks great. There aren't gaggles of animals around like in theHunter so it doesn't feel like you're tripping over corpses every 5 seconds.No charge to reload ammo. Just need to open the trunk on your jeep or open the safe in a lodge.You get perk points by just wandering aimlessly - something most people who buy hunting games don't mind doing.I really like the swamp biome. It's my favorite so far.Decent variety of animals to hunt.I have high hopes. I pre-purchased the elite edition after watching Raptor live stream the game. Currently, I recommend the game with a buyer beware - If you're into instant gratification, large selection of weapons, and dialog that doesn't suck, pass. I reserve the right to change my review however I feel like, whenever I feel like because Murica.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally reviewed this game when it was released, and it had a lot of problems back then, so I gave it a negative review.  I came back to it around October of 2023, and really began playing it anew at that time.  They've fixed most of the bugs, and the game is great.As a Hunter:  Call of the Wild (HCOTW) player for several years now, I think many of the negative reviews about the graphics are people who've come from HCOTW and just don't realize how exceptional that game's graphics are.  It's the # 1 thing about that game.  This game's graphics are good.  Not perfect, but still very good.  In most cases I suspect that the graphical complaints are sour grapes from people who have no problem running a 7 year old game (HCOTW) and expect a 1.5 year old game to run just as well on their older PCs.  I've played this game now on four different PCs, and a laptop, and in all cases it plays just fine.The other complaint I see a lot in the comments is that it's a, 'hiking game', not a 'hunting game'.  There's zero truth to that.  There are animals all over the place in this game.  If people can't find them in this game, it's because they don't understand the basic principles of hunting and they're simply trying to play above their skill level.  The solution in that case is to simply swallow your pride and turn your difficulty down, or consider a longer shot.The shooting experience itself is great, and much better than HCOTW.  Sighting down a scope feels much more "real" and less flat than HCOTW.  The story modes in each map are decent, and usually have more voice acting than HCOTW.  It's really a toss up as to which game's stories are better.  Then again, it's a hunting game.  If you want epic stories, you should probably go play The Witcher 3.The areas the game still lags a bit behind HCOTW are lack of weapon choices (though this has been improving quite a bit.  They really need a few more lever-action options and different bullet types - the latter of which I hear is coming.  They also need to polish and improve multi-play.  Other than that, though, the game is exceptional and well worth the asking price, imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Far superior to Hunter call of the wild, incredibly detailed animals, animal behavior, environment. World is huge and filled with details anywhere you go, even the most further edges of the super large maps. Every bit of game play is simulation, it is like real life. Those who complain that it is hard to line up a shot, they never hunted in real life before. This is not an arcade game, this is a simulation. If you like arcade like hunting call of the wild does that, this game is super realistic (and as such very difficult) hunting simulation. At that nothing comes close to this title, this is simply the best out there (not of the best, this is the best and only available in this category).I have seen lots of complaints of other open world titles where the game world is mostly copy / paste of the same features and layout of existing design, well Way of the Hunter shows large open worlds can be created without cheating the system, this open world is worth exploring, variety is everywhere (however it helps if you know how real world looks like, to someone who has never been to a forest, hiked a trail, a forest all the same everywhere (to my wife for instance a forest is boring and all the same everywhere - mostly). I recommend this title if you strive for realistic hunting experience.This is NOT a shooting gallery targets / animals appearing everywhere in front of you. Each achievement here is extremely rewarding for the amount of work, tracking, patience, skill you have to invest. Sometimes gets easy, but most of the time it will be hard.If you consider Way of the Hunter you have to understand animal behavior using the game's database. Each animal has sleeping, eating, drinking habits each linked to a time of day. First you need to discover where the animal eats, sleeps, drinks, its area of habitation (consider multiple lakes and eating areas, not just one). Then you want to plan your hunt to frequent these locations during the "right" time of day for a certain animal type. If you just wander around aimlessly your result and efficiency will show this, the game will not make anything here easy for you. Try difficulty "Adventurer", that is what I am playing on, this setting is still challenging enough to ensure you "simulate" real life hunting experience.Also, do not forget your scent and how the wind carries it. Open your map (TAB) and look at the icon representing you on the map. You should see a "pinkish fog" spreading in one direction depending of wind, this is your scent and its spreading in the forest. If you hunt 'downwind" most likely animals move away before you have a chance to spot anything.Map Size: After careful assessment I see each map (there are two of them) 100 square kilo-meters or about 38.6 square miles each. These areas are huge (I am 70 hours in and still barely left the few main roads and paths I managed to get to from the large network of roads and drive-able paths as I am always bogged down with tracking something), these are areas of 6.2 miles wide and about 6.2 miles deep. Also these areas are not system generated barren wastelands, these areas a handmade with highly detailed lands and shorelines, lakes, and mountain ridges and valleys, seemingly personal attention given to every tree branch, piece of grass, rocks, water flow in rapids, so forth and so on... This cannot be and should not be compared to google earth like environments (I would not even put them in the same class with other hunting games or even GTA5 level of world detail, while those maps are also considerably smaller), on such maps you zoom in a bit and details degrade fast, but this is not true here, details will never cease to impress in Way of the Hunter (also amazing animal detail and mechanics described above). Either way, this is a huge world, possibly never done before on this level maintaining this incredible world size all in one project.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another one of those games where Steam reallllly needs a neutral recommendation option (summary at end)..Way of the Hunter does 'some' things right Call of the Wild did not/could not. But currently, it does a little too much wrong..Animals look great, the animations are on point. But their behaviors are still unrealistic and quite stupid.. Young and Adult animals have one thing in common : they looked like they're being baited high protein diets.. seriously, young animals look buff. It's weird. Now for animal tracking : its lack-luster. Tracks are hard to see due to graphics (see below) and they are basically copy-paste. No real variety nor do they provide any unique information. In fact, there's absolutely NO need to follow any tracks. It's far more efficient to walk, spam calls, wait to see an animal in the distance or hear a call response. Its an element that feels like an after-thought. The environment looks great, at a medium distance. They did a solid job with bump-mapping texture..but the environmental graphics are still dated for 2015+. Textures up close are blurry and textures in the distance are blurry. They rely on vignette and depth of field to make the distant graphics look appealing.. but those exact setting cause nausea, eye strain and headaches. And I'm pretty sure the reason why we can't turn those settings off is ultimately because this game isn't well optimized (it's not).Now for weapons.. there's not a lot to choose from. Seriously. This game currently lacks content. And much of the content there is-is gated behind the WORST part of the game (standby for that). Crossbow ballistics are abysmal. Just absolutely horrible. And getting stuck in the reload animation is very frustrating. All-around, caliber ballistics are unrealistic. And again, there's not much to choose from; especially no option to choose different types of ammo.. Their 'bullet cam' is well done. Not surprising considering some of the devs came from Cabela (known for the bullet cam). There's a few glitches regarding the bullet cam/bullet pathing, but I'm sure they'll polish it out (glitches aren't common).Now for the worst part : missions/story/quests. They are HORRIBLY annoying. And you are FORCED to do them since not only is a lot of the content gated behind them, they are also the best way to make money. Yup. Be prepared to spend the beginning of your experience with this game knocking out useless quests, rather than enjoying a sandbox hunting experience..In summary, Way of the Hunter has a good 'foundation' to build upon. But it's NOT a finished game. There's a lot of work to be done, especially optimization to be had.. Their road map isn't very promising as a lot of issues/content players have been asking for attention aren't present on it. And knowing the past work of some of these devs isn't promising.. But the devs are at least active. If you're a fan of Call of the Wild, you WILL enjoy this game. You will understand much of what I have said in this review.."Way of the Hunter does 'some' things right Call of the Wild did not/could not. But currently, it does a little too much wrong.." What Way of the Hunter does right, is enough to throw $40 at it, if you have the money to spare. Else give it a wait. Also, if you are like me and your eyes are sensitive to graphical settings like depth of field and vignette, I would suggest giving this game a wait until the option to turn it off is added. I currently get about an hour of gameplay in before I have to step OUTSIDE and stare at trees in the distance.. the game makes me THAT nauseated (this is a game-breaker for many players). Hope this review helps some folks.. I suggest visiting their Discord for inquiry, and NOT steam's forums.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked how beautiful the game was, the nature and the sounds are amazing. However, the animal reactions and early game mechanics are terrible. I posted up 150m, downwind, crouching, unmoving, and lifting my gun to sight the deer was enough to spook it. Which forces you to make longer shots, no matter how perfectly I would set it up, would end up only barely injuring the animal, slow death, which with the realism of the game is agonizing. Also there must be some other adjustments that need to be made. Animals would occassionally just disappear. I'd hear a deer 150m away, get out my binoculars and then no longer hear it or be able to find it. Frustrating experience especially as you're slowly having to move every where. If you want to skip time, you have to either just wait it out in the stand (a little too realistically boring) or go back home/campsite, sleep, and try again. Pretty frustrating, I'm hoping these are just some game release issues and I'll try to come back later but overall very frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't pay the haters any mind. This game is a 'thumbs-up' for sure. Yeah, there are some kinks that need tweaking, but overall it's a very solid hunting simulator. I would even go as far as to say that the sense of immersion, attention to detail and overall realism on display here, beat out 'The Hunter: Call of the Wild' hands down. I think the $40 price-tag is within reason, and if you enjoy hunting and stealth simulation games, then you'll likely really enjoy this one. In my opinion, although TH:COTW is way more 'arcade-like' than this game, it will probably retain it's title as the top hunting game on Steam for now, but that is largely due to more than 5 years of constant updates, patches and 100's of dollars in DLC. Way of the Hunter can't quite compete with that kind of legacy just yet. Regardless, taken as a starting platform and more in the vein of an actual hunting simulator, it outshines it's competitor. The campaign, although kinda low-key, feels very believable, almost as if you're playing through a Discovery Channel documentary. The tracking and the various animal's behavioral mechanics are more dynamic, unpredictable, and realistic when compared to TH:COTW. Overall, this is a very promising start to a new franchise. I look forward to how this game will grow, improve and expand with new content. If you're an avid virtual hunter, then this game is a must.

Unfortunately with games nowadays it seems they are releasing with so many bugs and this game was one of them. Most have been worked out through patches but come on. This game is much slower paced than THCOTW, It's not possible to just run around shooting animals like you can in THCOTW. Overall this game is a recommend but is far from a perfect hunting game. If you like hunting in real life this game is for you. If you don't have patience to sit in a spot for awhile until an animal passes by then this game is not for you.

Like one of the perks requires you to crawl 7 kilometers to get it. The crawl speed is incredibly slow, maybe .3 meters a second. Someone can do the math on how many literal days worth of crawling that is.- To hunt in areas outside of the starter area requires a "private pass", of which there are currently 8, and they cost 4,500 currency each. A good buck gets you around ~300 currency. Hunting small game is worthless as they only yield ~20 currency.- Downed animals disappearing as you walk up to them.- Birds just sink straight to the bottom in bodies of water.- Shooting an animal in the lungs at 100 yards and the animal nor the herd reacting at all; ghost bullets?- Getting stuck in rocks and environment requiring a restart of the game.- Crashing to desktop.- Massive desync in co-op. Player models and animations look really wacky.Missions are bland, bizarre and seem like they give no rewards whatsoever. The 4th or 5th mission is As everyone else has said, no FoV or ultrawide support. Feels like a really bad console port. Framerate isn't very good on a near top of the line rig running at 1440p.Should have been an Early Access release for sure. Call of the Wild does everything better except for graphical fidelity. I hate to trash a game in such a niche genre that I enjoy, but maybe THQ pressed the devs into releasing this early. Needs at least another year or two in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand why people are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the game for no reason. Yes it will be nice if they add FOV options, but current FOV is okay plus its not a shooting game so its not like it even matters that much.  I can definitely understand being annoyed at the lack of key bind listings or being able to change the key binds but neither this or the FOV issue is representative of the quality of the game. Now lets go into the specifics of the game. Its an amazingly realistic hunting experience, although (as expected) can be difficult in higher difficulties. _childDocuments_.review: New Review:Yeah... They haven't done a damn thing for this game since release. They are too focused on releasing new DLC to actually fix the game. The graphics are somehow worse than at launch, to the point that you can ONLY play with DLSS on as Anti Aliasing, but even then, it looks as if im playing an arcade game from the 80's, the game is so pixelated and jagged. Not only that, but this makes it damn near impossible to see blood or tracks, or really anything, as its SO pixelated and jagged, the game ends up appearing blurry. This also causes moving objects to have terrible ghosting trails. Even the graphics aside, the game is riddled with bugs and glitches that have been around since launch. Your'e lucky to get a patch from the devs, and when they do patch the game, its maybe 6 fixes in total?! Its damn near unplayable at the current state, and while I was excited for it when it came out, after 2 years of nothing being changed, that excitement has long faded. Dont buy it. The hunting mechanics are fine, but you aren't able to appreciate them in a game that looks and runs worse than a unity asset flip. Hell, the devs even hide all of its downfalls more than asset flip devs. You can see the graphical issues in screenshots and videos of the game, but they rarely use still shots, and when the issue is brought up, it is ignored. Its horrible management top to bottom.Original Review:Okay, let me get this straight. This is by far not a perfect game. The graphics, particularly the AA is terrible, there are the occasional bugs, and there is room for improvement gameplay wise. That however does not mean it is a terrible game. This is by far one of my favorite hunting games compared to COTW or hunter classic. The story I find much better than those found in COTW. Unlike how every map is just helping out some old dudes jpeg image to clear a certain forest area of insert species here, you have orders to fill for local buyers, if you want of course. On top of that, there is a full story and background as to why you are there, what you are doing there, and why the place you are at is the way it is. Its a touching story, without being cheesy or a sobfest, and still focuses on the core gameplay. There are very few missions where you run around doing pointless tasks like in COTW. There are a few issues here and there however that are good to know before buying, but many will be fixed or implemented soon, according to the devs roadmap at least. Currently, there is only a small selection of shotguns, and no bows, handguns, or muzzle-loaders for that matter. On top of that, what you do have, you cannot select or buy certain ammunition, it is all locked to the firearm when purchased, and refills... somewhere, I haven't figured that one out yet. That however, is all set to be implemented, from more firearms, to different types of them. Alongside this, the new firearms are to be licensed, like so many products in game already are. This is one of my favorite parts, that I actually have heard of and possibly have used some of the firearms in real life. On top of this, It is planned for different ammo types, and the ability to select those ammo types, to be introduced. Many of the aspects lacking from the game, have been acknowledged by the devs, and are set to be put into the game. All in all, the game, while rough both at launch and even now, has potential that the devs are living up to, and i'm excited to see where it goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited months and hundreds of hours later review (original at the bottom):I'm changing my mind. Not really recommended. Yes, it's superficially very pretty, and yes, it can feel like a breath of fresh air initially compared to the utter mess that is COTW.... but WOTH is also fundamentally broken right from the core mechanics down. As already mentioned, the LOD and texture issues completely destroy any immersion, even at max possible settings. Also, the sound design is an utter mess. I have to have my sound cranked up way higher than any other game I own just to hear the things I need to hear, and then remember to effectively mute if I want to blow an elk call which are literally 10 times louder than the loudest ambient sounds (which is the wind. if there's even a slight breeze it sounds like some kind of white noise generator) and will blow your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ears off. Plus sound sticks weirdly as you change direction so you really can't trust what you're hearing and where from anyway. And deer 300 yards away cracking branches is exactly as loud as deer 40 yards away. So it's not only no use as audio cues, it's actively disorientating and misleading. Ambient sounds largely consist of annoyingly short loops with unbalanced sounds that really get on your nerves after a while.But by far the biggest issue is the animal AI; as just about everyone else remarks. The animals are basically completely blind and lack any sense of smell, but have ridiculously super strength hearing, such that you cannot get within about 200m without spooking them. Quite often before ever knowing they were there. And they seem to go from zero care to running away in a second with no indication it was a problem, often not 'alerting' at all. Cover does nothing. Terrain does nothing. You can spook a herd while flat on your belly 250m away on the other side of a hill. So basically, all the core mechanics - all the things that would immerse you in a hunting environment - are fundamentally broken. And despite many months of constant feedback from the rapidly dwindling community and despite the fact that the devs do address and acknowledge some of these issues occasionally on the (extremely toxic) forums, I see little to no evidence that anything is being done to address them. Third Edit To Add: Since Africa DLC, now appears to have much more serious and nonsensical bugs that basically render hunting pointless. Like the fact that it registers completely false information and calculates your scores based on that information; I took down a cape buffalo with a single shot, and it ran 39m and died (mid run, still in its running pose...) still in sight of me. It took me about 30 seconds to get to it and claim it, but the game decided that it took me 20.5hrs, and that meant 556kg of meat was 'lost by time', making my 580kg prize worth 20 bucks. So frankly it's really not even worth the effort of playing any more.As such, no, I can't recommend buying this yet. A hunting game where hunting is fundamentally broken and even when you take them down the recording and scoring is broken too.Original review:Somewhat recommended. One of the more authentic hunting experiences in beautiful locations let down by some bizarre omissions, irritating bugs and visually spoiled by disappointing level of detail pop even with all the settings maxed out at 5k res, which is something you really want to avoid in a game where spotting is critical and you can't make out what the random lumps in the near distance are without stopping and scoping every little thing, where it's hard to even recognise the detail you were just looking at because it's so drastically different once resolved. It kinda ruins the immersion. So why would I still recommend it? Because it's still less irritating than COTW who seem to manage to introduce a new range of game breaking bugs with every update. So I'll play it, and lots, because it's currently lesser of two evils :p

If you play on the harder settings and just walk around enjoying a walk in nature you are bound to barely see any animals (since they would all flee from your scent and noise), but this is a game that makes sense even to do just that, take amazing walks over hills and through forests far, far away from the madding crowds..

_childDocuments_.review: Just great,as many have said before, Way of the Hunter is a hunting game for people who want a more realistic hunting experience than many competing products.Especially in "Ranger" mode (hardest difficulty) this game unfolds a challenging but at the same time very satisfying hunting experience for me.Sure there are still a few things that should be improved, but as it is, it's already a top game in the hunting genre.The next patches are in the works and I can't wait for more maps and DLC to be added to the game. _childDocuments_.review: Early review after 15 hrs of playing hunter difficultyI love the game so far  :)Despite me having like no hunting experience whatsoever (neither rl or game wise) I was able to get the hang of it pretty fast. Which is amazing considering the complexity of the game. But the in-game encyclopedia does a great job at explaining important stuff like balistics, movement, animal behaviour, tracking, genetics, herd management and more.Sound, visuals and atmosphere are really good and I do like the slow pace of the game. Following animal tracks to discover their need zones or slowly sneaking up to animals to about 100m or even less (my record was about 40 m infront of a mule deer herd without getting spotted) is something I enjoy a lot. And landing your first shot to the heart so the bigger animals instantly drop with no need to track is such a rewarding feel. Also the game encourages you to pick targets of herds carefully with a herd management mechanic (instead of just shooting everything you see). If you take out the animals with "weak" genetics/fitness the herd is more likely to bring forth stronger animals, which yield better trophies. So sometimes you'll just watch a herd to see how they are developing. Awesome!Edit: Bug section removed since those I encountered seem to have been fixed completely. Still enjoying the game btw :)

_childDocuments_.review: So far into this game for almost five hours, I am enjoying the game. I have not had any bugs yet or major issues so far. I am playing using an x-box controller and it would be nice to have an ability to pick which gun is on my back and not have to go to the primary first and  secondary second every time. Example situation if i am hunting for deer and come across some ducks I would like to be able to pull out the shotgun first not the rifle. Maybe add a quick wheel for this?People are trying to compare this to COTW and in my opinion you cant. This is more of a slow pace simulator hunt forcing you to be quiet to get in close. Also COTW has had a long time to tune that game, and if the devs of this game are committed this game will become even better than its day one launch. In the end i do recommend this game for the people who want a challenging hunt. Also yesIi do have COTW and will continue to play it when i want that style of a hunting game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure if I have ever written a review on steam before. This game disappointed me so much, that I feel I have to write a review for it. I had reservations for this game almost immediately, it is so poorly optimized that the opening cut scene was stuttering. I have a good PC (an AMD 5800X3D and a 5900XT) and the game runs awful, despite my frame-rate supposedly being good (more than 100 fps). Even on max graphics settings the games visuals are fuzzy and often times, especially with fast moving animals, a blurry mess. As I am sure many reviews here have pointed out, this game launched without a field of view slider or the option to manually set keybinds. The default field of view is rather narrow. It is puzzling why the game launched without them.There are a number of small bugs, which mostly just made the game more frustrating. Bugs like going into the storage menu to find the mouse cursor invisible. Looking through binoculars to find that you have to hit the button six times to stop looking through them. Blood splatters being invisible when you looked the first three times in an area and after 15 minutes of frustrated searching seeing them where you know you looked before. Nothing game breaking, so I tried to be patient.My patience ran out when I encountered what I consider a serious bug, that has apparently permanently affected my game. I was tracking roe deer and found a drinking zone. I activated the zone, saw the information pop up on screen, and excitedly went to the encyclopedia entry for animals, just to find no entry. I exited the menu saw the pop up tell me it was a drinking zone for a roe deer, but no following pop up telling me an entry had been added to my encyclopedia. So I found another zone for roe deer. Same thing. No entry in my encyclopedia. I am afraid that the game bugged, because I hit the menu button after discovering the zone too quickly. Now I can not get an entry for roe deer, no matter what I do. I was really looking forward to hunting roe deer, as it was one of my favorite things to hunt in Hunter: Call of the Wild.This game clearly was released far before it was ready and I do not have faith these issues will be fixed any time soon. I have asked for a refund, but I am not confident I will get one because I pre-ordered it about a month ago and have played a bit too long. I regret pre-ordering this game. Strongly recommend waiting, if you are considering purchasing it. Honestly, you should look into Hunter: Call of the Wild instead. It is not a perfect game, but it is much further long from a development stand point and does most of the same things this game does, better. Maybe one day, Way of the Hunter will be the better game, but it isn't better today.
_childDocuments_.name: Way of the Hunter

_childDocuments_.review: Among the hunting enthusiast simulation games, this one stands out with the rather enjoyable stalking loop. I always enjoyed outdoor activities starting even before Scouting, but the "need" to hunt ebbed as opportunities increased as I grew up. But I never lost my love of picking carefully through the woods to discover who lives there, and peek at their lives, their homes, their schedules. Sometimes even walking right up on some poor creature that didn't expect me in his day.This game captures that part I love so much, getting to know the land and its inhabitants. No, it doesn't have a 100 combinations of rifles chambered with every caliber you can dream of.  It doesn't have a giant array of kit and tools for stalking, trapping, baiting, or ambushing. Hey, humans are cool, we make cool tools, and there are hunting games that let you power game endless trophy hunts. I get it. And those games exist.But I have hundreds of games about instruments of mass death. This is about the only one that lets me stalk through the woods. If that's the part that intrigues you, and not the tools, and you like it to look pretty good while doing it, you'll like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Way of the Hunter

_childDocuments_.review: Select Ranger difficultywake up at 4amride half the map till you get to 1km from the feeding zonewalk till you find a good place for spottingno callerssit on a highground for 2h till you spot the gamestalk white tails and elk for an hour(repeat till you manage not to spook them)with your face in the dirt get inside 15 yardscrouch, draw the bow backslowly peek from behind the tree till you see the vitals - send it.Track that fool down if you didn't dropped it right away.Be proud of yourself.Or just go night bow hunt for bears if you dig feelin' a bit paranoid, hearing multiple of them approaching you as you call, and get a little heart attack when they walk out of the bush 10yards away as you light up the flashlight.Stalking, bow hunting and herd management is way more fun/gratifying than in CoTW.If you dig misty gorgeous night scapes with dancing shadows of the spooked big game or snow maps, CoTW is what you want... for now;Hopefully not for long.Yes, it's kinda repetitive - it's a hunting sim - you walk, you spot, you kill, you go again.It's as good as what you want to make of it. Make it an adventure - not a grind.Especially if you play with someone. Spot, stalk, ambush, coordinate and enjoy the views and time spent together, tracking down those most majestic beasts of the land.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game but i can't for "technical reasons".Performance is kinda whack. This game has quite bothersome traversal stutters. On my older i9-10900F rig I even got actual frame drops down in the low 30FPS range. In addition there are quite intrusive screen space shadow artifacts and poorly filtered low resolution shadow maps. Honestly if you play the game during sunrise or sunset you'll generally experience quite a poor looking game full of graphical artifacts from poorly tuned screen space graphical rendering techniques. Long story short the game does not have the visuals to justify it's relatively poor performance. I suspect it's some limitation of UE4 related to asset streaming. I've experienced this on both my Ryzen 7900X and RTX4080 main rig as well as my older i9-10900F and RTX3070 rig. Both rigs are way above the required specs.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys hunting. I played The Hunter COTW on the console for over 100 hours and had a lot of fun with it. BUT: The game is very repetitive in the long run and the animals don't behave realistically. These problems don't exist in Way of the Hunter. The animals behave more realistically than in the competition. The graphics and map design are more immersive and make it easy to put hours into this game. Long-term motivation is also a given in this game. While in The Hunter COTW you could only grind for (far too expensive) weapons, in Way of the Hunter you have the opportunity to maintain your territory by constantly trying to improve the genetics. You are then rewarded with bigger and better trophies. I understand the criticism in other players' reviews. I also have the problem that the edges of textures often look pixelated. I hope that this will be fixed in the future. Personally, I would also like to see more content, such as tents, dummies, etc. (as they already exist in the game). (some of which already exist in The Hunter COTW).Overall, I am very happy with the game and I will invest many more hours in this game in the future. I honestly don't understand why the competition, The Hunter COTW, still gets a lot more attention than Way of the Hunter.  Way of the Hunter simply offers more immersive gameplay, which is why I will never switch back to The Hunter COTW.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: I usually hate these type of games and am very impatient, but this one is a blast. Way better than Call of the Wild (not that CotW is a bad game, this just does the core gameplay loop better). CotW comparisons like crazy below:Environment: Not really sure how to explain this, but the environments and forests feel "real" and organic in this game. In CotW all the environments and forests felt static and fake. Very very pretty and cozy/dreamy looking, but fake. Kind of like how Far Cry Primal's forests felt? Just a collection of trees placed w/ a map tool and nothing in between. IDK. Anyway, the landscapes and forests in this game are amazing.Hunting/stalking. Instead of taking out your smart phone and following glowing digital cones, you actually have to track in this game. You have to look at the footprints to see which direction the prints themselves are going. You have to look at the blood splatter and see which direction the smaller blood dots are headed, etc. Feels a lot more bad ass tracking this way vs magic phone GPS tracking in CotW.The XRay system after you claim a kill is great too. Very detailed, and you can play a little animation of how the bullet entered/exited the animal.I like the story this game has. Also cool you get your own hunting lodge right off the bat in a story way that makes sense and doesn't feel like you didn't earn it.Wish there was a dog. They need to add a dog as a companion ASAP.Oh and they also need to add bows and scents. Treestands and blinds? ehh I dont really care about those as I like stalking / exploring vs just sitting in a tree making calls covered in elk piss or w.e.Excited to see what further updates come.

_childDocuments_.review: Just literally can't be bothered with the game, sure if you're some crazed die hard hunting fan that isn't actually out there hunting, you might enjoy it? But I just found it more of an annoying ball ache than any sort of actual enjoyment. Tracking animals after you shoot them involves walking around the woods like you're lost, trying to spot a tiny red speck to attempt to follow.. Animals all have 'recommended' calibres of weapon.. yet when you use the suggested calibre, it feels like you're firing marshmallows at the animals. (Yes, I know, you're supposed to go for vital organs and such.. but when you shoot an animal, apparently THROUGH both lungs, and still have to chase it for 500 meters and shoot it AGAIN, somethings off there..) The animals seem to flit between entirely oblivious to extra sensory perception (Aka, wind in your face so no scent issues, using the most silent method of moving the game gives you, zero line of sight, yet at 200 meters they pick you up like you're coming through the woods in tap dancing shoes.) I think if we could somehow combine this game with 'The Hunter: Call of The Wild' that'd be a perfect game.. this one has better feeling shot mechanics, but the overall hunting experience, in my opinion, is vastly better in The Hunter. If you're looking for something that's less video game and more 'This is what we think real life is like' then I'm sure you'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to not recommend this, but the client has so many graphical issues on PC you basically need to start learning the entire workings of the Engine.ini config, your graphics card options and then some.Spent hours polishing up the graphics, but there's a still a hard "motion blur" on the edges of objects, terrain, etc that I can't seem to turn off (regardless motion blur is off in the ini, no TAA etc) and it's noticeable, distracting and immersion breaking, seeing edges of things 'dither' (rather than actually blur) on movement, the birds and the bees are little more than a cluster of semi-unidentifiable pixels. Dithering in general EVERYWHERE, 10m 20m in front, in reflections making them unidentifiable, in everything.Yo... You can still upscale without making the game look like it fell out of a 2002 games console. The abuse of effects on this game is simply astounding. I imagine this might work for a console visually, but PC wise the graphics are a massive mess.That being said, whilst this games a bit more 'realistic' than other games of it's genre and better difficulty settings. _childDocuments_.review: Way of the Hunter aims to be a realistic hunting simulation, but it comes with a few flaws.The game begins with a story where you step in the boots of River, a man on his way to the hunting grounds of his grandpa's. You're tasked to take care of his business while he's recovering in the hospital. As you play further, you unlock story bits, talk to people and do odd-jobs for them. Along the way you reconnect with Rivers childhood friends and other people who live in the valley. The story doesn't tie you up to anything, you're free to hunt and do your own things, but it is there if you feel like following it.The game world looks pretty nice. If you can crank up the details you have a very beautiful world to explore and hunt in. The sky is especially good looking. Though, water effects can look a bit off sometimes.In that beautiful world you have all the familiar animals to hunt; different kinds of deer, badgers, foxes, moose, bears, pheasants, ducks and so on. You know the drill. All the animals you meet belong to a herd that has their own territory on the map. The herd moves around the need zones within that territory, just like in real life and it's all very proper and good.The animals are very life like and they have neat little behavior details, such as hoof stomping or grunting when they sense the danger approaching. Generally it's all very well done, but the birds feel a little off somehow. I guess it's the animations and how robotic they can look sometimes.You can even do herd management. Take out the weak and sickly ones and let the better graded animals breed and produce off-springs for those five star trophies. It's a cool mechanic. You can observe in real time how different herds change depending on how you hunt.Guns feel pretty realistic too and there's nothing preventing you from getting the gadgets and weapons you'd like to use. No level gating or anything of the sort. Just get some money and buy the tools you need. It's great.If that was it, I'd be really happy to recommend the game to anyone, but as it stands for now, the game has a truckload of issues.The story is fine, if you care for such things. I don't so much. Not in a hunting simulation. I just wanted to create my own hunter, an avatar of myself and get out hunting. It's not bad per say, but as a simulation it takes me out of the experience when I'm not playing as myself, but instead control an established character. Some people like it, some don't. It's not directly anything that hurts the hunting experience, but it's more of a personal nitpick.Performance seems to be all over the place. The game stutters and sputters constantly and almost never works smoothly, for me anyways. The optimization just is not there yet.You're forced to use TAA anti-aliasing which makes the game look all greasy and smeared visually. Your only other options are to go with FXAA or without any AA and you don't want those, because then the game looks like it was rendered in 800x600 and up-scaled to your resolution, becoming a blurry, pixelated mess to look at.There's no FOV slider for now and that prevents me from playing the game for any length of time, because it makes me motion sick and nauseous. You also can't remap controls or even see which buttons do and what, unless you dive into the in game encyclopedia or just try them out. There is no keybinding menu anywhere. Console controller button layout though is neatly on display in the menu. This shows some serious oversight from the developers. Luckily, you don't need that many buttons to play so it's not a deal breaker or anything.There isn't a whole lot of guns or gadgets for you to get. No hunting outfits, scent eliminators. Nothing. Just a handful of rifles and a few shotguns and they only come with bird shots. There are no different ammo types either. You're going to run out of  things to spend your money on pretty quickly.None of the gear is very well explained in the shop either. For example, when you go buying a new gun, you don't really get a whole lot of relevant information about anything beyond magazine size, the "tier" of the weapon and the caliber. You just need to go and try them out if you don't already know the specs for each gun by heart.The Hunter Vision, a vision mode you use to track animals and spot objects of interests, is a poorly designed addition. Using it puts a very eye straining chromatic aberration effect around the edges of your screen and makes it difficult to look at. It also makes the game run a lot slower, dropping frames if you're not running the game on more recent hardware.I'd actually advice anyone to play the game without the Hunter Vision, because hunting without aids actually works in this game. It's just that if you're a more casual player your go to approach is probably using the vision mode as much as possible and it's such an eyesore.Tracking can be tedious. The game highlights tracks and such in white or yellow when you use Hunter Sense. The game world, the floor of the forests and hills is often yellow, brown or red toned and the highlights just disappear into the blooming colours of the visuals. You can't change the highlight colour either to make spotting them easier.Then there are little things, such as getting stuck to trees if you crouch too close to them while moving. Falling through the level geometry into the endless void, suffering from sound issues and audio balancing problems. Sometimes bullets just refuse to affect the animals. Sometimes your limbs get twisted into a knot. Lots of little things that annoy the hell out of you in the long run. I especially can't deal with that one weird bug sound that is like a miniature drone or a helicopter BRRRRRRing deep in my ear constantly during the day time. There are lots of other little issues as well, but I don't know if there's any point listing them all.There's a multiplayer mode too, but it is such a buggy mess that it's virtually unplayable.The game has a good core and it can be fun when it works and doesn't bug out too much, but I can't for now recommend purchasing and playing it. I'm going to advice you to hold onto your money until the developers come out with patches to fix the most glaring problems. In the meantime, your time is better spent playing something else, maybe a different hunting game.TL;DR: Game has potential and it can be fun, but the nauseating visuals and constant bugs and glitches drain the fun factor severely.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant possibly recommend this game to anyone in its current state. I feel as though the devs made this game out to be something its not. I get they wanted a realistic hunting experience however there are too many things  wrong with this game. Lets start with hunter sense. It's 100% useless. You might as well not even use it as a way to track your kill, you'll have better luck walking in circles up to 300m away with a lung shot. I'm telling you, they should get these animals to play for the NFL cause nothing is bringing them down in any distance remotely close to where you shot him. Blood trails? Not really. Tracks, forget about those if its a highly traveled area (read static tracks). So much for ethical hunting when you spend hours looking for your kill. And lets not talk about what happens if you don't hit a vital. Not to mention that hunter sense doesn't work while moving. Who would have thought that looking for signs of your prey would require you to stop moving? And why isnt "M" key bound to the map? Why do I have to hit esc then click on the map? Being able to pull up the map with one keystroke should be a basic in any modern game. I can live with bows not being available, but no hunting dogs? You want ME to flush out birds, then shoot them out of the air, then try and figure out where they fell without the use of a hunting dog? I thought they wanted this game to be realistic but instead its just needlessly pointless. Graphics are meh. Hunting blinds are put in the most useless of positions. Not being able to have a portable bind is insane. No scent eliminators? No ammo selections. And the achievements? Are you serious right now? 5KM in a prone position?  Sounds.. in general are just lazy, The river sounds are either full on, or non-existent. In a blind next to a river?? How would you know? They don't make any noise. Get out of the blind and its loud as hell. The ducks on the water quaking sound like they flew right over your head but are still floating on the water. But keep telling me how this game is realistic and ethical. Are you telling me that you couldn't take the time to actually use distance and location for the sounds in the environment to make it more realistic? The idea that you could improve a herd by culling the weak was a major selling point, however given the amount of effort it requires to harvest your kill.... I thought this was going to be a much better game based on what they said they were trying to accomplish, however every aspect of this game falls flat. Please, for the love of God, don't make another hunting game.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is primarily to be another counterpoint to the people review-bombing it.Pros:+ Animal models are very good, with good animations and transitions between animations.+ Foliage looks very good at a distance and not that bad up close.+ Tracking animals by the blood trail is pretty interesting, the blood splatters are detailed and show the direction the animal was moving without being an arrow pointing right to them. Tree limbs will be spattered with blood if the animal brushes up against them, and tall grass will also be spattered.+ "Hunting Sense" gives you the toggle-able ability to see animal tracks, spoor, need zones, blood trails, etc with a light outline. The fact that it is not on or off all the time and in an easy at-will keybind makes the game much more immersive and visually stimulating.+ The Perks system gives you a type of progression without being tied to "levels".+ Small touches. There are lots of these, far too many to go into in a quick review like this. From the blood spatters, the focus on ethical hunting, the calls and sounds of animals moving, to an extra-long-range rendering distance for animals (about twice as far as Call of the Wild).+ Animals age! That young deer already has an impressive rack (don't giggle), but it has room to grow. So let it grow. It will become a trophy buck after a few more play sessions. Though if you don't find it again, it may die of old age. Seriously.+ This goes hand-in-hand with the previous pro, and that is that you can essentially make trophy herds by careful selection and culling. That's an incredible level of detail in a game like this.+ Varied calls allow you to call in the specific type of animal in a herd you're looking to hunt. Does, low-quality males, and higher-quality trophy males.Cons:- No FOV slider on launch - Devs have already said this is coming in the near future.- Some people have had the game crash on them. Is this unheard-of on launch day for games?- No way to change or alter keybinds at launch - Devs are already fixing this in the near future.- Some controls are a bit sluggish, specifically weapon swaps.- The visual transition to and from Hunter Sense is disorienting to some people.- Multiplayer is unstable at launch - again, not unheard-of at launch (the game's been out for like 3 hours now) and I'd give it a week or so for them to get things much more stable.- Weapon descriptions are pretty poor, as is information on which firearms are better for which animals at-a-glance on the shop page.- Shotguns only have bird shot. Seriously?

_childDocuments_.review: At this time WotH has become my favorite hunting simulator. I enjoy the beautiful reserves and the new experiences they've added. The challenge of the hunt can be frustrating, but they do require skill which is difficult to find in game these days. The story is less desirable to me, but you're not technically forced to follow it.They are starting to apply the practice of DLC for the sake of income. This is something the typically deters me from supporting a game. DLC abuse is rampant across the gaming industry. If the developers can make certain the DLC always provide significant additional value for the price, then I can support them on it.As it stands, purchasing the base game will provide tons of challenging hunting. I don't know if the maps are worth $9,99USD a piece. I have a difficult time putting that price on something that doesn't really add much to the game itself except the same loop in a different scenery.The gun pack, for me, should have been free. There is absolutely no value in adding them to your options other than being a fan of the manufacturer. They add nothing to the game and are not worth $4,99USD by any means.The Season Pass does include the 1st two maps and the hunters pack. So... you save $2,98USD if you purchase the season pass. The gun pack should have been a part of the Season Pass. The developers need to PICK a monetization. Are we going to do DLC abuse or Season Pass paywalling? I hope it doesn't go the route of MTX predatory tactics.TLDR; The game is worth the base price. Save $3 and get the season pass to get a "full game" for ~$60. You can easily find 60 hours of enjoyable hunting simulation in this game. The gun pack is a bit of a cash grab and feels a bit dirty considering it should be part of the season pass system if they are going to continue that monetization system.Pay close attention to the monetization plans of this game. It could quickly spiral into repeated cash grabs via DLC abuse.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I strongly advise buying the game yet if you have an ultra widescreen or if you play with a left handed layout, it's already clear that that a patch will be rolling out for these issues, but please do not play if the lack of accessibility is going to be an issue.And even though I have rated this as positive for the review because I feel there's enough good here not to warrant a negative one, take it with a grain of salt that it's also wishful thinking for this being a better game. But at the time of writing I will say that my verdict is mixed bag for this one.Now with that out of the way, I will give first tell you what I find to be the good/eh/bad in the game so far.First of all, the game's visuals overall looks really good, in some areas the detail is mind blowing. however I strongly recommend you set foliage to low and TAA if possible with your specs. This is because with how the game draws loads of foliage, you get this really grainy look that can be very hard to look at, especially when on a vehicle. As a matter of fact try playing with everything else on medium settings first since I've found my game having stutter problems on a GTX 1650Second is the gameplay, even though it's not the most engaging video game you'll find (It's a hunting game after all), you have a very decent set of mechanics that can be turned on or off depending on difficulty, which can be a plus for appealing to everyone's type of play. The progression is pretty standard in terms of how it works, but that's fine for a game like this. The controls however need to be addressed as without any keybindings to change, there really isn't a solid way to know about going prone or how pacing works. Another issue arose when hunting pheasants, the only way to really hit them is on the ground, I've tried flushing them numerous times and lined the bead up, but it always misses, same with trying to adjust it to where it might land (Which isn't that relevant as I was aiming from 30 meters away, not a long distance) so that I think should be fixed if it can.Third would be the immersion, it's top notch in some cases with how serene it can all be, except for the part where you look to your right and the river suddenly just disappears. And even though it's not exactly an immersion issue, I would like to see some more out of animal populations, not the genetics and such, I just mean having lone deer or other game out in the forest foraging rather than everything being in a herd, plenty of game in real life wander alone away from other herds, something minor like this would help make the forests feel more like an ecosystem this way.I give this game a solid 6/10 when it comes to everything about it, it's a good 8.5/10 as a game when it works, but with the lack of basic features at launch and with several performance issues along with bugs, it's gonna stay at an "ok" for now.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is exactly what it looks like, a Hunter: Call of the Wild clone. Where Way of the Hunter doesn't do anything awful, it also doesn't do anything well. The game is the definition of a "meh" title. Overall, Way of the Hunter feels like a bland hunting game that did its best to imitate a more well rounded title.The gun play feels off and I don't know how the developer managed that. My rounds always land low, no matter how much time I spend ranging the target, adjusting zero, and steadying my shot. The firearm selection is very limited as well, and I'm guessing its so developers can flush it out later through DLC. The hunter sense needs some work as well. I feel like it could benefit from giving players the option to assign colors to different markers, i.e. droppings, blood, prints, sound cues, and deceased animals. The hunter sense gets confusing while tracking a blood trail and the exact same flashing effect is displayed for everything on screen. Not to mention the default color for the hunter sense is yellow, and blends in with the light greens and tans of the grass.The amount of money you need to purchase hunting certificates for different zones feels odd too. Not in the sense that they added something you need to work for, but because of the conservation aspect. If you kill too many animals, then the population on the map lowers. This feels counter productive for game play, since you need to kill animals to make money, but then that lowers the number of animals within certain zones on map. The last thing about the game that strikes me as odd is how few fast travel points are on the map. I don't want to skip all over the map, but I also don't want to spend 30 minutes walking to a feeding zone. All in all, I feel like the game has potential, but it lacks polish. If the developers continue to build upon what they currently have, I think it will end up being a great title.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the review bombing fool you, this game is easily better than CoW in every way. The issues people are griping about relate mostly to the FOV, which is annoying, but top priority in the next hotfix, ya'll are a bunch of babies.Having played The Hunter Classic and CoW, this game does just about everything better:PROS:-No microtransactions(!)-Free ammo-More realistic animal behavior-Herd health system is really cool-Animals age and grow-Ballistics are *chef's kiss*-Proper weapon zeroing-Tracking is far more intuitive and realistic-Damage model is closer to Sniper Elite series-Better graphics, environment, and sound design-Actually takes time to locate, stalk, and track animals (Some may consider this a con)CONS:-Limited weapons and equipment compared to CoW. (Still has everything you need, 30-30, .243, .223, .338, .22, etc. but no handguns or bows yet.)-Less maps than CoW-Audio bugs are annoying, sound is poorly mixed within 100m of water, and occasionally it  sounds like an aircraft is doing patterns over your head etc. Not huge issues for me personally.-Perk and character system needs work.-Story is a little cringe.-Blood trails sometimes disappear, seems to happen more frequently with .308 on elk imo-Foliage and fallen logs have no collision or sound yet.-Stealth system seems to be WIP, sneaking up on animals in wooded ar.eas is very difficult, as they sense you very far awayI didn't put the FOV or Keybind issues as those are on the short list to be fixed. If you like hunting, and play CoW because there's no good competitor, but find it a little too arcadey, give WotH a try. I was hesitant, but the game won me over within 15 minutes. Personally, the lack of microtransactions alone makes this game better than CoW, but it goes even further and improves the digital hunting experience in just about every way. If you're a sucker for realism like me, try it out, I think you will like it.
