name: Sheltered 2
detailed_description: It's been twenty years since the world as we knew it ended. The last of humanity splintered into opposing factions. Will you unite or conquer? Building upon the original 2015 fan-favourite, Sheltered 2 brings new challenges and deeper strategic gameplay. You are tasked with creating a leader and building up your faction whilst managing resources and tackling threats both natural and human. Everything from starvation and dehydration to radiation poisoning and enemy raids can prove fatal. Sheltered 2’s new Factions system is pivotal to a base’s success. Send out expeditions to explore the vast wasteland and forge relationships, or bitter rivalries with other camps. Trade resources to grow and thrive together; or go head-to-head with rivals in an expanded combat system and grow your foothold in the wasteland. Will you ally with or dominate the other factions? Features: Factions: New to Sheltered 2, the Factions system allows you to create relationships with other groups that will provide your base with resources and support. Or grab your weapons and take things the old-fashioned way. Resource Management: Balance the needs and wants of your survivors, manage scarce resources, craft what you need and maintain the shelter’s equipment to keep the group alive. Faction Leaders: New in Sheltered 2, the faction leader is the most important member of a shelter, boasting their own unique and powerful traits, the faction leader will be pivotal to success, with their death meaning game over. An Unforgiving Wasteland: Starvation, asphyxiation, extreme temperatures and combat are just some of the challenges you’ll face in the harsh wasteland of Sheltered 2, and without the ability to respawn, every decision could be fatal. Combat & Weapons: When negotiations fail, wield a huge variety of makeshift weaponry against hostile outsiders. Fight to the death in turn-based combat to win the critical resources you need to survive. Characters: Your survivors have their own personalities, traits, desires and a huge list of skills to acquire. Customise them to your liking and make your faction members unique and individual. Vehicles: Find and fix more vehicles to explore the wasteland with, from Bicycles to Pick-up trucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 1 was great, didn't have many games out there that had this type of base build and exploration. So picked up Sheltered 2. Unfortunately, only after a year of release the dev team stopped all updated. Msg from the Dev's on Oct 2022 below;---------We can only apologise for the lack of communications from us recently. It wasn't our intention to keep everyone in the dark, but it has been a turbulent time for us. The launch of Sheltered 2 was very negatively received, and for good reason - the game should have been early access, as it needed a lot of balancing and bugfixing, but unfortunately this option wasn't available to us.We had a lot of plans for the game, not just including the roadmap. Unfortunately, sales were not good enough to sustain development, and finding other means of funding wasn't possible. We tried to keep it going for as long as we could, but eventually we had to let our entire development team go. Myself and Dean also had to find work elsewhere, as we could no longer rely on revenues to sustain us. We're still supporting the game with bug fixes whenever we're able, but continued development on new features and content is unlikely for the foreseeable future. We appreciate those of you that have contributed so much to our community, you were paramount to us during the initial launch and beyond, and we hope you've at least enjoyed what the game currently has to offer. It's really a deep wound for us, as we know there's a very good game here, it just needed some coaxing to come to the surface. Again, we apologise that it came to this, and thank you for your understanding. - Unicube

_childDocuments_.review: Living in an apocalyptic world might be much harder than you think - at least if Sheltered 2 rules apply. I guess my bed was build by someone with a far higher intelligence than the maximum value in Shelterd 2. It did not break down on me nor did I ever have to repair it - a job that you have to do every single day in this game. I do get that you have to refill generators from time to time, however you would not expect having to repair them every few hours, as all the other equipment here in this game. Hey my guys probably looked twice through the binoculars during their trip, and yes maybe they did not handle the backpack with much care. I still find a bit exaggerated that these things break down beyond repair on a single trip.Instead of any interesting or challanging encounters, my fully trained and armed party gets frequently stopped by single unarmed level 1 characters, with only options to either fight or flee. Well, since fleeing depends on luck, I am very sorry to have them single hit killed. I really wonder how I managed to survive that long, but until now I have perfectly managed to eat something without getting food poisoning, although I did not take a shower or wash my hands (I usually use knife and fork). This does not work for my ingame fellas - maybe they are adding some bad spices I am not aware of. All items have now a 3 level quality range. I have got 300 2-star metal sheets but for the receipe I need a 3-star one. Yeah very interesting feature...adds a lot to the gameplay. Temperature is now an issue. Everything not close to an unknown and very narrow comfort temperature causes either heat strokes or freezing damage. Killing themselves by using freezers as break room should have been fixed by now, but still getting a meal from the fridge seems to be a hazardous activity. Oh yeah, I almost forgot: They call it "bugs". I call it "pre-alpha release". Now we are at "patch 9" - how many days has this game been out now? Apparently they do unit-testing only, meaning nobody seem to ever have test played a complete game. This would be nearly impossible. Look at the list of fixes - and I still cannot play because half of the stuff is still not working correctly.  Sheltered 1 was kind of fun. I wonder what the point of this sequel is? Nothing really new - better(?) graphics but the gameplay just became worse, not mentioning all the bugs. This feels like a rip-off.  Making some quick money with a badly designed an unfinished sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I have now played Sheltered 2 version 1.0.10 for 40 hours and I cannot honestly recommend the purchase.Sheltered 1 was a fun little game that I sunk a lot of time into. There are a lot of elements of this sequel that I really thought were good improvements over its predecessor. - The switch to 3D is nice.- The Faction system is an interesting idea.- Rations instead of water and being able to bottle water is great.-'Workable' locations for quality resources makes sense.-Expanded vehicle options is superb.-Combat is much more in-depth over the original.However, a lot of the new systems offer disappointingly little depth and the balancing for many mechanics is pretty bad. FACTIONS: You barely interact with the Factions outside of a very basic job system with repeating quests (acquire X materials for us, rescue a prisoner for us, etc.) which offers very few unique quests per faction. The weekly faction report is largely meaningless as which Faction controls what barely matters. Either you control a location or your don't. There aren't enough benefits for being a Faction's ally or risks for being a Faction's rival. With your Faction it would be nice if there was a general Wasteland popularity rating for your faction. Depending on your actions maybe you are seen as soft, aggressive, charitable, creepy, etc. You Faction is largely defined by how other Factions regard you, but the everyday folk never really have an opinion of you one way or the other. NPC ENCOUNTERS:The people that come to your shelter are traders, recruits, Faction goons to collect resources for quests and invaders. That's it. Would love to see more quest givers/ random people/ general variety arrive. Or specific survivors or traders you can build a relationship with either for good or bad. The people you come across the wastes are either Faction patrols, outpost guards, violence-prone survivors and neutral survivors. Each type has about two or three lines of dialogue that endlessly repeat making the encounters stale within the first hour.As I touched on in the Faction section, it would be nice if random encounters would be slightly different depending on what kind of Faction you have. If you're overly murderous maybe people are less willing to trade, or you get more psychotic types who want to join, but people won't want to mess with you as much? Perhaps if you're overly passive the opposite could be true, etc.Overworld Survivor interactions boil down to 'Trade, Fight, Flee' and Faction interactions are just 'Fight, Flee'. Even the first game had four options including Bully and Recruit. Again, there should be a lot more interaction options based off of your characters skills/ stats and possibly even your Faction's reputation.There are a few forms of hostile wildlife you can come across, but it's rare. Could do with a lot more variety here as well. CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION:This time around you can make your own Faction banner and bio which is nice. The options for character customization though are woefully underwhelming. You get about four kinds of tops, two kinds of pants, four to five hair styles and two kinds of shoes, each with very limited color options. Considering they have at least two items where you can change your characters appearance, you think the game would have offered a lot more on this front. The character creation screen has this intense (orange?) filter on it which makes every color choice look like washed out grey, and you won't be able to tell what your character truly looks like until you start the game proper.No pets or children like in the original, which is a big letdown.OVERALL BALANCE:It's all over the place. Your survivors are either super weak or overpowered. In combat if you kill someone with a punch you get a ton of XP, but if you merely subdue them with a punch you get almost none.Many of the skills are useless, especially the "gain XP faster" ones. They should be "increase level cap" or something actually useful instead. Would like more utility skills in general like one that has equipment degrade much slower, find better quality loot, or gain many more resources from working locations, etc. There are so many garbage skills that offer such trivial bonuses (10% chance to not use a First Aid Kit? really?) that every character build ends up being pretty much the same.It's a little silly that equipment like binoculars disintegrate after a day trip and items in general require way too many resources to repair things (almost as many as it takes to craft a new one in some cases.) Various weights of items are way too heavy as well. Bottled Water especially. This game introduces the idea of metal scraps to craft your own basic metal items as you need them. This is a great addition and they need more things like this. Maybe have a "textile scraps" too? Then said scraps could be used to repair items and not whole resources. The cooking is way too good at Tier 1 and subsequent tiers offer little more considering how much you must invest to get them. Higher tier food and medicines don't heal more, they are just worth more in a trade.As far as I can tell, it's the same with weapons, equipment and ammo. Higher tiers don't equate to more damage or durability. Again, just higher trade value.Tier 4 Equipment is locked behind befriending one specific faction. That is awful as it means you must always befriend them if you want access. Would be way better if all Tier 4 equipment were blueprints you could find.The temperatures are crazy. For being an underground shelter it provides little to no protection from the surface temps. Higher tier walls and lower levels should provide better thermal insulation, but they don't which is bonkers.BUGS:As you may have read from other reviews, yes, there are a lot of bugs. As of 1.0.10 many have been fixed but many still remain. To Team 17's credit they are knocking them out very quickly, but if you end up getting the game HAVE MULTIPLE SAVES AND SAVE OFTEN. I have had game breaking bugs occur twice which made me lose a ton of progress.UI:For the most part it's pretty solid fare, but there a a few things that hold it back. I cannot believe there is no option for Celsius to Farhenheit in the UI. From what I understand, this game does not support ultrawide monitors at this time either. The game's tutorial does not do a good job of explaining things like power generation and temperature management. (I was many hours in before I learned fans and heaters have adjustable thermostats thanks to a let's play, and even now am trying to understand how they actually affect different rooms temps.) The game's help menu is also lacking in many specifics, especially in said areas.Conclusion:Overall there is a fun game here, but it comes off as extremely unpolished and fairly shallow in the mid to late game. It feels like an Early Access game. If you liked the original or like survival sims, I'd keep your eye on this game for when it receives a lot more fixes and content, but as of 1.0.10, I can't recommend putting down any amount of money for it unless you have a high tolerance for jank (this game is right on the border for me personally). Team17 is updating it rapidly, and they are receptive to the community which is great. So maybe add it to your wishlist and check back in a month or so. I hope that one day soon this game becomes as enjoyable and engaging as what it really could be.

_childDocuments_.review: One year, 8 month Update (As of June 6th 2023The dev team announced in October of 2022 (Via private channels, not via steam or other sales platforms) that the game failed sufficiently that the game studio is shuttered. The staff have been laid off and the founders have been forced to find new work.Games dead, and that's that.Current state is still fairly buggy, and pretty incomplete. None of the issues below have been materially addressed.Fourteen Month Update (As of Nov 27th, 2022):DO NOT BUYThe development team has deleted the roadmap from the news and steam forums from the game. No futher community updates have been provided. Game has been abandoned. Do Not Buy. Six Month Update (As of April 9th, 2022):Well, its been a while. A hair over six months since release. Unfortunately for the game, all I can do is say everything I've said below is still true, with the following additional details:- The game has seen a fair amount of bugfixes and stability patches; but it also still regularly softlocks the game with freezing and broken characters and interactions for a lot of players.-  THE ROADMAP HAS BEEN DELETED, DISREGARD.- Thats it, really; everything else is promises and wishes and real far off stuff. The game is far from abandoned, but its barely treading water, much less becoming something real special.At this point, all I can say is Do Not under Any circumstances buy this game - Wait until the end of the year 1 Roadmap, so January 2023 - If the contents of the roadmap are delivered as advertised then there is a chance the game is worthwhile then. Otherwise, you're gambling money at a table where the dealer seems to have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off and you don't know when they're coming back, much less whether you're gonna actually win the bet.=================================Cannot recommend to avoid highly enough at this point - TL;DR game is pretty broken, obviously should have been early access, and the developer response to the community has been extremely distant and dismissive. Come back in a year and see what the reviews say then.Alright, now that the TL;DR is out of the way, lets dig into this.Sheltered 2 is an ambitious expansion to the original sheltered formula, but built on a very shaky technical foundation with large design gaps that are very confusing. At its most basic level, you send people out to scavenge the wasteland, which will let you bring back materials to build better things to expand your shelter and its capabilities. Like a lot of games in this style, it suffers strongly from a "Rich get Richer" gameplay loop, where the difficulty in shelter management rapidly evaporates as you get established. Resources are scarce and rare right until you get into the second tier, at which point you effectively triple your yields from scavenging, and the resource game becomes fighting RNG for enough rare high end parts instead of just quantity. Food and water also become relatively trivial problems as food is easily turned into an exponential grown situation, and water is easy to conserve with better equipment. Not a unique problem to Sheltered 2, but one that it none the less has failed to readily address.The shelter itself is a notoriously buggy place, with characters getting stuck in limbo, temperature management being an inconsistent, illogical nightmare, and stupid AI automated behaviors leading to annoying things like "I want all my people near the door because a raider is about to break in, but they insist on engaging in an idle wander to go three floors down because its 2c cooler there", and having to micro people and fight against their AI as a result. Temperature in particular is a nightmare as food now needs to be refridgerated, and the entire temperature system appears to be built on flawed mathematical assumptions leading to bizzare situations such as "A larger room is easier to refrigerate than a smaller room". Overall, the whole shelter side really feels half assed and rushed, with little consideration put into the design implications.Instead, a lot of Sheltered 2's design is focused heavily on the world outside the shelter, with middling results. The sections of the world are controlled by a series of factions, predefined groups with their own particular quirks and behaviors in the world. You can fight with them, or join them, but the only reason any of this matters is certain production buildings locked behind having to wipe out or ally a particular faction. We'll disregard the fact that allying is completely broken right now with buggy quest lines that often just don't work, and focus on wiping out instead. The tiles of the world map are grouped up into regions, and each region has a headquarters, controlled by a faction. You can attack this, capture it, and the territory becomes yours. This does absolutely nothing, other than occassionally spawn buggy missions where you have to try and defend it from counter attacks. You gain no resources beyond the immediate loot, no real advantages, nothing. Not even removing the faction from the area encounters is worthwhile, as wandering unaffiliated people are regularly more dangerous than faction members.None the less, this is an apocalypse, and people will fight a lot. Combat is at least better than the original sheltered, but its still really bad in its current balance. Firearms are either completely useless or ridiculously overpowered, depending on whether you are measuring by individual encounters, or accounting for the cost/value of all the ammunition that just got spent. I honestly don't have too much bad to say about this at the end of the day, it just needed a few more months in the oven to balance it out. I can say its easily the most improved part over the sequel.I'll summarize a few other issues here, in passing:- Skill system is really unsatisfying, with broken perks and an unclear stat upgrade path, with arbitrary caps on stats below max for different characters. Sounds good in theory, but in practice it just makes some characters permanently 'never good enough' for certain activities or combat.- Vehicles are a weird mix where they never seem worth the investment by the time they're available. A pedal bike sounds great until you realize it caps your party to 1 guy, so you'll save fuel and time when you go out to get shanked by bandits.- Androids: I won't spoil much but tl;dr there's an effort made to create an endgame and it really doesn't work.- Communication from the developers suck, and they seem to be determined to actively fragment their community. They don't want to talk much about current issues and concerns, are trying to fragment out the patch community in some bizzare belief that less people testing experimental fixes will mean they'll have less bugs to fix.- The first public large improvement mention is a complete replacement of character models - While this is nice, it also reeks of "We just rushed out some placeholders" and isn't acceptable in a full game release. If you want to treat a game like an early access product, release an early access product.I feel like I could go on, but if I keep going, the things I say will degrade into a disjointed, incoherent mess. Much like the design philosophy behind the game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Updating my review based on some recent updates to the game5th and Final update----In true Team 17 fashion, the game has been canned. And rather than post it on the steam page for everyone to see, they quietly announce it via discord. I mean they refused to let the devs put the game in early access because it would "look bad and affect sales," so I'm sure a "We forced a game out early then pulled the plug after getting the cash" would look even worse. Just quit supporting this publisher in general. They hide behind the "Indy" label while being a massive publicly traded company that resorts to buying up small games and squeezing them dry.4th update-----Nearly 9 months later, and the game is still a buggy mess. Rather than fix what's already messed up, they decided to double down on messing things up by adding new features that manage to be less polished than the ones already present. Nearly useless animals, rat hordes that can't be controlled, deer that will not shut the hell up. Updates are coming in slower than before, assuming they are horrified of the idea of a hotfixJust avoid it. Maybe one day it'll be balanced and well thought out. Or it will be dropped like anything Team 17 forces out the door before it's time to make a quick buck3rd update------Now we get a development road map. The game will be past placeholder assets in a year. Updates are flowing in at the speed of trickle down economics. All discussion for the most part retreated to the safe space of their discord, where any and all complaints are ignored unless you include complete worship of the team. They still haven't even completely implemented a functional Fahrenheit / Celsius option despite saying it was being worked on for some time now. The incinerator bug has been "fixed" in nearly every single update yet still exists. This game is still a disappointing mess months after release. Just don't.2nd update-------They announced a graphical overhaul is in development. They have also stopped posting change logs on steam since updates have grinded to a halt. You're now directed to their discord for all experimental updates as well as re-enabling the beta access code system so that not anyone can just get into it. Their reasoning is to "limit the pool of testers"So you would assume this is a big experimental. Serious crap going on, major things to test. Nope. You can finally paint walls and a few quality of life fixesDon't buy this game. It isn't done. And who knows when it will be----------------1st updateSome of the major bugs have been fixed so far, along with the developers increasing communication with the community. They've started an experimental branch to help with the bugs and issues. I've been using thatSo far, loot is respawning again which makes a huge difference. Some of the bugs involving combat and skills have been fixed smoothing the experience a bit. All base items that I've built so far have actually functioned as intended. Negative moods and injuries are actually disappearing when treated, or with time. There are still UI issues, sluggish animations, and a lackluster faction interaction system. However, it is on the road to being a game I would gladly recommend. At the moment, it represents a rough release rather than a trainwreck. If you're fine with that, you should buy. If not, you should hold off until some more polishing has been done. At the rate they're publishing fixes, I expect to switch my review to recommended in a week or two!-- Original Review --It's essentially the first Sheltered in 3D with a clunky interface, worse balance, less options, and non-functioning or buggy mechanics.Despite the major billing of being a faction, you're not. There isn't a diplomacy system. There isn't expansion. It's exactly like the first game, only now you're a group of random people rather than a family. You can occupy territory which just means you don't run into other faction patrols. This would give you access to the resource generating map tiles, but they aren't really worth it even with loot respawn not functioningThey added a temperature mechanic that is completely out of wack. AI that hangs out in freezers causing them to take damage with no way to keep them from going in there other than assigning a new job or issuing an often buggy move command that needs to be placed on a precise part of the floor or it doesn't work. Temperature outside also fluctuates at a way that in the middle of summer you have 28c days with 2c nights. So your "forecast" will say 28c, but it is only 28c for a small fraction of the day. There is also major issues with temperature control just not working, or the heat or cold in one room just dominating another rooms temperature in nonsensical waysThe UI is missing important hotkeys, while also having hotkeys that aren't listed in the controls menu for UI elements that you don't really need to look at. You don't need to see what's affecting your survivors mood because whatever is there will potentially end up stuck there due to bugs. And the tutorial never even shows you there is a perk menu. Unfortunately the vast majority of the perks are combat related or make little difference so whether you find it on your own is irrelevant. And rather than design an actual UI, they went with just making black transparent frames for everythingPerception either doesn't level up from exploring like the tooltip says or it levels up at a rate that is vastly lower than all the other stats. But it doesn't seem to matter, because the loot respawns are either bugged out or horribly unbalanced. I've yet to see loot respawn like the first game. So unless you manage to max perception on your character creation or hold off on searching map tiles, it won't matterUpgrading your facilities won't make much difference. At the 2nd durability upgrade I'm still repairing objects at nearly the same rate. My 3rd level water collector is still not providing more than the first level efficiency upgrade. You can't upgrade generators anymore, but you can build more as well as wind turbines. Sometimes they work, sometimes they don'tCombat has decent animations that are plagued with extremely long pauses. Combat itself is just full of constant pauses. And rather than building a large combat UI to house skills and items, they've opted for a "everything is in a right click menu" approach. And I'm not sure why they opted for that approach seeing as the combat screen has a massive amount of empty real estate. As far as I know, there are no combat hotkeysAll in all, the game has potential to be a great improvement on the first, but it isn't there as of now. I'm not even sure how it managed to pass a quality check, and the lack of communication with the devs makes me wonder if they even cared that they were releasing a buggy downgrade

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start off by saying that I have indeed played the first game beforehand. The first game to me was a massively entertaining game. Well I may be exaggerating that part a bit but I enjoyed it none the less. I especially liked the scenario modes that it gave you ontop of the classic survival mode.Anyways this review will be centered on the second game. Overall the game isn't necessarily bad per say. There are many improvements it made over the first that I quite enjoyed. Such as the 3d models, factions, jobs, trades, map layout, leveling up, etc. But there are countless issues that I have with the game in its current state. Some of the issues I encountered include: unable to craft crutch, leveling cap for all characters, traders not showing up at base, difficulty in recruiting pets, the heating/cooling mechanics, incredible difficulty with the collection of high quality items such as plastic, inability to access medical bed most of time, inability to call for traders/recruits, the poor variety of clothing options, auto clean and auto repair abilities locked behind skills, and a variety of unbalanced mechanics that need tweaking.This game isn't finished. Yet I have sunk 100 hours into it so trust me when I say I know what I'm talking about. In all honesty I would have defended this game and given it a positive review if it wasn't for the infamous traders and crutch glitches. Which essentially causes you to not be able to trade at your base and removes the ability to repair broken limbs. Which can also cause you to not be able to go out on missions if all your characters have broken limbs paired with no traders coming to visit will always result in a game over.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a good game waiting to happen here but right now it is still a product that should be in Early Access. There are TONS of bugs and features that simply don't function well and the game balance is pretty much non-existent as it stands.Bug example:Your Shelter (which you have painstakingly expanded and built onto) is breached or invaded. You use the very rudimentary control scheme to position your survivors right in front of the door as they are cutting through, ready for COMBAT!!!! Then, nothing as the collision detection fails utterly and every invader literally clips through your survivors to go on and loot whatever they want. Sinks either function to keep your folks washing their hands automatically or they don't. There will be no indication either way.Sometimes the build engine decides that you must have Masterwork level lumber to build something like stairs. No reason for this, no reason when it doesn't. Balance example:The RNG decides that it simply won't rain enough to get you through summer no matter how many water butts (containers) you build. You won't ever hit max levels and miss out mind you. It simply sometimes decides that it will rain 2 days in the summer for 2 hours each and that is it. "Working" a resource site like a water plant with a full 4 person party for 6 hours will result in something idiotic like 8 liters of potable water and 10 liters of unpotable water. Put together this simply removes the "feel" of satisfaction you would get from the game. You often feel like you simply wasted 15 hours only to find out that the RNG had pre-determined your shelter's fall from dehydration or unstoppable raids or sickness cascades from bugs etc.. Add in the extremely basic characters (good god the options are so limited it boggles the mind), the fact that every character uses the exact same skill trees (which are all wierdly combat focused), and the difficulty in keeping track of who has what trait etc and you get a game that feels both unfinished and unsatisfying to play. Come back in 12 months and see if they make progress.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I loved the first game and was desperate for this to be good. It wasn’t. The Sheltered series is a bit like the sims, if your sim was stuck in a post-apocalypse where they needed to fight racoons for scraps. (Sadly, there are no racoons, or scraps, in sheltered 2.) I was desperate to like this game. So much so I’ve put in double the hours than the original. “Just a bit longer, and it’ll get better.” I kept saying to myself. “It feels a bit like the original, I just need to push through and it’ll pan out.” Yeah. No. In this iteration there isn’t all that much at all, really. As per the first you need to expand a facility underground, build rooms, manage the characters welfare, and explore the wasteland looking for resources to do so. The core gameplay loop is actually really addictive, and feels extremely good. Very sadly, however, this game can be summed up as “While playing the first game did you, at any point, think to yourself ‘Wow! This game would be great if it were prettier at the expense of literally everything else!’? Because if you did, then this is for you!”  Coming to the recommendation portion of my review really breaks my heart. I wanted this to be good, I wanted it to be better than the first, I wanted to see where they had taken such an amazing concept and basis, and how they had grown it. But all I can say, when everything is said and done, is “Nope.” At this point in time I’ve hit the sunk cost fallacy. I want to finish it, but genuinely, this is a poor excuse for a cheap knockoff of the original sheltered. If you loved the gameplay loop of the first, you might still enjoy this, and if you enjoy this, then I recommend the first very strongly, I think you’ll be blown away by just how much better it is in almost every single way.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is the sequel to the 2015 original of the same name. A feature-packed strategy game of management and simulation set in a post-apocalyptic world, twenty years after the fall of mankind. Gameplay combines three strategic tracks that bring together a comprehensive survival-themed experience. At its core is the struggle for domination of the wasteland against rival factions that requires resolution by conflict or diplomacy. This plays out over the longer-term with an emphasis on task allocation and character fulfilment taking place while base-building, exploring the world and accumulating resources.The player takes ownership of a base that begins in the same shape at the start of every game. One that takes the form of a bunker that sits at the centre of a randomly generated game world, populated with locations and factions. Players create their own faction of three members; a leader and two subordinates, using a detailed customisation system to set the faction flag and name, but also set character appearance, traits, stats and skills to their preference.<Dig deeper below to read the full review>+ A randomly generated world map with a fog of war divided into territories and full of locations for the party to find and scavenge for resources. Encounters with other groups can lead to trade, combat or quests from factions or other sources.+ Comprehensive character creation using 8x categories: name, body, features, hair, accessories, clothing, stats and traits.+ Extensive shelter components for building facilities that deliver: accommodation, energy provisioning, resource generation, storage containers, character stat upgrading and crafting platforms.+ Intimate turn-based tactical combat fought on isometrically viewed, static locations. Menu-driven tactical options derived from character skills and carried equipment. Personal hit locations determine applied damage and statuses.+ A large inventory of useable items and resources to find and use. Split into numerous classes such as: food, crafting resources, weapons & ammo, medical supplies, armour, character equipment and junk to disassemble.+ Scores of simple animations portray shelter activity that are makes the bunker seem alive.+ Achievable faction goals open up advanced gameplay elements such as: crafting tiers.- No game continuation on leader death with the faction falls apart. Could have done with nominating a new leader.- Combat encounters require balancing. Some are terminal with the leader dying without the ability to flee or perform any actions against superior enemy parties.- Minor GUI issues. Unable to choose multiple options to eat from the same screen. Losing a character does not update a reduction in party carry weight. Cannot tailor actions on the action queue. Cannot select specific resources to use.- ‘Soft-lock are possible,’ by not having the resources to keep your survivors alive. Water conservation especially can overly punish progress, wasting many hours of play and requiring a reload at the very least.- There exist a number of bugs some of which can be game-breaking. Bug encountered: characters can get stuck upgrading shelter facilities and stops them from being reassigned tasks. No amount of restarting or loading previous saved helped.- Significant micromanagement occurs when fulfilment automation is set to off.- Other issues exist. GPU workload can fluctuate to extremely high. Some players have reported black screens and problems when changing resolutions and using windowed mode.* Automated fulfilment allows the AI to take control of mundane aspects of the game. Reduces micro-management but can use up resources to quickly.* Remains a work in progress with fans of the original reporting that some features missing from the original game. Such as no children or pets.* Some repetitive mechanics make base-building play out essentially the same in every game. There is some nuance to the experience. i.e. blueprints and floppy discs add to build options inside shelter. Fires can cause facilities to burn.* Characters can increase character stats by gaining experience points in disciplines through action. I.e. taking part in combat, reading books, using exercise equipment etc.* Finding the appropriate blueprints and components allows for the construction of vehicles.<Dig deeper below to read the full review>Sheltered 2 does not looks like it was ready for release even if it retains a good share of content. With so many issues to deal with, it is in no way complete. A feat that also afflicted the original game, released in a similar unfinished state, to be fixed and completed post release. In all fairness the game should be marked as an Early Access title, with the amount of work that remains.When it was possible to play Sheltered 2, it demonstrated some enjoyable elements. Only being affected periodically by unintentional pitfalls that stalled gameplay. The biggest being a real need to conserve every drop of water at the start of games. A handful of games of one to three game months were attempted. All but one of these concluded in unfinished restarts. Either due to early leader death or a crippling design aspect such as the need to conserve water or having my leader killed by an overly powerful enemy party. The last prematurely ended with a game-breaking bug, potentially one of several that were present at the time of playing. Potentially there are workarounds for some issues, but no way to tell if these work for everyone, every time. Developers are doing what they can to help bypass these problems.<Dig deeper below to read the full review>Sheltered 2 is not perfect. A game with the potential to be a very good survival management sim. Albeit not completely turn-based, it possesses the right blend of features and activities to make it a WORTHWHILE play, but needs more QoL and balancing. It remains playable but under-developed in certain areas, missing features that were present in the first game. There are game breaking bugs but not as many as when first released.<Dig deeper below to read the full review>Given Steam's restrictions on character limits, you can read the rest of this review by using the link below:

_childDocuments_.review: Played the first Sheltered to death, was so much fun and I was really looking forward to the second instalment of the series, now before I go any further I DO recommend the dev's are listening to the fans and tackling the issues at hand ,BUT I would wait 3-4 months before purchasing it and here's why:1. As has been said oh so many times before on this reviews thread the bugs are game breaking, such as being forced to flee from a friendly NPC because I don't want to fight them (I'll get on to this part of the mechanics in a sec) only to lose EVERYTHING i was carrying, or having floodlights continuously stop working even though there is fuel in the generator and they are at 100% durability.2. The saying goes something like "If it ain't broke don;t fix it" this comes to mind with the interaction system with NPC's you meet out and about, in sheltered 1 although a bit more basic was incredibly effective and user friendly with its four options: Bully, Flee, Trade and Recruit, instead in this game the interaction has been reduced to fight or flee unless you meet a trader which is really disappointing and restrictive as you are tied to either fighting a friendly NPC (which damages your rep with that faction or also injures your characters. Or you flee and risk losing all the stuff you have collected on an expedition and again damage your rep.Conclusion- The difficulty of the game as many others have said is subjective and not an issue although it was a step  up from the first game but I don't see that as a bad thing personally, when the game works it does work well and the new graphics and animations put into the game are a nice touch but various game restricting mechanics or breaking bugs soon stopped me playing it, that being said I am a very bug-tolerant player, but YOU the developers had the gall to release this game as a finished product instead of putting it as an early access game (which I think is still something you should consider) You've proven you make great games but you need to carry on fixing your game, if these problems continue to be addressed then I'll change this review.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re thinking the negative reviews out there are being overly critical like I was, think again. Things you build, like a basic treadmill, require constant maintenance (think daily), even when unused. Further, not only must you maintain things, but if you don’t – they will catch on fire. Yes, the unused treadmill will catch on fire filling your shelter with smoke and creating heat exhaustion(status ailment) for your characters. Despite your best prepping, you are limited by an upgrade mechanic that prevents you from being able to stock up on water despite an abundance of rain which you could have saved. You’re not able to build additional water collectors and are stuck with the one you’re given at start. It’s a lazy way to force other game content – namely going out and raiding other neutral settlements. You have no choice but to attack random NPCs you encounter in many cases. I don’t care for being forced to behave like a cannibalistic raider – that sort of thing should be an option. A great deal of time was spent on the crafting system, which is okay. But just okay. It’s a shame they only spent about 2 hours one Friday afternoon writing the game dialogue – this is going to sound harsh, but its about on the level of what an unmotivated 10 year old could come up with. I somewhat enjoyed the first few hours of play despite the poorly designed UI, as I was occupied with learning the games mechanics. After 15 hours of play I finally got sick of the lack of choice and exited. Game won’t be played again. I tried really hard to give this title a shot – it’s a good genre and there are so few games of this sort out there. $5 on sale, ~15 hours played. I can’t complain about the value for Dollars/hour spent. However, I would have spent 20x as much for a properly finished and balanced game I could have played longer.

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE IT!!!!! TLDR is at the bottomIf you are reading bad reviews and thinking do I want this game, just try it.  I doubt you will refund it in time. Super fun and a great sequel. Very much in the spirit of the first game but no families or pets :( Start this game on easy as it is brutally hard even at that level.Main tip to survive is to upgrade water intake efficiency first. That is by far your most important early survival issue. You don't even need more water storage because you can't even take in enough early game. Grow potatoes in a greenhouse as they don't use water to cook them and trap rabbits outside your base.Bathe your people outside in the rain and don't even build a shower early until you can get the second level shower. Deal with puking by letting them go outside to repair until they feel better. If they have to defecate or urinate; well that is why they invented the great outdoors. Don't go outside during a sandstorm or black rain or they get radiation poisoning. Don't take in too many people. Likely 5 people is plenty early game, until you are swimming (literally) in water. It's probably Autumn by the time that happens. Always be upgrading your peoples traits (get a bookshelf and read damn it) The character skill system is quite deep and very fun but needs more explanation. For example; is the autopsy table broken? No, your character just doesn't have the skill needed. Overall there is a lot of complexity here and the lack of explanation of these complex interrelated systems is the worst part. Devs should add tool tips so if you hover over things everything is explained. The most important data for these tool tips is WHERE you are likely to find the material at the quality needed to make high end items. Knowing where to get 2 and 3 star wood, metal, and plastic is super confusing. (Working at sites around the map, and trading with factions) is the answer, but who knew that? I thought you could make them. WRONG!Other annoying bugs are guys stuck in place. Makes you have to reload a save. So save frequently! It autosaves, so it's not too bad. The main issues with guys getting stuck are, 1. picking two people to clean at the same time2. putting too many bodies (items?) in the incinerator at onceTLDR::;If you loved the first game like I did, this is even better in every way. Graphics, gameplay, tons of items and stuff to build. It is a new release game and has tons of bugs, but a great game is hiding under them.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most of us I loved the first game! And like the most of us I'd like to love this one too but there are too many game breaking systems in here. Just to mention a few things I stumbled upon:- There are not enough spots on your map to gather resources! Gathering resources is a real pain in the a$$ in Sheltered 2. At least in your own territory and as soon as you want to gather resources in another factions territory you get constantly attacked - Durability is ridiculously annoying in Sheltered 2! First of all the durability of your items and devices depend on the "Intelligence" stat of its builder. Which means everything you build in early game must be replaced later anyway (which costs again ridiculous amounts of resources!). And what comes on top of that is the rate with which durability declines in in this game. It's just insane! I mean, how often does an oxygen filter need to be maintained in real life?! Or a water filtering system?! Once or maybe twice a year?! In Sheltered 2 every 2 days as you can watch the numbers decline within seconds!- have you ever suffered from food poisoning just because you haven't taken a shower for 2 days? No? In Sheltered 2 you do get food poisoning INSTANTLY!- or have you ever had a heatstroke when you were outdoors at 27 degrees celcuis (80 degrees F)? Here you get a heatstroke within SECONDS, not hours exposed to the sun, I'm literally talking about SECONDS!- My crew can't take medicine, it just won't work (at least the antidote for poisoning)- in a post apocalyptic world the one thing you should be able to trade with is in my oppinion WATER! but here you just can't do that (in Sheltered 1 you could do that)- you can automate some of your crews needs like hunger or thirst and so on, but sometimes if you manualy order them to eat or drink in a queue of different other tasks, they get to do it twice and waste valuable resourcess because the automated needs get to interrupt that queue- diplomacy is horrible in this game! Even though you have a "neutral" relationship with another faction they'll still attack you on sight or raid your bunker! You have a bare minimum of interaction options and those are really not satisfying- you can make rations for your outdoor expedition by preparing food. But let's say you have no other food left in your bunker except those rations, eating those doesn't lower your hunger bar! It makes literally no sense at all having your crew eat those rations!- and now my biggest issue with this game: RAIN! When your weather bar tells you it's going to rain on a certain day, it just doesn't! And from day 30 or so, it stops raining at all! All my crew members are dying from dehydration from that moment on and that's pretty frustrating because reaching day 30 is really really hard in Sheltered 2!- and last but not least: a bear, a giant grown a$$ bear gives you less flesh and leather than a RABBIT! xDLike I said, I'd really like to love this game and give it a postitive review but I just can't do that at its current state. All I mentioned makes the game unplayable for me and I hope these issues get fixed soon, because the potential to be a great game is definitely there.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I reccomend this game? Not YET. Here is the short of it: Sheltered 2 is an unbalanced, overly complicated, and difficult game to play – even on the easiest settings. I have clocked in my fair share of hours in the original Sheltered and in my 10 hours of playthrough since release I have to say this game has a MASSIVE balancing issue. Yes, it’s a good take on the classic resource management / underground colony game - but unlike the original game finding resources is way too hard. The original game had multiple places that you could go to to gather the materials you need. I cannot stress this enough - there are not enough places to travel to outside of the forest. This game essentially forces you to trade with other factions and the trade value on each item is RIDICULOUSLY high. Unless you’re planning on giving up some of your medical supplies (which are an absolute pain to craft at a low level) or a heap of food … you’re stuffed! The Dev’s really need to step up the balancing issues, and I would really encourage them to take what their community is saying into careful consideration to make this game the best version of itself.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was a little hesistant because so many people gave bad reviews, especially about the "new rat problem" but that changed pretty quickly.So first of all: This game is by no means perfect but after 33hours I have not encountered anything thats gamebreaking or making the game less fun. Yes, sometimes you have to save and reload your file, because you get a sound bug or a character is stuck after rearranging the shelter. But that can be fixed in like 10 seconds by just reloading! It happened about 4 times now? Which is absolutely okay with over 30 hours! There are better or more expensive games that give you these kinds of bugs more frequently hahaNext point on my list is: This game is sloooooow! Getting ressources takes time and I have yet to start real fights over territory with the 6 other factions! Maybe that is the reason it's so slow and I would get more if I had more territory for my own? I doubt it but I certainly don't know!The furniture tier one breaking nonstop: If you pay attention you know you have to change, not the game. Because citizens with higher intellect build furniture with more durability. Start with int 5 in your character creation. If one has 5 intellect let him/her build your shelter interior! As easy as that. You can always get a higher int stat and "rebuild" your stuff. Just build a new one and destroy the old.The rat problem: I can't see it. If you want to have it "easier" against the rats start with a cat when you create your first character. You can add a pet from the beginning but cats are really powerful at the start. They not only kill rats if they encounter them but they also go "hunting" at night and bring home whatever they find outside your shelter. This may be meat, but this may also be ressources and gold/silver things.If you maintain a clean shelter (above 75%) there won't be a huge rat problem. There just won't be any rats. Maybe one but if you have a rat trap or a cat the rat gets beaten up really quick.I did have a pretty bad rat situation once where my citizens got really sick of it, were vomitting pretty much half the time and set half of the shelter on fire.BUT! And here is the point where I absolutely DO NOT agree with other/bad reviews: You can get rid of it! Get all your citizens back to the shelter and have them cleaning nonstop, meanwhile you put rat traps down, in case you haven't before and a fireextinguisher is very helpful aswell against all the mad lads breaking stuff and the rats nibbling on all your furniture. My cat was my hero in that situation though! It killed like 4 rats a day before he went out hunting for prey and bringing me more stuff to build more rat traps. My hero I tell you. I think the cat was smarter than me at that point.It took me about 3 ingame days with nonstop cleaning and emptying rat traps to get rid of them completely. Of course my citizens had to take turns to take care of their needs but with 5 or 6 people this was absolutely doable. My shelter had 3 layers at this point with 6 sections (or whatever is the maximum per layer) and one and a half layer was just dirt at this point. I honestly don't know if it makes a difference, but if so it was probably not very beneficial for me, having 50% of the worst tier rooms. I don't know how it would be with more or maximum shelter size or citizen count! After 33 hours I am still far away from that.All in all I can say: The only downside of this game is beeing slow, but you can also say it is very relaxing and you can spend a lot of time with it! This game has more aspects than the introduction shows you! Pay attention! Read the provided ingame information. Sometimes you do lose a citizen or two in battle but I personally didn't reload at that point because it was nobody, that was super needed. I just got two new ones :xA tip for everyone: When you rearrange your shelter, zoom in as close as you can. You do get more "room" when you squish everything together and zooming in has helped me A LOT! Sometimes it's just a pixel or two needed to place some new furniture, so zoom all in!I would absolutely recommend this game ♥

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. It's got everything I want from a resource managing survival sim (well, maybe it's missing a few automation options that would be nice but it's pretty solid overall). The problem is the game has significant bugs that have ruined my several attempts at a play-through. The problems are generally one of two categories - people or built items. For people, 3 times in 3 different games I've had a player freeze and refuse to follow commands. Once was after a prisoner was recruited and twice it happened while somebody was sitting down to eat. They are clickable, I can assign them a task, but they don't move, they just slowly die of thirst or dehydration. I was able to work around this by going back to a previous save point because it's noticeable pretty quickly.With the other bug, it's usually too late by the time I notice it. What happens is something becomes inaccessible, with the reason being that another person is using the device, even when that can't possibly be true. It has happened to a planter and a lab bench, and I solved the issue by deconstructing and remaking them (a waste, but not game-ending). However, twice (on different playings), one of my 4 survival utilities fell victim, and there was nothing for me to do about it. When your water collector is no longer able to be upgraded because the game thinks it is in use, there is no way to reconstruct it and you're just stuck for the whole game with an inferior water collector. This also happened to my oxygen filter, which capped my shelter at 6 people for the whole game. I've put a lot of hours into this game, hoping that next time I won't run into one of these bugs, but at this point I need to stop and play something that works. Until these issues are resolved, I would stay away from this title.

_childDocuments_.review: My extremely honest opinion of this game:I feel like people rated it so badly because they expected it to be like the first game, which in some ways it is but mostly its not. This game is interesting and fun and has a lot of neat aspects, such as the moods and ailments, Sheltered is a great game and I think a lot of the charm is from the pixel-y game look which this one doesn't have. I still think this game is worth the money(I got it on sale for $4.99) I have enjoyed playing thus far and will continue playing because in its own way this game is fun.Similarities to Sheltered-The idea of living after nuclear falloutThe idea of building and preparing your vaultMaking your vault peopleDifferences-You can customize your character's clothes and accessories differently than the first gameYou can train your pets to have skillsthe graphicsbeing able to switch from side view to top down above groundbeing able to use the land above your shelter for growing crops or having animalsbeing able to complete jobs for other factions and gaining trust with them or losing trustItems, tools, food, and pieces for building all have ratings of how good they are (1 star to 3 star)All in all I think this game got more hate than it deserves. I hope my comment will help someone try it out and see its a decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Word at the beginning:-------------------------I dont understand why people write a review for a game they played less then 5 hrs. Its impossible to fair judge a game and saying that the content is less then in Part 1 just proves they didnt really play the game. That beeing said, i played this game over 70 hrs (i Played about 72 hrs nonstop and then fell asleep at the computer) you can be sure that i do a fair review.Sheltered 2 Review:------------------------Graphics: Compared to Sheltered 1, the graphics are alot better (even though its not the best graphics ive seen in other games) still it is nice looking at The Yard which u can build stuff on. The Objects you can place look nice, all in one i like the changes.Gameplay:Gameplay is straight forward, you build your Shelter go out and scavange the area. But in addition they added a Faction system, and this is where it gets interesting, u can either be allied with em or go full crazy and try to kill em all. Everything u do has consequences towards the faction you are dealing with.Another really great addition is that you can take Prisoners, If u threat them good you can maybe convince them to join your Faction, or you can decide to execute him and just use him as Food or Fuel for your incinerator. By building a Garage you can build up to 3 Vehicles (Bicycle, Motorcycle or the PickupTruck) The Parts you can find by scavanging Carparks, Parkinglots or Scrapyards to name a few. In Fights you have several new abilities you can choose if u want, and you can choose to attack certain bodyparts which gives you extra things to do. Overall i think the Gameplay is ALOT better than Part 1 and i really like the changes they made. The Devs allready stated that they will add Pets in a later Content Update.Bugs:As for nearly every game this game has Bugs too, i agree with alot people that it would have been better to do a early access or atleast do some more beta testing. Unfortunatly its too late for that. The Devs are working alot to fix the Bugs which are present. I know it can be frustrating but its not a reason to write a negative review after playing for less then 5 hrs)Difficulty:this game (at least i feel like it) is harder then the first part. If you dont Plan ahead of the Seasons you will end up losing your people. Water is just one of the problems u will have in Summer ;) Summary:-----------Pros:- Better Graphics- Faction system- Nice new Buildings/Objects- Surface Buildable- 3 VehiclesCons:- BugsSo you see the only negative i can say are some Bugs you will come across. The devs are working on fixing them pretty fast (4 Updates in the first 3 days) I hope you wont read all these negative reviews, because most of them didnt play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first off, I played the first game and looked forward to this game, the many concerns of other players are usually about rats and bugs, i also agree with the bugs, but for rats you really only need a cat and to keep the shelter clean with a mop to avoid the infestation also rat traps help when they spawn at night when the cat isn't there.Disclaimer:I've played about 20 hours on record and basically figured out what to do for the scenarios some people have problems with, minus the bugs so i'm not some "ALL KNOWING BUDDHA" at the game, no i just basically tinkered around my first play through and am now on my second which is doing CONSIDERABLY well compared to the dehydrated idiots on my first run, so here are my thoughts, but firstSolutions i found for anyone looking for it:-If the place is dirty use the mop every day or so, just basically assign someone to clean before the end of the in game day if you want to keep efficiency up, i've only had a cat as a pet so far so a litterbox will help and cleaning it when its up to 70% should help out a ton since the pets usually poop in the shelter thus leading to more hours cleaning.-mood going down fast? try not to kill anyone you see, essentially just knock them out, you still get their crap that way.-the "In the dark" negative mood? no idea why it does that even though you have lights, but just basically have electric tier 2 lights on the floor the settlers all hang out in, more or less make sure the lights cover the whole floor. Note: the survivors hang out in rooms/levels that have temps between 12C-18C temperature, so should be easy to figure out where.-food going bad? use the partitioner to section off the pantry, have a fan in there if you want and set the temp to the lowest, food will stay fine for a LONG while.-durability so crap? Use only one settler for construction and crafting, preferably one with high int stat.-slow game? speed it up, find the keybind, or if thats not what you mean, speed it up yourself. You can start a fight with any faction out there, just make sure to leave some people at your base OR, put the storage and pantry next to the door, and just give them what they want, they will leave without a fuss, its what i did at first and it was effective.-Most common problem i found scrolling is rats, the damn rats? Clean the shelter using a mop, have a cat as a starter pet, i dont care if you're a "dog" person, you can find a dog later, to survive even a little bit longer with the attention span of a goldfish (like me) you need a cat, they will murder any rats that wander in, bring you food if you level "prey drive" enough and also boost survivor mood in the shelter, a dog can be found in the wooded areas of the map, right click on the tile and bam options should show up. thus giving you dog, just basically let your explorers run around an entire set of wooded tiles on the map and should give you an encounter with a dog at least once (Also have a dog whistle equipped to one of your settlers).Main problems i found: -how slow the game feels, the base is comparatively bigger than the last game, so why not allow running? Maybe at the cost of getting tired quicker? Because fires happen suddenly and how leisurely they go extinguish the fire, and by then the fire has spread to multiple furniture thus being barely controllable. -upgrades, i hate this new upgrade system, you basically have to gamble with resources you find and hope you get a tier 2+ crafting material-Absolutely crap percentages. A 70% chance to flee from 1 person is impossible you say? 2 times in a row? yeah hard to believe.-Stats, they only level up fast if you keep fighting, which is dumb since you really should avoid fighting ANYONE you wouldn't want to piss off (just yet) since if you get enough encounters they will turn into enemies and be hostile. if you make enemies of 2+ factions they will attack your base and they will attack your base at the SAME time, no breaks, which is HORSE CRAP.-THAT!, they attack you in tandem if you piss them off enough, it was pretty punishing, i almost lost 2 survivors to this lunacy, they also didnt like each other as well, so there was also that.-RnJesus either loves you or hates you, item spawn is essentially a gamble, since the map is generated, there is no way you could spawn next to a farm, a scrapyard,  etc. i once spawned next to basically nothing, just a caravan and the next lootable place was in unfriendly territory. so had to restart.-Hit chance is somewhat dumb, i have a high dex survivor in my current playthough miss a body shot, the one without a % chance to miss, make hit chance obvious please.-Game is super punishing very early on since you spawn in only DESERTS, what with the droughts and such, hopefully the devs will add in some different spawn locations even if they are random so you could at least stand a chance early on.-automation of bodily needs needs to have a tweak, if there are free beds and your settler is too far, sure why not just collapse on the floor, but there is an open bed RIGHT THERE on the same floor as them, they somehow still choose to sleep on the floor. The bugs i've encountered:-A sound bug occurs when you've played the game for too long, if you speed it up the sound starts breaking, then eventually it starts breaking even if you dont speed it up-Fixing things sometimes doesn't fix things, a reload fixes that issue but reloading is too tedious for that one specific thing that needs repair.- Also the game starts losing frames the longer you play.try the solutions i've found in your next playthrough, maybe you'll stand a chance, because i HAVEN'T encountered a single infestation yet. and fires dont start randomly, remove the pyromaniac from your base, easy as that.

_childDocuments_.review: We can all agree on that the initial release of Sheltered 2 was a major let down coming from the original Sheltered, however, albeit the slow progress of which the devs are updating and bug fixing, it is slowly coming together, and start to reach some of the potential that this game has. _childDocuments_.review: This is not a finished game. It's tremendously buggy. Certain functionalities are non-functional and the balance is awful. I'm at the point where no matter what I do, I cannot fail. The original game had that issue as well, but I feel to a lesser extent. I have a lot of complaints about the functionality and the basic behaviors of the survivors in your shelter. For example, running three floors down to get water for a fire that is on the same floor as them, with a free water source just a few feet away. Standing in the freezer long after their health starts ticking down. Had a guy go to sleep in a bed right next to a fire, unperturbed. You have to micro-manage or they will get themselves deleted. There are too many things like this to list here, and more bugs than I can count.People throw a lot of accusations of dead games around, this one is legit dead. They have a roadmap completely left untouched for a long time. There are broken achievements that you need to download a third-party fix to trigger if you want to complete the game. They fully released an unfinished game and then bailed on it. That all being said, I bought it for like 2$ and I have enjoyed it immensely. It's not a good game, but it's an enjoyable game. If the grinding in the first Sheltered scratched an itch in your brain nicely, this will probably scratch it similarly. Perhaps not as much, but it's a difficult itch to scratch sometimes. I don't regret my purchase and I do find it entertaining. I wish steam had a middle hand-wiggle with an 'eeeeeeh' instead of just a thumbs up and a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I have played only about 18+hrs, and already noticed quite a lot of bugs. However, this is not a review to bash the game.I have about 280hrs on Sheltered 1, so you can imagine I am definitely going to compare the two. It's inevitable. If you don't want it to be compared, don't release it with the same name and a number at the back.The Good Stuff:"Improved" graphics (Some people loved the pixel art)FactionsCooking(!!)Traits and skillsNew Temperature / Weather systemStuff that used to exist:PetsI absolutely adored Pets in 1. Nobody ever said it was a terrible feature, so why was it not implemented?KidsIs this some kind of PC censoring? Isn't making a family part of the Sheltered identity?OthersOn that note, I have not played far enough to know if the "Psycho" feature is removed as well. I sincerely hope not. I'm just waiting for some fool to snap and try it in my shelter.Not-so-good Stuff:BUGSUn-upgradable doors/generators.Game breaking BUGSResource / Loot balancingItem tiers (Why? For what purpose? A false sense of challenge? When the loot respawn feature is broken?)Soul-crushing BUGSOverall, it's clear this game was rushed to release. It definitely is getting some things right, as I'm able to play past the "never-touch-it-again" 12hr mark. But for Team 17 to "get some things right" is setting the bar pretty low. They do, however, seem to be making some effort to fix it, and generally responsive. Even came up with an experimental branch recently to, maybe, hopefully, get the game on it's way to full potential. As far as completion is concerned, this game is certainly not ready.I will recommend it, for now, since it'd be unfair otherwise. But's it's only because I don't want people to give up on this, just yet.Only heed this: Prepare to be frustrated by glitches and bugs.90 hours gametime edit: Sheltered 2 truly is a gift that keeps on giving (unwantedly). It's actually impressive how the game finds creative ways to introduce new bugs. This game isn't just buggy, it's bloody infested. I'd still recommend it, purely for the hilarity of still finding new head-scratching bugs 90hrs later. If you wanted to pay to beta test a game, now's your chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a survival management simulator. Build, defend, survive, make friends or foes, kill or get killed. 20 years after the end of the world, six fractions dominate the wasteland. Your fraction is the seventh and pretty new. Your goal is to bring peace into the lands. How you do that, depends on your decisions. You can make runs easier or harder, depending on the options you choose (how often people gonna break into your home, how many resources spawn, etc.). Either way, you start with a leader and two side characters in your faction.The faction creation is as simple as choosing a name and a crest. Creating the leader goes way more into detail. Aside from changing his looks, you can change his attributes and give him character traits. You start with 5 points, "good" traits will lower your points but you can add a bad trait to get more points. This allows you to add more good traits in return. In total, this allows for a unique character overall because there are over 50 traits! The tutorial will explain the basics very well. It will guide you through your first expedition, building a new room, and shows you how to satisfy a few basic needs. After that, you're on your own. You already know the goal but how you will achieve that, or even if you will, depends on you. My run started with one bus on the map. I got a few resources there but not nearly enough to build enough, so I needed to go into the territory of other fractions. They will immediately notice and ask what you want. There is no chance to steal from that in the very beginning. Make friends first. You can build chairs, beds, toilets, new rooms, and much more. I don't want to say there are no limits but it's enough for an in-depth experience. For everything you build, you will need resources like wood. You can get these things on expeditions, by recycling trash or even other things you don't personally need (right now). A good way to survive would be to build everything helping you in satisfying basic needs (A way to get food (vegetables), a bed, toilet, shower, etc.). After that, you can see what else. Technically, this is still the beginning but let's call it the middle. The tutorial is over and you're on your own. You now can do whatever some people will feel lost now. If you don't know what to do, look for your fraction's goals. They can guide you a bit and you will have something to look forward to. This helped me a lot. Meeting other factions and people can be dangerous. This can result in fights (especially if you are friends with a faction and meet their foes or have foes yourself). Another reason to send your people prepared. Give them weapons. Fights aren't tactical deep when you compare it to turn-based strategy games but Sheltered 2 isn't mainly one so it would be an unfair comparison.Battles aren't the only way to die through. Hunger, cold, and infections can result in death too.   Sheltered 2 is a fun survival and management game. It's deep enough to be tactical demanding while still not being overly complicated. Most of the time, you will have an idea of what to do and keep an overview of everything. You can decide how you want the events to play out. This doesn't mean it's easy nor that you can as you like. It could be a bit more beginner-friendly and have more QoL features but aside from that, it's a good simulation. You should definitely check it out on sale if you want a survival management simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the first one so I bought this one immediately on release. Then, I saw the torrent of negative reviews. So I left it untouched for two years. It's clearly been abandoned since, but I was looking for a new game to play so I dusted this one off and gave it a shot. The 80 or so hours I played have been in one big stretch. The core game play loop - build things, upgrade things, go out and scavenge for things to build and upgrade more things, with some combat here and there - is very satisfying. The stuff you need the most - metal - is annoyingly hard to come by in large quantities which stretches out gameplay. Lots of stuff is locked behind RNG. All that said you can feel its been abandoned, and its rough around the edges, but ive not encountered anything game breaking. Im also not sure if everything thats seemingly in it is functioning. For instance, ive had zero problems with bad moods, breakdowns and whatnot, even though there are a ton of skills and drugs to mitigate these things. You can just not invest in them and things seem to turn out fine. Anyway get it on sale if you like the first one, or games like it like Mr Prepper.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loved the first Sheltered, the sequel has definitively lost the charm of the original.  I loved the pixel style of the original and the new 3D style (while showing a lot more) feels quite bland and needlessly complicated, which more or less surmises how I feel about Sheltered 2. ---But I digress. I will still go into detail as to why I can't recommend this.  Firstly, the whole premise really annoys me.  I don't particularly care for the dev's reasoning why there wouldn't be children or pets 20 years later in a post-apocalyptic nuclear wasteland, but the whole draw for me with the original game was that you started off as a family in a bunker.  Now that they've gone the whole "build your squad/faction" route rather than build on the original's premise, the game feels fundamentally generic and doesn't really bring anything new to the table. Even the music sounds pretty dull.I don't demand a sequel (or a new game) has to reinvent the wheel every single time. But a game should at the very least execute its mechanics well, especially when measured against similar types of games.  To me at least, Sheltered 2, at its gameplay core is eerily similar to The Last Stand: Dead Zone (a free-to-play multiplayer game on  that's probably dead now because of the end of Flash). I feel Dead Zone (from memory) still fundamentally has stronger core gameplay than Sheltered 2.  If I have to elaborate through another example, Dust to the End (while a more merchant oriented game) is another post-apocalyptic base-building squad builder with an over-world map, turn-based combat encounters and a social interactions system.  In comparison to Sheltered 2, Dust to the End has a far more enjoyable experience to offer than this game.  Furthermore, Sheltered 1 may have lacked detailed social and faction interactions, but what it did offer felt satisfying to play through and compelled me to revisit the game every now and then.This is not to say that I haven't noticed the more positive aspects of the sequel. I can still attest to having some interest in the new game mechanics (expanded faction and social interactions, prisoner/hostage system, more building options, temperature system, body-targeting turn based combat etc).  Unfortunately, I don't think these mechanics are an enhancement of gameplay but rather an over-complication of gameplay.  The gameplay issues I have are more or less surmised by the whole interface.  It doesn't feel particularly intuitive; you are immediately overwhelmed with information and systems that feel like chores, rather than things which compel me to be comfortably immersed in.  I understand it's a fine line between deep, meaningful complex mechanics and overly-complex confusing mechanics but with Sheltered 2 its sadly a case of the latter rather than former.While contemplating writing this review, I saw some discourse complaining about some reviews being released only after an hour of gameplay and people should play more before they give their opinion.  I was initially going to play more before writing this review just to be above question.  But I fundamentally disagree with the whole "it gets better after 100 hours" mentality.  First impressions are everything, especially with games. What you do at the start should set up your audience to want to continue playing the game.  Unfortunately, all that Sheltered 2 does is just set up a lot of busy work that doesn't fundamentally feel enjoyable to slog through, at least for me.  And the biggest detractor of the enjoyment and immersion is (as I've said previously) the interface design.---Though I have thought about refunding it, I think I will still keep the game and play things through until I feel I've seen everything that the mechanics have to offer.  But just know that its curiosity more than enjoyment that is keeping me sticking with Sheltered 2.---Edit 1 (23/09/2021): ---Edit 2 (26/09/2021): ---Edit 3 (4/12/2023): I don't know if any of the bugs I've listed above have been solved but I do know this game has more or less been abandoned by the looks of it.  So I've struck all my edits because honestly, it doesn't matter anymore and I'm never going to touch this game again.  Stay away.
