_childDocuments_.review: The release of this game was VERY disappointing BUT the latest version of the game is very playable.Sheltered 2 is just as good as the original Sheltered but it's a different game. It doesn't have simple pixel graphics, simple game mechanics and it doesn't have personality/humour. So kind of forget Sheltered (1).You still live in a bunker, you still send people out to discover/loot/kill/gather and you still get to upgrade your gear and some structures and that's good fun.Instead of bringing water with you on expeditions you bring food rations.The random meetings on expeditions are either with civilians who either wants to kill your team or trade with them OR with faction members and then your options are fight or flee. None of the options have any meaningful (or fun) dialogue.If you chose to fight factions they will storm your bunker eventually, sometimes two factions at once if you've been very naughty.With the right charisma skill the factions can be totally avoided. Build a bookcase and let the expedition team read to level 6 charisma and choose "Mission of Mercy". Bingo.The skills are mostly a load of BS so you pick the ones that help in a fight. The developers seems to have been really bad at coming up with useful skills and/or how to implement them in gameplay.Making food stuffs is a bit more nuanced and you can actually make different dishes with the food you grow. The temperature restrictions on what you can grow is overly constricting. It IS very possible to grow what you need but and it takes planning and a lot of shelves to get the later game dishes on the menue.The shelter environment consists of heat, water, air and goop (and sometimes fire). The heat managing  seems to be hard for some players to get a grip on. If you put a radiator and a cooling fan, both set on the same temperature, in the same area they keep the temperature at a comfortable level for the inhabitants all year round. They only use energy if they are working against temperature differences, so you will not use up more energy using them at the same time.The incinerator is very useful for conserving energy. If there's a breach you can burn the intruders' bodies for many hours and save fuel.The pets (only cats and dogs, I miss my trusty horse) are a bit more of a nuisance but they are helpful. Don't forget to clean the litter box. You can have chickens.The easiest way to get through the game is to kill off all the faction leaders but you miss out on the little bit of narrative there is in the game if you do.For some reason the game puts my graphics card (Gtx 1660 super duper ding dong) at 100% even at the lowest settings, and it really shouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 has a lot in common with the original Sheltered, but with some fresh twists. I've started a handful of games, my current, longest, game is on day 21. Pros: - the crafting system is great, and allows for creative recycling - bugs I saw on launch day were fixed and released 24-48 hours later (nice.) - I'm really enjoying the factions now that I've looted a few of their POIs and done some jobs. - I don't miss the pets or kids from Sheltered 1, which I could never keep alive. Sheltered 2 is dark, but not Sheltered 1 dark. - the character point mechanics are very nicely balanced, and added a lot of excitement to leveling up- it's a challenge to keep my small (5 people) faction alive and with moderately full needs bars while trying to move my whole faction and my base forward. I think that's also nicely balanced, I have to plan ahead and think carefully to succeed. - I like that there's a lot to figure out on my own. The tutorial is a great introduction, but it doesn't hold your hand to cover all the game play. I had several "ooooh" moments when I figured out what I was supposed to do. Cons: - the early grind is a lot of grind, I've started updating all my equipment and it helps, but poor Anna is out there fixing the water collector every day, lol. - I've started seeing some performance lag in the past few (18-21ish) game days, and one of my characters appears to levitate where ever he goes. Which is a pretty fun bug, if I'm honest. Fly, Ronald, fly. - the faces are a bit mush, but you only see a close up of your characters in the start up screen, they look fine at game distance. And who has time to worry about how pretty their character is when the water collector is down to 48% again. - there's a lot to like about the factions, but I think they're fairly generic. The descriptions for each faction imply an interesting backstory, but there's not a lot of distinction I've seen so far in how the faction AIs behave. - I'm one aloe vera plant short of being able to make a base defense against raids and I can't find it anywhere. All in all, I'm having fun and I'm excited to start the game again.

_childDocuments_.review: is a survival colony simulation with a focus on management and offers 4 difficulty settings. I never played the first game so I am unable to compare the two.You will start out with 3 people in your colony and get more inhabitants later on. You have a 2D view in your colony where you can scroll up and down, and this goes really smoothly.Outside you will have a water collector, an oxygen filter, and a patch where you can plant seeds. Whereas inside you can recycle items or junk that you won't need in order to craft new items.In addition to building, your colonists will also need a bed to sleep in, a place to shower and keep clean, etc. You can also build other things to help them improve, such as a bookcase so they can study and improve their intelligence, a treadmill so they can exercise and improve dexterity. There are 4 tiers of unlocks so you will be going through quite a lot of iterations.As expected, things will also break down over time, and you will need to also take care of the repairs as things wear down, in addition to making sure that your folks are also kept clean as to not get ill.You can go on expeditions in order to get new items or to meet other groups. After getting new items you can bring them back to base. When you meet other people you can trade with them, take on some jobs for them, or fight them.Likewise you will also face raids to your own base. There are 4 different difficulty settings so this determines how often this happens.Some of the in-base tasks can be automated such as eating and sleeping, so you don't have to worry about feeding them on time or making sure that they get to bed.The game offers a nice in-game tutorial to get you started, so even though it might take a little bit of time to get used to what you need to do, you still have a good starting point here.The graphics are okay, there isn't much variety in the appearances, but that is okay.The music is a bit sad and gloomy, as it should be in these kind of games.The game can be fully played with a mouse.I think the price of €19.99 is a fair price. You will get plenty of playtime for this price.It took me quite a while to get used to what I needed to do. For example, it was not clear that I should be scavenging enemy locations for new items, so it was a  bit slow going at first. After finding out, things became a lot smoother. The colonists do not always do the most logical thing, so the AI actions could be improved.I like the game because it's fun and doesn't have a lot of action--which is good for me. Mostly I am just finding items and creating new things, repairing items as they wear down, and building. The game has a management focus and is suitable for me.Verdict: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE/UPDATE: Changed my review to thumbs down.  All the cons are still the same.  There hasn't been an update or any word of an update in months and it looks like game has been abandoned by the developers.  It's a shame, the first game was amazing.  This as is isn't worth any amount of money.  I loved the first sheltered.  As some of the other reviews mentioned, this is similar, but is a bit more frustrating.  I have put this back on the shelf until they fix the issues with balancing positive and negative modifiers and fixing the rat issues.  Starting out with a cat and even with a cat, this feels like a hunting rats simulator instead of a survive the apocalypse simulator.  I recommend the game for 10$, it has potential, but as is, it's not worth full price.  Go play the first one instead and pick it up on sale until they fix it.Pros: - It's hard and gives you a good feel for apocalyptic living.- I do like the new factions system.  - The various ways to get food keeps things interesting.  It's fun, at least at the start.- My favorite part of the game is the new locations and how you can work them, however, because of the cons listed below, I never enjoyed or could play the game long enough to make use of the factions and the new location types.- Vehicles also sound cool, but again never really had the chance to test any of them out.Cons: - The killing rat simulator needs to be balanced.  Rats spawn way to fast and even with the antibiotics, there doesn't seem to be a way to cure the plague that comes with the rats, or at least be able to cure it faster that it kills you.  - The factions are a great idea, I am just not sure it works as is - there were bugs when I tried to trade and get jobs.- While the pyromaniac affliction was funny at first, it's really got to go.  Two games ruined because of rats and 2 games ruined because of the Pyro.  If you 1 dude back at the ranch becomes a Pyro, your done.   - Now, if there was enough positive modifiers to counteract the bad ones, Pro could be dealt with, but there just aren't.  For example, my last playthrough, the main guy had -70 for rats, -20 for dark (even though all areas had lights on), -20 for an argument (even though my guy had 10 charisma with all the + charisma affects going), -80 for killing someone - 75% chance of running and failed 3 times on the same excursion, led to me killing all 3 times, you would think you would eventually get used to having to kill people.  There were at least 5 other negative modifiers totaling over 400 negative.    That was with a guy who was specced for all the positive mood stuff you could have.   Recommendations for the Devs: - Fix the rat spawn rate or include that in the difficulty settings.- add a way to pick what type of terrain you start in - desert, hills, arctic, etc.  I didn't see rain for the first 30 days, so I assume you always start in the desert.- Fix the mood modifier balance.  Add more positive, reduce some of the negative ones - for example, the more you have to kill people, reduce the amount of stress it causes and the longer you have rats, the more you get used to them.  - Allow more customization for difficulty levels.  This could be part of the terrain options.

_childDocuments_.review: The AI and quality of life aspects of the game needs to be majorly polished. You can set the inhabitants to fulfil their needs once it hits below 75% (default) or 50%. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't in good conscious recommend this game. I've spent a hefty amount of time to give it a reasonable review, having a love for the original. The Bad. This game is not beginner friendly, a few of your first playthroughs will just be understanding the mechanics, how to work with the absurdly bad UI and how to manage things that should be simple like taking prisoners, doing quests and otherwise. Unfortunately all of these things can unceremoniously break at any time. Eliminate 4 out of the 6 factions? Suddenly 2 of them revive, having no base and no way to actually destroy them a second time. They can, and will, continuously attack your outposts with nothing you can do about it. Horrible quests lines. If you manage to not break a quest, your reward is an abrupt end, no explanation on how to continue or just a fond "Thanks" without reward. Bad, horribly bad, faction reputation management. Killing a single member of another faction, if one gets away, nets you a 50-60 reputation loss. Doing a supply quest to -help- your reputation? 30 rep gained, and costs you 20-40 resources and you can only do this once in a blue moon while you can, and will, have 10-30 different faction encounters on each decently long looting trip. The only option you have when you encounter another faction is fight or flee, and flee is a percentage chance.Constant game breaking bugs. This one is a CONSTANT and I have encountered a game bug that has, in some form or another, entirely broken every single one of my 5 playthroughs. If you save a file right before your people return home, one of them will continuously stand by the door, not be interactable and have absolutely no way to do anything about it. Sometimes if you call a trader and it says one will arrive shortly, one never comes. This not only stops the traders from coming to your base on their own, but suddenly every aspect of someone visiting your bunker vanishes. No more attacks on you, no more factions coming to collect items for you to boost your rep, nothing. It's all gone. To the devs credit, they are smashing out these bugs, but it's one at a time... but this is a full -release-, not early access. To not being able to fix your generator(Devs fixed this one, but I'm still including it), to my leader dying from heat exhaustion despite being in a 0C freezer.The Good.If you like the first Sheltered, the mechanics are more or less the same with a few additional tweaks and new additions to keep your interest.Not only can you customize your three starting characters, your faction leader gets additional trait points for you to tinker about with, allowing you to customize each playthrough to your liking. Some of these perks, such as never having to sleep, are absolutely game changing. You also can find datadisks while looting in the world, allowing you to pick more of these traits, but not all, later in game. The updated in graphics is quite nice, and the base management is a lot more enjoyable. You're, to my knowledge, not limited by how far down you can dig and how expansive you can have your base. The surface of your base also serves as a garden, a place to build power generating buildings and otherwise. It adds a lot of fluff that was missing in the first game. The combat is a lot more RPG, with each attribute tree giving you abilities that will aid you and potentially your allies. There's a vast amount of combat items, from knives to sledgehammers, pistols to rifles. You can customize each of your characters loudout and there's numerous items to help further tailor your combat experience such as armor, grenades, etc. Looting feels nice and there's new ways to traverse, such as bikes, cars and motorcycles. These have to be repaired, but feel rewarding when you can finally kit your explorers out on looting runs. Conclusion.The frustration from this game stems from the fact that there is an absolutely wondrous game here, but someone made the choice to release it in a state that is obviously not completed. Each joyous occasion you'll have in this game will be met by an equally frustrating one that you have no choice on how to handle it due to bugs, broken mechanics or uncompleted quests.Once all the bugs are cleared out, I'd give this game a solid 8/10 and my recommendation. How this game currently stands 3/10, and my recommendation to avoid it until it's actually patched.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't honestly recommend the game, even though it does offer a fair amount of short term entertainment. Late game is pretty much just terrible micro management.Things that need to be fixed:- UI inconsistencies. Buttons vary from screen to screen, often causing you to click the wrong thing. Things like the recycler don't have the ability to sort by junk. Its just a mess.- Complex bases just light on fire all the time because you can't keep things in running order. Even if your survivors have the perk to automatically repair, they simply don't do the task. Either you have to spend all your time manually sending people around to repair stuff (super boring) or things break and light on fire.- Fires happen so quickly, that you often don't have time to even respond, or it takes to long to get there in large bases.- Crafting higher level materials is just a gamble. Even in late game, its nearly impossible to get the required materials to craft top tier things. After 40 hours I still hadn't been able to construct any T4 base stuff.- There are mechanics in the game that seem to be impossible to trigger. Such as the top int tree skill that supposedly gives the ability to raise another survivors max stat, I never found a way to actually access it.- Certain points in the game you can't get to the menu. For instance, if you start a combat that you know you're going to loose, you cant open the menu. I resorted to force quitting the game and reloading so I didn't waste my time in the slow combat.- Tons of arbitrary waits and button clicks in the UI. Takes way to many clicks to do basic things like having an exploration party try and flee combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only scratched the surface, but so far I have been really enjoying the game. I LOVE the first game, so I'm glad I wasn't [completely] disappointed with this. There are some pros and only a couple of cons that I have so far gathered in my short time with the game. I'll start with the cons.CONS: 1. Food: In my entire time playing, I have not encountered a single trader/location with any food. Not one morsel. I have tons of non-edible resources that I can just trade for non-edible resources. I found some seeds after desperately raiding a new order outpost, but that's about it. I'd get it if the devs were trying to be canon and made it seem as if all the food had been gathered, but there's no hint of this. I just... scouted until my food supplies were depleted. I know it's a survival game about the wasteland, but so was the first title and I had tons of food available then. At first I was like "cool, they made food more scarce, i like" but after four hours of not finding anything, it was more annoying than immersive.2. Customization: I don't want to be rude, but... well, here we go.It freakin' sucks. Worst part of my experience so far. Most of the faces look like versions of Sloth from the Goonies. The hair choices are boring, generic, and lifeless. There's like two shirts and three pants, each with maybe four colors (if that even). Years of development, and that's all that's been made? No shirts with logos? Tank tops? No shorts? Dresses? Only boots or converse shoes? For everybody? It's just so... bare. Huge turn off. Made my nipples soft. Not much negative I have to say. Like I said, I enjoy the game, but those two things really need to be addressed. Okay, now onto the things I like.PROS: 1. Visuals: Although I really dug the charm of the first game's pixelated style, I love the new 3D perspectives and I think its an improvement, at least atmospherically. The introduction of the z-axis is really cool, and I like the lighting/weather effects (ex lightning, sandstorms, rain, sunlight and fading shadows, floodlights during night cycles and how lurkers are only faintly visible in the dark). I give the new look a thumbs up. 2. Traversal: I like the new map. I love how you can take over regions, and I think the addition of factions created not only opportunities, but a sort of tension that wasn't as prevalent in Sheltered 1. 3. Combat: Combat is waaaay better than the first game. A lot more options available, both offensively and defensively. it actually feels like an old school turn-based rpg now instead of just feeling like a super simple fight-or-flight sort of deal. You can target specific limbs, steal mid-combat, daze, blind, cripple, analyze, IMPRISON (which is a cool new addition). It's much better.Overall, I can see how some people feel that the game isn't as fun as the first, but I really think that's only because they haven't given it a fair chance. The game really picks up once your base becomes somewhat stable. Once you have enough amenities, automating players removes that initial stress that feels like such a killjoy early on. Once you get going, I feel like the game is way more enticing than the first. All-in-all, I'm glad I tried it instead of listening to some uber-early reviews band-wagon-bashing the game. IT IS NOT the same game. Also, thank you for the loyalty discount. Paired with the launch sale, I got the game for only $15. I'm looking forward to all the improvements I know you will be addressing soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Man.... a hard game to review. I both recommend it but at the same time don't. It's...... fun? But full price fun..... perhaps now. The issue is the wee annoying issues. There's a number of wee bugs that will just ruin your day. Suddenly things you've built can't be used. Games will just freeze after fights. I can forgive some bugs but it starts to add up.It also suffers a bit from having a lack of end game content. Sure playing on normal isn't exactly a stretch but there will come a point where fights are just too easy. Once you've mastered Backstab which is OP as hell then fights become trivial and once that happens it's just a repetitive slog to clear territory but once you reach a point...... why bother? Sure you can build a more efficient shower but if you've already got 1000 units of water does anyone care?All in all it's probably a good steam sale game but the Devs need to put more thought into the end game and just general quality of life fixes

_childDocuments_.review: I still feel a bit hesitant about recommending the game, but I enjoyed it.  If you like base building, tech trees and scavenging materials, you'll have a blast.In my opinion, this game, while in a release state, due to bugs, balancing issues and placeholder text is still at the level of being an EARLY ACCESS game.  There are game breaking bugs and often I have had to edit the save file to solve massive rat infestations making the game unplayable and characters and pets stuck interacting with objects.  And there are certainly Quality of Life changes that would make some areas easier.  Anyone who has played a Bethesda game has probably encountered the same types of issues - great game, if it wasn't for the bugs.Base Building, scavenging, the simplicity of the fighting and interactions with factions are all fun.  The constant repairs to everything gets annoying after a while, and when you become more familiar with the game it becomes more and more fun.  Just remember that when you leave the shelter, its ok to secretly kill off other faction people and enter their land to scavenge locations.And now to start my 6th playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing for over 80+ hours now and enjoying so far. Played the 1st game and Sheltered 2 had some decent updates. All good stuff!!Not sure what happened to most folks after the rats update. I had one person solely tasked to cleaning up the shelter and though had a short challenge at first figuring and working things out, didn't have much of an issue. They keep bringing back lots of "desperate" meat which I end up feeding them anyway... lol hopefully they won't develop an "appetite" for it. Also got a lot of eggs now from the chickens, so cooking lots of breakfast meals... All and all it's a well developed game, considering there are only a few devs working on this game currently. _childDocuments_.review: This game is sequel of the 1st game that almost unrecognized from the prequel lol. The graphics now 3d, quality of nowadays game and finally we can distinguish our characters. Not only graphics, some new features also implemented into the game and make explorations and combat better. But there still some things that 1st game did better than this sequel.+ Ofc, the graphics enhanced 100%, fully 3d with lightning and shadow.+ The base buildings much more resembelance to Fallout Shelter than Sheltered 1 tbh,+ It fixes the problem choosing workbench/players/things if you get them stacked in one places.+ Now pacing of game is much slower than 1st game bcs its also much to do in shelter than 1st game.+ You can train peoples with many leveled training equipments including your pets.+ Explorations also enhanced, now it felt like myth & magic explorations.+ There is 6 factions that you can encounter in game, you can either side with everyone, side with few or one of them, or kill everyone. Affecting to your ending in this game.+ Crafting items a bit easier than 1st game, nothing too rare as long as you looting/killing and know what you recycle is+ There is a leveling in this game, either for combat, surviving, and mood. But mostly for combat.+ The number of survivors in this game is increased much more than 10 persons.+ The stacking and storages is much forgiving, you can level up to carry more and even wear 4 equipment for 1 person+ Rations for travelling also forgiving, you can create 2-10 rations depending of what food you based in, if you got meat from snare/cats in early game plus farming broccoli is good. You will never run out except if it get fire smh..- 1st game have this family format of 2 adults and 2 kids. While in this game your 1st start survivor is 3 of random strangers get together in one bunker- The relationship and talking in this game is questionable, I rarely see anyone praising or get to good talking. Mostly is insulting and idk why if you interrupt. It considered as rude an negative the relationship. It happen autonomously so idk how to raise relationship in this game.- There is no kids, they completely disappears. No more kids that can craft armors, guns and fixing things again. No more child labor lol- The gameplay felt slower inside the shelter. Even if you can fast forward there's nothing get faster. They can't run inside shelter- The 1st game have more surprise elemtn that if random survivor visiting you, you can either be murdered or when you reject them to join you they will tamper with oxygen or rain filter. This game only have random visit by survivor that need join or someone to pick up your side job missions items. Nothing else.- The extinguishing of flames is too long, they act so leisurely than panic. Resulting all of them goes to flame. This is why we should be able to run.- The hunting deer now need bullets, an expensive thing especially locked to tier 3. And so far no upgrade for weapon workbench to craft guns.- Finding good weapons also harder since you need requirement to used it and your stats is so much lower than many weapons you can find. Don't forget guns need bullets and if your char is low on Dex and never upgrade ranged skills, you basically wasting ammo.- Repairing equipped items need to use the equipment menu not automaticly registered by workbench. you need to unequip them but game never told you how until i start tinkering- After long play, I noticed audio started to laggy and downgraded in quality. Causing those 8 bit ear stabbing music.- The durability of items here is too weak. and crafting give chance of 3 tier of that items/weapons. But ofc you will mostly get it to 3 stars rarely.- The manual recycling vs recylcer is day and night in early game. Recycling in bench took much slower time even with fast forward it didnt help much. this is so punishing- The leveling system is too much favor in combat, while there's many things that can actually improve or diversify roles of each survivors. But if you upgrade it the same, they are identical.- The amount of clothing, hairs, hats, etc. of your customizing looks to your survivors is baffling me, even some of colors not shared somehow.- The base defense that actually work is landmines. While other's not so much. Buffing your survivor doing much better than using them.- Food now can be rot, but left no purpose at all than filling your pantry sadly.- No matter how you light the base, its still dark. And its hard to see if its dirty. Resulting you keep over and over cleaning the bunker.- the autonomy only cover sleep, water, eat, and bathroom things. No repairs, clean, harvest, watering plants, etc. If you manage 6+ survivors this will be becoming a chore.- I encounter one thing that infuriating. Some of the items in my base get burned bcs its durability destroyed. But I can never fix/repair them. They are wasting crafting spaces and there is no way how to get rid or repair them.- There is some crash in the game if you crafting items in workbench. dunno what cause it but its only happen when you crafting and in middle of crafting I chose other items to fill the empty queue task.If i can give mixed reaction, I will give it, but in the end its not a bad game. It could be more polished and have a bit better features such as running and more autonomy but the game seems to be getting better and better. So let's see it. So bcs I leaned to recommended, yeah why not.

_childDocuments_.review: Annoyance over difficulty.Nothing in this game posseses a challenge unless you want it to.Example: I met a military faction. I expected bulletproof vests and firearms, serious stuff.Except they are like anyone else. They have "zone difficulty" which means you control the difficulty of your encounters.I killed first two outposts of "military faction" with one knife.But this somewhat okay. I understand that faction system is super basic and just there to be.Example 2: You don't actually need materials to repair stuff. So no challenge in this. BUT this is where it becomes a mobile-click game. Cause every single thing except for toilet for some reason will be on the verge of a break once a day. ONCE A DAY, KARL! The amount of annoying senseless clicking you will need to make in this game is astonishing.I like difficult management in a survival game. But difficulty must come from planning and forced sacrifices. Here i just need to make another thousand clicks to fix things. _childDocuments_.review: Well, if you played the first Sheltered game you will be prepared for a majority of what this game offers. they introduced factions so instead of you and your family trying to survive (I personally really liked that aspect of the previous game) you are a faction trying to take over the area. You can have relationships with your faction members which is a welcome change of pace but its random. You cant engage with them. The pace of the game and all of the mechanics are the same. The game is now rendered in 3-D as apposed to pixels which actually made the previous game more charming. You would think this would add problems to the games operations but it actually runs 1:1 to the original as far as movement and how animations operate. It does look alright but I feel like if you going to go through the trouble of making everything more detailed at least make it look nicer. The art style (in my opinion) is gross. I simply dont like the way anyone looks. People are ugly. Combat is exactly the same as the previous game, just rendered in 3-D and at a top-down angle. The added skills and attacks add a bit of strategy to the game so you can overcome some pretty one-sided matches with status effects like blindness.Do I recommend? Yes. Its more Sheltered with more content. It enters the 3-D realm quite well and the price is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this is a game I would like, it has all the things I like. Base building, resource gathering, upgrading etc. But it is sooooooo tedious, starting a mission and not realising you forgot to bring bullets or take a vehicle. Constantly having to water things, repair things etc If this had a better layout for missions with your group and a standard fitout or change it as required and name the groups party 1, 2 etc that would have been nice. Also little things like letting you know the name of the character when you are upskilling them. Also the ability to change your base rooms around, moving garages etc. And allowing upgrades to be done direct to the item rather than 'deconstruct' and build new. I like the nitty gritty of placing stuff in my bunker and upgrading things. I even got used to which plants to grow in the various seasons. But I think stuff like that should come with info like onions in spring etc. I dont like having to fiddle about second guessing. The same with mixing drugs with 1-5 options. As the toons get smarter they should just invent stuff rather than me having to guess from 100's of combinations. The little toons should be able to be fully automated. One set on maintenance or cleaning etc. There is an option to assign a room but I dont know what it. The toons just wondered off to dark corners for some reason. Also the heating / cooling, I think having it more automated so you dont have to constantly adjust it for the rooms. The toons also never will go to the closest item be it a toilet, fire extinguisher etc. They go in a weird way to put a fire out with the extinguisher in the room (set up in case there is a fire) they instead go up to a different level to get one. Some aspect I liked but others were a real tedium. These games need double and triple bunks as well and the ability to add decorations like pictures to raise morale. The exploring is fun to find things and work certain workable tiles. It gets repetitive in the battles over an over and meeting traders or encounters all the time. My advice if you like this war of mine of fallout shelter avoid Sheltered 2. Perhaps if they made a Sheltered 3 give that a go. I never played the first Sheltered. The little toons all look the same and it is annoying 'trying' to find them. The skill tree's are good. Overall it is just too tedious to be lots of fun, I wont be replaying it.

_childDocuments_.review: NEGATIVE REVIEW WITH A CAVEAT: I enjoyed the game for the most part, but it's pretty buggy and you can run into game-breaking problems still. Fortunately the devs and other players on the official Discord are super helpful in getting stuff fixed. However, if you don't want to deal with that, don't buy this game. I will also say, after dealing with all of the six factions I got a message essentially saying: "WARNING: You are entering the endgame, which is designed to increase in difficulty until you are destroyed" and I gotta say - that was such a tonal shift that I never lost interest in a game that I had previously been enjoying so quickly in my entire life.PROSFun crafting system. Feels like a weird little post apocalyptic ant farm. Some great IDEAS for management even if the execution is not always there.CONSThe execution is not always there. Lots of talents, and items are poorly designed or don't seem to do anything at all. Music is repetitive and generic, when it's there at all. Combat - though challenging at first - is ridiculously easy once you learn what you're doing. Seriously once I got a few basic pointers on how to play the game I never once felt like I was ever in danger. The game is buggy, and often downright unstable. I've had it just flat out lock up on me a few times, ending my game. I enjoyed it until the stupid "You lose no matter what actually lol" endgame, but lots of people have run into serious bugs and problems, myself being one of them. I was fortunate that the most serious one was ironed out on the discord. That being said, It's only twenty bucks, though. Maybe pick it up on sale, like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, but terrible implementation. The outside world doesn't feel right and is clunky, the factions are just plain and insignificant, the trading system is useless in the late game and the resources needed for upgrades are way too much. The achievements are just designed to artificially extend the game time. The most annoying were the 50 bear kills.If the game mechanics and world gets some polish, this would be a relatively good game. Hopefully the developers will stick with the game and continue to improve it. The roadmap already lets some hope shine through.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is way too tough. When travelling around the map, interactions tend to have three options, Trade, Fight or Flee, and this can become a bit repetitive, and if you come across a rival faction, it is just fight or flee. A couple of lines of dialog and that's it.The whole crafting system is overly complicated, meaning a lot of back and forth, whether it is trying to see what ingredients you need to craft, then trying to figure out what you need to recycle, and so on, you will be left stuck pretty quick, forcing you to explore outside the shelter, which is fine, but this seems to happen way too quickly, not giving a new player chance to feel settled. There are way too many things to worry about in the Shelter, leaving a new player feeling overwhelmed.Bugs are being fixed pretty quick by Team 17, but this plays like an Alpha release and not the finished article.OverallThere is a good game in here, but it takes time to find it, and restarting once you figure certain things out will help you, but the game still struggles to really grab you. There needs to be a simplified mode, and a tutorial that really explains things.With all my complaints, I just feel that there is a great game here, but it is stuck in some kind of hole, that the developers don't have the time to get it out of.I will keep an eye out for updates, and maybe they can improve things moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: There were some bugs in the beginning but I feel like many have been ironed out.  A lot of things that I thought were bugs later I figured out.  I finished the first game on Normal by taking over all the factions - alliances don't seem to be worth the trouble. I'm now playing my next game on Difficult.  Things I've learned:1) conserve water early; put all auto-actions on red; build out water tanks; upgrade water filter efficiency; upgrade toilet and shower2) fight encounters - you get experience and loot; or trade so you at least get some charisma experience3) I don't bother with any alliance jobs anymore; I'm taking over outposts4) though it seems like you can put a pantry over the bed, I've stopped doing that since in my last game, characters wouldn't eat5) I'm not sure the sink actually works to stop food poisoning; characters are supposed to wash their hands before going to the food but they often don't so I have to order them to do it6) temperature management is still wonky; now a medium sized fan works pretty well even for a large room7) I didn't even figure out how to hunt/forage in the first game; I'm not sure it's worth making the lab to craft your own medicines8) blade proficiency seems pretty good so I max out on that and then build electric blades in the armory9) in the first game, I was late to build the exercise equipment so now I've built them pretty early on and have my characters who stay in the shelter rotate through them10) I now have 6 characters on D47, and I rotate 3 out at a time on trips; I had 8 in the first game but I don't think it's necessary to have the extra 2 characters; 4 per trip is great for fights but if so far, I seem to be able to manage fights, often just using melee instead of skills; another benefit of a blade is that it only uses 3 stamina so I can sometimes get 2 attacks per turn11) there's some skill - I think close combat proficiency - that allows double attacks - that's awesome12) I don't think the emergency tourniquet skill work - it seems to always fail13) I didn't check on Faction Goals a lot but I realized it's helpful to check to see if you're close; I think crafting items = tier 1; crafting objects = tier 214) In game 2, I'm not bothering calling traders or new recruits; I took in recruits slowly, waited til the fresh recruit got leveled up and loyal before taking the next one15) In game 1, I finally got the truck and all its parts.  that was great just to drive around but by then, my team was overpowering all enemies so it was just a matter of mopping up16) indoor planter seems to more trouble than its worth; I just have a small greenhouse outside and plant spinach, peas, and broccoli; everything else doesn't seem to be worth it17)  I now have 3 windmills but their power is unstable / uneven - I don't know how to get the battery power bank; I think I got the blueprint for it but not sure when I can build itAnyway, that was just a random brain dump.  Hope it helps.  I love the game - 117 hours so far.

_childDocuments_.review: My whole playthrough so far has been me shouting, 'please rain, please rain, please ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rain' at ever increasing volume.Unlike its predecessor, it's gone down this annoying route of making it challenging on a micro scale - for instance, my last playthrough, I had gathered 50+ food, dug out 4 floors, had 20+ fuel, all my survivors were lvl5+ for each skillset, but I lost because it hadn't rained for 10 days and the temperatures were now 30 degrees or higher over 4 days. No water means dehydration and then my survivors started to piss everywhere, because the bucket they call a toilet needs running water apparently, so whilst they're pissing all over the place and being dehydrated, they're also getting heat-stroke and "food poisoning" from all the piss fumes seemingly, which also made them vomit.And then they died."Easy mode" is there, but it only really sets how long it takes for your neighbors to come knocking on your front door with Kalashnikovs & Machetes, and how many tins of baked beans you own at the start.NB: I know you can transfer water bottles to water storage, but after 10hrs or so, I had a grand total of 3 bottles. Also water filtration filters one unit of dirty water a minute and stores something like 20ish units total - I lost patience with the game and couldn't be bothered to do anything with upgrades after that.Challenges are fun when they're a single instance that you come out victorious over and have the time to appreciate the victory before moving onto the next one - that's the thrill of a challenge; persistently being in the same collective one for hours, isn't fun whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is pretty addicting and has potential like the first installment. If you can avoid many of its game freezes and annoying bugs (which are slowly being patched) then it is enjoyable and fun although may not be too challenging depending on the type of gamer you are. - Music was meh. I thought the first game had better.- The map user interface is a bit clunky and tedious to move around in. Travel rations does not show up in inventory and sometimes just disappears leaving your party exhausted when in combat. Workable locations do not stand out and you have to remember where they were. If you leave items behind due to full inventory, you have no way to find out what you left behind in that location until you go there again.- Map is divided into regions controlled by a single outpost. Take over the outpost and take over the region. The only thing you get is traveling through the region you will not encounter faction members but only regular people, similar to the first game. - There are six factions and members usually use different gear from each other and are stronger than regular people. If you head straight to a faction HQ outpost and take it over, you get control of all that factions regions as well. Most leaders have a strong item they will drop after you beat them. After killing or allying with the factions, you will encounter androids which have more hit points but do very little damage. They take over your outposts/regions and then you take them back, over and over and over. - Some quests are useful, others just waste your time and give you no rewards for completing them. - The temperature system is new but is very inaccurate and frustrating keeping your shelter at a set temperature. It can be 16-20 degrees Celsius with your members are freezing or sweltering with heat exhaustion but your vegetables are growing perfectly fine. - Obtaining certain 3 star ingredients takes forever due to high item costs, randomness of loot drops/location searches, and no way to craft or recycle for them yourself.- Some skill abilities are useless and new members recruited get abilities assigned randomly based on their levels. Its best to recruit them early so you can level them up and pick your abilities you want. One of the best abilities is the auto repair one, huge quality of life ability. No more need to micromanage your shelter anymore. It runs by itself as long as you plant some seeds and traps. Just pray your members stat isn't capped too low it can't be unlocked. - Vehicles are hard to assemble due to parts required. I managed to put 2 bicycles and a motorcycle together. Only needed to farm for 1 more tire for the truck but decided to stop. Motorcycle takes 1 fuel can while truck takes 2 and I only had 10 fuel remaining and no way to get anymore without respawns. - Pretty much beat the game with 8 members but really it was 6 since last two had low stats and somehow leveled up stats so slow no matter how much they trained for that they were basically useless. These are some of the things I encountered and may be different for everyone. There were a lot more but I think those were already patched or fixed in the test version.Anyway if you liked the first game, you will like this one. Graphics are a huge improvement and a big selling point over the first for me. Gameplay is very similar so try the first one to see if you like it or not before deciding.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this game has two major flaws: 1. lack of immersion 2. steep learning curve (not to mention minor flaws like bad ui and etc)1. lack of immersion is more like a subjective thing I guess, because some games are very immersive and some are not. But since sheltered 1 was very immersive, I think it's reasonable for me to expect it from sheltered 2.You don't start with your family, you have to start with two strangers. You can't customize two strangers enough to meet your imagination. In sheltered 1 it was way easier to imagine and relate to characters since there were no face details. Please either let me customize as I want or just give charming preset characters. Currently they are neither customizable nor charming. (technically you can customize but they all look same)2. steep learning curveEven from the start you already have 20~30 kinds of junks and should know the recipe to combine and upgrade facilities and what they decompose into. In sheltered 1, recycling was locked in the beginning and in the early game you only have to focus on the water, and then food etc. So there were also lots of kinds of stuff but you should only know what is needed to build water tank or upgrade water filter and things like that. There were few important stuff at the moment and you can't recycle at the beginning. There are also faction goals make things even more complicated.. Also ui and graphics doesn't really help the learning curve. Maybe the art is realistic but not really visible or distinguishable.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is at its core, a good game. The new graphics are appealing and freshen up the game more in comparison to the first Sheltered, whilst mechanics such as easier recycling, better trading and better salvaging give you more freedom as a player.Equally there are a few issues with it that I feel need addressing before it can be considered as a successor to Sheltered. Everything listed below was played on Normal difficulty:1. The stats of your characters degrade WAY too quickly, with food being a constant problem from the outset. EDIT: Still an issue.2. Tinned food degrades a little too fast, as the new temperature system (though a good idea) does not work properly. EDIT: ALL food degrades too fast and the temperature system is still an issue.3. Getting murdered by trigger happy psychopaths day 2, leaves the AI feeling too aggressive regardless of their ideology as a faction. EDIT: AI is still too aggressive.4. Some items could not be placed into my pantry/medicine cabinet after an expedition, even though I still had space. EDIT: This still happens, though can be ignored by pressing "Take all".Bugs:1. In my first run of the game I was unable to fix my generator at all, as the button would not appear after right clicking the generator. I had to wait for it to break down and burst into flames before being able to fix it, which causes heavy suffocation damage to my characters. Equally in my 2nd play through the button was there. EDIT: Fixed.2. On my 2nd play through, my weather vane and flood lights had a warning sign indicating a lack of power, even though I had more than enough fuel and had practically filled up my generator. I had to disable the flood lights and re-enable them to fix this issue, though that did not work for the weather vane, and upon reloading the issue remained along with the same warning sign on my shelter door. EDIT: Fixed.3. After a fight, I couldn't press the continue button to progress, thus having to shut the game down completely. EDIT: Fixed.TL;DR - Good game, but it still has some issues after all this time.EDIT (23/04/23): This game is significantly better now, though there are still issues that need to be addressed. Why are other factions super hostile and OP for no reason? Sheltered 1 had hostility, but a good chunk of the people you met were simply just trying to get by.Equally, though playable and somewhat enjoyable, it looks as if the game has been abandoned leaving it unpolished and unfinished. All in all this is quite tragic to see, and I for one feel scammed out of my money if this is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Updated after playing 56 hours from day 1 release. (see header)With more serious artstyle comes more serious gameplay.Sheltered 2 builds upon and offers more refined progression compared to and in relation to its predecessor. In contrast to Sheltered when one can easily skip tiers of equipment and max upgrade everything very easily and very early, Sheltered 2 offers a bit of a challenge. This challenge comes with accomplishment of faction goals that tracks everything the faction members do and accomplish. Although this may sound like "a bit tedious" as some reviews may put it, these are hurdles and not outright roadblocks. The doing and accomplishment of these goals not only puts a clear path of progression but also allows the player to experience what most of the game has to offer and ties neatly with its core gameplay of collecting, managing and crafting. The game so far balances it out to provide enough tension and participation from the player so as not to make the experience "too repetitive and boring" like eventually late game Sheltered 1 becomes.If you are a fan of management-survival games and do not shy from a bit of a challenge, then this is for you. But if you like a much more simpler gameplay with the option to be able to easily finish the game in no time, coupled with its pixelated art-style then the 1st Sheltered should do the trick.---------------The Update-----------------Bugs, bugs and bugs.I must admit that I ignored the game running a bit slow when opening the world map (kinda stutters with the forced motion blur even when I had it turned off in the settings).. but that was actually just a tip of the iceberg. A couple of annoying (but not game-breaking bugs):>item tooltip that remains even after closing the inventory window.>no descriptions for higher tier food recipes (only placeholder text like item.descrip.)>cannot autopsy corpses on the medical bed despite having the perk for it.>people going directly to the pantry even when there is a sink with soap on the way there and getting food poisoned (i think it says that people automatically use it when their hygiene meter exceeds 50%)>people keep wandering to the edges of the shelter and into my cold storage (suffering the freezing moodlet debuff). They should not move to non-ideal temperature areas when idle.>cannot raise a stat already maxed out with "experimentation perk" despite having the medical bed.>(already patched-I think) planter thief spawning immediately to take your fully harvested crops when reloading a save.>faction "rescue mission" bugged and remains on faction screen even after completed>"trade request location" remains stubbornly on map with the wrong faction after said wrong faction wins the territory of the intended faction (basically can't trade with the intended faction cause the other faction conquered their area - such that the intended faction always says that his representatives haven't returned on the faction screen)>trading in excess of your weight capacity causes traded items to disappear forever>destroying an entire faction by simply trading at their HQ... (traded them a lot of meat)Overall these bugs accumulated, make the experience quite annoying and sometimes frustrating when everything else, especially the gameplay loop is very solid and shows promise. I'd still recommend the game as the developers are doing their best to iron things out with each latest patch at 2GBs. I just wished that they released this game a bit better and not make people play-test it when it did not release as an early-access game.P.S. the game does run a bit slow even when by system meets the requirements....

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely builds on the previous game without losing what was so fun and addicting about it. I can say that if I went back to the first game, I would miss a lot of what they've added here. For one, I was never able to complete a vehicle in the original game, so this is a really nice change. I also appreciate how consistently they've been working out the bugs. That said, I haven't actually experienced most of the issues they've been fixing. In the nearly 70 hours I've played, I've had one bug that I'm aware of. As far as negatives— kinda minor but I actually don't think that the updated graphics added much to the game. I really enjoyed the minimalism of the the original pixelated 2D art style. I feel like a lot of game developers believe that updated graphics = better game, and that is so rarely the case. That said, the new graphics don't really bother me as much as they seem to bother some other reviewers. I'm sure they'll add more appearance options later on but it really doesn't affect game play, certainly not when you consider how few options in the original. Lastly, kinda bummed they don't offer this game for Mac like the original, so I have to borrow a PC :( maybe this will be available for Mac in the future?Overall, really enjoying it!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Game! Granted, I did not play the first game, so I don't really understand the reason for the negative reviews as I have no basis of comparison. It's a great little survival game with a solid spin on the genre to make it unique and distinct in it's gameplay and feel. The game is engaging enough to keep you plugged in; there's always something to do. You definitely get that feel of scarcity. Combat is straight-forward, as is base-building and maintenance. Strong emphasis on needing to maintain things and there is definitely a sense of having finite space with which to do things. All in all, I've really enjoyed it and I anticipate I will be plugging all kinds of hours into this as I try to scrounge my way through another apocalypse simulator. At under $20 CAD, this is a steal as far as I'm concerned. If you like the genre and enjoy survival / management sim type games, you'll definitely get your money's worth.9 / 10 on overall experience.10 / 10 on valueHope the game gets regular content updates. _childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2.I enjoy this game, and if you like base management games with a post apocalyptic setting I'd say give it a shot. HOWEVER there are some things in this game that have really aggravated me. ( Both bugs and game mechanics. ) And I could see them aggravating other people as well.Bug 1. Enemies getting stuck on each other at your shelter door during raids: One of the most frustrating bugs happens during raids on your shelter, and it happens ALL THE TIME after the first raid. The enemies trying to get into your base will get stuck on each other and cannot enter your base until they somehow get unstuck. Meaning that the raid will last much longer then it needs to, or if your really unlucky it’ll never end and you’ll be forced to reload a save. This happens every single time after the first raid. ( Because theres literally only one enemy on the first raid. ) And to my knowledge there’s no way to get them unstuck. It’s so annoying that I groan every time I get a notification that there’s a raid.Bug 2. Rations disappearing on expeditions: This only happened to me one time but it was very annoying. During one of my expeditions all of the rations that I gave my party just disappeared, and I didn’t notice until I got in a fight with a outpost attempting to capture it. Meaning that they had the weak status effect for the whole fight. ( I still managed to capture it for those wondering. ) I have no idea how that happened and I gave them up to 40 to 50 rations. It only happened to me one time but it was very annoying.Bug 3. Enemies fleeing combat makes the hud disappear: This one also only happened one time but it breaks the game when it happens. If an enemy leaves combat the hud disappears, meaning that you can’t do anything. You can’t even end your turn, meaning that your forced to reload a save. ( This has caused me to immediately target any enemy that attempts to flee out of fear that this bug will happen again. No one escapes my leaders wrath. ) Annoying game mechanic 1. The guns are very weak: Seriously, don’t bother with the handgun or shotgun. They are so weak that they will get your survivors killed in combat. You are better off focusing on melee, and getting the perk that allows your survivors to attack multiple times per attack. ( Although the rifle is actually ok. )Annoying game mechanic 2 Teleporting fire extinguisher?: If there are multiple fires in the shelter and if a survivor doesn’t get to the fire fast enough then the fire extinguisher will teleport back to where it was originally placed and the survivor will drop what they are doing, causing more of your stuff to catch fire and get destroyed. ( Also they are SO AGONIZINGLY SLOW when responding to a fire in the shelter and they get heat exhaustion when in the same room as a fire causing them to go EVEN SLOWER. ) Side notes: Combat is to easy once your survivors stats get high and they get lots of perks.During raids I’ve noticed that the enemies aren’t even armed, so there not really that much of a threat. ( If they can get each other unstuck outside of the door that is. )Speaking of raids it’s also annoying to have to go through the equipping phase each time a fight starts in your bunker because you can only fight four enemies at once.More guns then just “handgun, shotgun, rifle and crossbow” would be nice, but that’s just me. In conclusion I did enjoy my time with this game, and I’ll play it while talking to Friends so it makes a really good conversation game. But I’d say wait for a deep sale if you plan on purchasing this game. ( My shelter is still going strong as of this post. )Edit: A patch for the game was released shortly after I posted my review that made the guns more useful. They now deal more damage.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite downgrade from the first game. There's not much to say on this, it's largely the same gameplay and yet it's just worse in all regards except this time it's in 3D! I liked the choice of pet from the first game, that's gone, the "family versus the world" aspect is gone too, and then there's the annoying lack of certain structures from the first game that just don't appear in this one. (I want my freezer back) What you get here is some annoying hex-tile map with "factions" that I could not care less about and don't interact with me in any way besides getting in my way. A lot of the dark, frankly menacing, aspects of the pixel art are thoroughly absent in the sterile and uninspiring setting and everyone walks like they've had an accident in their pants. There's this dumb "leader" thing too, it's just more junk weighing this title down.What finally provoked me to make a comment was that there is absolutely no way to save anyone who falls unconscious after a fight in the shelter. Provoking a fight, or rather avoiding one, is seemingly at random since the game doesn't let you click a button and say, "Yes, I would like to engage in mortal combat with these intruders." I'm sure there's something resembling the rifle sentry gun of the first game, or at least I'd hope so, but this trainwreck won't let me upgrade the workshop to even see that so I suppose there's not much point in playing. There are greyed-out tiers, of course, but what they do and how to find that out is a mystery that I don't feel motivated to solve. I'm sure it has something to do with those idiotic factions.Oh, and for what you get, this game is extremely over-priced. Even the initial sale price was far too much and I really regret buying it, but that's my own fault.

_childDocuments_.review: Much as I'd like to recommend this game, I just can't. The general vibe is nice, looting feels reasonably rewarding, like it when a game lets you break things down and build things with the pieces. Well, once you figure out how vital to basic progress building a recycler is. Wish the upgraded version wasn't a random find.You need to endure a lot of grind in this game. Grind for reputation, go out again and again to find resources and hope for some good ones because even with the best crafter in the world you can't make excellent quality of raw resources. micromanage your people to excercise or read to grind up their skills, right click on every single machine in your base to have people go repair it, every couple of days. How I craved a, go repair stuff command, similar to the clean shelter command. But your people would be too dense for that.Your people won't stop what they're doing for their needs till its too late often times, but they will stop randomly. They'll stop wherever they are in the event of a raid, even  if that means they're slowly dying and you need to manually tell them to seek safe temperatures. They punctuate every task with an annoying random walk to, somewhere, so if they have multiple needs they'll make sure to delay attending to the others. And they'll gladly eat the depressing human meat on the shelf we keep for the animals before eating the non-human flesh alternatives as well as eating the non-perishable cans before perishable goods, just to be sure some rots. The animals are no better. I do tire of watching them starving to death, checking their bowls still have food and wondering if they'll die before they get there, or trying to train a dog, which only pauses once they start dying.Remember the hard to grind resources? Well the game doesn't give any warning if your people are going to use top quality goods for a low quality purpose, and I can't find a way to deny them. I assume they use lowest quality first, but I don't trust that.I only tried capturing an attacker once, decided to let them go, big mistake. They just stood there till they starved to death, not even deleting the holding cage got rid of their dead yet not dead body, they ended up eternally embedded in the wall, giving my people a -20 to their moods, or I presume the game thinking they were still here was behind the slavery debuff.Short version, the game has bugs, is laden with grind, allows minimal automation or control of which resources your people use and just generally keeps on going long after the novelty has worn off.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather than merely criticize the game, I'd like to point out my observations from the first several minutes. I will update this review as I spend more time playing. I wish Steam had more options that weren't "yes or no", because recommending a game is difficult and sometimes the answer is in-between.From the get-go, it's clear that the game has moved from the traditional pixel-art look to a more modern 3D look. Whether or not the game looks better (from an artistic standpoint) is debatable. The pixelated look gave it a unique appearance but offered less visual fidelity. The new look, while offering more fidelity, also looks rather generic if compared to other titles in the genre.In the previous game, the ultimate goal remained the same; survive. But with the addition of a family, I felt there was more emotional incentive and an obligation to protect them. While I like the faction system here and I appreciate the thought put into it, I simply do not feel an obligation to protect my faction when we can't even begin to develop these characters in a meaningful way. What is their backstory or connection to my leader? If this is an "RPG", why can't I roleplay as a lone survivor rather than deal with the baggage that comes with babysitting other survivors? Why are there no more than three types of bottoms by which we can customize each character- two of them being pants and one of them being shorts? If our characters cannot be defined by the backgrounds we set for them, we might try to define them by appearance.In life we are often led to believe that clothes & appearance can represent someone's personality, and if the means by which we can define them are limited- then our characters become no different from eachother. Each person seems generic, regardless of said backstory you have created for them. There is also the idea of wish fulfillment to consider. In games that offer various forms of customization, such as VRChat, the idea is that many people will enjoy making something based on what best represents their self-image. Much like some prefer to using face filters, because they feel  best represents their perceived image as a whole. There is a reason we see so many people creating these flawless, big-tiddied characters more than we see overweight characters. Because it doesn't represent what is closest to our reality and it sets us apart from others. Even if the truth is that we are all very depressed and fat on the inside. I'm not afraid to admit I just took a massive dukie after eating taco bell. Everytime I eat tacos I warn people to clear the room in 5 minutes. I want people to know how much I like tacos, but I don't want anyone to  just how much I like tacos. There is nothing wrong with this, it's just how we like to play our games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much suffering from a publisher-pushed early release, but the team behind it all is working so very hard to fix it.Some really big bugs for me are the ones that can suddenly and irreverisbly delete resources in a game where managing said resources is the main purpose. Easiest trap is that you can que up more than 10 tasks on your survivors quite easily - but only 10 tasks will actually be saved, 11+ will simply be taken from storage and never be seen again.It's the sort of thing I'd be more open to forgive if there were an 'Early Access' flag hanging under this game, but I really find it hard to accept 'Full releases' that struggle with beta-bug-issues. I believe it will be fixed over time as I think Unicube is a solid team, but pressured by Team17 into a rushed release that will hurt the game.In general, the game thus far feels "easier" and a LOT slower than it's predecessor. The content-exploration makes it feel like I'm barely getting started still. When I say easier, it may be because of bugs since factions do not seem to mind that I take their territory, they just defend the next place harder. Training your survivors to get their stats up feels a bit to easy right now, my crew barely 2 weeks in having increased from mostly 2-3's to around 10's. Not a serious issue outside of that the pacing of the game feels a LOT slower. Finding higher-quality materials and climbing into T3 is where I'm at right now and it is feeling like an RNG grind which bothers me a bit as well.I dare say that once bugs that can delete items from storage is dealt with, I'll trust the devs to provide a great game and give it a thumbs up. At the moment, the game just has to many things to keep in mind so it's exhausting to play knowing that certain clicks can unintentionally erase much needed items rather than block the player from such acts.These are on the to-do list so I've changed my case to a thumbs up and just hope the devs won't give up their health crunch-timing to much trying to deliver patches like a machine gun.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent successor to Sheltered. The updated graphics and change in focus from a family to a faction of wasteland survivors makes the game considerably less charming and unique but maybe ultimately a better "game." What I mean by that is that there are game-play ideas and features here I would have really liked to have in Sheltered -- faction relationships and perks,  RPG style character progression, a reworked overland map with better exploration and way better resource management (like you get a junk pile on the surface to keep things you can't store inside). But unfortunately there is a lot missing from the original. For one thing the UI and overall style was totally reworked and I think it's a net loss. While the move to 3D was a positive change in theory the implementation leaves a lot to be desired. The only utility you get out of the new 3D is an expanded surface area above your base, so you have more room to build crops and traps. That part is cool. What you lose is a lot of the flavor and art that the original game had. The 3D assets are fine but they don't really have much style or character. This is perhaps most noticeable in the UI, sheltered 1 had a more material and artistic UI that made use of actual books and clipboards. The Sheltered 2 UI is functional and generic, no personality, it's "fine." On top of all that there is also the problem that the game feels unfinished. I'm somewhat surprised that this game isn't "early access" and there are issues I've encountered that I expect the game to be improved and fixed by either patches or mods. for example I have burned out items in my bunker and I don't seem to be able to do anything about them, that has to be a bug, i'm sure it will get fixed. development continued on Sheltered for a long time after it was released so I expect at least a couple of patches going forward. All this is not to say it's not good. It is, I've played Sheltered 1 on PC and Android and like it and there is a lot in Sheltered 2 that makes it a better survival game. So far I've played it quite a bit and will likely continue to play it, it's fine and if you liked the Sheltered survival experience I think it's worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played nearly 20 hours (multiple tries) and I am still not enjoying this game as much as the first one.It's a difficult game and the many bugs make it harder (rain never comes, glitches, UI disappearing in combat e.tc). _childDocuments_.review: Don't you hate it when you're not strong enough to use a knife?This other day while I was in my bunker, I wanted to make a peanut butter sandwich but my strength was only a 3 and I needed a 4 to use the butter knife.Or I wanted to go play baseball with my nephew but my dexterity was only a 5 and I needed a 7 to hold a baseball bat! I just couldn't figure out how to pick up a bat!To break the character now, this game is nice but Sheltered 1 is better than Sheltered 2. This game feels like a completely different developer took the IP. First off my biggest problem is the random people who come to your base asking to join. 99/100 of them are men, I had only 1 woman ask to come join my base. I should've named my fraction the Sausage Bois! Or maybe all the women joined the Black Roses which is an all woman society. I wonder how well that group is gonna work out once the women become 40 and have no young people around. Please note how short life expectancies are when there's no modern medicine.The other problem that really bugged me was the high skill requirement for weapons. Imagine not being able to use an electric knife because your strength is a 3 and you need a 4. Most people who asked to come join my group had a lot of skills that were level 1. And although they do upgrade it is such a gamebreaking slog to see someone unwilling to pick up a baseball bat to fight with because their skills aren't high enough. This is like how you can't wear a certain T-shirt in Cyberpunk because it's level 22 and you're level 12. Don't you hate when you can't wear Forever 21 dresses because their level is higher than yours?What bothered me the most is the tier item system. To get tier 2, 3, 4 you have to complete certain quests. Quests such as "Become friends with the AFK Group" to get the reward of tier 4 items. In my playthrough I was actually able to build tier 3 items before tier 2 items because I had accidentally completed that quest requirement first. I don't even know what the quest was but it was upgrading one of the items on the surface. Just completely happenstance and I got the tier 3 before tier 2 items. _childDocuments_.review: Look, I get it. It doesn't have the cute "survival family" vibe of the original, not the graphical style that was one of the things that made it so unique. Going from a cosy little survival simulator to a full blow "let's take over the known world" is a big step that may be a little difficult to process for some of the fans of the original game. But it's really not that bad a game.I have encountered a few non-gamebreaking bugs, but other than that it's pretty stable and everything that needs to work, works well. Expanding and crafting and exploring is pretty fun most of the time and. Almost all of the mechanics of the original game have been preserved too.Is it a great game? No, it's not. The developers have made some serious shortcuts that keep the game firmly in 7-ish territory. The factions are kind of fun, but grabbing territory from them is utterly pointless - outposts don't seem to serve any purpose: other than to keep them out of the hands of others, it achieves nothing. The game would have been better off if every faction had one base, and attacking it would destroy the faction and leave the shelter in ruins. And the amount of clicking you need to do when crafting (whether it is food or anything else) is ridiculous. And if you don't, you are end up prematurely using those 3 star resources on something way too simple. It's tedious to the point of frustration at times.Combat is a bit more extensive than the original game, which is ok, but... the way that battles are presented, the scope of the battles feels much bigger than it is. It's simplistic and you can name one skill "confuse opponent" and the other "crush windpipe" but if the outcome is that the target is dazed, it's the same skill. And most of the rest of the skills are superfluous.But these things do not take away from the fun of building a thriving shelter. If this is your genre, you'll easily have a few full days of fun, and there's enough there for a replay or two.This game is being judged too harshly.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so I have played the first one, and have suck a huge amount of hours into this one.  It is a pretty decent game and worthy of the roughly $30 AUD price tag.The game was very buggy at first I must admit.  That has changed and been polished somewhat since.There are still bugs and glitches though.  The first bug I encountered was someone sitting and eating but were unable to get up and as a result ended up dying a slow death causing everyone who went past for a meal to feel sad.  This was a horrible bug that sucked the fun out of my first play through, and this happened some 40 hours into the game!  So yeah it was a simple but bad one.The next bug I encountered was I recruited a prisoner but she was still stuck in the prison! I destroyed the prison and she was stuck behind the walls.  Thankfully this one somehow resolved itself when the character was hungry and thirsty enough.  In the same play through, I was performing an autopsy on a corpse when I saved and exited, came back and I was able to infinite harvest organs.  Talk about gruesome!  The result was I had to remove the medical bed then harvest the corpse to fix this bug which caused the shelter to have a negative buff again.So yes, the game is still buggy.  The new pests addition can see rats get out of hand really quickly if you don't have a cat.It is stressful, and to be honest, it is a great game at creating stressful situations due to its own inherent and quirky bugs.The rats go from 0 to 100 in next to no time. So here is the good bad and the ugly of it.Good:It is actually a lot of fun, and can take a while to master or indeed not fail.It doesn't have too steep a learning curve but a steep mastering curve.Bad:Things break down so quickly all the time, constantly fixing stuff daily!So much micro management even with certain perks that help you not to need itDid I already mention bugs?
