_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a post-apocalyptic survival game similar in genre to Fallout Shelter, or This War of Mine. The idea is, a small group of survivors and a pet find an abandoned underground cellar and use it to survive for as long as possible in a post apocalyptic world dominated by gangs. The fun and reward in this game comes in you micromanaging a group of people's daily needs while transforming their small prepper-basement into a multi-level underground base with modern amenities and great furnishing over time.So the game is about real time base building, turn-based combat and selective looting. It's pretty much a copy of Sheltered 1, except the 8-bit pixel style graphics have been replaced with 3D realism. The con side of this, is the game looks rather drab in its shades of red and brown compared to the more colorful & charming artstyle of Sheltered 1, and is also way more GPU demanding than its predecessor. Yet the graphics arent the focus of this game, but a TON of micromanagement (clicking around to repair things, set up expeditions, answer the radio and assign tasks to your survivors within the shelter), so you won’t be too focused on the graphics anyway. In fact I recommend to pause often.Each survivor has a set of meters that keep filling up and need to be reduced: thirst, hunger, sleepiness, dirtiness, and the need to poo, initially into buckets that need to be washed out with plenty of water. Run out of water to flush the buckets out, and your survivors will pinch one out on the floor in desperation, raising their dirtiness bar immediately to max level. If a survivor then proceeds to go and eat while filthy, they will contract food poisoning and will find themselves retching all over the floor. So even if you have enough food, if you run out of water, your survivors will be reduced to a poo and puke stained mess within days, which is hilarious and sad at the same time.This brings us to the most important resource in this game: water. Which is automatically collected every time it rains outside, into your water barrels via the water filter that sits on the surface of your shelter (and degrades over time and one of your survivors has to go outside and fix it every now and then, just like the oxygen filter - unlike Sheltered 1, without having to don hazmat suits every single time they are outside). However, if the rain is black rain, it first has to go through the water purifier you also start the game with, something that requires energy to run (so keep it off unless it starts filling up during black rain). What appliances use how much energy is checked at the fuse box, and if you have more power draw than power generation, things start malfunctioning. And the more power draw, the faster you'll run out of fuel. In Sheltered 2 there is also the weather vane, which tells you the forecast for the next day (or more, if you upgrade it).So water is needed to slake the thirst of your survivors, to grow crops, to take a shower and flush the toilet, the latter two consuming less and less water depending on the quality of the shower or toilet you have built. MRE rations instead of water are now needed for the 2nd most important aspect of this game: sending your survivors out on scavenging missions. People say devs abandoned the game, but only a few bugs in Sheltered 2 remain, like your dog not regenerating AP after its attack, or that radioing for traders to come to your shelter never works, but every so often one stops by anyway. So scavenging is the only way to accumulate resources & expand your shelter over time. Resources are stored either in boxes you need to build inside the shelter that take up room, or they get dumped on the junk pile outside from where items will occasionally be stolen by passers by.Each scavenging party can consist of up to 4 survivors, and the dog if you have one. You have to create an exploration route (a loop that starts and ends at your base and formed by waypoint markers) for them to travel on, and they will visit any location that is on this loop. The bigger (further) the loop, the longer it takes.Before leaving, you need to equip your party. Each has 1 weapon slot, 1 rucksack slot (to increase carry weight) and initially 2 equipment slots for body armor, camo, whistles to attract stray animals, or binoculars to increase the visible tiles when exploring the world map.The sheer number of items that you encounter in the game world can quickly overwhelm new players. As you run out of inventory space while exploring, you need to start prioritizing which loot you bring back to the base and which things you leave behind. Thankfully, the devs have provided a “you have x of these back in your base” reference whenever you hover your mouse over a piece of loot you find at a location, so you have an easier time bringing back the stuff you desperately need, and leave the rest, usually heavier stuff, behind. Back in your shelter, you break down the items you brought back for their useful individual components, initially by hand, later by recycler.The third most important aspect in this game is fuel. Which powers your generator, which in turn powers your base by not just keeping the lights on, but also the oxygen filter working. If you run out of fuel, O2 levels drop and it’s game over far sooner than if you run out of water. Thankfully, fuel isn’t too rare, because the fuel canisters you find in most locations (rather than just at gas stations like in Sheltered 1), last a lot longer than the water you find this way, and you can build an incinerator pretty early on as an alternate source of fuel where you can chuck anything you don’t need to keep the power going, but preferably coal and fertilizer. Unlike Sheltered 1, the generator cant be upgraded for better fuel efficiency.This brings us to the long term goals of this game – fully exploring the world map, assembling vehicles and meeting all other factions and interacting with them (as i explain further below) but unlike Sheltered 1, Sheltered 2 has an even steeper initial learning curve that may make people ragequit. For instance, summer dries up all rain and your entire ecosystem breaks down without water which can after this point only be traded in the form of singular bottles from other factions (who offer it - not all of them do). Good luck washing yourself and flushing your business with the few bottles you bring back from a grueling 2 day march. And if you dont and just use it for drinking, good luck dealing with food poisoning every time you eat. Since crops wont grow without water, hunting rabbits and later deer become your only food source during summer. As a result, deaths and cannibalism can haunt your base, and you only lose the game if your main character (the base leader you began the game with) dies.But since new recruits keep knocking at your shelter door every so often, any survivor you lose can be replaced without worrying too much about stat loss as the newcomers also level up over time. Loot at visited locations respawns (but slowly, so dont revisit the same place too soon), and while enemies get stronger over time, your survivors also earn exp from combat or trading & can even train in the base using punching bags or reading books to increase their stats (and unlock perks).What is frustrating though, is the absolute lack of a combat tutorial. You learn over time though.Sheltered 2 also tries to offer more story than Sheltered 1 by introducing faction mechanics (you can expand your control zone by storming outposts, OR - and this is more rewarding - do various quests for every faction for an eventual alliance with them, while in the 1st game you just encountered them as variously clothed enemies). And then there is the endgame, an extra bit of sci-fi thrown in. Nevertheless, the DLC of Sheltered 1 was more interesting.So overall, I recommend Sheltered 1 over 2, but Sheltered 2 is addictive in its own way and took me 80 hours to finish

_childDocuments_.review: Alright guys, calm down. I have ~16 hours on the original Sheltered. I ALREADY have ~13 for Sheltered 2. The graphics are SO. MUCH. BETTER. The Tutorial helped me learn SO MUCH for the beginning. The character customization, and details to mental health(SCHIZOPHRENIA?!!), as well as detail to physical ailments, is so fun!! I mean, obviously Schizophrenia isn't fun. You know what I mean.ANYWAY. Yeah, the game has glitches. I had a guy get stuck after digging a grave. It was kind of fun. I just pretended he was a scarecrow. Developers should probably look into this. It seems that there is a possibility for corpses that are placed above ground to remove the body bags and still be seen by the game as "unconscious". You are able to select the corpse in excavations. I was REALLY HOPING to see Christopher Williamson zombie walk with the crew, but alas, the game just went through an endless cycle of waiting for him to walk. Lastly, the bug that bugged me the most was the eating function. It worked sometimes, giving the command to the character, but if you were to have them eat again, it would show the command and it would then IMMEDIATELY disappear. I had to step in. The hate is not warranted! After the loading screen, the game felt smooth! The tutorial (WHICH I RECOMMEND) helped me TREMENDOUSLY, and was very in depth. Please keep fixing the bugs! Otherwise, I am in love with this game so far!

_childDocuments_.review: So the game needs more work and balancing, but I'm giving a positive review because I do think a lot of the negative ones here are a bit unfair and so far the developer seems keen to develop the game a bit further and is reactive to feedback. Graphics, mechanics, some things like surface radiation having reduced after 20 years so you don't need hazmat suits always are a nice lore friendly touch. Also so far its looks like they've dropped the racist elements from the original.What the game needs: -Easier resources near your base or cheaper travel, because its a real dice roll if you get what you need to advance early on, and finding you're immediately surrounded by faction territory and need to tangle with them is a bit daunting. -More options when meeting folk, at least factions. Only being able to Fight, Trade or Flee is a bit shallow. Given characters have a charm skill, this would be used for some convo options to increase faction rep a little perhaps. -A subdue option. At least if you've got blunt weapons like the baseball bat. Forcing me to murder my way across the wasteland, trashing the mental stability of my characters for no real reason is annoying. Let us beat up, rob and then bail on people who attack us like in the original.-Love the automation of characters meeting their needs. Perhaps other tasks like repairs and that could be automated as well as eventually they do become a chore to keep clicking. Maybe a higher tier item you could build would be a work roster of some kind, assigning people to certain jobs throughout the day?Once again, its got promise. I hope they continue to improve it because it should outstrip the original given a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is an upgraded version of the original indie game. There's some new ideas, especially the factions and overland exploration that's been fleshed out compared to the original. You now move your team around a better graphical map. The game is fun overall if you like clicking.Speaking on clicking, You will be clicking. A lot of clicking. Items decay in your Shelter rapidly and you'll find you're spending an inordinate amount of time clicking on everything to repair.Bugs - The game was buggy at launch but at least the developers are aware and are fixing it daily. There are some critical bugs like losing all your rations, items going missing which in essence, will wipe out your Shelter. If you're ok with this sort of launch problems, Reload and start again.UI Issues - The game has some strange UI decisions making parts of the game not intuitive for what seems like mundane tasks. In a game of what essentially is about tasking, finding out how to do simple tasks from the discussion board is rather counter-intuitive.Combat is simple - very simple. Once you hit a milestone in stats, equipment and skills, You're Arya Stark wiping out factions solo. _childDocuments_.review: So far this is worlds better than the first game.  Exploration got much better and is quite enjoyable.  The bunker management feels similar however, just some more features and items for your survivors to mess around, with a good variety too.  Very dissapointed that the placement system is the same.. it lacks depth. A table and chair should be able to fit under the small pantry.. and why can I not put the weights under the cot? It fits... and the punching bag has a massive placement box that makes no sense.  After awhile it does feel like a chore issuing orders when you have 5+ people at home.  The AI however is terrible to the point where i wanted to quit.  They linger too much and will constantly just stand there in my freezer after eating and start to die... and on top of that they will somehow eat raw food when i have none and a full pantry of cooked food...  I get youre supposed to manage it all with help from AI assigning themselves tasks but sometimes you just hope the AI will be efficient while you focus on other things... they arent.  TURN OFF AUTOMATION FOR YOUR SURVIVORS!!!!(This seems to fix their stupidity) The bunker raids feel poorly done.  Picture fallout shelters bunker raids.. its exactly like that but slightly worse.  It was dramatic at first but the moment the raiders break in they just casually walk by my survivors i tried to place at the door(they kept walking away..turn off automation) and started looting... my survivor finally started the combat mode after they almost escaped... the combat is pretty good, its turn based so its pretty straight forward.  Was very disappointed after the fight because it gave no loot screen or an option to loot the bodies...Theres definitely alot of replay value here as its a randomised map every new game.  It just gets hectic when your bunker gets bigger is all and with terrible AI, it can be frustrating.  Hopefully the AI gets updated/acts smarter but until then turning automation off creates a better experience... and hopfully a reworked new bunker raid system but overall a fun game and looking forward to the improvement and development of the game.  In its current state its recommended, especially for $20, l i know ill get my monies worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 1 fan here, along with anything survival postapo-type games. I got SH2 on discount, because just like everyone else, I was worried about the reviews and the general state of the game.However today I come to tell you, the game is just fine. The first 11h of the gameplay definitely made me question what are all those bad reviews about (though maybe I didn't stumble on any jarring issue quite yet).What I did stumble on, is this:People who play in this type of games understand more than others that some games are just JANK - buggy, overambitious, but fun. If you ever played in games like Stalker or Kenshi, then you know what I'm talking about.And just like in case of Kenshi, Sheltered 2 visibly accumulates errors over long hours of gameplay, which then turn into bugs. And , all you gotta do is just quit the game and boot it up again as a break from your 6h marathon of playing the game.If you can do that, then great! If you can't, then I don't know what to tell you, other than stick to triple-A studios, instead of expecting the same quality from an indie dev studio that just upgraded this series from 2D pixels to quite beautiful 3D systems.Final note: For the current -50% discount it's a bargain. Though in all fairness it doesn't live up to its full price quite yet. I heard that devs are working on the game still so I'm having high hopes for it, but I'm also bracing for any possible issues that I may encounter later in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard Sheltered 2 no longer receive update, so i decide to try Sheltered 2 and find out whether it's fun despite issue mentioned by many reviewers. After playing a bit, i agree some of those issue definitely exist and find Sheltered 2 isn't fun. For comparison, Sheltered 1 is fun for me where I've wasted ~140h on Steam and few hours on Android. Anyway, here's my  thought and comparison between 2 games.* Better tutorial, although i expect more for game with $20 base price.* Somewhat better UI, but worse UX experience.* Some condition to unlock next tier of crafting object is ridiculous.* You can recycle item from beginning of the game.* Expedition now require food/ration.* From few expeditions, NPC always talk about fiction.* I like the idea of leader who have unique trait and usage.* Skill tree is interesting, but after reading some skill i think only some of them are useful or worth to obtain.* You can let the game automate certain basic task (eat, sleep, etc.) for certain character when the bar reach 50% or 75%.* Item with higher stars only lead to higher price. For example, canned from from 1-3 stars have exactly same integrity and hunger reduction value.* Better combat mechanics. Although i don't like the camera change back-and-forth whenever a character perform action.* Graphic/visual-wise, i prefer Sheltered 1 over Sheltered 2 where i feel Sheltered 2 has generic 3D style.* Only OKish music/sound effect considering $20 base price.* I experience few bugs such as character stuck or my command to stop existing task occasionally got ignored by the game.* No problem running this game on Linux.Obviously i can't recommend this game and suggest you to check Sheltered 1 or This War of Mine instead. If only Unicube improve 2D style (rather than switch to 3D) and not adding too much new mechanics, Sheltered 2 could be better or more enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is set 20 years after an apocalyptic event happened on Earth, wiping out most of the human race, what remains are splintered factions, all vying for their own land and resources.At first look the game will remind you of Fallout Shelter, and although there are similarities, Sheltered 2 is quite different and much more of a hardcore survival game.Your job is to run your shelter, grow your faction, all the while managing your resources, crafting items, exploring outside of your shelter, and generally trying to keep everyone alive.Now do not be mistaken, this is not an easy game, even on the easiest setting, the game is tough, it is probably a bit too tough, and the tutorial is about as much help as a Donor Kebab in a Vegan festival. With that said, each time you play, you do learn, and there is a lot to be said for just starting the game again, using what you have learnt, to help you make better decisions.Most of the gameplay will take place in your shelter, you need to keep an eye on your group, make sure everyone is happy and healthy, you will need to craft things like a toilet, a shower, beds, as well as expand downwards to make room for more things.When you are not in your shelter, you will need to keep an eye above land, set traps to catch rabbits, keep things powered, clean and working, plant seeds to grow food and so on. And when you are ready you will need to leave the area altogether and explore. You already control a small region, which is safe to explore on its own, gather more resources as well as grow the levels of experience of your group. But eventually you will want to explore outside of your region, and that is when you will come across other factions.The faction's system, is the main pull of this game, you will need to trade with other groups, forge relationships, and sometimes fight them, everything is a balancing act, choose who to fight and who to trade with and who to run away from. You will even complete quests, which become a big part of the game if you want your shelter to grow.The fights are all turn based, you can choose where to hit an opponent, what weapon or skill to use, and if you choose correctly, you will kill them, and then you can take everything they have.As you play, your characters levels will grow, you will get new skills and so on.Further into the game you will even find vehicles which you can fix up, to help you explore faster and easier.The GoodThis is a challenging survival game that fans of the genre should enjoy, the graphics are decent, and once you get the general idea of how to play, everything is pretty straight forward.The BadThe game is way too tough. When travelling around the map, interactions tend to have three options, Trade, Fight or Flee, and this can become a bit repetitive, and if you come across a rival faction, it is just fight or flee. A couple of lines of dialog and that's it.The whole crafting system is overly complicated, meaning a lot of back and forth, whether it is trying to see what ingredients you need to craft, then trying to figure out what you need to recycle, and so on, you will be left stuck pretty quick, forcing you to explore outside the shelter, which is fine, but this seems to happen way too quickly, not giving a new player chance to feel settled. There are way too many things to worry about in the Shelter, leaving a new player feeling overwhelmed.Bugs are being fixed pretty quick by Team 17, but this plays like an Alpha release and not the finished article.OverallThere is a good game in here, but it takes time to find it, and restarting once you figure certain things out will help you, but the game still struggles to really grab you. There needs to be a simplified mode, and a tutorial that really explains things. With all my complaints, I just feel that there is a great game here, but it is stuck in some kind of hole, that the developers don't have the time to get it out of.I will keep an eye out for updates, and maybe they can improve things moving forward.As the game stands right now, I score it 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Being a long term fan of the original Sheltered game, I was shocked to seeing it was getting a sequal, considering the game was stopped updating and finished many years ago, so as soon as Sheltered 2 was announced, I had to buy it being a fan myself. When I first started the game, I was very excited, but alot of things were disappointing (Which will probably be improved in the future) which is why I give this a 7/10, which I explain belowGameplay for Sheltered 2 is very transferable from the original game, just right clicking everything and selecting what you want to do. The addition of crafting really enchances the game, no more just meat and canned food, which really helped expand in the game itself. You are able to craft more things, not just what you could in the old game; medicine, weapons, guns, and items that you may use to build other items in your shelter itself. Recycling has been added as default, which is great. Going outside of the shelter does not grant you radiation poisoning, except in specific conditions, such as dust storms or acid or black rain. Going out and scavaging for supplies is pretty much the same than the original Sheltered game, only this time you do not need water to go out. You get supplies, then go to the next building. Meeting survivors is the same, only that your skills pay a part and may give you better results if your skill is higher Combat in Sheltered 2 has been totally revamped, having a whole new skill tree, stamina, and more. No more melee, subdue, or such, you now can choose which body part you want to hit, which has different effects, depending on what you do. As you level up your skills, you can get different skills, which do different things, depending on the skill itself.The introduction of the skill tree totally makes each character different from each other, meaning you have to decide which skills they should have, all have their own perks and benefits. Characters sometimes don't have max to level 20, meaning that you have to be careful which perks you spend on.There are 6 factions, all which have their own backstory, style, and objectives. They fight each other through out the game (But in my experience, it feels as its 5 of the factions against the 1, as they all wanted me to capture a specific faction member.) They have their own territory, and which if you enter, you are firstly introduced to the faction, and then after that, you'll have the choice to flee or fight. Throughout the game, you can do tasks for each faction, supply runs, freeing prisoners and capturing prisoners are a few tasks that gain loyalty points and to gain trust for that faction. Killing faction members deals negative points, meaning that they will hate you more. Depending on your playstyle, you can form an alliance with a faction, or kill the faction entirely in order to take over their entire land. Raids are very similar to how they were in the original game, except there are more traps for you to learn as you play the game. When a raid is activated, you have time to prepare, whether you want to fight or hide. This time, when you get close to an attacker, the person they touch is the one who will be in the fight, then you can choose 3 other people to fight. There are alot of bugs within the game, some of which ruin some of the things in the game itself. There was this bug where you could trade with a faction leader, and it would instantly wipe out the faction itself, another where corpses could not be interacted with, and some combat screen bugs. As playing the game, the developers are fixing these bugs, which is good. I really enjoy Sheltered 2, playing for 110 hours and in day 300 in my shelter itself is very rewarding, however, these bugs need to be fixed so that I can play the game I wanted to play. I imagine soon they'll add more content in the game to make it more fun, just like that they did with the original Sheltered game.

_childDocuments_.review: have played the game in different difficulties several times, and my biggest dissapointment is the unbalance in the game. bugs and glitches i beleve will be fixed, but the balance is "out the window".all my games ends the same way after an hour or two of gameplay. my shelter gets raided by other clans and wiped out emedietly either killed in the first round or starves to death when they get back to the shelter.update:desided to give it "one more try" and they have apparently fixed the balance, or my extreme bad luck is gone. so it is not impossible to defend the base anymore, but there are some bad bugs in the game atm. it is fun and i do enjoy the game. looking forward for the bug fixes.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Sheltered 1. It's better. Are there some iffy bugs or balancing acts going on? Sure. It's brand new. That said I am enjoying it greatly and expect to put in a solid few hours into this game.Updated Review after over 100 hours played: The dev expanded almost every aspect of the old game while not ruining the game play that everyone fell in love with from the original. I really do love this game but it is not ready for prime time. I still recommend this game because it is going to be great but late game is broken and glitchy. It feels far more like an early access game than a fully baked ready for public retail. It isn't very well balanced and the game starts to fall apart at the seems when there is too much going on in the shelter. That said, they are fixing a lot of the problems and are being very proactive with the community. They know they have some issues right now but they are also fixing them and I have no doubt this will be a great game in a few months.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: For now, I cannot recommend this game. It has a lot of good potential, for example the design overhauls from the first game are cool and you can see there's a lot of love poured into the game. But for me the biggest turn off for me is the fact that the faction system is very disconnected. Every faction generally starts out neutral with you, so you work with them, no big deal. But if you run into any of their patrols? You can't just simply say 'Hey, what's up' and part ways. Your only option is to either fight them, hope you can flee, otherwise they'll fight you. It really makes no sense and I've had to reload way too many times over this incredibly rigid and inflexible system and it really ruins a lot of the fun of the game for me. So for the time being, I cannot recommend this game until further patching addresses this issue.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is excellent, I love almost everything about it. But there is a bunch of stuff that makes the game unplayable. It's full of annoying bugs, some of them freezes the game, and you can't even exit it. Something that happens regulary is that the floating info screens you get when you point at some equipment lock on the screen, and don't go away easily.It's easy to survive, but the biggest problem is that your folks living in the shelter can't do anything by themself. It's a lot of micromanaging, and for some reason stuff breaks almost in a day, so you have to be able to fix thing quickly before they brake up. It does not make any sense. _childDocuments_.review: A game which the developers toke a big risk and lost.I loved the sheltered 1, but this one it toke the family out so you really don't care about who dies and doesn't. _childDocuments_.review: I love Sheltered. I've played it within the last month. They've done a great job building out the world in Sheltered 2. It almost feels more like a remake than a sequel. It's not ready though. There are still some balancing issues. Intruders will come into your shelter and one shot you. You're now limited to just two levels, which isn't enough room to built everything you need. There's no character wheel, so to select a character, you have to click on them in the shelter. If they're moving, it's twice the fun. It costs the same amount of resources to repair and item as it does to create it whole cloth. I've somehow unlocked Tier 4 of my workbench without unlocking Tier 3. I owned several outposts and regions at the start of the game. Not sure how it happened, not complaining about it either, just worth mentioning. My leader character is suffering physical ailments that  lower some of his stats, but not the cap, so I just have him raising those stats again. I didn't write down these issues, this is just what I can think of off the top of my head. Despite this, I'm addicted. The first game I started (before later patches) was a punishing experience. It took an in-game week of no rain, for me to realize there was a problem. On the day the weather vane told me it was gonna rain, it didn't. I was like, "Oh, this is a bug." It's definitely not done, but it is worth every penny. It's a discount at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Idk what the problems are of some players. Tutorial is small but explains all basics. HuD is good enough to help you without give you too much useless details. Stile and sound give you the fealing of post-apo scenario.There are just some small things that need improvement (besides bugs) but maybe I'm not far enough: maybe more wood out from recycling or lower weight + higher amount when looting. Wood should provide more heat when burnt.In general loot of equipment need much more quality. The amount of repairing is too much (in life time, ressources and man power). You will need more man in your bunker or its impossible to repair everything besides cleaing, cooking and building. More man means a higher need of food and water. Why a lvl 2 meal with the ingredians: meat + broccoli + potato gives you less value then roasted meat + broccoli soup + baked potato? I understand that the sim get a better fealing effect but I expectet in addition more value from a lvl 2 meal.All in all its a great game and I hope updates will come soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT Sheltered 1!  While there are a lot of similarities, the gameplay, goals, and challenges are significantly different.Although the first one was charming in it's own way, this one feels more gritty and tense.  It's not as forgiving as the first one, and you really have to think ahead and make some tough decisions.There are some minor bugs (the biggest one is losing materials when queuing a lot of meals to cook followed by a lot of workbench items--the items are never made, but the materials are lost forever).Still, on balance, it's a fun game, but you gotta spend the time to become familiar with the mechanics and the logic--you will be very frustrated if you go into it thinking it's just a slick repackage of the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a fun game (just like it's predecessor) but it is currently riddled with a lot of very annoying bugs. Some of these bugs are so dire that the actual progression is affected. I'm surprised that the game was released with such obvious problems.As an example: in a fight I wanted to switch my pretty badly wounded leader into the backrow but the game decided to move the only remaining enemy into that spot instead. The guy then decided to stab my leader and the game ended. Another example: I also had a guy who could not access the medicine cabinet due to a movement logic error and as expected he bled out. Reanimation only has a 50 % chance of working (without a specific trait) and he promptly died. Really weird bugs like that happen all the time. You will already stumble upon them in the character creation window with traits and stats points all mixed up when reloading your last selection.That is the reason why I suggest buying the game at a later time or at least playing it at a later time when all the really annoying things have been fixed. _childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of promise and fun in discovery and fine-tuning. But it feels unpolished. _childDocuments_.review: It's tough, but the apocalypse should be tough. Could it be balanced to be a little easier? Probably ... especially when it comes to water. Strategizing the early game to focus on gathering as much water as possible would likely alleviate a lot of the water shortages later, but it would likely add to the grind and alleviate some of the fun of playing other parts of the game early on. Some balance adjustments in this department would not upset me at all, but it's workable as is.The game is a lot of fun and very immersive as you become attached to the game characters as the game goes on. If you could edit the names of the random people who show up, once you take them in, it could add even more to the game. My first play through I wasn't even aware that you could level up the characters, which was a treat to discover in my 2nd run. This added a lot more to the game and I was already really enjoying it.There are a lot of little unexpected twist in the game, which adds a lot to it. Watching one of my guys go crazy and start lighting things on fire was hilarious and upsetting at the same time. Then when one of the ladies was tired and just squatted to take a leak on the floor I busted up and had to screenshot it for my friends who live in California (they're used to that kind of stuff, so I had to rub it in and tell them she must be from CA).I've played a little over 25 hours and feel like I've barely scratched the surface on Sheltered 2 and that's a good thing. I've yet to encounter a lot of what the game has to offer and it's obviously going to take me a lot longer to even reach some of the abilities I've become aware exist in the game, like driving trucks. I found one on a long journey, but didn't have the ability to bring it back with me at the time. So I have something to look forward to when I go back.If you enjoy survival games like Project Zomboid, then this is right up your alley but instead of zombies you have to deal with things like pissed off cartel members or crazy church groups. If you like games that are challenging, require planning and managing resources, get Sheltered 2, you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: How is it possible that in 18 hours playing this I managed to see SOOOO many bugs related to factions, I released a hostage, and never got a menu to call the faction to tell them that, there is no way to ally with a faction.Thanks for the game, but I will stop playing it until we get a major update on these bugs, I like this game, it is fun and addictive, but the last bug made me alt+f4 without saving, it is frustrating to level up to complete a quest that does not have the UI needed to complete the quest.I blame marketing and the stupid deadlines the devs must have had.Revised review on my other 17 hours. I completed the quest where I had to return the wife to a dude, no reward at all, just a pat in the shoulder and "good work" I feel at work, maybe it is me that I am expecting rewards on a game when I do a task and not doing it because "it feels good"Update 1.0.10 When you add a blueprint and then cancel it, it won't let you add blueprints anymore, another game disrupting bug.Update 1.0.10, Sometimes when you deconstruct a tier 2 bed, it won't allow you anymore to place items in that "ghost area"Update 1.2.11, To make things fair, finally you guys got it together! thanks, so, in conclusion, release after is finished is a good practice, I haven't found a bug in this gameplay, probably the memory leak you got on the audio while playing for long hours, but that gets fixed once you restart, so it is not game breaking. _childDocuments_.review: This game is micromanagement deluxe (and not the fun type). My colonists  seem to love their corner. They always, gather in the corner of the shelter and just stand there for no reason, everyone of them. Also everything break down almost every day in the shelter, beds, windturbins, showers, yes everything, so i need to repair everything constanly, in the begining that ok when i only have like 8 things that need reparing but later stages its just A LOT of unnecessarily micromanagement. If my colonist when they are idle (which they almost always is) could help repair the base, like maybe in rimworld without me clicking and telling them to do so. _childDocuments_.review: I loved Sheltered 1 and have been waiting for the 2nd one for a while.  Glad it finally released! Overall, I am really enjoying this and I look forward to more content updates from the devs to enrich the gameplay options.Well done Unicube & Team17!

_childDocuments_.review:
It's been twenty years since the world as we knew it ended. The last of humanity splintered into opposing factions. Will you unite or conquer?

Building upon the original 2015 fan-favourite, Sheltered 2 brings new challenges and deeper strategic gameplay. You are tasked with creating a leader and building up your faction whilst managing resources and tackling threats both natural and human. Everything from starvation and dehydration to radiation poisoning and enemy raids can prove fatal.

Sheltered 2's new Factions system is pivotal to a base's success. Send out expeditions to explore the vast wasteland and forge relationships, or bitter rivalries with other camps. Trade resources to grow and thrive together; or go head-to-head with rivals in an expanded combat system and grow your foothold in the wasteland. Will you ally with or dominate the other factions?

name: PowerWash Simulator
detailed_description: Halloween Seasonal 2024 Something filthy this way comes in PowerWash Simulator’s latest Seasonal Special. You’ll have to hose off more than a few cobwebs to take the Halloween House from mortifyingly mucky to party-ready perfection. PowerWash Simulator – Shrek Special Pack Playtime is ogre. Get to work cleaning up five fairy tale maps inspired by DreamWorks Animation’s Shrek. It’ll take more than pixie dust to restore these iconic locales to their former lustre, but thankfully, happily ever after is in your hands! PowerWash Simulator – Muckingham Files – Part 4 Part four of the Muckingham Files series brings you two new Bonus Jobs from friends in high places. Clean up local crypto enthusiast, Devon King’s vandalised modern mansion and pilot Floraine Perez’ fire plane following a flight over Mount Rushless. PowerWash Simulator – Cruise Ship Sun Deck – Summer 2024 Cool off with sudsy, high-pressured water this summer in PowerWash Simulator’s latest Seasonal Special. Take a vacation from Muckingham’s mainland to clean up the sun deck of Crab Bay’s cruise liner following a rather messy departure. Once you’re done, it should be smooth, sanitary sailing from there on out! Ticked off tourists, fried foods and greedy gulls do not make for most folks’ idea of a dream holiday - but you are not most folks. If the destination is dirty, you’re on board! With the sun on your back and cool mist on your visor, cleaning up feels like a breeze. Say “bon voyage” to dirt as you slough off the remnants of an avian air assault, revealing the vivid sun deck beneath. Ahhh, so satisfying. Whether you take on the task as a solo traveller or bring all hands on deck in co-op, you’ll be sure to feel the winter blues defrost in this summer muckbuster! You’ll also receive all-new summer threads to have you looking and feeling cool. Well, as cool as you physically can in a rubber suit. It is your singular honour to perform the ultimate purification protocol. Command potent power washing technology to restore a range of Imperial machines, ready to serve the Emperor once more. Crank that water pressure to 88 miles per hour and travel back in time to hose down iconic movie sets from the Back to the Future trilogy in five new maps for PowerWash Simulator! PowerWash Simulator - Tomb Raider Content Pack Grapple with grime in your ultimate quest to defeat all dirt covering Croft Manor and its grounds, along with Lara’s trusty vehicles. In this adventurous collaboration with Tomb Raider, wash and explore five new levels for PowerWash Simulator. About the Game Wash away your worries with the soothing sounds of high-pressure water. Fire up your power washer and blast away every speck of dirt and grime you can find. Build your own power-washing business and unlock new tools, upgrades and more – all with the simple satisfaction of power-washing to a sparkling finish.  Relax, unwind in single player, or play with friends in Online Co-Op; either way, have good, clean fun. name: Townscaper
detailed_description: Build quaint island towns with curvy streets, small hamlets, soaring cathedrals, canal networks, or sky cities on stilts. Build the town your dreams, block by block. No goal. No real gameplay. Just plenty of building and plenty of beauty. That's it. Townscaper is an experimental passion project. More of a toy than a game. Pick colors from the palette, plop down colored blocks of houses on the irregular grid, and watch Townscaper's underlying algorithm automatically turn those blocks into cute little houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and lush backyards, depending on their configuration.

short_description: Instant town building toy

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing town assembly toy. The build options are limited to colors, all other variation is determined by placement (grid shape and nearby buildings). Simple controls get out of the user's way, and the visual & aural effects are satisfying to experience. It is easy to spend more time in a play session than planned, so set a timer to let you know when to quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I want to begin this review by urging you to look up the painter Carl Larsson. The bright aquarelle colours of Townscaper must have been inspired by his paintings (especially since the creator is Swedish), and it works almost too well.I'm absolutely positive about this game - that, is if you can call it a game. Because it's more of a zen creative experience without any real end goal. It's more of an interactive art installation which allows you to create the sculpture. Just build whatever you fancy, play around, change colours, enjoy yourself while listening to music or a podcast, and then share the result with others if you feel like it. It's not for everyone, but if you don't enjoy it, then that should be quite clear even before you decide to pay for the product.It's bare boned, of course. It's Early Access after all, and it's cheap. I get the feeling that it's more of an interactive art experience, created to allow the player to not only be creative, but to experience imagination. It might sound vague, but I feel the game really does that for me.If you want to play something that allows you to create an imaginary town, coloured by Carl Larsson, and described by Charles Dickens, then this game is for you. It's given me a few hours of zen enjoyment already (and I'm not done yet), and given some time to be developed further, I'm sure it will be able to keep my interest also in the future whenever I have some time over in which I just want some kind of meditative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned this game for a few years now and it's always chill and relaxing. I use it for ideas when designing cities for TTRPG's or just looking to pass the time. While sometimes I do wish I could see little people populating my towns, it's a perfect companion for anyone working from home or just looking for a game that doesn't demand anyrhing from you yet allows you to be creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Way too overpriced for what it is. Now that the developer promised no additional content will be added and is focusing on ports to other consoles (abandoning it while not doing any actual "early access" updates beyond a customizable sun angle), hopefully the game will drop to lower discounts (I personally wouldn't get it under 50% off, had I the choice) and it'll then be a decent buy
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I like the whole concept of this game, but I wish the developer would add people and pets like cats sitting on the roof or dogs being walked by people. Another feature that is badly needed is hedges and benches and/ or fountains as you upgrade the environment. Also beach terrain to make a larger beach area. Boats would also look aesthetically pleasing, they don't need to do anything, it could just be stationary. There's ways around saving memory and engine lag from games. I hope the developer doesn't half-ass this game and leave it as is. This has a lot of potentials. Signs on buildings would help to distinguish stores from houses.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've just played for 2 hours but omg. The precious time is worth it. I've already built a big city and now I miss my Lego kind of childhood. Would be nice to have some people around though (it feels a bit lonely), also fountains. Not sure how that would fit in here, but it would be a very nice addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I never imagined that it could be so relaxing designing a town somewhere in the ocean.The game is nice, I wish I could also design more than streets. That you just could expand the little patches of sand you have at the edge.In general it would be nice to have more options to build with but I still like the way how the game is now.Love it hope the game gets more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really calm, relaxing and has a great and cute art style. With each new update it feels better if only for a bit. It really is a passion project because you can see the love put into it and it´s hard to believe only one person made it. The only con would be if you are a person who can´t live without symmetry because this game embraces randomness and asymmetry. It´s better not to plan and just "let the brush flow". Also, there is no endgame. The only endgame is to make something you think looks nice and maybe share the screenshots with people.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Really chill building. The graphics are really pretty and you can make large coastal towns and structures. It'd be lovely to see the game expand and include things like docks and terrain. I would definitely buy a DLC pack of such features since I know it'd be a lot of work to program and animate. Either way so far love the game, thank you!side note: The "bloop" sound when you make things is really pleasing XD haha
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and quick game to pick up and put your creative thoughts down. It is a little tricky to pick up how to move the camera at first, and it does take a little getting used to, but it's really easy to get lots of different angles to view your creation.I do wish there were buttons you could select so you could add staircases where ever you want, rather then needing them to be between buildings, but it's super quick to learn how they work. The little popping noises also make me laugh and makes the game feel very light-hearted.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily sink hours into this game! I only hope they add more features as it goes on, but I still have a lot of fun playing it. You can make cute little homely towns or massive cities. Sometimes the loading could be a bit smoother, especially if you want to do a really big town. I love it a lot over all though.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Nookrium made a video about it, otherwise I wouldn't have heard about this little gem.Was feeling rather sad and needed something simple. Something to ease my mind and relax a bit.Bought it because of the price and didn't regret at all!I love the artstyle and how the buldings generate. Camera controls are different than I'm used to but after a couple of minutes I already forgot about it and gotten used to.Works like a charm despite being Early Access.Thanks for making this dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: An addictive little tool that has a lot of potential use for setting design. Slightly limited in certain terrain options and the grid layout, but overall a delight to work/play with. Infinite possibility and new features to be discovered with each little tweak made to a building, and almost complete creative freedom (that still adheres to the laws of physics!) I also really appreciate that it autosaves as I am awful with remembering to save projects - the fact it has them saved as images rather than filenames is very helpful too, me being someone who tends to name all my files "AAAAA1" or "shsndjfkdj" or the like.Going onwards, I'd love to see a couple of things; ability to lock certain features in - if you want a stairway to remain in place once you place other blocks around it, you should be able to 'lock' that particular block - as well as the option for a more linear, square grid instead of the curved one, for people who want a more symmetrical build, or one that is predictable in how the blocks will fall. The ability to place sand and create beaches would also be great, and someone else mentioned the idea of villagers walking around the town, which would be adorable. I bought this yesterday at the time of writing and I already adore it, and I can't wait to see where the development goes!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and unique town builder! As an artist who draws backgrounds and as someone who plays DND, this simple game could open up a bunch of possible waves of creativity. From making maps to making a reference for buildings to doodle a picture inspired by it, i think something like this could be awesome once fully fleshed out. I also love how snappy things are too, like the auto fill of grassy areas and building extensions. It's definitely a fun and relaxing time.The controls were a little hard to get use to at first, but i definitely got use to them once i learned them. I would definitely recommend at least a tab that shows basic controls in the main menu, just in case for any really new players.Another thing that i would love is the ability to add more natural land. Like making the beach extend out a little further or the ability to add grass or natural trees in town. The possibilities are endless for additions to this neat little game! ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, serene timewaster. It is utterly impossible to create anything ugly or disharmonic.Now, developers, not all of us use gamepad. So, if I have for example, a rudder control attached for my flightsim, it is calibrated completely different than a gamepad, resulting in no control over spinning etc with my mouse, forcing me to find and disconnect it if I want to have a few minutes of Townscaper. Could you please consider a enable/disable switch when configuring gamepad?
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those rare games i had to buy within literally seconds after finding out about it. It wasn't a hard decision since it's really cheap. And for the price you get most relaxing playing experience & beautiful visual style. By the words of its creator it's not even a game, just a tech demo, well i wish there were more demos like this. There are really no reasons this game shouldn't be in your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: great town builder with an amazing amount of free play and creativity to unlock. it feels like finding a secret within the game whenever i place a building in a certain spot and magical balconies or fences and hedges appear. you must allow the game to play WITH you and your island, as we can't fully control the wonder
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game Is great. It is a small game about building cities in an Infinite (at least I haven't yet found a limit) 3D space on an asymmetrical grid, at the time of writing this the only real options are where you wish to place a building tile and what color the tile is to be. There are no other options at the moment but that being said this game has tremendous potential to be even better!With in the first five minutes of playing this game I found myself super relaxed yet focused, Playing a game yet working to build something cool. It was then I realized something, I got up went and got a snack as well as a drink then put of some chill music and it got even better. You wont notice the time fly when playing this game and it brought a similar feeling of peace and contentment that playing minecraft or slime rancher brings and is a great game to wind down after a long day. Despite first thinking about how I could use this to build visual representations of towns for my DnD games with my friends I now have a fuller respect for this passion project created by the dev solely because he felt that it was something he wanted to do, Just for fun you know? I think we can all agree that games made with the sentiment tend to be a bit more fun and have a lot more heart.So do I recommend this not yet finished and cheap game? Absolutely! though do keep in mind in its current state it may not be for everyone and it is my hope that going forward we can watch this game grow into something truly awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is one of those rare games that is a new genre. It's not really a game it's a toy you play with to create "cute" little (or not so little if you have the time) towns. It reminds me of the old "Kai's Power Goo" and "Bryce" unique toys to let you play with photos and create fractal landscapes. (google them) Apparently based on a procedural process you simply click way on the base of water and fun little structures magically appear, each click rewarded by accompanying cute sounds. The power of Townscaper is that is has a set of internal rules (some type of shape grammar like system) that understands the context of neighboring structures and builds meaningful structures. A single little island turns into a house of a church or all types of interesting structures. You can share your creations by saving the process as a little (unreadable) text file that other can import via the clipboard. (Would be nice to import via files) This is clearly a labor of love by creator Oskar Stålberg @OskSta a freaking game wizard. Just go buy this thing it's crazy inexpensive also!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game it is really good. I enjoy the flexibility to place where you want to place. I feel the colours really help give a little bit more life. I use the colours for separating different districts. I can't wait to see where this goes, and I would like to see more things added. Yes there are games where you can build your own cities, but they always come with managing and not failing. This is completely sandbox, there is no complicated systems to worry about. I think it is really good to just build and express your own creative freedom.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest i mostly play this game whilst doing something else to keep myself from fidgeting. It is really pretty and easy to play with but don’t go in to it expecting to build something symmetric.  Getting things to look good is quite easy and the game works well in that case. But getting something to look great is a whole lot harder I have found. But imo that is part of its charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: - Perfect when you need to relax,- aesthetically pleasing,- no matter what you do, it will look good.- For this price is a must.Changed my review to not recommended:- I think more mechanics should be added, like population walking through the streets, balconies maybe some other structures... It still has a lot of more potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I have been playing for a while and I am happy about how I found this! I thought it would be bad with such a simple premis but it wasn't it was very very fun! Also if the creator sees this add your other project to the game (you know, World Scaper) as a mode/seperate game and if it is a seperate game you should give free access to people with this game already.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It's low-stress, a little mindless and a lot of fun.I would like the devs to add the following content:Roads that don't gate or fence themselvesThe ability to create the beaches and stairs myselfMore colour palettes, the one it comes with is fun but it needs more optionsGarden and fountain features that I can add myselfMore roofing options that aren't created automatically; I'd like to add some different roofs myself.Otherwise, this is very fun and very relaxing. Building the world is a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game. Sandbox? Zen garden?First enjoy effortlessly create aesthetic small villages.Then enjoy the process of understanding, little by little, how the different interactions programmatically generate some elements (e.g. stairs, small flags, gardens) and awe in wonder when you accidentally discover something new.Then start being ambitious and start building bigger, more complex cities. Colorful towns. Impossible, intricate, architectures.Or just use it as you zen garden, placing blocks one by one, enjoying the really polished experience of building your little world.There is no right way to "play" this game, as long as you have fun all of them are right and I greatly recommend trying it and find your own unique way of enjoying this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Totally addicitve game, even when I'm away from the game I see these cute little houses in my minds eye and come up with new ideas for my buildings. I love how it is relaxing and therapeutic and how you can create both little islands and big towns as well as castles. There's even a Schwyzerdütsch translation for the UI!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Barely started this game but I feel a strong need to review it. Ever since I was young, I've been obsessed with old, precarious construction that is built in a way that appears so unstable yet has somehow lasted decades. I don't know why, I just love that kind of thing. It's weirdly comforting and and warm to see something that seems like such a mess,  like it would never be built today, and is still standing. Rusty and paint-chipped, maybe (which makes it even better in my opinion!) but still standing. Anyways, this game lets me make weird, archaic towns and I adore it. I already teared up playing it. It's just really really my thing.EDIT: There was originally a whole section of this review where I talked about having an issue with my colorblindness in this game and how it could be fixed by adding a color dropper feature to the game, but I was messing around in the game and just discovered that there actually is a color dropper that you just use by holding down left click on a building of the color you want! I officially have no complaints with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: First, I wouldn't call this a game as there is no goal aside from your own artistic expressions. Second, the zen-like, catharsis one gets from this type of experience is worth more than the admission price alone. In a perfect world, this would have swappable themes like Fantasy buildings, Sci-Fi, Punks, both Cyber and Steam. I mean the list is endless obviously. Id also allows for a little more refinement in the camera movement, it can get a bit cumbersome with larger cities. All in all, this was an easy recommendation because at this price you are basically guaranteed satisfaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper delivers exactly what the title promises.  This game is just a chill model town builder, nothing more nothing less. 15 minutes in and I already want more! Theres no instructions, just do. The controls are intuitive enough to figure out, at least with a mouse. I think what gives it personality is the little touches like environments popping in and leaving little bits of rubble that scatter around or fall in the water.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredible, it's so simple, yet, so good. It could have some other living creatures, like fish and other types of birds. If someday add little people walking freely around the city, maybe add boats that arrive on the city. They even don't need to interact with each other, but it would be fun to see they walking and entering and laving the building.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's like painting with small block houses. No ppl to feed, no economy to worry about.U don't have full control of how things join up but it adds to the simplicity. I believe its a fully released game and dev seems moved on to other things so not expecting huge updates but u never know, some active ppl creating cool mods tho.Very zen like, great if u have trouble sleeping v relaxing before bed.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Hey everybody! I wanted to play this game for some time and I finally did! ^^ The game is unique and amazing for me. building things..remove some. and transforms into something else... Day or night time to take screenshots. it was fun. Recommended for all ages for sure :DI will add Townscaper screenhots soon on my website - Roxanna Stefaniuc Fabiola AKA Pictures With Vulpoaica
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with some interesting building mechanics. It's like playing with wooden blocks that are constantly adjusting shape to match their surroundings. Vast variety of possible combinations may keep your interest for a long time. Also, it's quite easy to play for children without a help of adults.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The dev recently posted a message abbout his game and how he will be take'n this time to spend more time with his daughter, this is both my reply too his message and my heart felt recamendation for this game.I did not buy this game, i had it wish listed but never got around too it, yesterday a good friend bought it for me, he saw it on my list and gave it a try, he then sent me it, i love this game so much, and have reposted about it on two diffrent discords suggesting it as a great buy both for people need'n a simple relax'n way to let trubbles slip away or a stress releaver, my friend now plays it everyday before he goes off to work, he is a county sherrif so you know his days are stressfull, we love your game and thank you so much for it, and i know all too well how important dad is too a lil girl, i my self am a papa's little girl, i love my father so much so please, while you can, hold her, hug her, kiss that little princess, she will allways remeber it and hold it in her heart dad, Thank you, i love you as well for this. :Speech_Love: :ManaRegenerationYing:
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The store is upfront about not really being a city builder... or even a game. However, my problem is the grid is awful. All the tiles are irregularly shaped and don't use consistent angles at any point. If you want to build anything with symmetry, you're screwed. That alone is a deal-breaker for me. If there was an option to use it's 'free-form grid' or squares or hexagons or octagons and triangles then this would be a good timekill, but the only option is my least favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: i think this is perfect to play when i'm starting to get slightly overwhelmed because i can have a mindful moment but it's still mildly stimulating in that i need to decide where to put things architecturally to suit the surroundings and appear interesting. i think this is a great game for some neurodiverse people to consider if they like the look of the graphics and find committing to meditation really difficult as the brain may need a little something to focus on.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little toy (not a game, per se) with a good amount of enjoyment to be had from it. Graphically, it is simple but nice. Audio is adequate. There are lots of nice little touches to it.The only problem is that apart from a few birds, the towns you build feel empty. That's because they are, but still. What would REALLY make this shine would be townsfolk wandering around your construction, and the ambient sounds that went with them.  The ability to build on a field instead of just water would also help add to the longevity, I think.Either way, for the price, it's a nice little toy as it stands.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing for when Im anxious at night and cant sleep. No real purpose no goals, no time limits. Just a bunch of fun colorful buildings. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: In its current version, Townscaper is just beatiful.As the dev puts it, it's not a game. It's a toy. Wanna play it with a friend or family on the side? Why not? Wanna set challenges for yourself? You can do that too.Again, it's a toy. You invent your own fun. I made one "world" with it and I already felt it was worth the purchase half-way. If it looks interesting, I'd say go ahead and get it. This is not a game that you calculate bang for buck, just enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Slip away into a gentle fantasy world where tall towers rise above calm waters, birds perch on tile roofs above the twisty walkways and avenues below. It's a tool for the imagination, a device for storytelling, a place to dream in. Take a screenshot and picture the dragons flying there among the floating cities.Simple, yet subtle, it works its magic as you build; the balconies sport benches and telescopes; laundry lines cross gaps with washing flapping; potted trees and buses sway in gentle breezes.Wonderful, delightful toy. I only wish it had more to it: a tool to adjust the palette; a choice to build on un-level terrain; a choice of grid styles (oh, how I long for straight lines), a zoom that extends a little further back, and a way to import alternate building styles (imagine crafting a futuristic city). Perhaps the developer will consider enhancing it. Or offer an enhanced version for sale (I'd happily buy it). But you will enjoy what it is now: a virtual playground.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: When enjoyed as intended, Townscaper is an effortless stress-reliever and an easy buy at this price point. However, it could be so much more. Many players (including myself) see the immensely useful applications Townscaper has for map creation, worldbuilding, and even role-playing. Unfortunately, the game's intentionally minimal interface only allows you to build in the confines of a mid-20th century coastal town. What if there was an option for a grass base instead of water? Or medieval buildings? Or different types of blocks that created unique features like shop signs and display windows? What if the rooftops could be weathered and old? or covered with snow? The possibilities are infinite.This game's community is bursting with ideas on how to improve and expand the game, and I dearly hope the developers don't let these ideas go unheeded, because this game is truly a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I am new to architecture games, but found this game so easy to get into. It's so relaxing, and it really lets your creativity shine. You can randomly click until you have a masterpiece, or you can try recreating a map you found online. The only thing that bothers me, is I wish there were an option to be able to make things more symmetrical. If you can get passed that though, I highly suggest spending some leisure time creating your personal fortress. Also creator, if you see this..... the ability to add beaches, docks, and boats would be amazing to add.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Want to love the game (toy, really), but we NEED a way to place and remove more than one block at a time, and there just ISN'T. Imagine a paint program where you have to click. every. pixel. one. at. a. time. Literally any single other tool (a larger brush option? click and drag? line tool? area fill?) would make a world of difference, but none are available. Any time I think of doing a build, the sheer volume of individual one-block-one-click stifles creativity and frustrates the experience. It's maddening how close Townscaper is to greatness, but this one thing sinks it for me. If the dev ever adds even a single simple tool to help with this, I would change to a thumbs up in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy this, the game is EXTREMELY shallow, you'll get bored within minutes of playing due to the lack of content and very small amount of things to actually well, build with. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most relaxing, but also creative games I've ever played. Everything--the controls, the HUD, camera movement--is so straightforward that it doesn't get in the way of creativity. Even a little kid could pick it up and have very little trouble with it.Also--and this really goes without saying--it is one of the most aesthetically pleasing games I've played. You can make some pretty complex, beautiful structures with just a dozen clicks here and there, instead of having to rummage through a huge library of assets to find the right wall-piece to use for a house. It's like the game works with you to make exactly what you're imagining. It does take a tiny bit of experimentation, but that's part of what's fun about it. I was trying to figure out how to make stairs up to a higher level of my city, and a few clicks later the game was like "here's some stairs."I'd recommend this to anyone who likes creative games and/or slow-paced relaxing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for about 4 hours total (had it running in the background) and I would absolutely recommend this game/simulator/sandbox to people who just love to build it is very good at letting my creativity flow. I would love if there was different world to choose from like right now its just an ocean you build on but maybe there could be a land option. I love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: im really loving this game, the graphics are awesome. i just hope they add some people walking around or being able to walk through your cities. also some more saving features would be cool. simple gameplay and relaxing, im always trying to get the wash lines up but its not easy.lolfor this price i have no regrets at all!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is quite possibly the perfect game to relax. It is certainly more a toy than a game; there's no goal, no levels, just you building your ideal floating city in the middle of an ocean sunset. It feels more involving than other "toy" entries, likely because the level of customization is high enough to be engaging but not high enough to stress you out over little choices. Plus you can export the perfect photo of your island hamlet so it feels like you're working towards something. If I only had 2 minutes to play something but needed to chill, this is what I'd go to.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a chill indie sandbox game centered around building unique cities and towns by simply pointing and clicking. There are no goals or objectives for this game. While building stuff there are multiple special interactions that you figure out as you click and build, such as stacking and removing buildings to create different appearances and how to build grassy areas, paths, and stairs. You start off on a large open hexagon layout and just start building and connecting land together. There are not very many settings in the game, but you can change the colors of buildings with a color palette, save your creations, and change the lighting. I don't have a tablet, but this would be great on one. It's very easy to pick up and put down and has great replayability because you can create new townscapes endlessly. I bought this game in early access and wished there had been more content updates since I got it since the game had great potential. But if you enjoy creative, relaxing sandbox games like this, for $6 it's still worth checking out. Overall, recommended ★
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: really fun and relaxing casual game. it almost feels like you are doodling. really like the game and hope to see it get more cool features to further expand the creativity. things i would like to see are roads, better elevations, different building types, parks, bridges and so on. it would also be cool if there was people walking around the town to make the town feel more alive. i don't really know how much stuff can be added to the game since it can be laggy if you build a large city, but as the game is in early access, some minor bugs are expected. anyhow, it is a cute little game that is really fun and easy to get hooked ontldr: yes, i would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I wouldn't say this game is bad. It's a genuine fun simple little town building game. But, as many others have said, there's some big problems. I understand that it's in early access, but I think it's too early. There's not much to do besides choose which colors you want your architecture to be, then click around on a grid (which is also randomly generated, meaning you could end up with a shape you don't want in that place) and build towers. And this wouldn't be too bad, but for the amount it costs, at this early in development, I think it would be best to either lower the price quite a lot, or work on adding more features. This game might be for you if you like a simple architectural building simulator, but for me, I'd like something with more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I love this little art tool, even if I feel like most of the actual artistry comes from the developer and I am merely implementing his fantastic aesthetic vision :)Since it's early access, a suggestion: this game is obviously not ever going to be a city building sim, but I'd enjoy a "challenge" mode which would place some constraints on me as a player, or give me some goals. Like a requirement to use X blocks of each color, for instance, or a requirement as to how many blocks I can have at each level of the building (like 25  ground level, 20 one story up, 15 two stories up etc, or the reverse!) Or (not sure how possible this would be to implement) a requirement that all the ground level paths be connected... or a requirement that buildings be connected above ground. Just some prompts or pushes to make me solve problems and try designs that might not otherwise occur to me. I guess such things could come from the community, but it would be easier to track if the game either enforced the constraints or at least displayed some stats :)Kind of on the opposite end of feature ideas -- I also think it would be fun to add a random generator with some parameters the user could set, like maximum horizontal and vertical sizes and colors to use, so we could watch the game "play itself" :)

_childDocuments_.review: An architectural delight. Shine in its simplicity and lets you bring out creativity in an atmospheric moment. With additional tiles like greenery or simply having the option to create road the joints could be blown right open. Controls are intuitive and precise it's really as simple as launching the game and letting your creativity take the wheel. Add some of your personal background music or some lofi beats and you won't see the hours go by.I caught myself goofing off by building one of the tallest tower I could imagine as a joke but then I started tweaking tiles a bit and it really turned into an aesthetically pleasing-looking building.Easy to grasp, hard to master.
