_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up on a whim just to snag a 5 dollar discount during the Steam summer sale. Honestly, didn't expect that much out of it, developer said he wanted to see how people use it and I've always been a sucker for city planning and logistics. Now I need to clarify right now if you're looking for logistics in the same vein as City Skylines, that is not what you're getting out of this game. What you are getting is as much of a game as say wooden toy trains. It's not a game as of writing this review, it is a cute fun tool. You start with nothing but water. You click the left mouse button and boom. A little island on the grid you selected. Click on top of that island and a little structure pops up. As you continue building, you can delete certain blocks and stairways and arches will form. If you build high up and add more blocks on the side of a building, steel support beams will reach down to provide integrity. And that's really all there is to the toy. What's great about this is that it honestly allows you to plan our things like rpg cities and fully realize various structures like cathedrals, castles, lighthouses, and even canals. You don't see people moving around or anything, but you might see a bird perch on a roof. The architecture in of itself reminds me of something I'd see out of a Ghibli movie, and that alone makes it quite charming.For a few bucks, this tool is a great thing if you just want to unwind and create little towns with cute architecture. I can't wait to see what else is in store for this great little toy.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps the most helpful gimmick that this game has up it's sleeve is that the "grid" isn't fully square or rectangular; it's procedural. Some spots will truncate inwards creating a three sided building while others splay out with five or six points, making it  difficult to build a Manhattan-style grid-city. It subtly nudges the player to get more creative without them realizing it and that is revolutionary for this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a game developed and published by Oskar StålbergAll I have to say is... I love this game! _childDocuments_.review: This game is addicting. I've played for almost 3 and a half hours, and I'm in love with it. It lets you create without having to perform using very simple tools. Honestly, anyone could play it. It is what you make it. I'm sure you could build impressive fortresses or whatever, but you could also just click randomly until you get something you feel somewhat drawn to. I think the trailer shows the gameplay very well. Only that it's a bit sped up.I'm an architect student, and going in to this I think I expected more stylistic options. But honestly, I'm happy there isn't. The creator is Swedish, and so am I, and I feel really quite at home with this old European-esque architecture. And I'm happy the game stops me from choosing too much - I wouldn't get anything done. Now I just choose a colour and *click* - it's a house!Something I'd like to see added - since it's still in Early Access - is if there would be a bit more life and movement in the towns you create. Perhaps people moving in to the houses and walking around the streets. And that you could hold and drag left-click to create a row of buildings. But those are just small things I thought about, overall I'm very happy I bought this.In summary - a mesmerizing game, allowing you to easily and forgivingly create your own towns in a European character. I can't do anything else than recommend it. To the creator - riktigt bra jobbat!

_childDocuments_.review: I personally am not a huge fan of games that well... don't really have much to offer in terms of Story or Combat, Characters, etc. I can tell you, that this is more of a "Tool" than a game. I would highly recommend this game if there was some extra goodies in the works. Day night cycles, Humans, Populous, to make it seem alive, more so than a base tool to help other developers create concept buildings for their games, you know what I mean?It's relaxing and fun, but at the same time in this current state is a shell.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun & chill game to play around in. I've been having a great time experimenting with different building possibilities, & comparing with what friends come up with. If you enjoy designing things, this game could be one you'll really love. Townscaper is relaxing to play, & even better if you throw on some tunes in the background. What a great idea! I can't wait to see where the development of this game goes in the future, having said that I really like where it's at right now. : )
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing and aesthetically pleasing game that relies on you to unlock its secrets. The gameplay is smooth and enjoyable, and it's very easy to lose hours at a time creating beautiful little coastal hamlets, massive housing communities, and towers covered in balconies.The only real complaint I have is the lack of large-scale functions, like a multi-delete or height change tool. This is a very minor thing and rarely detracts from the overall experience.It'll be interesting to see where this game goes next, especially if we could get some options for different architecture or textures. Overall, a highly enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a great wee toy, something that's great for zoning out to a podcast or music to. People get the wrong idea and seem to be some big simulation with citizens and actual 'mechanics'. It will almost certainly never be that. You make pretty little towns that are satisfying and quick to build and that's it. And that's great, but don't buy the game thinking it will turn into a complex city builder in the future, this ain't that.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is the perfect  "game" to turn to when you want to relax after a long day. I love to test different things to finally get something I like, just get started, there is no wrong way of doing  things in Townscaper. After spending hours creating a town I like, it's picture time! While making  screenshots, you really can see the little details that they put in, just wander around in your little town, you might be surprised by what you will find. ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've messed with Oskar's other projects, and this is an exciting beginning to be sure. Though this is only in Early Access, it's still a great functional tool, and I only look forward to seeing how it evolves, and becomes a better experience over time. This is a Simulation Town Builder. It has Only Water as it's base (currently), it does not require code learning, or require you to be fluent in anything other than using your mouse to click or undo.It is in Early Access, therefore things are subject to change over time.I would not recommend this for extensive maps, people who do not like town-building games, people who expect lots of options early on. --Over all, supporting this artist in the early-time is what will make it better in the later-release. I am excited to see how it evolves, and hope it gets better, and better :)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice little project, which leads to many nice inspirations for other city building simulators. The graphics are stylish and very pretty and everything plays very dynamically.I would still like to be able to change the camera with the keyboard. Also, it is not always clearly predictable how the surrounding houses and roofs will change when you build new houses.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The art style, the sounds, the birds flying from building to building. its just such a relaxing experience. There are no goals, no achievements, no pathway, nothing to unlock, but that only adds to the game. This is the game you would play after a long day at work and you just want to sit down and chill for a few hours. This is the type of game you could fall asleep playing. This game has a dedicated community on the steam community hub and on reddit (r/townscaper), looking through either of those places you can find tons of people who have made amazing things in the game. I love this game and its community. I have spent hours playing it and could easily spend hours more.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't work with the keyboard and mouse, there's a conflict with one of my devices, I have a steering wheel with a pedal and gearbox for car games, it must be that, but there's no way I'm going to unplug all that every time I want to play a little casual game like this.The problem dates back several years I'm not the only one to have it and obviously the developers don't care.Too bad it will be a refund for me
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A simple game, or toy, that is reminiscent of building legos, lincoln logs, or tinker toys in a way. It is a very satisfying and relaxing experience to experiment with building little towns. It is immediately gratifying, however, I did feel a sense of getting better at designing cities and interesting buildings as I played. This is a perfect game for a creative child, or the inner child of a creative adult. I can't wait for more updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It was worth all the pennies it cost me ( 6.00$ CAN ) Simple, intuitive design. Minimalist UI that lets all the space to your creativity. I'm stuck in a positive spiral where I need to recreate all sorts of things, cities, buildings, landscape I saw or remember in Townscaper.  Like many have already said, some improvements could include non AI citizens just roaming the streets, boats, fish, and the ability to get those nice stone/bricks arch even when different colours blocks are nearby. I find it relaxing, easy to grasp and easy to redo part of your creation.Try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It has a lot of potential;Like many other reviewers, I too am a DM for a Dungeon & Dragons game. This program, in my opinion, has a lot of potential to be the settlement builder we're all after. Between the simplicity of usage, as well as the flexibility of the camera angles, this game could be, well, game-breaking, if it just had a few more options. Personally, I'd like to see:- Larger grid sizes, for large cities- Terrain options, such as grass vs water map, eventual build up of mountains (such as how houses build into towers) with grass to hills, to mountains- Themes! Typical fantasy, themes inspired by cultures around the world, etc. - More customizability; perhaps the option to choose what time of day you're viewing your settlement at? Options for what misc. items pop up?- Ability to export your map when you're done?Honestly, I feel as though this program has so much potential. A few updates and QOL changes, and this could be something truly amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: After an hour of mucking around, i can think of a few things that this game could make use of.-Ability to select whether you want to build the bottom level higher or if you want to place buildings. And maybe different styles of "walkway", like say, one without handrails so you can make a harbor or something-A tool to paint over whether you want something to be pathways or rooftops, and maybe the specific rooftop you want. Also, rooftop colors.-Option to recolor a placed building (unless I missed that, in which case maybe point out where to view the controls)-Different background options/maybe the ability to make a town that looks like its on land/coastal.-Move camera rotation off of left click so we can paint houses like in the trailer-Grid that is more symmetrical, maybe multiple grids for different patterns-Boats? If I can think of any other additions I will edit my review. I think this is a great product and I could see people using this to do all sorts of things once it receives more features,
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a very good game, with a lot of potential. First of all, it is meant for free building, for those with a lot of imagination, don't expect a lot of action, just let your mind be free. You can design almost everything. The graphics aren't very demanding but they look insane. The gameplay is also very good, the game isn't buggy or too crashy. Keep in mind that the game is in Beta and updates are expected. The price is also very good ( 5$ ).My suggestions for the future updates : Make the game moddable ( Very IMPORTANT )Make a day/night cycle.Add some people or animals on the street, make a population count. That'd be more fun.Add roads, cars and more...Add natural disastersMake the game multiplayerAdd more materials, texturesAdd seasons
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little relaxing building exerciseIf you want to walk around your town in first personYou can export the OBJ of what you build, put it into blender, scale it (around 4-or-so times the exported size), then enable walk with Shift+Tilde(~) and press G to enable gravity.play around with the lights in the scene to add some mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Less a game and more of a proof of concept as of now, but the mechanics are incredibly fun, satisfying, and creatively stimulating! I personally would like to see this game's ideas expanded to incorporate other base-building elements. Maybe a terrain editing system to help you craft the land and see with-which you can then build your town? Also I would love to see more of an extrinsic motivation to keep playing. For example, implement actual villagers or some type of population system, where you can house and employ citizens to perform basic tasks, and really get your town feeling alive! All in all, its a great concept that is already very polished and satisfying right now. I look forward to seeing what the developer does with it next!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm no artist, I've dabbled in 3D and game-design, so don't be discouraged that this is a game meant for artists.This game is simple, and by far one of the easiest to understand games I've played in a very long while. It makes you feel good, *really* good, by just clicking. It's a game that lets you be creative and think, without having to stress over anything. Something doesn't end up looking right? Then delete it and try something else. It's so stimulating and satisfying for something so absurdly simple and charming and I absolutely adore it. I've been building towns, pixelart, and experimenting and pushing the procedural buildings to their limits in a game that has so much potential you can't help but be on the lookout for what's next in this gameIt may not look or seem like a $6 game, but considering that there are plans for so many new features in the future, and with the dev being so supportive of this project, it's worth every penny.Regardless, it's very relaxing nonetheless, this is one of the few games my boomer parents actually approve of and I legitimately enjoy messing around with it and seeing what I can create, seriously looking forward to what the developer has in store for the future!8/10 - A little shallow, but hoping for more depth later down the road
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. I wasn't really expecting to be so sucked into a game where there's no actual "gameplay loop" as such, but the mere act of placing buildings and creating intricate multilayered megastructures was so satisfying I managed to play for about an hour without even noticing the time go by. I could imagine lots of little stories about grand adventures that the hypothetical citizens of my city could have, and the history of the place. I hope this game has more features added in future, such as the ability to make gardens and green spaces without having them walled off by buildings, and a sort of "challenge mode" where little AI townspeople roam around as you build outwards completing various tasks, and figuring out the most efficient routes to and from places that incentivize you to plan smart would be awesome. 10/10 as a proof of concept and I hope it gets more work done on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those casual, minimalistic, "feel-good and relax" games, one which despite having rather simple gameplay mechanics manages to be quite enchanting and addictive, constantly tempting one's creativity to indulge into further experiments and creations. Despite being sand-box with no achievements or challenges per se, the satisfaction factor of one's own creation is nevertheless high, provided one is into such types of games of course. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: See this game as a meal at a restaurant or a nice treat you bought to reward yourself. It is not something you would play for hours upon hours, but the experience is soothing. I especially like the sound effects. It would be interesting to have villagers walking around and doing stuff at some point in the future. Or some function that lets you walk around yourself. But even if it is unlikely that anything like that will ever be implemented, this is still a very pleasant game :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a small fun city builder, that strips away all the confusing parts and concentrates on the fun parts of city building: the BUILDING itself. With it's intuitive controls and diverse palette of possible combinations it kept me awake far longer than I planned for multiple times. I really love this game! I hope that even though there are a lot of different building combinations, that the developer will add some m ore in the future.But as of now I can really recommend this little gem of a game! 5/7
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a well-polished, relaxing, and beautiful game. I just started playing it and it's already so addicting. I'm happily surprised at every little detail and how adding/removing sections can open up extra little features to the town's layout/buildings. I would love to see this game grow with more customization options (like more architectural styles), but so far you get so much for such a small price. Thank you for making this game, I really needed a zen game like this to unwind from a long day at work. Much love! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could think of a way to describe this that would sell it more than what you can already see. Remember the first time you discovered paint on windows as a child and became totally absorbed in making random patterns by messing with the functions just because you could? Then this is for you.If you are expecting any kind of game then look elsewhere this is purely self absorbed aesthetics. But it does it so well.And now it has positional sun locations :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this game (if you want to call it that) is still a little rough around the edges, but it has massive potential and is already as addictive as it is soothing. I was having a pretty rough day, sank a couple hours into Townscaper, and it really helped to calm my mind and bring me a little bit of peace so I could get some rest.The visuals are simplistic but elegant, like a watercolor painting. The choice to not add music was surprising but I can respect the decision and see the merit behind it. Perhaps some other sound effects; seabirds and rolling waves on the shore, maybe some rain or thunder could add to that ambiance without upsetting the mood.The controls take a hot second to figure out because there's no keyboard guide, and there's no long click to fill or drag to make building any faster, just endless clicking. There's no black or grey buildings, and different colors are different buildings, so you can't really blend them together to make that nice iconic red and white lighthouse. I haven't figured out how the zoom or paths quite work yet either. I'd love to see some different roofing and path types, maybe a few more embellishments like a docked boat, expanded shorelines, simple things like that.Overall this is a very impressive and fun little building tool and I'm excited to see how it evolves.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing to just boot up and mess about in for a few hours at a time. Let that creativity flow free and make anything from small shanty towns to a large palace looming over the township. Or flying towns, for that matter. Certainly usable to design towns for pen & paper RPGs, although a bit limited when it comes to anything more than layout.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's the most literal example you can get of a sandbox. Just build your little towns on a randomly generated grid with a handful of colors to choose from. That's it. No resources, no people, nothing to keep track of. And I  that.I can only think of like, 3 things that I'd want changed/added.1: The option for non-random/standard grids. I personally like being able to utilize symmetry, and symmetrical islands are next to impossible to find.2. Custom building palettes. Apparently folks figured out how to change colors through file editing, but it's odd that it isn't a feature.3. Different environments/cultural designs. I love the look of the buildings, but other "skins" would be nice.But as of writing this, sounds like the dev is done with this project. He made what he wanted to make. Which, hey, good for him, I guess.My one warning is that this game  isn't worth 6 dollars, even if I was happy to dish out the couple bucks for it. If you're actually looking for a game, keep looking or wait for a sale. But if you're like me and enjoy chill little time wasters, I  think you'll like Townscaper.OH and you can 3D print your towns, apparently. I think that's really neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Oskar,Thank you for that game which helps me to calm down and take my mind away. One can see you do this with heart and love to the detail, which i am missing in many "big" games.As you are still developing here a few things I would LOVE to see in the future:- Town-Skins. Meaning you could make the whole town look medieval, viking, oriental, japanese  I love ancient settings, so the binoculars (even tho they are a lovely detail) keep reminding me its not 14th century venice,   so skin choices would be the most amazing addition. I know that will require tons of work tho..- Hold ♥♥♥♥ to fill a form (for making island)- a way to chose a roof. sometimes it's really tricky to get a roof or terasse in a certain point, to have a tool to choose would be great
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a very simple city builder where you use left click to build and right click to delete. Gameplay doesn't involve any complicated gimmicks but has a few ways to create certain buildings like arches, towers, gardens. I very much so like the washing lines that can appear between buildings and for the first time in my life even the perching seagulls on the roofs. The very cute visuals and peaceful audio effects make this a very relaxing experience. I only wish the game would still be expanded upon.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple but peaceful and cute. I sunk an hour in when I needed to go to bed without even realizing. Just pick a colour, click where you want a structure, click to add to it and let the AI do the rest. Very excited to see where it goes in the future, but even the current build is absolutely worth the price
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Spent 90 minutes making a multi-tiered city complete with poor, middle class, and ruling class districts before I pushed the game too far past its limits and it stopped loading in the features correctly. Enjoyed every second of it. Can't wait to see what other features and capabilities come out once it stops being early access. Hoping to see different styles of buildings, terrain, and maybe some specialized buildings and setpieces eventually. For $6 though, it's already a lot of fun as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special, there's no objective, there's no tutorial and there's no ending.Townscaper is strange, it is so relaxing and satisfying, you build a small town from the ground up and that's it. Nothing more, nothing less. The randomised grid makes building interesting looking towns easy and it works like a charm. This game is clearly unfinished though, the lack of music makes it slightly unnerving and without any objectives at all, the game has no real replayability. The randomised grid makes it hard to recreate something from an image or imagination, and the lack of customisability on each "block" makes it so your towns end up looking very similar.If you are looking for a game to create detailed towns from referances, as of now, I cannot recommend this game. However, this game is very relaxing and is very fun to watch your towns develop, it lets your imagination flow. I have had fun with this game and I look forward to seeing what it turns into in the future. As of now, I don't think you should buy this game for its price unless you really do want to chill, but in the future, I'd say this is a great game to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw this on Imgur, and have been waiting for it to come out here on Steam. Love everything but the camera controls so far (would like to see Q and E used for camera rotation, and R and F for panning up and down) and will spend some more time with it for sure thanks to it being soooooo relaxing. Could use some music and other audio controls as well, but overall I am really, really enjoying it. It seems limiting but it's stunning what you can actually create by just clicking and seeing what happens! (And just CTRL-Z if you don't like it).
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It would be a dream to be able to visit your creations in First Person, with the flight and song of the seagulls, the sound of the waves refracting on the rocks and a storm peeking out in the distance, with the wind opening and closing the shutters, with the rhythmic gush of a fountain in the square...

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo much fun! I love the colors and the cute buildings! The UI are very simple and easy to understand. The voice effect used are also very cute and calming. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really relaxing game, and very useful for designing simple layouts for towns and buildings for my dnd campaign tbh. The uneven grid makes it look a lot more natural and interesting, although i would like an option with a simple square grid for symmetry as well. If you hate making things that are asymmetrical, don't get this, but otherwise please do. _childDocuments_.review: So, this game (if you can call it a game) is very simple and relaxing. I bought it cause of the new export as .obj function which can be improved. The textures are really poor and it would be great if there would be more options for exporting as .obj. It would be a very nice tool for making towns for animations. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing this in the hopes that it gets popular and either gets a few updates or mod support.It's a great stress reliever. The fact that you can have it on only half on the monitor means you can run it along side whatever programs you want for quick additions to your spaces.I've been consistently surprised with the way the algorithm handles certain situations, such as bridges, stairs, piers, and even propellers.Definitely worth the cost of a beer.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I love the style of the game! The animations as well as the sound design are really nice! It runs smoothly and responds well to the commands.I do wish that there was an option to create bigger chunks of ground instead of heaving to click on every piece individually and that there would be more choices for the ground and streets and the option of placing parks, bridges and stairs. It definitely has immense potential and I'm looking forward to the day of the final release.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful little, well not game, but... digital toy? Whatever you want to categorize it as, it is loads of fun. The graphics are colorful and cute. The minimalist UI is elegant, working with you, not against you when trying to get your ideas out onto the canvas. Within a few seconds of opening starting I felt as though I was transported back to when I was a kid playing with Lego, building little worlds of my very own. It's early access, but the price of admission is more than worth it. I am excited to see where the developer takes it.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely enjoy this idea so far, I've only played it for a few minutes in an attempt to kind of flesh out an idea for one of my story worlds. I would like to see just a couple extra tools (like the ability to put down an area of grass instead of just road) or even the ability to choose some different building aesthetic (just so I can better differentiate between castle and house lol). Mostly, the ability to possibly drag something over a large area. Trying to draw in a coastline click by click can be a bit tedious, and difficult for someone with the pain issues that I have. Even if none of this were added, I absolutely will continue to use this in the future and recommend it for others. It's a neat little creative tool/toy that can allow you to bring an element to your stories, campaigns and whatever else you have in mind that you wouldn't otherwise have.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why this is described as a toy, it clearly has two life-or-death struggles1) against your own tendency for excess2) you vs. the camera controlsi've been following this project on twitter for years, and it came out on a day i  needed this kind of stress relief. not since Islanders have i enjoyed clicking a city into existence. (i know this is a stretch) simple interiors for the first person mode. id love to get lost in the strange town mazes i create. townscaper doesn't look half-bad zoomed in real close! here's a pastebin with my first big 3-island town! good luck getting the camera to cooperate!

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend playing this game and I feel like I got my money worth for how inexpensive this game is, however, I do wish there was even more to this game that would get updates in the future.I haven't played a lot of this game, since I played it during troubles with my internet, but I do intend to come back to his game and chill out working on creativity practice. I still got a lot on what I want to do, even getting into modifications to the game as to make and have different textures for different looks/themes. For example, having a more winter season to the builds I make. This game is mainly just a tech demo proof of concept type work, which is pretty well implemented rather than explicitly saying "this is a tech demo" with only basic textures that has no character to it.Also, I know this game is described as a toy. But I call it a game due to what I consider, and what a lot others consider, a game is. Some people had complained to me about my choice of words when describing this game, but they don't seem to understand I consider a game as anything digital displayed on a monitor display where the user is interacting with the medium. Legit, some of you need to calm down because I decide to use a word to describe this product. Before I get into this section, I'm happy with the game and I want to see the best for what this game has to offer. This is why I have criticisms of this game, so that maybe updates can come out in the future for improving the game.What I would like to see out of this game is more updates to it. There is a lot of support for this game and I would love to see the base game get more features for it to be better fleshed out. Like I said before, this is basically a tech demo and it will still have a lot of work I personally view as unfinished for it to be considered as a fully finished game. The asking price of this game is $6, which I do think is a bit too high considering this is literally just a tech demo. I would say the better price should be $3 - $4 for what you are getting in this game. I know some may say "why would it matter if it is a couple dollars less, it's not all that expensive at $6 anyway", to which I say, you are wrong. I care about the value of the game, this being the quality and quantity of content in the game relative to the asking price. Despite the content being great quality, there truthfully isn't much for this game to ask $6 out of me. Which thankfully I got this on the Steam Summer sale for a cheaper price more close to what I would pay for this game.If there were more features to this game, of the same great quality, I can see myself paying $6 - $10 if you added some more quality content. In fact, if you fully developed this game to be larger than it is now, I can see myself paying up to $15 for this game. However, the tech demo that it is now just doesn't seem worth the asking price of $6.Let me start off saying this, if they want to live up to the $6 asking price, they should have better modification integration for this game. This game doesn't seem to get any updates, but this one is a must if you want to meet up to the asking price and then just do nothing after that. I really don't want to have to deal with 3rd parties modifying the game as to make this game have all or most of the features I'd like to have.In no particular order, here is a list of updates I'd like to seer:I think this game was worth the money I had paid for, especially since I got it on the Steam Summer Sale. It is a fun game and I see myself playing it for more hours to come. I like to use this game to use during some downtime and for when I want to relax at the end of the day. However, it isn't without criticisms and I would like to see the best for the future of this game.

All the little things you can achieve by simple experimentation, and as you understand how the various details can be achieved, you begin to shape your little world, your village, town, or whatever else you construct. Townscaper gives you simple building blocks which allows you to create masterpieces; from the basic and realistic, to the absurdly fantastic and imaginary. If only I could populate the town with tiny people; that is my one yearning for this game. I wish there were tiny people.. That, however, is such a minor issue, when the product and execution of a concept has been so brilliantly executed. If dice had numbers greater than 6, this would have that score. 6+ on a die of 1d6.

_childDocuments_.review: "Townscaper" is a wonderfully relaxing game that I’d definitely recommend for anyone looking to unwind and unleash their creativity. The gameplay is incredibly straightforward: you simply click on building tiles, and the game’s AI takes care of the rest, constructing charming and unique townscapes with a few simple clicks.What sets "Townscaper" apart is its serene and intuitive design. There are no complex rules or objectives—just a calming, almost meditative experience where you can create beautiful, intricate towns at your own pace. The game's visual style is vibrant and appealing, with a lovely aesthetic that brings each building and town to life.It's a perfect game for those who enjoy creative expression without the pressure of deadlines or scores. Whether you’re designing a quaint village, a bustling city, or an abstract masterpiece, "Townscaper" provides a satisfying and enjoyable outlet for your imagination.Overall, "Townscaper" is a delightful and soothing game that's easy to get into and hard to put down. It’s a great choice for anyone in need of a relaxing and creatively fulfilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I thought this game was just placing houses next to each other and enjoying the simplicity of that but there is a lot more to it than one might think at first sight.The randomized alignment grid of rectangles, pentagons and hexagons is an interesting feature that forces you to improvise and to embrace asymmetric building. The game offers a multitude of connectors that spawn in depending on the building blocks' relative positions to each other which are a lot of fun to experiment with. The graphics are - while comic-like - surprisingly beautiful featuring many small details around the houses aswell as little animations when placing or removing blocks.I wholeheartedly recommend Townscraper as a unique experience to any fan of citybuilder games whether you are going to spend two hours or two hundred in it.

There is no way to connect districts with bridges that dont look like quays or houses.Townscaper offers some "secret combinations", though, which could help with giving certain parts of your town an individual feel. Spaces fully enclosed by houses turn into gardens, for example. Overbuilt gaps will shape into archways - and more. These are nice to discover when playing and do keep everything as simple as possible. They are way too few, though. I would recon you will find most of them within a few hours and not all of them are very big and noticeable. It would have been nice if more styles and elements could have been added by modding, allowing a potentialle endless repository of Doodads to allow for more individual Towns.Lastly, there is a lack of Immersion as well. I find it hard to understand why I cant walk in my city and just experience it like the townsfolk would. Why not have some random folk spawn in doors to make their ways somewhere, sit at benches or feed some birds? We can change the time of day - why is there no day-night cycle or changing weather to experience?

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a solid sandbox building game about erecting little coastal villages. It's a neat game to mess around with different town designs. The look of buildings like the roofs, additional hooks, windows, doors, clotheslines, and greenery changes based on the way you place adjacent buildings. The game is set on a wonky grid allowing for more 'natural' and uneven shaped structures. While messing around with the limited color pallet and the different designs that come from placing these buildings can be fun and suck you in, there are several things missing from this game which stop me from recommending it for many. I found the game disappointing because there wasn't really any soundtrack aside from one song in the credits, and while the splish-splashing noises and other sound effects in the game make it not totally barren I found the soundscape to be lacking. The game also felt pretty lifeless. There are some birds that flock atop your buildings but there aren't any fish or people to populate the rest of the game. In addition the game is aimless. With no objectives or challenges to complete there is not much to do except make your own fun, and for most there's only so long you can mess around without a goal before getting bored. A final aside; I couldn't figure out how to make the floating islands which was very frustrating. While the building component can be enjoyable it could be more fleshed out, the game lacks music and a more lively world, so all in all the game is about a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  This mobile app isn't even a game, it's, well, like a playpen or a fidget spinner, I guess.  You click around on a small 3D rendered map and buildings pop up.  Depending on where and how you click, the buildings may take various different forms like a tower or something.  You can choose what colours the buildings will be from a palette on the side of the screen.  That's all there is to this.  Visual bubble wrap. For those unfamiliar with what actually makes something a game, a "game loop" describes the interaction and feedback a gamer has when playing a game.  Tetris, for example, has a game loop where a random block appears, the gamer interacts with the block to position it, and then the game decides if that finishes a row or not, increases the players score if any rows were completed, then gives the gamer another block to position.  Counter-Strike has a game loop where a player seeks another player, tests their skill against that player by shooting them or being shot, the computer rewards the player if they win, and then if the player survives, they repeat that loop.  There's no loop here, no true interactive feedback.  It simply is not a game, it cannot be "played".It can be "played with", but then you can open up Excel and use your arrow keys to make the cursor move around in amusing directions if you really want... does that make Microsoft Excel a game?  No, it doesn't (except for the version of Excel that had that hidden flight sim easter egg... which is more of a game than this is!).   See what I mean?There's not much else to say about this because it's not a game, which disqualifies this for recommendation to gamers as a game.  I suppose it's worth noting it looks nice... which just means it's a waste of effort that could have been spent more wisely on making an actual game.  This could have been the foundation for a charming Sim City style game or something... but no.  There's also some technical defects that should be addressed if anyone still wants to go ahead and buy this non-game mobile app on Steam. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no options to change the resolution for the mobile app and not many meaningful ways to customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this mobile app is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this mobile app will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Townscaper has the preposterous price of around $6 USD ($1 more expensive than on the app stores, so that's a poke in the eye to PC gamers from these mobile devs), it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is, without a doubt, the most relaxing video game I have ever played, and at the time of writing this I've been playing video games for almost 23 years. I jumped in and before I even knew it, hours had passed. First, its beauty is in its simplicity. There are no directions and you don't need them. You just start building using your left mouse button to build and the right mouse button to delete. There's no punishment for making a move you didn't want to make or for adding a building or land piece you didn't want to create. You just right click and it's like the move never happened. You don't have to spend fictional money to create buildings, and there's no winning or losing outside of your own satisfaction with the town you've created. There's no complex system of traffic or electricity/power or civil services. You just build buildings. If you're looking for an intense city sim like Banished or Frostpunk, this just isn't for you. Second, this game is beautiful. Whether your creation is tiny island with just a few small houses, or a massive sprawling city, it's hard to make a bad looking town. While all buildings look very similar, there are definitely some really cool hidden surprises depending on how and where you create your  buildings. Seeing clotheslines extend from two tall close-by buildings or a point sitting atop a tall tower, I time-and-time-again found myself trying to replicate some of the special structures and details I made.Overall, Townscaper is just a great way to relax after a long day or week and allow you to be as creative as you want without being overwhelmed by a myriad of options or complex mechanics. Even if it wasn't in Early Access and this is all it will ever be, Townscaper would still get an easy thumbs up from me. If you just want to shut your mind off for a bit and create something beautiful, do yourself a favor and pick up Townscaper.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing and chill city builder with awesome aesthetics. The way the building interacts is very fluid and easy to catch on to. That being said I have also seen some other players use very unique building techniques so your imagination is really the limit to this game.Townscaper is easily a game that you can spend some time fiddling around with while waiting for friends to que in other games or if you just want to do something chill for a few minutes.Edit: Dev is constantly updating, bug fixing, and adding new features. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a ridiculously cute, utterly relaxing building toy. There are no citizens to annoy you with demands and side quests, and there is no stressful resource balancing. Just building. And what you build is a combination of the color you select and the shape of the spot on which you build.The interface is fairly self-explanatory. Scroll to zoom in and out. Click and drag to rotate your view in 3D. Click to build.I hope that Townscaper will be expanded with things like trees, gardens, parks, and other elements to really fill out the townscape. Definitely worth the price for those days when you're already too stressed to deal with a complex game and just need to zone out.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend of mine bought this for me saying I'd like it, and they were correct. What a mellow cool medievalish modern city clicker builder. No advisors telling me what to do, no citizens complaining about taxes and shortcomings in public services, no bank loans or money worries, to traffic planning, nothing but clicking or right-clicking nodes on a graph and watching building parts appear or disappear. A few things I'd recommend: *_ an additional "rainbow" color box that cycles to another color on clicking (i.e. every node/building is a random color)*_ world options (e.g.      *_ the floor layer is already filled with (or is) sidewalk,      *_ the floor layer is grass/natural cover,      *_ maybe elevation?)*_ feature: draw lines of nodes, e.g. click a node and drag the mouse along a vector until you hit a branch, and then all nodes along that grid vector are filled in*_ feature: a specific tool for drawing non-building features, or cycling through options if that makes sense (but more for adding gardens & greebles to sidewalks*_ co-habitant feature: more place-block sound variation*_ inter-nerdom feature: export top down maps for people who would want to use this for RPG/etc world building*_ load/save button?  I like other ideas people have posted, like inhabitants to go with the seagulls (as long as they don't want anything) or the ability to walk around the town sound pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to start by saying that I love city builder games. Ive sunk many hours into C:S and Tropico and all sorts of other games. If you're looking for a complex city builder with any kind of management aspects, this is not the game for you.HOWEVER, if what you are looking for is a great little time killer that is as satisfying as it is relaxing to play, then you've come to the right place. This game allows for hours of mindless messing around without any greater thought. However, if you'd like to really think things through, it'll allow for that as well. I think the pictures on the store page do a good job of illustrating the variety of what you can build in this game, as does the community hub, so if you're interested check those out.One of my favorite aspects of the game is something that I've always struggled with in other city builders; giving my creations a natural look. Due to the irregular tiles that you build on and the procedurally generated items that appear while you build, these cities have a very organic look to them that is very difficult to achieve in other games. This comes at the cost of detailed manipulation of the environment, as you can't decide what shape each tile will take, but the end result are fantastic looking towns or even bigger cities that just look real. If you're looking to kill time, relax and find a creative output for your free time, I can't recommend this game enough. I hope it continues to get updated as time goes on, as it is limited in its scope, but even in this current stage it is a great little game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a very simple game? Yes. Is this a fun and surprisingly addictive game? Also Yes.I'm not exaggerating when I say it's a simple game, so don't expect too much when you spend the $7 for it. It consists of being in the water, with a small colour palette to choose from, and you place down blocks (can't choose blocks, it will auto change to either street/building/etc) to make a town, that is all. That being said, it is still a very relaxing and chill game to play. I like building games like this so this is very much up my alley. The art style is cute and I really enjoy the different animations that play out when the houses change depending on the structure. You can make a lot of different things with the small palette you have to work with, from small villages to giant mansions.I've seen it said in reviews before and I also agree, that it'd be cool to have people roaming around the town as you're making it, would make it feel more alive, all we have right now are some birds on roof tops.I think another thing that could add a lot of fun to the game would be different town starting locations, not just water, although it is fun to build ocean towns.Overall, it's a cute fun little game, and if you have 7 bucks to spare I'd recommend giving it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fantastic tool for d&d town creation, i honestly couldn't recommend it more right now at the price tag.Wishlist for the future:- Other templates such as grass, desert, snow etc. rather than just water.- A black and grey colour pallet for structures.- I would absolutely love a tool for placement of featureless walls instead of buildings, this allows for walls around towns without the bottom floor looking like its part of a house with doors, windows etc.- Inclines & declines feature in the form of ramps etc- More building styles such as rustic, medieval, victorian, gothic etc. or at least workshop support so that others can make these themes.- A brush feature for highlighting certain areas of the town as districts and ability to make them nameable.Dev: Keep up the excellent work!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: After 6 hours and 3 townscapes, I really like this "game", and the price is a steal. Like many are saying, there is a lot of potential here, and I'm excited to see what features will be added later, but the game is really good as it is.I've been using it to digitize some of the towns and cities of my D&D campaign. I love how the grid adds a natural dynamic to the outlay without being too restrictive. If you have something particular in mind, you can just find a place on the grid that will fit.Of course there are a lot of elements you can't really control, for instance "street" width. I think the game strikes a wonderful balance between what you can and cannot control, and it does what I need it to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Just an honest to goodness chill time. It's definitely not a game, as the description itself even admits, but it excels as a tool to fulfill myriad purposes, be that of a creative outlet or simply as a way to unwind for a few minutes. No time commitments, no goals and no real deep mechanics make Townscaper one of the purest sandboxes I've ever had the pleasure to spend some time in.There is an easy joy in placing random blocks on the grid and seeing them develop into houses, buildings, towns while discovering new shapes or special interactions in the process.Pricetag wise, if 5€ seems a little steep to you or you're not sure if you're into the whole idea, then definitely wait until a sale comes around.I'll end the review here because, well, there really isn't much else to talk about. But to Townscaper's credit? That's not a bad thing at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly relaxing and fun to play.It is not a game in the traditional sense, but is more like the creative aspect of Minecraft, except more laid back.The graphics are charming and do their job well without being breathtaking.The sound effects are a bit twee and can be annoying (but they're not required, so just mute the sound).Having played the game for 107 hours now, I can really appreciate how relaxing and yet somehow compulsive this little gem can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome click therapy. The controls are flawless. The sound is tactile. The graphics are smooth, clean, and adjustable. But best of all, the building tile shapes shift from tile to tile. You're left with just enough asymmetry to leave your creations always needing a click or two more for perfection. It keeps the creative process moving along. There are endless possibilities and the block stacking morphs buildings with perfection. Well-made game and excellent price. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: As some commentators have noted, this is a toy, not a game -- but what a toy!  Addictive and soothing. Also, love the art style and color palette -- evokes Miyazaki, somehow.FOR THE DEVELOPER:  Features to consider adding:  - "Street view"  -  Would be cool to be able to drop down onto a sidewalk or into a square or courtyard and pan the camera around.- Along the lines of the birds, maybe add the odd cat or dog in gardens, etc.  Like the birds and the flapping clotheslines, these types of small, subtle movements really help transform the scene from something static to something living.- Some type of ageing / decay features?  I'd love to see some of these elaborate cities fray and crumble as if they had long ago been abandoned.Bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: This is chillest and prettiest town-builder on steam.It managed to do everything about these superchill lofi games to game to right. Every building and structure I created felt so aesthetic and filled with life, despite the only life in the game being birds and butterflies (possible inhabitants cause the town lights go on at night).The sound design is perfect, you can hear all the little bricks falling in the water and the structures and trees growing once you place them.Sometimes you don't need mechanics and capitalism in your builder game, just placing these adorable houses and watching them transform into giant cityscapes with castles and vistas brings me so much joy. And coming up with lore for my town and the buildings is some of the most fun I've had in ANY chill builder game.I only wish there were more building options, even though I love the restrictions cause they make for super aesthetic towns, I'd love it if you could have even more buildings and maybe some landscape options.10/10 MUST BUYAbsolutely got my moneys worth, this game is better than 95% major releases atm and also 95% cheaper

_childDocuments_.review: Cornish Venice Simulator 2020When I was at school I used to doodle towns and cities and make them flow organically, without really knowing what building would come next or how it would interact with the previous ones I had just drawn. It was so fun and my only limitation was being bothered to draw more with a pencil. I remember wishing for a PC game like it that would allow me to create more.My wishes, after many years, have come true with this game. It's extremely simple in concept, and there really isn't much more here than clicking. But, do you know what? It doesn't need it. The detail in the buildings and decorations is impressive and no matter how complicated you make things, it always turns out looking smooth. The pastel colour shades are beautiful and you can zoom out after half an hour or letting your creativity wander and be truly surprised at what you've created.Above all, this game is incredibly relaxing. Like I say, it's a computerised version of city-building doodling I used to do when younger (and still do).Maybe they'll add more features, it would be interesting to perhaps see people and different categories of structures, but to be honest, the whole needs system you get in advanced city building games generates a level of stress that is pleasantly lacking here. This game is highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a digital artist who mainly does character art, but has recently been trying to get into full illustrations with backgrounds. For city backgrounds, I always need a reference, but I often can't find one that fits what I'm thinking. This is a great tool if that's an experience you've had, I use this to make references for all my city backgrounds now. There are different ways to view the builds you make (with textures, without, you can change the lighting a bit, etc.), and if you play around with the camera enough you can view most any angle of your build. My only issues as of the build I'm using are that the camera as I said takes a lot of playing with to get it where you want it. I like to get very specific shots and it's kind of a pain to get the camera right where I want it. Some sort of camera/posing mode to make positioning the camera easier would if that kind of implementation is possible would be really helpful in that regard. My only other note is since the houses kinda get built automatically you can't disable the bushes that appear. Which I would like to be able to do since I don't really want bushes in my backgrounds all that often, but that's a very subjective thing. And the last and my personal biggest issue is having to individually place landmasses. I'd like to be able to make a big map I can reference more than once, but it doesn't really feel worth the effort when you have to click each individual box to place a piece of land. It's not as bad with the house pieces since I don't group them all that much, but if you do you'll probably notice it there, too. If there's already a way to mass place landmasses and I just missed it somehow, then you can ignore this point entirely and that's my own fault. If not though, one of those could be useful. Those three things are my only issues, I otherwise really enjoy using it and I love how easy it is to customize. The different color options are fun to work with, and it's overall been super useful for as cheap as it is. I highly recommend it to artists who need background references because it has helped me a ton.

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding in every sense of the word! Oskar Stålberg has somehowe captured the spirit of minimalism in a game. Your imagination is the main focus here, in the best possible way. I constantly find myself in the same mindset as when I was a kid, building away with my legos or laying a jigsaw puzzle. A unique kind of flow I've never encountered in a digital shape before. The resulting effect is an almost spiritual experience where you suddenly find yourself in a deep, meditative, calm. The only things I find myself wishing for is other materials to build from to help create even more immersive dioramas.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Something to relax for a change? Try this one! Easy to handle, lots of fun and many things to discover.Build cities, castles or whatever building(s) you desire. Your imagination is the limit (well, nearly)... There is no end, so you decide, when to move on. The game gets regular updates: Lighthouses were the most recent! I am very curious, what Mr. Orskar Stalberg brings up next! If you also want to support an independent project. here you are!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a game which manages to strike a balance between so many different factors, it's insane. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: After 7 hours of playing sickly and obsessively, I can say that when I close my eyes I see the constructions I made. When I go to sleep, I dream of myself walking across the cities I built. And when I see buildings in the real life, I realized  most of them are made of imperfect cubic blocks, just like in Townscape.Is like a combination of Cities Skylines, playing with your childhood blocks, and european cities like Bruges or Vernice in a subtle combination... but without problems. You can't lose the game, but you can't win either. I shared some of my cities in the not so much populated Townscaper sub-reddit .Well. I haven't found the "Save City" option yet. Would be a good aggregate. I've had to destroy my creations to build new ones. Only the vanishing memory (and a couple of screenshots) remain of my first cities.I recommend this game. You'll relax or become mad. Or either both.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I love Townscaper. As an Architect educated with history of urban planning, I can see it functioning like a simulator to review how a Italian town was established and built up. Something intriguing is that the multiple styles of bridges, balconies, buildings, plazas increases the variety of the elements in a town. It actually helps make it closer to a real one. And I just LOVE to zoom in to see the open space and gray space between the buildings, under the floors, in the corner of a plaza. There're potentials of the variety in types of buildings like the churches, houses, bell towers and assembly halls in this game. But right now I'm good and fulfilled. I wish I can simulate Suzhou, the ancient city in Italian style :D.

_childDocuments_.review: A simply fantastic game. I can't believe it's only $6 either. I found myself up till 4 am, slowly creating my own town, and thinking about story lines to go with it. I love the little details the game auto adds, such as the birds, clotheslines, park benches, etc. I found myself wanting to try out crazing shapes, to see how the game would auto generate it.Three ideas I hope/wish the developers would add in the future. 1. Have the game have a starting option of either starting out in the "water" or a "land" option. Perhaps if there is a land option, you could remove areas to then make water areas such as small ponds/lakes. 2. I wish there was a tool or a "click and drag" option for auto creating or deleting mass areas. I found creating the foundations can get tedious as times, especially if you want tiered layers, and wish there was a way to quickly add them so I can move onto building creation. (If there is a tool for this, I have yet to find out how or where in the game). 3. Different color roof options, just for aesthetic reasons, and I can see it being helpful for bird eye views if you are using this for maps. This game is also has amazing 3D and mapping tools for those who would like to use it for DND. I don't do 3D printing, so I can't make a review on the files you can export, but I am going to convince my Dungeon Master start using this program for cool town/city concepts.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The store page is sufficiently open about the lack of any goal to this game so I cannot give this a negative review, however this made it much more boring to play than I anticipated.To Townscaper's credit it feels amazing to play, the building mechanic is super slick however without any goal, story or purpose, even any means of scoring what you do in it, calling this a game is a stretch and as I write this I see that the store page itself refers to it as a 'toy' rather than a game which is apt.If aimlessly building quaint seaside cityscapes sounds like it might be your thing you'll enjoy this; just a quick word of caution, I thought I'd enjoy it too and didnt even last an hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't reviewed this game yet it seems. I thought I had. So here I go.Almost 5 hours in to playing. I've this game since the start of August. In this short time it already got some updates. Most of them in the art-direction of this game. But also minor bug fixes. Overall this game is bug-free, as far as I have noticed. The visual style is really cool. And the addition of birds and laundry (between the buildings) is also a nice touch. Some say you can't really call it a 'game'. Well what do you call it then ? Perhaps you call it how I nominated this game for this year's Steam Awards: Sit back & Relax-game.I hope the updates will keep coming. And it's almost fully done - in my view - for an Early Access-game.I like the way you can share your creations: copy-paste your clipboard. But I've also find the save-location(s).Now almost 12 hours into the 'game' I'm done with it. Once you have done most of the creative stuff you tend to get bored with it. At least I am. _childDocuments_.review: Unless you're some sort of sadist, this isn't going to be the sort of "game" you'll spend very long on. Simply by the fact it's not a game at all. Rather, a sort of point and click island building simulator. There's no goal here. Just place a block of pavement and stick houses of various heights on top of them. It does a very good job of handling various architecture scenarios (eg building over water) which keeps your interest that bit longer.Honestly, it's daftly satisfying and worth the price of a large coffee. I have some initial thoughts on the interface:1, Can we have a button hold (eg Alt) that allows you to drag around and create the pavements without having to constantly keep clicking.2. Can you let the user define the grid style. At the moment it's this wavy sort of quads. And although this makes for an interesting creative process, it doesn't account for a scenario perhaps where you have an idea in your head. So please. A square grid option.3. As others have mentioned, the island looks so lonely, except for a few birds on the roofs. Some people would be nice.4. Also, some way to add character to the houses. Perhaps be able to add a sign to make it look like a shop.I could see this becoming a game by adding achievements of some sort. Creating enclosed areas, having 100 houses etc etc. I dunno. This has weird potential this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the price I must rate this game 10/10. It's simple, fun, nice looking and addictive.On the other hand, I am missing few features:1) Especially larger buildable area. When you let your fantasy out, you can very easily hit the hard border and it causes some graphic glitches. 2) Custom colour palette. And surely more than 15 colors palette. Default set of colours is just not enough and it shouldn't be so hard to add this feature to let players create much better looking towns.3) Larger brush, at least 2*2 or 3*3, at least for painting base level or erasing. So without these features and not considering such a friendly price, I will say 8/10.Also would be nice to see more building themes, like Gothic castle with fortifications, Adobe/Pueblo architecture, Arabic/Mosque architecture, or some modern style... And the posibility to build on grass, desert or some kind of 3D terrain like rocks, cliffs. Or combination of more of these. _childDocuments_.review: There is no game here. It's simply a virtual stress toy which is fine to some, but not me. Although the game is clearly all about creativity, there is no form of progression which essentially locks the player into a small box of choices, rather than expanding slowly and inspiring the player to think outside of said box.. Unlocking new building types and being able to choose what types of buildings are placed would make this game way more enjoyable, encourage different flavours of creativity and increase it's longevity tenfold without hindering it's focus on relaxation and avoidance of a set goal.At 7 minutes I feel like I have seen everything that this "game" has to offer, that is probably a new record.Notice though that I haven't said that it is bad though, because it isn't. It does what it set out to do quite well, the issue is that what it set out to do is incredibly lacking in content and ironically creativity,since it entirely relies on the player's. On top of that after my 7 minutes of playtime and watching the trailers I really don't see any increase in possibilities, nothing stood out as "that looks cool, I should build that", I've literally done everything.The only downside I would say is that it bizarrely doesn't allow for player freedom, which inherently is an issue in a creative sandbox game with no goal. Want to have some stairs that go up to this other block? Nope, that's now a house.Want a long tunnel under a bridge? Nope, that's now a long solid block.Want to separate these to roads that are next to each other with a railing or gap? Nope, they are now attached and there's nothing you can do about it.It desperately needs a feature that allows players to alter a block's type or shape. The game would keep it's simplicity and flow, but will allow players to build what they truly want to. I would argue that this is the primary reason that 7 minutes was enough playtime for me to think I'd seen everything, because the blocks always play out in the same manner.It really gives off that feeling you would get while playing Minecraft where you're trying to build something but the blocks are just slightly too big for that thing you wanted to build, so now that thing needs to be twice as big as planned. And even Minecraft has started to fix that with the addition of different shaped blocks, fences, walls, windows and other decorative blocks.Again it isn't necessarily bad, but for a game that does so little it has no excuse to be anything other than perfect, which it just isn't.It's fine for players that just want to click and build blocks but there really isn't anything more to it than that. Personally I think I wouldn't have an issue with it if it was free as it comes off as a tech demo for something that might be bigger and better in the future, but right now it is a glorified fidget toy and not worth any amount of money.

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper, at the time of writing, is wonderful and very relaxing game, well worth the price tag even in its current state. I highly look forward to where it will go from here as it progresses and gains more features. As to be expected with an early access game it feels like it could benefit from there just being more content and features, something I'm sure will be addressed as it moves towards release.Currently there's a few things missing that limit it to being only a wonderful toy not a wonderful tool. _childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute game. Obviously, the distinguishing trait is that it is just about creating, the only game-play per say is figuring out what combinations of blocks do what: how to make stairs, terraces, gardens, towers, spires, etc.Visually, the game is utterly precious. The buildings are charmingly rustic, the birds are fat, the bushes jiggle, and there's lots of little objects that pop up with the buildings to give the towns you make some life.The towns you can make have a very... JRPG/anime feel to them... if you know what I mean... like Hydropolis from Ni No Kuni II or any cloud city... IDK...The only "downside" is that after a while, it starts feeling... empty... I'd say the game has a definite, 'room to expand' vibe: other building styles, different environments, maybe little people to compliment the birds. Basically, what's here is great, and more of it would be appreciated. It's a relaxing little toy with a lot of visual charm.

I haven't played it much, but I think one of the things I'm enjoying most is thinking about the potential it has more content, primarily with adding different aesthetics to it.
