_childDocuments_.review: I love this. It's really simple and chill, it's very easy to play and let lost in. It took me a bit to get used to the controls (as it doesn't really say when you start the game what they are) but once i had them figured out it became easier. I highly recommend if you need something to get your mind off things. Also, I don't know if this is just my game, but when i have a lot of things in one world, it becomes slow and doesn't load things, so i have to exit the game and restart it so i can see what things have loaded and how things look. (i'm not sure if that makes sense, but hopefully it does)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much a basic and very calming. It is a great game to pass by time. You get to build up your town however you want, anyway you want. I do hope more updates comes to it where more things are added such as more structures and whatnot. Would be nice to have people present in the game as well to make the town more lively. Other than that, I enjoyed this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, do you like making landscapes, purely out of buildings, in the middle of a nonspecific ocean?  If so, Townscaper, is the game for you.  Complete with absolutely no music (so you can play jazz in the background), Townscaper is an immersive experience, in which you create insane stacked houses, because anything else is boring and not what I like.  If you're like me, which none of you are, you enjoy sitting and doing nothing for an extended period of time.  Townscaper is like this, but with houses, which makes the experience 5000x better in every way, prove me wrong.  I've already made a stranded island of houses in the middle of the ocean, and I will surpass the size of the United States in five months.  My stack of houses is already higher than the Empire State Building. You've probably felt less power of your life in the past several years, but with Townscaper, you can BUILD it, MAKE it, CONTROL it.  You are your own president, and landlord, and house colorist, with a touch of a God's omnipotence.  Buy this game do it now.  I rate 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but it doesn't work presently with Steam/Proton on Linux. It works fine, however, using Wine directly (after installing the game with Steam!). This command can be used in the start menu or with a terminal:env WINEPREFIX="/home/[username]/.wine" wine /home/[username]/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/Townscaper/Townscaper.exeMy sys:Linux Mint 19.3 (tricia)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I just got the game and I already love it. But It's not really a "game", it's more like a toybox. You put blocks into place and build your lego city. Very charming and simple!It still Early Access so I'm excited for more updates. The game would improve greatly from features like a better free camera (maybe WASD-like?) and a brush-like block creation (click and drag instead of putting blocks one by one). Also different time of day and wandering NPCs could bring even more life to it.26 hours later update: Still great, and better!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's extremely basic. I thought this was going to get better over time but it's still basically the same product since forever ago. A passion project, tech demo, whatever. It pushes the boundary of casual and not in a good way, and certainly not 7.99 in value. Buy on sale if you really want braindead gameplay for a 3 year old that wants digital lego.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game that sucks you in for hours without you even realising it.Then it suddenly gets incredibly boring and you figure it was a nice few hours and you'll stop playing it and move on to the next game.But the colorful houses and sweet plopping sounds will invade your dreams and when awake the craving will have already set in.Oh well. Another day, another town. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The cutest game I've played in a long time and i can't recommend it enough. It's good fun for as long as your imagination lasts :) as cheap as it is. I'd say it's a steal for some 8/9 hours of town design heaven :) it's short, it's simple, it's easy and it looks pretty, sort of no matter what you do.1 problem, it feels very lonely and sad the pretty visuals look very lonely just...lonely the dev should add NPC's.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Please add people to the town! A weather cycle would be cool, And more colors, maybe like a hue selector. This game is so beautiful and the types of buildings you cab creat by using different colors and aranging the blocks certain ways has me playing this game for hours. If you like ONLY building in games  likes sims, minecraft, and city skylines, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Now that Townscaper is out of early access, it deserves the Sit Back And Relax award. It's the perfect way to just be aimlessly creative, whether or not you actually want the little town you're creating to make any sense. I have a short attention span, so for a game to hold me for 90 minutes on the first sitting says plenty about it. When I'm in the mood to do nothing, I'll play this instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm amazed at how much procedural details there are in this game, every combination of tiles gives you different details and looks. It is a bit simple for now and it's definitely more of a tool/toy than a game but that's what I was sold on and the promotional stuff on the store page shouldn't give anyone the wrong impression of what they're getting.I'd love to see more variety as the game grows and gets more features, different house types, different biomes. I can't wait to use this to make maps for TTRPGs!I can't overstate how much this is worth the five bucks!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: For its category and price, I think it is worth it. (When it's on sale especially.) They could have done a lot more with it, and it almost disappoints me that they didn't do more because there so much potential in what is there. But like I said, it's a great value game and I have enjoyed it! Additionally, I feel it could be a very helpful tool for visualizing, especially for artists.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought this game but I can already see myself spending HOURS building. I love the simplicity of the game, as well as how complex you can make your buildings with such a simple tap and click system. I cant wait to see what the developer adds in the future! I would rate this game 7 out of 6 plates of garlic bread.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The quality in this game is at the level of what exemplifies "early access".  While limited in scope, there is enough content, refined to a playable level that can be enjoyed for a number of hours.Townscaper is a very enjoyable creative building toy.  Perfect for those five year olds looking to break into learning to navigate a three dimensional space.  And, it's fun for adults too.  There is plenty to discover in play.The content is very limiting though.  For the completed game I'd love to see some more animations.  Trains, hot air balloons, sailing ships, and sea monsters interacting with the environment.  Weather events would be fantastic to see, and even witnessing the effects of the the passage of time on player creations could deepen the player experience. There also needs to be more architectural variety to play with, but that is the obvious.As it stands the simplistic style and approach to play is elegant (and probably the real art to behold in any finished product).  From the mechanics to the sounds incorporated, Townscaper is a brief but hot bundle of joy to wade into.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I just got this game last night and played around with it for a bit and I love it! The style is very nice and it makes excellent reference photos for drawing! I struggle with city lines and drawing buildings so being able to create a town/city that I vibe with and then putting it into my art is awesome! (The controls are a little wonky and take time getting used to.)A few things about it that I would add/change is maybe being able to choose a style of building? These buildings are beautiful but if there was a way to change the style to a more modern building or changing the style to a "New York" sky scraper would be nice. The colors are also great but I think there should be more. Definitely a black. This game is just a nice relaxing tool and it is such a good idea!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a delightful building game. The game is all about constructing your vibrant towns over the sea. There's no goal, no objectives, just the joy of making your little town to call home. If you're looking for a relaxing way to spend your time and distract yourself from the monotony and anxiety of everyday life, Townscaper is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A really easy way to get lost in creative freedom and waste time. There are still several features that other reviews have mentioned that would take this "toy" (as the creator says) above and beyond. I.e. pedestrians generated around buildings, music, etc.). It's disappointing the creator says there are no future planned updates for this game at the moment... Really hope the positive reviews this game is receiving change his mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little electronic toy that I've already sunk about 12 hours into. BEFORE YOU BUY, THIS IS NOT A GAME. This is an interactive and ever-changing lego box. There is no goal, no "gameplay", only blocks and houses which you can use to make your perfect scenery.The things i love about this game are:-The little details that randomly appear depending on your builds and patterns-The irregular grid that helps give an organic feeling to your town instead of a big cube, the grid has squares ranging from normal to big to the size of a small spire/tower, all connecting to star-shaped box. It reminds me of sea currents as they form twisting and turning lines that eventually connect to eachother.This is the perfect toy to help you relax and take your mind elsewhere while listening to some chill music as the game currently lacks a soundtrack, but doesn't really need one either, as you can choose your own playlist to help you unwind and relax while you build yourself an adorable little town.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

I might make a game to do with the wave-function collapse algorithm, seeing how fabulous Townscaper is!

Others will just have the same fun we've all had with building blocks. Either way (or any other), this is a fun bit of fluff, and extremely clever.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game an hour ago and I'm already inlove with it. I love how minimalistic the hud is, the colors and the cartoony texture. I would love to see this game grow more yet still have the simplicity in it, I love the grid pattern and in the future, I hope to see more randomized grid patterns and an infinite world. maybe a day and night cycle too with boats and people roaming around? just to make it more lively, but don't get me wrong, Townscaper is worth more than its price right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably what I was seeking when its about building stuff, the little details, the form that the building take and the possibilities + the graphics have such a charm, and the fact that is on Early Access means that it will just become better and better with the right things. Maybe adding some stuff like grass "blocks" (nature stuff with trees, plants, etc. To make gardens or parks) and "decoration blocks" (statues, fountains, etc.) are the things that came in my mind when I was playing.Be buildin' all them houses 'n castles
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is really fun! its a really good stress reliever and ive bought this today and already spent 3 hours on it! your imagination is the limit and you can very easily just unwind and play this for a while. my only two complaints is that if you make different layers of buildings you cant bring the camera down underneath and it makes it really uncomfortable and you cant customise or change the different effects and pieces the things have (like placing stuff in certain ways makes external stairs appear, but you cant just place them down yourslef) and hopefully if this gets updated i'd like to see that
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Games amazing, super calming and relaxing plus it reliefs stress and actually kind of helps with Worldbuilding at times. though i would suggest you could make "Skins" for worlds so instead of being sort of Italian/Venice styled buildings the builds could be more modern or medievel styled. Another suggestion is adding in an option for builds to have either a strieght grid, wavy grid, random grid (witch is the normal one) and maybe a few others.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's not exactly a game, more like having your very own folk-art seaside virtual lego set!   With no levels to pass or objectives to achieve, you're free to let loose your imagination and creativity.  And, as you combine the pieces in different ways, you get to not only build funky little towns but also to discover the various quirky attributes of each piece.  What must you do to make a pair of wellies appear on a doorstep?  Or create a garden?  Or make a flock of seagulls appear??  It's brilliant fun and very satisfying.  I hope they continue to develop this further as there's so much scope here.  I'd love to have a choice of different architectural styles to build with, or maybe some different terrains like grass and trees, in the future.  But as it stands, it's already very fun and engaging to play.  Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Cute "game" where you place multicolored houses that turn into buildings as you add layers. There are rules about how structures add together to produce architectural features. I paid $4.01 for it, and it's worth it for something akin to a set of blocks that you don't have to pick up when you're done playing with them. There are many how-to videos on Youtube which help explain the simple mechanics of Townscaper. I think you'll like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, very relaxing. You can make a lot of really cool structures or just close your eyes and let your hand do all the work. There are even ways to get new structures by finding special grid patterns. It personally helps me during tough times when I just need something simple I can build off of. You can do a city, or even flying cities! (if you can find the grid pattern)It's very simple and relaxing, and the developer does add new grid patterns every once and a while so there is still new content. Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up alongside Sekiro.... Has been a nice stress relief after dying to the chained ogre multiple times lolOn a serious note though, Townscaper is quite a relaxing game and you will lose track of time while you build your intricate Venetian cities (or cloud cities haha). There might not be a lot you can technically do now, but hopefully the Dev keeps pouring the same love and attention into this before it was released on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a simple game about scaping your town. (go figure)The core gameplay is simple, you click on the ocean tiles to raise the level, first being a street or sidewalk and every level above that being a story of a house.  There is a decent range of colors to make your town vibrant.  The tiles are mostly randomly shaped, so your town wont be just a bunch of boxes, but feel more natural.  Add on little details like windows, patios, flower pots, clothes lines, etc. that appear when you connect buildings in certain ways (mostly up to the tile shape).  Beyond the "place building in cool pattern" there isn't much gameplay-wise.Graphics wise its not "ULTRA 4K HYPER REALISM" but a nice laid-back cartoonish style that just looks pleasing.Audio is nice.  There is some nice relaxing music that plays in the background as you place these colorful residences. Play time varies from person to person.  To the average person you should get at least an hour out of it as you test town layouts and building ideas.  To the more creative person or those who love this kind of gameplay will get virtually endless gameplay.Overall opinion is this is a nice game and fair priced.  It's great for relaxing after a stressful day, just boot it up and plop down my colorful abodes while listening to that soothing background music.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: While it's hard for me to decide if this qualifies as a game or not i can tell without a doubt that with the care and time this dev has spent on this product i can expect nothing else but great titles from his future!I've taken this game as a tech-demo and i found myself with something that i would dare even call art, absolutely loved every single bit of it and hope i'll see more of said dev soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: NO cloud saving... I lost the entire town i made. The app should warn you that the game is saving only locally... Normally everything on steam is saved on the cloud.Lost everything i made after some hours, that is not something relaxing for me...If they had at least warned about this i would have copied the save files :/So thats a warning from me to the other users not to experience the same as me :/
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it!!!!!Understand the achievements are just in the satisfaction that you built a little town or a huge city.Worth the $$$$ whatever it costs.Just build and add-on or just keep it simple.  Brightly colored if you so desire, or not.  There are just too many little features to describe.  Funny little items pop up as you build or take away sections of your town; benches, trees, courtyards, laundry, etc.  The list continues to develop.Very easy on your own or if you want more lots of players have left little bits of code for helping you with ideas.It is very relaxing and just darn fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I was never able to get into the city builders or anything related to creativity. My OCD and constant needs of perfection wouldn't allow it. Then comes Townscaper. As someone else said in another review, 'perfection isn't achievable.' Not every road or house is straight. One of my favorite buildings had a sky bridge that curved right. And for once in my life, I don't feel pressured to build perfectly. I can actually just do what I want and make it as wacky or as sensible as I desire. This game is worth it's 99% rating. Get it, you won't be dissapointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no end. As the devs said, this is more of a toy box. perfect for just doodling around. If building a city of penis towers is your calling, go for it. Do note that camera movement is severely limited and very finicky when entering an enclosed area (it just becomes stupidly hard to control), and that you cannot edit the color of existing building blocks (you have to delete them first and replace it with the new color). I hope the dev can improve the camera control to be more sensible than what it currently is now.There are also some things that could be improved. of one particular annoyance is the lack of ability to mass-place blocks. that means if you want large landmasses, you need to INDIVIDUALLY PLACE THEM one by one. You can quickly see how this can get incredibly tedious when you want to build large islands (eg; a large island that requires more than 100 blocks. my hands are still hurting from that). The grid system is also confusing since the squares aren't actually showing where the block will be, but the crosses in them determine how the block will be shaped (and therefore the actual position, in a very painful to calculate manner).i would still recommend this game, but it's very tough for serious players that really want to be invested on this game, to actually be invested on this game comfortably.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. This is the cutest thing I've seen in months. Plop, plop, plop, and you have a little village. All sorts of colors and shapes.And I'm pretty sure every one is made of pure ticky-tacky.But then come the towers! And the bridges! And other things more surprising. Wait. No! Startling! Yet, as exciting as the adventure gets, everything is fine in the end. Everything resolves into a beautiful, soft order.The story is left to the player to create. The combat is purely PvE - mostly involving birds. And the world is open and easy to navigate.( Which is good, since there are NO mounts or fast-travel points. )I do miss having any character customization - or any character for that matter. The tower I just built could really use someone cheerfully waving from the topmost window!Anyway, I recommend this very therapeutic game.Now, I need this on my iPad. ( And wouldn't it be swell if I could move my build from one to the other? I think it would. ):-)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: My partner gifted this to me both because it's a really cute game and as a handy way for me to make city/architecture references for drawing. I thought I'd use it mostly for concept art, but what ended up happening was I got sucked into ploop plop plopping all the things and now I just like seeing what happens when I begin with a blank space and start plunking everywhere. I love finding the tons of little surprise goodies with block combinations and getting birds to land.The only things I wish this game had are being able to put down a random color with each click, being able to conveniently put down a bunch of blocks without having to go through a clicking storm, and an ability to walk around in what you've built (and/or a more convenient way to zoom in more easily than the current camera allows). But even if the game never received another update, I'm more than happy with it in its current form.Overall, it's a super adorable game that's great for relaxing and exercising creativity in a wonderfully intuitive way. Love the art style, its simplicity, and the sheer modularity!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, first time I opened Townscaper I was underwhelmed, thinking there could be more to it. BUT as I sat down and played it when my mind was overwhelmed, I felt super calm and it was really enjoyable. Something as simple as building little houses and seeing what shapes they make keeps you hooked, and you just imagine what little people would be living there. I'd love to see it expand to other architecture styles as DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! there are endless creative possibilities and it is very relaxing yet just stimulating enough that I don't get bored. the one and only complaint I have is how hard it is to change the colour of the buildings. I'm playing on a laptop, and about 50% of the time the colour I clicked didn't actually select and i end up building in the old colour. And one suggestion, as I've seen others wanting as well, is  to add the option to add some people to the town. I totally understand and love the sort of meditational quality of the game being just you, the buildings, and the birds, and it is quite nice to imagine what people might do with the town you make. But it would be cool to have at least the option to add in people.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating, addictive way to pass the time. Especially if you have a lot of time on your hands (rainy days, etc...) No resources to produce or sell, no opponents, no natural disasters, no invading aliens, etc... There's enough of those games out there if that's your thing. Just a great, amusing, relaxing world builder. My compliments to the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Great little chill and relaxing game to de-stress after a long day. Very simple, intuitive controls that let you quickly throw together new buildings and stretch your creative muscles in a objective-free sandbox environment.  The meager asking-price makes it an easy recommendation for those seeking a quick time-waster or zen sandbox game alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is fantastic - don't expect a game - it's more like an easy-go-to city designer with focus on overall layout. You place you house as you will and fantastic algorithms underneath makes everything match up. The whole city is founded on something which likes a bit like a Voronoi map - which makes like curves so your city becomes organic. The UI is first class - graphics very simple and elegant - an effects makes good feedback when you place building or foundations - water splashes, birds fly etc. Thanks for this lovely little Townscaper tool - hope to see add-ons - preferably a medieval theme if I could choose. Also the game only takes up 64mb, which is impressive - given what it can. Being a Mac-Catalina captive it's also nice the mac version is 64-bits. If more developers would ensure this for their releases - I would buy their games.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this simply because it's miscategorized. This has nothing that would make something a game. Just because something is 3D, that doesn't mean it's a game. A game should have objectives or a story or both. At least any kind of challenges, achievements, or metrics to show your progress as a player. Like, highest floor built, how many meters of pavement, or how many windows in total. This has none of it.As a tool to build 3D townscapes, it's also kind of useless. Sure, you can make screenshots of what you have built, but the .OBJ file export is half-baked (it exports 3D object with broken textures). Texturing the 3D model to replicate all the shaders is not something a regular person could do with 3D Builder or Paint 3D apps, it should work out of the box or not be an option at all (like on mobile).There is one cool thing about it though - you can share your creations really easily, you just copy the state of your build to the clipboard and send it to a friend and they can paste it back into their app. So, when Wordle became viral, I was able to build a tool that converted Wordle results into Townscaper buildings So, while I have tried Townscaper on desktop, laptop, Android mobile phone, Steam Deck, and even in the browser, it's just a cute tool for me, which gets boring after 5 minutes. It feels like a prototype, unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: It sucks that I can't recommend this because it looks like so much fun on paper. Just click and watch the town build itself! It prides itself on being this "relaxing" experience, but from my experience the only thing this game gets from me is undying frustration. And it's all because of just one tiny snag.The problem is that you can only place one singular block at a time, absolutely no exceptions. Despite literally showcasing the ability to drag the cursor in the game's trailer, you have no way to place multiple blocks in a row. This makes the "calming" experience into such a tedious chore. Any building or town I can think of requires multiple hundreds of clicks just to plan. All of those giant towns and villages you see on the store page and community hub? Forget about making those.I truly cannot play this for more than 5-10 minutes at at time because it causes genuine pain in my hands in order to play properly. 200 clicks. 500 clicks. 800 clicks. One at a time, no exception. I want to play this so bad, but I doubt we'll ever get a click and drag feature because the developer confirmed that the game is "finished" and shouldn't be receiving any major updates post 1.0. It's so heartbreaking that I have to give such a cool concept a scathing review like this, but I seriously doubt your idea of fun is destroying your index finger just for the outline of a cool city plan.Apparently I'm the only one who thinks this? All the negative reviews for this game are judging it for what it isn't. You having little control over the building process is the whole gimmick, if you want to position every window and bench yourself play minecraft or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, some flaws.I really enjoy this game, and everything it offers. I like architecture and worldbuilding, so I find this game fascinating. There are a few flaws though, mostly due to its newness.1. The grid is not straightAlthough it can make for interesting shapes, the different shapes on the grid can morph your town into something you don't want it to be. Part of the problem is that you cannot control which block is which shape.2. You cannot draw many blocks at onceThere should be a shift click mechanic that allows you to draw or delete a row of blocks at a time. Since there isn't this mechanic, it makes destroying buildings difficult.3. You cannot delete savesIf you create a town you don't like, you cannot delete the save. Because you cannot widely delete blocks multiple at a time, this is very tiresome.4. You can't chose what to buildI expect this will be different later on but for now you cannot chose which types of buildings you want to build. This can be especially annoying when you place 5 blocks next to each other. This automatically creates a raised patio instead of a house. 5. There is only one styleI know this will likely change, but for now there is only one style of building. I think it would be cool later on to incorporate different architectural styles.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, could use some quality of life changes tool though, for example : A fill tool.The option to change the shape of grid tiles, since you can't really decide what shape to make your .town, the grid is a repeating shape pattern so you're kinda at it's mercy to shape the base of your townKeybinds for switching colors without having to click on them.A way to click and drag for placement and deletion, currently you have to place each base/building down one by one.A color wheel so that instead of choosing from given colors you can customize them to construct your own palette.Workshop support so that people can add their own building skins, think like modern skyscrapers or old wooden shacks. And also for people to explore other people's townscapes.A way to place yourself in the streets of your city in a first person POV so you can see what it looks like from ground level. And also to be able to do this on workshop-downloaded townscapes. A way to construct bridges, currently you can't make high bridges because if you click on a base block it will always construct a building instead of another block which you could use to build your own custom bridges.Special buildings, like being able to designate zones for police/health and those buildings becoming a police station/hospital, not for use, just aesthetics. Also stuff like shops, clothing stores, patisseries, bookstores, with unique storefronts, etc. More street props, cars, animals (other than birds), signs, stuff like that.More building options in general, currently things are pretty limited, in order to create a park you MUST have an open space completely enclosed by buildings and sometimes that will glitch out and break if you build 2nd or 3rd layers around/in them. Let us build open parks, add it to the current sidebar or a new sidebar for special areas, pools, sports courts, stuff like that. That's all for now, obviously the game is in early access so I'm sure the dev is already thinking about and working on implementing many of these, just thought I'd put forward some suggestions that may be new to them. Overall, fun and relaxing game, I like to play it while watching other stuff on my second monitor since I don't think it's engaging enough to be played on it's own, at least not for me. It's pretty easy to build pretty settings without much, if any, thinking. Townscaper already has a very nice aesthetic, and I hope the dev can add new content while also staying true to the fundamental image of the game. I'm not going to give it a number rating since there's hardly anything to rate yet.

That's all it does.But for being a pointless tool, it is a  tool when coupled with the imagination. _childDocuments_.review: While I've only played for a very short period of time, I am absolutely in love with it. Being able to build up from the water and create whole towns/cities from nothing, coupled with the fantastic art style, gives the game an enjoyable and relaxing atmosphere. I was surprised at how well the game responded architectually when I would begin making multi-story buildings which would span over my roads. Loved the little arches and gardens which would automatically appear depending on how you placed buildings. On top of all the good, the developer seems to be very engaged with the community and cares about their feedback. I feel as though I can say, with reasonable certainty, that this is not just a money grab.With the good having been said (though there's certainly more which could be said), I do have a couple of things I hope to see in the future. For one, it would be great to have a mode where you could walk around the town you made in first person or something like that. Actually being able to explore what you've created would be a huge bonus. Another great thing would be the ability to choose where certain features such as the grassy areas could be placed. As of now, they appear automatically when you make a circle of buildings with an open space in the middle. While this is an awesome feature, being able to place these manually would be nice. And I might be the only one who thinks this, but I'd also enjoy being able to use a larger map. I found that I used all the space rather quickly.Overall, fantastic little (non)game. _childDocuments_.review: Great little game! I've only played for a little while but I'm already imagining all the cool things I can build. A few suggestions though to improve the controls of the game (without changing the game's content):1. Fix the camera by allowing it to move further away from the map constraints. Right now I have place little 1x1 platforms around anything I build so I can move away far enough from it to have a decent look at it overall. This isn't a solution when you reach the edge of the map entirely.2. Allow us to continuously add / delete blocks by holding down left and right click in combination with some other key. Like holding down shift + left click for example.3. Allow an option to only add or remove from a certain height layer. Adding to point 2, if I want to make a massive platform there should be an option that only allows me to build on that level (level 0 for example). When builds get massively tall it can be hard to tell what "level" a block is on, so there should also be an option to click on a block and have it be set to that level. Of course you can switch between level specific building and "free" building on any height level. 4. Allow a "paint" option to change the colour of blocks without having to delete then re-add them. If implemented along with point 2 and 3, multicoloured skyscrapers will be a breeze!5. Allow us to "select" some or all parts of the map to "copy to clipboard," then select a location on any map to paste it when "loading from clipboard." There should be a ghost version of where the copied material will be placed so we can see how it will look. This "select" function should allow us to delete all blocks in a selected section as well. 6. Let us change the controls for rotation and movement. I'd much rather use right click to rotate and left click to move!7. Let us completely delete maps we don't like. Now for a few suggestions about extra game content:1. Why not add some people milling around and walking? Birds are nice but people would be even better!2. More block types! Why not add grass / land blocks, cliff blocks, wall blocks, market blocks, and anything in between?3. Make the maps bigger (if performance allows it). I want sprawling metropolises! Overall fun game to play and build some nice looking things. You're pretty much guaranteed to end up with something good even if you just click around randomly.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid I used tom play with wooden blocks and other similar, using them to create buildings, realistic or as improbable as I could while keeping them standing. It's a lot of fun, and you'll easily get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: "Townscaper" isn't a game. Well, it's not a game yet; it might be in the future. Then again, it might not; it's still in early access, and at this point is probably best described as a technology demo. Right now, though, it's a city-builder at its most basic. Click on a square, and a building pops up. Click on it again, and that building gets a second story (or a third, or fourth, or more, all depending on how many times you click). The squares seamlessly melt together into larger buildings. The goal - in as much as there is a goal - is to build yourself a pretty town. And, limited as it might be, I'm perfectly fine with that. This isn't a game (or however you want to describe it) for everyone. It's extremely sparse in features; there's no real variety in building types, and the maps themselves are pretty small. Still, the underlying tech is pretty neat and its quite fun to see structures grow out of the ground. Even with the tiny set of structures, you can still create an impressive number of unique cities too. Do I wish there was more to this game? Sure, but even if it only managed to hold my attention for a few hours, I think it well worth the price (a mere fiver) and I can imagine drifting back to fiddle about with it numerous times in years to come, just to play around - even if only for a little while - with its impressive visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is beautifully simple with loads of room for growth. I recommend this game as a great way to explore your creative side within a beautiful architectural sandbox.

For example, I don't like doing intricate little coloring pages. If you enjoy that sort of thing, this is right up your alley!I'd love to see this game expand with little people and boats, or a simple unlock path to reward players with new colors or increased build height. None of that is necessary or expected, however. Kudos to the devs for delivering exactly what they said they would. Can't fault you!

But the further you dive, the more complex you can get. Different shapes (based on the randomized grid) and 16 colors for buildings allow you to mess around to your heart's content. You'll discover all the varieties of special things you can build (gardens, archways, towers, etc) the more you play.Above all, Townscaper is a great way to relax. The sound of placing building pieces is soothing, in my opinion. But if you don't like it you can always turn it off and enjoy the silence or put on some music.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review:
Build quaint island towns with curvy streets. Build small hamlets, soaring cathedrals, canal networks, or sky cities on stilts. Block by block.

No goal. No real gameplay. Just plenty of building and plenty of beauty. That's it.

Townscaper is an experimental passion project. More of a toy than a game. Pick colors from the palette, plop down colored blocks of house on the irregular grid, and watch Townscaper's underlying algorithm automatically turn those blocks into cute little houses, arches, stairways, bridges and lush backyards, depending on their configuration.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

name: Broken Pieces
detailed_description: Please wishlist the game to stay up to date! Mainly created by a team of 5 people , Broken Pieces is the first game to come out of the French game development studio Elseware Experience . When Elise and her fiancé decided to leave urban life and settle near the French coast, she could not imagine that she would end up completely alone. Now, surrounded by strange phenomena in a dark, post-Cold War climate, Elise will have to investigate and unravel the mysteries surrounding the region of Saint-Exil, its ritualistic cult, and its lighthouse overlooking the coast. Broken Pieces is an action-packed investigative and adventure video game set in France. The game puts you in the shoes of Elise, a woman in her thirties who finds herself in the village of Saint-Exil in an imaginary region reminiscent of Brittany. Following an unexplained paranormal phenomenon, Elise is stuck, completely alone and out of time. Your investigation begins here… Playtime : 9 to 12h. DLSS supported. Explore the area of Saint-Exil and its surroundings in the 1990s. Choose between either a standard TPS camera as well-known in modern TPS or a completely revised version of the camera system that accompanied legendary game franchises of the 90s, aimed at providing greater flexibility and player agency. Switch between 2 camera angles in any situation or drop into a first-person view to have a closer look around. Interact with the environment to learn more about what has happened to you in Saint-Exil. Your investigation will be rhythmically punctuated by cinematic sequences, with motion entirely captured from handheld cameras. Enjoy a thriller atmosphere in your adventure to the fullest extent. Keep an eye on the time with your watch; it is imperative that you get home before nightfall. Manage your inventory capacity and ensure that you carry about what you need to make progress. A variety of additional interactive elements, such as a vintage arcade machine, is available in your main and secondary quests. Change the weather of Saint-Exil to forge new paths or solve the puzzles blocking your way. You will discover tapes from which you can draw clues to help you in your investigation. Use the tape player to fast-forward or rewind the tapes and home in on the information you seek. Listen to your tapes while exploring the village of Saint-Exil and enjoy a seamless experience of discovery. Discover the music composed by Pierre for Élise that will accompany you in your adventure. Face challenging enemies with a unique combat system using fixed camera angles. Dodge your enemies or hold them at a distance using your powers to better defeat them. Restore your health by grabbing a drink in the fridge, catching a nap on a bench or spending a night in the safety of your bed. Craft high-quality ammo and upgrade your gun to increase your fighting abilities.

short_description: Broken Pieces is a psychological thriller taking place in a french coastal village somehow outside the flow of time. Solve the mysteries by putting the pieces of the story back together by figuring out the enigma behind this mystical place.

_childDocuments_.review: Story is intresting and the Game is pretty stable, never met any bugs. And the puzzles are great.However the combat is at its best decent and at its worst pretty bad. (I played in Normal)Dodging isn't reliable, your character misses 2/3rd of her shots which discourages using HQ ammo and instead just spam normal ammo. There's only 1 enemy type and as the game goes on it increases difficulty by putting more of them. Worse, you cant move while aiming, which is fine but its really hard to dodge attacks by moving and some combat requires mobility which the aiming mechanics doesn't give you.Its fine during the 1st half of the game but by the end it gets boring and frustrating. Specialy when at the end you see there used to be more enemies planned but they were scrapped in development.Still, the story and puzzles make up for it, so I still recommand the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler freeNot a Survival Horror game. Not a horror game at all really. It's a puzzler. Closest thing I can think of might be Siberia. It's a good puzzler. Story is intriguing.+ Visuals are overall gorgeous+ Solid music+ Story is overall intriguing+ Decent puzzle design+ Cool Weather mechanic, both involving storms and the other seasons+ English voice cast is pretty good.+ Puns- Combat leaves something to be desired. Maybe should've been left out altogether.- Another game that screams "tank controls" but doesn't include an option to use them. - Camera can get janky at times.- Typos and mismatched dialogue to subtitles.Yeah, it's worth a go if you like puzzle games with a cool story to tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pixel hunting "find the key" adventure game.  1000 locked doors, click on everything in sight, miss the one thing you need to progress, go back through all over again and click on everything in the entire world until you find the one key.  Open the one door, gain access to more rooms and more locked doors.  Keep clicking on everything in sight and hope you find the next key.  In the first 90 minutes I did not encounter a single puzzle, just locked doors.  I love the art, the music, and the general vibe, but the gameplay reduces it all to walking back and forth in a large environment, mashing the interact button hoping to find the one thing.  Got real old real fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent a bit of time debating myself about this, but at the end of the day, I just couldn't bring myself to give this game a recommendation. My main issue with this game is that it, in essence more closely relates to games like "The Park" as opposed to classics like "Resident Evil" or "Silent Hill" but has a system setup meant to replicate 3rd person horror games of the PS1, Dreamcast and PS2 era.What didn't work for me:The Story:I liked the approach that the developers went with to let the story unfold through collected tapes and recorded thoughts from our protagonist. But since you are thrown in the middle of these events with no real connection to anything, you are relying on the final scene to throw everything together, which it unfortunately doesn't. (I hear that the developers are patching the ending, but that should have been done before release)The story gets very interesting halfway through, which makes the lackluster ending all the more unsatisfying. Combat:Just bad. It took me a while to realize that you have to wait for the aiming crosshair to shrink in order to get a clear shot on your enemies. The dodge does not work well. Think of the dodge mechanic in the Dreamcast game "Illbleed" but instead of it being broken in your favor, it's the complete opposite. Thank goodness for the "Knockback ability". There is also a mode that tones down the combat, which I recommend. The combat serves more as something to break up the monotony of running around all over the place, but honestly in my opinion should have been left out all together.What I Have to give credit to:If you can get immersed in the game, the note taking system and cassette tapes do fill you in on what you are supposed to be doing throughout the day. Actually reading this stops you from doing too much backtracking.I thought the music was phenomenal!The graphics were pretty good!The puzzle tables were challenging!If I had to give this game a grade, it would be somewhere between a 5.5 and a 6, but I just found this experience too drab to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: All in all nice game, but I'd put it as neutral, if I could, as I couldn't recommend it.It simply has too many things wrong with it. There's a good game hiding in there, but it's hiding well. And it's not worth $25Some level areas are beautifully made. Some areas like the museum feel like there should have been more, but in general, the game looks nice and has many nice details.The journal with the clues and objectives was nicely done. collected all the clues related to an area in a central place.In general, the game feels like the devs cared about it, which is probably true for many/most indie games.But with the good stuff out of the way..The story is engaging in the beginning. But it goes nowhere. At the end of the game you feel like you played chapter 1 of 3 or so, because nearly nothing is resolved in the end.What was ? Don't know. Why did the cult do what it did? Don't know. Where did the stones come from? Don't know. What are those shadows? Don't know. Why weren't the birds affected from what spirited away all humans? Don't know. Why did the water fall upwards at sea? Don't know. And so on.When the outro rolls you really think "wait where's the rest of the game? we just got started!"The handling is really cluncy. you play third person, but your viewpoint is a random location, not over the shoulder (which would have improved this game greatly). They probably went for the silent hill 'look and feel' and I can't say if they nailed it because I never played that game, but it really doesn't work. Run one way in one direction, the camera switches and it's kinda random if holding the same key will continue you on your trajectory or turn you around. Thanks to the fixed, and poorly choosen camera perspectives, you very often have to hit the "switch perspective" button so you actually see things.The combat is dog poop. It could have actually worked, as simple as it is, if the controls wern't as unresponsive. Can't remember how many times I mashed space with her just standing there. And really, Elise or what your name was, you have to take 3 seconds to aim for the dude right in front of your face?Also, there is only one enemy types. Two if you wanna count the same enemy with a red energy barrier. The outro showed concept pictures with more, why is that the only one?The puzzles.. Also were pretty bad. Most of the time they were very easy, if voice lines didn't spoil it immediately. The times they weren't they required moon logic. For example, there is a circuit box out of your reach that you need to see the contents of. It looks bolted shut. So what do you do, search a ladder? get up there and try to loosen the bolts? Nah you summon a storm because it just looks bolted but flaps open in the storm. There was actually a voice line spoiling this, but at the time it played I looked at a truck with planes over it and thought you were meant to move them (they didn't)A smaller example was once you had to lure birds to press a button, because apparently the machine doesn't work with the birds there. No, don't ask me, I don't know why either. But from voice lines you know what to do. So you throw down the lure and sprint to the button. Thanks to the awful camera you can't tell what the birds are doing.Turns out you have to throw one lure for each bird, because nobody ever heard of multiple birds fighting after the same food, right?There are 7 puzzle boxes strewn about and those puzzles were though, at least for me, but they're side content.The whole thing being time based was anoying. Do I do this now or do I go back home, sleep and try to find my way back?Speaking of annoyances, the inventory. How did "you can only carry a lever or an axe" improve the game in any way? Instead it forces you to leave stuff behind and then later potentially search for a long time to find it again.Also, plenty of machine translation.The funniest thing is that the voice actress clearly didn't give a damn about that. An english voice actress without accent prooobably knew enough english to know that "The access is condemned at the top" doesn't make too much sense. I could believe it in cases like a blocked door and "the cult condemned this door", because she lacked context, but the example with the ladder really has no excuse.Oh and a long, unskippable credit sequence is always an automatic minus point for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is nice and it kinda feels nostalgic and fresh at the same time. But what kills the game in my eyes is that after finishing it not even the smallest detail is explained. Even if it was the prologue to a longer series that wouldn't have been enough. You have to give the player something; anything. You can't just stack mystery upon mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: In short:- If you expect an RE/SH experience: You will be disappointed.- If you expect an interesting adventure mystery game with easy-to-medium difficulty puzzles: You will love this.- Expect horror? The game has its emphasis elsewhere in storytelling and that field it does surprisingly well.This has potential to be the "next Siberia" series so to speak in my opinion, but with more varied gameplay.***Longer review:Small team did miracles with this, but even with its flaws this is a charming game for adventure game fans.Strengths:- Three dimensional protagonist that has her struggles and concerns/fears living as the only person in the town, alive.- Puns and humor are there to balance and protect her sanity and the toll the events have taken on her.- The background, events, town, locales are very well detailed.- Good enough game mechanics.- Authentic feel of the art and locations where the events take place.- Good blend of puzzles.- Surprisingly good level of animation.Weakness: - Short.- Some premises could have been taken further in the storytelling(spoiler free).- Shows they had a possible sequel in mind, and if this doesn't happen I'll start rioting.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to be brief. I don't recommend the game. I put "thumbs up" to support the developers, who I hope will read my comment.I'm an system's analyst, developer; have experience in writing, working in the media and several environments. I'm also very much a gamer. So I will try to give my point of view in a constructive way. I see a lot of work was put into this game There were plenty of good ideas laid on the table. Interesting mechanics, a lot of things to take advantage of.Main issue:-----------Guys, whenever you write a script for a video game, movie, etc.: Define a scope. A "circle" that states what is IN the game and what is OUT. Rule of thumb: Do not define THE story of the game as something that is OUTSIDE the scope: Who cares about Pierre? Who cares about his music, his instruments, his... everything? He is NOT within the scope of the game, same as all the 15 minutes of story that you tell in the "memories" tapes. Players don't buy your game to know if Pierre likes espresso or cappuccino.What you did basically is: making a game where you control a lifeless character, that gives obvious (not very clever) comments now and then and has no purpose other than to serve as an instrument for things that are out of the game!! You took plenty of great work and ideas, and wasted them in a VERY lazy way.This was the biggest mistake.Features:---------- Art: Very well done, plenty of work put there. Very detailed environments, full of decoration. A lot to see!- Technical Aspect: Again, a lot of work put there, plenty of mechanics. Inventory, upgrade, puzzles, shooting, etc.- Design: Same lot of work.Issues:-------What happened? You over did it. You added 2, 3, 4 cameras... I don't even know how many. No need for that. No need for having cameras following you, flying, travelling, 1st person, shoulder, semi-static. No. No, no, no. Again: define your scope, define your game. What do you want the player to experience? Resident Evil or Alone in the Dark? Shooter, point & click, or what? Sometimes less is more. You cannot have it ALL.Put 1 (ONE) good camera. Fixed. Design it good. It will work. Check Tormented Souls. It works.As you were building the game, you got ideas and turned them into mechanics (1st the breaker boxes, then the rain, then the levers and items, then the weather change, etc. etc.) All good ideas and good executions. But you cannot have them all properly. As you progressed developing and focused on certain mechanics, you forgot about the others. Same with the upgrade system for the weapon that served no purpose. Same for the 8pm -> go to sleep curfew.You built plenty of screens (rooms, areas) that do nothing. Serve no purpose. Why? They are visually nice, tons of work. But what for? To burden the player walking throw them? Certain sequences (bell tower) could have been simplified from 5 screens to 1.No characters: Usual lazy approach. Developers need to understand that this, while making things much easier, cripple the games. It's very limiting not having ANYONE to talk with, to help you or to help. It makes the game a huge desert where nothing really happens. Next time: you need to add NPCs.A couple extra details: ------------------------ Movements / controls. It never worked. But you know it already. I understand, it can happen. Next time it will be better, I'm sure. It has to be better.- Performance: Could have been better optimized. It runs at 40-50 fps (in 4K) in a modern machine.Positive elements:-------------------- Great ideas: All the research, spy stuff, radio, signals, mystery, maps, interactions, etc. That was VERY good.- Puzzles: Quite good. Not impossible, not super simple.- Secrets: many.- Graphics: Very good, effects, and all.- Sound: Quite decent.Future:-------You have ALL what is required. The ideas, the technical skills, the resources. You can make a great game. Don't over do it. Don't start adding things like patches. Design it from the beginning or just leave it out.Make the action happen IN the game, and not before or after it.

_childDocuments_.review: I want  to recommend this game but after spending the time I did in game I just can't. The story OK the mood great, the puzzle mini game is nice. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, over the shoulder view, mouse and keyboard controls, normal mode. This game is an adventure game, it is not a psychological horror, or even really a thriller game, but a 3D point and click adventure game where you interact with objects and put together very obscure clues to learn about what is going on.The puzzles are enjoyable, the combat is basically a mini-game that feels like there was more planned with it (Has a crafting and upgrade system that I literally had no need to use, and the trailer shows this sick looking fight with a giant squid that unless it is locked behind an optional side mission I did not get to partake in that encounter), but the real issue I have with the game is what many others have... the story... One of my biggest pet peeves in game design is playing a game that does not feel complete. I do not mean length, and I do not mean mechanics that feel like an afterthought, I mean when the game is over, you actually feel like you're not done playing your current game. Ending on a cliffhanger is okay, but the questions that get asked or that the player in this case should be asking throughout the play-through seem to be completely ignored in order to tease more content. Much more effective story telling leaves out the bigger picture things and throws a piece of it at the end for the cliffhanger but provides answers to everything going on that is in front of you.While I enjoyed the puzzles and the atmosphere, this is not a practice I intend to support when it comes to storytelling and games, and it was just too blatantly done on purpose.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: According to the store page, Broken Pieces was developed by a team of only 5 people, so with that in mind, it's a pretty impressive achievement. Sadly, this game seems to have flown completely under the radar. It definitely deserves more attention!The game was designed for a fixed camera view, but the latest update added a 3rd person mode. You can choose the camera placement at the start of the game, but you cannot change it afterwards. I actually really like this addition. Fixed camera angles may have made sense in the past with 2D environments, but now that everything is 3D, it's just so much nicer to enjoy the beautiful scenery with free camera control of 3rd person. I actually really wish that Syberia 3 and 4 had this option.There is another reason why I brought up Syberia though. While the screenshots may give the impression that this is a survival horror game, it really isn't. It feels and plays more like a traditional adventure game with some basic combat on top. While the situation that the protagonist Elise finds herself in is terrifying, there are absolutely no traditional scares for the player. There is hardly any inventory management either. There are two bullet types: low quality and high quality. HQ bullets deal more damage, while the LQ bullets are infinite. While it is possible to run out of inventory space, you will rarely ever have to drop anything for the sake of something else. There is also a chest at your home to store excess loot at. Any junk items placed there will get converted to high quality bullets overnight.Enemies can spawn randomly in certain predesignated areas. Unlike most survival horror games, they cannot be avoided, as a barrier gets created, trapping Elise and her enemies in an arena of sorts. The only way to escape this arena is to defeat all the enemies. Infinite bullets come in handy in this case, because you will never be able to find or craft enough high quality bullets to deal with all the enemies. The combat is simple, although the dodge mechanic feels a bit janky and unpredictable.The game has several time and weather manipulation mechanics. These are used to solve puzzles. Most of the puzzles are simple, which is a good thing in my opinion. The game is also on a timer of sorts. The time between 08:00 and 20:00 is considered safe, but everything outside of that is dangerous and Elise will refuse to explore further, insisting to go home "before it gets dark". There doesn’t appear to be a penalty for taking your time, besides missing out on one achievement that wants you to beat the game in 5 in-game days.You can save the game by sitting down on a bench. You can also rest to heal on those benches, but doing so will consume 2 hours.Voice acting is good, the puns are great, the story is interesting, although the ending leaves us more questions than answers. The story absolutely needs a sequel or an expansion pack at the very least.I would recommend this game to adventure any game fan. If you are looking for a survival horror game, this may not be quite what you're looking for, but it's still worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: The exploration and puzzles known in adventure games are somewhat compelling. The combat, however, is frustratingly shallow and unresponsive and should have been kept out of this game. If you want to play the game, play in Reduced Combat mode. The story is interesting for the most part, but unfortunately, the ending feels anticlimactic and unrewarding considering the buildup.As both story and gameplay are lacking, I do not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces starts off with all the marks of being an interesting game with a compelling story, but in the end it all comes down to ugly storytelling and repetitive gameplay, not to mention the sluggish ending. The game just can't get into the storytelling. Broken Pieces tries to make me empathize with the main character and some guy named Pierre, but the only way of doing it is "let's say every few minutes how the main character misses Pierre" and that's it. Who is Pierre? Why should I empathize with him and the heroine? Let the player think it out himself between solving the same type of puzzles over and over again and boring fights against phantoms.Also it's worth to mention bugs, which game is still full of. Especially if you try third person mode, which can softlock you walkthrought in curtain point of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: If Jacques Demy and François Truffaut adapted Richard Matheson’s I Am Legend as a computer game… and were so overcome by good French wine, food and sunshine that they forgot to make an ending… that game would be Broken Pieces.The combat is awkward (a common problem for indie Fixed Camera games!) and the narrative ends somewhat abruptly (maybe Broken Pisces would be a better name?), but Elsewhere Experiences fixed multicam survival-horror-lite is absolutely worth playing for its sense of place and time (1991, a fictional remote coastal French village!) and the lonely, wistful atmosphere conjured by audio diaries and sad gallic rock…!The (Unreal Engine) visuals are absolutely splendid - the game reeks of the refined, sedate decay of a beautiful little fishing village whose prime has long past, yet still retains a vibrant (though now, suddenly missing) community. Here you will find religious conspiracies, illegal military maneuvers and some very entertaining puzzles.It's somewhat unfortunate that Elise never gets to cycle around the countryside taking potshots at ghostly soldiers, but the village of St. Exile works quite well as a limited Metroidvania, especially when combined with a faux-24hr cycle (which adds a small charge of urgency to the explorations). Do play this on an SSD, if you can, however.Try the French voice acting… it's a swift-acting madeline to secondary school French classes! Unfinished, a little awkward but... on the whole... genial. =)PS: Be sure and finish your side missions before attempting to use some sea charts...!
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: I WANT to recommend this game.   I WANT to encourage more people to create games like this.  But I just can't.*)  Camera angles and movement are just way too weird and janky.  Walking along, camera sorta behind the shoulder and above you - all of a sudden changes to a different angle.   AND the direction in which you had been holding the left stick to move Elise is all of a sudden pointing in a different direction, OFTEN the way you just came!  So you hafta hold the stick in one direction, wait for the camera angle to change at some arbitrary location along the path, then quickly move the stick in a different direction, just to keep moving straight ahead.*)  "Hot spots", where you can interact with the environment, are usually - but not always! - indicated by a sort of glowing border, which means I ended up always circling around every object, pounding on the "interact" button, 'cuz I never knew when there might be something with which I could interact, but which wasn't identified as such.  At the very least, it should be consistent - either everything that you can interact with should be highlighted as you approach it, or else nothing should.*)  Strange inventory system with limited capacity.  Some items that I picked up were absolutely essential to make progress in the game, others were completely useless.  However, traveling back and forth to the storage box takes so much time (another sore point; time advances during the game, and forces you to return home every so often, even if it is inconvenient) that I ended up carrying a bunch around with me, not knowing if I would need it or not.  THEN I found more things, and couldn't pick them up because my inventory was full, so I had to go all the way back to the storage box, stash some things, then go all the way back just to pick up the thing I had just found (assuming I could remember where it was).  Towards the end of the game, there wasn't even any room in my storage box, so I had to just throw some things away (and hope they weren't necessary for future puzzles).**)  One more sore point about the inventory - you are only allowed to carry ONE "heavy" item, and I found myself carrying, for example, a lever (which I would eventually need, but not now), and then stumble across a valve-turning wheel (which I DID need right then), but I couldn't pick up the wheel because I was carrying a lever.  When I went back to the storage box, and stashed the lever there, and later found an axe (another "heavy" item), I couldn't stash the axe in the storage box AND I couldn't t take the lever out of the storage box.  Weird, clunky, annoying - I would even say buggy (game crashed two times while my storage box was open; see below).*)  MINI SPOLIER ALERTAs you progress through the game, you find several mini-puzzles that can be used to earn tokens that can be exchanged for prizes.  After quite a lot of work, and accomplishing side tasks, several of the prizes are completely useless, and just take up space in your inventory.*)  END SPOILER ALERTThe game literally crashed on two separate occasions, causing me to restart from the most recent saved point.  Also, I encountered a bug (somehow walked into a location that was supposed to be inaccessible, and I couldn't get back out) that required me to quit the game and restart.*)  The layout of the town and buildings is moderately complex and inter-connected -- which is great! -- but, while my younger self would have liked getting some large sheets of dot-matrix printer paper and made sketches of the village and its pathways, having an in-game map feature would have been a tremendous help.*)   Way way too much trudging back and forth; I found myself wondering sometimes if the developers made a mental note of how many different locations there are in the game, and purposely contrived the missions and tasks so that you absolutely had to go back and forth re-visiting each location many many different times.   No "lightning mode" or any sort of "run" button either.*)  Even on the "easy" combat setting, I was unable to survive a few encounters, and ended up watching part of a video playthrough just to see what happened.   Combat is really annoying; it doesn't seem to serve any purpose, I never - not even once! - got the "dodge" or "repulse" button ton my controller to do anything, and a few dream-like encounters were simply impossible for me to survive - I thought I was safely avoiding danger zones, but I still ended up taking hits anyways (and the only way to heal is BETWEEN battles, not during).*)  When all is said and done, I'm still not even sure I understand what supposedly happened during the story.Please try again, but get rid of all the annoying things, and just make a nice exploration puzzle solver next time...UPDATE -- UPDATE.  Ok, so apparently the developers have released a patch which addresses at least a few of the issues that I have complained about, so in all fairness things MAY be a little bit better now.  However, I most likely will never know, since I don't think I'm ever going to re-play this game, running around everywhere, picking up this and that, solving those mini-games, etc...  If only I had waited until AFTER they had (supposedly) fixed some of these issues before I decided to play it...

_childDocuments_.review: This became one of my favorites adventure games of recent. The area you start in is beautiful, a small French village and you get to explore all of it. But there is something dark going on, and you need to find out what. There is a nice sci-fi element to the game and story, which makes it even more intriguing and mysterious. There are also some nifty puzzles, but none too hard. And every so often you will meet a board game puzzles that you can solve for rewards later on. There is also an element of day/night, which is done really cleverly. It's a game with a big heart, and with such a small team behind it, it really feels much bigger. Very much recommended if you like any kind of adventure/exploration/puzzle games, with a bit a of action in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces contains a bunch of different parts that come together well, even if none of its individual bits are outstanding. Visually it looks nice with plenty of detail, useful alternate camera angles, and neat weather variations. The adventure components fit together the best, with some good puzzles and steady exploration of a beautiful coastal town through a few zones. Cassette tapes fill in the many gaps in the story, even if the start lacks context and the ending is too sudden. Inventory annoyances, a missed opportunity with the day-night cycle, and the bland combat are the biggest blemishes that players must endure. But those looking for a lightweight adventure should still enjoy this walk by the sea.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky movement, weak story telling, horrible combat and abstract sci-fi time loop crap, combined with puzzles that had me running around aimlessly, back and forth due to lack of information. _childDocuments_.review: I played this in VR with the UEVR mod + the 'behind the shoulder view'  game update, which take the game to a whole new level of immersion. I was very surprised by the quality of this title, really polished and excellent in pretty much every aspect. VR made it even more special and almost felt as if the game was always meant to be played that way.THE GOOD- Superb artistic design- Great sound- Fantastic puzzles with just the right amount of difficulty - Exploration is great, the way places connect to each other, the views, everything about it makes exploring the town a real pleasure- Very interesting story until the end (which I didn't quite understand, truth be told)- I loved having to go back to the house from time to time, it felt real and it made me feel I was really a part of that world)- The weather changes was a very nice touch- Great graphics (that look way more amazing in VR where you can really appreciate all the work that was put into them). Lots of memorable places like the Church.- It offers a relatively small town but it's packed with things to see and places to visit which IMO just works much better than a much bigger place where roaming around could become boring or repetitive. Perfect size to make you feel immersed in the story it tells, I loved that.THE BAD- The ending. I didn't particularly enjoy it and would have liked a better explanation of what happened. Not bad in a way that ruined the game, far from that, but it just wasn't up to the quality of everything else up to that point. THE UGLY- Combat. Not bad but nothing too special either, just ok. It's not an action game so even if it was removed completely the game would have been just as good. It offers some nice change of pacing from the exploration, though,  so it was fine, I kind of enjoyed it despite not being by any means the best part about the game.I deeply enjoyed this game and will be looking forward to any new projects by this team. It was a fantastic exploration/puzzle game which reminded me in many ways of the old Resident Evil games, which is a big compliment, by the way. Certainly a must-have title if you're into good exploration and puzzles.The 'behind the back' camera option should have been there from the beginning, it makes the game way more immersive that way though the fixed-view system is also very well done and even more reminiscent of the RE games I was mentioning before. A matter of preference but personally even though I love the classic style I prefer the behind the shoulder perspective.And if you can play this in VR please do so, it enhances everything about the game in a way that turns it into something truly special.  the mod works perfect with it, no tinkering needed, no issues whatsoever. Press a button and you're good to go, totally worth it, it's like playing a different game almost.Congrats to the team for their game, it should be way more popular than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Another lovely adventure game that I'm glad to have played.The best part is definitely the mystery presented. I took my time to gather anything that could help me understand what happened. And I would say it was well worth it. The premise (at least from what I can piece together) here is that you play as Elise who recently moved together with her boyfriend Pierre (who is mysteriously gone) to this coastal french village in the 90s. Apparently the village has a rich history of cultists, government intrigue, and sci-fi research and all these things collide at some point before the game starts. All of that just made more intrigued and want to play through the game.As for the gameplay, the best aspect would definitely be the puzzles and lore gathering. Elise is a great narrator and her commentary was cool, even if the english translation felt too literal from the original french script. Like it was a word by word translation. Still good enough though. There is combat here and before the 1.3 patch was all reliant on old school fixed camera and "tank" controls, meaning character movement can easily be inverted depending on the camera angle. Good thing there's an option to essentially remove all but the tutorial and story related combat encounters. Otherwise, there would be what felt like random enemy spawns anywhere and at any point in the game. Even after the 1.3 patch adding in an over-the-shoulder camera, I would say I don't like the combat. So best to just turn on the lessen combat option from the start.Speaking of the 1.3 patch for a new camera option, that brings me to next best part about the game and it's the visuals. Even with the old fixed camera mode, I could tell this game has fantastic visuals. The new over-the-shoulder camera just made me appreciate the visuals even more. There is incredible detail even in the little stuff in this game. Great job devs! Also, major plus to the music. Love that I can pick and play tracks whenever I want.Overall, this game was great. Hopefully we get a continuation or something as I felt the ending wasn't enough to sate my curiosity about the mystery here.
