_childDocuments_.review: You can tell a ton of love went into this game with the storyline, lots of good dialog and "facts" about the town and it's inhabitants and the TAPES system was really cool. Plus I love interacting with machines and hearing mysterious broadcasts from another time. Some of the locations were big and cool. However the Church was too big and confusing. The graphics were really very nice but many of the doors and gates looked the same so a MAP would have been essential here! Way too much back-tracking and the some of the puzzles like the Furniture puzzle was absolutely terrible. Could've added a Skip button to the table puzzles. The TASK system was brilliant but still on more than several occasions I had no clue where to go or what to do next to the point I had to consult walkthroughs and even videos. It would've been nice if Ellie game some verbal clue or there was a hint button. The fact she was completely alone the entire game made it somewhat isolating and lonely and what the hell happened at the end? It never really explained it.. or did it? Don't know. Overall this was a very nice game. I found myself wanting to play it often. I would recommend but definitely not my top 10. Still a very good beautiful game. I hope this team makes more and they listen to our feedback and improve.

_childDocuments_.review: pl:Tak, ale:+ grafika+ ogólnie udany klimat miasta w połowie lat 90++ muzyka, chyba najjaśniejszy punkt gry, to utwory Pierre`a znajdowane na kasetach w grze-- system walki, wyłączcie to, nie wnosi to nic poza irytacją- podział na dni, tak jak poganianie gracza tym, że musi wrócić do domu o godzinie bodaj 20 max, bo inaczej stwory na ulicach, przez co gra staje się festiwalem loadingów- brak mapy w grze, za pomocą której po odblokowaniu drogi można by się teleportować do danego miejsca, zafiksowana kamera sprawia że będziecie się w tej grze po prostu gubić do samego końcaSama historia, z jednej strony mogła być ciekawa, z drugiej, sposób w jaki została przedstawiona sprawia, że się nią po prostu zmęczycie.Gdybym miał ją do czegoś przyrównać, to jest to Medium w wykonaniu medium (hehe), tzn. budżetowa wersja gry blooberów.Mimo wszystko, myślę że twórcy dobrze zdawali sobie sprawę z wad swojej gry, sugeruje to możliwość wyłączenia tych nieszczęsnych elementów walki, i to jaki ona ma ostateczny kształt jest efektem kompromisu pomiędzy zróbmy to dobrze, a zróbmy to teraz, bo nam się pieniądze kończą. Mimo wszystko, polecam jako eksperyment, nie do końca udany, ale ekspryment, i liczę że już kolejna gra w pełni wydobędzie potencjał studia, bo on tam jest. eng:Yes, but:+ graphics+ overall atmosphere of the city in the mid-90s++ the music, probably the brightest point of the game, is Pierre's songs found on in-game cassettes-- the combat system, turn it off, it give you nothing but annoyance- divide game into days, rushing the player with the fact that he must return home at probably 20 max, otherwise creatures on the streets, making the game a festival of loading- The lack of a map in the game, and teleport to a particular place, the fixated camera means that you will simply be lost in this game until the very endThe story itself, on the one hand, could have been interesting, on the other hand, the way it was presented makes you simply tired of it.If I had to compare it to something, it's Medium, a budget version of the bloobers game.Nonetheless, I think the developers were well aware of the flaws in their game, this suggests the ability to turn off combat elements, and what shape it ultimately takes is the result of a compromise between let's do it right and let's do it now, because we're running out of money. Nonetheless, I recommend it as an experiment, not entirely successful, but an experiment, and I hope that the next game will already bring out the studio's full potential, because it's there.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and great game! Def not survival or psychological horror so don't be mislead by the tags :|It's more of a mystery action game with mby some very light "horror" elements (don't except anything like Silent Hill or Outlast or to be scared generally)+ Great puzzles and side things to do. Very nice job devs!!+ Nice story+ Great location (wish there was more areas tho)+ Mystery from start which u try to uncover during the game. Very well done!- Game is kinda short (took me ~5-6h do beat it on my first play)- Some tapes u can only get after sleeping a few times after something happens which I think means u won't be able to beat the game in 5 in-game days and get 100% game (not a problem since u can easily beat it in 5 days and reload before beating and going to sleep a few more times for the last tapes :P)- Areas in which u can't run :| luckily if u enter them while holding shift u trigger a bug and run instead of walking- Combat is 2 simple and since the enemies just appear there is no feeling of threat while just playing (ok they can appear almost anytime but once they do u see the fog blocking an exit or something)- Only 1 enemy type and no boss fights (altho there is something interesting and optional where u could get a somewhat of a boss fight)Rnd note: 'Hide and Seek' tape is a bit bugged. _childDocuments_.review: "Broken Pieces" is a fun and entertaining mystery adventure game.The story is engaging as you play the character Elise. Elise has to solve the mystery surrounding why time has stopped in a small french coastal town named Saint-Exil. The mystery is slowly unravelled as she collects clues, items, and cassette tapes. The only catch is "time". Elise has to get back her home by 8pm every evening or else she will be attacked by ghostly military soldiers that appear through thin air.Time does fly by quickly when it takes one hour and a half to walk to a certain area in elapsed time. In addition, two hours in elapsed time is deducted when she rests on a bench to either save the game's progress and/or recover her health points after a battle with the ghost soldiers.The puzzles in this game do require some brain power but are easy to solve. The firearm combat against the ghostly military soldiers is challenging.I really love the "save game" function in this game. All you have to do is find a bench and when Elise sits down, it saves your progress. No worries about having to restart at the beginning of a certain area or restarting from Elise's home again.The graphics in the "Broken Pieces" world are beautiful, detailed, and top-notch. I love it when Elise uses her powers to change the weather from summer to winter to solve certain puzzles in the game.  In addition, there are three different angles you change to during game play that will make you visually see how beautiful and detailed the Saint-Exil village really is.I highly recommend this game for the story, setting, mystery, Elise, and the beautifully detailed world of Saint-Exil.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give it a "neutral" review if that was possible. I really liked the setting, views and the music in this game. Some of the mechanics had a cool concept to it, the other were quite repetitive. Puzzles and things you need to get to progress weren't difficult, and you got a lot of clues along the way. Combat is the worst part of the game, it's terrible and clunky.  Limited inventory in a way that you needed to get rid of stuff to pick up story items was really annoying. The ending was a big disappointment. I think that this game has a lot of unused potential, it sets you up in a fascinating setting, but ultimately doesn't tell you much in the end, which is a bummer. I just wish it was more polished - specially the story telling.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like this is an interesting game that is being held back by a few gameplay elements that would've otherwise made it a good game.  To get a potential misconception out of the way, this is more of an adventure game along the lines of a point-and-click adventure than a third person shooter with exploration/adventure elements.  While it does have combat, given the lack of weapon, enemy variety/tactics, and interesting combat scenarios along with the sparseness in encounters, it does feel like a filler that is meant to prevent back-tracking from becoming dull rather than serve as an interesting gameplay segment.  I wouldn't necessary say there needs to be more or longer and intense fighting, but making each encounter a little more cerebral would've been nice.   Also, doesn't help that the dodging and repel mechanic seem a bit unreliable, and that may be because it's hard to judge distances to enemies when using the classic view.The adventure and exploration aspect of the game is comparatively more well done.  The environment and audio design are much better than I was expecting, and the puzzles and their tie in with the story are fun and interesting.  The lore and story is well thought out, and the mystery pulled me in.  These are all definitely the highlight of the game.  The one unsatisfying part is it feels like the ending didn't quite hit the narrative payoff that I was anticipating, not necessarily from the idea that all plot/lore points need to be resolved, but more from the perspective of what the main character would be doing next or what would happen to her .  Felt like the ending could've lasted at least a minute longer.  This is probably the biggest point that's holding the game back for me from being good.As for a few other issues, first, not sure why there needs to be a restriction on the number of heavy items being carried or at least allow two of them to be held in the inventory.  Also, ran into an issue where I wasn't able to put more than one heavy item into the chest in order to swap for the one that I wanted to carry which felt like could've soft locked me from continuing the game; fortunately this happened at the end of the game when I didn't need them anymore.  Next, for the over the shoulder camera view, it feels like the using the mouse has a deadzone and acceleration that makes it hard to use (should just be raw mouse input) and the default sensitivity for analog stick didn't feel right which was why I opted to play in the classic view instead.  If I wasn't already used to the classic style in other games, I imagine playing this way would've been really off-putting to the game experience.  Felt like more attention should have been given for this addition, given its emphasis in the 1.3 update.  Lastly, feels like the performance can be better in some places, particularly in the optional combat areas.Overall, although I do feel a bit let down by the execution of the ending, I enjoyed the game and feel like this would still appeal to those who like adventure games.  However, for those who are looking for an adventure with equally interesting combat, unfortunately the combat is not quite there.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces is... a weird one. This is one of those moments where I wish we had a more granular system of rating as opposed to the binary "yes/no recommend." I do think it's worth playing but you have to understand what you're getting into. I initially thought this would be a survival horror kind of game, and on the surface that's the look and feel the game has going for it. But in reality I'd liken this more to something The Adventure Company may have made or published back a few years ago (think Secret Files: Tunguska, Syberia, Keepsake, etc), which in my eyes isn't a bad thing, since I quite enjoy those games, but if you were coming into this expecting a Resident Evil style challenge, you'll be very disappointed. To be positive, the game looks wonderful, it sounds great, the music is nice (except for the "songs" made by one of the characters, but that's more my taste than the quality itself), and I personally didn't really encounter any bugs aside from my character getting stuck once during my playthrough. I think the exploring and light key hunting/puzzling mechanics were an engaging enough backdrop to the mystery of the story, but I feel the combat is a bit ham-fisted. It never felt challenging, interesting, or diverse enough to justify itself, and only really served to slow the pace down. I think had this game been exclusively an adventure style title it would have been better for it. With that said, I quite like the story and all the mystery everything is surrounded in, but I think the pay off is inadequate at best. I'm no stranger to or detractor of open endings or things that require interpretation, but I don't think the narrative (while engaging in the moment) had enough thematic meat to really make an ending like that satisfying. The game's relatively bite sized though, so if you see it on sale though I'd say it's worth testing out to see if you dig it.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, I felt genuinely immersed by Broken Pieces. It actually puts many pieces of the great adventure game puzzle in all the right places: the visuals, the location design, the narrative, the gameplay mechanics (well, most of them) and the side activities altogether deliver an enjoyable experience. Not outstanding, but definitely worth its time.There is also a nice old-school feeling to this game. It has a bit of a Syberia (or maybe The Longest Journey) touch to it which I definitely loved. It could be because of a fixed camera angles in the first place but it still delivers this nostalgic 2000's experience.However, it's not all peachy. Broken Pieces could have ended in my favorite list if not for the several major shortcomings: - The bugs. The game has been released two years ago and it is still full of showstoppers. It took me three attempts to start a proper playthrough. At first, I started with the shoulder camera and was unable to get past the shooting cans tutorial as the game has just got stuck. So, I did a bit of reading and restarted my playthrough from the same slot but with the fixed camera only to realize that the saving of my progress is not working anymore. So, I had to restart again, but this time around from a different slot. - The combat mechanic. For some reason, it is becoming a norm in the modern adventure games to introduce some action-style gameplay element. In most cases, it fails miserably and Broken Pieces is no exception. The so-called combat here is a simplistic reaction-based minigame that is nothing but a major distraction as it suddenly spawns at random locations and times without prior warning. Thankfully, there is a reduced combat option in the settings to turn down this mess a lot. - Finally, the ending. For me it felt absolutely flat, without leaving any real emotions or thoughts to carry around for a few hours after completing the game. It definitely plays better than it ends.So as a final verdict, Broken Pieces is still worth your attention is 2024 if you're an old-school adventure games lover just like me. It is likely that you will get some 10-15 hours of an enjoyable playthrough but will not walk away completely satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game having played 21 hours. I am not anywhere near the finish. The ga,e has many glitches that are proving very irritating. Let me describe the glitches. This requires using the windows key on the keyboard and bringing the Steam interface forward. Secondly the WSAD keys really don't work. They don't keep track of the orientation of the Avatar, Elise. For example depending on the movement of Elise the W key may have her walking backwards. I had to switch to using a gamepad. No big deal. Lastly there have been numerous lockups and getting stuck physically in the game. The point of view button occasionally does screwy things like having the whole scene spinning in front of you with no apparent way to stop it. There are also the occasional screw ups where Elise is on one side of the wall and the scene remains on the other side.  I have been hoping these bugs could be fixed. The start up problem is constant but the other bugs occur say every 25% of the time you play. Its too bad because the plot is excellent and the visual impact is also excellent. _childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is a beautiful old school adventure game at its heart.  It felt like throwback to a 1990s adventure game, but updated to modern standards.If you love adventure games, and do not get bored easily searching around for items and solving puzzles, then this game is a 9 out of 10.  If you crave lots of action then this score will drop down to around a 5 or 6 out of 10.The graphics are absolutely gorgeous on ultra settings.The voice acting is superb, best I've heard in a long time.The story was really interesting also, but it is not spoon fed to you. You will have to piece together everything slowly over hours and hours of playtime, listening to tapes and reading documents.One thing I did not like was that there was no map option, I got lost often and could not figure out where to go.Most people do not have the patience these days to play games like this, but die hard adventure gamers will surely be rewarded!

_childDocuments_.review: Offbeat indie title here that combines Resident Evil/Silent Hill camera work (with actual switchable fixed angles!  Pretty cool!), gorgeous yet desolate scenery ala Kona and Firewatch with a plot-line that toys with post-apocalyptic Omega Man/Logan's Run sorta themes...and there's a dash of tentacled Lovecraftian malice bubbling under the skin.  Everything that I mentioned is something I enjoy quite a bit, so Broken Pieces was an instant pick-up whenever screenshots and the Steam bio caught my eye more than they do on just any random underground title.  It's got some hitches but this is certainly a unique piece of work and I had mostly fun with its measured exploration + puzzle solving + world building + time management + combat (the weakest link).  So, come along with me and let's have a few martini's on the fantasy French coast line (you can down the martini's, I'll stick with the sourmash!).  You play as Elise who's been living alone in a house in a fictional French coastal village that's nearly completely abandoned.  It seems everyone in the town was taken by a dark force and only the echoes of what and who once was whispers in the air around you.  Our heroine must make forays across the village and landscape to stay alive and uncover the creepy plot of what happened to her boyfriend and those in the town who were missing.  You'll run, climb, changed the weather (neat mechanic there with awesome graphical changes), pull switches, rest in bed to avoid the hostile darkness and even shoot it out with hostile ghost soldiers that make your life hell, especially if you decide to stay out after night.  Time is a very effective mechanic with a day/night cycle that will have you checking your watch (yes, also a game mechanic!) as the tension of even more frequent appearances of hostiles is a huge likelihood during dusk's suffocating embrace.  There's a main plot line here of Elise's ambition to find out where the hell everyone living went while trying to utilize the town's numerous locations to aid her quest.  Whether it's powering up systems at the lighthouse, uncovering and working with projector maps and tape players in a spy's former hideout near your property or even delving into the depths of a freaky gothic church (one of the game's best set-pieces) to find out what secrets there and why a large gathering at the place of worship never left the building.  You'll literally do all kinds of puzzle solving from the traditional to the imaginative and I felt that the systems, player controls and solutions were mostly engaging and fun to figure out for each one; pulling switches, using your psychic weather abilities to use rain to drop bridges or summoning snow to make new paths reachable, you'll need axes to chop down trees, tools or keys to break gates.  Even if the hazy plot didn't always make my intentions clear, I liked that I was always using different puzzle solving techniques.  Not only do you get a main narrative here that's the primary goal but you can unfold it on your pace while doing several categories of side missions that reveal all sorts of lore about the world.  I got an even 10 hours out of the game until completion, finishing 10 out of 14 achievements and yet the game's still on my desktop, beckoning me to find the rest of the tape recordings that flesh out the rest of the story or tie up a couple of other loose ends.  Going back to the tape player for a second, you can listen to tapes recorded and left of your beau's music, tapes uncovered by the spy, tapes from people that existed in this world and it all goes down in real time.  Elise can drift off into these moments while sitting on a bench to save and recover health, while tackling the locale's gorgeous terrain, milling about your house and having a drink from the fridge, etc.  It's a cool, seamless aspect of the gameplay that fits perfectly with the material on offer here.  As I mentioned, there's combat in Broken Pieces and not to jump on the dogpile but it was the weakest part of the action.  I don't think it's as terrible as some though its strange nature is a mix of disparate ideas that don't always gel.  You'll get jumped by foes and herded into a general perimeter to fight in; the battles popping up like an old Final Fantasy/Dragon Warrior RPG dice roll.  You'll raise your weapon to shoot and aim at foes like survival horror while throwing in some of your mixed moves like dodges, a wide ranging area attack, or just scoring more accurate shots with upgrades found in the game world, etc. to crush your opposition.  Despite all of this it feels weird and a bit too arcade-y for its own good.  It's hard to explain.  I didn't mind the style but I just found it odd.  The constant threat of it at night does add a desperation to reach home as quickly as you can and certain shortcuts that you might want to take will eat up a lot of extra time in the exchange of shortening the distance.  It's this cool trade-off for the decisions you make and getting killed at night is a very possible thing...the constant fighting putting a steady hurt on your health since dodging is dodgy (oh you're damn right I finally threw in a crummy pun!) at best.  I will say that the foundation of a cool combat loop is totally built into Broken Pieces' foundation but it needs some fine-tuning.  I could say more about all of the various tasks and things to do on the French coast but I think a lot of it should be left a surprise because I didn't even touch on some of the other missions that you can undertake.  The price is a little thick on the game but there is content and things to do to back it up...which is damn nice to see.  Ontop of that, the presentation of the world sucked me in.  The graphics are nice on the eyes and these fine 5 folks did great work on creating a classic-feeling, interconnected world that threads survival horror camera work and 3rd person dread into a world that can both be awe-inspiring and threatening.  Each location has its own distinct personality and it does a lot for the world-building.  Sound is also exceptional; the tapes you listen to all trippy musically, or fitting when other unique (but unmet) characters are introduced.  I also thought Elise's voice actor did a solid job.  She had big shoes to fill being the only living, present character in the story and the emotions from serious to bits of humor never got on my nerves. Broken Pieces was a cool ride and one I plan on finishing up a few more tasks in.  It's imperfect but hypnotizing, frustrating yet satisfying and serene n' subtle though eerie.  I can't say I've played anything like it and I'm glad I picked it up.  Just don't expect survival horror grade combat and come for the puzzles, explorations and atypical mix of puzzles/abilities and I think you'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with: I had fun playing it for most of the time. It's a slightly positive review, close to being neutral. _childDocuments_.review: I think Elsewhere Experience has crafted something quite remarkable here. Benoît Dereau, a level architect on Arkane's original Dishonored, co-heads the studio's first effort: an amalgamation of survival horror's fixed camera angles, the intuitive puzzle design of point-and-click adventure games and fast-paced combat not unlike Remedy's Alan Wake. I am especially fond of the game's interchangeable weather system, which is a welcome layer of surrealism that adds variety to puzzles and level design. Broken Pieces isn't entirely successful, however. I did encounter some visual bugs in an otherwise gorgeous looking game that competes quite well against larger titles, and I was a bit unhappy to have Elise blurt out the solution to a puzzle; additionally, while some reviews complain about the overall ambiguity of the game's plot, I would have actually preferred a bit more, to be honest. Some of the otherworldly sights on display in this game are stunning, often resembling paintings in texture and atmosphere, so I found a bit of that upended when the game shed light on some of its inner workings, though I understand it may not have been the intent of its developers to obscure every aspect of Broken Pieces' narrative. Above all I am eager to see what Elsewhere does in the future, whatever that may be.

The story is there also although kinda weird and takes a bit to build up to it. One huge downside is many items in game that you interact with are in what i am guessing is french and rather hard to know what to do as i do not know french. Aside from that it seems pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Think twice before buying this game.Almost nothing about this game works. I guess the atmosphere is nice and that's all.An annoying heroine who makes ridiculous bad jokes about literally everything around her.Bad voice acting.A plot that explains nothing at the end.There are a ton of bugs, some of them will not even allow you to complete the game, you will have to start over.Ridiculous opponents and battles.There are few locations, but even in them it’s easy to get lost, how bad backtracking is.And riddles... after the Church location the game begins to collapse. I'm not even sure that some riddles have solutions inside the game, only in the official guide.The only good thing about the game is Bryan Dechart (Connor from Detroit: Become Human), who voices a secondary character.But it is obvious that the developers really tried their best and maybe in the future I will replay the game again, despite everything the atmosphere really saves the day. _childDocuments_.review: I'm in two minds about Broken Pieces. On the positive side, I really like exploring the lush coastal setting with its detailed graphics, listening to the many tapes scattered about and having the ability to mess with the weather is unique. The protagonist is nicely modelled with a welcoming soft voice and the dialogue never gets on your nerves - it's short and sweet. It's a shame her mouth doesn't move when she talks but I've become accustomed to it now. The ball and block puzzles are fun and it felt satisfying completing the two I've found so far. On the negative side, I'm not enjoying the combat (I wanted to play it the way it's supposed to played). I guess I could of restarted afresh in exploration mode but I was a few hours into the game before I realised just how much of a slog it is shooting phantoms for the umpteen time (reminiscent of the foes in Alan Wake) with the help of an auto-aiming gun that projects a gigantic cross hair. To make it worse, enemies re-spawn when revisiting an area and I soon figured it was a necessary evil in order to proceed. Additional to this, there are a few bugs and crashes that led me to frustration (feeding the birds is one) and for now, I've put it aside until errors are ironed out. It's a tough game to rate because there are elements I really like and I think the devs have done a great job overall but right now I'm sitting on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative yes for adventure game fans on reduced combat mode. If only the combat wasn't so bad that its preferential to dial it down but this leaves the game without any meaningful combat at all.  It seems like the developers wanted to at least try to get things Resident Evil functional but ran out of time/budgetThe story and graphics are decent if you like this sort of thing but the game is fairly short <10 hrs. . Worth it at discount or bundle only

_childDocuments_.review: This game might look like a 3D action puzzler, but it has the soul of a point-and-click adventure. In mood, tone, and and pacing it most reminds me of the  series: beautiful, quiet, foreboding, mysterious. The protagonist is a pleasant companion on this journey, though it's never quite explained why this gentle young woman is so good with guns. Actually, very little is explained here and you might find the ending abrupt.What "point-and-click" means in terms of gameplay: lots of backtracking, little hand-holding, and many moments in which you might feel stuck. Conveniently, the game collects all the objectives and clues for you and you don't have to be a master code-breaker to finish the game. The optional objectives are a bit harder, though, and unfortunately one of them is buggy. For people who hate playing on a timer, be warned: there is one here. You do need to get home before dark. While you have a generous amount of time, the timer does cause some anxiety. I hate timers, but for me  was tolerable enough.The worst part of the game is the action: combat is annoying, repetitive, and just not fun. I could never get the "dodge" button to work and controls are generally unresponsive. This caused me to struggle with some of the harder optional areas. I suggest others not make my mistake and choose the "combat reduced" mode when starting the game (it's not the default). Get your action fix elsewhere, not here.And it's not the most stable game in the world. I had several crash-to-desktops.All in all,  has problems. Both gameplay and storytelling could have used more time in the oven. And yet I still found the game alluring: the puzzles are challenging, the town is charming, and the writing is decent. Despite the frustrations, I overall enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this straight: I'm not writing this review because I enjoy bashing on small indie studios but in the hope I can spare other players some disappointment and that maybe the devs learn from their mistakes and make a better game next time. Clearly, a lot of passion and talent went into making this game but in my opinion it just didn't work out.I played through this game after missing the two hour refund window. I had a bad feeling about it right from the start.You're thrown into this weird setting without any explanation, world building or character introduction. I'm expected to just accept what's going on, like that the main character can magically alter the weather somehow. And that it makes perfect sense to shoot bullets at ghosts apparently made of some kind of vapor. And that a small French village has electrically locked doors everywhere. It was already challenging my capacity to suspend disbelief.And when you later learn more about what's going on, it feels like too many mysterious things haphazardly thrown together. But I did feel slightly motivated to see where this was going.Unfortunately, nothing in this game was actually fun to play except George's puzzle tables.I found most puzzles to be either trivial or really difficult, simply because I missed a clue telling me to go to a seemingly unrelated location. In both cases, the puzzles where never interesting or fun. And there's so much walking and at a pace that just feels slightly too slow. I also found the layout of the world extremely confusing. Oh and by the way, taking the short-cuts is not optional because some might take you to places you cannot reach otherwise.The combat is awful as well. It's unresponsive and clunky and just not fun at all. At least you can lower the difficulty which makes it much less painful. The tacked-on crafting and survival mechanics are pointless and shouldn't be in the game at all.I ended up forcing myself to finish this in the hopes of maybe getting a somewhat satisfying ending that would tie up loose ends and give some explanations. Of course that didn't happen either. This game definitely needed better writing and game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was more story as the game seems to end right at the climax. The atmosphere is absolutely on point, and the mechanics such as the need to sleep every night do a good job of adding tension. The mystery is well done, and I was propelled through the plot by my need to uncover it. I did not do much side content during my playthrough as the puzzles required took additional time which seemed like a bad thing. The worst thing about the game is the combat; the dodge button never seemed to work, and there's only one enemy type. If I ever replay the game, I will definitely lower the combat as much as possible. In my opinion game is worth playing for the atmosphere alone, and the well crafted mystery adds to its appeal and helps make up for the combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces is an engaging mystery game. I had already played the demo, and immediately I wanted to delve into every corner and immerse myself in the story of the protagonist Elise. After playing the first quarter of the game, I'm already charmed by the soundtrack, the seaside environment, quite rare in a game, the gunfights with their simple but effective system, and the autonomy left to the player to solve the puzzles. It's nice to feel that we either have to go get the information, rather than have it brought to us on a platter. Basically, that's why we play, huh.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: A-Game has some rough spots but really a knock out effort.  Takes you all the way back to to intrigue of OG Alone in the Dark with the emphasis on story, puzzles, and characters with some combat.  The combat is arguably the least polished in the game; not including any combat sequences would've still made this game a fun adventure.  The upgrades were fun to track down but by the end, and I got them all, I didn't even need to use them.The level and sound designs are grade A efforts.  The ambiance in the game really added to the immersion.  Since the general feeling was creepy (but not scary) I would've loved more scenes like the church where the darkness by itself plays a character.For Adventure gaming and walking sim fans.  Story was fun, alluring, and keeping you guessing what's behind what door.  The twisting paths and metroidvania style pathing unlocks were fun.  Can't wait to see what you cook up next!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Broken pieces is a story about a woman named Elise who moved to a city with her boyfriend and the town was taken over by soldiers and a mysterious phenomenon that seems to keep the city at a stand still.This is more of a puzzle type game with some really bad combat. The combat is so clunky it’s better to just turn it down to explore mode where combat will be less frequent and easier. The puzzles are fairly easy to solve but can require you to run around the game to gather pieces of information or key items.You are also limited with how much you can explore as the game forces you to go back to your safe house as night falls to either avoid enemies or to read files to let you advance the story. This was okay at first but gets highly annoying later in the game when you are far away from your house and it takes you a couple of hours of in game time to return.Graphically the game looks decent and has quite a few locations to visit and revisit as you progress. The voice acting was good and probably the games strongest thing going for it.While this isn’t a bad game, it could have used more time to iron out some things like it’s terrible combat and clunky character movements. The story could use some fleshing out as well.6.5/10

I'm in the park near the house and everything is stuck - saying "I'm going to need something to break those" for everything. Game is caught in a loop, stuck. Can't proceed. Pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥, frankly. _childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces is a game set in an isolated French coastal village stuck in a temporal loop. You play as Elise, the sole remaining inhabitant, as you try to piece together what happened to the village and if you can break the curse it's under, with only cassette tapes for company. The game is a throwback to old school horror/thriller games, so it includes a limited inventory and fixed camera angles, as well as an emphasis on ammo conservation. I want to get this out of the way: most of the game isn't actually scary. It's more a mystery with  elements. However, while it won't deliver straight scares, it does an excellent job building an increasing sense of suspense and intrigue as each day passes; even though I couldn't quite follow the story all the time (the game requires you to do a LOT of reading and listening), I kept playing because I was genuinely fascinated with what the heck was going on. It also does a good job of using a time limit mechanic; Elise only has 12 hours a day to gather clues, and those hours tick by FAST; you will dread opening up your watch to make sure you aren't too late in the day to continue! My only complaint is the combat. While the game isn't TOO combat heavy, it feels extremely lacklustre, especially compared to games like the original Resident Evil. Simply put, the enemies aren't scary. You don't get up close and personal with any of them, there is no gore to hammer in how they will kill you dead, and they just flat out don't LOOK scary. They're more annoying, and encounters with them felt tedious rather than tense. It's almost pointless to even have combat in the game; you'd be better off playing on the combat free mode to just focus on the puzzles and story. Still, Broken Pieces is a slow burn mystery/thriller in the best sense of the word, and a great debut title from the developers; definitely worth checking out at least once. Or, TL;DR for those who want a quick summary if they should buy the game or not:

_childDocuments_.review: For this to be developed by such a small team, Broken Pieces is a great game. Very much like old school Resident Evil. Similar camera style. It has an engaging story and atmosphere. Challenging (but not TOO challenging) puzzles. I ran into one bug a couple of hours into my playthrough that I thought would make me start the game over. Luckily I was able to mess around a bit and workaround it, but one of the devs caught me playing it on stream and I was able to point out the bug to him. He assured me it would be fixed in the next patch. Now a minor downside to the game is the combat. It's not the best and can be a little annoying at times. It's a super simple combat system but it works for the most part. The rough combat doesn't ruin the game by any means. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys old school RE and puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: First two hours gameplay: So far I liked the overall experience, it's a modern take on classic games like RE and Silent Hil (or other similar classics that I am not aware), although I am not a big fan of fixed camera style, they added secondary camera and first person view which you can switch between in anytime, they help a little bit.The game has a unique way of story telling which I liked so far, it drops you in middle of nowhere without telling you why are you here or what happened, but slowly it tells pieces of the story by finding hints and clues during your gameplay which I think adds to the mystery of the game and make you feel good finding those information.Puzzles so far haven't been so hard and usually game tells you what to do or where to go in objective menu, I highly suggest listen to cassette tapes and interact with all objects to understand what is happening in game and find some clues.The only small negative that I can tell is about game progress and story telling speed, I think the game was little on slow side and during my two hours gameplay nothing major happened although it made me more interested to know what is happening in that city.Combat was not interesting so far, at least for me, maybe it gets more engaging and fun later but I feel combat is a secondary thing in this game.Visuals are really good and performance wise I didn't have any issues, turned on DLSS and was getting 150fps at least in most cases with 3090 at 1440p reolution.Overall I think this can be a good game and I am going to finish it and see what is happening under the sea!
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: First off, beautiful graphics, nice music, and decent voice acting, so that's good. was quite interesting, the mystery was intriguing, and I was interested in learning more about it. The tapes you get from going through the memory zones and all that were also a nice mechanic to learn more about it, and the tape controls made that easier as well, so that was great. Unfortunately, the closer I got to the ending, it didn't feel as if I had all the answers, or at least it didn't feel satisfying. I think that's because it leaves too much open, we can certainly assume some stuff, and we get some answers, but, especially with that ending, it just leaves with WAY more questions and nothing to answer them. So the story elements although were good and all, in my opinion, I would have loved to have gotten more answers, especially to do with the ending. was pretty nice, the daytime mechanic was interesting, making it more unique, George's little mini game tables were an interesting thing to do on the side as you explore to find more clues to the mystery. The combat was decent, with the rock powers being cool, although I never used them much. Puzzles were pretty good, overall it was cool, although speaking of puzzles, depending on the camera mode you chose one puzzle in particular was just straight up impossible, the boat license plate one, unless you pick the fixed camera point, you're out of luck, so for me who chose the camera over the shoulder, my only option was to look up the code, because there's no way I'm replaying the entire game for it, because the ONLY time you can choose the camera mode is at the start, you can't change it mid game, so that's a change they should do.Some other bits that I found interesting were, for example, the train mini game in the attic, a fun little thing to play through. I liked it., besides what I've already mentioned above, bugs, so many bugs, visual, audio, collision, controls, game-breaking, you name it, they got it. Pardon the size of this section as I'm gonna explain a bunch of them.Some I came across were voicelines being cut off, being able to see through the wall if your camera got close to it, for example, in the cliff in the lighthouse area, or seeing outside the map if you go to the bell tower and just look to the left a little bit, or a bit more difficult, looking to the right at an angle. The flower house had some weird collisions with being able to be a bit too into some stuff like the sofa, but these are all minor things, so here's some bigger ones.The house chest, I opened it, closed it, then opened my inventory and accidentally dropped some mushrooms because I kept forgetting that the button for closing the inventory was different. I picked up the mushroom and went away, all this while the chest was still highlighted. Every time I clicked, it would open the chest, no matter where I was. No worries though, easy fix, just go up to the chest, open it, and close it, but still, kinda annoying.In the crypt, if you're holding 2 circuit breakers like I was and grab more from the box, the game gives you 3, except it doesn't, the item maxes out at 4, so 1 gets thrown into the shadow realm, I guess.Now for the actual game-breaking ones.I cut down the tree by the church and started crossing it. The rain stopped, I think, just as I got off the tree on the other side with the special thing. As I was looking at it (standing normally on the ground) and was about to go to it, the screen did its white flash thing when the storm part is over, and when it did, I couldn't move, and was now stuck in the animation of getting off the tree, over and over again, I couldn't press any buttons, I couldn't move anywhere. The only thing I think I could do was move the camera, but you know what? Thinking back now, I don't think I could even do that. I was quite literally animation-locked, as I'll call it. The only solution was to close out of the game and reopen.Possibly relating to the above, after reloading in a bench on the other side of the church that you need to climb rubble to get to, I started going out to the tree again, and I went up to the church door in a roundabout way, going near the gate to some other place and then using the stairs up from the cemetary door, and I tried to go into the church, only for me to start falling through the map because the church map wouldn't load. As an aside, the outside map background goes from blue to white after a while, so that's neat. This is unrelated to anything; I just felt like mentioning it.At the very least, I could actually use buttons this time, so I could open the menu and load the game again. The worst part, however, It kept happening over and over again; different routes and different weather didn't matter, so I was forced to go the long way round of using the gate to leave the church area. This, however, won't be my last encounter with map loading failure, I'll get to that later.Speaking of the memory zone near the church, inside it, in the area where you choose where to go, specifically the one that has an axe that is out of reach because the gate is locked, which I assume is just decoration, If you go that route, I think it's the right side, you will get combat but there is no smoke stopping you like usual ahead, so you can just go through and the enemy AI bricks, if you get closer, they start walking again towards you only to be stopped by an invisible wall, which I assume is the smoke. You can shoot and kill them, and for me, combat even ended earlier than it was supposed to because one enemy was still alive, so that was something. Also, if you then go to the other area, it will trigger Elise to talk as if we had chosen the path correctly, neat stuff.Speaking of smoke not stopping you, if you're straight up just fast enough before the smoke can fully form, assuming you're close enough, you can just leave the combat area, and the same situation will still happen. It happened when it reached 20:00 and I was heading home. The combat triggered to the left of my house gate, and it was just a quick U-turn around the barrier. This time, 2 enemies managed to TP past it, not that it mattered, once you get rid of them, the new ones don't TP to you.Infinite loading screens, encountered it once. Can't even begin to imagine how I managed to do it.Finally, for the final game breaking bug I'll mention, map loading failure a 2nd time, this time  I was coming from the last memory zone in the white manor water system, I went to the lighthouse area, except the map where I was standing on deloaded first, throwing me off the map, only for the game to show me the other side and then nothing, I was standing under the door, I could interact with the door, the door animation would play, it would show the correct side loading, but my character would not be there, and would remaing under the respective floor of whatever, for example, I go out to lighthouse area, it shows lighthouse area loaded, but then actually the lighthouse area map isn't loaded, the inside is however, and regardless of that I'm still under the map. I think I fixed this by going in and out of the room that contains the door leading outside to the lighthouse area, like 5 times, just to make sure the game understood where exactly my character was., a beautiful game with nice music and voice acting, decent puzzles, and an intriguing and mysterious story whose ending will be up to each person to determine if they like it or not. Beware of bugs, you will likely encounter them, there will likely be a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: this game could be a lot more and a lot better if it didn't opt for unnecessary game play elements like inventory managemenet, time management and last but not least, extremely clunky combat mechanics. those only drag on the game and frustrate the player. it's a shame because the atmosphere set is right, the protagonist is likeable and the story could be much more fluent and enjoyable to follow if it weren't for those elements, which look like they don't even belong to a game like this. also the game is poorly optimized as even after turning down a lot of graphical details, my GPU continuously ran in max. heat. unfinished game, unhappy gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Great adventure/puzzle game. The combat is okay - the combat isn't woven into the gameplay but rather happens as standalone encounters (think of the random encounters in the old FF7 game) and you basically fight the same one type of enemy repeatedly (it seems more spawn as you advance in days) - the dodge and push mechanics during combat are neat though. The game really shines in the puzzle and exploration departments - without spoilers I can say there are a few interesting player abilities you can take advantage of throughout the game that can help solve puzzles in addition to the logic of solving them. The story was okay for me - I felt it was very vague and conspiracy-theory-like and a bit hard to follow.

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Pieces is a psychological adventure game with horror aspects, about a woman trapped by evil entities in an abandoned coastal French town. She must fight back against these creatures and solve puzzles to escape.Visually and sound wise this game is excellent for an indie and has almost a "AA" feeling to it. Gorgeous visuals that really make the locals feel alive, with traditional fixed PS1/2 style camera angles, each line is fully voice acted and the world is brought to life through a excellent selection of sound and music. It's a joy to both look at and listen too.Gameplay wise this game is predominantly a puzzle game, you must explore the village, solve mild puzzles and occasionally shoot enemies that especially on easy difficulty do not pose too much of a threat. If your not keen on horror and want to avoid the games somewhat clunky mechanics playing on easy almost eliminates any need to engage entities for more than a few seconds at a time. On normal the combat is a little lame and underwhelming just feel clunky and "off" it's not that it's difficult it's more just, not very fun or well realised.So puzzles and exploration are the games key aspects. Most of these puzzles are simple but often involve the games biggest weakness. Backtracking. The environments are large and while you unlock shortcuts through the village a lot of the time the game will have you going back and forth between points to get items/find locations and it is pretty tedious. Once you get to certain locations to solve puzzles the game IS fun and the puzzles are smart but it's the running around between that makes things a little dull. It's not enough to ruin the game but it is enough to make you roll your eyes, especially as you must return home to rest before nightfall every day which involves going back to your home from wherever you are. Story wise I found the story to be very engaging, the ending isn't amazing but it's a reasonable resolution to your adventure and for the most part everything slots together nicely as you head into the plots big reveal. I thought the story was considerably above average for an indie horror title and was definitely really gripped at times, it made traipsing back and forth through town feel worth it. Overall Broken Pieces is a great looking and sounding game marred by fairly needless combat that feels bolted in to the game to hook more players in and some tedious backtracking-esque exploration. The games strong puzzles and excellent plot however make this worth checking out as it's faults can be overcome (or removed by playing on easy) to make the game something fairly unique and engaging,.

_childDocuments_.review: we had a real hard start.I bought the game after Patch 1.3 and played on PC only. I tried the free camera at first, this never worked for me. Personally, for me it responds too sturdy while shifting, make it hard to play with. Technically, I endured several known bugs, like getting stuck repeatedly at the shooting range and non-existing save-files. It was one step before dumping the game.But then my first try with the fixed camera changed the feeling for this game fast. Since then, the game runs with no serious disorders. That gave me time looking at the details - and they are fantastic.The whole village of St. Exil is created with great amount of detail and makes is look lifelike. There are minor flaws like retarded texture files, but I do not mind in that case. The atmosphere is unique and it is pure fun exploring this world. The possible change of season ads extra charme. And of course, extra details.I appreciate the sounds being reduced to ambient moods. The seagulls are great, even when scripted. And the spray caused by the atlantic ocean adds the cherry on the cake.Elise is a character I like to accompany on her journey through this fascinating and disturbing universe.Able to choose between two levels of combat helped me getting into the right sort of reactions.Finding some of the items took me a while, the puzzles are good.One disadvantage is that the story feels unfinished. I like the phantastic/ dream/ nightmarish proportions of the story. And I did not expect a total rational explanation. But what we are offered is nothing finalized.There are rumours for a second part. I really hope for that. I would appreciate a lot returning to St. Exil with new areas, interiors, puzzles. etc!For only 5 people building this game, some technical flaws are OK. This is a mass of work, errors happens. But I want the story to be thougth out well.I am very much in hope for a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: The game just isn't for me. The puzzles feel obscure and overally complicated with frequent backtracking for seemingly trivial things (the night mechanic forcing you to go back to the house at the end of every day is frustrating). The combat feels awkward and clunky, whilst the lack of variety in enemy leads to a repetitive and boring experience.I will say overall that graphically the game is pretty pleasing to look at, but I just couldn't bring myself to care about the story. The lack of motivation to play through the game, plus the frequent backtracking and unpleasant combat mechanics, led to little incentive to finish the questline.Unfortunately I would not recommend the game. It's not awful by any means, and it certainly isn't the worst game I've ever played, but the forced backtracking and lack of an engaging storyline just leads to very flat, stale and quite frankly, boring gameplay. I can however see how this could be interesting to a different type of gaming audience, so if purchasing this game just keep an open mind and consider that this is a very slow puzzle based game with a minimal storyline (at least at the first 3 hours of playing).

_childDocuments_.review: Shaky-cam, so much shaky-cam.The thing film makers spent close to a century trying to eliminate, game developers have put in with a vengeance during cut-scenes.A nice static shot, seen during a low-grade tremor apparently.Still playing through the rest of the game to see how much I enjoy it, but I literally roll my eyes when I see movie directors using shaky cam and "documentary" style movements since it completely breaks immersion for me. _childDocuments_.review: Unplayable if you don't speak French.Even though the game supposedly has English language, all textures with clues are still in French and no translation is provided after the initial reading. Apparently they didn't care about the rest of the world. Coding is subpar too. It slows down a lot on maximum settings and the graphics in general is nothing special to warrant the slowdowns. Textures and models are in fact rather ugly on close ups.Animations are extremely basic. The character doesn't move during interactions with any objects except doors, ladders, and levers. All ladders and all levers have exactly one model. There is exactly one type of "enemy", if you can even call it that. The fights are as basic as they can possibly be. A 90s survival horror much? It's been 25 years, grow up. And even in the 90s it was done better than this.The character moves like a fat lazy cow. I walk faster than it can run. It stumbles at every corner, too, and there's no animation for blocked movement or even turning. The combat is dumb, repetitive, and random. Constant cutscenes further take away from whatever "gameplay" you might scratch out of it.They try to use the old and tested French method of giving the protagonist a music player and a lot of benches to sit on and listen, but unlike Life is Strange, this does not seem to be user friendly or even atmospheric. And their "music" sucks. The worst kind of pretentious ear-torture you can find.Oh, and the plot is non-existent, too, with a lazy abrupt ending (yes, it took less than twelve hours to reach it on the first ever playthrough with 95% completion). There can be no redemption for this "game". It is absolutely awful.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a video reviewStreaming the game Broken Pieces is the debut of the French studio, which, with the efforts of five people, released a game presented as a psychological thriller. The trailers of Broken Pieces have been compared to just about everything. And with Silent Hill, and Syberia, and even traces of Life is Strange were found. Elisa, a woman in her thirties, and her husband Pierre, who is a fan of music and instruments for performing it, heard about the town of Saint-Eggsil on television. Love at first sight, a spark in their hearts - and they decided to move closer to the sea. They bought a big and cozy house, but battered by time and sea salt. It is our fortress for the rest of the game. The prototype of St. Agesil was the French region of Brittany.Happiness and intoxicating freedom did not last long. Something lurked in the region's waters. A Lovecraftian ancient horror, a scientifically explainable anomaly, a UFO base, or something else - in general, a signal emanating from the bottom interested the competent persons and a group of sectarians. As the doctrine of the leader says, there is an ancient deity in the waters, and the time has come to pay the bill for their sins. Aggressive citizens began defacing city property, desecrating graves, and performing mystical rituals.And then, in the spring of 1993, the military conducts an operation after which everything changes. The plot begins with Eliza's dream and awakening. Walking around the house, we go outside - and there's no one there. The heroine finds herself in a kind of bubble, locked in time and space. It is always April 3, and only insignificant things change from day to day. For example, fluorescent mushrooms grow and shrimp appear in fishing nets.Before starting the game asks whether to pass as intended by the developers or choose a simplified combat mode. The essence of this proposal becomes clear later, but it's done, you can not change anything. Ghost battles are disgustingly implemented and annoying, at least when playing with a keyboard and mouse, although the developers again recommend using a gamepad. It is very interesting how this idea came to someone's mind, given the genre of Broken Pieces. A lot of ammunition is not going to scrap, and Eliza dodges like a cripple, although she seems to be a young and agile woman. Also trains in the yard. As a result, by the end of the game, when the fighting gets more fierce, poorly drawn spirits can seriously hurt. Eliza's skill at driving enemies away saves her a little. Weapons, hits and all that sort of thing called impaction certainly don't feel like it, it's out of the question. Totally unnecessary and annoying mechanics. Broken Pieces comes out just in time. Exploring coastal Brittany in the fall is like taking a little trip filled with secrets, beautiful architecture, and uncomplicated riddles.PLUSES +++. Charming coastal townCharming protagonist with a pleasant voiceExploring Saint-Egzil and solving riddles doesn't bore you to the end of the walkthroughThe ending is abrupt, despite the completion of the general task. The ending is so clumsy that it sweeps you off your feet with its directness and leaves you with an understatement. The effect of surprise is revealed through the excessive simplicity of the final episode. MINUSES --Horrible combat systemPerhaps a little too chambery.Questionable ending Score 7 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing gaming experience in all aspects. I wanted to share my thought even before finishing the game, but I finally finished it recently. This is a classic silent hill or resident evil like game, with some very interesting additions. The game has an amazing storyline and plot which makes you feel lonely some times but it enhances this way the whole experience. It's like living the life of the character you play totally. There's a lot of mystery and the story is very well thought out and meticulously made. The cameras used are really outstanding. They give you the old good vibes of silent hill aspects but with even more dynamic views where you can control the the cameras and even see from a first person perspective, something really useful with some puzzle solving and to get into the mood of the atmosphere. The sounds is phenomenal, maybe one of the best I have experienced with games and it is adapted perfectly to the different viewing angles! Some sound-based puzzles are unique too! Speaking of puzzles, I found them really interesting! I had so long to experience something so unique puzzle-wise. The mini games are very interesting too! I solved all of them and I really enjoyed them! I finished the game without any guide. I stuck several times, but I found solving those puzzles myself very satisfying and rewarding! To me this is a masterpiece, and taking into account the fact that is made by a new gaming studio, this is a very brave and pationet attempt! I was impressed with medium quite a long ago, but to be honest it felt too brief and the gameplay was very naive comparing to this one in al aspects. I believe Elseware Experience deserved to make the next Silent Hill games or remakes more than Bloober Team. Of course this is just a personal opinion, but that's what I believe. I'm looking forward to the next creation of Elseware Experience. If you are a fan of Resident Evil or Silent Hill series, I believe you have to give it a try! It won't disappoint you!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow, I did not expect that this game would be such a great experience. I mean seriously, how a team of 5 people create such a deep and interesting story, detailed worlds, fantastic soundtrack, and diversified gameplay that does not let you get bored. It has a healthy mix of world exploration, storytelling, puzzles and side games, and survival / combat. Survival and combat while being present in the game is not the core experience, so don't expect something like RE or Us and Them experience from this game. I'd draw parallels with Alone in the Dark games in some sense. Voice over is great, the heroine has a lot to say about everything around her and never repeats herself. Music is fantastic as I already said and the addition of audio cassettes that you can find in various places with more music tracks to listen adds even more depth. Once I started the game I was instantly "sucked" in and sunk another 12 hours into it just that night. Wow, just wow, one of the best puzzle/adventure/survival games I've played lately. I totally recommend it, so underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. But it has a few "little" flaws that i would like to address here. (Spoilers)Fighting:This system is the thing that is most annoying (for me)While aiming you can not move at all. Running from the enemies makes no sense, since you are always fighting in a little arena. You are forced to fight. Fighting boils down to: Aim, shoot, dodge (too tricky) or push the enemies away, repeat. Hoping you will not die in the process.This system feels not finished at all. If you want more fun with this game, just go for the "lower" difficulty without fighting. Just enjoy the story. Navigation:You have no map. Well yes, i am not using am map in my city...but in this game, where every transition between "maps" costs you ingame time, i would wish to have an ingame map. Sometimes i forget the right way or where i have to go at all. This is rather painfull.Changing the season: You can change the season at some point in the game. At first i though of it as a nice new feature...but basically you can only decide if you want frozen water or low/high tides...thats all. Other than than you get a few new obstacles. Elise can not open several doors. bacause there is a liitle bit of snow behind the door ;)Ground hog day:You can expect to encounter fights AT THE SAME PLACES. Over and over again. It is okay at first...but it gets annoying after a while. I need to go home to sleep or to heal and i have to pass a certain area to go there - BOOM. Enemies are attacking!What i like about this game:The graphics: Everything looks nice. It feels like the developers really wanted to build a nice looking village and put a lot of effort into it. Having to watch the clock:It builds a little pressure if you change places and this takes time. If you do not look after the time you might encounter problems later. This is something if have not seen in other games like that.A female Character:Yes this is nice. And in this game it does not feel like the "This has to be a girl" type of thing. She is a believable character for this game. Just for the protocol: I am a man.Environmental puzzles:Besides the fact, that some features do not make sense to me, i like the idea that you have to "interact" with the environment to solve a few puzzles. May it be by using her powers of else. Her diary and hew cassette player:The only game i remember where you can collect cassettes to listen to on the go. Hearing Elises thought about her experiences is surely a nice idea.Overall a nice game with some cool ideas that need a little more work.Dont get me wrong, this is not silent hill and definately no resident evil. At first i expected something alike, but this game goes its own way and that is ok. If you want a cool looking village at the french coast, while exploring a lot of places, solving puzzles and try to find out what is happenig for a few evenings, then this might be for you.But it would wish that the devs would bring back the demo so you can get a first impressing of what is awaiting you.

_childDocuments_.review: so i needed 20 hours to finish the game, including frequent use of a  walkthrough. let me get to the cons and pros:CONS:1. control of my character was nasty. the game is not designed for a keyboard and mouse. after 20 hours of play, i still was banging into walls and moving the wrong direction most of the time. so that was really tiring and annoying, but it did not affect my success in the game. action didn't really require hand-eye coordination or anything.2. i got lost a lot. the world is big, with new locations introduced regularly and doors leading to and from them. i would have liked a clickable map where i could see which doors were best to use. too much time was spent running around the world not finding what i needed to find. 3. the inventory system didn't work so well for me. for example, using a key or an axe, sometimes i had problems how to activate them. 4. i think i completed the game without encountering a single other human being. got a little lonely i guess. 5. the story was ok, but i didn't always understand it. 6. i did not like having to watch the clock and not be at certain places during certain times. that became stressful. PROS:1. the game has a list of constantly changing objectives which is very helpful staying focused. 2. there is some shooting involved, but this is the first game i played that has a fabulous setting to make combat easy. and it really did!  aiming and shooting was simple and successful 100% of the time, although there doesn't have to be much shooting involved at all, if you follow the rules for avoiding bad things.3. although it was not an easy game for me, i kept coming back to it and got a lot of satisfaction completing tasks, even when i had to use the walkthrough (which was almost always). 4. real nice graphics and appropriate music. 5. a lot of work was put in developing this game i think. so all that being said, i definitely recommend the game! most of you are better at solving and figuring stuff out, so i'm sure would finish much sooner than i did with less assistance needed. i don't think my experience would necessarily be yours in this game.i was happy to finish it, and i think i know what happens, but i'm not really sure. so i'll check the discussions or youtubes. i think you'll like it in spite of my cons. i give it 4 stars out of 5, but a little too hard figuring out what to do for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, atmospheric puzzle game ala Silent Hill. The biggest (and imo really the only) issue is the combat; very lackluster and fincky. However, there is an option to 'reduce combat' so that you can focus on puzzles and narrative; I recommend taking this option as you'll probably just be frustrated with the combat mechanics.Outside of that, this game has a fantastic original score and is quite pretty. The story is a bit ambiguous but it unravels very well, primarily through audio tapes you find around the levels. There are some very fun side-quest puzzles and plenty to explore. Not so much scary as it is surreal, but very dark vibes. Overall, I definitely recommend if you like classic Metroidvania-style puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but also far from being great.This is clearly a game in which the developers have put a lot of attention to detail and the fixed camera works perfectly. Graphics are really good and its fun to explore the coastal town. But again, it's not a great game by any means and really close to a thumbs down.The story is The game overwhelms you with 4 different plot lines that seem impossible to fit into a coherent story.It takes around 4 hours until you start to see the connections between all these different plot lines and even then it's still messy.The rushed ending does not help.While the developers spent lot's of time designing various side activities and items, the main quest is basically a loop of using the same three items, solving the same environment puzzles and lots of backtracking. Combat feels totally out of place, it's like once they had already finished the game someone had the idea to include a bit of shooting to appeal to the RE fanbase.I really hope the developers use the experience they gained with Broken Pieces to create another fixed camera survival horror / adventure game. But please, ditch the story, make the combat feel less out of place and include a bit more variety with the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommending this game to anyone who likes survival horror or adventure games especially from the PS1/PS2 generations but with some big caveats. If you go into this game with the proper expectations you will get much more out of it than I did...First and foremost I would recommend Reduced Combat difficulty, because the combat in this game is easily it's weakest feature. The enemies are not fun or engaging to fight on top of the fact that you get an ability that can one shot entire groups anyway AND the strangest feature is the infinite ammo. In survival horror games especially, combat is a strategic trading of resources. When the enemies are random, infinite to a certain degree, and you don't need to worry about resource management, the combat needs to just be fun, and here it is absolute butt cheeks. Then get ready for copious amounts of meaningless backtracking in the second half of the game, to solve some of the lamest puzzles I've ever seen in the genre. Because of the open ended nature of the level design, you can never tell what is needed for progression and what is optional and because so much is left out of the character's journal you will feel lost even when you have already come across all the information you need to progress. Compounding this issue is the fact that you can solve several puzzles needed for late game, even endgame progression near the beginning so you will be even more confused on how to solve the related puzzles later in the game. For more open ended, exploratory level design, it's important to provide context to the player for key items, i.e. flavor text/character dialogue that let's you know whether or not something is useful now. One example is a key you can get near the beginning, needed to obtain one of the final key items of the game. You can get it whenever you want to, and there are doors that remain locked the entirety of the game that you will actually never be able to open. But you may try when you come across keys like this one. What makes this worse is that there are doors you WILL find, even in the starting areas that you can't even interact with. So the developers were not consistent enough in this regard and it will add to the confusion. All of these thing made EVEN worse because you can solve puzzles and certain story elements out of order, as is intended, but when you throw in all these other issues it makes for an overall bad experience imo.The best things this game has going for it are it's incredible atmosphere, sound design, and OST. The music, especially the cassettes you can listen to whenever you want to, are wonderful and honestly the most fun parts of the game are when you're exploring the streets with one of these playing and just soaking up the atmosphere. It's truly wonderful, and almost makes the game worth it's price point on its own. The story also started as one of the most intriguing mysteries I'd seen in an indie game in quite some time, but as I started to suspect after the halfway point, the payoff is almost non-existent. Even with every document, and cassette available to you, there isn't enough to make the ending worth the journey. But to reference the atmosphere and music again, the journey alone may be enough.To conclude, get this on sale, play on the reduced combat difficulty, and focus on the tone, music, sound design, atmosphere, and exploration, and if you can become immersed in this world, you may find some magic in it. But no matter what kind of games you like, I cannot recommend this game at full price to anyone. Don't let my played time at the time of writing this fool you. At least a third of that was spent doing optional stuff (which will not help you in the reduced combat difficulty) and getting lost in a game with unintuitive level design that also doesn't have a map. Not all games should have a map. This game severely needs a map and these developers honestly should've known better.One last thing... for added immersion, play with French audio and English subtitles. I think this is probably the best way to experience the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100% ambiance. It wants you - needs you - to take it slowly, gently.Unfortunately, everything else suffers, especially the combat. _childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting game with a good difficulty level, ultimately undone by a weak ending. I grew up playing point and click adventure games and puzzle games, and I enjoyed the nostalgic gameplay of "running around, finding secret codes and necessary items." The shortcuts between areas helped with this quite a lot.The story hinges on a mystery, though, and it's a bit of a slap when the storyline neither advances nor clarifies any of that mystery. I didn't feel any more enlightened at the end of the game than at the beginning. Edit: After a patch with a short clarifying scene at the end of the game, I've changed my review from negative to positive. I'm still confused about some aspects of the story, but I appreciate the devs listening to player feedback and adding context. Making a video game is a really, really hard thing to do, and Broken Pieces is likely to be a solid experience for people who enjoy adventure/puzzle games. (And maybe I'm just picky when it comes to narrative.)Pros:-beautiful scenes-finding tapes and playing the music you like was a neat angle-weird and interesting supernatural mystery-the combat and daytime limits add a feeling of tension to the gameCons:-some resolution at the end, but still a lot of mystery (some players may not consider this a con--I admit I'm the kind of person who likes to know "what really happened" at the end)-occasional frustrating bits of running back and forth-limited inventory space adds difficulty but not much fun
