_childDocuments_.review: As more and more classic survival horror adjacent action adventure games arrive lately, I keep being occasionally pleasantly surprised by the inventiveness of some of the projects. Even if the title ultimately disappoints, the creativity behind it can show new ways this genre can be done, as if it’s finally trying to break the mould it has been stuck in for decades. Broken Pieces is not a disappointment, however, even if it is a bit of a mess.This is an action adventure with a sci-fi/eldritch horror story twist elements and very light, but impactful, survival concepts. It plays as a third person perspective game with fixed camera angles, although each angle is actually 2 angles you can switch between at will with a press of a button. The character controls are handled with camera-relative/directional controls, so those who have an allergy of tank controls need not worry. You get the typical for the genre item collection and usage, puzzles and mini-games, some of which are optional, and combat. Combat here is quite poor, but I have to credit the developers for seemingly basing it on Parasite Eve 2, which is a great example to follow. Sadly, this has none of the tightness and nuance of PE2 and controls very awkwardly and some of the later game (and optional) challenge fights are stupid. Also stupid is the fact that combat is basically partially random and pops up like a jRPG random encounter. There are fights that seem required and somewhat consistent, but a lot of the others can not happen or have a completely unpredictable amount of enemies.What makes these base mechanics interesting is the attempt to set it all on a concept of a daily schedule and light survival features. Essentially, you have a timer and once you wake up in the morning you have until 20:00 each day to do whatever you plan before it gets too dangerous and you need to go home and sleep. Traveling between major locations takes time (that is shown above the door that takes you there), so you have to be careful about where you are as the deadline gets closer. Crafting resources that you’ve found during the day can be put into the item box and will turn into resources you can use in the morning. It’s extremely basic and really is all about higher damage limited ammo type for combat apart from rare moments when you run out of space in your inventory and decide to backtrack home instead of dropping items. But it does set up a very cool pattern where you plan your day and follow certain simple rituals.It’s also neat that many of the things you get are optional, a lot of things can be done out of order (though there is an “optimal” way to play) and there’s a genuine sense of discovery as you learn more and more about the strange situation the main character has found herself in. The conclusion to this whole story is underwhelming, have to say, and the developers are seemingly busy with thinking of a follow up already, but there’s enough interesting stuff here already to be fun. Even if the English translation (the game is originally French) is problematic at times.Speaking of problematic – some of the poor design choices in the game stand out especially well in contrast to how many cool things are in the game. One optional mini-game is extremely unfun, some of the puzzles are more of a busywork thing than a fun challenge. One optional challenge puzzle, for example, is extremely poorly designed and on top of it you can do it incorrectly, but the game has no way of telling you that you’ve failed or providing you with a restart option. So you must realize what happened and load the last save to undo the situation. And the whole fixed camera gimmick hurts the game far more than it helps, as more often than not you won’t see stuff that you should be able to see, unless you enter the first person mode, which shouldn’t be a requirement since your “puzzle” here is “we designed the camera system really badly and you must suffer for it” and it feels.Still, I have to say that despite many frustrating elements, Broken Pieces has left me inspired. It’s full of cool ideas, some of which are implemented well, and it tries to do something fresh and new out of something old and familiar. Instead of just following trends or copying formulas that have worked for decades by the numbers. I recommend checking out the game, though if your patience with crappy combat is lower than mine, you can set the difficulty to disable lots of that. The game won’t become a smooth experience, but it’s an experience still worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: If the game looks interesting to you, I'd say grab it and give it a shot.As someone that grew up in the area of Resident Evil and Dino Crisis, I love the attention to atmopshere and the style of control. It captures much of the feel without the frustration of the old tank controls. Rather than survival-horror, I would describe it more as a mystery -- why is everyone gone, what's the deal with the lighthouse, the cult, and the attack, and so on.The story is mainly told through documents and tapes you encounter along the way, not pushed very heavily beyond progression. Puzzles are doable if you find the clues and search all over. Combat is relatively easy and most of the time you can explore safely unlike classic survival/horror. If you're not content to explorer and unearth the mystery, you'll be bored; if you like exploration or find yourself wanting to know what Elise's story is then you'll enjoy the game.For a small team, I think the game was excellently done in terms of quality work. Especially nice attention to details. I especially love how Elise wears headphones when listening to tapes :D. The developers seem to be making an effort to support the game (at time of release), and the game is pretty stable for me. The worst thing that I can say about the game is that it feels a little dull, like there should be more action as part of the game play or more to drive you forward than there is. Honestly, I hope they make more games in the future because I'm sure they would be worth playing.Personally, the only thing I can complain about is having to bait seagulls and crows with food when the character has a handgun. But at least no animals were harmed, or turned into emergency rations, in the course of this game. I like the more laid back approach and the adventure style of game more than the old survival horrors, so for me it was fun if not exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: Broken Pieces

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay was satisfying and the puzzles were not overly difficult but felt rewarding to complete. I appreciated the way the narrative was told through tapes you could listen to while exploring the world. The combat was a little difficult to get a hang of, but 1) it wasn't specifically difficult just a little clunky at times 2) you could choose to play without combat as an option, and 3) once I thought of the combat as resource puzzles to be solved it felt like it made more sense. Overall, worth the time to play, and I hope there's more to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! If you are into mystery adventures, go play this game. The graphics are gorgeous and the atmosphere is great! The puzzles are clever and fun. Just don't expect survival horror. There is combat but this game is not there to scare you all the time. Also the daytime restrictions are very relaxed. _childDocuments_.review: I really liked Broken Pieces.The game is really nice and the story is great to follow. It's a bit cryptic at first but you discover all the elements as you go along.- The sound design and the musical atmosphere are really cool. There is no music as such but you use a cassette player to listen to music whenever you want. But above all there are narrative tapes to listen to in order to understand what's going on, there were many details hidden in the tapes.- The graphics: the game is very pretty and the setting is a bit different from many other games as it takes place in France. It's impressive especially when you see that it's made by a small team.- Level Design: I liked the fact that the levels are connected to each other and that you can unlock a lot of different paths and accesses. You often discover little hidden things and there are lots of bonus levels to do too.- The puzzles: Lots of interesting puzzles and there are several optional ones. Some were really hard but that was a bonus.I recommend this game which reminds me of the old point and click games or silent hill but in a modernized version. I find that you quickly get used to the changing of the camera etc.

_childDocuments_.review:
When Elise and her fiance decided to leave urban life and settle near the French coast, she could not imagine that she would end up completely alone.

Now, surrounded by strange phenomena in a dark, post-Cold War climate, Elise will have to investigate and unravel the mysteries surrounding the region of Saint-Exil, its ritualistic cult, and its lighthouse overlooking the coast.

Broken Pieces is an action-packed investigative and adventure video game set in France. The game puts you in the shoes of Elise, a woman in her thirties who finds herself in the village of Saint-Exil in an imaginary region reminiscent of Brittany. Following an unexplained paranormal phenomenon, Elise is stuck, completely alone and out of time.

_childDocuments_.review: FH4 is the best arcade racing game. It has a lot content, great selection of cars, fun gameplay, good controls and physics.I'm extremely happy that Forza Horizon 4 is finally on Steam, I wanted to play this game for years. But xbox app was testing my patience.It's an open world racing game. I guess by cranking up the difficulty and realism settings you could bring it closer to sim-cade level, but mostly it's arcade, a fun one, where laws of physics still exist and different cars handle differently.A while ago when there were mainly arcade games on the market I always wanted more simulators or something arcade but which makes sense when it comes to handling. But then the age of simulators started. Sure they're fun, but they're tiring while Forza is relaxing in a way. Well, you can make it relaxing or challenging. It's the most fun racing game on the market.Car handling is awesome. The weight transfer physics work which is especially useful in dirt racing, you can drift which requires some effort unlike in other games. It's just that awesome feeling, fun and slightly realistic.Car selection is amazing. Everyone will find a car they adore. There are hundreds of cars, something like 700 maybe? Cars have classes and the selection is very diverse. From vintage cars to modern supercars, from regular road cars to rally cars or even trucks or vans. There are even Lego and hot Wheels cars. Just insane.Maybe one downside is that you get a bunch of cars really quickly so there's no sense of progression because you're being given the fastest cars in the first hours of the game. I prefer starting with regular cars and make my way up to earn faster, more expensive cars. Fortunately you can choose whatever car in exhibition races but still it lack progression.So you race in England. At first it's slightly confusing to drive on the wrong lane, of course you can drive however you like but still coming from other games like ETS2 it's a bit confusing, especially the roundabouts. Not in a bad way though.The map is huge and very diverse. Highways, dirt roads, small roads, forests, mountains, lakes, city, everything you want is there for you to explore. And exploring is fun. There are hidden barns and other collectables. While barns are fun, they give you a new car but other collectables are just there for the sake of...collectables. But again – not a bad thing, some of them are fun to find. One of the fun collectable types are beauty spots. You see a beautiful cut-scene of the area/object.The game revolves around competing in a festival. There are various challenges which give you rewards when you complete them. Most of the time you'll need to win races but there are other challenges, like speed traps where you must drive as fast as possible or the ones where you need to jump off a ramp and be in the air for as long as possible.But of course racing is the most important here and you have few types of races. Circuit racing, point A to B racing. But that's not all. There A to B races where you need to follow the road and there are ones where you just need to get to finish line as quick as possible by driving wherever you like, no rules. Team racing where one team competes against drivatar team or other players. There are also races against trains or planes. On top of that there are taxi missions. Which bring us to story events. Those are events/races with some story to it. They're fun and challenging and will keep you occupied for a while.Now multiplayer activities. Racing is obviously one of them but there's also capture the flag where you must carry the flag to destination and other team needs to stop you. Matches where infected team need to touch other cars to infect them. Protect the king matches which is similar. And the most surprising one – battle royale.There's also ranked play. It has stricter rules like you can't hit the walls because you get penalized.But it's not all multiplayer only. Amount of single player content is insane. You can choose to race solo on your chosen difficulty level, a coop race against drivatars and story missions.The game basically gives you a choice how you want to play it.You can customize your character and own a house, multiple houses which serve as your garage and home where you can tune your cars and your appearance.You can also tune your cars accordingly to race you're going to participate. Don't want that? Just download the setup straight from the game. You can apply liveries to your cars by creating your own where the only limit is your imagination or just download a livery.To get new stuff you spin a fortune wheel and rewards are ranging from money and clothes to some cool cars. You earn wheelspins by playing the game.You can drive anywhere, hit bushes, smaller trees, rocks, fences – the environment is destructible. But the best part are seasons. There're four seasons which change over time. Each season has its challenges to compete for you. And season changes could even change your driving. On winter it could be harder to drive but lakes are frozen so you can have fun on the lake. Seasons along with dynamic weather change the map drastically.This is one of the best looking games. Seasons change the map so much that it feels fresh each time. All the seasons are absolutely beautiful.Cars look amazing and they're all are fully modelled. You can look closely at every part of the car.Environments look great. Distant objects are lower quality but overall the game looks stunning.There's also a photo mode where you can take beautiful pictures. But I find most filters pretty poor so it's better to tune the colors by yourself.When the game looks that good I don't expect it to run smoothly. But this is probably the best performing game currently in my library. Runs on max graphics, 80-100fps, smooth as butter. I'm playing on 5800x, 2070s, 32GB @3440x1440.There's native ultrawide support. Although cut-scenes are cropped for some reason.It has a lot of loading screens so I suggest to install this to m.2 ssd. They're usually short, 3 to 15 seconds, but there are so many of them that it gets annoying. It's especially annoying in mp because everyone must wait until the slowest PC will load the game which could take 15 minutes. How fun is it to wait 15 minutes for a 5min race?I noticed many people complaining about stuttering cut-scenes. But cut-scenes are actually loading screens.One more minor annoying thing is unskippable voice when you open the map and there's something new on it. It tells you about new activities but after 20th time I just don't want to hear it anymore it's the most annoying thing in the whole game besides clueless online players.Sound design is perfect. Cars sound great, the festival site feels alive.There're radio stations so most people will find something to listen to but t lack a metal station.Overall an extremely good racing game for anyone who at least slightly enjoys racing games. It's great for everyone's taste due to plenty of different activities and modes to play.I suggest buying the ultimate edition. It only lacks two dlc's. Not at full price obviously.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimate Edition review.Great graphics, lots of stuff to do, fun online events/connectivity...you know what everyone says.But there's two things I cannot STAND. The menus and ui are horrible. My God. There's loads of important things buried between tabs, menus, and different shape and size boxes selecting just simple stuff. Played the game for 76 hours and never got used to the ui. Plus, passive notifications after you do something don't tell you enough information a lot of the time, which means you gotta go back into the menus. It actually drove me nuts. Probably the worst aspect of the game. Notifications are also very obtrusive (FH5 is slightly better though about the notifications but still needs improvement). The seconds thing is progression. It's cool to earn cars, but when you get a fast car early on, there's no reason to want/buy slower cars. You can do any event in almost any class car anyway. There's also no real story. There's a narrator here and there but it's extremely bland. There's events called "story" that each have about 8-10 separate things to do, but again, it's bland. What's worse, every single camera angle and panning Is. Exactly. The. Same. Both characters are in the exact same spot with the character who is talking to you conveniently has their back to you, probably as a way for the dev to save time/money so they don't have to do lipsync. However there was one "story" that was really fun and exciting to me. It involved going through a history of racing video games which was awesome. So basically it's just do stuff, get car. They try to spice it up a bit by added wheelspins and super wheelspins where you can earn cash, emotes, clothing, horns and of course more cars. But a lot of those wheelspins have some really terrible low value "prizes" too. One game that did both of these things right was The Crew 2. I know, a Ubi game. But the menu navigation, progression and notifications are spot on. And the game is still supported as of this review too. It may sound like I'm being too hard on the game but no, I had a lot of fun. I did every event, found every collectible and did the same for Fortune Valley and The Lego expansion. I bought at a discount for $35 plus the $3 dollar treasure map because I'm lazy. Got a lot of playtime on this one, however also consider I got The Crew 2 for just $10 on sale with the better ui on top and I played that for almost 60 hours with more event variety and plenty left to do, I'd go for either the base game of FH4 or The Crew 2.  -------------------------------Fortune Valley:Basically it's a much smaller map with the exact same event types and stories. For some reason I though there were going to be natural disasters in this one, but nope. -------------------------------Lego DLCAn even smaller map with much less to do. There's an excessive grind if you want to complete the Master Builder though. And the challenges are again, laid out poorly in a grid of I think 16*17. Oh my God is horrible. You always earn toward them even if they're not pinned but you can only pin one at a time which was annoying.  Also, there's no passive notifications during gameplay telling you how far you are in something you just triggered and maybe didn't know it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Forza Horizon 4. It's not as realistic as other racing sims out there but I like the arcade part. I like upgrading my cars up to the limit allowed and tweaking it to just get that slight edge that makes you win the race.The map is pretty big and it's fun to explore new areas. You'll see most of the map if you do all races and stories. Apart from racing there's also other game modes where you can play battle royale, infection, capture the flag and other style games with other players.Most of the story missions are alright but some are just annoying but thankfully just have to be done once and they give decent rewards when completed.There are also a few annoyances about FH4: once in a while you'll have to restart the game because some mechanics stop working (like rewind will suddenly stop working in the middle of a race or even in free roam), online session will not be able to connect, online (ranked) matchmaking can sometimes take ages to find players, especially ranked can sometimes take like 20-30 minutes if you're unlucky. Many cheaters/modders/hackers ruin the gameplay by getting impossible results in races/speedtraps/etc leaderboards. It's been like this for ever and nothing is being done to remove the clearly cheated numbers like driving 9.000 km/h through a speedtrap or finish a 6 km race in 0.05 seconds. I wish these people would get banned/accounts deleted and their entries removed from the leaderboards. It's been a long-term complaint from the community but it's very obvious the developers couldn't care less because they have never bothered to fix or do anything about it.Also the winter season sucks, don't bother doing storyline or regular races in winter because you'll have to adapt to the snow but still be expected to perform equally as if the road isn't a big ice rink. I would recommend getting FH4 on sale or get the game + DLC pack when it's on discount, which really increases the value because the DLCs can get a bit expensive when they are added up.If you enjoy arcade style racing sims, this one is really a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the racing game Steam has been missing for years! As an arcade racing enthusiast since the days of Gran Turismo on the PlayStation and Sega Daytona in the arcade (and OutRun and Chase HQ even before that, but I don't want to date myself ;) ), this game fills the empty hole in my gaming life created by a lack of good racing games.I tried getting into Wreckfest, but having been burnt by the early access and looooong development, plus the fact it's more simulation than arcade, it never really did it for me. There are the NFS entries on Steam, but EA...So I waited and waiting. I even played the demo of Forza Horizon 4 on the Windows Games Store, but I'd rather burn my money than throw it away on that empty shell of an excuse for a digital pc games store.And OMG, it was worth the wait. There is so much content here. And it's great, GREAT fun. There's so much to do. The best part? You can tune the difficulty settings to have as simulation or arcade as you like. The DLC is tremendous and expands the game in great ways. The racing and activities are challenging but not impossible (l2drift). The car selection is licensed, very real, and very large (like 800 cars? more?). Plus, the cars can be customized to your hearts content with upgrades, tuning profiles, and personal paint jobs. And the map, jesus. It's Britain, literally. A large portion of Britain. Driving around just feels immaculate. The world is highly detailed and almost entirely destructible. It feels as detailed and vibrant as a GTA world map, except I can't get out of my car. It's Burnout Paradise, Gran Turismo, and Need for Speed all rolled up into one massive racing game. Buy it on sale, buy the $60, go for broke and buy it all, it doesn't matter because you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 stands out among racing games, carving out a niche of its own. Unlike many other games in the genre, it offers a unique and immersive experience that truly draws you in from the moment you start playing. As soon as you fire up the engine, you're transported into a dynamic world where every element seems alive and responsive to your actions.In Forza Horizon 4, the gameplay is designed so that it's not you who has to adapt to the non-player characters (NPCs), but rather the NPCs who adjust according to the class of car you are driving. This creates a more personalized and engaging experience, as the environment and opponents adapt to your choices, enhancing the realism and excitement of each race.The game offers a wide range of vehicles to choose from, allowing you to enjoy the thrill of racing in everything from slow, classic cars to ultra-fast hypercars. Each vehicle type provides a different feel and challenge, whether you're cruising through smooth city streets or tackling treacherous, muddy roads. The diversity in terrains and weather conditions adds another layer of depth, requiring you to adapt your driving style and strategy to succeed.Reflecting on my experience with Forza Horizon 4, my biggest regret is not having owned this game from the day it was released. I missed out on many thrilling moments and events, and now I can only enjoy the Festival Event that is soon coming to an end. This game has provided countless hours of entertainment and joy, making me wish I had been a part of its community from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: What you’ll likeThe ideal of the Horizon formulaThis series has been excellent since its debut in 2012. The Xbox 360’s Forza Horizon was a great way to take the physics, customization, and cars from Motorsport add in some lighthearted fun. Somehow, each game has improved on that.Forza Horizon 4 maintains the series’ reputation. Once again, I’m left wondering how you make Forza Horizon 5 better than this. Among the reasons this entry is so solid is because the world never gets in the way. The environment looks detailed and realistic, but Playground is not going to destroy your momentum to give a stone wall. You can tear through obstacles like tissue. This series has done that before, but it has never felt quite as friendly as it does here.Another example of how Horizon 4 squeezes more fun out of its traditions is the progressions system. You steadily level up everything in this game. You have separate progression for street races, cross-country, and rallying. Even each individual car has its own leveling system. That might sound exhausting, but it gives you both a reason to stick with a car and a reason to start working on the next one when you’re ready.Unmatched presentationPlayground presents its games better than any other developer working right now. Forza Horizon 4 is more evidence of that. Its clips before and after races are gorgeous. They feature your driver and their car standing in front of massive stylized menu or display. This tells you what race you’re in or how many experience points you just earned. It looks stunning, and it makes the game feel lively and expensive.Great Britain is beautiful over seasonsForza Horizon 4 is stunning. Racing games are always technical showpieces, but I don’t think you could get a better looking game for your Xbox One X right now. I’ve mostly played in performance mode on console, which is getting me 60 buttery smooth frames per second. And sure, you notice the dip in resolution, but it’s not distracting. And even in performance mode, it still looks beautiful.It takes place in Great Britain, and that means you get some pretty roads, green pastures, and plenty of cozy-looking hamlets. Playground then adds variety to this already mesmerizing space through the use of different times of year.The conceit of Forza Horizon 4 is that it’s the car festival that never ends. That means a green pasture might sometime feature some fall colors. Or it could end up covered in snow or flowers. It’s not all just cosmetic changes. Rain and ice will cause handling differences as well. But it really keeps the game feeling fresh.It also looks stunning in 1440p running at 144 frames per second on ultra settings on PC. I recommend experiencing that.Forza Horizon 4 is a good dumb online gameThis game has character customization. That’s because it has a living online world where you will naturally come across other real players at any time. When this happens, you don’t want to embarrass your friends by rocking some ugly default icon. Instead, you want to rock a chicken suit or James Bond’s tuxedo.More important, you’ll need a decent emote when you challenge that online rando and beat them. For example, make them watch you do the floss dance or maybe the Macarena.You can even do these dance emotes at special scenic locations, and it’s just … well, watch.What you won’t likeMore of the samePlayground has made a lot of smart improvements. The progression system does a better job of stitching together the space between races than previous games. And Forza Horizon 4 has seemingly added content without taking any of the other modes away from earlier entries.But you are still primarily doing the same things as always. You’re still racing fast cars around a detailed world. And sure, the setting has changed, but that doesn’t feel too drastically different in the end.That said, Forza Horizon 4 has so much going on, and it’s all so rewarding and satisfying. What you are really getting here is the ultimate refined Forza experience.Conclusion (so far)When a game series is this good for this long, you can sometimes find yourself taking it for granted. Forza Horizon 4 once again refines its formula in a number of notable ways. But those improvements are getting diminishing returns. This is the best Forza Horizon game, and that makes it one of the best racing games ever. And, at first, I didn’t think that would wow me like it once did. But I can’t put the game down. It’s so good. The progression keeps me coming back, and every car is so much fun to drive.If you haven’t checked in with the franchise for a while, you’re going to love it. If you just picked up an Xbox One X and a 4K TV, it is a wonderful showpiece. And even if you’ve played every Forza, you’re going to fall deeply in love with this one.Score: 95/100

_childDocuments_.review: The good: It's a beautiful game that runs well and has a ton of content. It's the most fun I've had on a racing game in a long time.The bad: The devs engage in a lot of shady, unethical practices. Unskippable video ads for DLC in between certain events; bugs that are known, old, and will never be patched because they're already focused on the next game; buggy and often unplayable multiplayer (which is a shame because a lot of season rewards are bound to multiplayer events); and "matchmaking" that does nothing to match you up with players close to your skill. It's a shame they don't care enough to fix these easily fixable problems, so I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is an exceptional racing game that deserves all the awards and accolades it has received. From its stunning graphics to its immersive gameplay, this game is a true masterpiece that will keep you hooked for hours on end.One of the standout features of Forza Horizon 4 is its dynamic seasons system. As you race through the game's open-world environment, the seasons change in real-time, creating a constantly evolving and immersive experience. Whether you're racing through autumnal forests or drifting across frozen lakes in winter, every season offers a unique and thrilling challenge.The game's car selection is also a major highlight, with over 450 vehicles to choose from, each with its own unique handling and performance characteristics. Whether you're a fan of classic muscle cars or high-performance supercars, there's a vehicle in Forza Horizon 4 that will suit your style.But perhaps the most impressive aspect of Forza Horizon 4 is its attention to detail. From the realistic physics engine to the intricate car models and environments, every aspect of the game has been crafted with care and precision.Overall, Forza Horizon 4 is a must-play game for anyone who loves racing, simulation, and open-world exploration. It's no wonder that this game has received so many awards and accolades, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a thrilling and immersive gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game is amazing in so many ways, but I cannot in good conscience recommend it considering that the devs have made it clear that they do not plan meaningfully continue support for the game.There was nearly 6 months of a major crash bug affecting Nvidia users, and now we're more than half a year into a bug where players just don't get rewards they've earned from weekly/monthly seasonal/series challenges, specifically the Horizon Backstage Passes.These are essentially coupons players can redeem for very rare cars, except for many months now players haven't been receiving them, meaning that if you're trying to complete your car collection you basically cannot, because many of the Backstage cars cannot realistically be obtained any other way and are never on the auction house.The devs have clearly stated that they know about the bug but that they have "no plans" to fix it because they're too busy working on FH5 (which just got new microtransactions that have upset the playerbase).I'll happily change my review if and when this gets fixed, but currently the game owes me literally about two *dozen* backstage passes.AT A MINIMUM, they should just start giving the players a free backstage pass every week to compensate for the bug they refuse to fix.

The driving mechanics feel responsive and satisfying, striking a balance between arcade fun and simulation realism. The diverse range of events, including races, challenges, and stunts, keeps the gameplay fresh. The introduction of the new "Forzathon" events adds a layer of community engagement and regular content updates.Multiplayer and Community: Forza Horizon 4 excels in its multiplayer mode, allowing you to race against friends or join online events with players from around the world. The shared world concept enhances the experience, making the game feel alive with other players driving around, completing challenges, and participating in seasonal events.Content and Longevity: With an expansive map, a plethora of cars, and continuous seasonal updates, Forza Horizon 4 offers hundreds of hours of gameplay. The inclusion of the Horizon Festival and various themed events provides motivation to keep returning, ensuring that players always have something new to experience.Performance: On PC, the game runs smoothly with customizable graphics settings that can accommodate a wide range of hardware. Whether you’re on a high-end rig or a more modest setup, you can expect a smooth gameplay experience with high frame rates.Negatives: While Forza Horizon 4 is an outstanding game, there are a few minor issues. Some players have noted that the AI can be inconsistent, occasionally making races feel unbalanced. Additionally, the in-game microtransactions have received criticism, though they are not necessary to enjoy the game fully.Conclusion: Forza Horizon 4 is a must-play for any racing game enthusiast. Its stunning graphics, varied gameplay, and strong community support make it one of the best entries in the racing genre. Whether you’re a casual player or a hardcore racing fan, this game offers something for everyone. If you’re looking for a vibrant, immersive racing experience, Forza Horizon 4 will not disappoint.Overall:Highly recommended for its engaging gameplay and beautiful world, with minor flaws that don’t overshadow its many strengths.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.This is what I would imagine an ideal open world street racer to be like lots of fun. I enjoy being able to just cruise around and drive where ever I want, the game feels kinda like a sequel to Midnight club and Test Drive Unlimited the location is set in Edinburgh Scotland which is nice and great to explore, the map is huge and the car selection is massive, there is so many different types of cars to choose from its crazy.The game play is quality, the cars handle nicely and the difficulty can be adjusted, The single player experience is excellent I never really run out of things to do, I enjoy being able to play multiplayer mode with my friends, it can be really fun with the various different modes, capture the flag and Infected are really good. I like all the different race events, searching for collectables is fun, doing side missions against the clock or stunt challenges etc can be cool and rewarding. Some times I find the race tracks can be a bit recycled or unorganised but to be honest its not really something that bothers me that much, I do think it would have been great if they added cops to the game kinda sucks that there isnt any.Something I should mention is that I had two problems with the game. The first issue I had was stuttering, to be fair it was mostly during cut scenes, I did notice it during game play and between transitions like when ever I finished a race event or when I was about to start one however I was able to fix this issue. It was kinda my own fault for not keeping my graphics card drivers up to date, as soon as I opened a tool on my computer called "Geforce Experience" I updated my video card drivers and this prity much fixed the issue for me. The game only stutters a little bit now before starting events but a part from that the game is smooth and runs great.The second problem was a crashing issue, basically the game would randomly close and go straight to desktop for no reason. This took me a while to actually get fixed it really gave me a headache trying to solve it. There was a lot of things mentioned by different sources such as: updating Windows to the latest version available, disabling my firewall and running the game as Admin then moving the game from my Hard drive to my Solid State drive etc. None of these worked. In the end one of my friends was able to figure out what the issue was and fix it for me. I had to change the Windows Sound depth on my computer to "24 Bit 44100 Hz" the settings I was using was 48000 Hz after I did this the game was no longer crashing and I was able to play it at max settings just fine with no more issues.Another thing that bugs me about the game is every time I load the game up it always brings up the Steam overlay then displays a web page asking me to link my Steam account with my Windows account which is not something I feel comfortable doing and there is no option to select NO so I always have to click the X icon to close the web page down some times it can be annoying it would be nice if the game stopped asking me. I was rather gutted when I ran into these problems but I am glad I was finally able to get the game working properly. Right now I think its one of the best racing games currently available. I would still totally recommend it just beware you may encounter some issues and have to fix them before you can play the game.Overall a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to say that as an American, I NEVER thought I would own this game, given that all the driving is done on the left side of the road, not the right side. I thought it would be a bit difficult to get used to it. My thought was correct, and it did take a while to get accustomed to driving on the left side. Once you've gotten past this, you have several things to enjoy:A large map to explore (About 10 x 10 miles)Plenty (as many as 420+) of cars to drive and tune to your likingFantastic optimization (I am literally running the game at 30-40 FPS medium graphics with an Intel Core I5 4th Gen Processor, GeForce GT1030, and 16 GB of RAM) In other words, you can run this game on a potatoA splendid sim-cade (Simulation Arcade) driving system, where the handling feels like a mix of sim-racing and arcade driving games.Beautiful overall visuals (once again I am basically running it on a potato)And So. Many. Damned. Races. You don't have to grind. The game gives you money. I could go on and on about how I have not had to do much of anything and was able to buy my favorite car during the first thirty minutes of gameplay. But, like every game, FH4 has its downsides.Odd stuttering issues (they seem like a CPU Usage issue, which I can't do anything about, it's NOT the game's fault) Occasional issues loading stuff in (again, probably my computers problem, not the games problem)Atrocious Force Feedback issues (Using a Gear/Cog driven wheel, I'm guessing that its the wheel at fault) Force feedback causes the wheel to sort of click (or feel as if it is being smashed and broken to oblivion) as the FFB does it's thing.The Traffic AI are at the top of the "Stupid-Ass Video Game NPCs and AI" list. I followed the traffic around on the highway for a bit and not only did they crash into each other, they kept switching lanes for no reason at all, and completely neglect to look on either side when doing so, resulting in the crash of the player car as well.So yes, I do recommend the game, seeing that all but one of the issues in the cons section are probably my own or my hardware's fault. But, I do strongly recommend buying the Ultimate Edition of the game when it goes on sale, free cars, credit bonuses, stuff like that. Do I know that Forza Horizon 5 has been released? Yes. Do I still recommend Forza Horizon 4? Well duh, its still a great game, buy it before the Devs take it away from the stores!

From the vibrant colors of spring to the icy landscapes of winter, each season not only alters the visual appeal but also transforms the driving dynamics, ensuring a fresh and exciting experience with every race.The attention to detail in the cars is nothing short of extraordinary. The freedom to explore this vast environment creates a sense of adventure, and the seamless transition between solo and online play ensures a seamless and enjoyable multiplayer experience.The game's progression system strikes a perfect balance between accessibility and depth. Whether you're a casual gamer or a hardcore racing enthusiast, Forza Horizon 4 caters to all skill levels. The Horizon Festival, the game's central hub, serves as a social space where players can engage in races, challenges, and events, fostering a sense of community among virtual racers.The soundtrack deserves special mention, featuring an eclectic mix of music that complements the game's energetic atmosphere. From pulse-pounding electronic beats to classic rock anthems, the soundtrack enhances the overall immersive experience and adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the game.In conclusion, Forza Horizon 4 is a masterpiece in the racing genre, offering an unparalleled combination of stunning visuals, realistic driving mechanics, and an expansive open-world environment. Whether you're a casual gamer looking for a thrilling joyride or a dedicated racing enthusiast seeking a comprehensive experience, Forza Horizon 4 delivers on all fronts. _childDocuments_.review: The Good:The core gameplay (driving) is good. It can be customized to be more arcade-like or more sim-like, depending on what you want. There are more arcade-like games out there (e.g. Need for Speed series) and there are more sim-like games (Assetto Corsa) but this game hits the perfect balance of both. Like if you only had space for 1 racing game in your library, this is a good choice.The game support Ultra Widescreen resolutions quite well, but you can tell it didn't start out that way and Ultra Widescreen support was just added along the way. The splash, intro and cut scenes are not in ultrawide. But all the core gameplay modes support ultrawide and the game looks great in it.It makes me want to invest in a racing wheel and building my own racing cockpit for the sim-like experience, but unfortunately there's not enough space in our house for a setup like that. But that's an option for people to get a more realistic "driving sim" experience. It'll be a safe environment for the wife to practice driving 🙂.The sceneries are gorgeous. In between intense racing, you could just sort of drive around, admiring the views. There are many moments where I'm driving to my next mission, but there's a vista or beauty spot I happen to pass through (driving along a beach, or a waterfall) and I have to stop to take a few pictures. It's a nice change of pace from all the breakneck racing. This is what separates it from all the other racing games out there, IMO. It has a photography mini-game.Speaking of mini-games, there are lots of options to earn money in the game aside from winning races. I created a design for my own cars and made it public. A few days later, I was pleasantly surprised to find "Design Reward" messages in my inbox saying I earned 100 credits for each time my design was downloaded and used by other players. There's also a taxi business I invested 100,00 credits into, and it's slowly earning back the in-game credits I invested. There's also an auction house for cars, but the implementation is better than it was in Diablo 3, in that it wasn't short-circuiting player progression. Cars are so easy to acquire, there's no real need to go to the auction house unless it's for a particular rare car you're looking for.🙂Drew and I bought this game to get a preview of what Forza 5 Horizons might look like, and so far I'm not disappointed.The Bad:The UI is a bit cluttered. It took me some time to get used to it. I thought there was no quick way to go to your garage to customize a car you just bought, but it was just hidden in one of the tabs. There are fast travel options to some destinations, but not all. When completing races, new destinations will pop up on the world map, and over time this WILL make the world map super cluttered.The not-so-bad:Car acquisition and collection is easy.Car customization is not as extensive as in Need for Speed Underground. You can only paint the body, hood, side mirrors, spoiler and tint the windows. So far I haven't seen an option to purchase body kits, unless it already came with the car.Car upgrading and tuning is not as extensive as Gran Turismo 2, but it comes close. You can adjust gear ratios to balance acceleration vs top speed. I haven't dived too deeply into it, but there are options to tune the tires, alignment, antiroll bars, springs, damping, aero, brakes and differential.If you stop a multi-race session (e.g. a story mission that has 10 races), there's no easy way to just pick up from where you left off. The game will drop you off in your Home starting point, and you have to drive all the way to where you picked up the mission to resume it.There's no unified, cohesive storyline. Just chapters that pop up all over the place 😃.This being a game released in 2018, there's a lot of content to grind through, and someone new to the game will feel a bit overwhelmed by all the content.The Ugly:Online Multiplayer with friends.Oh my God, Drew and I had such a hard time setting up a convoy so we can drive around and race together. I think it's because the network architecture is housed by Xbox, and we're playing on the Steam platform.

_childDocuments_.review: As driving games go, it's the best I've ever played, not only because of its irresistible scenery, exhilarating driving and perfectly-recreated cars, but because spending time with it puts me in a lasting good mood. It is uncomplicated and thrilling escapism in a shared driving paradise. The game rewards exploration and silliness just as much as careful racing. Like the "Burnout" and "Need for Speed" games, "Forza Horizon 4" encourages plenty of "arcade-style" car gameplay. If you take your car off-road, for instance, and do a bunch of crazy jumps, "Horizon 4" actually rewards you for it. The absolute fastest car in Forza Horizon 4 is the Ferrari 599XX Evolution, which can be modified to hit an amazing top speed of 320mph.

_childDocuments_.review: I think you could pretty much take my "The Crew 2" review, word-for-word, cross out all "Crew" references with a marker and write "Forza" and nobody would notice the difference.  But that's good.So it's a car porn game.  We're not talking super-detailed handling models or anything, just a game with an open world and a lot of cars.  If you're the sort of person who knows the difference between a Z4 and a Z4 GT3, or goes, "Cool!" if there's a Lotus, well, then this is for you.Also coop, which is nice.This game's plot didn't make me cringe in the same way that The Crew 2 did, but it's not exactly going to be winning any prizes for writing.  Look, there's people doing races, and you race the races, and you get money and put more vroom in your cars.  If you want more plot, I donno, maybe an evil car killed your orphan parents and the only way to avenge their deaths is by, uhh, racing cars really hard?Anyway, seriously, it's a fine enough example of the genre.  I'm satisfied.  I'll get some mileage out of it with my wife and we'll drive goofily-painted cars around for awhile until the next distraction comes along.

But you are on PC, you will figure it out- Lots of crashes, especially in online. Random crashes too.- Online loading time is a joke 50% of the time (there are memes about it)- Lots of broken in-game counters (like star card)- Lots of broken achievements. _childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. _childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is remarkable game. It's a racer that's for everybody, instantly accessible for people who don't play racing games, but with enough depth and difficulty to satisfy gamers who prefer simulation. The very premise of Horizon 4 is fun. The quirky, bouncy voice-overs and the festival vibe keeps things free and light-hearted. Races are aimed at creating tight, balanced races that are fun no matter what vehicle you drive, and it does this well. It's fun to just jump in a random race you find.There is a lot of depth to the game, multiple race disciplines keep things interesting and all are genuinely fun. If you get bored of one discipline you can jump in another and get the hang of it really quickly. It doesn't force you through awkward drifting mini-games or shift orientated drag races.Graphically the game is stunning. There is no other word, the cars and environments are photo-realistic. Set any screenshot as my desktop background and I wouldn't even suspect it wasn't the Lake District. The cars themselves look fantastic, lighting is done very well.The seasons mechanics is one of the main attractions to Forza Horizon 4 and have to say it is an interesting one. Certain driving disciplines are more tailored to different seasons, so Winter is good for dirt for example, and Summer more for road racing, and that can get frustrating if you want to change seasons. Seasons are locked to the servers, meaning every week they change, you can't change them in game by moving ahead seasons for example. Each season though does look amazing in it's own way, and adds diversity to game campaign.The long game though is predictably more tailored towards casual gamers. It can be easy to get a big roster of cars without actually having bought one yourself. In this way the game can be easy if you're more of a simulation racer, but Forza Horizon 4 isn't trying to be.Pros-Beautiful graphics-Embodiment of fun-Accessible to all types of gamers-Reasonable roster of cars-Celebration of car culture-Good map-Fantastic amount of tuning abilityCons-Season mechanic can get old, with no way to change to a favourable season-Extensively long tutorial; which keeps you in single player until it's complete-Generally gameplay music is not my cup of tea. That's why I listen to my own radio stations in the background when I play this masterpiece:PForza Horizon 4 is a beautiful game, well polished and full of cars and stunning environments. One more for the casual crowd but fun nonetheless, a fantastic celebration of car culture.Note: All of these ideas are based on ~150 hours of playing experience on the Microsoft Store. You can be sure to see more here^^

Be ready to spend substantial time checking every one of them.- The map is not that big compared to the сгеш for example, but it has dynamic seasons and weather. It doesn't annoy (me at least) cuz it changes. It's a variety. What else do you need?And thankfully everything matches the location. Cuz snowing in Miami like in the game mentioned above is ridiculous.Cons:- Its multiplayer is harder to fix than the сгеш one. And ofc it doesn't work outta the box. Intensive brainf-_- is obligatory. Otherwise, you don't get full experience of the game.- Unstoppable Kieras, Joels and whoever that might be make you wanna press alt+f4 after you open a map to hear a minute or two of absolutely useless crap that no one asked for.-  Menus are just weird and unreasonably complicated. If you don't know where to find what you want it may take you some time browsing through endless tabs and pages inside pages in order to fulfill a simple task.Conclusion:Is it worth your time? Yes. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely blown away by Forza Horizon 4! This game is a masterpiece in every sense of the word. From the moment you start playing, you're immersed in a stunning, dynamic world that shifts with the seasons, each one bringing new challenges and breathtaking visuals. The level of detail is unbelievable—whether it's the autumn leaves falling on country roads or the crisp snow crunching under your wheels in winter, the atmosphere is pure magic.The open-world aspect is one of the best I've experienced. The map is massive, and exploring the beautiful British countryside never gets old. There's always something new to discover, whether it’s hidden barns with legendary cars, speed traps, or stunt jumps that keep the excitement alive. And the variety of cars? Insane! Whether you’re into hypercars, off-roaders, or classic muscle, there’s something for every type of car enthusiast.The online experience is smooth and engaging. The way the game seamlessly integrates multiplayer with single-player is a game-changer. One minute you're cruising solo, and the next, you're in a race with players from around the world without any interruptions. It’s such a fun way to connect with the community.But what really sets Forza Horizon 4 apart is how it manages to balance being accessible for casual players while offering depth for hardcore racing fans. The customization options, tuning capabilities, and difficulty settings give you complete control over your experience.Overall, Forza Horizon 4 is not just a racing game—it’s an experience. Whether you're racing, exploring, or just enjoying the ride, this game nails it in every way. I’ve sunk decent hours into it, and I’m still finding new things to do. They're all a bit different.The tracks? They go left, right, there are elevation changes, but... Meh.Every time you win a race a series of glossy screens flash info at you about all the something or others you've won, unlocked, whatever, Not rep amongst the hardcore street racers, or another sneering rival though. No. Comedy car horns or a tee shirt for your avatar. Yetch.Collisions are entirely without consequence, even with damage turned up to simulation.  Everything from lampposts to dry stone walls (!?!?) can be driven through as though they have the solidity of a light mist.And at the end of a race your competitors politely applaud and nod. Like yeah, you deserved it. It's all so unrelentingly blandly sort of .... nice. But nice like the doctor's upped your meds. As though everything is slightly distant, filtered through a pastel sunbeam.There's no grit, no oil, no body. It's southern comfort and diet coke with an ice cube. Offending no-one but forgotten as soon as you put the glass down, Eventually, mid race, my eyes just drifted off the screen as I slowly realised I didn't care at all. Not frustrated, not beaten, just completely uninterested.Alt-F4.Done

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first try on the 'Forza Horizon' saga. And it was amazing! This game is for every car lover. I was first amazed by 'Project Cars' (1 & 3) games but the bar is almost set higher here. I don't know where to start.There are numerous cars you can buy and drive, even on the base version of the game. It is arcade at its best, but not only : you can choose the difficulty, and even set the level on 'simulation mode' to have the closest feelings of driving the jewels you are into. You can open doors, hood and trunk to visualize the mechanics, take pictures of them if you are a real hardcore fan. The sound effects and the motors sonic mechanics are just insane.The game offers dozens of challenges and ways to surpass yourself while exploring new roads and ways. You can buy houses, find ancient cars, take part in online or offline tournaments, make drift challenges, complete the campaign, explore until you can't anymore, find panels, change seasons, modify cars, complete specifi missions, perform stunts... Ride on roads, small dirt roads, highways or obviously taking it offroad.Landscapes are mindblowing, colours are vivid, changing seasons makethe environment change in one of the mostperfect ways. And you are rewarded for all the exploration you do. Well, basically, you will be rewarded if you do anything... Sometimes at a point where it is almost childish. You could gain points by doing nothing.The atmosphere is exceptional, it feels like you are in a festival or a huge playground. The soundtrack could have been more diverse though.The online is as diverse as the offline mode, with classic coop or pvp modes, but also with battle royale mode (you'll have to test it to get what it is about) ('The Eliminator'), challenges mode ('The Super7'). Too bad some online challenges (like match ones) aren't possible because of having too few players in addition to lasting like 2 hours (why??)!Unfortunately there are way too much and too long loading screens. It takes long minutes to launch the game (I have a recent PC), to launch a race, etc. We should have the opportunity to skip cinematics as a race is about to start!Another major flaw is that I could race (or win any race) with buggys, even if I turned down the difficulty... They just slide in the mud over and over. Plus there a way too many dumb collectibles : did we need to have a character to design? I also would have added more secret treasures or something like that, because everything appears on the map, it's too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Funnily enough, about a week before Forza was released on Steam, I was getting back into racing games. Personally, I am much more of an arcade racer rather than a sim racer, having grown up on games like Need for Speed Hot Pursuit 2, Burnout, and even Mario Kart (if you count that, though it's more party than arcade racer).Forza Horizon 4 leans into that, bridging the gap between arcade racing and sim racing, all tied up in a casual-feeling and fun "festival" setting. The game feels rewarding in just about every action you take, almost encouraging you to get better through any way you can control your car. It feels welcoming to enter the game and not feel as though I need to be a car junkie to enjoy all the details placed into everything, from the car designs themselves to the tuning that goes into what's underneath the hood.However, if there is any one issue I would have with the game, it's the stability of the game itself. There's nothing more frustrating than having a blast with friends then having the screen go black and hearing my computer fans ramp up as it reboots. The fact that the developers say that Forza does not play nice with *Discord* or MSI Afterburner feels like an absurd oversight. Frankly, if Forza Horizon 5 is announced within the next month or two, I may recommend instead waiting for that to discover if it will have a simultaneous Microsoft and Steam release and if it will no longer have issues with popular programs for PC gamers.If you are fine dealing with such issues, I absolutely recommend this game. It is a blast to even simply drive around with friends, let alone actually do races. However, I cannot overstate the annoyance that this game gives through its crashes and compatibility issues on startup.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horzion 4 is a great game for newcomers but returning players should probably steer clear of unless they want to start from scratch.---------Quick answer---------Pros: Massive car library to choose from, multiple tasks to keep you busy,you can customize your cars look as well as to how it is tuned, not pay to win, when an achievement is unlocked on the steam version it is also unlocked on xbox account, improved loading times, less intensive load on PC compared to xbox app, new challenges with season change, improved controller support (PS4 controller)Cons: Cutscenes you cant skip, dialogue that is pretty boring, bugs (mostly the steam version of the game), can customize avatar but leaves a lot to be desired, most avatar items are behind a roulette wheel system, non skippable ads about the games dlc, achievements from xbox account don't transfer to steam version, save file from console/xbox app don't transfer to steam version, some minor frame rate issues---------Complete Answer---------I will start out by saying that I have played almost all of the Forza Horizon games and that in specific I played the three versions of this game (console, xbox PC app, steam version). Between the 3 versions I have 70 hours played on the steam version and 61 Hours on the PC and console versions together.This version of the game has improved load times, in certain places, such as fast travel and changing vehicles. But there were several bugs that had become apparent, such as when restarting a story mission like drift club the game might restart you and send you through the map. Another is with the players star card, a card that tracks certain milestones and gives you a icon next to your name depending on the accomplishments. As of now one of this is bugged and will not record any progress meaning the user can't get it until its fixed. One that happens on occasion is a stuttering effect, but it only appears once in a while. Some achievements also don't register when their unlock requirement is achieved such as The Tortoise and the Hare achievement and others unlock earlier then they are supposed to like The Noisy Cartographer. On the issue of achievements, users who have played this game on console or the xbox app on PC will have to earn their achievements all over again. You will also have to start your progress on the game from the beginning as none of the game save data transfers over to the steam version. But on the bright side any new achievements do unlock on both accounts.Besides these slight issues the game is still a very enjoyable game. The game has a variety of different events and race types that should make all racing fans happy. There are vast amounts of things to complete for every achievement hunter. Per usual Forza greets new users to their increasing library of cars to select from and users can even get free cars via wheelspins which are given upon leveling up. The game map gives users a giant playground to explore and that changes with the seasons. For those who don't want to race there are also playground games which allow users to play team based games like capture the flag with their cars and infected vs survivors(basically tag). Users who want to gain more income in the game can even do stories such as Isah's Taxi to get a passive income every day. On the car side of things there are hundreds of cars to collect and sell, some only attained through special means. Besides collecting users can tune their cars and share the tunes with other players. If you fancy more of the artistic side, you can customize your cars exterior and share that with other players. When you have too many cars or their are cars you want you can head to the auction house to sell or bid on cars.When users bore of the stuff mentioned above there are things like the dlc (Fortune Island & Lego Speed Champs), but if you don't wish to spend money you can instead play the game mode The Eliminator, which is Forzas take on a battle royale. If you do choose to get the dlc I would recommend Lego Speed Champ as it gives the users so much to do and change the game in a variety of ways. As for Fortune Island it is more suited to people who want to do offroad races as well as drift. This isn't to say that those things are all the dlc offers but it makes up a majority of it.For some closing criticisms this game could have changed a lot in this version of the game. The leaderboards in PR stunts could have been fixed so there weren't so many obvious cheater results. Cutscenes and voice dialogue could have been skippable, even just in things that you wanted to redo they could have changed this. If you played the console or xbox app version this game will largely feel the same as before. There are some new bugs and the player base is not as big as it used to be. But this is still a fun game, it just comes with some flaws, the biggest being transferring data. Returning users could have been greeted with their car collection, level, milestones or just at least the achievements but instead are made to start from scratch. Halo Master Chief collection welcomes returning users to access to their achievements so they don't to unlock the same achievement again. Lets just hope the next Forza will be improved and solve some of these issues.Oh one last thing, for you Initial D fans, if you want a AE86/Trueno, yeah it ain't cheap, prepare to grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4. The magnum opus of open world racing game. A safe haven of hundreds of cars. A canvas to pour your inner creativity. It's almost unnecessary to introduce this well-known franchise. Chances are you already knew what Horizon is all about, and you're reading the review section just for fun.Horizon is a sim-cade game, a balance between realism and arcade fun. Vehicles on simulation setting behave and feel almost like a real car, over correcting often resulting a date between your car and a tree. There are 4 discipline of racing. Road Racing is the normal road surfaces, Street Scene is the underworld illegal races with traffics, Dirt Racing are basically rally. And Cross Country is the heavy 4x4 offroad branch. Multiplayer are a blast with drift adventures, ranked matchmaking, playground games, you name it. Although sometimes you get stuck in menus for like 2+ minutes.Graphics are amazing, somehow they made a scenery that's both realistic and surreal. There's alot of car details, world details, etc. One of Horizon's unique feature is the camera. It lets you capture beautiful pictures in the game with actual photography properties like focus, aperture, shutter speed and many more. There's actually too much in this game to write a review instead of a novel.It's a shame everything is in slideshow mode a.k.a heavy stuttering. Let's be honest, Horizon was never a stable game in the first place. Unfortunately, the steam port was even much bigger disaster. In racing games, every single piece of time is precious, even miliseconds. Combining stuttering and racing is like a complete paralyze and blindness in a moment while racing. Imagine going 300kmh then stutter, suddenly you lose your braking point. Some people experiencing CTDs, freezing, server issues and so on. Personally I've been experiencing heavy stutter, the devs did actually know about these but have yet propose a solution. I hope the devs actually care about this game, and patch out these major problems. I and alot of other people really want to enjoy this game. It's a great game with miserable execution.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Pros:+Looks great+Lots of cars+Plenty of places to drive+Interesting setting/seasonal change mechanicCons:-Poorly balanced AI-No qualifying in single player (you usually start last to prop up AI that can't overtake)-Loading time bug making major part of online game unplayable-Not much reason to try most cars-Many cars unlocked by RNG-No rear view mirror in bumper/hood cam-Tracks get repetitive-Delisted-No more live service features================Full Review:While the game is fairly fun... there are some massive game design holes, meaning the most unfun part of this game is... the racing, which is kind of an important part. It seems whoever was in charge of how races work really phoned it in with the most basic experience you can get.Plus now the game has been delisted (not before a final discount to lure people in to the sinking ship) the live service festival playlist (possibly the most interesting part of the game) is no longer going to be updated... they aren't even just letting it randomly generate new events forever more, or looping old content, just turning it off, great!So yeah, while it is a great looking game, and is fun to drive around, the content gets pretty burned out quickly.Other notable issues:- AI difficulty that scales via rubberbanding (Rather than drive better, they will just get unrealistic performance boosts, not to mention once they are far enough ahead they no longer get slowed down by breaking through walls and other debris, not leaving a hole for you to pass through, making catching up more difficult as you have to smash them yourself), I recommend only setting the AI as high as "highly skilled " as anything above that is just a chore, and doesn't really offer much outside of a few live service events (ended) and a few extra credits.- Always start at the back of the pack in single player, leaving you to get through the melee while the boosted AI speeds off (presumably there is no qualifying as the AI can't overtake so, starting first would have no competition, though that would be better if the only competition is from these bargain bin AI)- 30min loading times for online adventure races (despite the name, these are just regular PVP races, it's due to a known cross platform bug with MS store, which has never been fixed)- No reason to invest in more than a handful of cars (Most races you can just take the same car into, so unless you force yourself to try something new, it can get very repetitive, feels like there could have been much more effort from game designers to regularly encourage you to try something new)- Tedious RNG car unlocks (Also bogged down by a high chance to unlock clothing or cash instead)- No rear view mirror in bumper/hood cam (even though in the cockpit cams there are working mirrors)- Checkpoint system is lacklustre (super easy to miss checkpoints, and it's often hard to see where the next one is, especially if you use bumper/hood cams)- The tracks often feel very similar, as they are mostly just random checkpoints scattered across similar feeling roads with some random barriers and stuff thrown in to jazz it up- The best way to beat the AI is to just slam into the leader on corners, though this could be a pro as it's quite fun, and then you can just block them/rewind if they try to overtake. (Even though anti-troll mechanics exist when racing vs humans, which will slow you down for smashing into walls, or ghost you if it thinks you're going to ram someone)-If doing an event, and during the after race flow you accidentally click 'retry' (for instance if you check your score on the leaderboard and press the button to back out twice instead of once, your progress will not be saved, even though your leaderboard entry will persist, not to mention it takes 10x longer to load retrying from the results screen than retrying mid event.-Coming out  of photo mode your controls are locked for a second or so (not good for high speed photos)-cant pause the game during the race intro, have to wait till after the green light.-The markers for drift/speed zones can be destroyed, often leaving no marker for where the zone ends, which can make it tricky to see where the objective isSo in conclusion, there are large parts of a decent game here, but also large holes in that too, so you might have a decent time, you might have a frustrating time... the game is best enjoyed casually because anything else is going to throw up issues.

_childDocuments_.review: As seen by a casual gamer with a life long passion for rally and racing games that enjoys playing on keyboard and external camera view.Forza Horizon 4 is one of the best car racing games I have ever played!!Strong :✔ Insane variety and list of cars!!!!!✔ Physics and graphics are super well done, the environment is gorgeous and the most mind-blowing thing is that every week the map changes to each one of the 4 seasons including all sorts of weather conditions✔best rain I have ever experienced in a racing/rally game to date. Rain has actual sense of depth just like IRL when you can see it fall on the street or on lakes from distance. it's not just a simple animation layer on your screen any more. ✔ Also water drops are actually dynamically and individually rendered on your car - which is a detail that blew me away. ✔ Even wetness on the tarmac is interacting with your tires going through it (sound and splash effect depending the amount of water)✔ Car design is absolutely magnificent. The attention to the detail is insane, even the car lights are done with so much detail. The detail is so great that at some moments you will be able to even notice the speedometers and RPM-meters animate and display fully real time accurate measurements while driving with external cam view ( ! ).✔ Satisfying amount of car customization. Not too much or chaotic and not too little. Just about right. From engine upgrades to body paints.✔ Pretty cool voice acting and some times a nice drop of humor. also a good cameo for top gear in there. some of the special missions include some very enjoyable historical and factual story telling about some specific cars.✔ Some secret specials here and there like a Halo themed mission that lets you drive the Warthog (you can also obtain if for your self when you can afford it), and a head to head that can let you unlock the QUADRA TURBO-R V-TECH from Cyberpunnk2077!✔ Not much for dirt effects but splashing through water is extremely satisfying.✔ The music selections are so damn awesome and some tracks are so memorable I eventually found them on Spotify and added them to my favorites!✔ SH*TTONES of things to do. Like seriously from the standard race events to the weekly events to custom events created by other players!!!✔ The 2 map expansions are actually worth playing and super cool to experience!!Weak :❌Rewind button response will fail way too many times❌If you select retry at the end of an event the loading time is going to ridiculously slow (extra ❌ given here because some times the reload finished and the car falls through the map) in order to avoid this either restart an event before you reach the finish line. or simply collect the whatever reward you would get, go through the event scores and restart it once you are on free-roam again (that's seriously faster than selecting "retry")❌tiny detail but it's slightly off-putting: old design flaw where the shadow of the tires does not actually start from the point of contact to the floor allowing light to be seen under the tires. This "floating" tire effect is such a very very old design flaw, i was surprised to come across it a couple of time.❌Car damage is limited to some very very basic visual scratches. best thing you can see is loosing a mirror or a spoiler (in case you have any) or some mad-protectors depending the design but that's it.I am left without words to describe how much fun I had playing this game. My time tracker speaks for itself and I'm not into any repetitive gameplay. It's super rare for me to reach anything above 100h for a car racing game. This is a truly awesome game with an open world design that keeps things fresh with an easy UI/UX design and the diversity of the environment combined with the seasons made me not get bored to even drive from one corner of the map to the other without fast traveling. From super cars to rally cars, from hyper cars to drift cars and trucks. This was a real journey and I will look forward to the next title from this studio for sure!!This is hands down recommended!PS: note to self, it's amazing how great the graphical details are evolving in racing games. i'm keen to experience more!
