_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love racing games. It’s not reflected on my Steam profile very well, but the racing genre is easily one of my favourites, and has been since I was very young. I experienced countless different titles on the Xbox and PS2 when I was still primarily a console gamer. From bigger names like Need for Speed and Gran Turismo, to plenty of other lesser known titles like Crash ‘n’ Burn, L.A. Rush, Midtown Madness 3 and so many more, I spent countless hours messing around in those early open worlds and improving my lap times. Most Wanted 2005 is easily my favourite racing title, with a great map and sense of progression, intense and rewarding cop chases, and an all-time great soundtrack; I didn’t think anything could ever top it…until I played Forza Horizon 4.I haven’t had any direct experience with this franchise until this game. I played quite a bit of the spiritual predecessor to Forza Motorsport, Project Gotham Racing, back on the Xbox, but that’s where my experience with Forza started and ended prior to FH4. And wow, what a first impression this franchise has made on me. There are so many things that I love about this game:- It has an absolutely staggering amount of content. 145 hours is what it took me to get all the achievements throughout the base game and expansions, and there was still plenty of races to do, plenty of cars to unlock, lots of online content to engage in, and I only really experienced one full festival series. Each activity in the game has a separate progression tracker which lets you know what there is to unlock if you keep playing or complete a specific mission with a higher score, which is really helpful when deciding what you want to work towards.- Handling and difficulty is highly customizable. You can turn on and off assists to your liking, and pretty much every car has access to a large variety of parts and a highly in-depth tuning menu to give you complete freedom over how you want your car to feel. There’s a plentiful number of AI difficulty settings too; I settled on the highly skilled setting as the cars always kept up to a good degree without feeling like they were guaranteed to pass me as high rubber-banding usually results in. Higher difficulty settings usually have at least AI car ahead of the pack that is rather annoying to catch up to even with well-timed laps, though you are forced to experience the highest difficulty AI in the weekly trial races, and in these settings, they are incredibly fun if you have a group that knows what they’re doing.- The setting of Great Britain was not something I expected to see in a major racing game like this, but I was really glad to see how well they executed it. Maybe I’m a bit biased, but the buildings, landmarks, country drives, the city of Edinburgh; they all feel perfectly translated from the real-world into a more condensed setting. I also quite appreciated the car culture that was explored in some of the more structured Horizon story missions, as the country has quite an extensive history of car manufacturing.- The tone of this game is infectiously positive; it genuinely feels impossible to feel negative emotions while playing it. Even when losing, I was always having so much fun that it never bothered me. This means it can act as a comfort game, something I could always imagine playing no matter how I’m feeling. Also, the soundtrack has plenty of great tunes, from rock to rap, drum and bass to classical; as someone who loves a diverse range of music, it’s lovely to see a modern racing game with so many great tunes.- The level of freedom this game provides is unlike anything I’ve ever seen. Hundreds of car options, dozens upon dozens of races and missions, and you’re not directed to do anything in particular as there are very little restrictions put in your way. In most cases, you can attempt most races with any car you choose, and the difficulty comes from the AI choosing cars that are of the same performance class to you, so it never feels like you’ve won the game by getting a supercar as a reward. The only real goal the game mentions is to reach superstar status at like Level 150, and how you get to that point is entirely up to you once you complete the opening few hours.Forza Horizon 4 became one of my most played games on Steam and one of my favourite games ever made in a matter of months. It is a truly best-in-industry example of arcade racing, and reflects a development cycle of games which has been iterated and improved upon for over a decade by this game’s initial release. Any complaints I could make are grasping at straws, though I will say that the game is quite pricey for a three-year old release which has just received a new entry. Save yourself some money and pickup the premium edition on a sale; if you like arcade racing, I can almost guarantee you will love this game. And the fact that there will be entries past this suggests to me this series is only going to raise the bar even higher than it already has for years to come. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good, the realism in the scenery is beautiful, the cars and their tunings are very customizable, and there are lots of events for multiplayer or solo experiences.LIKES:It's everything you want in a racing game: lots of events, challenges, and fun! The game is visually beautiful, including the change of the seasons, so even if it's the same map you get to do different things in different seasons. You can change your car's setup depending on the challenge or the season, and can get great setups from other players. There are challenges that are "businesses", in which you complete a chapter and then get credits the next time you login. For example, you can own a taxi, a delivery, or a car improvement business and if you get 3 stars in each of their chapters then you get profits. The multiplayer is amazing, you can see the ghosts of other players in the open road, can challenge them or ask them to join your convoy to take events/races together. Every single playing mode is fun; I bet I haven't mentioned them all, but this game is worth it.DISLIKES:The seasons are from Friday to Thursday, and sometimes I don't have time to finish all the season challenges. Maybe it's a personal problem, so you might do better than me. Also, you can't import images or logos to decorate the cars, so any realistic vinyl design you see is made by hand by other players, so appreciate their work.I love that there is always something to do in this game, and it doesn't get repetitive; it took me 80hrs to post this review because I was having soooo much fun! You definitely should get it if you wanted the fun of NFS and the realism of Grand Turismo, plus with a great non-invasive multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4, the latest installment in the acclaimed racing franchise, sets a new standard for realism and variety in the world of virtual driving. Developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios, this game delivers an unparalleled experience with its authentic car controls and a diverse array of vehicles and tracks that cater to every racing enthusiast's desires.Forza Horizon 4 shines brightest in its dedication to delivering realistic car controls. The attention to detail is evident from the moment you take control of your first vehicle. The responsiveness of the cars, the way they handle various terrains, and the nuanced physics make for an incredibly immersive experience. Whether you're drifting through the tight corners of a city circuit or tearing through the open countryside, each vehicle feels distinct, providing a true-to-life driving sensation.The game's realistic weather effects further elevate the driving experience. Rain-slicked roads affect traction, and the changing seasons introduce dynamic challenges, such as snow-covered surfaces that demand adjustments to your driving style. Forza Horizon 4's commitment to authenticity sets it apart, making every race feel like a genuine test of skill.One of the standout features of Forza Horizon 4 is the extensive roster of cars spanning different categories. From sleek sports cars and powerful muscle machines to rugged off-road vehicles, there's a car for every taste and preference. The inclusion of classic and modern cars from various manufacturers adds depth to the game, ensuring players can find their dream ride.While the variety is impressive, some players may find that certain categories receive more attention than others. However, regular updates and expansions continue to introduce new vehicles, ensuring the game remains fresh and engaging for the long term.Forza Horizon 4 doesn't just limit itself to standard racetracks. Instead, it offers a diverse range of environments and terrains, providing players with a true adventure in every race. Dirt racing, off-roading, drag racing – the game caters to all tastes, offering tracks that challenge your skills in different ways.The meticulously crafted landscapes, including a dynamic day-night cycle and the breathtaking beauty of changing seasons, contribute to an immersive racing experience. The attention to detail in track design ensures that each race feels unique, whether you're tearing through the streets of a historic city or navigating the treacherous paths of a cross-country circuit.Forza Horizon 4 sets the bar high for racing games with its realistic car controls, diverse car categories, and thrilling tracks across various terrains. While no game is without its minor imperfections, the overall experience is nothing short of exhilarating. Whether you're a casual racing fan or a dedicated enthusiast, Forza Horizon 4 offers an unforgettable journey into the world of high-speed, high-stakes racing. Buckle up and get ready for a ride like no other.

_childDocuments_.review: I will perhaps redo the review later but I just have to vent.I paid about $60 for the ultimate edition. I was in one of those moods where money was no object and I was sick of myself penny pinching on here. Everyone swears this is the best racing game on PC. Fine. Let’s go.*Pros*Yes, it's gigantic, open world, tons of things to do, 450 something cars to collect, fine tune (so to speak), create or download custom liveries for, go completely bonkers in with no concern for damage to your rig or harm to others. Online functionality keeps things lively, at least in an artificial sense until you specifically try to match up for individual competitions.*Cons*Music is absolute cancer and severely limited, and there’s no way to apparently even mute it at an options level. Just make it quiet at 1/10 setting. You have to turn off the radio all the time over and over. So have fun trying to play your own music. That'll get annoying. And if you do, you will still be missing out on DJ commentary that’s related to what you've done. Apparently prior games allowed custom music but this one did away with it.The game does run great but the visuals, and I truly mean everything your eyes will take in, feel .... like plastic. This game is plastic. It’s a shiny-happy-people, AI-designed, nerf padded, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ball pit of a game. The car models are good but the world feels like a bucket of public domain assets that got bathed in modern post processing. And then there is all the voice acting. The entire cast of actors are snorting adderall before and after their individual lobotomies, because not one of them has a personality. Coated with sanitizer. No souls. Aural equivalent of gingers, everywhere. They make noises with their mouths but they say nothing of value. It's maddening to listen to these people talk. I'm losing my own contact with the earth realm as I play this game. Is this the extent of humanity? I know I once played games where people could act out a range of emotions, but they are a distant memory now. I only know to….drive, and to…be stoked. I….I must…resist….The only other character in any other video game in my entire life’s experience that resembles what you’ll find in Forza Horizon 4 is perhaps this good wholesome boy from Dragon Age: I don’t really know where to go from here. I will keep playing. I know I wont get my money’s worth. Ultimate edition should be $30 max, base game should be $20 max. If you want a racer and you don’t care about open world, you could do better with countless other titles, especially from Codemasters. If you DO want open world and Steam is your platform, well I guess this is the best.Play this for the car modeling. Inside and outside. Very nice dash cams which is a rarity these days. The car modeling is obviously where all the effort went. Just dont expect anything to drive realistically. This is the most arcade-y of arcade racers ever concocted by man. Everything is on ice skates. Every object you hit is made of paper mache, except the objects made of adamantium. Good luck figuring out which is which.Edit: March 2024. It is done. I dont need to 3 star everything or get every car, but I did at least basically do every event within reason. Didnt quite get the final upgrade to my lego house but otherwise I feel the game is now complete and I will never touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was highly skeptical of this game given what I heard about its open world and gacha-esque "wheelspin" system. For context, I highly disliked almost all open world games I played prior to this game.However, I eventually warmed up to the game - mostly because of the driving and car customizing aspect (e.g. liveries, car body parts, etc). While I did not specifically come into the game with an expectation of extensive customization features, what *was* present did pleasantly surprise me. Another thing I'd like to add - one that's a positive for me, but as I understand might be a negative for others - is the lack of strict progression enforcement. This game is self-paced in nature with multiple reward tracks, and the "PI class" (i.e. speed class) system for cars serve as a means to limit car eligibility for certain events instead of being an arbitrary progression marker. Therefore, a D-class car will be grouped with other D-class cars; S2-class cars with other S2-class cars; and so on, and so forth. You *don't* start from the bottom and follow some "win your way to the top" plot. So if you want, you can right away get to driving and racing in hypercars or offroad rally cars.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4Genre	Racing gameCampaign	YesGame length	135-200HDifficulty modes	8Score	9/10Forza Horizon 4💡Overview🔸 In Forza Horizon 4 – It even makes our weather beautiful. As the season's change, the weather and the nature of the light change with the driving conditions. Edina's New Town shines in the faint sunshine of spring, and in winter the snow in the Highlands sucks all the light out of the sky. Ambleside cottages are beautiful in summer when the trees are very green and you can almost smell them. If you have a 4K TV, this is what it is made for. From time to time, like the first time I passed Edinburgh Castle in a completely yellowish blue on a summer night in Scotland, its beauty became quite emotional.◼️ In Game You unlock seasons by earning Influence, one of the two in-game currencies. The other is gear-centric Credits. The XP-like Influence is earned by entering races, finding cars, and successfully completing challenges. In fact, Influence, along with the new My Horizon Life campaigns and fresh customization features, causes the racer to lean into RPG elements more than ever before.◼️ You now progress through the game by exploring more than 25 My Horizon Life story threads. Each of these represents a different way to spend time in the game world, including Road Racing, Drifting, and Stunt Driving. Everything you do in these career campaigns earns Influence, be it nailing stunts, taking photos, or creating sharable car decals or Blueprint race challenges. Even better, you aren't locked into a My Horizon Life campaign; you can jump to a different one at any time.In the depth🔸 This is a game about the driving experience rather than the mechanics, and Forza Horizon 4 welcomes tourists as well as the gears. You can wash through low-rise walls and shrubs without scratching your paint, ride in a Ferrari in the rain, or take an Alfa Romeo up the mountain with just a little difficulty. Although you can go under the hood and tricks with any conceivable aspect of a favorite ride, share tuning settings and create and load custom levers, it's great to pick the car you like and head out into the countryside. Go to town to see what you like can work with it◼️ Your character is also seen when you interact with NPCs or venture into a house. In Forza Horizon 4, you can buy houses—hubs that act as your avatar's base of operations. They each grant different bonuses, such as cars, fast travel options, and character customization gear. Houses don't come cheap, starting at roughly 200,000 Credits and venturing into the millions.🕹️ Gameplay🔸 Forza Horizon 4 is as much an offline game as an online one, but, thankfully, PlayGround Games doesn't force you into matches with strangers. Like Forza Horizon 3, this game uses Drivatars, AI-based competitors that are based on the driving data of the people in your Xbox Friends List, to populate your game world when playing solo.Your Drivatar does the same when it enters your friends' game worlds. You can also team up with Drivatars by rolling up to one, honking your horn, and forming a Convoy. With the right Skill perks, the cars in your Convoy can help you accumulate Influence at a faster rate or discover Barn Finds.◼️ Barn Finds are rare cars that you find in barns scattered through the landscape. Some barns are easy to spot, while others require true exploration. Several Barn Finds are only available in certain seasons, so you're encouraged to revisit landscapes as the temperatures change.◼️ Included are many graphics options, including Dynamic Render Quality, Motion Blur, and VSync. There's even a mode for people who suffer from colorblindness. The game supports 4K Resolution 🔍Forzathonlive🔸 On the upside, you can earn credits in #ForzathonLive that let you purchase exclusive vanity items and emotes from the Forzathon Shop. If you aren't in the mood for #FozathonLive happenings, you can challenge others to standard multiplayer matches or participate in co-op missions.☣️The best racing game I've ever seen☢️🟩 Pros+Online functionality creates the impression of a dynamic world+Stunning amount of detail and visual variety+ Freedom to progress through the game as you desire.+ Changing seasons alter how you approach races+ A ridiculous number of cars.+ Features over 450 licensed cars+ Solid handling as ever with a huge number of vehicles to unlock🟥 Cons- Tedious #ForzathonLive online contests.- Lacks a custom music station.-It takes a while, though repetition eventually sets in-Road textures would occasionally vanish during testing.

Rainbows appear after rain, snowmen build on the roadside in winter, and fireworks are set off at night in the main camp. The competition part was very enjoyable, especially as I watched myself being bullied from the beginning to gradually challenging higher-level AI and leaving them behind. At the same time, I also had leisure to enjoy the scenery. If I could come across beautiful songs, it would be even more wonderful. The day and night weather season system is complete, and there is no shortage of drifting, speed measurement, and long jump that racing games should have. There is also a variety of multi-purpose vehicles for multi terrain competitions. Wealth Island DLC is very exciting. Lego DLC God of the Gods.Disadvantages, to be honest, unfortunately, the biggest drawback is that I found myself not enjoying the racing theme and many of its fixed gameplay. I came to play this game from Ubisoft Extreme Country's hundreds of hour retreat pit. I thought I would like it because it's all about racing, but the problem is here. I only enjoy playing the content of racing races, and I can't enjoy the rest of the racing themed content. Horizon 4 is a game that completely revolves around racing, with many gameplay and content that are very addictive. Racing is only a small part of it, and it is even different from the Need for Speed series that I had a great time playing with. Due to the elements of police and bandit confrontation, Need for Speed is still a racing part, which accounts for a considerable proportion compared to other content. On the contrary, Horizon 4 weakens the proportion of racing content, I have done too much tedious numerical challenge content, and the focus is clearly more on the online multiplayer part and high-quality model performance. Coincidentally, these are not the contents that I care about. In fact, by the time I played the game for half an hour, I had already felt bored and felt that the content was highly repetitive and scattered. Unfortunately, I couldn't get a refund for the key I bought. I thought I could play it as an achievement driven game, but in the end, the difficulty of my achievements successfully persuaded me to quitAlso, because I came from an extreme country, I would unconsciously compare myself during the gameplay. I didn't mean to use Extreme Land to step on the horizon, but I found that one of these games focuses more on racing, while the other revolves entirely around racing themes. Grab this if you have friends playing or you don't have an SSD to play FH5.Pros : -Relatively cheap at discount-Well optimized and can run pretty well on older rigs-Lots of cars-Quite photogenic (autumn and winter are pretty)-Photo mode of course-Still gets a regular festival playlist content (although recycled and PG has moved to FH5)-Community tunes is available for players who are lazy to tune their cars.-Community maps and races are available to try for fun.Cons : -Worse physics than FH5 (driving feels much better in FH5)-Worse graphics than FH5 (not really a problem)-Being forced to use snow tires for winter unless you love a slippery experience-Drifting is not bad but FH5 absolutely wrecks FH4 -For some reason, I can NOT join my friends via Xbox Game Bar's social. The game always crashes every time I try this. Fortunately, this does not happen in FH5. -Abysmal pvp loading experience. This is also fixed in FH5.-Time-consuming festival playlist experience (need to win more/unnecessary races & events that not everyone likes). You can get two Festival Playlist car prizes WITHOUT being forced to play Playground Games PvP or qualify in Horizon Open in FH5.-Does not get new content anymore from PG. Okay for some people but not for me. This diminishes my reason to play this game. -Minor QoL, the game doesn't tell you info on tires and suspension for community tunes. Fortunately, PG fixed this in FH5.

_childDocuments_.review: Best arcade racer since Burnout Paradise. I'm almost 200 hours in and have yet to even touch the expansions. There is plenty to do. Still has an active online community most of the time, and the weekly seasonal challenges area great way to expand your garage. It's not without its flaws though. Biggest gripe I have is the inability to mute other players in the game. If you get into the seasonal multiplayer challenges, you sometimes get really lucky and enjoy the sweet sweet sounds of some random guy, chewing his food while his girl yells at his screaming kids the entire time you are doing the challenge because some ***hole forgot to mute their mic. There is literally no way to mute them nor is there a way to turn off VOIP. How this feature, which is in literally evey other game i've ever played, gets ignored is beyond comprehension.Also, occasionally there are infinite loading loops and long load times during multiplayer events that cause other players to quit instead of waiting, which can ruin an in-progress multiplayer championship.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game, good graphics, good physics, good systems.BUT :IF you want to pull your hair out in frustration because of the "AI" NPC racers (named "drivatars"), buy it and lose all your hair.NPC NASA rocket launch starts :Physics do not apply to the NPC racers, at the start some of the cars behind will have rocket boosters attached to their cars and blast past your Agera RS in a freaking Porsche Macan with a 40-50 kmh difference in the first 3-5 seconds.NPC cornering :Very inconsistent, and as mentioned, they do not adhere to physics. Try to follow their cornering speed ? Nope.  Sometimes they have bubblegum tyres that just sticks and turns and fly past but sometimes they become normal. Seen a Zonda R turning a corner while tyres screaching but still gets shoved to the roadside by a Land Rover blasting past with a higher cornering speed ? Come to FH4 and experience it !NPC Super Teamwork :NPCs in your immediate vicinity will just keep doing brake checks and ram you off the road like you are just a balloon, while the few NPCs far out front fly off into the horizon. Their catch up system are so great that a racer can come from behind 50kmh faster, move into your racing line and shove his butt with glowing brake lights into your face.It's not a bad game, BUT be prepared to be pissed AF playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is undeniably super fun, offering an engaging experience that keeps players coming back for more. This aspect not only adds a layer of excitement but also encourages exploration and experimentation with different vehicles. The game boasts superb scenery, immersing players in vibrant, beautifully crafted environments that capture the essence of the game’s setting. The attention to detail in the landscapes enhances the overall experience, making each race feel unique and captivating.Additionally, the nice soundtracks complement the gameplay perfectly, enhancing the atmosphere and keeping players engaged throughout their racing adventures. With lots of resemblance to real-life locations in the United Kingdom, players can enjoy a sense of familiarity while racing through stunning replicas of iconic landmarks and landscapes. _childDocuments_.review: - USING WHEEL & PEDALS IS POSSIBLE!!- BIG UPDATE (Now I give 5 stars to the game)I wrote that this game was almost impossible to play with Wheel and pedals. I was WRONG (fortunately)- The cam inside the car showing "hands" is NOT realistic: The wheel CAN go lot furher than 45º to each side. So the way to use your wheel is NOT  taking into account the drivers hand!! You can use the HUD vision that actually shows the Wheel Rotation. THAT is the way to set it (and test driving to confirm you feel comfortable)JUST DO THIS:- Set Wheel rotation to about 600-700º in your device provile (I use Logitech G29 with Logitech G Hub software) IN THE GAME: You will have to spend a bit of time tunning the right values to use the wheel:- In Controls select the Wheel and go to Advanced settings (pressing Space bar or the button to acces) THIS IS THE TAB YOU NEED TO "TUNE".- At 1st set Force Feedback almost to zero, so you can adjust the right values to turn the wheel without confusiion with the force feedback response.- I lowered to about "20" all force feedback settings- You have to test Linearity of Wheel and Dead zone, so you can get nice control with small rotation of the wheel, and also good control with full rotation.- Once you get it, you can increase the force feedback effects (although it will make more difficult to drive) ----------------------------The game is GREAT.  "Free world" driving is THE REASON why I purchased this game. I have many car simulators but wanted something to drive "out of a track", in highways, cities, etc.HOWEVER something is VERY WRONG (NO, see the update above):- Using Wheel & Pedals (Logitech G29 in my case):I cannot believe nor understand how Developers didn't take more care to allow a WIDER range of Wheel rotation. It's unaceptable narrow, just about 45º Right/Left (90º in total aprox.) That's a BIG MISTAKE if you want REALISTIC driving!!!If you use "inside car" camera, you CAN see the hands of the driver will ONLY turn that range. It is NOT a wheel problem, it's a game design problem (I DO HOPE they release a patch to fix this)I spent many hours setting up the Wheel the best possible (in the game and Logitech driver profile) to get the most realism driving experience, but since the Game only turns left-right in so narrow range, it's impossible to get a realistic driving.AT LEAST it should turn left/right 90º, making it a total of 180º wheel range.It seems the game was planned/designed for gaming pads, making it easier to control with keys. (but getting rid of any realistic driving feel) BUT those who use a Racing Wheel will suffer this incredible mistake. NONE of the Racing Simulator I have has so narrow turning range. The narrower is F1 2021 which simulates the real F1 cars with a 360º total range (180º left/right).NONE of the online reviews at Youtube showed nor mentioned this awful limitation...- SUMMARIZING: The game is AMAZING, with GREAT graphics, and fun events. "Free world" is AMAZING, but it's a real frustration that you cannot get a "realistic" driving experience, ESPECIALLY CONSIDERING THE FREE WORLD CAPABILITY...- OVERALL I still recommend this game, taking this into account. I never expected it, but fortunately I purchased it in a discount offer for a short period, so I don't regret.Hope this helps to other users!! Feel free to comment and rate this "review".

_childDocuments_.review: The ultimate edition is one of the most expensive games on Steam. Even on sale I´ve had to pay the price for an undiscounted AAA title. The game requires an Xbox account and the publisher isn´t your favourite indie company in need of your money ;)The game was released on Xbox some years ago and Forza 5 might be released on Xbox this year. So Steam users are asked a premium XXL price for something that´s nearing the end of its life cycle. The port to PC is ok, but some players experience micro stutters in MP races. I´ve had about one ctd per 20 gaming hours which isn´t ok, but would be tolerable (if not for the premium price tag).After all those cons, why do I recommend this game?Because it´s a BLAST!!!!Most fun I´ve ever had in an arcade racing game! A zillion cars to use and abuse, fluent transition from SP to MP and such a lot of things to do and experience, that you need hundrets of hours to play through. Difficulty can be adjusted in a lot of clever ways. The rewarding system is perfect and keeps your playing for more cars, houses or just avatar cosmetics.From races on streets or through the woods, to stunt driving and playing tag there´s no activity that´s not implemented. There´s even a battle royale in cars that´ll entertain you for hours. The main advantage to buy a game that´s been released years ago: all the additions that Xbox players had to wait for are already there. 2 extra maps (dlc that are included in the ultimate edition), nearly 500 (!) cars to chose from and a great variety of player-made car settings and cosmetics.For achievement hunters: all achievs work and are doable. It took me around 200 hrs to get them all - without any grindy stuff and with a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played more than a hundred hours, I decided to write this short review. So, let's get started! First of all, I want to highlight the graphics - they are just great for a game of 2018 with good optimization. I also liked the fact that the game has an open world and it is created perfectly! Here you can find both big cities and small towns, and even completely deserted forests and plains (well, almost deserted xD) and driving through some location it becomes clear that the developers have devoted some time to the location of each object on the map to make it look as beautiful as possible, of course it's nice. I want to highlight the highlight of the game - the change of seasons - a great and successful mechanic from the developers! Playing the first dozen hours, it is impossible to convey emotions when the season changes and you don't recognize the map! It adds a significant atmosphere to the game. (These beautiful sunny summer days, or rainy autumn with flying autumn leaves that you dispel flying by car at 150+ km/hour, or winter... this beautiful winter when you wanted to drive for the first time on snowy roads but for some reason you flew into a ditch because you forgot to install winter tires).As for the cars, there are about 700 of them, for different tastes, ranging from cars of the last century to modern hypercars. It should be noted that all cars can be tuned.As for what you can do in the game after completing the tutorial, you can do anything! You have a choice of 100 or more races, which, by the way, are well made, with both regular circular races and off-road races, and much more. In addition, you have at your disposal a dozen interesting projects with no less interesting tasks (for example, Taxi or Top Gear). Isn't that enough for you? You can fly at the speed of sound next to police cameras, competing with your friends to see who can be faster, or jump off a springboard and try to beat your previous record, or score points in drift zones.The game also features several online competitive modes. These are regular PvP races and team games with interesting modes.Of course, no one forbids you to do whatever you want in this beautiful world and play by your own rules.As for what I didn't like. The first is a bug that hasn't been fixed yet, the essence of which is that in 40% of cases you will have to wait 5-10 minutes between rounds. The second is the absence of any bans, warnings, or anything else in ranked games, you will simply be pushed out of the way and your opponent will not be punished for it. Unfortunately, such toxic players in the rankings are the norm in the game. I would also like to write about the disadvantages that do not negatively affect the gameplay, but their presence upsets me. The first is the lack of possibility to connect to another open convoy. What do I mean by that? For example, I want to drift with someone and to do this, I select a drift convoy and I will be connected to players who also want to drift. Unfortunately, there is no such function.Secondly, it is very disappointing that the game will no longer be developed by the developers, although the game has an online presence of 5-10k players. I would like the game to have several modes similar to Forzathon, so that you could have fun with other players.It should also be noted that the game has 2 full-fledged DLCs. The first of them is Fortune Island, a place for fans of drift, where every turn is made to drive sideways! The second DLC is Lego. We will get a great map that is partly made in the Lego style, there are many interesting tasks and much more.That's probably all I can say. Of course, my review is not perfect, and I might have forgotten to write something. But the idea was to write a review from the first time, conveying all the emotions I got from this game.Summarizing the above, I would like to recommend Forza Horizon 4 in 2024, the game is still relevant. Good luck!UPD (28.06.2024): Well, that's the end of the legend. From July 25 to August 22, there will be one last playlist. I recommend everyone who collects achievements to hurry up, soon you will not be able to get achievements that require online mode. Forza 4 is forever in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best arcade racing game up to this date, with a beautiful open world that changes by each season and a huge amount of content. It can be enjoyed alone or online with other players. Online can be unlocked only after completing a series of races that serve as tutorial. There are many customization options for both your car and your sim, including clothes and emotes. No microtransactions, you can unlock all the stuff simply by racing, exploring and levelling up. There are some cars DLCs and a VIP membership that double your rewards and give you some exclusive stuff but honestly there is so much content in the base game that you won't feel the need to buy those. The rewards are pretty generous, with the wheel of fortune you can get rare items and super cars from the very beginning.Now the Steam version is unpolished. There is still some random stuttering and no support for impulse triggers on Xbox controllers, but hopefully these will be fixed soon. The biggest problem is the lack of cross-save between Steam and Xbox/Game Pass, which is awkward considering the game requires an Xbox Live account. It's something that Microsoft should immediately fix for all their games available on Steam. In any case the game is massively overpriced. I would only recommend it at a 50% discount or more and only if you're planning to get some DLCs too. If you want to play just the base game then Xbox Game Pass is a much convenient option, at least until Forza Horizon 5 comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's easily the best racing game like 10/10. However, there are major downsides that bottleneck this game to like 8/10.+ Car customization : To the deep. Both Performance and Visual. You could install other players tunings and designs. You could swap engine/major parts. For example, you could make an All-Wheel-Drive car change to Rear-Wheel-Drive car to make it suitable for drifting. Suspension parts can make your car run 150 km/h on dirt or max 70-80 km/h on dirt.+ All around physics : You can play normally just like Need for Speed or you could play like Grand Turismo/DiRT by selecting a simulation control. The game will add a HUGE +% bonus point for you when you play with a harder control. When you close all assist and play like a simulation, you will get +100% (Double money per race).+ Create your own events : You can create your own event and grind for money to buy car parts/new cars.+ Rewarding free roam : You can get influence points and money just from free roaming.- Unskippable cutscenes : Yes, It's so annoying. _childDocuments_.review: For me, a 'triple A' game has always meant a game with a huge budget released by a major studio. And usually all this really meant in reality was a steep price tag and impressive graphics. So I've played literally dozens of AAA releases over the years but have been genuinely blown away by only a few (the most recent being The Last of Us Pt. 2 on PS4). That was until I decided to throw down the dough for Forza Horizon 4 Ultimate Edition. And man did my jaw drop. I played Forza Motorsport in the past so I knew the car physics would be good (if a bit more on the arcade side of the fence for the Horizon series) and the graphics would be really impressive. And FH4 impresses on those fronts, no doubt.What caught me by surprise is how down immersive and downright fun the whole Horizon festival non-stop motorsports party is. The game that has come closest to this for me was Dirt 2, and that was a fun game. But FH4 is all of that with more cars, more event types, more content and more pizzazz. I mean Top Gun Maverick levels of pizzazz. I spent and HOUR AND A HALF simply downloading all the free cars and setting up their paint jobs/liveries and opening and closing the doors and bonnets and turning the lights on and off and and... For fricks sake where does it end?My kids made me go to Lego Speed Legends as soon as the area unlocked and that in itself is stupid fun and a game in and of itself. I feel a bit lost in it all at this point but it's a great kind of lost, you know? Pick an every, any event, and get your socks blown off kind of lost.My policy is, typically, to keep my game purchases to $20 or less. This baby set me back $52 on sale and it is - with no exaggeration - the best $52 I've spent on gaming EVER. I wholeheartedly encourage you to beg, steal or borrow the funds to get yourself FH4. Do whatever it takes. Hands down, this is the best racing experience on console or PC there is (except for maybe FH5, but I wouldn't know 😂).

_childDocuments_.review: **Forza Horizon 4: A Masterclass in Racing Games**Forza Horizon 4 stands as a remarkable testament to the evolution of racing games, blending stunning visuals, an expansive open world, and an exhilarating driving experience. Set in a beautifully recreated version of Great Britain, the game captures the essence of its diverse landscapes—from the rolling hills of the countryside to the bustling streets of Edinburgh.One of the most impressive features of Forza Horizon 4 is its dynamic seasons. Each season dramatically alters the environment and driving conditions, adding a layer of strategy and variety to the gameplay. Whether you're racing through autumn leaves or navigating a snowy winter landscape, the changing seasons keep the experience fresh and engaging.The car selection is nothing short of spectacular. With a vast array of vehicles ranging from classic muscle cars to cutting-edge supercars, players can truly customize their experience. The attention to detail in each car is astounding, from the engine sounds to the handling characteristics, making every drive feel unique.The game's online multiplayer mode is equally impressive. Players can seamlessly join friends in events or explore the world together, creating a vibrant community that enhances the overall experience. The Horizon Festival events are diverse and entertaining, catering to various playstyles and ensuring there's always something new to tackle.Graphically, Forza Horizon 4 is a feast for the eyes. The attention to detail in the environments and the lighting effects create a stunning backdrop for racing. Coupled with a fantastic soundtrack that perfectly complements the action, the game immerses you in its world.In summary, Forza Horizon 4 is not just a racing game; it's an exhilarating adventure that invites players to explore, compete, and enjoy the thrill of driving. With its innovative features, breathtaking graphics, and extensive content, it sets a new standard in the genre, making it a must-play for both racing enthusiasts and casual gamers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well ballanced racing game that found a sweet spot between arcade and realism, while still keeping the fun.Plus the overall the game has very relaxing feeling as it' great to jump in, do a few races and then jump out.Pros:- The unique 4 season UK themed map.- variety of weather conditions and day-night cycle- the driving model is well ballanced between arcade an realism - each car type feels different, each track ground feel different, even different track state is different (dry, wet, snow, ice), you simply can't be bored and always find something new and fun.- good soundtrack and radio stations.- variety of race types (sprint, drift, off-road, city races).- fun mini-stories (like Top Gear, Delivery Company, Insurance Claim company, Upgrade Heroes)- bazilion of cars to choose.- many collectibles and challenges.- customizable difficulty (the default one was relaxing for me, while giving me a challenge just from time to time)Cons:- unskippable victory animations.- choosable player characters are absolutely ugly, there are only 2 or 3 that doesn't make your eyes bleed.- chothes accessories can only be won in lottery, but most of them are stupid/meme clothes.- the overall concept of lottery completely destroy the progression - either you're showered with tons of cars liek no tommorow, or you get junk clothes that even clown would be ashemed to wear.- some mini-stories and characters have really cringe and corny dialogues (e.g. The Taxi company).- there is not much progression beyone a few initial rounds of racing.- the car selection screen GUI is very poor and gets worse with the amount of cars we get.- suprisingly, there is waaaaay to many cars - I got like 60 cars from lottery, but I use 4 at best.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: It has to be said now and quickly before any of the people who weren't around when the arcade racing scene was at an all time high in the 00's come to bite me.So many different and wild takes on what it means to achieve speed in a four wheeled missile. Split Second, Blur, Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit, Motorstorm, Burnout Paradise, Test Drive Unlimited. All of these seemingly disappearing over night, almost like people's general interest for car culture in the 10's came and swiped all of the fantastical joyride video games away with it. Arcade racing was brimming at the seems with potential ideas but is now simply non-existent in today's video games. I say this because the Forza Horizon franchise seems to hinge desperately to this fact. I can't say it any other way. Horizon 4 is a very over-rated game in an empty market that seems to distance itself from racing games in general, masked in the obscurity of it's old rooted genre. thus giving it leverage with younger audiences. A familiar feel of loose steering and loud engine noises, the freedom to go anywhere, do anything will sound tantalising to any new video gamer. But when put in a broader perspective, it is anything but that.  'There is nothing quite like it' that's because nobody makes these types of games anymore, It's as straight forward as that - but I don't want to stop there.This game could have been better, it could have less moronic dialogue and less pedestrian-esque friendliness hammering you over the head all of the time 'Well done! you're so great! didn't I mention you're fantastic?', and maybe they could've toned down the unskippable DLC ad's for the very video game you're trying to play (f... seriously?). Turning the wheel feels like an ice rink. Just the odd sensation of disconnect I feel when driving puts me off, between the road and the wheels that feel like they float just above the surface. I just can't express it further than that.Drivatars range from borderline brain dead to blatant cheating, as much as deliberately slowing down to help you win by the end of races (seriously look it up). The game simply pausing itself in multiple ways to tell you something constantly, bringing you out of your zone. The UI is atrocious, bloating itself with tabs filled with DLC, strategically placed so that you have to pass through it every time you need to edit or change car, or even do the simplest of tasks. It's engineered in a really scummy way to suck more cash from your wallet. It's a horrible feeling. An open world game that touts freedom of expression and ease of access offers probably the worst character customisation system I think I've seen in an open world. Bombarding you with a slot machine themed prize system that rewards cars you never wanted in the first place and clothes that almost never resemble what you wish to wear. Honestly just give me the ability to reach for anything I want If you're preaching about freedom so much. It's a shallow and flat experience across the board but it isn't the worst experience ever, there is some joy to be had here despite it being short-lived. I'm just really shocked that this is apparently the 'gold standard' of racing games. The consensus surrounding this title really does boggle the mind... Because this game could be so much better at doing the things that it wants you to do, it just can't seem to get out of it's own way and let you just.... drive.*but* nobody has anything else to compare any of this to. Nothing even remotely similar and of recent release = so I guess Horizon 4 is a great game. Surely that's how it works?

_childDocuments_.review: This is obviously very subjective, but here’s my review.  Spoiler Alert: 9.5/10 from me.Overview:I was a PlayStation gamer for many years prior to branching out to PC gaming a few years ago, so I never got to experience the Forza games until recently.  Forza Horizon 5 was my introduction to the series.  I really enjoyed it and scored it an 8/10 in my Steam review.  I then decided to try out Forza Horizon 4, and I just love it, can’t get enough.  FH4 is a fantastic game and far superior to FH5 in my opinion.  Driving / Difficulty:I generally opt for more simulator-type driving games, i.e. realistic driving.   It’s safe to say that this game definitely does not fall in to that category, instead leaning more towards the arcade style... there’s nothing wrong with that at all!  There are 8 difficulty (Drivatar) levels to choose from, ranging from from new player to unbeatable.  This allows the game to cater to most skill levels… unless you’re either really bad, or play like Jarno Opmeer or SuperGT (lucky you!!).  There’s also a huge amount of assists which you can opt for, such as, auto transmission, TCR, STM, ABS, assisted steering, assisted braking, damage on/off, tyre wear on/off, and driving line.  Whatever way you choose to play is up to you, but there are options to suit almost everyone.  Gameplay:The FH4 world is outstandingly beautiful.  The landscape is stunning, and I love how it changes through the seasons.  The attention to detail in the world design is superb.  The story was… meh.  Not memorable, with some very tedious moments and a few non-skippable cutscences.  But it was more interesting that FH5’s story imo.  The game has heaps self-contained storylines and businesses too which are fun, a nice challenge, and encourage you to explore parts of the map you may not otherwise experience.  There's a vast range of cars to earn (~500) by completing various races, events, stories, accolades etc.  You can also win cars, money, cosmetic items etc. through Wheelspins.  The game is very generous with how easy Wheelspins are to earn, especially when compared with how stingy many other game series can be.  Cars can be customised via upgrades and tuning options.  These are great to experiment with to find the right set-up for your favourite cars and to fine tune to suit specific types of races.  I love this feature personally, but for those who don't, there's also a feature that allows tunes made by other members of the community be downloaded.  You can also create your own paintjobs and liveries with infinite possibilities.  There’s endless amounts of stuff to do, along with seasonal (weekly) championships, challenges, and events.  I haven’t even mentioned all the PvP and user-created challenges - people's creativity will never cease to amaze me.  You’ll never be bored!!  After a hard day at work / uni, it's just nice (therapeutic even!) to drive around like a complete lunatic destroying fences, trees, drifting, racing at stupidly high speed, doing massive jumps etc. all while earning points and combos to gain fast XP.  It's even more fun with friends!  The tracks are decent and offer lots of variety in racing styles from drifting to cross-country to circuit to rally.  Performance:I run everything on max settings, and FH4 genuinely looks phenomenal.  A number of the negative reviews I've read mention issues with performance.  The game runs fine for me, with just a couple of minor stuttering issues and one or two freezes in ~100 hours of gameplay.  I’ve had no connection issues to friends / other players either.TL;DR – FANTASTIC game if you're looking for a fun, open-world driving experience.  Lots of styles of racing and tonnes of cars to choose from.  Looks incredible.  Lots to do.  9.5/10 for the fun factor.

_childDocuments_.review: Its an amazing game, hell probably one of the best racing games out there. It mixes sim like racing with arcade style racing in such a flawless manner that I often think to myself "Why can't all racing games be like this?". Its fun and a very chill game. However, if I'm to criticise this game, the very praise I give the game becomes its dark side. The game just gives out rewards, leaving the player unsatisfied with the achievements they receive. For example, in Horizon 1, each purchase of a car was calculated, as every race event in that game required the player to meet certain criteria when entering the event. This made the player competitive when it comes to races as they have to win in order to get money so that they can buy a great car. But in Horizon 4, the event changes according to the car wit which you enter. Yes, it becomes more player friendly, but i feel it removes the challenge aspect. A game can be in the form of a stress free capsule like ABZU, but Forza Horizon isn't such a title. You have the open world which is amazing and calm to drive in, but the races are to challenging. The game fails to balance challenge with the sense of relaxation. What I'm trying to say is that the sense of progression is not present in Horizon 4. You can complete 3/4th of the game with the cars they provide for free in the initial stages. There is no sense of achievement when one shows in a Chiron in Horizon 4's multiplayer as the obvious thought which goes into the opposition's mind is "Oh, they must've gotten it in a wheel spin!" Even though the player might've played and bought the car with the credits he earned. To complain that a game is giving out huge in-game rewards for free feels like a douchy thing to say. But it removes the challenge from the game. With that being said, Horizon 4 isn't a bad game. Its an amazing game. The graphics, the gameplay all checks out. But I'm not so happy with the reward system. Its too REWARDING. Balance it out, THEN you have the best racing game in the world

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 simulates a large area with a variety of terrain hosting all sorts of races, from city streets to offrroad rally stages, from super-downhill to stunt jumping, in addition to multiplayer content where the server coordinates players to participate in regularly scheduled events. The game also moves "seasons' every few days for changing circumstances. Muddy terrain becomes snowy terrain, for example. Lake that used to be unpassable becomes a frozen mass in the winter and can be driven on (and some secrets can be found!) add specialized content from Top Gear, Lego world, Hot Wheels, as well as a car collection system where you can bid and buy rare vehicles to add to your collection, as well as gain access to different houses around the country-side, collectibles, free-roam, and much more, this game really tries to be an open-ended "be everything" sort of game, and it mostly succeeds. The fictional background is not that important. You are invited to the Horizon Music and Speed Festival, and you can compete with others in races, and as you win, you'll be invited to more prestigious events, which you will of course, need better cars. You can win cars, and as you win more events, you get lottery spins that may give you anything from outfits to liveries to cars. And if you fulfill certain objectives during the "season", you get some more cars, of course, provided you meet restrictions. But the idea is there is ALWAYS something to do, and if you got bored of one thing, move onto something else. Tired of multiplayer? Go racing instead. Had enough city streets? Do offroad racing.  Had enough bumping other cars in a race? Go do some special events like the Top Gear challenge, or Movie Stunt Driver. Want to race something wacky? How about race a giant hovercraft downhill, or race the Flying Dutchman steam locomotive for a lap around the countryside?  Heck, can you beat a Vulcan jet in an Aston Martin Vulcan?  There is even a HALO level where you drive the Warthog as the Master Chief (yes, you get Cortana voiceover too)The graphics are gorgeous, and terrain looks terrific, and almost all land can be driven on, if you can see it (except water, and there are certain  limits, but sand is usually okay) so if you're just trying to get from A to B, you don't always have to follow the road. Heck, there are events where you are trying to achieve the farthest jumps off of cliffs and such. The driving model isn't the best, but it's fine for an arcade-ish game. Different cars do feel different, but there really is no damage model per se. And you'll be crashing through a lot of wooden fences and small stone walls along the way, without a scratch on your vehicle. But there is no need to race. Just do a free roam with your favorite vehicle. There is no police and accidents are ignored. Drive anywhere, look at anything (some areas are harder to get to though, may require AWD vehicle)   There are even some hidden surprises known as "barn finds" where you found an antique classic that can be restored and added to your car collection. And I'm barely scratching the surface of what can be done in the game. However, after a while, everything started to look the same. There are dozens and dozens of different cars, and you can have multiples of each (as each one is customizable).  In fact, you can improve you car so much, they become a car of a different class all together. A Ford Focus RS can be configured as a road racer or an offroad rally car, depending on what parts you put on it. And often, to join a certain race, you will need to reconfigure your car completely. If you like the idea of a free-roam car game where you can choose from dozens of activities, both single and multiplayer, give Forza Horizon 4 and 5 a try.

name: Read Only Memories: NEURODIVER
detailed_description: You Are A Psychic Agent Take on the role of ES88, a young esper employed by MINERVA, a powerful organization specializing in information science, neurotechnology, and extrasensory phenomena. She has been tasked with tracking down Golden Butterfly, a mysterious psychic entity hiding in and fragmenting the memories of Neo-San Francisco's citizens. Who are they? Why are they doing this? And how will you stop them? The Neurodiver The Neurodiver is a bioengineered psychic creature made to assist in boosting an esper's natural abilities. With its help, you'll be able to collect clues and thoughts in your subject's memories in an effort to piece together distorted fragments inside them, pushing Golden Butterfly out! New and Old Read Only Memories: NEURODIVER is a return to the vibrant sci-fi world of Neo-San Francisco from 2064: Read Only Memories with a whole new story, and a whole new cast of characters. It's an adventure that newcomers can easily dive into, but those familiar with the original game might notice a lot of familiar faces making a comeback! An Fm Sound Sensation! NEURODIVER's soundtrack is inspired by the OPNA/YM2608 sounds of the PC-8801 and PC-9801 series of computers, brought to you by Scarlet Moon composer and sound designer, Ken 'coda' Snyder ( Tree of Knowledge )! If you love the sharp and glossy tones generated by late 80s and early 90s FM chips found in a variety of old computers, sound cards, arcades and consoles, then you'll be right at home here. Long live the power of FM sound! 🎹 FEATURES The Sequel to 2064: Read Only Memories The long-awaited sequel to 2064: Read Only Memories takes you back to Neo-San Francisco in an all-new 'psy-fi' adventure. Meet new inhabitants and reconnect with old favorites from the world of Read Only Memories. A Mystery in Memories Take on the the role of newly-qualified ESPer, ES88, to track down the mysterious Golden Butterfly. Work with the Neurodiver, ES88's psychic sidekick, to dive into people's minds and repair their wrecked recollections. Anime-inspired Pixel Art Immerse yourself in the beautiful pixel art world that takes you around Neo-SF, the halls of the secretive Minerva agency, and within the depths of people's memories. A Cast to Remember Beautifully drawn and animated characters are brought to life with superb voice-acting. New heroes and villains are joined by old favorites Lexi Rivers, Turing, and TOMCAT from 2064: Read Only Memories. Retro Fm Synth Music Indulge your senses in the sharp and glossy retro tones of Neo-SF's FM synth soundscape as you dive deep into people's minds to track down the cunning Golden Butterfly.

NEURODIVER's soundtrack is inspired by the OPNA/YM2608 sounds of the PC-8801 and PC-9801 series of computers, brought to you by Scarlet Moon composer and sound designer, Ken 'coda' Snyder ( Tree of Knowledge )! If you love the sharp and glossy tones generated by late 80s and early 90s FM chips found in a variety of old computers, sound cards, arcades and consoles, then you'll be right at home here. Long live the power of FM sound! 🎹 FEATURES The Sequel to 2064: Read Only Memories The long-awaited sequel to 2064: Read Only Memories takes you back to Neo-San Francisco in an all-new 'psy-fi' adventure. Meet new inhabitants and reconnect with old favorites from the world of Read Only Memories. A Mystery in Memories Take on the the role of newly-qualified ESPer, ES88, to track down the mysterious Golden Butterfly. Work with the Neurodiver, ES88's psychic sidekick, to dive into people's minds and repair their wrecked recollections. Anime-inspired Pixel Art Immerse yourself in the beautiful pixel art world that takes you around Neo-SF, the halls of the secretive Minerva agency, and within the depths of people's memories. A Cast to Remember Beautifully drawn and animated characters are brought to life with superb voice-acting. New heroes and villains are joined by old favorites Lexi Rivers, Turing, and TOMCAT from 2064: Read Only Memories. Retro Fm Synth Music Indulge your senses in the sharp and glossy retro tones of Neo-SF's FM synth soundscape as you dive deep into people's minds to track down the cunning Golden Butterfly.

Explore the rich world with an intuitive point-and-click interface as you take on the role of a young psychic agent tasked with tracking down a mysterious antagonist hiding in people's memories.

_childDocuments_.review:
Return to the vibrant cyberpunk world of Neo-San Francisco from 2064: Read Only Memories, filled with friendly and familiar faces including Jess Meas, the gene-spliced, hybrid lawyer, TOMCAT, the notorious hacker, and Lexi Rivers, former police officer turned private eye.

Take on the role of ES88, a telepath with the ability to delve into memories employed by MINERVA, a powerful organization specializing in neurotechnology and extrasensory projection phenomena. Tasked with tracking down the Golden Butterfly, a naturally gifted psychic on the loose and wreaking havoc through the subconscious minds of Neo-San Francisco, by using the Neurodiver to search the memories in which it hides. Read Only Memories: NEURODIVER's Deep Dive mechanic enables ES88 to identify, manipulate, and unlock information, though overuse can irreparably corrupt her target's memory.

NEURODIVER will introduce new characters, locations, and mechanics, including the ability to dive into and change other characters' memories, as well as overhauled art and an unsolved case to crack with multiple endings.

name: Rollerdrome
detailed_description: Rollerdrome is a BAFTA award-winning third person action shooter that seamlessly blends high octane combat with fluid motion to create an action experience like no other. Dominate with style in cinematic, visceral combat where kills net you health and pulling off tricks and grinds provide you ammunition, in this adrenaline-pumping action shooter. The year is 2030. In a world where corporations rule and the lines between reality and performance are blurred, the public are kept distracted by the violence and excess of a brutal new blood sport — Rollerdrome. Will you have what it takes to become the Rollerdrome champion and unravel the mysteries behind the Matterhorn corporation’s true intentions? From Roll7, the minds that brought you the award winning and critically acclaimed OlliOlli series comes Rollerdrome, an intense shooter-skater hybrid set in an evocative retrofuture. Key Features: A third person action shooter like no other – an original hybrid shooter-skater that blends high octane, visceral combat with fluid movement and tricking mechanics into one complementary and challenging whole. A test of skill – Take on a unique challenge throughout the Rollerdrome tournament. Establish your dominance in the field with online leaderboards and push yourself to the limit with the unlockable 'Out For Blood' mode for the most extreme test of skill and agility. An original identity – An all-new fully original soundtrack that merges iconic era sounds and tones with cutting edge production to provide a heart-thumping backdrop to the carnage, brought to life with a unique comic-book inspired art style. A dark conspiracy – Discover a mysterious, sinister plot in this distinct retrofuture universe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater in that you have a checklist of things to do in each level but made even more complex with the addition of gun-based objectives.  It is hectic keeping your combo and ammo up, dodging sniper bullets, shooting rockets out of the sky while swapping guns to get specific kills off specific enemies. I can already tell this has a high skill ceiling and it will be fun to get better and better at it..
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: (For any reviews saying the game is "TOO HARD" If you went into the options you would have seen options to make it easy, examples, Invincibility/Unlimited ammo/unlimited slow motion/change the damage taken for your character, skip challenges to progress to the next stages) Below is my review, just wanted to mention to the dummies that never seem to make an effort in checking the accessibility options in games. I seen the Dev Paul on Twitter prototype this game years back and it looked amazing, happy to see all the positive and well earned good reviews for it, I highly recommend Rollerdrome, it's extremely fun! And just gets more and more hectic, I wish more game developers out there took the top tier fun and innovation of some of the great titles out there, combined them and gave it a little twist of its own, because this title certainly does that. It's taking the likes of Tony Hawks/Jet Set Radio, and mixing it with Max Payne slow motion shooting and the insanity of Doom almost, just enemies trying to murder you from all directions near the end of the game. I'm excited to see what's next for this dev/devs

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a few negative reviews on the game's difficulty, so I'm just going to say this: unless you care about leaderboards, or are a hardcore 'easy mode is for suckas' gamer, don't hesitate to use the assists. If it makes the game more fun for you, go for it!This game is super fun and addictive. I'm not typically into sports but this has been a blast to play. The perfect game when you just want to shoot things and challenge yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Tony Hawk meets Max Payne.This game hits the sweet spot for a fast-paced violent shooter that is tough but fair. Very arcadey in its mechanics and presentation, once you get the controls down you can really reach a flow state during the intense battles. Dodge a shot, grenade an area of enemies, head toward a vert ramp for a 540 grab to get your ammo back, line up a crit shot with your shotgun in bullet-time to finish an enemy and heal yourself, then pull out your pistols to take out incoming missiles. Just pure reaction -- high-adrenaline action.Highly recommended if you're into challenging shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's a skater / shooter / puzzle game. The skater and shooter aspects are self explanatory  so I guess I should go into how this is a puzzle game.   For each map, the game gives you a list of challenges to complete. Some of them you'll achieve just by beating the map, but the others require you to collect tokens or kill enemies in a particular fashion. This means that in order to complete challenges AND get a high score, you can't let the combo meter drop. You need to think about the enemy types, placement and ammunition at all times- plotting out how to best approach the collectibles while taking out enemies at a pace that allows for exploration as well as keeping the combo. Easier said than done, sometimes that means managing what order to take enemies out and which ones are faster to deal with when a combo is close to ending, all in order to give yourself a buffer to complete the challenges. In my opinion, playing it like a puzzle game is part of the fun.   Apart from that, the style is OFF THE CHARTS and the gameplay is fast paced. Exactly the kind of game I hoped it would be. If it holds up till the end, it'll be a favorite of mine for sure.Edit: It held up till the end!As far as the story goes, while there are interesting ideas and world building being hinted at, we don't really see any of it unfold. We hear announcers on the radio and get notes pinned to cork boards, but we never really interact with any people. It wasn't a deal breaker for me, and I understand it mainly serves as the set dressing for the gameplay, but if you're looking for a story focused game this may not be your cup of tea.   Having completed the main campaign, I have to say that it is MOST DEFINITELY a new favorite of mine. Where I feel lots of skater games get bogged down in the number of button presses needed to perform a combo, Rollerdrome keeps it simple to understand, but still has variety in its move set. All the weapons have their place in combat and it never felt like one was the obvious answer to everything. All in all, this game is such a breath of fresh air and I'm glad I found it. Highly recommended for anyone that enjoys some challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art style and graphics which are kinda reminiscent of Moebius style.Rollerdrome gameplay is so damn satisfying it's an absolute blast to play while your in the groove and nail the tricks and combat.The controls are spot on, it certainly will take a while to get used to and master them but oh boy the possibilities this game offer you are awesome.The arenas are really well designed with many ramps and spots to wall grind or wall ride.Pretty much everything is here to have a good time, honestly it feels really good to play.Sadly the game is single player only and I imagine the game may be a bit short or might get repetitive after a while.Rollerdrome is still highly replayable if your the kind of person chasing the best scores.Man it would have been dope if there was some coop or pvp modes !
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a very important game for me. I’ve been following the development since it was just a clip of a concept posted by an indie dev. And said clip is actually the only reason I created a twitter account, specifically so I could follow the project. And now, four years later, Rollerdrome is out and unlike anything I ever could’ve imagined. It is hands down the most fun gaming experience I’ve ever had. Such a simple (and unique) concept expanded into a high paced and thrilling game. The controls and options of tricks may seem complex at first, but they are so tight and carefully constructed, that once you master them you are able to achieve some unbelievably cool moments. The gameplay would’ve been enough of a selling factor, I mean who wouldn’t want Tony Hawk Pro Skater mixed with Doom? But the biggest surprise was the story. It kept me completely engaged, and I was constantly rooting for Kara against the other side characters (who have so much personality even though they are never seen). The team created a beautiful world with complex and detailed lore that makes me even more enthralled with this game. Needless to say, I played through the entire campaign in one sitting, and will continue to replay this for the rest of my life. I love Rollerdrome, it’s the most fun game i’ve ever played, and i hope everyone can one day experience the excitement this game captures.  Thank you Roll 7 and thank you Paul.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: What if John Wick could skateboard?Or what would Tony Hawk Pro Skater look like if it had been a shooter?Rollderdrome gives us a gaming experience that is both action-packed and addictive in which you have to pull a lot of tricks & hits to defeat a whole army of soldiers and robots in each level!Watch gameplay from a later level in the game here: I think a lot of gamers who grew up around the millennium switch would like RollderDrome, this is undoubtedly a great game that is both immensely entertaining and nostalgic, also the appropriate soundtrack in the game ensures that your reflexes are on point!The plot of Rollerdrome revolves around a future dystopia in which players join the Rollerdrome to fight for a better life.It's run by an obviously corrupt supercorporation, which you'll slowly learn more about as you play through a backstory.Here you can watch videos of more levels:  In each level you will get a series of challenges that you must or can achieve, it is also very clearly described what you have to do,to unlock new levels you must have achieved a minimum of challenges, so you may get to a point where you will have to replay some levels to get some extra challenges, but that's no problem, playing the same one will never be different unless you train yourself to speedrun the levels, then you would dare to stick to a fixed route.For this title cel shaded graphics have been chosen with a rather abstract design.All this together creates a unique taste with its own and new identity.The fun of Rollerdrome is ultimately in getting a feel for the game. Feeling for the skates, feeling for the weapons, but especially feeling for the different arenas and opponents. Which targets pop up where and when, and most importantly, how do you best defeat which enemy?you will acquire all the weapons you can use during the first half of the game, it is then up to you to figure out which enemies take the most damage from which weapon, and which weapon works the best and fastest against certain to attack,you will therefore have to react quickly, decide quickly and, above all, anticipate a lot,the slow motion in the game is then a perfect tool that not only provides comfort but also great images that you can admire in the middle of the battle.The game is also fantastic on a steam deck!: Rollerdrome is unbelievably cool!Fast gameplay, cool action, an entertaining gameplay loop, high replay value and a delicious audiovisual sauce make Rollerdrome special.Rollerdrome also has perfect support for ultra-wide resolutions, you can see an example of this here:

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Max Payne meets Tony Hawk, but on rollerskates. There's a highly satisfying flow of doing tricks, shooting enemies, dodging attacks and playing around with reflex time (slowmotion). Increase your score by never stopping that flow and building up a combo. Get a high combo, complete objectives, kill your enemies as fast as possible within the allotted time and you win the match. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The way the game teaches you to get better and rewards you when you do should be an example to good game design. I wasn't able to do anything fancy at first and by completing challenges the game taught me tricks and mechanics and enabled me to perfect them. Best thing is I could complete those one by one without losing progression and honestly there was no frustration completing any part of the game.By the end of second campaign I was a god skating on the blood of my enemies and it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun.Honestly the game fxcks
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was stunned - the graphics, the music, the gameplay, the little story in the background. I enjoyed it, but after a few levels I hit a wall. I felt like the game was too difficult and I couldn't properly progress.But then it just clicked! And the gameplay became just so much more satisfying and fun, suddenly I found myself doing high combos and scores without noticing. Rollerdrome is a really good action game, with a pleasing style. There's even a new game plus mode!Although as much as I cherish and wanted to play this game badly, I didn't play for that long. And I worry that if I aimed to reach the high scores and finish the Out for Blood gamemode, the maps and enemies could become boring. The maps, even though some of them are different, don't stand out that much and the variety of enemies is not that high. But that's just a thought I had. Other than that, this game is wonderful!
