_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is incredibly addictive and fun. The difficulty comes from the amount of enemies that are thrown to you and how you manage to get ammo. I do think that needing challenges to progress is bad, the amount of visual clutter can be overwhelming at times and the game over (eliminated) screen can overstay its welcome. _childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: There's a slight disconnect between the seemingly stylistic lack of punch to the sound design, music, and action, and the robustness of the visuals, but Rollerdrome's foundation, while underutilized, is a lovely skate in the park. It's focused purely on the mechanics, with enough of a story (with unusually well-directed mundaneness in the voice acting) to at least put the setting in a non-distracting location, no doubt. Quick, clean, satisfying combat and tricks, top to bottom. Some clunkiness in the inputs (being very intentional with your button presses is key to actually performing the vast majority of the tricks) makes it a little difficult to feel truly fluid, but the reflex mode is more than enough to make chaining together kills, if not combos, a very good time. The biggest failing of the game is the lack of content - only four true maps are used (as tilesets), so any intrigue in locale disappears by the second round of the tournament the story is based around. Instead, it's easier to view the game as a sporty, thrill-of-the-play-rather-than-the-game experience, one that's easily and pleasantly digestible for a few runs while in-between other things. Overall, I'm disappointed that the guns are audibly shooting rubber bands, but Rollerdrome's smooth clickiness makes it a slick, mechanical success.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: GREAT. I love fast paced games like these, especially when they let you slow down time to do badass stunts and kills. Fantastic gameplay that wasn't too hard, but hard enough to keep it challenging and engaging (with a New Game + of sorts with a harder difficulty). Its a gem of a game and I couldn't be happier that picked it up. If you like fast paced action (kinda like Severed Steel or 505's Ghostrunner) please pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fun set of core mechanics that combine Tony Hawk-style extreme sports with *Max Payne*-esque bullet-time shooting, and with great art direction to boot. unfortunately, the actual game that Roll7 built around all that is rather lacking; it fails to significantly iterate or expand on its core mechanics much beyond the first few stages, even with a few new weapons, and levels are too long, with their repetitive level and encounter design getting stale awfully fast. I also found the most basic enemies to be the most fun to kill, which is kind of a problem for a shooter, and the game only intermittently lands the feeling of flow that should be so essential to such a combo- and score-driven game.Maybe it’s just that I suck at it, but it’s ultimately not for me; still worth checking out just to play around with the mechanics for a few stages, but I’d only recommend it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great concept for a game, it feels good to control, has a good soundtrack and a nice artstyle. I did have some fun with it for a little while, but unfortunately there's not a lot of content here, and the content that IS here is stretched to the game's detriment.in order to progress you not only have to beat the stages, but also complete a number of sub challenges within them, like pulling of specific tricks or killing enemies in a certain way. This feels like something that'd be optional in most other games, and has been included here in order to get the most out of the 11 small maps. About 2 hours in when you reach the midpoint of the campaign you've seen every enemy type and weapon there is to discover, and from there on the game increasingly relies on creating challenge by putting you up against large numbers of bulletsponge enemies. The quickest and most efficient way of taking out enemies is by using near miss dodges to increase your damage while in bullet time for a few seconds, but outside of this state even when using the correct strategies it takes all the ammo you can carry to take out anything besides the basic grunts and snipers. Doing tricks is also not as fun as it should be, as you'll be too busy spamming the dodge button to avoid the various types of projectiles that track you across the entire map. I understand the appeal of the gameplay loop is switching between tricks and combat, but there's not enough variety or character progression to keep things from getting tedious. you're basically doing the same thing over and over again. I was also kind of let down by the final boss, which is the same thing as the only other boss you fight earlier in the game, just with more hp. I think it could've been fun including other types of challenges besides fighting waves of enemies. I get why the devs focussed on the core gameplay here, but i think a variety of challenges would make a lot of sense considering the game's premise. It also could be fun to have actual rival characters with unique abilities and designs to take down, instead of just generic enemies. It's honestly very confusing how your last opponent isn't another rollerdrome contestant built up throughout the game as your arch rival, but instead a giant robot you've already fought before. the fundamentals for a great game are here, so i hope the devs make a bigger, better sequel that fully taps into its missed potential. Unless it's steeply discounted i don't quite recommend this one though.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. a blend of jet set radio future style with tony hawk, accept you have weapons. you skate around parks and do tricks for ammo and have to kill enemies as they try to eliminate you.progression is locked behind doing certain tasks around the park which can be annoying and gets harder as the game goes on; but overall this game has amazing replay value. for a cheaper game this blows away many AAA games that lack this type of creativity.update: 6/22/2023   i just found out you can change settings to be able to progress thru the levels without having to complete all those annoying challenges. great news!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: perfect game to pick up if you happen to get murderous tendencies while playing tony hawk pro skaterminimal complaints on this one: good weapon coverage, interesting enemy types, and a solid difficulty curve that eventually sees you frantically weaving through what feels like a never-ending artillery barrage, from squads of skater haters
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I have played in a very long time.1) The art. I am in love with this art style. A sleek, cartoon style that's simple and easy on the eyes, but not boring to look at.2) The movement and controls. It feels so good just to move in this game. I haven't felt movement this smooth since Titanfall 2 - and I don't say that lightly. It will take you a couple rounds to get a hang of it, but once you do, it feels amazing. Just do yourself a favor and play with a controller, as it's the way they intended. And if you don't have a controller - go buy one to play this game. Trust me, it's worth it.3) The gunplay. It really fits this style of game. The two guns that you will likely use the most (dual pistols and shotgun) automatically lock on when you get close enough to your enemies, which really suits this rapid, fast paced style of arcade-y gameplay. But if you prefer to aim yourself, then you will unlock two other guns (a grenade launcher and a sort of charge-up energy rifle) that reward timing and good aim.4) The music. Not much to say other than that it is really incredible. So good that I have added most of the songs to my regular listening playlist on Spotify. (Thank you guys for making this music available on there.5) Difficulty. Just as soon as you get used to one enemy type, they give you another to fight against, so there is always something new to challenge your skills and reflexes. Each level has 10 challenges that are appropriately difficult to complete. Very few of them felt too hard, and they were very rewarding to complete. The challenges also add a lot to the replayability, too, because if you like to chase down the challenges, you'll be replaying these levels a few times to knock them all out.Just so you know going into it - this game is FAST, and will test your reflexes and critical thinking in a really fast paced environment. There is a lot going on once you get further into the game. And that is one way that the art style works towards the game - the simpler style means that there aren't any unnecessary details grabbing for your attention.I could write a book on all of the things I love about this game. It's absolutely fantastic. I can't think of any complaints, here. I guess one or two of the challenges were just a little too hard for me? And a couple of my deaths have felt a little undeserved, but that's mostly just bad luck. And I want there to be more. That's not saying that there isn't enough - There is plenty to justify $30USD. This game is just so good that I can never have enough of it lolIn a time when most huge triple-A title are starting to feel more and more stale, it was so refreshing to stumble upon a fresh, interesting game that shook things up in a great way. My only regret with this purchase is that I didn't make it sooner.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I call this game T.Payne because it really is Tony Hawk + Max Payne.  And it's done so damn well. I'd still recommend it on sale (I bought it for 15USD) as it is an incredibly Arcade/score video game that pushes you to your limits with a genre that's never really been done before. _childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so slick. I'm in love. The mechanics are tight and smooth, the combat feels satisfying and heart-pumping, the music is on point, the visuals look great, and the difficulty curve feels challenging but well-paced. Once you start learning how to pick up speed, quick swap your weapons, and dodge effectively--getting into that "flow" state--the gameplay becomes really rewarding.Only complaint would be you're required to finish a certain number of "challenges" before unlocking the next bracket of levels. I feel like the challenges are distracting more than engaging (or better focused on after you've completed the story), and pausing to look at what you need to accomplish takes you out of the flow of the game.A couple gameplay tips that aren't obvious right away:The gameplay in Rollerdrome is super well executed. It's just pure fun. I thought I wouldn't be bothered to go after the challenges because those features feel meaningless to me in games, but I was having so much fun I ended up 100%-ing the game and was wishing for more at the end of it all. Highly recommended if you're into fast-paced, reaction-based gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a video of this game a long time ago, and I thought that the mechanics are cool, so I wishlisted it, then later bought it. Best steam purchase I've ever made. _childDocuments_.review: Many other reviews have said it as well. Tony Hawk tricks, bullet time and an awesome sound track make this a ton of fun to play on PC and a dream on Steam Deck! _childDocuments_.review: This game's visual language is pretty fantastic. You can see the sniper lines, and many other attacks coming at you. If you get hit, you didn't dodge, because the dodge is very forgiving. Enemies are visually distinct by silhouette, usually a good sign there will be good "modern" character design.Warning: Harder than I expected. There's some moments where everything is coming at you all at once. Time slow is your best friend.My only wish is that I could see those far-out dudes. The maps can be big, and snipers can be hard to pinpoint (maybe my sensitivity is too high?) There's no aim-down-sights, right click is time slow instead. But then time slow does it anyways, as you can line it up more carefully. I noticed some additional aim assistance too for the 4th weapon, another reason why this complaint doesn't really matter.The game is beatable in a short speedrun time if you aim for challenges as you go. But perfecting the levels will be fun. Some other skater games have very poor replayability, but this game has a great mixture of "arena shooter" and "combo building" that makes you want to go back and play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Fun. Looking for a game that you can play in short bursts, or even grind without feeling like you're achievement hunting or speedrunning? Well, this is your game. I hate to beat a dead horse with the comparisons but this game takes the bullet-time and chaos from Max Payne... the bullet hell from Enter The Gungeon... the controls of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater... the skill gap and adrenaline of Rocket League... slaps it into a horde mode... and... it...  it just works. Great soundtrack, and aesthetically pleasing, as well.The game itself is simple enough to button mash your way through the early levels, but it gets progressively difficult and you're forced to actually fuse a few brain cells together. The campaign "technically" requires you to farm challenges to unlock the next set of levels. However, they are not difficult to do and the levels feel easier every time you beat them. You're also not required to beat the stage to retain your completion of each challenge, so you can easily go in with a few objectives each run and bail if you wish.The game can be hectic and overwhelming without many checkpoints, but it's also forgiving. If you just want to mow through the Campaign, go into the settings and disable the Challenges requirement. If you can't beat a level, they have a Game Genie... or for the younger audience, Celeste-esque "Assist Mode" setting to enable invincibility and unlimited ammo among other things. If you want to 100% the game... well, git good.I've yet to beat the game, but I would only call out two gripes. Bullet inventory... you may have 3 weapons in your wheel with full ammo, yet they all share the same magazine. For example, if I have 6 bullets in my (dual) pistol, 2 shotgun shells, and 1 grenade, emptying my dual pistols, means I've somehow lost my shotgun shells and grenade?My other gripe would be that there are some boss fights along the way that took a bit of trial and error to figure out due to a lack of visual cues. I've literally done laps for several minutes, being chased by endless heat-guided missiles before the strategy finally "clicked". Perhaps that was user error?Checkpoints, and perhaps an Endless Mode with randomly generated enemies would be a welcomed addition.Either way, fantastic experience and I would not mind an expansion in some capacity.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: pros: tony hawk with guns and bullet time, it's perfectcons: tutorial is ten tedious tutorials instead of just one covering everything.... no wonder half the people don't get past it. just show the controls, all basic skills, and tick them off as they do it...... to those quitting the tutorial, just go back and do it, the game is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game with unique gameplay combo of jet set radio style of "rollerblading" with tribes ascend'esque shooter + movement combo. And it has some cool cyberpunk background flavor + character build through walking-sim intermissions. The only thing I didn't like is gate keeping by completing challenges which personally destroyed the pacing of the game, but judging how nobody is writing about it, it seems to be a me problem. :D With that said the game does have some great QOL such as keeping track of the completed challenges even if you die and allowing you to repeat from a "checkpoint" if the level has multiple stages, really well done on that devs. <3P.S. I think a sequel with co-op and/or pvp, cutomization and "free skate" mode would be awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Tony Hawk and John Wick made out for 20 minutes in the back of a van, and then the baby was raised in a brutal fascist state where human life has no value.Imagine if, while you were doing grab tricks in the quarterpipes to collect the SKATE letters, keeping an eye out for tapes, and trying to ring all the schoolbells to 100% the level... several dudes with spiked bats, sniper rifles, missile launchers, beam weapons, etc were trying to kill you. But also at any time you could bullet-time and auto-lock and unload full mags from your dual-wielded pistols into their face while doing a 720 twistflip far above them.It gets hard but not too quickly, and it's executed very well. Gameplay is smooth and fun, the mechanics around ammo and health are cleverly done in a way that really keeps this an even mix of shooting and tricking.  For me it just hits the perfect balance between challenge and frustration, the same feeling i got working my way up to Expert in Guitar Hero 3 if that means anything to you. I haven't even come close to finishing it yet but I already know this is a Yes so I'm writing this now without getting into a lot of the replay content.  Just like the original Tony Hawk games, there's a lot of stretch goal objectives that require replaying each level several times, coming back later when you've got the other weapons, etc.  So there's a good amount of content here, but I will echo the other reviewers who say that the levels aren't all that varied.  There are a few pieces in each level that kind of give it a feel (ie some have fall-off areas, some have elevation changes with lots of rails, some are like huge bowls with a couple big hills in the center), but a lot of the actual gameplay does not vary much from arena to arena. The objectives (just like Tony Hawk) tend to follow the same patterns in each arena as well (collect these tokens, do that trick, do this grind, beat that score, etc).Overall tho, I recommend this game especially in the Humble Monthly!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The game is certainly interesting in it's theming, delivery and gameplay, but I'd recommend not getting it from Steam directly as even the discount price of 20 euros is too high for what you're getting. (I got it at a lower price thanks to Humble Bundle.)It's a 10-12 euro game where a controller is pretty much a must.The game certainly does a great job at bringing you into the world only as much as you want with all the lore bits being entirely skippable if you're only here for the gameplay and don't care that you put yourself in huge debt in order to sign up and risk your life in this deadly competition and so on.The world around you is mostly cold and emotionless towards you or your hardships, which is fantastically portrayed through the game. The game revolves around completing challenges within levels to unlock further levels. These challenges are persistent over multiple runs on a level so you never have to push yourself hard to complete them all in one go. You can simply just get them out of the way one by one if you so desire so it's not overly challenging in this regard.The challenge of the game mainly stems from introducing simple mechanics and then overloading the environment with stimuli. You ride, jump, do tricks, grind, shoot, dodge when an attack is going to hit, etc. It starts off slow and easy but once the training wheels come off, you'll be facing a lot of these threats at once which forces you to think on your feet and adapt to the situation at hand. You are assisted by aim-assist (As the game is VERY well suited for a controller.) and a bullet-time mechanic which recharges quite quickly, but it still doesn't make it a cakewalk for literally anyone as you need to have at least some semblance of flow in this game. (But there's quite a bit of leeway for error.)Overall it's a very nice game, with the price tag being set a bit too high. If you manage to find a good deal on it, it might be worth picking up if the premise seems interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The base campaign is fun. However, it can be difficult if you can’t master how to do a perfect dodge. The grinding challenges can be a bit frustrating, and the fact that you have to replay previous levels to complete them can grind the game to a halt. I'm just not a fan of stopping a player from progressing until they complete them. That aside while I think it could use some more content, I enjoyed the mix of Tony hawk with bullet time combat and the game felt fairly polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a mix between Tony Hawk and Max Payne with addition of gun juggling from Doom/Devil May Cry. Although those don't really seem like they would work together, Rollerdrome does a perfect job mixing those three into one very unique experience.- Aesthetics and art style- Soundtrack- Overall gameplay and the flow that it creates.- the story that is happening in the background- Game gets progressively harder as new enemies are added and you unlock new weapons.- Lots of challenges.- It's a bit short- It would be cool if there was some sort of replay editor.- It may be a bit too difficult for some people.It's fun. It's challenging. It's just perfect. Please make a sequel. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The idea sounds extremely cool, but the execution fails to deliver. The game heavily encourages you to only ever shoot in bullet time, which makes the actual enemy engagements slow and awkward. Most enemies are very tanky, and some either immediately teleport away or bring up an invincibility shield as soon as you shoot them,  you have bullet time active. You also get a massive damage boost if you activate slow motion immediately after dodging an attack (but only while slow motion is active), and your bullet time meter regenerates so quickly that there's no strategy to it at all. Approach an enemy, slow time, shoot, run out of ammo, do a trick, repeat, over and over, in a few small arenas that are recycled in later levels. You don't even get many opportunities to do cool tricks mid-combat, because you'll be dodging a cluster♥♥♥♥ of laser beams, lingering trails, homing missiles, and a huge assortment of AoE attacks, and breaking lock-on is only possible by breaking eye of sight or dodging. Dodging, by the way, interrupts any trick or grind you're doing and instantly resets your momentum while on the ground. It feels graceless and incohesive, like the skating is entirely mechanically separate from the shooting.The bulk of the content is in beating your high score and completing the ten challenges in each match, but they're not particularly remarkable. In fact, most of them are basically the same for each level: kill a certain enemy while doing a certain grind, kill a certain enemy with a certain weapon, do a certain trick next to the trick pickup, beat this score, beat this other score, collect all the combo collectibles, etc. The game's aesthetic is great, but after a strong start I mostly just found the game frustrating and tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I will make it brief.People is comparing this to Tony Hawk but... i really see nothing related to it.Don't misunderstand my words, the game is good, not to a point i will praise it.The idea is AWESOME, the execution however screams "we could have done better"I find the controls a bit meh, i mean, tank controls are ok, but in a game like this? This fast and frantic? Is a hard passThe gameplay itself is, once again, ok, i just don't find it appealing.Doing combos is a nightmare, combos you can achieve by ONLY killing and shooting at enemies, tricks are mainly used to fill your ammo, and you will do a lot of them, A LOT, too bad you will find yourself surrounded by tons of enemies shooting at you from a great distance and with stuff chasing you, to a point where doing those is a death wish.The flow is there, but pretty hard to "feel" and keep, to a point you will just shoot stuff and that's it.The soundtrack is ok'ish, you can hear it banging, but not enough, is screaming "I AM ALMOST THERE, HOLD ON A SEC"Don't misunderstand my words, this game is ok, not bad at all, simply, you can feel there's something odd, something that could have been done better. It dosen't explode as it should be, if is clear what i mean.I hope to see a "Rollerdome 2", maybe with tons of improvement :D I love this concept :D
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed any of the skating games of the late 90's and early 2000's (Thrasher: Skate and Destroy or Tony Hawk's Pro Skater) then you'll enjoy this, no doubt about it. If you've played those games then there's a good chance you're pushing close to 40 and your reflexes aren't what they used to be. Don't let that stop you from trying Rollerdrome, because there are ample opportunities to slow time in order to take careful shots at the enemy (on top of an auto-aim system for certain weapons). The game play is fast and smooth with an art style that's still going to look great 20 years from now. I don't know what else I can say that hasn't already been said in the other reviews.It's fun, check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Such an addictive game, the controls are tuned to perfection and the later challenges are a great test to mastering its mechanics and levels.Very much on the short end but unlocking a tougher version of the campaign after completion was a nice way to keep the fun rolling. The story is just aesthetic, its well presented but doesn't amount to much, transitions into gameplay from narrative sections were brilliant.I binged this game over the course of two days but you can definitely %100 it in one sitting if you wanted to, after getting %100 im still gagging for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a stylish skating-shooter game with a focus on racking up score by defeating enemies, dodging attacks, and doing tricks. As someone familiar with shooting games but not skaters, there was a learning curve figuring out the skating controls, but after several sessions the control scheme mostly felt natural (mouse+keyboard). As for the shooting, the combination of auto-aim with the ability to temporarily slow time at-will is fun. However, the mechanic of perfect dodging enemy attacks to enter "super reflex" (slow time with much greater weapon damage) encouraged aggression and felt very satisfying. The weapons (dual pistols, shotgun, grenade launcher, railgun) are solid and feel like they have their own roles, to an extent. The only weapon I didn't use on a regular basis was the railgun, which I just found a little tricky to use with its charge time combined with the need for precise aiming, and I found the other three weapons to suffice.The skating and shooting elements are (compared to pure shooters or skaters) simple, but I think this was necessary to keep the mechanics from being overwhelming. As it stands, they complement each other well and you are expected to do both (tricks refill your ammunition).The base campaign is fairly short, but there are plenty of challenges to complete on repeat runs. Also, there is a second campaign (effectively new game+) that adds more difficult enemies to each level, which really pushed me to learn both the shooting and skating to complete all the challenges. Some of the challenges in the base campaign were a little frustrating or inconvenient to get, primarily ones that required me to get to difficult areas (often requiring the use of the "air out" maneuver that I found finicky), but nothing too bad.The art style is simple, but it's well done and appropriate for the kind of gameplay on offer. The soundtrack is great, with many remixed versions for the new game+ campaign. I liked the game enough to go back and finish all the challenges, which largely stay on the right side of challenging vs. frustrating. Overall, I can recommend this to anyone looking for a stylish action game, even if you aren't an expert in shooters or skaters.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Neat Rollerball inspired game about preserving momentum, timing dodges, and taking out enemies. You have to figure out how to keep your ammo replenished with tricks while taking too long to kill the next guy or you drop combo. Damage will also end it pretty fast so you need to also be mindful of distance to your enemies, which ones threaten your combo the most, how much ammo you have and what you can accomplish with it, and which weapons suit the situation best. I do appreciate how they kept the arsenal relatively simple (There are only 4) but each one has a unique and important place in combat. Probably me only real "gripes" with the game are that the tricks of the same type are all functionally interchangeable, which makes tracking them mentally a bit of a pain to prevent stale moves, and that $30 for this much content seems a bit much. That said I would highly recommend picking this up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdome is a stylish blend between a third-person-shooter and Tony Hawk Pro Skater including a fantastic 70s-style synth-wave soundtrack. The game controls great, looks great and sounds great. The first few hours truly are a blast to play, but then the problems become more apparent. My biggest issue with the game is that you can't just progress the levels after beating them. To reach the next stage you need to fulfil a certain amount of "optional" challenges. A common practice to artificially lengthen games that don't have much content. Grinding these challenges wasn't much fun for me. Another issue is the sheer amount of enemies in the later levels. The game can become quite the cluster-**** with tons of enemies shooting you from all sides, creating harmful areas of burning acid, fire and laser-walls. Doing longer tricks and having a good flow becomes incredibly difficult in these stages and I quickly switched to just dodge-spamming and doing the easiest tricks just to get my ammo back. With a bit more fine-tuning this could have been a very special game. It's still an overall fun experience but could have been so much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best new games that i've played in a while. It is one of those games where you barely survive a level at first (if you even do) but quickly become better. It demands skillful play but it offers such a good variety of intertwining elements that can sum up to masterful play that it is just endlessly motivating to figure out, what you could do better. And the game let's you do this at your own pace, it doesn't hold your hand. It supplies all the parts and tells you how to use them but it forces you to become creative with your style - and this demand works super well in this game. If you like games like Hotline Miami or Neon White for their difficulty and simultaneous motivation to get better at the them, this is for you. You know, actually, if you like games, this game is for you. Seriously, i highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't super long, but it's challenging and a fun twist on a Tony Hawk arcade game. I would say it heavily focuses on the combat, which involves 3rd person shooting and lots of dodging. The tricks are less important, even though they do matter for high scores and getting ammo back.My one complaint is sometimes it's hard to figure out what's happening on the screen on the later levels. Also, the New Game + mode seems way too hard for my tastes to the point of just being frustrating.It played really amazingly on my Steam Deck and made my servicing of my car very enjoyable since I got to play this in the dealership lobby!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: To call this game Tony Hawk with guns is unoriginal and reductive, but also a good starting point for explaining what makes it so great.Do tricks to earn points and regain ammo, get kills to raise the combo multiplier and reset the combo timer. Compete on the leaderboards for the highest score on each of the game's 2-5 minute arenas. It's a simple setup but if you love these types of games, that's what makes it so great. It just sets you loose with a smooth control setup, a flexible scoring system, and a set of great levels to hone your skills on. The scoring system in particular is very well done, forcing you to take bigger risks and learn more advanced techniques and tactics if you want to chase the top spots on the leaderboard. And unlike the old Tony Hawk games, you are rewarded for strategy and decision-making far more than your ability to mash buttons at hyperspeedIf you miss the old-school Tony Hawk games that were all about figuring out how to hit every challenge and get the highest score in a run, this might be the best game of that type to come out in decades.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: So, Rollerdrome. You ride the roller skates, you shoot the baddies, you get the ammo back by performing various tricks & challenges from one arena to another. It sounds fun on paper but also in the game! It all comes together quite well and there’s definitely “a fun zone” that you find yourself in after a couple of levels.I’d say that overall this is a much better game from beginning to the end, compared to Roll7’s other game that I’d played - OlliOlli World. The difficulty curve is definitely smoother and the game doesn’t all of a sudden turn into a “sweat-lord competition” halfway through. All challenges are very doable and I’d argue that with enough practice, most (if not everyone playing the game) can complete them. You can do one challenge at a time at every level. Although note that to progress to the next section of levels you’d need to complete a set number of challenges (again, that is very doable).Though the base campaign is short (about 5-6 hours), there’s another mode - “Out for blood”, which is essentially a remix of the base campaign with higher difficulty, so you can get another 5-6 hours of playtime.The game runs very well, the soundtrack is fine, enemy design is cool and the game loop is fun and addictive, which is why I can easily recommend Rollerdrome.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: What sets Rollerdrome apart from other "Tony Hawk with guns"-style games are its beautiful cel-shaded 1970s Michael-Crichton-novel-turned-feature-film aesthetic, its understated story mode that provides enough hooks to intrigue you without bogging down the flow of the action, and its absolutely drum-tight controls. The violence feels satisfying to commit and to watch, which is exactly what the villains want the athletes and audience to feel in the story. The challenges scale nicely as well, and I was satisfied with what I could accomplish with only my limited skill. It kept me coming back hour after hour for just one more run, where I felt sure that I'd be victorious next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is kinda hard.As in i'm having a hard time remembering much of this game. I know that i took some time to get all the achivements but it wasn't all that long? I mean, 15 hours isn't that much. I do remeber however that i Impulse bought this game after seeing a five second clip in Jacob Geller's "Top Ten Games of 2022". Other than that it was seemingly not that memorable. I do recall the Story being about how a Sport gets way more gloryfied and gorified for the Audience that keeps growing more Numb to all the violence inflicted onto the participants, so much so that the make them go up against a big robot equipped with a literal Minigun and homing Rockets. And that the were legally able to pull that off because the mega coorperation bought the law, simply put. So yeah, I guess that kinda stuck with me.What i can tell you about the Gameplay i remember is that this is the first game where the "Plays better with Controller" Message might be true, because it wasn't that fun the get the differents stunts for the 3 Million Combo to work. (Still did it with keyboard tho) So yeah, not that great. It is also on the shorter Side and does'nt feel that replayable to me. Still fun as far as i remember. Get it on Sale tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely unique and well designed game. One which has a low skill floor and an extremely high skill ceiling. I just beat the final campaign stage after 7 hours, and I certainly enjoyed the whole ride. But, to my surprise, the game then opened up the 'out for blood' mode and was like "OK good JOB, we were holding back the WHOLE TIME :D".Its great, with a nice lil narrative thrown in. And the challenges really add to the progression. They actually literally challenge you to get batter at the game. Its seriously really well designed.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: On their own, the combat and the Tony Hawk-ing are simple but fine. What's fantastic is how well incorporated they are and how fun they are to try and master simultaneously. If you're not into replaying levels just for the sake of getting better and getting a better rank/score, you probably won't get much out of this game. But if that does sound like your speed, I heartily recommend this game. Also the soundtrack is perfect, the art style is fantastic and the story kind of exists.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play all that many shooters these days but this is pretty amazing. I've read a few people saying that the skating part is sort of too easy (in terms of not failing tricks and that) but with all of the other frenetic action it needs to be a bit like that. I'll go play Session if I feel like repeatedly falling over.Well executed graphically, sort of retro futurist with I dunno maybe a bit of Gatchaman/Akira sort of (not really but a certain type of anime I can't quite put my finger on), with modern gaming enemy type sensibilities.Noice (so far)Grown up cel shading. Exciting bullet time.Jet Set AkiraMatrix
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a perfect example of why I still love video games. It honestly makes me upset more people haven't played this yet. Elements of horde shooters and Tony Hawk (kinda), what an amazing combination! It definitely helps that it runs amazingly well! (I was able to run the game at 4K and 300+ FPS for context) I've seen a fair amount of people saying they can beat the game in 4~6 hours but if you're bad like me it'll probably take 10 hours or so (not counting the harder campaign you unlock at the end). The story is solid, the art/graphics are great and the gameplay is awesome! 5/5, I'm pestering everyone I know to play this!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a really good game, but it is really short - you can beat it in around 3-4 hours. That being said, there is a lot of replayability to be found within the levels, with Tony Hawk-style challenges that can definitely lengthen the playtime by a huge margin. The challenges are mostly fun, but I found some absurdly hard and pretty annoying. There is a lot of fun to be found in Rollerdrome's mix of Tony Hawk, Doom and Max Payne,  the team over at Roll7 did an amazing job with the game. I liked the little bits of story sprinkled here and there, so kudos to the narrative designer, as I think the worldbuilding is done really well here, which helps convey the rules of Rollerdrome's world.All in all, I highly recommend this game, it's truly a breath of fresh air.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game that is a tight roughly 8 hour experience for your first set of full clears. Essentially Tony Hawk with shooting and tight enemy layout that lets you flow through the level when played well. Makes for a fantastic speed run game as well due to that if thats something you are interested in.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish, memorable, unique, incredibly fun. Has everything I love in a game and executes it very well. Conceptually the game seems very simple and easy but I've actually struggled quite a bit, at least to get decent scores. The abundance of mechanics is tastefully executed, allowing for a good variety of techniques at your disposal without senselessly overwhelming you. Putting it all together is incredibly fun and satisfying. Ironically enough, I'd say the main issue I have so far is it may be too forgiving? Failing a trick or a flip doesn't have any real consequences other than loss of momentum, so theres no downside to haplessly throwing them out at any chance you get. Except of course for losing your internal style points. This game is really inspiring in terms of design, and I hope to execute something similar myself one day. Love this game a lot :^)
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It can get hard, but I didn't find it annoying. However, you have to do stuff like performing tricks to get ammo while dodging attacks and alternating between different weapons. And I can see how some players might struggle with this dynamic. I know some people who find this sort of multi-tasking tricky to get into.It really does help if you spent your teenage years getting combos in Tony Hawk and SSX.Luckily, the developers have some mercy and allows the player to dodge constantly with no penalty and you don't need to worry about how you land. There is also a long slow-mo aim that recharges very fast, it's the bread and butter of the combat. It's great.It also got some great progression, as you get better, you start to get into stuff like getting high combos and completing challenges. As you get used to the enemies and levels, you become more elegant in how you skate around, tricking and shooting, and you learn how to best handle tricky enemies.It also unlocks a extra hard campaign when you finish it, just to kick your ass a bit more.Overall, I am impressed, and I am gonna go back and try to this new hard campaign and finish up the remaining challenges. If you like sharp, fast and accurate gameplay, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun at first and it has a Rollerball/The Warriors 70's movie vibe with a bit of 2000AD's Mean Arena and a hint of Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe for good measure. All of that is good. However, while there's a series of easy training rounds to start with that guide you through the moves you need to master, the campaign becomes excrutiatingly difficult by around the 3rd or 4th arena. It's not so much a learning curve, more a learning precipice. Trying to constantly pull flips and rail grinds for points (and more importantly, precious ammo) while dodging snipers, seeker missiles, mines and increasingly harder-to-kill respawning enemies can become too overwhelming too soon, and stops it being fun. While there are assists available in the settings (or rather cheats, such as infinite health/ammo), using them prevents the player from being included in the leaderboards, which I'm sure most players won't care about anyway. While it's certainly different, there's nothing especially groundbreaking about the skating or the shooting mechanics, and the arenas aren't especially interesting either. In fact they are kinda boring. While there seems to be lots of them (no idea how many in total as I haven't completed the campaign) the themes appear to be limited to just; Gymnasium, Snow, Desert and Shopping Mall. Is that really the best they could think up? I'd enjoy it more if the game didn't relentlessly punish me, and I'm sure the difficulty curve will put a lot of players off once their initial fun slams headlong into a brick wall. Of course it could just be that I suck at it and I need to get better, but old timers like me tire easily, so we try a few times, go off and have a cup of tea, try to calm down and maybe try again later. Whether we stay interested long enough to keep on trying, that's another matter.  So, different is good, but it's not really what this game has, it's what it lacks, that spoils the experience for me. No adjustable difficulty level to ease us in, no multiplayer or co-op, and a pitiful lack of variety in its arenas. It's the absence of those key features, plus the pointless addition of a leaderboard to give the false impression of competing against other players, that makes Rollerdome feel more like a demo for Rollerdome 2, which I'm sure will be awesome. It's with that sentiment in mind that I can't honestly recommend this game at the moment, at least not at full price. I do sincerely hope that it leads to better things however, as I enjoyed the premise and the art style. I just feel that it needs a bit more padding out to make it fun and accessible in the mid to later levels, rather than frustrating and somewhat limited in fun potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game!!  They managed to mix two styles of games very well.  I like the aesthetic, and even though it's mostly about the in-level action, there's still a bit of exploration (if you want it) and story.  Gameplay is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic!  Incredibly smooth, very well thought out, and just a blast to play.  You shoot enemies with one of a few guns, then to get more ammo, you need to do tricks.  It becomes a fast paced game of avoiding and dodging attacks while killing enemies, and in-between you use tricks to navigate the terrain (once you've done a few tricks your char starts to move faster/jump higher), and keep your ammo flowing.  It might take a little to get used to if you aren't used to Tony Hawk style games, but this is much easier, and you can't bail (fall on the ground and take a few seconds to stand up); if you don't finish a trick before hitting the ground, your char just rolls out of it.  This game is a masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't even aware that this existed until the poster caught my attention while going through a list of 2022 releases, and then turned into an impulse buy after watching the trailer - which somehow turned out to be underselling it. There's a lot more action in the actual game after you get out of the opening stages, and for such a gimmicky setup, it knows very well that a good shooter is one where you're always moving, where every weapon has a purpose, and where every enemy fills a role, not to mention the incredible clarity in communicating gameplay elements through high contrast visuals and sound cues that help you keep track of the action. The "Tony Hawk with guns" pitch is great but it's also a bit misleading; at its core Rollerdrome is a distillation of the newdoom formula of constant replenishment through aggressive play, unburdened by the constraints of being a triple A entry in a storied franchise. This is an arcade shooter first by a wide margin with the skating being an accessory to the shooting and not the other way around, even though it's what makes it completely unique, and what will separate the great players who can afford to show off from the merely competent enough to get through.If there's one questionable move which might actually turn away more impatient players, it's that it withholds most of your guns until you've played a few levels, in particular the last one you get - a charge-up, full-piercing, ricocheting laser sniper rifle that not only is the coolest of the bunch but will also allow you to keep your precious combo by getting kills on the other side of the map - but that's a very minor problem when you realize that your first run through the campaign is just a tutorial for getting used to the basics you'll need on your path to those S-ranks, or to simply survive the substantially increased intensity of its NG+ mode (where you'll probably want to eventually get the S-ranks too, because why wouldn't you).Also: rather amusing that the extremely minimal story still manages to find the time to sneak in two gigantic continuity errors. Cool nods to 1975's , too, in particular the font on the VICTORY/ELIMINATED screens. I haven't actually watched  tho, the trailer looked like ♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely fun game combining Tony-hawk game era tricks with style based combo gun combat. I never felt out of control in the game during the entirety of it and the difficulty of it felt fair with enemies all having their unique quirks but being fairly manageable on their timings and abilities. And if for whatever reason YOU want it to be easier? There's assist settings you can adjust to make it easier. Want it to be harder? After the main campaign you unlock "Out for Blood" which is going through the entire lineup of maps again but all the enemies are there, weapons are unlocked and they hit 50% harder, Devs were smart tho and DID NOT increase their health meaning if you're already dodging effectively, the harder difficulty won't be too bad.Gameplay beyond difficulty felt tight and with little issue, I never really felt that any situation that resulted in a combo drop or worse was because of the game. While sometimes the enemy effect clutter can get a bit much in VERY specific scenarios, I always was able to figure out WHY I got hit.Art looks good and has that timeless feeling where you could probably start this game up in like 10 years and it'll feel right at home. The effects look cool as well and do give a good idea of their hit ranges.Music is amazing, I only wish I could download it properly and not off spotify which is where it seems to solely be. Though I did have an issue in one of the Out for Blood maps not having music on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: An addicting fusion of Tony Hawk and arcade shooters. Really easy to pickup and have fun with, and the game does a good job of organically teaching you to get better. Which you will need to do as it ramps up in difficulty quite a bit. I had a as great time playing around on lower difficulty just freeform trickking and styling on enemies, and trying to hone my skills to beat the challenges and tackle the later levels and harder 2nd campaign. Between the accessibility options and the way the game teaches you, don't let the difficulty be a turn off. This can definitely be a push you challenging game or a chill drop in and skateshoot game depending on what you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Great mix of stuff you could do in Tony Hawk games and a really good third person shooter with a good variety of weapons and enemies.Controls are great (on gamepad at least), soundtrack, artstyle and story fit all really well together. Levels can vary a lot in difficulty, either due to enemy placements or layouts, but the game expects you to get better and play again for better scores anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: THPS, Max Payne, and Sonic thrown into a blender with a fantastic visual style.  That combination probably shouldn't work that well but it absolutely does.  Buttery smooth game mechanics and punishing difficulty.  Beating levels is incredibly satisfying and rewarding but you may find yourself overwhelmed.  I suck at this game but it's still really fun even if I can't beat the fourth level.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Max Payne's Pro Skater. Tight, fluid, and challenging game play, (that can be slowed down with assists, so dum dums like me can actually play the thing) against a backdrop of Wipeout, with the shady politics of the FIA/FIFA. Throw in some hella funky music straight outta Tron, and whew baby, you gots the Rollerdrome stew right there.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat feels like a highly polished tech demo since gameplay is the only thing it has going for it and the variety is just high enough to not fell old after a while. Though this is not a bad thing since it is kinda a new concept and experiment are costly.It's fun but lacks some depth and personality to have me coming back year after year. If you decide to go for all challenges like I did, you will have mastered the game at the end of the main campaign and will go throught the motion in the extra campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest news in 2022 is that Tony Hawk and Max Payne had a baby, and the result is a wonderful fusion shoot em up with some tough as nails challenges and simple mechanics which, when chained together and mastered can create satisfying style that may even give Dante a run for his money (or pizza slices).
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: First thing that attracted me to this game is exactly why I love it. Tony Hawk + Guns. It's exactly what you'd expect from that description with a really creative art style and fun gameplay to boot. Perfecting your runs to beat the highest scores and complete every challenge for a level is hard but still doable with some skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed stuff like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater and Max Payne and decided "These games are great, why shouldn't they be combined?" The Devs here strive to answer that exact question, and I think they succeeded. Like any good game the mechanics are simple enough to grasp yet really enjoyable when mastered. Nothing quite captures the feeling of doing a 360Backdash-Hoverwalk-Moonlanding then hitting a group of dudes with a grenade launcher. There are a few dashes of story here and there but it's ultimately unimportant in comparison to the main game play. Rollerdrome is very stylish, very fun, doesn't outstay it's welcome, and it's something you should be playing right now instead of sitting on the fence and reading my review about it!Very good, Rollerblading/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is easily one of my top 5 games this year. It's the perfect mash-up of third-person-shooting and Tony Hawk Pro-Skating. You are always doing something and once you master the controls and understand how the tricks work, you can rack up some crazy combos and score BIG. This game is one of the most satisfying experiences I've had in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game upon seeing it on frontpage. Being a massive fan of the Jet Set Radio franchise, I was instantly sold. Though, gameplay wise, I would compare it more to a Tony Hawk Pro Skater kinda vibe, the focus on combos playing a bigger role, compared to JSR's time-rush kinda tempo. It integrates thrilling gunplay, exhilarating enemy types, and obscene replayability into a juicy mess of explosions and kick-ass flips. It's something that lends well to that "one more try" kinda game loop. It's a fun romp that takes you through a good variety of themed stages filled with baddies just asking to be blown to bits, said baddies being delightfully designed, all with unique pressures that can make the game look like an absolute light show, all while keeping legibility of what's going on. Within the mid to later stages, you'll be kiting gnarly 540 Melancholy Backflips while shooting down heat seeking missiles, dodging lasers and blasting lowly grunts and snipers into orbit with your rail gun. All of this insanity is managed by Rollerdrome's Max Pane-esque bullet time mechanics which are fundamental to the game's comprehensibility. es good. ver y good. would be cool if there was a park builder, but the Out For Blood newgame+ suits my hunger for more Rollerdrome quite well.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is probably one of the best game I picked up this year. I love its game-play mechanics where the player have to manage their ammunition by doing tricks to reload gun and kill the enemy at the same time. The enemies are very well designed. They are strong enough to make you feel threaten but not too strong to make the game too hard. The inclusion of challenges is very entertaining as well. Although some challenges have weird and hard-to-understand wording, they are satisfying to complete. I highly recommend this game for those who are looking for a fast-pace shooter that is unique in its own way and challenging to play. It might be a little hard to get used to the controls in the beginning but when you mastered it, its hella fun!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's like that movie Rollerball, but, ya know, good. And cool. And fun. So, nothing like Rollerball. Tony Hawk x Max Payne x Running Man Way too fun, easy to understand, tough to master. Visually stunning gameplay. Great soundtrack(s). Cool story elements that are totally optional. I challenge you not to like this game.Kara rules! Great job Roll7! Crushing it again!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not usually the biggest fan of shooters but this game is an exception. It looks and feels amazing to play and unlike some AAA games out there it’s actually difficult and has risk, not just flashy looks and animations (I’m looking at you spider-man). Some levels got pretty difficult but because the same enemies spawn in the same waves you can strategize and figure out your best course of action over multiple attempts. Overall one of the most fun, crazy, risky, stylish games I’ve played in a long time - play this if you want to feel awesome AND feel like you actually earned it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I am ass at skating games, but the intense satisfaction of blazing around blasting people pulled me in. It took a while to get used to nailing combos and moving where I wanted. I still have difficultly getting anywhere high up.  Having to constantly hold down so many buttons was murder on my fingers for even short play sessions. Once you meet the skill floor, though, this is exhilarating. The short build-up to the first jump in every level paired with the music popping in kicks ass. The art direction is stellar. The disco-future style makes everything look like a 70s movie poster and the sound design is solid. The levels are compact but dense with opportunity to flex for the crowd, and I like how you have to complete challenges to unlock new levels. The main campaign keeps things interesting dolling out new maps, enemies and weapons at a solid pace, but the only boss fight is repeated twice. The story, bare-bones as it is, has touches of intrigue. I like the subtle world building of tricks being named after different Rollerdrome competitors. While it is clear the narrative wasn't the focus for this game, finishing the campaign isn't satisfying. Rollerdrome the sport is centered as the apex of a broken society, with rebellion and social collapse all around. Your character seems to be involved to pay back substantial debt. Any interaction with these ideas is in the margins. You could argue this makes your character either an unwilling participant, keeping your head down and claiming your bag, or perhaps relishing the thrill of the sport, as I found myself doing, but there's too little for this to add up to anything more than momentary interest.The gameplay is enough to carry this snack-sized experience. I could see some players spending hours mastering the controls and climbing the leaderboards for each level. Still, there is SOMETHING holding Rollerdrome back from being great. Something to break up the arenas like a huge chase wouldn't have been remiss here. A "Mount Wario" from Mario Kart type scenario with pursuing enemies. Maybe a harder soundtrack ala Carpenter Brut's contributions to Furi, keeping the icy synths of the game's current soundscape but driving the beat. Maybe the enemies could have less health, as the levels with the starter enemies i found to be the most satisfying. Maybe the laser enemies can GET ******. Regardless, the core gameplay is rock solid and this gets a hearty recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game and it gets you into such a flowstate, feels awesome. Takes some getting used to for sure, definitely go with a controller as the controls get kinda complex and on keyboard it gets uncomfortable. Soundtrack and aesthetic are top notch, gameplay is pretty fun though the trick inputs can be pretty picky. Very solid game

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, but I beat the main campaign in one sitting. The final boss wasn't so much difficult as it was frustrating. A single explosion makes it hard to see the 3 other missiles going at you, as well as the additional set of mines it threw right in front of you when you dodged the first... and this is in addition to the finicky collision on the boss itself, making it difficult to actually get in position to shoot its weak spot.And perhaps I just need to "git gud" but I found it difficult to perform specific tricks, especially the more advanced ones that are required to do the challenges at later stages. Perhaps there are more hours of play if I want to beat the second hard mode campaign, but the final boss really left me not wanting to continue playing.For those wondering, you can indeed beat the game with just a keyboard and mouse, but it seems that there is a bit of an issue with the game recognizing the inputs for the various tricks.Overall, I'd only recommend getting this game on sale. Even then, as you can likely see in most of the reviews, you likely aren't going to get more than a few (5 or so) hours out of this game unless you're dead set on 100%ing it. So if you're the type of person who cares about $/hours played, perhaps save your money for something else.P.s., don't button mash :)

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun addictive gameplay, but a few things stop it from being a 10/10 for me.- The final weapon upgrade is easily the least useful, and other than using it for the specific challenges that required it, I didn't see any need to use it.- Most of the arenas felt samey, with the only thing separating them being the environment and that sometimes you could break glass and go inside certain areas. Would love to see environmental hazards other than just falling off the map.- A lot of people in the reviews are saying the game is really difficult, and while I agree it's a challenging game, I felt like some of the later maps were more tediously long than hard. Wouldve liked an enemy counter somewhere on the hud to tell me how much longer it was going to take.- - That being said, a great game that I will continue to play and wish was a little bit longer.

_childDocuments_.review: A really awesome game!!It's like everyone is saying; take Tony Hawk and mixed it with Max Payne/My Friend Pedro and there you have it! _childDocuments_.review: Woah, this is an interesting surprise. It caught my attention with its extraordinary design, but it came out that the concept of Rollerdrome is even more interesting than I could have expected. The game has its own story, it takes place in a retrofuturistic universe, where people are crazy about the bloody new sport, which is simply a combination of extreme roller skating and killing dozens of armed to the teeth opponents. We play the role of Kara Hassan, a rising star in this discipline. The game allows us to get to know the world and our hero in short additional playable cutscenes, wich is really neat. However, the gameplay is really unique, because it's based on an unconventional combination of two different genres, shooters and sports games like Tony Hawk Pro Skater, where your progress is based on difficulty of tricks you perform. In this case, kills are counted as combos, and you have to perform skating tricks to refill your ammunition. This is really something new for me, but I'm enjoying it so far. The game is very dynamic, the levels are nicely designed to perform tricks, and the fighting element gives it a fast pace.Rollerdrome offers 11 arenas, 4 guns which differ in their effectivness agains each of 7 types of opponents, and 27 unique tricks you can combine however you want. This makes a huge field to show off for tryhards, but it also allows casual players to simply enjoy the game. The feeling of skating and shooting in game is really satisfying. I would say that it's pretty easy to learn the basics, but everyone needs to find their own style of play, and it takes hours to master that.However, I really feel that this game deserves an extension of some kind. Maybe some new campaign in the future, new enemies, guns or arenas, I would buy that kind of DLC. Most of all, I think Rolledrome has a lot of potential to be a great multiplayer competetive game.If you found my review interesting, I could bet you'd get into this, believe me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun as heck!  The enemy variety and difficulty does indeed level up, but so does your arsenal. _childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game embodies everything that makes one say "yes." The style. The soundtrack. The shooting. The dodging. The slow-mo. All of it. Just yes.I don't know of any other game where the animated trailer is exactly the same as what the gameplay is actually like and feels like.Movement and tricks are inconsequential to get right and while that may seem to be a downside at first, it really lets you focus on what matters: Taking down enemies and feeling cool while doing it. Each level must be played at a consistent focus level to succeed, so if you start to slip up, you get eliminated. So once you finally get rid that final enemy, it's a very satisfying feeling.Combat takes on a plan and execute vibe where you have to time your tricks and position with longer range enemy attacks. This happens constantly because the level design and enemy placement is ever so slightly different for each interaction. As a result, there are no dull moments.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, what a stellar name. Rollerdrome. It’s evocative and bold. Rollerdrome has you playing the roll of Kara Hassan who has to quite literally skate-or-die, for the enjoyment of corporate overlords. The game wears its inspirations on its sleeve with a mashup of Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater and bullet time a la Max Payne. It’s a novel idea that I think works very well. To replenish ammo you must do tricks which turns into this dance of shooting enemies but also making sure that you squeeze in a nosegrind to refill your double pistols or rocket launcher. I think the minute to minute gameplay is quite engaging and can get quite hectic towards the end, in an exhilarating way. I do wish that I didn’t have to fight with the camera as much as I did, but other than that I think the game really accomplishes what it set out to do.I also really appreciated the inclusion of the assist options. Like Tony Hawk, each level contains objectives that you must complete a certain number of before you can proceed to the next stage. One of the assist options includes turning that requirement off, so you don’t have to grind those objectives if you do get stuck. There’s a number of other assist options, which is a big plus in my book as I am an advocate of letting people play how they want.While the regular price may be a tad high in my opinion, I would have no reservation recommending Rollerdrome on a sale. It’s a unique game and one that is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels amazing to play! You really get into that skating game flow of: Pick a line, refine it, master it and then you mess up one jump and screw up your combo :D Its fast, action-heavy and always keeps you on your toes. If it's too tough for you, there's a great assistmode menu to tone it down a little bit.Plenty of fun challenges to keep you playing for a while! Awesome soundtrack

_childDocuments_.review: The reductive take is that Rollerdrome is Doom Eternal meets Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater. But it really nicely sums it up. You have the movement, the tricks and the level challenges very reminiscent of Tony Hawk’s and a fast paced combat that relies on good enemy design, resource management and a fine balance between planning and improvisation. What makes it brilliant is how these two systems overlap. Landing tricks replenishes your ammo and killing enemies quickly without getting hit increases your combo multiplier, so you need to constantly weave between shooting and doing tricks in order to play effectively. It is just so satisfying flipping over an enemy in slow motion while filling them full of bullets. The cel-shaded style is a bit hit and miss, I understand what they are going for, but sometimes that game look flat and barren and especially over longer distances the render technique makes the otherwise crips strokes outlining every object jittery and janky. But the whole 70/80s violent animated series look is spot on for the tone they are going for.Furthermore, the soundtrack is what ties the whole experience together. It fits the style so perfectly, it feels retro without being derivative. Everytime the beat drops when you jump into the arena is pure hype and the intensity of the music matches the frantic gameplay. There are a moderate amount of levels and if you play well and just rush for the ending, the game would be very short, under an hour. But, that is likely not going to happen on your first playthrough. I found the game so difficult at first that just clearing a level took several tries; learning how to play decently enough to complete a level will take you some time. Each level also has several objectives you have to complete in order to progress and some are quite hard requiring several attempts. You will be replaying every level a few times, but it never became boring, it was just so satisfying to master a level and beat the high score. It took me about 10 hours to beat the first time and complete almost all objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard someone describe Rollerdrome's gameplay as Tony Hawk's Pro Skater meets Max Payne, and I knew I had to check it out. It lived up to the hype for me. The game handles to me exactly as I expected it to given that sort of description. I remapped the controls to be more akin to THPS, and that actually made it a ton easier for me to just jump in and play. Like THPS, it's easy to learn, but insanely difficult to master. The bullet time mechanics are handled perfectly, and once you get into a rhythm, the game just flows. The controls are great. Gameplay is amazing. I -love- the game's aesthetic. The music is perhaps a bit too understated, but I could probably just play with the balances overall. Sometimes the "Do trick X by the trick icon" is a bit... finicky... but other than that, everything handles just fine. Interesting story to it, and I'll admit, I'd love to see more of the world itself, since there seemed to be an interesting subplot going on.I'm hooked, and I hope for a sequel/expansion/etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Brief and fantastic. Finding out the most efficient ways to tackle each enemy is core to doing well. Soundtrack is also enjoyable with a visual style that's smooth and clear. _childDocuments_.review: This game caught me off guard.  This is definitely one of the best games of 2022, hands down!  It's non stop action, the physics are amazing, the graphics are what they are supposed to be, which is comic book/cell shaded..  It's like Tony Hawk physics meets 3rd person shooter in the Matrix.. slow down time in mid flip off a kicker ramp to aim and shoot your opponent.... with rocket launchers, shot guns, dual pistols, while dodging rockets, snipers, frozen laser beams, and much more.  The soundtrack is perfect for this game, as it is much like the futuristic tech slammer music that the 80's inspired.  This is a must have, and the price is great for what you get!  I consider this a must have, this game could have saved the long dry spell of games in 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, challenging game. Perhaps one of the coolest indie ideas I've seen in some time. Its a great feeling sniping an enemy across the map in bullet time after doing a 720 grab. The soundtrack feels completely on point as well.My biggest gripe with this game is progression. I think they were going for an old school feel of locking levels behind completing challenges in earlier levels, but it feels like a bit of a drag if you complete a tough level and want to be rewarded with the next one only to find that you have to grind challenges. A more minor gripe is that while theres a story, its almost too minimalistic, and ends up not really leaving an impression.At the discounted launch $20 price, its a solid recommend, but should have been the permanent price. $30 feels like its pushing it a bit on this one.Nevertheless, great game that deserves more love. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game which needs more attention. You'll be completely zoned in and pulling off 720 triple air-flip snipe combos nonstop once you get to grips with the controls. _childDocuments_.review: Audience☐ Beginner☐ Casual Gamer☑ Normal Gamer☑ ExpertGraphics☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☑ Beautiful☐ FantasticMusic☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☐ Beautiful☑ FantasticDifficulty☐ Easy☐ Average☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Hard☐ UnfairBugs☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☑ Nothing encounteredStory☐ There is none☐ Bad☑ Alright☐ Good☐ FantasticGameplay☐ Frustrating☐ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun☑ ChallengingGame time / Length☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☑ Short (4 - 8 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☑ Few hours (10 - 30 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Long (40-60 hours) ☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)Price / Quality☑ Full price☐ Wait for Sale☐ Don't buy☐ Refund it if you canRollerdrome is a truly excellent game. Don't let any naysayers discourage you. If you want to grind for challenges, you'll really have to push yourself (I just finished the out-for-blood difficulty as of writing this review, and it can be truly brutal at times), but regardless, this game is just pure arcade-style fun. When you perfectly time the dodge with an enemy's attack and get the bonus damage, it literally feels like bullet time from the Matrix. Even just experimenting with the gameplay sandbox by replaying levels is awesome. As far as I can tell, the skill ceiling is pretty much endless since you can continue to improve your combo awareness and mix up trick usage in a level playthrough, and optimize damage with weapon swaps.Even the story and world-building, while not amazing, is still intriguing enough to hold the campaign together and hold your interest between levels. Couple that with a beautiful artstyle that just pops off the screen, and you're easily looking at one of the top 3 best games I've played this year. Do yourself a favor and just try it, full price or otherwise.I've seen others complain about the controls in other reviews. I have no idea what they're talking about: this is an incredibly responsive and smooth gameplay experience. Sometimes doing special command input grabs/grinds can be harder with an analog stick, but that's probably the only control scheme-related problem I've encountered. I've also only seen one or two gameplay glitches in my entire playthrough; it's a well-constructed video game in almost every way. The control scheme is also somewhat difficult to master if you want to fully take advantage of your character's abilities, but the basics are still very approachable for casuals. While the game is very punishing when you reach the harder difficulties, in my opinion it's never unfair.I've also seen some people complain about how campy the game feels, and how you have to play defensively. Absolutely not. Certain weapons in the game actually reward you for using super reflex time effectively, and if you time your encounter with a close-quarters enemy, you can actually charge up the Z-11 to snipe full-health enemies all the way across the map. Similarly, you can time a sniper shot super reflex to make short work of enemies closer to you. There are so many ways to customize combat given a particular situation; you're never forced to play super defensively or super offensively. You can get punished for lingering in one position for too long, but that's pretty much it; it's very free-form and fun to experiment with overall.There are only two real complaints I have about this game: first, the . Second, while the replayability is there from a combat and combo perspective, I do wish there were more maps to play around in.Roll7, if you're reading this, PLEASE add DLC maps, or a level editor. I will happily pay full price for both of them.

_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you combine Tony Hawk's with The Matrix? Rollerdrome.Buttery smooth gameplay that just feels so damn cool to experience. Nailing that transition between slow motion shooting and scoring tricks is very satisfying.Campaign itself is short but the levels demand to be replayed. Whether it's to complete challenges, chase a high score or just jump in for a quick session.The only let down for me were the boss battles — made sense for the campaign story but felt lacking compared to the main gameplay loops.Much of the quality of Rollerdrome is wrapped up in game feel — you really need to play it for yourself to understand what makes it so good. _childDocuments_.review: RollerDrome is perfect if you're looking for a singleplayer experience with replay value. Max Payne meets Tony Hawk meets Jet Grind Radio meets Mad Max.
