_childDocuments_.review: This is not a great game. Even if everything worked, I would have difficulty calling  a good game.But I wanted to give it a thumbs up anyway. Partially because I find the hate bandwagon surrounding this game distasteful. I loathe the hyperbole in the negative reviews. I've played worse. A lot worse. I played  on release.  is not a terrible game. It is... aggressively mediocre. does not feel or play like an Arkane game. It is painful to reconcile that this came from the studio that gave us  and . But it  feel like a Bethesda game. It feels appropriate for a studio trying to pick itself up after the trainwreck (of a train carrying dumpsters, all of which were on fire) that was  and deliver something that's not half-bad.The open world is well-made. The island of Redfall is fun to explore and have firefights in. The graphics are usually solid, with some occasional greatness. The characters are conceptually unique and fun.Sadly, the story could be a lot better. I found myself daydreaming of better stories for the game. Worse, the lore is dull. The bits that aren't related to the vampire apocalypse don't flesh out the world in any interesting way. The bits that are about the ongoing horror rarely provoke empathy and never offer intrigue. An example of a particularly bad offender is one of the first notes you find: "Fear". The note is a father saying how his wife and baby are staying behind in a shipping crate while he goes out for supplies. He asks how so many normally good people could become cultists for monsters, and tells us the answer is fear. The note isn't written to anyone in particular and has no reason to have been written at all. The father isn't asking for help or pleading for his family or railing at the enemy. There is no quest attached, no exploration it points to. The note is in the cargo container it talks about, and everyone is there dead (except the devs aren't going to show us a dead baby). Worse, the note points out something bizarre, something , and then tells us there isn't a mystery here and the explanation is as banal and cursory as possible. It reads like the devs telling us not to bother looking beyond the surface level for narrative content.Still, I had a lot of fun running around the world with my best friend, shooting vampires and cultists as we set up safehouses and stalked the vampire "gods" that rule the island.And there were moments of brilliance. I won't spoil with an example as they are few and precious. But those moments told me the kind of game this could have been. And should have been.I would have given this a thumbs up despite so many lackluster elements, but the game has bugs and issues that just started to sap the fun I had found in it. Monsters scale to your level, so those bigger damage numbers never feel meaningful. To the contrary, I find myself avoiding combat because I didn't want to level. Leveling just meant that the guns I found which I liked would lose their effectiveness. Sure, it meant I also got skill points, but that brings us to other problems.The characters are not well balanced. And even when their powers work right, some of them are too situational or limited to be desirable. While Devinder's teleporter is beyond amazing, Layla's elevator is clunky to use and drastically less versatile. And I seriously question the mindset of the devs who decided that a powerful female character's ultimate power should be having a man come and save her. Honestly, that feels gross.I mostly played Jacob, whose power set seemed custom-made for me. Except of his powers, only the invisibility cloak worked properly. The scouting raven was a crapshoot at best who would regularly fail to notice enemies I could directly see and whose damaging ability procced once in a blue moon. Likewise, by the time we reached Burial Point, the "powerful" headshots that his ultimate was supposed to supply regularly did almost no damage. The ultimate became a liability, locking me out of using effective weapons whenever the spectral sniper rifle decided it wanted to be a nerf gun. Beyond invisibility, Jacob's best and most reliable ability was the special skill of carrying more lockpicks and rewire kits. And even that had an issue: when starting or joining a game, any ammo or supplies carried above the amount allowed without skills would often be lost as the game applied your skills after loading your inventory.My best friend and I will likely finish the game together. I have no desire to continue to play solo. Nor will I return to it after we finish. The game is not worth full price, but I can still recommend it on deep discount if you have someone to play it with. Just don't expect an Arkane game. Expect a fairly fun if generic looter-shooter with a vampire theme.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I assume 95% of the reviews posted thus far are by people who got through the "tutorial" mission and decided the game was trash so don't trust most of the reviews here with "0.10 hours on record" because that's nowhere near enough to get a fair feel for the game. Maybe wait for a Steam sale to pick this one up, it seems like a $30 title rather than $70 but overall, it's been a decent ride. Gameplay is smooth, open world fills out as you unlock more content, and the open world is very vertical, so maybe try climbing before assuming there's nothing to do. Let's rip the bandaid off. Not sure this is a full-price game. I'd say wait to get it at a decent discount from what I've played so far. The AI is not fantastic, and that's my biggest gripe, but in general I'm having a lot of fun exploring the world and making my way through the early missions. Also, to be transparent, I'm not having any performance issues. I have a very high-end rig, and the game runs just fine, but that may just be a little "ivory tower" syndrome. I feel the need to step up and defend this game a little, however, from all of the smoothbrain takes here. People are complaining the "open world is empty" then have like 20 minutes in the game. Did you even try? As you complete progression missions, there's more and more that is being added to do in the world. There's also a lot of verticality to most of the world. There's a lot of buildings you can't just walk into, but you  parkour up to the rooftops or climb scaffolding and get into a lot of places via a higher floor window. I've finished roughly 5 main missions, and the world is starting to fill out with more side-objectives to complete, so it takes some time to "unlock" those features. Sure, this is a little linear than most people would expect from an open-world title, but them's the breaks now and then. Secondly, I've seen some reviews of people who have 4 - 6 hours in the game and their review claims they have beaten the whole story and I find that dubious. Now, I'm not speedrunning the game, and I'm not sure how long it is, but with around 4 - 5 hours myself, trying to see more content than just the main story, I'm only - as I said - about 4 or 5 missions in. Maybe the game's main missions are super shallow and if you just bust your way through only story missions, you can finish that quickly, but I expect the story missions will take probably 10 - 20 hours to beat, at least? I just seriously doubt that - even at breakneck paces - you could beat the whole main story so quickly. There's no published speedruns of the game yet, so there's no fair frame of reference, so I just may be overestimating the length of the story. Ultimately, I feel like this is just a bandwagon "review bomb brigade" where people spend 10 minutes in the game, decide that progressing to unlock features is for chumps, and refund the game because a lot of the takes so far are hot garbage. Thanks for coming to my TED Talk.

Reload speeds are just awfully slow like there's a vampire chewing on you, maybe put a tiny bit of effort into speeding up that reload. Skip the tactical reload, dump that mag on the ground and get the next one in like maybe your life depends on it, lol.  I realize I'm playing a young college girl who probably never touched a gun in her life but damn it just feels awful to play.Finally, dodging.. I spend most of my play time in a sprint away from the fight while I reload, trying to guess the exact moment I should slide to avoid the claws.  All this without being able to see, so it's pretty much a guess.  When in close quarters there is no way to mitigate or avoid vampire damage.  No dodge mechanic, no block, it's face tank and shoot or do the run and slide thing. Thumbs up because I got 11 hours of entertainment about it even if I finally realized it's just not fun for me running away, sliding, spinning around shooting, running away, sliding ... you get the point.  Maybe "end game" or later in the game guns actually start hurting the vampires fast enough that you don't need to do the run and slide stuff, but as I aged I stopped playing games that weren't fun while "leveling" because what's the point really.I haven't tried the co-op because none of my friends own the game and nobody is playing online, but I think I could kill some more hours with a buddy at some point and not totally hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated after 55 hours of gameplaySolid 8/10 game. Recommending because it's been fun for me and i've really got a huge amount of enjoyment out of this game. Despite what people think this is very much an Arkane game with lots of their style and gameplay elements littered if you just give it some time and go looking for them.You can't play this game like its Division. Neither is it Left 4 Dead. Its an Arkane game with some looting RNG. But primarily this game is about the story. It is about finding different ways to aproach a situation and it is about exploring the game world for the huge amount of detail and care the developers have put into it. Only then will you uncover a trully wonderful game that falls a little flat of its ambitions. But a great game is still there for those that can look past the few bugs. Coop is way more of a mess. I play mostly single player and experience very few bugs. I tried coop and it was filled with all kinds of bugs.What i see here is Sea of Thieves at launch. A game that has potential and has been crafted with love and ambition but that has fallen a little flat. I believe if the developers are given more time and support from Microsoft they can turn this into something really wonderful. That said with many many hours of gameplay, the more time you give this game the more it will give you back. The more i play the more i love it and i'm still not bored. I look forward to playing this at the end of each day when i've finished work and the kids are in bed.Are there issues? YesDoes the game feel somewhat half baked in places? YesIs it as terrible as the discussions or steam reviews want you to believe? Not at all. The main issue is at the price point its horribly underwhelming and from a studio like Arkane people expected much more.Games like Dishonored, Prey or even Deathloop were unique worlds and instantly fun and different and while its great to see the Arkane style out in an open world and its nice to see them try something new it just lacks some of the stuff that really makes an Arkane game great.  The environment and atmosphere are all fantastic and the game feels creepy. The storytelling is also wonderful but you have to work for it. It's like a big book that is difficult to get into but once you allow yourself to be come immersed the more it gives you back in return. For example, one of the best legendary perk pickups in the game isn't signposted. You may or may not come across a house with some clues and locked doors. You then can choose to follow the clues and read notes to uncover a pretty chilling and grim tale of three sisters who murdered a sibling as an offering. In return you get a really powerful legendary. But none of this is handed to you or signposted.There are plenty of things like this throughout the game. Nothing is handed to you other than the main questline and even this has pieces you really have to slow down and pay attention to or notes to read or recordings to listen to if you want the full picture. For me that is great. I love it as it immerses you into the world and it all feels very Arkane.Graphically its fine. Its stylised. Its Arkane through and through. Some have performance issues. For me i get a smooth locked 60fps at 4k on max settings which is just fine. I'm playing two characters and really enjoying both right now. I'm looking forward to seeing what the other two characters will bring to the table.I also hope that they add another map to the game but somehow i don't see that happening as it would be a pretty huge undertaking.Are there improvements needed?Yes. Of course. Lots of the broad complaints are valid. The way people are going about making them is not. Its childish and indicitive of a very problematic issue that plagues gaming communites. People have no clue how to interact or behave. This is an issue you see over every game launch and getting worse over time. Steam harbors this toxic behaviour and does nothing to stem it. I'd be surprised if the devs bothered to even read some of the stuff posted here just because of how its being presented. The irony is if these things were presented in a sensible fashion they might actually get listened to.Right now their behaviour is no different from a toddler who doesn't get exactly what they want so they have a tantrum and then get even more upset because they don't understand why no one takes them seriously.Regardless i'm happy that Arkane were given the space to try something new and i hope that they are given the space to turn it into something even better.

_childDocuments_.review: I can sum up this review in two words - wasted potential. If you can, snipe this game for cheap. $20 at the most. Grab a friend too.Game has its moments and its appeal. I really wish they had more time to cook but unfortunately, the game was bogged down with a poor launch that kept folks away. They tried to address the issues in a timely manner but bug fixes and upgrades were not coming fast enough.Gunplay feels arcade-y but not goofy. It doesn't come off like Call of Duty or Battlefield either. With only three weapon slots means you are forced to go into your inventory a lot and swap out weapons. I found myself keeping the UV weapon in slot three equipped at all times because it was just too valuable to unequip, meaning I was constantly swapping out the first two weapon slots to whatever was needed for the situation. My one gripe early on was you hold so little ammunition and feel forced to invest in the ammo perks early on if you don't want to swap guns all the time.Movement is basic, not including abilities or perks. With more perks and abilities, movement allows you to get into some interesting places rather quickly, bypassing (sometimes locked) doors or repositioning yourself into a higher area for an advantage.Voices are good but your character just WILL NOT SHUT UP. After every fight they comment and it will most likely force people to disable voices. I found myself forced to disable voices to continue playing and retaining my sanity.Exploring and scavenging felt natural and not forced. I did not feel compelled to go out of my way to farm or focus on something in particular, outside of collectibles.  My one gripe is lockpicks and hacking tools were limited you being able to carry three at a time. There are certain perks that reduce the chance to use one but still, only three being the cap? Jacob has a perk that increases his lockpick count to 8 and there are, usually, ways around locked doors such as windows in certain places, etc. Lockpicks only work on doors, safes and certain chests. If you're a loot goblin like me, you are compelled to open all the things.Menus were straight to the point. The information you need is categorized in a way that's easy to find and navigate with minimal fluff, with text that's easy to read. You will also be spending a lot of time in the inventory screen swapping out weapons so get comfortable with that. I also enjoyed the red text format. Quests are pretty standard but a few twists here and there kept me wary of approaching certain quests the way you normally would. "Go here, find X" but X turns out to be a trap. Don't trust things you hear over the radio or TVs.Characters have their own identity and skillset, meaning playing with friends as different characters comes off as necessary, sorta. Each compliment one another but you can still solo without anyone. Skill trees are expanded through skill points, acquired from leveling up, killing mini-bosses, doing certain quests, etc. My first several bunch of points went straight into increasing my ammo count because I was tired of having to swap weapons so often.Enemies ranging from standard melee vampires to humans with guns. The AI for the standard vampire comes off as jank because they seem to have no real sense of self-preservation while saying they'll eviscerate you. They also run at you in some strange angles and weird ways that the animation looks goofy while looking at you with a >:( face. There's a few other types of special vampires as well as unique variants of humans such as humans that summon help or build turrets to attack you. I won't spoil the vampire variants but I do recommend you aim for the head. Also as a side note - If you are using an RTX card, do not enable DLSS. Your game will crash a lot. A shame the game will most likely never get patched to improve it.Overall, the game is just okay. It's very unfortunate the game will not receive anymore updates. If this game had more time to cook and had a better launch, I daresay this game could've been pretty damn good. Maybe not GOTY material, but still enjoyable all the same.

_childDocuments_.review: About 6 years ago i was in a bad car accident that left me paralysed from the neck down and mute. My only real, effective way of communicating is by blinking (once for yes, twice for no etc). I have always been a huge gamer and my brother has too. When i lost the ability to play for myself i fell into a spiralling depression. All those hours i spent with steam friends, all those amazing memories, never to be repeated. My brother, bless him, picked up on this and offered to play the games I wanted to FOR me while i sat behind him in my wheelchair and watched. With tears in my eyes i agreed and i have been playing vicariously through him ever since. When Redfall was announced we both became super hyped and i couldn't wait to watch him play it. After pre-ordering it and waiting about 3 weeks the wait was almost over. He pre-loaded the game and after 2 more excruciating days of waiting we finally got to play it. He wheeled me into my favourite spot just behind my old computer chair loaded it up and selected our character. After watching him play for 4 agonizing hours i couldn't take it anymore, with the holy will of God himself i screamed internally at my muscles to obey me, I just needed them this one last time, I had to make it stop. With every ounce of strength i had I slowly pushed myself out of that wheelchair and hobbled over to the computer. Not knowing how long this divine power would last i shoved my brother aside and desperately fumbled with the mouse and keyboard to write a refund request. As i watched and waited for my confirmation e-mail with tears in my eyes i knew that while my body had been healed, my mind would never be the same. God bless you Arkane Austin for giving me my autonomy back.

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a tentatively positive review.I loaded up the game for a short while to test the performance claims of other reviewers, concerned that this game might have been unplayable and result in a refund. I was pleased that the game ran flawlessly on max settings with DLAA (not DLSS) and frame generation with a completely stable 120fps@4k. GPU usage was between 57-81% & temperatures not exceeding 56 degrees.The very minor issues I encountered were a handful of textures for the landscape took ~2 seconds to load in after rebooting the game instead of being instantaneous like the rest and there's a very brief, maybe half a second, stutter when loading areas as you move further through the map but that's not unheard of in games so I don't mind.I always keep my system perfectly optimised for gaming and every software component updated so if you're encountering issues I'd recommend doing the same as there's more to a computer than just your graphics driver. Additionally, I've noticed a lot of reviews that are disappointed with performance are running old hardware. Try to keep your expectations realistic for how old your system is and check the system requirements, you won't always be able to play a modern game at the same resolution and quality presets that you could for one 6 years ago with the same tech.I'll update my review as I play more with the wife in co-op later on and include any issues we might encounter but for now I've no real complaints.Update: Co-op worked perfectly fine, no issues or bugs that prevented progression or hindered what we were working on at that time. Smooth performance persisted, never dropped below 120fps. Though after experiencing more of what the world and story had to offer I'm changing my review to not recommended as the game is for the most part quite lifeless and you'll spend more than half of your time just running through empty streets, finding a handful of enemies here and there but they never seem to be doing anything which makes them feel alive past being targets to shoot for a few minutes before you mop up their loot then continue trekking down the barren streets. The difficulty is also ridiculously easy, I didn't once feel that I was in any danger despite playing on the highest difficulty which further takes away from the enjoyment in my opinion as I enjoy being challenged.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10.  This was a baffling game.  On one hand the story and voice acting were intriguing and engaging.  I enjoyed learning about the main story through a well thought out combination of in-game notes, voice recordings, and in-game  "psychic flashbacks."  Reminded me a bit of FEAR where you're trying to figure out what caused this, who the mysterious cast of characters are, what are their backstories, etc.  On the other hand, the open world gameplay is barren of enemies and the enemy AI that is around is just plain awful.  It's downright embarrassing for a AAA game that was $70.  For much of the game you are just walking around between the town and coming across set pieces where you think, "this would be fun to fight around if there were enemies," but they're nowhere to be seen.  There's also a ridiculous amount of bugs.  Enemies that are stuck standing still, enemies that are there moving around but can't be attacked, loading to black screens where other players can see you but you can't move, killed enemies falling through the floor so you can't loot them.  Bottom line, don't buy this game for anything more than $20.  Maybe ever.  Even if they fixed the bugs I think the core problems with enemy AI may be too much to overcome.  High five to the story writers and voice actors of this game.  Everyone else involved, shame on you for releasing this garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Very first impressions. If you enjoyed Dishonored you will enjoy RedFall albeit in a different manner. The game is playable, 7900XTX 4k 60/70 fps on Epic quality without FSR. The game, IMO, need low level tweaking since I can observe notorious 'VRAM leaking', you start your play with 11GB of VRAM used and with FPS in the high 80's/low 90's and end the session with quite near 15GB VRAM used and FPS in the mid 70's, quite a loss.Perhaps a lot of money for (again) a half baked game, but playable (and quite enjoyable so far), nonetheless.I will update my review at around 20hUpdate, stay away, or play it if you have X pass, the rest wait till it matures and be on sale. Fair price if full baked, stable and mature  50$/€, the actual price (70€) is a scam. I have tested the game in anothe rig, at 1440p using and RX6800XT with Epic quality, and the results are worst, for example in a closed environment (the Fire Station) the FPS jumps from 50 to 70 between the basement (the worst) and the lobby (the best) in no case the card can reach its max TDP, nor its percentage of use (ranging from 60% to 75%). The culprit? I don not know, could be the game that is clearly not optimized, could be AMD drivers, optimized for 7000 cards, could be DX12 or all of them. All in all a faulty and painful experience. For a comparison, with the same rig Cyberpunk 2077 1440p Ultra no RT no FSR, 80 FPS sustained, droping to 65/70 FPS on one of the more graphics demanding areas of the game, Lele Park - Chater Hill. Stay away of this game, for now.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay.Not great, or even good, but certainly not terrible.It has a lot of glaring issue. Textures don't load, AI bugs out, it gets very slow at times, and is lacking a lot of polish. It's embarrassing.But to say this game is awful, or one the worst games I've played, would be lying. The main texture that doesn't load is the pocket map (not the in-menu map), and that's only once every so often. AI problems only happen once every, say, 30 minutes. Even then, it's usually just a walk cycle not loading. The combat abilities of the AI are mediocre, but they still pose a challenge.I can run the game at 60 FPS with most of my settings on high with lag spikes only happening in very cluttered areas. And the lack of polish is in places that I don't really care about. Sure, cut-scenes *should* be animated, and chimneys *should* not be copy pasted on top of houses, but I'm not in desperate need of a mini-movie or wanting to inspect every house for flaws.I'm not here to defend these noticeable issues, but if these ruin the game for you, you're probably not here for actual gameplay.And the gameplay is fine. Not great or the most unique, but if you genuinely hate it, you should not be playing this genre of game.While I still cannot recommend this game due to it's price and issues, the amount of hate for what is present is mostly unwarranted.

On the other hand, being also a Dev, it hurts me to speak ill of the work of another, of which I know how difficult it is to do something like this.I'm going to be fair with the game without falling into the review bombing.The game is in a Beta state. It has performance and balancing issues that can only be achieved with player iteration and time.There is no matcking for coop op. Only by invitation you can play the multiplayer. The AI needs to polish its behavior. The stealth mode is pretty bad in its mechanics. The shotting is also poorly achieved. For an open world it feels a bit empty. The class builds are not very dynamic, to unlock the ultimate ability of a skill you have to have all of the above. They are 40 lvl max and getting to the top of a skill takes about 12 points.I think many things can be improved with time. For those of us who pay for the game without the game pass. It's not worth the price. If you have it for the game pass and you have nothing else to play, go ahead.I hope the game will improve but its current state does not show anything that motivates or helps me recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so bland and half thought out.  The missions are dull, all the weapons feel the same, the world is small, and the enemies are very stupid.  The story reminds me of Destiny 1 when it first came out.  You really have no idea who you are or why any of this is happening in the world.  The performance of the game is also terrible.  Stutters for days and inconsistent framerates the whole time.  Everything just feels so juvenile.  Not fully thought out and the "mechanics" were just thrown in.  But there are no quality mechanics.  "See enemy, click till dead."  Your "powers" are worthless.  Find a weapon that has the highest damage number and use it.I am still playing through it to at least get some of my money's worth, but honestly just don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I would Recommend to play this with a friend. Otherwise i wouldnt recommend it if you're going to solo. Ive seen a lot of downvotes from people with less than an hour of playtime. Also only 14% of players have finished the tutorial. This gives you a steam achievement and you can see how many other players got it. Now i understand if you dont have a great rig (cpu specifically) and you dont wanna suffer through 20fps. But then i also think its not enough to base a review on.Ive played the 18 hours with a friend of mine. and there are a few major things both positive an negative that id like to point out. StartPositive:* The world is really interesting to explore. Even though the story isnt that special. With fun collectibles that provide passive stats. * Different systems that are explained over the course of the first  location you play on (yes you go to a 2nd map) for instance:- the rarity of weapons determine what attachments could be on it. (but isnt guarenteed) so even the same weapon with the same rarity can have different attachments like a silencer on it.- The Rook. In the world, the vampire gods can get mad and this can get to a critical point, where they call on the Rook. This "boss-type" enemy isnt too hard to beat if you can focus him. He drops a guarenteed legendary weapon. But he's really bad if he is summoned when you're doing something else. * Really nice game for Dishonored fans. A lot of the artstyle is similair and the story telling mechanism is exactly the same, with still images of the involved characters with narration. Negative:* It isnt clear at the start, but the game gets an insane difficulty cliff once you get a little further into the 1st location. it seems like it is a tutorial area that isnt pointed out as tutorial. (i dont know this im just speculating) because many people played this game for like an hour and have decided the AI is ret*rded.* The AI can definitely get a difficulty increase. Even if i haven't played the highest difficulty yet.* The AI doesnt provide a big enough challenge to use your characters abilities. Especially at the start me and my buddy would forget we had skills we could use. Later this changed with the Vampire nests coming in.* The game still need a lot of work and sometimes the developers seem a little tone deaf to the situation of this game and its reviews, (for instance publishing a buzzfeed style "wich character in Redfall are you" quiz when people were begging for updates and improvements. TLDR:RECOMMEND?YES -> With friendsNO -> Solo

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.  I liked the Dishonored games and loved Prey, so I assumed I would get something along those lines and pre-ordered. Don't spend more than $15 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: My opinion of this game hasn't changed. It's disgusting that a  dollar company decided to close this studio over a bad game they didn't even want to make. These major companies worth ridiculous amounts of money are awful for closing studios on a whim. Instead of judging this game based on what it should have or should have been, I'm going to review it based on what is actually in the game. I bought this game on sale for about $17. I played the entire game solo. I would absolutely not recommend getting the bite back edition at this point. The new characters haven't been released and all you get are cosmetics. For the price it simply isn't worth it. Also, for just characters I still don't think it's worth it considering how shallow the characters feel that are already in the game. For about the first ten hours or so, I actually had a ton of fun with this game. The first area is pretty fun to run around and explore. The gun play is very satisfying. The slide you can do after a big sprint is also a lot of fun because you will slide an obscene distance. The events, missions and encounters are decent enough to be engaging and push the game forward. You can approach some of the missions in different ways such as distant and stealthy, tactical, or guns a blazing. I had a good time experimenting with different approaches to groups of enemies. The second area of the game is where things started to run thin. You'll realize at this point that there is very little variety in enemies. In this second area, the enemies are significantly spongier without offering anything significant to reward you for the effort in taking out a challenging enemy. Almost my entire time in the second area was spent avoiding combat as much as possible and when I was detected just running away. Bosses in this part of the game are equally as frustrating and not fun in the slightest to have to deal with. Regular enemies could take me out in a few hits, and to add insult to injury, the AOE of the regular vampire is so huge it is almost impossible to avoid. I can be so far back from a vampire that I could see their entire model and they'd swipe and I'd take 1/3 to 1/2 damage. Not to mention that at this point in the game my guns seemingly barely damaged the vampires unless I could land headshots. There's a money system in the game that makes little sense to me. Throughout the world you can find items to pick up that are worth an arbitrary value and you can accrue money. I primarily spent money on reviving after ridiculous deaths, buying ammo, and occasionally lockpicks. There are shops for guns and other things but they never offered anything actually valuable compared to what I would find out while exploring. I never found any significant use for money despite the game giving you tens of thousands of dollars easily. I only played as one character. Character's have special abilities that frankly I almost never used because I never saw much of a need for it. The skill tree isn't great. I maxed out the ammo and healing options right away. In my one playthrough I got to level 23 and there were still a lot of skills I had never accessed. There is a NG+ but frankly it would be hard to recommend one playthrough let alone a second. I nearly maxed out one of the skills and when I would remember to use it I never even noticed a difference between the beginning and upgraded versions of the skill. I'm not one to jump on a bandwagon and hate on something because it's the thing to do. I gave this game a fair shake. I do think it has some decently fun elements. The gun play is pretty fun. Exploring the environments was interesting because there is some decent environmental story telling. Some of the missions could also be pretty fun as well. What significantly brings this game down, though, is the lack of variety. There are only six weapon types and you're really only going to be using one or two of those once you find the ones you like. The difficulty spike feels unfair or poorly implemented. This is a very under baked product. The ingredients are certainly there for something that could have been quite good. Maybe they can patch this game up and make it a more enjoyable experience in the future? It's hard to say. We'll see. As it is this is technically a functional video game (even with some glitches here or there) but not one that's really worth the time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: It's depressing. I really see the potential for such a good co-op shooter in here, but it's bogged down with so many technical issues and unpolished elements. The characters are unique, the atmosphere is good, the controls are smooth (when not getting tagged with visual lag and screen shredding) and I love the city and map design, but the game itself feels like it was taken out of the oven before it had finished cooking. I put the blame on Bethesda for that one. This should have had another 6 months of fixing up and polishing before release, especially given the $70 price tag. This game could have been so much better than what we all got.May be worth it at a much cheaper price, and/or after the devs get the time to iron out all the technical issues and patch it up to be visually playable. A shame really. I was looking forward to this one for a while as I really want a good, new non-Borderlands co-op shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Redfall is bloody good (for $15)! Get it now while its on sale!Just to be clear, its not great, its not nearly as good as Prey, Wolfenstein etc, but its the most fun "post apocalyptic survival fps" Ive played, and at ~$15 its great value.Basically its an open world vampire/military first person action RPG. Guns feel pretty good to shoot, enemy AI is a bit dumb but its OK enough to have fun, you can scavenge a bunch of stuff - what more do people want?! (Oh wait, after playing a bit more, I have more on this later).Music is fine, as is the voice acting, character models, animation, etc - it would obviously be better if this was all outstanding, but oh well.It very much has an Arkane game feel (think Dishonoured2) - but not as good as their normal stuff.3 weapons to hotkey between isnt enough - 5 would be good, and 10 even better. Im using a keyboard Arkane!You cant return to areas after moving onto the next area? And There are gravelocks (secret-ish collectibles) to collect? Wow, that design decision sucks.PS - Im playing solo, but playing with some friends would be even more fun.I might be a complete dummy, but I dont know how to host a game with random people dropping in... this is a thing right? OMG, no its not. OK, so this is why Redfall flopped! Its a perfectly fine single player FPS action RPG (at a $15 price point), not as good as Arkanes previous games, but its OK. It requires an always online connection, and you cant pause the game which is obviously complete faeces. But thats because its not really supposed to be a single player game right, its supposed to be an open world action RPG version of left for dead. But There isnt the ability to team up with random ppl, you need to host a game, invite friends (friends only?!) then and there as there is no drop-in drop-out functionality - so as a multiplayer coop game its completely nerfed and has zero chance of being successful.  Arkane should work to add in 1/ the ability to team up with random people, and 2/ drop in, drop out, this is the critical functionality they need to have so this stands a chance of success (see Generation Zero for a comparison).Edit: I think Ive figured out what may make people think this game is jank, and thats the music in the fire station/hideouts - it is *complete* jank, this carefree piano and hip hop tune that says "you dont have a care in the world and everything is even kinda cool". It completely sets the wrong mood, and subconsciously contaminates the rest of the game. I dont recall hearing any good music yet either (and never ever discount how important music is for setting the feel of a game), so I will shortly turn off the music entirely, and listen to something which I think would suit better.Edit2: Im got to area 2, and ennui set in. Im bored. I dont think I'll continue this unless it becomes more fun to play. Could be more fun if they make it into a decent SP game. Could be more fun if it gets drop in MP. As it is, Ive had enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game and have already refunded it. Despite the already negative media surrounding the game I wanted to give it a shot. I did and here is why I don't like it.- $70? Why is this game even $70 in the first place- The opponent AI is horrible, it is not hard at all to avoid the AI. They just mindlessly chase you and can get stuck on stuff easily.- If you play Co-Op on another players save you do not progress individually and will have to start over (your level and gear is local, and will transfer, just not your game save)- The optimization is bad.- Not enough content, you can speedrun this game, especially if you avoid enemies. - The world is empty and meaningless. The only point of exploration is to find locked containers with gear. - This is basically borderlands with a smaller amount of content, side objectives, weapons, and features. Not worth $70. A healthy price for this game to include its current content with the promise that the future updates will fix the optimization, and AI issues would be $30. in my opinion. Vampires that are non-responsive and can't be killed, NCP sliding across the ground instead of walking, terrible AI on enemies, characters that don't interact except to say "Hi!", and many other annoying issues. I bought the game because I liked Arkane Studios previous games, but now will be more careful about buying them on the release date in the future. The game should have either been released as a lower cost alpha, or should not have been released until finished.The story is boring, almost absent, and there is no real interaction with the other characters. The so-called story is just narration over bad still images. Characters in the game just stand there and look at you and there is no sense of interaction. Most of the town is just an empty place with houses and stores that you can't enter. No throwable explosives or any other such things. Lots of glitches where the game just stops working and you can't complete the mission, forcing a restart. I am fairly certain that many people at Arkane were very upset with management that this game was going to be released at this price range when it was in this horrible a condition. I just hope these many negative reviews from Arkane fans will get the out-of -touch management at these game studios to stop doing this to their fans. I will never buy an Arkane game again without waiting for reviews to come out. That is what you have done to your fans, made them very skeptical of your honesty in marketing and releasing games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to say that I recommend this game to players for the dream that it represents, not because of what is here... and I will elaborate on that first.The Dream: Have you ever wanted to be a badass Vampire Hunter in a post-apocalyptic setting, gunning down hordes of Ghouls, Freaks, Vampires and the like? If that box is checked then this game is for you.However:And this is a strong one... due to the way the game is set up, I cannot recommend this for anyone who doesn't have an extreme hard-on for the idea of being a Vampire hunter... because of numerous bugs, one of the characters being basically useless (We'll get to this) and the game-progression/ general gameplay system being overly flawed (I will loosely explain this... but since its so new, y'know...)Numerous Bugs: So sometimes vampires will just not attack and not be attackable... sometimes certain numbers glitch out, the party system will sometimes not work and if you don't play in Borderless Windowed Mode then the screen will essentially ♥♥♥♥ up and you'll pretty much be screwed.Broken Character: So Layla, the Psychic doesn't really feel all that Psychic... her first ability only affects humanoids... because they're the only one's shooting bullets... her basic passive increase point literally makes food items more potent (you can't pick up food for later)... rather than do something exceptional, like get more lock-picks or get more money or have a bigger health stack... her second ability is literally a aerial traversal skill that is beat entirely by another team member's (Devander's Teleporter), leaving her ulti... which isn't even a psychic power, the only really useful skill in her tool-kit. In a game where people have invisibility, teleportation, explosives and robots, would it of killed the dev's to give the psychic girl actual psychic abilities rather than dollar-store green lantern powers and a Vampire Boyfriend? I'm just saying... some things in her kit need a SERIOUS rework because the others can ez solo while she's lagging due to lack of utility.Game Play/Progression: This is a serious one... Dev's, you better read this one CAREFULLY. It is 2023... we do not make a multiplayer game where a restart is required to play a specific section of a gameworld... fix it. Now. You are killing your fanbase before it begins... also, when you do fix it... and you know what I mean, since you put a literal ENDING in a multiplayer game... add some end-game content loop. Need inspiration? Look at skyrim, go play as an imperial and do nothing but collect rare gems, wealth and priceless artifacts and stick them in a chest... you will be BEYOND inspired to do some badass Vampire Hunter ♥♥♥♥. Just saying.Final Thoughts: What's here is fun... its great! But seriously... the things I listed, the negatives... they need to be addressed... and soon. I'm going to give this game the benefit of the doubt... I did pay 100$ for this game after all... but if things go sour, all I've got to say is that more love and care needed to go into making this game a more seamless and enjoyable game... because I also gifted it to someone for, yes, the same amount... I payed 200$ for this game with the hope and intention of it being good... so while I'll be patient and wait... I will seriously be considering how I spend my money in the future... as for the gameplay... don't finish the main quest till you get bored of the first area... and so on... You'll get a lot more hours out of the game. In fact, I haven't left the first area... and I've played every character in it, but friends of mine have and I'm none too happy about what they've told me the, "End-game experience," is...

If you have people to play with, or enjoy just solo stuff and shooting things, this is an "eh" kind of game. It's a game. It's fun to play a game. That's all this is. _childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: I was trying to finish the game but finally tapped out. There are progress gates that make you do all of the games side quests before you can start the final quest and the game suddenly refused to recognize my GPU on restarting the game so it was running the ENTIRE GAME off my CPU. I'm not burning out my PC to beat this dumpster fire of a game. I got it for free and still feel like I got scammed. Edit: made a Youtube short version for anyone that might want some visual proof of the jank (or a shorter version of this review): If I could summarize for people that don't like reading, just look up a gif of someone sighing and leave it looping for awhile. That was me the entire time I played this game.Seeing this happen to Redfall and Arkane is kinda like when I watched the Seahawks, my favorite team, throw the ball at the 1 yard line and get intercepted instead of running it and winning two consecutive superbowls in a row. Arkane has an *amazing* catalog of games, Prey 2017 was probably one of the most genuinely great games I have ever played, and yet here they are, pulling a Ubisoft and releasing an unfinished, half baked game that barely runs on solid hardware. To start with, if you have any interest in this game, I would NEVER tell you to go spoof an email to get gamepass for a dollar and play it there. That would be morally wrong, and you shouldn't do that instead of spending money here on steam ;)Lets get this out of the way at the top. I have an RTX 3070, 10700k and 32 gigs of ram. I should be able to run any functional modern AAA release at ultra settings with at least 60fps on 1080p no problem, and I normally do. I feel like my rig is fairly representative of what most people playing new AAA games are gonna have, and Redfall absolutely CHUGS. The main problem (a few people in my chat surmised) was my 3070 only has 8gb of VRAM, whereas everyone saying the game runs fine has a 3080 or newer which all have 16+ gb of VRAM, hence the game runs smoother. Performance is dogwater for me, and for a lot of other people, not because our hardware is lacking, but because this game isn't finished in a myriad of ways, the least of which being optimization. As an example, headbob detracts from frames because there isn't a headbob in the game, but there's a setting for it, so its a script running in the background calling for assets that aren't there lolEVEN IGNORING PERFORMANCEThe game is wholly and irrevocably half baked. I can't even try to name all of the issues I encountered, but to start, the AI is one of the worst I have seen in any game I've ever played. You can make an enemy into red mist and their patrol buddy right next to them won't react. They don't pay attention, they funnel down corridors, and thats just the human AI.The vampire AI are either far too lethal, or far too passive. I don't think the devs found the right middle ground with them and it feels like the hitboxes on their attacks are smoke and mirrors. The game decides when you get hit, and dodging around doesn't do much. I did manage to get one accidentally stuck on some garbage cans between me and them and they just sat there attacking the garbage until I killed them. Its *bad*The story is yet another part of this that might've been interesting but ends up being horrible. The town itself is actually pretty cool, but it feels empty and lifeless (not just because all the people in town are pretty much canonically in one building the vampires mysteriously won't attack).All of the cutscenes are these weird, in-engine still frames with voice acting over the top, and they have these unengaging missions where you watch ghosts of people talk, but the music is always too loud to hear them? Subtitles don't even help because enemy NPCs talk outside and it covers up the subtitles for the pseudo cutscene. Atrocious. Its also abrupt and incoherent. They do a whole lot of talking and yet still say nothing, the people praising the "lore" of Redfall are missing brain cells. I chose Layla for my hunter, and I am VERY annoyed with the writing staff for having a black lady as a main character and then deciding that her ultimate ability is to call up her ex boyfriend to fight for her. Seriously lol, her ultimate is calling her ex to come beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of people. You don't even meet him, he's just an ability. There's no storyline where you save him and maybe start to rekindle your romance, nothing. Just "I'm too weak, call my ex" and that sends a super lame message about an otherwise badass character. The gunplay ends up being a worse version of Destiny, the powers aren't very interesting and the upgrade trees are absurdly boring. "Ability does more damage, carry more ammo". You don't get any new abilities to pick from, its the same all game and they just hit a little harder over time. The game, even in singleplayer is "always online" so you cant actually pause it (or play without internet, I assume), and I got sent a code for the game + dlc from Arkane (I was surprised too) but let me tell you what you get for the DLC. 4 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ outfits, one for each character (the regular character design for Layla is better than all the unlockable outfits) a skin for your stake and a skin for your gun. The gun skin looks like rust, I put it on and genuinely thought it just made my gun rusty. You also get 2 DLC characters down the road :) You know, after you've beaten the game and don't care to play anymore? ALL OF THAT COSTS 30 DOLLARSCharging 70 bucks for this mess is already a crime against humanity, and maybe the beginning of the end for Arkane.We're seeing a lot of the legacy-once great dev teams fall, and this feels like another. I have a feeling that Microsoft acquiring Bethesda and therefore Arkane has something to do with this being put out OBVIOUSLY not finished, so don't jump at the devs just yet, but absolutely don't buy this game. I'm gonna finish it tomorrow and will update if there's anything new, twitch link in my steam profile if anyone would rather watch someone else play it than buy it themselves, but I'm not expecting anything to improve. I was surprised to see there was at least one more section of map (so Redfall is just the starting area), but I'm only expecting 3 total zones at most.Seriously disappointed in this. One of the biggest wastes of potential and quickest falls from grace I've ever seen.

_childDocuments_.review: ...It's not good. I'm glad I didn't pay for this. In fact, it's really bad.I definitely wanted this game to be good. The premise is great, a vampire hunting game with 4-player co-op and an open world created by Arkane (Dishonored, Deathloop) so I thought: Count me in.However, the launch is HORRIBLE. I tried to ignore the IGN reviews of the gameplay being shoddy. Optimization is horrible. I have decent hardware (3070 RTX, 9900K overclocked to 5.0 GHz) and I had to fine tune the settings to see 60 FPS, and even then it's very unstable - you can tell the game is loading enemies because of the hard stutters I experience.The gameplay is NOT smooth. Playing this game with a controller and even M/KB is crap, aiming and fine tuning your crosshair is not existent. In order to get better feedback, you have to use a higher sensitivity with the input speed set to low. Why isn't this the default?There aren't any cutscenes in the game either. Everything is a slideshow with dialogue. Hell, there's not a single interactive NPC in the game. For $70 in 2023? No.This game is NOT finished. It had potential but I do not see them bouncing back from this one - will probably take more than a year to get this game to a finished state, and that's being optimistic.

I really had some insane situations happening to me, from stupid death after having barely survived and close to my goal, having to run for my life after a situation escalated with some vampires in an abandoned railroad track surrounded by kinda cliffs, so no way around but trapped on a straight line, finally escaping this too much closed area, fleeing through the bushes to cross a main road, attracting various factions to the dance, and survived with a lot of sweat.In higher difficulties, enemies track you way way longer, that's really a manhunt sometimes; I've just (10 mins ago) been followed from a main road to a dried sea zone pretty far away, and as I felt safe down there by the rocks but decided to lounge them, and I did well because a lot of guys did follow me to the edge of the rocks, but didn't penetrate the dried sea, as 3 vampires were already killing some cultist there.The thing also is that night is way more dangerous than "day" because vampires activity is way higher, almost no sleeping ones or hiding by the environment shadows, they can roam more freely, and altogether with packs of allies (cultists).So moving at night feels a lot different than by daylight, also a really interesting contrast and change in gameplay. There's actually a lot of subtilities to discover, things have been thought pretty deeply.What is cool is that there are some interactions within the world between vampires, cultits and another corporation, so when you move forward in the game, the world actually feels more alive as they fight each others, lots of random events...I started on Dawn difficulty and moved to nightmare just to get feelings back from the very beginning, when you're poorly armed and every single threat is dangerous, and believe me, a lot can happen and it can turn surprising pretty quick.There's also a lot of verticality, you can access almost all rooftops, there's pretty much always a way to climb up to take advantage of being above things, even if you play Jacob, who can't "teleport" himself or throw himself in the air like Devinder .

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. Gameplay is nothing spectacular, storyline is absolutely standard, NPC are not interesting, weapons are generic.I was awaiting this game because I'm easy to please when it comes to vampire games, and had planned to play it with a friend. While I had fun with my friend, this is not really difficult : having fun when playing coop is dumb easy, as long as there is a vague gameplay.Still, the fun I had killing enemies with terrible AI doesn't make the flaws of the game less apparent. But the real shame is that it could have been so much better. There are ideas beneath the pile of blandness. The bits in "memories" have interesting visuals, for instance, that hint at environments that could have been spectacular to play through. Some skills are somewhat amusing to use.But... this just doesn't come close to being enough. Also, the storytelling is terrible : why so much text, in my fast action-paced shooter ? Who's got time to read tons of diary entries or letters ? Why do the memories kill the pace so much too ?The enemies : not very varied. Four or five types of vampires, and cultists that all act the same (shoot you), and they take a crazy long time to react to having you in front of them.We played in highest difficulty and took less than 12 hours to finish, while doing all the side quests we found on our way and liberating all safehouses we found.All the time I found myself comparing this game with another, far superior "Coop FPS with set characters and quests" : Borderlands. And Borderlands is better in all regards :- Fun, varied weapons- Varied builds- Amusing quests- Entertaining dialogs- Broad type of enemiesThis is not worth 70€. I had much higher expectations of Arkane and it's a shame they delivered this.If you want to play a coop shooter, just buy Borderlands instead.

_childDocuments_.review: At time of writing this i have just over 10 hours on the game. i played this game when it first came out, i was hyped for it and was excited to play... but it was actual dog water. i payed 70$ for it and returned it after only around 30 min, as it was unplayable with frame rate issues and lagging while playing co-op. I was very disappointed, the game felt empty and just not finished. I saw that update 2 came out and wanted to give it a try to see if it was savable so I got it on sale... and I will tell you, this game is actually pretty fun now. I'm about half way done the game going for 100% and enjoying it quite a bit. Don't get me wrong the game still has issues but it is definitely much better and shouldn't get so much hate. Need to do with game:Fix ai still - When sniping ai they stand around when one of them have been shot, they need to become more alert, actively take cover and search for you better.Vampire nests - These are fine and all but they should be limited and not respawn as you destroy them, maybe keep one somewhere on the map after completing them all for replayability. Also why not throw a achievement in there for taking them all out.Vampire combat - Vampires definitely feel much stronger then your normal enemy but sometimes they are just boring, they run at you, swing, sometimes teleport away, and repeat. definitely could use some improvements.Weapons - There's definitely a lack of weapon variety with limited customization. modifying attachments, a gun store, etc, would be niceInventory - This isn't all to bad but an ability to lock some of your weapons so you don't get them mixed up with all the guns you just looted would help, there's times I scraped the wrong gun just to find out it was my best gun.Skills - Skills are pretty decent with neat ability's but the leveling system feels slow, I'm level 13 after completing half the game and still need so many skill points. a few more skills would also be nice. like carrying capacity for med kits and even inventory space for guns.Safe-houses - These are lacking heavily, run past enemy's, turn on a generator, repeat. a more outpost feel would be nice with them enclosed with walls or something. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game. And now ive used it as a learning experience to wait for reviews. This game is a dissapointing mess, and honestly, i don't think any amount of updates could save it. This isn't just an undercooked game with a blatant lack of polish, this feels like a concept more than an actual game. All the pieces are in the game that couldve made it good, but it doesnt do ANY of them well. STORY:The story is incoherent at best and non-existent at worst. The most part of a story you can actually get is through notes and collectibles. The main missions are literally "go here, grab thing because we told you too, maybe kill a thing, and report back." There are few exceptions, but those are found in boss fights. I haven't completed the game to see the rest, and honestly, i dont think I can push myself to complete it. I know the game itself is short. You can complete everything in 12 hours. And some things are brought into the game that just dont make sense. Theres a third type of enemy thats like a private security, and it is never TRULY explained what their purpose is. Like at all. They exist, JUST to exist. And they play the EXACT same way as the cultists. In the notes, there is a DECENT story. But it is never given proper showing. There arent even actual cutscenes in the game. Not one single, actual cutscene in this game. Just models frozen in settings while the characters monologue over them. GAMEPLAY:Couldve been good. As i said, all the pieces are there, the just do NOT work. Its a generic shooter that doesnt reinvent any wheels. The loot system is NOT rewarding. You can find the highest tier gear with a 30% damage buff and use that for most of the game straight from the jump. The abilities are laughably bland. I found myself not using them, ever. And the skill tree is beyond pointless. It doesnt change things to cater to a playstyle, or do anything interesting. None of them do. Granted, i only played one character, but you only need to play one to see how little thought went into it. The AI is some of the worst ive seen in a AAA title. You kill an enemy right next to another one and half the time theyre not even aware of it. Constantly running into walls or standing in front of whatever theyre shooting only to get obliterated. As for the vampires, the main focus of the game, once youve fought one, its the exact same fight. Over, and over, and over. There are a few "specials." and by specials, i mean they do one thing differently, or just have more health. They basically just rush you. In groups, its a little challenging. But more annoying than it is engaging. The CORE element of their game, feels like a chore to deal with rather than a rewarding aspect. And most times you can just avoid them. Just run through everything. Its insane. I finished one boss fight, and it isnt even that good. Nothing rewarding about it. I have nothing to say on this end. It was just BORING. I imagine all boss fights feel the exact same. There is weapon variety, but it doesnt matter. All weapons feel the same. OPEN WORLD:This is probably the worst out of all the things in this game. The open world is not only relatively small, it is EMPTY. Sure, enemies are fairly placed around, but when every fight feels the same, it doesnt matter. The loot system isnt rewarding enough to care after awhile. If you were expecting to try and search for specific chests that contain great loot, well i hate to tell you, that isnt the case. The "looter shooter" aspect of the game is as bare bones as it gets. There is nothing in this map. Aside from side missions, like "vampire nests." which are very short dungeons with maybe 5 enemies in it that are supposed to give you higher tier items, but again, when every weapon feels the exact same, it really doesnt mattter. No weapon has anything interesting going for it. Even the Highest tier weapons. They just look different. ATMOSPHERE:This is probably the only thing the game does well in. Its creepy. The music is actually pretty good. The setting and set pieces feel like a stephen king novel. And the core of Arkane with enviornmental storytelling is definitely there. If this game took a direction that Arkane was naturally good at, it could have been a decent game, and it shows. MULTIPLAYER:No matchmaking. Havent played with anyone but ive heard its constantly bugged. They advertised it as a 4 player co op and didnt even bother to cater to that. If you cant make it accessible and easy to play with others, then why do it?PERFORMANCE:AI, as I said, is atrocious. It doesnt make the game fun. You can steamroll through almost everything. Stuttering is not CONSTANT, but it is frequent. FPS drops in almost every area with multiple buildings or enemies. There is a significant lack of polish in this game. It actually makes me question if this product was actually rushed or they just gave up.Textures take awhile to load in, graphic bugs are frequent. It just does not feel polished.GRAPHICS:Not terrible, but for a AAA in 2023, could be better. This studio has other games that came out YEARS ago that look better. Prey, and Dishonored 2 GENUINELY look better than this game. Not to say its terrible, but for those of you that care. OVERALL:Again, i really wanted to like this game. and I pushed myself to try and complete it before making this, but honestly, it came to a point where I was pushing myself so hard I wasnt having any amount of fun. The first mission feels decent. They tell you to play your way when finishing the first mission, but there is no REAL way to play. The lack of choice at all is masked by the "open world" aspect of the game. Arkane has made absolute BANGERS in the past, and i genuinely cant see how they thought this game was anywhere near ready to come out. Even if they patch it over time and fix things like the framerate, the AI, maybe difficulty scaling, change the perk system, that doesnt fix the main problem with this game. The game has no identity. It has a bunch of elements thrown into it to cater to as wide of an audience as possible and does none of them well. I truly dont believe Arkane is to blame. I think Microsoft made them create the game in the safest way possible, at the risk of the studio itself to make as much money as possible before people realize how unfinished this game is. Ill say it again and again, this game isnt a finished product, it feels more like a CONCEPT of a game.Rating: 3/10 Bad game, bad time, sad time.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall, the latest release from Bethesda, is a game that falls far short of the expectations set by its predecessors. While the premise of a vampire-infested open world had great potential, the execution leaves much to be desired. It's evident that the once-revered Bethesda company is struggling to maintain its reputation for delivering high-quality gaming experiences.One of the major shortcomings of Redfall is the technical aspect. Glitches, bugs, and performance issues plague the game, detracting from any sense of immersion. It's disheartening to see a title released with such blatant technical deficiencies, and it reflects poorly on Bethesda's commitment to delivering polished products.The narrative, another cornerstone of Bethesda's games, lacks the depth and complexity that fans have come to expect. Redfall's storyline feels uninspired, failing to captivate players with the engaging storytelling that made previous Bethesda titles memorable. The characters are forgettable, and their interactions lack the emotional resonance that could have elevated the overall experience.One redeeming aspect of Redfall is the visual design. The game showcases a visually appealing world, with well-crafted environments and atmospheric lighting. However, even this positive element is marred by the subpar animations and character models, further emphasizing the lack of attention to detail in the game's development.The most disheartening aspect of Redfall is the apparent mishandling of Arkane Studios, a once highly-regarded developer. It's clear that the studio's creative prowess is being stifled, and their potential is not fully realized in this title. The lack of innovation and the recycling of gameplay mechanics from previous games indicate a stagnation in Arkane's ability to push boundaries and deliver fresh experiences.In conclusion, Redfall is a lackluster addition to Bethesda's portfolio, showcasing a company that seems to be losing its touch. The issues plaguing the game, from technical problems to uninspired storytelling, underscore the need for a reevaluation of Bethesda's development processes. It's disheartening to witness the decline of Arkane Studios under the Bethesda umbrella, leaving fans longing for the days when both entities were synonymous with groundbreaking and captivating gaming experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: The story was a cool concept, but unfortunately its poor execution leaves Redfall as a wasted opportunity. Bloated with unnecessary open world features Redfall would perform better with a more linear approach. Blood sucking vampires won't be the only horrors you will be encountering in Redfall bugs and glitches are ever present in the game if the characters aren't T-posing they're running on the spot stuck in rocks and objects. Redfall is like the first draft of an essay from a first year uni student. Theres good concepts and ideas to evolve the co-op shooter genre with unpredictable vampires in combat, but this alone cannot carry the many problems with this game.Costing over £50 Redfall will leave you with buyers remorse, and contemplating on how we got to this point in the video game industry. Just go play Left for Dead 2 or Dead Island 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game for free."I'm getting stretched out," moans my character as I walk towards a cultist, firing my gun. He doesn't realise I'm there - he's got question marks over his head and he's looking directly at me, but no one around him retaliates. The AI is less responsive than my grandma before we pulled the plug (don't worry, she was brain dead and electricity ain't cheap in this economy.)I've got special abilities - I don't  need any of them on the hardest difficulty.I stand beneath a giant, frozen-in time tidal-wave: there's something off, though...The shadows make no sense, shadows are cast on objects that aren't consistent with their position to the light sources.A vampire tells me I'll never see the sun again as we stand in a sunny street.My friend doesn't walk, and neither do I: most of the time we simply *slide* when we're not half in the ground. Redfall thought it had a problem with Vampires, but it's really the gun-toting psychic mole people.I return to my special Firehouse to find the NPCs all T-posing. Often, there are duplicates of them. The priest - who I think is a man every time I look at her - has a clone. This clone has ascended to Godhood: her head IS a light source.There's a story. The kind've story where a greasy, slick corporate representative walks up to you with a skateboard and their hat on backwards and says "Hello, fellow kids," or Hillary Clinton tries to convince you she's not a bearded-dragon wearing a human-suit by telling you cute anecdotes about how she has hot sauce in her purse.There are games with this same formula more than a decade old, with a lesser budget, that work better than this game. Everything feels wrong: the walking, the gun play, the vertical tool tips that take up a quarter or more of your screen in combat and require you to hold a key for several seconds to dismiss them. It's almost like Redfall got very cursory play testing. I can't blame Bethesda though: Fallout 76 ended up being successful, so why wouldn't this? Why bother releasing games in finished states when you can just push them out like an unripened turd and still have people buy it. Thank God Phil Spencer apologised for the state of this game, because that really makes up for this being pushed out. Someone cue up the clip of the BP Oil CEO saying "I'm sorry" that South Park did a few years ago.The only thing Redfall got right is that it has an "uninstall", but you could argue it's deadliest flaw is letting you install it to begin with.Some additional research has revealed that the Austin Branch of Arkane Studio is looking for an entire team of people to develop a game. Probably the one they just released.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point, I bought this knowing It was too good to be true. So many advertisements and CGI trailers for marketing leading up to a pretty disappointing gameplay experience.AI Is pretty busted, a lot of the time the vampires can't even get down from house roofs. Close combat feels super clunky because there's no "dodge" button In the game, so you're stuck running In a circle around the enemies waiting for them to take a swing and miss to then continue attacking.Optimization Is just non-existent, like I cannot believe this got the green light atleast for the PC version.Textures pop In and out. Now this Is something that gets on my nerves really quick In games, If you got textures popping In and out because you tried limiting the stress on peoples computers by not rendering things a set distance away from the player that's all fine. Lots of big games stop rendering things that the player can't see anyways, but we got an Issue when you're not rendering things the player CAN see and STILL lag optimization. It's just a disaster honestly.Gunplay Is fine.The Eagle dude Is semi okay too, that's the only one I've played so far.Skill tree Is fine, no Issues there. Map Is terrible, I get the artstyle they went for that's fine and all. But the map could reaaally use some love on the Information side, It feels way too bland and just empty. Settings could use some looking too. Why does controls under settings not an an option to scale the ADS sensitivity?. Game has no fps limiter besides Vsync.Loot that you can find In the world has NO Indicator whether It can be picked up or not until you mouse over It, this means you have to mouse over everything to find out whether It can be picked up a not. Looking at the artstyle I think It'd have been perfect to have a small white'ish border around Items that's Interactable, this would save so much time and headache. Overall for the 70/90$ I gave for this game I would have guessed a lot of the above would have been the most basic things to have In check before release, I cannot recommend the game at all In Its current state. It has a LOT of fixing to do, I'll be finishing the whole game and side stuff and then most likely update this review with further things that could use some work etc If any but that's about It for now.an overall 2/10 score from me, gunplay Is the sole thing keeping me bare minimum Interested atleast until I've gotten my moneys worth In playtime. Take care everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Redfall with little expectations, aside from it seeming like Borderlands with vampires and I was not far off. My main confusion was with the campaign and how it would progress or keep me interested being isolated to a town map. It does a decent job at keeping you on task as you roam across the city and recapture safehouses that each have their own area questlines. You fight a boss for each area after doing enough quests and pick up side quests along the way. The gameplay itself feels surprisingly good, each character has branching skill trees and you're constantly changing out loot for better stats or rarities. The map is littered with loot and guarded treasure, while most houses or buildings require lockpicking or hacking to enter, along with tripmines, safes, and alarms to disarm or loot. I was worried about the difficulty being too easy, but there are four modes to choose from and it's giving me a run for my money on solo hard mode. There are also lots of cosmetics to unlock just by completing quests and challenges.My biggest gripe is that the co op was not thought out at all. Hosting a game is invite from friend's list only, which means you'll likely be playing solo unless you have friends to play with. It's annoyingly difficult to play co op at all otherwise. They need to get public servers and allow public hosting if they want co op to happen.Overall I wouldn't jump on the hate bandwagon just yet, Redfall has potential. If you aren't bothered by pretentious FPS gripes and you enjoy looter shooters then you should pick it up, it's actually a solid game with decent challenge and detail put into it. The more you look around the more you seem to find.(Since the developers have been unable to deliver on key features involved with the genre like multiplayer matchmaking, I can't leave a positive review so I'm changing this to negative. There WAS potential here if you focused in the right areas, but you've proven that you could not deliver. We haven't even seen the two additional characters promised at launch and I would get a refund if I could. Redfall is a crippled experience from what it could have been.)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been reading the reviews of Day One release and I have to say... I don't know what anyone is talking about. I haven't had ANY graphics issues, and so what if its not super-realistic on the level of Cyberpunk? I love the artstyle being used, perhaps not what folks would expect for a vampire horror shooter. Some people say the graphics are "old" and choppy, but I've yet to have glitches or anything of that sort.So sorry that AI isn't overtuned to one-shot players who have spent half their lives in COD doing flick-shots and PvP. Starting the game, I had a sense of immediate dread when enemies were 100ft from the opening scene and gave me cause to stealth around instead of just going in guns-blazing. Not that one style of gameplay is better than another, as it all comes down to personal preference. If your preference is Destiny'ing your way through waves of enemies until you happen to die and expect to just keep bashing your head against a wall until you win, this might not be the game for you. Maybe try to enjoy the game for what it is and not compare it to other games that it isn't?The negativity I'm seeing is, frankly, baffling. Is it a perfect game? There's no such thing. Is it broken on Day One? Not that I see. Everyone is entitled to their own opinion and this is mine; Enjoy the game or don't, but don't let reviews guide your hand and avoid this one, play it for yourself and be your own judge of what this is. Every experience in a game is going to be different for each person playing it. I am enjoying what I've played, so far, of Redfall and I hope the experience gets better with time.
