_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to write this review as a big fan of Arkane games.To put it simply, the game just isn't fun. I didn't hate it, but I couldn't bring myself to like it either.Gunplay is fine, and I didn't have technical issues.My opinion of the game started to drop right after clearing the first base you get. The transition from freeing this building with survivors to it suddenly being a safe haven and immediately apart of some little community you run errands for was really jarring to me on a story standpoint.You then accept your next quest from a mission board instead of narrative storytelling, further plummeting my current low opinion of the story thus far. Going to the quest location felt very bare and bland. The scenery and setting was nice, but I couldn't find any excitement. The enemies are bad. The humans with guns had horrible AI and the vampires were chumps with easily avoidable attacks. I was playing on the hardest difficulty I could and I felt no danger.I encountered a few minor bugs, like shooting a still enemy and the bullet not hitting them. I was disappointed to find a major lack of different and in depth character abilities to pick and choose from like previous Arkane games, instead left with a few very lackluster skills with plain skill trees. I didn't bother with the multiplayer, heard it was broken anyway. Very disappointed in the game, maybe I'll revisit it in the future after some updates and heavy sales. The game is in no way worth $70 and I'm requesting a refund. Save the money and go play Dishonored or Prey if you haven't.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Arkane games and I actually enjoyed the game...until it started non-stop crashing. After about 8hrs of no problems in two days, it started crashing with UE4 errors and within an hour I lost count of times it crashed.I tried disabling steam overlay, and every third-party tool in system tray, verified game files, I know I have the latest nVidia 4090 drivers, 24GB VRAM etc. Basically no apparent reason for it to crash but it kept going and took the joy out of the game. When the game crashes, you lose not only time, but also progress and loot. For example, I cleared a vampire nest, got out and got the rewards a min later game crashed and all were lost. Nest did not show up in the map either.Update: I really wanted to finish the game but it is still crashing. I considered uninstall / reinstall, which had helped a bit with recent Star Wars. I reset all settings in case I may have changed something that was causing this (for example, I had increased FoV a bit). I actually thought it got better, but was probably placebo, it still crashes randomly, sometimes fine for 2-3hrs, other times crashes 5mins apart. Still no clue what the UE4 error is about, nothing on google. OK, will stop talking about crashes, although it is hard to ignore it. Gunplay .. OK, though I don't like the choices much.  Aim down-side is not great, view blocked most of the time, especially with pistols (yet how I loved healing from "Painkiller"). Each level almost obsoletes the previous lvl guns, so constantly trying to get back favs. A few combos are  sometimes OP (UV + saw).Loot ... kinda annoying that in the second half I got greens and blues from most, rook was the only guaranteed way to get legendary.Story / Quests .. OKGameplay in general ... Fine, I would rate this 3.5/5 if it was not crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was 12 years too late...and I'm here for it. The gameplay reminds me of older shooters like the original RAGE, Aliens: CM, Borderlands 2, etc. Let me be clear; this game is an AA title, and shame on Xbox for marketing it otherwise. Overall, I enjoy the atmosphere and the way combat feels. The moment to moment gameplay is simple and entertaining. Redfall's gunplay feels just like Deathloop and can get intense. Also, the sound design is decent, the weapons sound nice, and the music is very unique. I've played this on the Steam Deck (which is why my hours are so low) as well as the Legion Go (the Xbox PC version where I have 20+ hours clocked) and I have to say that the game performs very well. It's probably one of the best performing games in my library (both on the Steam Deck and Xbox PC).If you're into older FPS titles from the PS3/Xbox 360 era, then chances are you'll probably enjoy Redfall. The story is intriguing enough to pay attention to and the ""cutscenes"" are literal slideshows, but what really makes Redfall enjoyable for me is the actual gameplay (as simple as it is) and the feel of combat. Swapping weapons depending on the enemy type and dwindling a vampire's health to eventually stake them in the heart never gets old.

I feel the next game will be very good but till then, wait for updates and you know ... don't expect too much.other problems I have with this? leveling feels ... lengthy. there are a lot of nice upgrades for your characters but it takes a while to get the exp. for it. if you did nothing but quests then maybe, but I am very explorative, and I feel I should get more exp. out of searching around and doing a good chunk of the side stuff.characters? great. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game for free and I still feel ripped off.The game runs Okay if you have literally some of the best hardware money can buy, but even then it is dire.Yeah the framerate and frametimes were fine... but everything else just feels so unpolished and bad.I got through the tutorial mission and just had to stop because it was giving me a headache.I was playing on ultra, had a solid 120 FPS as 2k with DLAA, but also tried just native (native was worse looking).Ultra shadows... shadows are pixely and crusty.Ultra textures... they're fine.I didn't have any of the stuttering others have had... but the game just feels unpolished and janky.The models and the animations are ugly as sin.. even for the stylized stuff Arkane goes for, which I typically adore.The character models look like souless copies of borderlands characters after squeezing their heads in a vice.And the biggest, most headache causing issue by several miles.LOD pop in.It is AWFUL.Especially with bits of set dressing in the fire station, good lord.You can be about 20 feet away and it pops between some terrible LOD that has missing faces (the windows were the worst) to the full detail when you take one step closer.This is in a room that has hardly any items in it, just a corner with a shelf and 2 windows.Why in whatever gods you may pray too would this happen to this degree on ULTRA SETTINGSI had to stop playing due to that alone because it made me want to vomit. I have never had this issue before, it legitimately made me feel nauseous.Next is the animations.The character animations especially are just Bad.Some of the worst I have ever seen. Its like freaking five nights at freddies animatronics up in here.Enemies snap from animation to animation with no perceivable smoothing between each one, they go from running and holding a gun in both hands to aiming with no frames of animation in between, arms snapping from bent downwards to forward in a microsecond.There are clipping issues galore, I know its an open world game but if I can casually wander around the opening area of the game and see props clipped into each other, floating, or half in a wall... you need to do better. That just shows how much the poor folks who had to try to make this were rushed.This game could have easily spent another 6 to 8 months in the oven.Give your devs more time to actually finish products jesus christ.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to get it out of the way, I give this game a 4/10 with a friend but a 3/10 for single player. Me and my friend bought xbox game past for $10 to play this game and give it a try instead of wasting $70 on this piece of crap. In our 9 hours of game play we both realize how bad this game is, without a friend I don't even think I can play past an hour. Don't even think about playing with randoms because there is no public matchmaking, yeah...$70 game. Here are the reasons why this game is good and bad(mostly bad).Pros:-Some variety of enemies, some vampires look pretty cool and have unique abilities-Lots of content and places to explore and things to do so you don't always feel like there's nothing to do-Environments/atmosphere can be pretty good at times especially when you head into these areas where it would shape shift and morph the environment as you play. Cons:-The biggest Issue....AI! Ai is so bad in this game that you can say its nonexistent in this game. You can literally run around the entire world and punch these guys to death with just your fist if you want without using a gun because that's what me and my friend did. You can even go full fist against these mini bosses they have around the world. The Ai is so bad it makes the difficulty setting pointless because of how dumb they are. They can't shoot at anything even with highest difficulty setting, you can get so close you can lick their ear and they would turn around saying.."whats that." They would run at you backwards and would literally sometimes never know whats going around them until you hit them. -This cost $70-With $70 you will get no cutscenes with animations because almost all of it is just still images with your character narrating the story so you will feel no connection to the story and characters itself. Even during an investigation where you watch the memories of these characters reenacting their tragic moment, were just still frames with no animations or movement-No public matchmaking, unless you have a buddy that's willing to spend $70(or $10 for xbox game pass) you're on your own- Gameplay is clunky and doesn't help that the game is unoptimized with frame drops at times. -Shooting feels awful, there are roblox games with better shooting than this game. Pistols can't hit target at times and feels like crap to shoot, almost all shotguns feel sluggish and they all feel and handle the same. Assault rifles are the best weapon in the game currently. Sniper rifles are alright but don't ever bother trying to use them on vampires, you won't hit crap-The characters and their skills doesn't feel that impactful to the gameplay, they can remove the skills these characters have and you will still get the same experience. Sometimes you even forget to use them-Because Ai are so brain dead this game is very easy even on hardest difficulty, like I said you can just run around and punch people and vampires if you want. When me and my friend got to the second area for some reason everything was easier to kill despite being on the hardest difficulty setting, might be a bug who knows.-The open world feels very bland, its as wide as a lake but deep as a puddle. There are enemy zones to conquer but their usually guarded by only 4-7 guys and almost always die to one shot, even on hard its not a challenge. -The side characters are terrible, they can be removed from the game and nothing will change. Nothing note worthy about any of them. You can try and talk to them but mostly all of them will either have only one line, cough at you, just a "hmm", or nothing at all. In conclusion, save your $70 its not worth it at all. They ask for more but deliver less, I wouldn't be surprise if most of these positive reviews are payed for.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is a blast but a flawed one at that. A bit of a looter shooter shoved into a well crafted world ripe for exploration, both narrative and mechanical. The art team did a great job really bringing locations to life and the sfx and music work ties in to create this wonderfully pulpy setting. Currently playing solo but I am deeply enjoying the writing for Devin, the Cryptid hunter, it's smart and witty with just the right amount of b movie cheese. There is quite a bit of jank with the AI that is undoubtedly holding back the combat which otherwise has some serious potential. Ex. As I pushed to the main theater I decided to deploy my relocator to a nearby roof. I then engaged with my shock staff and took out the first 2 of 5 targets. Popped my re locator and from the rooftop used my sniper rifle to take out the remaining targets, two of which I killed by shooting an nearby explosive barrel. Problem is the AI mostly just stand about as I pick them off even on Nightmare difficulty and while the Vamps have some interesting attacks and powers they get stuck on doorways, walls and generally struggle to be a threat as consistently as they should.The game is also lacking as a pc port and I would also love to see some additional options here on PC for stuff like ADS sensitivity and HUD elements. All in all it feels like an ambitious project that didn't quite come together but I am nonetheless having fun with. If I had to give it a score now I would say a 6/10 and if Arkane can fix up the AI and port issues that would quickly become a 7/10. Not a flawless gem but a fun romp with plenty of those classic Arkane set pieces through a wonderfully atmospheric setting.It's likely to be a discounted pickup for most folks but if you can wrangle together even just one other friend to play in co-op when that faithful bargain bin pickup day comes you'll hopefully find a slightly more polished game, several patches in and you'll def get some fun out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game. 20+ hours spent figuring this game out. Here is an honest review after trying almost everything. This review is from a  SOLO experience. Cons-Lack of Story depth, its what we seen hundreds of times with zombie horror games all they did was replaced the monster. They going throw in some sob BS side quest. Evil megacorp made monsters. -The human AI isn't just bad, its corrupted and broken They try to take cover, rush you or sneak up on you but they don't have terrain awareness. They are constantly running into walls and tripping over boxes. Now they do significant damage when they do hit you. Killing you in 2-5 shots on normal difficulty( Dust). Vampires have similar AI problems but not as bad. - Character builds are uninspiring, and don't exist. All you do is max your main damage skill to bypass the STAKE mechanic. They don't make your character feel  or play any different. It all comes down to how many bullets you have and whats the best gun you can find. -Loot, I've only seen 6 guns repeated out of the 10 times killing the Rook( loot boss that always grants a legendary). They say vampire nest are best way to get loot but farming specials to get the Rook to spawn is far more rewarding. Legendaries spawn inside the safehouse if you refresh or keep buying and selling items. Had 3 back to back legendary items from just spending cash at the base.-Boss fights, Outside of the first boss the fights are not difficult with minor gimmicks.- Only 6 vampire variations. Exploder, basic, invisible, one that drains you, grappler, Shielded, and the Rook that calls down lighting strikes. Few will experience shielded or the Rook.No public matchmaking. Game that promotes co-op but doesn't allow you to pair up with randoms? Yeah some people can be horrid at the game but the point is share your experience with another person. Only the host saves story progression. Whats the point of playing together if you have to wait for the one Host friend to be on to continue gaining progress? Pros ( not many)- Gun play feels good but it lacks some features to make it better. Guns vary, same model have different attachments, bonuses etc.-Legendary loot looks and feels good to use- Abilities at least on the character Dev feel very powerful and useful- many ways to approach a fight, enter a building Verdict. No! Not even for Bethesda. We won't tolerate a buggy mess for $70. Studio that made Dishonored, Copy and pasted ideas from Dishonored. What this game plays like, Dead Island, not the new one but the decade old one that came out over 10 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I received a review copy without seeing any of the game's promotional materials, so I went in with no expectations at all.There's a good concept at the core, especially surrounding the day/night cycle...but then the vampires just stroll around in broad daylight after the second morning? I couldn't figure out if that was a glitch or not, but it certainly killed any sense of tension and pacing that could've been created there.Many things felt unfinished (the first wave of cultists attacked me by running backwards while i was standing in the open, yelling about how they'd find me - that bug was worth the download size on its own), the AI pathfinding needs serious work (the vampires can fly and teleport, so if im standing on a ledge they cant reach, maybe they could just throw something at the player while hovering there? currently they just kinda freak out, run in circles, then go full-on "it must have been the wind"), the gunplay is seriously lacking feedback and the enemies don't flinch from most hits short of a point blank shotgun, melee is an afterthought, and performance/optimization is abysmally uneven. the option to play with locked framerate (other than just vsync) would have been nice, too, since that tends to work a bit better with streaming clients like OBS.I'll be revisiting this game once it gets a patch or two, but I simply can't recommend it in its current state.

The setting, the location... reminds me of The Secret World's first location. Sea side east coast stuff with utterly ruined residence with personality, the setting is awesome. The vampires are really creepy and you can hear them whispering and sneaking about, the solo playing and team plate are completely different experiences and it takes a while to really get used to the game. My friend and I have gotten jumped by too many vampires at once and died many a time and it was pretty fun because eventually we started -not- dying against them. And again, the location, the scenery, the graphics (Doctor Venture's voice actor snuck in there kind of surprised me and.. creeped me out a bit). Im still working through it with my friend and enjoying reading the little bits of lore, learning the rules of the vampires and how they got there and their backstories and just absolutely ruining them. Its an expereince. The character dialogue is entertaining and when you co-op they occasionally have exchanges and talk about stuff and make jokes.Would recommend... maybe a bit later when its on sale, in a year, when perhaps they clean up a few more of the bugs too. _childDocuments_.review: A Promising Concept hindered by Short Length and Development BugsOne of the most glaring issues with Redfall is its brevity. Despite boasting a captivating world filled with rich lore and interesting characters, the main campaign feels disappointingly short-lived. Players may find themselves completing the primary storyline in a matter of hours, leaving them craving more depth and substance. This lack of content ultimately detracts from the game's potential longevity and replay value.Furthermore, Redfall is marred by several development bugs that hinder the gameplay experience. From occasional framerate drops to AI pathfinding issues, players may encounter a variety of technical glitches that detract from immersion and disrupt the flow of gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Things that are good:- Gameplay: Different classes and their abilities are fun! The variety at which I can go at enemies isn't a new formula for Arkane, but enjoyable in this game like their others.- Freedom of movement: Again, like in other Arkane games, the ability to sneak, climb, and move about freely allows me to decide when and where I want to engage enemies.- Variety of guns: My favorite so far has got to be the UV gun and crisping up the vamps for shattering! Hopefully they add more later, I think a modified brass knuckles with a stake would be hilarious fun at some point.Things that need work:- Loot: finding a gold weapon every few minutes make them seem less special, and I shouldn't find them in random bags that don't require a lockpick/wiring kit. Perhaps tweaking the %'s at which certain loot is dropped can help with this.- AI: definitely needs improving, enemies run into walls a lot!- Optimization: I have a 3070, i7 10700K (4.0Ghz), and 32 gigs of ram and on avg I get between 70-80 fps on Ultra settings, but it certainly dips to 30 fps on cluttered fights and looking at the big water wave in the distance (and that's with DLSS on). Definitely needs some work here to ensure a bit smoother gameplay across the board.- Enemy density: at times it feels TOO empty, but on certain fights feels overwhelming. There should be some tweaking here. I'm not saying there needs to be enemies on every street corner, but also I shouldn't feel like there suddenly an overwhelming tide of baddies because I want to check out a new POI.- Progression: Give players who join their friends the option to tie progression to the host or not (at least with new characters). - Back and forth banter between characters: feels repetitive at times is all, I will have to see if it improves with the "trust" building system Overall the game is a great time in co-op, haven't played it much solo though beyond the intro mission. A lot of the extra lore bits feel unnecessary, but I understand it is part of the world building. I would say pick it up, but maybe wait until some tweaks are made, or price drops. I personally don't feel like it is a waste of $70 because me and my spouse are having a lot of fun together in the game, but others who are solo playing or saving money, may want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a bit silly to review a game after spending only a few minutes playing it but such are the times, yes? (and for those that missed it, this is intentional irony)I was one of those fellas who saw this game from a distance, had his interest piqued, added to wishlist and then forgot about it until just a few days before release.  Like many folks here, I balked at the price - 70 bucks is already pretty steep but I'm also one who likes to spend that little extra and gets some goodies too.  100 bucks is a lot of cheddar to throw down on a game that you know little to nothing about aside from what the devs have released.Still, I took the gamble and made my purchase.  The premise sounded fun and playing a game that supposedly can be enjoyed either solo or in co-op mode made the choice a bit easier.  Plus, I just need something to tide me over until D4 launches in over a month.I played until I cleared out and established the first safehouse.  For some folks, this is only a few short minutes of gameplay.  Personally, I took my time and explored.  By the time I encountered my first cultist, I was armed with pistol, shotgun, and sniper rifle, had full med packs, and already a fair bit of what passes as currency.My immediate impression was that this felt like Funcom's Secret World (anyone remember that?) from way back - but in FPS mode.  Lots of bits and pieces of environmental storytelling - humanizes some of the dead bodies you encounter all over the place.  I like the art and graphics style.  Some folks have called it cartoonish or reminiscent of '90s quality but I have to disagree.  It's a style choice on the devs' part and I think it suits the game just fine.  In fact, my son came in and watched me play a bit and he immediately recognized the Dishonored vibes.  (I never played Dishonored so I am not sure what he was picking up on)I am typically a cautious gamer so I go slow, peeking around corners, using flashlight sparingly, and taking note of voices and the clearing of throats.  I was a little surprised at the lack of enemy density but again, still early.  I didn't have any trouble dispatching cultists (they are terrible shots) and my little robot buddy kept the basement bloodsucker busy until I blasted him enough times to eventually stake him.  I like the tense moments leading up to the basement encounter and I hope there ends up being a lot more of that.  Gunplay wasn't bad.  I felt that it was a bit sluggish at first but I quickly acclimated and soon wasn't having any issues. The sniper rifle seems to miss half the time - which could be some of that latency that folks have complained about.  Otherwise, the other guns I've tried (pistol and shotgun) work great.I didn't experience any technical difficulties or performance issues, though I did have textures sometimes not render fully in some cases.  I don't have an uber setup but am running a 1070 Ti with 32 gigs of RAM - I really didn't have any major issues at all (still early though).Yes, I would recommend the game if you enjoy a slower paced, open world, story driven experience that also has a co-op component should you want to play with some buddies.  Plus, you get to stake vamps and murder cultists - all great fun. That said, the hefty price tag is a justifiable deterrent and I expect that they will continue to bring a lot of heat for releasing a game in its current state at such a steep price point.  It's worth picking up on a sale and/or waiting on them to patch with some fixes and improvements though - especially if you like the above noted attributes.I am enjoying myself so far and hopefully the game will get to a state where more of you can as well.  Sláinte!

There are things like birds circling houses which is cool and the storm before a Rook arrives is very cool. I played as the coast guard character and found it fine, playing as the psychic character I found the internal monologue eye-rolling. The gunplay is balls, characters become bulletsponges instead of becoming smarter or more elusive, some builds are just useless, you'll never need the sniper person like ever because most skirmishes don't merit actual prep planning when you can just cheese everything. The story is very hit and miss, there are some beats that are really cool, but the throughline is garbage. Finally, and it might seem nitpicky. Put some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cinematics in the game. It's just jarring to do to the comicbook thing because it's basically a sign to tune out and go grab a drink.On a sub-twenty discount with a friend, it's worth going through for sure. The bite back edition is definitely not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ worth it. But the real issue is that, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ play L4D or Borderlands instead. They still hold up fabulously and also hit these notes better.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most peeps, I don't usually write reviews, and I wasn't looking forward to this title, I knew it was looking bad, the only reason i decided to pick it up was cause someone gifted me jedi fallen order the game I was actually interested in and out of morbid curiosity.So with lowest expectations in mind...and  a few beers in hand on a sick day...I realized it was worse than I expected. I would like to preface this by saying that for me the game performed well except for an occasional micro stutter moving between the zones, but I do have an RTX 4090 paired with a Ryzen 7 5800x3D, 32 gigs of DDR4 3600 RAM and one of the fastest PCIE 4.0 SSDs, but keeping this in mind, a game this small, this unpopulated and ugly has no business neither weighing 100 gigs on your hard drive nor giving you performance issues even if your are still running a gtx card.In the words of Gordon Ramsey...ITS BLAND! It's got bland visuals, bland sounds, bland gameplay and bland RPG mechanics and story. A lot of this can be forgiven if gunplay was fun...but its not, I am not normally sensitive to these things but when a shotgun feels like a peeshooter you know there are issues. Enemy bodies don't respond appropriately at being shot and the guns have zero impact or kick, for nostalgia sake I tried Borderlands 1 a few days ago and it had more impactful weapons than Redfall. The RPG mechanics themselves are nothing to write home about either and loot feels inconsistent and largerly pointless as all enemies are pushovers in both stats and AI. Two of the 4 characters are also pointless, well 1 if you place co-op I imagine 2 if you play solo as one is a healer which has no purpose in solo and one is a sniper with a cloak ability and a revealing ability both of which are useless because the AI is really weak and you are might as well just run up and blast them in the face.It does feel like the game had an ounce of vision behind it at some point, as some of the details around town are clearly inspired by the actual location and someone giving a crap about authenticity and the whole occult theme has not yet been repeated in triple A to death but a confused and troubled development has clearly impacted on what little original inspiration and vision there was...until a husk remained, that kept what little life it had by sucking the life of other better games dry...a bit sad really...

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall - Bite Back Edition ..... is a game.Oh.  Should maybe say some more huh?  Okay.The basics of an Open World Loot-n-Shoot with story elements RPGish game are present.  The world can seem empty, but more target rich or loot filled would unbalance the game play.  Leaning to maintain stealth, ADS toggle, and other QoL options would make this game better.  The skill tree may be okay, but have not leveled enough to see how it works.  I wish some crafting, and weapon modding, had been implemented.  Story is interesting, and I am hoping to learn more.  I am not sure if this is a graphic or game mechanic problem but enviromental damage (fire, explosions, etc) are not always easy to notice.  I walk into a burning area that looked more like fluttering dead leaves.  So for this far I remain middle ground of Redfall is a game, and some may like it.As for the graphics I will say that things did not work as I expected.  The optimized preset for my hardware did not work well.  My rig is okay: AMD Ryzen 5900X, 32 GB DDR4 3600Mhz, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, NVME SSD, Win10 22H2.  Monitor is a 2560x1440 144Hz display.  It was 40 - 60 fps with grainy odd looking textures.  Eventually I got this to improve to 144 fps avg.  Turning off FSR/resolution scaling was the first big help.  Then I could tweak other setting to where I tend to run games.  Hitching is still a minor thing.  Also minor visual effects that do not look right (some flames, random item physics).  Not sure if Nvidia problems are for the same reasons.So I plan to wait and see how things improve.  I will thumbs up, but this is a very minor thumbs up.  Bethsoft and Arkane make good games.  Seems more time for quality will be needed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've played a game as frustrating as this one, one of the ads or intro vids I saw presented it as "play coop or by yourself" (paraphrasing). no, it's not meant as a SP game, it's tacked on as an afterthought. First play through I selected tutorials but they're very limited, so I didn't know that vampires may leave a collectable residue when killed and since the residue glows weakly, especially during the day it's virtually unnoticeable. yes you might see the ashes but not realise that they're collectable.  I killed several dozens before noticing a weak glow during a sundown. also not explained by the tutorials: the meaning of the chomping jaws that occasionally appear in a corner (red teeth) or on storage box contents (white on black), or the fact that the ultra-vast majority of objects you can pick up are not stored but instantly converted to cash. the backpack has 40 slots and I could never fill it, well it turns out that this is shown in text that can't be made larger and I am vision impaired. I needed someone to tell me what was happening. There's no pause function, understandable for online/coop play but not offline. I was killed very literally hundreds of times while tweaking the settings or answering a call and of course it's one of those games where you get charged for dying... all that cash collected, gone tweaking settings. Ah, the settings, the settings... I have a 1080p monitor, but the game has no FHD option; maxres is 1366x768. WHY? because I have an RTX capable card? no idea, what if I do and I don't want to upscale? enemies spawn within seconds of you clearing an area, and if you approach a group of enemies by stealth - and therefore slower, I've lost count of how many dozens of times I was killed by enemies that spawned in an area I just cleared. You go back to your last death locations where you have collectables from dead enemies, and in the 3 minutes you were gone the area has changed drastically. going back to a T  intersection where there were drops from 6-7 enemies, the drops were gone but there was a road block, a van, a UV trap with a stone vampire. and the two biggest mind-fuzz ever since X-Com, which also was guilty of this: Once enemies lock onto you, they will hit you even from behind cover. So far I've been killed: behind a tree, crouching on a path running at the edge of an (empty) river with rocks, soil and cement between us, and by an enemy who was obviously below ground. as far as I was able to determine, if you can see their !!! or ???, they WILL hit you. and the greatest perverse peeve: use a pistol, the vast majority of drops will be shotgun shells or combat rifle. switch to combat rifle/shotgun and the drops will switch to pistol and sniper rifle. i suspect it will only provide you with a little of your most used ammo to force you to switch. once again as with the resolution, what if I always want to use the same weapon, what's it to the devs? reason to rage quit: the game is online only, even in SP. if your network connection drops, you get booted out to the main menu. My internet connection has always been sketchy, so between all of the above and the disconnections, you go ahead, guess how much fun i'm having in this game?

_childDocuments_.review: In the short time that I have played, Redfall has been a legitimately boring experience. I have no desire to hop aboard a hate train for clout or to go wherever the wind is blowing, thoughts are my own.The AI is ridiculously stupid, the world feels empty and devoid of any substance, gun-play is mediocre at best and if anything, feels stiff compared to other FPS titles I've played over the years. I don't care about any of the characters because the game right now hasn't done a good enough job of getting me to give a damn about them. I'm not expecting deep characterisation in under two hours, but I expect to want to get invested into the world & characters and nothing about it so far has been even REMOTELY compelling.Most of my time has been spent running from bland location to bland location, looting cans of spaghetti hoops and cereal boxes that auto-convert to funds, of which I've used to buy lockpicks and re-wire tools to get mostly boring loot. The skill-tree is also uninteresting. I came across a locked door and looked around the property to see if there was a clever or interesting way to break in. Nope, turns out I can just smash the front window next to the door and climb in, then unlock the door from the inside. Maybe there are some interesting puzzle locations in the game that reward outside of the box thinking, but I hadn't found it yet. I came across a safe-house where the power generator was locked in a shed behind a locked door, I saw a small window, climbed up on something and thought maybe I could hit something to turn it on or do something to open the garage door to get in? Nah, nothing at all, unless I missed it and I'm just stupid.Performance is also not the best. Running an RX 6600 + Ryzen 5600, I kept it on medium settings and found that the game all over the place performance wise. Sometimes it'd run smooth, then it would stutter or hitch, there was noticeable texture pop-in as well. Bugs all over the place, I've walked into locations where the enemies have no health bars and didn't even notice I was there, no reaction, shoot them and nothing happens, I had no idea whether that was a bug or feature but I assume it's the former.AI is a comical joke, imagine being excited to finally get some in-game action, only to be met with what feels like some of the most primitive AI I've seen in modern day. They aren't particularly threatening, nor do they make me think about how to utilise the environment or skills.I'm sorry, this needed more time in the oven. Whether it was six months to a year, doesn't matter. I'm glad I won this via a competition and didn't fork out £60 for it. Why waste that kind of money on modern AAA games when they're like this, when I could spend a third of that on early access games and end up with better results? I'll continue to play as I have mates that wanna vibe on it, but I don't recommend paying £60 / $70 for it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall is a solid game that delivers what you should expect from a game like Generation Zero. The world is well-designed and does not feel empty, with a wide variety of vampires and other mobs roaming around. While the game could be optimized, this is typical for many games upon release and should not detract from your overall enjoyment.However, it's important to note that Redfall is not a game designed for solo play. It's best enjoyed with friends, as this will make the experience more engaging and enjoyable. Playing with others will also give you a chance to take the game at a more relaxed pace and fully explore the world without feeling rushed or overwhelmed.Overall, if you're looking for a game that offers solid gameplay, a well-designed world, and fun co-op experiences, Redfall is definitely worth checking out. While it may not be perfect, it delivers what you should expect from a game of its type, and its flaws are minor in the grand scheme of things. So, gather some friends, dive into the world of Redfall, and have a great time!

Here's a couple of things I can list that would make me not recommend it:Very low quality 3D model work and low quality animations, pushes your pc like next-gen but looks like a 2012 game, very low quality AI reacting either slow or seemingly glitched, a ton of strange graphical oddities e.g ambient occlusion continuous artifacting or pitch black looking garage interiors when its light outside, confusing storyline where your character knows more than the player leaving me play catch-up, lackluster cinematics (if you can call them that), boring environments where nothing notable happens most of the time, enemy design appears unimaginative, weapons don't feel good shooting and their design appears uncreative (don't just add stakes to everything...), characters are uninteresting to deal with although I've stopped playing about 2 hours in as of this writing.I've not had performance issues like most others aside the occassional hiccup entering zones/points of interest, it's everything else about this game that's a head scratcher. I'll be honest: you're better off getting Dead Island 2 for less than this on another platform or wait for when it launches on Steam.Sorry Arkane devs, I know you've been pressured by your publishers to release this as-is. It would take a substantial amount of work to levitate this game's fundamentals into a place of better gameplay but its core is, by design, just not cutting it.

_childDocuments_.review: Original 2023 review:I have nothing clever to say.  I bought and tried this game, and immediately refunded it.  I then tried to overcome my hang ups with the games performance in order to experience the games mechanics by subscribing to Game Pass for one month.  I spent another 4 hours or so trying to push my way through the main story and quests and ultimately I just could not find any enjoyment or satisfaction in this game.If the performance issues were resolved, and the AI was tuned/balanced better, this game could become serviceable, but it will never be fun for me... and I will likely never play it again.  I don't see myself buying a copy... If anything, I'll just subscribe to Game Pass for another month if I really feel the need to test these waters again.I would advise against buying this game, and instead... play it via Game Pass or just give it a skip._______________________________New 2024 review:Update: Got it on a deep sale.  Yup.  Three patches later, the performance and AI was improved, and the game is now serviceable, but still unfun.  Still... for $18, it's hard to pass up, if for no other reason than morbid curiosity.  The game world is very pretty... but everything else is just as DOA now, as it was at launch.Update 2: Well, that's all folks.  Arkane Austin has been shut down as of 5/7/2024.  We all got scammed out of DLC and deluxe edition content, fed false promises, and probably will never see our money back.  I wonder how many people will casually forget this tragedy, and buy an Xbox, or whatever live service trash Xbox slings at them in the coming years.Update 3: They released the final update with offline mode and major game improvements.  I would argue the game is now fun.  It's clear that if the version of the game we have now was the version released at launch, the game would have likely seen more success.  More proof that management is/was to blame for 90% of Redfall's failures.  Hopefully Xbox/ZeniMax was able to see that there is talent to be retained from Arkane Austin, and simply fired management... but I doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: OLDER GAMER HERE, I started gaming on a Sinclair ZX-81 back in the early 1980s.I found this to be a masterpiece of a game, STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. 10 out of 10 — one of the most enjoyable games I have EVER played.It was wise of me to disregard the negative reviews. I bought a Steam code for €15.74 from Fanatical (March 2024), and I have to say that I am loving every minute I have played so far. Here is what I enjoy:(1) The game code is very well optimized. My nVidia RTX 3060 12 Gb fan barely makes any noise while playing the game, with most settings maxed. The game never crashed on me even ALT-TABing out of it, e.g. in order to check something on the Internet, and ALT-TABing back into the game.(2) The game is first-person view only, and open world, of medium size. The in-game map is clear and easy to read. Lots of houses and locations to investigate. You can fast travel between safe houses and monuments or walk — no cars or other vehicles (not that they are needed, the world is not that big).(3) The graphics are very well done and very atmospheric. They remind me of Fallout 4 and The Sinking City. The attention to detail is amazing and so is the movement of the character. You step over every little object — and I never got stuck even moving into tight corners.(4) The story is absolutely gripping. You have to deal with cultists and vampires. The game scratches my zombie itch in that respect.(5) The interface is simple and elegantly done. Not super confusing as in other games I love, e.g. The Division.(6) There are skills to unlock that are organized on a skill tree that does not feel overly complicated.(7) There are safe houses to unlock, usually after turning their power on and occasionally after beating the cultists that defend them. The game reminded me of Far Cry and Dying Light in this respect.(8) You can parkour! In addition to jumping, when you press the SPACE BAR, your hands reach up and you climb to whatever you are looking at. Moving from one roof to another in the city at night is just amazing.(9) Destroying a vampire lair is a lot of fun. You enter the lair through a door, and the lair feels like an alternate reality, sort of like a neighborhood that looks wrong, in which you have to find and destroy the heart, and after that make it out of the lair in less than a minute.(10) If you enjoy searching houses, yards, and other locations for items, you are going to love this game. And whatever you collect, get converted to currency immediately — you don't have to sell it anywhere.(11) Finally, daylight, the easiest difficulty, is doable for kludges like me, although it can get challenging when more than one Vampires are attacking you. The boss fights don't seem unfair.TIP: When you first start the game, you may have to disable any external displays (that are in a different resolution than your main one) in order to get all resolutions to show up in the Settings.I may update my review as I continue playing the game, but felt I should provide some immediate input, considering the mixed response this wonderful game seems to have received so unfairly, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on Midnight difficulty (Highest setting without NG+) with 2 friendsInteresting premise but executed like garbage- No animated cut-scenes- Poor story telling- Forced story events are usually still transparent models talking with no graphical aid for visualisation- Majority of the lore is hidden in notes and world curious that are annoying to find and interact with and boring to read- Because of poor story telling, villains are not very interesting aside from "Typical megalomaniac on a power trip"- Meaningless/non-existent interaction between the playable characters, almost like it was designed to be a single-player gamePerformance is garbage despite mediocre graphics- Mid-tier laptop (6800HS + 3070 Mobile) cannot keep 60FPS on 1080P minimum settings (DLSS does nothing and sometimes makes it worse)- Decent PC (5800X3D + 6900XT overclocked) can hardly keep over 90FPS on 1440P medium preset- Turns into a slideshow in some scenarios with drops to 4-5FPSGameplay- World is 95% (approximation) empty space, 5% Points of Interest with enemies- Boring travel point to point due to lack of enemies, despite heavily implying the town is overrun with vampires- Character personalities are anaemic- Character skill trees are uninspiring, with one character having major advantage in utility compared to the others- Some skill upgrades are conflicting: Jakob's scanning Raven's damage upgrade means enemies become alert and stealth is lost, not exactly beneficial when sneaking or long-range sniping as they will always know where you are and rush you- Dumb as bricks AI for both Humans and Vampires- Most vampires can be circumvented by being on higher ground (insert Star Wars reference) like car or van or having a chest-high object between you and them- Inventory and Shop UI is very clunky and annoying to useGuns- Uninspired choice of standard weapons (Pistol, Revolver, Shotgun, Assault RIfle, Sniper Rifle)- Weapon balancing is terrible- Vampire-specific weapons are unique but sometimes unwieldy as most engagement involves human targets- 3 active weapon slots felt restrictive as at least one is taken up a vampire-specific weapon (though this is personal preference issue)- Most gun stats such as accuracy are not well explained- Attachments on guns are seemingly randomised and not indicated in any way.: Sights on an Assault Rifle can be iron-sights or Holo/Red-dot, despite the model and rarity being the same: Sniper rifles can be silenced or un-silenced and has no indication unless you equip it and inspect the model or shoot the gun- Numerical Bonuses on rare guns (green and above) tend to reset when reloading game session : Increased mag size from 15 to 20 on a rifle will revert back to 15 after quitting and resuming your game- Unique bonuses (non-numerical) such as being able to kill a vampire with a bullet weapon without staking them is keptGunplay- Most guns feel clunky to use- Aim-Down-Sight sensitivity is VERY low with no dedicated sensitivity setting, making it hard to track moving targets, much less getting head-shots with precision weapon(Although the AI are generally dumb and loves to randomly stop moving quite often, they are also prone to making micro-movements to the left and right which can be incredibly frustrating for anyone not using a shotgun)- Not much variation in engagementsAfter giving it a solid play, finishing the story as well as all the side-missions we could find, it had no redeeming qualities.The only upsides were the laughs my group had when a silly bug happens from to time to time.Though all said and done, I bought the game on STEAM while my friends played it on Game Pass like smart people, so I'm the only one left bitter over this experience where they have moved on

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent about 70 hours in the game at the time of this review. Completed the story on all difficulty levels including New Game Plus. I also played every character and did all quests including side missions and collected all collectables.My review is therefore not a short half-hour impression, but the gaming experience in all its width and depth.To be fair, I initially gave the title a negative review because I was struggling with technical difficulties and couldn't even start the game. After two tedious hours of internet searching, I got all the errors under control and was finally able to get started.First impressions were mixed and I wasn't sure what to think of the game for a long time. But the deeper I dived into the world, the more loving details came to light. For example, the story about the fire department, the first hub of the game, is very detailed. There are newspaper articles hanging on the wall that you can actually read and if you look around carefully you will discover even more cool story bits. You can also follow the characters' storyies and find their jobs or homes. and that level of detail is found in almost every aspect of the game world.The environmental storytelling is also very well done, for example if you follow a trail of blood you can often find loot or other secrets. Also reading the notes (which I skipped completely at the beginning because it unnecessarily slowed down the game... I just wanted to explore and not read) gives an interesting insight into the happenings of the world.The biggest problem of the game is probably the AI ​​and the many big and small bugs. The heroes' skill trees aren't really well thought out either. For example, why doesn't the game's Sniper, who relies on good position more than any other class, have not any movement-ability? Or why does the Closerange shotgun character have a springboard skill that toss you out off the optimal distance for his weapons? I don't see any real synergy there. they should have thought more carefully about that.But still, the world has charm and is full of things to discover. The explorer in me just wants to find them all. I can only hope that after the launch fiasco, this game still has a chance. Maybe the team behind redfall can do the impossible and win back their fans with some good updates. I can only wish it for them, because the potential is definitely there.

_childDocuments_.review: From my observations, this game received a harsh review bomb, and everyone else jumped on the band wagon. Now, let's get into the review. I have had more issues with the latest CODs, including Warzone & BLOPS4; I have had more issues with Dying Light 2, Elden Ring, and others. All of which could be mitigated by tweaking settings. The initial wave of people who tried this game did not keep an open mind and went into it thinking it would not work. Hence, no effort was put into making it work. While I agree a game should come ready to play when released, I don't think that is a fair assumption to have in the gaming community anymore, as we all do not account for the extra work that goes into making the games for multiple different platforms and trying to use the same mold. I have a great analogy for it: picture a road; in this instance, the road is the game. Now put one person in a semi-truck with all 18 gears and manual transmission, one in a forklift, and one on a generic 4-door sedan. All vehicles would need to use the road and would drive the same, especially, but to get them to drive is another story: different controls, different speeds, and different training. The vehicles are your hardware pieces. Eventually, things will smooth out as we learn; however, the launch is expected to be rocky.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall is a game that promised a lot but ultimately fails to deliver. From the outset, it appears to be a promising open-world FPS action game with a unique storyline. However, as you progress through the game, it becomes apparent that the gameplay is shallow and uninspired.One of the biggest issues with Redfall is the lack of variety in the missions and activities. There are only a handful of missions, and they all feel repetitive and unchallenging. The combat system is also lackluster, with only a few basic moves and attacks that quickly become boring. The Vampires, which should be the highlight of any action game, are poorly executed and lack any real sense of excitement.Another significant issue with Redfall is the graphics and visual design. The game looks dated and unpolished, with low-quality textures and character models. The environments are bland and lack detail, which makes exploring them feel like a chore.Furthermore, the game suffers from technical issues, including frequent crashes and bugs that disrupt the gameplay experience. The controls are also clunky and unresponsive, making it difficult to perform even the most basic actions.Overall, Redfall is a game that falls short of its promises and fails to deliver an engaging and entertaining experience. It's a shallow and uninspired game with repetitive missions, lackluster combat, poor graphics, technical issues, and unresponsive controls. I would not recommend this game to anyone looking for an exciting and immersive open world FPS game. *GAME WAS FREE WITH PURCHASE OF GTX 4090**

_childDocuments_.review: Not as horrible as some have said.  For me, video optimization and such are things that can be patched, but game SYSTEMS can't really be changed after launch. It would have made more sense to have a sytstem to upgrade the weapons a la Dishonored upgrade system at the Black Markets.But ultimately what killed the game for me is that it is NOT fun for single player.  The powers of the characters are clearly meant to be for co-op.  And the story isn't as rich if you don't play co-op (and have the characters befriend and talk to each other).  I love Arkane games because I love great single player, story driven game with cool powers and excellent level design.  This has the elements of all of it, but it was clearly designed for co-op as its primary focus.In the final analysis, the video issues and bugs probably would have been overlooked if the gameplay was actually fun. _childDocuments_.review: Bethesda lives down to its reputation.(1) We "pre-loaded" the game over the weekend so we'd be ready to play on Monday. Nope. We all had to re-download all 77 GB. So... what was the point of giving us the opportunity to pre-load?(2) My version crashed when I first ran it, then crashed again when I tried to use the Steam overlay to join my friends. All of us have had at least one crash in under 2 hours of play.(3) My version skipped the 5-minute intro scene, which is minor, but I *like* watching cut scenes so I was disappointed having to sit there in the ferry waiting for my friends to finish the scene.(4) We finally managed to get to the fire station, at which point the game completely bugged out. There were no enemies, we couldn't interact with anything, and the quest line started progressing as we walked through rooms. "Defeat the cultists?" Check, without firing a shot. "Rescue the captives?" Success! Even though we never saw them. We quit out for the night.(5) Today my friends tried to start up again with new characters. Nope. The game remembers everything you picked up as your old character, so they couldn't even get off the ferry because all the guns had already been looted.Long story short, between the four of us we've had six crashes, had to restart the campaign three times, haven't managed to even make it to the fire station with the game working, and haven't managed to go 5 minutes without some interactable object being bugged out.Dare I say this launch is WORSE than Fallout 76?==================UPDATE AFTER FINDING WORKAROUNDS FOR THE BUGS:(1) To play multiplayer at all, we learned that you need to use the fastest machine in the group. Otherwise if the fast machine loads before the host, the game bugs out and you can't play. Once you've worked that out, it's buggy but playable. It still crashes every time I launch it for the first time (so it's start it, quit it from Steam, start it again), and one of our other players had such a catastrophic crash he had to unplug his computer.  So we have it "mostly functional", but the machine speed bugs, saved game bugs (see below), and nightly crashes make the game painful and frustrating.(2) Unfortunately, even without the bugs, the saved game system is still hosed. I expect any modern game to allow me to have multiple saved characters and campaigns, and to be able to save wherever I happen to be with minor exceptions. In Redfall, if you quit in the middle of a mission you lose all your progress on that mission. That's unforgivably bad programming. Also, even though you're supposed to be able to play multiple characters, it seems to store all the campaign progress in a single file so you can't host two campaigns on a single machine.Which, combined with the, "This only works if the person with the fastest machine is the host," puts you in a situation where you simply can't have multiple campaigns going at once. Inexcusable.(3) Once you overcome all the bugs, you get to the actual gameplay, which is pretty meh. You have a handful of gun types to choose from, a Borderlands-style gun selection menu, and otherwise extremely basic movement, abilities, and skill-ups. Nothing surprising nor exciting. The fights are easy, the missions are routine, and it's a fairly boring paint-by-numbers first person shooter horror game. Even Back 4 Blood has a more interesting plot and more interesting NPCs.In short, the game has nothing I haven't seen before, even in single games, it does its stuff poorly, and it's WAAAAAAAY too easy for its target audience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an OK $17 game. At full price it's a hard pass.  I recommend it only if you can get it on a 75% or higher discount.I never played this game on launch, only picked it up in Jan/2024 so it's had several large patches. The AI is janky at best. They run around and take cover, then attack and then go back to cover in spurts and fits. It feels like they had all the proper behaviors programmed into them, just no logic on when to do them.  So instead of procedurally knowing when to take cover, or when to attack... they just kind of randomly pick a behavior or action, and then randomly choose another. The graphics are good, they have a nice cartoon style to them. It runs very well. Parts of the game feel like State of Decay. Rescuing civilians, gathering supplies and clearing out the vampire infestation. It's just not as fleshed out as State of Decay by any means... But you get that vibe.  Granted I have only done 2 quests so far. Co-op play is fun for the bit of it I have played. Difficulty is not very hard for being set on the hardest difficulty allowed without unlocking "Eclipse" mode.  And I should mention I was only playing with one other player. (2 of us in total)  The enemy don't feel too spongy, they just kind of overwhelm you because the Vampires can teleport to you instantly, so you have no way to run away or take cover. If they do add more patches and improve the AI, and beef up the difficulty options I think this game could recover some of it's bad reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of ink's been spilled over this game already, so I'm going to write about a couple specific reasons why I don't recommend it, at least at its $70 face value. Before diving in, I want to say the graphical issues haven't really bothered me. The art style is very Arkane, and if you like the look of the DIshonored games, you'll like the look of this one.First and foremost, this game is most like Borderlands, but unlike Borderlands, lacks for variety in its gameplay. Go to a slightly different area of town, shoot the same 10 bad guy models, of which there are 3 variations (SMG guy, shotgun guy, sniper guy), hope for loot. Instead of weaponry exploding everywhere, maybe a bag with some loot in it drops.Which leads to the second big issue with variety. If it's going to be a co-op loot shooter, the loot and gun play needs to feel great. The UV gun is hilariously fun against vampires, but overall there's a maybe 15-weapon pool, and not a lot of diversity in that pool. However, that's not the most infuriating aspect. That award goes to silencers, which actually work and give you stealth, but there's no way to tell if a gun has one unless you equip the weapon, and you can't add them on later! Not to mention shooting just doesn't feel very tight. You'll line up a headshot with a sniper rifle (with no stabilize button, btw. Come on, it's 2023, and my character is THE SNIPER GUY), and it'll whiff by a foot. You can't tell if it's you, the game, or both.I have primarily been playing this game in co-op with a friend on Gamepass. The multiplayer is...decent, if I'm being generous? The game certainly feels better with friends, but is hamstrung by bugs, missions hard-locking if your friend takes some actions, etc. Even more annoyingly, there's no drop-in, drop-out element. If your friend DC's, your session terminates and you're back to main menu. Friends can't join on you either--they have to be invited to your session.What's most upsetting though is that this is a game I actually wanted to like, and just...struggle to find positive things to say about. If my buddy isn't available, it just lives in my library gathering dust. It feels like even after the long delay, this game still walked out the front door feeling unpolished.

The game has crashed on me 4 times. It's making it very difficult to play.3. Graphics. Screen tearing, frame rate drops, and very poor graphical fidelity for a game that is supposed to be brand new.4. The AI is pretty poor. Fallout 3 and Skyrim have better AI than this game. It ruins what would otherwise be fun gun play.5. This is nitpicky, but the cut scenes are really weak. From a game like this, I want full blown and gorgeous cinematics. Not these still cuts with very little voice over. Makes the game feel cheap and not finished.6. Price. This isn't an issue that is specific to this game and in general, it's a worthwhile debate to be had. Personally, I think raising game prices is greedy and lame, but with this game even more so. Specifically, because the game has clearly been released in an unfinished state. If I had forked over 70 bucks for this mess, I'd be pissed too.I think this game should have been delayed while they polished it up, the bones are there, but they absolutely failed on the execution. Maybe they'll fix it and make it better, but I have little faith in developers these days. My bet is that they will make minimal changes and fixes and eventually just write the game off as a wash.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't deny performance could be better, occasional hiccups aren't that big of a deal for me but I'm already "used to this" in the Unreal Engine games, because the engine itself is flawed. Game wise, this is fun, open world reminds me of Dying Light a bit, but here you actually use guns, instead of just whacking at things in close quarters combat. Main characters look like they would in any Arkane game, but other NPCs, aside from vampires, look bland, enemy cultists all look generic and friendly NPCs are missing some of that charm from their previous titles. Weapons feel punchy and fun to use, not sure how I feel about the "rarity" so far, as high tier weapon drops seem too common. Dynamic day/night cycle makes it really fun to roam the world and engage into different threats during the day/night. Vampires are less likely to be encountered during the day, which is precisely when cultists like to roam around. Hard to say for now but if enemy encounters are random this will work nicely as it won't get as stale so fast.Currently my only gripe with it is the fact that idle AI really does seem broken, cultists seem to get stuck on random objects when idling/patrolling, vampire AI is fine as it doesn't physically walk unless engaging you, so they move around just fine. This is impression from a few hours and second im a rookie to arkane games.Now is this game as bad as the reviews and youtubers make it out to be?Yes and no.While yes this game has some nasty flaws like a enemy ai that belongs in an asset ripoff quality game and way to much graphics issues like a little map your charather pops up when fast traveling that becomes a blurry mess even if it has loaded in several times in one session.No its not the most horrible game for sure. But if you think arkane is up to pull a no-man's sky and fix this game with enough support as they have claimed then go ahead. But if you do wait for a sale. Its nowhere worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: - It's a good shooter- Interesting open-world exploration or sight-seeing- Stealth and Action possiblity with AI adatpting to it- Idea is somewhat new and unexplored- 4 playable character with distinct combat/stealth mechanics- A full skilltree with manifold skills- A loot system with alot of items laying around, making the world "lived-in"- A rarity system that adds boni on you weapons- A level system that make your old weapons obsolete and keep you searching for better- A variety of weapon types to choose from and to customize your playstyle- Horrible shooting animations, lagging reloads (rubberbanding magazines lagging behind the animations)- They made so much effort to be interesting and diversified but then just plain copy-pastat all the rest of the assets. "Dungeons" (Hearts) are only just not enough variety to stay interesting- The Human-AI is not optimized for neither stealth or shooting and they switch between those two modes it jarring and results in T-Posing, gliding around, rubberbanding, deforming (e.g. holding their weapon behind their back to shoot at you and more)- Vampires is not your everyday concept for horror, but could be soooo good if they wouldn't have littered the whole world with them and made them extreme push-overs - Don't bother about every one of the characters, one has UV powers and teleport. Every other it focused on the humans that are already easy as all heck. Please make at least TWO usefull against the 2 types of enemies...- Every skill needs to be skilled in order to get in the upper skilltree, rendering the possibility to decide obsolete- No item is used in any meaningful way, the give you health by chugging any drinkable, eatable (may it be chips to full on bottles full with alcohol) and the other give you "support" what is essential just a unfitting word for mula, money, kaching-kaching. You EVEN SPEND IT. Where on earth you spend "support" on weapons. Make it money ffs.- The "rarity" system is completely obsolete, because every unique weapon is not at all unique and you find them at specific points after a short wait of a in-game day or smth like that- You always need the new weapon, because the enemies scale with your level so even your best weapon ts bad fast. Not like other games where a "normal" weapon is worth a level or two and unique weapons worth five or more. It feels immediately outdated and you need to skavenge more robbing you essentially of gametime that could be spend playing the story and having fun- 2 weapon variations for every type of weapon for a looter shooter is just not enough and boring as HECKIt's sadly the principle of "death by thousand cuts". Map Problems:- Small bugs in Models, - off-limit housing in an exploration game,- to little loot in a looter shooter,- HOLLOW-MAN VOICE LINE SPAM,- detection through solid objects,- Hitscan in a 2023 game,- Damage range dropoff (like I play a game of nerf against aimbots with nailguns)- Enemies plain missing / not spawning inCoop Problems:- Coop Partner interaction voice line spam (all two of them),- Coop Hit-box Wandering,- Coop animations are bugged,- So.much.missing.collisionNo eye for detail:- floating world-objects- models clipping through walls,- low-res textures,- bugging/skipping/vibrating/missing assets all over the gamePoory optimized rendering pipelines- textures blurry,- laggy on mid-to-high settings on a high-end-pc,- framedrops of doom,- stutters- and crashesI want to like it, but it drained every drop of fun out of the experience for me. That's the only "Vampire"-Mechanic they nailed. It's dry as bones, sucked empty by the lack of creativity, attention to detail and plain "don't care" attitude by the devs/publisher to the obvious flaws this game has.

_childDocuments_.review: An open world role playing shooter with vampires. Sounded fun to me, so despite all the negative reviews, I gave it a try. Didn't expect to face the worst shopping system in video game history tho. That's because:- you can refill your ammunition at the shop. The price for that is based on your character's level, not on the amount of missing ammo, so if you're level 1 and have exactly 0 ammo left, you'll pay 50 credits; but if you're level 20 and are missing only a single bullet, it'll cost you about 3000 credits. Even better: you can refill your ammo even you don't need to (because you're full), it will still cost you credits. Basically, you can get rid of all of your credits by simply refilling your ammo a couple of times without shooting a single bullet in between.- like in other RPGs and shooter games, you'll need a lot of lock picks. Here, you can also hack electronic devices with a special kit, but these you'll only need once in a while. Once you've progressed a bit in the story, every item you buy in the shop will be replaced by another item. So if you buy a lockpick (which you need plenty of), it will be replaced by something else, most likely buy one of the electronic hacksy-kits (which you need like 1 per hour). Long story short: you can carry up to 8 lock picks, but most of times only buy 1. That's connected to the next point:- shops/hideouts: You can unlock shops in hideouts, which will also sell more or less rare items/weapons and also lock picks. But: same rule as above applies, so once you buy a lock pick here, it will be replaced. Of course you can fast-travel to another shop to buy another single lock pick and do so over and over again, until you visited each and every single hideout.- shops/hideouts part 2: there is a chance that the shop in a hideout will sell you a rare weapon, but to check that you have to visit that particular shop/hideout. Meaning if you're in an area with 5 different hideouts, you'll have to check each and every one of them to see if they offer anything of value. (It would also mean that you can get only 5 lock picks + 1 from the main shop, so not enough to meet the needs since you can carry up to 8 of them).Now, I know that you don't have to pick every single lock you come across, but for me, that's part of a good RPG. I want to know if there's anything special hidden there, after all. But this lock pick / shops / hideout ♥♥♥♥♥♥ really ruined the game for me. If I had a penny for every time I already fast-traveled, I'd be a billionaire by now. Apart from that, there is an open, but mostly empty, world to explore. Sadly, you don't get any helpful tools to explore, so every time there is a high cliff you'll waste minutes of looking for the right way to climb it.The enemies you encounter range from ridiculous stupid humans to vampires which can either two-hit you or don't give a damn about line-of-sight or not. So far, you can choose between 4 different classes, each of which have sklills that range from "meh, that sounds boring" to "how in the wide blue yonder is this supposed to be helpful?". It's also mildly frustrating that at least one of the characters is never shy to mention the obvious, e.g. when you're standing in front of a (so far) unknown hideout he'll say "there's a hideout". Oh, really?I'll try to muster enough resilience to finish the story and will most likely never touch that game again afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall launched to a LOT of issues. Had it been delayed six to eight months, it might have been received better. Another reviewer summed up the game best when they called it "Far Cry, but with vampires". In Redfall, you're going to assault locations full of bad guys, hunt sub-bosses, and then square off against proper bosses. Every time you do, you'll unlock loot and gain experience points to unlock new abilities. Rinse and repeat. If that's all you want out of the game, you'll have a good time. The gun play is good, the abilities are fun, and since Redfall is a "looter shooter" you'll get that dopamine drip of new goodies constantly. I bought the game for about $15 on sale through a 3rd party site and I can honestly say I've gotten my money's worth out of it. Will that change as new DLC and whatnot drops down the road? I'll have to wait and see.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, what to say about Redfall...Its a dissapointment. Simple. Its almost like Arkane made the game with one hand behind their back, while running out of money and being pressured by Bethesda to release it.The world is characterful and detailed in most places like you would expect from an Arkane game, like Dishonoured or Deathloop. Shops and houses are full of items and are believable. The subtle story being told through the cultish markings and unfortunate victims of the Vampire invasion are true to Arkane's brilliant story telling. BUT, the world is just..empty. There are so few enemies.. and what enemies there are can all be killed without you taking a scratch, in seconds. Streets are full of market stalls full of detail, picnic benches, and parked cars. All with explosives, power boxes, ignitable oil, or detonatable cars. Environmental hazards to help you fight the vampires. The problem is, there are never any enemies to fight you near them. Ive been downed more by me shooting an electrical substation and it electrocuting me in a fight, than the vampires.For content ive played the game for about 5 hours at this point, on Midnight difficulty, the equivalent of Hard at release. All of which has been done with coop with one other person.Enemies die instantly, to a single pistol shot to the head. Which is cool, guns feel powerful, but it makes stealth gameplay, something Arkane basically specialises in, pointless. Even in the tutorial it suggests you sneak past some cultists. Why bother? You can kill all of them with a simple headshot. Enemies seem to wait about 3 seconds to before they choose to shoot at you, Vampires, while slightly more challenging can be dispatched easily with a couple of shots while their attacks are easily dodged just by walking backwards. Its almost as if the devs put the game in easy, low population mode for testing and forgot to take it out of it again before release. Where are all the civilians? Did they all go on holiday prior the the Vampire invasion? You find the odd person to rescue, a few in safe houses, but other than that, they  are clearly all dead or turned into cultists. Weird.Weapons are far to frequent, with you getting legendary weapons straight out of the gate. The looter shooter system is pretty basic and you cant sell weapons in the traditional sense, instead you just scrap things  which gives you dollars/credits. Picking up random items in the world, like brandy, pipewrenches and packs of toilet paper (a covid joke which I appreciate), also awards you with cash. The shops are basically useless however. Weapons like the stake gun need nerfing as you can easily 2 shot a boss with it, and im only level 5... Enemies as a whole need to be tougher,  more frequent and far more intelligent. My buddy and I set off a shop alarm while breaking in, and expected a horde of vampires and cultists to swarm us. Despite the building across the street having enemies in, non came.Lets talk about graphics abit. The game is on Unreal Engine 5. Some of the cool new physics are present, but overall, while the game does not look bad, its hardly looks next gen. This i think is more to do with the art style. Arkane has always had a very cool, dystopian art style, with over accentuated, grim, almost caricature like characters. This is evident in the vampires and player characters design and proportions, but it is much more subtle than something like dishonoured. The colour palette of the game is similar to their other games with subtle pastel tones, however its like a "Lite" version of an Arkane game. Where as Dishonoured lent into the style 10/10, Deathloop about a 8/10 and prey about a 6/10. This game is only about a 2/10, as if they wanted a hint of their other games but nothing more.Sound design is good, with decent music and the voice acting for the most part is enjoyable. The characters interact well to each other (I played as Dev the plucky British cryptid hunter).Coop worked fine but you can only host a game then join in. You cannot join mid match and no matchmaking. So thats bare bones. Bugs, game is buggy as hell. Enemies that are immortal and cant see you are semi frequent, forcing me to reload the game to fix it. Nice to get close and admire the character models and hear some of their passive dialogue but other than that, annoying. T-posing characters, jittering in the floor and enemies stuck in floors to name but a few.I really hope they patch it and improve it and don't just abandon it. At this stage im enjoying it for what it is, but only with the hope that it is improved upon. I cannot recommend buying it now. See if they patch it. Arkane, I am dissapointed in you. Let people publicly test your game next time, and remember to test it yourself, because, if you did and didnt see these flaws, then you deserve the negative press you are getting.
