_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to put this into words, really. This isn't a game in the most conventional of senses. It's more-so an interactive bundle of stories, where the meanings and motivations are up to you and your own perspective of life and the way you interpret the music accompanying each piece. I truly don't believe this is for every single person out there, as it is slow and the interaction is nothing more than a couple clicks in-between the music. However, as an art piece and form of expression not just from the creators, but for a way for the viewer to express their own thoughts and feelings into the art and music, I cannot recommend it enough. Each of the four stories has many outlooks you can see it as, and it all really depends on how you analyze the visuals and music cues. That's special, if you ask me. I can't tell you what it's "about", as that would only be my own opinion, but I can tell you that somehow, without dialogue and complex 'gameplay', I still felt a personal connection to each character, through projecting myself through them. Loss, gain, the burden of existing and growing. It's unique, but I feel only certain people will truly appreciate that, and that's just fine.Go in expecting more of a music album with visuals than a true game. You'll enjoy it more and analyze it better without wondering what the game is 'telling' you. What its saying is up to you, entirely. I have a lot of respect for that, and I became incredibly emotional by the end of it all. Short, but enjoyable, like a film.
_childDocuments_.name: The Longest Road on Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I really really had high hopes for this one to be honest. Was expecting at least a comprehensible story with subtlety, but the presentation is too vague: it's a slice of life with not enough context to form an understanding of what the creators wanted to show. Except Chapter 2 and Chapter 4, I am almost completely in the dark..and the game has  What this is in essence, is a long interactive music video that unfortunately suffers from over pretentiousness. I get it, the longest "Road" on earth is life itself; but making me literally walk a character for hours is not the way to show that.The songs are good, I most likely will also get the OST later on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Longest Road on Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A good experience of a game.  Not much too it, but that's fine. Pros- Good pixel art.- Amazing music.  The game IS the music.  Like, actually somewhat literally.  The gameplay is sort of restricted by the music that is playing.  And that's fine.  The game is really just an OST that provides an interactive narrative w/o any dialog.  - A good reflection on life, its mundaneness, how it changes, how we're all ppl living our lives and can come into each others' lives w/o really any thought (think of the movies Crash and 21 Grams). Cons- Brainwash Gang is super minimalist in their style based on this and Nongunz.  The gameplay is simple, just has a prompt icon and you press a button.  Which is fine.  But sometimes the game isn't progressing and you do not know why.  But it is because the music has to finish.  This is nitpicky, not really a big deal, but it may throw some ppl off.Overall, a good experience for the price, especially if you like narrative games.  Can finish in under 2 hours.  And the OST is great.  Props to Beicoli.
_childDocuments_.name: The Longest Road on Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is heartbreaking(In a good way), I haven't gotten that far, but I already feel emotionally impacted. I am in a place where I need to allow myself to cry, and this game does that. However, it can get so intense, that even I need a couple breaks. But that is a good thing, because it encourages me to slow down and really enjoy the emotional journey that The longest road on earth takes me on. I truly encourage anyone reading this review to buy it just to take that time, and allow themselves to just FEEL. Don't think, just let your mind meld away and tell you your own story as you enjoy this experience.If the devs are reading this, I want to really thank you, this is the type of experience that I really need in these times of crisis, and it would be amazing for the game to get more. I know that might be asking a lot, but this is an amazing experience, while 3 hours can really be expanded when I take my time, I know it will be over sooner than later, so basically, I'm just asking for more, either way this is a great experience, and I recommend it to all, except for those youngin's who haven't gotten far enough in life to truly understand the importance of this game yet. But yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: Mesmerizing, overwhelming, right in the feels. This experience is imbued with melancholia and takes you to a trip with you emotions. _childDocuments_.review: Best described as an interactive novel, 'The Longest Road on Earth' is a pixel-art tale told in four chapters, each from the perspective of a different character. The game is an auditory and visual experience, with the story told through images and songs, rather than words. Each chapter focuses on aspects of everyday life, from strolling to work, to learning your first steps, to riding a bicycle. The simple things many of us take for granted, or rarely stop to think about.  The chapters are contained within an overarching narrative featuring an elderly crocodile who runs an antique shop. Items from his shop trigger moments from the past featuring the different characters. Without words, or any real context, the four stories are solely down to the players’ interpretation.  Since finishing the game, I’ve spent some time ruminating on what it all means. It’s certainly the type of game you’ll want to talk to others about.  The game explores universal themes we can all relate to – particularly with regards to time and its passing. For better or worse, things change, people grow up and grow apart. The four chapters are tied together by this thematic unity.  Special mention must go to the soundtrack of the game. The 20+ songs that feature were written specifically for the game by Beicoli, who also performs the songs which lyrically link to the text-less narrative. And these atmospheric songs are just sublime, many featuring euphonious swirling choruses that, like the story, provide a timeless quality.  The game does have some draw backs; it’s a short experience, lasting between 90 mins to a couple of hours. The player has little to do, other than move a character left and right and occasionally interact with items. And everything is deliberately slow paced; expect to spend minutes walking a street, or sitting down on a train waiting for your stop. But that’s life! And that’s what the game captures so well.  'The Longest Road on Earth' is a unique game; a transcendent gaming experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Each player will interpret it in different ways; perhaps in relation to their own lives. It’s also a prime example of the creativity that comes with indie games – and a great showcase for games as art.
_childDocuments_.name: The Longest Road on Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story about you or about seeing yourself reflected inside the special moments that the characters show. The OST masterly underlines every passage of their lives. These bits of life are perfectly featured through the curated pixelart. All these elements are properly combined to deliver a different narrative experience. Totally recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: NOT A NARRATIVE GAME. Already my #1 all-time favorite small indie pixel-art game ever. Steam has refund, so why not give it a try and make up your own mind?Long version:Most importantly: again, not a "narrative" game. I think most bad impressions about The Longest Road on Earth come from trying to interpret it as "telling stories", in the way narrative games usually do. Looking at the game through this lens could probably result in a frustrating experience. But NOWHERE within the game itself is a narrative experience promised. I mean "narrative" in the sense of "this is a story made of words" - whether directly, or indirectly translated into words from images or interactivity. A "story" like A wants to B therefore they C but D happens so they have to E which takes them to F etc. There's no such thing here, at least not at the level of the whole game as perceived by the player. And if such plots do form, they form intuitively and _very approximately_ in the player's mind. They're anything but spelled out, or meant to be deciphered like some code. Instead:- your ears are flooded with lyrics-heavy music and no other sound at all- the on-screen stuff contains no text (except a newspaper title and a few fictional brand names and such) - the one-button interactions are as minimalistic and non-story-driven as I've experienced in possibly any game except mobile hypercasual ones, with which this game has otherwise nothing in commonI think, for lack of a category, people are automatically classifying it as "narrative game" - and the devs/publisher seem to be somewhat using this as a selling point (still there's no mention of narrative or story in the Steam tags, and I think that's a good thing). In my opinion, selling it as "narrative" could be a mistake on their part.It's definitely an art game. There is _narrativity_ to it, both cinematographic and ludic, if we think of these concepts in a very academic sense. But it doesn't necessarily amount to what we usually mean by "stories", particularly in games. At least not in my immediate perception as a player. It's much more of a poetic piece.It has a reference to THE RED STRINGS CLUB, of all games (among others).The Longest Road on Earth feels extremely artsy and even pretentious - but somehow pulls it off in a very self-aware, satisfying and meaningful way. It often feels like the video game equivalent of a good European arthouse film. For furries.Not fitting any genre. I think this is the most important point.Not technically a game, I we need to be old-school purists about what games are - but do we? Also one of my favorite games ever. Probably my absolute favorite small indie pixel-art game from all I've played so far.And the most aesthetically mature game of any kind that I played. By aesthetics I don't mean just visuals. I mean the aesthetics of the actual game, the entire thing, the experience.I dare say it's low-key redefining game design with its minimalistic, discreet excellence. But the point of this can probably be missed if you enter the experience with a lot of game-literacy and expecting gamer's game conventions to work they way you know they work. The game does away with all that, and sets off to address a different audience.100% must play if you like the trailers.Also, as far as I know, Steam allows refunds, right? So why not give the game a try, despite some negative reviews? The reviews for such a game can only be HIGHLY subjective.
_childDocuments_.name: The Longest Road on Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A thoughtful and deeply personal title with stripped-down mechanics. The lack of dialogue or text allows you to create your own narrative through your time with four characters. Each short story will allow players to be swept away by the haunting lyrics of over twenty original, nostalgic songs.

name: The Mortuary Assistant
detailed_description: Having completed your degree in mortuary sciences, you have taken on an apprenticeship at River Fields Mortuary. Over the past several months you have logged many hours aiding the Mortician in daily tasks along with learning the ins and outs of the embalming process as well as how to properly handle and care for the deceased. Late one night, you are called into work to handle some embalmings. Death doesn’t keep day time hours. But there is something different about these bodies because there is something different about you. The phone rings with the Mortician on the other end. The rumors are true, and you can not leave. Perform embalming tasks while keeping demonic forces at bay Practice occult rituals to identify demonic entities Piece together clues to banish the demon and save your soul Uncover the gripping history of Rebecca Owens, the haunting past of River Fields, and a sinister secret that lies just beneath the surface… Ground breaking system makes every playthrough unique, guaranteeing you will never feel completely safe. A story that unfolds through multiple playthroughs. Each demon you banish is just a piece of the puzzle 10+ hours of content with more to find for inquisitive eyes Perform embalmings, handle the various jobs around the mortuary, and exorcise demonic forces. All in a day’s work.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a fantastic game, really entertaining and interesting! However, in my opinion, it's a bit too short, and the graphics could use some improvement. Just a slight graphics upgrade would make the experience even better. It's already a great game, though, and I hope they add more levels because I found it a bit too short overall. As for the scares, they could be improved as well since they become a bit repetitive and lose their impact quickly; you start memorizing them pretty fast. All in all, though, it's a solid game, and I’d definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Very unsettling and tense. I love that the game uses jump scares but is not reliant on them for it's entire scare factor. The atmosphere they've created is amazing and is psychologically terrifying. The mechanics are easy to use and overall it is a very very fun game to play. Definitely would reccomend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games for sure. I love that the devs make seasonal changes to the game, from decorations to new bodies. Santa Claus was a surprise for sure lol. The jumpscares no longer get me, but that's to be expected after the amount of time I have spent with the game. I also like that they added an update where you can turn down the amount of story lines you get, especially since I have finished all the endings and just want to work on the bodies without the constant repeated mini game memories. I just love how involved the devs are and they didn't just put a game out there and forget about it. They keep up with it and make changes! I'm excited to see what they add to it in the future. And even if I don't play it for a month or two because I get busy, I always check in around a holiday because I can't wait to see what they added for that specific holiday. Always cracks me up!

Lot of repetition. ~~However~~ Despite all that, some actually pretty good cheap jumpscares and spooky psychological horror moments.Pick it up if it ever goes on discount and the bugs are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Scariest game ever. Absolutely the best horror game I've played.  10/10 would crap myself again. The game doesn't rely on cheap jump scares or roaming enemies but uses its randomized jump scares to build an oppressive atmosphere of tension. A lot of the time nothing is even happening but you own imagination and fear will have you trusting no window, no closed door, and trust no dark corner.There need to be more horror games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often I write reviews for games, but The Mortuary Assistant is an exception. First, I'd like to say that of course this game is not perfect, I experienced a few bugs and glitches however it's only been a week since release. Ignoring those, the game is amazing, visually and story-wise. The mechanics are simple to understand - although a bit scary at first - and the story isn't a cliche, crazy protagonist who's just hallucinating, the scares are real and genuine that come out of nowhere and a few even made me jump. My only gripes with the game is the mouse sensitivity when it comes to moving the gurney, it's not too annoying that it makes the game unplayable, but MAN is it slow when returning them back to storage. Still, the devs made an AMAZING game and I had been so excited for TMA since the demo, and the full game did not disappoint!!TL;DR game is spooky, graphics good, a few bugs but nothing too bad and a few scares made me jump. WORTH YOUR MONEY!!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Phasmophobia? Are you a fan of subtle, yet terrifying jumpscares? Done right? You need this game. They say they will continue improving the game through patches and exciting updates as well. Are you brave enough? Play the demo for a sweet taste of the mechanics, then dive in and banish the demons!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very cool game.The atmosphere here is really well made, from the lack of music to the subtle creaks and noises; it made me feel wary whenever I so much as got close to the corpse being worked on.I failed on my first real shift . While I haven't continued past the first shift (have to work in the morning after all) it left me intrigued and wanting to continue as soon as possible.I don't know much about the protagonist's story yet so I don't have an opinion per se. When I played the demo I feared this would turn into the Nth "It was all in your head/it was all a dream/you were the killer!/you are not even a mortician, you are in a psychiatric hospital!/nobody ever suspects the butterfly!" psychological horror game.Thank God . There are, from what I've seen so far, some elements of the mind playing tricks on you, but the threat is real and it doesn't look like it's the main focus of the supernatural elements that occur.There are some bugs here and there, nothing major.For instance, since I like to click anywhere around me and try to open all the closets and cabinets, especially to weird out my boss who's in the same room as me, I managed to accidentally pick up a notebook that I wasn't supposed to get just yet. I couldn't interact with it nor did I trigger any strange events or cutscenes or anything, so all was well.There was one "event" that triggered from a different angle than was probably expected, which made me jump regardless.Also, there are some funny things that can happen if you activate the "high dpi mouse" option and change the dpi settings while moving the gurney.Other than that, so far so good, and even the bugs I encountered weren't even annoying. I was itching for a horror game already and this game is really providing.Would recommend! I'd like to add, since I read some complaints about longevity, there are several endings, each shift seems to play different, and the developer has pointed out that there's more lore, story, etc. to unveil with additional runs (shifts).
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A great, spooky, puzzle game. You will need to play through the "entire game" multiple times to get the entire story. There are five endings, which is fun since there are only two obvious ones you can see from the start of a play-through.Overall the spookiness is great but not overdone. The audio is the best part - the whispers in your ear and the knocks on the windows and doors will keep you on your toes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it enough to recommend, although at the moment there are frustrating bugs that can cause one to necessitate a restart of the game. Won't bother naming the ones I've encountered as many other reviews have done a good job exposing the worst.  The atmosphere is good with creepiness and jump scares for those that enjoy such. The level of fear you will feel is subjective and only the one playing it can judge adequately if they're enjoying it. I did.  The tidbits of story interspersed through the loops is enough to repeat the "grind" and find out more about our protagonist but it can be tedious for some.  All in all, a good spooky little game that I've thoroughly enjoyed thus far, with the hopes of more content to be added later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Mortuary Assistant is a unique entry in the realm of video games, combining elements of morbid reality with chilling paranormal thrills. This game masterfully balances the macabre world of mortuary science with the adrenaline-pumping excitement of supernatural encounters, making for a truly gripping experience.Morbidly EducationalAt its core, Mortuary Assistant serves as a surprisingly educational journey into the process of embalming a corpse. While the game's mechanics are simplified for accessibility, players still gain insight into the key steps involved in preparing a body for burial. Tasks such as cleaning and suturing the body, draining blood, and injecting embalming fluids are all depicted with a level of detail that respects the real-life procedures, albeit in a more digestible format for the general audience. This educational aspect, though rooted in morbidity, offers a fascinating glimpse into a profession shrouded in mystery and often misunderstood by the public.Paranormal ThrillsWhat truly sets Mortuary Assistant apart is its seamless integration of paranormal elements into the gameplay. The game doesn't merely rely on the eerie atmosphere of a mortuary; it actively incorporates supernatural occurrences that keep players on edge. From ghostly apparitions to unsettling noises and unexplained phenomena, the paranormal side of Mortuary Assistant significantly enhances the game's tension and overall enjoyment. These elements are not just tacked on for cheap scares; they are intricately woven into the storyline, adding depth and intrigue as players uncover the dark secrets of the mortuary.Enhancing the ExperienceThe combination of realistic mortuary tasks and paranormal activity creates a unique gameplay dynamic. On one hand, players are grounded in the methodical and clinical process of embalming, which is morbidly fascinating in its own right. On the other, they are constantly aware that something otherworldly could occur at any moment, which keeps them engaged and on high alert. This dual focus not only makes the game more enjoyable but also ensures that it stands out in a crowded market of horror titles.ConclusionMortuary Assistant is a compelling game that successfully merges the educational aspects of mortuary science with the thrilling unpredictability of paranormal encounters. Its morbidly educational content is balanced perfectly with its eerie, supernatural storyline, making it a must-play for fans of horror and those intrigued by the macabre. Whether you are drawn to the realistic portrayal of embalming or the spine-chilling hauntings, Mortuary Assistant promises a unique and unforgettable gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, definitely very spooky, lots of jump scares, I'm not typically easily spooked, but this game definitely did creep me out to play home alone late at night. Not terribly gory, but you do have to prepare cadavers for burial, so if you're squeamish or turned off by any kind of body horror, be warned. Once you get into the swing of it and learn the games mechanics it's basically just a spooky puzzle game, but still fun. Definitely more fun to play with friends or in a stream so you can get the reactions of everyone else also being super creeped out.

_childDocuments_.review: So I found this game a bit later in the development cycle and played the steam demo a few times and fell for this game. It sucks you in from moment one and makes you start questioning what the heck is going on even in the quote on quote tutorial level. I have to say I love that the tutorial helps set up for that nights events over just being a way to teach you how to play the game. Makes suffering through it for people who know what to do in this game a bit more manageable.I also love how the game gets to know you and is ever changing what scares are happening when or what pieces of the Rebecca storyline you get from the demon who is trying to possess you. No two gameplays are the same at all. I mean there is the basic mechanics that don't change but the bodies change, the demon name changes and the events you deal with change. It's just a brand new experience each time.I will say the bad revies, which I think is just wrong to have considering age of the game, are a bit valid. There is a few annoying bugs here and there that are a bit game breaking. I have had issues with doing a new shift for endings and being forced to carry a mark with me that I cant set down. I have had issues getting a mark on a different body so I could burn the right body and survive. Yes, it has issues but keep in mind it is a day old and is a one man developed game. For something that ONE guy created by himself, I would say its a great game with decent graphics. Of course the graphics aren't AAA quality, but they are not the same quality as most indie games that use free assets.overall, it's a great game that just needs time to have some minor/major bug fixes. The dev is working as fast as he can to solve them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: My boyfriend got me this game. *mild spoilers for some random gameplay*  I get on, starts out pretty scary, flickering lights, voices, doors opening.  But i get used to it.  I'm chilling, just doing my work.  Not feeling scared.  It's a simulator game at this point, I am just working alone in a morgue.  I turn around and she's there.  A woman with red eyes, staring at me from the pitch black hallway where I *definitely* left the light on.  I flee to the corner of the room, behind the computer desk.  She slinks back and leaves the light off.  I *need* to close the door.  I can't stand there with the door open.  I slowly go over, and she grabs me.  My character wakes up outside.  I sprint to the front door, and the hall way light is still off.  I turn off the sound, close my eyes, and sprint through the dark hallway.  Nothing happens.  I am ELATED and flip on the light switch.  Something big just happened, nothing else will happen for a while, I think.  Turn to my right and the same woman is crouching in the door way.  I stare, look away, look back.  Still there.  Felt like I was staring at her forever.  Was so terrified I had my sister sit by me while I played. This game is terrifying.  The random encounters really mess with your head, and lure you into a sense of false security.  I was fine, until I was so scared I paused the game for an hour.  Then nothing happens, and you're just waiting for another thing to happen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I gave the game one more shift to make sure I didn't get unlucky, and I've decided to change to a "not recommended". I had  repeated, unskippable story events and once again didn't get the event required for the good ending. No wonder there's a setting to turn them off. Always good to bring up, so you know if it's "worth it". The game is quite short at about 3 hours. That will get you through 3 playthroughs with most of the content if you don't lose (and it's really hard to outright lose). Once you find HER, that's pretty much the whole game. It says there are 5 endings, but that's a lie: There are 7. 3 of them are natural story progression, 1 of them is being bad, 1 of them is a meme, 1 of them is being  bad, and 1 of them relies on a specific story even that isn't guaranteed after the third shift - meaning if you're half-decent you  have duplicates before getting it. So, realistically, 3 hours. It's  I just think the reviews have been hyped by Youtube. It's a decently spooky game, but it does rely on jump scares. A couple times it had phenomenal sequences of just pure atmospheric/psychological horror, but that probably lasted 5 minutes of my 4 hours playing.  Just... implementation makes this less than what it  have been, which is a shame.For instance: they didn't implement a system to only give you unique scares/scenes until all of them had been exhausted. In my 4 shifts, I saw the same unskippable minute-long scene three times. I looked at my phone during a horror game - that's bad. On the third shift, the minor scares started to repeat as well. And while they're still scary if they catch you off guard, you become desensitized to it pretty quickly. On my fourth shift, the game was mostly just a repetitive embalming simulator while I waited for the 1 or 2 story events in the shift. I might do one more shift to give it a fair chance - in case there's more content and I got unlucky with RNG.Another example: the scares themselves. Subtle events are so easy to miss once you get in the groove of treating the dead. You'll go to enter data in the computer and will turn the corner so fast the spookster doesn't even register. Then you're in the computer menu by the time the "scare sound" happens. Or you'll run around a corner to fill the IV bag and clip right through the spookster. And some events can be outright ignored with no consequences: there was a ghost at the end of a hall and I just closed the door and kept working. I still heard spooky music, then the light in the hall clicked off. Not superbly spookstery.The game just doesn't set up the atmosphere needed to really have those subtle scares pay off continually. This works in the quiet parts of Outlast or Amnesia or Dead Space because there's a fear of being harmed or attacked, with the ambiance playing off of it. There's a constant tension at play. But this game is just too comfortable. I thought it would change once  but all but the first shift completion resets the timeline, I guess. It's pretty clunky. Once you've seen an item once, the descriptions that pop-up and require you to press "E" are just annoying. Gurney movement is atrocious, the mouse sensitivity plummets to near 0 and you have to throw your mouse across the table to make a 10* turn. The sliders are finicky. It's pretty buggy and it's easy to screw up the controls or a scene by, say, taking out the clipboard on accident. Turn off two settings: (1) holiday decorations, they're not well done and interfere with the events. You have to turn them off BEFORE a shift, the setting does not apply to a shift already active even if you reload the game. And (2) the item location randomization. Who thought that was a good idea as a default setting?

Its a game you need to be engrossed in. There is a heavy story-line that is being overthrown by them. Streamers try to speed run it while forgetting that it's a game of horror. _childDocuments_.review: After playing the free Demo, I knew there was something special about this game. I was thrilled to see the full version was close to release. I purchased the full version of the game, hoping that the full version would live up to the Demo. After playing my first shift as the Mortuary Assistant, all I can say is WOW!! I have never been so scared playing a game. The movement in game was for the most part smooth. No major bugs, No game breaking glitches. A few moments where the game seemed to "hitch" or drop frames but it was extremely minimal and never hindered your performance in game. Accessing in game inventory is quite simple and after your first few embalming's, you start to get the rhythm of what to do and where items are located. I HIGHLY recommend this game to those who love a good jump scare/puzzle solving game. I streamed my first play through on Facebook Gaming (Yes I know It's for old people) as That One Teacher Gaming. If you are looking to see game play before buying, feel free to check it out! My streams are 18+ because I couldn't help but swear while playing this game. I cannot wait to play my second shift of The Mortuary Assistant tomorrow evening. I wonder what surprises await me! Pleasant Embalmings to you all!

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to write a review as I saw that the developers have claimed that there are 10 hours of content behind this game, which is simply not true. I am usually a big fan of the games published by DreadXP, and I was excited to get this game too with the little money I had, thinking that I would get a game that would keep me entertained for a long time, but I was left with the feeling of disappointment. The gameplay loop is extremely simple, you ferry out bodies to embalm them, run around the building to look for clues, and then when you had enough clues, burn one of the bodies. During all of this, you will come across randomized events (I recon this is what the developers calculated for extra content) that range from red herrings to jumpscares, but after playing 5 or so shifts, you will already be tired of them, as you will see the majority of them. If I want to be honest, gameplay wise the game at maximum has 2 hours of content behind it. Anything extra is basically a random event that will last for a minute or two at best. 90% of the time you will be embalming bodies, which you will always have to do in the same order, with zero modification to the process. It gets tired fast, and jumpscares won't be working forever to deter the player from noticing this. What I also don't like is how the game weaponizes RNG to extend your playtime, as some of the RNG events are tied to the "main story" of the game, meaning that it will absolutely depend on luck if you come across something related to the main characters or not. Basically, you are guilt-tripped into playing more to be able to get every single fragment of the story, while the core gameplay does not change or get modified based on these events at all - it will always be about embalming bodies and running around for a few seconds to find clues. For 21 euros you get at max 2 hours of content, (depending on how quickly you pick up on the embalming process) and anything after that is just a repeat of those 2 hours. It's a shame, as I can clearly tell that the developers behind this project have the talent to make games and they have great ideas and systems, but the gameplay loop is just insanely boring to me. If you are looking for a horror game that will keep you occupied for a long time with non-repetitive gameplay, look elsewhere, especially if you are on a budget. If you are someone however who likes zoning out while playing a horror game, hey, this could be your thing. I would give a neutral review if I could, but sadly Steam does not offer that option.

_childDocuments_.review: The blood doesn't bother me except for the draining of the bodies, and the developer didn't just stop there he added in the noise of the pump which forced me walk behind the front desk to just get away from that noise. It frays the nerves. I've never been all that great with dead bodies but to have me touch, and get them ready to be burned along with demonic possession made me cringe. Two things I don't like doing is looking at a dead body, and the other is dealing with possession, and couple that with all of the freaky things which happen in the dark corners of every nook, and cranny of the mortuary had me reach my limit of self abuse. Mortuary Assistant is seriously one of the most scariest games I've ever played, and I've played many but nothing even comes close.Mortuary Assistant has the same shock value as the movie Exorcist, and the original Evil Dead. The visceral shock of these two movies effected people to the point that some folks had to go get some help.I played the game for about 3 hours (maybe a bit longer than that), and I had to give up because it scared me so bad. I have no idea who this person is who made this game but he has a talent for knowing what scares people. Only reason why I haven't uninstalled it is because there is nothing else like it sold today on steam or anywhere else for that matter, also I enjoy the thought I might return to it for a scare once in a while.To end it all off, the game haunted me for many days afterwards. It's one of the most scariest experiences I've ever had, and that's saying a lot.@Dev: I appreciate you're ability but I can't thank You for scaring me so badly.Final: Do I think the game is worth it? _childDocuments_.review: Horror Fans....Who are patient.  I honestly wish I could give this game the thumbs up, as the atmosphere of the game and the creepiness of some of the gameplay mechanics is pretty good in the horror genre. The game understands that keeping the player on tilt while not just blasting jump scares at the player. You're waiting for the next issue to come around the corner, and the sound/visual design does a great job of putting you on edge. The story behind it isn't anything special, but the different “stories” that you come across like the drug scenario does want me to push forward. The gameplay is simple but effective, although when it comes to some of the demon/spiritual elements, the game doesn't do the greatest job on the tutorial. The game in essence has all the hallmarks of a great game. So you're probably wondering why I'm giving it a negative review.Well, the game can't seemingly stop breaking on me, and sometimes it's even hard to tell when the game has broken. Like, the game messes with you, and yes, there are times where your inputs are not being taken in because the game is waiting for you to hit a scripted event. That's not what I'm talking about. I'm talking about scenarios where a rune on a wall literally disappears, so you have no idea what symbol you need to use. Or doesn't even appear in the first place. Or it starts a cutscene and then just leaves you in a black room......forever. On top of that, based on other footage that I've seen, I'm not sure why the symbols aren't always appearing on the corpses heads once everything is ready to go, sometimes the game just decides.....nah. It doesn't help when the ending in the stream clip below......well it's hilarious, I'll give it that, but it points to the game's biggest problem. It's bug prone: and bug prone in a way that doesn't allow me to complete it fairly. That's the only reason why this is getting a negative review, and quite frankly, I'm really hoping that it's a just me scenario. But until that can be proven, I have to tell players to avoid the game....for now.

_childDocuments_.review: A great little horror simulator with high replayability!It is your first night-shift on the job as a mortician, and you will find out it is quite different from the daytime shift. You'll be trying to do your job as best as you can with constant distractions throwing you off track. It is scary like hell but after the first shift you'll hopefully be more prepared and used to the mischievous demons and their little mind-games. Just show them who is boss and you'll hopefully be OK!Very graphic (obviously), visually realistic/pleasing and lots of jump-scares, but there's no combat and you can mostly do everything in your own pace, which I really appreciate for games like this.Highly recommended!

Once it finished downloading, I started the game up and only spent 25 minutes playing it before I freaked out and turned it off.  The atmosphere itself was enough to do me in! I admit I wouldn't say I liked messing with dead bodies once I began playing the game. That alone was enough to make my skin crawl. Then you add a bit of ghost activity, find out a Demon is after you, and have to find a way to get rid of said Demon or risk being consumed by it for eternity! It's a lot to throw at you all at once! With all that being said, this game was terrifying, and I did scream a few times during game play. It builds up suspense and makes you not want to go into the next room when you hear voices. Even if it's a jump-out-and-scare-you game, the timing is perfect, making your heart race! The perfect horror game, indeed! I do recommend this game. Happy Demon Hunting!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I'LL HAVE TO REVISE THIS BECAUSE I GUESS SINCE I LAST PLAYED THE GAME 2 WEEKS AGO A BUNCH OF CONTENT WAS ADDED SOEDIT 2: Continued my save file only for it to freeze on the inventory screen right as I was about to burn the body :))),Very mixed feelings about this game. I really enjoyed the concept and the execution of the game, especially considering I at first glance thought this was a kitschy, cheaply made little horror game made for streamers to scream at (you know the type), but was pleasantly surprised at the thought and effort put into this.However, I feel like it didn't live up to its potential. First of all, the game is super short, even if you play it multiple times to reach all the different endings it still doesn't take that long and the $25 asking price feels a bit insane to me. I got it on sale for $15 and that felt more fair.However I presume there  be more content added eventually since there achievements in the game you can't actually unlock yet. So that is nice. The game is made by a single dev afaik and so I'm sure it might take a while but I'm down to reassess the game when that happens.My biggest issue is the lack of content and the scariness factor. The game does absolutely have its horrifiyng moments, and some of the scares are pretty unique and well thought out, but it took only 2 or so games to start getting repetitive scares, and there also were just  enough scares in the game in general. Atmosphere is top notch at first, but it really starts to wane when you realize after a two playthroughs (which a single play-through you can finish in like 30 minutes, though my first took probably took an hour and a half) that there are very few time when something will actually happen. There were an infinite amount of times during my first games where I got in my head about the atmosphere and thought something scary could happen at any time or around any corner, but the scares quickly became easy to predict, and I feel there were SO MANY MISSED OPPORTUNITIES FOR TERRIFYING MOMENTS THAT JUST WERE NOT UTILIZED THE WAY THEY COULDVE BEEN. Makes me want to make a horror game (somehow lol) to implement the vision. Idk, the game was good there just isnt  to make it worth the price. Brilliant concept though, and fun enough if you get it on sale. Top notch atmosphere and the gameplay revolving around having to slowly and patiently embalm bodies (among other things I wont spoil) while hoping nothing will get you as you meticulously go about your business was great. there just needs to be a little more.

Although the developers obviously made the game so that you would learn and see more as you play through multiple times, it still seems to get a bit repetitive, especially when scare sequences are reused. And the concept of having to replay a relatively short game multiple times *feels* like a lazy tactic for developers to stretch out their gameplay (although I'm sure they did work very hard on this project, and it's otherwise really quite good for what it is). All that said, I did enjoy the game and would certainly recommend it to other horror game enthusiasts. However, the $25 price point seems a little too ambitious, and I'm glad I bought it on sale. $20 seems about right to me for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun and genuinely scary and is pretty unique compared to usual horror fare.  The entire experience takes place in a small mortuary where most of your time will be spent between the embalming room and the cold storage room.  Each 'shift' is different and pretty much randomized - the haunts are not the same and there seems to be many different ones.  Some are small like creepy faces peeking in at you through windows all the way up to full blown entities (one of which is in the top scariest things I've ever seen in a horror game and legit will haunt your nightmares.)  The pacing is also really good, you are on an unseen timer to complete your tasks which you can 'check' with an item in your inventory - when you start the night it will just be small things like tapping at the window and lights flickering but as the night progresses the haunts get more intense and hard to ignore.  All in all I've really enjoyed this game and it has a high replay value.  I can't wait for updates with more haunts, cadavers etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Delve into the somber depths of The Mortuary Assistant, a game that dares to tread upon unsettling grounds with an unapologetic allure. The experience, while initially challenging, thrives on the elusive pursuit of confronting demons, a task that resonates with a gratifying sense of difficulty. What sets this game apart is its narrative complexity, where each ending unfurls layers of a profound and haunting tragedy, enticing players to revisit and unearth its melancholic depths.Visually arresting scenes, though disquieting, captivate the senses with their intricacy, drawing players into a realm where discomfort intertwines with fascination. The game's ability to evoke unease while immersing players in a narratively rich environment is both commendable and unnerving. It's a testament to its ability to engage on multiple levels, offering an experience that is as disturbing as it is compelling. I found myself captivated by the morbid elegance inherent in the game's style, as well as by the profound exploration of the inner workings of a mortuary.Yet, amidst its atmospheric prowess, there lies a slight repetitiveness that may diminish the overall impact for some. However, The Mortuary Assistant remains a commendable endeavor, offering not only a glimpse into the intricacies of its titular occupation but also a journey through distressing landscapes that leave a lasting impression on the psyche.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game to make you want to buy it?Well, The Mortuary Assistant has to be one of the best pieces of Horror I've played in recent years, because it achieves so much more than a cheap JPEG jumpscare here and there.The biggest praise for The Mortuary Assistant comes down to its generic atmosphere, it takes a relatively normal 'uncomfortable' topic, being death, and dials it up to 11. There is no point in The Mortuary Assistant where you as the player feel truly safe and comfortable, even outside of the game's haunts, the way it has built the environment is just unsettling, preventing you from feeling like you have a "safe space" at any point for what may come next.Following on from that we have the writing, whilst the Story may not be winning any literary awards of Genius, it's actually a great story. Especially within the genre. Without spoiling anything, the story actually serves to augment the horror, providing some very uneasy grounding for the player that further adds to the constant questioning you'll finding yourself doing. "Was this purely a haunt?" "was some of this true?" "who really am I?" "why am I seeing this?" are all questions you will ask yourself constantly as you play through which in my personal opinion only adds to the incredible atmosphere this game creates. It even takes the time to ground some of the 'things' you see in the haunts with lore, so you feel more uneasy when you see these things, because there is a subconscious link in your mind that then attaches some 'reality' to the thing you're seeing. (Today I learned it's hard to write about a horror story without spoiling it).If I had to pick one flaw, it's a flaw I often pick when I'm reviewing games, The Achievements. 100 Bodies and 50 Burns is a big ask. At the time of this writing I have done 5 shifts and have almost all of the endings and have seen most of the haunts 2/3 times at this point. So pushing for those two achievements will takes some time, however as you can blitz through a shift pretty quickly, it's not a huge real time sink. Just repetitive. HOWEVER to give this beautiful title the benefit of the doubt, it was made by one person, and perhaps we will see even more events and haunts added to the game to further increase the variety that you can experience, if that happens, not even this flaw will apply.To summarise:Pros:-- A story written with a degree of care to compliment the horror instead of ruin it- A great variety of experiences for the first few playthroughs- An absolute gem of atmospheric eerieness and a masterclass in horror elements.- Soundtrack, where it exists, also pretty spoopy.Cons:-- Does get a little repetitive- 100 body/50 burns achievement is a grindI can't recommend this game enough though. Get it. Seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to be fair and wait a few weeks before adding a review, so that this single dev could have a chance to squash some game-breaking bugs. So far, he's been very dedicated, diligent, and communicative about it so that's already a plus for the review as a whole. This might be the scariest game of 2022. It has a good balance of jump scares, creepy ambiance, and tension. The story is interesting, albeit simple. If you manage to find the right secret, the story will expand in a way that makes it even more disturbing. DO NOT RELY ON SPOILERS! Avoid the forum discussion as much as you can and find everything yourself. Some points to make:- No, the bodies are not naked. This takes away from the realism of being a mortician, but the dev wants his game to reach a wider audience. While unfortunate, it's a fair compromise. - This is not a mortician simulator. The actual embalming gameplay is simple and streamlined, and is just there to give you something to do to move the story and scares along. Do not judge the game for something it was never designed to be. - At present, this game has limited replay-ability. Once you've done about 6 or more shifts, and you've found everything that you can do, you've pretty much burned out any reason to go back to it. Some games are just like that, but it was still a hell of a ride. - The dev has future plans to add to the game to expand replay-ability, but I have to review it for what it is today, not tomorrow. Pros: Extremely frightening and interesting story to keep you going until the end. Cons: Finite replay-abilityWish I could go back and do it all over again for the first time. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: When you deal with a lot of trauma, the last thing you need in life is an awful boss who won't tell you that the paycheck comes with a duty to fight off demons. But this is exactly what happened to our MC, and now we have to help her fulfill her nightly responsibilities while saving her soul.Pros:- the game is great in keeping you uneasy (people with vivid imagination, have fun playing it at night, in an old house where you can hear every step and crack, which is how I did it);- the story has its own lore, it's interesting to explore it;- more details as you progress through all endings;- haunting events are fun and creepy in a good, chilling way;- MC's story tackles important subjects. such as guilt, grief, and recovery;- winning against the demon is very satisfying.Cons:- even after the Definitive edition, the game is somewhat buggy. I got locked out of doing anything two or three times (which can be solved by reloading, but it is frustrating because the reload can take much of your progress in the shift);- really hate one of the endings (it paints MC as kinda stupid);- 2 very boring achievements that basically need you to play 50 shifts. _childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant.When I play this game I can't help but remember a series of books I read years ago. "I Am Not a Serial Killer", by Dan Wells. I'll leave some quotes here:“Embalming was like... I don't know how to describe it. It was like playing with a giant doll, dressing it and bathing it and opening it up to see what was inside.”"Is a Demon your best friend?" - Mills said."Look who suddenly got judgmental." - John said.On the other hand, I've always thought that it'd be interesting to work in a mortuary or funeral home. And this game gives you that little experience in a simpler way of what it'd be like to have a job like that. Furthermore, you have to discover which body is possessed by the demon and get rid of it, but not before finding out its name. Sounds fun, right?At first it was a little difficult for me to play. I tried to use control but couldn't. When I wanted to change the button configuration, something happened and I simply couldn't. On the other hand, I didn't like the default keys on keyboard so I changed them to my liking and was able to play properly. When you know exactly what to do and how to proceed, that makes everything easier, although the game itself is quite simple.Although the dynamic is the same on each shift and THIS for many players would be repetitive, for me it's not like that. After 20 hours and having gotten all the endings multiple times, the game still surprises me with new scares and manifestations. You always discover something new. I like this very much. There really is a great variety of manifestations. You can see the dedication of the developer here. The game is so well designed that it makes you feel part of it. I wonder if it could be compared to those "Enigma Rooms". If there was one with a Morgue/Mortuary theme, I'm in!It's a different, fascinating and immersive experience. You'll feel watched all the time, and when you let your guard down, BOOM, there's "he" or "she" or.. Corpses walking strangely in the Hallway or corpses levitating while on the "analysis table" or arms pointing places.This game varies mainly in certain events related to the past of our protagonist Rebecca, and the visions that she sees, these being a way of the demon to scare you, break you and make you give up and forget your main purpose: find out its name, the body in the mortuary that is possessed and burn it.I love the fact that the bodies smile in a macabre way sometimes, these are almost always the possessed ones, however, it can also be a deception. Pay attention and use the  wisely.Most of the "scares" are demonic presences, and they're so subtle, that when you realize them it's normal to be a little surprised. Even when they're silent.This game teaches you that the devil is in the details. You turn around to take the Formaldehyde or Methanol, and suddenly the corpse in front of you quickly moves some limb or levitates in the air.The game in general is very good, however, sometimes there are small bugs. In any case, just go back to the Main Menu and continue.The voices are good, especially Raymond Delver and his.. Possessed mother.This game was a gift from a good friend. I appreciate it, it's one of my favorites now. I highly recommend it, and it's even better if you increase the frequency of "Hauntsystem Aggressiveness". I love it! (not recommended if you have heart problems). But be careful. After a few games (shifts) in a roll, the time seems to be reduced and not enough, so you lose faster before embalming the third corpse, or so it has happened to me. Somehow ignoring certain events like phone calls and dark shadows calling you prevent you from 'unfocusing' on your mission, so.. Avoid them.This game will definitely be in my "💙" collection.Conclusion 1: The game is great and the demons are trolls.Conclusion 2: I'm ready to work in a Mortuary. PS: I'll wait patiently for Halloween and Christmas.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like the game, but it just got stale really fast. It doesn't help that a lot of things are incredibly vague, especially when it comes to the achievements. "Obtain all endings", which there's a tally for 5 endings, but it doesn't unlock (there's a hidden 6th ending that I have yet to find I guess). Had a bug where you have to essentially lose to unlock an achievement, which that didn't pop. There's a hidden achievement that can only be obtained during the very beginning, and if it's missed the only way to achieve it is by resetting game data. At least it's in the beginning, but it's a bummer that you lose out on any endings/embalming/burning that were accumulated before realizing you were locked from the game. Achievements aside, the RNG components may or may not trigger, or specific clues may not appear. I've had symbols not appear after burning letting slips, or a box where they should appear just appear as empty. Specific events may trigger repeatedly between shifts, while there may be other events that you've yet to see that you've just not encountered the right RNG for. There's different variations of some of the major events, which was really awesome to encounter for the first time. After the 4th or 5th time I was just going through the motions to end them faster so I could progress through the achievement.There were multiple times I was soft-locked out of the game. Things like not positioning the gurney just right which makes it so you can't pass, an event where a figure appears that doesn't disappear even when looking at it (the ones that you don't engage with), or getting to a spot to use items but the right-click menu doesn't appear (the coins in the hands is where I was locked out).I may try the game again at a later time. I put 7 hours which came out to 6 shifts (which I did three times, it never progressed past 6). Eventually I was just rushing through the motions, and the game stopped being fun. I don't really want to give it a thumbs down, because you can tell there was some effort put into the game, but when the core gameplay loop just repeats the same motions over and over, and there's a good chance that you'll experience some type of bug which can ruin a run entirely, the game just stopped being fun.I'd say for someone not going after all the achievements, you'll get a solid 4 hours out of the game before it gets old.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm personally a huge fan of horror games. Ranging from jump scares to a consistent feeling of dread and tension, many good horror games tend to capitalize on these elements and Mortuary Assistant isn't any different. Even after so many playthroughs where I start automatically doing the tasks, there are audio cues, things out of the corner of my eye, and quick jumps that still get to me no matter how long I play the game. Early on there were a few bugs (like every game) but the developers have done such a good job at weeding them out and squashing them. Every once in a great while I'll be soft locked out of a task and, when exiting and entering, might have to redo some stuff, but honestly it's otherwise really well done.My biggest complaint, I guess, would be that the story-driven events/scares and exposition can happen too frequently. In the game you can be hit with audio and visual clues, jump scares, etc. but your character, Rebecca, has her own story and some events happen that progress that story. Unfortunately there are a lot of times in which the same "big" story-driven events happen several times in the course of a few nights in a row or repeat. When this happens, I normally just bide my time until it's over.

_childDocuments_.review: I've found the game to be a solid horror experience so far, and I'm enjoying it! There are some solid jumpscares which are made scarier by the overall unsettling atmosphere of the game. As far as gameplay is concerned, it's a very focused simulator/puzzle experience (embalm three corpses, but burn the right one before the timer ends). However, once you have it down, it works well to allow you to start exploring some of the other secrets in the game. I've completed the game twice (failed the first, and figured it out the second time), and both times had revealed different bits of lore and story. In terms of shortcomings, I will say that there isn't much sense of danger beyond the timer (at least none that I've found so far). You either run out of time or burn the wrong body. This might not be a problem for someone primarily looking for a puzzle-solving experience, but might be a bit dull for others. Overall, I'm looking forward to getting the other endings and finding out the rest of Rebecca's story!

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the unfortunate opportunity to play "The Mortuary Assistant," and it was an absolute disaster. This game is so infested with bugs and technical issues that it is virtually unplayable. From start to finish, my gaming experience was marred by constant glitches and frustrating problems that prevented me from enjoying the game in any meaningful way.First and foremost, the game suffers from severe performance issues. Even on a high-end gaming rig, the frame rate would frequently drop to unbearable levels, causing significant stuttering and lag. It was as if the game was struggling to keep up with even the most basic actions. This not only hampered the immersion but also made the gameplay frustratingly sluggish.Furthermore, the game was plagued with numerous game-breaking bugs. Quest objectives would often fail to trigger, leaving me stranded without any direction. NPC interactions were riddled with glitches, causing characters to freeze or disappear altogether. These issues made progressing through the game an exercise in frustration and wasted a considerable amount of my time.The controls in "The Mortuary Assistant" were also a nightmare. They were unresponsive and clunky, making it incredibly difficult to execute even the simplest actions.On top of all these technical issues, the game's visuals were subpar at best. Poorly rendered textures, bland environments, and lackluster character models made for an unappealing visual experience. It felt like I was playing a game from a decade ago, rather than a modern release.To make matters worse, the developer's support for "The Mortuary Assistant" was practically non-existent. Despite numerous bug reports and requests for assistance, there was no response or acknowledgment from the development team. This lack of support left players to fend for themselves, struggling to find workarounds or fixes for the game-breaking issues.In conclusion, "The Mortuary Assistant" is a prime example of a game that is simply not ready for release. The overwhelming number of bugs, technical issues, and poor performance make it an unplayable mess. The lackluster visuals and unresponsive controls only add to the frustration. Save yourself the headache and steer clear of this buggy nightmare of a game.

Your first or second run through the game might be fun or spooky, but the repetitiveness sets in insanely fast. I've gone through the cycle a few times already and am bored to tears. I wanted to 100% the game but there's no way I can stomach it any longer. The scariest thing about this game is how much it wastes your time with mind numbing tasks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I'm seriously enjoying this game, which ended up being even better than what I expected from the demo! I really appreciate being able to have a direct, somewhat realistic experience of embalming and mortuary practices. I felt a bit overwhelmed with the demon hunting mechanics at first, but I feel like it's very easy to get comfortable with them and get into the rhythm of it all. What I'm a bit disappointed about, tho, is that it feels a little... Too easy? I know a lot of people seem to be struggling with identifying demons and which body is being possessed, but if you're NOT having troubles with it at all like I am, it feels honestly too easy. I would love to be able to pick a higher difficulty level. For instances, you can keep windows open, and that's never quite used in the gameplay (putting aside the few events where an "enemy" will be watching you from outside the window). I would love to see, for example, windows being open at random moments and having to patrol them, otherwise the demon would be able to attack you and slow you down... It's just an example obviously! I feel like there could be more to this game, is all. But it's a hard recommend from me!

_childDocuments_.review: Length: First Playthrough <2hrs then 15min - 1hr per run.A Horror game that in reality is somewhere between a simulation game and a puzzle game, while having a fairly interesting narrative behind it. Throughout the game the player will be playing as a Mortician preparing the deceased, this is fairly simple to do in game, though is well made. Collect the body from the back, place it on the mortician slab, inspect the body and then find the tools you need from in the room to perform each action on the check list. You have multiple different tasks needed for the body, and it feels realistic in the game. Honestly 10+ bodies in and I was still finding it fun, you just get into the rhythm of doing it, and the hauntings really break the monotony.Each night the player will have three bodies they need to work on, the problem is one of these bodies is possessed and if you take too long or burn the wrong body the demon will possess you. Identifying which body is the puzzle, you only have one attempt. While the game may seem confusing at first it really is not, it’s like starting a new board game, the rules overload you but the game is fairly simple. Beyond the tasks of the mortician working out which body is possessed is really simple. While in game it does not clearly tell you, I’ll give you a quick overview below.Spoiler StartFollow the rules of SIT for easy Possessed hunting.Search - Using the Letting Slips search around the mortuary till it catches on fire this will reveal a sigil somewhere around where it immolates. There are four that will appear each night, though they spawn gradually throughout the night, one will already be there when you arrive. Once you have enough use the night computer and match up the four found to the correct demon, this will also identify the demon's house.Identify - While dealing with the bodies you will notice haunting happen, while playing you need to identify which of the bodies are causing the most paranormal events. I always found that one body will basically have nothing happen, and will ignore it leaving two bodies to choose from. Keep an eye out for new injuries appearing on the bodies; this can be from big slices across the chest to small injuries across the wrists. These injuries can already be on the body when you bring it from cold storage, and can be identified as you can not select them when doing the initial body check.Test - Once you know the demon, then choose the body you think is most likely possessed, gather the match from the front, ash in a bag from the back furnace and place the body on the mortuary slab. Chuck the ash on the body, ignite with the match to reveal the demon house. If the house matches the demon you know. Chuck the sigils onto the tablet, slap it onto the chest and burn it. Got the wrong house come up, well you have a 50% chance that the other body is the correct one.Follow SIT and you should be good, once I worked out this method it became really easy to complete the night.Spoiler EndThe haunting moments happen throughout the game, and these are some of the best horror moments I have seen in games. The frigid movements, combined with the creepy appearance, it’s like the developer drowned in the best J-Horror movies, while taking some of the creepier moments of modern horror. This really has made for some of the best visual horror moments I have seen in any horror game I’ve played. You can’t fight me on this, this year alone I have played more than 500 horror games and recorded them,I know my spooky moments. The combination of the amazing horrors that haunt you throughout the nights, distracting you from your tasks really makes for a fun experience. While comparatively to the previous works on Darkstone Digital, the puzzles are ok, there is no comparison to Our Secret Below, just the perfect escape room game. Honestly even though I would say the Mortuary Assistant is a great game, the horror moments are amazing, and really the mortician job was engaging. It just really felt like the demo was still the better experience. While there are a lot more different hauntings in the base game, they are not as active. There are not creepy things happening whenever you turn your back and if anything it feels really spaced out. Honestly still it is worth playing both, just someone who has played the full game really check out the demo, the game just feels different.Now, is the game worth buying, that is a resounding yes. The Mortician job is designed well so that it neither drags or is unengaging. The haunting is amazing and makes the little horror child in me scream for freedom, while the puzzles are not as strong and really if you read the spoilers now nonexistent for you the game is still fun enough. I really recommend you play the other games by Darkstone Digital, while the Subject is not an impressive game, Our Secret Below is a phenomenal game that really deserved more attention.Below is my playthrough to those stuck, or simply want to be generous with your time: Those looking for the Spoopiest of horror can check out my curator page, it is growing and will be one of the largest horror pages on Steam:

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard of this game back when Dazplays had showed the original demo on Youtube and had been looking forward to this game for a while. One of my partner's gifted it to me for my birthday during the Halloween sale and I absolutely love this game. I love the story line and the graphics went above and beyond from the demo. The game eerie and every time I thought I had seen all the scares, something new would appear. I bet despite having done over 50 runs there is still stuff I haven't seen. (I really hate the pale white mimic ghost, something about his eyes and mouth just makes my skin crawl.) I like how the items would rotate between at least for different layouts so you didn't get too comfortable with their placement so the grind for the achievements didn't get boring either.I like how the game adds Holiday content for Halloween and Christmas as well, such a neat little touch to add.My only "problem" I'd have with the game is the numbers needed for the "Light Em UP!" achievement vs "Well Preserved." For "Well Preserved" it takes 32-33 runs to preserve that many bodies (that's including the bodies you get to do in the intro.) but for "Light Em UP!" you need to burn 50 bodies. That is a ratio of 3 to 1 for that achievement which means you'll only have had 32-33 bodies burnt by the time you hit "Well Preserved" so that's 17 more additional runs you need to do to burn a body. While you can just enter a shift, leave your house, get out of the car and just beeline to open the doors, grab the gurney and pick a body to throw in the furnace, you can't skip the cut scenes. So, you're stuck  (which takes about five minutes each time) and then rinse and repeating for an hour or so. I feel like the number should be lowered to about 40 bodies preserved if you want to keep some of that grind but be more generous. That's just my opinion though.Despite that I really recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of horror and finds a lot of the games recently put out don't hit that mark. The game is fantastic and really unique in it's play style. 8/10

_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING! I have been playing since DAY 1 and honestly I am NOT really a fan of Horror Games, but that doesn't stop me from trying them out at least and this is the first one that I have ever put over 100hrs into. Even if you are not a horror fan, this game is well worth having. The atmosphere is extremely eerie and its what a lot of us would imagine a Mortuary to be like at night mixed with all the thoughts we may have with working as a Mortician. There are jump scares, and plenty of them.....the Mimic on the other hand is just simply goofy....goofy looking, shows up in goofy places, and just an all around goof....now with that being said, there are still some times where he may scare the hell out of you. Since the game changes each time you plan, you can never really plan for whats to come, which makes the game even more interesting. With each playthrough, nearly everything changes, from chemicals and instruments being in different locations to strange events occurring in places they haven't occurred in before. Just when you got used to all of your things being in the same place, it will be placed in areas you wouldn't expect them to be in, which can sometimes cause you to overlook something that you may need. There may be times where you just want to pause and take a small break from the game, possibly to prep for an upcoming scare, or you paused because you heard a noise in the backroom. That could potentially be a decent safe haven for some horror games, but not with this one. Things can STILL occur....or worse, change all together....and STILL scare the hell out of you at a different time than when you thought it would. Mortuary Assistant is one of my top favorite games, which says a lot being the fact that no Horror game has ever been a favorite of mine. If your read my review up to this far, then take my word.....and DEFINITELY get this game. This is also my very first review, so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely scary horror game with a morbid gameplay mechanic that forces your attention onto methodical step by step processes on cadavers so when the scares hit they hit hard. My only complaints are that a couple of environments you can interact with don't feel a bit janky and the inventory system is too small for the amount of items you're expected to carry. The process of taking a body out of cold storage and transferring it to a gurney never felt as smooth as it should and when filing bodies you cannot carry the clipboard and the file since the game counts both of those items as 'large' items.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided just to rewrite this review! The Mortuary Assistant has turned out to be my all time favorite horror game, and it makes it onto my top 3 list of favorite games from all genres. I'm a fan of horror movies, books, games, etc, and I don't scare easily. But even after playing this game for almost two years I still jump occasionally!The lore is very rich and well written. There is a lot to discover. I still enjoy resetting the intro and replaying each of the 6 possible endings every few months. The characters have excellent dimension. I am bummed that the developer is going to do one more update and then move on from this game. _childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a fairly simple game on the surface, and draws from the typical horror walking simulator that we're all familiar with (think the Slender era of horror games). That said it meshes that with just enough tasks to keep the player busy and distracted to create the sort of lulls that make the scares really work! The randomness of events and scares does a lot to make each shift unique and enjoyable, I'd say it'll take at least 6 shifts before you see something twice, and even then that doesn't mean you've seen it all. The sound is at its best when going unnoticed. The smaller details like having to walk backwards with the gurney, or focus zoom on the computer compliments the random nature of the scares imo as well. As far as criticisms I have 3: Each ending is relatively the same, not a dealbreaker by any means I would've enjoyed more variety is all, the mouse sensitivity setting didn't seem to work for me and I had to lift up my mouse 2 or 3 times to turn around, and I experienced a few bugs that caused me to have to restart, that said I did play on release and at least the latter 2 issues I'm sure will be fixed in time.TL;DR Great spooky game, good for at least 7 times around if you're uncertain I say buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I advise playing this game, one shift a day or week or every two weeks. I am a scaredy cat and I assure you the game is creepy and scary. The supplies to embalm the bodies are always in a different spot at random so that you can't get bored with knowing what to do ASAP. I love that kind of puzzle aspect of embalming the corpses. Since I'm a scaredy cat too, part of the puzzle becomes pushing through being freaked out. I did try playing this game three or four days in a row and the game became quite a bit less scary. I recommend playing it every few weeks, show it to a friend one day, end a date night with it one day, show your kid nephew or niece it one day, etc is the best way to keep it scary. It's great because of the shifts and their length, you can pick it up at any time. Players who sit down to sink 30 consecutive hours or some such are the critics of the game in my opinion. If the creator sees it, I have had a blast scaring myself while my fiancee laughs at me. I really would love to see a MA2 with even more events. Also how about creepy normal events? For example a deer staring at you outside the window and it merely walks away? A bird hitting the window. Plumbing bursting, light bulbs blowing and needing replacement. I think incorporating the outside would be so scary too. Hearse pick ups and body delivery could add a corpse into the mix and give chances for outdoor haunting scares.

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game with PLENTY of scares and a surprisingly extensive backstory that is revealed the longer you play the game!I recently purchased this game for my Halloween Subathon and we probably played this game a majority of the time! _childDocuments_.review: This game is my new standard for what a great horror game can do. I've played Outlast, Amnesia, Resident Evil, and while they all have their appeal in different niches, this game is the real leader in the horror genre. Spoiler free review.So the story starts with Rebecca, as the title suggests, the new mortuary assistant. The game has a unique way of telling the story that honestly can't easily be described without spoilers so I'll simply say that I'm very impressed. It's something I'd easily point to as how horror games should introduce their backstories. It's dark, it's raw, and the game doesn't shy away from the disturbing parts of peoples lives. The game has multiple endings and it is definitely worth it to replay the game to get them all for the story.You spend each night doing accurate, if somewhat simplified, mortuary tasks as you embalm bodies. Although it's a rather simplified version of the real life job, it's definitely accurate in what it does. The horror aspect takes place at the same time you're trying to work and it flows together really well. The one negative aspect is that controller support is a bit awkward, but not game breaking.The graphics are entirely average. It's built in unity and it clearly isn't a big budget title. They aren't bad by any means, but it's not something that's going to stress any modern hardware. The game runs well and looks decent enough.I never really consider sound design outside of soundtracks when I talk about games, but this is something that deserves it. From the background noises to the demons, everything works really well to constantly give off a creepy vibe and I love it.Overall, this game is a 10/10 for fans of horror. As a complete video game for general players, I'd still give it an 8/10. Great story, good gameplay with some controller issues, and average graphics. I haven't run into any bugs yet, and I definitely plan on going back to play for all the endings.
