_childDocuments_.review: To the Developer, Bravo Zulu. this game has been fun to play and explore. there are plenty of reviews going discussing some of the cons of the game which i agree with particularly the not being able to multitask nor make mistakes but the scares are positively wonderful. i started the game and after about 5 minutes i needed to take a break. eventually i came back and played. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not a horror game buff, but I do enjoy solving puzzles/mysteries, and I also enjoy this developer's take on achievements in both this and another game of theirs called Kohate.So with the multiple endings and various bits of story to find and uncover, I have enjoyed quite a bit of replayability.Without spoiling the story, I would say I found the contents of those parts plus some of the backstory pieces of how the mortuary got into this state way more harrowing and gritty / adult than anything else, plus I'm not really phased by pure gore/horror/jumpscares anyway.The embalming process is a 'task', once you get over the gruesomeness of the activities and have done them a number of times, they do become fairly routine.I don't have a problem with that though.  I feel like this task could be viewed just like those you come across in games like Among Us - the tasks themselves aren't the core of the game's longevity, they're just a distraction to force you into multitasking, to put you under some time pressure, and so causing you to make the occasional mistake.  Still, you got to get them done, can't just skip them in order to make the game easier.I did bump into a few bugs/issues when playing the first few days but a flurry of patches took care of the worst ones and the quality seems to continue to improve with time.

They also continue to update and add fun holiday and seasonal aspects to the game as well as a NEW ending! I'm looking forward to seeing if they add any more to the story as it seems like the devs have left it open for more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: So, before giving an honest review, I'd be hard-pressed to say it's worth the full $25. If it's on sale, absolutely snatch it up! If it's not, read the rest and decide if it's worth it for you.I appreciate how this game gets away from every other Ghost Hunting/Horror Indie game that has bombarded the market. I absolutely love those games, but as others have stated, sometimes I want to do mundane task and not run around with a spirit box shouting obscenities. It's eerie, creepy, and the jump scares are fun. It's definitely something easy to stream and enjoyable to watch others play. It's pretty straight forward, and depending on the demon/you choices, it does have some variety. But that's also where it bottlenecks itself. With only 5 endings and only so many events that can occur, the game isn't much fun playing more than 2 or 3 times. It becomes repetitive super quick and though it has enough difference between endings to make it worth grinding it through to get them all, the initial novelty wears off and the jump scares become a bit predictable.Absolutely buy it on sale. At full price, I'd maybe give it 4 out of 5. I will continue to play it and stream it because it's fun, especially with an audience to interact with you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Becoming an employee of a mortuary, where you can work as an exorcist as an unwanted "sidekick" is possible in the game The Mortuary Assistant. In terms of the story, the introduction smacks of a particular cliché. Apparently, the creators did not want to deal with the story so much as a different experience from the horror itself.In the introduction, you will get to know your job and the steps necessary to perform the given profession. Once you've nailed the initial training, it's time to tackle your first night shift. You already know here that the situation is a little different and that in addition to your work as a pathologist, you have to face the evil that lives in the morgue building. As a complete novice in the field of demonology and exorcism, you are provided with guidance from your superior, who has been involved in these fields for several years.Most of the instructions are straightforward and clear, others require you to wade through a sort of homemade wikipedia system available on the morgue computer. Here, I sometimes had trouble deciphering what the author wanted to say. Basically, there are a few types of demons and a few names. The goal is to find the right one and perform the exorcism. In the meantime, you can "calmly" go about your work.As I understand it, each kind of demon haunts in a different way. I had the feeling that the game tried everything possible on me. Not to mention that among the various ways of being scared, there was actually one that had a big effect on me. So horror enjoyment is great for me. I got what I expected.The game lasts about two hours. However, there are five different endings to how this night shift can turn out. Given the experience, I'm really looking forward to playing through the next playthrough and seeing what other conclusions might occur.My rating: 9.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool idea this game presents. Horror in a simulator is pretty innovative and the Mortuary Assistant excels in both departments. This game actually scared me which is an art lost in most modern horror games and I'm interested to keep playing and get all the endings. The simulator mechanics are super in depth but can get a bit monotonous when you just can't seem to stop getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ possessed.My only major gripes are finding which body contains the demon can be a little convoluted and the decoy scares when you're looking for tells can really throw you off track. I also wish there was a little more to the Mortuary itself, whether they add a chapel or some kind of catacombs. I think the demonic lore of the Mortuary can be better fleshed out and hope at some point that can come to fruition.Either way this is a refreshing horror full of plenty of scares and story beats that keep you invested. I'm excited to see more from these devs in the future.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't worth the price. I'll avoid spoilers as I explain why this game should only be purchased on a heavy sale.If you play the demo you have done literally everything that the gameplay has to offer. The game is divided into "shifts", each shift you are responsible for embalming 3 different bodies and then trying to figure out which body is possessed by the demon. While embalming these bodies, you have different "horror" encounters where the demon will do something creepy or pull you into some other horror scene for a short time. This is all the gameplay has to offer. Each shift you are doing the same exact things gameplay wise and the only difference between these shifts are the horror moments you encounter. However, it's very common for you to experience the same exact horror moments you experienced in a previous shift (I experienced the same horror moments in my second shift that I experienced in my first shift, which cheapens the whole experience). For as simple of mechanics and gameplay as this game has, it also does a terrible - TERRIBLE - job at explaining these mechanics. It goes through an obtuse approach of using a pc in game to explain how you are supposed to decipher which body is possessed and has multiple web pages that literally take time to load. Why the hell would they not make changing webpages instantaneous is beyond me, I'm assuming to probably to pad out the game time length. Half of these webpages are entirely irrelevant by the way, but when you start playing the game you don't actually know which ones are relevant so you end up reading all of them. This makes what should be a very simple explanation of the mechanics into an affair that takes anywhere between 10-30 minutes depending on how fast you read. The mechanics are so simple they couldve been explained in less than a minute. There's a mechanic in the game where you can use a match and a bag of ashes to eliminate one body as the potential possessed, but it doesn't explain this mechanic really at all. If you use the match and ashes on the wrong body - welp you're kinda out of luck now cause there's only one match in the game. Guessing between the other two bodies is pretty much 50/50 cause what the game states as examples of a possessed body (random markings on the body or the body moving) can appear on bodies that aren't possessed as well. One of my playthroughs none of my bodies moved except for one, and the one that moved had random markings appear on it so of course I ended up thinking this was the possessed one so I burned it and, low and behold, it was the wrong body and I ended up getting possessed. So deciding which body is the correct one becomes a 50/50 guessing game where its seemingly random.The description of the game says it has 10 hours worth of content - but this isn't even close to being true. I have less than 3.6 hrs on record and already have most of the endings. I also had a weird bug where the mark I left on my first body disappeared randomly and I spent like 40 minutes looking for it before giving up, so realistically I have more like 3 hours. The remaining endings I already know the solutions for so I could knock those out in less than an hour probably. Best case scenario this game has somewhere between 4-5 hours worth of content, and of those 4-5 hours you are doing the exact same thing the entire time, with the only difference being some different scripted moments that you get to see. Buy this game when it's like 10 dollars or less, besides that it's not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If your horror game can't make the player feel like they're fighting for their life, then it failed as a horror game.I won't fault this game for being made by a small team of developers, since I'm sure that making a working game is no easy task. That being said: I was told that this game would scare the hell outta me. I came away from this game feeling nothing but disappointment. I'd put most of the blame on YouTube gamers' word of mouth, likely trying to boost their view counts by attracting the attention of kids who wouldn't know descent horror if it slapped them in the face. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me.It delivered a few jump-scares and a halfway decent story, but that was about it. The embalming process starts off as disturbing and morbid, but it loses its novelty fast and you get desensitized to it (like an actual morgue tech would, I'd imagine). In order to identify the demon possessing a cadaver. you need to use an item with the correct runes. In order to accomplish this, I'd recommend drawing those runes on actual pieces of paper, in order to keep track. The game has 7 endings total, which does give it some replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: ⚠️Spoilers ahead. If you didn't watch YouTube, read the wiki, or explore other reviews, be warned.⚠️📝 TL;DRLet's play Sam Raimi's non-endorsed The Mortuary Assistant of the Evil Dead. This game has you helping a Mortuary owner but things take a turn in that you're actually being recruited to be exorcist of the dead. Can you properly identify the correct corpse that one of the many demons is hiding is, or are you going to be it's perfect living host? The game is is creepy, unsettling, and at times campy, but very soon becomes worn out and tedious. Voice action and atmospheric music, or droning, helps sets the scenes. and immersion. There really is no replay-ability past getting the endings. This is not to say it isn't fun, which it definitely it, but after getting most of the endings and getting all the events and encounters, the game or experience is done. Now for the serious take...🎨 AestheticWhen playing a few games, you'll notice that there are a limited number of corpse models, I think 7, so they can come off as just generic bodies after a while and give less immersion. The design of certain possessed corpses appears to be a homage to Sam Raimi's the Evil Dead. The general design of the game isn't too realistic but isn't plastic or generic either. 🔈 SoundsI feel the voice acting is very well done, nearly natural as if it was dialogue in a movie and not reading from scripts. The voice acting and dialogue of some corpses, I won't mention which, are partially reminiscent of Sam Raimi's the Evil Dead. This is definitely a game that is needed to be played with headphones as the atmospheric sounds are directional and sometimes can be really low to nearly miss-able to blatantly obvious. Sounds created by the player are nearly realistic, but repetitive with no variation, like all the windows or cabinets don't need to creek the exact same way. The music is atmospheric and at there's there is an ominous droning, adding the tension and unease.There wasn't much music other than from the radios found within the game that cheekily repeat, and repeat and repeat, but for gags. Throughout the game there is a slight underscore that plays, which turns into a tense droning when something is happening or about to happen, creating a feeling of tread and anxiety.⚙️ AssemblyThis is the tedious part. You're given a limited inventory to hold all that you need, so you'll find yourself going back and forth to grab items. You can only hold one of each item or can only hold one large item at a time along with your trusty clipboard. With some, you can't hold them at all until you need them. With time, things become easier with repetition, but even then trying to perform the actions of certain required steps are clunky and makes you want to bang your mouse to dislodge whatever might be stuck as you can't reach through the screen and do it yourself.Depending on certain actions of the previous play-through, there would be additional items to interact with. What is standard in the game is that, through a note found, it will be explained that tools and materials needed to perform your job are set up in randomized locations every play-though. This is never truly explained, as obviously this would take you longer to do your job and make it easier for time to run out and for you to get possessed. ❕ NOTE: This is my opinion and thoughts, not an overall view of the game for general audiences, as opinions and experiences vary. As with all reviews, take this as one of many viewpoints, and do your own research. _childDocuments_.review: For me, The Mortuary Assistant came out of nowhere and scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. Then it did it again, and it hasn't stopped yet. (minimal spoilers ahead)I'm obsessed with horror games (especially survival-horror), and this game arrived when I felt like I was running out of old and new spooky games to play (even through emulators), reduced to digging through mysterious indie demos and Doom/Half-Life mods and such. I've become desensitized though playing so many of these games and I thought nothing could really terrify me anymore, much less surprise me. Terrifying moments aside, what I find most surprising is either the sheer replayability of this non-action horror game, or the fact that it was CREATED BY ONE (1) PERSON (not counting VAs, publishers, etc).You can have a successful "shift," as runs through this game are called, on the first try in theory. You can even get each one of the endings in as many shifts. But the pressure and unpredictability never lets up. I'm 15-20 shifts in and while I can see certain spooky events coming now based on subtle signs, I'm still made very uneasy when the paranormal elephant in the room takes its time to show itself. I find the Resident Evil games very replayable, but even the least action-y of them lose their scare factor after the first run or two and become action roguelikes going for trophies. I've also replayed Outlast a few times, but The Mortuary Assistant still makes me feel as scared and defenseless as I did my first time playing that game.The lack of action elements, even though the game isn't really a walking simulator, should make it boring on paper. On the contrary it's extremely engaging and makes you want to get better at the embalming procedure to spite the dark forces harrassing you. The actual terror you face as the protagonist can't be fought directly. All you can do is go through the motions of a mortician on the night shift, and hope you've correctly identified the source of the increasingly unpleasant hauntings that you'll have to try your best to ignore before it's too late. It hasn't gotten old for me yet.The only evidence suggesting that this was developed solo is the somewhat disappointing variety of corpse models that randomly populate the morgue in threes on each shift, but I can tell this is being addressed gradually through updates. It's truly my only complaint about the game, period. The models that are there look great (for dead people, anyway), but it would be nice to see a wider range of body types and some new faces for the immersion. It makes me wonder if mods will ever be a thing for this game. There were only 5 or 6 different corpses when I started playing the game last month, and the Halloween update gave us three more. If there were closer to 20 models, I think this game would be just about perfect.To the dev, thank you very much for this game. To anyone else reading it, buy it already!

You have to FIGURE out which body is the proper body to cremate... only the signs are so subtle so minor so tiny you'd never figure it out. But NOPE! none of that for me! no markings, no indicators, nothing, so it became a guessing game... That reason alone turned me off of it big time. _childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant has lots of quality scares, an interesting story, enjoyable gameplay, and excellent graphics and sound design. It is a horror game that I would certainly recommend to horror enthusiasts. All of that should be said, and I do have some grievances with the game. I feel like the game does not do a good enough job of telling you how to tell which body is being possessed by the demon. I feel the database in the game tells you that ultimately, a body that moves or is more active is the one with the demon in it... or maybe not because demons like to play tricks. My first few shifts had a bunch of bad endings because I was relying on the information in the game - as soon as I looked up some IRL information about which happenings are actual tells of being possessed, I started doing fine. I think the game should do a better job at telling you what to look out for, even in small, subtle ways. However, after looking up a guide, I found the game to be very enjoyable and it somehow maintained its spook factor even after seeing the same events multiple times, which is honestly pretty impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like adventure/puzzle games, I highly suggest The Mortuary Assistant. I've been playing it nonstop for a good 2 weeks. It's massively replayable too. Everything is randomly generated every time you play. You don't have to worry about your aim, or running and hiding, it's all about figuring out the mystery. I particularly like it because of the slow burn each round has, and how perceptive you need to be to the point that you can start playing tricks on yourself and see clues that aren't there. It's extremely fun, I very much enjoy it. As someone who needs a lot to get scared by media, this one does the trick. Get it. You'll love it. It's exactly what you're looking for

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Solid voice acting- Doesn't swing into cheesy (demonic voices are easy to overdo, both in the VA and effects/filters departments)- Rock-solid scares. There's enough variety that you're never sure what will show up next (longer sequences aside). The atmosphere can get *very* taut sometimes and the design of the scares gives a much more cinematic feel than most other horror games I've played- The game looks good, especially for a small indie title. The bodies look "properly" dead, so there was some real effort put into the character models- Great soundtrack. The game overall isn't afraid to use silence to build tension. Cons:- The longer sequences can get repetitive- The mechanics aren't explained well, I didn't know about the match + ashes until I looked it up on a wiki. - The animations for the bodies on the gurney are really choppy sometimes when you're rotating their torso to look at their back- Hitboxes for light switches and other vital things could be made bigger for us plebs using gamepads rather than M+K- It would be nice if you could do the embalming in a slightly non-linear way. The best example would be using the moisturizing pad on the corpse's face *while* the tank cleaner is running through the machine, rather than having to wait until it's doneOverall, I *HIGHLY* recommend this game. The cons I mentioned are negligible to me. Adding to what I said about the design of the scares: some are very brief things you catch out of the corner of your eye or while you're walking past a cabinet, some are full apparitions, but the majority of them depend on you looking directly at them before any jump scare one-shots or soundtrack cues play (and sometimes they're omitted for just a visual scare). This really brought to mind the way the first Exorcist movie's scares were done. For an indie title especially I've been very impressed, most of them become very one-note very quickly. 6hrs into this game and with only one successful exorcism under my belt, I'll be heading back in for a lot more though. Also, in a strange way I find it comforting to perform the basic tasks of embalming a body; seeing the process even just on my TV screen demystifies the process of death. It's the same process, the same care is taken with all of them (assuming an ethical mortuary). The part at the end where you apply moisturizer to the face is a nice way to end the process too. It feels respectful.Great game. 8/10 from me, easy 9/10 with the minor fixes like I laid out in my Cons section. If you're a forensics nerd or love paranormal horror, you'll love this one.

_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Are you someone who loved House Flipper or Gas Station Simulator? Then you'll love The Mortuary Assistant! No, wait, come back! Hear me out!A big part of The Mortuary Assistant is having a predictable gameplay loop. The game gives you a clipboard with your "tasks," just like any other simulator game. There's something very comforting and soothing about knowing exactly what you need to do and how to get there, though unlike House Flipper, you're embalming a body instead of renovating a house. The basic gameplay loop satisfies that "simulator" itch......and then immediately subverts it with hauntings and demon infestations. You'll be minding your own business, mixing embalming fluids together or moisturizing the corpse, when the overhead lights will flicker or you'll hear the distant chime of the front door open or some unseen entity will rudely trip you in the hallway. You can ignore these distractions and carry on with your good work, but things escalate over time. That escalation is how the game's story unfolds, ultimately revealing its full self over each subsequent "shift."The story is pretty decent, though I'm not sure if all the questions I had really ever got answered. Ostensibly speaking, there are five official "endings" to unlock, but I think there might technically be more. No spoilers, but I did find one ending that was outside the five standard endings and broke one shift loop, leading me to assume that there might be more hidden endings. It's this drive to find all the secrets, along with the very satisfying "simulator" loop, that kept me digging around and trying out different things each shift on the hunt for more secrets.If you like simulator style games and enjoy getting spooped, give this game a shot! It's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a horror game this good in a very long time!Scary enough.Well-timed jumpscares and scares!Good story and good story lead-up.For the price, I think it does a lot of what you need, so it's worth the price!The graphics, the atmosphere and the mood are something amazing!The game is very grossly addictive and you won't even realize you're playing it even though it's scary!A must-have for those who love the horror genre and horror games!I think the character models, the map, and the gameplay are perfect!I didn't encounter any bugs in the game, and nothing annoying.Each replay has different scares, the objects you use are located differently, etc.So it's worth playing the game several times, if only because there are more endings!Hats off to the developers, I think this is a damn good game!I recommend it to everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: While some horror games have given me scares and unease, this is the rare game that actually gave me goosebumps and chills.The fear in this kind of game is driven by several subtle layers, rather than blatant gore and constant jumpscares.  Working on a cadaver is already an uncomfortable process, providing the unease of a medical setting with some mild body horror as you work your way through mundane, but kinda gross, tasks relating to your work.  This game's greatest strength is that it does an amazing job utilizing blink-and-you'll-miss-it spooks, where you might find yourself catching something out of the corner of your eye only for it to vanish when you turn to look at it.  Or perhaps you notice something horrifying has been perched in your workspace for God knows how long and you only just noticed it leering at you after all this time.  I really would like to see this dynamic explored more in horror games!This game follows has several different endings and some secrets to discover along the way.  The background lore is pleasantly deep and fleshed out, waiting for you to discover it by reading notes or browsing through an in-game database, or through flashbacks or hallucinations.  The storyline, such as it is, isn't entirely unique or unpredictable but it still remains satisfying to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few horror games with a unique concept and an almost accurate representation of how a mortician does their job excluding the game's gimmick of banishing demons. I'm almost convinced the dev either worked in the morgue or did a lot of research because I learnt so much of that line of work. For my experience playing through the first 5 shifts did tense me up while training myself to remember the steps which the game wonderfully does well on scaring you. The scare factor does lose its crunch if you try to go for the multiple endings since there is no skip cutscene button at all for every haunt that you encounter but the 5th ending is worth it just for a cry  if you manage to do the correct steps. The story itself is simple and effective at accomplishing a believable story of a I could see this game getting a sequel or maybe its a one time thing but if there's one thing to improve if a sequel does happen is to improve the gameplay loop since it does get repetitive seeing the same scares over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a game where you have a set tasking to do per play, and the world shifts around you as you attempt to uncover what demon residing in one of the three bodies you are set to embalm is trying to possess you. I wanted to wait until I got all 5 endings before posting a comment, because there are so many little things that really bring the atmosphere of the game out. The bottom line: Story 5/5Graphics 4/5Gameplay 4/5 (Had one bug where the PVC piping didn't fully connect and I had to restart the checkpoint)Scares 5/5Demon Possessions 666Let me in, Rebecca.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant.When I play this game I can't help but remember a series of books I read years ago. "I Am Not a Serial Killer", by Dan Wells. I'll leave some quotes here:“Embalming was like... I don't know how to describe it. It was like playing with a giant doll, dressing it and bathing it and opening it up to see what was inside.”"Is a Demon your best friend?" - Mills said."Look who suddenly got judgmental." - John said.On the other hand, I've always thought that it'd be interesting to work in a mortuary or funeral home. And this game gives you that little experience in a simpler way of what it'd be like to have a job like that. Furthermore, you have to discover which body is possessed by the demon and get rid of it, but not before finding out its name. Sounds fun, right?At first it was a little difficult for me to play. I tried to use control but couldn't. When I wanted to change the button configuration, something happened and I simply couldn't. On the other hand, I didn't like the default keys on keyboard so I changed them to my liking and was able to play properly. When you know exactly what to do and how to proceed, that makes everything easier, although the game itself is quite simple.Although the dynamic is the same on each shift and THIS for many players would be repetitive, for me it's not like that. After 20 hours and having gotten all the endings multiple times, the game still surprises me with new scares and manifestations. You always discover something new. I like this very much. There really is a great variety of manifestations. You can see the dedication of the developer here. The game is so well designed that it makes you feel part of it. I wonder if it could be compared to those "Enigma Rooms". If there was one with a Morgue/Mortuary theme, I'm in!It's a different, fascinating and immersive experience. You'll feel watched all the time, and when you let your guard down, BOOM, there's "he" or "she" or.. Corpses walking strangely in the Hallway or corpses levitating while on the "analysis table" or arms pointing places.This game varies mainly in certain events related to the past of our protagonist Rebecca, and the visions that she sees, these being a way of the demon to scare you, break you and make you give up and forget your main purpose: find out its name, the body in the mortuary that is possessed and burn it.I love the fact that the bodies smile in a macabre way sometimes, these are almost always the possessed ones, however, it can also be a deception. Pay attention and use the  wisely.Most of the "scares" are demonic presences, and they're so subtle, that when you realize them it's normal to be a little surprised. Even when they're silent.This game teaches you that the devil is in the details. You turn around to take the Formaldehyde or Methanol, and suddenly the corpse in front of you quickly moves some limb or levitates in the air.The game in general is very good, however, sometimes there are small bugs. In any case, just go back to the Main Menu and continue.The voices are good, especially Raymond Delver and his.. Possessed mother.This game was a gift from a good friend. I appreciate it, it's one of my favorites now. I highly recommend it, and it's even better if you increase the frequency of "Hauntsystem Aggressiveness". I love it! (not recommended if you have heart problems). But be careful. After a few games (shifts) in a roll, the time seems to be reduced and not enough, so you lose faster before embalming the third corpse, or so it has happened to me. Somehow ignoring certain events like phone calls and dark shadows calling you prevent you from 'unfocusing' on your mission, so.. Avoid them.This game will definitely be in my "💙" collection.Conclusion 1: The game is great and the demons are trolls.Conclusion 2: I'm ready to work in a Mortuary. PS: I'll wait patiently for Halloween and Christmas.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, with a true sense of what horror means. Being a horror fan, very rarely I feel scared or impressed with horror games nowadays, since most are copy pastes of either P.T. or Outlast, but this one was a day one buy for me. Made by a one man team, I cant even imagine how much work went into this. I hope the developer reads this, and let me tell you, sir, congratulations, your work, sweat and tears paid off and you created one of the most terrifying games I've ever seen.I have a few pointers, though, as always. The corpse embalming and treatment needs reworking. For the life of me, I cant imagine why is it that everything is so scattered around the place, instead of being more organised, as it should, with a work station, but that is just my opinion. The act of returning the corpses to the cold storage seems bugged, and it usually will make you loose precious time, on a game where time is a luxury, (yes, for those who didn't knew, this game is time based. Not so punch in the face, but time based). Secondly, the lack of cloud saving makes this more painful than it needs to, when switching between PC and the Steam Deck, or any other PC, for the matter. And secondly, but not least, and this is going to be a personal choice, the horror that seems to work here is the one who doesn't rely on jump scares, like voices, eye glowing shadows, etc, this is truly nerve wrecking. I have to admit that after a while, I got used to the jump scares and found them more of an annoyance than something I should be terrified. I would be glad to provide some pointers to make this even more terrifying if the developer wishes so, and one of them is: reduce the jump scares, and increase the horror that seems to interact directly with the player, like it is seen in SOMA, where the horror is environment related. Another point of horror is to change the ambient around you, like a picture, a common item like a pen, etc, just subtle things that the eagle eyed will notice. This will truly make it look like something is indeed following you all the time, not only specific moments. If you work in a place like this, how horrible is to feel that something is in the room that you passed 20 times already, but you cant see it? I'm giving this 8/10 and I understand that my pointers are taste related, since some will have no problem with jump scares, but I've seen so many that I don't find them entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do wish I had an option to give a mid range review. The game is not terrible by any means (I've played 5 hours already so.. ) but there are def places to improve.I think it's a good technique to get a player in a tedious mindset, where you're focused on these simple, but repetitive tasks; it sort of eases your mind a little and sets you up for some good scares. There are some too, but then there are places where things fall flat. The events do seem to be randomized, and there are 5 endings, so it lends itself to replayability, which I DO like. And for 5 hours of fun (I mostly just streamed it to friends), 25 or so bucks isn't that big of a deal. There is a story to it, and you do seem to uncover more of it as you play, which also bolsters that aspect. I don't mind the realism. I really enjoy it, but I can see how it might put someone off. If you're squeamish, this might not be the best game for you. I haven't tried it with lower graphics, so I'm not sure if that'd help. There were some bugs, and still are, though the devs were pretty quick to get a large bunch of them fixed. I appreciate that.My biggest gripe is that I can't skip the ending scenes, so there is a scene I've seen three times already, and oof.. that's annoying. I'd like that option so if I get the wrong ending, I can just move on. I think there is some way the events could be improved, but if you do some a few good hours of fun, and replayability, I think it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: After 2 playthroughs, I'm torn about this review. This game is obviously a labor of love, and for a short spook-fest with some engaging game play, it feels alright and accomplishes exactly what it sets out to do. It has some scary moments without being overly campy, the dialogue is alright and it's neat how some of the "cut scenes" and scare moments are not always the same, with different bodies and different animations that happen. In general, I liked it and I think it was worth the buy for a few good hours of entertainment. It sounds like it's a pretty small dev team, so congrats to them for putting out a neat little horror game that's overall pretty fun.That said, I do have some pretty big issues with the game that make me hesitate to fully recommend it, and I don't know if I'll go back to play through it again. My main issues are:- The inventory system is AWFUL. You can't do anything out of sequence, and if you happen to be holding something in both hands, "large" items can't be picked up. Proving to me that I only have 2 hands is NOT immersive in any way, especially since I never actually see my hands at any point during the game. The inventory restriction is unnecessary and horribly disruptive to the flow of play once you get the hang of what you have to do with the bodies. The sequence doesn't vary, so at a certain point, ESPECIALLY if the devs want me to do multiple playthroughs, I really don't want to be needlessly time- or item-stalled when I'm trying to speed things up a little. It's even more irritating in that a simple fix, like making the clipboard its own button instead of an inventory item, probably avoids most if not all of this issue. - The other frustrating part of this is that you MUST do everything in sequence. You can't multitask. Want to quickly do some things at the body before you go drop off the embalming report? You can't, so buckle up and connect the dots the only way the game knows how. Got the embalmer running and you want to go mix the tank cleaner? Nope, and by the way, if you pick up the tank cleaner, get ready to jockey around your inventory yet again. It starts to feel REALLY clunky, especially since you're doing this to several bodies in a row on a given run. - Checkpoints are laughably sparse, given how often this game seems to crash. In two playthroughs, I've had the game freeze on me 3 times, and two of those three times, it loaded me into the very beginning of the main game, which meant I had to listen to the SAME several-minute sequence of introductory exposition before I could get into the game play, which I'd already done multiple times and once in the tutorial. None of these moments are skipable, so you just have to sit there and wait, which again makes me not want to do it over again. TLDR; Good game, but pretty repetitive. UI/inventory issues get in the way of a smooth game play experience and there are some issues with crashes, all of which IMO make it a bit less replayable than it seems the devs intended.Edit: I'm changing my review to "Recommend" based on the fact that the dev is already very active in and addressing and adjusting some of the issues I have with the game. I also think that, while I might not play it for 20 hours, it's definitely been fun for the time I've put into it, and that deserves some recognition and acknowledgement. I also removed some of the more "spoiler-y" parts of the review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game builds up the tension appropriately so that when the scares happen, they're deserved.  Many smaller indie horror games rely on just jump scares for anything scary, and while there are some jump scares in this game, it really works hard to earn them.  The mortuary aspect is gross enough, and I was worried there would be full autopsies.  There is not.  It is embalming only.  Not that it necessarily makes a huge difference, but it's certainly nowhere near as gory and filled with cutting and sewing as I thought it would be.The process of embalming in this game involves many steps, but it is relatively straightforward.  You follow the steps, then take a body back to storage, and move on to the next.  Some of the controls are not explained particularly well, namely the way you sew the mouth shut.  You have to pull the plunger on screen, then click the button in the middle to nail it down.  I do like the quick menu for accessing items.  Very good idea. :)Overall this is a story that goes into bigger detail about our main character.  It isn't just about dead bodies and monsters.  It ties in with her life and her struggles, and I think that makes the game that much better honestly.  The best horror isn't exclusively about the scary monsters and killers, it's about the tragedies the characters go through beyond just that.  It makes the characters more interesting, and sometimes actually has something to say beyond just the horror itself.  This game is pretty small in scale, but it is absolutely terrific, and WORTH the $25 I paid for it.  So is every other Dread XP game anyway.  Go buy all of those too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I have obtained 3 of the 5 endings so far but I think I have played enough of the game to give a proper review for the game."The Mortuary Assistant" is really a solid horror game that blends suspenseful storytelling, effective jump scares, and psychological fear and confusion. This game manages to create a few chilling but quick moments that make you question what you may or may not have seen. This takes careful planning on the part of the devs because these scares must happen when the player least expects it, but is looking directly (or through peripheral vision) at a common area in the environment. Do it too often and the creepy feeling is lost. Do it at the wrong times and the player may miss these brief scares entirely.While Rebecca's story isn't anything groundbreaking, I did find myself morbidly curious as to what her backstory was. Each shift allowed me to find out pieces of her story until the full picture was revealed. Again, it's nothing incredibly original or mind-bending but it provides the angst needed to make the psychological aspects of the game have some impact.The whole process of embalming the bodies was actually quite satisfying for my OCD. Granted, I didn't have to embalm every single body but it would allow the scares to last a bit longer as Rebecca became more and more on the verge of possession. One aspect of the story is definitely messed up when you consider Raymond's motives. I mean, As for what I didn't like about the game, well, as interesting as the embalming process was, it does get tedious after several shifts. The routine is easy to learn and you can basically run through each shift without much thought. Granted, if you pay close attention at key moments, you may be able to unlock all 5 endings sooner rather than later. However, if you don't find all the clues early, then you have to keep going through the motions with each shift until you do locate them.The replay value is not very high, mostly because the more shifts you work, the more repeated flashbacks and scares you encounter. After so long, you end up seeing certain aspects of Rebecca's past more than once, and see the same scares more than once. I wish each shift could have been truly unique so we don't get the repetition. Perhaps having a set number of shifts would have been best, and each shift would have had its own scares and you would only see new and different flashbacks of Rebecca's past. Despite it's flaws, I still think "The Mortuary Assistant" is well-done horror game that provides the creepy, chilling, suspenseful moments you hope for, and also has a decent backstory for the protagonist to add some depth.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright.  Scares are VERY predictable and it's mostly reliant on jump scares.  Animation work is pretty weak, but the game is overall enjoyable and the voice acting is better than expected.There isn't really much to gameplay, and this sharply limits the amount of play you'll get out of this.  You're essentially solving a "puzzle", wherein you have to identify the demon and then correctly identify which body (out of several) it's possessing.  But the steps of the puzzle solving are the same, every time (which makes sense, you ARE embalming cadavers after all!), so it's not even really "puzzle solving"?I had fun with my first couple of shifts, but I don't think I'll be playing for much longer.  There's just not much to this game.  I think it's overpriced at $25, but the $16 I paid for it is within acceptable limits.I'm giving it a thumbs up because I believe in supporting indie developers, and it's clear they put real effort into this.  But for me, personally, it's more like a "no thumbs."  It's definitely not a thumbs down, but I can't get excited enough to give a thumbs up, either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really torn on this one. I think it's kind of an interesting experience, and a pretty good idea for a short but very replayable game. Then again, since by some miracle I managed to nail the demon on my first attempt, I didn't feel at all compelled to give it another go. I may have read a little too much about this game before I actually played it, which is my fault. I think the basics of "The Mortuary Assistant" are very fine - the repetitive embalming process is not particularly exciting, but there's a nice routine to it, and you feel good about doing it efficiently because of the ticking clock element. Though I'll be honest, I'm not sure if the aforementioned ticking clock is an actual in-game time limit, or just an empty threat. All I know is that the demon told me  at some point that it's already too late, which was kind of disconcerting; but it was clearly a lie, cause a few minutes later I burned his *** in the furnace and won. I personally didn't find the scares to be all that scary, but that may well be because I knew too much going in. The only actual flaw that I want to point out is the execution. By God, if you like your games polished, do not touch this one. The gamepad controls are awful, the graphics are pretty bad, the game runs terribly, and there are a lot of bugs. Sometimes you won't even know if you can't progress because there's a haunting in progress, or because the game just glitched out on you. This almost makes me want to give it a thumbs down, but I can't bring myself to punish a game this creative. So whatever, let's say I recommend it. Why not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible horror game.  One of the best that's come out in years.  An amazing premise, great story and dialogue, a repeated loop of nightly shifts as you unlock more and more of the macabre tale, and a terrific ending which wraps things up but also sets up possibility of yet more in the future.  And more importantly, a non-stop rollercoaster of horror.It took me over 5 hours to get the final "true ending", and it was indeed terrifying that whole time.  Nearly for the entirety of that runtime I was getting consistently new content (except for a repeat of a grandma scene which seems to occur in nearly all of my 5 runs for some reason), it was only at the end I started to notice a bit of repeats of the scares creeping in.Absolute must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: My thoughts: This game is fantastic. The atmosphere is incredible and it is one of the only games I have played that does procedural generation right. After nine and a half hours, I was still seeing new random events and even the repeated ones still caught me off guard. The story is ok, good but not great. Fine but not outstanding. My biggest issue though is the scripted haunting events. These are all very well made and scary... the first time. After the second or third time, they become tiresome, they break up the pacing, and they stop you in the middle of the surprisingly entertaining mortuary process.My girlfriends thoughts: I enjoyed that you get to learn about Rebecca's past, and how the demons used her past against her in a way to scare you, and her, and in a way that let you smoothly learn about her history.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty unique game, though it can get repetitive. _childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A spectacularly terrifying game. It kind of reminds me of Phasmophobia in that it has a lot of random events that will scare the ever loving crap out of you. What I like about this game the most, is that most of the scares are subtle. A shadowy figure ducking out of sight, a face barely seen through the window, a flash of pale cracked skin gone in an instant. These are most of the scares which are punctuated with larger hallucination scares. These scares are bigger and more obvious, some of which being downright terrifying. The entire time you are trying to do two things. Embalm the dead bodies and, more importantly, survive the night with your soul intact. You work through the night while solving a puzzle and guessing which body is the target. The game has a couple of minor issues, I ran across bugs that stopped or delayed my progress, and the voice acting is hit or miss. The animations for the other non-ghost characters is stiff, but those are forgivable. My only real big complaint, is the very high mouse sensitivity. Even on the lowest setting, my mouse swings wildly across the screen at the barest hint of movement. That problem is highlighted further when attempting to move bodies with the gurney which drops the sensitivity to nothing, and then brings it right up in an instant when the gurney is released. All in all this game is easily worth the money. Between multiple endings and a bunch of random events, you'll be entertained for a while.EDIT: They have fixed the sensitivity issue. The gurney now feels sluggish, but intentionally so. There is less disparity between the regular looking sensitivity, and gurney sensitivity. They also added more events since I last wrote this review. Even better now. Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Mortuary Assistant to me is something special. It´s one of those games that come along every few years where right from the start I feel like I´ve got a little gem on my hands.This one-person-project captures a very specific kind of horror and dread that I can immensly appreaciate. The key is atmosphere. The location the main game takes place in is compact with easy to learn tasks that one has to accomplish as a, well, Mortuary Assistant, quickly becoming your place of work. The structure the game takes makes it easy for the player to build a routine all the while things happen around you that further the horror atmosphere. While there are heavy themes at play here which I will not disclose as to not spoil the fun, the horror-elements rarely if at all rely on cheap jump-scares, which is kind of rare these days and much appreaciated by someone who values dread and horror over disgust and frights in terms of genre-elements. The game builds a very solid and interesting foundation upon which it expands every playthrough (which take around 45mins give or take). There is quite a bit to find and discover. Mortuary Assistant is a compact, well crafted game, designed by someone that knows that the horror-genre can work very well with a more subtle approach. The Dev is also very active in tracking down remaining small bugs and very quick in releasing patches.Do the dev and yourself a favor and give this game a chance as it will probably become a comfort-horrorgame for me over the next months.There´s a Demo too if you want to try it out first.Glowing recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, wooo boy can I go on about this game for a long, long time. For the TL;DR version, skip to the end of this review. For those of you that need a little more convincing however... The spawn/generation of this game is so randomized, it's insane. You become a little numb after 20 hours to the main scares, IE the story progression scares. However, the possession scares have such high RNG that I didn't find some of them until I was finished with all 7 endings and 11 hours into the game.The story is a little fast, a little lifeless but that's not really what were here for, is it? No! We're playing this game for the scares, the spooky sounds and an insanely strong granny throwing you neck-first down the halls. On x-mas there were the cutest lights and snowglobes, on halloween there were pumpkins and ghosts. Oh and a clown body that definitely LOOKS possessed. Not to mention you get to embalm Santa! Holly Jolly THAT you break-and-enter-cookie-monster! This game is phenomenal when you stop and realize a single person was able to make it, with glitzy graphics that stream pretty seamlessly and such high randomization, you'll keep getting got by the same entities!Think of the game Layers of Fear, or Silent Hill PT. Turn around, nothing there. Turn around again, something is in your face and looming. Did that bed just creak? Why is the door shut now? Did the lights cut off? Better flip the switch and reveal the thing is now behind you! But don't look away! Something else is there now. Even after speed running and creating a quick strategy to embalm bodies, there have been several times where I got so startled all I could do was pause and gasp for air like a blubbering fish. (One of the entities spawned inside my character and it was traumatizing, even when the game has a tiny glitch it's super effective... ;_;) Now for the slight bummer side? The game doesn't get a lot of updates but to me, that's fine. If you can make something you don't have to constantly take care of? Why wouldn't you? That's also incredibly fair when again, a single person is in charge of creating the entire thing. The other bummer is, of course you get used to some of the scares and they don't change when it comes to the main endings and story arc you are chasing. However, with how random the generation of the possessions are, if you're any bit frightened by sudden horror elements like me, you'll get far more playtime out of this game. Seriously, even if you wait for a steam sale, it's worth every penny!TL;DR VERSION ---PROS-1. Lots of random scares, high randomization. 2. Easy, consistent game mechanics that feel linear enough to remember the core task. (Embalming, duh.) 3. 5 different endings and two bad end variants, some easier or harder to get to than others but each unlocks more of the main story. 4. Interactive UI, nothing too sticky or many errors/glitches with picking up/dropping/interacting with items.(Which you're gonna need to rely on if you plan to play through enough to get all the endings/achievements.)5. Fun updates for seasons, cute little Easter eggs as well as items that don't do anything yet but more than likely will in the future. (A fuse box, a few other embalming tools/ingredients that you can look at but not use.)CONS-1. Shallow story depth, don't expect a triple A plot line but what is conveyed is clear enough to answer most questions. Just remember, demons be demoning. 2. Predictable story driven scares, repeated 'quest' cut scenes that give-way to what ending you're going towards or could possibly get. 3. Slow development, one man team and not much more to really add to the game that can be foreseen as far as story mode goes. 4. Little bit of a RAM hog but has improved drastically since launch, high hopes for even more processing improvement. 5. F**k the Mimic. (You'll see.)

_childDocuments_.review: Still working toward all endings but this has some of the darkest atmosphere in any horror game. The basic idea is that you perform simple tasks to examine and then embalm three dead bodies while trying to deduce which is host to the demon. The embalming tasks by themselves are very unsettling, but demonic stuff starts ramping up in the mortuary as the night progresses. The scares are very potent, for example an entity peering out from behind a filing cabinet or tapping on the window pleading to be let in. If you like scary games and don't mind performing tasks in a small building as things creep in from the void then this is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking forward to this since the demo and the full release did not disappoint.  Mortuary's Assistant is downright terrifying with a surprising amount of replayability-- you cannot beat nor unlock the story in a single run.  Each run is unique-- horror events will reoccur, but the outcome can differ based on what you do.The dev seems like a sane individual in his vlogs, but he must be bleeping crazy to have created this.  Everything about Mortuary Assistant is dark, twisted, and demonic.  I don't know if the symbols and signs included in the game have a real basis in the world, but I will say that they convey the hellacious atmosphere of the game.For horror game fans this is a 10/10.  Mortuary Assistant will make you dirty your pants for 5-10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Tedious game loop where you are spending all your time doing the exact same thing over and over. Follow the checklist, guess the ghost, sit through the scares, then you Win or Lose. Lather, Rinse, Repeat.  Oh also sometimes you have to wait for a scare event to happen before you can keep playing the actual game. Breaks down to a guessing game with unskippable cutscenes from my own experience and watching others. If you like  the deep lore style/genre of games that require multiple playthroughs and dives to get all the story or films like Amittyville  Horror, The Conjuring or any of the other Based on a True Story Haunting Movies that exist, then this is something you'll love. Otherwise its a waste of 25 bucks imo.  Ending positively, at least there is clearly effort being into it, but its just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Moderately spooky game. The atmosphere is just right. Every scare is telegraphed before it happens, so the jump scares are not that cheap, but still effective. I like the ones where you turn around and there's that pale guy just sitting on the shelf or peeking around the corner for a while. There is no fail state, so if the monsters get you, you just wake up on the floor in a short while and carry on. Once you realise that they can't hurt you, the scares lose their scariness a bit.Gameplay gets quite tedious after a while. Playing in short bursts helps to mitigate that a bit. Every body has the same checklist you follow. You check the corpse for bruises and other markings, file the report, sew mouth shut and close the eyes, mix embalming juices, attach tubing and drain the body. Then you fill the belly with cavity fluid and clean the embalming machine. Finally wipe the face clean and done.There are three bodies per shift, and you need to know which one is possessed by demon, by keeping an eye out for which one keeps moving on its own. Each shift has some scares that happen and after each scare you uncover another letter of the demon's name. Once you know which body is possessed and what the name of the demon is, you burn the body and that's that. The deductive element could have been more fleshed out.A fun game, but has some serious game breaking bugs. Mine was the Old Apartment bug, where you get to the Rebecca's old apartment and there's a giant checklist telling you to gather supplies, but you can't interact with anything there, so the game is stuck.Kohtalaisen pelottava peli. Ilmapiiri on juuri sopiva. Jokainen säikytys ennakoidaan hieman ennen kuin se tapahtuu, joten äkkisäikytykset eivät ole niin halpamaisia, mutta silti tehokkaita. Itse pidin eniten niistä, joissa ympäri käännyttäessä on se kalpea kaveri istumassa hyllyn päällä tai kulman takana tuijottamassa. Säikytykset eivät tee pahaa, vaan jos hirviö nappaa, päähenkilö vain herää lattialta kotvasen kuluttua ja jatkaa puuhiaan. Toki kun sen tajuaa, pelotteilta lähtee vähän tehoa.Pelattavuus muuttuu ajan mittaa puuduttavaksi. Lyhyissä pätkissä pelaaminen tasoittaa hieman. Jokaisella ruumiilla on sama tehtävälista seurattavana. Tarkista keho vaurioilta, arkoistoi raportti, ompele suu ja silmät kiinni, sekoita balsamointiaineet, kiinnitä putket ja vuodata ruumis kuiviin. Sitten täytä vatsa nesteillä ja puhdista balsamointikone. _childDocuments_.review: Ok ... So we start off with something that (let's face it): not many of us choose a career path on - keeping dead bodies preserved in a funeral home, strictly for the purpose of allowing a grieving group of family and loved ones, to see them at peaceful rest, as they make the journey to their spiritual afterlife. Personally, I could never give that the most honest of tries. But the game sets out to provide you with a very educational experience of what needs to be done. That said, for those who *may* be interested on said career path, this actually may serve as a good "primer".But in the game, just as you complete the embalming procedure tutorial, well ... folks, that's when all hell literally breaks loose. The protagonist Rebecca you play, finds herself in a TRULY unenviable position of a demonologist and exorcist. It ain't what she signed up for, but the journey that must be completed is actually ... engaging, and fun.There are some truly scary moments in this game, that rival the scares from some of the greatest modern and classic horror flicks. It's impossible to put into words, because I strongly feel that revealing too much of the gameplay mechanic in my review, would serve as a major spoiler within the game itself.It's not simple point'n'shoot. There's a lot of intricate systems that must be learned, and ultimately, memorized. But like I said, it's all at the end of the day, engaging and fun. 4.5 out of 5 stars. Highly recommended!P.S. I am looking very much forward to the August 2024 update ... 😁

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic little horror game with a very creepy premise. It has a great atmosphere with some cool art design. The initial setup is perfect for a horror game and really puts you on edge. Then things start to get more intense as the supernatural parts of the game play out. There is kind of a ‘work sim’ style to the gameplay at first that slowly creeps you out because of the setting. Then the game unfolds into something more interesting with some really cool ideas. I’d be curious to know if the examining bodies gameplay was inspired by LA Noire because the way it works is very similar. The Mortuary Assistant is very clever over all and I can see why it has gotten so much attention online. I’m curious to see what these devs come up with in future games because this game is awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more like a neutral review rather than negative. The game feels amazing in the first hour, but I think it has serious "balance" problems.The idea of the multiple endings (which is very common in small indie games) could mean more replayability, but this is really kneecapped but the repetitivity of what re-playing everything means. The multiple endings are also not really alternative endings, but they add to the lore and give sense to the story (every different ending adds something to it). The lore / story events happening during the normal game are few and are not skippable, meaning that given how many times you are going to repeat the chores (cleaning bodies, which for the same reason becomes tedious instead of tense), you'll be stuck with the repetitive unskippable story events and haunt events, which are already not scary at all by the third shift (and I am really weak at horror games).There is even an achievement of embalming 100 bodies...I mean why is there even such an achievement? You don't nearly come to half of that number even when unlocking every ending, and it's not like the embalming is a challenging puzzle or anything...it's cool in the beginning but then everything is the same. There are maybe 4 or 5 body stamps...never seen a fat woman, nor a child or a black woman. The bodies wear underpants and bras - totally unrealistic and less scary but I understand it could be because of some legal reason. After the third body, it's everything on automatic pilot, trying to figure out that little hint pointing to the other different ending.I think it could be (is?) a nice game but really many flaws in this sense. Technically I only found that sometimes the voices were either much too quiet, or completely mute...so, given that sometimes you hear demon voices etc, make sure you have subtitles enabled so you know you are not missing any line (the subtitles are working).

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Worth it at full price.I find this to be an absolutely phenomenal horror game. The premise is straight forward, and I found the gameplay oddly satisfying.The embalming process is fairly repetitive, but throughout you have a puzzle to solve based on a multitude of clues and goals. The scares range from straight up jump scares to subtle, to feeling like there's something right over your shoulder and the hairs on your neck are standing up. The game gets an A+ for atmosphere and presentation. I also found the story very well done. It may be repetitive, but the journey through the seemingly monotonous job is where things tend to go off the rails. There is a demo that gives you the basics of what the game is.GAMEPLAY:As stated above the core gameplay is straight forward and repetitive. The goal of the game is to solve a puzzle based on surrounding clues. There is more to the game that you have to find on your own. I will say there's enough there to keep you going, and there's enough endings that fill the whole story and world up very well. The act of embalming the bodies is satisfying on its own, and once you get 2 or 3 done, you'll remember the steps to do it. Finding clues to further your goals also adds some variety to the presentation. Go in blind, and have fun! There is a mode where you just embalm bodies as well. A nice added feature.CONTROLS:The game controls fine. Some of the embalming actions can feel a little janky, but it's easy enough to get used to. Otherwise your typical controls.SOUND:Honestly they did an amazing job with this. It always feels eerie. They set the silence and most minute sounds in all the right places that really add to the eerieness. The silence is also quiet enough that when things happen, it will make you want to look over your shoulder in real life.GRAPHICS:Overall the graphics are fine. Not bad by any means, but they won't blow your mind. The design of things that happen throughout the game are unsettling...at worst.-Is that body smiling? Ohhh no it's just the angle that I'm pus......ohh.....ATMOSPHERE/ENVIRONMENTAs stated above, they nailed atmosphere almost perfectly for what they set out to do. Working in the mortuary already feels off, the visual aesthetic of the mortuary is already off-putting without having any scares done. Once you start your shift, you will start to notice a variety of things.-What was that by that cabinet?! Oh a shado-......ohhhh no no no no no noThere are occasional jump scares, but the way everything is placed is pretty much perfect. Eventually the events may become repetitive and you know what to expect, but I still felt the hairs on my neck standing up on end while playing the game.STORY:I really like how they handled the story here. You have to do some work to put everything together nicely, but when you do I feel it pays off majorly. This is one where everything is given to you once you find it. There are connections you have to make, but everything is there and very apparent once you get the information. I really like what they did, and adding the FREE definitive edition upgrade made it even better than it already was. The main character and anybody else involved in the story kept my interest the whole time.IN CLOSING:I think this game is very much worth your time, and very much worth it even at full price. The game may take about 5-6 hours to get everything, but I enjoyed every minute I spent in this game. I've even completed it twice now. If you're still unsure try the demo, it will give you basically what you're going to be doing, but with so much more involved. I could tell the developers definitely wanted to make something special here, and they did a fantastic job. I look forward to see what they do with this little universe they've created, and where the story goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a really fantastic horror game often muddled by general jankiness and bugs.It's a cleverly designed horror game that has such a unique approach to design and is just so much more interesting than your standard walking simulator. While the writing is not fantastic, the narrative design or approach to story within the context of an interactive medium, is incredibly well done and is something I really hope other games can learn from.The spooks range from silly to terrifying, there's kind of a range of quality to them to be honest. Some are expected, some are definitely not, and some of them feel like they were designed when the game first began development and have been grandfathered in with new, better scares. It feels as though the developer has honed their craft since they began, and it could be worth revisiting some of the older scares which don't have the same level of creativity or animation quality.Final note, in regard to revisiting animation quality, that opening cutscene needs to go or be completely redone. The animation is not there, and it really sets you up to believe the game you're about to play is much worse than it ends up being. It looks like Food Fight.Other than that, it's a creative, fairly robust, replayable, and sometimes terrifying horror game with more going on under the hood than 90% of horror games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and fun to playDoes't rely on loud cheap jump scares, it actually has subtle jump scares like things appearing out of nowhere or at the corner of your eye with no load audio cues (unlike most horror games nowadays) but them just showing up is enough to scare you.It is fun to repeat tasks a lot in the game (some may not find it enjoyable) because each task is short, which makes going through each "Shift" more quick and fun.You can turn off story events to make it even more quick (which helps for the 100% achievements)The problems I have in this game are:. The opening video's background audio kept glitching out. Can't skip the ending scenes (which is annoying when you are going for 100% achievement). Some times controller support glitches out when examining bodies or on the computer and will not allow you to leave the body or computer by removing the "back out" button and to fix it you have to use a mouse to switch to keyboard controls (i think it happens when you pause)overall it is an enjoyable game and I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: is an entertaining cross between an embalming simulator, demonic horror, and detective game. During a lengthy apprenticeship, the protagonist is called in late one night to take care of three new bodies … except something isn’t quite right.The Mortuary Assistant is a fantastically fearful experience that blends its horror, detective, and simulator gameplay to great effect. It is reminiscent of games such as Phasmophobia with its methodical and paranormal undertakings and success is highly satisfying. The scares, though they do include some recognised tropes, are implemented in a tactical way that prevents them from feeling tired or overused meaning the game feels genuinely creepy, fueling the player’s adrenaline and creating an intense atmosphere.The systematic yet disturbing process of embalming is very grounding in comparison to the more full-on task of demon hunting and these two prominent gameplay aspects work in tandem with one another. Additionally, the realistic art style and imposing sound design really help immerse the player and emphasise the visceral and threatening nature of the experience.Overall, the game has a lot to offer and has few drawbacks or flaws. It is a brilliant horror game and would definitely appeal to fans of the genre. It is perhaps not one for the faint-hearted due to its’ gruesome and intense style but I’d happily recommend it to anyone looking to feel genuinely frightened and I’d suggest playing it at night!My full review of this game where I go into detail about gameplay, narrative, and styling is available on .

_childDocuments_.review: So... my thoughts after getting four out of the six endings to the game:1. I love this game.2. Normally games with jump scares irritate me (I prefer slow dread like Silent Hill, Fatal Frame, or Phasmophobia), but this gamer does them very well and they make sense from a plot standpoint. Hell is literally bleeding into reality.3. Despite the same motions for each body, the game never felt stale or too repetitive. If anything, the repetitive nature of the mundane job was a good counterpoint to the hellish intrusions going on around you.4. They got the AA/NA coins perfect and the addiction and guilt subplot was pretty cool. Would love to have seen more of it. 5. Some of the endings are emotional roller-coasters and others bury you in a pit of despair.  Nice. So far I liked all of the endings I've uncovered.6. I do wish it was longer. And the numbers of bodies varied between 3 and 5 to change things up a bit. But that's just me really liking the game and not wanting each run to end. 7. That "true" sixth ending was NUTS.8. I wish the demon tricked you more, making you have to use other forms of deduction to figure out which one it is. Also would have been cool if the House the demon was associated with colored the hauntings more.8. Any complaints are small compared to the praise I have for this game. I was NOT expecting it to be this good, this scary, this entertaining. I haven't yelled "OH GO ♥♥♥♥ YOURSELF GAME" at my screen this much since Outlast first came out.
