_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:This game is not worth the asking price. The systems are too shallow and the game is too unpolished to justify it. It feels like a gimmick after a few hours. Buy on sale if you really want to try it. Someone needs to just make a game dedicated to performing extensive autopsies and funeral prep. This ain't it. This was a hard one to vote on. There's a lot to like in it. There's also a lot to not like in it. For the price and what you get out of it I cannot recommend it as is.The hook of this game got me when I saw that you actually did the prep work on cadavers. I initially hoped for some kind of extensive autopsy and mortician simulator. I feel like the game was even kind of marketed as such, with the exception of all the scary stuff added into it. What a cool concept! Something that hasn't been tried in the world of simulation gaming and I was so excited to see what they had in store. I saw the pictures of a dead man's mouth getting sewn shut and was certain this game would have hours of cool and macabre duties to get into. But it doesn't. In fact, after you play it for a few hours you realize its a shallow gimmick. Let's break down the game-play loop.If its your first time you have to watch a few cut scenes and get acclimated to the story and characters therein. The story feels more like a scenario than a fleshed out story. Basically your a person who needs a job so you decide to work as an assistant for a mortician -like the name...There is a main character and a few supporting characters with a very tenuous plot that gives you just enough to get invested. Voice acting is not too bad, but the animations feel a little exaggerated and running it on ultra still leaves you deep in the uncanny valley. You go through a tutorial section where you learn the process you will perform throughout the rest of the game. After that, the mortician sends you home and you hang out in your apartment for a bit before heading back. That night, you go back and work on three bodies that need to be taken care of. Its rainy and spooky and you will certainly poop your pants. The game will make you jump and scream and feel uncomfortable -its great at that at first.  You'll be working on things or entering data and something will move in the corner of your eye and when you look up its some it will be gone. You'll walk up to a door to open it and something will be on the other side peeking in at you and its so subtle you don't notice it until you're getting the crap scared out of you by it. I loved that. It isn't all about big bang scares in this, its got a nuance to it that respects the art of the scare and makes you feel like it was an earned scare and not a cheap jump. They really nailed the atmosphere and horror, but the problems arise with the illusion that this game has enough content to justify its price with multiple play-throughs. After my first few shifts, I was noticing the same events happening over and over. The night is exactly the same, the weather is the same. Everything in the mortuary is the exact same as it was the first time. The second play-through is not as unique as everyone's been saying. In fact, the gameplay is so linear that you cannot do anything besides a series of specific things in a specific order until the next cut scene happens. I'm gonna spare you details but heres the loop:Your goal is to find out which body is possessed by a demon and burn it. To do that you have to uncover 4 sigils around the building, and figure out what the demon's name is, as well as the correct body its tethered to. Don't worry, you'll figure it out. Its purposely vague to both pad game play time and to make room for the spooky stuff. Arrive at mortuary.Loot the same items each time: Clipboard, notepad, letting strip.Grab one of three corpses out of cold storage.(spooky stuff happens in background)Wheel them to lab where you perform your tasks.Use your clipboard to document any moles, lesions, abrasions etc the corpse has.(spooky stuff happens in background)Put the info you copy to to clipboard into the computer database. (spooky stuff happens in background)Get a little spooked. Use the letting strip to find your first demonic sigil.(That part can be done whenever I think, just do it periodically)Print the document you just filed.(Yeah you gotta use an inkjet)Take the printout to the front room and put it in a file holder.(spooky stuff happens in background)Go back to the lab, grab a needle, mouth wire and some eye caps and sew the cadaver's mouth shut.(spooky stuff happens in background)Apply eye caps to eyes and close themCreate embalming mixture by mixing different ingredients in a specific order into a really loud machine.Grab scalpel, pvc tubing and artery forceps.Cut cadavers neck open and install tubing using the forceps.Run the loud machine and drain the blood.Remove the tubing and sew the neck shut. (two clicks)(spooky stuff happens in background, maybe even a jump-scare. Possibly a unique cut-scene providing lore into your character's background and history.)Get a bag and fill it with cavity jelly. Grab a trocar and mumble foul language under your breath as you wrestle with the most janky and cumbersome activity in the game and fill up the body's stomach with this stuff. (The trocar is by far the worst part of the game and you have to do it to every body. There's no rhyme or reason behind controlling the trocar. It just has to go in at the right angle and right depth before it discharges its contents, if you don't get it right your wrestling with your mouse to get the trocar to do what its supposed to do. Its terrible and if its supposed to be simulating the difficulty of using such a device, its simulating it wrong. Its egregiously frustrating to use.)After you fill the body with cavity goo you gotta go get some tank cleaner an clean-out the embalming tank.Go to the bathroom, get jump-scared in the mirror. Make the cleaning agent and bring it back to the lab. Run the agent through the loud machine again and wait for it to complete.Next, grab a wetnap from the counter and "moisturize" the cadaver's face. You can now wheel this body back to cold storage and start on the next one. You will do everything I just listed in that exact same order each time you play through. You cannot skip steps, you cannot multitask. You cannot do anything more than what I just listed. Once you start the process you cannot stop and change out bodies. You must finish what you started in the order that's required on that clipboard. Cool for the first play-through, literally to be avoided in subsequent play-throughs. While you're going through this tedium you'll be trying to figure out the demon's name through the letting strips and sigils you find. Once you figure out the demons name and put this mark together with the right configuration, you put the mark on the corpse and burn it, face moisturized and all. If you're right you get one cutscene, if you're wrong you get another. Both are very similar but not too bad the first time through. Second and third play-throughs feel like they told us that it was unique each time to justify charging 25 bucks to have it. The actual game is less than an hour long and it baited me into spending 10 hours trying to find out more about it. First time you play through all of this you'll start to feel like the game has tons in store. But it really doesn't. I like that it has little secrets and different cut-scenes in the play-throughs, but I found myself encountering the same ones over and over. I put ten hours into this game and I could beat the loop within 20 minutes, so I feel like I've explored it. Can't type anymore. Out of space. Game is a gimmick demo. Buy when its like 10 bucks. Moisturize your face before setting yourself on fire.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of horror games struggle to find the perfect middle ground between holding the player’s hand too much and doing too little to offer the player any direction. Both can lead to the player being taken out of the horror experience. Mortuary Assistant finds that middle ground pretty well and for that reason alone it’s worth a play.Are the graphics the world’s greatest? Nah, but they don’t need to be (and during the process of embalming the bodies it’s actually maybe better that they aren’t because ew), it manages to be plenty creepy with what it offers. If you’re in the mood to be spooked, Mortuary Assistant is solid, and it’s interesting enough to where friends or family will find themselves watching you play and not getting bored. That’s a big plus on a movie night!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect little game for Halloween. The story is very well-paced, there are multiple endings and it's easy to make a mistake unless you're very observant. The creator of this game knows what tension is and how to build it. The sounds and visuals enhance the mood of the story. If you'd like to get some chills but are a bit tired of shooting zombies, this is your go to game. I hope there is a dlc or a sequel as the lore for this one can certainly be expanded.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique kind of job simulator with frequent, but generally unobtrusive, interjections of jumpy or helpless horror.I haven't played much so far, but overall I really quite like it. The atmosphere is quite good, not as slow and drawn out and suspenseful as some titles, but not a constant tidal wave of jumpscares, either. As a Mortuarial Ignorati, it's fun to get little bits of info about the chemicals being used and things. I would personally enjoy seeing more comprehensive flavour text in future!Overall, it's interesting, and it seems to have an attentive Developer and Supporting Community. There aren't many titles like this, and a number of them are geared towards a more lustful audience, so I think this is a good addition to the Steam Store.I definitely recommend this game more-so for people who like atmosphere more than action. Of course, if you like morprohilogy, then hooray!== BEFORE YOU BUY ==- The Demo is misleading, little problems like gurney control are not present in the full game!- Game Length complaints can be misleading! What may seem like 'Replaying' in other titles, is apparently 'Continuing' in this one, though that is debatable in some ways.== BEFORE YOU PLAY ==- Be Sure to Press the 'CLOSE' Button after changing your Settings, if you just hit [Esc] they can look changed, but remain unchanged in-game.- Turn on Subtitles, if you do so during a Cutscene they will not start showing until the game loads the next 'section', as it were.- Consider turning down the Volume more than you think is wise. The Dynamic Ranges in this game may be a little high for some soundsystems. Your Character, certain FX, and some Cutscene Dialogue can be very loud, but the Phones and Tape Recorder, for eg, tend to be very, very quiet. Categorised Volume Controls are planned, but right now it's a Global Volume setting.- Consider turning your brightness up a little. I know it makes games less scary, but in this game the 'main' room (as I choose to label it) has a central light, and useful objects against the walls, meaning that your own shadow is usually in the way of the things you need to populate your inventory with. As you grow used to the objects you may well be able to reverse this, but at first it can be a little obstructive.- If something is occurring, and you can't seem to interact with anything, try moving around the 'map' a bit. Some instances expect you to be in a certain spot.---If you genuinely have interest and wanna buy, just buy. Otherwise, here are the things that irk me...TIME WASTING!- Putting Form details into the Record System is fine, but entirely pointless, so it would seem thus far. If we had to choose specific things from the total data collected, that would be different. In a Detective game for eg, you may be tasked with deciding which traits are relevant to a suspect's involvement in a scenario. However, this is just clicking every clickable option on screen back and forth for 20 seconds, with no options that would cause you to fail or do any better. Ultimately, this could be handled automatically without having any impact on the process of the game.- You can no longer select a marking on the left-hand side of the torso, when interacting with the right-hand side. In the Demo and even in the Tutorial of the full game, this was possible, but on Shift 1 it is not? I really have to close menu and walk all the way around the table to open the same menu and click something I could already see clearly? Animals are kind of programmed to be annoyed by stuff like that...- You have to do everything on the Clipboard in EXACT order... You can't Mix Tank Cleaner and bring it into the room early, and please, please let us apply moisturiser while the Machine is washing itself. Standing there for no reason, waiting for the next interactable icon to pop up, really emphasizes the staggering of pace.Similarly, you cant open one eye, place an eye cap, then close that eye, you have to place both caps to close either... It's just odd- and again - staggers the player's pace. Thank the devil that you can fill an IV bag while the body drains!- You can't skip the ending Cutscene. I got the same one twice in a row and I had to listen to it all over again...Similarly, I have to pick up keys and click on my front door at the start of every shift? If nothing happens in the apartment, and I can't do anything in the apartment, why am I in the apartment?NO CONSISTENT QUICK-CLOSE!- Some [LC] interactions can be cancelled with [RC], that's good, that's intuitive. Quick Inventory opens  closes with [RC], also good.But there is no fully consistent Close/Back key! I'd personally lo-o-ove if [Esc] closed ANY menu or interaction, and ONLY opened the Pause Menu when other menus and interactions (such as looking at the Clipboard or inspecting a limb) were closed. Alternatively, it would be nice to have a Keybind specifically for backing out of things.It's a small thing, but it makes games feel so much more fluent that I tend to miss it.---PS It is a Criminal Offense, that I cannot mix Coffee and Toothpaste, and make a lovely minty drink... IN MY OWN APARTMENT! T.T

_childDocuments_.review: I do not get scared by many things, but this game certainly is one of the most terrifying games that I ever played. You play as a single woman all alone in a creepy mortuary. You actually embalm bodies as a real mortician would, and, meanwhile, you notice creepy activity, a light goes out, or you hear a knock on the door. I do not want to spoil all the things you might hear and see while with the corpses, but, suffice to say, this is no ordinary mortuary. As if dead bodies would not be unsettling enough, this mortuary is haunted by demons. This is a game you want to play if you want to be scared, or if you are just dying to learn the mortician's trade because there is a realistic simulation element to the game as well as the spooky stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Mortuary Assistant since its initial release, and I absolutely love it. The game offers great replayability, with six different endings and various achievements to hunt. While the scares can become predictable over time, some still manage to catch me off guard. The recent major update introduced new events, making the experience feel fresh again—I found myself jumping and screaming like when I first started playing. Even though I know I'll eventually get used to these new scares, the game remains one of my favorite horror experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Quite frankly, I don't understand all the hype behind the game... Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game, it has some good jumpscares/ghost events, it's also kinda cool to get to know more about the mortician job, but as someone who plays/streams a lot of horror games, I've seen way scarier stuff (like Visage or even MADiSON that came out recently).I hadn't seen a lot about the game before I played it so I didn't really know what I was getting myself into, some of my friends suggested it to me. It was fun the first hour maybe, but I encountered so many infuriating bugs that it made me give up after the second night shift. I've seen people say the demo was actually more polished than the full release. I'm expecting to come across bugs when I play games, but not that many "gamebreaking" bugs that just ruin the player's experience. Maybe I wasn't lucky, but the bugs broke the rythm of the game and I just didn't feel as immersed as I should have been...I also think it gets repetitive quite fast, you do the same tasks over and over and there are many redudant ghost events/visions as well (when they're not bugged out). Also, at certain moments, you can't interact with anything before a certain event happens, but the delay can be quite long and the game doesn't really let you know what's happening until it happens... It's hard to explain, but it just feels messy.I might sound rough and I truly wish the game does good/improve, but at its current state, the game might be worth $15, not the $25 it's going for on Steam rn. I might give it another try when they fix most of the bugs, but as of now it is what it is imo, a somewhat scary, but underwhelming game. At the moment, I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played other survival horror games similar to this before, but Mortuary Assistant has a different vibe. The atmosphere created by the developer, combined with the music and sounds effects and the unsettling nature of the game create quite the immersive experience.  It's part horror survival, part mortuary simulator (which would have been fun on its own).  The jump scares are actually scary, especially if you are wearing headphones or have audio turned on.As a former licensed funeral director and embalmer, I was surprised to see certain elements included in the game that were accurate (or close enough), and others of course that were not so much.  I would love to consult on games like these, so if anyone is considering a mortuary simulator type game, I would be happy to help!!IF YOU ARE SQUEAMISH, I DON'T RECOMMEND READING ON FROM HERE:What's accurate you ask?  1. Storage of the bodies in a cooler or refrigeration.2. The setup of the embalming room is fairly accurate, although the desk, computer and other "office" essentials would not be in the same room. The tank cleaner would have been kept in the embalming room for convenience. 3. You would not be embalming a body without wearing PPE to some degree--an water resistant apron or cover, shoe coverings, rubber gloves and a face mask or splash guard although I usually worked without shoe coverings (RIP dress shoes) or a face mask or shield. Old school embalmers did not wear any PPE or gloves even. Ew.4. The implements used in the body preparation sequence including eye caps, needle injector and the wires used to close the mouth; the embalming machine and chemicals used (although you would use formaldehyde OR gluteraldehyde, not both. Gluteraldehyde was supposed to be a more "user friendly" option and less likely to cause cancer from overexpsoure.)  5. The trocar is accurate enough, although most had a tip for piercing that would not require incision, there was a rubber hose and apparatus for connecting the trocar directly to the cavity fluid bottle, and you would also need to inject the organs in the lower quadrants of the abdomen. The game only does the upper quadrants. The sounds the fluid makes going into the cavity are eerily realistic!6. The incision in the neck is too high up in the game and would be visible at a viewing unless you were dressing the body in a turtle neck or using a scarf. The accepted method would be an incision just above the right clavicle that runs parallel to the bone and allows for easy access to the carotid and jugular.  There would only be one PVC tube connected to an arterial tube for injection, and we typically used a long angled forceps for drainage from the jugular. The game does a good job of depicting the process with the blood running down the table into a drain. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I cannot believe it was developed by one person, alone.Granted, there have been some bugs that I have run into which have been pretty annoying (though I number of them have already been patched out). But, the overall experience has been well worth the cost of admission.From the developers explanation, the game has something running in the background called the Haunt System.  This system is setup to provide Dynamic scares based on a number of different factors. Some of the factors mentioned: What stage are you at in the shift, how quickly are you running through it, what have you interacted with, what direction is the player facing. The Haunt System uses all of these factors to determine the best scare to serve up to you at any given time.It's pretty awesome, I highly recommend the purchase.If you are not inclined to purchase the game but still want to see what it offers. _childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant (TMA) is a horror game with a unique premise and randomly generated scares. It is designed to be played multiple times to uncover the full story and experience the other endings. I have had this on my radar for a long time, but with its short play time and repetitive game design, it is not a title that I would look at going back to, but it does manage to still deliver a haunting experience that horror fans will enjoy.The protagonist, Rebecca, is a recent graduate in Mortuary Sciences and has begun a traineeship at River Fields Mortuary. Rebecca has worked hard in the role and is on the cusp of being signed off and given a permanent paid position, when the rumours begin to become a reality. The protagonist then suddenly finds herself thrown into the world of the supernatural and is trapped at her workplace, but she is not alone. There is a demonic presence connected to one of the bodies in the morgue, but which is it? Finding the answer to this question will determine Rebecca's own survival.The story is simple, and Rebecca's past is only referenced vaguely. This aloof description of her personal life is purposeful, as it is slowly revealed in the story sections scattered throughout the gameplay. This game design choice to only reveal crucial story elements during multiple replays of the game and to have them only randomly spawn, is not something that appeals to me. Replaying multiple times to try and grasp a better understanding can result in the same events repeating,  the same ones previously seen in the last playthrough. Not to mention the already repetitious embalming process going alongside this as well. To me, this was tiresome and a poor way of trying to keep people replaying.TMA immediately appealed to me with its uncommon setting . To work alongside cadavers, experience creepy, randomly generated spookiness AND complete the embalming process, I thought, count me in! This element of the game, its setting, did not let me down. It is such a small environment, yet the developer(s) use this to its maximum potential and deliver some decent scares.Being a mortuary assistant, players must embalm bodies, repeatedly. This process is made easy with a step-by-step checklist on what to do. drain the liquid within the body, inspect for physical markings, enter data into the computer, sew the mouth shut and so forth. Just a normal day of work. After the introduction, supernatural events begin to occur and  through a series of tapes left by your boss,  you learn your main objective is not the embalming, but to locate the demon that is trying to possess you. This is done by locating  sigils which are scattered around the building, only becoming visible after using the Letting Paper which burns when a symbol is nearby. Gather the four sigils to make The Mark, put this on the body (that the demon is bound to), burn it and voila, job complete. I found the process very straight forward and too easy to guess. After my first playthrough and learning the basics, the second and subsequent attempts are simple and brief. I did not need to even inspect all of the bodies to work out which the demon was bound to, nor did I need to try and find all of the sigils. Having found only two, there was only one combination it could be out of the nine patterns. I suppose I could have purposefully guessed wrong, or let myself be possessed by waiting down the timer and receive a different result, but this seems null to me. Yes, the title is creepy. It does not rely on jumpscares which was a big relief, as these become tiresome fast. Instead, the scary moments are mostly random and some you may not even notice, perfectly building up tension within the players. Some examples include, a figure popping up in the window when you are at the other side of the room, a figure crouched on top of the cabinet. Eyes looking at you from afar, the lights going out, subtle noises and the list goes on. I very much enjoyed my initial playthrough. I found the gameplay to be innovative and interesting and I did not know what to expect. Unfortunately, this did not carry through in subsequent playthroughs and I experienced most of what I had already seen and done previously. Embalming the bodies was once an exciting and new task, but after already doing it four times in my first playthrough, to continue to do it (in the exact same checklist style) for each and every "shift", multiple times... is boring. It is clear that the developer(s) have great ideas for the horror market, but a repeated formula in this instance did not appeal to me. I imagine it would appeal to streamers, people who are new to the Indie horror market or those who simply scare very easily. Perhaps these are the developer(s) target audience, but at least for me, an Indie horror enthusiast, this design choice was a bit of a disappointment.The introductory scene with the awful lip syncing and character models was shocking, but thankfully, this was not indicative of the game as a whole. Graphics are decent, nothing breathtaking, but detailed enough to make the cadavers appear haunted. Majority of the demons are seen in fleeting moments and have a simple design, such as the ceramic-looking crouched demon, always lurking around corners. Its all-white flaky appearance with bulbous, dark piercing eyes is sure to catch players off-guard.Voice acting is decent. There are the odd door closing/creak sounds, light switches and even some demonic voices. However, I think the audio could have been used more to keep players on edge, or at least to mislead the process of trying to find out the demons name, which I found painstakingly easy. Took me around 2.5 hours for one playthrough, subsequent playthroughs less than 30 minutes. Player choice, but I imagine entering data into the computer would be more difficult using a controller. Yes, to achieve the five endings, find the extras and see the full story events (but see Story section for a more detailed summary).This review may come across as quite mixed, which it is, but I still enjoyed my time in TMA. In summary, I loved my first playthrough, the setting is fantastic and unique, the scares and intense atmosphere is chilling, but the game design choice to rely on replays to learn the protagonist's story, which may or may not even trigger, combined with the already repetitive embalming process is not encouraging for subsequent playthroughs. Overall, The Mortuary Assistant is a short but enjoyable experience for horror fans,  but at least for the moment, I recommend it at a heavy sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love horror, but I've seen so many horror movies and played so many horror games that for a long time nothing managed to even slightly scare me anymore. _childDocuments_.review: It's a huge step in the right direction for indie horror, relying more on atmosphere than jumpscare, while still being very scary at times.Like most indie horror games, it's unfortunetly too short and doesn't have that much replayability. The game however is well designed and I can see the creators updating it and making it something bigger and more complex, like Visage, for example.

_childDocuments_.review: While I've only gotten one ending so far, I'm very excited to see what's in store for this game. It makes the player feel not just scared, but unsettled, in a way that not many modern horror games have been able to achieve in recent years. Also, the developers did an amazing job in fleshing out enough of Rebecca's story so that we as players can get attached and relate to her, but not too much that we lose interest and become bored. My only critiques, if I was forced to make them, would be to flesh out some of the other characters such as Grandma and Rebecca's boss, especially the latter. I think that if we got more details and information about how he ended up in his position and not just what he's been doing to stop it from happening would make for an all around better experience. Also, I think a little more variety in the bodies we're embalming and the states we find them in to make it more challenging to pick the demon's name would be very fun. Overall 8/10. For a game to crawl out of demo hell, they have to be doing something right, and The Mortuary Assistant is definitely doing something completely right.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game would be boring, but it's actually really fun. I like the atmosphere of the game as well as the designs of the characters and demons. The Halloween seasonal content was a lot of fun, especially the clown, which I'm sad was only there for a limited time. There is more variety to the gameplay than I expected, with finding demonic sigils and preparing the bodies. I enjoyed the different endings too. Overall, it's a spooky game with quite a few jump scares. Jump scares aren't scary to me, but they are done well in this game. There are also "quiet" scares that I enjoyed such as figures just silently slipping into view before disappearing. It's fun spotting them each shift.I like that each shift is different and you have to pay close attention to figure out where the demon is, so it would be fun to have more content added. I'd like to see different types of shifts and a couple new characters. Maybe you get a visitor wanting to see the body of their deceased loved one and you have to deal with that on top of everything else. Or you have to visit another mortuary to help a fellow mortician. I did not like playing as a specific character. It would be more fun to me if you could create a character (or choose from multiple ones) and select different backstories that influence how the demons scare you.Honestly, I find the gameplay to be a bit... "cozy" in a way lol. I get so involved in the work of embalming that I don't notice the haunts half the time and find them annoying, like let me do my job, demons!

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is one of the most unique and compelling horror games I've ever experienced. I have to commend the solo developer responsible for this game, as it outshines the bulk of AAA studios and their comparably poor output in the horror market. I greatly appreciate how tastefully employed the jump-scares are in this game - I don't believe that jump-scares are strictly off-limits for horror games like a lot of people do as they're perceived to be fairly cheap ( they often are I'll grant you that ) but in this game they feel earned and are typically spaced out enough to let you recover, but never fully. It's a great one-off experience to have either alone or with friends as the core gameplay loop does eventually become quite stale and repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say this was one of my favorite horror games that I've played this year. _childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of the best first person horror games I've ever played. What makes this game so much better is the scares are silent - you can be working or walking around and suddenly you'll notice something has been staring at you from the corner the whole time. The game's main goal is to find out which body is possessed and what the demon possessing said body's name is. Sounds simple enough; just make sure you are right, because otherwise...

_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game with:* A good story* Effective jumpscares* Difficult puzzles that you can still figure out without having your hand held* Good voice acting* Randomness done well* Lore that can be entirely uncovered in-game without a wiki or ARG nonsense* Grim sense of humor used sparingly* AND a perfect level of self-awareness for the inherently goofy parts of the macabre subject matter...It's like threading the eye of a needle while the needle is still buried in the haystack.  I watched Let's Plays of this game first before purchasing it and it *still* scares me.  The story is *still* heartbreaking.  This is the least "indie-horror game" I've seen an indie-horror game be in years.  There are still some visual bugs, control frustrations, and even the sadly random run-ending bug if you're unlucky, but the dev seems very proactive in patching bugs and making improvements, so I 100% recommend this game regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: 65/100 Decent Indie Horror ExperienceThe game looks great but performs like butt. I don't have a horrible P.C. But I don't have a top of the line build either. This game CHEWED through my GPU so badly I can only imagine what it would have done on full settings or if the map had been just been a bit bigger. But to be fair, that is my biggest gripe. The rest of the game was a pretty standard horror experience.What they did right:- More creepy scenes than actual jump scares- Alternate endings- A ton of things to investigate and prolong your entertainment- A thorough objective based process that is sort of therapeutic. - Unnerving distractions to keep you from said goals-The game also is an investigation that requires you to pay attention- Some damn good scares. Best I've seen in a while.- price was fine; could be a lil cheaperWhat they did wrong:- Story had potential but was bland- After only 5 short hours the scenes got repetitive- to a point it annoyed me to go through them- GPU usage was bananas- causing a good bit of frame drops but i got it stable enough to have a good time.What I would love to see:- maybe a dlc about Raymond or just updates adding more scenarios and demons so that I could play this again- an endless shift mode where bodies keep coming in, in batches and you play until you are possessed.- some stream of content to prolong the longevity of this gameWhat I really enjoyed was how this game actually tried to be creepy more than in your face. I respect and hope for more games like that in the future. The genre has been oversaturated with tedious jumpscare and run games. This game is definitely a nice change of pace. You actually have a way to fight back, though these method (for such a short game) get very repetitive and so do the scenes. But overall it was a positive experience. It just overstayed its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite horror games to come out this year! A one-man dev team, this guy REALLY knows how to creep under your skin with subtle scares rather than loud jump-scares. Every time I play this game, I do have some trouble falling asleep at night because some of the scares keep me up thinking about them. Very cool story, and I like that there are multiple endings. Make sure to play this game several times to get the full story! Highly replayable. Very much looking forward to enjoying the game even longer because he is updating the game with new features!

_childDocuments_.review: Going against the grain here and giving this a negative review. To be edited later, if things suddenly change and take a better turn... I will try again later too. Maybe it will change my mind and I can change my review, but this is first run view point and  I bought this on a sale. It was initially pretty spooky. Had some shock and awe factor... I was early on infuriated at the random items strewn about the room. It really broke immersion for me. Then later found the game setting to stop the randomizing items...which omg.. godsend. I enjoyed it a bit more but then.... the tedium kicked in... the first few times I ran through the scripted events they were genuinely interesting and spooky... but that quickly waned. By the end of the night I was yelling at grandma to just go away so I could get my work done and frustrated because I couldn't figure out which paranormal scripted event was preventing me from doing the embalming part of the job... I'd already got all the runes, figured out the demon and just wanted to burn it with the mark in the fire, but one of the many different incarnations of activity were preventing me from finishing the job.Then the bugs... the shadow, who I named Charlie... just kept popping in and getting stuck in the area for long periods of time. Sometimes I'd get stuck sitting down with no head...have to restart. The key binds and ui feel janky and irritating. The story has potential of being interesting but the way the game is designed to have random events along with the bugs and the randomness of the story scripted events, it doesn't really let me see the story in a linear fashion and that's just a bit off-putting for me. I wanted to know her story...and by the end of my session I wasn't scared by any of it and was more frustrated by the events preventing from seeing the story. I would love to see a linear mode, where each shift gives you a piece of the story until you have everything sorted out. I wanted to like this, but it's just not scary being stuck in a scripted event I've seen for the tenth time.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hyped for this game after reading some of the reviews, that it was a true piece of horror and not the same jumpscare bs abundant these days. So in order not to spoil the surprise for myself, I jumped in as blind as possible and... wouldn't say I was entirely disappointed but... it was pretty close.So first things first, the tutorial SUCKS BALLS. It is ridiculously unintuitive and I had to google how to do even the most basic tasks because the tutorial box just showed a simple motion and you can't access it ever again. It's gone. After getting a hang of the simple, repetitive movements, I noticed that the game's collision detection also sucks. I would not normally hammer on something like that as much in a small game, but considering a huge part of the game is literally noticing strange things and patterns in the 3D model of the deceased, having a huge ass slab clipping into the body and protuding from the back, because devs never coded rotation, is pretty immersion breaking.There are also things that are never explained to you, such as the ashes, and there's nowhere in cutscenes or whatever that tells you there's that option. Game has very little replay value, despite that being the literal game mode, and overall feels boring and unpolished; once you've seen what there's to see, you've seen it all. Did I mention getting an ending relies exclusively on RNGesus?No thanks. Not my cup of tea, and certainly not at full price. Maybe on 50% or more it would be what this game's worth. You can get more mileage out of a free browser game.

_childDocuments_.review: -------------------------ADDITIONAL UPDATE-------------------------So I dug it back up and started over, again, to get a fresh, bug-free run. Also, I'm playing on Linux and the game honestly runs shockingly well, considering it's on Proton AND on my workhorse's limited architecture. ANYWAY:So I beat it and got the good ending, and I can officially say that all salt has drained from my blood and mood and I can be fully objective. I will say that what's here is quite good, and it's really impressive for the dev to have produced it. But we're not quite there yet; there are some gameplay conceits that I really don't like (please don't take control away during hauntings; maybe make 'backstory' hauntings optional for a more 'pure' run mode?), but there's also a good number of bug and instability problems holding this one back. I would say I WOULD recommend, but not before either a significant reduce in price (I'd say $15, max, but everybody's judgment is different) or a more stable and less railroaded experience is available. I look forward to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around a little more and also picking this one back up during the holidays to see how far it's come. Good idea, good execution, good work.-------------------------UPDATE-------------------------I've had one of those things where you pull a game out of Hidden because you're not COMPLETELY sure you didn't like it, and after starting over, I got stuck in two different haunts because the things I had to do were unclear and couldn't be done out of order. The first time, it was the apartment, and not knowing I couldn't pick up the Needle item that I COULD find up before finding the Tubing that I could NOT, I was stuck in there for quite some time. Ended up looking up a guide to get through it, and then when I finally did, game just flat-out crashed. It did so again in the blacked-out hallway to cold storage; the lights went completely out and then the game never came out of the black void. Even tried moving around to see if I could catch light off of something or see a light where I supposed to go and there just wasn't.. When I quit out of THAT, now I can't even get to the main menu anymore; it's just a black screen with the save symbol in the center of the screen while the main menu music plays and I can't change it or make any choices to get past it.It is because of these things that I am adding "buggy, railroady, and not ready for prime time yet" to the pile.That said, damn game gave me the itch; I've been having a hard time putting it down and forgetting about it. So maybe I'll pick it up around Halloween and/or Christmas to see if they fix it.-------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW-------------------------One of the few games to actually manage to get under my skin, but there are mechanical irritations that keep me from really enjoying it. The visuals are super good, the atmosphere is great, it's very spooks, but the controls are obnoxious and inconsistent (why do I have to use a key from the inventory sometimes and other times I just use the door while having the key in my inventory?). Beyond which, there seems to be a scripted sequence of events, or at least scripted points where one of a series of events CAN happen, so repeat playthroughs, you'll get repeat visions and events or whatever. The annoying part comes in in that the game locks you out of working once you've "entered" a scene until you finish it. So for instance, you can be working and you'll notice the color change on the screen. Look up and there's a stringy-haired woman in the hall way. "♥♥♥♥ you", I says, I'll just keep doin' what I'm doin. "No," says the game, "you are locked out of interacting with any bodies or equipment until you have experienced the minimum number of spooks. Now go walk up to that ghost lady and get grabbed."That's already annoying, but it gets worse. Things are conveyed very briefly with tutorial screens, and you can't call them back up. Granted, you can look everything up on the net; you'll pick up your moves pretty quickly, but the fact that I was as confused as I was in my first game, right up until the end, seemed unfair. On which note, I thought I was supposed to be managing my fear because the game says the more scared you get, the worse the hallucinations get. Instead, there seems to be an invisible time meter that you just run throughout a... well a run.The final straw came in when on my third game, keeping in mind the game tells you to look for a reaction (which can be subtle or very unsubtle) when you place the binding tablet in order to know it's the right body. I burned the wrong body on game 2, and I remember nothing happening when I placed the tablet. This time when I did, a symbol burned into the forehead of the corpse and it started talking and the lights flickered like crazy. Seems like a reaction to me, so I burned him. Wrong body again. And I know, the game says that while you're working, the demon may try to mislead you, but I was under the impression that the mark-placing reaction was a unique one, because otherwise, if the demon could still be screwing with you, why would they tell you to look for a reaction specifically when placing the mark?It all seemed obnoxiously esoteric and inconsistent, and after three tries, I wasn't confident enough in my understanding of how it worked that I had anything I wanted to try anymore, so I think I'm done. And that's a shame; I really wanted to like this. Also not a super great use of 25 bucks, but whatever, I guess; that's the chance we take.Anyway, visuals are good, so just wait for the LP scene to get a hold of this game, find someone who does 'em that you don't hate, and enjoy the game that way. I don't think it's worth the expense. Not at least until it tunes its ♥♥♥♥ up pretty significantly.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What a game. This is absolutely one of the best horror games I've played - especially one that's not a big budget AAA game like F.E.A.R. or Dead Space. It goes extremely light on the jumpscares and extremely heavy on atmospheric horror, which is by far the best kind. The whole game is eerie and finds ways to put you on edge that I would never have thought of.The first playthrough is absolutely flawless in setting the stage. The nebulous "time limit" you're on creates a real sense of urgency, and while you're given copious amounts of direction and "tutorial"-type guidance in the form of notes and tapes, it is a lot of information to take in quickly, which immediately immerses you. It's very much a "learn or die" type scenario, which is incredible for creating tension.Further playthroughs lose out on that as you learn the ropes and become more efficient, but the randomness of the "haunts" and the way the game functions does lend it quite a bit of replayability. Additionally, there arl=e multiple endings (many of which can be mutually canon, with at least one non-canon bad end) which encourages exploration and continued play, as well as a sense of continuity between shifts. Furthermore, it appears the developer(s) are intent on adding more content and expanding the game, which is excellent given that it has a very strong base.My one complaint is that you're tasked with investigating and deciphering many small mysteries within a shift, one of which is identifying a certain body - however, many of the "tells" for identifying a body are also shared with major "haunts", aka semi story-based events that occur, which can lead you very much astray. It is frustrating to fail a shift because you were not able to determine which was the correct body. I will expand on this in a spoiler, should you like elaboration.Overall, this is a fantastic game that is absolutely worth the price tag, and I would say a mandatory purchase for any fans of horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: First, i just want to say, there's not a lot to this game. you're a mortician, you do a handful of tasks to do your job, and that's pretty much it. Now, while you do your job, you get random visits from various entities and may even find yourself being transported into a completely other location. There are also a handful of secrets you can look for and discover, but in general, it's a pretty small world that you play in, and the tasks you do, if you want to experience most of the game, you'll need to complete multiple times. As far as the scare/horror aspect of the game, most of it is tied in jump-scares. However, I do want to say, the jump-scares actually startled me in this game, when usually they have zero affect on me. This is because, in many horror-type games, you're always expecting jump scares. You're moving through much larger maps, and are essentially always expecting random things to occur - because that's just how those games work. But, in this game, you're literally just doing your "job," and it's a pretty chill, quiet job. You're in a quiet building, quietly embalming dead people, and you get kind of in the zone, when something will appear out of the corner of your eye, or charge at you, or a loud sound, and you're just not expecting it, and it's quite startling and disorienting. So, the jump scares in this game actually do stuff, because you're just so calm most of the time. That said, after about my 3rd shift, even the jumpscares stopped having any impact on me, so you do get used to it. It really just becomes part of your routine, and you're no longer surprised or startled. What i'm trying to say is - the setup for the jumpscares works much better in this situation, as opposed to most other games with jump scares. Now, that said - i ran into multiple bugs that caused me to have to restart the game in its entirety. I prefer subtitles on in my game, and even though i checked the box to turn subtitles on, they literally never turned on. Some of the other bugs i ran into include: not being able to burn a body. I'd literally do everything i was supposed to, it'd lock in place, i'd click the red button, but nothing would happen. Another issue was some menu items getting stuck on the screen, and i couldn't click anywhere, not even to escape and exit the game cleanly. Had to task manager that issue. So, if you're looking for a more calm, yet jumpy-horror game (not really sure how those 2 fit together, but this game managed it quite well, i think), where you don't really die unless you can't identify a demon, i recommend this game. I enjoyed it. If they ever come out with expansions, like new characters to play stories with, or just even new things to explore with the main character, i'd absolutely get back into this game and be a mortician a few more times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: While I did end up refunding this game because it was so terrifying to me, I could not recommend this game enough. It is incredibly well made, does an amazing job of creating a generally unsettling and eerie vibe that is quick to be bone-chilling without needing to lean on conventional jumpscares. The process of embalming is fairly accurate for the time period the game is set in, and overall the look of the game is phenomenal. If I wasn't such a scaredy cat I would have kept this game and it likely would have been one of my top games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Sept 20, 2022Full game completion update (11 or so hours in)The difficulty in this game is basically, they move the items/tools around to makeyou take more time getting lost looking for them. Feels like a weird way to add "difficulty". This is actually where my original confusion came from during my5 hours of night/shift 1 (where as most people beat it around 2hours). During theday/tutorial the items are in a specific place, then in night one they're somewhereelse. I can't imagine what the "lore-friendly" reason is, the demon/s are walking aroundcarefully re-arranging your items on the shelves/counter/cabinets. If you want toblame it on the demons, it would make more sense to just toss all the interactablesall over the room (but allow the player to place things on surfaces, instead of justdropping them at our feet on the floor only).A nice QOL change would be to allow the player to place things on surfaces.Currently you can only drop items on the floor at your feet. Another QOL change,would be to put the clipboard (that uses an inventory slot, even though it's not ausable item) on the wall somewhere so we can still hold 2 large objects. Or just a whiteboard/chalkboard/markerboard with the checklist on it. No matter how I thinkof it, it shouldn't be a thing. From a game standpoint or realistically.I like the different endings and how's there's a little replay value. I wish more gamesdid stuff like this. An idea I had (maybe for a sequel?) would be if it was limited to a certain amount of nights, all with multiple endings to unlock (like how it is currently, but not infinite nights to play). Then depending on the endings collected for the nights you played, you get a unique ending as a whole.___________________________________________________________________Probably a bug, but the "high DPI" setting seems to turn itself either on, or off at random times. In the apartment, my sensitivity is always sluggish, no matter what it'sset to. So i'll either turn it off or on (which ever it isn't, because no matter what it's setto, I HAVE to toggle it to the opposite setting). Then when I leave the apartment and play the night the controls are sluggish again (even though the setting is still set as itwas in the apartment). This makes me toggle a few times between high DPI on/off. Sometimes it fixes it with it off, sometimes on. I tried to find a pattern, but couldn't.___________________________________________________________________On top of this, there are several different buttons that interact/return-from-interacting. I'd like it if there was a global interact/drop button. Some things you interact with E, or space, or left click, or right click...and you put them down with q, or right click, or Esc (sometimes not the same button you used to interact with them). ___________________________________________________________________(Original review posted after first play-through of 1 shift, lasting 5hours below)The Confusion Assistant This game is so confusing, most of it I don't understand. Huge info-dump at the beginning, with no tool-tips/verbal cues to keep you on trackof what to do. You have a clipboard but that's only partially helpful.I've spent 20-30 minutes trying to find chemicals before (on to that later), or what Ishould do next. I really feel like the "post tutorial/training" activities should bepracticable, especially with how much of an info dump it is. Hey, it's later. I played on the lowest graphic settings. When you do this, one of the chemicalssitting near the connecting-corridor doors becomes completely illegible. Oddlyenough, the back of your bosses card can still be read fine.Unfortunately, these problems persisted throughout my entire play-though makingit almost unbearable to enjoy. When I finally started having fun, I died. I bet you're wondering why I chose to "recommend" this game?Because of the scares. That's it. Most horror games don't have SUBTLE jumpscares.You're usually bleeding from the ears at horror games. Not this one. The scares arethere, but they're quiet. They lurk in the dark like batman. They just waiting for youto notice them like you noticed senpai. Horror games need more subtle scares,lurking scares like this game has.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most (if not, the most) unpredictable and uneasy horror games I've ever played...and I think it's pretty great.The fact that this game is randomly generated every time you do a new shift really adds a different take, even if some of the scares are similar from the last shift you've done, they can still get you off-guard and you don't know when they or what will hit you.The only downsides I can say about this game is that due to it's small, condensed nature, the process of embalming 3 bodies in each shift can get repetitive, so I'd recommend doing each shift at your own pace (as the scares can also get to the player a bit much at times) and due to the unpredictable nature of the game, there maybe some events that may not trigger that can allow you to get a different ending.Still, the concept and mechanics work very well (despite some bugs here and there and turning the gurney can feel rather stiff), the sound design is solid and the atmosphere is nicely done. All this crafted by a solo developer is astonishing.The full retail price may seem a bit much for many, so I do suggest waiting for a sale, even for the most curious. I got this during launch week at a 10% discount and I haven't regret it since I streamed this game online via Twitch and has been quite of an experience. Definitely worth a look (if you can handle it).UPDATE: They've added a new ending to the game which expands the lore of the story in a very intriguing way that I cannot spoil and it does leave the player wanting more. That's one positive I'll give is the developer's dedication to not only improving the game but adding more post launch. Wish them all the best!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is a *touch* expensive but it is a good experience. There's a couple bugs to be wary of as of this writing, one of them potentially game blocking but most don't get the bug as far as I can tell.The pros:- Good atmosphere- Good build-up to the end of a "shift"- Fantastic story in general for what's thereThe cons:- The animations are off-putting. They're not "smooth" enough... I'm not sure how to explain it but it's very evident in a couple of the endings- The graphics could be better- The game isn't very optimizedOverall, the game is really fun for what's there. Depending on if you care about the story, you're going to get anywhere from 1.5 to ~4 hours out of the game probably. It's a bit pricy for the $25 but it's not too awful. I think $20 would have been far more reasonable. I can't really talk much about the story other than it's too short but interesting.The jump scares have a good balance with atmosphere but they *definitely* held back some punches in the scare factor. The game could be 2x scarier if they wanted it to be. But given that I see people who are too scared about the game as it is, perhaps that was a good thing. Personally, I like a horror game that has me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants involuntarily but the game is just shy of that.I'm not a fan of the UI or controls in general. The gurney is difficult to move for some reason, sometimes the damage you have to input into the computer doesn't "register" for some reason, but it's serviceable and I ended up getting used to it fairly easily.There could also have been a bit more variation in cutscenes and bodies that you work on.Overall, a good game to play and also a good game to watch others play. 7.5/10 (an actual 7.5 meaning well above average)Bugs I've run into as of this writing:- Sometimes when a cutscene moves your character model, it gets "stuck" so you can be literally laying down and walking around at the same time. This isn't a big deal (and more funny than anything) but it makes viewing whatever you're holding impossible... including the clipboard and letting paper.- There's a fairly annoying bug where two demons can have the same mark sigils... meaning it's impossible to accurately choose the correct demon, it turns into a 50% chance of choosing the right one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really impressive one.Plot:You start off as a student who is looking for an internship at mortuary and eventually find one. Your grandma doesn't really support your idea of working there but won't tell you why. You arrive for your first shift and embalm a body which turns out to be haunted. Raymond, your boss makes excuses for flying stuff won't let you finish up the embalming and tells you to go home for the rest of the day, in the meantime you complain to your friend about your problems on the phone until you get and unexpected call from Raymond, who is asking you to work a night shift on a short warning. He claims there are three bodies and nobody else could make for now. You approach the mortuary only to find Raymond nowhere and he locks you in the place. He then calls you and instructs to pick up different kinds of items and promises to unlock the door. You may try to escape but it's no use. When you go to the cold storage you'll find three different bodies which need to be embalmed and as you do that, you will soon find out you're not alone. Raymond tells you on the phone that you must banish a demon, and as he speaks you will be confused and bitter due to thinking he's just pranking you and trying to scare you. Raymond apologizes and persuades you to start working and has left some instruction tapes for you to play on your tape recorder, but watch out, sometimes it's not Raymond speaking. He also tells you on the call that he isn't gonna call again so you should forget about the phone. He wishes you luck and tells you to keep record with notepad and gives you only hours of time to banish the demon before you succumb to its power. The review:In my opinion the game has a lot of interesting events and haunts which you have to endure while operating bodies. Funniest thing is that the body might snap its fingers or stand up or start moving around the room which scared me sh#tless. I recommend the game to everyone who is interested in ghosts and demons.Guessing the demon tends to get hard due to having to find sigils and combine them to find the demon's name from three different name tables. If you get it wrong, you're done while burning the body.The graphics look good and are suitable for this type of game, no need to go overkill and waste a lot of money for AAA graphics on a game like this. Controls are easy but require some time to get used to since there is a quick inventory and inventory itself.Got this game as a gift, but would pay the whole price just to experience this interesting story

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem.As far as I understood there is a bit of randomness in the game and you cannot predict most of the events, at least when you're playing first time. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely giving this game a 10/10. Its a short game (I got all 6 endings in 23 hours), but it's absolutely worth it if you like jump scares. Not a whole lot of cons, it's just an all-around solid game. I recommend headphones and playing in the dark, and if you can, keep a pen and some paper next to you. There's some symbols you need to remember, and drawing them helps.It CAN get kinda gross. If you're not a fan of seeing wounds or teeth, you probably won't enjoy the game. The ick factor is kind of low, but if you don't like those things, I recommend watching a playthrough of the embalming process before buying.For achievement completionists (Is that a word? It is now.), I will say here: If you want to not have to erase your data for two achievements, look up an achievement guide for The Phone's Dead and No Way Out. You need to do those on the first night.The game is short and repetitive, but after the third shift, you won't even need to look at your clipboard anymore (especially if you don't have the item randomization on). However, your redundant tasks are spiced up by the different kinds of hauntings you can see throughout the night. After the first night, you can adjust how aggressive the hauntings are - I recommend keeping the low default until you get your bearings, it's easier to see the hauntings if you know what you're doing. Once I got comfortable, I cranked it up all the way, lots of fun!The storyline is pretty interesting - leaving you enough to be curious for more without feeling disappointed. I'm hoping they add more stuff. Also I got this around Christmas, and the seasonal themes were hilarious, my friends and I decided there was a string of Mall Santa murders, to explain why Santa was always there.All in all, a short but excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

It's confusing.- Processing the bodies is really repetitive- Endings are boring and not worth it- The special endings require specific *random* haunts to trigger.The only positive aspect about this game is some of the haunts/scares, but they only work once of course and tend to repeat.

_childDocuments_.review: Horror titles are pretty much dime a dozen in the world of Indie gaming, so it is always pleasing to encounter a game which strives to do something a little differently. It is this desire for a new, fresh experience which inspired me to come across "The Mortuary Assistant", and why I since first playing the game's Prologue teaser I have been champing at the bit to play it. Mortuaries and funeral homes are pretty unsettling places at the best of times. Films like "The Mortuary Collection" and "The Autopsy Of Jane Doe", and the stories recounted by the likes of such famous names as KoRn's Jonathan Davis (from his time working at a mortuary in his hometown of Bakersfield), have done well to establish their notoriety among the annuls of American Gothic popular culture. Much like with those who work in cemeteries and morgues, it takes a very specific type of person to work a job where the majority of their time is in company of the dead, and this game directly confronts the player with the stark question of whether THEY are that sort of person? You play as Rebecca, a bright-eyed bushy-tailed young intern seeking her first real job at a small town mortuary under the supervision of the somewhat strident and off-kilter proprietor Raymond Delver (who visually resembles a cross between Viggo Mortensen and Dolph Lundgren). During her first few nights on the job, it is    revealed that Raymond has set Rebecca up for a night of terror in the company of a demon that has attached itself to her. The only way to banish the demon? Trap it within one of the corpses using the skills employed by the mortician's trade and burn the corpse in the on-site incinerator. As the aforementioned description would suggest, the game is part-medical simulation, part-supernatural Horror. The process of learning how to properly prepare the deceased for a funeral is presented with such systematically clinical precision that it becomes more enlightening than unsettling. being guided through the process of readying the dead for the last hurrah is definitely where the game shines. It opens a window on an aspect of the world that many of us have previously not been privy to, especially with regard to how a corpse is properly drained, embalmed and then maintained. Less intriguing are the game's genre aspects. As you can imagine, there is periodically all manner of "Conjuring" style ooga-booga, and the latter segments of the game increasingly see you play exorcist rather than mortician. It is an uncomfortable collision of science and superstition which doesn't make for a great fit. And it is this insistence on genre which is the game's biggest flaw (in my opinion). Often, the game will suspend all interactions within the environment in an attempt to force players to experience a "spooky" moment or jump scare. Considering that an integral plot element - and indeed a related achievement - is to largely ignore these occurrences so as not to be deterred from your task, it would have been nice to have had the option of a 'rationalist run' where one could focus solely on the job rather than being constantly corralled down the path of 'spooky house' thrills. Otherwise, the game is an impressive and enjoyable experience. Aesthetics, gameplay and soundtrack are all done very well; and the story has a few nice twists and turns to break the usual predictability of the demonic possession sub-genre. Even then, there are a few genuinely frightening moments. Most of the time, the game will telegraph when something eerie is about to go down by way of a few visual echoes or a sudden cut to darkness. However, every so often, the game does throw a curve ball in the form of random unannounced visitations. On more than one occasion, I nearly leapt out of my skin because I suddenly came face to face with an unexpected nasty whilst going about my duties. Therefore, even amidst the sea of cliches, some inspiration shines through.  In short, the game is but another example of a 4 star game which could have been a 5 star game. It is  definitely a refreshing change from the usual fare of "wander around in the dark and flee in terror" and for  that it is definitely worth a look, especially if you have a medical background or come from a medical family. Be advised however that it is a short game, albeit one with five different endings to keep you guessing.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)The Mortuary Assistant is one of the best horror games you can play if you are looking to get scared and experience a horrific experience that is never quite the same due to its random paranormal events. You play Rebecca, an assistant at a mortuary who works under her boss, Raymond; her job entails putting corpses into storage after treating them with specific processes. The game is proficient in distraction and surprise, as you must manage your work as an assistant and deal with the demonic entities. The more time you take to perform the duties, the more Rebecca will lose her mind, making her susceptible to the demon's influence. It creates a pace of juggling your responsibilities while avoiding getting spooked.The Mortuary Assistant starts slow as the game gives you a tutorial on how to play it, and there is a big respite to get used to the title's mechanics. As progress is made and time goes by, the game will ramp up the scares to the point that there is no respite between the attacks specters and ghosts perform on you. That is an excellent design, as a horror game that sets the stage and atmosphere before the scares make you tense and more vulnerable to becoming afraid.The task also plays a massive role in that atmosphere of dread and horror, as while they do not change between corpses, the interactions you will experience while working on them are entirely different. Focusing too much on the checklist leaves you open to attacks, while not performing it fast makes paranormal activity more likely. While the map is small, as it's only the Mortuary, it works in favor of the game as it gives a sensation of being trapped in a secluded space and, more importantly, a dreadful realization that you are completely isolated from other humans. Your only company is the demons that are out to get you.The game's strong point is that the player shapes the experience, so it has no specific linear path. How the player plays and what the game presents in a single run creates a variable that makes it so that there is no way to prepare for what will happen or when. Coupled with the atmosphere and tension, the game slowly introduces, and you have a formula for a title that, while short for a single run, can be pretty intense.The Mortuary Assistant visuals are excellent; the game features high visuals that make the graphics look crisp and realistic, reinforcing the immersion when you play through it that you are in the Mortuary. The corpses all have good detail, making looking at them a sight that can make you nervous as you wonder if they will move out of nowhere. The demons themselves come in various shapes resulting from figures that give comfort only to them crushed into despair, uneasy forms that can provide terrible frights and even shadows that chase after you when you least expect it. Not having a single design for the demon and using multiple forms makes the game feel jumpy, for you do not know what shape they will take the next time they go after you.When it comes to sound, the game does a solid job. Noise, phone calls, sound effects, and voice acting all add to the game's suspense. The demon can communicate with you, and choosing to let them speak can result in discomfort as you don't know how to answer the opportunity of speaking with another human as you let the phone ring. The voice actors do an excellent job of portraying characters and making the story believable.Replayability is something that The Mortuary Assistant keeps in mind, as five different endings can be unlocked, and the game always presents each run with some differences, holding the title fresh even after beating it. If you are a player that beats a game and then moves to another videogame, know that a run of the game takes around 2-4 hours, while getting all endings can result in about 10-15 hours total.Performance-wise, the game runs well, and the glitches are few; that being said, some game-breaking bugs could require a restart of the game, but very little progress is lost due to these errors, which are rare to witness. On an RTX 2060, the game ran at 70 fps with the graphics in ultra.The Mortuary Assistant hits all the notes of what a good horror game should aspire to be: a dreadful sensation that slowly crawls up to you and then bursts into a horrifying experience that lets you feel fear. It understands the pacing for crafting horror and uses all its elements beautifully as it combines them into a blend of fear and nerve-racking gameplay. This game is a must-buy if you like horror titles and want to be stressed and scared. If you are not into replaying titles, consider getting it on a sale, and if you are looking to get into the genre, consider other games before jumping into the abyss. 10/10  MASTERPIECEIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, creepy horror puzzle game!You play as a freshly-educated and interned assistant, called in to help with a night shift. Upon arriving you find you’re locked in, and your only way out is to embalm up to three cadavers while figuring out which of the bodies a demon is hiding in. Guess correctly before they possess you, burn their body, and survive to do it again the next night. Fail, and you won’t like the experience.There are five official endings, two of which are very tricky to achieve, and a dozen or so story elements unfolding Rebecca’s past. You’ll need to complete at least 6 or 7 shifts to get every possible ending and see all story events, so don’t expect to dump hundreds of hours into a long-running game.Still, worth every penny.
