_childDocuments_.review: Archvale, a small indie game and – I believe – a first outing for the developer. One part SNES-Zelda, one part Dark Souls, and one part Binding of Isaac, Archvale is a bullet-hell hack-n-slash RPG with cute graphics, bright colors, and addictive gameplay.Set in a fantasy world that has been closed off from all other realities, you play as a nameless and mysterious character who is the first person ever to stand up to the giant, dungeon-dwelling boss characters who guard the fragments of the arch, a gateway to a realm that has sealed a great evil. You travel the lands encountering enemies, towns full of aid, and secrets to find around every corner. Its a simple game, with simple combat and an easy to understand loop; you dodge incoming projectiles and toss your own, gaining enough gold and materials to buy and upgrade your equipment and getting stronger the whole time.The array of combat options is delightfully robust but still small enough to be tight. I ended up playing as a mage because I found the elemental damage and firing rates of some of the wands and books to be better, but the melee weapons (everything fires projectiles, even swords and axes, mind you) still pack a punch. Though if you look around every corner you can find and complete a weapon so powerful that it trivializes the final bosses of the game, though you can’t get that until near the end.The progression is blocked, really, only by skill to a certain point. There are a few roadblocks that require you to complete certain challenges and obtain certain items, but you can’t get to the credits without completing every dungeon anyhow, so “sequence breaking” isn’t really a worthwhile tactic. Plus, the dungeons are fun and the right level of difficult and the boss fights are MOSTLY well put together and paced. More than once though I found a boss that was a bit much and required quite a few attempts. And that’s where the Dark Souls mechanic comes in (as well as the mentioned BOI similarities).When you die in this game, you transport back to the most recently “active” checkpoint (of which there are a large number and each one gives you a permanent but small stat boost) and you have to trek through the enemies you killed, again, to reach your point of death. You also lose some resources forever in this process, but you can save a bunch of money in towns at the banks, each one unlocked upping the cap for how much you can save. This comes in handy for keeping a steady upgrade to your weapons and armors as you go (the armors also change your appearance which, while unnecessary, is cute and adds an extra touch of character to the game). The bosses, meanwhile, are sometimes ripped from Isaac in obvious ways (the slime bosses are just Monstro clones, for example) and you deal with them like you would bosses at the end of floors in that game. Its addictive and fun and you never feel like you can’t win, ever. You just gotta “git gud”.Overall, a solid, fairly short game. My 100% playthrough took me just about 11 and a half hours and that was only to get all the achievements, which aren’t really necessary, so probably a 8-9 hour game, really. Its cute, its fun, there were no bugs and no giant difficulty spikes that made progress a chore, and the music – which wasn’t anything particularly special – was inoffensive and helped move the game along. An enjoyable little indie and I hope, based on the ending, there is a sequel coming at some point because I’d play the heck out of it!

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun adventure game with bullet hell action and some Zelda vibes.You go around the world to find the Arch pieces, which are in dungeons guarded by a boss, using your weapons, dash and bombs.There are melee, ranged and magic weapons at your disposal. Magic weapons are weaker than the others, but enemies release stars that increase your fire rate when hit by magic, which kinda compensates. Some weapons can be bought, but most of them will be crafted with the materials dropped by enemies or found around the map.There are also badges that can be equipped to get various benefits. Some can be bought, but most of them will be found in the challenge orbs scattered around the world map, where you have to touch a crystal multiple times while dodging bullets for 3 rounds to get them. There isn't a penalty for failing besides restarting the round, so just keep trying until you win.Combat is fine, but there's little invincibility frames, which can lead to quick deaths if one's not careful.One of my complaint is about the roguelike elements: I think it doesn't add much to the game and it makes exploration feel kinda artificial in some cases. As an example, there are minibosses on the world map, but it feels like they're placed randomly, and same goes for the special rooms with chests and challenge orbs.I also would've like Zelda-like puzzles in the game. Dungeons have some rooms that requires using the dash skillfully, but nothing besides that. The bombs, for example, could've been used more, since they're basically useless outside of combat.Still, the game is very fun. Definitely a recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A bullet hell game about saving a mediaeval fantasy world from the forces of evil while constantly improving your character and gear.Archvale’s world is made up of small rooms, which require you to kill all enemies in them to advance to adjacent rooms. You respawn at set checkpoints, which are found every couple of rooms, dividing everything into bite-sized chunks for you to tackle. The map is split into different zones, each with its own difficulty and enemy types, which keeps the game decently fresh. Dungeons top off each of these zones, adding bosses and parkour challenges to the gameplay loop. Challenge rooms are also spread around the map, tasking you with collecting gems while different instakill projectiles are shot at you in varying patterns.The world map is randomly generated to a certain extend, although I’m not sure if this has a positive effect on gameplay. Mostly leads to dead ends and some sections between checkpoints becoming just a bit too hard but isn’t really noticeable otherwise.Your character’s gear can be improved in towns, through drops from enemies or simply by advancing through the game. Difficulty felt mostly fine, given you stay on top of upgrading your character, although some of the later parkour stages and challenge rooms went a bit overboard with the precision required to beat them. Similarly, the final boss felt just a bit too hard, with no way to further improve your character to overcome it.Archvale’s story and setting are rather generic but fine for getting you through the game. Coop is a bit glitchy but mostly works fine and is certainly fun.All in all, a game that doesn’t overstay its welcome and is both challenging and fun. Especially enjoyable with a coop partner.

This was from the same pattern by the big slimes in Murkmire area.Hitboxes:I swear the hitbox for either the character or some bullets is just slightly bigger than the sprite itself, I swear the sprites weren't even close yet I still take damage, (swear it's not a skill issue, at least not for the specific cases I'm complaining about. I'm not expecting as small of hitboxes as 2hu, just for the hitbox to be accurate to the sprite)Balance:As a preface, I like playing a game to my full ability, which includes using equipment that I think is the best, I don't like using worse equipment just because I know my current equipment makes the game easier (unless it's super DLC items that are actual cheats or something, won't use those)1) The almighty magic weapon type. Why would nerf yourself and use any other type, even the shopkeepers want you to use magic weapons by selling magic damage equipment (not sure if shop is randomized, but mine only sold a rapid fire fireball book, mage hood, and mage coat for a cool +15% magic attack damage)!They look weak by the numbers, but attack at least twice as fast, thrice as far, and most of the time they are multi hit and/or AoE.2) Magic weapons have higher DPS, higher range, safer to use, are more consistent, and comes with homing most of the time.All of those were without the special mechanic of your magic weapon gets stronger when picking up the magic stars that drop from enemies taking enough damage or dying, those magic stars make the disparity between magical and nonmagical weapons even greater3) I'm pretty sure the wooden sword you start with and the iron sword you can craft have literally the same stats4) Even the craftable weapons using material weapons don't matter since by the time you get both the weapon and the mats needed to create them, you can just craft the next area's ore weapon, which is probably 50% stronger.5) Upgrading feels a scam. I dumped 1000 into a single weapon to get maybe a 25% total bonus, or you can save that money for medals that can do the same thing for all weapons of a type or other more useful things.Maybe it's better late gameOther Stuff:1) Pretty sure the iron ore and darksteel ore have the same sprite before you break it, or at least very similar2) At least have like .1s of I-frames when you fall into a pit, but make it deal like 20% of your HP. Tired of getting trapped into losing half my HP because of the respawn. It's a lot less frustrating and more consistent when you just take damage from a fall rather than being spawned inside of bullets. I feel like the punishment for falling into a hole should be damage from the hole, not respawn RNG from getting out of the holeAll in all, it's not a bad game even if not very deep, but I think there needs to be a little bit of rework and polishing before I can recommend it, but the trials were cool though
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "small" RPGs I've played - almost on par with Nobody Saves the World,  just with bullet hell roots instead of aRPG ones. I don't play bullet hell genre, but the Easy difficulty in Archvale is very forgiving and welcoming -  wish more action games had this!It's not all great, though.The game has some of the worst reflex-based puzzles, EVER. In few cases, it's really a broken mess - because it requires input and reflex of 6-10 consecutive combos, faster than the game can process them, and the "dash" is unreliable by itself. How the dev considered this terrible mess "good enough" for a 1.0 release and did not fix (or remove!), is beyond me.Some of these puzzles are mandatory to complete the game (water temple..why is it always water temple?).While the rest of the game was excellent (at least for tiny indie team) - these things soured the experience.You've been warned :P
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the full price, despite some flaws.Bullet hell describes most of the combat, but it has some RPG elements. The game also takes place in an open world., but suitable for a game of this length. Essentially world is split into biome areas. You can see exact area layout the moment you enter it, but you can't see whats in each room. The world itself is fairly boring, but loot makes exploring feel rewarding despite your exploration rarely feeling like exploration. are badges (swappable upgrades), equipment, various upgrades and smaller stuff (like gold or materials) to get the former. keept me on my toes. There's a good variety of enemies, and attack patterns, which made progressing through the game a learning process and very small part a grind. It's not easy even on normal difficulty. It can only become somewhat easy with strong builds.Movement is a bit clunky for a bullet hell game. You can only move in cardinal directions (up, right, down, left and diagonal). Why is that a problem?Projectiles can fly in any directions and you often need to weave between them. When projectiles fly at you at some angles and you need to go between them, you effectively need to tap movement to position yourself. It's workable, but you'll have to build some muscle memory to compensate for lack of complete freedom of movementMoreover, dashes are short and have precise invincibility frames, which means you lose invincibility the moment you stop. That is a problem because dashing in cardinal direction does not allow you to evade precisely and will sometimes land you in a bad spot wherever you dash.It's mostly beating the game completely, but it features a few achievements that might have you grind a little (depending on how you manage resources).Very little padding and I appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I found myself enjoying this game much more than i anticipated... 100% it in less then 10 hours so i guess you could say it lacks a bit of content, but i really loved the time i spent on it.The Gameplay is engaging and with some enjoyable "minigames" throughout it.Also it looks absolutely gorgeous for a pixelated game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard, but it never feels unfair, everytime you die, you either have the oppurtunity to get stronger, or room for improvement. This game takes alot of inspiration from other games, Terraria, Enter the Gungeon, Celeste and a few others. However it isnt a copy of any of them. This game is incredible, the story isnt too interesting but not boring either. The bosses are amazing. My only problem, is that sometimes the game is too easy, and the gem trials. The gem trials suck dont do them unless you want achivements. The music is great and definetly something I would listen to outside of the game. And it looks nice too! There really is no reason not to get this game. Even if the difficulty scares some people, it really isnt that bad with all the upgrades and room for improvement.9/10                                                                (Would be a 10/10 if not for the gem trials)

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing! Took me about 12 hours to beat the game for the first time on normal mode... but the game has so much more replay-ability. Combat is responsive (never locks you in place), and most melee weapons have slash projectiles that actually make them interesting to use and less risky than typical melee weapons in games. The gameplay loop of clearing out rooms, upgrading gear, and defeating bosses gives the game a very well designed pace. Archvale is very linear compared to other bullet hells (the procedural generation is honestly not noticeable), but the loop is very fun so it doesn't matter too much. Ultimately, it's very clear this game was really well designed.Keep in mind, this game is a bullet hell, meaning that it's not for everyone. There are bullets, EVERYWHERE. They can be hard to dodge if you're not accustomed to dozens of bullets on screen at once. This game really does the genre very well and actually solves a common major issue with melee weapons (by giving them projectiles). As much as I hate to say it, I feel most of the negative reviews here are just people with skill issues.I do have some complaints, which are mostly QOA things, which didn't really detract from the game, they're just things I wish were done differently:- A sound effect for dashes being refreshed is more important than the bomb refresh sound effect, and would be very helpful- The damage certain projectiles do needs to be more uniform; The Exiled Wizard specifically has some projectiles that do significantly more damage (more than double) than others.- Zooming out on the map would be nice.- The blacksmith is relatively hidden. I didn't even realize he existed until I looked up how to get the achievement for fully upgrading a weapon, when I was in the last area.- The bomb felt pretty lackluster. I honestly forgot about it most of the time. It also does damage to yourself, which even though it's small, just serves to discourage me from using it.Overall, really fun game!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Neat game for $15.  Played on normal difficulty and beat the game over the course of a few days.  Good if you want to play a game that isn't intensive.You go around from room to room killing enemies.  The main objective is to find the the 7 arch pieces that are hidden in each biome.  Each biome comes with its own set of unique enemies and materials.Along the way you'll find short minigame areas that'll test your movement skills.  Completing them will give you badges, which can give you various buffs when equiped (think Paper Mario's badge system).You'll also find towns that come with a couple NPCs, an item shop, a bank, a badge shop, a crafting area, and a universal storage chest.  Once you talk to the vendors you'll be able to buy their wares in any other town, making it so you don't have to remember which shop sells what.There are a lot of weapons.  Each one falls under one of three damage types:  Melee, Magic, and Ranged.  Melee requires you to get close to the enemy, ranged allows you to stay away, and magic is like ranged but it has a gimmick.  Attacking enemies with a magic weapons drops little mana stars that give an attack speed boost for magic weapons.  There are many weapon subtypes.  To list a few:   These aren't all of the subtypes, but they're the ones I used in my playthrough.  Each subtype has its own unique attack pattern, so you can mix up your combat if you feel like it.  Some weapons can even apply debuffs.The story is pretty simple, but it's not that important for this game.Some tips:- Don't get attached to your items cause you'll be crafting/finding new ones often.- You can't sell your items to anyone so don't hesitate to trash them if you don't need it.- Crafting can pull from your universal storage chest, so store crafting ingredients in it.Would be neat if the game had a highscore gamemode.  The combat would serve such a mode well.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent bullet hell RPG. Completed and 100%'d in about 10 hours. I went with a magic build first playthrough. Might go again for a ranged or melee build. Overall though a pretty solid 8/10. No performance issues but half of the crafting recipes just straight don't need to exist since no one will use intentionally crappier weapons than the unique ones you get.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have too many expectations going into this game. I watched all the devlogs and it looked to be a pretty short experience, but I was pleasantly surprised. My first playthrough provided me with 22.1 hours of playtime, as I am a completionist and 100%ed everything I could (including getting all the best weapons fully upgraded). It was infuriating at times, but fun overall.My main issue with this game is that it feels unbalanced at times, and also feels like the progression system is too clean cut for each run to be different, despite the random generation. I think if a lot more were added I could see myself getting more use out of this game. Despite this, I can see this game being very fun for challenge players, people that like to limit themselves to push themselves farther.Overall, get game, it worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing Archvale for a while now and at the beginning, it is a very fun game that provides some good challenges for people with all levels of experience in bullet hell games. However, I am about halfway through the main part of the game and I'm struggling to want to play it anymore. If I were to pick one aspect of the game that keeps it from being more entertaining, it would be the severe lack of variety. My biggest gripe is that none of the weapons in the game are particularly interesting. You start with the basic weapons, and they really don't get much more interesting than that. Overall my rating for this game is a 7/10 as it's still enjoyable to play, it just needs more diversity.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: This is a twin stick, bullet hell, classic zelda-like dungeon crawling, souls like action game. I can't classify it RPG, because there really is no experience or skill based progression system, just getting better weapons and armor. It is a really challenging game, it being a bullet hell and all. There isn't much story per-se. Theres NPCs in the towns that give little tidbits, but the story is rather shallow. Its the gameplay and level design that really shine in this game. The pixel art style is really well done, the bosses (and if i'm being honest regular fights) are so challenging and give you that 'just one more try' feeling. You die, a lot, as is typical of soulslike games, until you absolutely master the fights. It is the only way. Room by room you slog through the game, mastering each fight, until you get to the bosses, which you then die over and over again trying to beat until you know their movements like the back of your hand. The main 'goal' of the game is to collect all 7 pieces of the Arch. For what purpose? I don't know. Saving the world I guess. Its one of those games that's all about the journey, not the destination.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed the development of Archvale for months, ever since the second devlog came out, and this game turned out to be even better than I imagined. This game is hours of fun, even though there's its flaws (including a game breaking corruption glitch), and it's as if Gungeon turned into a faster-paced, less RNG-focused, RPG that takes you through a beautifully crafted world with vibrant, detailed pixel art across various unique biomes, as you progressively unlock upgrades and craft stronger gear to defeat dozens of types of enemies and some of the most interesting boss ideas I've seen. If you love bullet hell, rogue-likes, RPGs, or all three, then Archvale is definitely a game you should play, especially if you want to support developers who've put their heart and soul into creating an amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such an unexpected double dose of fun. It's topping my hidden gem list so far this year. Fantastic gameplay, great travel system, and Mega Plums for Mega Pints! _childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I'll finish this for the sake of being a completionist, but in all honesty, most of this game is sheer frustration, which is saying something considering my past experiences with similar games, such as Enter the Gungeon.Health scaling is frankly awful, dodges don't recharge fast enough in many cases, and most rooms don't offer the chance to use healing flasks until everything is already slain. Weapon scaling is shallow at best and resources mean almost nothing, as the game hands you more than enough for whatever weapon type you prefer and then some in every region. Challenge rooms aren't fun, they're just dodgefests with no proper commensurate reward (Badges, whilst some are effective, most you'll want aren't even gated by challenge rooms).Game is also quite short. I'm about 70% of the way through the game itself and I've only played 5 hours.Ultimately, you may enjoy the game more than myself, you may not, but I wouldn't recommend purchasing this at anything close to full price for what it provides. Save yourself the money & effort and play another twin-stick bullet hell instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: This game is telling you all the time: "Hey, that would be cool if there was (...) in this game.", but we just have the illusion of it. At the end it's just a random twin-stick shooter because they don't develop what they put inside, every mechanic stay very basic and feel frustratingly unfinished. - Example: The game makes you think there is another world behind the portal, but when you reach the portal, it's just the final boss.- The game is telling you there is an inventory, yay... but itemization is scarce : 1 weapon, 1 helmet, 1 body armor, 1 ring.Frustrating, we could have a complete inventory.- The games is telling you there are specs: melee, ranged and magic. In fact it's just related to the weapon you use, so there is no spec at the end; do not even wish for a mix. It's just a flavor thing and that's frustrating.- The game is telling you there is a build system (badges) to change your game style. But truth is the badges are useless, for two reasons: the first one is the value of the effect is not specified, so you don't know if it's 1% or 10% or more, most of the time there is no difference visible. The second one is the nature of badges, they are not game changer at all, it's just random bonuses that doesn't change the gameplay. In the end you're just *slightly* better.Half of them will never be used, the other half are just depending on which weapon you use.Frustrating, we could have a real game changer builds system or skill tree.- All the elements in the game are yelling at you it's an RPG, but there is no levels at all. The whole progression is made through gold, and that's sad you only have to rely on it to get better. Oh yeah, you get *slightly* more resilient when you unlock new fountains (which means when you just go further in the game).No way to farm to get stronger, you're limited by the gear of the game. - The game is telling you there craft and blacksmith... well no, only weapons are leveling and level max is 5, you can't upgrade armor/ring. Another frustrating aspect.The craft is also useless, most items are jank and you'll end the game with thousands of resources you'll never use.- The game is telling you that you will have many tools and weapons to deal with in combat depending on situation (you have like 10 slots). No, you'll only stick to one weapon until you find a better one. There is no situation where you have to switch.- The game is telling you that you can store valuable thing in a chest in town, like in hack'n slash. But once you'll put something into it, trust me you'll never get it out, because there are not item builds.- The game is telling you there is gold, inventory, chest and such... but you can't sell anything.I guess you got the idea of the frustration thing I'm talking about. There are glimpse of lot of things, but not a full functionality.- The game is "short", i.e. there is nothing much to do, just some events take time but at some point are not satisfying (what you see in the first hour is the EXACT thing you'll do and only do during the next 10 ones).At the end you'll think "that's it?"- For some reason you lose half of gold when you die (no corpse to get it back), unless you store it at the bank.The thing is like you can teleport from any fountains (there are plenty in the game) to any city at will (they all have banks) and teleport back to the fountain you were... then there is no need of such a mechanic. It's just a waste of time. Better remove the bank and remove the death penalty as it brings nothing to the game, it's just an artificial way to increase game length.- Running mini-games to avoid projectiles are not fun at all. They're just boring and either extremely easy or extremely hard.- This is the kind of game where you get the best weapon of the game just at the end, just before the last boss, so you have no opportunity to have fun with it (no new game+ for example).At the end you just have two special weapons. Why not the rest of the gear? Because you've already understood how the game works.- Story is boring, even if it's rare that could be good to skip the boring one-eyed-man monologs.- All the NPCs are telling you 2 sentences (all the same during the whole game) before they do what you want them to do (merchant, bank, badges vendor...). Why do we have to push 3 times the action button each time just to have the effect? Omg that's extremely irritating.(PS: The french version have some errors in the text, like missing characters, wrong words, or spelling mistakes)At the end it's just a waste of time.I'll hope they'll do another game but with flaws fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game. I played it a few months ago when I first found out about it, and it really tested my sanity. It's a game that looks easy at first, but then get progressively harder as you go along. There is somewhat of a steep curve in enemy difficulty depending on which way you go through your play through. If you enjoy challenging games that make you REALLY think how to beat a stage/boss, then this is the game for you. The story is pretty cool. The final boss took me close to 2 hours to beat just because it keeps going, but it is amazing. I would definitely recommend playing this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Archvale is the first bullet-hell that I really wanted to play and that I actually liked. The story could be more polished and developed but it isn't a problem thanks to the good gameplay for which you probably bought the game if you eventually pick it up. I would definitely recommend it because of its fun experience that can offer replayability if you want to challenge yourself for example with weapon usage (some guides about challenges already exists). I am not disappointed at all (some argue that it is rather short but I think that for they went for in terms of story and gameplay its playtime is perfect) and even in normal mode it can be challenging in the begging until you get better weapons. There is additionally much freedom in what weapons you use, badge you use, items you buy in the shop and which biome you choose to attack first, the order is pretty much your own choice depending on the materials and weapons you have. To move around is really fast thanks to a teleportation system and everything is optimised for a good time. The game loads quickly and you jump into it really fast. Good job developers I will recommend it to friends for sure.Along with a more detailed story, to be able to make combos with your weapons so you're not tempted to use the same "overpowered" weapons all the time would have been great as well as having other potions other than the healing potions. Nevertheless its fine and I'll for sure be looking for new realeses and DLCs if they are happening.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews but I felt like Archvale deserved it.Pros: Fun, challenging game play.Con: A few features of this game are not explained and due to that, have received negative reviews because of it. There actually IS fast travel to statues & back to town, you just need to hold "E" at the shrine.The game is a bit short, but it really feels that way because the game really is quite enjoyable. There's a bit of mystery of which direction you should go next, which can lead you running into some very tough enemies before you're prepared, which in my opinion, adds to the danger and adventure of the game.8/10 - Wish there was more items, with different RPG elements. Crafting was enjoyable but adding some RNG element to crafting would really add a lot of replayability, which this game is lacking unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Archvale is a satisfying linear (with some freedom) bullet hell style game. The experience is pretty tightly designed and overall it was a great experience at a great price. I have a bit of experience with the genre so my playtime to 100% may or may not be faster than yours. It took me just shy of 8 hours to 100% and I enjoyed my time greatly.Tip: Rebind dash to RMB. The normal binding was a bit awkward for me.Only major feedback I have is on the balance of available weapons. It has Melee/Ranged/Magic, but at no point did I feel better served using anything but Magic. The Magic perks and weapons just felt better than the other two in every way. Additionally the game does give you a lot of freedom in the path you take, and only has 4 'checks' into zones. This can create a kind of 'where do I go next' feeling and can lead you to running a route that gets a bit too hard, a bit too fast. If that happens try a different path and see if it's better. I recommend doing all the trials - this is where the game tries to teach you how to dodge different kinds of attacks in a zero risk environment. Overall, great game - if you enjoy the art style or are looking for something easy to pick up and a relatively short experience, this is for you!

It successfully fuses some of the better aspects of LoZ/RPG games; but at its core it's a shmup.2. The RPG elements of the game trivializes the difficulty later on in the game -- typically the opposite of shmups; it's still a blast none-the-less and some of the latter dungeons focus more on movement puzzles rather than straight fighting.3. The crafting / inventory management system in this game is not great.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like i rarely do serious reviews on games, but this one kinda deserves it.Now, of course i might feel biased since i haven't actual played a bullet hell game before, but this game has some major difficulty spikes at early game. Such as the Hammer dude (i forgot his name) as the 3rd boss felt surprisingly hard, and some of the later bosses i could no hit with ease. I'm also going to discuss 3 other problems,1. I-frames. There are almost none. you can tell that they're are there, but once you get trapped in a very specific corner in Dust-crag with 2 turtles with scythes that hit you back to back, with no dash, I frames feel like a tenth of a second.2. Balancing classes. Mage almost feels like it was designed to be op, and people were supposed abuse to that. Mage has the benefits of both of the other classes, except better, Mage has good range, probably more than a few ranged weapons, and has good dps up close. Also the mana stars, which are a just feeding the fact that its broken. Mage op, don't use anything else.3.Replay ability. I have beaten the game on easy, and then on medium. The only reason that i played on medium after i beat easy is because i couldn't find anything else to do. replaying kind of lacks, and i still haven't 100% it due to me getting burnt out after around 10 minutes.I would say that its bad, only thing preventing me is that i'm a sucker for pixelated games. so, i would say a 5/10 for this game, buy it when its on sale, and maybe you'll think differently then i did.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game.  Comes in a bit on the short side, call it 10-15 hours total, but it plays really smooth and the pacing works really well for that time.  There is enough loot upgrades to keep things moving and feeling like you are progressing your character in a meaningful way throughout the entire game, which is nice.  I would have loved a little more variance in the form of min/max items like talent trees, level ups with stats, or randomized affixes on gear, but there was enough meat on the bones to keep me playing until the end.The difficulty is a little spiky at times, being kind of hard at the beginning, extremely easy through the middle and end, culminating in one of the hardest, most frustrating boss fights I've ever had the misfortune of playing through.  I think the one thing this game needs most of all is a window of i-frames when you take damage.  Almost every negative post about this game mentions that, and I agree completely.  You can easily get hit 4 times in a second, and just insta die because of it.  Combine that with the fact that potions take like a full 1.5 seconds to charge up and use (making you immobile during), and you have a pretty unforgiving mechanic.  I think if some i-frames were introduced, things would smooth out nicely.Aside from the wonky difficulty issues, the game is quite good.  It plays super smooth, and feels crunchy when you get a new weapon that you really like.  It's also extremely varied.  There were a ton of zones in the game, much more than I was expecting.  You can rip through them pretty fast, so I'm glad the variety was high.  I would rather spend 12 hours flying through a bunch of different zones than spend 12 hours slogging through less varied but larger zones.  Again, pacing.  This game nails pacing really well.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is awesome. watched all the devlogs and they didnt even compare. i do have some unique stuff aside from "cool game, awesome mechanics"pro; the game is HARD. i gotta admit i raged a few times, but thats the beauty. never played any other bullet hell games before so this was a great introduction to such games. the mechanics fit very well, wether you play easy or hard. (PS: easy is NOT easy. if you have a huge skill issue, do NOT play this game. or at least expect to struggle. in comparison to the other difficulties, easy IS easy.)con; lack of updates... man i wish this game wouldve lasted longer. dont get me wrong, i played this game for 46 hours but i feel like there is so much missed potential in the game and opportunities in the story. i dont get why the developers didnt add a mods place or something. you couldve made an editor, custom boss fight maker, anything! unless the idea was to never update, or they are working on an update, or theyre working on a different game which if so, cool! but this game shouldnt go to waste.sorry about my rant...some cool memories i made and stuff that happens are;the final boss fight. easily the best thing i have played. without spoiling too much, its awesome and you will remember it from time to time.literally all the boss fights. they are ALL unique and yet equally as cool as the last, maybe even more! i do wish areas took longer and boss fights had more phases, or something easy to make them longer. so much missed potential there...co-op; GREAT! i played the whole game, almost TWICE in co-op, thats how fun it is. co-op makes everything better.conclusion: GREAT GAME! AWESOME GAME EVEN BUT YOU WONT PLAY LONGER THAN 20 HOURS SINGLEPLAYER. maybe you find challenges you like...its really sad to see the community just go to waste like this. if you see this devs, this is probably recent, so you could do something! please... would be cool :)

_childDocuments_.review: Archvale is a fun little mashup between 2D Legend of Zelda and bullet hells like Enter the Gungeon. The art and music are good but nothing special. It's mostly linear and pretty easy on normal difficulty if you have played other bullet hells. My main negative is that the balance feels real strange sometimes. The rooms leading up to a couple bosses are relatively easy and then you'll get hit with crazy patterns and new mechanics that have a steep learning curve. Some rooms feel like damage cannot be avoided. Also, some of the dashing puzzles are pretty difficult if using keyboard. I had to switch to one hand for Shift and the other for WASD. I tried it on controller and it was much easier. It's pretty cheap and even cheaper on sale but there isn't much replayability unless you want to try different weapon/badge combinations. Solid pick for 8-10 hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really fun to play, a very nice pixel style room based dungeon crawler bullet hell game.I would recommend you buy and play it, yourself, just..as long as one doesn't foolishly choose hard difficulty.Being a bullet hell game, part of it are bullets, obviously.Some room enemy combinations can be very difficult to take on and cause you to fail conquering it over and over but once you identify the attack patterns, enemy behavior and with a sprinkle of luck you will come out ontop.The bosses are a different matter entirely. If it was easy or normal, maybe it would have been a more fun time but hard was really, well, hard.For the most part of the game it was a fun challenge, doing whatever you can, progressing and leaving bosses in the dust. Once lategame rolls around, be prepared to spend atleast half an hour on bosses.There is no such thing as an impossible to dodge attack, probably but sometimes bullet pattern rng makes it really hard with the last boss being the worst, for clear reasons.   tl;dr hard is hard, agonizingly so, play at your own risk but still very rewardingMost of the achivements already lay on your path to the end normally so I suggest trying for yourself to get 100% achivements when doing your playthrough since it enhances the experience.It was a very fun time and I would play it again, maybe try a melee build run instead of having to rely on ranged magic attacks due to sheer deathliness of everything around you, just not on hard difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a very good game.However, what this game does is try to take roguelite's to a different place no many games do.What this game does is take a roguelite and turn it into an open world game without progression loss.Most roguelite and roguelike games have permanent character death and procedural world generation.This game just generates one world and plays more like you would play an rpg.This has some serious pro's and con's to the game.Pro'sDying in this game feels much less annoying as in a regular roguelite, This is because you don't lose anything besides money which you can also store in the bank up to a certain ammount.Getting new gear is much nicer in this than in a regular roguelite since that upgrade is permanent and makes it actually fun to grind for materials to craft new gear.The cons of this game really come from the fact that it doesn't have permanent character death which is funny since it's also the main mechanic that makes it unique.ConsThere's basically no risk to dying which makes you want to put less effort in since "oh well, i can just walk back"After getting the controls down the game becomes surprisingly easy to rush through. As a downside this also means the game becomes pretty short after you get it down.Lastly this game has barely any replay value, there's no different bosses you can beat like in the binding of isaac or enter the gungeon. This means you'll have beaten every boss after just playing the game once. There's also no randomly available weapons that are rare to get in a run of the game which means you can technically get every item in the game in just your first run.I beat this game in my first save and managed to get pretty much every achievement in just that one save which really made me not want to play any more since it felt like there was nothing left to do.Still, if it's on sale and you wanna get a new game to sink around 20+ hours into it's definitely worth it

It has cute, vibrant pixel graphic, engaging/tough gameplay, good sound track.If you're into Enter the gungeon, Realm of the mad god, darza's dominion and the likes, I think you will like this game.---------------To developers: really really REALLY looking forward to some kind of expansion/late game contents/sequels. Despite being rather short according to other reviews, this game is already a really good foundation you can build upon.---------------Problems I notice so far, I'll update if there's more:- lacking in inventory management: no sort function, i item that are crafted once should be marked as such.- the amount of mobs/projectiles presented on the stage can be overwhelming, but sometimes the stage is small and cramped.- The dodge challenges: very good, but you can only complete them once. Personally I would like to be able to redo them.- beside/instead of just bomb, few more skills would be cool.- So far you can only craft weapons and armors. _childDocuments_.review: Good stuff:1. Good movement.2. Very satisfying weapons.3. Each area and dungeon is unique. (but each area gets repetitive the more rooms you clear)4. Progression is fun, but it's easy to get confused as the wiki is very underdeveloped.5. Visually the game is awesome.Bad stuff:1. No immunity frames. You can literally die within milliseconds if there are attacks stacked on each other.2. Inconsistent dodge patterns for bosses. They say it's skill based, but its more of "get lucky on your 20th attempt (most likely 50+ on hard mode)". Having randomness on bosses paired with no immunity frames makes the game difficulty artificially inflated. 3. Hard mode. This is just... not fun to be honest. My first playthrough was hard mode, and enemies do unreasonable amounts of damage. You can die in 2-3 hits in most if not all enemy rooms if not careful, and bosses, well, they can also 2-3 shot you.4. The healing system. I can't understand why they made it so you cannot move while healing. On top of that, you have to stand, vulnerable, and wait for the healing cooldown to finish. If you let go early, you heal less, if you get hit while healing but you heal at the same time, you still die. This actually happens quite frequently. 5. General enemy design. By themselves the enemies are very interesting and are pretty unique. I don't think they repeated the same attack once. (there are upgraded versions of attack though) However, when put into a tiny room, with more than 4 enemies, it suddenly becomes a bullet hell verging on impossible to dodge since the enemies are ruthless. They can move faster than you in most cases, and all of them fire projectiles. Paired with the no immunity frames, you can't do much if the enemies aren't dying fast enough. 6. Need to shred enemies and bosses. Since there are no immunity frames and enemies are relentlessly chasing you, you usually have to be killing them as fast as possible. Same goes for bosses, as their attacks have randomness, along with little to no cooldown.7. The checkpoint system. How this works is you have to clear at least 4-5 rooms between the checkpoint statues, and each time you die, you go back to the previously activated checkpoint. While this sounds fair, its really not. Each time you die, every room you clear is reset. All the enemies respawn, and you have to redo all the rooms. But that's not all: Every time you activate a checkpoint, all the enemies respawn in the rooms you have already cleared. It makes sense for farming purposes, but for general exploration and map clearing, it's pretty awful to deal with, especially on hard mode.8. Dashing mechanic. Its almost necessary to dash in this game. While the dash itself is well designed and fun to use, the use is limited. The default maximum is 3 dashes, with around a 2 second cooldown after you use them all. You can increase this up to 5 dashes with the badges and rings. Since the dash is limited, if you use them all you have to wait to use them again, but that's not all. Some attacks require dodging to avoid them, such as the shockwave attacks. You can avoid them if they dissipate when you are far enough away, but sometimes a boss corners you and then decides to do do a shockwave attack.9. Bosses. They are really cool looking and unique, but all of them have the same issues. There is no consistent pattern between attacks. You can go into a boss room, and it will always choose attacks in a random order. Paired with the lack of cooldown between attacks, you have little chance of dodging sometimes. 10. Room design and randomness. The world is randomly generated with a couple set parameters. While this is fine and makes sense for the game, some areas have unreasonably small rooms. As well as that there are usually 4+ enemies in each room. As for boss rooms, they are usually bigger than the enemy rooms. I say usually because in my run of hard mode, I got some really tiny rooms for some of the non-dungeon bosses, making them harder for no reason.11. Bugs. There are a lot of them. You can get stuck on cracks in the wall. Enemy healthbars show up on the death screen. You can collect items on the death screen. You can dodge into the water/lava/void, and still get hit while reappearing on solid ground. Hitboxes are wacky in general. You can rarely take damage after you die. There are probably more I haven't mentioned.12. Attack design. They aren't fun. Some of them are completely random, and inconsistent to dodge. Some of them even require dashing, but since they are limited, good luck avoiding them. There are also homing attacks. Need I say more?13. Damage inconsistencies. Bosses and enemies throughout the game can do little to no damage, or half your health. Very inconsistent.FINALE:Q: Do I recommend this game?A: Sort of, but only if you like brute forcing your way through a game.MY OPINION:I like it, but it needs lots of work. However the game hasn't been updated in over a year, so I don't know if anything will be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Archvale's a pretty solid game. There's nothing about it that will blow you away and the game has a few cracks here and there but the price, all things considered isn't that bad.The story is alright. It didn't really have me engaged until the last 30 minutes of my playthrough and just when I started to get invested, the game was over. To me, most of the game was just the classic "collect the MacGuffins and kill the big dude." While the story is nothing interesting, I didn't walk into this game expecting to be invested.The graphics are nice. I've always been a sucker for pixel art and this game has some really nice art direction. The game has a charmingly silly feel to it and it rarely goes off that track. Each area in the game has a distinct feel to it. For a 10 hour game, you travel to a lot of different biomes. Most of which are the generic ones, stuff like 'forest' 'tundra' 'fire world' but the design of these areas are still really nice to look at. There's also some areas you don't see often, like an area themed around autumn with a beautiful colour palette.The last thing I want to bring up before I get into my main issues is the music. I like it. Most tracks get you excited for the next fight, the town themes are all great and the sound design is very satisfying.The best and worst part of this game is the gameplay. At its heart, it's so fun. It's a top-down bullet hell game. The weapons can be separated into 'ranged, melee and magic.' However, most weapons have enough differences, like attack rate and secondary effects to feel unique for the most part. The game also does a good job in switching up the gameplay. Across the world, you'll find shrines, which will bring you to bullet dodging minigames. Some people who aren't very good at bullet hells (such as myself) may find some shrines frustrating but they help bring variety to the gameplay, so I don't mind them. You also have some platforming puzzles in some of the game's dungeons, which are used sparingly enough and aren't very punishing, making them a nice change of pace whenever they come up.The game has a badge system which really brings some much needed strategy to the game. Without the system, combat would be a lot less engaging. Badges may vary from minor buffs like "two extra heart containers" to more interesting effects like "a fairy that will lock onto an enemy and decrease its defence." Badges can compliment each other in really cool ways, making for some really fun builds outside of the minmaxed "Best badges for ranged weapons" and such. I personally had a great time playing with the game's plenty of health based badges. However, everything else in the game varies from passable to bad. Enemy variety is a mixed bag. Sometimes you get areas with all unique, all interesting enemies that you need to think about, some areas just have the "here's an old enemy, now it shoots more bullets" difficulty curve. Slimes especially don't feel very unique and they're used in 3 different areas, each variant just shoots more bullets than the last (although some slime enemies are more interesting). Magic weapons have an interesting role in the game. They start off worse than melee or ranged weapons but work around your badges, eventually becoming the best weapon type once you know what badges to use. However, once you reach the endgame, melee weapons become useless, as standing close to an enemy is simply a deathwish and normal ranged weapons just have a hard time catching up to the magic weapons. Bosses are the biggest offender of this issue because, while I love the bosses, there is no reason to stand so close to some of them and dealing as much damage as possible is ideal, almost forcing the player to pick up magic weapons, which makes the game feel a lot less engaging as two out of the three weapon types become completely useless.Some other systems are a little rough. Crafting rarely had a use for me. I used it early on, when I was scrounging for better equipment but I eventually just found better stuff in chests. Finding stuff in the wild encouraged exploration but it left crafting in the dust. The two other times I used it after the 3 hour mark was to craft the best magic weapon in the game, as well as to get the crafting achievement. There's also nothing interesting in the form of gear adjustment which really sucks. There's some aspects to weapons that makes them more unique, such as bleeding, armour penetration, and elemental damage over time effects. I was hoping that you would be able to add one of the effects to a weapon later in the game, but the most item customisation you got was leveling up weapons to level 5, which was really disappointing in the face of how customisable the badge system was. Overall, crafting and item leveling wasn't very engaging.Finally, the world balance. Some areas are great. They have unique and interesting enemies, the stuff you find is useful but not too good and bosses are put in interesting places. Some might be in front of the dungeon, some might be in a hidden area and some might even be in the first room of the area. However, some areas just feel linear. Sometimes it feels like there's a clear route you need to take. Some enemies will be way harder than anything you faced before and wipe the floor with you, forcing you to go somewhere else. If you insist on going to the harder area, the easier area becomes a cakewalk. Some areas also just have walls. The fire area requires you to have a certain amount of HP to pass, the jungle requires a certain level of DPS, etc. The later areas also suffer from less interesting areas than the early game. One of the dungeons is literally a 4 room straight line into the boss. While the map looks open, the game really wants you to do areas in a certain order.Overall, I enjoyed my time with Archvale. The gameplay at its core was fun, graphics, music and sound design were all great and the badge system was phenomenal but the little systems and the game being less open than it looks is a bit of a bummer. For an asking price of $15, it's a for sure buy if its on sale and still a recommendation without the sale. A flawed but solid 7.5/10. It was so close to a great game but some systems held back the game.

Class wise I would say Mage is best for consistency dps, range, and badge compatibility which kicks off when you unlock ultra shards. ranger is the middle ground with the best progression and badge conservancy though the cannon weapons are quite bad and many weapons don't work with the badges like axes and boomerangs (darksteel boomer is kinda broken progression wise). _childDocuments_.review: If you have played and enjoyed a game like Enter the Gungeon I strongly recommend this game. I would also recommend that you do your first play through on hard mode because every review that I have seen that did says really enjoyed the game. This game gets really hard but the boss and enemy design is really good. I played my first play through as a melee class and found that learning the enemy AI in order to find an opening to do heavy damage was super fun but the final two bosses didn't feel designed with that class in mind. This game feels really fun to play but the progression is a bit repetitive and most of the weapons just feel uncreative. I would have also liked to see that certain NPCs were only found in a specific village in the game so you would unlock them later on instead of them all just being in the second one and nowhere else. The world being procedurely generated is a large detriment to the game and it shouldn't have been in there. I also felt that the game did not cheat the player enough with there being pretty much 0 I-frames after taking damage so on the hardest difficulty you can die within a fraction of a second from full HP. The game also doesn't have enough badges and dedication to a class. I want to do side quests and craft badges instead of getting them all in the same way. By the end of the game of only playing through one class it feels like you have played them all because you have all of the gear from the other classes without doing extra work. Finally, I think that the final boss is overall kinda lame and difficult in a not fun way, he really should have came through that portal with a massive blade swinging instead of just standing there and launching projectiles. Overall, the bosses, artwork, and story feel VERY good but the game is held back by a boring map and awful progression. I recommend this game only to those who are down for a challenge and want to play on hard mode. (P.S. The weapon smith was lame as hell and shouldn't have been in the game if they just adjusted the health values)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty easy one to go over.  It feels like Enter The Gungeon/Wizard of Legend style bullet-hell in an old-school Zelda-esque world.Pros:--Smooth movement/combat--Lots of items to try--Mostly gradual and reasonable learning curveCons:--Virtually no story--Moments of unpredictabilitySo, probably only need to explain that last one.  In a bullet-hell type game, obviously being able to learn patterns and get better at reacting to them is a HUGE part of it.  The combat does this extremely well.  The CHALLENGE rooms, however, do not.  Basic premise of the challenge rooms is you grab a crystal that moves each time you grab it, while things shoot at you while moving around the edges of a circular room.Granted, you get as many tries as you want (on Normal, I think you take a small amount of damage per failure on higher difficulties).  You have to catch the crystal 10 times without being hit.  Here's the problem.  A few of the challenge rooms have turrets that move extremely fast, fire fast projectiles, and...here's the important part...don't have a pattern to their fire.  They fire randomly across the arena.  From these few, you can't learn anything, and there was one that took me over 400 tries (I ended up doing it by just rushing the crystal and getting lucky).Anyway, that's my big gripe, but most of the game is tons of fun, and about 10 hours long.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good, the game isn't stingy and gives you a lot of quality of life things right off the bat.Enjoyed my playthrough and even completed all the achievementsThe weapons all feel very niceBig fan of being able to choose a classInstantly having access to fast travelLots of unique weapons and bosses but there are a few things I didn't enjoyFirst was the trials, the trials are just so frustrating and some feel way to hard. _childDocuments_.review: Just a note: I haven't played the entire way through Archvale, I still have 2 arch pieces to goArchvale is an amazing game that I definitely recommend trying out. But this game has been praised so many times, and I don't really want to bother going over everything it does well because there's just so MUCH. That said, I'd also like to just say some feedback I have for the game and some bugs I found. Firstly, the button to open the map on the controller definitley shouldn't be L3. It's just not a very obvious button for a map, so I just assumed there wasn't a map at first, until I accidentally pressed it randomly while doing the parkour and died. I've accidentally opened the map on the parkour a lot, and with seemingly no way to bind it to another button (I checked keybindings and it doesn't seem to show the map button anywhere) I really think it should either be changed to another button, or even just be openable from your inventory. Also, I think I found a bug where the aiming is locked to either up or down, and the only way to be able to aim correctly again is to attack. It makes it so I can't really throw vases properly. Also, when I fought the desert boss, literally no music played. I'm not sure if this is a bug or intentional, but either way, it would still just be a lot better with music. It just made the bossfight feel really empty. Finally, the ice. The ice is actually a really cool idea, but the thing that kept messing me up was I would keep accidentally sliding diagonally (I'm playing on a controller) Basically, I would just tilt my stick a little bit and I just go completely off course, which felt really annoying. My suggestion is to just either make it impossible or really hard to slide diagonally on the ice. Anyways, that's basically it, so definitely go check out ArchVale and get it, it's really good aside from a couple small issues that I hope get patched up soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Played from – to: (2021-12-22 – 2021-12-23) – PC keyboard.‣ 8.5/10 – I am an architect.‣ Game Audio / Soundtrack - 8/10‣ Graphics – 8/10‣ Atmosphere – 10/10‣ Main Story / Characters – 5/10‣ Side Activities / Exploration – 10/10‣ AI – 10/10‣ Ragdolls / Physics – 8/10‣ Movement – 9/10‣ Combat –8/10‣ Final notes: Archvale is a great bullet hell game that combines elements from Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Isaac and Realm of the Mad God. Anyone who played any of the mentioned games will find similarities that will appeal to them. I honestly don’t have much to say about this game. I beat it in records time and can’t complain. It is a nice quick journey. There are great variety in enemy types and locations you get to explore. Boss fights have their own charm and there are some puzzle jumping areas for those who like a bit of timed jumping. My only complaint is that once you get a strong endgame weapon you won’t switch back, and your gameplay becomes the same. Sure, locations change and so do enemies, but you repeat the same moves over and over again. This could easily be fixed if more than 2 weapons were powerful or useful. For example, a fire staff would come in handy in snowy areas while being useless in others just to give you more options. Overall Archvale is a decent quick game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out really really great, it feels good to play. The combat is smooth, the controls feel good (other than in the dash challenge things with a keyboard) and it looks good. The crafting is an okay additional feature, it doesn't feel like enough was done with it it's there to progress armor / weapons and that's about it. The more I played the more I realized there are some things that are increasingly frustrating as the game went on. I didn't know how nice having iframes after a hit were until I played this game, one mistake and 8 bullets can hit you at once doing all 8 bullets worth of damage (probably intentional but still frustrating). The dungeon design starts great, and you would think they would build on it but as the game went on they got less and less interesting, one of the dungeons only had one room in it and most end up being a straight line of enemies to fight until the boss. Overall the game was really enjoyable though, even with the frustrations, if you enjoy any form of wave based enemy killing games or bullet hell games this is pretty fun and a lot longer than I expected it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Great bullet hell RPG game exactly as described. Plays a bit better single player than co-op since the camera movement follows 1P around and it makes it harder to dodge. Same issue as in Gungeon co-op, but that's not necessarily a deal-breaker. Had some issues getting Mouse & Keyboard + Controller to work on a single game setup but also not a deal-breaker.Hard mode has been taking me a while to get through but I'll find a way. The game definitely ramps up in difficulty and rewards you for playing consistently. Enemies are varied and most spawns are fair if you know which enemies are most dangerous and how to play around them. Hard mode is not for the faint of heart as you may die in 3-4 hits. There isn't any hand-holding or abuse of invincibility frames.There's a decent amount of weapon variety although some definitely feel better than others. If you can manage to dodge while in short-range, melee has the most damage potential. There's also just enough badge combinations to help vary your playstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: I just came back to this game after a year, decided to play on hard mode this time. Definitely would suggest you play on medium or easy, it's not very fun on hard mode. The biggest flaw in this game is it's lack of iframes. There are other ways to make the game harder that don't make the player feel as though they didn't have a chance. If an enemy throws multiple projectiles at a time, there's a possibility they will all hit, and your health can go to 0 very quickly, making the player feel cheesed. On easy or medium, definitely recommend, on hard mode, only for people who enjoy a major challenge

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I want to clarify that I am not a professional reviewer nor a writer.That said, for those who want a straight answer to the question, "Should I buy this game?" the answer is a big "yes".Now for the readers, this game does not reinvent the wheel, but it has some points in his favor that make me play it entirely and love it since the beginning of it.I'll split my opinion into different sections.This game has a really, really beautiful pixel art. Am sure the creators invested some time doing the sprites and animations. Not only for the main character and some NPCs but for all the entire world.Just mention that the music in general is great and keeps you in some sort of peaceful place while exploring the world, but knocks you out of  Zen status while fighting.Just say that it is big enough to keep you exploring and searching for those materials you need to improve your weapons and potions.One thing I want to highlight about the world is the many different types of zones and biomes you encounter during the game.Simple yet awesome in this game. The fighting mechanics are not something out of the ordinary. You have different types of weapons that will suit everyone's styles allowing you to combo or focus on one type. In my case I went straight for magic and, near the end of the game I felt that I could destroy anything.This is my biggest "Well done!" point, progress in this game is constant, but each improvement is equally distant from the other, letting you on a great pace of leveling up things. Could be a new weapon because of new materials, or improve one you already had, or improve the healing potion, or buy new badges from the merchant, etc.Enough for a challenging yet peaceful play.Some enemies will be  harder at the beginning, but hey, fight them again and again until you know how the move and behave.Again, am not a professional reviewer, but I will recommend this game without a doubt.It took me around 20 hours to complete  the achievements and I think that's a great amount of time.Obviously there are some minor bugs or things that the developers are addressing at the moment I am writing these lines, but they are not heavy enough to take you out of the mood.Take a try and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun bullet-hell game with a Metroidvania/Terraria-esque progression. Story kinda meh. Enemies and bosses have interesting bullet patterns. Weapons and badge system allows for a few different playstyles. Don't forget to upgrade your weapons in the second town, you can add a lot of stats to your weapon by doing so. I prefer Enter the Gungeon's take on the bullet-hell because of the diversity in items and weapons, but this game is great if you prefer a steady progression over a "don't die" roguelike, though Archvale does have less replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game this is! If you love bullet hell type of games and don't want to spend anymore money at Roguelite games, then Archvale is for you!What I loved about it is how smooth everything is and how challenging it becomes in hard mode, the later dungeons are a huge step up in difficulty and it's awesome. And the only thing you lose when you die is 50% of the money you're carrying! No big deal actually :)This is typically a classic Zelda-like mixed with bullet hell elements and some loots (but not as much as a hack'n slash game). Musics are awesome and the weapons are pretty varied, although I ended up playing with the boomrangs as I'm more of a ranged players.A must have for people looking for a cute game with an interesting (yet classic) story, a fun and smooth gameplay and a good length (finished in 13 hours on hard mode).Also, for achievements hunters, the game is easily doable at 100% (altough i'm missing a fruit and i don't know where the hell it is)

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Exploration is varied and celebrated part of the game- Build variety for how you wish to tackle combat- Bullet hell challenge without a completely punishing resetCons:- The few shop menus have limited to no sorting features- Effects of some combat elements left to attempted player discovery which has left them feeling underwhelming for me so farOverall, I've been having an absolute blast and am excited to see if/when more content for it comes out or any follow up in this style!

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. It does an excellent job at training the player how to react to certain situations. I love all of the easter egg nods to games that this one draws inspiration from, most notably Terraria. The power creep system is similar to that of Terraria, as well.One thing games of this genre seem to struggle with is the role that melee plays. I am sure that melee is viable, but it just doesn't feel optimal, like ranged and magic. Unfortunately, this game doesn't innovate in any meaningful manner, but the melee weapons are still fun and nice for very niche circumstances.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if I'll come back to it so I review it now.Really cool pixel art, fun combat, fun diversity in weapons. It did start to feel more of the same before the end. I think a lot of the map is preceduraly generated, so it feels a lot like you are always in the same levels, same zone, just different art. The story is kind of bare bone and generic and there is just no memorable characters.I still give it a possible review, cause I had fun exploring while it lasted, I reached 4 parts out of 7, I stopped because I explored it all, unlocked it all, except where I needed to go and it was really similar.It was still worth the money, I had fun, I'm a "gameplay first" kind of guy and the gameplay is definitly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in easy mode and I enjoyed everything about it. As a casual player, this kept me engaged, didn't really feel any dull moments while playing it. This is also my first ever review on a game. I just had to make a review because I love this game. You don't have to spend much brain cells thinking on how to go to the next part, everything is intuitive and you can explore the entire map on your own volition. I love the art style and the default controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game - Mind that I played on hard difficulty from the get go so this one complaint might not apply on lower difficultiesHowever, there are very few handpicked attacks from bosses that feels a bit dogsh*it, the slime boss doesn't care about your dash invuln frames and can therefore just annihilate you at a whim if he feels like it (RNG)There are also 2 more points in the game where you just RNG grind for a possible pattern.This is a minor complaint anyhow, and the game is incredibly well done, the combat and controls feels fluid and reactive, hitboxes feels 99% fine and the "puzzles" are okay-ish.If you want a bullet hell zelda-ish game, this is right up your alley, it's decently short but I really enjoyed 95% of my 14h with it.Would recommend to devs to make the upgrade smith a bit more obvious though, I didn't find him until the last boss.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted Enter the Gungeon or Nuclear Throne to be a full (indie) action-RPG, with a bit of Disc Room sprinkled in, this is that game. 8 hours for an almost-100% playthrough (fully cleared map, all achievements, didn't finish one weirdly-imprecise movement puzzle). It was fun all the way through, and I could easily see playing through 2 more times, as I used ranged weapons basically the entire time (magic and melee are the other options). Don't let my feedback dissuade you, these are very minor gripes.Some things I'd like to see changed: 1. The Crafting UI is too small, and it's hard to check what new recipes you can access. I'd like to see it organized by the tier/name color of the item, instead of metal tiers in order, and everything else jumbled at the bottom. 2. Three of the four ranged-centric medals only effect arrows, even though there's throwing weapons and "cannons" besides. I think they should either apply to all of them, or have non-arrow medals. Also, you get homing early, and the others *way* after the others 3. The "puzzle" to get into the jungle could use a better hint. I got through everything else I could, assuming there was a bomb upgrade to open it. Nope, it's a DPS check.

Would've liked more.Places that could be improved:1. Crafting menu sucks.No sorting options and filters. Need filters for weapon/armor, weapon class, and rarity.Crafting menu item hover box needs to show what material it needs.2. Repeating lava area boss dialogue.Please remove the dialogue after the first attempt.3. Jungle area is cancer.Highly recommended to go to lava area first for better weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and lives up to all of the other comments praising it... except two glaring things that make the gameplay much more frustrating than it has to be.1. The game does not teach you how to fast travel so you may find yourself trying to walk everywhere, which is a problem since you have to clear every monster per room in order to advance and they respawn every time you save which you need to do to heal. 2. There is no way to get your gold back if you die.Otherwise the game is pretty solid, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very enjoyable game. Best defined as a "Zelda-like Bullet Hell". Very polished, graphics are enjoyable. While just recently released only encountered a couple very small bug (1 weapon missing certain effect, some graphical glitches w/statue placements).Purchased the game after watching a video review as it looked like I might enjoy it. Bought the game and beat it in one day, enjoyed it the entire time. Managed to pull all achievements and do what I wanted in the game without needing to access an outside guide, wiki or similar website. Very rare that a game is self-contained and provides you the information within the game itself and is not so obtuse you need outside resources.Very much enjoy that weapon-types are thrown at you very early and you can figure out what type of weapon you want to use and don't get stuck making a bad choice, as there is no barrier to using a different set of weapons / armor / abilities (called badges in game).Biggest complaint would be that a couple of the dungeons rely on dashing mechanics for certain rooms which I found to be the least fun part of the game. Movement is normally pretty great but the movement + dashing mechanic could be improved.If a 2nd game were made, or DLC, I'd greatly look forward to purchasing and playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game, fairly priced. Had a blast playing this game and had been looking forward to it while following the designer's YouTube videos discussing its build. _childDocuments_.review: Although the story is short and fairly straightforward, the game is quite charming. The pixel graphics are beautiful and the combat experience is excellent.I will say that at the moment magic is rather broken and melee felt really weak to me until a late point in the game and I felt that was kind of limiting my build options, though I imagine this will be balanced out with patches.I kind of wish there was more to do in the game, like maybe a new game+ or an endless mode where you try to go through as many rooms as possible. _childDocuments_.review: A simple but fun game that is definitely worth the money, though I do have a few gripes I'd like to lay out.1. Progression isn't laid out well, as there is no actual direction on what areas you should be going to first/next once the game opens up a bit more. This led to me completing much harder areas first and then being bored and forced to grind through less challenging areas due to my much better gear. On few occasions there were some limiting factors to halt progression to areas you shouldn't be in yet, but I feel this was not enough or implemented well as I ended up completing the hardest area in the game well before I should have.2. Inventory/Storage should have been set up better with some sort of sorting/organizing as you're going to get a lot of items and go through things very quickly. Especially because of the mentioned above.3. Personally I felt like despite the large variety of weapons, they all end up getting out classed by just a few items and I really only found myself using melee toward the end as everything else lacked damage. (But maybe I'm just dumb).Despite all this, 100% worth my time and money as it was something simple but fun with great music in some areas. The swamp especially reminded me of a Banjo Kazooie soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: If you like bullet hell games with pixel graphics, and a light emphasis on building out a character class of Mage, Ranger, or Melee, you owe it to yourself to pick this game up! It has crafting for weapons and armor, plus a badge system so you can spec yourself out for surviving the onslaught of bright pixels. There are dungeons, and a lot of treasures, trials, and mini-bosses to find in between. Each playthrough changes the map design, and order in which badges are obtained for replayability.An amazing indie for the price, and I'm only entering my 3rd dungeon as of this review!
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Great 10 hrs of fun for the price and I would love to see some more! There is a lot to like about Archvale. From my perspective its a quality fusion of Forager and Enter the Gungeon with a splash of Celeste thrown in for flavor. It does a lot of things right, the biomes, the badge system, the weapons, and most of the ux. You will never feel locked into a build and can quickly transition your specs for any style or weapon. Much like Forager though you scale wildly above and beyond the difficulty, at least on normal. If you are coming from The Binding of Issac or Gungeon you will find the game simplistically easy on normal and should do your first run on hard at the minimum. Which leads to my only major complaint. Having no new game+ and the fact that you can change builds at the drop of a hat, you can see everything the game has to offer in a single 10hr run. As it sits now there is essentially no replay value, for me at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Archvale

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. The art is gorgeous, the combat is fun and the weapons are enjoyable to use. Never feels like upgrades are TOO far away; progress is always close by.
