_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could leave a neutral review. There just isnt enough here for the asking price. I understand its early access, but the game really needs some work. Items are too OP and will make the game pretty boring. I was averaging 30k damage on my second run of this game which led to an extremely easy win. It got to a point where you don't even need to aim. Just click, and no need to look. Unlike peggle, aiming was a big part of it. Music is boring and gets repetitive quick. The pixel art is a little plain and could use some more depth at the very least. I don't really know what could make this game better, but for starters some of the artifacts made need a nerf. I also wasn't a fan of some of the maps. Peggle did a better job of having moving elements. Maybe its because of the size of the pegboard, but it just was very crammed and clunky. I think a bigger play area would drastically enhance this game. Also whats with the ball just disappearing when it gets "stuck". If you have Durable on, then it should just take x amount of time to run through the layers then just drop. Not disappear!!Regardless, I'll follow this games development until 1.0 release. I had to refund for now. Hopefully then it will have $20 of content worthy of replaying over and over. I would still rather play peggle. Dont get me wrong I had fun with my play through. But it doesn't last long. Maybe this wont work after all?

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game when you don't feel like playing anything overly complicated but definitely not worth the price unless you get it on sale. It's a bit too lacking in content to warrant the $20 price tag but highly recommend if it's on sale.It can be incredibly fun or insanely frustrating depending on RNG. You could get a devastating combination of balls and relics and still get wiped depending on how the pegs are oriented or you could have a godly combination of balls but get them in the worst possible order of use. But that's just how RNG goes, so yeah. The castle REALLY needs some balancing though since if you don't have any balls that hit any or all enemies in the lineup you'll get rinsed by archers and mages that can attack you each turn from any distance, and they're very frequent no matter the RNG so you'll run out of money to heal very quickly if you're don't have a relic or ball to help with gathering money. In fact the more money you're able to collect the easier the time you'll have...just like IRL! How immersive! Overall yeah I'd recommend the game when it's on sale. Just remember that it's got some balancing issues but it's cute and a lot of fun when you just need a time killer.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is a game with promise, but no polish - or at least, the polish has been applied in the wrong places, leaving huge expanses of dull gameplay. While I understand that it is an early access game, as of June 2022, .Visually, it is an engaging game. The cute pixel graphics are lovingly-crafted, and they're definitely the main thing that will keep your attention for at least 2 hours of gameplay. It also has appealing audio design, which is great, because every good Peggle-style game needs to have satisfying "plinks". The graphical design of the different orbs you can obtain in your run is also interesting, even if they don't have as much of an effect on gameplay as you might expect.I found the best parts of this game to be the parts inspired by Slay the Spire. The relics system - although not quite as robust and varied as StS - did keep me engaged, at least until I realised that not only were there relatively few relics, they also had little to no synergy with each other. Even the ones that you might think pair well together don't seem to make a tangible difference in how the game plays from round to round, fight to fight, or act to act. Similarly, the random events with extreme parallels from "that other roguelike" (probably one of if not the best roguelikes of all time) were also enjoyable for the first few rounds, until you start to see repeats. And believe me, you will start to notice the repeats very quickly, likely long before you finish the game. Enemy design is interesting, until you realise that there is little to no variety in what they actually do. Normal enemies are minor annoyances that die quickly, elite enemies are annoyances with a dash of bullet-sponge. They overstay their welcome. There is little difference between the types of enemy you face. Occasionally, you'll find gimmick enemies with a special mechanic that actually impacts your strategy, like the mirrors. These were cool the first time I encountered them in Act 2. Finding out that they repeat into Act 3 was a bit of a bummer, and make me feel like .The finest example of the ideas running dry is the Act 2 Wall Boss. Literally a wall with a high health pool and no interesting mechanics. It does not attack for however many painstakingly slow turns it takes to reach you, at which point you are dead. You are playing Peggle with/against a brick wall that does nothing to you, and your only goal is to complete the damage-check. That's it. No strategizing whatsoever.There isn't much strategy behind the random events and what choice you pick. Often, either way, your build gets shafted, and you end up with a hodgepodge of special-effect pegs which don't feel very special or synergize with each other. Peglin is missing that element of control over your destiny. You have very little control over your build, very little control over the path you navigate down (if you're blocked by pegs after finishing a level), and ultimately, very little control over the outcome of the game. You will immediately begin to feel the drain as soon as you finish a run for the first time, if not before then. I cannot imagine this fundamental failure of the game becoming any better without significant changes throughout future development, which is a real shame, because I want to like it very badly.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game because it looked fun, and never played a game like it before. Game has a lot of potential, despite the flaws, but the game is still unbalanced. And at the current moment in time  the devs are simply nerfing any good item in the game (specifically ones you get as a reward for beating the game's *bosses*), thus making runs feel... just average at best. Keep in mind the game also has a hard mode that is, at the time of writing this, been said to be unbeatable by the devs. Why not balance the game around challenge mode, while leaving normal mode for anyone that wants a fun experience?And by balance, I don't mean further nerfing items as that seems to be the case, but to stop overwhelming players with 6-7 enemies, but give us two or three that has lots of health instead?Or nerfing a crit boosting item that needs another two-three items to actually work properly? Sure some players have gotten an attack to deal over thousands of damage, and I've managed it once. But without pierce damage, all of that damage only hits one enemy in a line of five. That's not even mentioning enemies that shields, that can absorb all of that damage.But as it is, like I mentioned before, if any relic even hints to being good deems it as needing a nerf so it's just... average. As much as I want to like the game, I do, but the devs are focusing on the wrong things to make the game 'balanced'.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Peglin boasts a good gameplay loop with a neat base and an active dev that has more coming down the pipeline, pick it up and give it a few runs and see if you are charmed by this game like I was.I have seen a few reviews saying that this game is too short to justify the price, and although I can understand that; I overall think that this game holds long term value because the gameplay loop is enjoyable. Considering this game is still in active development and I can see that the developer is receptive and ready to tackle any issues, the future of this game seems very bright. I must admit, after a few runs you will feel like you have seen most of the game, but I think this is just because of how this game is still being developed. In my opinion, this game is great for ending a tough or long day and want something to play while you watch a show or video and want to keep your mind on instead of turning it completely off for the day. If you want something to dive super deep into like you can with slay the spire or the like; Peglin is not there yet, but I believe that with the things that are planned to be launched will bring a larger variety to the gameplay and replayability.Update: Coins and shop update adds some more fun and save-ability to a run, still recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this game's release, my assessment remains unchanged. Without going into detail, you are at the mercy of random chance when playing this. While skill and learning are crucial for success, no amount of skill gets you anywhere close to guaranteeing a victory. Even the best runs are liable to end virtually at random when a couple unfortunate events and combats line up to end you. If you enjoy the randomness and the chance at an unexpected overpowered run, then this game may be for you. I do enjoy those aspects myself sometimes. But, overall, it can be extremely frustrating when a decent run ends specifically because it never had the chance to be incredible.===Prior to the Game's Release:Many runs will fail based purely on unpredictable and uncontrollable factors. Again, at lower difficulties this problem is not a problem, but this is not because the difficulty modifiers introduce it, simply because the lack thereof grants a sizeable buffer to random punishment that makes it manageable. Most of the game's problems are built right into its core. It would benefit greatly from a minor reduction to the difficulty of the modifiers and a serious overhaul of many of its random attributes to be more reliable.I will amend, however, that the game is still in beta so my concerns may be addressed, and, for some, they may just be an aspect of the rogue like experience. My specific complaints may come from a dissonance of how much control I wish to have in a style of game that hinges inherently on random factors. I believe it could be much better, but perhaps that is just me. All in all, the game is probably worth checking out, but at the higher difficulties its randomness can make it exceptionally frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game's current early access launch content doesn't quite live up to its price tag, if the final product is destined to include a few more levels and additional items to match, then it will very much be worth it.Honestly, Peglin's basic description basically sums up the game. It's a pixel style peggle-themed fantasy game where you play as a goblin with an inventory of orb weapons. Whilst part of the game involves aiming your ball toward specific pegs, there's also a strategic element in what orbs you choose to pick up and what you don't, as well as rogue-like luck. It's a fun way to pass the time for anyone who just wants to bounce balls around a screen and watch damage numbers go up.I think the only negative I have on the current build is that the way everything ramps up, from the second map onward, aiming actually becomes kind of a moot point, as you start to find the board absolutely filled with pegs to hit, and you'll have (hopefully) plenty of power-ups and upgraded orbs to the extent where you can just let them loose and watch the damage numbers tick higher and higher. Therein, strategy of your inventory becomes the most important thing, and maintaining synergy that won't turn round to bite you in the rear.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many elements of RNG layered on top of each other.Most post-battle rewards are kinda bad. This leads to a couple restarts until you get something good early on. That said, there is so little content in the game that there are only a handful of ball types, so you won't be restarting too often. Saved for the wrong reasons here.Navigating through the map is done in a rather obtuse way. While I'm sure it's a neat concept to actually have to launch the ball left/right through the board, some of these boards are intentionally designed with so many pegs on the board that navigation is basically random, and this can really screw you over and set you on a very bad path. What's the point of intentionally saving up money if the shop is just going to spawn on a side-path that you can't reach? Time to restart the run again because the game didn't let you go to a shop.Development on the game is really slow and content is drip-fed into the game over a way too long time. But when an update does happen you should be fearful, as it almost always ends up nerfing something that's fun or interesting. A good balance is achieved by nerfing OP items and buffing bad ones. But the only thing that happens is the latter, slowly neutering everything to be homogenous and ♥♥♥♥-tier.The game is dictated too much by RNG, most builds are very bad and some are brokenly good (like bombs). Player agency is removed by world path selection being very wonky and making some of those (forced!) paths a very bad deal (such as 6 basic encounters or 3 shops in a row) which screws you for the rest of the run because a ball went the wrong way once. Want a skill-based roguelike "deck"builder? This isn't it. If you want a slot machine then just go play a slot machine.I can't justify spending the money on this, so I'm going to refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: I never fathomed a game that's essentially Peggle mashing up with Slay the Spire, and I certainly never fathomed it being this GOOD. Peglin is a deckbuilding roguelike in which the cards you add to your deck are pachinko balls that have added effects - some have multiball, some deal more damage, some pierce through a row of enemies and some pierce through a column of enemies. The game's only been out a week, but I'm hooked. I really hope the devs stick to this game and keep it fresh with updates, because it's a little barebones right now - you'll notice repeated boards and enemy encounters a lot. But this game certainly has an amazing gameplay loop that I hope keeps getitng worked on. One thing I'd start with is balance. Some orbs and relics can lead to absolutely busted builds (looking at you, electromagnet) and some orbs and relics are borderline worthless. A good roguelike should try to make the "bad" items more situational, make the player look at the item and think "that's not great" but when they see an item that may synergize with it, make them look at differently. At the moment, it feels like there's a list of "good items" and a list of "bad items", without much synergy between them. Criticism aside, this game is SUPER fun. If you like Peggle, and if you enjoy the roguelite genre, give it a spin. That's what the demo's for!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Peglin since the demo was out. I used to play it quite a bit and while there was a really fun core to the game, I always felt that the experience as a whole was way too swingey and inconsistent. More often than not, you were only really just waiting to get all the big, broken stuff that auto-won any run you were on and every run that you couldn't secure that, you just kinda had to cross your fingers and pray that you can somehow scrape by. Since it's official early access release, it seems that direction the game has taken at this early point is to completely double-down on the inconsistency. Whereas before you were able to just weather the storm and just barely make it by, if your run isn't already good before you reach the first boss, you might as well just hit reset, because the rest of your run is just going to be a slow, methodical march towards inevitable failure.Before going on to list alot of my gripes, I need to emphasize that I do think that the core game itself is very fun. It is just basically just using Peggle to supplement an RPG battle system and it works well enough. When the game is actually firing at all cylinders, it has alot of the elements that I enjoy from roguelikes. It has a great breadth of variety of options to change the way you play and there is a thrill to finding a combination of items and balls that works to melt enemy formations before they get a chance to even move. It's just that alot of the systems that are built around this core are currently incredibly discouraging and brutally unforgiving, to the point, where your runs feels more like a luck of the draw than anything else.I place much of the blame of this on alot of the new items that have been introduced since launch. The game has had a bit of a time experimenting with alot of "Risk vs Reward" items, things that have benefits counter-weighed by drawbacks. In most roguelike games, I would see this generally as a positive, as it encourages playstyle and defines how you play. In Peglin though, it doesn't quite work. Mostly because your control over the game is already very limited by the fact that you are still playing Peggle and while aim is a part of it, aim can't help you if you have just bad placements for refresh and critical hit pegs. With the way alot of these items work, getting a certain item can actually just completely brick your run, unable to deal almost any damage without a very specific lineup of balls and other items to support that playstyle.However, there is still alot from just the initial demo that is still causing issues. The rate at which you heal at base, while good enough to get you through the forest, will most often mean you are basically losing the run, because you are losing out on potential upgrades. Not only that, but upgrades being random between upgrading balls or getting new ones can very easily leave you in a bad situation, where you either lack the tools needed to deal with future levels or lack efficient firepower to deal with enemies fast enough, which means you take damage that needs to be healed, which means sacrificing upgrades, etc. These kinds of slipping game-states can occur far too easily with just a single bad luck of the draw.While there is alot of potential for this game and while I do have confidence in the team to address these issues, the game is currently in an unfortunate position, where their first few steps forward have felt a little iffy to me. The way the game is right now, I can't say I can fully recommend people pick the game up just yet, especially for the price it's asking.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic little roguelike with a unique combat system and the dopamine hits of a pachinko machine. However, it currently has mixed reviews as of November 18th because a large update just fundamentally changed the secondary gameplay loop. As expected, some people are resistant to change, but I genuinely believe it was a good update that many of those people will come around to once they're used to how things work now.So what was this divisive update? Goblin capitalism, that's what. Numerous pegs on each combat board now contain a little coin that will gratifyingly *ping* when popped. Previously, after combat, you were randomly given the option to pick one of three random orbs, or the option to upgrade an existing orb (or in either one you could opt to heal instead). Now you're presented all three options after every combat, but you need to pay gold for each service you use. Haglin has also set up his shop finally, offering orbs, relics, and a removal service for some gold as well.You're no longer at the complete mercy of RNG to upgrade your orbs. You now see more orbs in the post-battle rewards per run since they always appear. You can buy an orb after battle and then instantly upgrade it to max level if you have the gold for it, where previously it would take at least two combats (and RNG to get two upgrades in a row) before maxing your new toy. And possibly the biggest upside of this is that your post-battle rewards never feel wasted. If you're on max HP and don't want any orb you're offered, then you just save your gold so you might be able to grab two orbs in the future, or an upgrade + a heal, or get to Haglin and get him to remove one of your useless basic stones. The game is now far more flexible and makes your between fight decision-making more meaningful, while retaining the gambling-esque nature of the roguelike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend playing this if you are a Peggle / Pachinko enthusiast or a masochist, however you can play the free demo and try it yourself.These are my balance complaints at the time of this review (next paragraph is my hope for future content if you want to skip the negativity):Level 2 cannot be beaten unless you get a bouldorb or polterorb (or get really lucky and get an artifact that lets you do piercing damage or refreshing bombs) as most single-target balls do not do enough DPS to kill knights even at tier III (you might get lucky after sacrificing every upgrade and artifact for 20% HP after battle and survive to die to four legs in stage 3).Mystery (?) spaces feel more like punishment spaces so I avoid them entirely as losing 90% of your HP to an elite enemy (or death) is much more preferable as opposed to randomly losing your best ball in a coin flip.Multiball artifact makes most of the balls actually deal 0 damage which is depressing and run killing as opposed to exciting.Most of the time bramble orb is only good for a specific elite enemy in stage 1.The "Super Effective Hit" artifacts could do with a boost in damage as +10 extra damage might be good for a stage one slime with 60 HP but by stage 3 enemies have 777 health and it would be negligible likely when slimes reappear in the future; a 10% increase in damage would be much better suited instead (or even 10 + 10%).Hopefully it becomes more balanced in the future.I'd like if in the future they added starting unlockable characters or starting unlockable game-changing artifacts to help up gameplay variety (personally I'd love one that you unlock after losing a few runs that gives you +50 max HP at the cost of not trashing balls until you find the artifact for it as a sort-of beginner friendly one or all balls gain a level of persist at the cost of less max HP and doubled ball refresh time for a challenge).In regards to their future planning notes the developers might want to update it with a more formal one as the game becomes more popular because saying WE ARE GOING TO ADD 900 MORE BALLS AND ARTIFACTS in bold font followed by (that's actually a lie XD) and emoticons comes off as unprofessional and might lead to people to refunding or contacting business bureaus for misleading advertising which would be a dumb way to ruin what appears to be an otherwise great game development company.Overall if you like Peggle / Pachinko I would recommend it despite the balance issues and hope in the future things will get better and better.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin shows some promise with its decent presentation and some interesting ideas in its Peggle/Pachinko game space. But I think it falls short on showing potential on what it can deliver as a Roguelike, at least in its current state.Each Peggle level layout has an interesting theme and design based around its enemies. Spiders will put you inside a peg web, a Slime Boss fight that once captured will get stuck in the center of a slime shaped peg layout, Mirrored arenas and more. The bad part is that some suffer from their own ideas - particularly the invisible enemy fights which cause the arena to be entirely invisible. There's nothing meaningful or fun about just tossing out your balls out blindly and hoping for the best, and it really needs a way for the player to have a meaningful way to approach that fight. As currently it's just blind luck.Overall though I think it presents some interesting ideas in the Peggle space that could be interesting to see fleshed out. It would be great to see the shape of the arena be influenced by the different areas to give each a more unique feel.Unfortunately, I can not say I see the same promise in its Roguelike elements. As the game is now it is easily solvable on your first run, and there's not enough variance or variety to make each run actually feel unique. By the time you beat its three short levels which is easily achievable in an hour you'll have seen 90% of what there is to offer. The weapons you use don't have a meaningful impact to how you play the game, upgrades are linear and uninspired, and even the majority of the the relic items fail to have any real impact, with their effectiveness ranging from utterly pointless, to mindlessly overpowered - but in pretty dull ways. When the biggest gameplay impact to the Peggle never goes further than Multiball, and the biggest impact to the Autobattler never goes further than AOE damage there really isn't anything that interesting being delivered.It would be great to see if the same creativity could have been put into its Roguelike elements to actually see it have potential. But my honest opinion is it really has failed to show promise in this design space. Where other Roguelikes push you into entirely different strategies and give you the opportunity to delve into synergistic designs with amazing combos, this doesn't have any penalty at all for going wide and taking everything, where the majority of your upgrades standalone and impact almost nothing outside of the turn you use them on. If it's a Roguelike that you are after, Peglin is going to fail to deliver what you're after.Cost is also something that can not be ignored. Any potential I or others think this could have, the game currently on its Early Access release only contains three short levels worth of content beatable in under one hour. There are no unlockables, no alternative characters, no different starting loadouts, no narrative, no branching paths, and no secrets, it offers nothing beyond the Peggle you see. There is at least one alternative boss to fight in its early stage, but that's about the only real thing you might miss on your first successful run.But yet they are asking for a price that is the equivalent of much more fleshed out games like Slay the Spire, Inscryption, or even Hades. Games that offer fleshed out experiences - while this for its $20 price tag is offering at best an hour of content. And even now the developers are publicly stating that they're considering increasing the price on its release - where I don't even think they've yet to develop the game to a point it actually shows any promise of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good if you can get it on sale. Regular price is probably a bit much.Very fun and smart concept. The execution is a bit lacking, but having looked over the reviews from a year or two ago, it's clear this game has gone pretty far in the correct direction since then, so I'll give it a weak thumbs up in hopes that this game gets even stronger with time.Despite what a lot of other players seem to think, I don't really have an issue with this game's balancing. I think you can make a lot of different builds work, and it's a lot of fun to play around with different set-ups! This is especially true on low cruciball runs, where the game feels much more fair and rewarding to play. The issue, especially in high cruciball runs, is that you need to really rely on RNG. Most builds seem to be viable, yes, but you have to really commit to those builds and get most/all relics and orbs that lean into that play style, which is a massive ask. The game just doesn't give you enough options, especially not for relics. There doesn't really feel like there's enough time to pivot either - once you pick a build, it feels like you must stick with it, and if it doesn't pan out, then GG, start again. Peglin can be really frustrating and anticlimactic to this end.However, when things align well (or you're playing lower difficulties and having a more relaxed run), this game is super satisfying. Designing some maps to looks like the enemies you're facing is really creative. Others move about in really fun ways. The dragon fight was a personal favorite. There's just a lot of cool stuff going on. Wish there was more variety - 7 total bosses across 3 stages is pretty minimal, and each encounter's map has no variations. But I still think the gimmick is quite fun for quite awhile regardless.Fun game for $10-$15. Hope to see a full release with much more depth in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know what it is about pachinko-style games that I’ve always enjoyed, but I think it goes back to Plinko from The Price is Right. Sadly though, there aren’t a lot of options out there. Peggle was really the only game of this type I’ve played in the past, so when I saw Peglin, I was pretty excited about having another opportunity to bounce a ball on pegs. I didn’t even care that it was yet another roguelike.Abbreviated Review: The first thing I noticed – well, technically the second thing after the cute little goblin – is that now-familiar webbed progression path that precedes the numerous card battle roguelikes on the market right now. I was a little disappointed to see that yet again, but I guess it’s just the simplest way to provide a slightly interactive method of progression with a bit of chance. Peglin uses it to invoke a choice between one of four outcomes. A regular fight, a fight against a miniboss, a chest with a buff trinket, or a randomized encounter that could be a fight, but is often a text-based event where you make a choice with mixed results.While the random events can shake things up a bit, the bulk of the gameplay experience is about bouncing balls on pegs and converting that to a deadly projectile against your enemies. The setup is fairly simple – the battle starts and enemies come slowly across the top of the screen to your goblin parked on the left. Each ball you launch into the screen of pegs bounces around slowly becoming more powerful with each hit. Once it falls out of the bottom, it’s launched from your character at the targeted enemy – which, in most cases, will end up being the first one in the line. Each ball creates a ‘turn’ for the enemies to advance however far they’re able or attack if they’re close enough (or ranged). When they’ve all been defeated by your assortment of ball attacks, you pick your path by launching a goblin (peglin) shaped ball into the hole of your desired choice. Then you chug on down to the next event.This is essentially the entirety of the overall gameplay through the three maps. You’re usually only ever presented with two choices at most among the four overall nodes on the map and it’s hard to pick a strategy that is anything other than avoiding the minibosses – which can be pretty rewarding if you do land on them. Of course, given that you’re selecting by launching a ball into the pegs, there’s a chance it could potentially bounce into another path. Some end-round choices have fire pits that damage your character and force you to relaunch to try again. This creates a minor, but still noteworthy, additional aspect to the progression system. However, the most compelling part of Peglin is how the combat plays out.Much like roguelikes you may be familiar with, Peglin is all about putting together a progressively stronger kit of tools and buffs while trying to keep enough health in your pool to not get obliterated when things go sideways. Yet, an inherent part of this pachinko-style system is that you’re at the whim of the ball. You can launch it in the best possible direction, but one random bounce can send it careening into oblivion and your attack will be a fart in the wind. So it becomes necessary to anticipate the potential failure of even your most powerful attacks and that usually means keeping your health as high as possible.That’s not too difficult though, every battle ends with you having the option to gain a certain amount of health back. Yet, the alternatives are either upgrading one of your existing balls or adding a new one to your collection. These balls can vary between simple basic stones that do nothing outside of bounce on pegs and do set damage and more complex magical selections. Some might be extra bouncy or perform special actions like slowing enemy progress and attacking more than one monster at a time. Upgrades will augment these abilities in addition to adding to their overall attack power.The pegs you bounce upon also add to your attack capabilities. Regular pegs just add whatever your ball’s attack power is to the total with each hit. Critical pegs, on the other hand, will shift the addition over to the second (higher) number on the ball’s capabilities. It also turns all of the pegs red so you know that it’s hot and ready. Some balls are designed to take advantage of this and trade-off low base damage for very high critical damage giving you a higher chance of unleashing brutal attacks. Attacks that are sometimes a requirement if you don’t want your run to end on just about any boss or miniboss. You can compound this damage with the bomb pegs that, as you’d expect, explode after being hit twice. This launches your ball giving it a chance to multiply the damage, but it also gives your goblin a bomb that he tosses into the battlefield dealing 50 damage directly to all visible enemies. Each peg bomb hands him another bomb to chuck and, with the ball that turns every eighth peg hit into a bomb, you can end up with a devastating screen-clearing barrage in the right circumstances.Peglin has mechanics that I found quite enjoyable, but an early access badge is well suited for this game. It’s very limited right now with only three zones and not a whole lot of replayability. The “Cruciball” has been added since launch, but it only adds a minor shift in the way the game plays at the start. With the minimal variation in the combat and zones that are mostly just a visual change with a new tiny set of additional enemies, playing the game through again didn’t have as much of the magic. It also doesn’t help that it’s not particularly challenging if you stack up enough of the trinkets you receive from chests and tough battles. These can have you healing often, dealing far more damage, and synergizing with certain balls a little too well.The novelty of the pachinko held its fun for me, and I’m certainly hoping to see where it goes in this Early Access journey, but I think a lot of people would find it underwhelming for $20 right now. Yet, I think bringing anything new to this table covered with cookie-cutter roguelikes is worth giving some praise. So I want to recommend this on the merits that it’s currently fun – at least for a while – and competently made without any notable issues. Plus the soundtrack is pretty catchy and I like that little goblin dude. I just think it needs a couple more layers and some proofing before it’s worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's always difficult to judge a game in beta, but the rule that I have is to judge what is in front of me for what I spent. $20 for this is too much. There's no sense of progression from run to run other than getting custom starts and unlocking difficulty modifiers. The rooms that you go to aren't particularly numerous, I felt I had seen pretty much everything within 8 hours. The fun part of the game comes with discovering new combos from items and orbs you discover on your run, like when I discovered the interaction between the Reorbanizer and the relic that keeps copies of refresh and crit pegs when they move, or the interaction between the cheese and the buckler, followed by removing all your orbs. Discovering those combos is a lot of fun, but not enough to bolster the short repetitive gameplay. Maybe in a year when there's more content I can change this to a thumbs up, but as it stands I feel like my money would have been better spent elsewhere.

I like the game so far, it takes the fun twist of pachinko and overlays it over slay the spire-like roguelke.In my experience the gold system is a positive part of the balance - it adds a lot of fun mechanics with regards to gold, and a trade-off decision making with healing / upgrading / drafting vs saving for a shop ahead.The negatives as of 0.8.13:- the crucible system does not feel very balanced, the difficulty step up is very noticeable with the bombs strength falling off, as the HP of act 1 mobs goes up. It is not uncommon for me to get stuck and lose a lot of hp on the early act 1 levels.- surprise elites in ? is very punishing in act 1, the pathing gets so unpredictable when you encounter an elite on floor 2, and you have no tools to get out of this battle alive- navigation between floors can really screw you over, and careful planning of the route can go out of the window with a single bad bounce. Min-maxing gold in the navigation also feels too risky, as of today.- maybe it's the fault of my own, but I kinda figured out 2-3 viable orbs, and I stick to them in every run. Some orbs do not feel very viable / not balanced well, and that hurts discoverability of new strategies.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: Yet more updates have happened. The **FUNDAMENTAL** problems with this game are not being addressed. More content is being added, but it doesn't make the core game better. Whether you have any control over your situation is up to the whims of the physics RNG and the item RNG. I'm probably come back once more a long while from now (cause I forgot how infuriating it is), try it, and just hide it from my steam library.  I literally cannot have fun with this because I see so much potential. And the devs are just letting it sit there, neglected. There's some promise here. But as is, the game is **WAY** too infuriating too often. There's a focus on the boards being quirky or having interesting mechanics. Sometimes it adds to the game. A lot of times, it causes you to be literally unable to hit 90% of the board without wasting 3 or 4 shots to start. Even better is when you've cleared most of the board and the SINGLE refresh peg is hidden behind 4 or 5 other pegs that can't be cleared in 2 or 3 shots, let alone 1. And given how imprecise the aiming controls are, and how even the smallest of differences will give you effectively random results, it doesn't *FEEL* like the game rewards skill. I expect the game will improve as it approaches release, but as is now, I cannot recommend this game. Just stick with the demo for now.Edit: I've let 2 or 3 updates happen in about 2 months. It's not any better. The balance is non-existent, it feels like you have no control, your options are more or less all completely random.  The degree to which so many of the design choices in this game offend me makes me want a refund. The game hits the same place for me as Dicey Dungeons; the place of "this could be something I enjoy, but I don't have enough options so I just hate this".

_childDocuments_.review: Is it weird that the "if Peggle was an RPG" game involves less skill than Peggle? Sure you can try to put together a certain build, but for most of my runs I didn't even bother discarding orbs in a fight because it seemed like the outcome was just a dice roll based on what's currently in my inventory. Pair that a lot of poorly explained mechanics (a relic that gives "2x" bomb damage makes 50 dmg bombs do 300 dmg) and you begin to wonder whether strategy is worth anything in this game.Also for a game that's essentially a deckbuilder, there are countless ways to overload your deck and almost no ways to remove orbs from your deck. Completely backwards

_childDocuments_.review: In the distant Past:I did really like this game...once upon a time. Let me take you back to the ancient past, when wild youtubers roamed free, grazing upon the green grasses of early access games. It was in those days, a rouge like, simple and yet satisfying found its way into the common diet. Ah yes, Peglin was fun, runs could get overpowered, enemies and events were interesting, and the gameplay was truly something special and unique. Not every run was a win, but more often than not you could make something work.A creeping death this way comes:Update after update was churned out. New mechanics and relics were added to the pool, and with this variety... everything became muddied and samey. New relics added an abundance of... weakness. Every new addition made anything decent far more difficult to find and punished the player for playing the game. Congratulations for winning that tough fight, here are a bunch of options that either do nothing for you or make your run objectively worse. While this increase in base difficulty wasn't necessarily welcome or necessary, it was tolerable... but all that changed when the coin nation attacked. Cash, Mint, Money, It hit like a sack of coins wielded by a heavy weight MMA champion. Now upgrades cost you, healing cost you, relics cost you. You would be locked into a spiral: Take damage because your run is weak -> skip upgrades and pay to heal so you don't die in the next fight -> take damage because your run is weak -> repeat. When MOST runs ended up like this and mechanical skill was left by the wayside with finnicky controls and RNG hell, the writing was firmly plastered all over the wall. An unfavorable comparison:In the binding of Isaac, one's skill means that technically speaking, with no damage upgrades and a single spirit heart, you could win (extremely unlikely but possible). While not all runs could clear slay the spire, or monster train, or spelunky, or dead cells, or rouge legacy... every run made progress| maybe an unlock, maybe a skill increase, maybe just knowledge of the game that could make the next run a little bit more likely to progress further. Here though, abandon all hope ye who dare to take a boss relic. When there is only one or two relics that can facilitate a specific orb working or vice versa, taking them isn't just a risk, it often immediately acts as a penalty as they come with inhibitors. Matrobshka might just end your run on the spot if you take it after the first boss fight, or your next relic could bring everything together and almost guarantee a win... if it is one of 3 within the entire pool of items, or an orb that you might not see the entire run. If it were one or two relics, maybe a handful, it would be fine, but with more often than not ALL boss rewards being risky, if not impossible to take with the damage spiral expressed earlier, one can not experiment, especially since you'll likely lose to the next elite fight before anything has a chance to show up. (side note* Lord help you if you leaned into survival to avoid the damage spiral and you come up against the wall boss, another guaranteed loss with no potential way to use skill to win). The current state of the game is active anti-fun, even winning works against you.A future with bleak potential:This game wouldn't take much to re-balance (and don't think the new characters help, their unlock conditions alone are heavily anti-fun, just check the forums), a few number and RNG shifts here and there would bring this game back to its glory days. That, however, is not the direction the game is taking. Every change further limits what works and makes the game just that little bit less fun. It seems it wants to become the "dark souls" of peggle while forgetting that DS isn't an RNG hell and that if you are going to have insane difficulty you need an insane skill ceiling. It seems that the definition of "fun" here is hitting the restart button over and over again and the "skill" is learning enough to not waste your time with 50% off attempts because they are doomed just before or slightly after the first boss.Conclusion, DO NOT BUY:If there was an option to  roll back the game to the way it was when it was first listed, it would be an easy buy. Even with how bad the current state is, the old game, as incomplete as it was, was at least fun. This... this game is miserable now, don't torture yourself and instead buy any of the other games I mentioned above. Maybe this game will one day recapture what it had but I have gone blue holding my breath. Alas sweet peglin, I knew thee well... Rest in peggle my friend.Rating: 3/10, frustration incarnate

_childDocuments_.review: Has promise, but poorly balanced in a lot of areas, some issues going a very long time without being addressed.Update after 1.0 release. There have been some good steps towards balancing the experience, namely in making some insufferable maps more tolerable. However, there are still a lot of remaining issues that have been present for a long time. Money is shared between shops or having to spend around 25 per fight, making many shop nodes/shops in events dead nodes. A lot of boss relics are truly punishing, not rewarding enough to warrant the downsides. Many many act 2 fights still require piercing or overflow to an inordinate degree, and somehow, there are STILL not enough reliable ways to access piercing/overflow. With how hard it is to thin your orbs, single target, "target any enemy" orb often aren't enough to deal with the archers and mages on act 2. Certain events, such as the yellow mirror, or "gain three stones or take 9 damage" event still exist for some reason. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I watched Northernlion play it on Twitch.  It is a lot of fun, even in its current state.  Some of the encounters feel less fair than others, but for the most part the balance between RNG and player control is nicely done.  The game feels a lot like Slay the Spire to me, if you replaced the combat part with Peggle mechanics.  The branching map, the random encounters, the relics all remind me of StS and the orb selection feels a lot like simple deck building.  Really solid twist on a couple of beloved game concepts.  It's a bit addicting and even when I was mad that I lost a boss fight, I still felt compelled to click the restart button and go again.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin truly is something else. _childDocuments_.review: Fun pachinko, STS-style, deckbuilding game. The concept is really solid and I can't wait to play the final version. I was pleasantly surprised with the updates the devs have been releasing.However, there are a few issues with the game that are causing me to not want to play it in its current state.1. Balancing - So many of the orbs are straight up bad. They seem to mostly just have a random grab bag of effects and it doesn't feel like you can really make a cohesive "theme". If you do, they are usually pretty bad anyway. One in particular is "self-damage". While there are tons of orbs and artifacts which inflict self-damage, there is very little healing in the game. There's just 3 healing orbs, two of which are usable once per battle, and one of them which deals increasing self-damage every time it is used. And it's possible that they won't even be offered during your run at all. You can heal yourself once after every battle, but it is expensive (costs as much as upgrading or buying an orb) and you only heal for 20%. Disregarding the self-damage, healing in general is very weak and feels somewhat frustrating. In most battles, taking damage is completely unavoidable. You often suffer a slow attrition of HP throughout the stage, get to the boss, then get instakilled from a large hit. It feels bad to lose this way. Not even STS is this stingy with healing effects.2. Currency - I did like the update that introduced coins. It gives us something to farm during the battles and we get to choose whether we want to end the battle quickly, or farm. However, it could still use some tweaking. I'm finding that I NEVER have any coins saved up for the merchant, as I am always using them on upgrading/adding orbs, or healing (which always feels bad to have to do). I would prefer upgrading/adding orbs to be free like they were previously, but being able to use the coins at the merchant. Right now, there's no reason you would really want to save for the merchant, so it feels like a useless stop. Adding/upgrading orbs and healing is just too important.3. Level design - Maybe this is just me, but I feel like a good amount of stages have very awkward design, which don't allow very much bouncing. As a result, many stages just feel frustrating to play. When you play a pachinko/brick breaker-style game, you really expect to see that satisfying bounce.4. Path selection - This is the BIGGEST one for me. I absolutely hate the path choosing system. This alone is the reason I give up runs and stop playing more than anything else. For those who don't know, at the end of each fight/event, you have to shoot your ball through the pachinko again and whichever side it lands on is the path you take. It feels SO bad to carefully choose your path, only for you to encounter some unavoidable obstacle or random bounce that changes your path completely. I can't even tell you the amount of times I have rage quit after being denied a path with a treasure chest or 2 to a random bounce making me go in the complete wrong direction. It is the most anti-fun part of the game and is the main reason I only have only 14 hours on this game despite buying it back in August. I know it seems trivial, but I'm sure I'm not the only one who feels this way.All that being said, the game has entertained me, and I did have fun playing it. I believe that it has the potential to be great, so I will still give a thumbs up in hopes that the devs will take the feedback to heart and release an awesome final product.

The cruciball challenges adds some more difficulty to the game, however it quickly becomes more of a hassle than fun. I noticed that I restarted quite often because the relics I got were not reliable enough to be able to get through the first stage, which made the first stage more of a chore than anything. Since the cruciball challenges stack, early cruciball challenges that felt fine to play through becomes very cumbersome later on. I like the idea of the cruciball challenges, but how it works right now it forces you to play more and more towards a specific playstyle and not try something different. _childDocuments_.review: i think the game is good in certain points but really lacks in other i'll go over the good points first : the  artstyle is quite nice . however i feel there lacks a certain continuity between them with thing like the minotaur being quite realistic and your character being a really cartoony gobling . and that's really the only thing good i can tell about the game because the rest is just really lacking . first of all the most important part about a game . it's gameplay . it is for me the main reason why i dislike this game . the gameplay is repetitive . all you do is throw a ball wich after like 3 bounce max you got no clue where it's gonna go ; there is very few skill involved . it really just feels like a point and click most of the time . but that's wouldnt be such an issue if my next point didn't exist : the game truly lacks replayability . every single ball in the game works in the same way : throw it rack , rack up damage and heal/deal dmg . sometime with an extra  thing on the side . there isn't anything that changes the gameplay fundamentally . like there isn't an object that makes the balls act differently from any other ball . at the end you trow the ball at the peg and wait for it to end . and while some object try to fix that . with thing like the pie thingy . all it does is add another layer of randomness . because when you don't have a lot of skill based gameplay rng is all you have to rely on . and i don't say that because i find rng based game bad ; they can be really good . it's just that there needs  to be something more then pure random luck . and this is only intensified with the cruciball . the only replayability this game gets . and the only reason  why it makes it replayable is because it's hard as all hell  . and that's quite ♥♥♥♥. because  now instead of having a decent amount of different build you can pray to get and slightly influence yourself to get . you just need to rely on a few easy to get one that works consistantly . also the lack of level is a really big inderence to the game's replayability . i think instead of focusing on adding more balls and doing more collab the game should have more level and other thing that make it replayable . for example what about a daily challenge where you get a specific build and need to win with it . or even better item that fundementally change the gameplay ; like one that transforms your orbs into a beam meaning you destroy a straight line instead of bouncing . that'd fundementaly change the gameplay in a new way . or what about adding an item that makes you able to redirect your orb after each bounce with an addition of a force . it'd make it so good player can get really higt damage and make more unique runs . and i feel like i strayed a bit too far from my point so let me get back to it ; while those problem are really something that make me not like this game . there is still something to take from it . it is a unique concept ; and i'd just wish it was executed better .

_childDocuments_.review: I love SO much about this game, but the aiming mechanics are so broken on my macbook trackpad when it should be buttery smooth. Please play Peglin and Peggle side by side and notice the differences. In many ways Peglin is actively getting in my way of making a shot. If the mouse cursor goes off the play window, like when you are making a high angle shot, you instead start highlighting the enemies and are no longer able to shoot your ball, you instead have to move your mouse even closer to the character which makes finding the right angle even more difficult. There is no mousewheel or hold ctrl+right/left to make minute adjustments. Again, I don't know how much of this is osx, and there being support for actual mice and this is a dev oversight, but not all of it can be. Additionally, the peg board is way too small, there are all these side bars with information that, while important, would be better hidden and only show up when you move your cursor to the edges, that way the board could be much better. I have beaten the game twice so far, in spite of the aiming bug; on a trackpad you never have any semblance of accurate aiming of your ball, it will skip entire sections of a peg, skipping either way, but if I move it quickly and try to reset it, then I can get it to rest on a better angle. It's totally busted. That said, there's a lot I love about the game, but for a casual game I really want it to run on my mac and not my pc.edit: Confirmed, this game is bugged on macos and trackpads, it skips and doesn't allow you to position everywhere. It also loads really slowly on my modern pc but it does allow you to aim correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin could have been a really fun game. Unfortunately, it's a buggy, unbalanced, mess. I don't think it uses true physics. _childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is a game that combines Peggle with roguelike elements, in which you help a cute goblin claim treasure from the depths. The entire art style of the game is on the cute side, between the characters, scenery, and even most of the foes. The fun upbeat, perhaps pleasantly goblin-ey music adds to the atmosphere as well.The Peggle element shows through a variety of pegboards (and pegs) specific to each possible encounter, but various items and weapons (Orbs) affect how a ball gets sent through the board each turn. Some may hit multiple pegs, heal after hitting enough pegs, or help with refreshing the board for more hits, to name a few - not to mention dealing with various foes in different ways. A large variety of builds can make each run unique if you let them!On top of that, the game is highly replayable. Different classes each have specific passives, as well as item pools both shared and specific to each. The Cruciball offers numerous difficulty levels that each add a small bit of extra challenge, adding up to what will most likely be twenty levels.On that note, the game is currently in development even now! Updates from time to time always add polishing to the graphics, more variety in the events, and better balancing. Even in early access the game feels highly complete, with a lot of potential playtime - and a variety of funny orb silliness along the way!
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cute and highly addictive!At the game's current state, it takes approximately 1 hour to complete the game. Apparently that means I must have played it more than 70 times by now. (It took lots of attempts to beat all the currently available cruciball levels and then I went back to play it again and again on normal difficulty just for fun.)I'm super excited for all the content that's going to be added in the future and even though I think the game's pricetag is set way too high right now I guess (and hope) it will be worth the money when it's finished. I would recommend you to play the demo before buying the game and considering that after that forest area there are only two more areas coming and that's it.The game does a great job in wordplay and even the German translation is pretty nice (usually puns are hard to translate and often get lost but not in this case). And besides some really annoying bugs that will surely be fixed by the time this game is finished, Peglin consists of adorable characters, pretty backgrounds and it is a lot of fun. _childDocuments_.review: Do you like peg-popping and dragon-slaying games? Well, "Peglin" might just be the new ticket. It's a little game that came out on Steam recently, and it is garnering quite the attention. I have to say, it's one of the most exciting releases I've seen in a while.The game is a fascinating synthesis of two major gaming pillars: "Peggle" and "Slay the Spire." It perfectly meshes the fun of physics-based gameplay with the intrigue of strategic deck-building. It's got an addictive loop that speaks volumes about the depth and complexity of its design, something that might not be obvious on the surface.Take the way you can synergize orbs in "Peglin". It's a small detail, but one that I find quite intriguing. It offers the player myriad ways to engage with the game, making each playthrough a unique experience. The game also features relics, which add further layers to the strategic gameplay, a bit reminiscent Risk of Rain. It's a feature that adds a lot of replay value.Now, let's talk about the game's aesthetics. Its visuals are bold and colorful, delivering that sweet dopamine hit every time an orb strikes a peg. And the soundtrack? It's catchy, to say the least. It's one of those tunes that just embeds itself into your subconscious, continually luring you back into the game.Despite its many merits, "Peglin" does have a few areas that could use some polishing. The game feels a little short and left me wanting more. It desperately needs a level loop (repeat from the beginning after defeating the last boss at an increased level of difficulty) or additional levels to maintain the challenge and excitement. Plus, more unlockable characters, items, and orbs would be a significant boon, adding an additional layer of depth and personality to the game.Also, I can't help but feel that once you master the mechanics, the runs become significantly easier. This can lead to a dip in the overall challenge, making the game feel a little less satisfying for seasoned players. This is an area where the developers could surely improve."Peglin" is an intriguing title that any fan of indie games should seriously consider. It's an exciting blend of strategy and action, with a few hitches that keep it from being perfect. However, the potential it holds is immense, and though I'm a master now - I still come back to it daily. I'm eagerly waiting to see what the future holds for my little green peglin.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game is cute, and a lot of effort went into it, and- at least at the beginning- it's a fun and kind of ingenious experience. Lots of clever gameplay concepts and good ideas! I want to like it.But- the higher "Cruciball" difficulties (STS ascension levels) are just such a terrible idea. They make me, no joke, *the* angriest I've ever been while playing any videogame, ever.You've built a roguelike, and the roguelike, per the constraints of the genre, sharply limits healing and the resources you have available. In theory, as the player gets better at the game, you can ramp up those constraints and increase the difficulty as the player's skill increases. But you've also built a game around a core mechanic of playing pachinko, where there's a hard ceiling on player skill. You've done your best to raise that ceiling, with clever level design that rewards careful aim and understanding of the ball motion- but fundamentally, after two or three bounces, the ball's trajectory (and consequently the shot's effectiveness) is out of the player's hands. That's part of the fun of the game, is watching the chaos theory unfold and being surprised by the outcome.So, fairly quickly, the "skill requirement" of the difficulty outstrips the skill ceiling of the player. More and more frequently, situations present themselves where the player cannot win. The most common of these is through the refresh mechanic- the R peg, by default, doesn't move, which is a baffling choice because it's SO easy for it to get stuck somewhere you have no hope of hitting it before you run out of health. (You put a relic in the game for this that makes it not suck this way! Why is that an optional reward instead of basic functionality?!) You don't notice this as much on the normal difficulty, because there's two of them, and they probably won't *both* get stuck- but take one away, and this happens almost every single fight. It feels horrible. It forces you to restart fights over and over, because you hit random dead ends where you simply do not get to continue playing the game because the pegs are gone and you can't get them back.As resources shrink, and the margin of error shrinks, the game just starts to feel increasingly... bad to play. A flubbed shot goes from "ah, nuts, better luck next time" to "better restart the fight". Huge ricochet combos go from "oh, sweet!" to "whew, barely managed to scrape by that time". Sometimes I'll find myself restarting the fight before even making the first shot, because I can see the random ball order has put all the payoffs before the setups and I *know* it'll be impossible to do enough damage to survive the fight in time.But the worst part is- every time you fail, you don't think "dang, I messed up, I need to do X thing better next time". You don't see the path where you could've done something differently and succeeded. You don't sharpen your skills. When you fail in Peglin, the reaction is always "This is BULL****! I was ROBBED! This one random-a** thing happened and completely unavoidably F***ED me!" This kind of moment will happen sometimes in any game with random elements, but in Peglin it's what happens by default, constantly.I don't know how to fix this. It's pachinko. It's kind of baked into the design of the game. It was an ill-advised idea from the start- pachinko just kind of fundamentally can't support this kind of compounding difficulty progression without becoming a miserable slog. And it's, like... the headline progression mechanic of the game, prominently displayed on character select and celebrated as your reward for clearing a run. What do you even do about that?Like, for my part, what I even do about that is uninstalling the game before I let it torture me more, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I really do. Or mostly did...The game in demo was fun, relaxing and altogether a great experience. But specific updates has made most runs unbeatable. Some bosses are suited for very specific builds with very specific orbs which are given out at random, so if you do not have that specific build, sorry, you are either going to never win, or have to pray to the gods above for RNG to smile upon you. There are two main culprits.A) The wizard in the castle. This wizard is completely unbalanced. Don't do enough damage early on? say goodbye to your run. For shields appear on every hit, and unless these shields are destroyed (which take around 3-5 hits, unless you have an orb that destroys shields in one hit) then his shield perk goes up... To the point where if you reload, it goes up twice, meaning you now need to deal over 100 damage in one orb to even start damaging his health. And if thats not bad enough, RIP if your refresh gets locked behind a shield, cause you will be wasting so many orbs trying to get to it as you have run out of orbs to deal any damage.B) The upside down creature. Although the gimmick is clever, and unique, that is the only positive thing i have to say. MASSIVE health bar, DOUBLE MOVEMENT (so he gets to you in 3 turns) and since some update, the black holes don't have a strong enough pull most of the time to get the orbs hitting where majority of pegs are. Which means you watch as you get one or two pegs and the ball falls down the holes. These two bosses are ridiculously overpowered against the player, and I have found myself turning the game off for days after fighting them, just because it saps the fun from the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review:Coming back to this game after several updates I find it a lot more annoying and tedious to play. Sadly it is the kind of roguelite that gets more difficult as you unlock more things. The amount of stages you go through doesn't change but there are more stuffs in the item pool so the game become a lot more RNG heavy as it keeps getting more difficult to find synergy in your builds. It's really frustrating when every run ends up having a half-build that doesn't work because the game refuses to give you anything that works well together and every wins felt like you got the better roll instead of having a better build.Initial review:Surprisingly fun and addictive roguelite. The balancing could use some more work and due to the nature of the game I feel like the balance will never be perfect and you can't really get rid of RNG ruining runs because of it. As of the time of this review the game currently has 3 maps with 2 bosses each (6 bosses in total). The bosses all have their own gimmick but none of them really play upon on peggle gameplay and more of a test to your build. There is also the usual ascension system from other roguelike in the form of Cruciball in this game, but they felt more tedious than challenging. With all that said it is still a really enjoyable experience with more updates to come.

_childDocuments_.review: You probably know basic mechanics of this game, so I'll just skip some things and I recommend this out of 2 main reasons.1. It's frustrating and getting through the whole wheel of disadvantages makes this game really challanging and frustrating as hell, as known for pachinko games, they are RNG.2. If you want to chill and have some youtube in the background, you can choose to play without all disadvantages and go for possibly fun builds while chilling.There is a problem for a long term. It lacks more throwables and feels repetitive even with many possible combinations of decks and relics. Same goes for battles. Every battle has 1 map, and every Stage of this game has few battle variations and ''mobs''For those who want to get frustrated over and over again, I can guarantee after getting to 8. stage of disadvantage wheel, you won't be able to get through first bosses very often.Balance of this game is quite questionable:1. I lose more to SLIME RELIC BOSS than the final boss of The Forrest - Games first stage. this exact map lacks pegs and is indeed 90% random and unbeatable with right relics and orbs.2. If you get Slime for your last boss, you are probably doomed. Slime pegs around middle makes orbs slower without possibilities to bounce from peg to peg, making it impossible for high values.3. After getting through The Forrest it's almost impossible to lose, as you will probably have enough orb upgrades after 7 battles, that will make your build do thousands of damage after 2 throws.4. Healing through corn relic or through doctorb makes you immortal. Corn is OP from start to the end. Doctorb is well used for 2. and last stage.There are probably more things I could point out in details, but I think you should find your self, as I still like to get back to this game quite a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept and something that you just don't want to put down. It's fun getting a build together and just see everything light up. But I have a lot of constructive criticisms:- I dislike how hard it is to unlock other characters, it makes it a real grind and not fun to work for. - When you finish a run you don't get anything. Just a button that goes to continue and nothing, just back to the main screen. No reward. No character unlock. Not even a skin for your peglin. It's kinda disappointing. - I wish you could unlock more orbs and relics for future runs to make you feel that you're working towards more. - The game needs balancing. The only really effect builds is lightning orbs and focusing on bombs. Very little else works well or is nearly as effective. Why make a poison build when I can just delete everything in a 1-2 turns with a bomb build? - Events aren't as varied or have more options. Need more different creatures as it gets samey very quickly. - It would be nice for a shop that you unlock a currency by playing runs and can spend on all sort of things.I know it's in early access, but after wining just one run, I don't really have much urge to continue playing... It should be half the price of what they're charging. So I can only recommend this on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Goblin ProtagAdorable character design and artCool sound effects.Cons:Bad gameplay. Like a lot of roguelikes, RNG is super important. Almost too important, as unlike other roughlikes, you cannot get any bonuses to swing it more in your favor. Your Peglin run will easily be decided for you within your first few rooms. The adding of new orbs and events does not help if you want to 'progress'. Progress in this case is The Crciball which only makes the game harder, not easier. Playing with it will result in your deck be just made entirely of stones, and with the changes to shops, removing them will not be easy. Some encounters upon starting the game can result in death, no matter what you do, depending entirely on rng. It's just very punishing. If you find being hit with a club entertaining, then you'll love the current game a ton of fun.Low Replay-Value. You will get bored fast. If you plan on collecting all the things, unlocking the classes, and maxing the Crciball, you won't be experiencing anything unique. You'll come across the same boards all the time. The enemies only do a handful of things. Some are unique but that's only in the last stage. Otherwise, there's just three types. "Melee" which walk towards you one block at a time, "Ranged" which will stand still and just shoot you every turn (or every other turn), and "Flyers" which move two spaces towards you, and have the ability to fly over their slower counter parts. The bosses for each zone are always the same. There's only 4 zones. There's like 3 miniboss encounters per zone, one of which is unique/interesting, the other two are just melee or ranged enemies that do more damage. There's no surprises, no draw to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most frustrating games I've ever played.  The game itself has a great concept, but the game is far too luck based right now.  Most of the time when you lose, it's because of bad positions on your critical pegs, an unlucky order of your pegs, or some other chance based issue.  And that's a problem when you lose 2 hours on a single run only to die at the final boss because of it.  This needs to be addressed.  I have now lost 3 times on the final boss and wasted 6 hours of my life because of sheer chance.  Most rougelikes that involve RNG have ways to reduce the RNG as the run goes on (think how in Slay the Spire you can rather easily filter your deck to suit your needs with cheap, accessible card removal.  This is nearly impossible to do in this game, making synergizing incredibly difficult and mostly luck dependent.  If they made it easier to remove orbs (such as offering the option to do them after regular encounters instead of taking a new one, or perhaps instead of upgradingIt is especially bad on the final fight (you know, after you have already sunk far too much time into the run), making losses incredibly infuriating and feel like wasted time.  I think the main reason for this is the incredibly questionable decision to make the boss gain strength as the fight goes on.  It is nearly impossible to kill them before they output so much damage you can't do anything unless you get insanely lucky, even with a strong synergy of orbs and artifacts.  Even if you bring three healing orbs, it isn't enough.  Please either reduce the luck aspect or nerf the final bosses, and the game will improve significantly.  And also make me and probably a lot of other people way less frustrated.I still put recommended because I think the concept is really strong, and if you don't get as frustrated as I do with losses nearly entirely because of bad luck instead of an actual lack of skill or strategy, you will probably enjoy this game a lot more.  But if you hate unfair losses like that, I'd stay away from this until they (hopefully) address this in a patch.  Just play the original Peggle.  Even if you lose there, it doesn't take 2 hours to retry the stage you lost on.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, I like the game and it's a really fun time killer.  Throw your orbs, throw bombs, defeat enemies and don't get killed. And stay on cruciball (ascension system) 2-8 if you want the game to be enjoyable, otherwise it's just rolling the dice until you get extremely lucky to grab a few relics/orbs that synergise well. I actually liked the addition of money system instead of upgrading or healing for free, it makes you think and plan what to do next during a fight or where to go in the map. Somehow it added some level of control to players. And player's control is my main complaint. You are not in control. You may think you are and you may assume that you know just the right angle to throw your.. well, peglin (?) during navigation to get to this chain of relics, still it somehow bounces through the board to the opposite site in good 30% of the cases.  Recent update with new classes and new orbs and relics (were they supposed to be class-specific? Cuz they're not and different classes do not fell much {if any} different since the pool is the same) only made it worse.I'm on cruciball 12 with the default class and on cruciball 8-9 with new classes, I don't see classes to significantly influence my runs. It's the same RNG-fiesta most of the time. I like the game and I have over 100 hours played, yet it's rather a neutral review, 4-5/9 and I'm leaning towards 4 tbh. New content is usually good, now it only brings more chaos. And it's not that I'm not willing to adapt to new stuff, quite the contrary, it's that the new stuff made the game less fun. It's even more random but much more predictable now. Get a few ballad orbs and a few more crits on the board and you're good. Get relic/orb that gives muscircle for every 3/1 refreshes and get rid of the crit? You're set.  No more swings: "Oh, this can be really good if I find this particular relic" or "It will be terriball if I encounter this elite", you're better off just throwing stones and skipping relics until you find what you need and then you're OP, otherwise you're just dead in a few common encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive gameplay with a fair amount of variety and replayability but it has some problems in its current state. There are only 3 fairly small maps with a sort of new game+ mode so you can see pretty much everything in under 2 hours. The Cruciball New Game+ mode does make things more difficult but it accomplishes this by adding tedium and making you feel powerless by giving you more useless orbs and making them do less so it doesn't feel very satisfying to play. The enemies should feel harder but a watered down pool of orbs and fewer opportunities to crit and refresh just makes you feel weak and makes the gameplay less engaging. The biggest issue right now is probably he difficulty curve where the first map seems to provide the most difficulty and ends most runs with the only challenge past that being an inverted level that hard counters certain builds by making it so you can't play the game unless you have the right weapons. The final boss isn't much more than a victory lap that won't provide a challenge to any build capable of making it that far.Still enough here to scratch that itch for anyone who's been waiting nearly a decade for a new installment in the Peggle series but it could use some tweaks to make the beginning less tedious and make the later levels feel like an appropriate challenge as your build gets more refined.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I feel a bit dirty paying 20 bucks for a pachinko game, everything else about it makes it somewhat justifiable. If the price tag seems a bit steep, perhaps follow and wishlist Peglin and see what comes of it.The gameplay itself feels fine, having played the demo I was pretty interested in what else the game had to offer. The blend between pachinko and rougelite mesh well. I do look forward to what other areas will be left to discover, what new potential relics and events might be added, and most importantly- what new boards might show up. Getting stuck with the minotaur as often and as early as I do in runs can really sour the potential of a run. I don't mind the minotaur as a unit since he's pretty scary and all, but the board the minotaur uses doesn't feel like it has too many good shots. Hopefully more variety in units or boards will alleviate that issue for me when more content becomes available.Peglins themselves are super charming and adorable and I kinda want a peglin plush. Deffo going to include peglins in my next DnD session. If it weren't for their cute factor, I probably wouldn't have bought this game if I'm going to be honest with myself.
