_childDocuments_.review: For what the game is, it's amazing and will become even better with future updates. There's glowing potential in this game and even in early access the game is super fun, though after 2-3 hours you've seen most content and around 6-8 hours it feels like you've exhausted build potentials.The game lacks replayability after these few hours. There's another harder mode but with the first world needing some touches in terms of level design it can be somewhat annoying starting a run despite the difficulty. (The next two worlds have better, more dense designs expanding on gameplay features within them) I hope that with future updates there is some sort of progression to gain from doing runs, similar to slay the spire where you unlock more cards, items, whatnot. I also hope for there to be some sort of "Looping" after you defeat the final boss like there is in Risk of Rain 2, not just a "?" event that allows you to loop if you find it, hopefully as an option added to the final end game screen or something similar.Despite all this I believe that the game will "eventually" be worth the 20 dollars that you spend on it now, but with the content in the game at the time of writing this I would say it's not "currently" worth 20 dollars. (May 1st for those who don't see the post date) With time and love this game will become even more enjoyable and fun. If you have an extra 20 dollars and some lovely memories of Peggle, you'll love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So Peglin isn't the most polished or original game between glitches, unfinished content, and literally beat-for-beat the Slay The Spire formula. . . but it is kinda funThat said, over time I've come to dislike the game more, and a huge part of that stems from the fact that the player lacks agency in so many things. Part of it is the randomness in everything, which is expected with the Pegle influence, but the worst of this is that most damage is almost completely unavoidable and so higher "Cruciball" (Ascension) levels are not just difficult but frustrating because you NEED to get lucky and get the correct relics or you just lose, period. Slay the Spire handles this by giving the player the ability to gain block, but Peglin is basically about pure damage output and trading blows.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very good, a surprising amount of content, plenty of cool relics, enemies and orbs. Definitely buy it. POGlinBut the viability of builds is a balancing mess. Especially the cruciball, which is playing through the game with difficulty modifiers, feels like throwing your runs against a brick wall and waiting for the RNG to give you good orbs. This can be fixed - Slay the Spire, which this game is extremely similar to, has 20 "ascension" (cruciball-ish) levels and it very, very rarely feels like you're cheated out of a win, once you know what you're doing. Peglin, however, is perfectly content to give you zero AoE options and put you into an act full of AoE fights while your lifeless peglin bleeds out. Don't get me started about the final boss (or the bosses in general). This is not helped by what I've seen in the recent experimental builds, which feel like they're constantly buffing enemies, this time adding a new mechanic that just says "nah you're not getting that" and preventing you from hitting the pegs. Pls fix.Also add a 2x speed modifier for us multiball enjoyers.

_childDocuments_.review: Complicated feelings with this game. It's cute, it's innovative, it's fairly well executed. But at the end of the day... It's peggle. It's insanely RNG based.Sure, you can sort of aim where you want your ball to fall in the first two or three bounces, but after that all you can do is pray that your ball doesn't do something stupid like falling straight down. It sounds like a little grievance, but because of how often that occurs, there's a decent chance that in any given run you will have one disastrous fight where your ball falls 5 times in a pit doing like 10 damage each time, and you end up dying. That's all it takes to lose.Just a clarification for people who have't played the game. In the first world, some of the basic enemies have up to 200 health. You basic balls do 2 (or 4 with crits) damage each hit. Meaning you need to hit between 50 to 100 pegs to kill one enemy! With no control whatsoever over how many pegs you will hit. And of course those are not the only enemies in the fights. And that's  the first world.The core issue is that there's little to mitigate that RNG. There's a really solid base to do that that's currently in the game – the different balls you can buy, and the relics you can get – but it does not go far enough. There should be more options to buy and sell balls. There should be more control over what relics you get. Most of the relics are useless. Most of the balls have questionable use as well. The navigation system is cute but adds another layer of grievance when for some reason the path you want to take is full of pegs but the other side is completely open. The fight rewards are frustrating as hell too – too often do I get the option to upgrade a ball when I need health, and no upgrade option when I'm at full health. The game needs  RNG but instead adds more of it. And I know that's a big ask, but just one ACTIVE mechanic during the peggle shots would make the entire game feel less like a gambling simulator. Like the nudge you could do in Space Cadet for example.Don't get me wrong, I beat the game like, 10 times? And it was fun! _childDocuments_.review: Combine the playstyle of Peggle and the Slay the Spire ascension mechanic and you have Peglin. If you have an insane amount of hours in Peggle, you need this game. I've been stuck on a Cruciball level that I can't pass and am at the mercy of the RNG. _childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty fun overall, and has some interesting orbs and relics to pick from. I've noticed that a lot of the orbs are really underwhelming even in the base game, and that the amount of control you have over which orbs you can use makes it really hard to make things useful, since the ordering is random each time you reload your orbs.At higher levels of difficulty, the game really starts to break down in an unfun way. Because of how random it is to obtain, use, and deal consistent damage with orbs, you really end up in a situation where you basically need to fish for runs in the first zone to even have a chance of clearing the first boss at all. By this point, almost all orbs are pretty bad, and there are only a few viable options to really choose from.To make things at higher difficulties even more frustrating, enemy encounters are randomized, and not all of them are equivalently difficult. This applies to both elites and regular combat. Some normal combats simply have far more enemies to work through with no additional support from the board to deal with them. There are some elite counters which will simply be unbeatable on higher difficulties if you happen to run into them.I think its a good game overall, but it needs a lot of polish and a balance pass that really tries to provide more synergy or support for less powerful builds and combos. I'm not convinced its worth the full asking price with how sparse it is on content, given its a fairly short game, but as they add more content the value for the game will go up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm tentatively recommending this game because the combination of pachinko + roguelike is a totally awesome, fresh concept and should be picked up by anybody who loves the roguelike genre. With that said, I have some caveats--this is a ridiculously unbalanced game. It is very difficult to build a 'successful' deck of orbs and relics that can kill the different varieties of enemies and bosses. You can likely glide by the end of the first map with a pretty mediocre deck, but you will quickly get overwhelmed after 2-3 enemy nodes in map 2 if your deck was only just 'okay.' Compared this to, for example, Slay the Spire Act 2 where there is still some wiggle room to 'fix' your deck before the 2nd boss. This game is great if you want something that gives you gambling-heavy dopamine with some light strategy, but I wouldn't consider this a serious deckbuilding roguelike contender. Not yet, at least--here's hoping Early Access gives this game better direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Peglin has a fun concept, but once you start digging for depth its hard to find any. If all you're looking for is "cute peggle roguelike" then you'll be satisfied. Peglin follows the Slay the Spire formula, but isn't finely tuned enough to make it shine. Instead, the StS formula holds Peglin back from achieving its potential. The overall systems encourage deck building and shifting your strategy as you go, but Peglin's combat seems to actively punish going all-in on a single strategy. This is because the game has so much inherent randomness that no matter what "build" you aim toward, the best strategy will always include the same few items. That randomness is also applied to the map navigation, which can be incredibly frustrating at times. You could argue that it's not "randomness" because yes, there are ways to mitigate it. That is, get Unicorn Horn to expand your "aim line" and clear each battle stage more completely to maximize your chances of going where you want to go. There are times though, like right after a "?" stage or a chest stage, where you really are just up to The Lord's Mercy.There's also a NG+ system similar to StS Ascension: The "Cruciball". However, the first few levels have done nothing to noticeably change the game. Again, I really don't know why they chose to mimic StS systems so much. StS works because you are given incredible amounts of information, and lots of agency to act on that information. Peglin gives you that information, and acts like you're supposed to use it to your advantage, but your ability to do that is restricted by RNG, and the difficulty isn't high enough to warrant the risk of specializing into a specific strategy. I had fun for a few hours, but given whats out there I don't think it was worth my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. As much as I love when things go right in this game, I moreover just find myself utterly frustrated at it, and I think it's a core design issue.90% of strategies in the game simply don't work. You might go, okay. I have a small deck with a bunch of reload relics, so that'll beef up my relics and make me stronger. Sorry, that doesn't scale fast enough. You're dead before you have a chance to scale to anything, making all those relics useless.You might have a really powerful orb, that can one shot enemies every time you use it. You've got a ton of damage. Oh, sorry. There's shields that absorb your entire attack while ranged enemies chip away at your health.I'm not frustrated that the game is hard, or that it's "unwinnable" or I think it's unfeasible to win runs. My complaint is that there's currently two strategies that work, and everything else is kinda useless.Those two strategies are: Bomb builds, and Orbelisk builds. Even with all the updates, these are the two builds that reign supreme. Everything they've added in the update for the most part is next to useless. There's just not enough AOE for how many enemies the game throws at you. You WILL take damage on every single room, and a lot on elites unless you have one of those two builds, leading to you eventually dying.Not to mention, whether you get orb upgrades or more orbs is entirely RNG. I had one run where I duped all my orbs, and made it all the way to the second boss without getting offered a single orb for my deck. I just wanted an Orbelisk, due to having like 10 stones. But no, every single fight was "upgrade or heal". From a quarter of the way through act 1 all the way to the act 2 boss that I died to. Between navigation, rewards, whether you get upgrades or orb offers all being pure RNG, I feel like there's minimal strategy and you just bang your head against the wall until you win. I'm finally calling it quits due to how frustrating this game is.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is competently made and designed; the primary character is very cute and I do want him to get complete his journey with mysterious, and as far as I can tell, entirely undisclosed goals.  You are some sort of goblin creature that uses pachinko balls to destroy enemies, get to end of the level, and kill the end boss; which is the standard for a roguelite.I will say that I thoroughly enjoyed this game, and will probably continue playing it, but the pachinko mechanic is perhaps not the best way to build around a roguelite game.  It has a tendency to miss the mark on consistency, and while standard for the genre, in this game you it can cost you a run on the basis of one bad bounce off a peg.Overall, I'd give this game a 7/10; while the gameplay itself is quite fun (it reminds me a lot of peggle), the inherent randomness roguelites combined with the randomness of pachinko can be a bit tilting when you inevitably lose a run because you wanted to get the treasure chest and now have to instead deal with a combat you didn't want to do.  Overall, this game is worth the money, and you should give it a shot if you like roguelites.

_childDocuments_.review: A Peggle-esque roguelike is an interesting concept on paper, but how well does Peglin execute it?Long story short: Pretty decently, actually.Early in its development, I thought it was a fun idea, but the execution was definitely stifled a bit with how frustrating the randomness got in tandem with the mechanics of the game. It just felt way too out of your favor, and the harder Cruciball challenges made that even worse.As mechanics got added and refined, it definitely feels like you have a lot better chances at winning, even with the Cruciball modifers enabled. It can still get really challenging, but with the variety of different orbs and relics that influence your game, you can get a surprisingly vast amount of synergies, which is definitely a huge factor of getting a fun/satisfying run in other rougelikes.It's still maybe a tad rough around the edges for the time being, and the satisfaction I felt playing Peggle isn't *quite* there, but seeing as the developers have a Discord server and are continuously accepting feedback on it, I'm going to keep an open mind as things progress, as this game does really seem like a passion project.Peglin's just fun. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, however the randomness of choosing navigation is frustrating to no end every time it happens. I get that the game's whole theme is Peggle, but the way it affects the navigation currently is just not great. There's no gain from this system other than the novelty of "look, where I decide to go is even Peggle-ified!", and so many times I got bounced out of an entire path that was clearly more beneficial by miles simply because i didn't calculate my shot and it's bounces all the way down to the 15th bounce with 100% accuracy. And with a game that is choosing to be a roguelike where you pick your path for different benefits, the novelty is not worth it. This problem has recently been made so much worse with the addition of shops, since it is now possible to get RNG'ed not only out of an entire path, but now into a shop when you had already recently spent your gold, meaning that you get NOTHING now, as opposed to the (still bad) choice of 3 orbs at the end of a fight, worst case scenario.I still recommend the game, but bear in mind that this feature alone has me almost not recommending it.Edit: after months of taking a break from this game because of how frustrating the navigation is, i decided to play it some more, since they added two new classes.the way you unlock the classes is often pretty difficult, but only because you have to rely on having a VERY solid build specifically for getting them, and getting that build going almost kind of feels like its pointless to unlock the class, since the what you have to do is related to the class you unlock. For example: to get the class who's gimick is debuffs, you have to stack 50 stacks of poison on a single enemy. if you arent offered the orb that doubles current poison stacks, then your next best option is an orb that applies 6 stacks at max rank, which would take 10 hits on a single enemy (1 stack falls off each round), and the orb does some damage itself so unless its a specific boss that doesnt have many adds in the fight, its extremely difficult. Its only moderately less difficult with the poison doubling orb since it can target any enemy, but the only other orb that can hit any enemy and apply poison applies 3 stacks at a time, so its still an uphill battle. So you get this insane poison build going to stack 50 poison, you're enjoying the build, and then you realize that youre doing this to get a class thats advertised as some sort of debuff stacking class. But... isnt that just what youre doing now?So you get the class, and see that it applies a random debuff with each hit. 1 stack of a random debuff. Not exactly strong, but it is nice, and you can pick up some piercing orbs. But here's the thing: to make the class worthwhile at all, you NEED pierce, and some debuff synergies. Otherwise it just isnt worth not grabbing the default class, since you will be offered one less relic everytime youre offered one. Which.. makes building around the class you chose harder..Beyond that issue, there has also been some bugs that have cropped up but not been addressed as far as ive seen. These were not here when i last played, but i guess theyre here to stay now.- when you break the shields that the knights hold by using bombs, the shield no longer fades away before you attack, unlike every single other enemy in the game. This results in you breaking the shield with bombs, firing a 100+ daggershot or something, and having all that damage eaten by a shield that has 0 hp and ignores any consistency in the game.- In the mines level, the aim preview for your orbs used to properly adjust for if your orb was going to be influenced by the pull of any black holes. It still shows some sign of trying to tell you where your orb will go, but its very misleading. The worst part is that as far as ive seen, its hit or miss on if its actually an accurate prediction, meaning you cant simply be like "oh ill just adjust the aim myself to account for the bug", because it will be just as likely to not shoot how you wanted it to.fat "Do Not Recommend" from me

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is a very addicting rougelike pachinko game that combines Peggle, Deckbuilding games, and Puzzles & Dragons all in one. Not every seed is meant to be winnable, but it is still extremely addicting nonetheless.There's a few builds that you can set up throughout the playthrough. There's builds centering around: poisoning the enemy, dealing crit damage, utilizing a very overpowered orb to deal extreme amounts of damage, building defense, stacking buffs, and lots of double edged sword relics that can spice up the run. I would love to say that all of these builds are pretty fairly balanced, but I've ran into a few of the builds where even if I had the build pretty dialed in, I still found the game way too difficult and unfair. The two biggest examples of the games sheer lack of balance is the defensive builds and the crit builds. The defensive build in particular suffers from not having any reliable way of building up defense. The best orb is only 1 per every 4 pegs hit, which is pitiful on a lot of stages where you're getting hit multiple times per turn. It is made much worse that the tank builds give you no way of dealing strong damage; which is understandable, but you can't tank very well so it's a pain. The crit builds just suffer from not having a super reliable way of getting crits. You have to get way luckier with this build compared to others to take advantage of this build. It's kind of frustrating.I feel like they could just introduce more orbs dealing with crit damage and then buff all the defensive orbs; then it'd be more balanced. The class that is centered around defense is so hard to unlock. You have to get 100 defense to get it, and the most I've gotten is around 50. It's really annoying.Despite all this; I am very addicted to this game. It's extremely fun, and the builds that are actually good, are super fun to play with. I just hope they balance this game out more, and we maybe expand on certain builds that deal with buffs.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite recommending the game, I'm going to put down a few issues as to why I refunded it.1) No run variance. The variety in your runs stems from the relics you gain, the orbs you pick up, and a few other factors. Normally this would sound fine, but two things are missing: Class and enemy variance. From what I can tell the amount of bosses in the game is pretty low at the moment. Especially considering how little each boss has in terms of animations or complex interactions. On top of this whenever you go through an area you always face the same 3-5 enemies. You might argue "Other roguelikes are like that" to which I would agree, but then argue that STS, Dead Cells, and Risk of Rain have multiple "paths" at every given level. Stage 1 is not the same everytime, however here it is.2) The price. This game is comparing itself to the likes of roguelike giants. Risk of Rain, Dead Cells, Hades, etc. If the game was 5-10 dollars, I would say pick it up, but when you're charging sometimes MORE than these games, you need to compare yourself to them. Now despite these downsides, there are upsides. Otherwise I wouldn't recommend the game.1) The developer actually cares. The team is showcasing off the next few updates, and they are promising to fix the issues I have above. There is a lot of potential.2) The content which the game does have is superb. Even someone like myself, who hasn't played games similar to this one (peggle) in over 10 years, can see the depth in the game and the polish it has. Give this some time and It'll be great. 20 dollars great? I'm not sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly enjoyable game to start with,But when your constantly forced to start runs with 5 balls with low damage that take far too long to remove or luck and you end up with consent failed runs just to the first boss because you don't have enough gold or ball chooses completely the wrong route, like having a car with a sat nav you tell to go left but car decides to turn right, you'd soon get rid of that car.Starting off with 1-2 balls and go from there would be a far better option

_childDocuments_.review: This game gained traction though the "Going Rouge" Event on Steam, as well as a mention from "Roundguard" Dev's around the "Roundguard" 2.0 update. "Peglin" was cute enough and seemed to have a lot of potential, especially for people that were fans of not only "Roundguard" but "Peggle" as well. After seeing the way the Dev's of "Peglin" dealt with critical posts on Steam Discussions about a week into the release, and also after a very nerfy update around the same time, I began to have doubts. Aside from pulling posts that were mildly questioning of the price point, they seemed to not really care to listen to customers input if they offered constructive criticism. Combine that with no real road map as far as development is concerned, and lackadaisical attitude in general towards suggestions from people that clearly want to see the game succeed, more alarm bells began to ring. Now that posts are being pulled from Steam Discussions by the Dev's of "Peglin", I had to review it. I don't recommend supporting this title as it is, especially at a $20 price point. If they really want to make this title succeed, they need to listen to ALL the players, not just the ones that support every single thing the dev's state they are going to do or "maybe implement at some point *add dismissive tone*". Follow the game, sure. Read the discussion's and give feedback on the Demo, sure! I would simply ask that people observe before purchasing. Play the Demo, ask questions, and engage the Dev's, that, I think, is the only way to squeeze value out of the game for folks that already paid full price. To all those people that played "Peggle" and had the satisfaction of "I made that shot happen", don't expect that here. It all seems so directionless... much to my disappointment.::Edit:: The day after I poster this, they released what they call a "RoadMap". It is lackluster at best, and not very much direction is given, hardly a "RoadMap".

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is an amazing game. It is like Peggle meets Slay the Spire. It plays out that you fight through three areas with a boss in each area. You beat the game when you get to the end of the third area and beat the boss, but that is where the fun begins.When you win a run, you unlock Cruciball, a more challenging mode with modifiers. You go up Cruciball levels as you beat each level currently up to 15, but each adds more modifiers on top of the previous ones. When you first start playing this game, there is a lot of trial and error. If you take the wrong Relic, you can easily ruin a run or make it much harder. The gold update changed this game so much by adding shops that give you more opportunities to build the builds you want, and you can now get a new orb, heal and upgrade all at the same time. Also, gold builds are one of the most insanely broken builds. There is still a lot of RNG, but that is the core of most Rogulike Deckbuilders.  Ran great with no tweaks on the Steam Deck.Well, I know that this game is not for everybody. It is my type of game. I have so many hours in Peglin, yet I still enjoy every time I go into the game. I look forward to every new update, with a new one around the corner as I write this. There will always be parts of the game that I am not going to like and that other people will not like, but overall I think the game is still a wonderful experience and just a fun time. It is one of my favorite games on Steam and one of the best Roguelikes I have ever played. Except for when I'm bashing my head against a crucible level first 10 hours plus trying to beat it. Just kidding kinda, that is still fun.Find more reviews from me on my Steam curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, because I love the idea and the style and it should be right my pocket. But it is just not there yet. The last upgrade was a good start, but it wasn't enough. Before the upgrade you could do one run and feel like you've seen it all. They now added a lot of stuff, which is good and the game feels a little more diverse. But as others here already said, not all the added things are great. Why is it so hard to unlock 2 more basic characters? Why do you have to go far and beyond for that? Not to mention if you just play ingame and don't read stuff, you would maybe not even know that there are 2 more characters to unlock! And the new possible builds feel more than underwhelming. Having a orb giving you ballwark that maybe helps you block 5 dmg? When there are literally tons of items who can easily heal you up for more. Why would anyone want that. Ballution might have potential, but still you need to stack 5 to do even the same amount of dmg than a bomb (which would also be aoe while ballution only targets one). And then again, after two runs you probably encountered all possible events. I hope this game will get more stuff and upgrades and versatility, because it could be really really awesome. But as it is I just can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly blown away by how great this game is - such a simple concept that ends up being such a massive amount of fun, almost 8 hours in and I'm not bored despite the simplicity. Despite the somewhat random nature of the game, I do genuinely find myself becoming more skilled at playing, and it's fun trying out new tactics and play styles. Sometimes I'll have a build that focuses on making the most of board refreshers, other times it'll be reloads, or maybe I'll just hoard as many high power orbs as I can? All of these playstyles feel rewarding, and the others more imaginative people might be able to bring together undoubtedly will too.If you're on the fence give the demo a go - there's a few differences between it and the final product, but I'd argue that the new changes are for the better.

_childDocuments_.review: Its great fun, don't get me wrong. But the game state is closer to a demo than a game, and the price tag is higher than even a full game would deserve (unless they add way way more). The game is 3 stages, no endless mode to enjoy your crazy builds. Some builds are nearly impossible to get going, for a mediocre result (Healing -> dmg build), and other builds are basically a free win blindfolded.The enemies are super limited, and even with different sprites, their attacks are limited to 4-6 mechanics.Some relics are build defining, some relics are top tier for every build, some relics are generally strong, and some are...... OK.The orbs are very varied, and all of them have some fun mechanics.EDIT: The first review was more than a year ago. A lot of changes got pushed out, and new content added. The big negatives have been fixed, enemies and boards are now way more interesting and varied. Relics are still unbalanced, but now in a more fun way, and the worst relics have been remade.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Don't be fooled early, as difficulty ramps up the game will challenge you. Cruciball 5+ will demand you start paying attention to the maps and enemies and play progressively more strategically. Great roguelike for when you "don't want to think too hard" but still want to play a challenging game.One caveat I will add is please include, on all platforms and not just Steam, an "unlock all" button or alternate unlock conditions for characters. I want to buy the game on my switch and have it available there as well. But, I've already bought for my phone (I'm an addict, sue me) and am so far at Cruciball 10 for our little pal Peglin, but I haven't even unlocked Balladin yet...I'm trying to win runs and make cruciball progression, the idea of grinding to unlock a character when it's 100% RNG is pretty gross.This is a feature starting to pop up in other cross-platform indies as an alternative to true cross progression, and I implore you to adopt it. The character unlock system is my only one true "This is foolishly designed" complaint about this game, because of how it is primarily RNG, not linked to skill, and makes you stop playing the game the way you want to in order to unlock new characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is very fun but also problematic. This would normally all be fine for an early access indie title but the $20 price tag seems way too high for the level of early access we are seeing here. A solid experience for $10, but $20 suddenly changes all the standards.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Game can be fun but it really only shows how good it could be in the first world.Health pools become inflated going into the second world forcing you to rely on either relics that make your orbs stay on the board for much longer but usually sacrifice any sort of tactical aiming whatsoever or just running all the orbs and relics that create bombs or refresh bombs. On top of that issue is that both of these strategies are basically interchangeable at any time they both synergize very well together since most of the bomb orbs and relics just want you to hit more pegs on the same shot. What makes this especially boring is that there is no dependable way to remove orbs from your bag so going for any other fun or crazy build is hampered by carrying around 4 or 5 rocks the whole game or going to random encounters hoping to remove something and just ending up with more filler orbs making your strategy even less dependable.Personally i think having the most dependable and achievable strategies basically play the game for you just makes it tedious they're fun the first time you roll the entire game without effort, with what you think is a crazy combo, until you do it again and again because its that easy to pull off.What makes this especially boring is that there is no dependable way to remove orbs from your bag so going for any other fun or crazy build is hampered by carrying around 4 or 5 rocks the whole game or going to random encounters hoping to remove something and just ending up with more filler orbs making your strategy even less dependable.Overall I think the game shows a lot of potential but lacks any reason to get better at it or try new strategies and that just makes it boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I... *really really* want to recommend this game. I got it when it was in much earlier access than it is now, and loved it.The problem is physics updates.I don't know why, but around the time they added classes the devs changed the way ball physics worked, and what had been a solid, predictable Peggle experience changed into something more akin to a pachinko machine, with much of the skill involved in ball placement and trajectory targetting being lost.This, IMO, harms the roguelike nature of the game, since it renders the skill side of the equation more or less moot, often as early as the initial launch of your ball. This is disappointing, because a LOT of what this game does -- from the ball abilities to the visuals to the music -- is great, but without that element of control in your play, it stops being a roguelike puzzle game and, instead, turns into an experience where all you can *really* do is pick abilities and hope they work out.Before the changes I got multiple completed runs in the game. Since the changes, my completion amount has dropped to zero.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a big wall of a discussions post an hour or more into my time with Pachinklin, which I've linked just below, in which I outlined all the issues I had with the game BUT I concluded that none of them were enough of a deal breaker for me to refund or negatively review this game.I have now refunded Peglin, and here's that negative review.Here's that post, if you're wondering:Now, what changed my mind on Peglin?Two things; the content-to-price ratio, and the comically overpowered third boss.I finished the game in a couple hours, tried to give it another go but it's just... playing again. Sure, you can do it on their hard mode demo, but it's just... the same thing but the enemy numbers are slightly bigger. What you have here is... Fine, it's fun enough, but it needs a lot of fixes from my discussions post - and a lot, lot of content. After I finished it, I didn't really have any desire to go back to it any time soon; though that may be the third boss's fault...The Third Boss:It heals every turnIt gives itself an incremental and permanent damage buff every few turnsIt's four enemiesThat all have a bunch of healthThat all attack you every turnThat rotate and you can't focus one down because it hides behind the othersIts arena moves (and clips into itself, which causes wonky ball physics)Its arena is bad and is designed to cause early pitfallsYou can quite easily get STUCK in the arena and lose your throw.Basically it's Darkest Dungeon's Shambler and Collector rolled into one, slapped onto a bad moving pachinko board.Other bosses had one, or maximum two, of these tags and this one's just like "nah fam what if ALL the buffs". This is comically poor balancing, and I brought this up on the discussions and was told that it's easy actually, one guy said "it was the easiest boss in the game" which must mean he sucks pretty savagely at the others which pale in comparison to this bloated mess... I don't hate this because it is hard, I hate it because it has so many tags in comparison to the others, and a few of those tags are just crummy design; the arena's faults, for one. It is so comically overpowered that I genuinely thought it was a joke. There's no reason for this boss to have ALL OF THOSE descriptors... Or is it just because that's the end of the current content, and you want to end runs here... That'd be kinda sad if it were the case.Especially because you've made savescumming so easy. Which is what I did. You pull unfair bosses out your butt at the last minute; I use the tools you've given me to cheese it. Fair's fair.Anyway.It needs love. It needs content. It needs a big ctrl+a delete on whatever document the third boss's descrtiptors are stored in.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that is very re-playable but...due the the relics being mostly random with you having little choice over them and the main synergies coming from orbs-relics combos rather then orb-orb combos (other then stone orbalist) you are often put into the position of picking the same orbs every time and ending the game with the same deck every time. If previous orb choices had an influence on future orb choices such as lighting orbs combo-ing with water orbs you would get a lot more end of game deck differences. that all being said this is a very fun game with more content to come and i can only hope that the game moves a little away from pick the best orbs and hope you avoid the killer relics.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I feel my review is a little harsh, this game is only 5 months old. So bear that in mind.Maybe this is all just me, but I'm going to give my honest view regardless.I keep wanting to like this game, but I just think they miss the mark.The first world has so many maps with such poor peg density that you get maybe like 5-10 max bounces per orb launched for the majority of the maps in world one. Which makes a bunch of orbs so much worse than they should be, and is just incredibly boring to experience.Pegs often lack bounce (Not including the ones that have that programmed, such as slimed or webbed ones) and feel weak all the time. Also for the record, the maps that have the web/slime, have too much web/slime, it makes half your shots the exact same short as the previous one, and that makes the start of the game quite boring when you happen to get the web ones early. The slime boss that puts you inside itself, is maybe the least fun boss in any game I've ever played. His pegs are far too spread out, you rarely ever get a good bounce worth a damn no matter how good your orbs are. The idea of the boss I love, the execution I abhor. Just give it more pegs, even if it's more of the gross bounce stopping slime ones. His WHOLE BODY is made of slime, not just a layer externally coating him.There are far too many ranged enemies half them and increase melee enemy damage. It makes bramble totally useless when more than half of the enemies you encounter do ranged damage for equal damage to the melee guys half of the time. Not enough penetrating weapons or splash damage weapons or luck based weapons. Bomb orbs are easily the strongest and it's not even close how much better they are.This game is supposed to be about bouncing, maybe have less things that either don't bounce or reduce bounce.The cruciball is absolutely completely and utterly awful. 1 more stone (a bad thing) but also your stones are weaker (also a bad thing) why would literally anyone with even a single brain cell, want that? Obelisk builds, sure. Let's make a whole new game system just to make 1 build better to start with. That's trash and boring.Having finished a few more times, my cruciball is now level 4. Just adding difficulty isn't fun, especially when it's in such mundane ways. Oh enemies have more health, your stones are even worse, extra fire hole damage? that's the most boring thing you could possible do to add difficulty. I think I've hit those fire pits (misnavigation) maybe 3 times in 100 runs...Adding no new complexity is just lazy. These wheel options should be buffs with bad caveats, otherwise there's literally no improved replayability after you complete the game... come on guys, roguelike:101 here, could not be a more basic mechanic for a roguelike.You literally have items with amazing caveat buffs, they far more fit in the cruciball than the truly so damn boring difficulty increase in there so far.The more I have played this game, the more angry I have become. Hopefully some of the classes and balance tweaks will improve this game enough, because I'd like to enjoy and recommend this game.Here are some suggestions.An orb that every time it's the one you are throwing, ramdomises somewhat. Perhaps some times it's high crit low main stat, some times it's medium both but penetrates, some times it has neither but converts blocks hit into crits or into refreshes, things like that.A cruciball buff where you pegs start with needing 1 extra bounce to break (forgot the name of that stat, durable maybe?) but your orbs pass through crits, refreshes, bombs, and other non standard pegs, rather than bouncing off of them? (still activates them and breaks their peg)An orb that is a boomerang. Normal orb in the peg board, but when you fire it, it penetrates through all enemies once and then comes back maybe? Lower stats but deals damage twice could be fun and interactive with mechanics like blind on hit, and any others that apply on hit.Perhaps an orb or an item, that lets your shots hit only above and behind the target (like a grenade going on kind of thing, small aoe splash damage on the orb, could even be only 50% of the main shot's damage, for balance sake)Also I think you need to nerf the item that increase crits multiplier for hitting multiple crit pegs. It's just too strong, it truly is so easy to start hitting 5000-10000 damage shots, once you have that. Especially when combined with Durable and the electromagnetic item. You can get to 3x crit in a single crit node and that happens almost the instant it touches the crit. I've gotten to 10x crit before and had I think over 20k damage from shots.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually a tough challenge. What makes it a tough challenge is where the peg balls fall isn't guaranteed, you sometimes have control, but somethings not. _childDocuments_.review: The design of the game is nice to look at but it feels like everything is made to be detrimental to the player. From the get go, you don't really get to feel powerful unless you get lucky with some orbs and relics. It feels surface deep so the game is fun until the novelty of a new Peggle-like wears off.The level design is less based around bouncing and sliding off stuff like in Peggle that's there to be satisfying and more about trying to make the ball hit the bottom of the screen as fast as it can unless you get a few certain orb types. There's only a handful of levels I like and many I hate. There's many orbs that are bloat or have negatives to using them and the same goes for relics.Random encounters are best avoided because instead of being a mystery, it's likely just going to contain something you don't want. Enemy encounters range from being fine to just annoying or unfair. Combat feels really detached from the gameplay which doesn't help. You play Peggle and either your continue playing bar or your stay on this level bar depletes and what happens, happens.The game is overly reliant on luck as a whole which isn't ideal for me. IMO rogue likes need to allow skill to offset luck and allow players to complete a full run. Sadly this isn't it.All that said, it is in Early Access and things could improve drastically. Great idea, it has some great moments and it has a lot of potential. I just can't recommend it in its current form.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin fully commits to its peggle roots, which is to say, every mechanic revolves around how well you can hit pegs. This includes navigation. This has caused some chagrin amongst some of the players, but it should be noted that navigation is not nearly as random as it first may appear.The map for a given area (and as such, the routes you need to navigate) is given in advance. From there, you can plan out a wishlist of nodes, so to speak. Battles are the easiest to navigate from, as long as you do some planning in advance. It happens to be the case that any pegs fully activated during battle, disappear completely afterwards, for navigation. As such, during the battle you can already carve out a route roughly in the direction you want to go. Question mark nodes are more difficult to navigate from, as some events do feature a proper pachinko board (though even with that, you can significantly increase the chances of hitting a correct path by angling your navigation orb appropriately).A fair bit of gameplay does involve navigation. There is, for example, the risk reward consideration of chest navigation, where you can either pop all the bombs for a second chest, or navigate to the node you want with relative ease. With all of that said, navigation is still not guaranteed. If that sounds like it'd upset you, avoid this game.I would, however, heartily recommend this game to anyone who wants a fairly chill game that you can sink a fair few hours into while listening to a podcast or similar. It's, once you get into the swing of things, a game that can be fairly mindless to play, in the way that it can keep you busy.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin has the honor of being my 100th Steam review. And it's even a positive one!I think we've all seen roguelite elements applied to many game genres by now, but roguelite Peggle is a new one for me. Peglin is refreshingly unique. Each run starts out a little slow, but they get fun once you get deeper into it and start collecting orbs and relics. The effects of these items interact with each other in interesting ways, and THAT'S what makes every run feel different; not the enemies or the boards, but your build. It's fun, and it almost has an addictive mobile game quality to it. You'll die only one or two turns away from defeating a big boss, you'll get frustrated, and then you'll hover your mouse over the quit button for a few seconds before thinking "...nah, I can do one more run." Peglin's a good time waster. And it's really solid for an early access title. There's not really any game-breaking bugs or anything like that. Peglin just needs a little more variation when it comes to its boards and levels, the ability to choose classes, and a drop of polish. Considering it's status as an early access game, I'd expect all of those things to come with time.I don't really have anything glaringly bad to say about Peglin. It's good for what it is, and it'll probably only get better with time. If you like Peggle or other pachinko-esque games, and if you like roguelite elements, give Peglin a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun for when you want to play something more passive but not enough content yet by a long shot.You'll have seen pretty much every board and every ball by the third run. _childDocuments_.review: Peglin never reached the level of critical and public success to realistically rival the ever-growing list of Roguelite titans. Even so, for twenty dollars, it provides a consistent, excellent, and dynamic experience. Skill and tactical progression remains relevant despite appearances, and the ascension system tests both in equal measure. With respectful nods to its inspirations and a sprinkle of comedy, it is a very replayable experience with runs that range from fifteen to forty minutes.For its price, Peglin is a game I would be happy to recommend to most Steam users.

_childDocuments_.review: the game is a little short, so i hope more levels are added in the near future. other than that, it's a lot of fun. it's like a more interesting version of peggle, and very obviously inspired by it in the early stages.after having played a significant amount more of the game, i have some issues. the normal mode is far too easy for someone who has beaten it once or twice, and actually seems to get easier as the levels progress. the cruciball demo is great in theory, but too many of the stages have pegs placed in such a way that it's nearly impossible to hit more than two or three pegs per shot. the difficulty of the enemies isn't the issue, it's just that the level design is not really so great. we need like 5x as many stages, and for some of the worst ones with very empty boards to just be removed or be much rarer. while looking for a higher difficulty experience, what i'm finding after 10-15 attempts is that it's just more frustrating and not as fun due to difficulty leaps and lack of opportunity for damage. i loved peggle a lot, and peglin has some solid improvements on the model, but the game should be 5 dollars if it remains in this state, not 20 dollars. i'm fully in favor of peglin *if* they plan to add a lot more content, but right now i feel that it has about the same amount of stages as the *free* peggle demo does. because of the above reasons, i hesitate to give the game a thumbs up. it's simply far too expensive for the amount of content offered. it seems like all they need to do is revise a few of the existing stages and add more of them + a few more enemies for the game to be much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: I played up to level 12 in the "difficult" mode, but when I saw that bomb damage had been reduced, I finally couldn't continue playing. In the new version, not only is it difficult to use bombs, but their damage is also low, and I don't see where the new fun is. Other Roguelike games increase the game's difficulty as the game progresses, while also allowing players to unlock new powerful items. But in this game from your studio, there are no unlockable contents except for two characters that are weaker than the starting character. The difficulty level of the "difficult" mode has simply been increased without any new content, not only increasing the pressure to survive, but also greatly increasing the difficulty of building a proper strategy. It is possible to restart dozens of times before being able to get a successful run, and in all other instances, sudden and unsatisfactory situations can cause one's blood pressure to rise, truly spending money to suffer.

_childDocuments_.review: God I want to like this game so much. I really, really do. The packaging and screenshots are nice, art is wonderful, gameplay is largely smooth and unencumbered. I'm just not quite sure the itch this tries to scratch and just doesn't get there somehow. This disappointment (only slight, I do plan to keep the game and keep playing) only compounded small annoyances and made them stick out to me more over time. Of course, this could easily be rectified by playing more than 2 hours of the game.The orbs don't really affect much of the gameplay, the gameplay doesn't make sense as to how attack damage is dealt (maybe I'm just unobservant idk), the RNG is a little wonky, the paths are generally the same regardless of direction you head, and the thing that got under my skin (as pedantic and nitty gritty as it is, I'm sorry) at the end of the most recent playthrough were the imitation SquareEnix menu sounds that get way overused and have way too much echo/reverb on them for my taste. Again-- very pedantic and snobby of me, I know. But I want to hold on to this game because it's possible I've just scratched the surface as in StS near the beginning. Make no mistake that this is definitely NOT a Peggle/Pachinko version of Slay the Spire.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a player of Peglin for a while. I even got a few of my friends playing it. When Peglin first started the game was easy to feel powerful using 3-4 strategies and it was easy to enjoy the progression of the game. Now the game feels like the balls fall faster then they should, don't bounce enough, and you now have to consider spending gold coins on life vs upgrades. The fun curve significantly reduced. The game left the casual category and went more into every turn and decision requires considered strategy. The game is still good, but i'd be lying if I said Peglin since launch has retained the "fun factor" it had when it was first launched in early access. I likely won't be playing this game as much as I had previously which is a shame. Peglin In it's current state I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this a bad review for the lack of depth thanks to no economy and it's initial lack of a difficulty curve making choices extremely obvious. Now that we have a lot of Cruciball and an economy, I feel the need to update this review.The game is still chaotic. I struggle to say it's a particularly strategic game. It's not Slay the Spire where you really dig down into how to build a deck and deviate interesting directions based on what you get methodically. That being said, it's got it's own appeal to it as a passive game and what they did add addressed a lot. Boss variety and enemies variety over time has been made to account for throwing a wrench in strategies, as well as Cruciball modifiers changing up what you do. The money aspect especially adds a lot if not strategy than at least decisions. Now you don't just cross your fingers after battle hoping you get an upgrade instead of a new orb, removing orbs is no longer exclusive to "?" events, and now you don't just 90% of the time chuck the ball directly into a direction to end a level. I always found the end navigation by way of peggle cute, but pointless because it was very rare you'd risk ending up in the wrong well. Now you get to go for coins. Now you don't necessarily just finished a battle off in 1 shot, you find time to go for coins. It's getting significantly better and I fully recommend it now. I just have my fingers crossed multiple characters turns out just as good, but am also hesitant they might go the easy route and just make minor starting item differences rather than Slay the Spire style where each character has access to vastly different cards.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting to like this as I really like pachinko as a genre and roguelikes but this game fell flat for me. The price of this game ( normally $20) of over $5 is way too high for the gameplay of this game and eventually why I did a refund after playing for a short period.It's kinda boring in which it doesn't feel like a good pachinko game. The idea of the game is really cool- but the actual gameplay is very one-note. The ball types you get don't really change the overall feel of the game with their effects/impacts on the round. I don't feel any growth or progression outside of a variety of ball-types and leveling these balls effects.I feel like the "pachinko" aspect isn't really the highlight as it tries to adapt a pinball-like physics when interacting with the pegs/stages. The RNG of physics doesn't feel heavy. Everything is a bit too bouncy imo and there's no real weight behind the ball you shoot- maybe for the best player-wise to get more pegs but it doesn't feel like pachinko outside of the way the game is framed.I'm sure this hits for a certain audience as this game is generally well reviewed- but I really didn't care for this as a pachinko game nor as a roguelike. Maybe it's the graphic style or overall physics- but nothing hit despite being on my wishlist for a long time thinking that this game looked interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're going to play a video game, play one where you have some agency. 99% of this comes down to luck. What trinkets are offered, what balls, and as the difficulty level increases the game brazenly cheats, causing your orbs to bounce in ways completely contradictory to any known laws of physics. Indeed, playing on a higher difficulty and then going to a newer character on a lower difficulty setting makes this blindingly apparent, as you can rather easily predict the path the ball will take from a given bounce as it approaches the peg.On the higher difficulties this becomes impossible, as the ball will sometimes lose all momentum upon striking the peg, despite it not being a slime peg, or bounce in the same direction as it was going when it hit, when it should very obviously have rebounded.The first few difficulties are quite entertaining, but as the cheating becomes more and more apparent the higher you climb, the game loses all appeal as your input means less and less.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:  The game is still in early access, and unfinished, but the devs have added more content. Mostly in the form of new balls and a couple new characters, that add a little bit of diversity. Could still use more. It doesn't quite scratch that gameplay loop itch that makes me want to keep hitting "Play Again" at the end of a rogue like. YMMV  but giving it a tentative thumbs up, in spite of the price being a bit too high still, and the content being somewhat lacking.In time this could be a really fun game, but in its current early access state there is not enough content to justify the cost, even at sale price. I bought the game in a bundle on sale, and 11 hours in I feel like I've seen everything the game has to offer. I've won three or four runs now. I feel pretty sure I've seen all of the bosses and combat encounters, and there isn't much variety in them. There is a NG+ mode similar to STS ascensions, as most roguelikes have these days. It's fine, but nothing you haven't seen before. I also feel like I end up in the same builds every run. Attempts at experimenting with synergies or weak balls and items in hopes of hitting "dream" synergies just haven't felt worthwhile. Hopefully this will all be more fleshed out later in development, but for now this has the content of a free demo for a $10 game that is being sold for nearly double that.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to really like this game.      After buying it I had fun for a bit. Until I realized the game wasn't about skill at all but about luck, just as others are saying.  The relics and orbs are random and you need so much power to get through the levels but you may not get it and enemies become impossible mainly bosses.  So its not set up well.  The idea is great but there needs to be patches to make this game more enjoyable as In not making orbs so random.   There needs to be a mode where you can continue your progress because as soon as you die you have to start all over again.   Some relics as in random buffs dont make any sense to be on the board as they just give you negative affects but you dont even have to take them you can just walk away.   So why have them if we dont have to take them?  I find myself having fun for a short while but always frustrated at the end.  When there is nothing i can do to prevent eminent death.Issues I have come across:Coins at the end of a round, would be nice if we could always hit them and get a few extra coins before navigating to the next location. This however does not always work and you get no coins for your last orb thrown.Medieval scorpion device on level 2 (BOSS) it is way too hard, I could see it being a later boss but most often you do not have the abilities to get through it and it hits hard. I had 200 hp from a buff and some great dmg dealers yet still failed. only get past this level if a different boss shows up.Take un-needed relics off completely that give the character loss effects.  As we wont use them anyway.  Or give every ball a positive /negative outcomeMake relics per map/level  not all the way through the game at random. This would make it easier for devs to make strategic decisions players will overcome and eventually learn.when choosing a new orb, let us see the other orbs easily by tapping tab or somethingmake an easy and hard mode
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanic of having to fire a ball to choose which path you take completely ruins the entire game for me.  Being able to choose your path in a roguelike like this is so insanely important, it can effectively tank your entire run just because your ball randomly bounces into the wrong path option.Most of the time you have clean shots to go where you want, and only risk ending up on the wrong path if you get get greedy and try to grab some extra coins on the way.  This is fine, as a risk-reward mechanic.  The problem is when you have paths that randomly spawn impossible mazes of pegs before you choose, making where you end up almost completely random.  This happens, at least once, literally every run.  Imagine if, in StS, you moved to click on an elite to get a sweet artifact, and the game sometimes says 'no' and moved you to a random, much worse spot on the board, that then locks you into a chain of bad options that you didn't want.  It's a pretty awful, no-win, feel-bad mechanic.  This is extra bad because, in Peglin, some paths are just obviously, objectively worse than others.  In StS and most games, no matter which path you take you get the same number of nodes.  Some are better than others, but you always get a chance for an equal *number* of rewards, if not reward quality.In this game, some paths just have significantly fewer reward nodes (in addition to being worse); they will just skip over free chests altogether, not replacing them with anything else.  And sometimes this is completely out of your control.  In a game that is already 100x more random than most skill-based roguelikes, the fact that you can't even guarantee agency in what path you take kills the whole experience for me.  Solid thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: If your not a fan of Peggle, this may not be for you. The item combos, can get rather comical. To have 5-6 beefy enemies on the screen at once, and to wipe them all with a long chain is just fun. The game is kind of short however, Once you beat the 3rd campaign region, that's it. The game is the hardest early in my opinion when you don't have many item/ammo synergies, late game it gets easy and if you have a good synergy set up, the final region boss is little threat.

_childDocuments_.review: Heeee, for now, the balance is way too broken.Most "build" simply cannot works when you ramp up a bit the difficult, some totally break because of random event you have no control over it, some boss are downright impossible to deal unless you have a specific type of build (easy to notice when you start increasing the difficulty).Boss, event, relic, stone you get, everything is random to the point you are just restarting stage 1 but you need to not get the slime boss, not get the random encounter with spiders or purple slime depending on your setup, get some correct relic AND ball AND money AND upgrade them. Because increasing the difficulty ramp up the HP so much, you need very high damage.And if you just want to play on lower difficulty you still see how thing get broken, some build can do 10000+dmg a turn while some other barely do 100 to 200.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a good concept but the balance and creativity of the orbs and relics really let it down.I've played a total of 4 runs of this game. The first one to the first boss, and the next 3 all beat the last boss. I did different things every time but the differences in strategy don't really feel interesting enough to offer more replayability. There just aren't that many relics or orbs that are all that interesting and after just a couple of runs I feel like I've seen enough.The balance is the main problem of this game. The game is incredibly easy if you get past the first boss and it gets progressively easier as you get further on. The last boss is one of the easiest fights.On top of this the later stages kind of ignore the actual core peggle style mechanic. In the beginning you actually have to try and hit crits and bombs or you will lose a lot of health. After the first zone you most likely can just fire wherever and still do fine, this is compounded by the fact that a lot of later relics (like magnet) essentially make the aiming pointless. Then the level designs later on have invisible and moving pegs, which just further makes it clear that the developer didn't intend to you to have to even aim here.I will be interested to see on full release what the game is like but in it's current state to make it into a game which has some real longevity the orbs/relics and later stages would need to be entirely redesigned.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 1: dev has updated the game and I'm continuing to have fun. Leaving old review below for reference. There is a giant crossbow boss that is overpowered and needs to be adjusted.A fun little indie game for the first 3 hours during which I got my first clear. I started on the harder version and stopped playing after another 2 hours of not getting anywhere and feel that mode needs more balancing. The game is more of a true rougelike since you don't unlock powers or become stronger after a playing for a while. Replayability isn't there yet as the three levels don't give you time to build out a strategy and your more of just going along for the ride.Technically the games controller support and full screen windowed mode worked flawlessly for me. I'd say the game should be priced at $5 right now for 3-5 hours of play. Hopefully they will add a lot more content and bring its value up. Some sort of money gathering system that allowed you to buy power-ups would add more depth to this game. It could really borrow a lot from Slay the Spire and it would be more fun.The magnet power-up is overpowered compared to everything else by a large margin.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game. I've been playing since early access. But there's so many boards that are just unfun. The mushrooms, the upside-down man, and the bomb guys have levels where it's incredibly easy to hit like 5 pegs against enemies with thousands of points in health. But the worst is the ghost, Peg-ta, where you're basically forced to take 50+ damage throwing away balls with like 2 hits each.

_childDocuments_.review: Camera shake is used heavily and there is no way to turn it off.If you are hoping for a roguelike Peggle, this isn't it. The physics on the balls makes for very lackluster shots. Every bounce the ball gets extremely heavier to make sure more bounces are less likely. The levels are sometimes okay, but most of the themed levels are just designed to look like something and are not well thought out level designs for a Peggle-like experience. Peggle has various mechanics that make the game feel better to play and makes it more exciting to hit a lot of pegs in one shot.Choosing where to go on the map requires shooting a ball into a hole with pegs blocking them in various ways, but that will often mean you don't get a choice in where you go. On top of that, there is often a fire pit hole where you will just take damage if the ball goes into it. Both of these mechanics are just anti-fun.Random encounters will often have "take damage" on all possible choices. If you have too low of health, choosing any of said options will just straight up kill you and end the run.Ranged enemies shoot you every shot and is incredibly unfair.There's a small number of ball types that are fun, but the rest are not.After every fight you can choose to get a new ball, upgrade a ball, or heal. All of these options cost money though. If you have no money, you get nothing for beating a level and it feels terrible. There is a shop you can visit on the map that lets you buy balls or remove a ball, but the cost of everything is expensive, so you will rarely be able to buy anything. You are likely to buy a ball or upgrade a ball every time you are able to after a fight, so you rarely will have money for the shop. Healing and upgrading could stay as a cost after fights, but the balls should be free. The shop could also offer healing and upgrading at a reduced price.Overall, the many, many games I've tried of this have not even remotely come close to reaching the level of fun I have had in Peggle games. The game is just designed to not be fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This game is in Early Access. There's a pretty good chance that the current issues will be at least mitigated before the full release, and I know that. This review is specifically covering the current build.I wanted to like this game so badly. I heard about its announcement ages ago, and grayfruit's playthrough of the closed demo back in late 2020 had me decently excited for the release of the game. However, at least in my opinion, the game fails to provide a fun experience on nearly all aspects.The music is okay. I wouldn't go so far as to call it "bad", since it takes a genuinely talented musician to make bad music, but the tracks are more average than anything.The general style and direction of the game is quite endearing, and it's probably my favorite part of the game. The ball puns are cute, I like the creativity with the item designs, and the different boards for each enemy group are really cool.The gameplay is... Well... Pachinko. I wouldn't necessarily call it worse than pachinko, but it's definitely worse than Peggle. Part of the joy of Peggle was how easily controllable the ball is, and being able to do trickshots, slick shots, and bucket bounces feels REALLY good when you manage to pull it off. I can't quite place why, but the ball feels unruly and hard to manage in Peglin, especially when you're trying to refresh the board. Combine that with the necessity of hitting specific pegs in order to actually deal serviceable damage, and it quickly becomes VERY frustrating.The roguelike elements feel very forced, and as much I want to like the interesting ideas put forth by the game, I can't shake the feeling that the twists and interesting mechanics of the game are derivative and downright lazy in places. The Slay the Spire formula just doesn't work if you can only draw up to two cards per turn (three with a very specific relic), and you can only play one, and enemies have ludicrous amounts of Health, and you can (usually) only attack one enemy at a time.On the subject of enemy health and AoE damage, the balance is easily the worst part of the game. You either make a bomb build, or you're playing the game wrong. I know that sounds very pejorative and closed-minded, but I'm being serious. Sapper Sack increases your odds of winning by 500%, and every Bob-Orb increases your chances by 100%. Bombs are the only thing in this entire game that can deal enough damage to push through the stupid amount of health and numbers of the enemies. And oftentimes, even that's not enough. There is a specific miniboss in Area 3 that is a darkened room completely filled with enemies, each of which have something like 777 Health EACH. Even with a bomb build, the room is completely ridiculous. As well as that, the Wall Head has over 7000 health, and if he makes it all the way to the player, you instantly die. I don't think I've ever beaten the boss without either Sapper Sack or Electromagnet (which was nerfed to hell in a recent patch). Animated Ruins is also a ridiculous boss, but I've only ever seen that boss three times, and beaten it once. In 11 hours of gameplay, I've only ever seen that boss THREE TIMES, and the one time I killed it was before the balance patch that made it harder.I sincerely hope some major changes are made to the game, since I really want to like it. But as it stands, I just don't have fun when I play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: This ones a cautious yes from me because while I love this clever fusion of Peggle and an RPG roguelike, there's some severe balance issues going on. There's definitely certain rooms you can just look at and know you aren't going to win (because of a combination of not great layout of pegs, lack of bombs, and a mob of baddies with ranged attacks.) And with no progressive carry over of anything between games, it makes it rough to start over again knowing you just lost a decent run because of a bum level. Beyond that, it's great to play and the powers are neat and fun to use together in interesting ways. I just hope they keep working on this and really flesh it out, especially for the current price (feels more like a $10 game.)

_childDocuments_.review: Tough choice.I did enjoy it, but its incredibly short and difficulty is just way too low.  Finished game in an hour.  New game+ might add a few hours but don't think that will fix the issue.The base game is great and has lot of potential.Biggest issue I usually see in roguelikes is balancing and adding enough variety where you can and have to be a bit creative.It becomes easy to powerhouse everything.  But simply upping enemies numbers makes it not fun.There can be added clarity when hovering over enemies to know what they even do.Maybe special blocks you have to hit to do extra damage, unlock shields, push enemies back, etc.  It can help add a bit more variety and thinking more of how to use your shots.  Maybe some ideas from peggle where you can get abilities or skills.  A bit more creative than various balls.  Variety of enemies that take various ways of strengths and weakness.  Maybe ways to delay attacks.  Enemies that get stronger if you crit or reset.  Maybe enemies that is defensive against bombs.  Enemies weak to elements, etc.Range enemies that maybe have a timer of when they will shoot instead of shooting right away.  Personally dont like damage that is unavoidable that pretty much takes first turn enemy wipe.Weird dark room where you just shoot and pray wasn't good imo.In end...this is a developer I never seen so only time will tell.  I did read the april 25th update on the general path they want to go.  It just seems more characters and harder difficulty which I don't think will fix the core issue for me.  Its not a bad game and of course not every roguelike has to be challenging, but after the initial enjoyment, the game I can see getting stale quickly.While I enjoyed it for a very short time.  Its potential is high.  Its lacking way too much.  Currently, can't recommend it.  I hope for the best as I really love the idea of this

_childDocuments_.review:
The dragons have been popping peglins and stealing all of your gold for as long as you can remember. Enough is enough. It's time to venture through the woods, conquer the fortress, and delve into the heart of the dragon's lair to take back what's yours and teach those dragons a lesson.

Peglin plays like a combination of Peggle and Slay the Spire. The enemies are tough, and if you're defeated your run is over, but you've got powerful orbs with special effects and incredible relics that influence both your enemies and the physics you'll use to defeat them.

name: Forgotten Fields
detailed_description: Check out my next game! About the Game Sid is a writer struggling with writer's block, attempting to recapture the feelings of inspiration he felt when he was younger. In order to pay the bills, he needs to think up a story and apply for a grant - the deadline is today - a lazy Sunday in the middle of summer. On this Sunday, his struggle is disturbed by an invitation to attend an unavoidable family obligation - the place Sid grew up in is about to be sold, and his mother wants him to come home for a small party so he can say goodbye to it. With the deadline approaching and his creative juices having frozen, this is not something he's looking forward to. Talk to old friends, run through the fields, swim in the ocean, and solve relaxing puzzles in this warm, slice-of-life narrative about nostalgia and the passage of time by the developer that brought you Rainswept. Features: A warm, slice-of-life narrative about nostalgia, appreciating the present, and the passage of time by the developer that brought you Rainswept. Take part in Sid's creative process as you play through a parallel story set in a fantasy world - right out of the book that Sid is attempting to write. Simple, relaxing puzzles that keep gameplay interesting without slowing down the story. A friendly and supportive cast of characters with deep histories and fleshed-out personalities. Cinematic presentation accompanied by a beautiful soundtrack by micAmic (Rainswept, The Cat Lady, Lorelai, Downfall) An atmospheric, warm, and cozy world to lose yourself in as you get immersed in Sid's journey back home.
