_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an atmospheric sojourn into the depths of Lovecraftian horror, replete with wonderfully-crafted grotesque art, replete with writhing tentacles, incomprehensible entities of cyclopean proportions and sights to drive you to the edge of madness and beyond.  With a plot drawn directly from the works of H.P. Lovecraft himself, and featuring a tour-de-force of Cthulhu Mythos entities, The Shore is a beautifully made experience, albeit a briefly one.  I ran through it in just under 3 hours, similar to watching certain movies.  While it was heavy on the atmosphere and grotesque beauty, it was light on the gameplay.  If you're looking for intricate systems and engaging combat, look elsewhere.  If you want a lengthy game that will occupy you for weeks and months to come, don't play The Shore.  But if you're fan of the Cthulhu Mythos and want to immerse yourself in a lovely piece of artwork, give this one a try.  Especially if it's on sale, it's spectacle alone is worth the small price it has.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I enjoyed The Shore for what it was, I feel odd recommending it because if there's a chance that my review will tip you over the edge into buying the game...well...you just might want to show up to my house wearing a pair of steel-toed boots and repeatedly kick me in the groin.  As I'm wincing on the ground and telling you that you fight like a cheap little hussy, I'll still stand by liking The Shore while you get even cheaper and beat me with a hockey stick for not backing down.  This is an odd slice of Lovecraft that has you exploring an island as fisherman Andrew who happens to be on the hunt for his lost daughter Ellie.  Things start out as an ethereal point n' click style of adventure which doesn't really prepare you for the fact that jarringly and quicker than expected you'll be running from fishy sons of swordfishes and later even gaining a magical weapon that becomes your proxy to fight off even uglier monstrosities.  First things first, The Shore looks absolutely phenomenal for an indie and it sounds great too.  The screenshots don't really tell any lies.  The island itself is gorgeous and foreboding to explore as you solve puzzles, search an abandoned lighthouse, find notes in bottles, traverse to harder to reach places that reveal all manner of Lovecraft callbacks/collectibles and do the usual adventure/horror stuff.  It's somewhat standard issue but the allure of the location that you are exploring does a lot to make up for any feelings of "same ol', same ol'" in the gameplay department.  I enjoyed doing these things in the early goings of this game more than I have in some of the other recent horror offenders that I played once and put on probation from ever gracing my PC again...they're also on probation from my memory because I can't remember several horror games I've played over the last few years but this one I will.    The trippy esoteric hysteria soon gives way to the first stumbling chase and then things are a sorta mixed bag from there in terms of mechanics.  I didn't find any of it overly difficult like some players but the stealth/running is basic trodding meat n' potatoes where you either run real fast or plod along underwater SOMA-like to get away from slimy big uglies.  You can try sneakier approaches but you'll probably get beat to a pulp.  And then...just when Andrew seems like he's gonna bite the dust, the island starts changing him.  It seems to beckon him to A WEAPON.  Now, we are f'ing talking.  I like shooting idiots back in horror games instead of taking a smacking since I got my start with this mayhem back when Alone in the Dark, Resident Evil and Silent Hill were new games.  And yeah...the shooting.  Well, it's there.  It's piecemeal and sure could have used some further excitement but it works.  So, the next phase of the game has you walking backwards through tunnels, shooting a laser with a cooldown time at monsters that don't seem to die, hoping to bump your ass into the right passage and get out of wormhole tunnels into the next strange area.  The monsters are fantastic looking, even without VR and there is a certain tension to these escapades of escape but your weapon of endless power is just a straight, static beam that you've got to lean to with until you turn on your beeping back-up lights and get your rear end literally out of the mazes.   The fighting gets a little better when you can take on your enemies and walk straight into the brawl as you fight some of the bigger beasts towards the game's finale (including the final boss) but the combat feels like it should be on some n64 port of a PC game than such a modern, surreal looking graphical masterpiece.  I honestly didn't hate it but I'm not going to run around in public and tell you to buy this game for its combat, that's for sure.  Some of the combat sequences are set up as puzzles too and honestly, if I'm allowed a choice here, those are probably better than the run full speed and hold down the fire button till you can't sequences.Aside from the increase in combat, the puzzles get stranger and some of the ones that you solve will free a few of the Old Gods from their shackles.  These scenes are always worth it as these monstrosities coming into gargantuan, towering life are certainly spectacles to behold.  For everything that The Shore handles averagely in terms of mechanics, it makes up for by delivering some kind of absolutely stunning visual reward that kept me pushing forward through my roughly 3 hours of game time.  That's pretty much The Shore in a nutshell.  I don't know what else to say about as if you're coming to see what visual triumphs it unveils, those are best experienced in your own eyes as opposed to reading me ramble on at 2:40 in the morning.  I liked it but I can see someone else hating the everlovin' Dagon sh*t out of it as well.  Some of the more direct horror sequences are effective despite the so-so mechanics but The Shore is at its absolute best when it pauses, visually creeps over your mind like a hallucinogen, reveals revelations of Elder God splendor to you and leaves you with several quiet yet possibly dangerous paths to explore and see what lore you can dig up.  7/10 for me.  I'll definitely check out the devs next game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Lovecraft, you will enjoy this game. In some ways, the game is amazing, though it's let down a bit by the story. _childDocuments_.review: is a first-person narrative adventure set in the mid '900s, inspired to the Cthulhu mythos' lore. Players impersonate the member of a sailor crew, that got stranded on a mysterious island where unexplained events happen regularly. Between distorted space-time and elusive dark beings, the protagonist will have to make his way through a madness-inducing land.The Shore features a definitely solid art direction level, when it comes down to world representation and environment design. Each location has a distinct color palette, chromaticity and dominant theme that sets it apart from the others. From the calm but eerie island shores to much more disturbing locations, every setting is well crafted and rich in details. Documents and examined items also have good levels of care in their making.The ambient sounds and music tracks dominate the atmosphere of this game, kicking in mostly at the perfect times to emphasize events - as it should be with any good cinematic-oriented production. Voice acting on the other hand is only of passable quality overall, with some ups and downs depending on the situation. The sound compartment's contribution in building the eerie feeling that dominates each location, is surely significant.For a narrative adventure, The Shore has an above-average diversity of gameplay situations. From exploration and rather classic item-based puzzles, to more unusual combat phases and chase sections, the game proposes a good variety, especially in relation to the total short duration. In addition, several achievement-related secondary areas are present, to also shed a bit more light on the lore... or the opposite.The proposed price of 21€ (25 USD) is really out of line considering the short duration of the game, and no replay value (as expected from the genre). While it proves to be a good quality adventure, that doesn't justify a price to content ratio of 7€ / Hour, which is actually pretty grim all things considered. I highly suggest waiting for a significant discount before buying, even to fans of Lovecraftian settings.Even on a reasonably high-end system, The Shore has proven to be quite an heavy task to run, and unoptimized at that too. Especially in open-air areas, slowdowns and framerate drops were not uncommon at all in 1440p. The fact there is no Exclusive Fullscreen and as consequence no in-game Vsync, further accentuate the already present issues. There surely is more work to be done in this field.While most of the puzzles, action sections and exploration segments are fairly well designed, a few of them stand out for being rather subpar. Certain combat situations prove frustrating due to infinite-respawn enemies and unreliability of the "weapon" at players' disposal. A few puzzles prove to be especially obscure in their logic, without even a small hint to guide players - that can definitely become frustrating.Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Puzzles and Action Sequences.Is performed on foot across the island, and later on also in caves and other depths. There is no map, however environmental clues lead the player, such as signposts or strategically placed lights. Location layouts are fairly linear, with but a few secondary areas where one an find collectibles, lore items and the occasional achievement-related goal. There is no point in exploring out of the main path, except for finding such things, that given the game's short duration, give some more longevity to it. Generally players can't die while exploring except a few select locations, and in that case checkpoints are rather abundant.Are generally based on finding the correct item for unlocking a passage or path, especially in the first part of the game. Later on, when more tools are at players' disposal, puzzles may become a bit more elaborate as they involve the operation of unknown machinery and other "arcane" structures. This includes rituals as well in some parts. Apart from a few quite obscure puzzles, they are never too difficult or tedious.Involve escaping from or fighting unimaginable horrors straight out of the Lovecraftian mythos. At some point, an artifact is acquired and used to defeat such monsters. However, in some situations escaping is the best solution. Combat proves to be rather unreliable at times, because the artifact isn't consistent in effectiveness or accuracy. There is even a proper boss fight at a later stage, which is something not often seen in this genre at all.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is complete nonsense and you can tell the game is budget by the animation and scripting quality. However, the atmosphere in the early areas and the environment design throughout the game are very good. The sound design is also pretty good, mostly due to a couple of standout tracks and some sounds that stand out individually. There are some basic adventure game mechanics but nothing complex or puzzling outside of one specific puzzle, which isn't so much complex as it is poorly conveyed to the player.Overall, I recommend playing the game purely due to the environments. The gameplay's nothing special and the story might as well not exist. But man the environments are sensory overload and you should experience them.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out with the typical mystery and lore hunting of a Lovecraftian walking simulator. That was its charm. Then it spirals down into chase scenes (some you can fight back, some you cannot) while navigating dark tunnels where its easy to get stuck on a wall or object. Not fun at all. The visuals were great, but even the implementation of Lovecraft's various entities felt thrown together at random. No real consistency between each one that you meet. It sort of gets put together at the end but it felt empty. And yes, there are strange audio issues as some have mentioned. Best to have subtitles turned on.I got it on a really great sale so I'll give it a thumbs up. I'd definitely stay away from the VR version of this, considering how clunky this one is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concepts, poor execution. Lacks polishing, misses a few basic game design things, bad performance. Couldn't bring myself to keep going, the game's missing a lot of things that make playing a game a pleasant experience. Stopped playing after interacting with a note softlocked the game.Lots of invisible walls, no good sense of direction or progress, and what little dialogue I've come across felt bland. I might give it another try at a later date, but a game like this could've benefited a lot from play-testing and feedback.From what I understand this is a fairly new dev who's getting started in the game industry, and I do feel like he's put a lot of love into the game; but as a player, these issues stand out to me too much, and if the very few first minutes aren't engaging it's difficult to buy into the idea.As far as polishing goes, a few examples:The menu could borrow from the game's aesthetic, it's very basic and clunky. There's no pause either, which makes it weird when I want to mess with the settings.I went through a portal which transitioned me to a different area. No screen effects, just a jump between two different places. Felt like I just moved my character's position in a console or something to that effect.Huge chunks of text in the subtitles covering almost half the screen with some notes. Splitting it makes it less distracting from what should be an immersive game experience.First "puzzle" I messed with felt meaningless, just had me interact with 3 different stones in whatever order I wanted.That's what I've got from my first 30 minutes into the game. Is it a bad game? Hard to say, but I wouldn't recommend it based on my personal experience with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Good sides :- Great atmospheric game. Big spaces, impressive and awe-inspiring landscapes.- Puzzles in general are satisfying : you get into them with no explanation but you never really find yourself not knowing what you're supposed to do. They're not "easy" but not convoluted either.- Love all the references to Lovecraft's works.My personal criticisms :- Big spaces make for a lot of walking, and it can be frustrating to walk all the way back when you feel like you've forgotten or missed something somewhere.- I would love to see the game have more achievements and easter eggs. All these empty spaces and deadends are wonderful opportunities to plant a plot piece that tells me 1. I didn't walk all the way there for nothing, and 2. Yes, I found all there was to be found in that corner, I didn't oversee anything and I don't have to come back. As it is, a lot of open spaces are just rocks, bushes and waves, and sometimes you're not really sure if a pile of rocks is supposed to be climbed on or not. Again, not bad per se as it contributes to the space feeling aerated and the player feeling small in comparison. Just a bit of a missed opportunity.Other comments :- This is not a classic Lovecraftian game, in the sense that you get very close to the "monsters" and they feel like they have human emotions and goals. They're tangible, they speak English, in short, they're not really Great Old Ones, they're just very big harbingers of doom.- It's weird to not have a sanity bar going down when you stare at monstrosities.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the Mythos. The universe our beloved Howard Phillips Lovecraft created is so complex, so immense in every level! From the lowest creatures, whose fate are to be enslaved to extinction, to amorphous chaotic masses of tentacles, eyes and mouths that created everything in his dreams. Quite a huge, amazing and interesting universe of unthinkable cosmic horror.This game, however... It makes it no justice at all. This game is quite a big disappointment to any fan of the Mythos. Spoilers ahead.1) The plot. It's nothing but a rought draft of a fleeting idea. Absurdly bad. You're a guy that wakes up in the shore of a foggy island, with nothing around but fog, water, broken ships, half the population of France rotted to skeletons scattered around, and dark sand. All you know and all you're ""told"" (narrated through the guy speaking to himself) is that you're looking for your daughter. Then you follow a voice in your head that forces you to free several Great Old Ones in order to give you your daughter back in exchange for following his intructions. Once you've done everything he's told you, he tells you your daughter was never real, she was just fake memories the voice (Nyarlathotep) created in your mind cuz why not, but then encourages you to make it so Azathoth believes your daughter is real, and hence creates her in his dreams, which is everything that exists. Simply nonsensical.2) It lacks the main theme of the entire Mythos: HORROR. INSANITY. Seeing your grandmother coming out of the shower, naked, after barging into the bathroom without knocking first is way scarier than this. What about insanity? Well if you think you're gonna find insanity in this game, you're partly right! It exists! But only as the backstory of a sailor crew that ended up in that island. They ended up insane and dying this or that way or just killing themselves. That's it. Your character, Andrew, goes around freeing Great Old Ones, even standing in front of Cthulhu and freaking talking to him as Cthulhu talks about how he's gonna destroy humankind before epicly launching a boat towards you, but nah, Andrew's sanity is still there, he probably saw worse stuff than a literal god-like creature that wipes out every drop of sanity from any living being foolish enough to look his way or even being near his presence. He can even see Azazoth, The Nuclear Chaos, The Blind Idiot God, and not give a crap. They justify it as "Andrew's lack of sympathy made him lose fear", which is stupid. He probably just saw something way worse than all of that. He probably saw his grandma naked after coming out of the shower because he barged into the bathroom without knocking first.3) Textures. Absolutely disgusting. Even in Ultra, the sand, the damn first thing you see when you start the game, looks like Minecraft. Not even joking, it's so pixely that it feels like a recolor of Minecraft's gravel texture. Then there are floating rocks here and there, and big rocks that don't connect to the ground and you can peek inside the texture if you crouch a bit... Oh, also, everything you interact with and inspect up-close looks like a blurry 144p texture before focusing after a second or two. Don't even want to talk about the animations where things just shabbily go into the ground without any kind of effect to hide the textures going into the ground... The only good point I can see, is that some of the monsters in the game are properly designed, and have pretty good designs. Although I didn't check their textures from up-close for obvious reasons, so I can't say if they were good or shabby. Although, I did walk into the Deep One that was doing push-ups behind the whale corpse cuz I didn't know it was an enemy, and it was just... disappointing.4) Gameplay. This game is some kind of amalgam of several mechanics. First, it starts as a sorta phylosophical narrative walking simulator where you walk around figuring stuff out by yourself (because the game won't tell you anything about what you have to do), find a few pages of lore, -if you can call it lore-, and do some dumb puzzles with even dumber "rewards" for completion. At least they give achievements. Those are cool. Oh, also, you can't run or jump at first, you *unlock* those "actions" as you "progress". Apparently Andrew forgot how to run and jump at first... Then, the game introduces some sort of a failure of action/combat mechanics, where at first you're chased by a Deep One that was doing push-ups begind a whale's corpse, then sees you and runs after you *as fast as you can run*, which means if you didn't notice him and he catches you, he will attack you until you're dead, and you can't outrun him at all because the shabby attack animations doesn't even make him stand still or reduce his speed. After you die and try to run away again, and succeed, you start getting teleported into horrific "worlds", which to be honest were better than the previous areas of the game, where you go around solving more stupid puzzles where you aren't told anything nor given any hint at all (which isn't that bad cuz the puzzles are made for Primary Schoolers), and sometimes you were hugged by some weird humanoid thing and you had to push it back with the brand new combat "mechanics", and some other times some weird flea thing or a Shoggoth would pursue you and you'd have to escape. That is, until you obtain The Eye of the Gatekeeper! An artifact which shoots a beam to activate things, solve puzzles and hurt your enemies! Although it doesn't work half the time and you have to click and hold several times for it to actually shoot. Oh, of course, when you kill your enemies they just disappear with a shabby "blood" texture of a fourth of the size of the creature. And then you face this spider-like enemy that runs super fast and attacks even faster, which you can only kill by kinda bugging it by attacking it with the beam, backing away, and kinda hiding so it stays still. There's also a boss, who I believe is Shub-Niggurath, who is the shabbiest boss fight I've fought in a long time. Shub-Niggurath made for a way tougher boss in South Park, and it isn't a Dark Souls-type of game, to be honest.5) Immersion. Absolutely none. I tried my best to feel any immersion, but everything was just so stupid that I just couldn't. Even the few seconds I took to admire some giant creature like Dagon, or the walking monolith, or the giant walking flea in the distance, it'd be ruined by seeing the creatures calmly walk off. All I could admire was Dagon climbing onto the walking monolith like King Kong climing the Empire State, and Cthulhu's thicc ass. Seriously, he had quite a booty.6) Sound. Two things, voice acting, and soundtrack. To be honest, the soundtrack was pretty good in my opinion. The voice acting, however... It was... Mediocre. If you're drunk enough.7) Duration. I don't even know if I should say it's good or bad... My gameplay only took 2 hours, which is quite underwhelming and short for a 10€ game. Terraria costs 10€ when it's not on sale, and you can get HUNDREDS of hours of fun with it. I, personally, believe it was good that this game was only 2 hours. It was too atrocious for me to want it to be longer.Conclusion: This is an awful game. I don't think the developers wanted to disrespect the Mythos with this game, but they accidentally did. And I don't blame them, making games is hard. But even so, if you decide to make a game... TRY it before you sell it. Ask your friends to try it, so they can tell you "This game's ♥♥♥♥" before you sell it and decide to do something better with it, like trying to fix it, even redoing it, or just deleting the files and erasing it from existence. This game just fails at 96% of the things it has. I regret paying for this, and wasting 2 hours on this game. I could've spent them reading the wonderful Metro 2033 book.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game after 2.7 hours gameplay. Oh man. I have a soft spot for lovecraftian horror. Unfortunately for lovecraft, his fiction has almost always produced horrible games (and I say ALMOST always because of the existence of a game called bloodborne). Unfortunately, I cannot say that this game is an exception. The writing is just terrible. Really awful, boring, and drably unimaginative. The gameplay is practically nonexistent. It consists of running away from monsters through tunnels while occasionally using an artifact to slow them down temporarily or the occasional puzzle that seems like they exist purely to pad the play length of the game. They are really hardly puzzles and more of "go here, click this, go there, click that, do it one more time, go back to the main area and click the thing".Also what was with the voice acting? It sounds like they paid an Argentinian 5$ to voice a bad guy and then used SFX to make his voice deeper. All of the other voice acting is done by vaguely european amateur voice actors while the protagonist is voiced by an American. The protagonist doesn't do too bad of a job voice acting to be honest, maybe that's why they didn't have the budget to hire real voice actors for the other characters?One thing that game and movie developers consistently get wrong with Lovecraft is that they try to put an image to the unimaginable. They try to render unspeakable horror and mind bending terror in kitsch character models . One of the key elements of lovecraft is that he leaves the real horror up to your imagination. In this game, Cthulhu was laughable as he struts around the ocean with his megalithic ass cheeks puckered. That said, I can't say only negative things about this game because there were things that I liked. The art design was pretty solid (except for the designs of cthulhu, dagon, and some forgettable characters that chased you around). The soundtrack and sound design was well done but could have used slightly more variation, I really liked the inclusion of the meteor from The Color Out of Space. The environments felt very lovecraftian. I thought the final azathoth level was interesting with the black hole in the sky and there was a flesh level at the end where they put squelching sounds in binaural audio right up against your ears which really added to the ambiance of body horror. I also really liked the anthropomorphic statues whose eyes followed you around as you walked as well. There were also some neat scenes where you turn around and see tentacles appear behind a rock or your daughter briefly. I would have liked more of those moments and less chase scenes. TL;DR: This game has decent art and sound design but the atrociousness of the writing/voice acting mixed with the mind-numbing banality of the gameplay drag what could have been an interesting game into the deepest pits of R'lyeh.

_childDocuments_.review: Some nice visuals and ideas, but simply to short for my taste and at some point even within this short time it managed to feel repetitive. There is a little problem that can happen for some when it comes to the resolution, i post a possible fix below (worked for me).Resolution fix >>>Go to the install directory of the game (right click on the game in your steam library, properties,Local Files and then click Browse...Right click on "TheShore.exe", Properties, click on the Compatibility tab, then go to "Change high DPI Settings" then at the bottom it says "High DPI scaling override", click the tick box to enable it and make sure it says "Application" in the drop down box and then click on Ok then Apply then Ok on the previous properties box for TheShore. _childDocuments_.review: The Shore is made for fans of Cthulhu lore. That means that this isn't a run-n-gun FPS (although oddly, there is some first-person "shooting" in the game). It isn't survival horror (yet, there are quite a few cat-and-mouse chase scenes). And it isn't strictly a walking simulator (and then, you'll do a fair share of walking in the game). It's a combination of all three of those set to an interesting tale of a man who lost his little girl and his dark path to find her.It's a surreal journey which is equal parts horrifying as it is beautiful. The game is gorgeously detailed and dripping in atmosphere. The narration and voice acting overall is above par as well. And the musical score and sound effects are great.There are a few puzzles in the game, which aren't too hard. Only one gave me a headache and it turned out to be a trial and error combination that I just hadn't completed yet (it's the prism room; PM me if you need a hint). But largely fairly simple.There's a few areas of the game where its a little tricky to navigate the shore's craggy rocks. And the destructive ray you "shoot" from your artifact has like a half second delay which I found a little annoying, especially when its needed in the chase scenes.Other than that, this game is an excellent find. I beat it in just under 4 hours and 100%'ed the game from an achievement angle in about 5 hours. For an interactive Cthulhu mythos story, it's a nice little pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a decently well-made game that honors the eldritch horrors born from the wickedly genius mind of H. P. Lovecraft. The game may not appear great graphically in the shed but I grew to love the game more and more as I kept getting immersed in this Lovecraftian world. The game likes to put fast flashing eldritch symbols in your face sometimes, so if you have a thing against that then expect quite a few in The Shore.You play as an old fisherman named Andrew who wakes up shipwrecked on an island in the middle of a vast ocean. You notice your daughter is missing as well as other wrecked ships, skeletal remains, and alien artifacts on this strange place. You set out to find your daughter by checking out the large lighthouse stationed nearby the beach. Who knows what could possibly be slumbering underneath the island? What dangers could be hiding? What will you unleash?I won't spoil much else for you but I will say that the plot is purely based on , so if you know what goes on in the genre then you already have a basic understanding of The Shore's plot. I will say that I kind of liked the abrupt twist at the end of the story that left quite the cliffhanger. Still it left me satisfied with the game and who knows if there'll be a sequel?The game first begins as a  in which you walk around the island looking at possible collectibles and lore items. You could find some hidden events that show just how messed up the island can be to its inhabitants. The game does a great job of balancing what to show and tell you because you pretty much experience it firsthand. The only issue with exploration are the  that block areas that seem very walkable.The next gameplay mechanic are the  that require you to use your noggin. They are very, very simple which isn't necessarily bad if you're thirsting to see some old gods. You can get this puzzles over with quickly as most of them are pretty intuitive. There's a couple of puzzles that I felt were too monotonous to add any real gameplay value.The last one would be the interactions with the monsters that you'll encounter. You'll be either  or eventually . Once again this one is very simple like the others. For the chase scene you pretty much hold sprint and 'W' then move through a obvious path. For killing monsters, you literally hold left mouse button to user your laser beam on them until they die.First off, the font and design for the main menu selections could have been a lot better. It just looks very amateurish but doesn't devalue the game, I just wish the font didn't hurt my eyes.In all seriousness this time, the graphics aren't that bad as the island looks pretty decent. I can't say the same for the human models as even their animation is janky. The ELDRITCH models, on the other hand, are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ . I absolutely adore the art direction the developers made with respect to Lovecraft's work, they just look so otherworldly and awesome.Voice acting is decent, I mean some people may not like the Eldritch voice but I found them to be satisfactory even though it's just deepened voices. It still sounds cool and not cringey.Music was great in keeping up the suspense of exploring unknown territory as well as encountering the dangerous abominations.The Shore is incredible in showcasing a world of humanity being ruled over by fearsome Eldritch gods. The story does an amazing service in honoring the legendary genre created by H. P. Lovecraft. However you will disappointed if you're seeking for a challenge in gameplay. So .

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of the game was great. The second half feels like the developer lost creativity or got lazy. Really enjoyed the first half on the island and exploring. _childDocuments_.review: I completed this game in 5hrs including a decent amount of AFK and exploring for secrets. Overall, it's an okay game. I'm sure people who love Lovecraftian lore will enjoy it a fair amount. The jump scares weren't scary, at least not to me, and once you enter the void area, the game runs like hot trash. The solution to the problem in the void is to go into the game settings and turn the  music volume all the way down. It still had some stutter, mostly when entering new areas, but that fixed the game for the most part. It's not that difficult, and the voices tend to be a bit uneven. There's a "memory scene" toward the end of the game where the main character's voice is basically the only audible one; definitely play with subtitles on. Plus the entities are sometimes hard to understand.That all being said, the visuals were fantastic! The puzzles were okay, fairly easy. And the lore is pretty good. If you're into this kind of game and/or are a huge lovecraft fan, then this may be worth a purchase when, and only when, it's ON SALE.

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game to have a really nice atmosphere and world. Just what I wanted from a Lovecraftian game. You can feel the people who made it really wanted to do well.BUTYou can tell it was made by people who only had visuals in mind.The game is very short and has little to no gameplay. The "fights" are all boring since you have only one weapon and the monsters all die in 2 hits or you just need to kite them in a giant room where you can't see where you are going because you need to fire the monster constantly and thus walk backwards. Something else that bothered me too. At some point you meet Cthulhu. In the novels, his very sight is supposed to drive one mad and his awakening seals the end of the world. In this game you have a chat with him and he throws a boat at you ...???And I noticed some game design problems too. Like you have the possibility of using an inventory in the begining but it suits no purpose as you don't collect anything you can use in any way and about halfway through the game the inventoy is not reachable anymore until you finish it. Also sometimes I had no idea I had to click something or where to go next. (I take for example the room full of heads for those who finished the game, I had to look up a solution on google)At the very end, I didn't notice I had to click on the shadowy figures to trigger something and just walked towards Azatoth, as Nyarlathotep tells you to, but then after a few minutes I realized I hadn't triggered something at the very begining of that hallway and had to walk through it all over again while follwoing some story I didn't care about because the game is so short it didn't have the time to build characters I would care for.Anyway, the game seems alright at first, but falls flat very quickly. (I mean you only need 2,5 hours to finish it). The price the devs are asking for the game is ridiculous. DO NOT BUY THE GAMETotaly not worth that much money.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game.  It was beautiful, and the soundtrack was super awesome!  I thoroughly enjoyed the  concepts, atmosphere and story.  Hats off, my friends!! _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wish I could say that The Shore was a good game. Lovecraft always works for me. And the graphics, I mean, look at them! They are gorgeous! The maker of this game has a GREAT talent for graphics. The game sparks and shines with atmosphere, perfectly catching the Lovecraft theme. Thumbs up for that! But - as you may have expected - here comes the big fat "but". The game around the awesome setting and graphics is bad. Really bad. It would have worked PERFECTLY as a walking simulator. Nothing wrong with walking simulators - there are many great examples out there! Take the fantastic setting, add some smart puzzles maybe, have the developer shine where he shines and focus on that. It's so sad that the decision was made to add combat to The Shore. And this for me ruins most of the game's magic. It's so poorly implemented, so annoying. So much trial and error. Big monster pops up, bam bam bam yer dead, way too long loading screen, try over until you figure out what the hell the game wants from you. Zero fun. Also, I hate invisible walls. Sometimes when I walk along the shore, not exactly knowing where to go next, I constantly kept bumping into invisible walls. Not fun either. And part three: lame teleports from scene to scene. You don't fluently move through the game, but you solve a situation, and then you get teleported to the next. I am sure there would have been smarter solutons for this.Real sorry to say, but in my opinion this was a missed chance. Die-hard-Cthulhu fans may still give it a try when on sale. It's a great design showcase, but sadly not a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the tag, this game is very light on horror.That being said, it's an amazing treat for Lovecraft fans! It manages to work in many aspects of Lovecraft's lore and it does so in a logical way. That being said, it doesn't really explain much of the Lovecraft mythos, so if you aren't already familiar with the lore you may feel a bit lost as it name drops god/creatures without explaining much about them.Also, this game has some great creature designs based on the Lovecraft mythos. Especially since the game is only about 3 hours, they could've gotten lazy and just reused the same few creatures over and over. Instead they regularly throw new ones at you. They all look great!On the negative side, this game is pretty buggy, though not in a game breaking way. I never encountered a freeze or something that stopped me from progressing, but expect to regularly clip through objects, see graphical bugs galore (seagulls perched on nothing, etc.), and encounter various weird controller issues. Still, I found these issues to be minor.Also, though I liked the environments overall, there are way, way too many invisible walls. I think the dev wanted to keep the vistas an open feel, so the player can revel in the cool views, but that means that you'll constantly encounter invisible walls preventing you from getting to places you clearly should be able to go. This becomes a much bigger issue during chase sequences, since I never knew if I could walk over a low pile of rocks or if I would hit a wall. I recommend the dev just use natural barriers (i.e. high rock walls, dense trees, etc.) in future games. It will hurt the views a bit, but invisible walls are way more annoying.Last, as many reviews mention, the style of gameplay changes quite a bit in the second half of the game. I enjoyed it, but there was clearly less polish on some of those gameplay aspects. Still, the great level art/creature design and lore will easily sustain Lovecraft fans though the few rough sections.Overall, the game is only 3 hours, but I say if you can find it for $4 or less, it's a great deal. Lovecraft fans won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

An easy 4-5 hours to 100%  as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a long time to complete this game over a series of play sessions picking it up and putting it down again. Ultimately, I do recommend it on sale; however, this is with some caveats which I'm sure I share with many of the other reviewers here. My feelings towards this game are complicated. On the one hand, the art, visuals--all of that--is quite well done. The general atmosphere is all there. The scale of things is great. Forgiving a few clunky elements, it is a good looking work of art. Beyond that the story is fine, and the first half of it I would actually say is pretty great. At around the halfway point in the game the gameplay and the tone take a major shift. There are some puzzles throughout that might feel a bit arbitrary or difficult due to some element of level design (hard to read surfaces, etc). There's probably something worth saying about how separated some of these "incomprehensible and otherworldly" eldritch entities should be from the player who is just a human person, but it is what it is. At the end of the day, I think the average player will find this less scary (fine by me, a coward), but might find some elements frustrating until they get the hang of it. Even so, if you find this on a really good discount, want to do some achievement hunting, and like games which operate mostly at your own pace without holding your hand, then this game could be of benefit to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Game play here:   Holy heck this game has some of the scariest monster designs I've seen in a horror game and it came out in 2021. I love that it's an h.p. lovecraftian eldritch horror type game, but instead of it just being subtle is my character crazy it's full on eldritch beings getting real tired of your nonsense, but Andrew is nothing if not a man of perseverance. If someone is looking for a horror game to play this is a great one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: THE SHORE is an immersive walking simulator with puzzles and combat taking place in a mysterious island in what can be assumed to be the 1900s, where you play as a shipwrecked sailor looking for his daughter. Behind a cliched narrative hook lies a beautiful game with tons of enviromental detail and charming sights and setpieces, where you'll be taken on a wild ride through several of Lovecraft's mythical creatures and their schemes to forestall humanity. If you can overcome a couple of pesky puzzles, it's a well worthy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing to the right person and garbage to anyone else. If you're a fan of H.P. Lovecraft and you've thoroughly read his works then this game is like a beautiful buffet of references. The indescribable horrors of deep space and old forgotten gods visually represented in high graphics. Now if you've never read a single one of these short stories then literally none of this will make any sense. It's a walking sim with extremely simple puzzles. I suppose if you like strange indescribable creatures you might also still get a kick out of this. The only two cons in my opinion is that the voice acting is abysmal by anyone other than the main character and its incredibly short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Plays more like a walking simulator which is fine but the direction of the game is confusing and at times easy to miss but my main gripe is the combat, which became very frustrating especially combined with the lack of direction. It's hard for me to quit a game but this one did. I wish I could refund it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not horrible, but it is not worth $25. It looks pretty great and has great atmosphere. The beginning is the best part. The last half is just walking a mostly linear path and constantly seeing monsters to the point they get kind of boring. I got it on sale for $11.74, which I think is a better price. This game will take you around 3 hours max to beat, maybe a little longer if you replay part of it to get 100% achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere but the writing and gameplay was awful. It was more of a bad Hollywood film than an adaptation of Lovecraft. The chase sequences, invisible walls and puzzles were just annoying. Not fun.After thinking for a few days, I have changed my review to recommend this game. Apart from all it's problems, it is a very memorable experience. I wish it was more just set-pieces with narration from the books as that was the strong point of this game. Watching these giant beings in the sea is amazing. I do have a fascination with large objects in the sea and sky so this is definitely my bias coming through.Overall, it would have been much better as a "walking simulator", for lack of a better term.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend not buying this game.I repeat: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!It's pure trash and much too expenseive for like 3 hours of "gameplay" aka. walking around with extremely limited objects to even interact with. The absolute worst about this game are the areas where monsters hunt you. Since there is no map in this game and you almost can't even go along a wrong path, whenever monsters are hunting you there are wrong paths and you will run these wrong paths, because these sections are just trial and error, which is extremely frustrating. The character can't even run properly, so you just walk away from monsters like you go walking in a peaceful forest and try to enjoy nature.I beat the game in like 3 hours (while around 45 minutes came from starting over and over again after being killed be the monsters).I can just repeat: DO NOT BUY THIS CRAP!You can burn your 20 Euro and will still have more fun than playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Short and beautiful.It's a good step above being a walking simulator, there are puzzles and interactions with the game world, but otherwise a fairly simple game. Sometimes it can be annoyingly obtuse with what it expects you to do. Unfortunately it's a bit trial and error-heavy; chase scenes where you need to learn the map and puzzles that have no real clues.Environments are great looking as a whole, though the level design can be a bit wonky. Your most common obstacle are waist-high rocks you should be able to climb over and there's at least one early moment where you have to traverse something you won't think you're able to.It's a little fanservice-y for a fan of the Cthulhu Mythos, but at the same time there are some strange things even I can't recognize. You do something early on that's just haunting and unpleasant to look at while you continue to exploring the island. You do get to see some all-stars of the Mythos but the game doesn't treat them as bosses to beat, you're an ant they're prodding and poking for goals you don't understand.Get it if you're a Lovecraft fan, it's worth a play through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved every second playing! The story was enjoyable and I really hope more will be added as It does feel rather short for the price.. Atmosphere with simple but great puzzles made it really fun to play and the graphics are nice! figuring out what the next step was maybe involved dying once until I figured it the way but overall really enjoyed the game.. I am a fan and cannot wait for more updates and hopefully a longer story.  Great music and voice acting could be better but overall fun to play!8/10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is gloomy. The sounds are eerie. The art is absolutely stunning. Mind that I called it art, not graphics. And that's why. Landscapes are amazing. Details in everything are incredible. Animations are, well, embarassing. You see the walking monolith in the trailer? Isn't it embarassing? Yes, it is. I also caught a glimpse of a tentacled thing behind a rock, I tried to see what it was despite being scared, but it was gone as I tried to get close, all I can say it was a ridicuolus shiny green color. I shudder at the thought of action sequences, but the setting got me hooked.Another thing I loathe: railroad movment. You know, being confined by rocks so amazingly tall and steep that a three legged turtle could easily climb them but you can't.Edit. My judgement was positive until now. But then I met a Deep one chewing a whale's tail. There's no way to evade it (the surrounding rocks are almost a foot tall, totally unsurmountable), no way to go back. The whale is a pin cushion of harpoons but sure as Hell nobody would think about taking one to defend against the nasty looking critter who is about to attack. There's a limit to my tolerance of not-being-able-to-do-anything. I'm sure there are a couple of pixels somewhere that I should notice to solve the puzzle, but I don't care anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: As of 27/02/2021 this game has "mixed" reviews with 51% and it definitely doesn't deserve this at all! Especially if you think about how tiny the dev. team is. I think a slight price reduction would be a benefit.POSITIVE:++ amazing visuals+ great optimization after first patch++ eerie yet beautiful soundtrack++ stunning monster design+++ wonderful atmosphereCons:- invisible walls- sometimes unclear what to do next- sometimes walking speed is annoyingly slowoverall I rate this little gem with a 7.5 out of 10! If you consider the great effort by and for such a small team, I'd even rate it with a 8/10!The developer is already listening to the player base and improving and tweaking things pretty fast! So I am confident, that we will soon see a "positive" review rate! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Has a lot of nice scenery to chew on, feels a little unfinished at times but only ended up with a bug that forced me to reload like twice. All in all it was pretty short but I got it cheap so there wasn't much to complain about. Has a Lovecraftian vibe but not a ton of substance. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: If your looking for an exploration walking sim with an interesting and creepy atmosphere, then do not buy this game. The negative reviews are accurate. The first part of the game is excellent, the second is unbearable. The change in gameplay is complete disjointed and frustrating. I bought this on sale and it still feels like I wasted my money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I am an absolute fan of Lovecraft and I find this game to really satisfy that niche I have.PROS:The graphics and aesthetics are amazing for a one-man creatorMany references are made to Lovecraft's original stories Sound and soundtrack quality is top notchThe encounters with enemy AI meets standardsCONS:It will be boring if you expect fast-pace game play and constant battleIf you do not know Lovecraft stories, you will not understand anything.There are certain bugs in game but they are not too terrible and hopefully will be corrected.My final rate 8/10, I give huge props to this one man creator for this pleasing game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Confusion and deduction simulator proved to be working fine.In order to explain this game I will resort to the following: Think of drinking a beverage made up of whale oil, squeezed bull testi mixed up with powdered rabbit toes and then just going to an island and walking around for like hmm four hours. Well same feeling here. Trust me, you should give it a try (even if you hate bulls)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game pleasantly surprised me. From how good it looked and sounded to even what kind of gameplay it expected out of you, nothing was what it seemed... and yet that is somehow fitting for a game of the mythos. Honestly if you like horror games in first person and enjoy the build up as much as the intensity of the payoff, you should absolutely give this one a shot! And if you have a taste for Lovecraft in particular, welcome... make yourself at home.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The cosmic horror/lovecraftian genre doesn't have enough content so im always curious about games like this. This is a fun 2-3 hour game to play through. Most of the puzzles are pretty easy and the game is very atmospheric. It does feel a bit limited by the engine the game is in (it can be a little  hard to determine what you have to interact with and what you dont) and occasionally their is a bit to much dialog from things that should be more unknowable rather than talkative but the ending is exactly in line with the genre so overall id def recommend it to anyone interested in cosmic horror.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't just another horror sci-fi game. Oh no, that would be a grossly understatement.This is a story, a movie, a journey into Lovecraft's work and legacy.Game-play wise there is not much you can do, it has some interesting mechanics and some puzzle solving but not much in that regard.The world is limited to what the dev wanted us to see/explore, only.Graphics wise this game is fairly good, you might encounter some "clipping" but thats because the hit box of the models are what they are.My only regret is that I watched the walk-through videos before playing the game and many of the jump scares lost effect on me. Don't do the same mistake as i did.Will gladly pay for part 2. :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece. From the dramatic and fear inducing music and audio to the stunning graphics, I loved every second of it. I definitely thought this game was going to be a bit longer but I definitely was not expecting that ending. Only con was the story got a bit lost on me at some points but that's probably just because I haven't read enough Lovecraft to catch the small details.8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral rating for games, but I guess I can tentatively recommend this for the right sort of person.  If you really like H.P. Lovecraft, this game does one thing very well, and that is capture the visuals and tone of his works.The plot is a bit on the confusing side and never really made much sense to me, but the journey itself is beautifully grotesque.The biggest negative is the combat.  I think this game would have been better designed like an old school game like Shadowgate where death comes from touching the wrong thing or making bad decisions in general rather than the first person shooter thing they did with this.  It doesn't really ruin the game, but if I could remove everything that involved shooting at monsters, I would enjoy it more.Also, the asking price is such that this is a game which I'd pick up while it is on sale.  It only took me about 3 hours to complete, and I got stuck at a couple points.  It is also not a game which has a lot of replay value.  Sure, it would be fun to go through it again later on, but it will only have that surprise and mystery once.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an big fan of the Lovecraft universe and mostly seek out games that is bringing homage to the lore.I'm also an big fan of these type of first person photo realistic horror story telling games and just immerse myself fully when playing them.In an age where AAA titles are 80% trash and overpriced incomplete garbage indie games/developers makes up for it.We need to support indie developers more and let AAA companies rot in hell with their unfinished and bug filled games.Enjoyed everything The Shore had to offer and leaves me wanting more.Game is visually stunning and beautiful and the story is gripping... is he awake?The animations of the larger set pieces was done perfectly and I could not keep myself from staring at what is happening right in front of my eyes.Cannot wait to see what this developer comes up with next!10/10Recommend to any Lovecraft fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: let me start off by saying i feel like the shore has a lot of potential. but the game is just overwhelmingly average in its current state.a lot of the spoken lines are really difficult to understand. i relied heavily on subtitles for any of the non-human characters, as the effects and overlays on their voices make it incredibly difficult to understand them. that, and some of the effects just felt a bit cheesy and like the stereotypical "big bad guy".the game also lacks a sense of direction. theres a story there, sure, but its a bit barebones and a lot of stuff doesnt feel like it makes sense in the story, given the very little context behind anything. however, i feel like one of the major faults of the game is just how little things are explained. theres a lot of walking and running around, trying to find objectives. other than walls of rock or flesh(?) blocking your path, theres really no indicators of where your next objective is. to me, i got confused pretty quickly. in each of the areas, the textures and areas all look the same. by the lighthouse, the rocks and paths looks pretty similar. later in the game, there are literally no landmarks to guide you, so you kinda just run through a maze-like area while some monster chases you until you either die or find your objective.theres also quite a few puzzles/interactables. there is literally nothing indicating what youre supposed to do with these. youve just gotta look around until the little eye/interaction icon pops up, and use context clues (or button mashing) to figure out what you have to do. theres even a room full of heads, with only one head being the actual "key" to the puzzle. i frequently found myself referencing a guide because its really not explained how to do anything.overall, i think the game could go somewhere. but in its current state, its maybe a few hours of really confusing gameplay with a less than satisfactory experience and ending. a lot of other reviews call this a walking simulator, and i have to agree.

_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Screw all the negative reviews. Atmospherically this is the BEST Lovecraft game I have EVER played! Several very H.R. Giger-esque areas as well. People who dislike it misunderstood what this was supposed to be.Game Play:So yes, it is a walking sim with minor chase/combat sequences. That said people ragging on the combat fail to realize it isn't supposed to be great. Lovecraftian cosmic horror isn't supposed to be Halo, in all of his literature it's supposed to feel horrific and hopeless going against the strange and horrific beings from beyond. So it not being fair for you to fend for yourself in some areas & having to get out by the skin of your teeth is built into the formula of some sections. You get a tool later on that helps you "defend" against them while you escape, but it is hardly meant as an offensive weapon, more a path clearing / slow down tool while you gtfo of there. If you were trying to play for combat you played the game wrong.Atmosphere & Visuals: For one dev this is beyond uncanny. There were 1-2 spots where textures left a bit to be desired (boats on the shore in some areas).... but that hardly mattered with how many things were done right, from the occult talismans & coins specially crafted in true Lovecraft fashion to all the strange monoliths & altars.... later on like introducing Giger elements as you are in more cosmic areas. It is WONDERFUL. 10000/10Sound:The atmosphere & soundtrack fit amazingly & when facing the creatures the "squelch & wriggle" sounds had the perfect amount of disgusting and tense. Loved this games sound. The voiceover work was good. I'm not a sound engineer but I'd prefer some effects that were more in line with "Dear Esther" to have the voice sound more "in-game" but it wasnt far off & was an easy adjustment to get used to.Story:Many people here are pissed about the ???? ending for the dude looking for his daughter. Sorry bro, but that wasn't the story, that was a plot device to allow you to explore & gather the real story through the things left around the world unfold the lore & whats going on through the narrator. If you didnt explore & rushed through the game then it's no wonder you didnt enjoy yourself. Why are you playing atmospheric walking sims anyway? That is how they all work.Tone: Is it scary? .... no. Eerie, gross, awesome, yes. This game was never going for "scary" it's going for the melancholic feeling of curiosity, being lost, & impending hopelessness, and on that it nails it. The tone of trying to piece together what is going on while learning about the area youre in and what has happened there lead you to feel an ever growing sense of dread & futility. This game perfectly accomplished what it set out to do, other people just missed the message because they were too focused on looking for their preconceived expectations vs experiencing the game. I'm now going to follow this dev & buy anything Lovecraftian they put out. To the DEV: PLEASE KEEP GOING. THIS WAS AMAZING!!!! THANK YOU FOR A GAME TRUE LOVECRAFT FANS NEEDED!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an okay and interesting lovecraftian horror game, so this is the part where I talk about the story, but it's one of those games where talking about the story will spoil everything, so I'll just say this is about a man looking for his daughter.Well then the likes, the story was okay it can be a little bit confusing at times, but it is based on lovecraft's work and sometimes his work could be a bit confusing. The references to Lovecraft were very good from the Cthulhu to nyarlathotep, to the color out of space. We even get a nice reference to the Lovecraft movie The Lighthouse.The graphics are very good with a very nice use of colors, especially vibrant colors as we get to see more alien worlds. The levels are very good each one with its own unique look and feel that invokes Lovecraft with its grotesque alien worlds.The gameplay was okay, it was pretty simple as you explore around and don’t get killed by monsters, there's even some combat which was okay, nothing too complex. The monster designs were all really good each one definitely captured the feel of lovecraft's work with their own unique design I especially loved Cthulhu and Dagon designs, they both looked so badass and cool looking.The voice acting is okay, honestly I've heard better voice acting in other indie games, but this one was serviceable. The music was nice and definitely fit Lovecraft’s epicness of his work very well. The puzzles were okay, although they could be very vague sometimes. The atmosphere despite being Lovecraft it is actually kind of relaxing which I didn't mind. Now is this game scary since it's a horror game, not really it's more grotesque and disturbing than actually scary.Well then the dislikes, the game can be pretty frustrating at times of how vague it is, I'm not saying the game should hold your hand, but it could be too vague a lot of times as you’re wandering around not knowing what to do. Sometimes the game can be kind of cheap, like this one puzzle where if you're not careful you can be killed by a Shoggoth which got really annoying really quickly. The story can be slightly confusing and it does end on a cliffhanger, but I heard there's going to be a sequel someday so it's not too bad.Now then with that done The Shore is an okay and interesting lovecraftian horror game, with an okay story, very good references to lovecraft and really good monster designs. So do I recommend this game, if you read lovecraft's work and you are  looking for an okay Lovecraft game to play this one might be up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: the story for this game is great. but the world is incredibly frustrating. the invisible walls at every turn make it very time consuming to progress, and not in a lore filled "this is interesting, i want to explore" kind of way but in the "oh this looks like a path, nope, another damn invisible wall" kind if way
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A short but well done horror game that goes more for the "Make you feel uneasy" feeling. The amount of times I just felt like something was watching me was crazy. But overall it was well made if not a little confusing with the story. For $12 though it is definitely worth it.Time it too me to beat was 2.3 hours and from what I am reading in other reviews it is about that length for most.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game's strength lie in its artwork. The island is quite bland to begin with but as you delve deeper into the cosmic realm you get to see some amazing and repulsive sights. A great deal of attention has gone into many of the sculptures of Cthulu mythos gods that appear as items in this game. They are beautiful to look at and I actually would probably buy one of those sculptures if it existed in the real world. The game music and sounds, especially later on in the game really fit with the atmosphere of the game.However, the game is short. I played it in 3 hours. This isn't necessary a bad thing if you go into the game considering it a piece of art. It might also be better playing this in VR if that becomes possible. One thing that really rubbed me the wrong way with this game and caused me great frustration were the invisible walls. I understand that this type of game has to limit my movements in the game but they could have been handled with a bit less abruptness. There were also quite a few glitches. Floating stones, spelling mistakes and at one point I even had to restart the game from the save point because a bug stopped me progressing.Overall, if you want a game that assaults your visionary senses, a thin plot, has you run from enemies to get to the next puzzle, but will still show you some sights you've not seen in a game before, you might want to try this one. The fact that it was done by one person or a small group of people, at least, made me want to buy this game. I think this game could have been so much more though. It feels like a patchwork of scenes that don't quite fit together but it was an interesting ride.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: What a God awful abomination of a game. Not in a good Lovecraftian scary sense, no. it's rather stupid, full of bugs and barely working, I lost my whole progress because apparently you can't close the menu in-game other than leaving to main menu and there is no way to load a save game. Since, we'll who would want that...
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a great game for Lovecraft's fans. It has one of the most incredible environments I've seen in a Cthulhu-themed game. The start of the game is incredible, it completely draws you into the mystery of that secret island.But halfway through it changes from exploring the island to teleporting between one area to the another, using an artifact to solve puzzles. It's not bad, but it's a bit repetitive: use the artifact against something; that something rotates and becomes activated. Do it again, and again and again. And the teleporting is a bit too much imo.I prefer the first part of the game, and I think it would be best if the game would have stuck to that formula, but still, it's a great game that is definitely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the puzzles could be a little more clear, and some of the items could stand out a bit more.  Aside from that, my complaints are few.  The game world itself looks amazing, there's a constant sense of dread atmosphere wise, and despite being a walking sim of sorts it manages to not be too slow.  Graphically the game is impressive.  The Shore looks great from the environment to the various creatures you'll run into.  There were many times I felt like stopping to look at things.  I do wish that you weren't running away from creatures in the coolest areas of the game, as I'd of liked more time to observe everything.Overall if you're looking for a adventure game that's linear, fairly short, and looks great - this is a good pick.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple: I loved this game! If you like Lovecraft and his universe of unspeakable horros, this game will push all the right buttons for you. Atmosphere and graphics are great, it has voice acting (which can be a bit funny because of the russian accent, but that's just the way the person speaks, and it's only a handful of people who did this game, so cut them some slack!) and there is no part which feels like dragging on or which is unneccessary.I can understand the reviews that give a thumbs down because of the price, because 20$ for 3 hours of gameplay (1 or 2 more if you get all achievements) can feel pretty unbalanced. All I can say is: If you can spare the money and want to have great 4 hours, get this game! If not, wait for a Sale at some point and get it for cheaper.But it is a project from a handfull of people, and I can't imagine the effort and time they took to create this game. And I think there are worse ways out there to spend 20$.The FPS drops and technical issues that people complain about are mostly fixed as far as I can tell. I played the whole game yesterday (2nd of march 2021) and didn't run into any problems while playing it, and I saw in the forums that the devs work on patches and fixes constantly to improve the experience, which already helped a lot.So yeah, I had a ton of fun, the graphics are great and the enemy design is top notch. Puzzles are mostly pretty basic and easy, and battle mechanics are just "press button to shoot laser at enemy", but the fighting isn't the focus here and therefore the majority of battles are over quickly, so it doesn't bother too much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a walking simulator where you're kind of locked into literal walking until the 2 hour mark where sprinting is randomly unlocked. There is "running" before, but it's barely faster than walking and is more akin to a powerwalkYou start off confined to a very small area, but you're going back and forth trying to figure out what to do and it seems like there's more going on due to how long it takes you to walk back and forthThe atmosphere is hit or miss. Lovecraft stuff is cool, but sometimes it's just not landing well. Some parts are really well made visually, but then they give you absolutely no time to look around and take it in. This game seems like they wanted to have puzzles, but all you're really doing is picking up objects and then using them in specific locations and you don't even get to guess which items are used where. You just automatically use the thing you need so there's no real "puzzle" there. The closest I saw to an actual puzzle was rotating some blocks so the mural lined up and I wouldn't really call that a puzzle even by the most lenient of standards.There is "combat", but it's horrible. You can punch if grabbed(strangely not unlocked when first encountering enemies), but it's quickly swapped out for a kind of laserbeam that has a range of like 5 feet and it's very underwhelming. There's no real depth to the combat and it boils down to "hold attack button down until enemy dies" and it even stunlocks them so there's no real danger. At that point, you might as well just take the combat mechanic awayI put in about 2.5 hours in and I was taking my time and trying to absorb the scenery, but I get the feeling I'm more than half-way through alreadyAs others said, there are definite graphical issues. Numerous small floating rocks and even some missing textures here and there. Nothing too bad, but it is noticeable. I'm not a huge graphics guy who will nitpick tiny little things, but if you're gonna go all out and try to make it realistic looking, I feel you can't really skimp outThe script and writing are pretty bad. You'll find notes that are written like "he's.....he's gone" when nobody ever writes like that unless they are quoting someone who verbally spoke those lines, but that will literally be written on paper. Nobody writes like that. The MC will literally say things like "there's no way that was my daughter" when talking to himself, which seems odd as nobody would talk like that to themselves, even in inner monologue. There are also spelling and grammatical errors here and there, but not too much to the point I'd say it's a major problem, but still noteworthy. The voice actor is also not greatA noteworthy problem is the initial beach design. There are an assload of invisible walls and barriers preventing you from accessing certain areas, but logically, there's nothing really stopping you. There are rocks all over the beach, but most of them are rocks you'd casually step on and climb around on with ease. I'm not even talking like you'd even need your hands to get up them. I'm talking rocks you'd barely have to fully raise your leg to get on top of....and the game puts invisible walls all around them so you're stuck on winding paths. If you're going to try to make people stay on paths, make the rocks taller and not something you'd easily be able to climb on
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.  It's not what I hoped, though.  I hoped for some adventure game with multiple endings and branching stories with hard choices to be made in dialogue, siding with this person or faction vs the other.Instead, I got a walking simulator with plenty of H.P. Lovecraft references in it.  A nice little game.  The devs really tried to keep the mystique and not overplay the grotesque too early.  Some puzzles were actually clever.However, I also join other in criticizing the running segments.  The 'obstacles' are too aggressive and fast.  Slow them down so there's no RNG deaths and this is a nice, humble little story to be told.2.7 hours to finish the base game.  Another 0.7 hours to start a second playthrough to collect the missing collectibles for 100% completion.  I got this on sale for $12 and I'm happy with it.  I do not recommend the full price of $25 as it's not polished enough and just a tiny bit light on content for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for around 2 dollars because of a sale. But I really enjoyed the experience this game gave me. I am not into Lovecraft, nor know anything about it. So threw out the game I was a bit confused, but that didn't really change my experience. This game is not really scary, more unnerving or unsettling. Complements to the music composer for this game. The music is the main factor in most scares and unnerving scenes. If I had a main complaint it would be that some of the levels are poorly designed. It looks amazing but most of the time I get confused on where to go or think I can go somewhere just for the game to block it off from me.  I recommend this game to horror fans, Lovecraft fans, and monster fans. But keep in mind I got this game cheap, and it took me roughly 2 hours to fully complete. Do with that information as you must.

_childDocuments_.review: "You, Andrew, you're my favorite."Oh, Andrew. However, while I feel for him and his journey, I won't lie: it's brilliant. This game manages to nail the ambient and unknown dread and awe that comes with Lovecraftian works. While short, this game was thoroughly enjoyable and I highly recommend it to anyone even slightly interested in cosmic horror. The journey you take brings with it interesting and jaw-dropping sights and curiosities. While this game was clearly crafted with passion, there are a few minor bumps in the road such as grammatical errors or object collision, but these are easily ignored in favor of the overall game. Really, my only complaint was the combat. It felt kind of tacked on as a way to avoid the game being solely a walking simulator, but it wasn't the worst, just a bit boring after a while. However, I'm sure this was improved upon in other releases. Besides, the unique and interesting enemy variety and monster designs more than make up for it. This game deserves nothing less than a strong 9/10.Ares Dragonis, I look forward to more from you! Now onto Eresys..
