_childDocuments_.review: Autumn is a season of upheaval, so the Old Gods grow ever restless. They will not fade into obscurity just like the controversial author of our current source material has found his own little patch of fame and infamy. I’m talking about Howard Phillips Lovecraft and it’s almost ironic how he died penniless and with a firm conviction that he amounted to a complete failure, only to emerge post-mortem as one of the most influential fiction writers of the 20th Century. Just like our buddy Franz Kafka from my previous review, Lovecraft would also inadvertently create his own literary and stylistic subgenre which has been “bleeding” quite profusely into gaming as well. The Shore marks Ares Dragonis’ Steam debut, case in point that you don’t need to have previous titles under your belt in order to leave a positive impression. Originality still shines within an abyss of reboots, remakes and remasters!Not going to dwell a lot on the narrative since its initial ambiguity holds few secrets: main character is a fisherman called Andrew and he’s searching for his missing daughter along the shorelines of what appears to be volcanic island, judging by the pitch black terrain. A deserted lighthouse and numerous shipwrecks confirm that the place is deserted, yet you’re not alone. Like a slow descent into madness, things and thoughts change their shapes the more you push on seeking answers and closure. What starts as a seemingly benign walking simulator, eventually shifts towards survival horror with a few puzzle sections thrown in for good measure. The pacing is on point, you feel compelled to explore since The Shore does an excellent job at offering the needed incentives in the form of Lovecraft references and collectibles scattered off the beaten paths. Linearity is less of an issue if you provided the necessary illusions of alternative choices. It helps that the developer made full use of the source material mythos. From Outer Gods, to Deep Ones and of course infamous Great Old Ones such as Cthulhu himself. Once you start questioning the perceived reality, you know you’ve gone too far to turn back. All roads will lead towards a rather ambiguous conclusion that leaves plenty of room for a sequel or interpretation at the very least. The Shore is powered by the Unreal Engine 4 in a very stable manner, leaving me no cause for complaint. I applaud the decision to remove any potential HUD elements, they would have only eroded the experience since I firmly believe adventure titles of any subgenre are best played without keyboard prompts or hand holding tips. You’re left to your own device from a clean first person perspective. Whether you choose to take screenshots along your journey or not, you’ve been provided with plenty of opportunities in the form of eye-catching scenery, events and creatures. It goes without saying that the environment gets increasingly surreal as the story progresses. Just as expected. The sound department also received the necessary attention in the form of skilled voice acting for the narrator in equal measure to certain side characters. Soundtrack was spot on as well, never becoming repetitive or feeling out of touch with the scenes playing out before you. Almost relaxing at key points through the story but that's the literal calm before the storm, so stay alert.While I wouldn’t consider it a lengthy experience (you can probably finish it in under 4 hours if you’re not keen on exploration like I was), The Shore is cleverly structured in a manner that won’t allow boredom to set it. Exploration and peaceful collectible hunting is briskly interrupted by a totally different hunt in the form of chase sequences. Running for your life can only get you so far however. You will eventually gain the ability to fight back, Andrew’s own resilience growns as strong as his capabilities in time and the autosave implementation ensures that failure in combat isn’t unforgiving.I will advise that you constantly check the inventory for new clues as well as gaining further insight into the intricacies of the Lovecraft mythos. There will be numerous objects to pick up and study in detail, from abstract sculptures to seemingly incoherent texts. Expect some puzzle sections which will require a modicum of effort, but they’re not going to strain you too much. It’s a well balanced challenge in the end, the game never felt frustratingly hard while I definitely didn’t expect a cake walk either. Come to think of it, walking sims certainly evolved a lot since the initial days of a little Half-Life 2 mod called “Dear Esther”.If you’re itching to get those lovecraftian desires finally sated, look no further than The Shore. It’s the closest you’ll get to a Cthulhu love letter in 2021 minus hitting the rock bottom of controversies like a certain sinking city on Steam. It’s more than decently priced for what it offers and I can say for a fact that the title has been nurtured by its dev team constantly with updates both fixing any bugs and enhacing the gameplay with a handful of previously inaccessible areas and more Steam Achievements than it had on its release date. + Steam Achievements.+ Beautiful visuals and game design.+ Diversified gameplay encouraging exploration.- Quite short and with little replay value.- No Steam Trading Cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehh, I love most things associated with Lovecraft, but I can't stand run & hide mechanics in games. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, I’d like to address the big Lovecraftian elephant with tentacles in the room. This game was developed by 2 people with 2 months-salary funding. At least according to the crowdfunding campaign that I participated in. That said, I would probably review this game differently if it was made by KONAMI.I thought that this will be a game focusing on the story aspect and didn’t expect rich game mechanics or deep systems and apparently, that was the case. The visual style was one of the main selling points as well and for me, that was the most consistent aspect from start to finish. When it comes to the story though, there is a bit of a paradox happening here. In most games of this category, I expect the story and the visuals to go hand in hand and enhance each other. Here I felt that the story was mostly an excuse to have cool stuff show on the screen but not much more than that. It felt like a competent 3D artist made those cool 3D models and was dying to place them on a game, so he created a story that can fit all of the things that he wants to fit. The visual part is great, but all the Gods feel more like references than meaningful parts of the story. So, the paradox I mentioned above is that the great visuals make the story feel like an afterthought instead of offering more depth. Even so, the love for Lovecraft’s work is quite clear and there is a lot of detail and passion put into this project. The game offers some unique visuals and it really gives the feeling that you are experiencing a horrible nightmare that won’t end.The gameplay aspect is quite basic but as I said, not far away from what I expected. I could do with fewer monster chase sequences though. Unfortunately, I think those parts don’t add to the experience but more of the opposite since the game’s controls are not optimized for satisfying fighting. If it happened only a couple of times it would come as a surprise and it would have worked a lot better for me. Oh, and I have to mention that I had a huge problem interacting with things. There were parts of the game where I got stuck for 5 minutes because I couldn’t get the prompt to interact with something even though I was straight up facing it. I mostly played on a controller, so I don’t know if that made things worse.The levels look really nice visually and the claustrophobic atmosphere works really well later in the game. The problem for me was the shore part. The level looks quite open but there are a million invisible walls that make movement very restricting and sometimes frustrating. To my understanding, this was done so players have to visit the lighthouse before they gain access to other parts of the map and then linearly move from place A to place B and so on. I think this could have been avoided very easily and allow the players to traverse the map more freely.Last but not least, the game is quite overpriced for something that lasts 2-4 hours. I think lowering the price will help the devs in the long run.In conclusion, don’t play this game expecting to get the same experience as Resident Evil or Silent Hill. Dear Ester or the Vanishing of Ethan Carter is a lot closer. If you liked those games there is a high chance you’ll like this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get irritated by the many 'not recommended' reviews. I was mostly worried about the length of the game, but to me length and scope of the game was sufficent. Yeah, it's a rather short game, but it's okay.You can play it through in under 2 hours for sure, if you want to, but I have taken a lot of time to explore the game. Unfortunately you are quite narrowed down to relatively small accessable areas with (too) many invisible walls, but all in all there was quite a bit of content.I liked the rough sea atmosphere and that the story was told via several documents and letters which are spreaded all over the shore etc. I hoped that all those information pieces would in the end puzzle together to a whole story picture, what they unfortunately did not. This is a story-driven game and the potential is great and it is well done in the beginning. But during the second half of the game the story gets lost a bit and the focus is more on horror elements and spectacular monsters. Those are very nice, but story should be most important!Otherwise I really liked to play it. Very good voice acting and graphics are overall pretty good (except of constant graphics glitches in the water or occasional blurry rock textures and not so dense vegetation). Battles were not very tricky or demanding, but those action scenes were a must for me to make more out of the game than only being a walking simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a "horror" game with a lot of "jump scares"... or a "horror" game with a lot of "action" in it... then this isn't a game for you. However... I don't think you're here because that's what you're looking for. I think you came here for the same reason I did... you're a fan of H.P. Lovecraft. If that's the case... then you're in the right place. This is a nicely done lore based game... where you can read up on the Old Gods from Lovecrafts mythos... and actually see a few of them in all their glory. It took me about three and a half hours roughly to get through the game... and I wasn't disappointed at any point in the experience. There are a few puzzles you can complete... and there's some fighting... but this game is a heavily story driven walking simulator. I wouldn't recommend this for fans of the "action horror" or "survival horror" genres... but fans of Lovecraft and most of the psychological horror community might find something interesting here (especially if you get the VR version of this game instead of the standard version).

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game!  Yes, the beginning part on the island was a bit Alice in Wonderland feeling where you are dropped into this world and have no idea what you are doing, but once you get past that initial part, what a trip! _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts as a fairly linear experience building tension through familiar images of a shore and lighthouse, but with anomalies scattered about to show you are far from any place welcoming. It's eerie, has a great grasp on immensity, looks beautiful despite some graphical glitches, and really compels you go further into the lingering madness.Then the rest of the game happens. Once I got a glorified gun and had to run from monsters while shooting them, I wondered why this needed to be included. The environments become too samey and enemies are not disturbing to me, merely annoying. Horrific creatures from a completely alien place shouldn't be annoying, they should be intimidating. Also your daughter is missing. I forgot about that. In fact, I think the player character does too unless reminded. Then the puzzles become trial and error. Sometimes you're accidentally hitting the wrong thing or you're not noticing that an item goes onto a very particular place. It slows things down too much when five minutes ago you were running and gunning. You have to ease into different mechanics so the game is cohesive and engaging. And while interpreting the ending a certain way may explain why the Great Old Ones are so personable to you, I really disliked how the player character was relied upon too much to help these gods. I think witnessing a distant force far more powerful than yourself is naturally demoralizing. Being old chums with one is less world-defying. Despite these things, I still loved the beginning of the game. I mean, I liked it enough that I got all the achievements to experience more lore. The game after the island and underwater section is simply too phoned in and hurried. New room, outrun enemy, new room, solve puzzle, new room, outrun enemy, etc. The game looks excellent when it's not just black tentacle, fleshy room stuff, but it doesn't make the gameplay any better. I'm on the fence about it, honestly. But since these reviews are black and white with no grey, I'd say recommended while on sale. This game does well, but it seems like the developer wanted to put too much into their first game and it became cluttered. If you read this, Ares Dragonis, subtlety, simplicity, and brevity can be very powerful when used right. I look forward to your next game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

Voice acting is insanely bad, story is just funny, game sometimes simply does not work at all (Sprint doesn't work and you have to just try again and again until game decides to work), however very solid performance and insanely beautiful Lovecraftian visuals. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best lovecraftian games I've played. In fact, The Shore is more an experience than a game, focussing on "walking" through the story with some minor action sequences (escape, shooting). But if you let yourself drag into the beautiful graphics and the outstanding, surreal atmosphere - including soundscape! -, The Shore's experience is incredibly intense. Definitely a must-buy for Horror-fans willing to experience more than the ordinary!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I am such a sucker for all things related to lovecraft's stories, but there is so much disappointment in so many of those purchases. Seeing that author's name has become synonymous with half-hearted efforts and half-baked ideas. Maybe there is something about creators not having complete autonomy in the creative process of the story. For whatever reason, the shore has a rough story, no intuitive signposting for player movement, annoyingly vague puzzles (such as putting a figurine in a chess board, doors unlocked by seemingly random keys, and bad monster chase scenes), and a lack of interesting level design. I also had technical problems with the video cutscenes not displaying correctly. (The videos show okay when run from the local file directory.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: If you're in the mood for a short but well made lovecraftian horror game I'd definitely give this a recommendation. It's assets and design are really well made alongside a strong opening atmosphere at the start of the game. There are certain parts of the Shore that are a little rough around the edges since the puzzles aren't all that challenging and there are a few occasions where the game goes a bit too fast but these were easy to overlook by the end of the game. Would definitely recommend to a lovecraft or horror fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: As intersting as this game looked on paper, unfortunately after playing it cannot help but feeling underwhelmed.The overall concept behind this adventure is neat enough, and there are interesting design choices. The island itself has this ominous and timeless atmosphere, and the feeling of loneliness is heavy... however, we dont' really get to explore much of the island itself, despite it seeming it rather big! Now that would not be a problem if the landscape looked more... unfriendly? instead, if you stray from the intended path, you'll simply run into an invisible wall, preventing you from wandering too far. It breaks the immersion and feels like a waste. Why not put some physical barriers instead? Chasms, thick bushes, rocky spikes, and the likes.The second part of the game, once you acquire the artifact, feels... rushed? You solve a puzzle, hear some otherwordly sound, and then just fade-to-black to some other place. This happens several times and transition once again is very immersion breaking: instead of getting the wormhole-like sequence we get sometimes, we are instead treated with a transition with black spots filling up the screen. Why not choose a less artificial transition?The Lovecraft mythos also is implemented a bit superficially. Names get thrown here and there, but the things that do happen feel rather inconsequential. It's... not clear why you do the things you do, or how the puzzles relate to the things that happen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The artistry, the sound design and the atmosphere are amazing. Yes, it´s short, the mechanics are a bit wonky, the landscape is very restrictive and the puzzles could be more challenging. I still think the creator captured the essence of cosmic horror very well. It was really nice to see some of the entities from the stories. If you are a hardcore H.P Lovecraft fan, you really should give it a try.However, maybe wait for a discount. it´s just too short for that price right now and it feels somehow unpolished.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. Get it on sale, maybe. I've never played a game that isn't actually on a rail, that feels so much like it's on a rail. It's super linear and nothing is particularly challenging, BUT having said that, it's got a nice atmosphere and the setting looks pretty good. Also if you're a chievo hunter, I only missed 3 just doing a pretty straightforward playthrough, and those would have been REALLY easy by the looks.

_childDocuments_.review: 1-3 hours of gameplay (deppends on if you will be like me exploring every single stone on beach, or just go for the end).There are 2 stories, one of the main protagonist and second on papers you may or may not collect, nothing special.What this game excels at are visuals, both sound and graphics are really great... except few things, like leaves and stuff at the beach which are all same and I don't really like the way Cthulhu himself looks, I'd say the game would be a little better without him.Atmosphere is actually one of best I found in games, at some points it actually felt pretty sureal and getting you feel like you are really getting insane... until it breaks with transition.On the oposite side, I discovered several bugs and combat was pretty awfull, mainly the part with hands which felt almost like playing meatboy by the necesity dogding everything.Overall if you want the real feeling you'd expect from Cthulhu world, this game will (most probably) give it to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I played The Shore on stream a few days ago and I genuinely really enjoyed it! I've only played 2 lovecraftian horror games (including this one) and this one by far topped the other game I played. Loved the creature/enemy designs as well! Cthulhu kinda thicc tbh. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great exploration/action lovecraftian game. I loved it. It's very unnerving, which is something I almost never feel while playing games. It really kept me feeling tense, masterfully displaying what makes Lovecraft's stories so great: the atmosphere. You really feel the cosmic horror in this one. And the art... It's just amazing. It starts out pretty standard (for the first few minutes, I felt like I was back at Dear Esther, an exploration game I actually didn't like at all), but it doesn't take long for it to take you out of your comfort zone with some pretty bizarre happenings. From there, it spirals down into total madness; I'd rather not spoil it by describing anything, I'll just say, it pleasantly surprised me. I definitely wasn't expecting what I got from this. The sound design was also (mostly) fantastic. This is definitely a game to play with headphones (I realized it in the first few minutes and went to get mine). Now, for the not-so-great stuff: it's definitely quite unpolished. The indie feel is strong with this one, and you will definitely find a few visual glitches here and there; feel annoyed by the walking speed on some occasions; get weirded out by some bad voice-acting (not the main character though, he was great); or even die a couple of times when the action comes along and you keep clicking your mouse and nothing happens. But really, to focus on these gameplay problems instead of on everything so great and so different that this game presents, is totally nitpicking. I have played my fair-share of lovecraftian games, and have never found some of the stuff done here. For me, the good aspects definitely overcame the bad. As an example, just a couple days ago I left a review on another lovecraftian game (more like a demo) that tried to do the "color out of space" thing, and I thought "that's a bad idea, how can you truly show an 'indescribable color' in a game"?. Well, somehow, this game did it right (and it's quite a coincidence that I played this right after the other one xD). The imagery in this one is so awesome... It definitely turned me into a fan, and whenever I manage to get myself some VR goggles, I'm definitely checking out the VR version. Many times I found myself thinking "man, how great would this be if I was seeing it through goggles...". Anyway, great game, I totally recommend it, especially if you are a fan of H.P.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: For a few £'s this is an engrossing and scary little story. It only takes a few hours to complete, the combat is basic and the puzzles dont take long to figure out, but theres lots of atmosphere & Lovecraftian lore to keep you hooked. Considering this was put together by just one guy is amazing, you can only wonder what he could have accomplished with a bigger budget and more time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I do not really recommend this game. The beginning of the game which focused on slow exploration and intrigue was awesome. But the second half of the game introduced the "combat" it is not enjoyable. The puzzles also could be improved upon. The visuals though, especially of the monsters and environment, are really good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Just started playing this game, and I've got to say, I have read every single story in the Cthulhu Mythos, and other related works, and this game brings them all to life in such an amazing way. I have been dying for a game like this for so long, and to actually have it and be able to witness the sheer Lovecraftian terror is amazing. I'm in love with the artwork, music, and the story. I wish the game could be free roam, and I could just walk around messing with all of the weirdness for hours. I'm not huge into fighting games, and thankfully there isn't a high level of combat, I can just immerse myself in the story and feel like I'm living in a Lovecraft novel. It's a dream come true. If you are a big Lovecraft nerd, this is seriously the game for you! It has the whole package!Edit: Just finished the game! OMG for the real Lovecraft fan, you will love the ending! There is absolutely nothing more pleasantly surprising and poetic than the ending that was given! Such an amazing game. I will keep coming back to play it, and probably will never ever stop playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I understand that it's not for everyone and that some folks may be disappointed in the length (about 2.5 hours for me) but I enjoyed every minute of it. I have long been a fan of Lovecraftian/Cosmic Horror and this game really did that well. Seeing some of Lovecraft's more...strange monsters on screen was a delight. For a mostly one person team, this game was clearly full of passion for the mythos and I'm glad I got to experience it. I'd love to see what could be done with a bigger team/budget. I was happy to spend my $25 on this and if you're a fan of this universe then you should be too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: as a fan of lovecraftian games and atmosphere, this game nailed it, it has a short playtime and might not be worth it at full price, but if you can get it on sale its an amazing game through and through, once things pick up you are constantly stopping to take in the scenery every chance you get, easily one of my favorites, if not my number 1 lovecraftian game ive ever played
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While I can admire a good walking-sim any day of the week and this appears to be done by a single person. A good Lovecraft story is generally the first 30-50% completely ordinary mundane life  30-50% Of creepy tension building upLast 3% all out shock encounter with cosmic horror. This game throws in all the last 3% of every famous lovecraft story into a single game, giving you monster after monster without ever building any psychological tension or fear. Weird 3d shooter level parts that harken back to the days of when developers hadn`t figured out 3d mechanics yet feel really out of place.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks good by the trailer. ITS NOT. Its not open world, its very linear. The textures are awful, the game runs horribly. I have a very good rig and hardly broke 40 fps even on low graphics. The audio levels are all over the place, the gameplay is poor. The puzzles are silly, the story is no interesting, the voice acting is barely passable sometimes and other times it just sucks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'll devour negative comments before buying indie stuff like this first, I learned my lesson now.Atmosphere of it is great. This is literally the only thing about the game I can talk positively. First of all, controller keybinds doesn't work properly. I couldn't inspect any of the photos I got via controller.The game doesn't tell you what are you going to do, in some cases you need to solve how to progress by frustratingly trying stuff. If things you needed to do were a bit more logical, I would not care too much about this.Since keybinds were a bit problematic in controller, when I find myself unable to sprint I thought it was bugged in a certain part. But no, in an escape sequence, you can't run and the game doesn't tell you that. Puzzles don't make any sense, and pretty much every action is you turning behind, slowing the enemy that is following you, and keep running to the next part. You can kill lesser ones, too. Voice actors were so bad, other than the main character. Her daughter talks broken English with a Russian accent but bro talks like a classy Englishman.It is honestly such shame. A game that has this good atmosphere could be a better experience, but hey! At least it was short.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, i'll try anything for 1.67.....For the price? I can't really complain much honestly.It's voice acted, graphics are fine, music is a little lackluster but i swear one scene was using music from Godzilla.....Hear me out...the main character becomes silver surfer. You can't change my mind, the end boss is the world eater. The 'combat' sections of this game hurt it more than helped for sure. Interesting visuals at times, the fleshy areas are way too dark and half the time I didn't know where I was going.I don't regreat the 1.67 either way. Thanks devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with the negative comments. Game was good for the first 20 minutes. After that it's trash. It's a shame, game had so much potential. At some point I actually had goose pimples. But once you have to run from monsters pointing the triangle at them - tedious, annoying and frustrating. All immersion is gone. Plus, if you die on your first chase sequence, before you own the triangle, you will be re spawned way too far away AND facing the opposite direction plus running is disabled - takes ages to get to the place you died in, just so you can die again. Why the hell is checkpoint so far away? I didn't bother completing the game. I was too annoyed with having to point triangle at 2 monsters simultaneously while navigating a labyrinth of corridors walking backwards, listening to monster sounds repeating on a short loop. Such a shame, it was SO GOOD the first 20 mins. Eerie, uneasy, immersive... But also, too short as apparently I have missed out on a couple of things as I learned from watching a play through online. I just don't understand why change the genre a third of the way through? At least include this in your trailer. I only paid 15% of the price so I suppose I got my moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: After i read the call of chutulu i bought this game a while back and today i decided to play it and it was good i loved how it kept me on my toes and how the game made you felt calm yet at the same time anxious of what was behind the corner and i  liked how the game didn't go easy on you yet did make it hard for you either so that way you can enjoy the game and i liked when you got the lazer thing as a way to fight back but you still felt helpless at the same time and i loved the design of the game the ppl who made this really did the best on keeping the details just like something out of a hp lovecraft book. and the ending wasn't anything at all as i was expecting i really hope that they make more games like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully realised, with tons of atmosphere, this is a must for all Lovecraft fans.Some of the puzzles are a bit obscure, but nothing utterly show stopping.What this game does absolutely nail is the gargantuan scale of the cosmic horror, the sense that mankind is nothing more than tiny insignificant insects compared to these ancient, unknowable beings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So this game has issues. It's short, it's sometimes buggy, the story is.. not great, but... The atmosphere, dude! It's ll about the atmosphere! It feels like you're inside a dream that you can't escape. You're walking around the island, then.. something happens and you're alredy running from a huge shoggoth, then ... again on the shore, releasing Dagon, etc.You'll see Dagon holding the monolith, Cthulhu rising from the sea, Shub-Niggurath spawning the Dark Young, Nyarlathotep above the pyramid and even Azatoth in space!  One thing really bothered me. Cthulhu laughing and talking like your typical villain wanting to destroy the world and some kind of conflict between him and Nyarlathotep. This is too.. Derleth-y. But you can ignore that, that's just a short momet, and the atmosphere is still great.If you want an other Call of Cthulhu or Amnesia - move along, if you want soomething more dreamy, closer to Dagon and Silver Key and can look past some typical indie problems - get it!Also the developer is reading all the bug reports and fixing the game, so it;s gonna be more polished.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so far; it's beautiful, the story is compelling; despite me not really knowing 100% what's going on, and it's all around just a very good game. I will say, though, it suffers from probably the worst case of "where the ♥♥♥♥ do I go?" of any game I've played. Like just a little more guiding the player, and this game would've been, like, perfect. Oh, also, the controller support has Photo mode key-bound to pressing the left thumbstick. I think that's blatant poor game design, as the vast majority of games use that button to toggle your sprint function.I, personally, think it would've been a better idea to swap what your sprint and Photo mode are bound to, just for user ease, 'cause I've lost count how many times I've toggled Photo mode on while trying to escape a monster because literally every other game I've played uses pressing the thumbstick to toggle sprint, not Photo mode. It's more intuitive, since your thumb is already on the thumbstick to move, so it just makes sense to have the sprint function bound to pressing the thumbstick the user is already using to move, as opposed to have to press some random trigger or whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a long video on Youtube looking at a number of games set in the genre and asking why it's so hard if not impossible to get Lovecraftian Horror right in computer games. Won't post the link, but it's easy to search for.The point is that this game does nothing to break the chain of "nope, this ain't it". While it covers eery, creepy, haunted with some great sound, music and beautiful graphics, it shoots itself in the foot with all the force of an FPS.Invisible walls everywhere: they actually gave me motion sickness because they are so jarring and then force your character into weird lateral motion that my inner ear couldn't cope with what my eyes were telling my brain. Talk about playing games and chewing gum at the same time! You don't get to enjoy some of the most fascinating scenes and graphics: you go from carefully and methodically studying your environs to running away from some monster that will kill your unarmed toon in 3 hits. It has zombies - the most overused trope in games and one that is pretty much non-existent in HPL.Mind you, I haven't even finished the game. I'm about an hour or so in and not even sure I'll finish it. Maybe if I discover a god mode cheat that let's me just continue to look at the surroundings while ignoring some annoying pest to try and stomp me into paste. Shockingly, going by some of the walk-through video time markers as reference I'm already halfway through! The hell? Anything I've done so far would barely count as tutorial or prologue in a proper game!

_childDocuments_.review: Looks good and the background music & effects helped a lot with the creepy atmosphere. But the controls is very rigid. It's like gravity is missing or physics does not work in this world. The dialogue presentation also needs more polish. The text box is quite ugly.Furthermore, I think some parts of the game needs clarification like when the player is first introduced to a new mechanics (e.g. being chased, complete chess, etc.). I also suggest making the highlight for interactive objects more visible. A World Map would also be a welcome feature. At present, this game kinda feels like a school thesis. It is a pain for me to play and is very far from the quality of . I hope the developers will release better games in the future as I can see their potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it was short & there were a few confusing moments of not knowing exactly where to go/invisible walls, as an huge Lovecraft fan, I really enjoyed this game. The atmosphere & mystery feel behind it IS what a game based on Lovecraft's work is supposed to be like. I honestly thought it would just be Cthulhu who would be appearing, (which would have been fine) but was very pleasantly surprised about the other Lovecraftian deities that appeared throughout the game, especially at the end. The alien puzzles were wonderfully bizarre, not so difficult that it's frustrating, but not too easy (some people may find them a bit too easy if they're avid puzzle solvers). I'd love to see some actual stories adapted into games with this much quality atmosphere & head tripping visuals as this one.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR looks and sounds excellent, though with some badly thought out bits, really uninteresting and sometime clunky game play.Despite good points, being the atmosphere and visuals, there are too many troubles with this game to recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Clearly an art project wrapped in a thin veneer of a game.Whilst its clear that a lot of effort has gone into creating a Cthulu environment, this game barely qualifies as a walking simulator. The 'puzzles' are not really even puzzles, you just have to do some actions in the right order which can be figured out by trial and error.There are some instances where you can die, and at least one of those has an unnecessarily long reset time due to the amount of walking needed after loading at the last save point.There are some chase events which are extremely frustrating as you have to figure out what to do through trial and error, whilst dying over and over.The main character has good voice acting but most of the other voices are terrible.The story... what there is of it isn't great.Overall I cannot recommend, even at a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this as a must-play to anyone who is a fan of, and already pretty familiar with extended H.P. Lovecraft Lore.Anyone else, I will give a disclaimer that you may end up disappointed and confused by the end of the game if you are not really into Lovecraft.The gameplay, puzzles, exploration, collectibles, and combat are all very simple and not very deep, the point of this is the submersion into Lovecraft's extended lore, and that job it does with flying colors.I also noticed bad texture pop-in until I increased texture streaming capacity, which also dropped my frames sometimes while playing in 4k on a 3080. _childDocuments_.review: Really good lovecraftian horror. For it's discount price it's a really good experience, although for how short the game is its full price is ridiculous. Only issue with this game is its lack of direction. It varies from segment to segment, in some parts I got completely stuck for a long time. I really think the item indicator (the little squid that sometimes appears when you can pick up an item) should've been a bit bigger and used more often. Other than that, fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this only with the caveat that the purchaser is a huge Lovecraft fan.Good:- The Lovecraft elements are great.- The puzzles are generally not over-complicated, although finding some of the pieces you may need can be a little frustrating. - The overall look of the game is very good, especially for a single developer.- The music and sound effects are fantastic.Bad- The combat stuff that begins mid-game is TERRIBLE!  Several of the creatures are indestructable and are often barely "stunned" by your "weapon."  Furthermore, the combat almost always takes place in a dimly lit maze that is very difficult to find your way out of.  I very nearly gave up on the game completely a few times but finally managed to get lucky just enough to finish.  Also, the combat portions are very incongruent with the puzzle portions.  It plays like two separate games at times and really took me out of the overall story.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interactive spectacle, not really a game. It has some great visual set pieces, but the game itself is poorly crafted. Lots of invisible walls in otherwise open spaces, lots of clipping into terrain, character walks painfully slow. Strictly linear paths with no exploration. Several 2-3 second cutscenes all unrelated to one another showing different creatures and not explained.  Feels like someone took all their student work and stuffed it into one thing. If you're a diehard Eldritch / Cthulhu fan, you'll probably like this. Otherwise, steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard of the game and it took me 2 years to check it out. Wow Great Story and atmosphere . Sound was top quality an the world was great. I'm glad i played this after skorn as it shows me a perspective on this story/horror style is more enjoyable if you sit back and enjoy the ride. I recommend to any one who hasn't tried it yet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a better rating system for its games because thumbs up or thumbs down doesn't really give me much options, but I guess I'm going to give this game a thumbs down, even though it doesn't really deserve it. The game is very pretty, some very strong visuals, a so-so story, basic puzzles, basic combat mechanics, some very good and disturbing environments. I didn't dislike the game, but at four hours (and honestly you could beat it in far less) it isn't worth getting unless it's on sale, and I think even the $4.99 I got it for is a bit much considering the content.  The game could have used better puzzles, and a number of the puzzles have very little strategy to them. The game sometimes likes to plop you into a room make you do a puzzle and then transport you out of the room for no real reason other than doing a puzzle.There's nothing to the combat, you have an artifact that can blast enemies and kill them with a little effort, but it is so simplistic that I would have preferred a stealth game more than combat. There seems like a number of elements in the game that an idea was had for but never got fleshed out, especially early in the game when you are collecting items, but some of them never get used, and then later you lose access to your inventory, which makes me ask what was the point of it?And unless there is a better, alternate ending, the ending of the game is simplistic and poorly thought out, like it was rushed to finish.I would say give it a try if it is on sale, but don't expect more than you moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my! That was a great experience. The Shore is a rather short game (not necessarily a bad thing), took me about 5 hours or so to complete and to be honest in the end I wanted some more of it. Considering though that it's an indie game from a small developer with very few people working on it, those 5-6 hours of gameplay make it seem like Triple A for the effort.The visuals and the sound design are simply top notch and they are the main strengths of the game. The art direction on that regard, along with the color palettes used, make it a very atmospheric experience. Being a loveletter to H.P. Lovecraft and his Cthulhu Mythos will help scratch that itch for eldritch horror if you are a fan of the genre like me and the whole artistic direction really helps with that. The best part of the game is, of course, the "creatures" (to put it mildly). The graphics for all the abominations, protoplasmic forms, powers and so on are simply amazing, grandiose and highly detailed, really bringing the whole thing to life. The great ambient soundtrack and sound design really help to make it even better and more atmospheric. The game clearly oozes passion from the developers in that regard and the whole project seems to be made out of love and not as a "job".The exploration is ok, with much attention to detail. You need to take your time and look. I would prefer a more open world approach than hitting invisible walls that force you to go places, but the rather linear path is well made as it is. I managed to get stuck a couple of times on the textures while trying to explore the edges, but that's just me, nothing game braking.Story-wise was ok as well, it was rather simple, but the good voice acting and the visuals mentioned earlier pretty much make up for it.The gameplay is on the walking-simulator side, you can use and react to certain stuff, and there is some basic "combat" later on in the game. Some say in other reviews that it is clunky. Well... that's because this game is not an FPS or even a pure walking simulator in that regard, and shouldn't be treated as either. It is what it is, don't go expecting snappy COD style combat, it's a basic mechanic that it is part of it's story, so you are not getting into this game for that.All in all, I really enjoyed my time with it and I think it's a must play for all the Cthulhu Mythos fans, so go check it out!To the Developers: Greetings from Greece and keep up the good work guys! Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this knowing nothing about the game aside from watching a trailer.+New to Lovecraft, top notch audio/visual creature design from my perspective.+Atmospheric, immersive setting is really well done.+Even things that I literally saw coming still scared the pants off of me --- outstanding for this alone.-Almost criminally short considering the price, so I cannot recommend at full price. Price aside, some elements that I thought would get stale did not, as the game was over with before that happened. Silver lining I suppose. -Unpolished or incomplete feeling at times, with regards to some gameplay elements, level design, audio glitches, voicing, and graphical settings & performance. Nothing too egregious, but enough to notice.-Story felt pretty vague and generic to me (I know nothing of whether it references or relies on Lovecraft's original works), and it seemed to be more a prop to make a fairly disconnected protagonist walk through it all rather than to add anything to experience.Verdict: Absolutely get it, but get it on sale and be thrilled and/or terrified for an evening.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: When you row your boat merrily down the stream, you may be inclined to wonder: IS life just a dream?Then your boat hits The Shore and you find out that it's more of a Lovecraftian nightmare, and it's being dreamt not by you, but by Things Man Was Not Meant To Know.There's not much "game" here, since mostly it's about walking around creepy environments, with brief interruptions of fleeing in terror from squidgy Horrors From Beyond. Your mad gamer skillz will not save you. You will not stand triumphant atop a mountain of monster corpses, holding your plasma chainsaw aloft while a buxom damsel in distress clings to your leg and gazes up at you adoringly.It's not that kind of game. And that's appropriate, because it's not that kind of genre.But what The Shore does, it does incredibly well. The visuals, sounds, and atmosphere are brilliant. I felt genuine dread at several points in the game. I bought it on sale for about 6 bucks and at that price it was a bargain.Two tentacles way up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While a fairly primitive gaming experience full of invisible walls and bare bones mechanics, lovers of weird lovecraft visuals like me may find a lot to appreciate after the unpromising first quarter. A lot of the classic usual suspects make an appearance in awe inspiring ways. People who aren't genre-addicts might be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale and while it may not be the most complex or challenging game, I must say I enjoyed it. I have loved Lovecraft's work for a long time and it is rare to find a game which captures the feel and look of Lovecraft's Mythos. This game wasn't particularly long (I clocked in at 2.2 Hours from start to finish), nor does it have the most riveting story, but I found myself captivated by the locations and Lovecraft's monsters. There were perhaps two moments in this game that I found very frustrating, one where the game glitched and wouldn't let me put down an item (I ended up having to hard quit the game and go back in and just not pick it up again) and another where I kept getting killed by this one particular monster before I realised how to get past it. This is an Indie Game so if you go in expecting something AAA you will not find it here. At times the game can be clunky and the controls aren't perfect BUT all things considered I had a good time with this game. I would be very keen to see this developer take on one of Lovecraft's stories and purely focus on it, such as the Mountains of Madness or Shadow Over Innsmouth, as I feel this game was a good introduction to all of the monsters but never really had the chance to explore any one fully.Overall, good game but wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Enjoyed some parts but simply too short, unpolished, and downright flawed to recommend. Maybe try it if it is on sale for under $8 and/or you don't care about gameplay or story and just want to look at cool monsters and environments.I don't usually write reviews but this game was just not what I expected. I don't think I will refund it as I still admired some aspects like the atmosphere and art direction, but because of its many flaws and short run time I cannot recommend it, at least at its current price of $12.The game does a few things right, and by right I mean it does them beautifully. The art direction of the creatures and environments was incredible and reminded me at some points of H.R. Giger and at others Z. Beksinski. I especially enjoyed the atmosphere of the misty island and some of the more open sections mid-late game. While some may brand this game as a walking simulator (a term thrown around way too much), this game has plenty of puzzle solving, chase sequences, and combat which is always at least somewhat engaging.Unfortunately, all of the things this game does well are far outnumbered by the things it does not so well. The graphical quality was inconsistent. For most of the game the graphics looked amazing but some things like water splashes, those weird points of red or purple light in the otherworldly sections, and even the texturing of the entire  were ugly and made the game seem unpolished. The level design also seemed in dire need of polishing. I saw many floating rocks and low poly edges that really took away from the otherwise wonderfully crafted landscape. Invisible walls blocked me whenever I tried to go somewhere I logically could which made finding the "correct" path very tedious. The text seemed badly translated at times and there were many spelling and grammatical errors in the notes and subtitles. The voice acting was just plain bad, at times laughable, but mostly cringy. The audio quality of the voice acting in particular was distracting as some lines sounded like they were professionally recorded, and others sounded like they were recorded with a cheap cell phone. However, all of these things are forgivable as this game was made by an indie dev and it did not seem like English was their first language.What I don't find forgivable from a technical aspect is the design of the gameplay. While the presence of puzzles, chase sequences, and combat was appreciated they were often not that good. The puzzles require no brain power once you get past their frustrating obscurity. I especially had problems with . The chase sequences were either too easy because all you have to do is run from a slow moving enemy down an alien tunnel or too hard because you are trying to navigate a maze while being chased by an invincible enemy that is faster than you. Plus, you can't take in any of the stunning scenery when you are running from Shoggoths. The combat is uninteresting after the novelty of the singular combat mechanic wears off and consists only of  until it simply pops out of existence with a little splatter of black ooze.The worst thing, and the reason I cannot recommend this game especially to sincere fans of Lovecraft is the quality of the story, or lack thereof. As the description says the main story is you are Andrew and you are looking for your daughter and spooky Lovecraftian stuff happens. Believe it or not, the description oversells the game. You do play as an old fisherman named Andrew who is looking for his daughter, but that is where the similarities end. I did not uncover any "secrets lurking within his own sanity", I did not feel like I faced "overwhelming odds", there were no "moments that make you question his sanity", I did not feel like the game was a "series of slow-burning scenes", and I did not think the story was "deep and multilayered". The pacing was terrible past the first third of the game and there was no build up or payoff for any of the story's big moments. The majority of the game is just awakening Lovecraftian beings because the voice told you to and that is the only way to progress. Speaking of awakening Lovecraftian beings, I felt that the game lacked subtlety in that aspect. You are shown eldritch horrors (all popular Lovecraft monsters) in their entirety and in full detail. One of them even has a cheesy monologue. Then you just move on to summoning the next one without stopping to think about anything. Because of this the themes of fear of the unknown, the insignificance of the narrow scope of human comprehension, and the fragility of the human psyche that define Lovecraftian horror are completely absent. The only thing that makes this a "Lovecraftian" game is spooky tentacle things and references to some of Lovecraft's specific works that have no place in the game other than fanservice.

_childDocuments_.review: From an artistic standpoint, the game is great. The graphic artists really nailed the alien geometries of the void and the Lovecraftian creatures. There are visuals in this game that you'll simply never see anywhere else, and that's a shame.The sound was decent. The music was pretty good, but was ultimately just the same track looping over and over throughout the game. Occasionally you'll hear these really bassy sounds when approaching certain objects which really improve the atmosphere and alienness of the world.The problem is the gameplay, and story.The game starts out as a walking sim. While not great, this is something I can live with, and the game was pretty up-front about this. The problem is that about 1/3 of the way in it stop just being a walking sim. First you unlock the ability to jump purely for the sake of hopping onto a ship to grab two items. After that, the mechanic is basically never used again in any meaningful way. The game is littered with invisible walls, so anything you can jump on (e.g. rocks) will likely have a wall preventing you from actually progressing further.The second gameplay problem is that about halfway in, the game also decides to give you... let's call it "combat". You gain an alien artefact that can shoot out a beam that stuns and occasionally/arbitrarily kills certain creatures. You see, by this point the game frequently sprinkles in chase sequences. You either have to keep moving (as some monsters move at the same pace as your sprinting speed), or turn around and shoot them with the beam to stun them. Occasionally, some monsters will die, though some will then just respawn either right where they died, or in your path. You will die several times for no other reason than because you weren't standing far enough away from a monster when it popped out.The other problem is story. The game basically teases you with a few tidbits about your character's past. It never really comes out and tells you a meaningful story, but you can piece together the fact that you were a fisherman, your wife died, and eventually your daughter died too. Your father often spoke about the island, and cryptic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about making offerings to the sea/elder gods. There are some notes at the beginning of the game that hint at other people being stuck there, but it was disjointed, and most of the notes were "We've been stuck here for an indescribable amount of time | I'm starting to go mad | We may have found a way off the island".I could go on, but ultimately this game just completely fumbles after the first 30 minutes or so. And even the intro sequence wasn't great to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: The length of the game does not justify the price of 25$.  I took my time and in general I complete games a tad slower than the average gamer. This game took me 2.2 hours to beat. My biggest gripe with this game was the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ invisible walls. What could have been a cool island to explore is simply an illusion and it quickly becomes apparent that the seemingly big open areas are actually small confined spaces, there are invisible walls EVERYWHERE. I'm not even kidding there is an invisible wall in the most ridiculous spots where they are not needed at all. Like I understand that ok, it's not an exploration game it is a linear walking sim and the player can't just go run off into the boonies so you gotta stop them with invis walls sometimes... but this is just next level. The visuals are ok. The audio is ok. The story is is ok. There are some really creepy moments and some disturbing visual moments that are pretty good but I wouldn't call great. The gameplay is bad. There is combat, kind of, and it is really clunky and not fun. You have an "artifact" that can disintegrate anything you shoot. But when try to use it on a bird (or anything living thing) out in the wild, nothing happens.  Only if the dev allows it. There is some kind of inventory system I think but I only opened it once because it doesn't actually do anything. The puzzles are pretty bad, and leave you with a "you gotta be kidding me" feeling. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game, and it's coming to VR. This is a cosmic horror Lovecraft inspired walking simulator. TL;DR - it's not *that* short, per some of the more sensible reviews. I don't know if it's a $25 game, but wishlist it and when it's 50% off do NOT hesitate. This is one of the most fun and (weird to say) relaxing games for me in a long time. During the pandemic, horror survival has helped me realize it can always get worse. =)If you are into typical horror survival, this may be too slow or too obscure for you. This won't make a lot of sense, and it's not a AAA style game... this is made by a dedicated, thoughtful, passionate single developer, not some studio, about a universe of cosmic and body horror, which isn't your typical blood and guts torture porn. The concept is more metaphysical and existential. Think a version of Myst with endless philosophical dread.If you get Cosmic Lovecraftian comment, you're going to see so many delightful literary Easter eggs that you will giggle with glee, while being both scared, awed, and amazed by the game.This single dev put his heart and soul into a game, and most importantly after the release is constantly updating it with both patches and new content. I'd seen some of the kneejerj immediate launch gripes that are coloring the aggregate review score.... and it's nonsense. Look at the trend in reviews over time. What's important is the guy cares, seems that he'll keep patching, and that's enough for me. He keeps saying VR will come, and that will be sublime.

Following closely after were then the immersion-breaking invisible walls, which despite the lack of the later unlock-able jump command, made the linear experience entirely apparent. The story elements also seem patchwork, with multiple characters being introduced to conflate the world before being entirely forgotten about in the next epistle, doing nothing to expand the anemic first-person narrative. Such did the gratuitous amount of skeletons you find in the first half - Whether or not the physical plane of the Island does anything for the story at all I don't know, as I quit during the other-worldly trapping of the game. (The purported actions of other survivors seem of dubious credibility due to their apparent knowledge and mastery of the game's ultimate power, confusing the elements of human fragility and the dark.)Which brings me to my main frustration and criticism of a lot of indie horrors: a puzzle / or puzzles that shouldn't be hard to complete, yet that leave me baffled. For fans of the genre only.

_childDocuments_.review: ... One of those authors, who never published a single book during their lifetimes, but ended up getting a cult following after their deaths. And you can easily see why. Despite being pretty simple story-wise, 's works perfectly captured the feeling of primal fears. And not just any primal fears, but those that can't even be explained properly. Those fears of the great unknown, in which there are powers beyond our limits and apprehensions. Those things you're afraid to even think about just because they're way bigger than everything you know. While reading 's stories, it's hard not to feel... uncomfortable. That certain feeling his characters used to get from the mysterious ancient artifacts? The same exact feeling people usually get from his works. And honestly, there's nothing like it. Hence the legacy.Surprisingly, though, most of the adaptations failed. It doesn't even matter which kind of the adaptations we're talking about. Movies, comics, video games... Those just don't feel... right. It's not like we can't still enjoy them, but... you know. There's not enough  in them. On the other hand, when you think about it, it's not really that surprising. I mean, it's not the stories themselves (in which  tried to imitate  and  a bit too much here and there) we all fell in love with. It was that certain feeling. A crawling anxiety, somewhat similar to panic attack. And to properly reproduce it? It takes  himself. Still, some of the imitations did pretty well. For example, up to this day, I'm a  fan of '  game for . Which did surprisingly fine job imitating everything that 's works were all about (“”). So, even though I never expect much, I always welcome more of the games inspired by  and his works. Especially when it's  we're talking about.And that's exactly what we've got here. Even though  isn't mentioned in the title (heck, nobody even thanked him in credits, like... what the heck, ?),  is a game based on . , , ,  and, of course, , they're all here. We'll be dealing with some scary artifacts, awakening deities, fighting and running away from  and so on. In other words, it's  lovecraftian game. And guess what? Atmosphere-wise? It's not really that bad. Exactly the opposite. This game's approach is a bit too direct, which heavily ruins “the great unknown” feeling (or to put it in a simpler way, dealing with all of those deities directly kinda make them feel smaller and therefore less scary), while story feels a lot like “too much of a good stuff” (heck, even that meteorite from  is here for whatever reason), but still, atmosphere-wise,  does pretty well. You  feel  in here. Looks fine too. I mean, on high resolutions it still looks pretty crappy (another lovecraftian game, 's , had the same exact problem, so, keep in mind that this game looks better on  screens, while forcing  on it kinda ruins things), but still, the color palette feels right and so does the design. So... yay? We finally got ourselves a proper new lovecraftian game? * Sigh * Well, no. Not really.First of all... yeah, yeah, you guessed it. It's yet another one of those “walking sims”. All we need to do in this game is to walk around and interact with every thing possible. Technically, there are some puzzles, but all of them are exactly that – press all the buttons and enjoy the result. You can die, though. Unfortunately, it's a problem too. Instead of focusing on things like sanity and fear,  just added a lot of enemies who'll kill you with a couple of hits. And while it's not really a bad thing per se (let's not forget that  the survival horror genre was born from such an approach), in the way they did it here? It is. It  a problem. Just because it works like this: you arrive at the new place. The one you haven't seen before. And suddenly, there are strong enemies trying to surround and kill you. While you have absolutely no idea where to go and what are you supposed to do here. Again, it's not like there's a lot of room for exploration, the game is painfully linear and there is only one ending, such an approach still makes it confusing and very unpleasant at times. It just... isn't fun. You know? Just because trial and error stuff never,  feels good.There also isn't much to do here. Isn't enough content. If you'll decide to use the guide, which will tell you exactly what you can ignore, you can beat this game in about an hour. Considering you won't die too much that is. While getting  completion, which will require you to pick up boring notes and useless coins, would take you about two. Can't say I feel robbed, of course ( price tag is perfectly fine for something like this, especially if you'll pick this game up on sale), but still... Let's just say that  is yet another one of those “why bother?” games. One of those that don't make you feel that bad, but at the same time fail to provide you with anything special.So... what's in conclusion? Yay or nay? Well, as long as you enjoy “walking sims”, you can do way,  worse than . If you think that filling a couple of hours of your life with the images from 's works is a good idea? You may as well go for it. Sure,  is far from being perfect. It's too short, it feels rough and unpolished, while there also isn't much to do here, but like I said, if “walking sims” are your thing, you can do  worse than this. Then again, if, like yours truly, you never considered all of those tiny little “walking” games to be a real deal? I'd say, it's a no. Personally, I don't even think that  saved it for me. Even though technically, the atmosphere is the only thing this game did right, it just... isn't enough. Dixi.

_childDocuments_.review: To begin this review, let me say I was looking forward to playing this game since it came out and I saw a YouTube video showing the graphical quality/atmosphere - other than this one video I knew nothing else about the game - and I picked it up on sale for $5.I'm always down for some Lovecraftian horror - but when it's just Lovecraft for the sake of Lovecraft with no real cohesive story or purpose, it may as well be a fun-house ride. There was a lot of Elder God-Name dropping and not much else in terms of story beats. First off - I loved the graphics, and most of the visuals. There were a lot of inconsistent moments in the story telling, and I ended up getting sick of the loading screens breaking up the action. Writing was weak - nothing wrong with non-English speaking developers creating games in English but hire a native English speaker/writer or get someone to help you with spell-checking to make the writing flow better and make things more comprehensible for the language you're creating the game in. Immediately takes me out of a game when I have to guess what someone was trying to say - especially in a game where you have the player collecting several pieces of written word to form the backstory.Sound design was rough at best (voice lines would randomly get louder and quieter without reason) and most of the time it seemed like the audio sliders in the menu had no effect on volume.In terms of game objectives - I often found myself just sprinting through while being chased by various random tentacle beasties and straight up guessing what I was supposed to be doing - definitely not a good sign for a game as linear as this. I got where I needed to go but having to guess so much and having items around the place that you can pick up and look at but not use for anything was tantamount to having empty drawers in horror games like Layers of Fear, or Outlast. The feeling of exploring and finding what you were looking for is fantastic but not when mired deeply in the illusion of choice and discoveryOverall, a pretty average experience. More like a collection of "oooo look at this elder god, and here's this guy too!" moments than any kind of cohesive, story driven experience. Had a lot of potential but fell short. All I can say is, I'm glad I didn't pay more than $5 for it and even then, I almost wish I hadn't.Props to the dev(s) for pushing this out and attempting to create something awe-inspiring and terrifying but I hope they learnt a lot from this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm....probably not the response the developers were hoping for, but there you go. Followed by ehhhhhhh??This is clearly meant to be an epic, mind-blowing take on H.P. Lovecrafts Cthulu mythology, with awe-inspiring scenes and tense game-play sequences. Whilst it does do a pretty good job visually, and is quite atmospheric, I don't think it succeeds with its narrative or the parts where its more action-packed.And that's a shame, as it does have some excellent design and fairly impressive technical prowess. There are some combat elements and chase sequences, but these fail to rack up tension and fear. You either just have to run away from an indestructible creature, or can shoot the enemy with an artefact that never drains out of power, making it somewhat redundant. If they had limited the energy of this device and you had to wait for it to recharge whilst avoiding enemies, then it could have been more frightening. Instead you can just keep blasting away and the creatures will quickly die. They still can't find that sweet spot between being making you feel powerless (like most games in the genre do) and giving the player some agency within the world.To be fair to the developers they're far from the only ones to bodge up these elements, and it's pretty rare for this type of game to actually succeed in being scary or involving. Often there's a lack of substance, and 'The Shore' is no different to all the other failed 'Amnesia' wannabes that include these simplistic challenges. I wouldn't say that Frictional (developers of Amnesia rebirth / SOMA etc) do anything massively different, but they do know how to squeeze out terror from these sequences in a way that the developers haven't managed here. The final nail in the games coffin is that I have no clue what the story is about, with it having some confusing elements introduced right at the end that don't make a whole lot of sense.Now, part of the Lovecraft mythos is that these entities are beyond the comprehension of mortals, but here it just seems that the author of the plot has invented some gibberish nonsense and then hand-waves it away with "who can explain the un-explainable?" In some ways this is pretty ambitious, and for the spectacle I would applaud them, but as a game, and a story....not so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I rate this an average game.  For the positives: Nice graphics, some cool set pieces, beautiful music (when they're designed to be calm and atmospheric), easy puzzles, interesting myth, and a touching tale.  For the negatives: invisible barriers in the world seemed weirdly placed (like tiny mounds of rock that our character could jump atop, but not walk across); battle segments felt like they clashed with the game's calm beginning & middle; knowing where to go was sometimes obtuse; and I wish there were more lore.  I'm glad that I played through & beat this experience, but I shan't be returning to replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Nice atmosphere and enticing visuals overrun by tedious design choices, simple mistakes and fanfiction writingExploration game with endless invisible walls. Story is no more complex than "I lost my daughter, I'm gonna go through a Lovecraft haunted house to get her back" and at no point did I care about the protagonist or his daughter. Lore conveyed through several message-in-a-bottles is a cool idea, but riddled with spelling errors. Notes also often have watermarks of the monsters you encounter and are assumedly drawings by the note's author, but are clearly just images of the actual models of the creatures.Once you leave the titular Shore the nice atmosphere and excusable errors are replaced with constant teleporting between rooms accompanied by the disembodied narration of a kid trying to deepen his voice on Xbox Live. Run away from a monster that is either faster than you or laughable, fade to black, next room. Complete a puzzle that consists of "put object on pedestal, hold left click on thing using the artifact", fade to black, next room. This seems to only serve to pad the run time.As previously mentioned, the Lovecraft mythos is reduced to a haunted house of characters from stories. This seems like a new developer that is clearly passionate about the mythos and wants to include every character possible, but they have lost the meaning of the work along the way. The infinitely large forces of nature that existed formlessly and incomprehensibly by men now screech and pose like Godzilla before riding away into the sunset on an obelisk.The positive aspects are really strong, but are dragged down so badly I couldn't come to finish it. Apologies for my harshness, I understand this is a new developer and their effort is commendable, but I believe this kind of harsh but fair (I hope) critique is important for artists and will only benefit you in the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended only with heavy caveats.  I absolutely love a good horror walking simulator. It's like a haunted house: immersive atmosphere + light scares + few frustrations = pure thrills. I started out thoroughly enjoying the atmosphere, from the beautifully desolate shoreline to the lonely, mangled skeletons, to the creepy ritual sites. Then about halfway through they introduced some clunky combat mechanics (being able to beat the spawn of eldritch horrors, for me, defeats half the horror of eldritch horrors) and I started just wanting to be done with this BS so I didn't have to go through it again. Dying over and over because you're not sure where to go for the next warp, which monsters are killable and which aren't, or you're getting stuck on the scenery is not fun. A few of the load-points are really freaking far back too. Fortunately the game is short enough to push through.  Go in for the atmosphere, but don't be surprised to find yourself flipping to a walkthrough before the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly surprised.I bought this game for two reasons. First one is, I am never able to pass on a Lovecraft game (except the stupid mobile types). Second reason - this game is slated for VR support. I have been waiting ages for this, but it looks imminent  - so I tossed a coin in anticipation. I had no intention of playing this game flat, but curiosity got the better of me. I have to say that I am presently surprised. This is more of a first reaction, as I have not played that long - but it has me impressed. In fact this promises to be one of the very best game adaptations of Lovecraft. The atmosphere is spot on, and in this regard it beats all of the other Lovecraftian games I have played. The graphics are really impressive - from all of the highly detailed sculpture and pages from arcane books, through to the misty expanses. There is a real feeling of eldritch dread here. The voice acting stuck out as being particularly good. I think the clincher for me was the game style - this is not really a walking simulator, but it sort of felt like one. Oddly, this is what made it work for me as a good adaptation of being in a novel. I did not expect much, but happily got far more than I had hoped for. Recommended. Cannot wait for this in VR, if it has the same visuals and sense of dread - will be spectacular. (BTW, I *did* play this in my headset - although flat - the difference between watching a Lovecraft movie in a theatre, rather than on the TV).

_childDocuments_.review: While I would not, at all, recommend The Shore for its gameplay (and no, i knew it was a walking simulator before going in, but it's other elements I disliked, primarily combat).......As a Lovecraft fan I would 100% recommend the game for its story alone.
