_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an atmospheric story-driven walking simulator game. It does offer some solid Puzzle-solving missions and some combat as well which is pretty unique for a game of this genre. The game was developed and published by  which is a small studio.Release Date: 19th February 2021.Last known update: 5th March 2021.I mean I can easily understand that a lot of work got thrown into this game but looking at the price from a consumer standpoint I will have to say that this is a little high for a game with a 2-3 hour story. There isn’t much replay value either. The story is obviously pretty good as well as the overall feeling of the game but once again the asking price is a little high for my liking and I would honestly suggest waiting for a sale (at least 50%) in order to get this pretty solid game.Once again this game is mainly a walking sim where you explore the beautifully crafted island but there are some puzzles and combat sections in this short game that are pretty okay in my opinion.As mentioned The Shore takes place on a mysterious island and the map is basically built for exploration. It is a pretty linear map without you really realizing it really quickly. The map might look as if you can go wherever you want but this just isn’t true. Some rocks and areas have invisible walls or you cannot even climb these areas. This does make the map seem a lot smaller than it actually is simply because I cannot go and explore all of the areas. Luckily there are still a lot of things to explore and find as there are small items such as letters inside of bottles or small mementos of various creatures.Puzzles are a usual sight in this game, most of them are pretty straightforward and do not require much thought behind them. Usually, you will have to take the corresponding symbol or statue and match it up with the bigger version of it or something identical. The puzzles do actually do a decent job and they will not feel like a chore and a timewaster which is always a positive in my eyes. Now combat sure as hell isn’t something that I would consider amazing but I think we should keep in mind that this is a story-focused walking simulator. Adding combat section made this game feel a little more realistic if you think about the entire story of fighting or running away from these creatures.Spoiler Free story section.The storyline is obviously the main selling point of the game. The characters are pretty memorable as the main character constantly mentions his backstory. Even the random letters you find inside of bottles tell detailed stories about each character which is a pretty nice addition. The entire map as well as the atmosphere it gives off is truly matching to the entire story as it really achieves that mysterious island type of vibe. What I really liked about the story is the plot twists that do happen in this game. Obviously I will not spoil anything but the game and its storyline have a nice slimax that will surely surprise a lot of players. Other than that I can only say that the story is a nice experience.Now the length of the story is an entire different discussion as I finished the story in just 2 hours despite going slow and taking a lot of time to see each detail in the map. Another thing is that replay value is almost non-existent in this game which basically makes this a one and done type of game. The quality is obviously very good but still, the amount of content is very very little.The game makes use of the well-known Unreal Engine 4 which is the main reason this game has such magnificent visuals. The Shore is a unique gamewith an amazing atmosphere, beautiful visuals and great voice acting. Sadly due to its short story and high price I will have to say that this game only makes sense in a good sale as the normal asking price is just too much.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 3/27/21:  I want to revisit my review and acknowledge that the developer has made a significant effort to improve and correct issues with the game.  First of all, they provided a save game file (and instructions to recover your existing save) that allowed me to restore my progress from the update on 2/22/21 that had deleted my game (though it wasn't actually deleted, just moved to a different location).  I give them due credit for that, though they could have avoided the problem entirely by not changing the save location or having the game copy your save automatically.  And, after a few additional patches, I was finally able to progress further beyond the sequence that was crashing out my game and make more progress.With the additional work being done on the game, and the future goals of adding VR and such to the title, I have to change my review to a positive one and recognize that the developer is very active in improving the experience and the overall game is much better for it.  It still isn't perfect but it is clear it's a labor of love and I think they deserve credit for that (since some games never fix the issues).Original review follows:I backed this game on Ulule (a crowdfunding platform) because I enjoyed the demo and thought it had promise.  I regretfully have to conclude that I can't recommend this game in its current state.I want to take a minute and praise the game from a voice-acting, music, and visual standpoint.  It's clear the game was lovingly crafted from that aspect.  While I can't speak for how the game appears after a certain point or even the story (more on that later), the island and the early game sequences are pretty gorgeous looking for an indie title, and the music fits the mood perfectly.  The voice acting is also well done, though sometimes the on-screen subtitles don't exactly match the voice script.  Minor gripe there, but a little sloppy.Where the game fails is from a technical standpoint.  It runs awfully,  FPS drops are a common theme, and I reached a sequence (the "protoplasmic abomination") after about 50ish minutes of play where I simply could no longer progress because the framerate dropped to nothing and the sound became stuttered and glitched, the screen jumped around and my character could barely move causing me to be killed by AI and unable to get to the next area.  Today (2/22/21) the dev team announced a patch that supposedly fixed the FPS issues, so when I logged in to try it out and hope I could finally progress, I was extremely frustrated to discover that the patch had erased my save game completely.  I wasn't about to re-do the entire first section of the game just to get back where I was, so barring a solution from the dev team I'm done with this title.Additionally, the menus are lacking basic setting options that any modern PC game should have for graphics (for example, only offering "borderless" and "windowed" but not standard fullscreen, and displaying resoultions in terms of "1080p" or "720p" instead of the actual WxH screen resolution.  Again, minor nitpick but it comes across as super-budget. So yeah, while I hate leaving a bad review for a game... I have to in this case.  I was extremely hyped for the Lovecraftian design of this game and what I thought it was going to offer me based on the demo I played, and the final product here is a total mess of frustration that I wouldn't wish on anyone.  If the dev team fixes the problems (and makes it possible for me to resume where I left off originally) I will be more than happy to revisit this review and update my recommendation.  But right now, steer clear, especially at this price.It's a $10 game at a $25 price point that runs like $1 shovelware.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOODThis is a VERY good H.P. Lovecraft Cosmic Horror game. There are MANY mindblowing experiences with . And I mean... MINDBLOWING up-close moments!One of my favorite aspects of this game, is that it isn't the typical... "You are a detective that needs to solve a murder, or take down a cult" type tropes, which you usually see in EVERY cosmic horror game out there. The creatures in the game are amazing, and if you are a "H.P. Lovecraft geek" like me, it will fulfill some fantasies that you won't see in other cosmic horror games. Make sure you investigate and read notes to get the best experience possible. :)THE BADWhile the game itself blows my mind and is my favorite cosmic horror game to date, it does come with some "quality test issues" hehe...You will frequently encounter floating assets (like the seagulls), and awkward invisible walls, to the point where it makes you wonder if the developer had anyone play test his game. And some textures look VERY low ress compared to other high ress, which makes you constantly go... "wow the game looks beautifu.... nevermind" hehe. ':D Essentially my point is that it feels like the last 10% effort wasn't put into the quality of the game and to fix obvious bugs.The water in the game has some weird visuals from time to time. As well as having a weird "line" at the bottom of the screen when the player stands in the water.The default audio in the game is extremely unbalanced. Voice acting is VERY low, and I recommend turning it up in the options.The voice acting of all characters are top notch! Except for , who is EXTREMELY ... and I really mean it... EXTREMELY bad compared to the rest of the characters. ':D I'm usually not very critical about voice acting, but this person stuck out like a sore thumb... It kinda felt like professional voice actors were hired for all the characters, except for this one character who might have been a "non-voice actor" the developer knew and did a favor for... The main menu and options look VERY "indie game"... Or "prototype'e".(Not a "bad", but just an observation) Screen recorders have trouble capturing the game.CONCLUSIONThis is a unique experience that ANY cosmic horror fans should play! While the game has some technical issues, they won't in any way outweigh the positives. :) Even though I might have written more "negatives" in this review hehe, it still is one of my favorite indie games of all time! :)

_childDocuments_.review: An Enigmatic Journey Through the Uncharted - "The Shore"ReviewOverall Rating: 9/10"The Shore" is a first-person horror adventure game developed by Ares Dragonis and published by Dragonis Studio. This indie title offers players an immersive and atmospheric experience that delves into Lovecraftian horror and cosmic mysteries while exploring the enigmatic world of a deserted island.Storyline : 8/10The game follows the journey of Andrew, a man in search of his missing daughter, who stumbles upon a mysterious and foreboding island. As he explores the island's eerie landscapes and encounters otherworldly beings, he unravels a complex narrative that blends elements of cosmic horror and psychological torment. "The Shore" stands out for its captivating storytelling, and it keeps players engaged with its intriguing and enigmatic plot.Gameplay : 7/10"The Shore" emphasizes exploration, puzzle-solving, and a sense of dread rather than action-packed gameplay. The puzzles are well-crafted and contribute to the game's overall sense of mystery. However, some players may find the pacing slow, and a few mechanics might feel a bit clunky at times. Nevertheless, the game's eerie ambiance and intriguing world make up for these minor shortcomings.Graphics and Atmosphere : 9/10Visually, "The Shore" is a striking game. The island's environments are beautifully rendered, and the attention to detail in its eerie landscapes is impressive. The lighting and sound design work harmoniously to create a palpable atmosphere of dread and wonder, immersing players in the otherworldly island setting.Horror Elements : 8/10The game excels in delivering a slow-burning, psychological horror experience. It relies on unsettling visuals, eerie soundscapes, and a sense of impending doom to build tension. "The Shore" effectively captures the essence of Lovecraftian horror, making you question the nature of reality and your own sanity as you delve deeper into the island's secrets.Conclusion : 9/10"The Shore" is a captivating and atmospheric indie horror game that manages to create a compelling Lovecraftian narrative and a sense of unease. Its well-executed storytelling, stunning visuals, and psychological horror elements make it a must-play for fans of the genre. While the gameplay may not be action-packed and could use a bit more polish, the overall experience is hauntingly satisfying. If you enjoy thought-provoking horror games that immerse you in a world of cosmic mysteries and existential dread, "The Shore" is an island worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game, I'm changing my review to a negative one. That's because after the incredible opening hour, the game takes MASSIVE nosedive in quality. The titular shore is incredibly atmospheric and immersive, to the point my initial review called it "the most atmospheric game I've ever played" - and to about half point of the game that is true.But later on we trade the moody, misty seashore for a more otherworldly environments, and those are less than stellar. Confusing, murky, repetitive. And the game starts trowing chase sequences at you. Again, and again, and again. It's seriously the only gameplay trick in its book, and those are done horribly - they're confusing, repetitive, and so overturned that I had to restart each of them at least 10 times.The atmosphere also goes to ♥♥♥♥. Long gone are quiet moment and environmental storytelling. The game becomes an endless gallery of monsters shown of with little buildup and fanfare. I truly was done with the game when it introduced Cthulhu, in a scene that lacks any semblance of buildup of pathos, and he started monologing about "mere mortals" and "seeing my world destroyed" in an accent so thick that I believe it to be the developer himself. It seriously felt like a joke.I do not recommend The Shore. Not because its without merit - parts of it are truly great- but because of how disappointing it is. It will take me a couple of days to get that anger out of my system, this could have been something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of walking sims and usually when I stumble into one, labeled as something with actual gameplay, I end up annoyed, disappointed and ready to write a negative review. Especially when most of them are very similar, relying on cheap jumpscares or closing and opening the doors until something happens. But this one? This one I like. It's by no means perfect, some of the more action like sequences were frustrating and I got stuck on a puzzle or two, but it was easy to forgive, when the game got something else perfectly. The lovecraftian atmosphere, the eeriness, the quiet, cold dread of something ancient and incomprehensible. You find objects and see creatures you don't understand. The more you look at the world, the little details, the less sense it makes, yet at the same time it's somehow believable. On this vast, nearly barren shore the main character meets with the eldritch and the further he goes, the more he is unable to turn back. Was it actually *scary*? I'm not sure, not really. But deeply unsettling, it left me with a quiet sense of dread as I watched something rise from the sea, or stood in front of imposing obelisk, purpose of which I was unable to understand. I feel like few games actually nail the cosmic horror. And despite its' lackluster gameplay and some frustrating action sequences, this one manages it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages to fail at being a walking simulator and at conveying any sense of fear despite basing itself on the Cthulhu mythos. The "gameplay" could hardly be more bare : you pick up seemingly random stuff, use said random stuff as a key on some random contraption — congratulations, that was actually a "puzzle" — then some tentacles show up and do basically nothing for a few seconds. Thought that was spooky ? No ? Then nothing in this game has any chance to scare you. Oh, sometimes you have to press "run" for a few seconds to run from a monster in a corridor until some script ends the chase. Thought that was tense ? No ? Too bad, that's all you get. The only challenge you'll encounter is figuring where to go or what to do next because the game even fails at making your objective clear at any point. Conclusion : run away if you have any real expectations from a game about Lovecraft's universe. This is just a tasteless cash grab made by scrubs who thought that showing tentacles after 10 minutes is what cosmic horror is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: A stricken Arthur awakens to sand, sea, and shipwreck. Weathered igneous formations loom formidably over fields of augite pebbles that lurch down to the lapping tongue of dark water’s edge. A phantasmal phalanx of dense, twisted palm emerges from wistful mist and hectors from higher inland ground, menacingly mocking both freedom of movement and clarity of perception. A memento, a clear memory of a dear moment with young daughter Ellie, stands in flagrant dissimilitude to the unimaginable horrors ahead. Dearest readers, I bid you a solemn welcome to The Shore; leave now… if you can.Still here? How unfortunate.Steel your hearts then, readers, and humble your mere human ego and prepare to crawl as though ants among a veritable who’s who of the caliginous Lovecraftian pantheon, where friends are few and self-serving, and foes are immense and unstoppable.And butt-ugly. Lovecraft=off. BeatYourHeadIn=on!The Shore is a faithful delve into the beloved mythos. It adheres to the general Lovecraft vibe, from the towering immortals and gods, to the unwholesome bestial talismans honed with skill beyond that of human craftsmanship, and including the incredulous characters who initially and foolishly dismiss the supernatural as observed by their own eyes with deficient secular explanations, such as psychosis, madness, and somnambulism; it’s all here. Even the usual binary of outcomes for most Lovecraft protagonists who have seen too much—either a self-euthanization as an escape from the un-cope-able or a shockingly willing embrace of dark forces beyond the knowable—both seem to be in play as possible conclusions right up until the closing action. No spoilers, though, as to which way this episode turns.As a story driven walking-simulator, The Shore exhibits a potent—though not flawless—execution. Puzzles of various sorts act as barriers to plot progress; the majority are simple to solve, with a few challenging ones sprinkled about to spool up your think-noodle. The puzzles themselves are done well. Solving them indeed lends a sense of accomplishment, and they and their outcomes tie into the plot in a sensible fashion. Sensible for Lovecraft, that is; the man dreamed beyond three dimensions and five senses, after all. The progression of the story is at all times kept in sharp focus, which is fine as it is a good story, but I feel that the linear nature of the journey along the beaches represents a missed opportunity and, in my opinion, contributes to the short time in which the game is completed.Thus, the game falls somewhat short in the exploration aspect due to the extensive use of invisible walls to corral you onto the linear path set forth by the developer. This should have been addressed properly by the use of blocking terrain features such as higher rock bluffs and dense jungle thicket, and/or some sort of feedback that insinuates something like, say, dark energies that are preventing the player from traversing the open areas. It was a little frustrating to climb boulders and see places beyond only to be obstructed from further exploration by a poorly placed invisible wall. A tough pill to swallow, indeed. Even something like a dense mist with a spooky ambiance that induces such a level of fear as to cause Arthur to utter a verbal refusal to enter it would have been more appropriate. Regrettably, I’m left wondering what a more open exploration of the island setting would have played like.What the game absolutely nails is the hair-raising and unsettling experience of a Lovecraft story. I felt genuine dread of and reluctance to witness the malevolence that the plot on several occasions built up prior to the reveal. Due to active participation in the story via the gaming medium, one’s sense of fear and nerve-tingles is heightened beyond that delivered by a reading. The Shore serves as another example of how videogaming has cemented itself as a worthy component in the history of storytelling.However, I hold that reading is still superior for this purpose, as there are details in Lovecraft’s works which I am convinced cannot be rendered by 3D modelling. Passages that hint of infernal interdimensional travel like “…one night a mighty gulf was bridged, and the dream-haunted skies swelled down to the lonely watcher’s window to merge with the close air of his room…” just cannot be visualized outside of the minds’ eye. High five to all my bookworms out there!Another rock solid segment of The Shore is its soundtrack. The music shifts from hopeful but subdued operatic scores, to musical denials of certain doom that hang over scenes of terror frozen in time like a ghostly echo of forgotten trauma, to the sinister ambiance of a technological environment produced by wholly alien industry, and swelling to impactful crescendos during scenes when monumental, awe-inspiring power has been unleashed, and does so with appropriate timing. The audio is tied to the visuals in a sincere and effective manner so that the sum of the two is greater than the parts alone. The game absolutely thrives on this photo-phonic unity.So, while not being a match for the exemplary exploration gameplay of The Solus Project—an excellent walking simulator horror game made without invisible walls by a similarly sized indie developer—The Shore more than holds its own as a delivery of an immersive atmosphere. Since the price of setting foot on The Shore is one half of the cost to crash land on more fleshed out creepy-island-to-cry-oneself-to-sleep-on of The Solus Project, it means that both games are on equal footing by my reckoning. In conclusion, there is no need to wait for a sale for this game, it is more than worth the full price of admission, even though it is a little shorter than it should be. An absolute must play for fans of H.P. Lovecraft.Helpful review?

_childDocuments_.review: As a game made by a small team on a budget, this is amazing, but perhaps a bit short, The gameplay varies from investigation and puzzle solving to lite combat and survival. I did play through twice for all the achievements, still can't figure out the last one! Dispite this, I do feel like it could have had more side content. As far as the price, its fine, your money isn't wasted here, its hopefully funding another great title like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's not perfect but I did like it. It's an epic piece of walking game-art. Epic scenes with all that monsters and other interior stuff - those are awesome! Really, those gigantic creatures makes your blood freezes.Form negatives there are only animations as for me. I really liked this 1 hour story. Much better than many other Lovecraft adaptations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game?  I like the Easter eggs from the Lovecraft stories (Colour out of Space, Dagon, etc).  The story seems nice and well within the genre.  Some of the puzzles can be frustrating and very little help is given which is fine; you shouldn't expect to be held by the hand in a game all the time.  It is very linear and there seems to be only a few achievements you can miss (chess game, secret ritual, coins).  The story needs more depth and choices.  There is so much more that could be added to this game and it seems a shame to be limited to only one path and one ending.  Overall buy it on sale or just watch a playthrough on youtube.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While I think the game possesses some very interesting imagery, a solid soundtrack and good (sometime almost photo-realistic) graphics; and would make a decent ride for die hard Lovecraft fans I can't recommend it to anyone because of many reasons :-The plot is nonsensical and just used as a cheap device to guide you through a Lovecraftian slide show-The puzzles aren't even worth being called this way-The level design is atrocious and combines the worst flaws of open world design and corridor design, filled with dead ends and invisible walls.-Voice actors are some random dudes from Fiverr with varying microphone qualities-The script is broken English and even the voice actors refuse to read most of it.-The "combat" is laughably trash and shouldn't even be in the game to begin with-The gameplay and chase sequences are broken and not fun to say the least-The big encounters with the Cthulhu mythos monsters are ruined with garbage choppy animations.I really liked the design of the monsters, the overall vibe of the game is alright but I really think it should have been a walking sim with a solid plot, this would have really suited the game better. The product we have here feels like it is some portfolio of a guy that is really into Lovecraft and wants to show us that he can design stuff.Buy it on a sale if you are desperate for Lovecraft content and you played everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing it as an Indie game. Difference is, it's not made by an army of developers in between 3 continents.On the Plus sideThe game has a great atmosphere, and nice graphics and music. The hero's voice is really good also!The controls are simple with the movement of the player being overall ok. The story is great, paying tribiute to all the good Lovecraftian stories. (Call of Cthulhu, Dagon, The color out of the sky etc.).On the Down SideThe game is short, and has almost no riddles. So it's like playing a novel with a few bits and peaces to put together that are very easy to figure out. Overall I enjoyed spending 3.5 hours on it. Would I pay 10€ for it? No. I paid 2 and I'm happy I've spent that much. If you like Lovecraft, and enjoy a good armosphere with an easy gameplay, don't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. The darkest Lovecraft Mythos game I've played yet. The atmosphere is excellent, and I'm glad everything is voice acted so I don't have to spend time reading every letter.There are a few minor issues, the game doesn't bother to tell you that sprint/jump/etc aren't unlocked at the beginning of the game.Overall This game is really impressive and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I usually really like Lovecraft inspired games, but this is not one of them.Besides the decent graphics, is a tedious, clunky mess.The game is extremely poorly optimized.Various functionality (running, jumping) gets taken away at random, seemingly with no real motivation, making this an extremely sluggish and tedious game.There's plenty of bugs, floating geometry, hanging game states (probably badly designed blueprints)The story is dull and uninspired. The Lovecraftian themes are too on the nose and uninspired, and leave nothing to the imagination.Then there's the endless invisible walls, dear lord, so many invisible walls.Oh, and the voice acting is something to behold, it's a Lovecraftian horror all on it's own seeing how bad it is.Give this a pass, as pretty as the pictures look like.It's a 2.5 hour shlog, and the only reason it takes 2.5 hours in stead of 1 is because the movement speed is like you're moving through treacle.Better spend your money on something like Call of the Sea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals and sound effects perfectly capture the eerie atmosphere and pure madness. If you are a fan of H.P. Lovecraft you will be pleasantly surprised. Not many games like this out there. It's short but does not hold your hand. The visuals have lots of inspiration from movies like The Thing, The Mist, Color Out of Space, Dagon and more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A good Lovecraftian walking simulator, but a bit rough around the edges.Good:The models & setting. The developer is clearly very well versed at modeling characters.The bad: The developer decided to voice a bunch of parts himself, and the obvious accent kind of seems out of place. The hired voice actors are good, and it probably would have been better to hire a whole cast. Also the "game" mechanics felt forced and unnecessary. Too many invisible walls, and tinkering with objects and switches with no logic or reason about what they were or how they work. The ugly:Animations were a pass. They conveyed the idea just fine, but at some times seemed twitchy or way to smooth. Also almost everything including the player clipped through walls.Overall the visuals of the game were decent, but a lot of small details brought me out of the immersion at times. The game certainly has an "indie" feel to it, so I suppose you get what you pay for. That said, I hope this game is successful enough to get another. The developer has a good mind of this and given a larger team, better resources and a little luck I could see him creating some very interesting games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This was a crowdfunded project that basically one dude did. I backed it as soon as I could as I saw the visuals and it looked promising. It delivered what I wanted. It had all the Old Ones I wanted to see, and the game play is not about action as much as it is figuring out a mystery and unlocking the Mythos. Some of the puzzles took me a bit to get, but overall I think this is a faithful representation of Lovcraftian horror. Considering this was a passion project from a fan, whom I supported on Facebook until it was live, I have to give this a positive review. All the negatives are from people who came in expecting a triple A experience from Ares Dragonis. That was never going to be the case. Buy this if you are a fan of the genre, because at it's core it is faithful to what we fans love. If you are a fan like me, "like" the positive comments like this one to make sure new people see them when they consider buying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A meagre 5 out of 10. To be honest, I deinstalled the game after 1.5 hours, I don't know how much longer it would have gone, but it had already started to annoy me about one hour in.Don't let yourself be fooled by the beginning and the visuals. Yes, both are great, but the rest of the game is not only very different but also ... just bad.While there is some semblance of a story in the beginning (shipwrecked on an island, searching for your daughter), it soon becomes clear that it is a mere varnish. It's really only two bucket loads of disconnected Cthulhu mythos icons, words and creatures all over the place, without any coherence or story telling about what happened here, what the point of it all is or what to do.After the mostly engaging beginning you are finding yourself fleeing from enemies, searching for exists, shooting a laser beam from some artifact weapon. And when they reach you, the screen flickers red and you die. There are some puzzles. Then more tunnels and fleeing from enemies. More laser beams. That’s when I deinstalled it. Nothing about this is scary or mysterious or engaging. I bought this on sale for 2.50, so it's fine, no reason to refund, but it still is nothing more than a pretty good starting scenario, like a proof of concept, for an unfinished game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for some time for a price reduction offer to buy this game, mostly by curiosity and support to my Greek compatriot Ares Dragonis, although I am not fun of this adventure like game genre. Haven't finished it yet, though I must say I am astonished by the atmosphere of the game. Very nice work Ares! The graphics, the music, the dialogues all work fine to produce a mystery and horror atmosphere. What needs more work to be done and somewhat ruins the experience is the control interface. There, some programming work is needed.To conclude is a yes! for me. Well done Ares. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Very short and visually impressive. A lot of jump cuts and the many chase sequences made everything feel a little bit clunky but overall enjoyable. Kinda feels like the many chase sequences were put in for time padding.Although I had a fairly fun 2 hours playing this game I have to say it's not worth the asking price. Currently on sale for $13~ CAD is a fair deal for what you get. Overall 7/10, a good narrative based on Lovecraft's works, some game but mostly story-telling.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game's strongest points are it's amazing visuals and great musical score, and these things alone are the biggest reasons why I enjoyed the game. One impressive thing about this game is that it was made mostly by two people, and while it is very good considering this fact, it does mean the game is unpolished right now and it will take some time and feedback before the major issues can be fixed. The biggest strikes against the game right now are repetitive chase sequences and confusing gameplay, like how it isn't clear what you are supposed to do for a lot of puzzles and it takes a while to get through some of them. Right now, I feel that the game's price is a bit high considering how unpolished the gameplay is, as well as how short the game is. Fortunately, the devs are actively gathering feedback on the game and are working hard to release hotfixes and improve the quality of the gameplay. Even though there are problems with the game right now, I'm sure that given time the devs will significantly improve the game. If you are a fan of Lovecraftian games, you should definitely buy this product. Despite it's flaws right now, it is still a great game, though you may want to wait a bit before playing to give the devs some time to smooth things out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice visuals, great setting, but I had no clue on what to do at a certain point. I didn't want to cheat and look up what to do. I can understand the difficulty in balancing something that can be easily figured out and something that is hard to figure out, but I seriously had no clue on what I was supposed to unlock, what I needed as a key, or where to go. Not enough direction.

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently it's mostly developed by one guy, and it's also his first game.Very enjoyable music and art design all across the board. Graphics look stunning in most locations, and it would be awesome in VR (if they add it sometime). They did a fairly good job making an immersive Lovecraftian experience, but even for its price tag it left me underwhelmed.The gaming experience as a whole was weak and short, with annoying level design and combat mechanics that are so poorly executed that I was constantly questioning why this is even in the game. Puzzles didn't feel rewarding, the story didn't engage me, and the immersion broke because of the transition (and teleporting) between scenes. The quality of the sound design was kind of all over the place. Voice acting was alright, but terrible at Not a terrible buy, but just barely not good enough to be recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game is called "The Shore" and you indeed begin your journey at a beach, however, this episode is only a short part of your wandering, which quickly grabs you into other Inter-dimensional places.First 30mins I was like "oh hey, another walking simulator". Then I turned to "сraр-сraр-сraр, run faster!!1".Wouldn't be a proper Lovecraftian game w/o "ewww" moments. Ever wondered what it's like going in a hands tunnel? Or... spinal, veins pulsing cave?Ever craved to be chased by numerous gnarly creatures? Ever dreamed of ripping hands of petrified humans, because you need them for a puzzle?Oh my Elder Gods. The sound in the game is great! Ambient: vibrations, voices in a head, footprints when stomping meaty corridors, oof!Creatures: they SCARY! they LOUD! I want to run away from those horrible beings! That Dagon though... what a roar and... the climb afterwards XDFrom a slow paced daily landscape gazing "yay, another sea shell" to a fast chase "I see nothing!" sequence and hold your breath moments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked The Shore. Lovecraft with a soundtrack worthy of the movie Annihilation.It's weird, it's grotesque, it's obscure. Short, but well-made, with a twist in the tale. If you're a fan of Lovecraft, like walking sims and the odd (but fairly straightforward) puzzle, with incredible sound and visuals, you won't be disappointed with The Shore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a real shame writing this. During the first moments I was reminded of games like Zeno Clash, Amnesia or Myst even where you had this bleak, exploration type of feel with that indie feel. 2.1 hours later, it was over, and a lot of that time spent on frustrating mechanics. I'll do a break down of the different aspects of the game to help you better understand where it succeeds and fails.The Good:-The monsters, they look great-The music, it's different and has this mix between creepy ambiance and cosmic noise.-The main character's voice actor. I know this will probably be controversial but I enjoyed it.Unfortunately, that's where the pros stop.The bad:-Length, it will take you 1.5 hours to beat it, going through at a regular pace. This depends on your luck with some puzzles.-The puzzles. Your hand isn't held with puzzles. At all. Which isn't bad, provided they made sense. One of the puzzles has you picking up skulls on the ground, until you find the right one and "feeding" them to a object on the ceiling. I say feeding because you hold them up and they drop to the ground when they are incorrect. There are like 100 of these skulls on the ground and only one of them correct I think. So every incorrect one creates a pile on the ground covering the other skulls....This is just one example.-The voice acting. Aside from the main character, it's BAD. Some of them are REAL bad.-Paths and level design. The game lets you crouch and jump, but you're going to laugh when you realize how little that means. The paths are linear in this game but you are given a fairly open environment. Which leads you to trying to go over rocks and obstacles that would not even require you to jump in real life to overcome, and be met with invisible walls. Invisible walls everywhere.-Optimization. Using a I9-9990K with a GTX 1080 I had stuttering throughout the entire game. There is never more than a few enemies on the screen at one time, so not sure what the issue is.-Interface. You have an inventory but you can't do anything with it. You can crouch but I think I used it twice? There is a section that tells you to avoid a monster and so I assumed I should crouch to "stealth" but boy was that a joke. Same with jumping. I think I used jump once to get over poorly laid objects around a puzzle.-Combat. Sluggish and confusing. Combat was implemented to basically slow your character down. There was only one true boss fight in the game. A second if you can call it that and both feature puzzles that require you to active a circle of objects around the "arena" that you fight in.It sucks, because if the developer had treated this game as a Myst style exploration game and just stuck to the allure of puzzles and the spectacle of the monsters, he would have had a winner. Instead poor dialogue, story, combat and cheap puzzles in a 1.5 hour package....all for $25. I wanted this to be my new Zeno Clash, an underappreciated gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: So before I bought and played the game I checked the comments and one of them said "Cthulhu throws you a ship". It made me not want to buy the game right away because I expect Cthulhu to have less action but more "existence". But the visuals and music were so charming, when it went to discount I bought it immediately. I had some small issues at first launch but i got over them quickly. Then I proceeded on playing the game and here's my scoring.10/10 atmosphere10/10 character design10/10 music7/10 story (I liked the direction, but I can't help but feel it could have been more detailed)6/10 gameplay but I didn't buy the game for the gameplay so it was good enough8/10 Cthulhu mythos (-2 because Cthulhu is definitely a bit out of character, throwing ship does happen, Dagon and Azatoth were good though)So basically I liked the game, but only because I knew what I was purchasing. If I hadn't known it was a short game with kind of hard gameplay (hard as in annoying). I listed a lot of issues there but if you are a fan of cosmic horror, not necessarily Lovecraft, you would like this game. I really appreciate developer for making this game, it truly does what it advertises in the trailer: shows you amazing visuals, has great music and does have some gameplay so you don't just sit and watch.

_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game, but not whole-heartedly.  It has some problems....it also has some really great aspects too.  The Shore is a Lovecraftian (boy, is it ever!) first person horror walking simulator with some light to medium combat (it's technically light, but it is difficult to get used to mechanically {for me anyway}, and very little of it is explained, so it's harder than it should be).Positives:-Graphics-  Bloody incredible!  Seriously, there is just some phenomenal creature modelling and environmental design/texturing, especially when it comes to depicting a wide assortment of Lovecraftian nasties ranging from Deep Ones to Nyarlothotep to Cthulhu himself and quite a few things in between.Meh:-Storyline/Writing-  Starts out strong but then just goes all over the bloody place and I'm not sure the pasta all sticks to the wall (if you know what I mean).  It tries to be coherent, but I can't help but think that English isn't the first language of the game-maker, and it really shows, not just for clumsy phraseology but for a meandering, not entire cohesive narrative.-Gameplay-  It's largely a walking simulator, with some definite failure states if you don't dodge some attacks or use the "weapon" to destroy the appropriate creatures at the appropriate time (or at least delay them long enough to get yourself closer to your goal....get used to running while shooting backwards).  So, it's sometimes press right to win, and other times a little bogged down in clumsy "shooting" mechanics.  Not awful, and only moderately detracts from enjoyment, but it's not exactly a 100% pleasurable experience either.To sum up, I am recommending this game because I love Lovecraftian horror/cosmic horror themes, and seeing the world brought to life was highly enjoyable (and some of those vistas......dayum!), but it is absolutely not without some flaws.  Caveat emptor and all that jazz.

Tries to be Cthulhu, has no idea what that means.Go play Fortnite, it got a better story than this.

_childDocuments_.review: A Hauntingly Beautiful and Terrifying Experience 👁️🌊The Shore is a thrilling dive into a world where the lines between horror and reality blur in the most atmospheric way possible. 🎮🌑 From the moment you step onto the eerie shores, you're greeted with an unsettling beauty that draws you in and keeps you hooked, despite the constant dread lurking in the shadows. 👀🌾The first-person perspective really pulls you into the story, making you feel like you're the one unraveling the secrets of this mysterious island. The creatures you'll encounter are chillingly unique, and every corner hides something that will make you question your own sanity. The storytelling is deeply immersive, with enough twists to keep you guessing at every turn. 🧩⚡The environment is beautifully crafted, with intricate details that set the mood perfectly. Whether you're exploring abandoned ruins or facing off against horrific entities, the game keeps you on edge while captivating you with its dark, atmospheric world. 🌒🖤If you're a fan of psychological horror with a gripping narrative and mysterious lore, The Shore is a must-play. It’s a game that sticks with you long after you’ve put it down. Prepare to question everything you thought you knew about reality... and maybe even yourself. 🌀👻Highly recommend for fans of atmospheric horror that doesn't shy away from making you uncomfortable! 🌙Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: Although I am not a particular fan of Lovecraft or Lovecraft-ian lore and monsters, I think this is a brilliantly original game with beautiful graphics, sound, and music.  It has its flaws in game play but the world-building and atmosphere alone are worth a couple hours of your time.I may never finish this game but I'm glad I spent the money to support this artist/designer and his team.

_childDocuments_.review: There is this beautiful illustrated edition of The Call of Cthulhu with art by Franсois Baranger. This game  reminds me of that one, at least the color palette. Although narrative in this game is its weakest point, it is really immersive. All this megalomaniac forms, compositionally verified environments and strong sound design creates the vibe necessary for lovecraftian adaptation. This game has the same flaws as Scorn, it is the closest analog to this game. I finished and enjoyed Scorn despite everything. If you enjoyed Scorn you will like this one. It`s like with Panos Cosmatos movies. You are not watching it for the plot. You either get it or you don`t. So, if you are tired of mainstream and are looking for something fresh, here is an interesting greek walking simulator for cosmic horror aesthetic enjoyers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Really impressive visuals and set pieces, despite the small team. Some of the "puzzles" felt a bit incoherent (the room with the heads on the floor being the worst), but nothing I couldn't really brute force my way through. Combat sections felt a bit tacked on, and I wish the artifact had a bit more "umph" to it in terms of audio and enemy impact. I did like that it was basically a Quake lightning gun though in terms of its functionality. Other than that, I think the overall audio design and voice acting is pretty good for an indie title. There's some pretty deeply unsettling sounds in this game.I finished the game in about 2.3hrs, but also got it on sale for $3.59, so I felt I got my moneys worth. The story kind of takes a backseat to the actual gameplay experience, but I enjoyed the constant sense of mystery and dread. I love that it's a Lovecraftian game that gets straight to the point and doesn't let off the gas. There are some collectibles and achievements, some of which are missable, so there is a tiny bit of replayability if you want to 100% it. I'd recommend picking it up on sale.Minor gripes (bug report for the devs): -Fullscreen option isn't selectable (have to use borderless)-Voice volume setting doesn't really seem to change anything. Voiceover volume was still a bit all over the place.-Changing pretty much any setting, or Alt+tabbing while playing caused me to be locked in place when exiting the menu/returning to the game (couldn't move camera or character) - hitting ESC twice was a workaround.-Discord Server invite link on the main screen is invalid ("may be expired, or you might not have permission to join")
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, if you are a fan of Lovecraft, you must experience this game. But, on a sale.The art team is the saving grace of this experience, they nailed the weird, cosmic, surreal feeling and aesthetic that is needed when you're dealing with a genre like this. This is one of my favourite games visually in a very long time, perhaps ever. I cannot stress enough how incredible this game looks. It bumps up a average story with a fantastic musical soundtrack to something truly special. Unfortunately, that's where the pros end.I honestly would've preferred a straight walking simulator than what I got. Long stretches of corridors and land where I spent 15+ minutes wandering around figuring out where to go next. The level design is appalling at showing where I am needed next or where I can go, where you consistently hit invisible walls. This includes crucial story items that almost entirely blend into the environment at times. The "puzzles" scattered throughout these areas boil down to arbitrarily clicking or spinning things and interacting on an object that looks like scenery or a random set piece. These are coupled with enemy and chase sequences that include running in a straight line and shooting a couple times. Gameplay sections are bookended with dialogue that posses voice acting that is maybe good 50% of the time. Just to add, I can right click to bring up a "modify text" box on the pause menu. Really guys?Saying all this, the art team and lore 100% carry this experience, and at only a couple hours in length it is well worth your time (on a sale). Especially Lovecraft fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The shore is a very troubled game. The gameplay for most of this is atrociously bad. If you are turned away from games for terrible gameplay alone, then do not buy this. If you love games with good atmosphere, setting, and visuals and you can overlook some bad gameplay, then you should consider getting this. Most of the gameplay in this game will be annoying chase sequences (that really aren't scary) followed by a short puzzle. I think the gameplay issues could have easily been solved by making this a walking simulator with a few puzzles sprinkled in. The audio here is really good in some areas, and not so good in others. Some of the visuals and locations throughout this game are really quite amazing and very lovecraftian.If you plan to get this game, wait for a sale. The game is about 2 - 3 hours long, so keep that in mind when choosing how much to buy it for.

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest this game was not what I expected. I saw a part of a play through for this game on the clock app and it looked incredibly interesting. Maybe my expectations were a bit too high but I feel as though this game has a lack of substance. To be clear i'm not saying its bad... its just not good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: If you have thalassophobia or megalophobia, this game might actually kill you. I had to stop to catch my breath several times so i didn't pass out while playing. That's not a negative criticism btw, the fact that a video game is able to trigger those phobias so effectively is a testament to the developers attention to detail. On top of that, this is probably the most accurate representation of what I call "the Lovecraft experience" that I've ever seen in a video game. It manages to satisfy curiosity while answering basically none of the questions it asks while simultaneously representing Lovecraft's work with layers of detail rich cosmic horror I've never really seen in a video game. It also does more with it's three hour runtime than something like Outlast does with it's 6-8 hour experience. Some might see that as a negative criticism as game length is usually a divisive subject and many people prefer quantity over quality, but I'm telling you that I will play this multiple times over before I ever revisit a pile of s*** like Outlast ever again. This is one of the best examples of what can be done within the confines of the highly stigmatized "first person indie horror" genre. This developer deserves a ton of credit for pulling this off. No AAA game, no television series, rarely any films have ever managed to create such a faithful adaptation of Lovecraft's work. If you're a fan of Lovecraftian horror, first person horror, or just horror in general, DO NOT skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: For one-man studio it is an adorable attempt. The visuals, the aesthetics and the atmosphere of this game stays at very high level, especially at the beginning.Unfortunately that's all the good things.As longer you play it, the game starts to look like an alpha version of a very promising huge project. Significantly it is a collection of ideas and beautiful small locations merged by the very weak plot and primitive mechanics. It reminded me a kind of similar walking simulator indie game - The Solus Project with a difference that the last one is a complete work (mediocre but still), while The Shore feels and plays as a sketch.There is still a potential.Hope Ares Dragonis will build a bigger team in the future to be able to fulfil his ideas into a big impressive project.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve seen a lot of lackluster reviews for this game; with all due respect they are wrong. This is simply one of the best horror games I have played in the last couple years. Not just a PT clone or reliant on jump scares; it is gorgeous, well-paced, atmospheric, and a treasure trove if you are a Lovecraft fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Full review: TL;DR:Despite there being some cool moments and designs in The Shore that I really liked, I cannot recommend it to even the most enthusiastic H.P. Lovecraft fan. In many ways, The Shore is like a haunted house ride that is going through all of Lovecraft’s ‘greatest hits’ as you wander the area. Unfortunately, its also like a ride that falls off the tracks and dumps you into a hall of mirrors, forcing you to wander for hours as you bump into walls you didn’t realize were there. There are some really cool things about The Shore that it does right to make you feel like you’re in a Lovecraft story, but they are quickly overshadowed by the miserable experience of playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a mesmerizing journey that transports players to a world of mystery and intrigue, offering a captivating experience that kept me enthralled from start to finish.From the moment I set foot on the eerie shores of a mysterious island, I was immediately drawn into its atmospheric and immersive world. The game's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking landscapes and hauntingly beautiful environments that create a sense of wonder and awe. Every step I took felt like an exploration of the unknown, as I uncovered the island's secrets and unraveled its mysteries.But what truly sets The Shore apart is its storytelling. The game weaves a rich and engaging narrative, filled with twists and turns that kept me guessing until the very end. As I delved deeper into the island's dark past and encountered its enigmatic inhabitants, I found myself completely immersed in the game's lore and mythology, eager to uncover the truth behind the mysteries that lay hidden within.In addition to its compelling narrative, The Shore also boasts atmospheric sound design and a hauntingly beautiful score that adds to the overall sense of immersion. From the distant cries of seabirds to the eerie whispers of the island's secrets, every sound drew me further into the game's world, heightening the tension and excitement with each passing moment.Overall, The Shore is a masterful blend of storytelling, atmosphere, and gameplay that offers a truly unforgettable gaming experience. Whether you're a fan of atmospheric horror games or simply looking for a captivating adventure to embark on, The Shore is a journey you won't soon forget. So grab your flashlight, steel your nerves, and prepare to uncover the secrets that lie hidden within the depths of The Shore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would like to like this game, I just can't.The controls are more than poor, the sound is far too variable in terms of volume and the gameplay is more like a tech demo than a game.The length of the game and the story, some of which makes no sense, are also suboptimal.Not a purchase recommendation for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this because we need more indie games but really is more of a mixed bag.This game really could have used more time in QA. I came across an issue with my character getting stuck when the window lost focus. The menu items were interactable when not visible. The 'combat' was really awful. It shouldn't exist in a game like this but it's even worse when it's implemented this poorly. There were a few moments when I was like, "This isn't Lovecraftian lore accurate and sort of make the characters feel cheap and not mysterious."Other than that, most of the puzzles were pretty great and not overly complicated (the head one was awful though). The atmosphere was pretty on theme, the music was fitting, and there were a good amount of creepy level designs. I liked getting story bits through the messages in a bottle but some of the other lore notes weren't voice acted which felt odd.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly surprised. The game is like "Scary Myst"I expected this to on the rails and story driven. What I did not expect is the amazing imagery and scenes that have been created in this game. Being in the cosmos recovering the ancient artifact weapon was so flipping cool. I also didn't think your dude could die. I was wrong. _childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a gift from my friend Giovanni.Graphically is well made. The atmosphere is really good.On the other hand it's very slow ( it's a walking simulator and the running and jumping mechanics will be unlocked further in the game ) and it was a bit hard to keep up to reach the ending.THE DEVELOPER HAS A REALLY HIGH POTENTIAL, waiting to see some other game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: GRADE: C+. The Shore is really more of a First Person VR Visual Novel. Its a chill game where you explore a creepy island straight outta Lovecraft's wildest dreams. Even when played without the VR set its  still optimized for keyboard and mouse, but its does get a little extra Shiny when you play through a VR head set. The Best thing about his game is the atmosphere and the stunning visuals. The Puzzles and actual game play are both pretty easy and I beat the game and got all the achievements in about 4 hours. However that's probably the right portion size for this game and it kept it from getting old, and since i didnt pay too much im happy enough with it.   The Shore is a walking simulator/visual novel steeped in the unsettling lore of H.P. Lovecraft. The game uses characters and references from his expanded mythos, crafting an eerie atmosphere that sets a creepy tone that does right by the subject matter. The Story is interesting but vague and not everyone will be pleased with the way it is concluded. Still there are some very striking parts of this game (especially in VR) and Some of the visuals are mind-bendingly awesome Also be prepared for some genre whiplash. The first act unfolds like a classic first-person point-and-click adventure. As you explore the environment you collect items and bits of story while solving puzzles. Click this, grab that, piece together some eldritch backstory. But the second act just throws you into a series of static scenes and adds some rudimentary combat. While its not inherently bad its just basic and these elements feel a bit out of place compared to the slow-burn exploration of the first act. Still some of the most memorable parts of the game are presented in these scenes. Overall i felt it was worth the handful of hours it took to run through this game. But i cant see why i would ever play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this, but at half the price. would give it a 5 out of 10.Overall The Shore is a very short game with some fantastic visuals worth experiencing, but with some noticeable issues towards the middle. Spattered throughout the experience are a number of nifty nods (sometimes a little more than nods) to various movies and books and it is clear that this is someone's passion project. Gameplay comes in at just under 4 hours (hence the lower price suggestion). Could have used some sort of objective tracking or hint system (a difficulty system perhaps). Combat when it arrived was a little clunky but not bad. Story needed a bit more fleshing out and planning. The ending left just a little to be desired. Despite the middle rating I feel like this was a fantastic first effort and would like to see what else the developer could produce.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well... Let's start with what all reviews say... The Shore is short (2.5 hours).The game is not bad, it has a wonderful soundtrack and beautiful graphics.The vibe and atmosphere are great and very lovecraftian.Voice acting in some parts is bad and even funny.But what makes me unable to recommend it is the fact that the game has no logic in it, not in the riddles and not in the story.There is no real choice here and it feels like you are tangling along the character and not playing it.Most of the time you'll find yourself die several times to understand what is needed to be done.All the above is summary why I can't recommend this game (unless it is in very high discount) and that's a shame because artistically The Shore is gorgeous and has so much potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to preface this by saying that if you enjoy the Lovecraftian, you should just play this game, no research needed. Otherwise, while I would love to say that this game was absolutely perfect, it definitely needs some polishing.      The atmosphere was always amazing, the graphics were  good, and in general the overall concept of the game is fantastic. That being said, it has a lot of minor issues that do very minorly detract from the experience. On the beach there is one shell that is untextured, and while it's not that obvious, there are probably >20 instances of that shell. The camera feels a bit floaty and the controlls seemed inconsistent at times. I spotted a few other oddities, like a creature that swam away, appeared in its original position t-posing, then disappeared again, but aside from just small things like this, there were never any major bugs. I'd recommend this to anyone who's a fan of this genre or even just enjoys good atmospheres and stories, but it would be nice to see some of those flaws patched out eventually, even though I doubt that will ever happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I received THE SHORE as a gift from my partner. I am usually a fan of anything Lovecraftian, so I do not know, how it went undetected by me for so long. Probably because it is a “small” game, which by no means is a bad thing.Positive:+ The story of the game is short but great. It worked well with the tone the Lovecraftian works have and while fans of those do of course know what they deal with, I found it to be very captivating and entertaining. + The visual aesthetics are really good. Of course, there is some clipping here and there or a floating small rock, but altogether the textures, effects and placements are neatly done. The animation of the creatures and environment is beautiful, although the walking animation of the human (Andrew) is a bit clunky in comparison. + The Audio (music and effect sounds) is nice to listen at, not too loud and thematic. The voice-acting is really good. I enjoyed it a lot. Neutral:> The mechanics and controls are very simple. Some like it, some don’t. > The game is short (around 3-5h)). It’s nice to have a game that I simply can turn on and play without investing days of gaming in it, to somewhat get started. But of course, since I think it was a nice game, I am a bit sad that the journey is over already. > The game has two parts. The first being more of an explorative walking simulator with little lore snippets and puzzles to solve. Some are a bit challenging, while most stay very casual. As a fan of puzzles, it is a bit too casual for my liking, but I see the point of making it approachable to as many people as possible. That said, I still had a lot of fun exploring and solving. The second part however dives a little deeper into survival-horror-action stuff. The horror, for my taste, is mild, though there were one or two points, where I actually got a little scared (mainly because I hate failing though). Negative:- The keyboard controls are not changeable (at least it didn’t work for me). Not a big problem, though I like to place keys as I want to have them. - With the second part being a lot more action then the first, there were almost no real puzzles to solve and with hardly enough time for me to enjoy the environment while I ran from whatever the game threw at me. Some might like the change of pace, but I did not. I’d rather have played the whole game like the first part. It did an excellent job there while the second half just seemed to lack stuff. I went through with it, because the story was still worth it. - The fighting mechanic is very simplified and I wouldn’t have needed it at all. But that’s on me. With everything said, I really recommend this game. I had a lot of fun playing it and probably will do again. I am impressed with what was created here. The creator did an amazing job!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's kind of okay. Sort of. Maybe. Not really.It's a nice looking game and it's impressive if it's really just one guy that made all of it, but that's all it has going for it.Gameplay wise, it's a frustrating mess. It's pretty much a walking sim with a couple parts you defend against monsters. Even those parts are sort of trial and error, and honestly, really boring.The opening of the game works well as you search for clues and items; slowly building up tension and atmosphere. The item hunt does become tedious and there's a few "where the hell do I go?" moments, which becomes fairly annoying due to your character running at the pace of a snail and some of the areas being pretty large. Despite this the first third of the game is somewhat enjoyable. The next thing you know half of Lovecraft's bestiary is just thrown in to make an appearance whether it make sense or not. It gets to the point where the game simply becomes checklist of monsters to go through. Eventually I lost the Lovecraft atmosphere entirely and started to see more Beksiński or maybe Giger influence than anything. That's not too much the fault of the creator, as Lovecraftian aesthetics can be vague. I suppose an art style needed to be pulled from somewhere. Some design choices are questionable as well. Cthulhu seems kind of small, and I find it strange that he speaks at all. I believe Dagon was made around the same size. It may be nit-picky, but these are just choices that don't make sense.What little story there is unfortunately feels like it was ripped from one of those poor Lovecraft-inspired compilation books. That's really all can I say about it.Not trying to be overly harsh on this; it's a nice time waster for $6 and I'm sure this took a lot of work to accomplish for one person. The soundtrack is great. The opening is cool and it's really nice looking, but it's really lacking in all other aspects.

There is no "feel" that you are holding something with power. Finally; the BIG guy was a bit underwhelming. Still very cool but compared to what came before it...PROS: Maybe not state-of-the-art graphics but still very good. Animations wee well done.Probably the very best representations of the creatures and Gods of the Cthulhu Mythos ever portrayed in a game. Better than any movie! BRAVO on that Devs!For the price this is a must-have for H.P. Lovecraft fans!

_childDocuments_.review: What starts as a wonderfully atmospheric walking simulator quickly devolves into a mind-numbing monster chase with obtuse puzzle solving thrown in between encounters. Gorgeous island visuals, painted with a grey-blue hue and an abundance of fog, coupled with the low crashing of waves and the gritty crunch of sand and rock as you walk, provide perfect ambiance for what could have been a pretty good game. Within the first 20 minutes or so, this all melts away into a hodgepodge of tentacles and H.R. Giger-inspired statues with constant wailing and warbling in the background as large tentacle monsters chase you around constantly. Instead of the slow-paced exploration you first grow accustomed to, the majority of the game actually involves holding down the Shift key so you can endlessly sprint and periodically doing 180's so you can shoot a purple beam to slow down your pursuers. Everything becomes a slimy, jumbled mess of pulsating fleshy things, and it becomes more and more difficult to make out not only what you're looking at, but also what the game is expecting you to do in order to progress.This is probably the first and only time I've ever been disappointed in the fact that a game ISN'T a walking sim. Instead of Dear Esther we're given an amateur attempt at something like Agony or Scorn. Very bizarre, and ultimately very disappointing. Such a massive letdown for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice, fairly short Lovecraft game.Overall the themes, graphics and atmosphere were fantastic. I particularly loved the designs and textures throughout this experience.Where the game falls a little short however is the build and some game mechanics. I'll expand on a few points below:-First, although the environments are beautiful there seems to be some overlooked areas where rocks are floating or geometry hasn't been placed close enough together it allows the player to possibly get stuck in areas that look passable but aren't. Overall not a bad issue.-Second, probably the most problematic are level collisions. In one level I accidently walked or pushed through the wall to the outside of the level. I walked along a bit and managed to jump back into the boss room. -Third, the camera sensitivity is a bit wild which was a little bothersome. The curser position for interacting with objects I found a little too small at times. -Fourth, although miner I found some of the dialogue was hard to hear at times but it wasn't a deal breaker.  Overall, I enjoyed it, I had fun. I'd say if you want to support the developer get this game at full price. If you're mildly interested but not sure, wait till it's on sale and pick it up. It's visuals and designs are well worth it in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere and visuals are great, gameplaywise not so much.It's a walkin' sim which in my case is fine, I like to chill back a bit and listen/see a story unfold from time to time. The issues I have with the game are that there's really clunky 'combat' mixed in alongside invisible boundries that are set way too far away from your linear corridor path (you can climb onto rocks but no further then 30cm where it feels like you should be able to get over em, just set the invis wall nearer to the path then).There's a final 'boss' which you even get an achievement for which is laughable compared to some of the run and stun sections.I'd say watch a playthrough on youtube and forget about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game opens up with some nice exploration and exposition to the island, but after passing a certain threshold you are just running down a corridor and enjoying the sights. The sights are quite interesting, although I felt somewhat thrown off by the sheer amount of lovecraftian things stuffed together without real connection.Towards the end you are basically "fighting" one of the elder gods and then get a *fade to black* to fight the next one, it feels like a series of minigames loosely strung together.I would still recommend this game if it is on sale, but it does not feel like it's worth even the low price of 10 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I've read lots of Lovecraft and I love the myths. Played the rpg and read more about gods 'n stuff. I loved how this game showed some of more notable characters from the myths. The game itself was way too confusing without any real reason to wander around the island until you get to the very and are given some kind of a closure. It was ambitious to try and get all the gods in to one walking simulator and I think that made this game look more like a patchblanket showcase than a real game.Bought from sale and I don't think my few euros were wasted but definetly not worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: there is a moment when Cthulu looks you dead in the eye and delivers a villain monologuethe fact Cthulu is aware of a single humans existance at all is insulting to the source material, but he bothered to LEARN ENGLISH!?!??! this game falls apart in the second half where things that should feel massive and dramatic (meeting CTHULU for one) just sort of happen... and then... the game just instantly moves on to the next thing and never mentions any of it again.also the ending sucks and seems to be a twist for the soul sake of having a twist that can pretend to be a "go mad from the revelation" part.Honestly if the game had never left the island, and had been far far far less in scale. BECAUSE YOU'LL BE DOING THAT A LOOOOOT" the game sure is beautiful though.

_childDocuments_.review: Its got its good points very immersive, but immersion won't survive the games mechanics, either be a survival horror, or a walking simulator, personally I'd rather do dishes then slog through this crap, whats probably an 8 hour game will take you 15 cause you'll have to smash your head against the death wall until you figure out what your next step is. Very disappointing I was looking forward to this since it was announced.3/10 at best, save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call this a game per se but more of an experience tailored around HP Lovecraft's work and legacy. I would definitely point to the graphics and soundtrack as a strong point since they do a great job of creating a sense of ominous dread, but the caveat is that the game is horribly optimized so you'll experience some unwanted technical issues (i.e frame rate dips/stuttering) which take away from the immersion. I was not a fan of the voice acting but it was serviceable and the puzzles were a bit too simple for my taste... but again, you're not buying this game for challenging game mechanics, but rather to experience the cosmic horror Lovecraft is famous for. I would only recommend this game if you're at all interested in the Cthulhu mythos.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to The Shore's gameplay, there's not a lot to write home about: there just isn't a lot of it. At the very least, the puzzles aren't frustrating, which is a lot more than can be said for similar games. The voice-over is also a little lacking - you can definitely tell it was not a priority, as the game's design lead does most of the monster voices.The game looks fantastic, though, and the story was fun, even if it was also fun-sized. Most importantly, you get to see all of your guys, and they look great: Dagon, Nyarlathotep, Azathoth, and all of your other Lovecraftian buddies are here, and their designs are all pretty unique and awe-inspiring. I was especially happy to see an Elder Thing cameo - probably the best-realized design of the bunch. The game did a good job with its enemy monsters as well - even though combat is limited to holding down the left mouse button - and the sequences where you had to either escape or fight various creature threats felt like they did the most with what they had on hand.I paid something like $2 for The Shore during the last Steam sale, and overall, I would say that's about exactly right: it's what you should pay for a short, but still enjoyable, game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out VERY GOOD. It should have stayed that way because as soon as the "battle" begins - as soon as you turn Dagon free - it begins to go straight downhill and that is really sad. It turns into a puzzle game with a lot of flash and weird mechanics, but drops from being one of the best Lovecraft games out there to a pain in the ass to play. Please developer, redo about the last 30 or 40 percent of this game and make it as good as the first part.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, short and sweet, and an interesting atmosphere and location. _childDocuments_.review: I nominated this game for "Outstanding Story-Rich Game" I did enjoy the story, but the visuals and sound were outstanding and are what set it apart for me, I enjoy  the Lovecraft mythos and the pen and paper RPG so I kind of new what to expect.
