_childDocuments_.review: My favorite Lovecraftian game to date. Where Call of Cthulhu takes 6 hours to show you some 3 creatures - The Shore packs twice as much in half the time.Most of the games in this niche genre seem to be 90% "1920s America film noir" vibe and 10% "cosmic horror". The Shore skips the boring part alltogether and throws you right into the full-blown Cthulhu mythos early on. And it keeps on escalating from there.The creatures are gorgeous and just how I imagined them. This game can be treated as an interactive museum of the Cthulhu mythos, since through it's short run it shows you all the "core" creatures.The mechanics are kept to a bare minimum, so you can focus on taking in the atmosphere and the story, rather than being constantly distracted by "gamey" things" like managing inventory and quests, etc.This choice must have also saved a lot of dev time, that would have been spent on features we don't really need in a game of this type.The only parts I disliked are:1. Invisible walls that are impossible to miss. Should be beter furnished with rocks, walls, etc, to make it more obvious that it's not traversible.2. A Great Old One actually engaging in a casual English conversation with a mortal. This felt awkward and out of character for the setting. Maybe it's just the specific lines though and it would have felt okay if he said something more "cosmic" and incomprehensible.Those are minor issues that don't spoil the overall enjoyment of the game.If you need to get your Lovecraft fix - "the Shore" is definitely money well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side it was made with love, and the first half hour really gives a lovecraftian vibe. The moment when I turned back from a strange humming obelisk and seen tentacles drawing back to the mountainside, or looking into a telescope and cache a glimpse of a deep one was really exciting, and the background noises made me feel unease. The huge old ones are really huge and impose awe.On the negative side, it is around 3 hours long and wants to put every sea-themed lovecratian motif into the same short game, creating an experience like you've bought a ticket to Lovecraft Theme Park. The story is a mess. You can lose direction because every rock looks the same. You get stucked then try the exact same thing and it works because you've completed a scripted prerequisite. This is especially annoying if you do a second run because you've missed something. After the first promising half an hour the game looks linear and strongly relies on shooting abominations with a pyramid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn here. It's a decent game but I beat it 100% in under 3.5 hours and with many deaths and backtracking. So I'd recommend waiting until it's on sale. Overall though, it was a fun game with great atmosphere if you're a Lovecraft fan.My criticisms are mostly with the level design after the first 1/4 of the game. The actual 'shore' portion of the game with the lighthouse is tense, lots to see and explore, and has interesting collectibles and voice over. Sadly, what follows sort of devolves into a 'run from this monster in a maze', then 'run from this other monster in a maze'. It's almost as though they started with a proof of concept for a walking simulator and tacked the rest on in a hurry.My second big criticism is the ending. I won't spoil it, but sadly, it lands with a pitiful thud. It wasn't at all a satisfying conclusion given all the buildup to that point. The journey, for what it was worth, was much more rewarding than the destination.Finally, my last gripe is with the animations. While the models and environment were aptly done, the actual animations for the various creatures in the game were very awkward. Given the supposed immense scale and mass of some of these creatures, especially the elder gods, their gestures seemed rushed and really distracted from their sense of scale. I would like to see some improvement in helping show just how large these creatures were. Also, the character movement and environment bounding boxes could have been far more refined.Now, the fanboy talk. I love HP Lovecraft and have read nearly everything the man has written. Anyone else who is a fan might find this game disjointed and a little silly as you go from realm to realm, interacting with one elder god after another. It was essentially a menagerie of Lovecraft lore and creatures in a 3.5 hour romp. It felt too packed. It was unnecessary and really took the 'cosmic horror' and sense of wonder out of the experience. It made The Shore feel more like the Casablanca of the Lovecraftian world; everyone passes though it. Had the devs spent more time developing a more compelling story and focused on a single dark god as the antagonist, it would have felt far more authentic.So, after all my complaining, why do I still recommend? Well, because of the fanboy in me really. That, and because I was so taken with the first 1/4 of the game. Is it worth 25 bucks? No. Is it worth on sale and would it be fun for a Lovecraft enthusiast? Absolutely. Is this game for everyone. Not even slightly. If I didn't know Howard's work, I would have found this pretty boring and nonsensical. So buyer beware.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy. Crab.I just finished this and if I wasn't already sitting I think I'd have to sit down for a bit.Even though I'm not a fan of throwing all sorts of creatures from various Lovecraft stories into one single medium like it's some sort of Lovecraft's Allstars basketball match, I gotta admit that this is, hands down, the most atmospheric Lovecraft-themed game I have ever played. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish is could give this game a "meh" or "huh?" rating. Not great, not awful. 6/10 Buy it on sale.Much like others have said, this feels like 2 different games. It's starts out all story & chill with a creepy edge to it, & then BAM! It becomes an action game. And we get a little bit more story added at the end & a wrap up that feels a bit lacking & not entirely worth the time & effort you've put in. Although games aren't only about the ending as the story early on is pretty on par with Lovecraft.Some of the fights are pretty hard if you're not used to it, like me who's just getting back into gaming again. Many encounters are nuts, unless you use a guide to tell you The graphics & scenery are pretty amazing. Lots of eerie, beautiful, decently realistic imagery all around. I just wish they'd give you a little time to really look at a couple of the creatures & surroundings that disappear quickly, or are too tall to see easily.DON'T PAUSE THE GAME! If you hit Pause/Escape, when you un-pause you won't be able to move the character nor your view. You'll need to Quit & come back in, losing some progress if you haven't just hit an auto-save checkpoint.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game has unparalleled art direction, fantastic atmosphere and outstanding music. Constantly eerie and odd, the game is worth playing for its aesthetic alone. Gameplay-wise, the first chunk of the game is a walking sim, but after a point you start interacting more directly with the enviroment; solving puzzles and escaping monsters. It fits the tone of the game nicely. The one big negative imo is the writing, and I mean REALLY negative. It's like bad fanfiction. The villains (yes, "villains") are so direct and banal in their manner, methods, and goals that they come across more as humans with superpowers than unfathomable beings from beyond the stars. There's no reason a star god should *need* a human's help to change things, and there's absolutely no room in proper cosmic horror for a sentence like "Your strong will can influence Azathoth's dream."The good greatly outweighs the bad though, so it's a high recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Impression of the ShoreThe good-Amazing environmental art.Well done world assets that pulls a player in visually.Clearly understands the core stories of Lovecraft.The bad- The Cthulhu Mythos is too heavy handed right off the bat. As a player you seemingly stumble around onto horrible things but it happens way to fast and too early and all at once.Lack of game intro- The game just loads, no information to build up to the moment waking up on the shore.The music is constant and does not allow for moments between the 'scare'. No matter if you are experiencing a madness inducing horror or just standing on the beach, the music does not allow for pauses in the audio tension. The protagonist has only one emotion and that seems of boredom. They comment on the strangest things as if they are just another day for a fisherman, but experiencing any form of horror they seem to never actually comment on it.Too much of a good thing- The game so far appears to try and draw from every example of the mythos at once without really giving the player time to delve into the mysteries of any of them. Some of the mythos moments do not seem to have a reason other than an easter egg.Final verdict- For 10$ it's a fun game so far, but it needs some better audio, dialogue and storytelling tweaks to make it truly worthy of a Mythos tale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's premise, visuals and concept stand out a lot compliment the Lovecraft aspect of them, even with certain flaws and a probably not fitting type of gameplay aside from just walking simulator.You get an over the top, extremely detailed and well put scenery that encases the style of majority of the Lovecraft characters, filled with references, winks, or straight up introducing every major entity of the booksHowever, this game goes from 0 to a 100, by reaching certain point of the game you just wonder how did you even there, when it only shows it's a game about walking across a cryptic shore.Yet the extreme it goes is nothing but intense and majestic. Adding combat, chases, puzzles all in different strange and messed up scenarios.By the end the story to me became rather secondary compared to the amount of insane imagery, enemies and situations you found yourself in.And even if some of its things didn't fit or didn't make sense, it was a solid experience that you can absolutely enjoy

_childDocuments_.review: Many people that will play this title may not understand the purpose of design. As a fan of Lovecraft, I found this to be a perfect title for me. Now, this is an atmospheric/story driven experienced based on an accumulation of classical horror stories from H.P. Lovecraft. All that means is that it is a slow burn and if you are not familiar with the classical works of Lovecraft (which I highly recommend) you may not enjoy this. If you approach this game looking for an experience, you will enjoy it. If you approach it looking for one of the fast paced poor excuses for a game such as {insert modern AAA title here}, then you will not. Simple as that. Enjoy and remember to listen when the sleeping one calls...
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Extremely good visualsDecent voice actingCons:"Combat"Poor puzzle designEasily missed pieces needed to progressInconsistent gameplay elementsErratic storytellingInvisible walls EVERYWHEREUnclear pathingThis was a game I wanted to like more than I did, but it just turned out to be a walking simulator with some light puzzle elements. More than anything, this was just a tour of the Cthulhu mythos. Dagon, Shoggoths, Deep Ones, Elder Things, even  make an appearance. However, none of them really make much of an appearance, or much of an impact on the story. They're all more just there as fan service, shunted in for completeness' sake than any real necessity. For example, Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth was ABOUT Dagon and the Deep Ones. It didn't need much more than that. Sure it had Mi'Go and Yith, but they were instrumental to the story. It didn't need to include EVERYTHING in the mythos, which is often the problem that indie devs run in to. They feel the need to shove in ALL of the things, and it leads to something that's unfocused and disjointed, such as with this game. Heck there's one point in this game where you [spoilers] wake up Dagon for no other reason than because Nyarlothotep told you to, and he rides off on a giant walking obelisk. One hell of a visual, but nothing more than that. [/spoilers]That being said, what little appearance the rest of the mythos makes is pretty impactful. The models are beautiful, and the animations are pretty solid. The gameplay itself is straightforward and shallow. It's more of an adventure game than anything else. Collect the things, solve the puzzles, move on to the next area. What little combat there is kinda sucks. There's no real feedback other than the odd stunning animation that happens every once in a while. You don't really know if you're actually damaging the creature or just stunning it so you can run away, which is frustrating at times. Thankfully, the game is short and doesn't make you endure much of what passes for combat. In my opinion, it would have been much better without it. The thing that really irritated me the most was the silly invisible walls everywhere. They were everywhere, and they were just so stupid. Nothing breaks immersion like running up against an invisible wall simply because the developer didn't want you to go that direction. Especially when it's something stupid or time saving, like jumping over a rock or a crevice, or off the side of a ramp. All in all, it's really not worth it. Buy it if you enjoy walking simulators with a side of scary monsters, but don't expect to be frightened by anything other than the odd jump scare.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: what a rousing romp through the lovecraftian weird and wonderful. quite eerie, if i dare say so. especially the craft that was on display with the mixing of the auditory qualities of the game. human voices barely heard even if all other audible brimborium is turned down to the slightest. as if to say: humanity is not welcome here and you shan't hear anything even remotely reminding you of the anthropic flesh tied to your waning sanity. spectacular.

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this game over on my Youtube channel (link below for anyone wanting to see a sample of gameplay before buying), so here are some thoughts.If you're a big fan of all things Lovecraft, then The Shore is worth giving a shot. By far the most impressive element of this game are the visuals, which are stunning. Most of the game involves solving puzzles, but there's a bit of basic combat later on and there are plenty of eldritch enemies to watch out for. The story does feel like a bit of a mash-up of Lovecraftian monsters and entities, as if the devs wanted to try and get as many elements of the Cthulhu mythos in there as they could. Again, if you're a big fan of Lovecraftian stories then this is basically fanservice for you - but players unfamiliar with Lovecraft may find it a little bit chaotic.Overall, whilst not the most amazing Lovecraft-themed game out there, I still recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed exploring the beach and the haunted lighthouse, reading letters, solving puzzles and finding collectibles. Too bad it's only the first half. In the second half, the game becomes a really bad first-person shooter where you're either shooting badly animated monsters or running away from indestructible ones. And you die and die and all the horror atmosphere dissipates. I don't know if the development was rushed or what, but the second part was so bad that I really can't recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, here's the thing about The Shore: If this is really the product of a single developer, someone needs to give this person a massive budget.Why?  Sure, The Shore isn't very long.  I suspect most players will complete it in an hour or two.  That's short.  However, the reason to play this game is all in the atmosphere.  The visual design is fantastic.  Modeling, animation and texturing are all great and really provide the visual atmosphere necessary for this kind of endeavor.  The sound design is also very good.Is it technically a "walking simulator"?  Well, sort of.  There is some light puzzling and while the game leans into action a bit more down the stretch, ultimately you're not going to get much more than basic FPS mechanics.But seriously: Who cares?All I know is after playing through this fun little cosmic horror romp, I want to see more from Ares Dragonis.  Even if you don't pick this title up, you're going to want to keep an eye on future titles from this developer.  As a game, The Shore is not going to knock your socks off with innovative design, but the quality of the effort is immense.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Great environment, and amazingly captures the embodiment and insanity of the Mythos.The game and story are, sadly a bit short though.I finished the game in around 4 hours, while trying to explore everything as much as I can, and I feel that, as great as it is, a game this short isn't exactly worth the price.That being said, it really is amazing, and I do not regret the purchase, and I believe the developer can very easily make the experience completely worth it with a few more content updates.Overall, great game for Lovecraftian fans and I completely recommend it!Although in my opinion, might be considered still an alpha or a beta release

_childDocuments_.review: The world and the creatures are beautifully designed. The voice acting is good, and I liked the music (when it wasn't overbearing). Very bad and a big shame, because I was enjoying it up until that point.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game to succeed so bad. Sadly, it did not deliver. As I said, the first half an hour is an incredible experience however, I cannot recommend the game unless you get in on sale and even then it is just meh..

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an intresting game, with alot of potential. you could call it a Lovecraftian explaination of the Flannan Isles mystery, witch i loved. But sadly the story got driven away.i absolutely loved the introduction, it was driving me to play the game. The letters wasnt boring, and the disorded notes made the player slowly assambel the story of the 3 missing fishermen, witch was intriguing and eerie. the island that was isolated from reality and civilitation was a nice mix up with the tales of lovecraft. my only critisism story wise is it felt very quick before the player got thrown into another mindset. some slower progression of the question your sanity part would be nice. but even though i really wanna like the game for its story only, there is some inevitable cons about this game that ruined the amazing story. the atmosphere was raw and colorless witch i liked, but i didnt have a good sense of scale. maybe a thicker fog, and refrencing would help on that aspect. Even though the design was raw (witch was well suited), it still felt unfinished. and the shadows just wasnt there, and the map was very limited. i was'nt driven many places in the story, because i just walked the presented way. i would love to explore the island of its mysteries, and forgotten stories. every path was blocked or dead ends, also the game didnt comunicate very well witch way that was the "right" way either. another important factor for the atmosphere is sound. the dialog was intresting.. the sound acting, not so mutch.i didnt have mutch of isue with the soundtrack, but neither do i feel an appreciation for it.the puzzels also felt bland, repetitive and was there just for the sake of it. to sum it up, it was just walking from a to b, with out making you think out of the box. witch is okay to a limit, but it felt more like an obstacle for the game than a feature.what is there else to say... i was stuck in the trap door besides the lighthouse and needed to restart. the fonds are nice but can be hard to read if you look at the corners of the scribbled notes, it could use a normal fond aswell on an overlay. you also could make interactive items pop out from decorations conclussion: so in conclussion i cannot recomend this game yet, and i really hope you take some of this feedback  to improve. im writing this because it has a lot potential good gameplay. and i love the core idea. its sad that these cons are ruining this fantastic story to be told, with alot of detail. like the sailors/fishermen that got insane by the color out of space,and all the other small hints that combine the universes, i see alot of research and passion from the develpors. So i would  love to come back and play this game in a year. but its not ready for realise, especially with the given price. i hope to see updates and improvements. overall: 5.4/10sound design: 3/10puzzle designs: 4/10grapichs: 6/10story: 8.5/10horror level: mehshocking plottwist at the end the sums up our questions about the main story nicly: Hell ya.my current valuation of game: 5 dollars - its playable for now

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-	Art design: Lovecraftian mythos is truly impressive. A lot of effort went into making the huge creatures very detailed.-	Length: 2-3 hours might sound short, but I think it’s just perfect to show everything the game has to offer. -	Achievements: encourages exploration because some items are optional and add some lore. All can be gained in a single playthrough. Cons:-	Item hunting: some items are very small and hard to find. There’s no glow or anything that would help them stand out.-	Shooting/running sequences: although the opportunity to defend yourself in walking sims doesn’t come often, it feels like it was shoved in in this game. Running sections surprise you; if you don’t start running in the right direction, you won’t be able to outrun the monster coming after you.-	Disjointed and linear gameplay: after the impressive start at the lighthouse, you go through a lot of scene switching with no context or story. You're on a beach one moment and then fleeing away from a monster in a maze the next.-	Invisible walls: when you can only walk in a specific area despite the obvious flat and open world, it leaves a sour taste in your mouth. You're forced to take longer paths and search for an object rather than simply walking around the rock.-	Unoptimized and some graphic bugs: most walking sims done with Unreal engine have this problem. They have a habit of consuming far more resources than are actually required. Also noticed some rocks and birds hovering in midair. Despite the shortcomings, The Shore has some fun moments. It's definitely not boring like other walking sims. I bet a better connection between disjointed sections would give it a few more bonus points.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Very short, but visually stunning. if you enjoy Lovecraftian horror and need your fix, this game will please in some aspects but upset in others. like i mentioned, the art is beautiful, the idea is there, but some executions weren't 100%. in some places this even felt like a interactive art piece more than a game, but is all still very impressive in terms of being made by 1 person. some places i could see improving would be:-not making simple things locked until needed. not being able to jump till mid game is kind of an odd choice, but to each his own.-some things just seem to be added for the sake of it. im not 100% well versed in all of Lovecrafts pieces or lore, but the fleshy level just seemed out of place, as did the obelisk and orb at the beginning-no prompting for very important things. it tells me how to jump when needed, but when a fleshy monster trying to kill me starts coming at me, there is no prompt that i can now attack when i previously couldntoverall, for what it is, 7/10, like i said. this feels more like an interactable art exhibit, seeing as it only took 2 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

The atmosphere is the only good part, but after one or two hours, the gameplay just kills it, and the narrative is really weak compared to other fanfic Lovecraft stories. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game, with a confusing plot, confusing puzzles, and boring game-play. I don't know much about Lovecraft mythos but it and the art direction intrigued me enough to buy the game. The game is very beautiful (of course if you look up close at the textures it doesn't look so good but that's alright). I didn't seem to comprehend the game-play which was just a walking simulator (I thought this was just a joke but it was true), and the few action set pieces that were there failed to be fun and engaging. I also believe the story didn't make much sense as soon as the more weird areas and monsters were introduced. The starting area on the shore, I believe was perfect in a story, voice acting, visual, and suspense, however the rest of the game was a chore to work through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. The atmosphere is blindingly beautiful and the score is really complimentary to the game. Those epic scores, when you uncover new creatures is amazing and sends goosebumps through the body. I get that the shooting part of the game is kinda mweh, but then again, would a fisherman really be able to hand an alien weapon. Further more this is not a FPS game, but a puzzlegame, so I can forgive the lackluster control of the small shooting parts. The normal pricing is a bit steep for a 3-5hour long experience, but I bought it on sale and was mindblown with the experience. If you find it on sale definately give this game a playthrough :) Grafix: 8/10 The water and in general the gfx of the outside world is as beatiful as can be (apart from stone looking abit odd). The other world is abit gritty, but it gives a good effect to the story.Sound: 9/10 Very good complimentary soundtrack with epic scores, when you encounter new creatures.Gameplay: 8/10 It's a walking game/puzzle game with some wonky shooting elements. For the most part it works great. Engaging story as well and you feel the need to find that next puzzle. And for achievementhunters this is a nice relaxing list :)Total: 8,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The shore had been on my wishlist for forever before i finally decided to pull the trigger  during the halloween sale.The first half of this game is amazing and i 100% enjoyed it. walking aorund, reading notes, collecting random things and just exploring is awesome and a really good way to present this mythos-inspired game. I loved the atmosphere, the lore, the statues you can find, walking along the shore and seeing all the creepy things....The second half of the game I didn't quite like as much, it is filled with monsters you have to escape or fight and i often found myself getting frustrated with these sequences. I understand that it is probably intentional because you are meant to feel helpless against these creatures but it still wasn't a good gaming experience. I also often struggled to find the way i was meant to go and kinda fumbled my way through or had to look up a guide because i was so lost. The lack of direction is an issue throughout the whole game but it didn't bug me as much during the first half. I sadly experiences some sort of bug during the last few minutes of the game, the subtitles didn't work for everything that was said and i missed large chunks of the dialogues. Sometimes there were also multiple audiofiles playing at the same time. The story was pretty good and i liked the little twist in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very pretty and had the correct amount of suspense and monsters to feel like you were on edge. The urge of finding your daughter was lost since the game didnt have much stakes about it. The ending just didnt have the impact it could have if the story was a bit more fleshed out, or your story would include steps to finding your daughter. There were a few times that the game got really dark (or load facing a black wall) and odd decisions (like items that dont get picked up; it's pretty, but misleading). Puzzles were alright, but no real direction so it was a bit confusing. It always felt like there was something missing. This game would be an amazing VR game. I would pay double for the game if it were VR. It would allow to really feel how eerie the world is, and how massive the monsters are. For a walking simulator like that, it would be  a perfect VR game in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, the ending was kind of bad, it felt rushed and I guess that's where most of the thumbs down come from.That's the negative out of the way. I enjoyed playing this game and can recommend it to anyone who likes HP Lovercraft's work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: 🎨 I thoroughly enjoyed this game, but there are basically two parts to this game: The gentle and eerie psychological horror with mystery elements where you walk along the coast near a lighthouse picking items and clues while coming across ominous and foreboding ritualistic objects and constructs, and the second which thrusts you away from the investigative walk on the shoreline and deep into a cosmic horror realm where you face otherworldly horrors and jump from one area to another within a matter of moments. With the focus surrounding the eldritch beings, the designers should have went by the "Less is More" option, leaving things to the imagination to fill in. The Lovecraftian horrors are designed concept-wise, but feel detached from the rest of the game's more realistic qualities. They seem too fake or cold when seen with the surroundings, lacking texture and some feeling like plastic or smooth digital models. More texture and detail would have made these eldritch horrors feel more realistic, while also using caution to not reveal too much as that would take away their mysteriousness and ethereal nature.All in all, this was a very well done game, enjoyable and definitely has many nods and homages to lovecraft's works. Even though they have no direct influence on the plot or puzzles, it definitely made you feel this island, this Shore, definitely was cut off and remote from the rest of the world, allowing these locations to be unknown only to certain few and allow such a cult or such worshiping to take place.🔈 Atmospheric.⚙️  Walking and experiencing with simplistic controls. No fighting.📝 A Lovecraftian-inspired game that starts off beautiful and amazing, and then just goes head-long into the campy and extreme in-you-face creatures of the cosmos, taking away all mystery of them as though they were merely seals you encountered on the shoreline.❕ : This is my opinion and thoughts, not an overall view of the game for general audiences, as opinions and experiences vary. As with all reviews, take this as one of many viewpoints, and do your own research. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, possibly a little short? For the overall experience of the game, i thoroughly enjoyed it. You had a mixed assortment of feelings going into different sections of the game; Fear, curiosity, confusion, relief and many more. You play through some rather infuriating sections too, which makes me feel the design of those sections were to try imitate the feelings of losing sanity which HP Lovecraft described many times that those Gods were meant to impose on the human race. We were never meant to be able to witness the aura of those Gods let alone the vision of confronting them and the creations of them.I loved the game and do highly recommend those who have an interest in HP Lovecraft and his work to play the game, it's a fun short game and for all the emotions you may feel during it, it was worth it. I played it for 3 hours ish and had a great time doing it, thought it might have been a little longer with maybe more Gods involved but there are potentially things I have missed?

_childDocuments_.review: Yes but only for the trip.Some reviews compare it to a walking simulator, but i disagree as after the first third of the game, it turns into a weird attempt at an FPS. I will be honest, this does not work well, and will be frustrating,But the game itself isn't that expensive, and the atmosphere it creates does work.I am glad I played it, but it is no masterpiece, If you are fine with that,  you may give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Silence.Real  or not.You don`t know.Standing on a Shore, it feels so surreal.But wait, it is not as silence as it seems.Yes, there is something … around?Welcome to THE SHORE.You are Andrew and you are stranded.Somewhere.Your Daughter is missing and all you can see are wrecks and a Lighthouse in the Distance.It is time to find your daughter, but it is also time to find out whats going on in this Place.But be carefull … it is not safe out there.At first i thought THE SHORE is a pure Walking Simulator. It is not.There are also „Combat Sequences“. Yes, you can die. But the Monster Design is really, really great.All the Graphics are really amazing and i also like the Sound and the Voice Acting.The Atmosphere is really unique. It is not also like that you know that you are alone, you can really FEEL that you are alone. That gave me Goosebumps.I love the Lovecraftian Material and it seems that there is very much from it inside. I recognized much familar Content from what i have read in the Past.The Dev put very much love and Details into this Game. That is something you feel in each Corner of it. It is exciting to explore and to find out more but sometimes it feels a little bit confusing, maybe i´m not deep enough into Lovecrafts Stuff.The Game Mechanics are simpel. Normal Walking and Running Options and also examing/taking Items, at least the Inventory, which looks optically really nice. A side laying Boat, where all your items are clearly arranged.  Nice done.Well, the Running could be a little bit faster, it feels more like fast walking, then Running and believe me you WILL need the Running Option very desperatly (sometimes).That goes also for the exploring. Sometimes it can be a little bit chewy to walk/run around, trying to find out how it can be going on.By the Way, here is a nice Vid to the Game from Ajay. Enjoy.So, in the End we have a really nice Game with an amazing Atmosphere, but it is special. This is not for everyone. Lovecraft Fans will like it, they get very much, maybe too much from it.  It is also a little bit short, but i love THE SHORE.A big thanks to the Developer who dropped me into this Lovecraftian World, i really enjoyed it.Thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game started out as a promising atmospheric Lovecraftian puzzle/exploration game. The first 30 minutes are really, really good.But then the game rapidly devolves into a really bad dungeon crawl chase-scene FPS. Once the game turns FPS it never truly returns to exploration and puzzle solving. More so, what the game doesn't warn you about, is that there's no real way to go back and resolve any unfinished puzzles without starting a completely new save.Great atmosphere, good music and feel, nice scenic graphics, but overall, extremely disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I think The Shore deserves a positive recommendation - with a caveat.It's important to keep in mind that different people have different visions of what, and how needed to be presented to make a game "lovecraftian." Absolute minimum: tentacles, the more the merrier.. Or Cthulhu, you need Cthulhu, everybody knows it! So many games just have a few tentacles, namedrop Cthulhu and call it a day.Dagon, Nyarlathotep, Elder Things, Azathoth being extras to show you know more than just Cthulhu. Alien landscapes and physics, mystery, vague and unexplained things, strange architecture and statues are (in my opinion) just as important elements, if not more. One of the basics of classic Lovecraft's mythos is an uncaring, alien universe, that is not there to be understood, but that's generally a really difficult thing to present.With these in mind, in my opinion  For about the half of it, it's a walking sim with "puzzles", that are more interactive elements than anything that requires a proper solution, but it works. For its another half, it's a about running from and/or shooting all kinds of eldritch monsters (while still having those "puzzles.").  To give credit where credit is due - they look pretty good, the presentation is really strong with the game. There were really well-crafted moments and locations to give space for some good old existential dread.But most of the game feels like a Lovecraft-themed ride, rather than a classic story. It depends on the player how much of a problem it is - it's not inherently a problem big enough to give a negative review, but it really can take out the wind of your sails if you get caught off-guard by it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm someone who enjoys setting and atmosphere above many aspects of a game, which this did have. Loved the beach in the beginning especially. Its clear the devs love Lovecraft's work with all the mentions and easter eggs here and there, but there is little cohesion. Great atmosphere, but just decent to alright story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:7.5/10, Excellent but not perfect.First things first:The game is short - I completed it in around two and a half hours without a guide and managed to get stuck a few times.I'm inclined to call this a walking simulator but unlike many of the other walking sims this has actual game elements.Would I recommend it ? Yes, if you can get it for around $10.If it was a bit longer without additional padding (example: fetch quests) then I would recommend it at full price as the quality is already there but not the quantity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is best described as a walking simulator with the occasional eldritch horror in the background, and weak FPS elements later on. It also boasts being the first walking simulator I've played, where dead ends are so frequent and do nothing but irritate you. Voice acting is clearly done with cheap microphones in bedrooms, and honestly the story is confusing with a "WHAT A TWIST" type ending.And yet... I really enjoyed this game despite its clear downsides, it came from people that had a clear passion for the source material and did the best they could with what they had. Although it could have been done ALOT better i respect the effort put in to make such a unique experience and i can honestly say, this game has some of the most unique visuals and scenes i have ever seen in a game. The contrasts of colors between sections, the clear handmade monster designs, and the music is actually beautiful during the more "epic" moments. The ending in particular is downright gorgeous and worth the whole effort of reaching that point.The Shore wont win any awards in writing or design, but does get my respect for trying their best with what they have. The Shore is a unique one off experience that could have been better, but the few epic moments it does have are truly worth dealing with all the shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: "The oldest and strongest emotion of mankind is fear, and the oldest and strongest kind of fear is fear of repeating a horrible monster chase sequence"I had this game on my wishlist since I first heard about it last year. The game looks very beautiful, the environment toward the beginning of the game reminds me of Dear Esther, some nice screenshot-worthy moments. There are some graphical glitches like the water effects and being able to stick your head through objects, and some of the invisible walls are pretty obtrusive.The first third of the game starts promising with a nicely designed, foggy shoreline surrounding a lighthouse, examining various curios and discovering details about the islands' previous inhabitants. This segment is semi-open, while there are invisible walls and a clear order of completion, you are really walking between connecting locations. There is one teleport segment early on, but you aren't locked out of the previous, you can enter and return as often as you want, this was not a sign of things to come.My enjoyment of the gamed dropped immediately upon receiving "the artifact", your weapon in the game. What follows is a maddeningly repetitive series of teleporting from room to room. From this point on in the game there is no backtracking, no returning to the lighthouse, you actually see very little of the eponymous "Shore" after this.There are no complicated puzzles in this game, just some poorly communicated tasks that really only involve pressing interact on things. I know this is pretty much a mainstay for story driven walking sims but I expected something trickier. You perform a simple task in a linear room, and then teleport to the next room. You run from a hideous monster in a room. The monsters. The monsters are fast and you only take a few hits before dying and reloading, but you can stun them by shooting the artifact laser beam at them. I spent the majority of these segments running backwards through the winding monster rooms, because the stun I mentioned does not last long enough for you to take the beam off them, and sometimes you have to juggle multiple enemies. This isn't how a game should be played, it's a good thing the environments during these sequences are super bland, purple flesh rooms or black oil rooms, I didn't feel like I missed out on seeing anything.The story tries to cram in as many mythos deities as possible. Though I admit, it is always fun to see references to Lovecraft stories in games; in the form of artifacts, literature, engravings on coins, symbols painted on walls, or a curious meteorite. It is not so great seeing Dagon screech like Godzilla and then hitch a ride on a monolith, or Cthulhu give a super-villain monologue about destroying the world. A few more fan-favorite Outer Gods are also named. It's just too much, the plot tries to fit them in but it was unclear what purpose they served. Perhaps I would understand better after another play-though. I don't think I will play this game a second time to find out why.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A truly haunting and ethereal depiction of the Cthulhu mythos.It looks incredible, that's for sure. But let's take a second to talk about the soundtrack. Holy heck, is it gorgeous. It's a mix of perfectly-timed instances of unnerving, thoughtful, and triumphant music. And it's all so very well done.For fans of cosmic horror, or simply fans of story-driven puzzle/adventure games, this is very high up there.Have a double feature night and play this along with Dagon for a wonderfully Lovecraftian evening.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning of this game was absolutely fantastic! It's what came after it that was not good. The slow intrigue and exploration and fantastic atmosphere in the first 30 minutes were honestly some of the scariest moments of any game I have played. What all came after... not so much. The puzzles were simple and had very little challenge, the level design was at times incredibly confusing. There were points where I was just walking backwards through a level to slow an unkillable enemy that if not constantly shot would have caught up to and killed me. It's also incredibly short. If the whole game was like the first 30 minutes but the game stayed this length I would 100% recommend it, but as it sits right now I just can't.I'm sorry. There's obviously a lot of passion in this game, but it just doesn't get there.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers, read at your own discretion. It saddens me to downvote this game, but i have to.  The main reason being - this is not a lovecraftian game, this is a short fan-fiction where the dev goes like "i want to see lots of the Great Old Ones and interact with them, NAO!" The guy is clearly passionate about the Lovecraft's entities and beings, but he totally misses the whole point of the H.P.L. works: the slowly unfolding fear of unknown and unimaginable, the creeping madness that invades your mind after the realisation of humanity's insignificance. This kind of fear requires a proper build-up, a story being told.  Remember the best lovecraftian game up to this day "The dark corners of the earth" - it starts out slowly. You arrive in town, you start your investigation, you see suspicious folks and strange shadows, the eeriness creeps in slowly only to explode later on in the iconic chase scene. This is perfect! You want another example of things done right? Here is your direct competitor "No one lives under the lighthouse". Same setup - small island with a lighthouse, same game length - between 1-2 hours. The 90's graphic of this game will make many people's eyes bleed and still it manages to do the thing that The Shore fails. It nails the lovecraftian essence and the fear of unknown, while keeping the slow build-up and escalation progress. (also you can take revenge and explode the freaking seagull into a bloody mess there, unlike here, where even the ancient artifact of an untold power cant even make the fu****g bird to flap it's wings) While the developer of The Shore utterly fails in the scenario-writing department, he did some other things exceedingly well and i have to give the credit where it's due. The Elder Monolith - Excellent. Nyarlathotep interactions - Excellent. Azathot devouring chase - Superb. Dagon scene - Veery good. The great C'thulu summoning scene and ship throw - Amazing! The whole otherwordly plane - Excellent. The grand ending scene - Beyond Fantastic. As you can see i rate some parts of the game very-very high. But despite that i still can't recommend this game as a Lovecraft fan. I have to repeat - this is not a proper story, but a fanfic made only as an excuse to make and animate the Great Old Ones and Elder Gods. If only the developer had a competent writer on hand, if only he bothered enough to create a longer story with a proper build-up, culminating in the epic revelation... ahh how cool would that be. I honestly think that the bigger developers can outright learn from The Shore how to make encounters with the lovecraftian pantheon exciting. But this is all this game is - a series of cool scenes involving H.P.L. entities. I would like to strongly suggest to the developer to find a skilled scenarist/author and make a new game from the scratch. But this time - longer, with a proper setting and slow build up. Don't mimick an excited kid emptying the whole box of his toys in one second only to brag to the guests. You nailed the pantheon, now it's time to make a proper story.  And work on the optimisation by the way. This game is not so graphically demanding as to have sudden fps drops on a PC that run Cyberpunk2077 at steady 50fps. And fix you music, because the "broken mic" effect doesnt add to the atmoshpere - it simply annoys.PS: and one more thing - invisible walls on literally flat surfaces are not cool, bro. The age of facing an impenetrable air is long gone in a videogames. At least make a visual obstacle of some kind or other excuse if you want your players to follow your rails. Being stopped by the thin air really sucks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game does a great job at exploring and recreating some of Lovecraft's most horrifying entities. If you want to see some of the more mind bending creatures, and hideous, otherworldly landscapes then this game is it. The creator really did a great job reflecting the horror of Lovecraft's ideas, and included some of the most famous gods/monsters. It is a shorter game, but well worth the play through! Some people say its not worth the price due to the length, but I got this on sale so I can't really complain. So if that's whats holding you back, then just wait for it to go on sale. I don't think you will be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore has a lot more  than meets the eye. I went into this expecting something of a walking sim, like a prettier Dear Esther maybe. And while it certainly starts that way, I wasn't expecting the game to evolve into a run-for-your-life-a-thon.I screamed a lot playing the second half of this game. I  being chased in video games, and this game has plenty of sections where you're being chased; Having to stun an enemy and then turn your back to it and run through maze-like corridors. It almost drove me to the point of quitting. But I persevered. Because I had to. I played alongside someone who knows a lot about the lore. She says they did a good job with all of the creatures and really enjoyed the references from various Lovecraft works. I on the other hand have never read a book in my life. I had no idea what was happening at any point of this game. All I knew was that I had to keep running and I did so.I think the visuals and set pieces are enough in and of themselves to enjoy this game. I had a few minor bugs like the menu making it so you cannot move (have to hit escape twice to get in/out of it). The audio also seems to be bugged and resets to full volume between set pieces, so mind your ears. And... Just be warned of the chasing. If you're a fan of Lovecraft, there's apparently much more to enjoy here than I got out of it, but none the less, I'd recommend this to anyone who likes a "casual" experience turning suddenly terrifying. I should have known this would be the case, but, now you know. You've been warned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: [waiting for the hotfix to see if i refund or not.]as of yet the games performance is mediocre and in addition to the sadly poor optimization suffers from progress-blocking bugs that require constant restarts of segments in the hope that the game logic maybe works the next time around. (portals not appearing, getting stuck on terrain, etc.)The Shore has great atmosphere, looks mostly amazing and the sound stresses the tone of the landscape and hightens the mood in a fitting manner. it offers quite some nice amount of fanservice. a multitude of references and hints to all lovecraftian and eldritch horror things imaginable. BUT maybe keep it at hints!? once again another game showcases knowledge of the lore / stories of the lovecraftian cthulhu- mythos, but fails to understand what makes cosmic horror so effective: the fear of the unknown. throwing tentacle-monsters at players is just not scary - even if the monster-models and sounds are nice and all that. it had me joyfully explore the titual shoreline trying to figure what is happening and wanting to find every tiny detail.but at some point i changed in pacing and gameplay. even hint-markers popping up all of a sudden on items from meters away, instead of letting me find stuff. INCONSISTENT is the best way to describe it.the controls feel a tad off and the lack of video-settings makes optimisation real troublesome.the poor translations and missing dialogue and subtitles do harm the otherwise oppressive atmosphere that the game builds up. a real shame.so with a heavy heart i can NOT recommend this game for the asking price. i really, really wanted to love this and enjoyed the first hour immensely, but it falls apart once it goes from confusing explorative walking simulator to combat and flight from monsters. show less and leave more to our imagination please.IF you are a sucker for everything close to eldritch horror and lovecraftian you may enjoy it - but be warned. maybe wait for a discount/sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: None of the Parts in this Game seem to be connected, while i would generally categorise it's elements as Cosmic Horror there is just no cohesion between any of them. A few easter eggs like the Meteor from Colour out of Space or summoning some tentacles are neat, but not if the entire Island is littered with them. At one Point i walked into a creepy green cave, realised it had no bearing on anything and just decided to walk back out. Got attacked by a fish guy, he died, didn't know there were any beforehand, only saw one more and he just left. Consequences are usually a major Part of Lovecraftian Horror, but here most of the things you can find are just nothing. No reason for them to exist, no relevance to the Story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The design and many details are a treat for Lovecraft fans. Unfortunately, the gameplay is awful.The "puzzles" consist of either menial chores or finding very tiny objects in the landscape. Some clickable items require you to be in a very specific position and angle. There is nothing thoughtful about these puzzles, nothing for you to figure out. And you'll be scrambling back and forth and back and forth a lot to "solve" them.The other kinds of challenges involve chases. Something is running after you and you have to not let it catch you. They are annoying rather than horrific.And the game's whole structure is very lopsided. The first third of the game is far more interesting, with notes to read and objects to examine, an actual story. But then it just plummets into a series of disjointed scenes that seem more like individual demos than components of a game.If this had been a linear "walking simulator" it would have been an easy thumbs up. Instead, the attempt to turn it into a puzzle game has produced a frustrating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the overall plot, sound design, and voice acting of the PC. I purchased this on sale.The controls are clunky. The puzzles range from being really easy to miss, to extremely simple. The combat is mostly just running away while trying to use the artifact which wouldn't work half the time (is there a recharge? it is unclear). Lots of dead ends in the level design, So I was left running around not knowing what was next a lot. This game is worth playing for some of the most interesting and cursed visuals of any game. Fantastic atmosphere. I heard it's a one-person developer and they've done a great job of crafting this little world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game recently and as someone who enjoys the works of Lovecraft, I felt like this game had some ups and downs. The setting was good, reminded me of the story Dagon a bit which was nice. However being met with a ton of invisible walls and odd inability to walk over objects any person could raise their leg to step over was annoying. I really wanted to discover the island more as the protag that just crashed there looking for his daughter. The first half of this for me really dragged. While the monolith and seeing the sea monster from the lighthouse were cool, there were many things just thrown in there for no reason. The meteorite from the Color out of space felt so disconnected if you read the story of color out of space. In addition they threw in the pillar from Utah or something next to a giant black orb that as far as I know was pointless to the story and felt threw in for "OOOOO SPOOKY WHAT COULD IT BE" without capturing the fear of the unknown whatsoever. Tossing in Dagon, Deep ones, Cthulhu, Azathoth, Nyarlathotep, the and all this extra monsters made it feel like a show and tell. For the story, using a mortal to ♥♥♥♥ around with things was interesting but, the ending twist just felt like a pointless slap in the face. While the dimensions were interesting and its setting was nice, the lack of exploration that railroaded me into the strange story. I didn't hate it and the fact it was made by such a small team was impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this recommended has several big fat asterisks that need to be mentioned. However a TL;DR can be summed up with "If you are a fan of HP Lovecraft, get this now." If you aren't a massive fan or are skeptical, keep on reading. So, firstly, lets go through the bad.THE BAD:* This game is rather janky in places, for literally everything.* The voice acting needs to be re-recorded and remixed for everyone except the main character. He's fine.* Some of the puzzles (two for me, but the forums seem to have other issues) are badly designed due to one major flaw that could be fixed with a light source or larger interaction area, such as not needing to point at a pixel to connect.* Every chase in the game will probably begin with you dying. The reaction time needs to be instant, which won't happen sometimes. There needs to be more of a delay for every one of them.Now the issues I've listened above can be fixed in a post patch. I wouldn't be surprised that, in a month or two, many of them will be solved.THE GOOD:This is probably the biggest wet dream any fan of Lovecraft could ever want. I'm serious. For $7 bucks, I played through the whole thing in one go just to see where else it'd take me. My God, does it deliver. The developer put all his effort into the animations, world design, and sound effects. If you are a fan of HP Lovecraft, you need to play this one. It works better via the gaming media because you can take in the size and scale of things.In conclusion, if you are a fan of HP Lovecraft, go get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Very weird. Greatly inspired by lovecraft. I wish it had more directions for linear progression, but wandering around felt true to cosmic horror. While I was never scared, the game was successful in making several things eerie and captivating. All bow before the mind squid!9/10 would have my mind scrambled again
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why this is rated so high - the gameplay is terrible. You only ever do one of three things:  search for keys, run from monsters, and solve very very simple puzzles. As for the Lovecraft monsters they're certainly there, but it feels somewhat awkward to just see these things lumbering about in the background as mere set pieces. Its supposed to be an intimidating attack on my mind, and yet I'm rearranging blocks like a kindergartner while an evil god paces back and forth like he lost his keys.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not write reviews, but I had to say something about this hidden gem of a game. If you appreciate the lore of HP Lovecraft then you simply should buy it. It is short, it could be classed as a walking sim to some degree and the puzzles are not tricky. Still, you can tell the dev really sunk his heart into this as it is just dripping with lovecraftian nightmares. I loved ever second. Put your headphones on, turn the lights off and bow to your elder gods.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing through this game. The visuals were stunning and it truly is an immersive experience. My only complaint is that there was little direction when it came to some of the puzzles and it was quite short. I've been left wanting more. If you are a Lovecraft fan this will absolutely hit the mark for you just based on the monster encounters alone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The slow-walking around gets really old really fast, as your character moves like molasses. You'd think that being chased by eldritch horrors from beyond the stars would be a good enough reason to be able to sprint.There's not much of a compelling story. but some of the sights are pretty scary. Overall, very mediocre game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game at just under three hours and I don't know how I did. I spent almost the entire time confused I don't know how I solved any of the puzzles and I don't know what it is I accomplished. I only comment on frame rate when I feel their is no reason for it do be as messed up as it was and the frame rate was often at almost slideshow levels. At first I thought it was an install or driver issue but as far as I can tell the game is just like that. I had similar issues with the sound. Which brings me to my next point I was often frustrated and annoyed by this game. With cryptic puzzles that I don't fully know how i solved, labyrinthian level design with never ending enemies that will kill you, and the audio and visual issues left me incredibly frustrated at times.The reason I recommend this game is because of the confusion and frustration. Out of all the Lovecraftian games I have play this one best encapsulates what it would be like to be a protagonist in a Lovecraftian world. Confused, insignificant, and frustrated. The story is also pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only game I've ever requested a refund for.  I was expecting better graphics and immersion. Map pathing is very confusing, and its hard to tell where/when you can jump or sprint making navigation and chases extremely annoying.  It's also very easy to wedge yourself into spaces that are impossible to get out of so you end up having to quit the game and continue.  Had issues with certain cutscenes where I could hear them but only see a black screen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: If you're intrigued by the premise and can find this game EXTREMELY cheap on a Steam sale, maybe give it a try. Definitely don't pay full price though, it's not worth it.Long version:Pros:-Engaging story/premise-Genuinely creepy and disorienting imagery in multiple places-Pretty graphicsCons:-Riddled with technical issues. A few hours of playing this game gave me more headaches than any 30+ hour game I've played all year. Fortunately these issues can be resolved pretty easily by quitting/restarting the game, though.-Bland puzzles.-A bit TOO pretty in some places. The underwater sequences look very nice, but they're not creepy. Fallout 4 had creepier underwater environments, and that one's not even a horror game.-Some parts of this game are just flat-out poorly designed. The monster chase sequences are more aggravating than tense or scary. They pretty much shatter the eerie atmosphere that the game has managed to build up to that point, and make the whole thing start to feel like a chore.-When you think of Lovecraft's work, do you think of artifact laser beams? No? Well, apparently the game devs did!It's too bad that so many aspects of this game were so poorly executed, because there's a fantastic idea here with the story and some of the visuals. Near the beginning of the game especially, it feels very otherworldly. The Shore does a better job than a lot of other titles at nailing scares and bizarre imagery that feel truly Lovecraftian. I wanted very badly to like this game. But sadly, despite all is has going for it, there are just too many issues with the design for me to recommend - at full price, anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Lovecraft based game, very enthralling story. Only complaints.. linear game with very specific non direction points that had you spending an extra 30 mins looking for an object. Had to restart a couple times due to bugs not allowing a specific mechanic... and for the love of everything that is holy.. is 2022 now in computer gaming.. make the cursor in games FIXED. Looking down and clicking at the wrong time and getting your Windows bar instead resulted in a couple of deaths, and is highly frustrating.. other then those few complaints.. excellent game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is kind of a mixed bag. Amazing first third, okayish second third, disappointing final act. Overall, for 5€ (50% off), and as a fan of Lovecraftian lore, this is worth it. The fact that it's been made by a small team (2 guys from what I can find) is why I'm a bit more lenient and give it a thumbs up.Not the best on the market, but crafted with care
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: It's essentially a walking simulator with minor FPS mechanics, but it's a really touching love letter to everything Lovecraft, chock full of references and nods to his writing, and probably the most bespoke deep dive into the mythos I've seen in games. A lot of things may be similar, but this felt much more open and passionate where other games lazily borrow from the man's visuals without understanding his worldview.With that said, the plot feels a lot like fan fiction, with more focus on fantastical drama than sanity-bending horror, and the ending didn't make any sense.Buy the game for the experience of the mythos, not for gameplay or story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, for  a walking sim. Controls are stiff and horrible, and combat is TERRIBLE. However, the music and voice acting is awesome. The most interesting part of the game is when you get to the color out of space part. In some areas the visuals are beautiful , other times they look like they were made for the play station 2. Real simple game, not much to it. I can tell this was someone's passion project, and it is really cool concept and really fun little walker. But for $25 dollars i can't recommend this, if it comes down to $10 pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A wasted potential and a mess of a game. The first portion of the game around "The Shore" is a walking simulator and a little bit slow but does provide a bit of a built up and I found quite enjoyable. But there are just some awful gameplay decisions. You get chased at various times and it's just bad. Then you get a pseudo weapon and just gets more (bad) combat focused.This doesn't know whether it wants to be narrative driven game, a puzzler or a shooter and it suffers from this lack of clarity. The puzzles are either incredibly easy or ridiculously poor. One puzzle has you matching patterned grey stones on grey plinths but one of the stones is missing. You can "find" it on the beach with all the other identically grey stones by scouring the beach one footstep at a time for a stone that is a very slightly bit greyer than the others.  Another room is full of 100+ heads and you have to walk around examining them all to find the "right one". No sense of achievement for doing either, they're just frustrating time wasters to block you from progressing the story.Some of the animations in the game are fine, others are just poor. Creatures slide up from  the (otherwise well animated water) like their in a pop up book that just grates with the rest of otherwise ok animation.The change of game style from walking sim to (bad) fps doesn't do it any favours. I got frustrated with that terrible combat and needless chases sections and despite being close to the end just couldn't bring myself to finish it. It's not a bad game by any means, but it's also not a good or even average game. On a scale of 1-10 (10 being the best) this would a 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Tay. I love  H.P. Lovecraft.  Great visuals, easy puzzles (so far) I have only gotten to stage 2 where you fight through a field of zombies (?) to get your weapon. I  run  a Windows 10 Box with a Logitech lighted keyboard (wired).  Unfortunately I cannot use the right shift key,  To use  a keyboard, I  need  3 hands, one to press the left shift key to run/sprint, one to press the Up arrow to move forward  and one to press the left mouse button to adjust  any movement other than straight ahead.  I have searched the interweb  for insights into the use of the 2 shift keys  and  (supposedly) they both function the same - for touch typing, one shift for the left hand and one for the right hand).  If you cannot sprint, you cannot escape the creature.   Lacking that third hand, I am unable to walk to the icon and  get the  weapon  to kill the critter that is after me. This may be my fault, or the fault of the system I use, but so far it appears to be  an issue with the game controls.  I have played the FPS shooter games since the DOS version of Wolfenstein came out.   I actually like the laid back pace of the game, but  I am unable to continue. You are correct, I am your granddad, 71 years old and not fond of the X=Box style game controllers. Any help would be appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Lovecraftian games and Walking Sims, try this out. It actually has a bit more interaction than I expect for a Walking Sim type game. I'm directionally challenged and did get lost a couple times. The music is great - I actually enjoyed it, quite a bit.My criticism of the game is that it could use a different background for the paper that notes are written on, as in a couple instances I had trouble reading what was at the edge of the page. I liked finding the various objects etc, but it would also be cool if it tracked them somewhere. :)The environments look really nice, particularly the one at the very end of the game (avoiding spoilers.) :) Anyway, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Guys, don't let bad reviews deceive you!This is one of the most beautiful and immersive Lovecraftian games ever!It's one of the very few games that convey what it would be like to become a mere human facing the great old ones.This game is an artistic experience and if you expect it to be some cheap entertainment or a combat slasher, please just steer clear, you will end up posting your misguided expectations here and ruining the mood for people who appreciate the game for what it is.Its best qualities: - Amazing atmosphere- Great area design like the amazing natural looking terraforming which very few artists can pull off- Subtle storytelling- Breathtaking music- Some object models you can get just mesmerized by- The feeling of grandeur, amazement, being a part of a mysteryNow I'll sum up the bad reviews for you:- Nitpicking, like "where is the invert Y axis option. Unplayable" (It was not a big deal and was added in a day upon release)- Outright false information "this game doesn't let me jump" (while it clearly does)- "the UI is not pretty boo-hoo" (that's a meter of taste. I loved it and thought of it as very fitting the art style and the narration)- A couple grammatical mistakes in the subtitles. (You'll be better of pointing those mistakes out to the devs instead of bashing the game for it. This is something fixable in the matter of an hour)- People expecting this to be Overwatch or some battle royal game, or I don't know what. (Combat is clearly not the point of this game, and for a story driven walking simulator the combat is amazing)You people, are the reason, why we can't have nice things! Games like this one don't come out often and instead of bringing it down you could provide your constructive criticism and give the devs a chance to smoothen the couple rough edges.Now I will do exactly that. What would I change so people could fully appreciate the game:1. Place save points right before the chase scenes. Having to listen to the same cutscene before you die is widely considered bad game design2. Make it more apparent where you need to go during the Protoplasmic abomination chase scene3. Make the creature underwater inside the purple maw a bit slower. I was running as fast as I could and dying anyway. (one of the very few places where the intense immersion has actually been ruined)4. Change voice actors for the Cthulhu and the wife. Their voices seem way out of place 5. Flash out the character model for the daughter. Right now it looks exactly like that: a bad puppet stiff computer model6. Make the transition between the "stuff collecting" part of the game and the action part more noticeable and pronounced. Like for example a cutscene of the character dropping all of his belongings to the ground. Right now the transition is a little bit odd and feels like you're playing two different games. Or maybe add some lore collection elements to the action parts if possible, so the contrast is not so striking.8. Do something to make the ending more impactful. Right now it's kind of open ended, we don't know either to believe Azatoth or not which leaves everything hung up in he air. On top of that strong emotional connection to the daughter is never established during the game which leaves the player not really caring for her all that much7. And for god's sake, turn that photo camera model on the beach towards the dead sailors. The lens is the part that absorbs light, not the photo film holder.8. Maybe bring the price down a little so people stop ruining the score. Although I was perfectly fine with the price. For me it's the price of a ticket to an art exhibition, and I'll take this experience over almost any exhibition any day!While these issues have somewhat distracted points form my experience, they are not even nearly enough for me to fall out of LOVE with this amazing adventure and the breathtaking scenes! I'm leaving the comments open for the people who have left their negative opinion in reviews, but can't get over the fact that I too have my right to give my positive opinion. Yes, I'm gatekeeping this game, get over it. Otherwise welcome to the comments, but I'm nasty to argue with, when I'm pissed, you've been warned ;)

_childDocuments_.review: The heavy atmosphere and constant sense of dread is what drew me in the most. It really feels like you are walking through a nightmare that you can't wake up from. The visuals are truly amazing with an awesome sense of scale, and many of the terrifying entities look like they shambled right out from the pages of an H.P. Lovecraft's bestiary. That said I enjoyed the survival horror aspect of the first half of the game much more than zapping away most creatures with the Artifact in the second half--that got a bit repetitive and lessened that delicious sense of impending doom I felt earlier. I see a lot of reviewers going on about how it's too short, but I think it's just as long as it needs to be. I like Shorter games that are able to tell a full story and take only two or three sittings to complete. I got it when it was 50% off and after playing it think it actually is worth the full price, especially considering this was a labor of love for just one developer!

_childDocuments_.review: I am impressed with this game's level of quality, given that it is an indie game with a small number of developers. I bought the non-VR version on sale for about $2.99. While I enjoyed the game, I do have to say that I would not pay anymore than that for it due to length of the game (took me about 3 hours, I think, even with my starting over about 30 minutes in) and the Cons list. (The VR version may be worth picking up at a higher price, however.)PROS:*Voice acting is much better than I expected.*Music and ambiance are very well done.*Settings are immersive and lovely, with wonderful color schemes!*Creature designs are awesome.*Based on H.P. Lovecraft's works.*Has that lonely, otherworldly feel that you're hoping it does. (Which is why you started reading these reviews to begin with, right?)CONS:*Invisible walls! There are many places you simply cannot walk, even though it looks like you should be able to. I understand that this is to help keep the story on track, but it is annoying to keep getting stopped by nothing.*The combat system. In many places you have to run BACKWARDS through winding corridors while yielding a magical beam that often only stuns your enemies for about a second and half. To top it off, almost all of the enemies that you face are WAY faster than you. This leads to even minor mistakes (which are tough to avoid because you can't look where you're going) causing you to die repeatedly and have to start the encounter all over again. This seriously detracts from the immersion; I ended up repeating some portions 3+ times and spent far more energy being angry about it than enjoying the story and beautiful areas. I ultimately felt like I missed out on these maps, being forced to rush through them and be salty about dumb mechanics.*The character's speed. Even at a sprint, your character is as slow as molasses. During some monster encounters YOU CANNOT RUN AT ALL; the ability seems to have been disabled by the developer at these points, possibly to increase the stress of the encounter. It's quite maddening.*I understand that this was likely a foreign language game, but there are noticable misspellings in the notes scattered around the island, and the English voice actor for the main character mispronounces several words.
