_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun little game. Worth the price of a movie, which is great cause it'll take you an afternoon to get through. But that afternoon is gonna have some entertaining platforming and combat.Olija is a short action platformer where you play Faraday, some guy who gets shipwrecked and then gets cursed by a magic harpoon. And you're trying to get you and your men out of this weird land of Terraphage. That's it. That's the pitch. There are moments of story and character dialogue, which are fine, but most of the story is what you see above plus a love story with Olija. Don't expect riveting twists and turns but also do expect to be entertained by the short stuff that's there.Amusingly, I'd liken this game to the Adventure Island series. Take your boat to a couple islands, each being a self contained little action platformer section, get new items and increase your ability to fight/explore/puzzle-solve.The meat of the game is the action. And the main gimmick is the harpoon. You can chuck it at enemies and certain things and it'll get stuck, and you can either call it back or bring yourself to it. A simple mechanic but it allows for some pretty fun movement and combat. The combat felt good and was more fun than I was expecting, and you get a couple subweapons that open up your options as well as hats that open up different powers. Not a huge amount but enough. Likewise, the platforming had a couple puzzles that you need to figure out but none took too long. I'd say the game is...relatively easy outside of a certain boss battle where the difficulty suddenly jumps.The music is decent, always fitting and never takes you out of the game. It's good. There's...not much to say.The graphics, for being a certain pixel style, are actually quite good looking in motion. Fun animations, easy character profiles so you can tell who's who.  Good spritework for the ambiance of the areas, as each feels very unique from each other.Any gripes I have are small. Screen transitions can get annoying due to the monsters being on one and you on the other then they hit you in between, it's hard to tell what's a safe place to fall down and what will damage you, the bosses can be cheesed easily with a certain hat. Nothing big.I bought it, played it, enjoyed it. What else can I say? Worth the money and a solid, fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A European ending up in a foreign Asian-inspired land very much mirrors the developer Thomas Olsson's living in Japan, developing this game over 2.5 years at Kyoto-based Skeleton Crew. Hopefully his life is not as fraught with black goo, spikes, hostile clans, haunting legends, and stalking monsters as Lord Faraday's quest is to save his crew who have been marooned on these islands after a whale wrecks through their ship. As Faraday, you come across a legendary harpoon and later on a magic sword that both focus on impactful platforming mixed with melee at the same time. You can grapple to eyeball tendrils or enemies by throwing your weapon at them and then flinging yourself like a magnet. The effect never gets old despite you only acquiring a further rifle, crossbow, and rapier. The combat feels great thanks to punchy sound effects and stunning animation work. While the Rottenwood Clan makes for mild fodder, the boss fights are explosive and memorable bringing all your grappling skills to bear. I rarely found the need for the crossbow compared to the rifle but the various hats with abilities made for some fun variety. It's tempting to just stick to the crocodile hat that gives you health points after defeating enemies but the weapon-producing hats are no slouch. The platforming sings as you grapple up and down and diagonally, making for some of the most enjoyable traversal in such a game. You can replay the levels to save all the crew members but afterwards there is not much else to do which is fine because I don't care for collectathons just for the sake of it that can seem like filler padding. , similarly named like  after a secondary character, is a swashbuckling 2D action romp with a heavy narrative emphasis much like a  or . However, the difficulty is more forgiving and the combat is fluid with some excellent gamefeel. The story itself reminds more of films like  and  with less colonialism and white saving. You do ransack the local jewellery like a -inspired colonialist and treasures but it's more for crafting hats that give you abilities than to steal and take back to your home country. There is a pleasing meet-cute between Faraday and Olija, who have to meet in secret and their own people don't take kindly to this cultural mixing. With gibberish voice acting over English dialogue, there is still a lot said by just foreboding environments and expressive animations like when Faraday looks more fatigued as the story progresses. The characters can be charming such as the alchemist (that converts your money into health upgrades) who breaks things over her cute goo pet or a poetic flute player who makes for one of the most memorable challenges. The more crew members you save, the bigger your seaside hub gets, populated by chefs, builders, and loot-seeking travellers. It's a short and sweet (well, more bitter-tinged with sometimes the horror and misery) journey that knows exactly where to end. There's a bittersweet and dreamlike quality to the way the story unfolds with its beautiful pixel-y cutscenes, evocative music, and narrative conclusion. One of the early 2021 GOTY contenders, don't miss out on this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A great game start to finish and not too long but not too short. Gameplay and combat is pretty simple, normal side-scroller or metroidvania type system. Story is cool and follows the captain Faraday attempting to save his shipwrecked crew. The art style is a big selling point; lots of detail with little pixels make for a beautiful eye-popping world. Soundtrack was hit-or-miss for me, REALLY liked some and just meh on others but at no point does the music NOT add to the experience. Definitely give this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting concept, though the game feels more like a demo or shareware game that's short and not very fleshed out. Unlocking hats is not the same as the claimed "crafting" of hats. The story is not great and there are a lot of long pauses. The game several times also went into a debug mode that couldn't be exited as well as crashed several times, but it could always be restarted and there was no problem playing through the whole game.If the game is on sale for a low price, it will provide a few hours of what is mostly fun gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun fluid combat and atmospheric exploration. Not very long but everything there is pretty tight and there are a few new mechanics as it progresses, albeit briefly in a way that left me wanting more.Beating the game erased my save so no post-game secret hunting or NG+. Still great package overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: My only knowledge about Olija was a trailer I've watched, thought it looked interesting and I decided to buy it and I can say I'm not regretful about that decision. I'll classify it as a cinematic platformer without the heavy movement that games like Another World has.Olija's whole premise is pretty simple, you play as a shipwrecked captain that arrives in an unknown and hostile land. You travel through islands collecting the needed keys to open the portal that will take you back to home. The plot is nothing new and was already used in many games and other medias, though it works well here.Besides the cleary Another World inspiration I feel Olija also drinks from Chinese and Japanese movies. The songs used also works well to set the mood. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A most excellent game.Just as long as it needs to be and knows exactly what it's trying to portray.Special mention goes to the game's audio, which is the rock-solid base upon which the rest of the game's atmosphere is built.But most importantly, the immersiveness of this game stems from the fact that the characters act... normal.Be it the boatman getting annoyed if you blare the horn in his face one too many times.Be it the meme-worthy "You haven't touched your food my Lord.."Be it Olija's followers showing up to take Olija away and dropping actual reasonable arguments.Or my favorite, the hidden couple in the Royal Domain, because *of course* that's what you would find there.My only gripes are that there are a few too many Ships-In-Bottles to collect (and collecting them is quite distracting too, not sure on that design choice), and that the difficulty spike between regular enemies and bosses is massive.Love the game's title.Bravo.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Being 43 as I write this, spending hundreds of dollars on discounted indies yearly (sometimes monthly) and all for what? I do it for that experience of being 13 again, sitting in front of a screen and seeing a new world open up in a way I never thought that it could. Maybe one out of every 30 or 50 or 100 games I play ever vaguely come close to that, Olija did from the moment I first loaded it. The sound, the pallet, the incredibly satisfying combat...the HATS. It's just perfect. I'm one of those players that buy a lot while I tend to play just a little, but as long as experiences like this come along every so often, gaming will always be worth it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot reasonably recommend this game. The art and sound design come across as decent, but not particularly special. The combat in particular feels lacklustre, and any success I had came largely from spamming keys until the enemies went away. Buy this game if you have a tolerance for this genre, otherwise it's best to avoid this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but it's price is to high for what it offers compared to other games, it's core mechanic of the harpoon is fun, but the combat isn't smooth enough to really enjoy it, for that matter the whole game has a weird flow to it, things feel really slow in some of the story sequences and the art style isn't clear enough sometimes, so things can look really cluttered, it has an interesting world, story, and gameplay ideas, it's just not a cohesive experence.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Impeccable vibes.The presentation from animation over mumbling voice acting (with intelligible names) to the music and ambient sound effects is perfect.It also had the perfect structure and length to me, with 4 areas unlocking one after another coming in at 4 hours total.There isn't any mandatory backtracking. You can play through pushing forward at all times.All areas that grant you a key to progress will however close up permanently.So when you do want to revisit areas, you may be locked out of some collectables.For such a short game and all collectables having no effect on gameplay or story, that is okay though.In fact, only the easy ones (your shipwrecked crew and audible music boxes) have steam achievements attached.The difficult and most numerous ones (bottle ships) aren't acknowledged anywhere. All they really do is confirm that you've found a secret corner.The only real problem I've run into is that starting the final boss fight is irreversible and locks the save into it. You cannot back out of it to restock ammunition, purchase remaining health upgrades or even just swap the only load out option you have: your hat. Different hats do various things once they are charged up from attacking, such as healing you, charging your weapon with electricity or adding additional attacks to your arsenal.I did not go into that boss fight using the right hat ... but I eventually made it through anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Like someone else said in their review, the game is just OK. It has a lot of things going for it, but none of it really stands out. The pixel art was pretty cool and the atmosphere was great, but those aren't what makes a game. It needs to have some great gameplay and Olija does not. The combat is fine, the story is fine, the platforming is fine... but none of it is really GOOD. It's just fine. It's a very forgettable experience. If you are really digging the trailers, get it when it's on deep sale. It's just not worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game, worth your time and money. Pleasing art and animation that never gets in the way, stylized so that I was rarely bothered by the pseudo-pixelated style. Great platforming and puzzle challenges, along with satisfyingly challenging combat that was surprisingly easy to learn. Each boss stands out on its own, with unique challenges and obstacles, as does each region.The hat system is mostly just fun, I think. Could they have taken it more seriously, perhaps used armor or attachments to the harpoon? Absolutely. Is this game all the more colorful that they didn't? Even moreso. There's myriad little touches that make you feel like you're really progressing, and the story manages to strike a striking balance between Lord Faraday being the protagonist and his being just a single part of the world.There's a straight romance story woven into the plot, but oddly it never really feels that major, despite several of the beats being required to progress. And the fight-flirting is a nice touch. The plot is simple, and you're immediately pulled into the story of the world itself; it's easy to accept the magic that flows through bones and spears and hats.I very much enjoyed playing Olija. If you enjoy platformers, beat-em-ups with unique mechanics, and metroidvanias, you're most likely going to enjoy this. I look forward to seeing speedruns of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: The game has just released and I got chance to try it. For the first two hours of playing I got excited and engaged. It is fun and promising. The sound effects, story, game mechanics, level designs are all good. The only problem with the game is sometimes it crashes when you attempt to go next level. Other than that everything is like clockwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: What a bonkers game. Its tone is all over the place: Sometimes gory and menacing, sometimes comedic, sometimes banal. Graphics are serviceable, but music and sfx are OUTSTANDING! They are so clear and good that they seem to clash with the rest of the game's flair. Combat is extremely crunchy, punchy and satisfying - but also ridiculously easy. You are overpowered in movement, weapons and health, and not even the final boss poses any threat. And before you know it, it's over. 5 hours of constant, weird and entertaining WTF?!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a game like this a long time.Movement feels incredible by making every motion create many effects and the leap requires skill to recover from or you'll be laying flat on your back.Combat is punchy and versatile. You can swap between weapon types mid-combo and fling yourself across the room for a better position. The impacts are weight and super satisfying.The world design itself incorporates the foreground, background, mid-ground, and characters that react to you in a way I would almost describe as cinematic. There's an immense feeling of presence within the first few areas that I never knew how badly so many games are missing.The artwork is where I would be most critical. Different sized pixels are occasionally mixed together which never ceases to bother the perfectionist in me and makes pixel art seem more like a limitation than design choice but for some reason I want to forgive it because the smoothness and control of the movement wouldn't be possible without fudging the pixel precision. Maybe it's the muted palette or color based atmosphere of the areas that bring it all together along with the music and sheer amount of unique effects (Wind blowing, leaves falling, light-rays, clouds, fog, etc.)You're not allowed to skip anything at all which can make you feel a bit like you're on a leash sometimes but it hasn't forced any unreasonably long cut-scenes or anything unforgivably bad. The font isn't pixelated which starkly contrasts the art-style and breaks the rule but it is far more readable because of that.The gameplay being the primary focus and having the narrative woven into the world while giving impact to the moments you spend simply walking or avoiding traps by looking ahead makes exploration a joy rather than a chore- which I'm convinced most AAA developers may not be capable of learning at this point!The sheer and obvious amount of work, love, care, time, and inspiration put into this game is apparent within the first hour. You'd be hard pressed to find another game that feels quite like this one. Don't pass it up without at least trying the demo first.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A clunky platformer with some janky mechanics. The main mechanic being the harpoon feels weird since it has a vague lock-on, sometimes shooting horizontally or at an angle. Played with a controller and it felt as if the joystick had to be nearly perfectly to the right/left in order to shoot that direction, even the slightest bit up or down making it diagonal. Final boss felt as if it's main challenge came from projectile spam and stagger-locking the player.A mediocre game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Simple description: short and sweetIt doesn't overstay its welcome and so the combat feels smooth all the way through.     Game is about 4-6 hours long depending on how obsessive you are about the collectables.Overall, the presentation is quite good and all elements of the game come together to make a pretty good title, albeit with low staying power.        If you are wary of the price for the length this is a pretty "get it on sale" candidate. You won't regret it at anything less than 25% off. But I would still recommend trying it at the base price.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Fun action and exploration, and the story has something to it. Enough that you want to keep going, but isn't the highlight of the game. Combat is fluid and actually cool to both pull off and watch. I had a lot of fun with this one.There's this one boss fight that can go ♥♥♥♥ itself, but other than that - the game's pretty darn solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a great and pretty short game that I really enjoyed and would definitely recommend. I really enjoyed the combat and traversal. You get a good variety of combat options as you progress through the game. Enemies often have clear tells so you can somewhat reliably avoid damage and there’s also a pretty decent amount of healing scattered through the levels so the game wasn’t too challenging but it wasn’t a mindless affair. The game also has a great sense of progression, the hub of the game grows and expands with shops and people as you go through the story and by the end what was a desolate little hunk of wood turns into a really nice and homely place. My favorite part of the combat/progression system was the hats. During the game you can find various materials to craft hats that change your appearance and combat style (The acid one is the best, don't @ me). The game also has some really cool boss fights, a highlight being a battle up a tower against an opponent with a similar moveset. The story was pretty basic, just you going to places and getting keys to leave. But the setting was really interesting, you’re kind of in the middle of a conflict between the dominant faction of monsters and the queenless and dwindling faction of noble-ish knights. You rescue their princess and that really kicks the conflict up a notch, they have a chance now and so do you. Once you rescue the princess that kicks off the more serious plot, both parties mobilize more. It also begins a silent romance between Faraday and the princess, Olija. Which leads to some really cool and memorable sequences, like sneaking past guards to give her a flower or a spear duel culminating in a romantic scene. By the end of the adventure I felt quite attached to this strange world I had grown used to and it was a sad goodbye.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, challenging, artistic, short but compelling gem. I liked how little to no guidance there was but it was just the right amount.*spoiler alert*  and at that moment when the generator is shut and it was all dark and hopeless with seemingly no hint of how to navigate in pitch darkness, as the narrator tells us not to fear , despite no hints for the player, so naturally you would either figure it out on the spot because you're a genius or go through all your options and stumble upon using your moonblade for no reason and ♥♥♥♥ HITS THE FAN in terms of writing and game design, a 10/ 10 moment right there. Also lovely depictions of romance and character design for a pixel art game. It makes you feel that there is more to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a charming action adventure side scroller with simple but highly satisfying combat. The animations are stylish, and the soundtrack is a blast, both fitting very well to the setting.I won't go as far as saying this is a must-play for sidescroller fans, though. Some late game level design oddities tone down the experience quite a bit, and there are only two boss fights that feel like actual boss fights, which is a bit disappointing. Also, I experienced a few crashes and soft locks. Nevertheless, if you like games where your attacks are impactful and make the opponents knock all over the screen, Olija is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A short but fun game, buy it on sale. I beat it in just under 4 hours having discovered half the secrets on each level. The combat is fairly easy but surprisingly deep (holding different directions will give you different attacks with all the melee weapons). I don't know that it is worth the full 15 dollars though.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 2D action platformers with killer movement mechanics you HAVE to play this game.  Devolver never misses man.  They just never miss.  The lack of hand holding is really delightful.  Everything about this game is charming.  Be sure to play around with the controls, up and down inputs have an impact on your attacks.  A delightful game that SHATTERED my expectations in the best ways possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: It feels satisfying without being hard, which is cool.It gives you a decent amount for game-play for the price without being too long. ( i finished it in one 5 hour sitting)I dislike that there isn't an arena mode or some post game challenges that let me vibe with the combat after I finish the story.It feels like a mix of a lot of different games, and gives you a unique experience which I had fun with.I recommend it if you want a short, not so challenging game to chill with for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a really interesting narrative-focused metroidvania that tends to focus more on set pieces than exploration. The game is a prime example of something being greater than the sum of its parts; Individually, the graphics, sound, story, and gameplay might seem simple at first glance, but they're executed so competently and confidently that they amount to a great experience. Gameplay - Combat is kind of like a platform fighter, you hit someone a few times before they're launched and then you can follow them with your teleport spear. There's also light platforming, exploration, and puzzles, and a reasonable number of secrets and upgrades. Never gets too difficult if you remember your tools.Sound - Good use of music stings and chunky hit sounds. I'm also a fan of the mumble talking.Story - Decent little narrative, does an especially good job of conveying tones
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Devolver has a finger on the pulse of modern-retro gaming. Olija has a strong reminiscence of older games, all the way down to the audio design. The story manages to be gripping, something that many other Devolver titles lack. The nautical-demonic themes are beyond fun, and makes the whole game play like a sailor's tale. I managed to beat every boss of the game first attempt save for the last one, which took me 4-5 attempts. I've played Hollow Knight and Salt and Sanctuary through, to give you an idea of the skill level. The game should be a quick play, even for beginners to the metroidvania genre. Good game! Give it a shot if you've got a couple afternoons to burn and you wanna feel like you're playing an arcade game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a short, but interesting sidescroller with pretty pixel art and straightforward gameplay. Stranded in a weird world, you are trying to collect keys to open the Shadow Gate and find your way back. On the way, you find a harpoon that you can throw onto specific tiles to then teleport to that tile. The puzzles in the game are pretty easy, but zipping around with the harpoon is fun. There are also a few side weapons that range from occasionally useful to "why would I ever use this"?Combat consists of mashing the attack button with an occasional harpoon teleport. This sounds much less fun than it actually is though, because the attacks feel weighty and the mobility from the harpoon makes fights a breeze, both literally and figuratively. It does get a bit repetitive after a while, but luckily the game doesn't overstay its welcome.Overall, it is an enjoyable 4 hour romp through a strange world with a few things to collect. Sadly the game is never really challenging as both puzzles and combat are very easy. The game also attempts to tell a story by using subtitles and visual storytelling - sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't, but it gives you a pretty good clue of what is happening overall.I would definitely recommend it, though the asking price of $15 dollars is way too high for what you end up getting. If you can pick it up for less than 10 dollars, go for it if you like sidescrollers - and hey, there is a demo too, so try that out if you want!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: story(=telling) + style (pixel art) equals olija equals brillance!this game is a reduction to what is important in a hack/slash-platformer with some rogue-lite elements. what stands out is the perfect timing and use of story-elements, pure immersion. from the first story fragments on there is a extremely building up tension. you get just enough to become addicted and grieve for more!i wannted to play only a little bit, to get to know the game mechanics, which are pretty easy and controls are as they have to be, and got hooked immediately. i stopped playing because i had an appointment. if you like pixel art & minimalism combined to an outstanding game, you'll love this!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of Pixel art but Olija got me from the moment I started playing it.The world building, characters, sound design and stunning backgrounds are incredible. Some of the best work in a 2D video game I've ever seen. (And it was all done by one guy.)Unfortunately, the game play isn't as impressive. The combat and platforming have their moments, but are stupidly easy and lack variety. You've see everything the game has to offer within the first hour. Minus the boss fights. Each one is a thrill and actually demand you think on your feet.The best part of the game though for me was the length. It was 5 hours and that was enough. Any longer and I probably would've stopped playing. But because the presentation is top notch and the game play has some really fun moments I'm leaving the review positive.Wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I was never really interested in Olija. It showed up on my feed a couple of times but it wasn’t a priority. The game was on sale recently for €3 (Steam), this made me give the demo a try. While the demo showed some positives, I was still hesitating. I got the game anyway and it was worth it! The full game starts much better and there are more options in the settings menu such as changing the resolution. In the demo it looked very blurry and that was affecting my enjoyment too. The game is quite unique, I didn’t expect it to depict this many emotions through cutscenes considering the very pixelated graphics. It’s an action adventure that could have been very typical but it’s kept fresh thanks to the harpoon weapon and the way the levels are designed around it. The game also has some cool bosses, everything around sound feels very professionally well made. I love the Mexican style of the music and the made up language. The achievements were fun to get and the game’s length feels right, it took me around 6.8 hours to complete.The negatives are more like nitpicks. There are 3 collectible types in the game, one of them is finding 40 ship figures. They’re very difficult to find, but at least there are no achievements for getting them which is the smart thing to do. The controls might feel clumsy sometimes, especially when you unlock the last secondary weapon but that might just be me. And lastly, I said the game’s length was right but there might be people who want to get more out of the game in terms of mechanics and exploiting what you have further. Don’t expect the game to get complicated. It has a few mechanics and the game’s length is just enough to not get bored of them. If the game was longer, then it would have felt too simple or too repetitive.What you have is a decent game that might impress you, its audiovisual quality is high but it’s not the best game ever. It’s just a good time. It might be worth considering when it’s on sale again. And if you’re unsure about the demo, as in you’re neutral after playing it, then give the game a chance. The demo starts later in the game with a lot of context missing in terms of gameplay etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A tale that happens all inside of a whale. my expectations were low going into it but by the time I was finished tears rolled down my face never seen a hack and slash side-scroller do justice to the theme of love before in fact I think this might be the greatest and best conveyed love story I have ever played in a game. really should go into as blind as possibly. the pixel work is amazing and makes the levels feel lively even if they are really simplistic and solid with the colouring. The OST is vast in how many different genres it includes and I couldn't imagine better fitting tunes to listen to while playing this instant indie classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the perfect game to have on the go on Steam Deck for example or if you want a tight gameplay with simple enough game that doesn't require too much thinking or too much time to see what it can offer which is surprisingly not little at all but it's so focused on what it wants to be that it becomes much more than it actually appears.The gameplay is fluid with a great central mechanic that makes the platforming in this game satisfactory to execute as much as combat to master which again doesn't require much time to master which means that the skill ceiling is pretty low for this game but in my opinion that is actually a pro in the game's favor. It doesn't require countless hours or a cryptic lore to be understood in a play session or being completed even. I think this game it is totally worth it for anyone really because of how easy it is to get into it and understand it and also be able to appreciate its nuances.I totally recommend the game for its gameplay, visuals which really does stand out with its art style and great pixel art and the music is also carrying the whole atmosphere to new levels. This game is amazing and I wish the developers great future because these kind of games are really rare this day and age.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect much from this game but what a surprise this was!It's a simple premise, a stranger in a strange land, executed with a lot of care. I love how the narrative is told through gameplay and your actions. In addition, the little bits of dialogue are very distinct with excellent voice work in a made-up language. In general, all the sound effects are amazing here.It feels great to play too. Until the end there were some new mechanics and the game never felt boring.Curious to see what the devs will do next!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: From my experience playing this game, this game is VERY FUN TO PLAY. I enjoy this game eventhough it's 2D graphic. I like how we can find some weapons, get more hats, the main character is really adept in battle. Brutal, Fast attack, Great Kungfu. I wish that this game has more longer story which can be more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry to say that this is by far the worst game I've played in a long time.I played the Demo when it was made available, and I was quite excited for a new action platformer.Sadly, this game is simply not good. - The combat is spammy and extremely easy. There are some interesting concepts with the weapons that you gather, but you never need to  use them as you can simply spam your way to victory.- This game is only 4 hours long, yet it still manages to feel like a slog. You frequently need to backtrack through levels, and you are forced to sit through many nonsensical cutscenes that seem to try their best at hitting every bad trope. In addition to that, this game has no replayability, unlike other similar short games like Katana Zero.- The story seems to actually be the main focus of this game, but it made me angry by how awful it was. Every cutscene or dialog made me cringe so hard, and there are many of them.In conclusion, don't buy this game. Buy any other platformer, you'll have a much better experience, and it'll probably last you for longer as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Short; beat in 3.5 hours. Quite limited mechanically, with few changes from the moveset you have once you get the harpoon (30 minutes in?). Very linear. Gameplay is ok but I found myself just pushing towards the end more than really enjoying it (motivated by beating it and the fact that I could tell it was short). If you really enjoy the pixel art and the sparse storytelling style or mood from the first 30 minutes...perhaps keep playing. Otherwise I would skip. Certainly wouldn't pay more than a few bucks for it. There are much more engaging games in whatever genre this is.

_childDocuments_.review: The pacing is off and wastes your time in the beginning. The combat is repetitive at least in the short time I played. The exploration is very annoying without a map, I quit the game when I accidentally left the first area out of frustration.I'm not sure why I don't see mention of this in other reviews (maybe a younger crowd), but this game is clearly taking a lot of inspiration from the original Prince of Persia. We are not in the 80's anymore. There's a reason games evolved since then and no point in going back.Olija failed to hold my attention and I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so its pretty.  Its fun.  Its pretty-fun. BUT what is this game exactly???  It seems to cloak itself in something a bit more pale & sinister...It starts out as the traditional tale of a lazy colonizer that embarks on a journey to exploit others for profit. But instead of a glossy adventurer of conquest, your savage-hero, Faraday, secures the quick fail when he shipwrecks right off the jump. Faraday subsequently indentures a naive native that ferries him about; syncs up with other marooned-savages; and then mounts a swift take over of their troubled colonial foothold.  As you play along, you will find Faraday appropriating local property and items to further metastasize (build out) the colonial village.  You will also observe Faraday stealing & robbing graves for weapons, and then use them it against indigenous life.  At some point, your little s-hole village gets a racist hat maker, that will make you a green backward baseball cap that grants you thievery and earns you an achievement referencing the Nile (racist american tropes).  That's just like in the first hour.  Gonna take a break from this game for a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't recommend this at the moment...the first 40 minutes felt like pulling teeth...I loved the demo when it came out and I've only just got a new PC so I thought I'd finally get round to playing this lil' gem...heard a lot of good things...blah blah...But man...this game is filler city...!! I know it's not going to be a long game but seriously,,,so many cutscenes...so many purposefully slow bits where you can't skip! Levels load in and end with a boat ride...the slowest boat ride in existence!! Honestly...I spent the whole time thinking "yeah sure...but where's the game?" You get a 2 min tutorial surrounded by about 5-6 minutes of text, cutscenes and the like...it's painful. Gonna persist through it and see what it turns out to be like but first impressions are not good. I have no idea where I'm going and nothing feels good or rewarding...just weird and interesting...but not fulfilling as everything is so vague, Who knows...I'll update when I've completed it...5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: * The game never really challenges you - you just hack through it all. No strategy or skill ever required, at all.* Scenarios are a bit repetitive and bland. Despite a few good efforts in this direction, it still falls short when it comes to diversity. Puzzles are bland.* It this a product of love? the intro animation is good on its own, but is made in a completely different style, one which does not return ever, and clashes with the rest. It makes me think that authors didn't really  their product, nor believe in it. This is clearly no masterpiece, and doesn't even try to be.* It's short. This may be a good thing too, but be warned. It's a bit shallow.* In spite of the evocative "dark-setting" premise, the "story", or rather the little bit of a story that there is, turns out to be bland, and adheres to the most trite standards. Hero is heroic, resurges from ruin, defeats evil, saves all, the end. No, there's no consequence in using apparently evil, possessed weapon or anything.* Basic mechanics are really fun to play.* MOST IMPORTANTLY: The controls/animations feel REALLY good. Responsive, controllable, a pleasure to play. It's FUN.* (this is only important for a few people but: bonus points for being perfectly playable even with just a  keyboard and no mouse -- which doesn't detract from it being enjoyable with any other controller)* graphics/style is amazing, That is, if you tolerate fake "pixel art", the one where sprites are rotated / re-scaled at will. In spite of the resolution being artificially so low that it leaves you yearning for more details at times, the visuals are  just great and will entertain you.* The sound is just amazing, including voices. Very evocative (like the graphics). No, really, it's consistently impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: very short game but WOW the most awesome game play i had for a while especially the boss. it really feel like you are a great warrior. then again the game is very short so yeah buy it if you have no idea what to play. i just spot this on the steam page front and said why not since it is on sale.definitely will look forward the devs next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I have to recommend Olija because the central mechanic of throwing the Harpoon and pulling yourself to it feels so good and looks so cool. I finished the game on Steam Deck in 5 hours.The visual design never quite grew on me. It wasn't abstract or beautiful enough to engage my imagination, like Moonscars does as a pixel art comparison. But combat felt good and most animations were clear.The story was obtuse to me, but I think it's easy enough to enjoy as an ethereal mood piece that suggests a narrative more than tells one. To that end though, the cutscenes and story segments often felt slow and time wasting.But again, the Harpoon rules, you might like the visuals more than me, the bosses were pretty fun, I never felt stuck or lost, and there were some clever bits of level design and bite sized puzzles for sure. Glad I gave this one a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Olija as part of a bundle alongside "The Messenger" and "Katana Zero". I had absolutely no expectations from the game, and was greatly surprised. Great atmosphere and satisfying game mechanics. I have spend a similar amount of time on this and "Katana zero" and this was much better, never got old or repetitive and music was used better in this. It seems criminally unknown. I highly recommend anyone to give this game a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a bit of time growing on you, but this game is definitely worth playing through.It's one of these games where a clear artistic vision and narrative needed a medium, and it just happened to be VideoGame, but the (simple) gameplay still felt pleasant to me.Never figured out what those bottled ships were for tho. '-'

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most memorable games I've ever played. I first played it on game pass years ago and really liked it, but from time to time thought I wanted to buy it and re-experience and finally got around to it and it's an amazing game. It has really good exploration, decent combat, and a really fun central mechanic. But the real draw for me is its story - which is both in the type of story and execution (largely through gameplay with very few voiced lines) is just fantastic. Do play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed 4 hours of fun hack'n'slash-, adventure-, easy-puzzler-, brawler- gameplay exploring the excessively violent world of Terraphage. I felt (over)powerful at times and that was OK. I really didn't like the final boss fight which took me an additional hour, because it was a level of difficulty that I was entirely ill-prepared for. I bought the game thinking it had that anime style from the trailer in the cut-scenes and some pretty pixel art for the main gameplay. I was wrong and I am admittedly a bit disappointed. The trailer was awesome, yet the cut-scenes in the game and even the pixel art are mediocre. Somehow the visual style (lots of muted browns) and scenery (undefined black blobs on many screens), despite trying to be cinematic, fell flat for me. I actually looked for mods to improve the textures and sprites, but couldn't find any. The animation, music, and sound design on the other hand stood out as phenomenal. And the setting was fresh and intriguing. I also liked the gameplay centering on uninterrupted combos and teleportation with the harpoon, but I felt there could have been more variation in the enemies that required me to change up my tactics.I recommend getting Olija, because it is unique. But I'd try to get it on sale to account for its flaws and the short playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: : Takes ~4 hours to complete: The artstyle for this game is really nice. It feel perfect for the world. I feel like if the pixel art was higher resolution it would have fit the serious style of the story a bit better, but I'm being nit-picky.: The story is where this game shines. It's a story about a man named Lord Faraday who finds a harpoon of legend which is cursed by an ancient evil. The game has a good mix of audial, visual, and cinematic storytelling. It feels like there really is a world on the other side of your screen.: This Narrative 2D Platformer has a strong mix of mechanics which kept me engaged throughout the 4 hours of gameplay. The combat can feel really satisfying at times when you get a brutal combo on an enemy, but you can also just mash buttons for the most part. I think it could be better, but it was pretty fun for 4 hours.: The music perfectly fits the world and you can tell that it was made professionally. The sound design is really nice as well and contributes strongly to a good gamefeel.: This game has some fantastic world-building and a good mix of mechanics that will help you stay relatively engaged while you uncover the mysteries of Terraphage.This game is definitely worth a play if you can pick it up for $10 or less, and I encourage anybody who reads this to leave a review that fairly critiques the game so that hopefully the developers can learn and make an even better game next time!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This was a short but fun game. The story was sort of vague in its lore but it was enough to keep you interested. The combat and mechanics with the spear/harpoon were good. Overall, some good platforming and puzzling but nothing too crazy. More of an artistic expression of a game to me but it was a great experience and had some cool scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A cool little game of about 3 to 5 hours, with a quite unique style. The way the story is told, the gameplay, the music, the graphics, the "mise-en-scène".. All of this is both simple and smartly striking.Maybe i'm too biased towards this genre, but it feels like dark souls is beginning to be an old reference. This game feels like it might be inspired by it without knowing it, or just borrowing ideas like it's a source of practical designs and that's it. For example, it's far away from the classic narrative of souls like, but it's pulling on the same strings to tell the story. The tone and the story, while told mostly by environment and laconic characters, reminds me of an old hollywood movie, with the main character quickly becoming the brave hefty hero. You could draw the same kind of parallels regarding combat, sound design, progression.. In short, it's nice and original :)
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Not too long, but also not too short. Just the right amount of feeling satisified.The Story is servicable, nothing unnecessiarily convoluded, but i wanted a tid more.The Gameplay is overall good, but has some problems here and there (those might just be personal preferences tbh)Overall A good short game that definietly feels you satisfied/10
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a epic action plattformer, in the spirit of the original prince of persia and first two zelda games. Dispatching enemies with the rapier, spear and the musket (shotgun) is truely satifieing. Levels and Bosses are fair well balanced. This is part Blackrock from the original Blizzard, this is a part of Sid Meirs Pirates! , truely awsome. I hope the developer will do some sort of Pirate Simulation the future. Poeple buy this game! Crafting is done without feeling tedious. Puzzle elements, plattforming and enemy placement is well crafted and it is fun explore the levels. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: "Olija" is a visually stunning action-adventure where you play as a downtrodden noble that shipwrecks and finds himself in a mysterious eastern naval-world. He gets his hands on a magical harpoon and fends off tar-like eldritch creatures ultimatively seeking his way home and and socialising with the downtrodden souls and an old dynasty living there. The atmosphere of the game is very dense and the worldbuilding is tragic and mysterious. The controls and the movement are solid for the most part (some platforming passages can be tricky) and combat feels good. It is ultimatively not very long and not that challenging and the collectibles (which is treasure for the most part) are not that impaortant, because there is not too much to unlock in the main hub area (but is fitting to the story of the game because "Lord Faraday" initially went on his quest to find riches in order to aid his land).Gameplaywise it is a very solid and aesthetically a sublime experience. Definetly check this out if you are a fan of 2D-Platforming-Action-Adventures with a bold setting!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a very hand-crafted kind of game that will remind you of Another World but with modern-yet-simple gameplay elements. I love that they kept it so concise and honest because that might just be its main appeal. The game has a both very classic and very nuanced story to tell you, it also wants to awe your senses with its atmosphere, and to thrill you with combat and puzzles that are only "difficult" enough that you feel a brain tickle when you beat them.Olija succeeds in all it tries to do. It knows there are games out there that could do all that better for you but still hopes that you'll appreciate that it's willing to spoil you just for a little while.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, neat, self-contained mostly-linear platformer-explorer.6-8 hours of story and exploration. There's perhaps a bit of slowness at the start but once you "level up" a bit things get moving. I found the story (and ) to be engaging enough to get me through the boss battles. Even the The exploration music was quiet and contemplative; well done. Overall art style is a treat however I found the juxtaposition of the different intro video style, cutscene style, and in-game style to be confusing. Given this isn't a AAA it's completely forgivable. I wish they had either stuck with a same/similar style or made it blend in better somehow. I also experienced a few lockups when transitioning from "gameplay" -> "cutscene" on the Steam Deck that caused me to hard restart the game but I never lost much/any progress due to the excellent checkpointing/save system.There's some side collectables and achievements but nothing that is hard to 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but a nice game. Story was palatable, and the words that weren't spoken were the most enjoyable. There seems to be lore you have to piece together yourself, which makes for some interesting theories. Gameplay was tight, and I loved the incorporation of mobility into combat, which was robust in itself. One of the most enjoyable aspects for me was the soundtrack. Good stuff.Overall, 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Good action-platformer is always appreciated, but when it's build around easy to learn, yet original mechanic, and feature so unique atmosphere, it's a must play. Awesome case study of action game that is truly driven by romantic, epic story. Crisp combat, distinctive characters, nostalgic landscapes, thoughtful sound design and mysterious setting to explore  - perfect for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: The combat was mostly just spamming the attack button while close to enemies, and there weren't any challenging puzzles. There's a roll/dodge you can do, and I played the game without using it. It only took me four hours to beat. The bosses are fun though.This game would be pretty mid were it not for the atmosphere and sound design which are phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: You ever find a game that, despite being quite short and simple, has a story and action that hooks you in much deeper than expected? That's Olija. Goldenhearted, slightly spooky, a slant of fairytale weirdness thrown over a passel of sailors' stories. Best harpoon in a metroidvania ever and possibly the best harpoon period. If a sequel's coming, it'll be played as soon as humanly possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the prettiest games I've ever played, and the gameplay was so fluid and responsive.Fighting is intuitive and feels fantastic. Exploration is a joy because every screen is so beautiful.And beyond that, the sense of community building up in the little shipwreck town was an amazing experience.Recommended for anyone looking for an adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is perhaps the epitome of short but sweet. I was really surprised by the tight gameplay and especially how well combat was handled, the weapons were varied and the animations made my fortune seeking Lord Faraday look awesome (there's also hats!).The game initially seemed quite open ended but instead is quite sensibly crafted into a series of fun levels that the game subtly steers you through and while the difficulty never really poses a challenge there are some fun mechanic focused bosses and ponderous puzzles.I really enjoyed how the story was told in Olija, the atmosphere was created through a series of scripted actions and the narrative was presented in a minimalistic but effective way, where dialogue was used sparsely and seemed better for it. The pixel art is basic but far from ugly and it is a testament to the games design how characters and relationships are formed through unspoken gestures despite the initial perceived constraint's in the games art style.Overall, this is a great indie experience I would urge anyone to play. Although my time was short in Olija, I found myself lost in it from the outset.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Decently fun action platformer. Controls mostly tight, except the harpoon throwing is a little wonky since it only accepts 8 directions. Throwing and shooting diagonally can be a pain. There were also some weird bugs when I played, sometimes at the start of an area certain sounds wouldn't play, like the background noise or the harpoon thrusts, and one time the game crashed during a loading screen (didn't lose any progress though). So minor stuff, not a big deal.Music was pretty cool.Not nearly worth 15 dollars full price, though. There's not enough gameplay (my run lasted 6 hours, and there are a decent amount of cutscenes), and the story is serviceable, not fantastic. Not an unforgettable gaming experience by any measure. Get it when it's on sale or something, and actually worth it to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5The game is pretty good, hence the positive review, BUT I feel like it doesn't meet it's potential. The gameplay has a very heavy set focus on the combat, having tons of combat encounters when the fighting is quite bland, and uninteresting. The BEST part of the game, the part I was most excited for, was the platforming via the harpoon.While it was a lot of good fun, it doesn't go full force into it, like I was hoping it might. It has a few sections of tight platforming, needing to string together throws and teleports, but it is more often than not a very simple puzzle, or just a gap closer in the aforementioned bland combat. Another nitpick I have with the game, is how it's bogged down by things constantly slowing the game down to a grinding halt, making me roll my eyes every single time I encountered it. Namely "Cutscenes" when still in pixel graphics being nonskippable, such as the boat arriving to the island, EVERY SINGLE TIME. Show it to me once, and then don't show it again-- I get how I got there. Also, if you are going to have that, remove the invisible walls from around the boat, if I wanna be stupid and throw myself into the water and lose some health as a result, you should allow it. Invisible walls are just lazy.I think the game is a good time, a fun time to just sit back and relax. It'll only take you a few hours to beat, so I recommend getting it when it's on sale. Again, although I was ripping on the game quite a bit, it's still a good time, but I think my above statements would elevate the game from a 3/5 to a 4/5. I'd love to see what the devs are capable of, if they lean off of the combat and more into the platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: More people should be talking about this game. Combat  is very fluid and hits hard.  Using the harpoon to warp around and switching to melee combat is seamless. It will make you feel like the John Wick of fishermen.Puzzles are rather easy but creative. They allow for quick "think on your feet" moments that adds to the  the game nicely. Only criticism I have hear is practically all the puzzles rely on the teleport feature of your weapon, a bit more variety would have been enjoyable.Story is a bit hard to follow and nothing super original, but works well with the art style and voice acting. It is a short (100% in about 8 hours) but i would buy it again even at full price. Overall very enjoyable experience that enjoys much more attention than what it has received thus far.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Perhaps a little shortlived in some respects, when the game really starts testing your exploration it seems to bring a level to a close. A latter gadget teases at complexity but is only used for a handful of simple puzzles. The satisfying combat does challenge during boss encounters but otherwise feels trifling; sporadically tossing a handful of weak enemies at the player. Combat also, like the exploration, does not invite much use of the gadgets. A final negative of the combat is the superfluous 'crouch' and the largely useless combat roll, both simply get in the way and maybe should have just been removed. Mild spoilers but a climatic encounter also completely limits your use of anything bar the harpoon which is disappointing and feels like a real misstep, even if the fight is pretty good.However the presentation is FANTASTIC, the best way i could describe it is that it feels akin to something like Uncharted or any other AAA prestige action adventure title, it's definitely Olija's USP. It goes for a 'minimalist' narrative but unlike say Hyper Light Drifter does not come of as pretentious or totally incoherent and has a handful of deft 'interactive storytelling' gimmick moments that work wonderfully. Basically Olija is Hyper Light Drifter but good.Art is great, especially the animation, but the pixel art does fall apart slightly when the camera pulls back, though these moments are rare, 2 or 3 in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: As long as you go into this game know it's not super long and it's somewhat of a metroid light, you'll have an amazing time. With character design like Nidhogg plus and a style and set up reminiscent of Out of this Wolrd/Another World. Very little text and purposeful unintelligible voice acting give this game a great mood as well. 9/10 great stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little adventure to go on, a solid game play experience, and such a good vibe. The best thing about this game is how solidly it creates a sense of experiencing the world you're in. From the first loading screen tableau, to character's voice, the music, movement, the whole thing is a total work. My one small caveat, and it's not  a spoiler, but
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Uuhh. It's fine. The demo did not make this look quite as story-focused as it actually is - several levels exist purely for cutscenes, there's slow loading and then slow boat rides to every new location, even most of the boss fights feel like playable cutscenes to an extent and the game does not really try to challenge you much (I died twice in total, both during boss fights) and on top of that I found the character sprites kind of hard to read at times - a lot of them look really samey especially with the matching outfits. So some of the story didn't quite feel... conveyed, even with for as much emphasis was put on it. The game also deletes your save upon beating the game which means I get to be left without four achievements I'm definitely not replaying the entire game just to get, which, okayyyy whatever then. There -is- a lot to like about this game - you're given a lot of combat options, and combat is fluid and fast-paced, the platforming and puzzles never get too intense but they are satisfying enough, there's secrets and exploration (for what purpose other than achievements I'll never know - none of the three bonus collectible types appear to do anything), the game looks gorgeous and the animation is top-notch, it -feels- good to play. It's just a shame there isn't really much to play. Basically four quarters of the main map that each have one small cutscene area and one large area, you collect the keys, fight the boss, move onto the next, and a (fairly underwhelming) final boss once you're done. It's... weirdly underdeveloped for how much time was clearly put into making the combat mechanics feel good. The harpoon gets a lot of use in both platforming and combat and it feels great, and while I didn't end up jiving much with the other subweapons besides the rapier I can see them all having uses. There's a number of craftable hats that each give different abilities, you can upgrade your health, the depth in the gameplay and progression system just feels unwarranted for how lacking in challenge and length the game as a whole is, though, and it's a shame really.It's definitely not a bad game - I enjoyed my time with it, though I don't think I'll be replaying it, and it might be priced a bit high for how little of it there is - but it's also not a game I can highly recommend either. Would be a certifiable "meh" if steam offered that option, but considering the quality of what is here, I did enjoy my time with it if nothing else.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, combat felt good, music and ambiance is also really well done, felt truly immersed. I only encountered a little bug causing the character to be stuck in the ground but that was the only fault i could find. It really goes to show that graphics do not have to be the best for the game to be great.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, it was a bit too short perhaps, but it was still an enjoyable experience. The platforming is fun, considering there is only one consistent way of doing it.Fights are ok, tho mostly i wore the same hat for half the game and just spammed attack, that can carry you through most of the game, though bossfights do require a bit more complex fighting. Graphics are pretty good, and the animations are smooth.Overall, 7/10, some aspects can be off sometimes, but it was still pretty decent.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: =Olija is a very beautiful indie game that is well worth it's price point. This game is about a tale of a captain who had been caught in a shipwreck and awakes to his crew vanishing. He stumbles upon a cursed spear which he wields for the rest of the game(to put it simply with no spoilers). While this story tells the basis of its story through its dialogue, I feel as if most of the story is told through its environment, its world building. The environment tells its eerie tone its old broken down buildings, and caves full of corpses. The music in this game is exceptional and adds to this eerie tone. This game's art design and music are all factors that allow for this game to flourish in its story. =While it may have a simple 8 bit like design, the animations are so well done that you are able to interpret any and every movement, which brings me to my next point... the gameplay! The gameplay in this game is a solid 10/10. The way you are able to move in this game while attacking is fantastic! Being able to pull off incredible combos in a room full of enemies is a very satisfying experience, and that satisfaction is very fun. However, there is some to be desired in the aspect of the wearable "magic hats" in the game. There is one specific magic hat in the game that is clearly stronger than others(which I will not name), where you would rather want to use this hat over the others. -While you could use the other hats during different runs of the game, I think that brings another issue into the game.. There is no real replay ability for the game in the fact that it is a generally linear experience with set rooms that never change. For most players, this shouldn't be that much of an issue, but it can be for those who hope to replay it for a slightly different experience. For the price of $15, it is worth it, but it is slightly disappointing to see that there isn't that much of a reason to go back and replay it. =This game is an overall 9/10 with the only main issue being that it struggles to run at times, where it would crash while attempting to load into the map.. which is a shame. Without this issue, this game would be a 9.5/10. The crashing I will say is at a very minimal state, but it still persists which isn't a pleasing situation to deal with. It is still worth it to pick it up and try for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Combat and movement is satisfying. The gameplay never got boring, and new mechanics are added regularly throughout this 5-6 hour journey.The mood is nicely crafted. The artwork, pacing and music work well together and create an immersive adventure.The plot is simple, yet has an interesting little story to tell, and at the end of it, you even get a glimpse of the world's interconnections.All in all, a pretty good platformer. One of the better ones I've played in recent years, albeit a bit short.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of old platform style games from the Playstation era. I would love to give it a thumbs up but seeing as how it has frozen and crashed twice during my initial playthrough I can't say that the optimization is there. This is disappointing because the atmosphere and design is very interesting and compelling. I have an above average system and can run triple A games with little to no issue. I am not sure what is wrong with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros.:- Smooth. Easy to play.- Some small Easter eggs.- Curious world.- Everything you want from the indie project.Cons.:- A bit off with the story at the beginning.Olija is an interesting yet underdeveloped game. The story could be told in a more fulfilling way. The levels could be more complicated. The puzzles more challenging. The game reminds of other indie projects, of tasks from other games and feels like the developers cut half of the content.Still, the game doesn't leave any negative feeling or emotions. And the last encounter with the boss is quite curious since you may feel like events in Olija are not the first time happening, that Faradey actually been there over and over again, and the vicious circle had repeated multiple times. Until he finally departed with Olija.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Cinematic but in a good way. It's really great at building tension and making you feel like a space is more than an arena for gameplay. The story is pretty simple, but it's kind of incredible how much you end up reading into the little 16bit faces of these characters by the end of it. There's also a really good romance subplot that feels earned entirely through unexpected mechanical shifts. It's also not afraid to use cutscenes, which is kind of rare for an indie game. Like proper, cutting to pieces of animation that have been edited in sequence cutscenes that are just dripping with character. The puzzles are good and the level design is well suited to teaching you how to use all your little abilities, but the early weapons never really felt that useful outside of the level where you get them, and the combat is never particularly challenging. I died three times (twice to the final boss and once because I got stunlocked in a pool of electrical water that I didn't see rushing into a room),  and I was never that close to dying anywhere else in the game. Check it out though, the vibes are immaculate and you get special combat abilities by building a collection of various hats which like, c'mon, pretty great.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a good game, but it does have some issues. My game crashed two times, and I've never had that happen with a retro styled game. I also wish you could upgrade your weapons with better stats and whatnot. Would make it a bit more fun. That said, the atmosphere is great, some of the levels and bosses are really cool and the music was good. Worth it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is an action platforming game with simple game mechanics and a great story.It's a short and not too challenging game, yet it hooked me in for the game's whole duration. I almost finished the whole thing in one sitting and also managed to 100% it in the meantime. Took me exactly 5 hours.I Can only recommend it, but try to buy it when it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR = Lots of games are done in pixel art style.  This game succeeds in being pixel art.It's tempting to be particularly critical when assessing pixel art games, because the gaming market is so full of them.  Olija manages to distinguish itself from the pack, and I noticed two things in particular that helped it do so.For me a common frustration of pixel platformers is that I find them difficult to become immersed in.  When I'm following a visual narrative I want the creator to take me somewhere and the lack of dimensions in pixel art often stops me from feeling this way.In Olija, cut-scenes, menus, levels,  is so consistently detailed and heavily layered.  There are always multiple layers in front of and behind the main character e.g. to show weather and background world events (e.g. layers of fog, or critters running in front of the "camera").  These extra visual layers really help to add texture and depth to the world.As in most pixel art games, Olija separates each screen presented to the player into "scenes" - with the player moving to the edge of one scene before the view will jump to the next.  It can be difficult to remain focussed on the narrative when games do this, because each view is treated (and presented) in isolation.  Olija overcomes this issue by keeping multiple scenes active around the player.  For example when Faraday throws his harpoon and embeds it in a creature, he can then "zip" straight to the creature's position.  Often, progressing through levels requires you to cast the harpoon across multiple screens to hit a particular creature so that you jump to its position and move forwards.  This is a neat trick which forces the player to consider each scene as part of a whole.
