_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a game developed by Skeleton Crew Studio and Thomas Olsson and published by those legends at Devolver DigitalThe game offers some nice graphics and environments, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the same and has a really great aestheticOlija overall, however, is a fun game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a good action-adventure and to play in short bursts
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: looks its best in motion. With the backdrop of its unique world, mysterious characters, and minimal voice acting, its fluid combat and simple (yet effective) pixel art starts to shine. The story beats are impactful, and typically very cinematic, which fits well with the game's swashbuckling themes. A very enjoyable experience, definitely recommend it, especially for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good action adventure game. The combat is surprisingly great, the setting and lore are interesting, and the levels are fun to go through, with a design similar to the old Prince of Persia 1 and 2 (with far easier platforming, though). The gameplay is overall very tight and well designed.The game has two major downsides IMO: The graphics style, with large chunky pixels of inconsistent quality that makes things hard to see in the middle of the combat, and the technical issues, such as the many freezes that required me to restart the game, or a bug that prevented me to use sub-weapons on the final boss fight. If you can get past this though, it's still very much worth it.I really hope the developer makes a sequel or expanded remake or something, because with a little more polish and better graphics, this has the potential to be a top tier game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, interesting world, blending something vaguely Spanish explorer-y with something vaguely Japanese-y in a way that works surprisingly well.  Gameplay and animations are fun, if on the easy side.  Every now and then an area doesn't load properly and I need to restart it, but no progress is lost and it doesn't happen very often.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: There are two things I immediately avoid when choosing a game to play: platforming and pixel graphics. (Or make that three, rogue-like included). I decided to give Olija a go because of a project. The experience was short and worth it. I was drawn in the atmosphere. Even when you know that you're just watching a few moving pixels, the small intricate movements and details can pull you in and even convince you that the characters are conveying their emotions and grief through the screen. There's no difficulty curve. If there is, it's just minimal. You can get the grasp of exploration and combat fairly easily. The actual platforming aspect of the game isn't that hard either. In fact, it can be considered very balanced and a much appreciated welcome for non-platforming enthusiasts like me. The combat is engaging and fast-paced. The only thing I don't like about the game is the non-interactive menu. You can only see the icons of the items and equipment you have. You can't highlight any of them or see their individual descriptions or tooltips. That means that every tutorial pop-up you'll see must be read and learned. (or just consult a guide)Olija is a short but wonderful experience. It's not outstanding and hardcore platforming masochists may even find the game too easy or boring. However, for average platformer fans or non-fans at all, the game offers a great balance of narrative, atmosphere, exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija paints a mysterious and dreadful world that I wanted to see more of.  It is very short at about five hours.  There’s little to do after the game is over, but that short run is oh so sweet.  Engrossing art style, narrative, and sound design are accompanied with satisfying gameplay primarily powered by the magical spear.  It’s abilities, though simple, push combat and exploration above your basic hack and slash platformer.If you're on the fence, try the demo.  It's good example of the gameplay and narrative.For some reason this game created a log file in my AppData\LocalLow that was 12GB big and didn't delete it when I uninstalled the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really short and sweet action adventure game. Great music and ambiance. Really fun but relatively simple and easy combat. This feels like the start of what would have been a great series of games back in the day. Lots to build and expand upon, both mechanically and story wise. I'd love to see and play the continued adventures of Lord Faraday.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a very tight, intriguing, satisfying, and unfortunately (or perhaps bittersweetly) short experience. Combat feels satisfying with meaty strikes and enough variety of combat style to keep things interesting. Movement options are an obviously emphasized feature and all feel great although somewhat disorienting at first. The art style of the game is an obvious draw - although simple it is very evocative and expressive. The music is also somewhat simple but helps set the mood and feels appropriate to the setting.The story of Olija is somewhat ambiguous as a deliberate choice. It provides just enough of a sense of intrigue to get the player interested in exploring without bogging down the gameplay. It won't win any awards but it certainly piqued my interest and kept me engaged throughout.All in all Olija is an excellent experience I would recommend to anyone who likes short but well-crafted games that offer some unique mechanics to play around with.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: pretty short as you can see by my playtime, but well worth it. not a hard game by any means but i had a good time playing it.pros-great sound design-very meaty attacks-animations and art style look nice-combat feels goodcons-puzzles felt a bit lacking as they were very easy-i felt as though the bosses were too easy, but the boss fights were still fun
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: The day this game became available on Steam, I played the demo, and not even a half hour later bough the game because of how much I liked it.  I must say, entirely worth the price.This is a beautifully made game.  I came into it expecting more content than there is, but I'm probably spoiled by the other games I play.Very minor spoilers ahead.Lets go over the pros and cons:+ + + Actually real fun game-play.+ + + Combat is fluid and overall fun.+ + + Controls very responsive, no BS.+ + Story is engaging and intriguing.+ I feel like the cut-scenes work perfectly, maybe a couple are a bit long, but it's definitely bearable.+ A fun amount and usage of side-weapons, although I didn't use the ranged ones much.+ Platforming works perfectly with this game.+ + Really, really good sound design.  Use headphones.+ + Boss battles are fun and well-made.(coming from someone with 100% in all 3 Dark Souls games and ER)- - - Many areas you cannot go back to once already explored, thus locking you out of some missed collectables.- There is only 1 (main) weapon upgrade, which isn't really useful for combat, but rather used for a few puzzles.- Not enough uses for the money you get - too few main-base upgrades.  I had so much leftover money by the end.- The health upgrade shop feels a little useless, and it seems like there could have been more shops at main-base, but not sure what for since the game is not very long.A suggestion based on the last con mentioned I have is to have some kind of weapon upgrade/smith at the main base that requires materials gotten from exploration.  A shop you can upgrade and just another place to use money.  Would make it possible to amp up difficulty of later game enemies if the game were to be expanded upon.That all being said, I love the game, it was very fun, but I nearly got 100% in under 3 hours.Lastly, the Fandom wiki is basically non-existent.  I'll be changing that :)I recommend this game fully.  I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I really liked this one and is an early contender for my personal GOTY. Pretty simple game overall, with really fascinating world-building, characters, and a sublime sound design. Hard to fault it for anything, and I thought the length was perfect as well. Every weapon in this game feels good to use, and the main Harpoon is a joy to wield, both in combat and traversal. There are also some very intimate moments in this game that I won't spoil, that is done extremely well, and you rarely see that in games. Some haunting set pieces, and very easy collectibles that are pretty meaningful I'd say. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: The game has beautiful pixel art and great storytelling done mostly with music and artwork. I especially loved the silent interactions between your character and Olija. The atmosphere the game builds through the art and soundscape is fantastic.I have played a lot of games of this type and they are often intended to be brutally difficult leaving you quite frustrated. This isn't one of those games with the difficulty ramping up just enough to keep it challenging. The combat was very fluid with varied weapons and combos.It took me about 6 hours to finish the game missing a couple optional collectables. This is the 2nd game listed on steam for this developer and I hadn't heard of the first. I really look forward to what the developer does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Olija

_childDocuments_.review: Olija is a game about Faraday's quest, a man shipwrecked then trapped in the mysterious country of Terraphage. Armed with a legendary harpoon, he and other castaways try to leave this hostile country to return to their homelands.
